title: The Silver hover can show only one sentence, and plans keep agreeing several
description:
Filed by Psylocke on 2026-08-25, at the navigator's instruction. P0 set by the navigator, not assumed:
it is blocking two other P0s, neither of which can be planned correctly until this is settled.

## The mechanism

packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts:744 is the whole of it:

  const note = SILVER_NOTES.find((candidate) => candidate.when(facts));
  return note ? note.say(facts) : null;

The Silver hover shows EXACTLY ONE sentence, ever - the first note in SILVER_NOTES whose 'when'
holds. The contract states this deliberately at :235-241: 'in precedence order: the first whose when
holds is the one shown.'

## The cost, twice in one day

Two plans have now been agreed with the navigator that the mechanism cannot honour, and both were
built faithfully and both failed verification on 2026-08-25:

- ah-awcm chose, as a recorded user-facing decision (round 2, question 5): 'O1 - taking, then gift,
  then given-away. Money in before money out, and a taking is the unit's own order so it leads.'
  That is an ordering of several sentences shown TOGETHER. There is no 'then'. Observed: a unit with
  both a TAKE and a GIVE shows only the taking sentence; a unit with a TAKE and no month-long order
  shows only the no-month-long-order sentence, and the take sentence appears only once WORK is added
  and that higher note stops applying.

- ah-moq3 placed 'shared-silver-pays-orders' immediately below 'shared-silver-pays-upkeep' with the
  reasoning 'upkeep is the more specific of the two'. A studying unit whose neighbour shares
  satisfies BOTH, so the upkeep sentence wins and the orders sentence - the one explaining why the
  unit is not short, which was the entire point of that bead - is unreachable.

Both are the same mistake: a planner reasoning about which sentence is 'more specific' or which
should come 'first', when the real question is that only one is shown at all.

## Why the existing guard cannot catch it

ah-hvt8 replaced a 25-branch hand-ordered first-match chain with SILVER_NOTES precisely so that a
shadowed note would fail a test rather than silently never appear. Its guard requires every note to
carry an example() it must win for.

That guard cannot catch this class. Each note's example() sets only its OWN field, so every note wins
for its own example and NO COMBINATION OF FACTS IS EVER EXERCISED. A note that is unreachable only
when two things are true at once is invisible to it - which is exactly both defects above.

This is not a regression. The chain ah-hvt8 replaced was also first-match, so one-sentence-only is
long-standing behaviour. What is new is the rate at which plans are being agreed against it.

## What needs deciding, and it is the navigator's

Not chosen here. The two obvious shapes, and a third:

1. The hover shows SEVERAL sentences - all whose 'when' holds, in SILVER_NOTES order, with some cap.
   Makes ah-awcm's O1 buildable as written and fixes ah-moq3 without re-asking anything. Needs a
   decision about how many, and about pairs that would read redundantly together.
2. The hover stays ONE sentence, and the contract is made loud enough that no planner agrees an
   ordering again - plus ah-moq3's and ah-awcm's wording decisions are re-asked of the navigator.
3. Some notes combine rather than compete - a small number of 'and also' pairs, everything else
   first-match.

Whatever is chosen, the example()-based guard needs strengthening in the same pass, or this recurs:
it must exercise combinations, not one field at a time.

## Blocks

ah-moq3 (P0, plan:revise) and ah-awcm (P0, plan:revise) should both follow whatever this settles
rather than each deciding the contract on their own.
design:
## Context `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts:744` is the whole mechanism: ```ts const note = SILVER_NOTES.find((candidate) => candidate.when(facts)); return note ? note.say(facts) : null; ``` **The Silver hover shows exactly one sentence, ever** — the first note whose `when` holds. The contract says so deliberately at `:235-241`: *"in precedence order: the first whose `when` holds is the one shown."* **Two plans were agreed against that in one day, both built faithfully, and both failed verification on 2026-08-25:** - **`ah-awcm`** recorded, as a user-facing decision, *"O1 — taking, then gift, then given-away. Money in before money out, and a taking is the unit's own order so it leads."* That is an ordering of sentences shown **together**. There is no "then". Observed: a unit with a `TAKE` and a `GIVE` shows only the taking sentence; a unit with a `TAKE` and no month-long order shows only the no-month-long-order sentence, and the take sentence appears only once `WORK` is added and the higher note stops applying. - **`ah-moq3`** placed `shared-silver-pays-orders` below `shared-silver-pays-upkeep` reasoning that *"upkeep is the more specific of the two"*. A studying unit whose neighbour shares satisfies **both**, so the orders sentence — the one explaining why the unit is not short, which was that bead's entire point — is unreachable. Both are the same mistake: **a planner reasoning about which sentence is "more specific" or should come "first", when only one is shown at all.** ### How often notes overlap — measured, not assumed `SILVER_NOTES` has **30 members**. The ten `doubt-*` notes all read `silver.doubt`, so at most one of those fires. **The other twenty are independent flags**, and a single unit can satisfy many: > A starving unit in a full hex is fed by its own food (step 1), then the hex's faction food (step > 2), then a faction-mate's silver (step 4), then the faction's unclaimed fund (step 7) — and may > have received a gift besides. That is **six notes at once**, and it is an ordinary unit. So the two failures are the mild end of the problem, not the whole of it. ### Why the existing guard cannot catch it `ah-hvt8` replaced a 25-branch hand-ordered chain with `SILVER_NOTES` precisely so a shadowed note would fail a test rather than silently never appear, by requiring every note to carry an `example()` it must win for. **That guard cannot catch this class**: each `example()` sets only its own field, so every note wins for its own example and **no combination of facts is ever exercised**. A note unreachable only when two things are true at once is invisible to it — which is exactly both defects. **This is not a regression.** The chain `ah-hvt8` replaced was also first-match; one-sentence-only is long-standing. What is new is the rate at which plans are agreed against it. **This bead blocks `ah-moq3` and `ah-awcm`** (both P0, both `verification:failed`), wired as bd dependencies. Neither can be planned correctly until this is settled, and both should follow it rather than each deciding the contract alone. When this lands: the hover says everything that is true, no note can be shadowed by construction, and the guard proves it. ## Files to change, and what to reuse Two files: `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts` and `packages/shared/src/workspace/UnitTooltip.tsx`, plus `unitTooltip.test.ts`. No core changes, nothing generated, no wasm. ### `unitTooltip.ts:744` — every sentence that holds ```ts /** * Every explanation that applies, one per line, in `SILVER_NOTES` order. * * **Not the first that applies.** Two plans were agreed against that contract in one day and both * failed verification: a planner reasons about which sentence is "more specific" when the real * question was that only one was ever shown (`ah-x36v`). A note can no longer be shadowed by * another, by construction - which is also why the guard in `unitTooltip.test.ts` changed shape. */ function silverNote(facts: SilverFacts): string | null { const said = SILVER_NOTES.filter((note) => note.when(facts)).map((note) => note.say(facts)); return said.length > 0 ? said.join("\n") : null; } ``` **`note` stays a `string`.** Making it `string[]` would change `UnitSummary`'s shape and every consumer and test that reads `summary.silver.note`, for no gain over a newline. Stated so it is not re-litigated. **The contract comment at `:235-241` must be rewritten in the same commit.** It currently says the opposite of what the code will do, and it is the sentence both failed plans were reasoning from. ### `workspace/UnitTooltip.tsx:95-97` — the newlines must survive ```tsx {summary.silver.note ? (

{summary.silver.note}

) : null} ``` A `\n` in JSX text collapses to a space, so **the join above is invisible without a change here.** Add `whitespace-pre-line` to that `className`: it preserves newlines and still collapses runs of spaces, so every single-sentence note is unaffected. **`packages/shared` has no jsdom**, so no unit test can prove this renders as separate lines. The string is testable; the rendering is a human check, and it is in *Validation*. ### The four upkeep-source notes become one Under the new contract a unit fed from four sources shows four near-identical lines. The navigator chose to collapse them. **These four are retired**, with their present sentences: | id | line | sentence today | |---|---|---| | `own-food-covers-upkeep` | `:503` | `This unit's own food covers 8 of its upkeep.` | | `faction-food-covers-upkeep` | `:543` | `Faction food in this hex covers 12 of this unit's upkeep.` | | `shared-silver-pays-upkeep` | `:575` | `A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays this unit's upkeep.` | | `unclaimed-covers-upkeep` | `:608` | `The faction's unclaimed silver covers 10 of this unit's upkeep.` | replaced by one member in the **earliest** of their four positions: ```ts // Who actually paid this unit's maintenance, in the game's own payment order: its own food // (step 1), the hex's faction food (step 2), a faction-mate's silver (step 4), the faction's // unclaimed fund (step 7). One note rather than four, because a unit fed by several sources // satisfies several and would otherwise show four near-identical lines (`ah-x36v`). { id: "upkeep-paid-by", when: ({ silver, countUpkeep }) => countUpkeep && upkeepSources(silver).length > 0, say: ({ silver }) => `This unit's upkeep was paid by ${namesInAList(upkeepSources(silver))}.`, example: () => ({ … all four sources set … }) }, ``` with the sources composed in payment order, **shipping verbatim**: ```ts /** Who paid this unit's upkeep, in the game's own payment order, each with its figure. */ function upkeepSources(silver: UnitSilver): string[] { return [ silver.ownFoodCovered > 0 ? `its own food (${silver.ownFoodCovered})` : null, silver.factionFoodCovered > 0 ? `faction food here (${silver.factionFoodCovered})` : null, silver.sharedSilverCovered > 0 ? `a faction-mate's silver (${silver.sharedSilverCovered})` : null, silver.unclaimedCovered > 0 ? `the faction's unclaimed silver (${silver.unclaimedCovered})` : null ].filter((source): source is string => source !== null); } ``` `namesInAList` (`:196`) already produces `"a"`, `"a and b"`, `"a, b and c"` — **reuse it; do not write a second list joiner.** **`ownFoodCovered`'s guard moves with it.** `own-food-covers-upkeep` is gated on `forcedOwnFood === 0` today (a unit fed at step 5 has a non-zero `ownFoodCovered` too, and that branch would otherwise swallow the step-5 sentence — `ah-eacd`). **That guard must survive into `upkeepSources`**, or the forced-food sentence and this one both claim the same food. **`countUpkeep` still gates the whole note**, as all four did: with upkeep counting off there is no Upkeep row to explain (`ah-7cdt`). **The four `forced-*` and `*-contended` notes are NOT part of this family** and are untouched: `forced-own-food`, `forced-faction-food`, `food-contended`, `unclaimed-contended` say different things — food taken as a last resort, and a pool that may yet feed the unit. ### `unitTooltip.test.ts` — the guard changes shape **Shadowing is now impossible by construction**, so `ah-hvt8`'s "wins for its own example" becomes "appears for its own example" — same test, one word, still worth having because it proves a note's `when` is satisfiable at all. What replaces the shadowing guard is **one test that exercises every combination at once**: ```ts // `ah-x36v`: the old guard set one field per note, so no combination was ever tried and a note // unreachable only alongside another was invisible. With every fact true at once, every note // whose condition that satisfies must appear - which proves reachability against every other // note in a single case rather than 400 pairs. it("every note appears when every fact is true", () => { … }); ``` with **one such case per `doubt` value**, since those ten are mutually exclusive and a single all-facts-true object can carry only one. Build the facts with `aUnitSilver` (`ah-uhnd`) so a new field added to `UnitSilver` does not silently drop out of the case. ## Increments 1. **Every sentence that holds is shown.** RED, in `unitTooltip.test.ts`: - `a unit whose neighbour pays both ways is told both` — **`ah-moq3`'s failure**, asserting the two sentences joined by a newline, verbatim. - `a unit that takes, receives and destroys is told all three` — **`ah-awcm`'s failure**. - `a unit with one applicable note is unchanged` — every existing single-note test still passes, and this one names the property. GREEN: the `filter`/`join` in `silverNote`, and the rewritten contract comment. **Every existing test in the file must pass unedited** except where one asserts that a note is *absent* because another won — those are the defect, and each must be changed to assert both, **named in the PR**. 2. **The lines render as lines.** `whitespace-pre-line` on the note paragraph. No test; see *Validation*. 3. **The upkeep family becomes one sentence.** RED: `one source reads as one` (`This unit's upkeep was paid by its own food (8).`); `two sources read as a pair`; `all four read in the game's payment order` — all three verbatim; `a unit fed at step five is not also said to have paid with its own food` — the `forcedOwnFood` guard, moved; `with upkeep counting off nothing is said`. GREEN: `upkeepSources`, the merged note, and the four deletions. 4. **The guard exercises combinations.** RED: `every note appears when every fact is true`, one case per `doubt` value. GREEN: nothing — if it fails, a note's condition is unsatisfiable or contradicts another's, and **that is a finding to report, not to code around**. 5. **Unblock the two.** Not code: say in the PR that `ah-moq3` and `ah-awcm` can now be planned against the new contract, and that `ah-moq3`'s merged-sharing-note revision is no longer needed — the two sharing notes stay separate and both simply appear. ## The test plan | Test | File | Pins | |---|---|---| | `a unit whose neighbour pays both ways is told both` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | `ah-moq3`'s failure | | `a unit that takes, receives and destroys is told all three` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | `ah-awcm`'s failure | | `a unit with one applicable note is unchanged` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the common case did not move | | the five `upkeep-paid-by` tests | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the agreed wording at one, two and four sources, and the step-5 guard | | `every note appears when every fact is true` (×10 doubts) | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | **the guard that would have caught both failures** | | `appears for its own example` (×27) | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | every note's condition is satisfiable | | every existing test in the file | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | unedited, except the shadowing assertions named in the PR | ```bash pnpm run check:fast ``` No Rust, no generated types, no wasm rebuild. ## User-facing decisions Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-25. Mockups: `docs/ui/ah-x36v-hover-contract.html`. **How many sentences the hover shows.** Chosen: **every sentence that is true**, in `SILVER_NOTES` order. Nothing can be silently unreachable again, and both failed beads become buildable exactly as they were agreed, with no wording re-asked. *Rejected — a few named groups combine, everything else competes.* Fixes both reported cases and keeps the hover shortest, at the cost of a second concept in the table and a judgement each time a note is added about which group it joins. *Rejected — keep one sentence and state the contract loudly.* Nothing on screen changes, but both failed beads come back to have their wording re-decided, and the guard against a fourth instance becomes documentation rather than mechanism. **The six-line case.** With every sentence shown, a unit fed from four sources plus a gift gets six lines, four of them variants of who paid the upkeep. Chosen: **collapse the four upkeep-source notes into one**, which makes that unit three lines. *Rejected — no cap, show all six.* Trivial to state and to test, and rejected because four near-identical lines push the hover past the figures it explains. *Rejected — cap at three and count the rest.* Bounds the hover and changes no wording, and rejected because the reader cannot see what was dropped and which three survive depends on table order — so a note could still be unreachable in practice, which is the defect this bead exists to fix. **The collapsed sentence, shipping verbatim:** > `This unit's upkeep was paid by its own food (8).` > `This unit's upkeep was paid by faction food here (12) and a faction-mate's silver (20).` > `This unit's upkeep was paid by its own food (8), faction food here (12), a faction-mate's silver (20) and the faction's unclaimed silver (10).` *Rejected — keeping the "covers" verb* (`Its own food, faction food here … cover this unit's upkeep: 8, 12, 20 and 10.`), which turns sources and figures into two parallel lists the reader must match up. *Rejected — naming the payment order in the sentence* (`was paid, in the game's order, by …`): true, and rejected as five extra words on every multi-source hover that say nothing on the common single-source one. **The faction-mate's figure is shown**, though that sentence carries none today: every other source in the list carries its figure, and a bare entry among numbered ones reads as a gap rather than as a deliberate silence. The number is already on the record — it is what the lender's own column drops by. **How much of the guard this bead fixes.** Chosen: **exercise combinations properly**, so a note reachable only alongside another is proved reachable. Both failures were invisible to the current guard and this is what stops a third. *Rejected — pin only the two known overlaps*, which is smaller and certain but leaves every other overlap unguarded until one bites. *Rejected — file the guard separately*, which would ship the contract change with the guard that could not catch its own failure mode. ## Out of scope - **`ah-moq3` and `ah-awcm` themselves.** Both are blocked on this and are re-planned against it afterwards. In particular **`ah-moq3`'s merged-sharing-note revision is superseded** — under this contract the two sharing notes stay separate and both appear. - **The wording of any note other than the four collapsed ones.** Every other sentence ships exactly as it does today; this bead changes how many are shown, not what they say. - **The order of `SILVER_NOTES`.** It becomes reading order rather than precedence, and no member moves — except the merged upkeep note taking the earliest of its four positions. - **The `forced-*` and `*-contended` notes**, which are a different family. - **Whether any pair reads redundantly together.** Nothing in the current table was written to be read beside its neighbours, so some pairs may read oddly. **That is a real risk and it is what the human check in *Validation* is for** — a pair that reads badly is a finding to file, not something to fix by reintroducing precedence. ## Validation ```bash pnpm run check:fast ``` All green, and no existing test edited except the shadowing assertions named in the PR. **Then, by eye, and most of this bead's risk is here** — `packages/shared` has no jsdom, so nothing above proves what a reader actually sees. Load `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` and hover: - a unit with **one** applicable note: unchanged, one line, exactly as today; - **the `ah-moq3` case** — mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra, `City Guards (13303)` sharing, a neighbour ordered to `STUDY`: **two lines, on two lines**, the upkeep sentence and the orders sentence; - **a unit fed from several sources**: one `This unit's upkeep was paid by …` line naming each source and its figure, in payment order — **not** four separate lines; - turn **upkeep counting off** in Settings: every upkeep line disappears and the rest remain; - **read the multi-line hovers as English.** Two sentences written to stand alone may read repetitively together. Anything that reads badly is a finding — file it, and **do not fix it by making notes compete again**. **A human must confirm all five.** The first four are what the two failed beads will be re-verified against, and the fifth is the only check on a risk this change introduces. ## Known traps - **The contract comment at `:235-241` says the opposite of the new behaviour.** Both failed plans reasoned from it. Rewriting it is part of increment 1, not a tidy-up. - **`whitespace-pre-line` is what makes the second line visible.** Without it every joined note runs together on one line, and **no test in `packages/shared` can catch that** — no jsdom, and the change is a className. - **`forcedOwnFood === 0` must survive into `upkeepSources`.** `own-food-covers-upkeep` carries it because a unit fed at step 5 also has a non-zero `ownFoodCovered` (`ah-eacd`), and dropping it makes two notes claim the same food. There is a test named for it. - **Reuse `namesInAList` (`:196`).** A second list joiner is a second set of comma rules to keep in step. - **Some existing tests assert a note is ABSENT because another won.** Those encode the defect. Change them to assert both, and **name every one in the PR** — a silently edited assertion is indistinguishable from a regression being papered over. - **`ah-uhnd`'s `aUnitSilver` builder is how the all-facts-true case is built**, so a field added to `UnitSilver` later does not silently fall out of the guard. - **A failing `every note appears when every fact is true` is a finding**, not something to code around: it means a note's condition is unsatisfiable, or two conditions contradict. - **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`: no effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** That is why this bead's rendering half is a human check, and why the check is written out in full.
acceptance_criteria:
The navigator has decided whether the Silver hover shows one sentence or several, and the decision is recorded in the code beside SILVER_NOTES where the next planner will read it.

A note that is unreachable only because of a COMBINATION of facts fails a test rather than silently never appearing - the example()-based guard exercises combinations, not one field at a time.

ah-moq3's 'shared-silver-pays-orders' reaches a studying unit whose neighbour also covers its upkeep.

ah-awcm's taking sentence reaches a unit that also has a GIVE, and one with no month-long order.

If the answer is 'one sentence', ah-moq3's and ah-awcm's wording decisions have been re-asked of the navigator and their plans amended; if it is 'several', both build as originally written.

title: A sailing passenger's PRODUCE is not judged against the region the boat reaches
description:
Follow-up to ah-jk9h (gh-679), which shipped as de0d49f4 (#682).

## What shipped, and what it left

ah-jk9h removed the false error the reporter hit: a unit aboard a vessel whose captain has a SAIL
order is no longer told it cannot produce where it is standing (semantics.rs:3840 sails_away, guard
at :3941). It does this by SUPPRESSING the finding, because the plan believed the destination could
not be known - validate_orders_state is given no map.

That belief was wrong, and the navigator had already chosen the better answer in a second interview
minutes later: FOLLOW THE SAIL USING THE REPORT'S OWN REGIONS. The two crossed - Cyclops built and
merged the first answer before the second reached the bead.

## Why no map is needed

The parsed report carries everything a short sail needs:

  every region's products                      report/model.rs:246
  every region's exits, each with a direction
    and the neighbour's coordinate             model.rs:249, Exit at :77-83
  the region's own coordinate                  model.rs:234
  a SAIL's steps as typed directions           movement/orders.rs:19-26  MoveStep::Go(Direction)
  the idiom for exit text -> Direction         movement/graph.rs:391, Direction::parse at :101

So the captain's Go steps can be walked exit to exit through the report itself. The one limit is the
report's horizon: a sail leaving the regions the faction can see runs out of exits, and there
silence is the honest answer.

## What this bead would change

Replace the suppression with a destination check:

  a passenger sailing to a reported region  -> judged against THAT region's products
  a passenger sailing beyond the report     -> silent, as today
  a unit going nowhere                      -> unchanged, 'here' wording

with a second message, agreed verbatim with the navigator on 2026-08-25:

  cannot produce wood there: the region this vessel is sailing to produces fish

## The plan already exists

ah-jk9h's design field carries the full plan for exactly this work - carried_away, sail_destination,
the coordinate index built only when produce-not-here is enabled, the increments and the tests. It
was written after delivery and describes this bead, not what shipped. Lift it rather than starting
again. A copy is at .cerebro/scratchpad/ah-jk9h-plan-beast.md.

## For Moira

gh-679's earlier comment promised the fix would consult the projected region. What shipped does not.
This bead is what would make that promise true.

Unranked at P4.
design:
## Context

Follow-up to `ah-jk9h` (`gh-679`), which shipped as `de0d49f4` (#682). **The design below is
Beast's**, written for exactly this work after `ah-jk9h` had already merged; Xavier lifted it,
verified every citation against current `main`, and reconciled it with the code that shipped in the
meantime. Three corrections are marked **[corrected]** where they appear — one of them would have
reintroduced a defect the shipped code deliberately avoids.

### What shipped, and what this replaces

`ah-jk9h` removed the reporter's false error by **suppressing** the finding. Live on `main` today:

```rust
// semantics.rs:3840
fn sails_away(hex: &Hex<'_>, ordered: &Ordered<'_>, ruleset: &Ruleset) -> bool
// semantics.rs:3941 - the guard
if says_here && recipe.inputs.is_empty() && !sails_away(hex, ordered, ruleset) {
```

It works, and it is honest about its own limit: a passenger's `PRODUCE` is never judged at all.

**The navigator had already chosen the better answer minutes later — follow the `SAIL` through the
report's own regions — and the two crossed.** Cyclops built and merged the first answer before the
second reached the bead. This bead makes the second answer true. The full interview record is under
*User-facing decisions*, preserved from Beast's plan.

### Why no map is needed

The parsed report carries everything a short sail needs:

| | |
|---|---|
| every region's products | `report/model.rs:246` |
| every region's exits, each with a direction and the neighbour's coordinate | `model.rs:249`, `Exit` at `:77-83` |
| the region's own coordinate | `model.rs:234` |
| a `SAIL`'s steps as typed directions | `movement/orders.rs:19` — `MoveStep::Go(Direction)` |
| exit text → `Direction` | `Direction::parse`, used at `movement/graph.rs:391` |

So the captain's `Go` steps walk exit to exit through the report itself. The one limit is the
report's horizon: a sail leaving the regions the faction can see runs out of exits, and there
silence is the honest answer.

**When this lands, a passenger is judged against the region the boat reaches, and told nothing only
where the report cannot follow.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` only. No TypeScript, no new code, no Settings row, no type
crossing the boundary.

### What already exists and must be reused

- **`sails_away`** (`:3840`) — **[corrected]** Beast's plan predates it and would have an implementer
  write `carried_away` from scratch beside it, leaving two near-identical functions. It does not:
  **`carried_away` replaces `sails_away`**, same body, different return type. Delete `sails_away`.
- **`sailing_requirement(fleet, Some(ruleset))`** (`movement/mode.rs:243`) — **[corrected]** the test
  for whether a structure is a vessel. Beast's plan names `parse_fleet_kind` for this, in its
  reusables, an increment and a *Known trap*. **That is wrong and the shipped code says why**
  (`:3836-3839`): `parse_fleet_kind` (`mode.rs:191`) *"reads any non-empty kind as a one-hull fleet,
  so a fort would pass it and every unit inside a fort would stop being checked."* Use
  `sailing_requirement`, which prices the server's own `Sailors: H/N` or a hull the ruleset knows.
- **`is_aboard(ordered, fleet_id)`** (`:4267`) — *aboard* as `check_sailing` defines it: the report's
  units in the fleet, plus those that `ENTER` this month, minus those that `LEAVE`.
- **`could_captain(ordered, fleet_id)`** (`:4302`).
- **`check_production`** (`:3864`), its `produce-not-here` block, and the products read at `:3942`.
- **`where_the_report_shows_each_unit`** (`:228`) and the lazy-index reason at `:275-278` — the
  pattern the coordinate index copies.
- **`review_turn`** (`:268`).

### The design of the code

**1. Who is carried away** — `sails_away`'s body, returning the intent the caller needs:

```rust
/// The `SAIL` that will carry this unit out of the hex, if one will.
///
/// `PRODUCE` is phase 10 and movement is phase 9 (`weight_after_orders`, `:4323`), so a passenger
/// produces in the region the vessel reaches (`ah-jk9h`, `gh-679`).
///
/// Returns the captain's placed `SAIL`, because the caller needs its steps. Replaces `sails_away`,
/// which answered the same question as a bool.
///
/// A vessel is one `sailing_requirement` can price - NOT `parse_fleet_kind`, which reads any
/// non-empty kind as a one-hull fleet, so a fort would pass it and every unit inside a fort would
/// stop being checked.
///
/// A `SAIL` that will certainly fail still counts. `check_sailing` may separately warn that the
/// fleet is overloaded or short of crew, in which case the boat stays put and the produce check
/// would have been right - but the player is already being told the sail will fail, and a second
/// finding true only *because* of the first is two warnings for one mistake, and the wrong one to
/// act on.
fn carried_away<'a>(
    hex: &'a Hex<'a>,
    ordered: &Ordered<'_>,
    ruleset: &Ruleset,
) -> Option<&'a PlacedIntent>;
```

**Both paragraphs of that comment are load-bearing and come from the shipped code** — they are
decisions already taken, not restatements. Carry them across.

**2. Following the sail, through the report's own regions:**

```rust
/// Where a sail from `from` ends, as far as the report can say.
///
/// Walks the `Go` steps through each region's own `exits`, looking the neighbour up by coordinate
/// in `regions`. `In` and `Out` steps move a unit within a hex and are skipped.
///
/// `None` the moment the report cannot follow: an exit the region does not list (the coast the
/// player is sailing off), or a neighbour the report does not carry (beyond what the faction can
/// see). **`None` is "cannot say", never "did not move"** - the caller must stay silent for it,
/// which is the whole reason this returns an `Option` rather than the last region it reached.
fn sail_destination<'a>(
    from: &'a ReportRegion,
    steps: &[MoveStep],
    regions: &BTreeMap<Coordinate, &'a ReportRegion>,
) -> Option<&'a ReportRegion>;
```

`Direction::parse(&exit.direction)` is how an exit's text becomes a `Direction`, exactly as
`graph.rs:391` does it — **reuse that, do not match on strings.** `DIRECTIONS`
(`report/region.rs:31`) is the parser's own list and is not the thing to compare against here.

**A sail with no `Go` steps ends where it started**, which is the region already being checked, so
the ordinary finding applies and nothing changes for it.

**3. The region index — built once, and only when it is needed.** `review_turn` (`:268`) already has
this pattern for `where_the_report_shows_each_unit` (`:228`), with the reason at `:275-278`:
*"`validate_turn` runs this on every keystroke once typing settles, so the lookup is built only when
the check that reads it is actually enabled."*

```rust
let by_coordinate = if options.emits(codes::PRODUCE_NOT_HERE) {
    report.regions.iter().map(|region| (region.coordinate, region)).collect()
} else {
    BTreeMap::new()
};
```

Thread it to `check_production` as one more argument, as `located` is threaded to
`check_transfer_targets`.

**4. The guard at `:3941` becomes a destination lookup.** **[corrected]** — Beast's plan writes this
against the pre-`ah-jk9h` code, which had no `!sails_away(...)` term. The term goes:

```rust
if says_here && recipe.inputs.is_empty() {
    // A passenger produces where the vessel arrives. Silent where the report cannot follow the
    // sail - a guess about a region nobody can see is worse than no mark (`ah-jk9h`, `ah-8myf`).
    let where_it_produces = match carried_away(hex, ordered, ruleset) {
        None => Some(hex.region),
        Some(sail) => match &sail.intent {
            Intent::Sail { steps } => sail_destination(hex.region, steps, &by_coordinate),
            _ => Some(hex.region),
        },
    };
    let Some(region) = where_it_produces else { continue };
    // …the existing products test at `:3942`, against `region` rather than `hex.region`…
}
```

**5. The message names the place.** Unchanged where the unit stays put; a second sentence where it
sails. Both quoted verbatim under *User-facing decisions*.

**`PRODUCE_WITHOUT_SKILL` is untouched.** Whether the unit has the skill is a fact about the unit,
not the region, and `check_production`'s own doc comment argues that suppressing one of its two codes
must never hide the other.

**Nothing else changes, and the phase order is why.** Market orders (`not-traded-here`) are phase 7
and settle **before** movement in phase 9, so they resolve in the hex the unit started in.

**Where state lives.** One `BTreeMap<Coordinate, &ReportRegion>` local to `review_turn`, threaded
down. No `Ledger` field, no new type, nothing persisted.

## Increments

**1. Who is carried away.**
RED, in `semantics.rs`'s tests: `a unit aboard a fleet whose captain sails is carried away`;
`a unit aboard a fleet nobody sails is not`; `a unit in the hex but not aboard is not`;
**`a unit aboard a fort is not`** — **[corrected]** Beast's plan says *"an ordinary building"* and
credits `parse_fleet_kind`; a fort is the case that matters and `sailing_requirement` is what
excludes it; `a unit that ENTERs the fleet this month is carried away`; `a unit that LEAVEs it is
not`. GREEN: `carried_away`, replacing `sails_away`.

**2. Following the sail.**
RED: `a one-step sail lands in the neighbour the exit names`; `a two-step sail follows both`;
`a sail through an exit the region does not list cannot be followed` (`None`);
`a sail into a region the report does not carry cannot be followed` (`None`);
`a sail with no steps stays where it is`; `IN and OUT steps do not move the boat between hexes`.
GREEN: `sail_destination`.

**3. The reported case, and everything it must not break.**
RED, in `check_production`'s tests:
- `a passenger is judged where the vessel is sailing to` — **`gh-679`**: fisherman aboard, sailor
  with `SAIL`, start region without fish, destination **with** fish. No finding.
- `a passenger sailing somewhere that cannot make it is told so` — same setup, `PRODUCE wood`,
  destination produces fish. The finding fires with the **`there`** wording, verbatim. **This is the
  case the shipped suppression misses, and the reason this bead exists.**
- `a passenger whose sail cannot be followed is told nothing` — destination outside the report.
- `a unit that is going nowhere is still told` — no fleet; message unchanged, **`here`** wording.
- `a passenger without the skill is still told` — `produce-without-skill` fires for a passenger.
  **This is the test that stops the change being written on the unit instead of the code.**

GREEN: the index, the threading, and the rewritten block.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the six `carried_away` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | who is aboard, including ENTER, LEAVE and the fort |
| the six `sail_destination` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | the walk, and both ways it can fail to follow |
| `a passenger is judged where the vessel is sailing to` | `orders/semantics.rs` | **`gh-679`** |
| `a passenger sailing somewhere that cannot make it is told so` | `orders/semantics.rs` | the case the shipped suppression misses |
| `a passenger whose sail cannot be followed is told nothing` | `orders/semantics.rs` | silence beyond the horizon |
| `a unit that is going nowhere is still told` | `orders/semantics.rs` | no over-suppression, wording unchanged |
| `a passenger without the skill is still told` | `orders/semantics.rs` | only one of the two codes changed |
| the existing `check_production` and `check_sailing` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | **unedited** |

**`ah-jk9h`'s own `sails_away` tests will need rewriting rather than deleting** — they pin who counts
as leaving, which `carried_away` still answers. Move them, do not drop them.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-25. Mockup, as chosen and committed:
`docs/ui/ah-jk9h-sailing-produce.html`.

**The navigator answered this question twice, and the second answer stands.** The first interview
(mine) settled on *staying silent for every passenger*, having rejected checking the destination on
the belief that it required threading the map onto the keystroke path. A second interview, minutes
later, chose *following the `SAIL` using the report's own regions* — and the premise behind the
first rejection turned out to be wrong: the report carries every region's exits, coordinates and
products, so no map is needed. **The later answer is both better and cheaper.** Recorded here in
full so nobody re-opens it from the older note.

**What the HUD checks.**
Chosen: **follow the captain's `SAIL` through the report's own regions** and judge the `PRODUCE`
against the destination's products; fall back to silence only where the report cannot follow.

*Rejected — stay silent for every passenger.* The false error goes and nothing new reaches the
checks, but a genuinely impossible `PRODUCE` goes unwarned even when the report plainly shows where
the boat is going.
*Rejected — say the check cannot judge it* (`this unit is aboard a vessel that is leaving, so where
it will produce is not checked`). It tells the player the HUD looked, at the cost of a new advisory
on every producing passenger, including the many whose order is fine.
*Rejected — thread the map into `validate_orders_state`.* Unnecessary once the report is enough, and
it would put new work on a path that runs as the player types.

**The two messages, shipping verbatim:**

| Case | Sentence |
|---|---|
| the unit stays put | `cannot produce fish here: this region produces wood, furs and herbs` *(unchanged)* |
| the unit sails first | `cannot produce wood there: the region this vessel is sailing to produces fish` |

**What the reporter is told.** The plan records what changed and what did not, so Moira's `PLANNED`
comment on `gh-679` can be accurate. For that comment:

- the false error on a fishing fleet is gone, which is exactly what was reported;
- the HUD now checks the region the boat is sailing to, using the regions the report itself carries;
- where the sail leaves the map the faction can see, the HUD says nothing rather than guessing;
- **her earlier comment said the fix would consult the projected region — that is now accurate**,
  which it would not have been under the rejected first answer.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** a `SAIL` that
`check_sailing` separately says will fail is still followed, because the player is already being
told the sail fails and a second finding true only *because* of the first is the wrong one to act
on; a sail with no `Go` steps is treated as staying put; and only `produce-not-here` changes.

## Out of scope

- **`BUILD` and `WORK`**, also phase 10 and open to the same argument. Neither was reported and
  neither has a region-products check of this shape. **Worth filing if anybody wants them.**
- **Market checks** (`not-traded-here`). Phase 7, before movement — correct as they stand.
- **Threading the map into the order checks.** Unnecessary; see above.
- **Movement cost, weather, or whether the fleet can actually reach the destination.**
  `check_sailing` owns that and keeps owning it. This bead reads where the orders *say* it goes.
- **The arrow and `trace_move_orders_state`.**

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core        # after each increment  [corrected: not `atlantis-core`]
pnpm run check:fast                    # before the PR
```

`pnpm run check:generated` is not needed: no type crosses the boundary.

**Watch `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`.** Its `EXPECTED` table counts findings over a
committed turn, and a producing passenger on a sailing fleet moves a `produce-not-here` row — in
either direction, since this bead both removes findings (the destination can make it) and adds them
(the destination cannot). **Read the finding before touching the table**; the table's own doc comment
records twice that a moved row was the bead proving itself.

**The human check:** load a report with a fishing fleet, put a producing unit aboard a vessel whose
captain sails, and confirm the message names the destination rather than the hex it left — then sail
it off the edge of what the report shows and confirm the HUD says nothing at all.

## Known traps

- **`sailing_requirement`, not `parse_fleet_kind`, is what makes a structure a vessel.**
  **[corrected]** Beast's plan states the opposite in its reusables, increment 1 and its own traps
  section. `parse_fleet_kind` (`mode.rs:191`) reads any non-empty kind as a one-hull fleet, **so a
  fort would pass it and every unit inside a fort would stop being checked** — the shipped code
  (`:3836-3839`) is explicit about this. Using it would reintroduce a defect `ah-jk9h` avoided.
- **`carried_away` replaces `sails_away`; it is not written beside it.** Two functions answering one
  question is what this whole epic has been about.
- **Use `is_aboard`, not `unit.structure_id`.** *Aboard* includes units that `ENTER` this month and
  excludes those that `LEAVE`.
- **`None` from `sail_destination` means "cannot say", not "did not move".** Returning the last
  region it managed to reach would invent a judgement about a hex nobody can see.
- **Build the coordinate index only when `produce-not-here` is enabled.** `review_turn` runs on every
  keystroke; `:275-278` records why this matters.
- **A `SAIL` that `check_sailing` says will fail is still followed.** Decided already; the comment on
  `carried_away` carries the reasoning.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: The cerebro bump moved the consumer's declaration and every role's project-conf now refuses
description:
Filed by Psylocke on 2026-08-24, at the navigator's instruction (P0 set by the navigator, not assumed).

## What is broken

676a11ce chore(ah-zuhs): bump cerebro (#676), merged 2026-08-24T18:01, brought in cerebro's cb-epr,
which moved where a consumer declares its own project facts:

  .claude/cerebro-project.conf   ->   .cerebro/project.conf

This repository's file is still at the old path. project-conf detects that and REFUSES rather than
falling back - deliberately, so a consumer does not silently read as 'no declaration at all':

  $ .claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf launch_targets
  project-conf: the declaration has moved - run: mv .claude/cerebro-project.conf .cerebro/project.conf
  rc=2

The refusal is before any lookup (scripts/project-conf:58-62), so it is EVERY key, not one:
install, default_branch, launch_targets, launch_<name>, launch_<name>_port, app_paths, fixtures_doc.

## Who it affects

Every role, because project-conf is the single place any of them asks the consumer anything.
Observed downstream already:

- app-paths exits 3 - 'no app_paths in .cerebro/project.conf - cannot classify anything as
  application-touching or invisible'. Psylocke cannot tell an application-touching bead from an
  invisible one, which is the first decision of every verification pass. It worked at 15:2x and
  stopped mid-pass.
- Any session reading launch_* cannot start the application, and its own instructions forbid
  improvising a command.
- Any session reading 'install' loses the project's install command.

## The fix is NOT the message's one-liner

project-conf's message says 'mv .claude/cerebro-project.conf .cerebro/project.conf'. Done literally
that loses the file: .gitignore:54 ignores '.cerebro/' wholesale, so the moved file is untracked and
absent from every fresh clone - which is exactly the failure .gitignore:36-45 already guards against
for the old path with its '!' exceptions. It needs both halves:

  git mv .claude/cerebro-project.conf .cerebro/project.conf

plus a '!.cerebro/project.conf' exception in .gitignore, alongside a comment saying why it is
tracked, in the shape of the existing lines 37-40.

## Check the siblings in the same pass

cb-epr moved three files, per scripts/lint:276 which iterates project.conf, roster.conf and traps.md:

- .claude/cerebro-project.conf -> .cerebro/project.conf  - BROKEN NOW, above.
- .claude/cerebro-traps.md     -> .cerebro/traps.md      - the old file still exists here; every
  agent file is linted for telling the reader to read the consumer's .cerebro/traps.md.
- .claude/cerebro-roster       -> .cerebro/roster.conf   - this repository has NEITHER file. roster
  currently exits 0 with the right names, so it is not failing, but .gitignore:41-45 still carries a
  '!.claude/cerebro-roster' exception for a file that does not exist. Worth settling in the same
  pass rather than leaving a stale exception.

Each moved file needs the same .gitignore treatment as project.conf, and the stale '!' exceptions
for the old paths should go.

## Validation

.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf launch_targets prints 'web desktop' and exits 0.
.claude/cerebro/scripts/app-paths --classify crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs prints
'application' and exits 0.
git ls-files .cerebro/project.conf lists the file - i.e. it is tracked, not ignored.
.claude/cerebro/scripts/lint does not complain about the declaration's location.
design:
## Context

`676a11ce chore(ah-zuhs): bump cerebro (#676)` brought in cerebro's `cb-epr`, which moved where a
consumer declares its own facts:

```
.claude/cerebro-project.conf   ->   .cerebro/project.conf
.claude/cerebro-traps.md       ->   .cerebro/traps.md
.claude/cerebro-roster         ->   .cerebro/roster.conf
```

This repository's files are still at the old paths, and `project-conf` **refuses** rather than
falling back — deliberately, so a consumer does not read as "no declaration at all"
(`scripts/project-conf:57-62`). Reproduced on `main` while planning:

```
$ .claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf launch_targets
project-conf: the declaration has moved - run: mv .claude/cerebro-project.conf .cerebro/project.conf
rc=2

$ .claude/cerebro/scripts/app-paths --classify crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs
app-paths: no app_paths in .cerebro/project.conf - cannot classify anything as
application-touching or invisible.
rc=3
```

The refusal is before any lookup, so **every key** is gone: `install`, `default_branch`,
`launch_targets`, `launch_<name>`, `launch_<name>_port`, `app_paths`, `fixtures_doc`. `project-conf`
is the single place any role asks this repository anything, so **every role is degraded right now** —
Psylocke cannot classify a bead, nobody can launch the application, and no session can read the
install command.

**This is a five-minute fix with one trap that would silently undo it.** The trap is the whole reason
this plan is worth reading.

### The bead's own suggested fix does not work

`ah-7l1c`'s description says to add *"a `!.cerebro/project.conf` exception in .gitignore"*. That
cannot work, and the planner proved it rather than reasoning about it. `.gitignore:54` is
`.cerebro/` — an ignored **directory** — and git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is
excluded:

```
# in a scratch repo:
.gitignore = ".cerebro/\n!.cerebro/project.conf"    -> .cerebro/project.conf IGNORED
.gitignore = ".cerebro/*\n!.cerebro/project.conf"   -> .cerebro/project.conf tracked
```

So `.cerebro/` **must become `.cerebro/*`**. Without that, `git add .cerebro/project.conf` silently
adds nothing, the commit looks clean, and the file is absent from every fresh clone — which is
exactly the failure `.gitignore`'s existing `!` exceptions were written to prevent for the old path.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Four files in the consumer. **Nothing inside `.claude/cerebro` changes** — the submodule is already
correct; this repository is the one that has not caught up.

- `.cerebro/project.conf` — moved, with `git mv`.
- `.cerebro/traps.md` — moved, with `git mv`.
- `.gitignore` — `.cerebro/` becomes `.cerebro/*`, three new `!` exceptions, three stale ones removed.
- `.cerebro/traps.md`'s own header — one sentence naming the old paths.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `.gitignore:32-36` — `.claude/*` followed by `!.claude/skills/` and friends. **That is the pattern**:
  ignore the directory's contents with `*`, then re-include by name. The fix makes `.cerebro/` match it.
- `.gitignore:37-50` — the three comment blocks explaining why each file is tracked. **Move the
  comments with the exceptions**; they are the record of why an ignored copy would be wrong, and
  ah-qled.1, ah-qled.5.1 and ah-qled.10.5 are cited in them.
- `git mv`, not `mv`. The message in `project-conf` says `mv`; that loses the file's history and,
  combined with the `.gitignore` trap, loses the file. Use `git mv` for both.

### The design of the change

**`.gitignore`.** The `.cerebro/` block (`:52-54`, the ignore rule itself at `:54`) becomes:

```gitignore
# Cerebro's own bookkeeping - agent state files, stop flags and the agents' worktrees. Live
# machine state, never part of the project (ah-v82).
#
# `.cerebro/*` rather than `.cerebro/`, because git cannot re-include a file whose parent
# DIRECTORY is excluded - the three exceptions below would silently do nothing (ah-7l1c).
.cerebro/*

# The consumer's own project facts, read by .claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf (ah-qled.1,
# moved here by cerebro's cb-epr). Tracked on purpose: unlike the personal .cerebro/models.conf
# these are facts every clone needs, and an ignored copy would vanish on a fresh clone and take
# the install step with it.
!.cerebro/project.conf

# The consumer's own fleet, read by .claude/cerebro/scripts/roster (ah-qled.5.1). Tracked for the
# same reason: which agents exist is a fact every clone needs, and a git-ignored file would vanish
# on a fresh clone and silently revert the fleet to cerebro's own names. This repository ships no
# such file - it wants the built-in fleet - but the path must stay trackable for one to be added.
!.cerebro/roster.conf

# The traps this project has already paid for, read by plan-bead and implement-bead before work
# starts (ah-qled.10.5). Tracked for the same reason: a trap the whole team has paid for is a fact
# every clone needs, and an ignored copy would vanish on a fresh clone and let each new machine pay
# for it again.
!.cerebro/traps.md
```

and the three old exceptions at `:37-50` — `!.claude/cerebro-project.conf` (`:40`), `!.claude/cerebro-roster` (`:45`),
`!.claude/cerebro-traps.md` (`:50`) — are **deleted along with their comment blocks**, which move to the new
ones above.

**`!.cerebro/roster.conf` is added even though no such file exists here.** That is deliberate and is
exactly what the existing comment says the old exception was for — *"This repository ships no such
file… but the path must stay trackable for one to be added."* Carrying the intent across is the
point; leaving a stale exception for a path that no longer means anything is not.

**`.cerebro/models.conf` must stay ignored.** It is personal, per-machine, and `.cerebro/*` covers it
because no `!` exception names it. Do not add one. Check it after the change — see *Validation*.

**`.cerebro/traps.md`'s header** (`:8`) says *"Tracked on purpose, beside `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`
and `.claude/cerebro-roster`"*. Update those two paths in the same commit; it is the file's own
explanation of why it is tracked and it now names two files that do not exist.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new. Two files move, one ignore rule changes shape, one sentence is
corrected.

## Increments

This is one small change and the fleet is down while it is not made, so it is **one commit**, not
four. The steps within it:

**1. Move both files, with history.**

```bash
mkdir -p .cerebro
git mv .claude/cerebro-project.conf .cerebro/project.conf
git mv .claude/cerebro-traps.md .cerebro/traps.md
```

`git mv` will succeed even though the destination is currently ignored — but the file will not be
staged usefully until step 2, so do step 2 before committing and check `git status` shows both.

**2. Rewrite the `.gitignore` blocks** exactly as set out above.

**3. Fix `.cerebro/traps.md:8`'s two stale paths.**

**4. Prove it, before committing** — run every command in *Validation*. This bead's failure mode is a
commit that looks right and ships nothing, so the `git ls-files` check is not optional.

## The test plan

**There is no unit test to write, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying so.** This is a
file move and an ignore rule; the repository has no harness that exercises `.gitignore`, and the
cerebro submodule's own `tests/` cover cerebro, not this consumer's layout. The verification is the
command list in *Validation*, run and pasted into the PR description.

**The regression net is the gate**: `pnpm run check:fast` must stay green, and `scripts/runGate.ts`
reads `disk-preflight`, which reads `project-conf` — so a gate that runs at all is itself evidence
the declaration is being found again.

## User-facing decisions

None. Nothing here reaches the application: two configuration files move and an ignore rule changes.
No message, no setting, no interface. The audience cannot observe this bead.

## Out of scope

- **Anything inside `.claude/cerebro`.** The submodule is correct; do not "fix" `project-conf`'s
  message to say `git mv`, however tempting — that is a cerebro bead, and touching the submodule
  here turns a five-minute consumer fix into a two-PR change while the fleet is down. File it
  separately if you think it is worth doing.
- **Adding a `## Where the project declares its facts` section to this repository's `CLAUDE.md`.**
  `scripts/lint:275` checks for one, but it lints **cerebro's own** `CLAUDE.md`, not the consumer's —
  running `bash scripts/lint` from `.claude/cerebro` today already prints
  *"ok - the consumer contract holds"*. So it is not a gate on this bead. It may still be worth
  doing; it is not this bead's job.
- **Creating a `.cerebro/roster.conf`.** The exception is added so one *could* be; this repository
  wants the built-in fleet, and `roster --role planner` exits 0 with the right names today.
- **Stale references in `docs/retrospectives/*` and `docs/ui/*`.** Retrospectives are a record of what
  was true when they were written and must not be rewritten. The three `docs/ui/` mockups are
  likewise historical. Two live comments do mention the old path —
  `.cargo/config.toml:22` and `scripts/runGate.ts:74` — and updating those two is **optional
  tidying**: do it only if the diff stays trivial, and never at the cost of shipping the fix.

## Validation

Every one of these, before the PR:

```bash
# the declaration is found again
.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf launch_targets     # prints the targets, rc=0
.claude/cerebro/scripts/app-paths --classify crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs   # 'application', rc=0
.claude/cerebro/scripts/roster --role planner           # rc=0

# THE ONE THAT CATCHES THE TRAP: both files are tracked, not ignored
git ls-files .cerebro/project.conf .cerebro/traps.md    # must list BOTH
git check-ignore -v .cerebro/project.conf               # must print NOTHING, rc=1

# the personal file is still ignored
git check-ignore -v .cerebro/models.conf 2>/dev/null && echo "models.conf still ignored - correct"

# nothing else broke
pnpm run check:fast
```

**Paste the output of the `git ls-files` line into the PR description.** A commit that moves the
files without the `.gitignore` shape change looks identical in `git status` for the *old* paths and
ships nothing for the new ones; that command is the only cheap thing that tells them apart.

**The human check:** on a fresh clone (or `git stash -u` and a `git checkout` of the commit),
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf install` must print this project's install command. That is the
failure the tracking exists to prevent, and it cannot be observed in the working tree that created it.

## Known traps

- **`.cerebro/` cannot host a `!` exception; `.cerebro/*` can.** Proved in a scratch repository while
  planning. This is the whole bead: get it wrong and the fix looks applied and ships nothing.
- **`git mv`, never `mv`.** `project-conf`'s own message says `mv`. Following it literally loses the
  file's history, and combined with the trap above loses the file.
- **`.cerebro/models.conf` must stay ignored.** It is per-machine. `.cerebro/*` keeps it out; adding
  an exception for it would commit somebody's local model choices.
- **`.cerebro/worktrees/` must stay ignored**, and does — `*` matches it, and no exception names it.
  If a worktree ever shows up in `git status` after this change, the `.gitignore` is wrong.
- **Move the comments with the exceptions.** They cite ah-qled.1, ah-qled.5.1 and ah-qled.10.5 and
  say why an ignored copy would be wrong. An exception with no comment is the next reader's mystery.
- **Do not touch the submodule.** See *Out of scope*.
- **Retrospectives are not to be rewritten**, however stale their paths look.
