title: A pillage warning says 0 combat ready men without saying why 19 men count as none
description:
Found by the navigator during verification of ah-lu0f.1 (2026-08-24, at origin/main 53b45720).

## What was seen

On tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep, giving PILLAGE to Taxers (10116) in
forest (36,0) in Reprau produces:

  "cannot pillage here: needs 24 combat ready men, this faction has 0"

The navigator's objection: the unit visibly holds **19 high elves**. Being told the faction has
**0** reads as a counting bug.

## The count is correct; the sentence is not

Two independent reasons the count really is zero, per combat_ready
(crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:1814, the navigator's own reading settled in ah-1ad6.2 —
'a man is combat ready when he has a weapon he can wield'):

1. Taxers (10116) carries the **avoiding** flag, and an avoiding unit has zero combat ready men
   whatever it holds — an explicit early return at silver.rs:1822.
2. Independently, it holds no weapons at all — 19 high elves and 13257 silver, nothing wieldable —
   so min(men, wieldable weapons) would be 0 regardless.

The threshold is right too: forest (36,0) has a tax base of $2356, and 2356/2/50 rounds up to 24.

So nothing about the arithmetic is wrong. What is wrong is that the sentence states a conclusion
whose entire content is a definition the player cannot see, and offers no way to act on it.

## Two things to fix

**The missing cause.** The message should say why the men do not count, because the two causes need
opposite actions from the player: clearing the *avoiding* flag is one order, arming the unit is a
different problem entirely. Something in the shape of 'this unit is avoiding combat, so none of its
19 men count' or 'its 19 men hold no weapons they can wield'.

**'this faction has'.** The count is over one hex, not the faction — combat_ready_in(hex, ...) — so
the phrase is wrong as written and could send a player looking at units elsewhere. It should name
the region.

## Not caused by ah-lu0f.1

ah-lu0f.1 moved PILLAGE onto the shared pricing seam and the navigator judged it passed: both silver
surfaces agree. This wording predates it (semantics.rs:3764, check_pillage_men, from ah-1ad6.2).

Unranked at P4.
design:
## Context

> **REVISED 2026-08-25, after this plan failed verification.** The wording work in this plan all
> shipped and the navigator accepted it — *"this region has"*, and the warning naming its cause. It
> is not what was wrong, and it is **not rewritten below**.
>
> **What the navigator reversed at verification: `avoiding` no longer zeroes a unit's combat-ready
> men for `PILLAGE`'s threshold.** That is half of `ah-1ad6.2`, settled 2026-08-23 and cited
> throughout this plan as given. The other half — `armed = min(men, wieldable weapons)`, a weapon
> needing a skill counting only at level 1 or better — is **unchanged**, as are the threshold
> (`tax_base / 2 / 50`) and its scope (a sum over own units in the region).
>
> **The blast radius is one line plus wording.** Verified while revising: `is_avoiding` is called at
> exactly one place (`silver.rs:1857`, inside `readiness`), and `combat_ready` has two consumers,
> both `PILLAGE` — the region sum at `semantics.rs:690` and the explanation at `:3825`. Nothing else
> in the codebase asks about combat readiness, so there is no wider sweep to do.
>
> Decisions taken with the navigator on 2026-08-25 are in *User-facing decisions* under
> **"What the verification changed"**. Read that before the design below, which still describes the
> pre-reversal rule wherever it has not been struck through.


Found by the navigator on 2026-08-24, verifying `ah-lu0f.1` at `origin/main 53b45720`. Giving
`PILLAGE` to `Taxers (10116)` in forest (36,0) of Reprau produces:

> `cannot pillage here: needs 24 combat ready men, this faction has 0`

The unit visibly holds **19 high elves**, so being told **0** reads as a counting bug.

**Nothing about the arithmetic is wrong**, and that is the whole point of the bead. Per
`combat_ready` (`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:1814`), whose reading the navigator settled in
`ah-1ad6.2` — *"a man is combat ready when he has a weapon he can wield"* — the count is zero for
**two independent reasons**:

1. `Taxers (10116)` carries the **avoiding** flag, and an avoiding unit has zero combat ready men
   whatever it holds — an explicit early return at `silver.rs:1822`.
2. Independently, it holds no weapons at all — 19 high elves and 13,257 silver, nothing wieldable —
   so `min(men, wieldable weapons)` would be 0 regardless.

The threshold is right too: forest (36,0) has a tax base of $2,356, and `2356/2/50` rounds up to 24.

**So the sentence states a conclusion whose entire content is a definition the player cannot see,
and offers no way to act on it.** And it says *"this faction has"* when the count is
`combat_ready_in(hex, ruleset)` (`semantics.rs:667-674`) — a sum over every own unit **in that
hex** — so the phrase could send a player looking at units in another region entirely.

**Not caused by `ah-lu0f.1`.** That bead moved `PILLAGE` onto the shared pricing seam and the
navigator judged it passed. This wording predates it (`semantics.rs:3764`, `check_pillage_men`, from
`ah-1ad6.2`).

When this lands: the warning names the region rather than the faction, and says which of the two
things the player has to fix.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the count says why, without changing what it counts

`combat_ready` returns `Option<i64>` and throws away the reason on the way (`:1822`'s early return
for `avoiding`, then `min(men, wieldable)`). The message needs both facts, and **there must not be a
second computation of either** — that is the defect this repository keeps paying for (`ah-abwx`,
`ah-ycuj`, `ah-moq3`).

So the existing body becomes the richer function and `combat_ready` becomes its one-line caller:

```rust
/// Why a unit's men are or are not combat ready, alongside how many are.
///
/// `combat_ready` answers the number and nothing else, which is all `PILLAGE`'s threshold needs -
/// but a player told `0` about a unit visibly holding nineteen men needs the reason, and the two
/// reasons want opposite actions: clearing `avoiding` is one order, arming the unit is a different
/// problem (`ah-cw75`).
///
/// `armed` deliberately ignores the `avoiding` flag: it is `min(men, weapons the unit can wield)`
/// as if the unit were willing to fight, which is what makes "avoiding **and** unarmed"
/// distinguishable from "avoiding but otherwise ready". `ready` is the number `PILLAGE` uses and is
/// **REVISED (2026-08-25): `ready` is now simply `armed`.** `avoiding` no longer
/// zeroes it — see *User-facing decisions*.
pub struct Readiness {
    /// The unit's headcount, for the sentence.
    pub men: i64,
    pub avoiding: bool,
    /// `min(men, wieldable weapons)`, computed as though the unit were not avoiding.
    pub armed: i64,
    /// What `PILLAGE` counts. **REVISED: this is `armed`, unconditionally.**
    pub ready: i64,
}

#[must_use]
pub fn readiness(facts: &UnitFacts<'_>, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) -> Option<Readiness>;

#[must_use]
pub fn combat_ready(facts: &UnitFacts<'_>, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) -> Option<i64> {
    readiness(facts, ruleset).map(|readiness| readiness.ready)
}
```

**`combat_ready`'s signature, return type and every answer stay identical**, so
`combat_ready_in` (`semantics.rs:667`) and `semantics.rs:657` need no edit and their tests prove the
move was behaviour-preserving.

**Both `None` cases move across unchanged** and must not be reordered: `men_estimated` first
(`:1830`), then the missing ruleset (`:1835`). A guessed headcount cannot be compared against a
threshold, and without a ruleset nothing says which items are weapons.

**REVISED — the whole readiness test, not just the `avoiding` clause.** The rules put the taxing
test and the pillage threshold in one passage, and the second is defined by the first
(`tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html`):

> *"A unit may TAX if it has **Combat skill of at least level 1**, has **a weapon and the appropriate
> skill to use it**, has **a mount and sufficient skill to ride it in combat** or is **a mage who
> knows a spell which damages enemies**."*
>
> *"To do this requires the faction to have enough **combat ready men** in the region to tax half of
> the available money in the region."*

So *combat ready men* **are** the taxing characters, and `avoiding` is not in the test at all — which
is why the navigator's reversal is a reading of the rules rather than a preference. But it also means
`armed` was only **one of four ways**, and `readiness` counts only that one: today a unit of ten men
with Combat 1 and no weapons counts **zero**, and so does one with horses and Riding.

**The count, agreed with the navigator on 2026-08-25:**

```rust
let all_men_count = skill_level(facts.skills, "COMB") >= 1;   // or a damaging spell - see below
let ready = if all_men_count {
    men
} else {
    men.min(wieldable_weapons + ridable_mounts)
};
```

- **Combat 1 makes every man in the unit a taxer**, because skills are held by the unit.
- **Weapons and mounts add up**: a man either wields something or rides something, so
  `min(men, weapons + mounts)`.
- **`avoiding` is gone entirely.** Delete the field from `Readiness`, delete `is_avoiding`'s only
  call site (`silver.rs:1857`), and delete `is_avoiding` if nothing else calls it — verified while
  revising that nothing does.

**A ridable mount needs its own required level, and it is only in prose.** Every mount's description
carries one fixed sentence — *"This mount requires riding [RIDI] of at least level N to ride in
combat"* — and there is **no structured field for N**: an item's keys are `capacity, description,
kind, moves, name, selfMobile, tag, weight, withdrawCost`. `WING` needs level 3; `HORS`, `CAME` and
`TURT` need level 1. **Parse N out of that sentence** (the navigator's choice) rather than assuming 1,
which would over-count a unit with winged horses and Riding 1. A mount whose description does not
match the sentence counts for nobody — under-counting, which is the safe direction here.

**The mage case is left out because it is separate work, NOT because it is impossible.**
*(Corrected 2026-08-25: this paragraph previously said the ruleset could not express it. That was
wrong — see the correction note in `ah-v585`.)* A skill's paragraph text **is** in the ruleset, under
`levels[]` as `{ level, description }`; only the top-level `description` field is absent, which is
what the planner checked. `COMB`'s own entry reads *"a unit with this skill may TAX or PILLAGE."*

Testing `deals N damage` against the committed ruleset selects exactly eight spells — `FIRE`, `EQUA`,
`STOR`, `CALL`, `SBLA`, `BUND`, `BDEM`, `DISP` — with **no false positives among the four shields or
the four summons**, which a match on *attack* or *battle* would have caught.

**It still stays out of this bead**, at the navigator's decision on 2026-08-25: `ah-cw75` is a P0 a
player is waiting on, and widening it now delays three implementable ways for a fourth. So a combat
mage remains under-counted here — a missing warning, never a false one — and `ah-v585` (P2) carries
it. **Do not hard-code a spell list**, which is the `ah-v9p2` failure class; `ah-v585` has the
derivation.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `check_pillage_men` explains the marked unit

The function (`:3731-3769`) keeps its whole shape: the `emits` gate, the `tax_base` and
`combat_ready_in` early returns, `pillage_threshold`, the `ready >= needed` return, and one finding
per pillaging unit on the first `PILLAGE` in its block. **Only the message changes**, and it gains
one `readiness` call for the unit the finding is on.

```rust
        let because = hex_facts_for(ordered)          // the same facts `combat_ready_in` builds
            .and_then(|facts| readiness(&facts, ruleset))
            .map_or(String::new(), |r| because_clause(&r));
        findings.push(ordered.finding(
            hex,
            codes::PILLAGE_WITHOUT_MEN,
            format!(
                "cannot pillage here: needs {needed} combat ready men, this region has {ready}{because}"
            ),
            Some(placed),
        ));
```

**`this faction` becomes `this region`.** One word, and it is half the bead.

**Build the per-unit facts the way `combat_ready_in` already does** — `hex_facts(hex, &Receipts::default())` (`:668-670`) — rather than constructing `UnitFacts` by hand. If that iterator cannot be addressed per unit without restructuring, extract the one-unit case from it and have `combat_ready_in` call that in its loop, so there stays exactly one way facts are built.

### The clause, and every string it can produce

```rust
/// Why this unit's men do not count, as the tail of the pillage warning, or `""` when they do.
///
/// Empty for a unit that is genuinely armed and not avoiding: the region is simply short, nothing
/// about this unit is wrong, and an explanation would be noise (`ah-cw75`).
fn because_clause(readiness: &Readiness) -> String;
```

Shipping **verbatim**, with `19` standing for the headcount:

| `avoiding` | `armed` | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| yes | `0` | ` — this unit is avoiding combat, and its 19 men hold no weapons they can wield` |
| yes | `> 0` | ` — this unit is avoiding combat, so none of its 19 men count` |
| no | `0` | ` — this unit's 19 men hold no weapons they can wield` |
| no | `> 0` | *(empty)* |

and the singular forms, for a one-man unit — a leader is one man, so this is reachable:

| Case | Clause |
|---|---|
| avoiding, unarmed | ` — this unit is avoiding combat, and its 1 man holds no weapons he can wield` |
| avoiding, armed | ` — this unit is avoiding combat, so its 1 man does not count` |
| not avoiding, unarmed | ` — this unit's 1 man holds no weapons he can wield` |

**`men == 0` produces no clause**, whatever the flags: *"its 0 men hold no weapons"* explains
nothing, and a unit with no men has a different problem than this warning is about.

**The em dash is ` — `**, spaced, matching the sentence in the mockup exactly.

## Increments

> **REVISED 2026-08-25.** The increments below were written for the wording work, which has shipped.
> The revision adds these, and they come first:
>
> **R1 — the count.** RED in `silver.rs`'s tests: `combat_skill_makes_every_man_a_taxer`
> (10 men, `COMB` 1, no weapons → `ready == 10`); `weapons_and_mounts_add_up` (10 men, 3 wieldable
> weapons, 4 horses, `RIDI` 1 → `ready == 7`); `a_mount_needing_a_higher_riding_level_does_not_count`
> (`WING` with `RIDI` 1 → those men do not count; with `RIDI` 3 → they do);
> `avoiding_no_longer_zeroes_anyone` (avoiding, armed → `ready == armed`). GREEN: the corrected
> `readiness`, with `avoiding` and its field removed.
>
> **R2 — the required riding level, out of prose.** RED: a unit test on the parser alone, against all
> four mounts' real descriptions from the committed ruleset — `HORS`, `CAME`, `TURT` → 1; `WING` → 3;
> a description not matching the sentence → the mount counts for nobody.
>
> **R3 — the sentences.** RED: `an_avoiding_unit_is_not_told_it_is_avoiding` (the deleted clause);
> `a_unit_with_combat_skill_and_no_weapons_is_not_told_it_holds_no_weapons` — **the trap named in
> *User-facing decisions***: the clause must key off `ready == 0`, not `armed == 0`. GREEN:
> `because_clause` matching on `ready == 0` alone, keeping the surviving sentence verbatim.
>
> **R4 — the region sum.** No new code: `semantics.rs:690` sums `combat_ready` and now sums more.
> Run the corpus and read what moved before touching any expectation.


1. **The reason is available, and the count is unchanged.**
   RED, in `silver.rs`'s tests:
   - `an avoiding unit with weapons is armed but not ready` — `avoiding: true`, `armed > 0`,
     `ready == 0`. **This is the case that does not exist today**, and the one that makes the four
     clauses distinguishable.
   - `an avoiding unit with no weapons is neither` — `armed == 0`, `ready == 0`.
   - `an unarmed unit that is not avoiding is not ready` — `armed == 0`, `ready == 0`.
   - `an armed unit that is not avoiding is ready` — `armed == ready == min(men, weapons)`.
   - `an estimated headcount answers nothing`, `no ruleset answers nothing` — both `None`, and
     **`men_estimated` is checked before the ruleset**, as today.
   GREEN: `Readiness`, `readiness`, and `combat_ready` delegating to it.
   **Every existing `combat_ready` test must pass unedited** — that is the proof the move changed
   no answer.

2. **The clause, every string.**
   RED: one test per row of both tables above, asserting the clause **verbatim**, plus
   `an armed unit that is not avoiding explains nothing` (empty) and
   `a unit with no men explains nothing` (empty).
   GREEN: `because_clause`.

3. **The warning names the region and the reason.**
   RED, in `semantics.rs`'s `check_pillage_men` tests:
   - `the pillage warning names the region, not the faction` — the full message asserted verbatim
     for an armed unit below the threshold: `cannot pillage here: needs 24 combat ready men, this
     region has 12`.
   - `an avoiding unarmed unit is told both reasons` — **the reported case**, asserted verbatim.
   - `an avoiding armed unit is told about the flag`.
   - `an unarmed unit is told about its weapons`.
   - `a unit whose men count is told only the threshold` — no clause.
   GREEN: the message and the `readiness` call.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the six `readiness` tests | `orders/silver.rs` | the two causes are separable, and `combat_ready` still answers what it did |
| every existing `combat_ready` test | `orders/silver.rs` | **unedited** — the move was behaviour-preserving |
| the seven `because_clause` tests | `orders/silver.rs` | all seven strings, verbatim, plus the two empty cases |
| the five `check_pillage_men` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | the region wording and each reason end to end |
| the existing `pillage-without-men` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | the threshold, the silence on unknowns, one finding per unit |

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

**`pnpm run check:generated` is not needed**: no type crosses the boundary. `Readiness` is internal
to the core and the message is a string in a `Finding` that already exists.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-24. Mockup, as chosen and committed:
`docs/ui/ah-cw75-pillage-warning.html` (PR #673, merged).

**What to say when both causes are true**, which is the case the navigator actually hit.
Chosen: **name both** — `this unit is avoiding combat, and its 19 men hold no weapons they can
wield`. It is the only option honest about that unit: clearing the avoiding flag alone would not
have helped, and this says so in advance. Accepted cost: the longest sentence of the three, on the
case where the reader is already confused.
*Rejected — name the first reason only*: shorter, and it always names one thing to act on. Rejected
because it is exactly the reported case — clear the flag, and the warning returns with a different
reason, a second surprise the first message could have prevented.
*Rejected — fix `faction` → `region` and say no more*: the smallest change, no new strings, and the
count stops sending anyone to another hex. Rejected because **`0` still reads as a counting bug**,
which is the thing the navigator objected to.

**Whose reason the warning explains**, given the count is a hex total across every own unit but the
finding hangs on one unit's `PILLAGE` line.
Chosen: **the unit the warning is on.** It is the unit whose order is marked and the one the player
can act on; where that unit is genuinely armed and not avoiding, no reason is given and only the
threshold is stated.
*Rejected — explain the whole hex* (`3 units here are avoiding combat and 1 holds no weapons`).
Truer to the number being shown, and rejected because it names units the player is not looking at
and has no single sentence when the units fail for different reasons.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** the singular forms
in the second table, which follow mechanically from the plural ones the navigator agreed — *"so its
1 man does not count"* rather than the ungrammatical *"none of its 1 man counts"*; a headcount of
zero produces no clause; and the clause is a tail on the existing sentence rather than a second
finding, because the two halves are one fact about one order.

### What the verification changed, 2026-08-25

The original interview above is kept intact and its wording outcomes **all shipped and were
accepted**. What follows is what the verification reversed, and one thing it uncovered.

**The rule — REVERSED.** `ah-1ad6.2` settled on 2026-08-23 that *"a man is combat ready when he has a
weapon he can wield, and a unit set to avoid combat has none who are"*. The navigator reversed the
second half at verification: **`avoiding` does not zero a unit's combat-ready men.**

**And the first half turned out to be incomplete**, which the verdict did not say and the planner
found by reading the rules at the navigator's prompting. The rules list **four** ways to be able to
tax, and *combat ready men* are the taxing characters. `readiness` implements one. See *Files to
change* for the corrected count, agreed with the navigator: Combat 1 (or a damaging spell) makes
every man count; otherwise `min(men, wieldable weapons + ridable mounts)`.

**The sentences — two of four deleted.** `because_clause` matched on `(avoiding, armed == 0)`. With
`avoiding` gone it matches on `armed == 0` alone, and only one clause survives:

| case | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| avoiding, armed | *"— this unit is avoiding combat, so none of its N men count"* | **deleted** — those men now count |
| avoiding, unarmed | *"— this unit is avoiding combat, and its N men hold no weapons they can wield"* | **deleted** — the avoiding half names a cause that no longer applies |
| not avoiding, unarmed | *"— this unit's N men hold no weapons they can wield"* | **kept, verbatim**, both singular and plural |
| neither | empty | unchanged |

Chosen by the navigator on 2026-08-25. *Rejected:* keeping a reworded combined clause, which would
name `avoiding` as if it still mattered.

**One caution the implementer must not miss.** The surviving sentence says *"holds no weapons he can
wield"*, and after this change a unit can be combat ready **without any weapon** — by Combat skill or
by a mount. So the clause must fire on `ready == 0`, **not** on `armed == 0`, or a unit with Combat 1
and no weapons would be told it holds no weapons while its men are in fact counted. If the wording
needs to change to cover the new ways of being unready, that is a **new** user-facing question and
goes back to the navigator; it was not asked here because the case did not exist when the sentence
was written.

**Scope.** The navigator chose to keep all of this in `ah-cw75` rather than split it: it is one
coherent correction to one function, and splitting would leave this bead shipping a half-right rule.

## Out of scope

- **What "combat ready" means.** `ah-1ad6.2` settled it with the navigator — a man is combat ready
  when he has a weapon he can wield, and an avoiding unit has none. This bead explains that reading;
  it does not revisit it.
- **The threshold.** `pillage_threshold(tax_base)` is right — 2356/2/50 rounds up to 24 — and is
  untouched.
- **Silence where the headcount is estimated or no ruleset is loaded.** Both `None` cases keep their
  present behaviour and their present reason.
- **The hex-total nature of the count.** The number stays a sum over the region's own units; only
  the word describing it changes, and only the marked unit's reason is given.
- **Any other finding's wording**, including the `taxed-a-pillaged-hex` and `taxed-a-guarded-hex`
  family.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green.

**Then, by eye, on the report the bead was filed from** —
`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, forest **(36,0) in Reprau**, giving
`PILLAGE` to **Taxers (10116)**:

- the warning must read, in full:
  `cannot pillage here: needs 24 combat ready men, this region has 0 — this unit is avoiding combat, and its 19 men hold no weapons they can wield`
- **not** `this faction has`;
- give the same order to a unit that is armed and not avoiding in a hex below the threshold, and the
  warning must state the threshold and **no reason at all**.

**A human must confirm the first of those**, because it is the sentence the bead exists for and no
fixture assertion proves it reads well in place.

## Known traps

> **Added by the 2026-08-25 revision, and these are the ones that will bite:**
>
> - **The surviving sentence must key off `ready == 0`, not `armed == 0`.** After this change a unit
>   can be combat ready with no weapon at all — by Combat skill or by a mount. Keying off `armed`
>   would tell a unit with Combat 1 that it "holds no weapons he can wield" while its men are being
>   counted. Named in *User-facing decisions*; `R3` pins it.
> - **`WING` needs riding level 3, the other three mounts need 1.** Assuming 1 over-counts, which is
>   the direction this module never errs in. The level is in the description prose only — there is no
>   structured field — so it is parsed, and a description that does not match the sentence counts for
>   nobody.
> - **The mage case is out of scope, not impossible.** *(Corrected 2026-08-25.)* Skill text is in the
>   ruleset under `levels[]`, not a top-level `description`. It is `ah-v585`'s, by the navigator's
>   decision, so this bead ships three of the four ways. Do not hard-code a spell list.
> - **`semantics.rs:690` sums `combat_ready` across own units**, so this change makes regional
>   thresholds easier to meet and will *remove* `pillage-without-men` findings. Expect the corpus
>   expectations to move, and read each one before editing it.
> - **`is_avoiding` has exactly one caller** (`silver.rs:1857`), which this bead deletes. Delete the
>   function too if nothing else picks it up; leaving a dead predicate about a flag that no longer
>   matters is how the next reader concludes it still does.


- **`combat_ready` must keep answering exactly what it answers today.** It becomes a one-line
  delegate; every existing test passing unedited is the proof. If one needs editing, the move
  changed a number.
- **`readiness` must not return early on `avoiding`.** The old code did, and that is precisely why
  the two causes are indistinguishable. Record the flag and compute `armed` anyway.
- **`armed` ignores `avoiding` on purpose.** It is *"how many would be ready if the unit were
  willing"*, and a reader who "fixes" it to respect the flag collapses the first two rows of the
  clause table into one.
- **The `None` order matters**: `men_estimated` before the missing ruleset. Swapping them makes an
  estimated headcount answer `None` for a different reason and changes nothing visible — until a
  ruleset is absent, when it changes which check is silent.
- **`this region`, not `this faction`, and not the region's name.** The agreed sentence says *"this
  region"*; naming Reprau was not what was chosen.
- **Singular forms are reachable.** A leader is one man. `its 1 men` ships as easily as it reads
  badly, and there are tests named for all three singular clauses.
- **Build the unit's facts the way `combat_ready_in` does.** A hand-built `UnitFacts` is a second
  way of describing a unit, and this bead is in a family whose whole history is two descriptions of
  one thing disagreeing.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**: none of the five apply. Core only, no browser suite, no persisted
  setting, no `packages/shared` test.
acceptance_criteria:
The pillage-without-men warning names why the men do not count — the unit is avoiding combat, or its men hold no weapons they can wield — so the player knows which of the two to act on.

The warning describes the count as being over the region, not over the faction.

A unit whose men are genuinely armed and not avoiding is still warned when the region's threshold is not met, and the threshold figure is unchanged.

Regression tests cover an avoiding unit, an unarmed non-avoiding unit, and an armed unit below the threshold.

title: A unit whose neighbour is paying for it is told it cannot afford its orders
description:
Found by the navigator during verification of ah-hvt8 (2026-08-24, at origin/main 53b45720).

## What was seen

A hex holds a unit with a large silver balance and the *sharing* flag, and another unit of ours
that is STUDYing and holds no money of its own. The studying unit's hover reads:

  "Wages arrive too late to pay for this month's orders, so this unit is 50 short when it studies."

and its Silver figure shows -50.

## Two separate things are wrong

**1. The shortfall should not exist.** Another unit in the same hex is *sharing* and holds far more
than enough to cover this unit's study cost and every other unit's needs in that hex. Sharing is
exactly the mechanism that pays for this, and the shortfall check does not appear to be consulting
the hex pool for a study cost the way it does elsewhere. With the sharer present the unit is not
short, so neither the -50 nor any shortfall finding should appear.

**2. Wages are not in the equation.** Even setting the sharing aside, the sentence blames wages —
but a unit that is STUDYing does not work and earns no wages this month, so 'wages arrive too late'
describes money that was never coming at all. Whatever the right sentence is for a genuinely short
studier, it is not this one.

Fix (1) and (2) may well be independent: (1) is a shortfall/pooling question in
crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs, (2) is the wording chosen for the note.

## Where to reproduce

Not pinned to a named unit yet. The likely hex in the committed corpus is
tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep, mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra: City Guards
(13303) is flagged *sharing* and holds 112061 silver, and the hex holds a large number of our other
units (Teachers 3824/6583/13805, Teacher 8447, several MinersA) that can be given a STUDY order.
Confirming the exact unit and the exact sentence is the first step of this bead.

## Why it is filed rather than folded into ah-hvt8

ah-hvt8 was a refactoring of silverNote that claimed no behaviour change, and the navigator judged
it passed: this sentence reads the same as it did before the refactoring. The defect is older than
ah-hvt8 and is not caused by it.

Unranked at P4, for a planner to triage with the navigator.
design:
## Context > **REVISED 2026-08-25 (second revision), and the answer is: the hover half needs nothing.** > > This bead's arithmetic was right and shipped. It failed verification because the hover said > *"pays this unit's **upkeep**"* where it should have said *"pays for this unit's **orders**"* — a > studying unit whose neighbour shares satisfies **both** notes, and `unitTooltip.ts:744` was > `SILVER_NOTES.find(...)`, so the first match won and the orders sentence was unreachable in exactly > the case this bead exists to explain. > > **Beast's first revision merged the two sharing notes into one.** That is superseded and must not > be built. It solved the shadowing locally, before the contract question was on the table. > > **`ah-x36v` (P0) has since settled the contract**, and this bead follows it rather than deciding it > alone. Verified against `ah-x36v`'s own design rather than a note about it: > > - *"Chosen: **every sentence that is true**, in `SILVER_NOTES` order. Nothing can be silently > [shadowed]."* — so the orders sentence now appears whenever it is true, and no reordering, guard > or merge is needed to reach it. > - *"Chosen: **collapse the four upkeep-source notes into one**"*, and **`a faction-mate's silver` > is one of those four** — so this bead's upkeep note is absorbed into > `This unit's upkeep was paid by … a faction-mate's silver (20) …`, which `ah-x36v` ships verbatim. > > **So both facts reach the reader and neither sentence in this bead changes.** The design below is > correct as written apart from two things, both struck through where they appear: > the placement instruction (*"immediately BELOW `shared-silver-pays-upkeep`"*), which no longer > decides anything, and Beast's merge. > > **Still blocked on `ah-x36v`** — the dependency is wired and must stay until it lands. Nothing here > is buildable before it. Found by the navigator on 2026-08-24, verifying `ah-hvt8` at `origin/main 53b45720`. A hex holds `City Guards (13303)` — flagged **sharing**, holding 112,061 silver — and another own unit ordered to `STUDY` holding nothing. The studying unit's hover reads: > `Wages arrive too late to pay for this month's orders, so this unit is 50 short when it studies.` and its Silver figure shows **−50**. **Two separate things are wrong, and they have different causes.** ### 1. The shortfall should not exist, and the warning system already knows it `Sharing` (`semantics.rs:2469`) is read per hex and its own doc says exactly what it is: > *"Maintenance is **not** pooled here … this pool is what a `SHARE` flag lends for **orders**."* So `report_shortfalls` consults it and correctly emits no `not-enough-silver` for this unit. But `short_for_orders` is computed in `silver.rs:1088` as `max(0, expense - (held + income - late_income))` — **per unit, with no knowledge of the hex at all.** The column and the hover therefore disagree with the warning. **That is this family's oldest defect.** `ah-abwx` is one surface pricing an order the other did not; `ah-ycuj` exists to catch exactly that, as a corpus test named `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — and **that guard deliberately excludes sharing hexes** (`:39-44`: *"the only warning a sharing hex ever gets: silver is a pooled tag … sharing-hex units while 27 hex-level findings go unread"*). The one test written to catch this class skips the case. **This reverses a recorded decision, deliberately.** `short_for_orders`'s doc comment (`silver.rs:139-140`) says *"Counted for this unit alone, like every other figure in this column — the hex's shared purse is the advisory check's business (`ah-1wcw.1`)."* The navigator has reversed that: a unit whose neighbour is lending it the money is **not short**, and showing −50 is wrong on the one screen a player reads. **Rewrite that comment**; leaving it would tell the next reader the old rule still holds. ### 2. Wages are not in the equation A unit ordered to `STUDY` does not work and earns no wages, so *"wages arrive too late"* describes money that was never coming. The sentence is right only for the case `ah-uwa3` wrote it for — a month that ends in credit because wages land in the turn's last phase — and it is applied to every shortfall (`unitTooltip.ts:365-371`, the `wages-too-late` note). When this lands: the column, the hover and the warning agree about who is short; a unit that really is short is told why in words that are true of it; and a unit paid for by a faction-mate is told so. **`ah-hvt8` has landed**, so `silverNote` is now the `SILVER_NOTES` table. Write against that. ### Revised after a failed verification, 2026-08-25 Psylocke failed this bead at `ee550858`, and **the arithmetic all passed**: the covered unit's Silver reads `0` rather than negative, no wages sentence appears on a studier, the lender's column drops by what it lent, the hex's total is unchanged, and both control cases behave — a sharer with an empty purse still leaves its neighbours short, and a worker whose wages genuinely arrive late still gets `ah-uwa3`'s sentence. **What failed is the sentence, and this plan caused it.** The version below said to place the orders note *"immediately after `shared-silver-pays-upkeep`, since upkeep is the more specific of the two"*. The implementer did exactly that. But a studying unit whose neighbour shares satisfies **both** notes — automatic sharing pays its upkeep (step 4, unconditional on the `SHARE` flag) and the `SHARE` purse pays its study cost — and the note table is first-match, so the upkeep sentence wins and the orders sentence is **unreachable in exactly the case this bead was filed to explain**. That reasoning was sound where only one note applies and wrong where both do. Everything else in this plan stands; the sections below are amended only where the failure touches them, and each change is marked **[revised 2026-08-25]**. ## Files to change, and what to reuse ### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the pool is read once, for both surfaces `forecast_hex` (`:682`) already computes the hex-level facts `forecast_unit` needs and hands them over — `pool_shares_for` (`:696`), `market_shares_for` (`:702`). The sharing purse joins them, **and it must be the same value `report_shortfalls` uses** (`:2717`, `Sharing::read(hex)`). One computation, two surfaces; a second implementation here is the whole defect happening again. ```rust /// What this hex's `SHARE` flags lend for orders, and how it is settled between claimants. /// /// The pool is the sharers' own silver, after what their own orders spend: a sharer cannot lend /// what it is spending itself. Claimants are the units whose orders cost more than they hold. /// /// **All or nothing, deliberately** - the rule `ah-e66j` set for maintenance sharing and for the /// same reason: where the pool cannot cover every claimant, which unit is fed cannot be told, so /// none is credited and every figure stays pessimistic. A player then sees a shortfall that is /// real for *somebody* rather than a guess about who. pub struct SharingPurse { … } pub fn sharing_purse(hex: &Hex<'_>, ledger: &Ledger<'_>) -> SharingPurse; ``` **Where it lives is an architecture decision and it is made here:** `Sharing` stays in `semantics.rs`, and `sharing_purse` goes beside it, because that is where the hex and its ledger are. `forecast_hex` passes the settled result into `forecast_unit` as a new argument, exactly as it passes `shares` and `market_shares`. **Do not move `Sharing` into `silver.rs`** — `report_shortfalls` is its other caller and would then reach across in the opposite direction. `Sharing::pool_trusted` (`:2485`) already exists: a sharer whose own sums are doubted makes the pool untrustworthy. **Reuse it.** An untrusted pool lends nothing, and every figure stays as it is today. ### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the shortfall consults it, and says who paid `forecast_unit` (`:731`) takes one more argument — the unit's settled share of the purse — and: ```rust // What a faction-mate's `SHARE` lends this unit for its orders. `0` for every unit nothing // lent to, and `0`, deliberately, for every unit in a hex whose purse fell short - see // `sharing_purse` (`ah-moq3`). pub shared_silver_for_orders: i64, ``` on `UnitSilver`, beside `shared_silver_covered` (`:168`), which is its maintenance twin and whose comment is the model for this one. `short_for_orders` (`:1088`) becomes: ```rust let short_for_orders = match (income, expense) { (Some(income), Some(expense)) => Some( expense .saturating_sub( held.saturating_add(income) .saturating_add(shared_for_orders) .saturating_sub(late), ) .max(0), ), _ => None, }; ``` **`at_month_end` gains the same term**, or the covered unit still shows −50 — which is the figure the navigator actually saw. It is `held + income + shared_for_orders - expense`. **`short_on` needs no change**: it is already filtered on `short_for_orders > 0` (`:1106`), so a covered unit names no order automatically. **The sharer's own side.** A sharer that lends 50 spends 50: its `expense` rises by what the purse settled out of it, so its `at_month_end` falls and the hex's total silver is unchanged. That is the navigator's decision (see *User-facing decisions*) and it is what `shared_silver_covered` already does for maintenance — **read how the upkeep case debits the sharer and do the same thing**, rather than inventing a second mechanism. Update `short_for_orders`'s doc comment: it no longer counts this unit alone, `ah-1wcw.1`'s rule is reversed, and `ah-moq3` is why. ### `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts` — one note splits in two, and one is added The `wages-too-late` member (`:365-380`) **keeps its id, its position and its exact sentence**, and gains a condition: it applies only where late income is actually coming. ```ts { id: "wages-too-late", // Only where wages are actually coming: a studying unit earns none, and telling it that wages // arrived too late describes money that never existed (`ah-moq3`). when: ({ silver }) => silver.shortForOrders !== null && silver.shortForOrders > 0 && silver.lateIncome !== null && silver.lateIncome > 0, say: ({ silver }) => { …unchanged… } }, { // The same shortfall with nothing on its way. Named by the order it bites on, because the // reader can act on knowing which one the game will refuse (`ah-moq3`). id: "cannot-pay", when: ({ silver }) => silver.shortForOrders !== null && silver.shortForOrders > 0, say: ({ silver }) => `This unit cannot pay the ${silver.shortForOrders} ${CANNOT_PAY[silver.shortOn ?? "orders"]}` }, ``` immediately **below** `wages-too-late`, so the more specific case still wins. Both need an `example()` — `ah-hvt8`'s table requires one per note and its suite proves each note wins for its own. The six sentences, **shipping verbatim** (see *User-facing decisions*): | `shortOn` | Sentence | |---|---| | `study` | `This unit cannot pay the 50 its study costs.` | | `buy` | `This unit cannot pay the 50 its purchase costs.` | | `produce` | `This unit cannot pay the 50 its production costs.` | | `cast` | `This unit cannot pay the 50 its casting costs.` | | `give` | `This unit cannot pay the 50 it gives away.` | | `null` | `This unit cannot pay the 50 its orders cost.` | **`give` does not fit the pattern** — *"it gives away"*, not *"its X costs"* — so build these as a lookup of complete tails beside `SPENDS` (`:156`), not by interpolating a noun into one template: ```ts /** The tail of the `cannot-pay` sentence, per order kind. `give` is not a cost, hence the table. */ const CANNOT_PAY: Record | "orders", string> = { study: "its study costs.", buy: "its purchase costs.", produce: "its production costs.", cast: "its casting costs.", give: "it gives away.", orders: "its orders cost." }; ``` ### The sharing note — **[revised 2026-08-25]** **One note, not two.** `shared-silver-pays-upkeep` (`unitTooltip.ts:572-582`) and `shared-silver-pays-orders` (`:590-598`) are replaced by a single member that says whichever of the two facts hold — and **both sentences where both hold**, which is what the navigator chose: ```ts // Step 4 of the payment order pays upkeep automatically, unconditional on the `SHARE` flag; the // flag's own purse pays for orders. A unit can be covered by both at once - a studier whose // neighbour shares is - so this is ONE note that says what applies rather than two that race. // Two notes were tried and failed verification: the table is first-match, so whichever sat first // silenced the other in the very case this bead exists to explain (`ah-moq3`). { id: "shared-silver", when: ({ silver, countUpkeep }) => (countUpkeep && silver.sharedSilverCovered > 0) || silver.sharedSilverForOrders > 0, say: ({ silver, countUpkeep }) => [ countUpkeep && silver.sharedSilverCovered > 0 ? "A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays this unit's upkeep." : null, silver.sharedSilverForOrders > 0 ? "A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays for this unit's orders." : null ] .filter(Boolean) .join("\n"), example: () => ({ … both fields set, so the example exercises the overlap … }) }, ``` It keeps `shared-silver-pays-upkeep`'s **position** in the table, so nothing else about precedence moves. **Both sentences ship verbatim and unchanged** — neither was at fault, and neither is re-opened. **The upkeep half stays gated on `countUpkeep` and the orders half stays ungated.** With upkeep counting off there is no Upkeep row to explain (`ah-7cdt`), while the orders half explains the `Out` row and the month end, which are on show whatever the setting says — the same reasoning `withdrawing` and `works-by-default` use. The merge must preserve that asymmetry, not tidy it away. ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/UnitTooltip.tsx` — two lines must render as two — **[revised 2026-08-25]** The note is rendered as one paragraph (`:95-97`): ```tsx {summary.silver.note ? (

{summary.silver.note}

) : null} ``` A `\n` in JSX text collapses to a space, so **the join above is invisible without a change here**. Add `whitespace-pre-line` to that `className`. It preserves newlines and still collapses runs of spaces, so every existing single-sentence note is unaffected. **`note` stays a `string`.** Making it a `string[]` would be tidier in the abstract and would change `UnitSummary`'s shape and every test and consumer that reads `summary.silver.note` — for a change that is one Tailwind class. Not worth it, and stated here so it is not re-litigated. ### `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — the guard stops excluding the case Its `shared_hex` exclusion (`:81-89`, `:120`, `:155`, `:165`) exists because the column and the warning genuinely disagreed about sharing hexes. **After this bead they agree, so the exclusion is the thing keeping the guard blind.** Narrow it to what is still genuinely hex-level, or remove it — and say in the PR which, with the count of units it brings back under the guard. **If it cannot be removed, that is a finding**: it means some other disagreement about sharing hexes survives, and the PR should name it rather than leaving the exclusion silently in place. ## Increments 1. **The purse, read once.** `sharing_purse` and `SharingPurse` in `semantics.rs`, wired into `forecast_hex` and passed to `forecast_unit` — which ignores it for now. RED: `a hex with no sharer lends nothing`; `a sharer lends what it is not spending itself`; `a purse that cannot cover every claimant lends nothing to anybody` — the all-or-nothing rule; `a doubted sharer makes the purse untrustworthy` (through `pool_trusted`). GREEN: the function. **No figure moves yet**, and every existing test passes unedited. 2. **The shortfall and the figure consult it.** `shared_silver_for_orders` on `UnitSilver`, `short_for_orders` and `at_month_end` gaining the term, and the sharer debited. RED: `a studying unit in a sharing hex is not short` — **the reported defect**, asserting `short_for_orders == Some(0)` and `at_month_end == Some(0)`; `the sharer pays what it lends` — the sharer's `at_month_end` down by 50; `the hex's silver is unchanged` — the two units' month ends summed, before and after; `a unit in a hex with no sharer is still short`; `a purse that falls short leaves every figure as it was`. Then run `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — it is the guard over exactly this pair of surfaces. 3. **The two sentences.** The `wages-too-late` guard, the `cannot-pay` note and `CANNOT_PAY`. RED, in `unitTooltip.test.ts`: `a short studier is not told about wages`; `a worker whose wages arrive late still is` — the `ah-uwa3` case, unchanged; and one per order kind asserting the six strings **verbatim**. Plus `ah-hvt8`'s own suite, which must show both notes winning for their own examples. 4. **The sharing note.** **[revised 2026-08-25]** One `shared-silver` member replacing the two, plus `whitespace-pre-line` on the hover's note paragraph. RED, in `unitTooltip.test.ts`: - `says when a faction-mate pays for this unit's orders` — orders only. - `says when a faction-mate pays this unit's upkeep` — upkeep only, verbatim as today. - `a unit whose neighbour pays both ways is told both` — **the case that failed verification**: both fields set, and the note is the two sentences joined by a newline, asserted verbatim. - `with upkeep counting off only the orders sentence is said` — the asymmetry, pinned. - `a unit paying for itself says nothing extra`. **The third of those is also the answer to `ah-hvt8`'s blind spot** — see *The test plan*. 5. **The guard stops excluding sharing hexes.** `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs`. ## The test plan | Test | File | Pins | |---|---|---| | the four `sharing_purse` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | the pool, and the all-or-nothing rule | | `a studying unit in a sharing hex is not short` | `orders/silver.rs` | **the reported defect** | | `the sharer pays what it lends`, `the hex's silver is unchanged` | `orders/silver.rs` | the navigator's decision about the sharer's column | | `a unit in a hex with no sharer is still short` | `orders/silver.rs` | no over-correction | | `a purse that falls short leaves every figure as it was` | `orders/silver.rs` | pessimism preserved | | `a short studier is not told about wages` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | defect 2 | | `a worker whose wages arrive late still is` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | `ah-uwa3` unchanged | | the six verbatim sentences | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the agreed wording | | `says when a faction-mate pays for this unit's orders` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the orders half | | `says when a faction-mate pays this unit's upkeep` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the upkeep half, unchanged | | `a unit whose neighbour pays both ways is told both` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | **[revised]** the overlap that failed verification | | `with upkeep counting off only the orders sentence is said` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | **[revised]** the deliberate `countUpkeep` asymmetry | | `ah-hvt8`'s per-note example suite | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the note is not shadowed | | `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` | `crates/core/tests/` | the two surfaces agree, **including in sharing hexes** | ```bash cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core pnpm run check:generated pnpm run check:fast ``` **`ah-hvt8`'s per-note suite could not have caught this, and that is worth understanding before trusting it again.** Every note's `example()` sets only its own field, so each note wins for its own example and **no combination of facts is ever exercised** — a note shadowed only by an overlap is invisible to it. `a unit whose neighbour pays both ways is told both` is the answer for *this* overlap, and it is deliberately a case in `unitTooltip.test.ts` rather than a change to `ah-hvt8`'s suite: the general problem is combination coverage across all 28 notes, which the navigator judged separate work and did not commission here. **Do not attempt the general fix in this bead**; if it is wanted, file it. The merged note also removes this particular overlap by construction — with one note there is no second note for it to shadow — so the test pins the *sentences*, not the race. ## User-facing decisions Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-24. Mockup, as chosen and committed: `docs/ui/ah-moq3-short-studier.html` (PR #669, merged). **What a genuinely short unit is told, when no wages are coming.** Chosen: **name the cost, not the gap** — the six sentences in the table above, verbatim. *Rejected — two sentences split on income* (`This unit has 50 less than its orders need when it studies.`), which keeps the arithmetic shape of the wages sentence beside it. *Rejected — one sentence that never says why* (`This unit is 50 short when it studies.`), shortest and impossible to get wrong, but it drops `ah-uwa3`'s explanation for the case that genuinely is about timing. The accepted cost of the choice is stated plainly: **five phrasings to agree and keep in step**, which is why they are a table in this plan and a lookup in the code. **The `ah-uwa3` sentence stays exactly as it is**, for the case it was written for — a month ending in credit whose wages land too late. It is now guarded on late income actually existing. **Whether the hover says a faction-mate paid.** Chosen: **yes** — `A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays for this unit's orders.`, mirroring the upkeep note's shape word for word. *Rejected — stay silent*, since the figures balance and nothing looks wrong: rejected because money appearing from nowhere is the exact thing the upkeep, food and unclaimed-fund notes all exist to explain. *Rejected — `covers what its orders spend`*, more precise about the mechanism but breaking the parallel with the upkeep sentence. **Whether the sharer's own column shows what it lent.** Chosen: **yes, the sharer's month end drops by what it lends**, so the hex's total silver is unchanged — which is what maintenance sharing already does. *Rejected — leave the sharer alone*: simpler, but the hex would appear to gain 50 from nowhere and a player adding up their hex would find it. *Rejected — a separate bead for the sharer's side*: keeps this bead small, at the cost of leaving the hex total inconsistent until that bead was built. **And the reversal, recorded.** `ah-1wcw.1` decided that `short_for_orders` counts this unit alone and that the hex's shared purse is the advisory check's business. **The navigator reversed that here**, on seeing what it looks like on the screen. Do not restore it. **The sharing note, revised 2026-08-25 after the failed verification.** A covered unit can satisfy both sharing facts at once, and the first version of this plan ordered two notes so that one silenced the other. Chosen: **show both sentences**, on their own lines, where both hold: > `A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays this unit's upkeep.` > `A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays for this unit's orders.` *Rejected — let the orders sentence win when both apply.* One sentence, no new wording, and it is the one explaining why the unit is not short. Rejected because the upkeep is also being paid and would go unsaid. *Rejected — one sentence naming both* (`…pays this unit's upkeep and its orders.`). Says everything true in one line, at the cost of a third string that fires only in the overlap — the least often read and the most easily left behind when either sibling changes. **Neither sentence's wording is re-opened.** Both were agreed on 2026-08-24 and neither was at fault; only which of them the reader sees has changed. ### What the two verifications changed, 2026-08-25 The interview above stands: its wording was accepted and **no sentence in this bead changes**. **The placement instruction is void.** The plan said the orders note goes *"immediately BELOW `shared-silver-pays-upkeep`, since upkeep is the more specific of the two"*. That reasoning is sound when one note applies and wrong when both do — and when both do, the orders sentence is the one the reader needs, because it is the sentence explaining why the unit is **not** short, which is the whole point of the bead. Under `ah-x36v`'s contract the question disappears: every true sentence is shown, so position decides nothing about reachability. **Leave the notes where they are.** **Beast's merged sharing note is superseded.** It merged `shared-silver-pays-upkeep` and `shared-silver-pays-orders` into one note emitting both sentences. Correct against a one-sentence hover; unnecessary against `ah-x36v`'s, where the two stay separate and both simply appear — and actively wrong, because `ah-x36v` collapses the upkeep half into its own four-source sentence, which a merged note here would then duplicate. **Do not build it.** **The `ah-hvt8` example-suite question is answered by `ah-x36v` and needs no bead.** Psylocke noted that `ah-hvt8`'s per-note example suite cannot catch this class, because each note's `example()` sets only its own field, so every note wins for its own example and no *combination* is ever exercised. That is true, and it is why two beads failed the same day. It stops mattering once nothing can be shadowed: with every true sentence shown, a note unreachable only in combination cannot exist. The suite is still blind to combinations, but the failure it was blind to is gone. **Recorded rather than filed** — say so if you would rather it were a bead. ## Out of scope - **Maintenance sharing** (`shared_silver_covered`, `ah-e66j`). Untouched, and the model this follows. - **Which unit a short purse feeds.** All-or-nothing, as `ah-e66j` settled for maintenance. - **The `not-enough-silver` finding.** It is already right — that is how the defect was diagnosed — and this bead makes the column agree with it, not the other way round. - **`ah-t2pn`'s pool splitting.** A purse that covers everyone needs no split; one that does not lends nothing. If a partial split is ever wanted, it is a bead with its own interview. - **Any other note in `SILVER_NOTES`.** ## Validation ```bash cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core pnpm run check:generated pnpm run check:fast ``` All green, `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` in particular. **Then, by eye, and this is the check the bead was filed from**: load `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, find the mountain **(36,4) in Slounspifra** — `City Guards (13303)` is flagged *sharing* and holds 112,061, and the hex holds `Teachers 3824/6583/13805`, `Teacher 8447` and several `MinersA`. Give one of them a `STUDY`. - it must **not** show a negative month end, and **not** carry any shortfall sentence; - **[revised 2026-08-25]** its hover must read **two lines**, on separate lines: > `A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays this unit's upkeep.` > `A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays for this unit's orders.` **This is what the previous attempt got wrong** — it showed the upkeep line alone — and **the two-lines-on-two-lines part is checkable only by looking**: `packages/shared` has no jsdom, the join is a `\n` in a string and the break is a `className`, so a passing suite proves the string and nothing about the rendering; - turn **upkeep counting off** in Settings and the same hover must read the **orders line alone**; - `City Guards`' own month end must be **lower by exactly the study cost**; - remove the `sharing` flag from the fixture, and the unit must be short again, reading `This unit cannot pay the 50 its study costs.` — **not** the wages sentence. The rest of this bead was verified as passing at `ee550858` and does not need re-checking beyond confirming it still passes: the figures, the wages sentence, the lender's column and both control cases. ## Known traps - **Read the purse once, in `semantics.rs`, and pass it in.** A second computation in `silver.rs` is this defect happening again — `ah-abwx`, `ah-ycuj`, and now this. `report_shortfalls` and `forecast_hex` must call the same function. - **`ah-1wcw.1`'s comment on `short_for_orders` is now wrong.** Rewrite it. Left in place it tells the next reader that the per-unit rule still holds, and somebody will restore it. - **`at_month_end` needs the term too, not just `short_for_orders`.** The **−50** is what the navigator actually saw; fixing only the shortfall leaves the reported symptom on screen. - **`give` breaks the sentence pattern.** *"it gives away"*, not *"its X costs"*. A single template with an interpolated noun produces `its give costs`, which typechecks and ships. - **`wages-too-late` must be narrowed, not replaced.** `ah-uwa3`'s case is real and its sentence is right for it; the new note sits **below** it, and `ah-hvt8`'s example suite is what proves neither shadows the other. - **The all-or-nothing rule keeps the figures pessimistic.** A purse that cannot cover every claimant lends nothing — the same rule `ah-e66j` gives for maintenance, and for the same reason: which unit is fed cannot be told. - **`silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` excludes sharing hexes today**, which is why this shipped. Narrowing that exclusion is part of the bead, not a follow-up. - **[revised 2026-08-25] The note table is first-match, so two notes that can both apply are a race, not a precedence.** That is what failed verification here. Where two facts can hold at once and both are worth saying, they are **one note that says what applies** — not two ordered by which feels more specific. - **[revised 2026-08-25] `whitespace-pre-line` is what makes the second sentence visible.** Without it the `\n` collapses to a space and the two sentences run together on one line — which no unit test in `packages/shared` can catch, because that package has no jsdom and the change is a className. The string is testable; the rendering is a human check, and it is in *Validation*. - **[revised 2026-08-25] Keep the `countUpkeep` asymmetry.** The upkeep half is gated on it, the orders half is not, and merging the two notes is exactly where somebody will "tidy" that into one gate. There is a test named for it. - **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`: no effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** Every sentence here is asserted as a string out of `summariseUnit`, which is why increments 3 and 4 are writable.
acceptance_criteria:
A unit given STUDY in a hex where another of our units is sharing enough silver to cover it is not reported short and its Silver figure is not negative.

The 'wages arrive too late' sentence is never shown for a unit whose orders earn it no wages this month; whatever note a genuinely short studier gets names a cause that is true of it.

A regression test covers both: the sharing case, and the wording chosen for a studier that really is short with no sharer present.

title: The Silver column ignores TAKE, so a taker's money is missing from it
description:
Found by Xavier while planning ah-lu0f.4 (2026-08-24), and deliberately not fixed there.

`Intent::Take` appears nowhere in `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`. The Silver column's intent
walk falls through to `_ => {}` (silver.rs:1013) for it, so a TAKE contributes nothing to the
figure.

The ledger does credit it. `semantics::apply`'s `Intent::Take` arm grants a stated quantity
outright - its own comment says "A stated quantity needs no such caution: the order says how much,
and optimism grants it" - and only declines for `TAKE FROM <unit not in this hex> ALL`, where the
amount is one only that unit knows.

So a unit ordered

  TAKE FROM 17 100 SILV

has that $100 in the ledger and not in the Silver column. The column understates what the unit will
hold, which is the mirror image of the divergences ah-lu0f.2 and ah-lu0f.3 fixed in the other
direction.

> **REVISED 2026-08-25, after this plan failed verification.** Two things were wrong with it and both
> are recorded in place rather than rewritten away — see *User-facing decisions*, which now carries a
> "what the verification changed" section at its end.

>    together; `unitTooltip.ts:744` is `SILVER_NOTES.find(...)`, so **exactly one sentence is ever
>    shown**. This plan cited that mechanism correctly in *Known traps* and then designed against a
>    different one. **That half is not settled here** — it is `ah-x36v`'s (P0), which this bead now
>    depends on. Do not build the sentence ordering until that lands.
> 2. **The absent-source divergence leaked, and has been reversed.** Reproduced: adding
>    `TAKE FROM 99999 100 SILV` moved `shared_silver_covered` 60 → 0 and `upkeep` 0 → 60 for a unit
>    that the column does not credit at all. The ledger's generous credit stops a neighbour lending
>    for maintenance, and the column — which ignored the take — then shows the unit paying upkeep out
>    of money it has not got. The navigator reversed the decision: **the column counts it too.**
>
> **This bead is blocked on `ah-x36v` and must not be marked `planned` until that settles.**


The Silver column ignores `TAKE`. `Intent::Take` appears **nowhere** in
`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`; `forecast_unit`'s intent walk drops it through `_ => {}`
(`silver.rs:1013`). The ledger does credit it — `semantics.rs:1662`, which grants a stated quantity
outright: *"the order says how much, and optimism grants it"* — and only declines for
`TAKE FROM <unit not in this hex> ALL`, where the amount is one only that unit knows.

So a unit ordered `TAKE FROM 6567 100 SILV` has that $100 in the ledger and not in the column, and
the column understates what it will hold. It is the mirror image of the divergences `ah-lu0f.2` and
`ah-lu0f.3` fix in the other direction.

Found by Xavier while planning `ah-lu0f.4` and deliberately kept out of it: the rest of that epic
reconciles two readings of one rule and moves no figure, whereas this **adds a term to a user-facing
figure**. That made it the navigator's to approve, and they did — ranked P2 on 2026-08-24, with the
whole interface decided in the interview recorded under *User-facing decisions*.

**Blocked by `ah-lu0f.4`**, deliberately: that bead adds `transfer_shape(what, amount)`
(`silver.rs`), which classifies a transfer's selector and amount into `Unpriceable` / `Exact(n)` /
`All { except }`. This bead is its second caller. Building them in the other order means writing that
classification twice and then merging two edits to the same `match`.

**When this lands, a unit that takes silver from a neighbour shows it in the Silver column, with a
sentence saying where it came from.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `gather_receipts` also reads `TAKE`.
- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — `Receipts` and `UnitSilver` gain fields; one new
  `SilverDoubt` variant.
- `packages/core-client/src/generated/UnitSilver.ts` — regenerated, never hand-edited.
- `packages/core-client/src/builders.ts` — defaults for the new fields (`:233-234` is the pattern).
- `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts` — one new sentence, one new doubt sentence.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `gather_receipts(report, ordered, ruleset) -> BTreeMap<String, Receipts>` (`semantics.rs:887`).
  **This is the home for the new reading**, not `forecast_unit`: it already walks the whole hex,
  already knows which units the report shows where, already reads holdings off the report, and
  already filters to silver. `forecast_unit` sees only one unit and a closure API.
- `names_silver(text, ruleset) -> bool` (`semantics.rs:967`) — the "does this order name silver"
  test. Reuse; do not compare tags by hand.
- `Receipts` (`silver.rs:535`) with `silver: i64` and `givers: Vec<String>`, reached from
  `forecast_unit` as `facts.receipts` (`silver.rs:527`).
- `UnitSilver::received` (`silver.rs:160`) and `givers` (`:161`) — the shape the new fields copy,
  including the `<name> (<id>)` label format.
- `transfer_shape` / `TransferShape` — **added by `ah-lu0f.4`**. Use it to read the selector and
  amount; do not re-derive the three cases.
- `namesInAList` (`packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts`) — already writes "X and Y" for the gift
  sentence.

### The design of the code

**Rust — three new fields and one doubt.**

```rust
// On `Receipts`, beside `silver` and `givers`:
/// Silver this unit's own `TAKE` orders pull from units the report shows in this hex.
pub taken: i64,
/// Those sources, as `<name> (<id>)`, so the hover can name them.
pub taken_from: Vec<String>,
/// Whether a `TAKE ... ALL SILV` could not be priced, which silences the unit's whole figure.
///
/// A bool rather than the source's name, because the sentence the navigator chose names the rule
/// rather than the unit (see *User-facing decisions*).
pub take_all_unpriceable: bool,
```

`UnitSilver` gains `taken: i64` and `taken_from: Vec<String>` the same way `received`/`givers` are
carried through, and `SilverDoubt` gains:

```rust
/// `TAKE ... ALL SILV` from another unit: what that unit will have left to give depends on its own
/// month, which this per-unit pass has not run. Not the same as a source the report never shows -
/// that is not counted at all and raises no doubt.
TakesAllFromAnother,
```

**Which takes count, and which do not.** Both halves were decided in the interview:

| Order | Column |
|---|---|
| `TAKE FROM 6567 100 SILV`, 6567 in this hex | counted; `taken += 100`, `taken_from` gains its label |
| `TAKE FROM 999 100 SILV`, 999 not shown here | **counted** — see the revision note; the column follows the ledger |
| `TAKE FROM 6567 ALL SILV` | **not priced**: `take_all_unpriceable = true` → `SilverDoubt::TakesAllFromAnother` |
| `TAKE FROM 6567 10 GRAI` | ignored, as the gift pass already ignores non-silver |
| whole class / `UNIT` | `TransferShape::Unpriceable` — already `GivesAWholeClass`, unchanged |

**The absent-source case is no longer a divergence — REVISED.** The original plan had the column
skip it while the ledger credited it, on the reasoning that *"the ledger is generous so it never
warns falsely; the column is exact so it never shows money that is not there"*. **That split cannot
hold**, because the column *displays* figures derived from the ledger's settlement:
`shared_silver_covered` and `upkeep` are not independent of what the ledger believes. Proven by
probe — a take the column ignores still moved both. So `read_take` counts a source the report does
not show, exactly as the ledger does, and its sentence says the source is unverifiable.

**TypeScript — one sentence, one doubt sentence, one slot.**

In `unitTooltip.ts`, a new entry with `id: "taken-from"`:

```ts
when: ({ silver }) => silver.taken > 0 && silver.takenFrom.length > 0,
say: ({ silver }) =>
  `Includes $${silver.taken} taken from ${namesInAList(silver.takenFrom)} in this hex.`,
```

**Its slot is decided and is not free**: it goes **above** the existing `received`/"given by" entry,
which itself stays above the "given away to nobody" entry. Money in, then money out — the order the
arithmetic runs. `silverNote` is a hand-ordered first-match chain and `ah-hvt8` exists because a
sentence in the wrong slot silently swallowed the one below it, so put it in that slot and add the
test named in *The test plan* that proves all three can appear together, in that order.

And the doubt sentence, beside the other `doubt-*` entries:

```ts
"Taking all of another unit's silver cannot be counted until that unit's own month is settled."
```

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new. Three fields on a struct `gather_receipts` already builds per
hex, two carried onto `UnitSilver`, and one enum variant. No store, no new pass, no new parameter
threaded anywhere.

## User-facing decisions

The whole interface, decided with the navigator on 2026-08-24 over two rounds. Mockup:
`docs/ui/ah-awcm-take-hover.html` (committed by the planning session; it was
`.cerebro/scratchpad/ah-awcm-take-hover.html` during the discussion).

**Round 1 — three questions.**

1. **How the hover names taken money.** Chosen: **B, its own sentence** —
   `Includes $100 taken from Workers (6567) in this hex.`
   *Rejected:* **A**, widening the shipped sentence to `Includes $100 from …` — it changes a
   sentence that ships today and "from" stops saying who acted. **C**, counting it with no sentence —
   money would appear in *In* with nothing accounting for it, the exact complaint `ah-fvzu` fixed for
   the taxing flag.
2. **`TAKE FROM 6567 ALL SILV`.** Chosen: **refuse to price it**; the unit's figure becomes `?`.
   *Rejected:* using the source's printed holding (silently wrong the moment that unit spends
   anything), and counting nothing silently (the very defect this bead was filed about).
3. **A source the report does not show here.** Chosen: **do not count it** in the column, while the
   ledger goes on crediting it. The planner flagged that this reintroduces a divergence; the
   navigator kept it, and it is recorded as policy rather than defect — *the ledger is generous so it
   never warns falsely, the column is exact so it never shows money that is not there*, the same
   split `price_tax` already encodes. *Rejected:* following the ledger silently, and following it
   with a sentence admitting the source is unverifiable.

**Round 2 — three questions.**

4. **The refusal wording.** Chosen: **W2**, naming the rule —
   `Taking all of another unit's silver cannot be counted until that unit's own month is settled.`
   *Rejected:* **W1**, `What Workers (6567) will have left to give cannot be said, so this unit's
   silver cannot be either.` (long, two clauses), and **W3**, `What Workers (6567) has left to give
   cannot be said.` (leaves the reader to connect it to the `?`).
   **This is why the doubt carries no subject**: the chosen sentence names no unit, so
   `take_all_unpriceable` is a `bool` and not the source's name.
5. **Where the sentence sits.** Chosen: **O1** — taking, then gift, then given-away. Money in before
   money out, and a taking is the unit's own order so it leads. *Rejected:* **O2**, leaving the
   shipped gift sentence first.
6. **Two sources.** Chosen: **the same list form as gifts**, through `namesInAList` —
   `Includes $210 taken from Workers (6567) and MinersA (16435) in this hex.`
   *Rejected:* one sentence per source, which gives a unit taking from four neighbours four lines.

Every string above is final and is quoted verbatim in *The design of the code*. Nothing here is left
for the implementer to word.

### What the verification changed, 2026-08-25

The original interview above is kept intact — the questions were asked, those were the answers, and
the rejections still explain why the alternatives were not taken. Two of its outcomes did not
survive contact with the code, and this section records what replaced them and why. **Nothing else
in the interview is reopened.**

**Round 1, question 3 — REVERSED.** Chosen then: *do not count a take from a source the report does
not show, while the ledger goes on crediting it* — "the ledger is generous so it never warns falsely,
the column is exact so it never shows money that is not there". The planner flagged at the time that
this reintroduced a divergence and the navigator kept it deliberately.

**It cannot hold.** The column does not merely display its own arithmetic; it displays
`shared_silver_covered` and `upkeep`, which are *ledger-derived*. Probed on 2026-08-25 with two own
units in one hex, one starving with no silver and one rich enough to cover it:

| | `upkeep` | `shared_silver_covered` |
|---|---|---|
| no orders | 0 | 60 |
| `TAKE FROM 99999 100 SILV` | **60** | **0** |

The ledger credits the phantom 100, so step 4 decides the unit can pay for itself and no neighbour
lends; the column ignores the 100 and is left showing the unit paying upkeep it cannot afford. That
is what Psylocke saw as the figure moving and the *"A faction-mate's silver in this hex pays this
unit's upkeep"* sentence vanishing.

**Now chosen: the column counts it too**, exactly as the ledger does. One story, no leak.

**And its sentence, which round 1 mocked up and rejected only because nothing was being counted:**

> `Includes $100 taken from unit 999, which your report does not show here.`

Chosen verbatim on 2026-08-25. *Rejected:* `Includes $100 taken from unit 999.` (says nothing about
the source being unverifiable, so the player cannot tell this figure is weaker evidence than the
rest); folding it into the ordinary sentence, which would say *"in this hex"* about a unit that
demonstrably is not; and counting it silently, which is the money-from-nowhere complaint the whole
sentence set exists to answer.

**Round 2, question 5 — SETTLED, 2026-08-25 [revised].** Chosen originally: *O1, taking then gift
then given-away — money in before money out, and a taking is the unit's own order so it leads.*

That was an ordering of several sentences shown together, against a hover that showed **one**
(`unitTooltip.ts:744`), which is why it failed verification. **`ah-x36v` has since settled the
contract with the navigator: the hover shows every sentence that is true, in `SILVER_NOTES`
order.** So **O1 is now buildable exactly as it was agreed, and nothing about it is re-asked.**

Two consequences, both checked against the table on 2026-08-25:

- **No note moves.** `includes-take` (`:660`), `includes-gift` (`:679`) and `given-to-nobody`
  (`:698`) already sit in that sequence. O1's ordering is satisfied by the table as it stands, so
  this bead reorders nothing — it only stops relying on one of them winning.
- **A fourth sentence may appear above them, and that is correct.** `works-by-default` (`:626`)
  sits higher and is what stole the take sentence in the observed failure (*"a unit with a `TAKE`
  and no month-long order shows only the no-month-long-order sentence"*). Under the new contract it
  appears **as well**, not instead. The navigator saw exactly this case when choosing the contract —
  it is case 2 of `docs/ui/ah-x36v-hover-contract.html`, drawn with all four lines — so it is
  agreed, not a side effect.

**This bead therefore writes no ordering code and no new sentence for the hover.** `ah-x36v` makes
the three appear; this bead's remaining hover work is its own new sentence (decision 3 above) and
the tests that pin all four appearing together.

### What this bead must now test — **[revised 2026-08-25]**

With `ah-x36v` landed, the case that failed verification becomes a test this bead owns:

- `a unit that takes, receives and destroys is told all three` — in O1's order, asserted as the
  joined string, verbatim.
- `a unit that takes and has no month-long order is told both` — **the observed failure**: the
  works-by-default sentence *and* the take sentence, in table order.
- `a take from a source the report does not show says so` — decision 3's new sentence, verbatim:
  `Includes $100 taken from unit 999, which your report does not show here.`

**`ah-x36v` must be merged before this bead is built.** The dependency is wired in bd; without it
