title: A unit is warned it will starve even when the faction's unclaimed silver would rescue it
description:
Step 7 of the rules' maintenance payment order is 'Unclaimed silver', and the rules say it happens by itself: 'If you have silver in your unclaimed fund, then that silver will be automatically claimed by units that would otherwise starve.' No CLAIM order is needed.

The upkeep path never looks at the purse. charge_upkeep (semantics.rs:842) takes only a Ledger and a Hex; report_shortfalls and check_resources take no purse either. FactionPurse is built at semantics.rs:260-263 and handed only to forecast_hex, so the whole warning path is blind to it.

The result is a false alarm in the commonest possible situation - a young faction with most of its 10000 starting silver still unclaimed is told its units are about to starve. semantics.rs:3919 a_unit_that_cannot_pay_its_upkeep_is_warned_about builds a report with no purse at all and asserts the warning, so nothing currently tests the case.
design:
## Context

Step 7 of the rules' maintenance payment order is **unclaimed silver**, and it happens without an
order: *"If you have silver in your unclaimed fund, then that silver will be automatically claimed by
units that would otherwise starve."*

The warning path never looks at the fund. `FactionPurse` is built once at
`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:261` and handed **only** to `forecast_hex`; `charge_upkeep`
(`semantics.rs:842`), `report_shortfalls` (`semantics.rs:1411`) and `check_resources`
(`semantics.rs:908`) never receive it. Inside `silver.rs` the purse is read at exactly one place —
`silver.rs:458`, the `CLAIM` arm — and nowhere else.

So the client raises a false alarm in the commonest situation the game has: a young faction still
holding most of its 10,000 starting silver is told its units are about to starve. Nothing tests the
case — `semantics.rs:3919 a_unit_that_cannot_pay_its_upkeep_is_warned_about` builds a report with no
purse at all.

When this lands, a unit whose maintenance the faction's unclaimed fund will cover raises no warning
and shows an `Upkeep` of 0 with a note saying what paid it; when the fund cannot reach everybody,
every unit that owes unpayable maintenance is named by a new `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` finding
carrying the faction-wide total.

**Two sibling beads move the same number and must not be fought.** `ah-e66j` (step 4, faction silver
in the region) and `ah-eacd` (steps 5–6, food after silver) both *reduce* the shortfall this bead
then settles the fund against. The seam below is designed so neither needs rework: they change what
goes **into** `UpkeepClaim.short`, and this bead owns only what happens after. Neither is a blocker
and no dependency edge is wired; see *Known traps* for the one visible consequence of building this
first.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The settlement, new, in `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`

`feed_from_faction_food` (`silver.rs:852`, `pub fn feed_from_faction_food(claims: &[FoodClaim]) ->
BTreeMap<String, Option<i64>>`) is the working precedent and the shape to copy: a pure function
taking a claim per unit and settling them together, living in `silver.rs` beside `FoodClaim`
(`silver.rs:815`) and `food_claim` (`silver.rs:830`). Do the same here.

```rust
/// One unit's unpayable maintenance, for the faction-wide settlement of step 7.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UpkeepClaim {
    pub unit_id: String,
    /// Silver of this unit's *maintenance* that its own silver cannot cover, after every earlier
    /// step of the payment order has already been applied. Never more than the fee itself: what a
    /// unit overspends on its orders is its orders' fault and no business of the fund's.
    pub short: i64,
}

/// What the faction's unclaimed fund does about the units that cannot pay their maintenance.
///
/// Faction-wide, like the fund itself: one settlement for the whole report, never one per hex.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UpkeepSettlement {
    /// Per unit, the maintenance the fund paid. **Empty unless the fund reaches every claimant** -
    /// when it is short, which unit it fed is undeterminable, so it feeds none of them here.
    pub covered: BTreeMap<String, i64>,
    /// Every unit that owed maintenance it could not pay, whether or not the fund reached it.
    pub claimants: BTreeSet<String>,
    /// What the claimants owed between them.
    pub owed: i64,
    /// What the fund had for them, after this month's `CLAIM` orders took theirs. Never negative.
    pub available: i64,
    /// `owed - available`, floored at zero. `> 0` means the fund could not reach everybody.
    pub short: i64,
}

impl UpkeepSettlement {
    /// Whether the fund is in play at all. `false` leaves every surface exactly as it is today.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn active(&self) -> bool { self.available > 0 && self.owed > 0 }
}

/// Settles step 7. `available` is `None` where the report header states no `Unclaimed silver:`
/// line, and `Some(n)` where it does - already net of this month's `CLAIM` orders.
///
/// `None`, or `Some(n)` with `n <= 0`, returns `UpkeepSettlement::default()`: an inactive
/// settlement that changes nothing. That is a decision, not a guard - see the plan's
/// *User-facing decisions*.
#[must_use]
pub fn settle_unclaimed(claims: &[UpkeepClaim], available: Option<i64>) -> UpkeepSettlement
```

Behaviour, exhaustively:

| `available` | `owed` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | any | `default()` — inactive |
| `Some(n)`, `n <= 0` | any | `default()` — inactive |
| `Some(n)`, `n > 0` | `0` | `available = n`, everything else empty/zero; `active()` is `false` |
| `Some(n)`, `n > 0` | `owed <= n` | `covered` = every claim's `short`; `short = 0` |
| `Some(n)`, `n > 0` | `owed > n` | `covered` **empty**; `short = owed - n`; `claimants` populated |

Claims with `short <= 0` are not claims: skip them, and keep them out of `claimants`.

### `Ledger` — two new fields, `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:774`

`Ledger` already carries `upkeep: BTreeMap<String, i64>` holding the **full** fee, read only to word
a finding ("orders and upkeep" against "orders"). Two more maps are needed, both keyed by unit id:

- `upkeep_drawn: BTreeMap<String, i64>` — what maintenance actually took **off the silver balance**,
  i.e. `charge_upkeep`'s local `charged = (owed - late_income(facts, region)).max(0)`
  (`semantics.rs:842`, the `if charged > 0` block). `upkeep` is the fee; `upkeep_drawn` is the
  overdraft it can be blamed for, and the two differ for any unit that works or entertains.
  Written in the same loop that already computes `charged`, unconditionally where `owed > 0`
  (including `charged == 0`, so the map's absence means "no fee", not "fee covered by wages").
- `upkeep_relieved: BTreeMap<String, i64>` — what the settlement takes back off that overdraft.
  Filled by the caller after `ledger_for` returns, never inside it.

**Do not credit `ledger.balance` instead.** `check_sailing` (`semantics.rs:2604`) and
`check_movement` also read the ledger, and moving a balance to make one message read correctly is
how two checks end up disagreeing about one turn. The relief is a term the silver path adds on top,
and nothing else sees it.

Add one helper beside `balance_of` (`semantics.rs:1370`):

```rust
/// A unit's silver balance as the shortfall check must read it: what the ledger holds, plus what
/// the faction's unclaimed fund took back off its maintenance.
fn silver_balance(ledger: &Ledger<'_>, unit_id: &str) -> i64 {
    balance_of(ledger, unit_id, SILVER)
        + ledger.upkeep_relieved.get(unit_id).copied().unwrap_or(0)
}
```

### `review_turn` — two passes over the regions, `semantics.rs:240`

The settlement is faction-wide and the checks are per hex, so the region loop splits in two. Build
every hex and its ledger first, settle, then run the per-hex work:

```rust
// Pass 1. `Hex<'_>` borrows `report` and `ordered`; `Ledger<'a>` borrows `ruleset`; both outlive
// the function, so holding them is a lifetime no-op.
let mut hexes: Vec<(Hex<'_>, Ledger<'_>)> = report
    .regions
    .iter()
    .map(|region| {
        let hex = Hex::read(region, &ordered);
        let ledger = ledger_for(&hex, ruleset);
        (hex, ledger)
    })
    .collect();

let claims = upkeep_claims(&hexes);                       // new, below
let available = purse.unclaimed.map(|n| (n - total_claimed(report, &ordered)).max(0));
let settlement = settle_unclaimed(&claims, available);
apply_relief(&mut hexes, &settlement);                    // new, below

// Pass 2. Exactly today's loop body, reading `hexes` instead of building as it goes.
```

Three things this must preserve, each of which a test in the suite already pins:

- `forecast_hex` still runs for **every** region, including one with no own units; the
  `if hex.units.is_empty() { continue; }` guard still covers only the checks.
- `silver` and `findings` are still appended in region order, and the existing
  `findings[start..].sort_by_key(...)` within a hex is untouched.
- `check_faction` still runs once, after every hex.

Cost: this holds every hex's ledger at once instead of one at a time, on a path that runs on every
keystroke once typing settles. The *work* is unchanged — each ledger is still built exactly once —
and only the peak memory moves. That is the price of a faction-wide term, and it is the same price
`check_faction` and `gather_receipts` already pay.

Two new private helpers in `semantics.rs`:

```rust
/// Every unit that owes maintenance its own silver cannot cover, across the whole report.
///
/// The overdraft is split before the fund ever sees it: at most what maintenance drew is
/// maintenance's fault, and the rest belongs to the unit's orders. A unit holding $10, buying $350
/// of horses and owing $40 is short $380 - of which the fund may pay $40 and never the $340.
fn upkeep_claims(hexes: &[(Hex<'_>, Ledger<'_>)]) -> Vec<UpkeepClaim>;

/// Writes `settlement.covered` into each ledger's `upkeep_relieved`. A no-op for an inactive
/// settlement and for one the fund could not cover, whose `covered` is empty by construction.
fn apply_relief(hexes: &mut [(Hex<'_>, Ledger<'_>)], settlement: &UpkeepSettlement);
```

`upkeep_claims` skips a unit in `ledger.doubted` — `charge_upkeep` already charges a guessed
headcount nothing, so it has no shortfall to claim.

### `total_claimed` — extracted, `semantics.rs:3073`

`check_claims` already builds the list of `Intent::Claim` placements and sums them
(`semantics.rs:3095-3110`). Lift that sum into a free function used by **both**, so the fund cannot
be spent twice by two pieces of code that disagree:

```rust
/// What this month's `CLAIM` orders ask for, across the whole report. `CLAIM` resolves during the
/// month and maintenance is settled at its end, so this comes off the fund before step 7 sees it.
fn total_claimed(report: &ParsedReport, ordered: &OrderedUnits) -> i64;
```

`check_claims` keeps its own behaviour exactly — including declining to fire when the header states
no purse (`semantics.rs:3084`), for the reason its doc comment gives. It is **not** widened.

### `report_shortfalls` — `semantics.rs:1411`

Three changes, and nothing else:

1. Every read of a unit's silver balance goes through `silver_balance(ledger, who)` rather than the
   raw ledger entry — the per-unit loop's `for ((unit_id, tag), balance) in mine` arm where
   `tag == SILVER`, and the pooled path's `sharers.iter().map(|o| balance_of(ledger, ..., &tag))`
   sum and its `balance_of(...) < 0` filter.
2. `spenders(...)` (`semantics.rs:1560`) is fed the **unpaid** fee, not the full one:
   `ledger.upkeep.get(who) - ledger.upkeep_relieved.get(who)`, floored at zero. Without this a unit
   whose fee the fund paid is told "its orders and upkeep spend $350" when its orders spend $350 and
   its upkeep is paid — the sentence's own arithmetic would not add up.
   The hex-level message's `owed` sum (`semantics.rs:1530`) takes the same subtraction.
3. Nothing else. The `sharers` / `pooled` machinery, the `doubted` handling and the item path are
   untouched.

### The new check code — `semantics.rs:80` (`mod codes`) and `semantics.rs:3073` area

```rust
pub const UPKEEP_EXCEEDS_UNCLAIMED: Code = Code("upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed");
```

Appended **last** to `codes::ALL`, whose length literal goes `[Code; 25]` → `[Code; 26]` — the
array's doc comment states that new-here-last rule and why (the generated TypeScript copies this
order).

The finding is raised by a new faction-wide check, called from `review_turn` after pass 2 beside
`check_faction`, modelled on `check_claims` (`semantics.rs:3073`) — same shape, same reasoning,
including naming every participant because none is more at fault than the others:

```rust
/// Every unit that owes maintenance it cannot pay, when the faction's unclaimed fund cannot cover
/// them all between them.
///
/// Faction-wide rather than per hex, because the fund is: what one hex's units eat is what another
/// hex's cannot. Every claimant is named and the message states the total, so a unit reading it is
/// not being blamed for a shortfall that is the faction's - the same reasoning
/// `claims-exceed-unclaimed` gives for naming every claiming unit.
fn check_upkeep_fund(
    report: &ParsedReport,
    settlement: &UpkeepSettlement,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
);
```

It emits nothing unless `settlement.active() && settlement.short > 0`. The `Finding` carries
`region_id` and `unit_id` and **no line** — maintenance belongs to no order, so there is no line to
point at; `check_claims` sets `line`/`column_start`/`column_end` from its placed intent, and this
one leaves all three `None`. Per-hex sorting already puts a line-less finding last within its hex
(`finding.line.is_none()` is the first sort key), which is where it belongs.

### The column — `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`

One new field on `UnitSilver` (`silver.rs:82`), beside `own_food_covered` and
`faction_food_covered`, whose doc comments explain exactly why such a field exists:

```rust
/// Silver of this unit's upkeep paid by the faction's unclaimed fund, at step 7 of the payment
/// order. `0` for every unit the fund did not reach - which is every unit whenever the fund
/// cannot reach them all, because then which one it fed cannot be told.
///
/// Carried separately from the two food figures only so the hover can say which paid: all three
/// leave `upkeep` at the same number, and a zero there reads as a defect until something says why.
pub unclaimed_covered: i64,
```

`upkeep` is reduced by it, exactly as the two food figures already reduce it.

`forecast_unit` (`silver.rs:388`) is per unit and pure and **must stay so**: it cannot compute a
faction-wide settlement, and it takes no new parameter. `Lookups<'_>` (`silver.rs:207`) is not the
place either — it carries closures that need `semantics`' help, not values.

**Copy the pattern already used for the faction-food pool.** `forecast_hex` pushes every unit's
forecast, then settles and mutates the pushed values in place (`semantics.rs:391-411`, the
`feed_from_faction_food` block). Do the same, in a second loop directly after that one:

```rust
// `forecast_hex` gains one parameter: `settlement: &UpkeepSettlement`.
//
// Positional, exactly as the food pass above: `into[start..]` was pushed one per unit in
// `hex.units` order, and the comment there says why a lookup by id would not do.
for (ordered, forecast) in hex.units.iter().zip(into[start..].iter_mut()) {
    let Some(owed) = forecast.upkeep else { continue };   // a doubted fee stays doubted
    if settlement.covered.is_empty() {
        // The fund could not reach everybody, so it reached nobody here: the figure stays as it
        // is (the navigator's choice - see *User-facing decisions*, round 2 question 1) and only
        // the hover's note changes, driven by `claimants` below.
        continue;
    }
    let covered = settlement.covered.get(&ordered.unit.unit_id).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    forecast.unclaimed_covered = covered;
    forecast.upkeep = Some((owed - covered).max(0));
}
```

The hover's "the fund is short" note is driven by `settlement.short > 0 && settlement.claimants
.contains(unit_id)`, which needs no field of its own on `UnitSilver` beyond what is already there —
**but the tooltip is TypeScript and cannot see the settlement**, so it does need one. Add a second
field rather than deriving it:

```rust
/// Whether this unit owes maintenance it cannot pay and the faction's unclaimed fund cannot reach
/// every unit in that position. Drives the hover's note and **never changes a figure**: the
/// `upkeep` on show is this unit's whole remaining fee, pessimistically (`ah-fjty`).
pub unclaimed_contended: bool,
```

**Note on the fee the relief is subtracted from.** The column's `upkeep` is the fee after food and
*before* late income; `upkeep_drawn` in the ledger is after late income. They are different numbers
on purpose, and `unclaimed_covered` is derived from the ledger's, so it can be smaller than the
column's `upkeep`. Subtracting it is still correct: the column already nets late income through
`income`, and `unitTable.ts`'s `shownSilver` computes `atMonthEnd - upkeep`.

**A unit id shared by two own units** is already conflated by `Ledger.balance`, which is keyed by
`(unit_id, tag)`. The settlement inherits exactly that and adds no new hazard — which is why the
loop above is positional over `hex.units` and only the *lookup* is by id.

### The hover — `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts`

`silverNote` (`unitTooltip.ts:169`) is a "one note, first match wins" table. Two entries join it,
both gated on `countUpkeep` like every other upkeep note:

- `silver.unclaimedContended === true` → `There is not enough unclaimed silver to feed every unit
  that needs it.` Placed **after** the `short_for_orders` note (an order the game will refuse still
  outranks an upkeep that was quietly paid — the existing comment at `unitTooltip.ts:210` states
  that ordering rule) and **before** the two food notes, because it is a doubt about the figure on
  show and the shipped `contested-faction-food` doubt sorts above the informational lines.
- `silver.unclaimedCovered > 0` → `The faction's unclaimed silver covers {n} of this unit's
  upkeep.`, with `{n}` the field's value. Placed **after** both food notes: the payment order runs
  food at steps 1–2 and the fund at step 7, and these notes are already ordered by that.

The two are mutually exclusive by construction — `unclaimedCovered` is non-zero only when the fund
reached everybody, and `unclaimedContended` only when it did not — so their relative order can never
actually decide which is shown. They are placed as above so that the table still reads in the
payment order's own sequence.

`packages/shared/src/unitTable.ts:333` (`shownSilver`) needs **no change**: it reads
`silver.atMonthEnd - silver.upkeep`, and `upkeep` already carries the relief.

### The settings row — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx:484`

A fourth entry in the existing **Resources** group, directly beneath
`claims-exceed-unclaimed`. No new group, no new machinery.

`DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS` (`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:43`) turns every code on except
`hex-unguarded`, so the new code is on by default with no edit — and
`reconcileAdvisoryChecks` (`settingsStore.ts:51`) starts from the defaults and copies over only
codes a stored blob actually names, so an existing user's saved settings pick the new check up at
its default. **No migration is needed, and none must be written**: this is the generic case that
machinery exists for, not the "old default must be migrated rather than clamped" trap.

### Generated TypeScript

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` and
`packages/core-client/src/generated/UnitSilver.ts` are generated from the Rust core and must not be
hand-edited. Regenerate with:

```
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

`pnpm run check:generated` fails the build if they are stale.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test.

1. **The settlement is a pure function.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`, `fn the_fund_pays_every_unit_that_cannot_pay_its_own_upkeep`
   — three claims of 60, 60 and 40 against `Some(8450)` asserts `covered` has all three at their own
   `short`, `owed == 160`, `short == 0`.
   Then `fn the_fund_pays_nobody_when_it_cannot_pay_them_all` — the same claims against `Some(100)`
   asserts `covered.is_empty()`, `claimants.len() == 3`, `short == 60`.
   Then `fn a_fund_the_report_never_stated_settles_nothing` (`None`) and
   `fn a_fund_the_claims_emptied_settles_nothing` (`Some(0)`), both asserting
   `settlement == UpkeepSettlement::default()` and `!settlement.active()`.
   GREEN: `UpkeepClaim`, `UpkeepSettlement`, `settle_unclaimed`.

2. **The ledger records what maintenance actually drew.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn the_ledger_separates_the_fee_from_what_it_drew_off_the_balance` — a unit ordered `WORK` in a
   wage-paying region, owing 60 and earning 40 late, asserts `ledger.upkeep` is 60 and
   `ledger.upkeep_drawn` is 20.
   GREEN: the `upkeep_drawn` field, written in `charge_upkeep`'s existing loop.

3. **A rescued unit raises no warning.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_unit_the_unclaimed_fund_can_feed_is_not_warned` — one 6-man unit
   holding nothing, no orders, header `Unclaimed silver: $8450`; asserts no finding of any code.
   GREEN: the two-pass `review_turn`, `upkeep_claims`, `apply_relief`, `upkeep_relieved`,
   `silver_balance`, and `report_shortfalls` reading through it.

4. **Orders keep their own shortfall.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn the_fund_pays_the_upkeep_and_the_shopping_is_still_unaffordable` — a
   4-man unit holding $10, buying $350 of horses, owing $40, against a $8450 fund; asserts exactly
   one `not-enough-silver` whose message is
   `short $340: this unit can have $10 and its orders spend $350` — **"orders"**, not "orders and
   upkeep", which is increment 3's `spenders` change proving itself.

5. **A short fund names every claimant.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn every_unit_is_named_when_the_fund_cannot_feed_them_all` — the three

   `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` findings, one per unit, each with the message in *User-facing
   decisions*, each with `line == None`.
   Then `fn a_fund_that_covers_everybody_names_nobody` — the same report at `$8450`, asserting no
   finding of that code.
   Then `fn a_report_with_no_unclaimed_line_warns_exactly_as_before` and
   `fn an_empty_fund_warns_exactly_as_before`, both asserting the per-unit `not-enough-silver`
   message is unchanged and no `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` is raised.
   GREEN: `codes::UPKEEP_EXCEEDS_UNCLAIMED`, `codes::ALL` at 26, `check_upkeep_fund`.

6. **CLAIM takes the fund first.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_claim_of_the_whole_fund_leaves_nothing_for_upkeep` — header
   `Unclaimed silver: $8450`, one unit ordered `CLAIM 8450`, another owing 60 it cannot pay;
   asserts the second unit's `not-enough-silver` is raised exactly as it is today and no
   `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` (available is 0, so the settlement is inactive).
   Then `fn a_partial_claim_leaves_the_rest_for_upkeep` — `CLAIM 8400` against the same, asserting
   one `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` naming `$60` owed and `$50` unclaimed.
   GREEN: `total_claimed` extracted and used by both `check_claims` and the settlement.

7. **The column shows what the fund paid.**
   RED: `silver.rs`, `fn a_unit_the_fund_feeds_shows_no_upkeep` — asserts `upkeep == Some(0)` and

   Then `fn a_contended_fund_leaves_the_upkeep_where_it_is` — asserts `upkeep == Some(60)`,
   `unclaimed_covered == 0` and `unclaimed_contended == true`, which is the navigator's chosen

   GREEN: the `unclaimed_covered` and `unclaimed_contended` fields, and `forecast_hex`'s second
   loop.

8. **Regenerate the TypeScript.** `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
   --test generated_ts`, then `pnpm run check:generated`. No hand edits.

9. **The hover says which step paid.**
   RED: `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts`,
   `fn the_note_names_the_unclaimed_fund_when_it_paid_the_upkeep` and
   `fn the_note_says_the_fund_cannot_reach_everybody`, asserting the two strings verbatim and that
   neither appears with `countUpkeep` off.
   GREEN: two entries in `silverNote`'s table, at the positions given above.

10. **The settings row.**
    RED: `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, asserting the Resources group
    renders the new title and that toggling it off silences the finding.
    GREEN: the entry at `SettingsDialog.tsx:484`.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core` (`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`)** — every test named in *Increments*.
Beyond those, three that pin the shape rather than a case:

- `fn the_fund_never_pays_for_orders` — a unit with no fee at all and a large overdraft, against a
  large fund: asserts its `not-enough-silver` is byte-identical to today's.
- `fn a_guessed_headcount_does_not_claim_from_the_fund` — a unit with `men_estimated`, which
  `charge_upkeep` already charges nothing: asserts it is absent from `claimants` and that a fund
  too small for the rest is still judged without it.
- `fn the_fund_is_counted_once_across_several_hexes` — three regions, one claiming unit each, owing
  60 apiece against a fund of 100: asserts `short == 80`, proving the settlement is faction-wide and
  not per hex. **This is the bead's acceptance criterion about counting once, and the one a per-hex
  implementation passes every other test but fails.**

**Two existing tests are rewritten, and must be**, since they pin the defect:

- `semantics.rs:3919 a_unit_that_cannot_pay_its_upkeep_is_warned_about` builds a report with no
  purse. Keep it exactly as it is — it is now the `None` case and still asserts the warning — and
  add a sibling `a_unit_that_cannot_pay_its_upkeep_is_warned_about_when_the_fund_is_empty` for
  `Some(0)`.
- Any test in the `validate_real_orders` corpus (`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`) whose
  expected finding count changes because a committed fixture has an unclaimed line. **Check this
  before writing anything else in increment 3** — several fixtures are real turn reports of young
  factions, which is precisely the case this bead changes.

**TypeScript** — `packages/shared`: `unitTooltip.test.ts` (both notes, both `countUpkeep` states),
`unitTable.test.ts` (a rescued unit's column figure), `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` (the row and its
toggle), `settingsStore.test.ts` (a stored blob without the new code comes back with it on).

Note the traps file: `packages/shared` has no jsdom, and its component tests render with
`renderToStaticMarkup`. Everything above is either a pure module (`unitTooltip.ts`, `unitTable.ts`,
`settingsStore.ts`) or a static render of a dialog — no effect-level test is asked for anywhere.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast` (lint, typecheck, unit/tooling, `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy`) and `pnpm run check:generated`. The browser and native suites are CI's.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator over two rounds against four HTML mockups. The chosen mockup is
`docs/ui/ah-fjty-unclaimed-fund.html`.

**Round 1, question 1 — where the rescue shows.** Three variants were built and put side by side
(`ah-fjty-purse-a.html`, `ah-fjty-purse-b.html`).
**Chosen: A — the column and the warning both move.** The `Upkeep` row drops by what the fund paid
and a hover note says so, exactly as `ah-7cdt` treated faction food.
*Rejected — B, warning only, column untouched*: keeps `ah-1wcw.1`'s settled rule that the column
counts each unit alone, and keeps the fund's drain visible as a red figure — but it leaves a unit
showing −60 in red with no warning and nothing explaining it, which is the divergence `ah-abwx` and
`ah-ycuj` were filed about. `charge_upkeep`'s own comment already rejects that shape: *"warning that
a unit cannot pay a fee its faction-mates' grain already paid is two surfaces contradicting each
other."*
*Rejected — B′, figures untouched but a hover note*: cheaper, and still shows a negative number that
will not happen.

**Round 1, question 2 — when the fund cannot cover everybody.** The total is exact; the blame is not.
**Chosen: shape 1 — name every claimant, each carrying the faction-wide total.** The shape
`claims-exceed-unclaimed` already uses, for the reason its doc comment gives.
*Rejected — one faction-scope finding*: quiet and it scales, but a faction-scope finding has no line
to point at, so nothing marks the units in the orders being edited.
*Rejected — rescue in report order and warn the rest*: precise-looking and invented. `ah-7cdt`
rejected exactly this for the food pool: *"The order is ours, not the engine's, so one unit would be
shown starving for a reason that exists only inside this app."*

**Round 1, question 3 — a stated `Unclaimed silver: $0`.**
**Chosen: today's per-unit message, unchanged.** Not arbitrary against the `$1` case, which does get
the new message: with $1 somebody is partly rescued, so blame is undeterminable; with $0 every
unit's shortfall is exactly its own. The same reasoning extends to a fund this month's `CLAIM`
orders have emptied, which is why `available <= 0` is inactive.
*Rejected — the fund-aware message with a $0 fund*: consistent, and it tells the player the fund is
empty, but it costs a broke faction its line-level marks every single turn.

**Round 1, question 4 — its own switch.**
**Chosen: a new `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` code** in Settings → Resources, beneath "Claiming more
than the faction has".
*Rejected — reuse `not-enough-silver`*: no new switch, but turning off "Overspent silver" would then
also silence every starvation warning.

**Round 2, question 1 — the column when the fund is short** (`ah-fjty-round2.html` §1).
**Chosen: 1b — show the un-rescued figure, in red, with a note.** The pessimistic answer: assume
this unit is the one that goes without. Always a number, never optimistic.
*Rejected — 1a, `?`*: this was the planner's recommendation and the navigator chose against it. It
would have been consistent with contested faction food and with `ah-1wcw.1`'s *never a number that
might be wrong*, but in a poor faction every short unit's column goes to `?` at once, and `?` is
less useful than a number.
**Consequence the implementer must not undo:** there is **no new `SilverDoubt` variant** in this
bead, and `at_month_end` is never made `None` by the fund. The known overstatement — summing the
column across units overstates the faction's real shortfall — is accepted deliberately.

**Round 2, question 2 — `CLAIM` spends the same fund** (§2).
**Chosen: 2a — claims first.** `CLAIM` resolves during the month; maintenance is settled at its end.
*Rejected — ignore claims*: simpler, and wrong in exactly the situation where the fund matters most.

**Round 2, questions 3 and 4 — the strings. These ship verbatim.**

| Where | String |
|---|---|
| `upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed` finding | `your units owe ${owed} of upkeep they cannot pay and the faction has ${available} unclaimed` |
| Hover, the fund paid this unit | `The faction's unclaimed silver covers {n} of this unit's upkeep.` |
| Hover, the fund is short | `There is not enough unclaimed silver to feed every unit that needs it.` |
| Settings → Resources, title | `Upkeep the faction cannot pay` |
| Settings → Resources, description | `Units that cannot pay their maintenance, when the faction's unclaimed silver will not cover the shortfall either.` |

`{owed}` is `settlement.owed` and `{available}` is `settlement.available` — the fund **after**
`CLAIM` orders, not the header figure. `{n}` is silver, not a count of anything, matching its two
shipped neighbours ("Faction food in this hex covers 10 of this unit's upkeep." and "This unit's own
food covers 50 of its upkeep."). The finding's `$` signs are literal, as in
`claims-exceed-unclaimed`; the hover notes carry none, as in the two food notes.
*Rejected wordings*: `short $60 of upkeep across your faction: …` (leads with the actionable number,
but breaks the pairing with `claims-exceed-unclaimed`); `this unit may starve: …` (names the
consequence, which no other message in this app does); "fund" for "silver" in the hover (the report
header itself says *Unclaimed silver*); "Starving units" as the settings title.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** a unit with a
guessed headcount takes no part (`charge_upkeep` already charges it nothing); the new check is on by
default, through `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS`' existing "everything except `hex-unguarded`" rule, with
no migration; the new finding carries no line.

## Out of scope

- **Steps 4, 5, 6 and 8, 9 of the payment order.** Step 4 (faction silver in the region) is
  `ah-e66j`; steps 5–6 (food after silver, for a unit with no `CONSUME` flag) are `ah-eacd`. Both
  reduce `UpkeepClaim.short` and neither is touched here. Steps 8–9 are allied silver and food, and
  are out of scope permanently: we cannot see an ally's purse.
- **Widening `check_claims`.** `WITHDRAW` also spends the unclaimed fund and is not counted against
  it — that is `ah-tdsi`, and `total_claimed` is deliberately named for what it counts today so that
  bead can widen it without ambiguity.
- **Any new `SilverDoubt` variant**, per round 2 question 1.
- **The `Upkeep` row's own setting.** Whether the column counts upkeep at all remains
  `ah-1wcw.4`'s toggle, untouched.
- **Contention for regional pools** (`ah-t2pn`) and the `PILLAGE` divergences (`ah-abwx`,
  `ah-cxxa`). The two-pass `review_turn` this bead builds is the hex-level structure `ah-t2pn` will
  want, but nothing here settles anything for it.

## Validation

```
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run check:generated
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (inside `check:fast`).

Checkable by looking, and worth doing once before opening the PR: load a committed fixture whose
header carries an `Unclaimed silver:` line and a young faction, turn the **Upkeep** setting on, and
confirm that units previously marked with `not-enough-silver` now show `Upkeep 0` with the note, and
that the findings list is shorter by exactly those units.

## Known traps

- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (`ah-nass`, and the traps file). Its component tests render
  with `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects and shows a zustand store only its module-load
  default. Nothing in this plan asks for an effect-level test there:
  `unitTooltip.ts`, `unitTable.ts` and `settingsStore.ts` are pure modules and are tested as such,
  and `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` is a static render. Store state goes through
  `testing/renderWithStoreState`; `packages/shared/src/testing/README.md` has the pattern.
- **`coreVocabulary.generated.ts` and `generated/UnitSilver.ts` are generated.** Editing either by
  hand passes locally and fails `pnpm run check:generated`. Regenerate with
  `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts`.
- **`codes::ALL` carries its own length** — `[Code; 25]` becomes `[Code; 26]`, and the compiler's
  error if you forget names the array rather than the constant you added.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array**, if you go reading sibling beads' plans.
- **The corpus test will move.** `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` audits every committed
  fixture, and several are real young-faction reports with an unclaimed line — exactly the case this
  bead changes. Expect it to go red in increment 3 and read the diff rather than loosening the
  assertion.
- **Building this before `ah-eacd` slightly over-spends the fund.** Until steps 5–6 model food after
  silver, a unit that would really have eaten its own grain still claims from the fund, so a fund
  that is nearly enough may be exhausted by a unit that never needed it and another unit is warned
  in its place. That is strictly better than today (where every such unit is warned) and it
  disappears when `ah-eacd` lands, with no change to anything in this plan: `ah-eacd` reduces
  `UpkeepClaim.short` and nothing else. Do not try to pre-empt it here.
- **`late_income` is shared** between `forecast_unit` and `charge_upkeep` on purpose (`ah-uwa3`),
  which is why `upkeep_drawn` must be recorded where `charged` is computed rather than recomputed
  anywhere else. Two copies of that subtraction is the drift `ah-uwa3` was filed to remove.
acceptance_criteria: A unit short on upkeep is not warned when the faction's unclaimed fund covers the shortfall, and the money is counted once across every such unit in the report rather than once per hex. When the purse is only partly enough, the warning names what is really left short. When the report header carries no unclaimed figure the behaviour is unchanged. Tests cover: purse covers it, purse partly covers it, several hexes drawing on one purse.

title: Every unit in a loaded report is shown as an estimate
description:
Loading the fixture report `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` marks nearly all units as estimates. Both the navigator's own faction's units and foreign units are affected.

Own units are the clear defect: their numbers come from the report directly and can never be estimated, so anything marking them so is wrong regardless of what the foreign-unit rule turns out to be. Foreign units may or may not be legitimately estimated depending on what the report actually reveals about each one — that part needs establishing against the fixture rather than assuming.

Worth ranking above cosmetics: the estimate marker is how a player tells a number they can act on from one they cannot, so while it is wrong on almost every unit it is not merely noisy — it is actively misleading about the whole report.

Reported by the navigator on 2026-08-23 while loading that fixture by hand.
design:
## Context

Every unit in a loaded report is marked an estimate — the player's own units included, whose numbers
come straight off the report and can never be estimated.

**This is not a parser defect**, and the bead's framing should not be built from. Measured against
the fixture the navigator loaded (`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`):

| | |
|---|---|
| units in the report | **372** — 182 own, 190 foreign |
| units that state what they hold | **372** — every single one |
| item tags used by them | all **known** to the ruleset (171 tags, 0 unrecognised) |

`classify_unit` (`crates/core/src/report/composition.rs:52-74`) clears `men_estimated` whenever it
recognises everything a unit holds. So with the ruleset loaded, **none** of those 372 units should be
an estimate. There is no separate foreign-unit rule to establish for this report: not one foreign
unit in it conceals its composition, so the bead's second acceptance criterion is satisfied by *no
estimates at all*.

**The classification never ran.** `men_estimated` is `true` in the parser's initialiser
(`crates/core/src/report/unit.rs`) and only `classify_unit` ever clears it — which is why the
navigator's correction, **every** unit rather than nearly every, is the decisive fact. A rule about
which units are estimable would spare some; a pass that did not run spares none.

It runs only on one branch:

```
ruleset "ready"        -> parseReportClassified -> men counted, flag cleared
ruleset anything else  -> parseReportFull       -> every unit an estimate
```

`reportParser` (`packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts:315-323`) chooses, and `AppShell` fetches the
ruleset in an effect (`:1414-1439`) while the Import control is already live. **A report imported
inside that window is parsed unclassified and never parsed again.** The navigator opened the app and
loaded a fixture immediately, in a browser, which is exactly that window.

**The pattern for the fix already exists three hundred lines further down.** The *restore* path is
guarded — `if (!game || ruleset.status === "loading") return undefined;` (`:1565-1567`) — and its
comment even names this case: *"the player imported a report while the restore was still waiting on
the ruleset fetch"*. Restore waits; import does not. That asymmetry is the bug.

**The ruleset is a local bundled asset, not a network call.** `rulesetUrlFor("neworigins")` returns
`/ruleset.json` (`packages/shared/src/gameSession.ts:88-94`), and `apps/web/vite.config.ts:22` sets
`publicDir` to `config/public`, which holds it. It works offline; `fetch` is only how a bundled asset
is read in a browser. The navigator made that a condition of choosing to wait, and it holds.

**Second half of the bug:** `RulesetState` has carried an `unavailable` case since it was written
(`AppShell.tsx:226`) and **nothing in the interface has ever mentioned it**. The app degrades every
number in the report and says nothing. Waiting cannot fix that case; saying so can.

Agreed design: `docs/ui/ah-6yj2-ruleset-missing.html`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — the wait

**`reportParser` keeps its signature and its tests.** It is a pure chooser and it is correct; the
fault is that its callers hand it a state that has not settled. Do not change
`packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts` — `reportLoad.test.ts:450-465` covers all three of its branches
and must stand unedited.

Three pieces, all in `AppShell`:

```ts
/** How long a load waits for the ruleset before giving up on it and parsing unclassified. */
const RULESET_WAIT_MS = 5000;

// The latest ruleset state, readable from a callback that was created before it changed - the same
// pattern `MapCanvas` uses for its viewport, and for the same reason: a closure would capture the
// state at the moment the callback was built, which here is exactly the stale value causing this.
const rulesetRef = useRef(ruleset);
rulesetRef.current = ruleset;

/** Settles when the ruleset fetch does, whichever way it goes. Replaced when the fetch restarts. */
const rulesetSettled = useRef<Promise<void>>(Promise.resolve());
```

`rulesetSettled` is assigned **inside the existing fetch effect** (`:1414-1439`), from the same
promise chain that already sets the state, so there is one fetch and not two. Assign it before the
`await`, so a load starting a millisecond later sees the pending promise rather than the previous
game's resolved one.

Then one memo the loaders use in place of `reportParser(client, ruleset)`:

```ts
/**
 * The parse every load goes through: waits for the ruleset to settle, then classifies if it can.
 *
 * Without the wait, a report imported in the moment between opening a game and its ruleset arriving
 * is parsed unclassified - and nothing parses it again, so every unit reads as an estimate for as
 * long as that turn is on screen (ah-6yj2). The restore path has always waited; this is import
 * catching up with it.
 *
 * The ceiling is not about the network - the ruleset is a bundled asset - but about never letting a
 * load hang on something that has already failed in a way the promise did not report.
 */
const parseReport = useCallback(
  async (text: string) => {
    await Promise.race([
      rulesetSettled.current,
      new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, RULESET_WAIT_MS))
    ]);
    return reportParser(client, rulesetRef.current)(text);
  },
  [client]
);
```

**Call sites to change — exactly two:**

- `:1136` `const report = await reportParser(client, ruleset)(text);` → `await parseReport(text)`
- `:1369` `return prepareBatch(files, reportParser(client, ruleset));` → `prepareBatch(files, parseReport)`

**`:1573` (restore) is deliberately left alone.** Its effect already returns early while the ruleset
is loading and re-runs when it settles, which is the same guarantee by a different route. Changing it
would mean re-reasoning about `turnAlreadyShowing` and the epoch, for no gain. Say so in the PR so
nobody "finishes the job".

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — saying it

After a load completes, when `rulesetRef.current.status === "unavailable"`, the status line carries
the warning instead of the counts:

```
The rules could not be loaded — unit numbers are estimates.
```

Verbatim, em dash included. Use `warningStatus` from
`packages/shared/src/workspace/shellStatus.ts:24` — the header already renders `warning` tone with an
amber dot, so **nothing new is built**.

**Where it goes:** `loadTurn` already collapses memory, draft and manifest warnings into a single
`warningStatus` (`reportLoad.ts:155`), replacing the counts. This follows that exactly — replace the
status the load produced, do not append a second line. A load has one status.

**Only for `unavailable`, never for `loading`.** After the wait, `loading` means the ceiling expired,
which is a different and much rarer thing; treat it as `unavailable` for the message's purposes
since the effect on the player is identical.

### Not changed

`reportLoad.ts`, `composition.rs`, `unit.rs`, the parser, the classifier, `rulesets.ts`, and every
other panel. See *Out of scope*.

## Increments

**1. A load waits for the ruleset.**
Failing test: `waits_for_the_ruleset_before_parsing` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.test.tsx` if one exists, otherwise in a new
`packages/shared/src/reportLoad.test.ts` case built around the same helper — **decide which and say
so in the PR rather than creating a file for one test.** With a ruleset promise that resolves after a
tick, assert that `parseReportClassified` is called and `parseReportFull` is not, for a load started
before the promise settles. That assertion fails today.

**2. The ceiling holds.**
Failing test: `parses_without_the_ruleset_when_it_never_arrives` — a promise that never settles, fake
timers advanced past `RULESET_WAIT_MS`, asserting the load completes via `parseReportFull` rather
than hanging.

**3. A missing ruleset is said out loud.**
Failing test: `says_so_when_the_rules_could_not_be_loaded` — with the ruleset `unavailable`, the
status after a load is the verbatim line above, with tone `warning`. Then
`says_nothing_when_the_rules_loaded`, which is the case that must not regress into nagging on every
ordinary import.

**4. The fixture proves it end to end.**
Failing test: `a_loaded_report_marks_no_unit_as_an_estimate` in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`. Load
the g3-f42-t82 fixture and assert that **no** unit in the units table carries the estimate marker —
own or foreign. This is the bead's own acceptance criterion, it is the test the navigator would run
by hand, and it is the one that would have caught this.
Include a second assertion in the same spec that a unit's men figure reads its real value, so a
future change that hides the marker rather than fixing the count cannot pass.

## The test plan

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `waits_for_the_ruleset_before_parsing` | the race, which is the defect |
| `parses_without_the_ruleset_when_it_never_arrives` | that the wait cannot hang a load |
| `says_so_when_the_rules_could_not_be_loaded` | the message, verbatim, and its tone |
| `says_nothing_when_the_rules_loaded` | that the ordinary case stays quiet |
| `a_loaded_report_marks_no_unit_as_an_estimate` | the acceptance criterion, in a browser |

**`reportLoad.test.ts:450-465` must pass unedited.** It covers `reportParser`'s three branches, and
this bead does not change that function. If it needs an edit, the change has gone somewhere it should
not have.

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=desktop-shell
```

**Both smoke projects.** See the desktop question in *Known traps* — it is the one thing this plan
could not establish from the code, and the desktop run is how the implementer settles it.

## User-facing decisions

Taken by the navigator on 2026-08-23. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-6yj2-ruleset-missing.html`.

**A load waits for the ruleset.** Offered as (1-i) wait, (1-ii) parse now and re-parse when it lands,
(1-iii) disable Import until ready. The navigator answered conditionally: *"If it is a local file it
is fine, then 1-i wait for it. If it is a remote fetch, we need to have a conversation."*
**It is a local bundled asset** — `/ruleset.json`, served from `config/public` by the build, working
offline — so **1-i stands**.
*1-ii rejected*: figures that change under the player a second after they appear are their own kind of
wrong, and it costs two parses of a large report per load.
*1-iii rejected*: it disables the app's main action on every open for a condition that resolves
itself.

**When the ruleset is genuinely unavailable, the report still loads and the status line says so.**
Offered against a persistent amber chip (the `ah-w544.2` pattern) and against refusing the import.
**2-i chosen.**
*The chip rejected* as a fourth chip in the header for a state that should be rare — noted as the
better answer if this turns out to be common rather than exceptional.
*Refusing rejected* because a report is still largely readable without a ruleset, so refusing costs
more than it saves, and it would make the app unusable if the asset ever failed to serve.

**The wording**, chosen from three and shipping verbatim:
`The rules could not be loaded — unit numbers are estimates.`
*Rejected*: `Unit numbers are estimates — the rules for this game could not be loaded.` (consequence
first) and `Running without the rules: some numbers are guesses.` (vaguer about which numbers, which
is the part the player needs).

**The bead's own framing was corrected in the interview** and the correction is recorded in its
notes: every unit rather than nearly every, in a browser, and no parser rule to establish. An
implementer reading the description alone will build the wrong thing.

## Out of scope

- **The parser and the classifier.** `unit.rs`, `composition.rs` and `classify_unit` are correct;
  this bead adds no Rust and regenerates no bindings.
- **`reportParser` itself.** Unchanged, tests unedited.
- **A unit whose composition the report does not state.** With classification running it has no
  items, so it classifies to *exactly zero men, not estimated* — which is arguably wrong, since
  unknown is not zero. **Not exercised by this fixture** (all 372 units state what they hold) and
  not fixed here. Worth its own bead if a report with concealed units ever turns up; do not
  speculatively fix it, because nothing today can tell you what the right answer looks like.
- **A persistent indicator that the app is running without rules.** The status line says it once;
  making it survive is the rejected chip.
- **Anything else the missing ruleset degrades** — order checks, study costs, the game-data
  dictionary. All are affected and none is mentioned by the new message, deliberately: it names the
  symptom the player actually saw.
- **The restore path** (`AppShell.tsx:1573`), which already waits by a different route.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=desktop-shell
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. Loading `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` marks **no** unit as an estimate — own or foreign.
2. `reportLoad.test.ts` is unedited and green.
3. `git diff` touches no file under `crates/`.
4. With the ruleset made unavailable (rename the asset, or point the game at an unknown ruleset id),
   a load still succeeds and the status line reads the verbatim line above.

**The check only a human can make**, and it is the one the navigator did by hand: open the app,
import that fixture immediately — before anything has settled — and confirm every unit shows a real
number. Doing it *slowly* will not reproduce the bug, so **import it as fast as the app allows**.

## Known traps

- **Reproduce it before fixing it, and reproduce it fast.** The window is the ruleset fetch of a
  local asset — small. A leisurely manual test passes against the broken build and will convince you
  there is nothing to fix. Increment 1's test is the reliable reproduction; the manual one is
  confirmation.
- **A closure captures the ruleset at the moment the callback was built.** That is the bug, and
  writing the fix without `rulesetRef` reintroduces it in a subtler form: the load would wait
  correctly and then parse with the stale value it captured. `MapCanvas`'s `viewRef.current = view`
  is the same pattern for the same reason.
- **Assign `rulesetSettled` before awaiting anything** in the fetch effect. Assigning it after means
  a load starting immediately sees the *previous* game's already-resolved promise and waits for
  nothing.
- **The restore path already waits** (`:1565-1567`) and is deliberately untouched. Its comment
  already describes this exact scenario, which is worth reading before changing anything near it.
- **Only two call sites change.** `reportParser` has three; the third is restore.
- **The desktop shell is unverified.** This plan establishes the cause for the *web* build, where
  `/ruleset.json` is served from `publicDir`. Whether the same URL resolves inside the Tauri webview
  was not established, and if it does not, every desktop load has always been unclassified —
  permanent rather than a race, and this bead's wait would not fix it. **Run the desktop smoke
  project and load a report by hand in the desktop shell.** If units come back estimated there, stop
  and file it: that is a different bug wearing the same symptom.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom, by decision (ah-nass).** Anything asserting on an effect or a
  timer must be a pure-function or smoke test. Increments 1-3 are about promises and status values,
  which are testable; increment 4 is a browser test because the marker is rendered.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a PWA run straight
  afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker.
acceptance_criteria:
- Loading neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep marks none of the player's own faction's units as estimates.
- Foreign units are marked as estimates exactly when the report does not state their composition outright, and not otherwise — the rule established from the fixture and stated in the bead's notes.
- A regression test loads that fixture and asserts the estimate flag across own and foreign units, so this cannot silently return.
notes:
Xavier 2026-08-23: cause established, and it is NOT a parser defect.

The navigator clarified: EVERY unit, not nearly every, and in a browser rather than the desktop shell. That is the decisive detail - men_estimated is `true` in the parser's initialiser and only classify_unit ever clears it, so "every unit" is the signature of the classification pass not running at all, rather than of any rule about which units are estimable.

Measured against the fixture, so the acceptance criteria can be settled rather than guessed:

  units in the report             372   (182 own, 190 foreign)
  units that state what they hold  372   - every single one
  item tags used                   all known to the ruleset (171 tags, 0 unrecognised)

classify_unit clears men_estimated whenever it recognises everything a unit holds (composition.rs:61-74). So with the ruleset loaded, NONE of those 372 units should be an estimate - own or foreign. There is no separate foreign-unit rule to establish for this report, because not one foreign unit in it conceals its composition. The bead's second acceptance criterion is therefore satisfied by "no estimates at all".

The mechanism:

  ruleset "ready"        -> parseReportClassified -> men counted, flag cleared
  ruleset anything else  -> parseReportFull       -> every unit an estimate

reportParser (reportLoad.ts:315-323) picks the second whenever ruleset.status is not "ready", and AppShell fetches the ruleset in an effect (AppShell.tsx:1414-1439) while the Import control is already live. A report imported inside that window is parsed unclassified and never re-parsed.

The ruleset is a LOCAL bundled asset, not a network call: rulesetUrlFor("neworigins") returns "/ruleset.json", and apps/web/vite.config.ts:22 sets publicDir to config/public, which holds it. It works offline. The fetch is only how a bundled asset is read in a browser.

RulesetState has carried an `unavailable` case since it was written and nothing in the interface has ever mentioned it - no banner, no status line, no chip. That silence is the second half of this bug and is why the fix is not only "wait".

title: A poked agent gets its wake typed into the composer and never sent
description:
`cerebro--poke` (emacs/cerebro.el:1829) and `cerebro--nudge` (:1806) each call `vterm-send-string` and then `vterm-send-return` back to back. The CR therefore arrives in the same terminal read as the message text. Claude Code's TUI is Ink-based and treats a character burst ending in CR as a paste, and a paste containing a newline inserts a literal newline into the composer rather than submitting it.

The observed symptom, on Psylocke: '[cerebro] Your wait is over - start your next pass now, exactly as your own instructions describe it.' appears in her input box and nothing happens. She stays waiting until a person presses return for her, so the fleet view's own cadence silently does not run.

`cerebro--nudge` has the identical shape and is broken the same way; it fires rarely enough that nobody had noticed. That is the second time one fix has had to be applied to both call sites, so they want collapsing into a single helper rather than patching twice again.

This is a change to the cerebro submodule, not to atlantis-hud.
design:
## Context

A sleeping agent is woken by having a line typed into its terminal. `cerebro--poke`
(`emacs/cerebro.el:1828-1834`) does it like this:

```elisp
(with-current-buffer buffer
  (vterm-send-string cerebro--poke-message)
  (vterm-send-return))
```

Both calls land in the same terminal read, so the carriage return arrives as the last character of a
burst. Claude Code's TUI is Ink-based and treats a burst ending in CR as a **paste** — and a paste
containing a newline inserts a literal newline into the composer instead of submitting it. The wake
text sits in the input box and nothing happens.

Observed on Psylocke: `[cerebro] Your wait is over - start your next pass now, exactly as your own
instructions describe it.` in her composer, and she stayed `waiting` until a person pressed return
for her.

**`cerebro--nudge` (`:1807-1813`) has the identical shape** and is broken the same way. It fires
rarely enough that nobody had noticed. That is the second time one fix has had to be applied to both,
which is why they collapse into one helper here rather than being patched twice again.

**The retry makes it worse, not better.** `cerebro-poke-grace` (`:1022-1030`) pokes a role a second
time when it is still `waiting` sixty seconds later — a sound design, and exactly right once this
works. While it is broken it means the same line is typed into the composer again, and again, so a
stalled agent accumulates wake messages rather than simply missing one. Worth knowing before you
look at a live session and wonder why there are four of them.

**Why this is a P0.** The fleet's whole cadence runs through this one call. An agent that should wake
every ten minutes silently does not, nothing reports it, and the only symptom is a row that stays
`waiting` — which looks exactly like an agent that has nothing to do. The navigator ranked it P0 on
2026-08-23 on that basis.

This is a change to the **`cerebro` submodule**, not to this project. See *Known traps* for the
two-repository shape; `ah-tz7m` is the worked precedent.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` — one new helper, one new setting, two call sites collapsed

**The fix is to separate the return from the text in time**, and to do it asynchronously so the poll
is not blocked. `run-at-time` with a zero-argument lambda is the mechanism; the file already uses
timers for the poll itself.

```elisp
(defcustom cerebro-return-delay 0.3
  "Seconds between typing a line into a session and sending its return.

Sent together, they arrive in one terminal read, and a TUI that treats a
burst ending in a carriage return as a paste puts the newline in its composer
instead of submitting it - which leaves a woken agent sitting on its own wake
message.  Any separation at all is enough; the value is a `defcustom\=' so a
terminal that needs longer can be given it without editing this file."
  :type 'number
  :group 'cerebro)

(defun cerebro--type-into-session (agent message)
  "Type MESSAGE into AGENT\='s session, then send its return separately.

The return goes on a timer rather than immediately - see
`cerebro-return-delay\=' for why.  The buffer is re-checked when the timer
fires, because a session can be killed inside the delay."
  (let ((buffer (cerebro--session (cerebro-agent-name agent))))
    (when (and buffer (fboundp 'vterm-send-string))
      (with-current-buffer buffer
        (vterm-send-string message))
      (run-at-time cerebro-return-delay nil
                   (lambda ()
                     (when (and (buffer-live-p buffer) (fboundp 'vterm-send-return))
                       (with-current-buffer buffer
                         (vterm-send-return))))))))
```

and both callers become one line each, keeping their own docstrings:

```elisp
(defun cerebro--nudge (agent)
  "Type `cerebro--nudge-message' into AGENT's session."
  (cerebro--type-into-session agent cerebro--nudge-message))

(defun cerebro--poke (agent)
  "Type `cerebro--poke-message' into AGENT's session."
  (cerebro--type-into-session agent cerebro--poke-message))
```

Four details that are load-bearing:

- **`buffer-live-p` inside the timer.** Sixty seconds of grace is one thing; three hundred
  milliseconds is short, but a session being killed exactly then is precisely the kind of race that
  shows up once a fortnight and is impossible to reproduce. The existing code takes the buffer once
  and uses it immediately; this one has to re-check.
- **`(fboundp 'vterm-send-return)` inside the timer too.** The existing guard tests
  `vterm-send-string` before doing anything; that guard now runs at a different time from the return,
  so the return needs its own.
- **`with-current-buffer` around the string only, and again inside the lambda.** Wrapping the
  `run-at-time` call in the outer `with-current-buffer` would do nothing useful — the buffer is not
  current when the timer fires.
- **The `defcustom` is the point, not decoration.** The 0.3 is a guess at a paste-detection window
  nobody here can read the source of. If it is wrong, a `defcustom` is one line in the navigator's
  configuration; a hard-coded constant is a submodule PR plus a pointer bump in every consumer. Given
  that the value is a guess, making it changeable is most of the value of this bead.

**Nothing else changes.** `cerebro--poke-message`, `cerebro--nudge-message`, `cerebro-poke-grace`,
the poll, and every caller of `cerebro--poke` and `cerebro--nudge` stay exactly as they are.

### The consumer, `atlantis-hud`

The `.claude/cerebro` pointer, and nothing else — the established
`chore(ah-y3j1): bump cerebro past …` shape (`git log --oneline -- .claude/cerebro`).

## Increments

**1. The return is sent separately.**
Failing test: `cerebro-test/typing-into-a-session-sends-the-return-on-its-own` in
`emacs/cerebro-test.el`. With `vterm-send-string`, `vterm-send-return` and `run-at-time` all stubbed
through `cl-letf` (the file's existing idiom — see the `cl-letf` around `cerebro--nudge` at
`cerebro-test.el:1121`), assert that after `cerebro--type-into-session`:

- `vterm-send-string` was called once with the message;
- `vterm-send-return` has **not** been called yet — this is the assertion that fails today and is
  the whole bug;
- `run-at-time` was called with `cerebro-return-delay`;
- invoking the captured lambda then calls `vterm-send-return`.

**2. Both callers go through it.**
Failing test: `cerebro-test/poke-and-nudge-share-one-typing-path`. Stub
`cerebro--type-into-session` and assert `cerebro--poke` passes `cerebro--poke-message` and
`cerebro--nudge` passes `cerebro--nudge-message`, and that neither calls `vterm-send-string` itself.
That is what stops the two drifting apart a third time.

**3. A session killed inside the delay is survived.**
Failing test: `cerebro-test/a-session-killed-before-the-return-is-left-alone`. Capture the lambda as
in increment 1, kill the buffer, invoke the lambda, and assert `vterm-send-return` was not called and
nothing signalled.

## The test plan

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `cerebro-test/typing-into-a-session-sends-the-return-on-its-own` | the fix itself, including that the return is *not* synchronous |
| `cerebro-test/poke-and-nudge-share-one-typing-path` | that there is one path, not two |
| `cerebro-test/a-session-killed-before-the-return-is-left-alone` | the race the timer introduces |

The existing suites that must stay green are the ones that stub these two functions and assert *that*
they were called — `cerebro-test/supervise-pokes-a-waiting-role-past-its-wake` (`:3414`),
`cerebro-test/an-external-waiting-role-is-never-poked` (`:3444`),
`cerebro-test/supervise-nudges-a-question-nobody-answered` (`:1070`) and the not-sprayed test at
`:1113`. They stub at the `cerebro--poke`/`cerebro--nudge` level, so collapsing the bodies beneath
them should not touch a single one. **If any of them needs editing, the collapse has changed a
signature it should not have.**

CI runs, on each Emacs version in the matrix:

```bash
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

Run both locally before opening the PR. The byte-compile step is not a formality here: docstrings in
this file escape quotes as `\='`, and a new `defcustom` and two new docstrings are three chances to
earn a warning.

## User-facing decisions

**None that belong to the navigator.** This is fleet tooling: nothing an audience sees changes, no
string an audience reads is added, and the one message involved — `cerebro--poke-message` — is
unchanged.

Two decisions were taken here rather than asked, and are recorded because they are visible to the
navigator in their own configuration:

**The delay is a `defcustom`, not a constant.** The bead's own design says the 0.3 seconds "is a
guess at Claude Code's paste-detection window and must be confirmed against a live session, not
trusted from this bead". A guessed constant in a submodule costs a PR and a pointer bump in every
consumer to change; a `defcustom` costs a line in an init file. Given that the number is explicitly
a guess, that is where most of this bead's value sits.

**Both call sites collapse into one helper.** The bead asks for it and the reason is recorded there:
this is the second fix that has had to be applied to both. Not a preference — a defect that has now
happened twice.

## Out of scope

- **Any change to what is typed.** `cerebro--poke-message` and `cerebro--nudge-message` are
  unchanged, and their docstrings' reasoning about naming no pass and no label still stands.
- **`cerebro-poke-grace` and the retry.** It is correct as it is, and once this works it becomes a
  genuine safety net for a return that is dropped anyway.
- **Detecting that a poke did not take.** A poked role that is still `waiting` could be noticed and
  reported rather than silently re-poked, which would have surfaced this bug in an hour instead of
  however long it sat. **Worth doing and deliberately not done here** — it is a change to the
  supervisor's logic, not to how a line is typed, and this is a P0 that should be small. File it if
  you want it.
- **Any other use of `vterm-send-string`** in the file. Only these two send a return straight after.
- **Anything in `atlantis-hud`** beyond the submodule pointer.

## Validation

In the `cerebro` checkout:

```bash
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

In this repository, on the pointer-bump PR:

```bash
git submodule status .claude/cerebro     # names the merged cerebro commit, no leading + or -
git diff --stat origin/main              # exactly one file, one insertion, one deletion
pnpm run check:fast
```

**The check only a human can make, and it is the one that matters.** No test in either repository can
prove that a real terminal submits the line — every test here stubs `vterm` precisely because it
cannot be driven in batch. So, against a live fleet view:

1. Let a `waiting` agent's wake fall due, or set its `wake_at` to the past.
2. Watch the session. The wake message must **appear and be submitted**, not sit in the composer.
3. Confirm the agent's state file moves off `waiting` without anybody pressing return.

**If it still sits in the composer, raise `cerebro-return-delay` and try again before changing any
code** — that is what the `defcustom` is for, and finding the working value is part of finishing this
bead. Record the value that worked in the bead's notes; the next person to meet a paste heuristic
will want it.

There is a free second opinion available: **every planner and verifier in the fleet is woken by this
call**, so a pass that starts on its own after this merges is the fix working in production.

## Known traps

- **Two repositories, two pull requests, and the order is not negotiable.** The `cerebro` PR merges
  first; only then does a commit exist on its `main` for the pointer to name. A pointer bumped to an
  unmerged branch commit resolves for you and for nobody else — a fresh clone running
  `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets "reference is not a tree", leaving `.claude/cerebro`
  empty, and every launcher command then fails with "No such file or directory" rather than anything
  naming the real cause. `ah-tz7m` is the worked example.
- **`.claude/cerebro` is a submodule**, so `git add .claude/cerebro` stages a gitlink, not files. Do
  not `git add` inside the submodule from the parent, and do not commit the submodule's own changes
  from there.
- **The submodule checkout is shared with every running agent**, since they all read their skills
  from it. Branching inside `.claude/cerebro` moves their HEAD. Do the `cerebro` work in a clone or
  worktree of its own and leave that directory on the commit the parent records.
- **Do not branch in the main checkout** for the pointer bump either — a worktree under
  `.cerebro/worktrees/`, removed once merged.
- **Docstrings in this file escape quotes as `\='`.** Copy the surrounding style; the byte-compile
  step is a CI gate and a stray quote is a warning.
- **`run-at-time` fires with no buffer current.** The `with-current-buffer` must be *inside* the
  lambda; putting it outside compiles, passes a careless test, and sends the return into whatever
  buffer happens to be current when the timer runs.
- **The existing tests stub `cerebro--poke` and `cerebro--nudge` themselves**, so they cannot see
  this bug and could not have caught it. That is not a criticism of them — it is why increment 1
  tests one level lower, and why it must not be written by stubbing the same two functions.
- **The Four Eye Principle applies to both PRs.** Neither is the `docs(<bead>): mockup` exception,
  which is confined to `docs/` in this repository. Request the Copilot review on each, once, when it
  opens.
acceptance_criteria:
- One helper types into a session; `cerebro--poke` and `cerebro--nudge` both use it and neither sends the return synchronously.
- Poking a real `waiting` session submits the message: the agent starts its next pass without anyone touching its terminal.
- The delay is confirmed empirically against a live Claude Code session, and the value chosen is justified in a comment.
- The helper survives a session buffer killed between the string and the return without erroring in the poll.
