title: The map repeats across the seam instead of running into emptiness
description:
The visual half of ah-brgo, and the one that closes the verification failure.

Draw the world so that it genuinely repeats east-west (and north-south where wrapY is set), so panning across the seam runs continuously into the next copy instead of into emptiness.

Two things have to happen and neither exists today:

  - MapShape has to reach MapCanvas. It reaches only four core calls, as a JSON string, via AppShell.tsx:561-577; the canvas has no idea how wide the world is.
  - The world has to be drawn more than once. Today it is one <g ref={worldRef}> with one transform (MapCanvas.tsx:1057-1521), and nothing anywhere in the app repeats geometry.

The renderer is favourable: hexes are a plain list drawn at worldOf(coordinate), nothing is clipped to data extents, and fog is already an infinite pattern.

Includes folding coordinateAt so a click in a ghost copy selects the real hex rather than returning x=73.

Navigator chose the true cylinder over a bounded pan and over a jumping camera, on 2026-08-22, knowing the cost.
design:
## Context

A game whose map is set to wrap still scrolls past `x=0` to the left and past `x=71` to the right.
The flag is recorded, `MapGeometry::wrap` (`crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs:134-158`) honours it,
and the movement planner plans against a cylinder — but **the map view has never seen the shape at
all**. Psylocke found it verifying `ah-0w7w`, whose notes record it verbatim: "the wrap flag is
recorded but the map view does not honour it."

Two facts about the code shape everything below.

- **`MapShape` never reaches the canvas.** It is serialised to JSON in `AppShell.tsx:561-577` and
  passed to four core calls (`:1980`, `:2039`, `:2292`, `:2321`). `MapCanvas` has no width, no
  height and no wrap flags among its 18 props (`MapCanvas.tsx:129-195`).
- **The world is drawn exactly once.** One `<g ref={worldRef}>` (`MapCanvas.tsx:1057-1521`) holding
  every pass — terrain, roads, provinces, routes, marks, the trade arrow, marquee, three kinds of
  ring, the hit layer and notes — under one transform applied imperatively in `applyView`
  (`:344-350`). Nothing anywhere in the app repeats geometry.

The navigator chose the **true cylinder** on 2026-08-22, over a bounded pan and over a jumping
camera, and did so knowing the cost. This bead delivers it. `ah-brgo.2` folds the ruler and the
arrow keys; `ah-teg0` refuses the odd-width combination at the point it is entered.

The agreed design is `docs/ui/ah-brgo-wrap.html`. Open it first.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The idea that makes this affordable

Two mechanisms together, and **neither is optional** — each is useless without the other:

1. **`<use>` rather than duplicated nodes.** The world is drawn once into a group with an id, and the
   ghosts are `<use>` elements referencing it. SVG clones it at render time, so two ghost copies cost
   **two DOM nodes**, not two copies of every hex, road, note and ring. This is the difference
   between tripling the biggest component in the app and adding a pair of elements to it.
2. **Folding the camera.** After every pan, `tx` is taken modulo the world's on-screen width. The
   camera therefore never leaves the central band, so **one ghost on each side is always enough**,
   however far the player drags.

**The fold is invisible, and that is the whole trick.** At the moment `tx` jumps by exactly one world
width, the ghost that was under the pointer is pixel-identical to the real world now under it —
nothing moves on screen. That is what makes an infinite-feeling pan out of three copies, and it is
why option C (a visible jump) and option A (a truly infinite strip) collapse into the same cheap
implementation.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts` — the arithmetic

Three new pure functions, beside the existing ones, all unit-testable without a DOM:

```ts
/**
 * How far apart the world's repeats are, in world units, per axis - `null` where that axis does not
 * repeat.
 *
 * An axis repeats only when the game says it wraps AND the extent is **even**: the lattice holds
 * only positions where `x + y` is even, so shifting by an odd width lands rows half a hex out and
 * the two edges genuinely do not meet. `ah-teg0` refuses that combination where it is entered; this
 * is the defensive half, because a game saved before that validation exists may already carry it.
 */
export function wrapSpans(shape: MapShape | null): { x: number | null; y: number | null };

/**
 * The viewport with its translation folded into the first repeat, so the camera never leaves the
 * central band.
 *
 * `scale` is `scaleOf(view.step)`, passed rather than recomputed so the caller cannot pass a
 * translation and a scale that disagree.
 */
export function foldViewport(view: Viewport, spans: { x: number | null; y: number | null }, scale: number): Viewport;

/** A coordinate folded into the map's own range, on whichever axes repeat. */
export function foldCoordinate(coordinate: Coordinate, shape: MapShape | null): Coordinate;
```

`wrapSpans` returns `shape.width * COLUMN_PITCH` for x when `shape.wrapX && shape.width > 0 &&
shape.width % 2 === 0`, and `shape.height * ROW_PITCH` for y under the matching conditions on
`wrapY`/`height`. `null` otherwise, including for a `null` shape.

`foldViewport` folds each axis whose span is non-null: the on-screen period is `span * scale`, and
`tx` becomes `((tx % period) + period) % period` — **not** `tx % period`, which is negative for a
negative `tx` and would put the world off screen the first time the player pans west.

`foldCoordinate` mirrors `MapGeometry::wrap`'s `rem_euclid`. Match it exactly: the view and the
movement planner disagreeing about which hex `x=72` is would be worse than either being wrong alone.

**`worldOf`, `fitTo`, `centreOn` and `isOffScreen` are unchanged.** They are correct as they stand:
`fitTo` frames the known hexes, which live in the real range, and a folded camera keeps that framing
valid.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — the ghosts

**One new prop**, beside the existing 18:

```ts
  /** The world's extent and where it joins back onto itself, or null when the game does not say. */
  shape?: MapShape | null;
```

The world group gains an inner content group with a stable id, and the ghosts become siblings of it
inside the same transformed group:

```tsx
<g ref={worldRef} data-testid="map-world">
  <g id="map-world-content">
    {/* every existing pass, unchanged and unmoved */}
  </g>
  {ghostOffsets.map(({ dx, dy }) => (
    <use
      key={`${dx},${dy}`}
      href="#map-world-content"
      x={dx}
      y={dy}
      pointerEvents="none"
      data-testid="map-world-ghost"
    />
  ))}
</g>
```

`ghostOffsets` is every combination of `[-spanX, 0, +spanX] × [-spanY, 0, +spanY]` **less the
`(0,0)` centre**, with an axis contributing only `0` when its span is `null`. So: no wrap, no
ghosts; east–west only, two; both axes, eight. Eight `<use>` nodes is nothing — which is the point
of doing it this way.

Three things about that markup that are load-bearing:

- **`pointerEvents="none"` on every ghost.** A click over a ghost must fall through to the
  full-canvas hit rect (`MapCanvas.tsx:1013-1055`), which already calls `coordinateAt` at
  `:1025-1031`. Fold that call's result through `foldCoordinate` and a click on a ghost of `x=1`
  selects `x=1`, not `x=73`. Without `pointerEvents="none"` the click targets the `<use>` element
  itself and selects nothing at all.
- **`<use>` does not duplicate `data-testid` for queries.** Cloned content lives in a shadow tree, so
  `getByTestId` still finds exactly one of everything inside the world. That is a benefit worth
  knowing rather than a limitation: no existing test breaks from a duplicated id, and the ghost is
  addressable on its own through `map-world-ghost`.
- **The id must not be assembled or made unique per instance.** One `MapCanvas` is mounted at a time;
  a stable literal keeps the `href` a literal too.

`applyView` (`:344-350`) is untouched — the ghosts sit inside `worldRef`, so the single transform
carries them.

### Folding the camera — `commit` and `slide`

Both chokepoints already funnel through `viewRef.current = next; applyView()`:

- `commit` (`MapCanvas.tsx:376-383`) — a settled gesture, which also writes the store;
- `slide` (`MapCanvas.tsx:386-392`) — mid-drag, deliberately skipping React.

Both fold before assigning:

```ts
const folded = foldViewport(next, spans, scaleOf(next.step));
```

`spans` is `useMemo(() => wrapSpans(shape ?? null), [shape])`.

**Fold in both, not just `commit`.** Folding only on commit means a long drag runs off the ghosts
mid-gesture and shows emptiness until the pointer is released — which is exactly the reported bug,
surviving in the one case a player is most likely to hit.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — threading the shape

`mapShapeOfGame(...)` is already called at `:561-577` to build `mapJson`. The structured value is
right there and is currently thrown away. Lift it into a memo and pass `.map` to `<MapCanvas>`
(`:3207-3234`) beside the props it already receives. **Do not re-derive it** and do not parse
`mapJson` back — one source, two consumers.

### Not changed

`mapMarquee.ts`, `rulerTicks`, `neighbour`, `fitTo`, `centreOn`, `isOffScreen`, every theme, and
every other panel. See *Out of scope*.

## Increments

**1. The arithmetic.**
Failing test: `spans_repeat_only_when_the_map_says_so_and_the_width_is_even` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.test.ts` — `wrapSpans({width:72,height:96,wrapX:true,wrapY:false})`
is `{ x: 72 * COLUMN_PITCH, y: null }`; an odd width gives `{ x: null, y: null }`; a `null` shape
gives both `null`; `wrapY` with an even height gives a y span.
Then `folding_the_camera_keeps_it_in_the_first_repeat` — a `tx` of one and a half world widths folds
to a half, **and a negative `tx` folds to a positive one** (the case a plain `%` gets wrong).
Then `folding_a_coordinate_matches_the_movement_planner` — `x = 72` folds to `0`, `x = -1` to `71`,
and an axis that does not wrap is left alone.
No component changes in this increment.

**2. The ghosts exist, and only when they should.**
Failing test: `draws_a_ghost_either_side_when_the_map_wraps_east_west` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.test.tsx`, asserting the rendered markup contains two
`<use href="#map-world-content">` elements at `x` of plus and minus `72 * COLUMN_PITCH`, each with
`pointer-events="none"`.
Then `draws_no_ghosts_when_the_map_does_not_wrap` (no `map-world-ghost` in the markup at all — the
common case, and the one that must cost nothing), `draws_eight_ghosts_when_both_axes_wrap`, and
`draws_no_ghosts_for_an_odd_width` — the defensive case `ah-teg0` will later refuse at entry.
These are `renderToStaticMarkup` tests, which is all this needs: the ghosts are markup.

**3. A click in a ghost selects the real hex.**
Failing test: `a_click_beyond_the_seam_selects_the_hex_it_is_a_copy_of` in
`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`. Load a wrapping game, pan east past the seam, click a hex in the
ghost, and assert the region pane shows the hex whose `x` is in range. This is a browser test
because it is about hit testing; the fold itself is already covered by increment 1.

**4. The camera folds, so panning never runs out of map.**
Failing test: `panning_east_forever_stays_on_the_map`, in the same spec — pan east by several world
widths in a single gesture and assert `map-world` is still showing hexes, not the fog rect. Then
`panning_west_past_the_origin_stays_on_the_map`, which is the negative-`tx` case increment 1 pinned
in arithmetic and this pins in the browser.

**5. The shape reaches the canvas.**
Failing test: `passes_the_game_map_shape_to_the_canvas` in `AppShell`'s existing test file if it has
one, otherwise fold this into increment 2 by asserting the ghosts appear for a game whose manifest
says it wraps. **Do not add a new test file for one assertion**; say which you chose and why in the
PR.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `spans_repeat_only_when_the_map_says_so_and_the_width_is_even` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the even-width guard |
| `folding_the_camera_keeps_it_in_the_first_repeat` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the fold, including negative `tx` |
| `folding_a_coordinate_matches_the_movement_planner` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | agreement with `MapGeometry::wrap` |
| `draws_a_ghost_either_side_when_the_map_wraps_east_west` | `MapCanvas.test.tsx` | the `<use>` markup |
| `draws_no_ghosts_when_the_map_does_not_wrap` | `MapCanvas.test.tsx` | that the common case costs nothing |
| `draws_eight_ghosts_when_both_axes_wrap` | `MapCanvas.test.tsx` | the y axis |
| `draws_no_ghosts_for_an_odd_width` | `MapCanvas.test.tsx` | the defensive guard |
| `a_click_beyond_the_seam_selects_the_hex_it_is_a_copy_of` | `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` | hit testing through a ghost |
| `panning_east_forever_stays_on_the_map` (+ west) | `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` | the camera fold, both directions |

Existing suites that must stay green, and are the real net: `mapViewport.test.ts` (eight suites
today), `MapCanvas.test.tsx`, `mapMarquee.test.ts`, `mapRecentre.test.ts`, `mapViewState.test.ts`,
`mapViewportStorage.test.ts`, and the map specs in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:3095-3225` and
`tests/smoke/map-export.spec.ts`.

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=desktop-shell
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/map-export.spec.ts --project=web
```

**`map-export.spec.ts` is not optional.** Export walks the world group; if ghosts end up in an
exported image the map is exported three times over, and no other suite would notice.

## User-facing decisions

Taken by the navigator on 2026-08-22. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-brgo-wrap.html`.

**The map repeats: a true cylinder.** Offered as (A) the world drawn repeatedly so panning runs
continuously, (B) panning stops at the edge — the planner's recommendation, (C) the camera jumps
round at the seam, and (D) B now with A as a follow-up. **A chosen**, with the cost stated in the
question: every render pass repeating, on the biggest component in the app.
*B rejected*: it fixes the reported symptom in one small change, but it is not a cylinder — a hex at
`x=71` still reads as an edge when its eastern neighbour is `x=0`.
*C rejected*: content leaping sideways under a dragging pointer reads as a glitch rather than a world.
*D rejected*: the navigator chose to do the real thing once rather than ship the cheap version first.
**The `<use>`-plus-camera-fold design in *Files to change* is what makes A affordable**, and it was
found after the decision — the cost the navigator accepted is larger than the cost actually being
paid, which is the right direction for a surprise.

**North and south behave exactly as east and west.** Offered against east–west only. **Same rule on
both axes chosen**, so the view never disagrees with the movement planner on a map that wraps
north–south, even though the ruleset default is `wrapY: false`.

**An odd extent does not wrap.** The navigator's words: *"We should not allow odd width and x wrap.
The same for odd height and wrap y."* That is stronger than the option offered, which was to treat
an odd width as non-wrapping in the view — it asks for the combination to be **refused where it is
entered**. Refusing it is `ah-teg0`, filed for it, blocked on `ah-0w7w` because it changes forms
Storm is still fixing. **This bead does the defensive half**: an odd extent draws no ghosts on that
axis, because a game saved before that validation exists may already carry the combination, and
drawing a seam that does not join would be a lie.

**Nothing else about the map is reopened.** Zoom, framing, themes, badges, notes, the selection ring
and the rulers all keep their behaviour; the map simply stops ending.

## Out of scope

- **Ruler labels and arrow keys.** `ah-brgo.2`, blocked on this bead. Until it lands, panning east
  past the seam still labels `72, 73` — a known, deliberate gap, not an oversight.
- **Refusing an odd width with wrap at the point it is entered.** `ah-teg0`, blocked on `ah-0w7w`.
- **Marquee selection across the seam.** `mapMarquee.ts`'s `MapRect` is min/max per axis and cannot
  represent a cylinder; making it wrap touches selection, export and the region list. **File it if
  you find you want it** — it is not filed today, deliberately, because nobody has asked.
- **Bounding the pan on a map that does *not* wrap.** Still scrolls into emptiness, exactly as
  today. That was option B, which the navigator did not choose, and quietly adding half of it here
  would be deciding something that was decided against.
- **`fitTo`, `centreOn`, `isOffScreen`, zoom, and the map export.** Unchanged; the export must keep
  exporting one world, which is what the `map-export` suite is doing in *The test plan*.
- **Any change to `MapGeometry`, the movement graph, or anything in `crates/`.** This is entirely a
  view-layer bead; no Rust, no regenerated bindings.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=desktop-shell
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/map-export.spec.ts --project=web
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. `git diff` touches `mapViewport.ts`, `MapCanvas.tsx`, `AppShell.tsx` and test files, and nothing
   in `crates/`.
2. A game with `wrapX` shows exactly two `map-world-ghost` elements; one without shows none.
3. Panning east through several world widths never shows the fog rect where the map should be.
4. An exported map image contains the world **once**.

**Only a human can check the thing this bead is for**: open a wrapping game, drag east past `x=71`,
and confirm the map continues rather than ending — and that nothing jumps as it does. That is
Psylocke's pass, and it is the same check that failed on `ah-0w7w`.

## Known traps

- **`tx % period` is negative for a negative `tx`.** The first westward pan from the origin produces
  one, and a negative fold puts the world off screen — the bug this bead is fixing, reintroduced by
  the fix. Use `((tx % period) + period) % period`. Increment 1 pins it.
- **Fold in `slide` as well as `commit`.** Folding only on commit leaves a long drag showing
  emptiness until the pointer is released, which is the exact reported symptom surviving in the
  commonest gesture.
- **`pointerEvents="none"` on every ghost**, or a click on a ghost hits the `<use>` element and
  selects nothing. The fold in `coordinateAt`'s caller is what makes such a click correct.
- **`<use>` content is a shadow tree**, so `getByTestId` finds one of everything inside the world
  however many ghosts there are. Do not "fix" a test that finds one element by making ids unique.
- **CSS classes still apply inside `<use>`** — the clones keep their classes and the document's
  stylesheet reaches them, which is what makes this work with Tailwind at all. It is worth eyeballing
  once in the browser rather than trusting: a themed map that renders unstyled ghosts is the failure
  mode, and no unit test would see it.
- **The map export walks the world group.** Ghosts inside it would export three worlds. `map-export`
  is in the commands above for that reason.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom, by decision (ah-nass).** `MapCanvas.test.tsx` renders with
  `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects — so the ghosts are testable there (they are markup)
  but the camera fold is not (it is an effect on a ref). That is why increments 3 and 4 are smoke
  tests and increments 1 and 2 are not.
- **WebKit's driver answers `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a Chromium smoke assertion can
  pass while the native shell shows nothing. The `native` CI job is what tells you, and both smoke
  projects are in the commands above.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a PWA run straight
  afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker.

Verification failed (2026-08-23, at origin/main ff01fa3d): the navigator panned a wrapping map in the running web app.

WHAT WAS SEEN. The left-hand side is correct at every zoom, including the furthest out. The RIGHT-hand side is not: the rightmost repeat of the map is swapped OUT too early and swapped back IN too late, so a gap of emptiness opens on the right when zoomed far enough out. The asymmetry is the tell - the same drag in the other direction never shows it.

WHERE TO LOOK (read during verification, not verified by test - treat as a lead, not a diagnosis).
ghostShift (packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts) returns -Math.round(translation / period): it places the three copies (-1, 0, +1) around the camera's ORIGIN, tx, which is the translation of the world's left edge rather than the centre of what is on screen. Rounding on the origin is symmetric about tx, but the visible rectangle is not symmetric about tx - it extends to the right of it. Once the viewport is wider than one period (which is exactly what zooming out does), three copies centred on the origin no longer span the screen to the right, while the left stays covered. That would produce precisely this symptom, at precisely this trigger.

If that is the cause, the fix is to choose the copies from the visible rectangle rather than from tx alone - and to emit as many copies as the rectangle needs at that zoom, rather than a fixed three.

NOT AT FAULT. ah-brgo.2 (ruler labels and arrow keys folding) and ah-teg0 (the odd-size wrap refusal) were verified in the same sitting and both passed.

title: A unit set to CONSUME FACTION is fed by its faction's food in the hex
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #556 by a player.

Where the application shows silver after maintenance/support, units set to CONSUME UNIT or CONSUME FACTION should have their upkeep met from available food rather than being charged the flat silver maintenance rate. The reporter notes that ALH (the existing tool) computes support but never accounts for food at all — neither at the old 30 silver per food nor the current 50.

So two things are in scope: knowing which units are set to consume food (and from where), and valuing that food correctly against the silver maintenance figure we display.

Open for planning: exactly where and how this shows in the UI, and whether the silver-per-food rate should be a constant or configurable (the rules have changed it once already, 30 -> 50).
design:
## Context

A unit set to `CONSUME FACTION` eats **faction food held by other units in its region**. Today
nothing models that, and after `ah-1wcw.4` it will still not: that bead pays a unit's upkeep from its
*own* food and then from its own silver — steps 1 and 3 of the rules' payment order — and
deliberately scopes out step 2, because `ah-1wcw.1` settled that the Silver column counts each unit
alone.

```
1. Food the unit owns                        ah-1wcw.4
2. Food from faction units in the region     THIS BEAD
3. Silver the unit holds                     ah-1wcw.4
4-9. regional and allied                     nobody, on purpose
```

So a unit set to `CONSUME FACTION` with no food of its own is charged full silver, when in the game
its faction-mates standing beside it would have fed it. That is the residual of **GitHub issue
#556**, and it is all that is left of it.

**Read the issue and `ah-1wcw.4` before this plan.** The reporter's two explicit asks — count food at
all, and value it at 50 rather than the older 30 — are **both already met** by `ah-1wcw.4`, which
carries `SILVER_PER_FOOD = 50` and `FOOD_TAGS`. Closing this bead as covered was considered
seriously and rejected only because `CONSUME FACTION` genuinely means something that bead does not
do. Do not re-implement the parts it already has.

**This bead is a deliberate exception to a settled rule**, for one term. The precedent is the shipped
`not-enough-silver`, which already pools silver across a hex's `sharing` units and blames nobody in
particular, for the same reason: the engine drains units in an order the report does not show.

The agreed design is `docs/ui/ah-7cdt-faction-food.html`. **Open it before writing any of the shell
work** — it carries both strings verbatim, both panel states, and a table of what was rejected.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The seam `ah-1wcw.4` leaves, which this bead extends

`ah-1wcw.4` adds to `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`:

- `UnitSilver.upkeep: Option<i64>` — its own field, never inside `expense`, because whether it counts
  toward the visible figure is a setting;
- `UPKEEP_PER_CHARACTER = 10`, `UPKEEP_PER_LEADER = 50`, `SILVER_PER_FOOD = 50`,
  `FOOD_TAGS = ["GRAI", "LIVE", "FISH", "MEAL"]`;
- the step-1 rule: for a consuming unit, `items_needed = ceil(owed / 50)`,
  `items_used = min(items_held, items_needed)`, `covered = min(items_used * 50, owed)`.

**All of that is its work, not yours.** If it has not merged when you start, stop and wait: this bead
is a second pass over numbers that bead computes, and writing it against a guess means writing it
twice.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the pool

Two passes, in the rules' own order. Pass 1 is `ah-1wcw.4`'s existing per-unit work. Pass 2 is new
and is a **hex-level** function, because a pool is not a property of any one unit:

```rust
/// What one unit brings to, and takes from, its hex's faction-food pool.
///
/// Built after every unit has fed itself at step 1, so `spare_food` is genuinely spare: the same
/// item can never feed its owner and a neighbour.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FoodClaim {
    pub unit_id: String,
    /// Food items still held once this unit has paid what it could of its own upkeep.
    pub spare_food: i64,
    /// Upkeep still owed after step 1, in silver.
    pub owed_after_own_food: i64,
    /// Whether the unit carries the `consuming faction's food` flag.
    pub draws_on_pool: bool,
}

/// Step 2 of the maintenance payment order, across one hex.
///
/// Returns the upkeep each unit is left with. `Some(0)` for a unit the pool feeds, `None` for one
/// that contends for a pool too small to feed them all - which unit eats is genuinely
/// undeterminable, so no number is invented. A unit that does not draw on the pool is absent from
/// the result and keeps whatever step 1 left it.
#[must_use]
pub fn feed_from_faction_food(claims: &[FoodClaim]) -> BTreeMap<String, Option<i64>>;
```

The rule, exactly:

```
pool          = sum of spare_food over EVERY own unit in the hex, drawing or not
claimants     = units with draws_on_pool and owed_after_own_food > 0
needed_i      = ceil(owed_after_own_food_i / 50)          // whole items; a partial one is consumed whole
total_needed  = sum of needed_i

total_needed <= pool  ->  every claimant gets Some(0)
otherwise             ->  every claimant gets None
```

**`Some(0)`, not a partial figure, and this is worth understanding before you write it.** The pool is
all-or-nothing, so if it can feed a unit at all it covers that unit's *whole* remaining upkeep — a
unit owing 60 needs 2 items and 2 items cover 100. There is no arithmetic that leaves a fed unit
owing anything. That is exactly why the hover note earns its place: an Upkeep of `0` on a unit with
six men looks like a defect until something says why.

**The pool includes food held by units that are not consuming at all.** A quartermaster holding the
grain and paying its own upkeep in silver (step 3 precedes step 5) contributes every item it holds.
That is the shape the reporter is describing and the commonest one in play.

**Why all-or-nothing rather than sharing the shortfall.** The rules waste food, so the total genuinely
differs by who eats — for two units owing 60 and 80 against a pool of 3, feeding the first gives a
total of 30 and feeding the second gives 10. There is no correct number to share out. The navigator
was shown that arithmetic and chose `?` over inventing one. **Do not add a tie-break**; report order,
neediest-first and proportional shares were each considered and rejected, and the mockup records why.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — where the second pass runs

In `review_turn`'s existing `for region in &report.regions` loop, after the per-unit forecasts for
that hex are built and before they are pushed. `Hex::read` has already filtered to `unit.own`
(`semantics.rs:369-383`), so the pool is your own faction's food and nothing else, for free.

Read the flag with the same case-insensitive comparison `Ordered::shares` uses
(`semantics.rs:474-479`). The exact string is `consuming faction's food`, which is already in the
parser's known-flag list (`crates/core/src/report/unit.rs:29-30`) — **`consuming unit's food` is a
different flag and does not draw on the pool.** A unit carrying that one eats its own and stops,
which is step 1 and `ah-1wcw.4`'s.

Do not walk the regions a second time: this loop already runs on every keystroke once typing settles
(`crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs:53-55`).

### `SilverDoubt` gains one variant

```rust
    /// More units are set to eat the hex's faction food than that food can feed, so which of them
    /// eats - and therefore what each pays - cannot be determined.
    ContestedFactionFood,
```

It doubts **`upkeep` only**, not `income` or `expense`: everything else about the unit's month is
still exactly known. `at_month_end` becomes `None` when the setting counts upkeep, and stays a real
number when it does not — a doubt about a term nobody is showing must not blank the figure.

### `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts` — two lines

`summariseUnit`'s note table gains two rows. Both ship verbatim:

| When | Line |
|---|---|
| faction food covered some of this unit's upkeep | `Faction food in this hex covers {n} of this unit's upkeep.` |
| `doubt == ContestedFactionFood` | `There is not enough faction food here to feed every unit set to eat it.` |

`{n}` is **the silver that faction food covered** — `owed_after_own_food` — not the unit's own food,
and not a count of items. The panel is in silver throughout.

Placement in the shared "one note, first match wins" table settled by `ah-1wcw.1`: the doubt sorts
**with the doubts**, before the informational lines; the covered line sorts with the informational
ones, beside `Includes {n} given by {giver} in this hex.`

**Neither note appears when `countUpkeep` is off** (`ah-1wcw.4`'s Settings → Global toggle). There is
no upkeep on show, so there is nothing to explain, and a note about a hidden row is noise.

### No other TypeScript, and no Settings entry

The column, the cell, the sorting, the warning and the panel's shape are `ah-1wcw.1`'s; the `Upkeep`
row and its toggle are `ah-1wcw.4`'s. **This bead adds no setting and no advisory code.** If you find
yourself editing `unitTable.ts`, `UnitTableDock.tsx`, `settingsStore.ts` or `SettingsDialog.tsx`,
stop and say so rather than proceeding.

## Increments

**1. The pool arithmetic.**
Failing test: `faction_food_feeds_every_unit_that_needs_it` in `silver.rs`'s test module — two
claimants owing 60 and 80 against a pool of 6, both `Some(0)`.
Then, each its own test:
`a_pool_too_small_doubts_every_unit_that_contends` (the same two against a pool of 3, both `None`),
`a_unit_that_does_not_draw_on_the_pool_is_untouched` (absent from the result),
`food_held_by_a_unit_that_is_not_consuming_still_fills_the_pool`,
`a_unit_owing_nothing_after_its_own_food_claims_nothing` (not a claimant, and does not consume the
pool on others' behalf),
`a_pool_of_exactly_enough_feeds_everybody` (the boundary: `total_needed == pool`),
`an_empty_hex_pool_leaves_every_claimant_doubted`.
No caller changes this increment.

**2. The second pass runs, and only on the right flag.**
Failing test: `a_unit_consuming_faction_food_is_fed_by_its_neighbours` in `semantics.rs`'s test
module — a hex with a quartermaster holding grain and a consuming unit holding none, asserting the
consuming unit's `upkeep` is `Some(0)`.
Then `a_unit_consuming_only_its_own_food_does_not_draw_on_the_pool` (the other flag, upkeep
unchanged), and `a_unit_consuming_nothing_pays_silver_beside_a_full_pool`.

**3. The doubt reaches the figure, and only when it is being shown.**
Failing test: `a_contested_pool_doubts_the_upkeep_but_not_the_income` — `income` and `expense` stay
`Some`, `upkeep` is `None`, and `doubt == Some(SilverDoubt::ContestedFactionFood)`.
Then the generated TypeScript: `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`, and
commit what it writes.

**4. The real turn is unmoved.**
Failing test: extend `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` with
`the_committed_turn_has_no_unit_consuming_faction_food`, asserting no unit's `upkeep` differs from
what `ah-1wcw.4` left it and that `EXPECTED`'s finding counts are **unchanged**.
If a unit in the committed turn *does* carry the flag, that is a finding rather than a failure: pin
the real numbers and say so in the test's doc comment, the way `EXPECTED`'s own comment does.

**5. The hover explains both states.**
Failing test: `the_silver_section_explains_faction_food` in `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts`,
asserting both lines verbatim, and `no_faction_food_note_when_upkeep_is_not_counted` — the state
that would otherwise ship untested.

## The test plan

| Suite | Pins |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` | increments 1-3, and the regenerated bindings |
| `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` | the committed turn is unchanged by this bead |
| `pnpm vitest packages/shared` | the two new hover lines, verbatim, and the note that must not appear |

`pnpm run check:fast` before the PR. **The smoke suite needs no new spec** — this bead adds no
interface, only two sentences inside a panel `ah-1wcw.1` already covers. Do not add one to "cover" it.

## User-facing decisions

Taken by the navigator on 2026-08-22. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-7cdt-faction-food.html`.

**The bead was rescoped, not planned as filed.** Offered: rescope to the regional-faction-food
residual, close it as covered by `ah-1wcw.4`, rescope wider to the whole payment order, or ask the
reporter what they meant. **Rescope to the residual chosen.** Closing was a serious contender — the
reporter's two explicit asks are met by `ah-1wcw.4` — and was rejected because `CONSUME FACTION`
means something real that no other bead does. The wider option was rejected for abandoning the
each-unit-alone rule entirely rather than making one deliberate exception to it.

**A short pool shows `?`. This reverses an earlier answer in the same interview.**
*First answer:* pool it and share the shortfall across the contending units.
*Then* the planner found that there is **no correct total to share**: the rules consume whole food
items, so for two units owing 60 and 80 against a pool of 3, feeding one gives a total upkeep of 30
and feeding the other gives 10. The navigator was shown that arithmetic and chose
**`?` for every contending unit**.
*Rejected:* optimistic (each unit may draw the whole pool — consistent with `TAX`, `WORK` and
entertaining, but it says everybody ate when four items were needed and three held, and understating
a shortfall is the dangerous direction); first-come-first-fed in report order (the order is ours, not
the engine's, so a unit would be shown starving for a reason that exists only inside this app);
feed-the-neediest-first (a stated rule rather than an accident, but still our invention); and pooling
in silver while ignoring the waste (always a number, at the cost of being optimistic exactly when the
hex is short of food).

**The pool is what is left after each owner feeds itself.** Offered against summing all food in the
hex. **Two passes chosen**, following the rules' own step order; the one-pass version was rejected
for double-counting — the same grain feeding its owner at step 1 and a neighbour at step 2.

**The hover says when faction food fed a unit.** Offered against saying nothing (the `Upkeep` row
already shows the reduced figure) and against two strings distinguishing full from partial coverage.
**Saying it chosen** — and the partial variant is moot anyway, since the pool is all-or-nothing.
Wording chosen from three: `Faction food in this hex covers {n} of this unit's upkeep.` over
`Fed from faction food held in this hex.` (says nothing about how much) and a variant naming the food
items as well as the silver.

**The doubt's wording**, chosen from three:
`There is not enough faction food here to feed every unit set to eat it.` — over
`Which units the faction's food feeds cannot be worked out.` (explains the `?` but not the situation)
and `Faction food in this hex is short, so what each unit pays cannot be said.` (both halves, and the
longest).

**Nothing else about the interface is reopened.** The column keeps its heading, position, red/⚠ split,
sortability and four-row panel; the `Upkeep` row and its Settings → Global toggle are `ah-1wcw.4`'s.

## Out of scope

- **Steps 4 through 9 of the payment order** — silver from other faction units, unclaimed silver, and
  anything from allies. Regional or faction-wide, and out for the same reason step 2 was until the
  navigator made this one exception.
- **Steps 1 and 3.** `ah-1wcw.4`. Do not reimplement the unit's own food or its own silver.
- **Starvation itself.** This models the fee, not the one-in-three chance, and warns about nobody
  starving.
- **The `CONSUME` order.** The report's flags say what a unit is set to consume; nothing here reads
  or writes the order.
- **Any new advisory code, and any change to `not-enough-silver`.** `ah-1wcw.4` already decided that
  the check counts upkeep and does not follow the display setting; this bead changes neither.
- **Any new setting.** `countUpkeep` is `ah-1wcw.4`'s and governs both of this bead's notes.
- **Food as a resource anywhere else** — stock, weight, or a warning about running out of it.
- **A tie-break for a short pool.** Explicitly declined; see *User-facing decisions*.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
pnpm run check:fast
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. Both hover lines appear verbatim in `unitTooltip.test.ts`.
2. `validate_real_orders.rs` passes with `EXPECTED` **unedited**.
3. `git diff` on `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` is **empty** — no advisory
   code is added.
4. `git diff` touches neither `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts` nor
   `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`.
5. A constructed hex with a quartermaster and two consuming units shows `0` upkeep on both and the
   covered note; reducing the quartermaster's grain until the pool is short turns both to `?` with
   the other note, and leaves the quartermaster's own figure exact.

**Only a human can check** that the two new lines read well beside the existing ones — Psylocke's
pass. Everything else here is a running test.

## Known traps

- **`consuming unit's food` and `consuming faction's food` are two different flags** and this bead
  acts on only the second. Matching on a prefix, or on `contains("consuming")`, silently makes every
  self-consuming unit draw on the pool and quietly changes `ah-1wcw.4`'s answers.
- **The pool is all-or-nothing, so a fed unit's upkeep is always `Some(0)`.** If your implementation
  can produce a fed unit still owing something, the granularity rule has gone wrong — a unit owing 60
  takes 2 items and 2 items cover 100.
- **`ah-1wcw.4` must have merged first.** Every constant, the `upkeep` field and the whole of step 1
  are its work. Its *Known traps* apply here unchanged.
- **The doubt must not blank a figure nobody is showing.** With `countUpkeep` off, `at_month_end`
  stays a real number even when `upkeep` is `None`. This is the state easiest to get wrong and
  hardest to notice, because the default has the setting on.
- **`ceil` on integers, not floats.** `(owed + 49) / 50` on `i64`; a float here reintroduces exactly
  the rounding sensitivity `ah-1wcw.1` avoided by keeping wages in hundredths.
- **Never ask for an effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** No jsdom by decision (ah-nass): its
  component tests render with `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects. Both new strings live in
  the pure `summariseUnit`, which is why increment 5 is testable at all.
- **`corpus_errors` compares against a committed generated table.** Nothing here should change it; if
  it goes red, stop and work out why rather than running `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1` at it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Units with CONSUME UNIT or CONSUME FACTION have their maintenance met from available food where food is available, rather than charged wholly in silver.
- The silver-per-food rate used matches the current rules (50), and is defined in one place so a future rules change is a one-line edit.
- The displayed silver-after-maintenance figure reflects the food allowance.
- Units with no consume setting, or with no food available, are unaffected.

Overlaps ah-1wcw.4, planned 2026-08-22 by Beast. Read that plan before ranking this.

ah-1wcw.4 models maintenance at 10 silver a character and 50 a leader, and DOES model food consumption for the unit's own food - steps 1 and 3 of the rules' payment order, including the branch that a unit not set to consume spends its silver before its own food, and that a fractional cost consumes a whole unit of food.

What it deliberately leaves out, and what may be all that is left of this bead: steps 2 and 4-9 of that order - faction food from other units in the same region, silver from other faction units, unclaimed silver, and anything from allied units. All are regional or faction-wide, while the Silver column counts each unit alone.

It also does not model starvation itself, only the fee.
Implementation (Cyclops, 2026-08-23): two navigator-approved deviations from the plan's all-or-nothing rule, both because it doubted figures that are exactly known. (1) An empty pool feeds nobody and doubts nobody - the plan's an_empty_hex_pool_leaves_every_claimant_doubted is inverted, because the committed turn has 11 units set to consuming faction's food in hex 1:26,52 with no food at all, and the plan's rule put ? on all 11. (2) A lone claimant against a short pool eats what there is and owes the rest - contention needs two contenders. Multi-claimant contention is unchanged and still shows ?. NOTE: a first attempt used the `consume faction` ORDER in the template and saw nothing happen - that was the fixture's fault, not the build's, because food_claim (silver.rs:68, CONSUMING_FACTION_FLAG) keys off the report's unit flag rather than the template. title: Say when a line of the turn report could not be read
description: The surface half of ah-w544. A line the parser cannot read is dropped with no trace, and ParsedReport carries no error channel at all. Add one, route it to the shells, and show the count plus the raw text of each unreadable line. Navigator chose the 'full' option on 2026-08-22: count AND the lines themselves, viewable. Depends on ah-w544.1.
design: ## Context A line of a turn report that the parser cannot read is dropped with **no trace at all**. There is no error channel on `ParsedReport` to carry one and nothing downstream that could show it, so a player looking at a hex simply does not see one of their own units and has no way to learn that anything was lost. That silence is what makes the sibling defect a P0 rather than a cosmetic bug, and it is what this bead removes. This is the surface half of epic `ah-w544`. The parser half, **`ah-w544.1`**, removes the commonest cause (a comma in a name) and **blocks this bead**. Read its plan before starting: it rewrites the exact functions this bead has to instrument, and the seams it leaves are named below. **The design is settled and drawn.** `docs/ui/ah-w544.2-unreadable-lines.html` is the agreed interface, chosen with the navigator over four rounds on 2026-08-22, and it carries every string verbatim, every state, and a table of the options that were rejected. **Open it before writing any component code.** This plan does not repeat the pictures; where the two disagree, the mockup wins on appearance and this plan wins on structure. The shape, in one paragraph: an amber header chip reading `6 unreadable`, absent entirely when there is nothing to say, which drops a panel listing every unreadable record in **file order** — its line range, a kind label, its raw text, and on a rejected region a red note saying how much went with it — with a `Copy all` button shaped for pasting into a bug report. **One existing type is deliberately not reused.** `ParseWarning` (`crates/core/src/lib.rs:151-163`) already exists end-to-end with `code`/`section`/`message`/`line_start`/`line_end`/`severity`, is already generated to TypeScript, and has exactly one producer (`turn-header-missing`, `lib.rs:369`) and **zero consumers anywhere**. It is tempting and it is wrong here: it lives on `ReportParseResult` (the flat summary from `parseReport`) rather than on `ParsedReport` (what the shell actually loads, via `reportParser` at `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts:315-323`), and it is a diagnostic *about* a report where this is a record *of dropped content* — a `text` field means nothing on `turn-header-missing`. Leave `ParseWarning` alone. ## Files to change, and what to reuse ### 1. `crates/core/src/report/model.rs` — the new types ```rust /// What kind of record the parser failed to read. Fixed set; the shell renders one word per case. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub enum UnreadableKind { Region, Unit, Structure, Battle, Attitude } /// What a rejected region block took with it. Only ever `Some` for `UnreadableKind::Region`. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct LostBlock { /// Source lines after the block's own header line. pub further_lines: usize, /// How many of those carried a unit marker (`*` or `-`). pub units: usize, } /// One record the parser could not read, kept verbatim so the player can see what was lost. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct UnreadableLine { pub kind: UnreadableKind, /// 1-based source line numbers, from `LogicalLine`. Equal when the record did not wrap. pub line_start: usize, pub line_end: usize, /// The joined logical line, exactly as the parser saw it. pub text: String, pub lost: Option, } ``` `#[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))]` is the pattern every type in this file already uses — copy it exactly, including `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, or the generated TypeScript will not match what serde emits. ### 2. `crates/core/src/report/mod.rs` — the field, and the region producer `ParsedReport` (`mod.rs:40-49`) gains one field: ```rust /// Every record the parser could not read, in file order. Empty for a healthy report. pub unreadable_lines: Vec, ``` `ParsedReport` derives `Default`, so an empty vec is the default and no other constructor breaks. In `parse_report_full` (`mod.rs:89`), the region loop currently discards a rejected block: ```rust let mut unreadable: Vec = Vec::new(); for (position, &start) in starts.iter().enumerate() { let end = starts.get(position + 1).copied().unwrap_or(lines.len()); match parse_region_block(&lines[start], &lines[start + 1..end], &mut unreadable) { Some(region) => regions.push(region), None => { let header = &lines[start]; let block = &lines[start + 1..end]; unreadable.push(UnreadableLine { kind: UnreadableKind::Region, line_start: header.line_start, line_end: header.line_end, text: header.text.clone(), lost: Some(LostBlock { further_lines: block .last() .map_or(0, |line| line.line_end.saturating_sub(header.line_end)), units: block .iter() .filter(|line| matches!(line.marker(), Some('*' | '-'))) .count(), }), }); } } } ``` Then `parse_header` and `parse_battles` take `&mut unreadable` too, and finally: ```rust unreadable.sort_by_key(|entry| (entry.line_start, entry.line_end)); ``` **File order is the agreed ordering** — ascending by first line number, kinds interleaved, no grouping and no floating a lost region to the top. The sort is needed because the header and battles are parsed from the preamble *after* the regions. ### 3. `crates/core/src/report/region.rs` — units and structures `parse_region_block` gains `unreadable: &mut Vec`. At `region.rs:246` (the `+` branch) and `region.rs:254` (the `*`/`-` branch), the `if let Some(...)` becomes a `match`, and the `None` arm pushes: - `+` → `UnreadableKind::Structure` - `*` or `-` → `UnreadableKind::Unit` with `line_start`/`line_end`/`text` taken from the `LogicalLine` (`line`, not `body` — `body` has had its marker stripped, and the raw line is the point) and `lost: None`. `LogicalLine` (`crates/core/src/report/unwrap.rs:30-34`) already carries `text`, `indent`, `line_start` and `line_end`, so **nothing has to be computed or threaded** — this is why the plumbing is cheap. ### 4. `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` — roster lines `parse_battles` gains the out-parameter and passes it down to wherever `parse_battle_unit` (`battle.rs:481`) is called from. A `None` from it pushes `UnreadableKind::Battle`. **Only `parse_battle_unit`.** `parse_casualty_line` (`battle.rs:362`) and `parse_headline` (`battle.rs:392`) both tolerate an unrecognised shape by design and keep the text verbatim in the battle — they lose nothing, so they produce nothing here. Do not instrument them. ### 5. `crates/core/src/report/header.rs` — Declared Attitudes `parse_attitude_level` (`header.rs:~208`) is rewritten by `ah-w544.1` into a greedy `while let Some(...) = split_leading_id(remaining)` loop. **That rewrite is what makes this instrumentation exact**: when the loop ends, anything left in `remaining` that is not empty, whitespace or `.` is precisely the part that could not be read. Push one `UnreadableKind::Attitude` for that remainder, with the enclosing `LogicalLine`'s numbers and its `text`. If `ah-w544.1` has not landed when you start, **stop and wait** — it is your blocker, and writing this against the old `filter_map` chain means writing it twice. ### 6. `packages/core-client/src/generated/` and `index.ts` Generated by ts-rs, **not hand-written**. `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` writes the files (`TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` is set in `.cargo/config.toml:38-40`). Expect three new files — `UnreadableLine.ts`, `UnreadableKind.ts`, `LostBlock.ts` — and a changed `ParsedReport.ts`. Re-export the three new types from `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` beside the existing generated re-exports at `index.ts:5-41`. `pnpm run check:generated` and CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:267-269`) both fail if `packages/core-client/src/generated` is dirty after a build, so **commit the generated files**. ### 7. `packages/shared/src/unreadableLines.ts` — new, and where all the wording lives A pure module with no React in it. `packages/shared` has no jsdom by decision (ah-nass), so this is the only place the strings can actually be unit-tested — see *Known traps*. ```ts import type { UnreadableLine, UnreadableKind } from "@atlantis/core-client"; /** The chip's visible text, or null when there is nothing to say and the chip is not rendered. */ export function unreadableChipLabel(count: number): string | null; /** The chip's accessible name. Singular at one. */ export function unreadableChipName(count: number): string; /** `Region` | `Unit` | `Structure` | `Battle` | `Attitude`. */ export function unreadableKindLabel(kind: UnreadableKind): string; /** `412`, or `998–999` (en dash) when the record wrapped. */ export function unreadableLineRange(entry: UnreadableLine): string; /** The red note under a lost hex, or null for every other kind. */ export function unreadableCostNote(entry: UnreadableLine): string | null; /** The whole clipboard block. ASCII only — plain hyphens, no en dash. */ export function unreadableClipboardText( entries: readonly UnreadableLine[], turnNumber: number | null, factionLabel: string | null ): string; /** `Borg (73)` from a header, or null when it does not name both parts. */ export function factionLabelOf(header: ParsedReport["header"]): string | null; ``` **The strings, verbatim.** These ship exactly as written; the mockup's *Strings* table is the same list and the two must not drift. | Function / place | Text | |---|---| | `unreadableChipLabel(n)`, n ≥ 1 | `${n} unreadable` | | `unreadableChipLabel(0)` | `null` — the chip is not rendered | | `unreadableChipName(n)`, n ≠ 1 | `${n} lines could not be read` | | `unreadableChipName(1)` | `1 line could not be read` | | Panel heading | `Lines that could not be read` (plural always — it names the panel, not its contents) | | Panel footer | `None of this reached the map.` (count-independent by design) | | `unreadableKindLabel` | `Region` · `Unit` · `Structure` · `Battle` · `Attitude` | | Cost note | `The whole hex was lost — ${m} further lines, including ${u} units.` | | Cost note, m = 1 | `The whole hex was lost — 1 further line, including ${u} units.` | | Cost note, u = 1 | `… including 1 unit.` | | Copy button, at rest | `Copy all` | | Copy button, 2s after a successful copy | `Copied` | | Close button `aria-label` | `close unreadable lines` | | Clipboard first line | `${n} lines of turn ${t}, ${factionLabel}, could not be read:` | | … turn known, faction not | `${n} lines of turn ${t} could not be read:` | | … neither known | `${n} lines of this report could not be read:` | | … any of the three, n = 1 | `1 line …` | The clipboard body, one row per entry, laid out exactly: **two spaces**, then the kind **lowercased and left-aligned in a 9-character field**, then the line range **right-aligned in an 8-character field**, then `": "`, then the text. A lost hex's note follows on its own line, indented to the text column, wrapped in parentheses. **ASCII hyphens throughout** — the en dash is the panel's, not the clipboard's. Increment 5 asserts the whole block against a literal, which is what keeps this honest. **The clipboard names the turn, never a file.** `LoadedTurn` (`packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts:60`) carries no filename, and a turn restored from storage after a reload has none to carry — one form that is always true beats two that differ by how you got there. **But `ReportHeader` makes all three of those optional** (`header.rs:42-49`: `turn_number`, `faction_name` and `faction_id` are each `Option`), so "always the turn" needs saying exactly. Three forms, and no others: | Available | First line | |---|---| | turn and faction | `${n} lines of turn ${t}, ${name} (${id}), could not be read:` | | turn only | `${n} lines of turn ${t} could not be read:` | | neither | `${n} lines of this report could not be read:` | Each with `1 line` at a count of one. `factionLabel` is therefore built as `${name} (${id})` only when **both** parts are present, and the parameter is `string | null`; `turnNumber` is `number | null`. This is a degenerate-data fallback rather than a fresh aesthetic choice — the navigator settled the principle ("always the turn") and this is what it means when the report does not say. ### 8. `packages/shared/src/copyText.ts` — new, and the first clipboard write in the application There is **no clipboard write anywhere in this codebase today** — no helper, no `navigator.clipboard` call — and the desktop shell has no Tauri clipboard plugin (`apps/desktop/src/desktopPlugins.ts` exposes only `save`, `writeTextFile` and `httpPost`). This bead writes the first one, web-first, and verifies the desktop rather than assuming it: ```ts /** Puts `text` on the clipboard. Resolves false when the browser refuses; never throws. */ export async function copyText(text: string): Promise; ``` `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text)` in a `try`/`catch`, returning `false` on absence or rejection. The button shows `Copied` only on `true`; on `false` it stays `Copy all` and nothing else happens — no error message, because the panel text remains selectable and a failed copy is not worth a second notice. **If the Tauri webview refuses `navigator.clipboard`**, add `@tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager` and route through `desktopPlugins.ts` like `writeTextFile` already is. Only then — the plugin is a native dependency and a permissions entry, and it is not worth paying for if the webview simply works. Increment 6 is where you find out. ### 9. `packages/shared/src/workspace/UnreadableLinesPanel.tsx` — new Copy `ProblemsPanel.tsx` and `TurnMessagesPanel.tsx`; this is the same pattern for the third time. ```tsx export function UnreadableLinesPanel({ entries, turnNumber, factionLabel, onDismiss }: { entries: readonly UnreadableLine[]; /** From `parsed.header.turnNumber`, which is nullable. */ turnNumber: number | null; /** `Borg (73)`, or null when the report does not name both parts. */ factionLabel: string | null; onDismiss: () => void; }) ``` Root is `PopoverFrame` (`packages/shared/src/workspace/popover.tsx:61-93`): ```tsx ``` `width` must be a whole Tailwind class literal — `popover.tsx:58-59` says so, and an assembled string is invisible to Tailwind v4's `@source` scan and produces an unstyled panel. Close button copied from `ProblemsPanel.tsx:51-58`: `className="rounded px-1.5 text-ink-dim hover:text-ink"`, `aria-label="close unreadable lines"`, `✕`. Each row: line range (`text-ink-dim`, monospace), kind label, then the raw text in a bordered, monospaced, `whitespace-pre-wrap break-all` block with a left border — `border-l-warn` normally and `border-l-danger` for a `Region`. **Never truncate and never use an ellipsis**; the whole point is that the player can read what the parser could not. Use `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H` (`primitives.tsx:15`) for the scroll bound, as the other panels do. **The narrow window:** the row grid is **stacked by default and three-column from `sm:` up** — mobile-first, so `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-[5rem_4.5rem_1fr]`. Below Tailwind's `sm` (640px viewport) the line range and kind sit on their own line above the text, which then takes full width. A responsive variant on the grid template, no JavaScript. A `Copy all` button. Rebuilt from the loaded report rather than stored (*rejected:* dismissable, because then the dismissal must be remembered somewhere and a dismissed loss is a silent loss again). **Q4 — what counts as unreadable.** Offered: only marker lines (my recommendation), every record-shaped thing, or region blocks as well. **Chosen: region blocks as well — the widest.** So the producers are all five, and this is why `UnreadableKind` has five cases rather than one. *Rejected:* the narrow definition, because it misses a whole lost hex, which is the largest silent loss there is. **Q5 — wrapped records.** **Chosen: the line range**, `998–999`, with the joined text. *Rejected:* just the first line, because the text shown is then longer than that line actually is. **Q6 — batch imports.** **Chosen: no grouping by file, ever** — the chip describes the turn on screen, and the batch total goes in `ImportSummaryDialog`. *Rejected:* grouping by file, because the chip would then mean two different things depending on how you last loaded, and it needs storage outliving the load. **Q6b / Q9b — the clipboard.** **Chosen: the full format with a kind per row and the hex cost note**, because a maintainer reading a pasted block has no panel to look at. *Rejected:* bare lines with no preamble, and dropping the button entirely. **Q7 — does a row say what kind it was.** Offered: no, a kind column with a cost note (my recommendation), or regions in their own group. **Chosen: the kind column and the cost note.** *Rejected:* grouping regions separately, because it reintroduces grouping on a new axis immediately after Q6 ruled it out, and adds two headings with their own counts and empty states. **Q8 — the footer.** **Chosen: `None of this reached the map.`** — replacing round 1's `Nothing on these lines reached the map.`, which understated a lost hex now that one can appear in the list. *Rejected:* keeping the old wording; adding a "please report it" sentence; and no footer. **Q9 — the chip's tone.** **Chosen: always amber.** *Rejected:* red with a different string when a hex was lost, because it is a longer chip in a header that already wraps plus a second string with plural forms in it. **Q10 — the narrow window.** **Chosen: stack the row**, so the raw text never loses width. *Rejected:* dropping the kind column when narrow, because that hides information at exactly the width where the raw text is hardest to read. **Q11 — the batch dialog's bullet.** **Chosen:** `6 lines across 2 of these reports could not be read.` *Rejected:* a shorter form telling the player what to do, and omitting the bullet entirely. **Q12 — keyboard and focus.** Proposed the chip behave exactly as the events chip beside it, with the caveat that I would go and read that chip and it would win on any disagreement. It disagreed on one point: **neither existing panel moves focus on open** — no focus trap, no `autoFocus`, no `.focus()`. Put back to the navigator with the conflict named. **Chosen: match the neighbour — focus stays on the chip.** *Rejected:* moving focus on this panel only (two identical-looking neighbours behaving differently is its own accessibility problem), and fixing all three panels here (right end state, wrong bead). **`ah-pdly` is the bead for fixing all three**, filed at P4 and awaiting a ranking. **The clipboard's first line.** Drawn naming a file, which cannot always be written: a turn restored from storage has no filename, and the chip is rebuilt from the loaded report. Put back to the navigator with three forms. **Chosen: always the turn** — `6 lines of turn 71, Borg (73), could not be read:`. *Rejected:* filename-when-known, and both. **Ordering.** Not asked; found by reading the mockup back and decided as **file order, ascending by first line number, kinds interleaved**. The mockup was corrected to match and now states it. A lost hex is not floated to the top — the kind column and its red note do that work, and file order is the one rule that needs no explaining when the player goes and looks at the report. **Copy all's cost.** Put back to the navigator once it emerged that this is the first clipboard write in the application and the desktop shell has no Tauri clipboard plugin. Offered: keep it web-first with an explicit desktop check (my recommendation), add the Tauri plugin up front, or drop it. **Chosen: web-first with a desktop check**, which is increment 6. ## Out of scope - **The parser fix itself.** `ah-w544.1`, which blocks this bead. Do not change parsing behaviour here — this bead only records what the parser already fails on. - **Moving focus into a header popover on open.** `ah-pdly`, deliberately, so all three panels change together. Match the existing behaviour exactly. - **`ParseWarning` and `ReportParseResult`.** Untouched. Do not migrate the one existing warning, do not add consumers for it, do not put `unreadable_lines` on `ReportParseResult`. - **`parse_casualty_line` and `parse_headline`** in `battle.rs`. They keep their text verbatim and lose nothing, so they produce no entries. - **Any error message when a copy fails.** The button simply does not change to `Copied`. - **A Tauri clipboard plugin**, unless increment 6 proves the webview refuses `navigator.clipboard`. - **Recovering or repairing an unreadable line.** This bead reports; it never guesses at what the line meant. - **A settings toggle for any of this.** The chip is absent when there is nothing to say, which is the only "off" it needs. - **`ah-lt0o`** — the unmatched-opening-bracket mis-parse. It is a *wrong* parse rather than a failed one, so it produces no entry here and this bead does not detect it. ## Validation ```bash cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core cargo fmt --check cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pnpm run check:generated pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test pnpm run check:fast pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=desktop-shell ``` Both smoke projects, not just `web` — the panel is new UI and the desktop shell renders it through a different driver (see *Known traps*). **One check only a human can make, and it must be made before the bead closes:** launch the desktop shell, load a report with an unreadable line, open the panel and press `Copy all`, then paste somewhere and confirm the text arrived. That is increment 6's open question and no test in this repository can answer it. ## Known traps - **`packages/shared` has no jsdom, by decision (ah-nass).** Its component tests render with `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects, attaches no refs and fires no timers — **silently**. A `*.test.tsx` that clicks the chip, or asserts the `Copied` label appeared, is a test the harness cannot run, and four beads have each paid about half an hour discovering that. This is exactly why every string lives in `unreadableLines.ts` and is tested there: the pure module is unit-testable, the click is the smoke suite's job. `packages/shared/src/testing/README.md` has the pattern. - **`PopoverFrame`'s `width`, `padding` and `textSize` must be whole Tailwind class literals** (`popover.tsx:58-59`). Write `width="w-[32rem]"`, never a template. - **Every `--color-*` token needs a light-theme counterpart**, and `theme.test.ts` enforces it. If you add a colour rather than reusing `warn`/`danger`/`edge`/`ink-dim`, add both. - **WebKit's driver answers `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a Chromium smoke assertion can pass while the native shell shows nothing. The `native` CI job is what tells you. This panel is full of long monospaced text in a fixed-width popover — precisely the shape that trips it. - **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a PWA run straight afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker. - **`crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs` names every `.rep` on disk** and `every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` fails when the two disagree (ah-v2l). Increment 9 adds a fixture, so this is a two-place edit. - **`corpus_errors` compares against a committed generated table** (`docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md`). Nothing in this bead should change it. If it goes red, **stop and work out why** rather than running `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1` — it means a producer is firing on a real report, which is the failure mode this whole design is built to avoid. - **The generated TypeScript is written by `cargo test`, not by a codegen script**, and CI fails if `packages/core-client/src/generated` is dirty (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:267-269`). Run the Rust tests and commit what they write. - **`ts_rs` export is behind `#[cfg_attr(test, ...)]`** in this crate.
