title: A unit or faction named with a comma is read instead of dropped
description: The parser half of ah-w544. split_trailing_id requires its input to end in (digits); parse_unit splits the head on commas first and hands it only field 0, so a unit named 'Smith, Jones' is dropped whole. The same hole exists at all six split_trailing_id call sites. Fix it with one shared helper and pin the other punctuation classes with fixtures. No UI.
design:
## Context

`crates/core/src/report/unit.rs` drops a unit whose name contains a comma. Not mis-renders it —
drops it, with no error anywhere, so a player looking at a hex simply does not see one of their own
units. That is silent data loss on a turn report, and it is why the navigator ranked this P0 on
2026-08-22.

The mechanism. `parse_unit` splits the unit line's head on top-level commas (`unit.rs:125`) and then
requires field 0 to end in `(digits)` (`unit.rs:130`, via `scan.rs:46`):

```text
* Smith, Jones (100), Wanderers (29), behind, 10 humans [HUMN].
fields    = ["Smith", "Jones (100)", "Wanderers (29)", "behind", "10 humans [HUMN]"]
fields[0] = "Smith"          -> split_trailing_id finds no '(' -> None -> parse_unit returns None
```

The comma is both a legal character in a player-chosen name and the field separator, so splitting
first and reading the identifier second cannot work. **The fix inverts that order**: find the first
top-level `(digits)` group and treat everything before it as the name, whatever commas it contains.

**Five call sites have this defect, not the six the bead's description implies.** Verified by
reading each one:

| Site | Broken? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `unit.rs:130` — unit name | **yes** | comma-splits first |
| `unit.rs:163` — unit's faction | **yes** | per-field `split_trailing_id` inside the loop |
| `battle.rs:487` — roster line name | **yes** | comma-splits first |
| `battle.rs:503` — roster line faction | **yes** | per-field, same shape |
| `header.rs:221` — `Declared Attitudes` entries | **yes** | `split_top_level(...).filter_map(split_trailing_id)` |
| `header.rs:168` — the faction header line | no | `parse_faction` never splits on commas; `split_trailing_id("Smith, Jones (95)")` already returns `("Smith, Jones", "95")` |
| `battle.rs:366/399/407` — casualty and headline combatants | no | whole text is passed to `split_trailing_id`, no comma split |

Do not "fix" the three that are not broken. `header.rs:168` in particular is correct as written and
a change there risks the faction-type parenthetical (`Borg TNG (95) (Magic 5)`).

The navigator also asked, in the same breath, that "other non-letter characters are ok". Increment 6
pins that as tests. One character class is **out of scope and already has a bead** — see *Out of
scope*.

This is the parser half of epic `ah-w544`. The other half, `ah-w544.2`, adds a surface that says
when a line could not be read at all; it is blocked on this bead. Nothing here adds an error
channel — `ParsedReport` gains no field and no behaviour changes for a line that is genuinely
unreadable.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/report/scan.rs` — two new functions

Both go beside `split_trailing_id`, which stays exactly as it is (three call sites outside this bead
still depend on it and are correct).

```rust
/// Reads a leading `Name (id)` from `input`, where the name may itself contain top-level commas.
///
/// Scans for the first parenthesised group at bracket depth zero whose contents are all ASCII
/// digits; everything before it is the name. `Ranger (scout) Bob (100)` therefore yields
/// `("Ranger (scout) Bob", "100")`, and `Smith, Jones (100), Wanderers (29)` yields
/// `("Smith, Jones", "100")` with `", Wanderers (29)"` consumed down to `"Wanderers (29)"`.
///
/// The third element is what follows the closing `)`, with leading whitespace and one leading
/// separator comma removed, so a caller can keep walking or compute a byte offset with
/// `input.len() - rest.len()`.
///
/// `None` when no top-level `(digits)` group exists — which is what every caller already treats as
/// an unreadable line.
#[must_use]
pub fn split_leading_id(input: &str) -> Option<(String, String, &str)>;

/// The next top-level field of `input` (trimmed) and what follows it, past one separator.
///
/// The slice-returning counterpart of [`split_top_level`], for callers that consume fields one at a
/// time and need the untouched remainder rather than a rebuilt list.
///
/// `None` when `input` is empty or all whitespace.
#[must_use]
pub fn next_top_level_field(input: &str, separator: char) -> Option<(&str, &str)>;
```

`split_leading_id` tracks depth the same way `split_top_level` already does — `(`/`[` increment,
`)`/`]` decrement — and a group counts only when it opens at depth 0. Reuse that loop's shape; do
not add a regex (the crate has no regex dependency and `scan.rs` says so in its module doc).

**`input` is scanned exactly as given — do not trim it inside either function.** Every caller
already trims and strips its own trailing `.`, and an internal trim would break the byte-offset
contract: `battle.rs` computes a position as `input.len() - rest.len()`, which is only correct while
`rest` is a suffix of `input` itself. Trimming a trailing `.` internally would make `rest` a suffix
of a *shorter* string and put that arithmetic one byte out — silently, since the line would still
parse. `split_leading_id` may still call `split_trailing_id` internally on a candidate slice, which
trims; that is fine, because only the returned name goes through it.

### `crates/core/src/report/unit.rs` — `parse_unit`

Replace lines 124–131 and the faction branch at 158–167. The shape:

```rust
let (head, sections) = split_sections(without_marker);
let (name, unit_id, mut rest) = split_leading_id(&head)?;
// ... build `unit` with name and unit_id exactly as today ...

loop {
    let Some((field, after)) = next_top_level_field(rest, ',') else { break };

    if let Some(flag) = matching_flag(field) {
        if flag == "on guard" || flag == "guarding" { unit.on_guard = true; }
        unit.flags.push(flag.to_string());
        rest = after;
        continue;
    }

    // The faction: at most one, and only before the item list starts.
    if unit.faction_id.is_none() && unit.items.is_empty() {
        if let Some((faction_name, faction_id, after_faction)) = split_leading_id(rest) {
            if !faction_name.contains('[') {
                unit.faction_name = Some(faction_name);
                unit.faction_id = Some(faction_id);
                rest = after_faction;
                continue;
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some(item) = parse_item_amount(field) { unit.items.push(item); }
    rest = after;
}
```

Three decisions bound into that, all taken here so the implementer does not have to:

- **The faction scan runs over `rest`, not over one field**, which is the whole point — that is what
  lets a faction name carry a comma.
- **`!faction_name.contains('[')` is the bound that stops it running away.** Because the scan is
  greedy across commas, a unit with a *concealed* faction could otherwise have a later `(digits)`
  swallow its whole item list into a faction name. An item or skill always carries a bracketed tag
  and a faction name does not, so a candidate containing `[` is rejected. **Known limit:** a faction
  literally named `The [Redacted]` is not recognised. Accept it; do not invent a cleverer bound.
- **Flags are consumed before the faction is looked for**, preserving today's behaviour for
  `City Guard (89), on guard, The Guardsmen (1), ...` — without this, the greedy scan reads the
  faction name as `"on guard, The Guardsmen"`. `records_a_guard_flag_that_precedes_the_faction`
  (`unit.rs:260`) is the existing test that catches it.

Everything after the loop — the `sections` match, `count_men` — is untouched.

### `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` — `parse_battle_unit` (line 481)

Same shape, and it is the site with the most regression risk because `body` is a byte slice of the
original line. Rewrite the field walk to mirror `parse_unit`'s:

```rust
let trimmed = line.trim().trim_end_matches('.');
let (name, id, mut rest) = split_leading_id(trimmed)?;

let mut faction = None;
let mut flags = Vec::new();

loop {
    let Some((field, after)) = next_top_level_field(rest, ',') else { break };
    if let Some(flag) = matching_flag(field) { flags.push(flag.to_string()); rest = after; continue; }
    if faction.is_none() {
        if let Some((faction_name, faction_id, after_faction)) = split_leading_id(rest) {
            if !faction_name.contains('[') {
                faction = Some(Combatant { name: faction_name, id: faction_id });
                rest = after_faction;
                continue;
            }
        }
    }
    break;                       // keep today's `break` — a roster line's body starts here
}

let body_start = trimmed.len() - rest.len();
```

`body_start` was previously the offset just past the last recognised field's comma;
`trimmed.len() - rest.len()` is the same position, because `next_top_level_field` and
`split_leading_id` both return the remainder past one separator. Keep the rest of the function
(`body`, the `BattleUnit` construction) exactly as it is.

**`top_level_fields_with_ends` (battle.rs:448) becomes unused — delete it.** It is a near-duplicate
of `split_top_level` that existed only for these offsets, and `cargo clippy` runs as a gate, so
leaving it dead fails the build.

### `crates/core/src/report/header.rs` — `parse_attitude_level` (line ~208)

Replace the `split_top_level(...).into_iter().filter_map(...).map(...)` chain:

```rust
let factions = if is_none_list(rest) {
    Vec::new()
} else {
    let mut entries = Vec::new();
    let mut remaining = rest.trim_end_matches('.');
    while let Some((name, id, after)) = split_leading_id(remaining) {
        entries.push(FactionRef { name, id });
        remaining = after;
    }
    entries
};
```

The loop always terminates: `after` starts strictly past a `)` that was inside `remaining`, so the
slice shrinks on every pass. Greedy-from-the-left is the right rule here even though a list like
`Smith, Jones (29), Bob (30)` is genuinely ambiguous — it reads as two factions when no name has a
comma (each entry ends in its own id, so the scan consumes exactly one), which is today's behaviour
unchanged.

**Update the doc comment above the function.** It currently reads "a faction name that itself
contained a top-level comma would be split — no such name has been seen in a real report." That is
no longer true and must not be left standing.

### `crates/core/src/report/import.rs`, `export.rs`, `merge.rs`, `model.rs`

**No changes.** `ReportUnit` is unchanged, so nothing downstream moves and no TypeScript is
regenerated.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test. Red, then green, then the next one.

**1. `split_leading_id` and `next_top_level_field`.**
Failing test: `reads_a_leading_identifier_past_commas_in_the_name` in `scan.rs`'s `mod tests`.
Asserts `split_leading_id("Smith, Jones (100), Wanderers (29)")` is
`Some(("Smith, Jones", "100", "Wanderers (29)"))`; that
`split_leading_id("Ranger (scout) Bob (100), x")` is `Some(("Ranger (scout) Bob", "100", "x"))`;
and that `split_leading_id("Ranger (scout)")` is `None`.
Second test `walks_top_level_fields_one_at_a_time`: `next_top_level_field("a, b (1), c", ',')` is
`Some(("a", "b (1), c"))`, and `next_top_level_field("  ", ',')` is `None`.
No caller changes in this increment.

**2. The unit's own name.**
Failing test: `keeps_a_unit_whose_name_contains_a_comma` in `unit.rs`'s `mod tests`. Parses
`"* Smith, Jones (100), Wanderers (29), behind, 10 humans [HUMN]."` and asserts
`name == "Smith, Jones"`, `unit_id == "100"`, `faction_name == Some("Wanderers")`, `men == 10`.
Change only line 130's read. Keep the existing field loop as it is by re-splitting the remainder —
`let fields = split_top_level(rest, ',');` in place of today's `split_top_level(&head, ',')` and
`fields.remove(0)`. The unit's faction is still read per-field and still breaks on a comma; that is
increment 3's job, and its test is what proves it.

**3. The unit's faction.**
Failing test: `keeps_a_faction_whose_name_contains_a_comma`. Parses
`"- Unit (5812), Wanderers, Inc (83), avoiding, hill dwarf [HDWA]."` and asserts
`faction_name == Some("Wanderers, Inc")`, `faction_id == Some("83")`, `flags == ["avoiding"]`,
`items.len() == 1`. Replace the field loop with the shape above.
The four existing `unit.rs` tests — including `records_a_guard_flag_that_precedes_the_faction` and
`does_not_split_a_name_that_contains_punctuation` — must stay green without edits.

**4. The battle roster line.**
Failing test: `reads_a_roster_line_whose_name_contains_a_comma` in `battle.rs`'s `mod tests`
(line 532). Asserts the name, id, faction and — critically — that `body` still begins at the item
list, unchanged. Then delete `top_level_fields_with_ends`.
Existing battle tests are the regression net for `body_start`; run them before and after.

**5. `Declared Attitudes`.**
Failing test: `reads_an_attitude_entry_whose_faction_name_contains_a_comma` in `header.rs`'s
`mod tests` (line 338). Asserts `Hostile : Smith, Jones (29), Creatures (2).` yields two
`FactionRef`s — `("Smith, Jones", "29")` and `("Creatures", "2")` — and that
`Unfriendly : none.` still yields an empty list.

**6. Pin the other punctuation classes.**
One test, `reads_names_containing_other_punctuation`, in `unit.rs`'s `mod tests`. A table of
(line, expected name, expected id), each parsed with `parse_unit(..., false, "1:7,53", None)` and
asserted to be `Some`:

| Line head | Expected name | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `- Advanced Carpentry Inc. (13762), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Advanced Carpentry Inc.` | full stop |
| `- -= [0] =- (7323), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `-= [0] =-` | square brackets |
| `- Ranger (scout) (7323), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Ranger (scout)` | balanced parens |
| `- Smiley :) (100), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Smiley :)` | unmatched closing bracket |
| `- Note: Bob (100), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Note: Bob` | colon |
| `- Bob; Jones (100), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Bob; Jones` | semicolon |
| `- Bob's & Co (100), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Bob's & Co` | apostrophe, ampersand |
| `- Sea\tWolf (100), Wanderers (29), 1 leader [LEAD].` | `Sea\tWolf` | tab inside the name |

The colon row is the one worth a comment: `split_sections` only cuts at `. Label:` for a label in
its closed `SECTION_LABELS` set, so a bare colon in a name is safe. `Note:` is not in that set and
there is no preceding `. `, so nothing splits.

**All eight rows are expected to pass without further production changes** once increments 1–3 are
in. If one does not, that is a genuine finding: fix it if the fix is inside `split_leading_id`, and
if it is not, stop and file it rather than growing this bead.

## The test plan

Rust unit tests only. No browser suite is involved — nothing here reaches the UI, no TypeScript type
is regenerated, and `ReportUnit` is unchanged.

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `reads_a_leading_identifier_past_commas_in_the_name` | `scan.rs` | the new scanner, including the `(scout)` non-digit skip |
| `walks_top_level_fields_one_at_a_time` | `scan.rs` | `next_top_level_field`, including the empty case |
| `keeps_a_unit_whose_name_contains_a_comma` | `unit.rs` | the reported defect |
| `keeps_a_faction_whose_name_contains_a_comma` | `unit.rs` | the same defect one field along |
| `reads_a_roster_line_whose_name_contains_a_comma` | `battle.rs` | roster name, faction, and `body_start` |
| `reads_an_attitude_entry_whose_faction_name_contains_a_comma` | `header.rs` | the attitudes list |
| `reads_names_containing_other_punctuation` | `unit.rs` | the eight classes above |

Existing suites that must stay green and are the real regression net, because they run the parser
over the whole committed corpus:

- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test parse_real_reports`
- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test corpus_errors`
- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test unwrap_real_report`
- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test unit_composition`
- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test merge_reports`

No new `.rep` fixture. `crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs` has an
`every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` guard (ah-v2l), so adding a file there is a two-place edit —
and nothing in this bead needs a whole report when an inline line does the job.

## User-facing decisions

The parser fix itself has no visible choice: the unit stops disappearing, which is the only correct
outcome. Two scope questions were put to the navigator on 2026-08-22 and both were answered.

**Q1 — Should this P0 also surface lines the parser could not read?** Today a dropped line leaves no
trace, and `ParsedReport` has no error channel at all.
Options offered: *separate bead* (recommended), *in this bead, minimal* (a count only), *in this
bead, full* (count plus the raw text of each line), *leave it silent*.
**Chosen: "in this bead, full".** Because that plus five parser sites is more than one increment-sized
bead, the work was split — this bead is the parser, and **`ah-w544.2` carries the surface**, blocked
on this one and at P0 with it. `ah-w544` is now an epic over the two. The navigator's choice is
recorded on `ah-w544.2` and is not re-opened there: the surface shows the count **and** the raw text
of each unreadable line, viewable. **Nothing about that surface is in this bead** — do not add a
field to `ParsedReport` here.

**Q2 — How wide should the fix go?** Options offered: *all sites in one bead* (recommended), *unit
lines only*, *split into an epic per module*.
**Chosen: all sites in one bead.** Hence increments 2–5 covering `unit.rs`, `battle.rs` and
`header.rs` together, on one shared helper. "Unit lines only" was rejected by the navigator because
it ships the same defect twice; the per-module epic was rejected as three implementers touching one
helper.

The two rejections that matter to an implementer meeting the same fork: **do not narrow this to
`unit.rs`**, and **do not split it further** — both were considered and declined.

No strings, labels or messages are added or changed by this bead.

## Out of scope

- **Any user-visible surface for unreadable lines.** That is `ah-w544.2`, which is blocked on this
  bead. `ParsedReport` gains no field here.
- **A name containing an unmatched *opening* bracket** — `Smiley :( (100), Wanderers (29)`. The
  depth counter never returns to zero, nothing splits, and `split_trailing_id` takes the *last*
  parenthesised number, so the unit is read with its faction's id. That is a silent mis-parse rather
  than a drop, it needs a different mechanism (a re-scan treating the unmatched `(` as a literal),
  and it has its own bead: **`ah-lt0o`**. The unmatched *closing* case is fine and is pinned in
  increment 6.
- **`header.rs:168` (`parse_faction`) and `battle.rs:366/399/407`.** Verified correct — see the
  table in *Context*. Leave them alone.
- **A faction literally named with a square bracket** (`The [Redacted] (29)`). Deliberately not
  recognised; see the bound in *Files to change*.
- **`split_trailing_id` itself.** It stays, unchanged, with its existing tests.
- **Any change to `.rep` fixtures or to `crates/fixtures`.**

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm run check:fast          # before opening the PR, as the repository requires
```

`cargo clippy` is what catches the deleted `top_level_fields_with_ends` if increment 4 leaves it
behind, so do not skip it locally.

Nothing here needs a human to look at anything: the defect and the fix are both entirely inside the
parser, and every claim in this plan is checkable by running the tests above. Verification of the
epic's user-visible half belongs to `ah-w544.2`.

## Known traps

- **`split_top_level` uses `depth <= 0`, not `depth == 0`, and that is deliberate** — it is what
  makes an unmatched *closing* bracket in a name harmless. Mirror it in `split_leading_id`. Writing
  `== 0` will pass every new test in this bead and break `Smiley :)`, which increment 6 pins.
- **`split_sections` runs before any of this**, and it cuts the line at `. <Label>:` for a label in
  a closed set. So the `head` you are scanning never contains `Weight:`, `Skills:` and friends. Do
  not add colon handling to `split_leading_id`; `unit.rs:41` explains why the set is closed.
- **`battle.rs`'s `body` is a slice of the original line**, so `body_start` arithmetic is
  load-bearing and silently wrong rather than loud. `trimmed.len() - rest.len()` is only correct
  while `rest` is a subslice *of `trimmed`* — never of an intermediate `String`. Both new scan
  functions return borrowed slices precisely so this holds; do not "simplify" them to return
  `String`.
- **The corpus tests are the net, not the unit tests.** `parse_real_reports` and `corpus_errors`
  read every committed report; a regression in the field walk shows up there as a changed count, and
  `corpus_errors` compares against a committed generated table
  (`docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md`). If that table needs regenerating, something in
  this bead changed parsing of real reports — **stop and work out why**, rather than running
  `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1`. This bead should change no real report's parse at all.
- **`crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs` names every `.rep` on disk** and
  `every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` fails when the two disagree (ah-v2l). Not triggered here,
  because no fixture is added — mentioned so nobody adds one casually.
- The project traps file (`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`) is about the web and native suites; none of
  its five entries touch this bead, which is Rust-only.

title: A unit whose name contains a comma vanishes from the report entirely
description:
The navigator's words, 2026-08-22:

  "it seems names with a comma in them are not displayed. This needs fixing and
  we need to ensure other non-letter characters are ok."

## The unit is not mis-parsed -- it is dropped

Traced in crates/core/src/report/unit.rs. parse_unit() does this, in order:

  let (head, sections) = split_sections(without_marker);
  let mut fields = split_top_level(&head, ',');        // unit.rs:125
  ...
  let (name, unit_id) = split_trailing_id(&fields.remove(0))?;   // unit.rs:130

and split_trailing_id (scan.rs:46) requires its input to end in "(digits)":

  let open = trimmed.rfind('(')?;
  if !trimmed.ends_with(')') { return None; }

So for a unit named "Smith, Jones":

  * Smith, Jones (100), Wanderers (29), behind, 10 humans [HUMN].

  fields      = ["Smith", "Jones (100)", "Wanderers (29)", ...]
  fields[0]   = "Smith"
  split_trailing_id("Smith")  -> rfind('(') is None -> None
  parse_unit  -> None, via the ? on line 130

The unit does not appear with a wrong name. It does not appear at all, and
nothing reports that it was skipped. That makes this silent data loss on a
turn report, not a display defect -- a player looking at a hex simply does not
see one of their units, with no indication anything was lost.

The same call is used for faction names at unit.rs:163, so a FACTION whose name
contains a comma is likely to take its units down with it. Worth checking.

## Why the existing hardening does not cover this

The parser has been hardened against punctuation before and those defences hold;
this is a different hole, not a regression.

  - Full stops survive because sections are found from a closed SECTION_LABELS
    set rather than by sentence splitting. unit.rs:41 says so directly: "a real
    report contains `- Advanced Carpentry Inc. (13762), ...`, whose full stop is
    not a sentence end at all."
  - There is a passing test does_not_split_a_name_that_contains_punctuation()
    (unit.rs:293) pinning the name "-= 0 =-".

Neither touches the comma, because the comma is the field separator itself.

## The second half of the request

"Ensure other non-letter characters are ok" is the more valuable half, since the
comma is one instance of a class. Characters that look dangerous by inspection,
each deserving a fixture:

  ( ) [ ]   split_top_level tracks bracket depth (scan.rs), so an unbalanced
            bracket in a name would desynchronise the depth counter and could
            swallow or split the rest of the line
  :         section labels are matched by name and a colon; a name containing
            "Skills:" or similar could be read as a section boundary
  ;         used as a comment separator in orders
  .         already covered, but should be pinned for names that end in one
  tab       a fixture in this repo was found on 2026-08-21 with a tab inside a
            ship's name, which is worth knowing is possible in the wild

## For the planner

The fix direction inverts the current order: find the trailing "(digits)" first
and treat everything before it as the name, rather than splitting on commas and
hoping the first field is the whole name. That is a suggestion, not a decision.

Argued at P4 as everything is, but this one is worth a look when ranking: it
loses a unit from the player's own report with no error, and the player has no
way to know it happened.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-w544.2, delivered in PR #563

title: A movement into unexplored country is drawn wrong at the map's wrap seam
description:
The navigator's words, 2026-08-22:

  "whsn starting a new game, you should define width and height as well as if it
  wraps on x and y. Redfault should be 72x96, wrapping on only x."

Read as: default 72 x 96, wrapping on x only. ("Redfault" is a typo for
"Default".)

## This is not only a setup form -- it removes a guess from the movement planner

crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs already names the missing fact as a known
limitation:

  "Atlantis maps wrap east to west, the rules page never says where the seam is,
  and a computed neighbour would be wrong exactly at the edge - where being
  wrong matters most. The report simply names the hex on the other side."

The module works around it by taking adjacency from the coordinates the report
states rather than from arithmetic. That works wherever the player has been --
but geometric_neighbour() is kept as a deliberate exception for unexplored
country, and its own doc comment concedes:

  "drawing the intent roughly right everywhere except across the wrap seam beats
  drawing nothing."

So today, a movement drawn into unexplored country is knowingly wrong at the
seam, because nothing in the app knows the map's width. Telling it would let
that arithmetic be right instead of approximately right.

Nothing anywhere models map width, height, or wrapping: no map_width, no
mapHeight, no wrap flag. The east-west assumption is baked into prose comments,
not into data.

## Where it goes

A game is created through createGame() in packages/shared/src/gameActions.ts,
which builds its manifest with newGameManifest(gameName, rulesetId, now,
gameId) in gameSession.ts:55. Dimensions and wrapping are per-game facts and
that manifest is where the game's other per-game facts already live.

There is also a "Per game" tab in Settings (settingsTabs.ts), which is the
natural place to correct them afterwards -- a player who guessed wrong at
creation, or who is importing an existing game mid-stream, should not have to
start over.

## For the planner

  - Are the defaults universal or per-ruleset? 72x96 wrapping on x is New Origin;
    the app is built to support other variants and the ruleset is already chosen
    on the same screen. Worth asking the navigator whether the default should
    follow the ruleset rather than being fixed.
  - What happens to games that already exist? They have no dimensions recorded,
    and a backup restored from before this change will not either. Whether they
    adopt the default silently, or prompt, is a user-facing decision.
  - Does wrapping on y mean anything for an Atlantis map? The navigator asks for
    the flag on both axes and defaults it off for y; whether the movement code
    should honour a y-wrap or refuse it is worth settling before it is built.
  - Should a stated exit from a report still win over computed arithmetic once
    the dimensions are known? graph.rs's rule is "prefer a stated exit wherever
    one exists", and that rule is probably still right even with exact
    dimensions, since the report is the map's own word.
design:
## Context

The navigator's words, 2026-08-22:

> *"when starting a new game, you should define width and height as well as if it wraps on x and y.
> Default should be 72x96, wrapping on only x."*

**This is not only a setup form — it removes a guess from the movement planner.**
`crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs` already names the gap:

> *"Atlantis maps wrap east to west, the rules page never says where the seam is, and a computed
> neighbour would be wrong exactly at the edge — where being wrong matters most. The report simply
> names the hex on the other side."*

The module works around it by taking adjacency from the coordinates the report **states**, which works
wherever the player has been. **`geometric_neighbour()` is the deliberate exception for unexplored
country**, and its own comment concedes: *"drawing the intent roughly right everywhere except across
the wrap seam beats drawing nothing."*

So a movement drawn into unexplored country is **knowingly wrong at the seam**, because nothing in the
app knows the map's width:

```
from (71,40) heading east  →  computed (72,40)   ✗ no such hex; the map wraps to (0,40)
                           with a known width    ✓ (0,40)
```

**Nothing models width, height or wrapping anywhere** — no `map_width`, no `mapHeight`, no wrap flag.
The east-west assumption lives in prose comments, not in data.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. 🔴 The default comes from the ruleset **declaration**, not the scraped contract

The navigator chose the ruleset as the source. **That must not be read as the scraped ruleset.**
`docs/ruleset-contract.md` is explicit about what the two scraped pages provide — movement points,
terrain costs, item weights, monster stats — and **the map's dimensions are on neither.** They are a
property of the *game server's world*, not of the rules.

So the field goes on **`packages/shared/src/rulesets.ts`'s hand-written `Ruleset` type**, beside
`ordersUploadUrl`, whose own doc comment makes exactly this argument:

> *"The upload address belongs to the game rather than to the build, and a game already records which
> ruleset it is played under — so this is where that id becomes an address."*

```ts
/** The map this ruleset's server usually serves, as a starting point a game may override. */
defaultMap: { width: number; height: number; wrapX: boolean; wrapY: boolean };
```

with `neworigins` carrying `{ width: 72, height: 96, wrapX: true, wrapY: false }`.

**And it resolves a weakness `ordersUploadUrl` still has.** That field's comment records the accepted
cost: *"two games on different servers sharing one ruleset would collide."* Map size would collide the
same way — **except that this value is only a default and the real one is stored per game**, so the
same shape of fact gets a better treatment here. Worth a sentence in the code saying so.

**Do not scrape it, and do not add it to `ruleset-contract.md`'s tables.**

### 2. 🔴 Per-game, optional — and absence *means* "assumed"

`newGameManifest` (`gameSession.ts:55-68`) builds the manifest with `manifestVersion: 1`. Add the
dimensions as **optional fields**:

- **present** → the player stated them;
- **absent** → nothing was recorded, so the ruleset default is assumed.

**That distinction is not bookkeeping — it is exactly what §3's answer needs**, and it comes free.
**No `manifestVersion` bump**: a bump implies a migration, and an optional field that older manifests
simply lack is the migration.

### 3. The create screen and the Per game tab

`createGame()` (`gameActions.ts`) gains the four values, prefilled from the chosen ruleset's
`defaultMap` and **refilled when the ruleset selection changes** — a stale 72×96 sitting under a
newly-chosen variant is worse than no prefill.

`settingsTabs.ts` already has a **`{ id: "game", label: "Per game" }`** tab; the same four values go
there so a player who guessed wrong, or imported an existing game, need not start over.

**In the Per game tab, assumed values must read as assumed** — the navigator's choice — not as facts.
Editing them writes them, which is what turns an assumption into a statement.

### 4. The graph stops guessing — but only where it was guessing

`geometric_neighbour()` learns the dimensions and wraps correctly.

**🔴 A stated exit still wins.** `graph.rs`'s rule is *"prefer a stated exit wherever one exists"*, and
that stays true with exact dimensions: **the report is the map's own word**, and a player-entered
width can be wrong while a reported neighbour cannot. Exact dimensions improve the **fallback**, not
the primary. If the diff changes which source wins, it has gone too far.

**`wrapY` is honoured symmetrically** — the navigator's choice, and the arithmetic is the same
operation on the other axis. A flag that records intent without acting on it is a control that does
nothing.

**Unknown dimensions must behave exactly as today.** A game with none, and a ruleset without a
`defaultMap`, fall back to today's unwrapped arithmetic rather than guessing a width.

## Increments

1. **The ruleset declares a default map.**
   RED: `rulesets.ts` tests — `neworigins` yields 72×96, wrap x only; a ruleset without the field
   yields nothing.
   GREEN: the type and the entry.
2. **A new game records what it was told.**
   RED: `gameSession` tests — a manifest carries the four values; one built without them **omits the
   fields** rather than writing defaults into them.
   GREEN: `newGameManifest`.
3. **The forms ask, and the tab corrects.**
   RED: the create screen prefills from the ruleset and **refills when the ruleset changes**; the Per
   game tab shows assumed values **as assumed** and writes them when edited.
   GREEN: `gameActions.ts`, `settingsTabs.ts`.
4. **The seam is right.**
   RED: `graph.rs` — a computed neighbour east of the last column lands on column 0 with a known
   width; **the same case with unknown dimensions behaves exactly as today**.
   GREEN: `geometric_neighbour`.
5. **`wrapY` works and a stated exit still wins.**
   RED: north of the last row wraps when `wrapY`; and **a stated exit beats a computed one even where
   the arithmetic disagrees.**
   GREEN: nothing new — increment 4 should already satisfy the second, and **if it does not, the
   precedence was changed.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `neworigins` defaults to 72×96 wrap-x | `rulesets` tests | §1 |
| a manifest built without dimensions **omits them** | `gameSession` tests | §2 — absence means assumed |
| a manifest built with them records them | same | §2 |
| **changing the ruleset refills the prefill** | create-screen tests | §3 |
| the Per game tab shows assumed values as assumed | settings tests | §3 |
| **east of the last column wraps to column 0** | `graph.rs` | the bead |
| **unknown dimensions behave exactly as today** | same | no regression for old games |
| `wrapY` wraps north–south when set | same | §4 |
| **a stated exit still beats a computed one** | same | 🔴 precedence unchanged |
| existing movement tests | same | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast` (which runs `cargo fmt`/`clippy` and the Rust unit tests) plus the
smoke suite for the two forms.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-22 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-0w7w-map-size.html`, committed
to `docs/ui/`.

**Q1 — where the default comes from.** Chosen: **from the chosen ruleset.** It is picked on the same
screen, so the right default is knowable rather than assumed, and a second variant later gets its own
correct default. Accepted cost: the ruleset declaration gains a field, and one without it needs a
fallback anyway. Rejected: **fixed 72×96**, which is New Origins' map given silently to every variant.

**Q2 — games that already exist.** Chosen: **adopt the default, and show it in Settings as assumed.**
No interruption to a game you only wanted to look at, and there is somewhere to find out. Accepted
cost: only found by someone who goes looking. Rejected: **asking once on next open** (an interruption
every first open after upgrading) and **adopting silently with no indication** (a wrong default whose
only symptom is a movement line drawn wrong at the seam — which nobody would connect back to this).

**Q3 — north–south wrap.** Chosen: **offer it and honour it.** The arithmetic is symmetric so it is
barely more work, and it costs nothing if nobody turns it on. Rejected: **offering without honouring**
(a control that does nothing) and **not offering it** (no way to say so if a variant does wrap).

**Not asked** (architecture): the field living on the hand-written `Ruleset` declaration rather than
the scraped contract; optional manifest fields with **absence meaning assumed** and no version bump;
and a stated exit continuing to beat computed arithmetic.

## Out of scope

- **Scraping dimensions**, or adding them to `docs/ruleset-contract.md`'s tables. They are on neither
  page.
- **Changing which source wins** in `graph.rs`.
- **A second ruleset.** Adding one is *"a scrape and a line here"*, and not this bead.
- **Anything else in the manifest**, and any `manifestVersion` change.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm exec playwright test --project=web
```

Then by hand:

1. Create a new game: the map fields are prefilled **72 × 96, east–west only**. **Change the
   ruleset** and confirm the prefill refills rather than keeping a stale value. (With one ruleset
   shipped, this may need a temporary second entry to exercise — say so in the PR if it was not
   testable by hand.)
2. Create the game and confirm Settings ▸ Per game shows the values **as stated**, not assumed.
3. **Open a game created before this change**: Settings ▸ Per game shows 72 × 96 marked **assumed**.
   Edit one value and confirm it becomes stated.
4. **The seam.** Plan a movement heading east from the last column into unexplored country and
   confirm it lands on column 0 rather than off the map. **This is the acceptance**, and it is what
   the bead is actually for.
5. Turn on north–south wrap and confirm the same at the top and bottom rows.
6. **Confirm a stated exit still wins**: find a hex whose report names a neighbour that the arithmetic
   would compute differently, and confirm the report's answer is used.
7. Confirm a game with no dimensions and a ruleset with no `defaultMap` behaves **exactly as it does
   today** — no wrapping, no guessing.

## Known traps

- **🔴 The default is a declaration, not scraped data.** `docs/ruleset-contract.md` covers the rules
  and data pages, and the map's dimensions are on neither. Putting this in the scraped contract sends
  someone looking for a field that does not exist on any server.
- **🔴 Absence in the manifest means "assumed".** Writing the defaults into every new manifest destroys
  the distinction the Per game tab needs, and it cannot be recovered afterwards.
- **🔴 A stated exit must still win.** Exact dimensions improve the fallback for unexplored country;
  they do not make arithmetic a better authority than the report. If the diff changes precedence, it
  has overreached.
- **Refill the prefill when the ruleset changes.** A stale 72×96 under a newly-chosen variant is worse
  than no prefill, because it looks deliberate.
- **Unknown dimensions must behave as today**, so every existing game and every pre-change backup keeps
  working unchanged.
- **No `manifestVersion` bump.** Optional fields are the migration; a bump implies one that has to be
  written.
- **`wrapY` is honoured, not merely recorded.** The navigator chose that explicitly.
- **`ordersUploadUrl`'s known weakness is worth reading first** — the same shape of fact, with the
  collision this bead's per-game storage avoids.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new game is asked for map width, height, wrap-x and wrap-y, prefilled from the CHOSEN RULESET's declared default (neworigins: 72x96, wrap x only), and the prefill REFILLS when the ruleset selection changes.
- The default lives on the hand-written `Ruleset` type in packages/shared/src/rulesets.ts, beside ordersUploadUrl - NOT in the scraped ruleset and NOT in docs/ruleset-contract.md. Map dimensions appear on neither the rules page nor the data page.

- A STATED EXIT STILL BEATS COMPUTED ARITHMETIC. graph.rs's "prefer a stated exit wherever one exists" is unchanged - the report is the map's own word, and a player-entered width can be wrong where a reported neighbour cannot. Exact dimensions improve the FALLBACK for unexplored country, not the primary. If the diff changes precedence it has overreached.
- Unknown dimensions - an old game, or a ruleset with no defaultMap - behave EXACTLY as today: no wrapping, no guessing.
- Existing movement tests are unchanged.
- `pnpm run check:fast` and the smoke suite pass.

title: The game data dialog reaches the screen edge, and the keyboard cannot scroll its list
description:
Two problems with the reference dialog from ah-5jkt.1, both reported by the
navigator 2026-08-21.

1. THE DIALOG EXTENDS TOO FAR DOWN. It should stop with a margin below rather
   than running to the bottom edge of the screen.

2. KEYBOARD NAVIGATION DOES NOT SCROLL THE LIST. Moving down the left-hand list
   with the keyboard stops working when the selection reaches the bottom of the
   visible area -- the list should scroll to keep the selection in view.

The second is the same failure shape as ah-yk6b, which shipped in this same
release: a list that has more in it than the player can see, with nothing on
screen to say so. There the fix was to show every match and let it scroll; here
the list scrolls but the keyboard cannot drive it past the fold.

FOR THE PLANNER. These are two symptoms in one dialog and could reasonably be
one increment or two. Filed together because they were reported together and a
player meets them in the same place; split if the work does not fit one pass.
design:
## Context

Two problems with the reference dialog from ah-5jkt.1, both reported by the navigator on
2026-08-21, both in `packages/shared/src/workspace/GameDataDialog.tsx`.

**1. The dialog runs to the bottom edge.** It is arithmetic, and it is on one line each:

```
:109   pt-[10vh]        the dialog starts 10vh down
:116   max-h-[85vh]     and may be 85vh tall
```

**10 + 85 = 95vh, leaving a 5vh margin at the bottom against 10vh at the top.** The navigator asked
that it *"stop with a margin below rather than running to the bottom edge of the screen."*

**2. The keyboard cannot drive the list past the fold.** The list has `overflow-y-auto` (`:195`) and
the selection moves correctly — `moveWithin` (`:76-90`) already calls **`paletteKeyReduce` with
`pageSize: PALETTE_PAGE_ROWS`**, so ah-yk6b's clamping and paging are in place here. What is missing
is the other half of ah-yk6b: **nothing calls `scrollIntoView`**, so the selection moves out of sight
and the list stays where it is.

That is the same failure shape as ah-yk6b, and not a coincidence: ah-yk6b's reducer was reused here
while its scrolling was not — and its scrolling was the half that **could not be unit-tested** (no
jsdom in this repository) and therefore lives only in a smoke test nobody carried across.

**One bead, two increments.** They are independent one-line-ish fixes in one file, reported together
and met by a player in the same place. No split needed.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. The dialog stops short of the bottom — `GameDataDialog.tsx:116`

```
max-h-[85vh]  →  max-h-[80vh]
```

**`80` because the dialog opens at `pt-[10vh]`**: 10 + 80 = 90, leaving **10vh below to match the
10vh above**. The margin is then symmetric, which is a rule a later reader can check rather than a
number someone liked. Say so in a comment beside it, because the two values are on different lines
and nothing currently connects them:

```tsx
        // 10vh below, matching the `pt-[10vh]` above (ah-vwdi). The two must be changed together:
        // top offset + max height must leave a real margin, or the dialog runs to the screen edge.
        className="grid max-h-[80vh] w-[56rem] …"
```

**Do not change `pt-[10vh]`.** Moving the dialog up would also work and is not what was asked; the
complaint is the bottom edge.

### 2. The selection scrolls into view — mirror `CommandPalette.tsx:33-46`

ah-yk6b already solved this next door, and its comment explains the choices. The mechanism:

```tsx
  const list = useRef<HTMLUListElement | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const rows = list.current?.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^="game-data-entry-"]');
    // …find the selected row and scroll it into view with { block: "nearest" }
  }, [state.selectedId]);
```

with `ref={list}` on the `<ul>` (`:191`).

**`block: "nearest"` matters**, for the same reason it does in the palette: it scrolls only when the
row is actually off screen, so stepping between visible rows does not jog the list.

**This dialog does NOT need the palette's `byKeyboard` guard, and that is worth saying rather than
copying it silently.** The palette needs it because selection follows the pointer on
`onPointerEnter`, so scrolling would move the row out from under the cursor and fire another
`pointerenter` — a list that will not stand still. **Here selection changes only on an explicit
click, on a keyboard move, or on following a cross-reference**, and none of those loops:

- a **click** on a row that is already visible makes `"nearest"` a no-op;
- **following a cross-reference** (`follow`) selects an entry that may well be off screen, and
  scrolling to it is exactly what a reader wants.

So keying the effect on `state.selectedId` alone is both simpler and better here. **Copying the guard
across would suppress the follow case**, which is a real improvement, for a hazard this dialog does
not have.

### 3. Nothing else

The tabs, the filter, `Left`/`Right`, the detail pane, `goBack` and the entry list are untouched.

## Increments

1. **The dialog leaves a margin.**
   RED: `GameDataDialog.test.tsx` — assert the rendered markup carries `max-h-[80vh]`. It is a
   string assertion and a weak test, and it is the only one available without a browser; the real
   check is step 1 of *Validation*.
   GREEN: the class and its comment.
2. **The keyboard reaches the whole list.**
   RED: **a smoke test** — open the dialog on a category with more entries than fit (`skills` or
   `items`), hold `ArrowDown` past the fold, and assert the selected row is in the viewport.
   GREEN: the ref and the effect.
   **This cannot be a vitest test.** There is no jsdom in this repository — the unit suites assert
   `renderToStaticMarkup` output only — so anything that measures scrolling belongs in Playwright.
   Do not add a DOM environment for it.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **the dialog's max height leaves a margin** | `GameDataDialog.test.tsx` | half one, weakly |
| **arrowing past the fold keeps the selection visible** | `tests/smoke/` | half two — the real check |
| `PageDown` reaches far down the list and stays visible | smoke | the paging path already wired |
| **following a cross-reference scrolls to the new entry** | smoke | the case the palette's guard would have broken |
| clicking a visible row does not jump the list | smoke | that `"nearest"` is doing its job |
| the existing dialog tests | `GameDataDialog.test.tsx` | **unchanged** — tabs, filter, Left/Right, goBack |

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`, plus the smoke suite, which is where increment 2 actually lives.

## User-facing decisions

**None to ask for, and no mockup.** The navigator reported both symptoms and stated the wanted
outcome in each case — *"stop with a margin below"* and *"the list should scroll to keep the
selection in view"*. There is no choice between alternatives here, only arithmetic and a mechanism
that already exists next door.

**Decided here** (architecture): `80vh`, chosen so the bottom margin equals the existing `pt-[10vh]`
rather than picked by eye — if the navigator wants the dialog taller or shorter than symmetric, that
is a one-token change and they can say so; and omitting the palette's `byKeyboard` guard, with the
reasoning above.

## Out of scope

- **Sharing the scroll-into-view mechanism between the palette and this dialog.** It is the same
  eight lines in two places now, which is a fair refactoring bead for Forge to spot on its own
  evidence — but extracting a hook while fixing a reported bug widens the diff and the blast radius
  for no gain the navigator asked for. **Note it in the PR description** so the second sighting is on
  record.
- **The detail pane's own scrolling** (`:221`), which was not reported and works by pointer.
- **The dialog's width**, its tabs, its filter, and `goBack`.
- **Any entry point to the dialog** — that is **ah-u44o**.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm exec playwright test --project=web
```

Then by hand, which is the whole point for both halves:

1. Open the game data dialog and look at the **bottom edge**. There must be a clear margin, and it
   should look about the same as the gap above the dialog. **Shrink the window vertically** and check
   it still holds — a fixed pixel height would fail here and a `vh` pair will not.
2. Pick a category with a long list (**skills** or **items**), put focus in the filter, and hold
   **ArrowDown**. The selection must keep moving **and the list must scroll with it**, all the way to
   the last entry. **This is the acceptance.**
3. **ArrowUp** back to the top, and confirm the list scrolls back.
4. **PageDown** and **PageUp**: the selection jumps a screenful and remains visible.
5. **Click** a row that is already on screen and confirm the list **does not jump** — `"nearest"`
   should do nothing there.
6. **Follow a cross-reference** in the detail pane to an entry far down the list, and confirm the
   left-hand list **scrolls to show it**. This is the behaviour the palette's hover guard would have
   suppressed, so check it deliberately.
7. Type in the filter to narrow the list, then arrow down again: still visible, still scrolling.

## Known traps

- **`pt-[10vh]` and `max-h-[…]` are a pair on different lines.** Changing one without the other is
  how the dialog ends up at the screen edge again; the comment exists to stop that.
- **Do not copy the palette's `byKeyboard` guard.** This dialog has no hover-selection, and the guard
  would suppress scrolling when a cross-reference is followed — which is a case that genuinely wants
  it.
- **`block: "nearest"`, not `"center"`.** Centring scrolls on every keypress even when the row is
  already comfortably in view.
- **There is no jsdom here.** The scrolling half cannot be unit-tested; it is a Playwright test.
  Adding a DOM environment to prove it is a far larger change than this bead.
- **`moveWithin` already works.** The selection was moving correctly all along — only the view was
  not following. Do not "fix" the reducer; ah-yk6b's clamping and paging are already wired here via
  `paletteKeyReduce` and `PALETTE_PAGE_ROWS`.
- **Do not extract a shared hook.** Same mechanism in two places is now a recorded second sighting,
  not this bead's job.

## Amendment, 2026-08-21 — the margin half failed verification

Psylocke's verification (origin/main `13ee4d2`, fix commit `793bd64`): **the keyboard half passed on
every case** — arrowing, paging, click-does-not-jump, and follow-a-cross-reference all confirmed.
**Only the margin half failed.** The navigator: *"There is no margin visible at all. All the key and
the navigation seems to work though."*

**Do not re-do the scrolling work.**

### What I ruled out by reading, so nobody hunts it twice

Psylocke's second hypothesis was that `fixed inset-0` might be resolving against a containing block
rather than the viewport — any ancestor with `transform`, `filter`, `backdrop-filter`, `perspective`,
`contain` or `will-change` does that. **Checked, and it is not the cause:**

- the dialog mounts inside `keyboardPanels` (`AppShell.tsx:2786-2800`), rendered at `:2816` and
  `:3347`;
- the outer wrapper of the main screen is `<div className="flex h-full flex-col bg-ground text-ink">`
  (`:2822`) — no transform, no filter;
- `theme.css:379-385` sets `html, body, #root { height: 100%; margin: 0; overflow: hidden }`, with no
  transform or filter anywhere above the dialog.

So `fixed inset-0` **is** the viewport, `10vh + 80vh` really should leave `10vh`, and the cause is
somewhere else. That leaves Psylocke's other two: whether `max-h-[80vh]` is winning in the cascade,
and whether the browser's `vh` matches the window the page actually gets. **Both want an element
inspector**, which is why this is an implementer's next step and not a re-plan.

### A proven alternative in this codebase, if capping the box cannot be made to work

**`CommandPalette` solves the same problem the other way round, and it shipped and verified.** It caps
**the scrolling list**, not the dialog box:

```
CommandPalette.tsx:84    fixed inset-0 … pt-[15vh]        the backdrop
CommandPalette.tsx:137   max-h-[70vh] … overflow-y-auto   on the <ul>, not on the dialog
```

The dialog's own height is then whatever its input plus its capped list comes to, and the margin
falls out of the arithmetic instead of being imposed on the box.

`GameDataDialog` caps the box (`max-h-[80vh]` at `:135`) while its scrolling rows carry only
`min-h-0 overflow-y-auto`. **If the box cap cannot be made to hold, cap the rows the way the palette
caps its list** — same idea, same file conventions, and a pattern this repository has already
verified in front of the navigator.

### Unchanged from Psylocke, and still binding

**Do not change the two values independently.** The comment at `:133` records that the top offset and
the max height must move together, and the symmetry (10 + 80 + 10) is the thing being verified — *a
taller dialog that still touches the edge would pass a naive re-test while failing the bead.*
acceptance_criteria:
- The dialog stops short of the bottom of the screen with a clear margin, and still does so when the window is shrunk vertically. max-h-[85vh] becomes max-h-[80vh], giving 10vh below to match the existing pt-[10vh] above, with a comment tying the two values together.
- Holding ArrowDown in a long category (skills, items) moves the selection all the way to the last entry AND scrolls the list to keep it in view. ArrowUp scrolls back.
- PageDown and PageUp jump a screenful and leave the selection visible.
- Following a cross-reference from the detail pane scrolls the left-hand list to the newly selected entry.
- Clicking a row that is already visible does NOT jump the list - scrollIntoView uses block: "nearest".
- The palette's `byKeyboard` guard is deliberately NOT copied: this dialog has no hover-selection, and the guard would suppress the follow-a-cross-reference case.
- moveWithin and paletteKeyReduce are unchanged - the selection already moved correctly; only the view did not follow.
- The scrolling half is proved by a Playwright smoke test, not a unit test: there is no jsdom in this repository and none is added.
- Tabs, filter, Left/Right, the detail pane and goBack are unchanged.
- No shared hook is extracted between CommandPalette and this dialog; the second sighting is noted in the PR description instead.
- `pnpm run check:fast` and the smoke suite pass.
notes:
Verification failed (2026-08-21, at origin/main 13ee4d2; fix commit 793bd64).

The navigator's words: "There is no margin visible at all. All the key and the navigation seems to work though."

So the bead is HALF delivered. The keyboard half passed on every case: holding ArrowDown keeps the selection moving and scrolls the list, ArrowUp scrolls back, PageDown/PageUp keep the selection visible, clicking an on-screen row does not jump, and following a cross-reference scrolls the list to the target. Only the margin half failed. Whoever picks this up should not re-do the scrolling work.

WHAT THE CODE LOOKS LIKE, AND WHY THE FAILURE IS PUZZLING

The arithmetic in GameDataDialog.tsx reads correct:

  line 126 backdrop: fixed inset-0 z-40 flex items-start justify-center bg-black/50 pt-[10vh]
  line 135 dialog:   grid max-h-[80vh] w-[56rem] max-w-[94vw] grid-rows-[auto_auto_1fr] ...

10vh of padding above plus a dialog capped at 80vh is 90vh, which should leave 10vh below. The comment at line 133 states that intent explicitly.

The usual grid trap is also already handled - every scrolling row carries both min-h-0 and overflow-y-auto (lines 180, 181, 215, 241) - so content overflowing past a correctly-sized box is NOT the explanation.

max-h-[80vh] is used by two other dialogs in packages/shared/src/workspace, so the arbitrary value is generated by Tailwind and is not a missing-class problem.

That leaves the cause genuinely unknown from reading alone, which is why this needs looking at in a browser with the element inspector rather than reasoned about. Lines worth checking first:

- whether max-h-[80vh] is winning: something later in the cascade, or a conflicting height/min-height on the same element, would silently defeat it;
- whether the backdrop is really 100vh: 'fixed inset-0' resolves against the viewport unless an ancestor establishes a containing block (any transform, filter, perspective, contain or will-change on a parent does exactly that), in which case both the 10vh and the 80vh resolve against something smaller and the margin shrinks or vanishes;
- whether the browser's vh includes chrome the window does not actually give the page.

A screenshot from the navigator is being attached to this thread; ask them for it if it is not here.

DO NOT change the two values independently. The comment at line 133 records that the top offset and the max height must be changed together, and the chosen symmetry (10 + 80 + 10) is the thing being verified - a taller dialog that still touches the edge would pass a naive re-test while failing the bead.

title: No map theme has ever drawn a lair, because the report qualifies every structure kind
description:
Every map theme draws its structure marks through `classify()` in `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts`, which matches a structure's `kind` **exactly** against sets of bare words - `LAIR_KINDS` is `lair, cave, ruin, ruins, barrow, crypt, tomb, pit`, `SHAFT_KINDS` is `shaft`. A real report does not send a bare word.

`parse_structure` (`crates/core/src/report/region.rs:139-170`) only splits a description out of `kind` when the raw line carries a **semicolon**. A lair's line never does, so the whole clause after the colon lands in `kind` verbatim:

```
+ Lair [1] : Lair, closed to player units.
+ Ruin [1] : Ruin, closed to player units.
```

`kind` is therefore `Lair, closed to player units`, which matches nothing, and the structure falls through to `building`. **No theme has ever drawn a lair mark.** The tests that should have caught it were written from synthetic bare words (`"Lair"`), which is the coverage gap that let it ship.

# The fix

Take the first comma-separated segment of `kind`, trimmed and lowercased, before the sets are consulted. `Lair, closed to player units` resolves to `lair`, the word the sets already check for.

**One trap, and it is the whole reason this bead spells the fix out.** `isShip()` must keep reading the **raw** kind as well as the cleaned one:

```ts
if (isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)) {
  return "ship";
}
```

`isShip` scans the whole string for `ship`/`boat` on purpose, to catch tails. A real fixture line depends on it:

```
+ Red Squadron [1027] : Fleet, 6 Airships.
```

That draws as a ship today only because `Airships` contains `ship`. Clean the kind down to `fleet` - which is in neither `SHIP_KINDS` nor the substring test - and a fleet that currently draws correctly becomes a building. Cleaning the kind for the *set lookups* while leaving `isShip` its raw string is what avoids trading one bug for another.

# What this is worth, measured

Run over all 66 distinct structure kinds in `tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep` (verified 2026-08-21), the fix with the `isShip` guard above changes **seven** structures and regresses **none**:

| Kind, as the report sends it | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Lair, closed to player units` | building | **lair** |
| `Ruin, closed to player units` | building | **lair** |
| `Crypt, closed to player units` | building | **lair** |
| `Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons` | building | **ship** |
| `Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons, 8 Corsairs` | building | **ship** |
| `Galley, 4 Galleons, 4 Galleys` | building | **ship** |
| `Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons` | building | **ship** |

Without the `isShip` guard, `Fleet, 6 Airships` goes ship -> building, and that is the only difference between the two versions.

# Where this came from

**PR #487** (`fix: shafts, lairs and roads not displayed`, head `63ac169`) implements the comma split and is worth reading - it found the bug. It is from a fork, so fetch it as:

```
git fetch origin refs/pull/487/head
git log FETCH_HEAD          # or: gh pr checkout 487
```

Cypher reviewed it with the navigator on 2026-08-21 and asked for the `isShip` guard; the review comment on the PR carries the same evidence as this bead. If the author supplies it, the PR merges and this bead closes with it. If not, this bead is how the fix lands, and the implementer should credit the PR in the commit message.

**Do not copy two things across from that PR:**

- Its **road** change. `parse_structure` already strips the trailing `.` and splits off `", needs N"` (`region.rs:157-161`), which is the only comma form a road takes - every road kind in every fixture is a bare `Road NW`. Routing the road path through the cleaner is harmless but fixes nothing, and its test string `"road n, a well-worn track"` is not something any report sends. Leave the road path as it is.
- Its **shaft** claim. No fixture contains a `Shaft` structure at all; the only line carrying the word is `+ Central Mine Shaft [10] : Mine`, whose kind is `Mine`. Nothing in this bead makes a shaft draw, and its description should not say it does.

# Testing

Take every case from `tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep`, not from invented strings - synthetic bare words are exactly what hid this. At minimum: a lair, a ruin and a crypt in the report's own `X, closed to player units` form; a `Galley, ...` fleet; and `Fleet, 6 Airships` as a regression test for the `isShip` guard.

# Not in scope

- The seven qualified kinds that still classify as buildings (`Ice Cave`, `Demon Pit`, `Whirlpool` and the rest) and the question of whether a `Gateway` earns the shaft mark - that is **ah-lcyn**, which assumes this bead is done.
- Any change to the Rust parser. The clause belongs in `kind` as far as this bead is concerned; the map code is what adapts.
design:
## Context

**P0, and it blocks ah-lcyn**, which is already claimed and assumes this bead is done.

Every map theme draws its structure marks through `classify()`
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts:207-222`), which matches a structure's kind
**exactly** against sets of bare words — `LAIR_KINDS` is `lair, cave, ruin, ruins, barrow, crypt,
tomb, pit`. **A real report does not send a bare word.**

`parse_structure` (`crates/core/src/report/region.rs:152-161`, read on `origin/main`) splits a
description out of `kind` only on a **semicolon**, and splits off only `", needs N"`. A lair's line
carries neither, so the whole clause lands in `kind` verbatim:

```
+ Lair [1] : Lair, closed to player units.
```

`kind` is therefore `Lair, closed to player units`, which matches nothing, and the structure falls
through to `building`. **No theme has ever drawn a lair mark.** The tests that should have caught it
were written from synthetic bare words (`"Lair"`) — the coverage gap that let it ship.

**I re-ran the measurement myself** over all 100 distinct structure kinds in
`tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep`, simulating `classify()` before and after. Cypher's numbers hold
exactly: the fix **changes seven structures and regresses none**.

| Kind | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Lair, closed to player units` | building | **lair** |
| `Crypt, closed to player units` | building | **lair** |
| `Ruin, closed to player units` | building | **lair** |
| `Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons` | building | **ship** |
| `Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons, 8 Corsairs` | building | **ship** |
| `Galley, 4 Galleons, 4 Galleys` | building | **ship** |
| `Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons` | building | **ship** |

Branch from `origin/main`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The whole change is in `classify()` — `hexView.ts:207-222`

Take the **first comma-separated segment** of the kind, trimmed and lowercased, before the sets are
consulted. `Lair, closed to player units` resolves to `lair`, which the sets already check for.

```ts
function classify(structure: StructureInfo): StructureKind {
  // The report sends a qualified kind - `Lair, closed to player units`, `Galley, 2 Galleys` - and
  // `parse_structure` only splits a description off on a semicolon (`report/region.rs:152`), so the
  // whole clause arrives here. Everything below matches bare words, so the first segment is what
  // the sets need (ah-o0d3). Before this, no theme had ever drawn a lair mark.
  const kind = structure.kind.split(",")[0].trim().toLowerCase();
  if (roadDirection(structure.kind) !== null) {
    return "road";
  }
  // `isShip` reads the RAW kind as well as the cleaned one, deliberately: it scans the whole string
  // for "ship"/"boat" to catch tails, and `Fleet, 6 Airships` is a ship only because of `Airships`.
  // Cleaning that to `fleet` - in neither SHIP_KINDS nor the substring test - would turn a fleet
  // that draws correctly today into a building. See ah-3pr9 for the six fleets this still misses.
  if (isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)) {
    return "ship";
  }
  if (SHAFT_KINDS.has(kind)) {
    return "shaft";
  }
  if (LAIR_KINDS.has(kind)) {
    return "lair";
  }
  return "building";
}
```

**The `isShip` guard is the crux of the bead**, and I verified it in isolation: `Fleet, 6 Airships`
is **the only kind in the fixtures whose classification depends on it.** With the guard it is a
`ship`; without it, a `building` — the one regression the fix could introduce, and the only
difference between the two versions.

**`roadDirection` keeps reading the raw kind.** `parse_structure` already strips the trailing `.` and
splits off `", needs N"` (`region.rs:157-161`), which is the only comma form a road takes — every
road kind in every fixture is a bare `Road NW`. Nothing to fix, so nothing changes.

### Do not copy two things from PR #487

The PR (`fix: shafts, lairs and roads not displayed`, head `63ac169`, **still open**) found this bug
and is worth reading — `git fetch origin refs/pull/487/head`, or `gh pr checkout 487`.

- **Its road change.** Harmless but fixes nothing, and its test string
  `"road n, a well-worn track"` is not something any report sends.
- **Its shaft claim.** No *committed* fixture contains a `Shaft`, so nothing here makes a shaft draw
  and the description must not say it does. (A real report does send one —
  `Shaft, contains an inner location` — and **ah-lcyn** adds it as a fixture. Out of scope here.)

**If the PR's author supplies the `isShip` guard, this bead closes with the PR** rather than being
built separately — check before starting. If not, this bead is how the fix lands, and the commit
message should **credit PR #487**, which found it.

### Nothing in Rust

The clause belongs in `kind` as far as this bead is concerned; the map code adapts.
`crates/core/src/report/region.rs` is **not** touched.

## Increments

One increment. It is a one-line change plus a guard, and the risk is entirely in the tests.

1. **A lair draws, and no fleet stops drawing.**
   RED: the cases below, **taken verbatim from the fixtures**. `Fleet, 6 Airships` must be written
   **first**, and must be seen to **pass before and after** — it is the regression guard, and a test
   added after the fix proves nothing about it.
   GREEN: the comma split and the `isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)` guard.

**Sanity check while building**: temporarily drop the raw `isShip(structure.kind)` and confirm the
`Fleet, 6 Airships` test goes red. If it does not, the test is not exercising the guard and the one
regression this bead can cause is unguarded.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `Lair, closed to player units` → `lair` | `hexView.test.ts` | the bead |
| `Ruin, closed to player units` → `lair` | same | |
| `Crypt, closed to player units` → `lair` | same | |
| `Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons` → `ship` | same | the fleet half |
| **`Fleet, 6 Airships` → `ship`** | same | **the `isShip` guard — the only possible regression** |
| a bare `Road NW` → `road` | same | unchanged |
| `Stockade, needs 20` → `building` | same | that `needs` kinds are unaffected |
| existing classification tests | same | **unchanged** |

**Every string comes from `tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep`.** Synthetic bare words are exactly what hid
this for the life of the feature; a test written from an invented kind proves nothing about what a
report sends.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. No Rust surface is touched.

## User-facing decisions

**None to ask for.** There is no choice here: the lair and ship marks already exist and are already
designed, and this bead makes them appear on the structures that should always have carried them.
Nothing about the interface is being decided, so **no mockup** — a picture of a mark that already
exists, on a hex that should always have had it, would tell the navigator nothing.

The navigator ranked it **P0** on 2026-08-21, knowing it blocks ah-lcyn.

**Decided here** (architecture): keeping `roadDirection` on the raw kind; and leaving `SHAFT_KINDS`
and `LAIR_KINDS` exactly as they are — this bead fixes the *shape* of what reaches them, nothing
else.

## Out of scope

- **The seven qualified kinds that still classify as buildings** (Ice Cave, Demon Pit, Whirlpool,
  Bog, Empowered Altar, Giant's Castle, Magician's Tower) and the Gateway question — **ah-lcyn**,
  which assumes this bead is done.
- **The six `Fleet, …` kinds that still draw as buildings** — filed while planning this as
  **ah-3pr9**. `fleet` is not in `SHIP_KINDS`, so only `Fleet, 6 Airships` is rescued, and only by
  the accident of `Airships` containing `ship`. **Do not fix it here**; the guard exists to stop this
  bead making it worse, not to make it better.
- **Any change to the Rust parser.**
- **PR #487's road and shaft changes.**

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by hand, with the turn-71 report loaded:

1. Find a hex holding a **Lair**, a **Ruin** or a **Crypt** and confirm it draws a **lair** mark
   where it drew a building. **This is the acceptance** — and it is the first time this mark has ever
   appeared from a real report.
2. Confirm it in **all four themes**, since every one of them draws through `classify()`.
3. Find a **`Galley, …`** fleet and confirm it draws as a **ship**.
4. **Find the `Fleet, 6 Airships` structure and confirm it still draws as a ship.** This is the one
   thing the change could break, and it must be looked at, not merely inferred from a green suite.
5. Confirm a **road** still draws its direction, and a **`Stockade, needs 20`** still draws as a
   building.
6. Switch the **Lairs** badge off and on: the new marks obey it like any other.

## Known traps

- **`isShip` must keep reading the raw kind.** `Fleet, 6 Airships` is a ship only because `Airships`
  contains `ship`; cleaned to `fleet` it is in neither `SHIP_KINDS` nor the substring test. This is
  the single way to turn this fix into a regression, and I verified it is the *only* kind in the
  fixtures that depends on it.
- **Write the `Fleet, 6 Airships` test first and watch it pass before the change.** A regression
  guard added afterwards guards nothing.
- **Split on the first comma only.** `Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons` must resolve to `galley`, not to
  the last segment or the whole string.
- **Check PR #487 before building.** If its author has added the `isShip` guard, the PR merges and
  this bead closes with it. Building it twice wastes the work and conflicts with an open PR on the
  same file.
- **Do not add `fleet` to `SHIP_KINDS` here.** It is the obvious next thought and it is a different
  bead (**ah-3pr9**) with a navigator question attached — a stack of forty vessels may not want the
  same mark as one galley.
- **Do not touch the road path**, and do not claim this makes a shaft draw. No committed fixture
  holds one.
- **Take every test string from the fixtures.** Synthetic bare words are the whole reason this
  shipped.
acceptance_criteria:
- A structure sent as "Lair, closed to player units", "Ruin, ..." or "Crypt, ..." draws a LAIR mark instead of a building, in all four themes.
- A "Galley, 2 Galleys, 3 Galleons" style fleet draws as a SHIP instead of a building.
- classify() takes the first comma-separated segment of the kind, trimmed and lowercased, before SHAFT_KINDS and LAIR_KINDS are consulted.
- isShip() keeps reading the RAW kind as well as the cleaned one: `isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)`. "Fleet, 6 Airships" must still draw as a ship - it is the only kind in the fixtures whose classification depends on this guard, and the only regression this change can cause.
- The "Fleet, 6 Airships" regression test is written FIRST and passes both before and after the change; removing the raw isShip call must turn it red.
- Seven structures change and none regresses, verified against tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep.
- roadDirection still reads the raw kind; the road path is unchanged. A bare "Road NW" still draws its direction and "Stockade, needs 20" is still a building.
- No change to crates/core/src/report/region.rs or anything else in Rust.
- Nothing claims this makes a shaft draw, and `fleet` is NOT added to SHIP_KINDS (that is ah-3pr9).
- Every test string is taken from tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep, never invented.
