- `pnpm run check:fast` passes.

title: Descriptions for skills and items, so a reference entry can say more than numbers
description:
Second half of ah-3cj4, and blocked by ah-3cj4.1, which touches the same parser.

The scraped ruleset carries 171 items and 96 skills, and not one description, rules note or flavour line for any of them - config/public/ruleset.json is numbers throughout. So a reference dialog built on it (ah-5jkt) can only ever show numbers.

The data page does carry the prose. Each entry is a name followed by sentences describing it, in the same uniform per-entry shape the buildings use - it is not running rules text that has to be matched by name, which is what makes this tractable.

Scope is skills and items, the two categories the scraper already reads, plus whatever other kinds the entry format turns out to cover (monsters and ships are item kinds today). The navigator's instruction was to scrape everything that forms its own section in the data.

The parser already walks every entry to read the numbers off it; this bead keeps the sentences it is currently reading past.
design:
## Context

`config/public/ruleset.json` carries 171 items and 96 skills, and **not one line of prose about any
of them**. So `ah-5jkt`'s reference dialog can only ever show numbers — which is most of the way to
useless for a reader asking what a skill is *for*.

The prose is already in front of the parser. `parseItemReference` (`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:258`)
and `parseSkillReference` (`:516`) both walk `entryParagraphs(html)` (`:157-163`) and read their
numbers **out of the paragraph text** with `readNumber`. This bead keeps the sentences they are
already reading past.

**Two measured facts about the page's shape decide the whole bead**, both from the committed fixture
`tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html`:

**1. A skill is written five times, once per level.** 480 paragraphs for 96 skills — exactly five
each, keyed `mining [MINI] 3:`. Level 1 carries the general description, the odd levels say what the
skill unlocks, and levels 2 and 4 usually read `No skill report.`:

```
mining [MINI] 1: This skill deals with all aspects of extracting raw metals and gems from the
                 earth. … A unit with this skill may PRODUCE iron [IRON] at a rate of 1 per man-month.
mining [MINI] 2: No skill report.
mining [MINI] 3: A unit with this skill may PRODUCE mithril [MITH] … may BUILD a Mine …
mining [MINI] 4: No skill report.
mining [MINI] 5: A unit with this skill may PRODUCE admantium [ADMT] …
```

The ruleset holds **one** entry per skill, so five paragraphs must become one field — and the
navigator chose a field that holds several. Measured across all 96: after the placeholders are
dropped, **71 skills keep exactly one level, 25 keep more** (7 keep two, 8 three, 1 four, 9 five),
and **none is empty at every level**. So the list costs nothing for three-quarters of the entries and
pays for itself on the quarter that say more than one thing.

**2. An item's paragraph opens with the numbers the ruleset already holds**, and the prose follows:

```
chain armor [CARM], weight 1, costs 150 silver to withdraw.  This is a type of armor. This armor
                                                             will protect its wearer 33% of the time…
leader [LEAD], weight 10, walking capacity 5, moves 2 hexes per month.  This race may study all
                                                                        skills to level 5.
Longship [LONG].  This is a ship with a capacity of 150 and a speed of 4 hexes per month.
```

**Blocked by `ah-3cj4.1`**, which touches the same file and the same generated types. Read its plan
first; its *Known traps* about rebuilding from the fixtures apply here unchanged.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree, **before** `ah-3cj4.1` lands.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Three files plus the regenerated data — the same shape as `ah-3cj4.1`, and deliberately so.

### 1. Items keep the prose after their preamble — `data.ts:258-300`

`ItemEntry` gains one optional field, and the entry gains one line:

```ts
  /**
   * What the page says about it, after the preamble of name, tag, weight and capacity that the
   * fields above already carry. Absent when the entry is nothing but that preamble.
   *
   * The preamble ends at the first full stop after the `[TAG]` - which is the same boundary
   * `classify` already reads across, and which holds for every shape the page uses:
   * `chain armor [CARM], weight 1, costs 150 silver to withdraw.` then the prose;
   * `Longship [LONG].` then the prose; `leader [LEAD], weight 10, …month.` then the prose.
   */
  description?: string;
```

Read with a helper beside `readNumber` (`:165-172`):

```ts
/**
 * An entry's prose: everything after the first full stop that follows its `[TAG]`.
 *
 * Not simply "after the first full stop" - a name may not contain one (the regexes here all refuse
 * sentence punctuation in a name for the reason `parseItemReference` records at :266-269), but the
 * preamble itself carries no full stop before the tag either, so anchoring on the tag is what makes
 * this exact rather than nearly right.
 */
function prose(paragraph: string): string | undefined {
  const after = paragraph.slice(paragraph.indexOf("]") + 1);
  const stop = after.indexOf(". ");
  const text = (stop === -1 ? "" : after.slice(stop + 2)).trim();
  return text === "" ? undefined : text;
}
```

**`. ` and not `.`** — `costs 150 silver to withdraw.` ends the preamble, but a decimal or an
abbreviation inside it would not be followed by a space. Check the three shapes above by test.

### 2. Skills keep every level that says something — `data.ts:516`

`SkillEntry` gains:

```ts
  /**
   * What the page says at each level, in level order, with the levels that say nothing left out.
   *
   * A list rather than a string because the page writes a skill five times, once per level, and
   * the interesting part is usually not level 1: mining reaches mithril at 3 and admantium at 5,
   * which is exactly what a reader opens the entry to find out. Levels the page fills with
   * `No skill report.` carry no information and are dropped, so a skill that says something only
   * at 1 and 3 has two entries here and not five.
   */
  levels?: { level: number; description: string }[];
```

The skill paragraph opening is already matched by `parseSkillReference`; extend the loop so that
instead of keeping only what it needs from each paragraph, it also accumulates a `levels` entry —
**keyed by tag, appended in the order the page lists them**, which is level order.

Dropping a level is exactly two rules, and both must be written down:

```ts
/** The page's placeholder for a level that grants nothing. Not a description. */
const NO_REPORT = /^No skill report\.?$/i;
```

— a paragraph whose prose matches `NO_REPORT`, and one whose prose is empty, contribute nothing.

**`levels` is optional and absent when empty**, the same rule `ah-3cj4.1` applies to `size` and
`cost`. In the committed fixture no skill is empty at every level, so this branch is never taken
today — it is there so that a future page which does say nothing about a skill produces no key rather
than `[]`, and it should be tested against a hand-built paragraph rather than against the fixture.

**`cost`, `maxLevel`, `cast`, `produces`, `requires` and `magic` are not touched.** They are read
from the same paragraphs and must come out identical; the counts must not fall.

### 3. The Rust side and the committed data

Whatever type mirrors `items` and `skills` for the core gains the same optional fields. Follow the
deserialisation from `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`, as `ah-3cj4.1` does for buildings.

Then rebuild `config/public/ruleset.json` **from the committed fixtures, not the live site** —
`packages/ruleset/src/cli.ts`'s `fetch --rules <path> --data <path>` — and run `committed.test.ts`,
which exists to check the committed file matches what the parser produces.

## Increments

1. **An item keeps its prose.**
   RED: `data.test.ts` — `keeps what the page says about an item`, asserting `chain armor`'s
   description begins `This is a type of armor.` and does **not** contain `weight 1`; and
   `keeps the prose of a ship` (`Longship` → begins `This is a ship with a capacity of 150`).
   GREEN: `prose` and the field.

2. **The preamble boundary holds for every shape.**
   RED: `an item whose preamble carries a comma list is still cut at the tag`
   (`leader [LEAD], weight 10, walking capacity 5, moves 2 hexes per month.` → description is
   `This race may study all skills to level 5.`), and
   `an entry that is only a preamble carries no description` (no key, not `""`).
   GREEN: the `. ` rule.

3. **A skill keeps every level that says something.**
   RED: `keeps what a skill says at each level` — `mining` has **three** entries, at levels 1, 3 and
   5, and the level-1 text begins `This skill deals with all aspects of extracting raw metals`.
   GREEN: the `levels` field and the accumulation.

4. **The placeholders are dropped.**
   RED: `drops the levels that say No skill report` — `mining` has no entry at 2 or 4 — and
   `a skill with one useful level keeps exactly one`, which is 71 of the 96 and so the ordinary case.
   GREEN: `NO_REPORT`.

5. **Nothing that was there has gone.**
   RED: none — this is the check. `keeps every item and skill it kept before`, asserting **171**
   items and **96** skills, and that a spot-checked skill's `cost`, `maxLevel`, `produces` and
   `requires` are unchanged.
   GREEN: any regression this finds. **If the counts move, a paragraph that used to parse no longer
   does, and that is this bead's bug.**

6. **The types and the committed file catch up.**
   RED: the Rust build fails on the new fields; `committed.test.ts` fails on the stale JSON.
   GREEN: the mirrored types, the regenerated TypeScript, and the rebuilt `ruleset.json`.

## The test plan

**TypeScript — `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`**, which already covers both parsers, plus
`committed.test.ts`. `pnpm run check:fast`.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| **`keeps what the page says about an item`** | `chain armor`, prose only, no `weight 1` |
| `keeps the prose of a ship` | `Longship` |
| `an item whose preamble carries a comma list is still cut at the tag` | `leader` |
| `an entry that is only a preamble carries no description` | absent, not `""` |
| **`keeps what a skill says at each level`** | `mining` → levels 1, 3, 5 |
| **`drops the levels that say No skill report`** | no 2, no 4 |
| `a skill with one useful level keeps exactly one` | the 71-of-96 case |
| `the levels come out in level order` | 1 before 3 before 5 |
| **`keeps every item and skill it kept before`** | 171 items, 96 skills |
| `a skill's existing fields are unchanged` | `cost`, `maxLevel`, `produces`, `requires`, `magic` |
| `committed.test.ts` | the rebuilt `ruleset.json` matches the parser |

**Rust — `cargo test --workspace`.** No new behaviour, so no new test: the point is that everything
still passes with a larger `ruleset.json`. **`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` must stay
green** — it runs a real turn against the real ruleset, so the rebuilt file reaches it, and its
expected finding list must not move.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `cargo test --workspace`. No browser suite: nothing renders
differently until `ah-5jkt` lands.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-19 over
`.cerebro/scratch/ah-3cj4.2-descriptions.html`, whose examples are real text from the fixture. The
chosen mockup is committed to `docs/ui/ah-3cj4.2-descriptions.html`. Nothing here is drawn by this
bead — the decisions are about **what the data holds**, which reaches the player through `ah-5jkt`.

**Q1 — a skill's description, given the page writes five per skill.** Chosen: **every level that says
something**, with the `No skill report.` placeholders dropped. It answers what a player opens the
entry for — that mining reaches mithril at 3 and admantium at 5 — at the cost of a list-shaped field
rather than a string. Rejected: **level 1 only** (one string, smallest change, reads well because
level 1 *is* the general description — but it loses everything the skill unlocks) and **all five
verbatim** (nothing judged, but two lines in five say nothing and it reads as though the data were
broken).

**Q2 — an item's description, given the paragraph opens with fields the ruleset already holds.**
Chosen: **the prose after the preamble**, so each fact appears once where it belongs. Rejected: **the
whole paragraph** — no rule to get wrong, and it would rescue `costs 150 silver to withdraw`, which
is in the page and in no field of the ruleset — but it prints the name and weight twice in a small
dialog.

**A consequence of Q2 worth recording:** `costs 150 silver to withdraw` is now captured nowhere.
Capturing it as a *field* is a different bead and is deliberately not proposed here; it is named in
*Out of scope* so it is not lost.

**Not asked:** that `levels` is absent rather than `[]` when empty (the rule `ah-3cj4.1` set, applied
for consistency), and the preamble boundary being anchored on the `[TAG]` rather than on the first
full stop.

## Out of scope

- **Buildings.** `ah-3cj4.1`, which this bead is blocked by.
- **`costs N silver to withdraw` as a field.** Visible in the page, held nowhere in the ruleset, and
  now not even carried as prose given Q2. Worth a bead; not filed, because nothing consumes it yet.
- **Monsters and ships as separate categories.** They are item *kinds* today (`classify`,
  `data.ts:174`), and they gain descriptions with every other item. Restructuring them is not this
  bead's.
- **Terrain, weather and races beyond the item entries** — named as unknowns by `ah-3cj4` and not
  established by either child.
- **Anything rendered.** No dialog, no palette entry: `ah-5jkt` owns all of it.
- **Refreshing the committed fixtures from the live site.** They are the input; refreshing them is
  its own act, and this session already found the live page and the fixture disagreeing.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
cargo test --workspace
```

Rebuild the committed data from the fixtures and read the diff — as with `ah-3cj4.1`, **this bead's
whole output is a diff to one JSON file**:

1. Every one of the **171 items** and **96 skills** is still present, with every field it had before
   unchanged. Diff against the previous file and satisfy yourself that only additions appear.
2. Spot-check by hand:
   - **chain armor** — a `description` beginning `This is a type of armor.` and containing no
     `weight 1` and no `[CARM]`.
   - **Longship** — a description beginning `This is a ship with a capacity of 150`.
   - **mining** — `levels` with exactly **three** entries, at 1, 3 and 5, in that order, and none
     containing `No skill report.`
   - **a skill that says something at one level only** — 71 of the 96 are like this, so pick any —
     `levels` with a single entry rather than five.
3. Confirm **buildings** is byte-identical to what `ah-3cj4.1` left. This bead touches no building,
   and a diff there means the rebuild used a different input.

## Known traps

- **Five paragraphs, one entry.** The skills parser is written per paragraph, and the ruleset is
  keyed per skill. Appending to the wrong key — or overwriting rather than appending — silently
  leaves each skill with only its level-5 text, which still *looks* like a description.
- **`No skill report.` is a placeholder, not prose**, and it appears at two levels in most of the 96
  skills. Keeping it makes the majority of entries read as broken data.
- **The preamble boundary is anchored on the `[TAG]`, not on the first full stop.** A name may not
  contain sentence punctuation (the parsers all refuse it, `data.ts:266-269`, for a bug that really
  happened: `Dormant Monolith: … a sacrifice of 50 leaders [LEAD].` once overwrote the definition of
  `LEAD`), but anchoring on the tag is what makes the rule exact rather than nearly right.
- **Use `. ` rather than `.` to find the end of the preamble**, or a full stop inside it splits the
  entry in the wrong place.
- **The counts must not fall.** 171 items, 96 skills. A description change that alters which
  paragraphs match is the one way this bead can do real damage, and the count assertion is what
  catches it.
- **`levels` absent, never `[]`** — the rule `ah-3cj4.1` set for `size` and `cost`, applied here so
  the file reads consistently.
- **Rebuild from the committed fixtures.** The live page and the fixture have already diverged once
  in this work; the fixture is the authority.
- **This bead is blocked by `ah-3cj4.1`** and touches the same file, the same generated types and the
  same committed JSON. Starting first means merging its changes by hand.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 171 items in config/public/ruleset.json carries the prose the data page gives it - everything after the first ". " following its [TAG] - with no field it already had changed, and no description repeating the name, tag or weight that are already separate fields. An entry that is nothing but a preamble carries no description field rather than an empty string. Every one of the 96 skills carries a levels list holding what the page says at each level it says anything at, in level order, with paragraphs reading "No skill report." dropped; mining ends with exactly three entries, at levels 1, 3 and 5. Measured against the committed fixture, 71 skills keep exactly one level and 25 keep more, and none is empty at every level, so an absent levels key is a defensive branch tested against a hand-built paragraph rather than against the fixture. The counts do not fall: 171 items and 96 skills, each with cost, maxLevel, cast, produces, requires and magic unchanged in value. The buildings ah-3cj4.1 added are byte-identical. The Rust types and any generated TypeScript are updated, the committed ruleset.json is rebuilt from the committed fixtures rather than the live site, and validate_real_orders.rs's expected finding list does not move.

title: Every building the game data describes, with its description and what it produces
description:
First half of ah-3cj4. Measured from the committed fixture tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html.

The data page carries 59 entries opening "<Name>: This is a building." The scraper keeps 10. parseBuildingReference (packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:604) matches the opening and then discards the entry unless it also finds "provides defense to the first N men" - one line, which is the whole filter.

What is thrown away today:
- 16 trade structures, each naming its product in its own prose: Mine/iron, Arcane Mine/mithril, Quarry/stone, Mystic Quarry/rootstone, Timber Yard/wood, Forest Preserve/ironwood, Sacred Grove/yew, Farm/grain, Ranch/livestock, Temple/herbs, Stables/horses, Mythic Stables/winged horses, Trapping Hut/furs, Trapping Lodge/floater hides, Inn/entertainment, Oasis/camels, Faerie Ring/mushrooms, Alchemist Lab/admantium.
- 6 roads.
- 27 lairs, ruins, caves, monoliths, ships and the rest.
- The prose of all 59, including the 10 that are kept.

Every entry has the same shape, for example:

    Mine: This is a building. Units may enter this structure. This trade structure increases the amount of iron available in the region.

The navigator chose to keep all 59 rather than only the ones a player builds: lairs, ruins and monoliths appear in reports, so a reader meets them, and choosing now which questions a reader may ask is the hole this bead exists to close.

Absent fields stay absent (navigator's choice). The 49 new entries have no size, cost, materials or mage figure because the page states none, and they must not be filled with zero - that would turn an absence into a claim. Crucially, Ruleset::mage_capacity must keep returning None for them, so ah-a2k.2's magic-study warning behaves exactly as it does today.
design:
## Context

The scraper reads every building the data page describes and then throws most of them away. A
**Mine** — one of the commonest structures in the game — is absent from `config/public/ruleset.json`
entirely, so `ah-5jkt` will show *"The game data does not describe this"* for it. That is why this is
a P0: it decides whether the reference feature is useful or mostly apologetic.

**Measured, from the committed fixture `tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html`** — the file the
scraper actually reads, and the authority here, not the live page:

| In the data page | Count | Kept today |
|---|---|---|
| entries opening `<Name>: This is a building.` | **59** (58 distinct names — `Lair` appears twice) | — |
| …that also state `provides defense to the first N men` — the fortifications | 10 | **all that is kept** |
| …trade structures, each naming its product in its own prose | 16 | none |
| …roads | 6 | none |
| …lairs, ruins, caves, monoliths, ships and the rest | 27 | none |
| per-entry prose, uniform and machine-readable | 59 | **none** |

The filter is one line — `parseBuildingReference` (`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:604-671`) matches the
opening, then `continue`s unless `readNumber(paragraph, /provides defense to the first (\d+) men/i)`
finds something (`:626-629`).

Every entry has the same shape, and a trade structure names its product in the prose:

```
Mine: This is a building. Units may enter this structure. This trade structure increases the
amount of iron available in the region.
Road N: This is a building. Units may enter this structure.
```

**The comment guarding the filter was right when written and no longer bites.** It says widening
would turn a Mine from *"the catalogue cannot say"* into *"seats nobody"*, *"which is a change to
`ah-a2k.2`'s warning this bead is expressly not making"* (`:608-614`). The only consumer is:

```rust
// crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1753
ruleset.mage_capacity(&structure.kind).is_some_and(|seats| seats >= 1)
```

`is_some_and(|seats| seats >= 1)` is false for `None` **and** for `Some(0)`, so a mage standing in a
Mine is warned either way. Verified against `Ruleset::mage_capacity`
(`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:641-645`), which is a plain `map` over the buildings table.

**And pass two gives the buildable ones their cost and materials for free.** `parseBuildingReference`
already reads `A unit with this skill may BUILD a Mine from 10 wood [WOOD] or stone [STON]`
(`:640-670`) and then discards it because *"a name only a skill mentions is not one"* (`:661`) — the
object list has no Mine. Once the object list has all 59, that pass fills `cost` and `materials` for
Mine, Quarry, Farm, Ranch, Timber Yard, Inn, Temple and the rest with no new parsing at all.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Four files, plus the regenerated data. **The parsing change is small** — the work is in the type
flowing through to Rust.

### 1. The entry type — `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:560-586`

`BuildingEntry`'s `size`, `cost` and `materials` become optional; `mages` does not.

```ts
type BuildingEntry = {
  /**
   * The description the page gives it, verbatim and whole - `This is a building. Units may enter
   * this structure. This trade structure increases the amount of iron available in the region.`
   *
   * Kept because a reference entry that can only show numbers is most of the way to useless
   * (ah-3cj4), and because it is already in front of the parser: the numbers are read out of this
   * very text.
   */
  description: string;
  /** What a trade structure increases the supply of, in the page's own word: `iron`, `yew`. */
  produces?: string;
  /**
   * Protection, where the page states it. Absent for a Mine, a road or a lair, which state no
   * defence because they give none - and an absent field says that, where a `0` would claim the
   * page had said so.
   */
  size?: number;
  /** What building it costs, from the skill entries. Absent for anything no skill can build. */
  cost?: number;
  materials?: string[];
  /**
   * Mages who may study above level 2 inside it. `0` when the entry says nothing: the data page
   * lists every structure and states the capacity wherever there is one, so silence is a
   * statement - and a Tower, which says nothing, really does seat none.
   */
  mages: number;
};
```

**`mages` stays required and stays `0` on silence, and this is deliberate** — the navigator was
shown the existing comment's reasoning and chose to keep it. It is the one field where the page's
own convention establishes that silence means zero rather than unknown, and overturning it would
also make the Tower's zero an inference, which is a different and larger question.

### 2. The parser — `parseBuildingReference`

Pass one loses its filter and gains two reads:

```ts
    const opening = paragraph.match(/^([^.:[\]]{1,40}): This is a building\./);
    if (!opening) {
      continue;
    }

    // Every entry, not only the fortifications. The filter that used to stand here kept the ten
    // that state a defence and dropped forty-nine - every trade structure, every road, every lair
    // - which is what ah-3cj4 was filed against. Its stated reason, that a Mine would go from
    // "the catalogue cannot say" to "seats nobody", does not survive reading the one consumer:
    // `mage_capacity(kind).is_some_and(|seats| seats >= 1)` is false for both.
    const size = readNumber(paragraph, /provides defense to the first (\d+) men/i);

    buildings[opening[1].trim().toUpperCase()] = {
      description: describe(paragraph),
      ...(produces(paragraph) === null ? {} : { produces: produces(paragraph)! }),
      ...(size === null ? {} : { size }),
      mages: mageCount(paragraph)
    };
```

and two small readers beside `mageCount` (`:589-595`):

```ts
/** What a trade structure increases the supply of, or `null` for anything that is not one. */
function produces(text: string): string | null {
  return text.match(/This trade structure increases the amount of ([a-z ]+?) available/i)?.[1].trim() ?? null;
}

/** The entry's own words, from the name onwards, whitespace collapsed and nothing else changed. */
function describe(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
}
```

Pass two (`:640-670`) is **unchanged**, and now finds a home for every clause it reads. Its
`existing.cost = …` / `existing.materials = …` writes still work against the optional fields.

**One thing to check rather than assume:** pass one currently initialises `cost: 0, materials: []`
(`:633-634`) for every entry, so pass two only ever overwrites. With those fields optional, an entry
no skill builds must end with **neither key**, not `cost: 0`. Assert that for a Lair.

### 3. The Rust side — `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`

The `Building` struct behind `buildings` gains the same optionality — `size`, `cost` and `materials`
become `Option`, `description: String` and `produces: Option<String>` are added, `mages: i64` stays.
Find it by following `mage_capacity` (`:641-645`); it deserialises the same JSON.

**`mage_capacity` and `knows_buildings` (`:654-656`) are not changed.** `mage_capacity` keeps
returning `Some(building.mages)`, which is now `Some(0)` for the 49 new entries rather than `None` —
behaviour-identical at the one call site, and pinned by the tests below.

### 4. The committed data — `config/public/ruleset.json`

Rebuilt by the ruleset CLI (`packages/ruleset/src/cli.ts`), whose usage is in its own header:

```
fetch --rules <url|path> --data <url|path> [--out <path>]
```

**Build it from the committed fixtures, not from the live site** — `tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html`
and `…/neworigins-data.html` — so the result is reproducible and reviewable, and so the diff is the
parser's doing rather than the site's. `committed.test.ts` exists to check the committed file matches
what the parser produces; run it.

## Increments

1. **Every building survives the read.**
   RED: `data.test.ts` — `keeps every entry the page calls a building`, asserting the parsed count is
   **58** against today's 10, and `keeps a Mine, a road and a lair` naming those three specifically.
   **58, not 59**: the page carries 59 paragraphs but `Lair` twice, and the map is keyed by the
   upper-cased name, so the second silently replaces the first. See *Known traps*.
   GREEN: delete the `size === null` filter and make `size` optional.

2. **An absence stays an absence.**
   RED: `a Mine states no size` (no `size` key), `a lair states no cost and no materials` (neither
   key — the `cost: 0, materials: []` initialisation must go), and
   **`a Tower still seats no mages and a Fort still seats one`**, which pins that the fortifications
   are untouched.
   GREEN: the optional fields and the spread-only-when-present writes.

3. **The prose comes through.**
   RED: `keeps the description the page gives` — a Mine's, verbatim, whitespace collapsed:
   `This is a building. Units may enter this structure. This trade structure increases the amount of
   iron available in the region.` — and `keeps the description of a fortification too`, so the ten
   that were already kept gain it as well.
   GREEN: `describe`.

4. **A trade structure knows what it makes.**
   RED: `reads what a trade structure produces` over the sixteen — at least `Mine`/`iron`,
   `Arcane Mine`/`mithril`, `Sacred Grove`/`yew`, `Faerie Ring`/`mushrooms` — and
   `a road produces nothing` and `a fortification produces nothing` (no `produces` key).
   GREEN: `produces`.

5. **Cost and materials arrive without new parsing.**
   RED: `a Mine costs what the skill says` — `cost: 10`, `materials: ["wood", "stone"]`, from pass
   two, which needs no change. It fails only until increment 1 puts the Mine in the object list.
   GREEN: nothing. **If this needs a code change, pass two was altered and it should not have been.**

6. **The magic-study warning is untouched.**
   RED: in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s tests —
   `a mage studying in a mine is still warned` (a hex whose structure kind is `Mine`, expecting
   `magic-study-outside-building`) and the existing `a_tower_seats_no_mages_so_the_study_is_still_halved`
   (`:4963`) unchanged. Both must pass **before and after** the ruleset is rebuilt.
   GREEN: nothing. This increment exists to prove the guarded comment's fear was unfounded.

7. **The types and the committed file catch up.**
   RED: the Rust build fails on the optional fields; `committed.test.ts` fails on the stale
   `ruleset.json`.
   GREEN: the `Building` struct, the regenerated TypeScript, and the rebuilt `ruleset.json`.

## The test plan

**TypeScript — `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`**, which already covers this parser, plus
`committed.test.ts` for the checked-in JSON. `pnpm run check:fast`.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| **`keeps every entry the page calls a building`** | 58 distinct, from 59 paragraphs, against today's 10 |
| **`the repeated Lair does not lose an entry`** | 59 paragraphs → 58 keys, deliberately |
| `keeps a Mine, a road and a lair` | the three classes the filter dropped |
| `a Mine states no size` | absence is absence |
| `a lair states no cost and no materials` | the `cost: 0` initialisation is gone |
| **`a Tower still seats no mages and a Fort still seats one`** | the fortifications are unchanged |
| `keeps the description the page gives` | a Mine's prose, verbatim |
| `keeps the description of a fortification too` | the ten gain it as well |
| `reads what a trade structure produces` | 16 of them, four named explicitly |
| `a road produces nothing` / `a fortification produces nothing` | no stray `produces` |
| `a Mine costs what the skill says` | pass two, unchanged, now finds a home |
| `committed.test.ts` | the rebuilt `ruleset.json` matches the parser |

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`.** `cargo test --workspace`.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| **`a mage studying in a mine is still warned`** | new: `Some(0)` behaves as `None` did |
| `a_tower_seats_no_mages_so_the_study_is_still_halved` (`:4963`) | existing, unchanged |
| `a_ship_is_not_a_building_that_houses_mages` (`:4999`) | existing, unchanged |
| the magic-study cases at `:4808-4843` | existing, unchanged |

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` must stay green.** It runs the real turn against the
real ruleset, so a rebuilt `ruleset.json` reaches it. Its expected finding list must not move — if it
does, the rebuild changed a check's behaviour and that is this bead's bug, not the fixture's.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `cargo test --workspace`. No browser suite: nothing renders
differently until `ah-5jkt` lands.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-19 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-3cj4-game-data.html`. The
chosen mockup is committed to `docs/ui/ah-3cj4-game-data.html`. Nothing here is drawn on screen by
this bead — the decisions are about **what the data may claim**, which reaches the player through
`ah-5jkt`.

**Q1 — scope.** Chosen: **structures and the prose the game data carries**, the navigator quoting the
Mine entry verbatim as what they expected to see. Then widened by them to *"everything that is found
as its own section in the game data — buildings, skills, items, monsters, ships"*, which is why this
bead is `ah-3cj4.1` (buildings) and `ah-3cj4.2` (skills and items) rather than one. Rejected:
structures without prose, and deferring prose to a bead of its own — the prose turned out to be
per-entry and uniform, so the fragility that argument rested on does not exist.

**Q2 — which entries.** Chosen: **all 59.** Lairs, ruins, monoliths and roads appear in reports, so a
reader meets them, and choosing now which questions they may ask is the hole this bead exists to
close. Rejected: the 26 a player builds or benefits from, and the 32 a player's own orders can
create.

**Q3 — how absence is modelled.** Chosen: **absent fields stay absent**, and specifically *not*
filled with zero, which would turn an absence into a claim. Rejected: zeros throughout, and a second
collection beside `buildings` (nothing could regress, at the cost of two names for one idea).

**Q4 — `mages`, asked after Q3 when the existing comment surfaced.** The scraper already documents
the opposite conclusion for this one field: *"`0` when the entry says nothing: the data page lists
every structure and states the capacity wherever there is one, so silence is a statement — and a
Tower, which says nothing, really does seat none."* Chosen: **keep `mages: 0`**, and apply Q3's rule
to `size`, `cost` and `materials` only. Rejected: making `mages` absent too (which would leave a
documented conclusion contradicting the code, and require rewriting that comment) and treating the
Tower's zero as an inference (which would change the magic-study warning — a larger question and not
this bead's).

**Not asked:** that `mage_capacity` and `knows_buildings` keep their signatures; that the rebuild is
driven from the committed fixtures rather than the live site.

## Out of scope

- **Descriptions for skills and items.** `ah-3cj4.2`, blocked on this bead because it touches the
  same parser.
- **A warning that a unit lacks the skill to build what it named.** `ah-bwly`, filed at the
  navigator's request during this interview and blocked on this bead. Note its open question: the
  skill and level requirement is on the **rules** page, not the data page this bead reads.
- **Terrain and what it produces**, which the rules page carries in a structured form
  (`"forest…wood (100%), fur (100%), ironwood (20%), yew (25%)"`). Nothing consumes it yet. Not filed.
- **Weather and races beyond the item entries**, which the bead names as unknowns and this plan has
  not established. Deliberately not promised.
- **Anything rendered.** No dialog, no palette entry, no pane change: `ah-5jkt` owns all of that.
- **Re-reading the live site.** The committed fixtures are the input; refreshing them is its own act.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
cargo test --workspace
```

Rebuild the committed data from the fixtures, then look at the diff — **this bead's whole output is a
diff to one JSON file, so reading it is the validation**:

1. `config/public/ruleset.json`'s `buildings` goes from **10 entries to 59**. Spot-check by hand:
   - **Mine** — a `description` reading `This is a building. Units may enter this structure. This
     trade structure increases the amount of iron available in the region.`, `produces: "iron"`,
     `cost: 10`, `materials: ["wood", "stone"]`, `mages: 0`, and **no `size`**.
   - **Road N** — a description, no `produces`, no `size`, no `cost`.
   - **Tower** — `size`, `cost`, `materials` and `mages: 0` **exactly as before**, plus a
     description. Diff it against the old file to be sure the ten did not move.
2. **Nothing else in the file changed.** `items` and `skills` must be byte-identical; this bead
   touches neither. A diff that reaches them means the rebuild used a different input.
3. Run the app against the rebuilt ruleset and put a mage in a **Mine** with a magic `STUDY` order:
   it must still warn `half of this month's study of … is wasted outside a building that houses
   mages`. Then put one in a **Fort**: still silent. That pair is the whole behavioural risk of this
   bead, checked by hand as well as by test.

## Known traps

- **The guarded comment at `data.ts:608-614` argues against exactly this change.** It is not wrong,
  it is out of date: the check it protects cannot tell `None` from `Some(0)`. Replace it rather than
  deleting it silently, and say why — the next reader deserves the same reasoning.
- **`mages` is the exception to "absence stays absent", and it is deliberate.** Making it optional
  would contradict the doc comment that survives above it and would put the Tower's zero in
  question. The navigator was asked and chose to keep it.
- **Pass one initialises `cost: 0, materials: []`** (`:633-634`), and pass two only overwrites. Leave
  that as-is and every lair claims to cost nothing — which is precisely the "absence becomes a claim"
  the navigator ruled against. Those keys must be absent unless pass two writes them.
- **Pass two must not be touched.** It already reads every `may BUILD` clause and discards the ones
  with no matching object; increment 5 exists to prove it starts working on its own. A change there
  means something else was wrong.
- **The rebuilt `ruleset.json` reaches `validate_real_orders.rs`**, which asserts an exact finding
  list against a real turn. It must not move.
- **Rebuild from the committed fixtures, not the live site.** The live page and the fixture have
  already diverged in this session's own research — I was told by a live fetch that the data page has
  no standalone structure entries and no prose, and the fixture shows 59 entries with prose
  throughout. **The fixture is the authority.**
- **`entryParagraphs` decides what an entry is**, and the name regex refuses sentence punctuation
  (`[^.:[\]]{1,40}`) for a reason `parseItemReference` records: a looser name wanders across a full
  stop and matches the tail of the previous sentence. Keep it.
- **`Lair` appears twice in the page, and the map is keyed by the upper-cased name**, so the second
  entry silently replaces the first: 59 paragraphs become 58 keys. Measured, not feared. Assert
  **58**, and decide deliberately that last-wins is acceptable rather than discovering it later — the
  two entries differ only in their prose, and neither carries a figure. If a future page repeats a
  name that *does* carry figures, this is where it will go wrong quietly.
acceptance_criteria: config/public/ruleset.json's buildings carries every entry the data page opens with "<Name>: This is a building." - 58 distinct keys from 59 paragraphs, Lair appearing twice and last-winning deliberately, against 10 today. Each carries the description the page gives it, verbatim with whitespace collapsed, including the ten fortifications which have none today. A trade structure also carries the product its description names, for all sixteen of them. The ten fortifications keep size, cost, materials and mages unchanged in value, verified against the previous file. An entry the page states no size for carries no size field, and one no skill can build carries neither cost nor materials - not zeros and not empty lists, so pass one's cost:0/materials:[] initialisation goes. Pass two is unchanged and now fills cost and materials for the buildable trade structures with no new parsing; a Mine ends with cost 10 and materials wood and stone. mages keeps its existing convention of 0 when the entry says nothing, so Ruleset::mage_capacity returns Some(0) rather than None for the new entries - behaviour-identical at its one call site, pinned by a test that a mage studying in a Mine is still warned and that a Tower still seats zero. knows_buildings() still answers true. items and skills in the rebuilt file are byte-identical. The Rust Building type and any generated TypeScript are updated, the committed ruleset.json is rebuilt from the committed fixtures rather than the live site, and validate_real_orders.rs's expected finding list does not move.

title: The scraper takes only fortifications, so most game data is missing
description:
packages/ruleset scrapes the game server's rules and data pages into config/public/ruleset.json. What it captures is narrower than the pages offer, and ah-5jkt makes that visible for the first time by putting the data in front of the player.

What is there today:
- items (171): tag, name, kind (man/mount/monster/ship/equipment), weight, capacity, selfMobile, moves, and for monsters a combat block, for ships cargoCapacity and sailingSkill.
- skills (96): tag, name, cost, maxLevel, cast, produces, requires, magic.
- buildings (10): size, cost, materials, mages - and ONLY the fortifications. See parseBuildingReference in packages/ruleset/src/data.ts.

What is missing:
- Every non-fortification structure. TOWER FORT CASTLE CITADEL, their four magical twins, HERMITS HUT and STOCKADE are the whole list. A Mine, a Shaft, a Quarry, a Temple, a road - none of them are in the data, though reports name them constantly.
- Any prose at all. There is not one description, rules note or flavour line anywhere in the file, for any category. A reference dialog can therefore only ever show numbers.
- Terrain, weather (explicitly a modelled: false gap), races beyond the item entries, and whatever else the pages carry that nobody has looked for.

Raised while planning ah-5jkt.1, which shows the player 'The game data does not describe this' for anything outside those ten buildings. That message is honest but it is a hole a reader will hit often - a Mine is one of the commonest structures in the game.

Unranked. Worth weighing against how much of the pages actually carries structured data: some of this may simply not be there to scrape, and the bead should establish that before promising it.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-3cj4.2, delivered in PR #452

title: Spare-teacher warning fires on units that are not teaching
description:
Raised by the navigator while replanning ah-dwk6 after its verification failed.

The navigator's words: "teaching warning should only be on units actually TEACHing this month. Only warn if they have free slots. Not someone not teaching."

Today the teacher-has-free-slots check offers any unit whose month is not otherwise spoken for as a candidate teacher for the students in its hex, and warns about the slots it is not filling. That is what Ordered::is_busy exists for (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:348-370): it answers "is this unit's month already spoken for by something other than teaching", and any unit for which it returns false becomes a candidate.

So a unit that is not teaching at all - and has no intention of teaching - can be warned about having free teaching slots. The warning should be about a unit that actually wrote a TEACH order this month and has capacity left over, not about every idle unit in the hex.

Evidence that the current shape is fragile rather than merely broad: is_busy's own doc comment records that getting its membership wrong once produced "one hex of turn 71 [with] twenty-nine findings that were all the same non-observation", and ah-90w had to write a regression test to stop BUILD dropping out of it. A check whose correctness depends on an exhaustive list of what everything else in the game does is a check pointed the wrong way round.

Narrowing it to units that actually TEACH would also remove the constraint that forced a compromise in ah-dwk6: the rules say CAST is not a full-month order, but ah-dwk6 had to keep is_busy treating CAST as busy anyway, because following the rules there would have added spare-teacher findings on every casting mage. If this check only looks at teachers, that exception can go and CAST can be classified by the rules everywhere.

Scope note for the planner: this changes a shipped warning's behaviour, so which units are warned and what the message says are the navigator's. Check whether the existing message still reads correctly once the subject is always a real teacher.

## Context

The `teacher-has-free-slots` warning is aimed at the wrong units. `offer_free_slots`
(`semantics.rs:1284-1349`) is called for **every unit in the hex** (`check_teaching`, `:1182-1185`),
and the only thing standing between a unit and the warning is `Ordered::is_busy` (`:1297`). So any
unit whose month is not otherwise spoken for, and which out-ranks a studying unit in that unit's
skill, is told *"this unit has 30 teaching slots free and could teach unit 700"* — including a unit
that was never asked to teach anything and has no teaching plan at all.

The navigator, raising it while `ah-dwk6` was being replanned: *"teaching warning should only be on
units actually TEACHing this month. Only warn if they have free slots. Not someone not teaching."*
Ranked **P0**.

**The check's original purpose has been made redundant by `ah-dwk6`, and that is the strongest
argument for narrowing it.** `offer_free_slots`'s own doc comment says it exists for *"a teacher with
slots to spare while somebody studies untaught"* — that is, to catch an **idle skilled unit**. Since
`ah-dwk6`, an idle unit raises `has no order that spends the month` against that same unit, in the
same problems list. So the parked veteran in the example above is still caught, by the check that is
actually about being idle. **Narrowing this one loses no coverage; it deletes a duplicate that was
wearing the wrong label.**

Two further reasons the current shape is fragile rather than merely broad:

- Its correctness depends on an exhaustive list of what *everything else in the game* does. `is_busy`'s
  own doc comment (`:348-353`) records that getting that membership wrong once produced *"one hex of
  turn 71 … twenty-nine findings that were all the same non-observation"*, and `ah-90w` had to add a
  regression test to stop `BUILD` silently dropping out of it. A check pointed that way round is a
  standing liability.
- It forced a compromise in `ah-dwk6`. The rules say `CAST` is not a full-month order, but `ah-dwk6`
  had to keep `is_busy` counting `CAST` as busy anyway, because following the rules there would have
  added spare-teacher findings on every casting mage. **This bead removes that exception** — see
  *Files to change* §3.

**Ordered behind `ah-dwk6`** (`bd dep`: `ah-vw63` blocks-on `ah-dwk6`), because it deletes an
exception `ah-dwk6` introduces and rewrites tests `ah-dwk6` adds. Read `ah-dwk6`'s plan first;
its *Known traps* apply here.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree, **before** `ah-dwk6` lands. Expect
`is_busy` to look like `ah-dwk6`'s version rather than today's when you get there.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

One file: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`. No new code, no new token, no settings change — the
`teacher-has-free-slots` toggle already exists (`SettingsDialog.tsx`, *Studying/Teaching* group) and
is untouched.

### 1. Only a unit that actually teaches — `offer_free_slots`

Two guards at the top of `offer_free_slots`, after the existing `options.emits` and `ruleset` checks
(`:1292-1295`) and beside the existing `is_busy` guard (`:1296-1299`):

```rust
    // Only a unit that actually wrote a TEACH order this month. Before ah-vw63 this ran for every
    // unit in the hex, so a unit that was never asked to teach was told it had teaching slots
    // free - and the idle-skilled-unit case this check was invented for is now `ah-dwk6`'s
    // `unit-does-nothing`, on the same unit and in the same list.
    if !teacher
        .intents()
        .any(|intent| matches!(intent, Intent::Teach { .. }))
    {
        return;
    }

    // A TEACH naming nobody this hex holds is already reported as `taught-not-here`, and its slots
    // are free only as a consequence of that mistake. One mistake, marked once.
    if !teaches_somebody_here(teacher, hex) {
        return;
    }
```

and the predicate, beside `taught_by` (`:1352-1366`), which it deliberately mirrors:

```rust
/// Whether this unit's TEACH orders name at least one unit the hex can resolve.
///
/// `Party::New`, `Party::Foreign` and `Party::Discard` never resolve: a unit formed this month has
/// no number yet, and another faction's unit is not ours to read. Those are doubt, not students.
fn teaches_somebody_here(teacher: &Ordered<'_>, hex: &Hex<'_>) -> bool {
    teacher
        .intents()
        .filter_map(|intent| match intent {
            Intent::Teach { students } => Some(students),
            _ => None,
        })
        .flatten()
        .any(|student| matches!(student, Party::Unit(id) if hex.find(id).is_some()))
}
```

**Keep the `is_busy` guard.** It is not made redundant: a unit that writes both `TEACH` and `WORK`
has an impossible month, and offering its slots would be advice about a turn nobody is playing. It
now runs *after* the TEACH guard, which is the order that matters for the CAST change in §3.

**Nothing else in the body changes.** `free` is still
`teacher.unit.men * STUDENTS_PER_TEACHER - taught_by(teacher, hex)` (`:1301`), and `taught_by`
already sums only students the hex can resolve — so a teacher whose slots are all taken still returns
early at `free <= 0` (`:1302-1304`). `could_take` (`:1306-1323`) already excludes the teacher itself,
anyone in the hex-wide `taught` set (which now always includes this teacher's own students) and
anyone leaving the hex, so the warning names only genuinely untaught pupils. The finding's anchor
(`:1343-1346`) is already `find(Intent::Teach { .. })`, which was `None` for every non-teacher before
this bead and is now **always `Some`** — that is the tell that the old shape was wrong, and it needs
no edit.

### 2. The message — `offer_free_slots:1339-1342`

```rust
            format!(
                "has {free} teaching slots still free and could also teach unit {}{and_others}",
                first.unit.unit_id,
            ),
```

was `"this unit has {free} teaching slots free and could teach unit {}{and_others}"`. Three changes,
all the navigator's: **"still free"** and **"could also teach"** both say the unit already has
students, and the leading **"this unit "** goes — the finding already carries the unit number, and
every message the recent warning beads added omits it. `and_others` (`:1329-1333`) is unchanged.

### 3. `ah-dwk6`'s CAST exception goes — `Ordered::is_busy`

`ah-dwk6` leaves `is_busy` carrying a deliberate exception, with a comment naming this bead as the
place to remove it. Requiring a `TEACH` order already excludes every casting mage that is not
teaching, so the exception has no work left to do:

```rust
    fn is_busy(&self) -> bool {
        self.intents()
            .any(|intent| spends_the_month(intent) && !matches!(intent, Intent::Teach { .. }))
    }
```

That is the plain form `ah-dwk6` wanted and could not have. **The behaviour it unlocks is real and
correct**: the rules say *"a CAST order is not a full month order; a mage may still MOVE, STUDY, or
use any other month long order"*, so a mage that writes both `CAST` and `TEACH` genuinely does have
teaching slots, and is now offered them. `spends_the_month` is unchanged — it already classifies
`CAST` by the rules — and this is the only caller of `is_busy` (verified: `semantics.rs:1297` is the
sole call site).

**Delete `ah-dwk6`'s `a_casting_mage_is_still_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher`.** It exists to pin the
exception this bead removes, so it must fail, and replacing it is increment 3.

## Validation

```bash

pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye, in the running app:

1. **The reported case.** Find a hex with a skilled unit and a unit studying that skill. Give the
   skilled unit **no orders**. It must **not** say it has teaching slots free — it should instead
   carry `has no order that spends the month` from `ah-dwk6`, which is the same observation under the
   right name.
2. Give it `TEACH <the studying unit>` and add a **second** unit studying the same skill untaught.
   The warning appears, against the teacher, reading exactly
   `has 20 teaching slots still free and could also teach unit <n>` (the number of slots depending on
   the teacher's men).
3. Add the second student to the `TEACH` line. The warning goes.
4. Change the `TEACH` line to name a unit that is not in the hex. Exactly **one** finding —
   `unit <n> is not in this hex to be taught` — and no free-slots warning beside it.
5. Give a mage `CAST shield` and `TEACH <a studying unit>`, with another untaught student present.
   The warning appears. Before this bead it did not.
6. Settings → Warnings → *Studying/Teaching* → untick **Spare teachers**: the warning goes and the
   other teaching warnings stay.

- **This bead must land after `ah-dwk6`.** It deletes a test `ah-dwk6` adds and an exception

- **`is_busy` has exactly one caller** (`semantics.rs:1297`), so removing its CAST exception cannot
  reach any other check. Verify that before editing rather than trusting this line — if a second
  caller has appeared, the blast radius is different and the navigator should be asked again.
- **Keep the `is_busy` guard.** It looks redundant once a TEACH order is required, and it is not: a
  unit writing both `TEACH` and `WORK` has an impossible month, and offering its slots is advice
  about a turn nobody is playing.
- **`a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher` is `ah-90w`'s regression guard**, and this

- **The finding's anchor is already `find(Intent::Teach { .. })`** (`:1343-1346`) and was `None` for
  every non-teacher this check ever warned about — meaning those findings carried no line. That is
  the shape of the bug, and it is also why no test noticed: nothing asserted a line on them.
- **`taught_by` counts only resolvable students** (`:1360-1363`), so a teacher whose students are all

  teacher's own students, so `could_take` never offers a teacher the pupils it is already teaching.
