title: Warn when a unit has been given nothing to do this month
description:
A unit that is given no month-long order spends the month doing nothing, and it is easy to miss one
unit among many when writing a turn. Warn when a unit has no month-long order this month.

The orders crate has no notion of order duration today - nothing in `crates/core/src/orders/`
distinguishes a month-long order from an instant one, so the classification is new work. In Atlantis
the month-long orders are the ones that consume the unit's month: `WORK`, `TAX`, `PRODUCE`, `BUILD`,
`STUDY`, `TEACH`, `ENTERTAIN`, `MOVE`, `SAIL`; the rest (`GIVE`, `BUY`, `SELL`, `ENTER`, `LEAVE`,
`DECLARE` and so on) leave the month free.

For the planner:

- **Confirm the list against the game's rules**, including the ones that are arguable: `MOVE` and
  `SAIL` occupy the month but are not "work"; a unit ordered to `TEACH` needs students; `PILLAGE`
  and `ASSASSINATE` and the combat orders need placing.
- **Which units should be exempt.** A unit deliberately left idle - a garrison sitting on `GUARD`, a
  new unit formed to receive goods, a unit that will be disbanded - is a normal thing, and a warning
  on every one of them is noise. Whether that needs a per-unit "intentionally idle" mark, or whether
  the warning is quiet enough without one.
- Which warning category this joins, and its place among the warning toggles.
acceptance_criteria: An own unit whose orders contain nothing that spends its month raises a warning against that unit reading exactly "has no order that spends the month", anchored at the unit's first block line, or with no line when the document has no block for it. The month-long set is taken from the rules and stated once as an exhaustive match over Intent: ADVANCE, BUILD, ENTERTAIN, MOVE, PILLAGE, PRODUCE, SAIL, STUDY, TAX, TEACH, WORK, plus IDLE and ANNIHILATE. CAST is NOT month-long and a unit whose only order is CAST is warned; nor are ASSASSINATE, STEAL, TRANSPORT or DISTRIBUTE, and a unit whose only orders are free ones such as NAME, ADDRESS, ARMOR or ATTACK IS warned - that is the false negative this bead's first attempt shipped. Silence is reserved for a unit holding a keyword in neither classification, which after this bead means a typo or an order the game has and the list does not. There are no exemptions: an empty block warns and a unit on GUARD warns. The existing teacher-has-free-slots warning is unchanged, which requires is_busy to keep counting CAST as busy even though spends_the_month does not; a named regression test pins that, and ah-vw63 is where the exception is removed. The check has its own toggle in Settings -> Warnings -> Orders, titled "Units that do nothing", on by default. The committed turn-71 template's expected findings go from eight to ten, the two additions being this code against units 14451 and 13432 and nothing else.
notes:
Verification failed (2026-08-19, at origin/main 1de7528): the classifier treats many orders as spending the month when they do not. The navigator's words: "Lots of orders pass for month long, but should not: NAME, ADDRESS, ARMOR, ATTACK, ..." — an incomplete list, given as examples rather than as the whole set.

The effect is the bead's own purpose inverted: a unit given only NAME, ADDRESS, ARMOR or ATTACK (and by implication other same-shape orders) is counted as busy and never warned, so exactly the forgotten unit this check exists to catch stays silent. It is the false-negative direction, which is the worse one here — a warning that never fires is invisible, unlike a spurious one.

Whoever picks this up should not fix only the four orders named. The navigator's list trails off deliberately; the fix is to go through the order set and decide, order by order, which ones actually spend the unit's month, rather than patching the examples. Note the design's own trap: is_busy deliberately omits Intent::Teach, and that exclusion must survive.
Wolverine (implementer) claimed this in the race window before the `planned` label was removed, and stood down at Psylocke's request without opening a PR. Nothing was merged. One thing worth keeping for whoever replans it — the order-by-order classification the navigator asked for, read off the NewOrigins rules page (https://atlantis-pbem.com/rules):

Two passages settle almost the whole set. The enumerated list: "The orders which take an entire month are ADVANCE, BUILD, ENTERTAIN, MOVE, PILLAGE, PRODUCE, SAIL, STUDY, TAX, TEACH and WORK." And the Sequence of Events, which groups every other order under 'Instant orders' and the phases around it.

MONTH-LONG: ADVANCE, BUILD, ENTERTAIN, MOVE, PILLAGE, PRODUCE, SAIL, STUDY, TAX, TEACH, WORK — plus IDLE, which the enumerated list omits but the page describes as 'do nothing for the entire month'. (So the enumerated list is not exhaustive and cannot be used as one.)

FREE: ADDRESS, ARMOR, ASSASSINATE, ATTACK, AUTOTAX, AVOID, BEHIND, BUY, CAST, CLAIM, COMBAT, CONSUME, DECLARE, DESCRIBE, DESTROY, ENTER, EVICT, EXCHANGE, FACTION, FIND, FORGET, FORM, GIVE, GUARD, HOLD, JOIN, LEAVE, NAME, NOAID, NOCROSS, OPTION, PASSWORD, PREPARE, PROMOTE, QUIT, RESTART, REVEAL, SACRIFICE, SELL, SHARE, SHOW, SPOILS, STEAL, TAKE, WEAPON, WITHDRAW.

UNCERTAIN, and so still unjudgeable: ANNIHILATE and TRANSPORT (with its synonym DISTRIBUTE). Each gets a phase of its own after the month-long block and the page never says whether it consumes the month.

Two of these contradict the current plan's premises directly, and are the reason a patch of the four named orders would not have been enough:

1. The rules are explicit that 'STEAL and ASSASSINATE are not full month orders, and do not interfere with other activities'. The plan uses `ASSASSINATE 4021` as its worked example of an unread line that 'spends the month as surely as WORK does', and pins that in a test (`a_unit_with_an_order_we_cannot_read_is_silent`). The premise is wrong; only ANNIHILATE and TRANSPORT actually need the unread escape hatch.

2. The rules are explicit that 'a CAST order is not a full month order; a mage may still MOVE, STUDY, or use any other month long order.' `spends_the_month` currently returns true for `Intent::Cast`, and `intents.rs` justifies it with 'the rules make no promise about which' spells take a month. They do make a promise about CAST itself. Flipping it would change `is_busy`, and so the spare-teacher check — which is why it wants deciding in the plan rather than by an implementer.

title: The halved-magic-study warning reads where the unit stands, not where its orders leave it
description:
Found by the navigator on 2026-08-17 while verifying ah-9js (origin/main 8d62fe8). All six beads in that sitting passed; this is the follow-up filed alongside.

## What the reader sees

A mage sheltered in a building that seats mages, already at level 2 or above in a magic skill, studying that skill AND issuing LEAVE in the same orders block, is not warned - though it steps out of the building before the month's study happens, and half of that study is wasted. The engine's own advisory ('Magic study rate outside of a building cut in half above level 2.') would appear on the following turn's report.

The cost being paid: the check exists precisely so a player does not discover a wasted month a turn later. In this shape it stays silent on an order the player wrote deliberately, which is the one case where a warning would change what they do.

## The cause is exact

check_magic_study_outside_building (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1545) computes 'sheltered' from the report's static picture alone:

    let standing_in = ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref().map(|id| { ... });

structure_id is where the report says the unit stood when the turn was written. The unit's own intents are never consulted, so a LEAVE in the same block is invisible to the check.

## The mirror case, which should be checked at the same time

The same blindness runs the other way. A mage standing outside, at level 2+, that issues ENTER <building that seats mages> and studies is presumably warned today although it will be sheltered when the study happens - a false warning, which is worse than a missing one because it teaches the player to distrust the check. This was not observed, only deduced from the same lines; confirm before fixing.

## The fix has a template in the same file

is_aboard (semantics.rs:1636) already answers this exact question for fleets:

    /// Whether the unit is aboard  once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run: the
    /// report's own structure first, then the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document
    /// order - which is the order the server itself would apply them in.

Intent::Leave and Intent::Enter { structure } are already modelled (orders/intents.rs:88, 313) and intents.rs:88 states the ordering rule this needs: 'LEAVE: the unit steps out of whatever it is in, before anything moves.' The shape wanted is the structure the unit is in *after* its ENTER/LEAVE orders have run, which is is_aboard generalised from a named fleet to 'whatever it ends in', and then the existing mage_capacity/needs test applied to that.

## Why this is a familiar shape

This is the ah-p1p / ah-l2i / ah-048 family again, one reader further on: a check answering from the report's static state where the player's orders have already changed the answer. Those three were about a SAIL order and three readers disagreeing about where a unit is; this is the same disagreement about what a unit is standing in. Worth asking at planning whether any other check in semantics.rs reads structure_id raw and has the same blind spot - a grep for structure_id would settle it - so this is fixed once for every reader rather than once per bug report.

## Acceptance

A mage at level 2+ in a magic skill, sheltered in a building that seats mages, that studies that skill and issues LEAVE, is warned. The same mage without the LEAVE is still silent. A mage outside that ENTERs such a building and studies is silent. An unfinished building, a Tower (which seats zero) and a structure the region does not list all keep their current behaviour. The warning stays advisory and never blocking.

## Out of scope

ah-9js's buildings reference and its source (verified, passing). Counting mages against a building's capacity - a Fort seats one, and two mages in one Fort is still unhandled and is its own bead. Every other rule inside the check: which skills are magic, the level threshold, the message wording.
design:
## Context

`check_magic_study` warns when a mage at level 2 or above studies a magic skill with nothing
housing it — half that month is wasted, and the engine only says so on the *next* turn's report,
which is the whole reason the check exists. It decides "sheltered" from the report's static
picture alone (`semantics.rs:1546`, `ordered.unit.structure_id`), so a mage that studies **and**
issues `LEAVE` in the same block is not warned, though it steps out before the month's study
happens. The check goes silent on exactly the order the player wrote deliberately.

**The mirror case is confirmed, not merely deduced.** A mage standing outside has
`structure_id == None`, so `standing_in` is `None`, `sheltered` is `false`, and the warning fires —
even when the block's own `ENTER <a building that seats mages>` will have housed it by the time it
studies. That is a false warning, which is worse than a missing one because it teaches the player
to distrust the check.

**A second check has the identical defect**, which is what the bead asked to be settled at planning
by grepping `structure_id`. `check_building` (`semantics.rs:1408`) reads
`worker.unit.structure_id` raw to decide whether the thing being BUILT is already finished, so a
unit that `ENTER`s an unfinished structure and BUILDs is judged against the structure it left, and a
unit that LEAVEs and BUILDs still gets the already-finished warning. ENTER and LEAVE run before
BUILD, so the intent-aware answer is the right one in both checks. This bead fixes both, from one
helper — which is what "fixed once for every reader rather than once per bug report" means.

Two readers below the orders layer ask the same question from the report alone
(`movement/mode.rs:286`, crew counted for sailing; `movement/fleet.rs:89`). They are **out of
scope** and filed separately; see *Out of scope*.

**When this lands**, a mage that studies and leaves is warned, a mage that studies and enters is
not, and the already-built warning follows the unit's own ENTER/LEAVE the same way.

`check_magic_study` was delivered by PR #393 and is on `origin/main` at `72c6cb8`. **Every line
number below is `origin/main`** — a checkout older than that does not contain the function at all.
Nothing blocks this bead.

## What the verification found, and what this plan now says (2026-08-18)

**This bead was built, verified and failed.** The generalisation it describes is sound and five of
the six verification cases passed; **one rule inside it is wrong**, and everything below has been
amended for it rather than rewritten.

Case A4, at `origin/main 43d1b73`: unit 1657 (unsheltered, force 3 / fire 2) in mountain (43,81) of
`neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f62-t17.rep`, given `@study fire` / `ENTER 5` / `LEAVE`, where Building [5] is a
Hermits hut seating one mage. The warning was shown; silence was expected.

The navigator, verbatim: *"Even though ENTER 5 comes before LEAVE in the order, they are processed
the other way around. I.e. LEAVE comes first and then ENTER 5. This means that the mage will be
sheltered during study."* Asked whether that is absolute or conditional, they answered **ALWAYS** —
every LEAVE is processed, then every ENTER, whatever order the lines were typed in. They were
certain rather than hedging, so this does **not** need re-confirming against the rules page.

So `structure_after_orders`' "last ENTER/LEAVE in document order wins" is not mis-ordered — it is
**the wrong shape**. Under LEAVE-before-ENTER, a block containing any ENTER can never end outside a
structure, so that branch has no correct use at all. The corrected rule:

> If the block has **any** ENTER, the unit ends in the **last** ENTERed structure. Otherwise, if it
> has any LEAVE, it ends in nothing. Otherwise it stays where the report found it. **Document order
> matters only among ENTERs.**

Passing in the same sitting, and not to be disturbed: A1 (study alone, unsheltered, warns), A2
(study + ENTER a Hermits hut, silent), A3 (study + ENTER an unfinished Stockade, still warns), B5
(sheltered mage studying, silent), B6 (sheltered mage + LEAVE, warns — the bug this bead was filed
for). The `check_building` reader shares the helper and inherits the same defect, so it takes the
same fix and needs its own case.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything is in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`. No TS, no shell, no boundary, no new
advisory code — `magic-study-outside-building` and `already-built` both already exist in
`codes::ALL` (`:104-126`), so `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` and the settings mirrors are untouched.

### The helper — generalise `is_aboard`

`is_aboard` (`:1633-1646`) already answers this exact question for one named fleet, and its doc
comment states the rule this bead needs:

```rust
/// Whether the unit is aboard `fleet_id` once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run: the
/// report's own structure first, then the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document
/// order - which is the order the server itself would apply them in.
fn is_aboard(ordered: &Ordered<'_>, fleet_id: &str) -> bool {
    let mut aboard = ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref() == Some(fleet_id);
    for placed in ordered.intents {
        match &placed.intent {
            Intent::Enter { structure } => aboard = structure == fleet_id,
            Intent::Leave => aboard = false,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    aboard
}
```

Add, beside it, the "whatever it ends in" form:

```rust
/// The structure the unit is in once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run, or `None` when it
/// ends the month in nothing.
///
/// **Every LEAVE is processed before any ENTER**, whatever order the lines were typed in - the
/// engine's own order, confirmed by the navigator on 2026-08-18 after a verification failed on
/// exactly this. So a block holding any ENTER ends inside the last structure entered, a block
/// holding only LEAVEs ends in nothing, and a block holding neither stays where the report found
/// it. Document order matters only among ENTERs; between an ENTER and a LEAVE it means nothing at
/// all.
///
/// Both run before anything else a block can ask for, so every check that asks "what is this unit
/// standing in when its orders happen" wants this rather than `unit.structure_id`, which is only
/// where the report found it.
fn structure_after_orders<'a>(ordered: &Ordered<'a>) -> Option<&'a str> {
    let mut entered: Option<&'a str> = None;
    let mut left = false;
    for placed in ordered.intents {
        match &placed.intent {
            Intent::Enter { structure } => entered = Some(structure.as_str()),
            Intent::Leave => left = true,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    match (entered, left) {
        // An ENTER always wins: the LEAVE ran first, and the unit walked back in.
        (Some(structure), _) => Some(structure),
        (None, true) => None,
        (None, false) => ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref(),
    }
}
```

The lifetime is `'a` from `Ordered<'a>` (`:280-283`, `unit: &'a ReportUnit, intents: &'a
[PlacedIntent]`), so both arms borrow for as long as the caller needs. `Intent::Enter`'s
`structure` is the raw number text (`intents.rs:313-315`), directly comparable with
`Structure::structure_id` (`report/model.rs:93`) — which is exactly what `is_aboard` relies on
today.

**Then rewrite `is_aboard` over it**, so there is one model of the rule rather than two:

```rust
fn is_aboard(ordered: &Ordered<'_>, fleet_id: &str) -> bool {
    structure_after_orders(ordered) == Some(fleet_id)
}
```

**This is equivalent for every block that holds one kind of order, and deliberately *not*
equivalent for a block that holds both** (2026-08-18). Today's `is_aboard` gives `false` for
`ENTER <fleet>` followed by `LEAVE`; the corrected helper gives `true`, because the LEAVE ran first
and the unit walked back aboard. That is the same correction this bead is making for buildings,
applied to fleets, and it is right — but it means increment 1 is no longer a pure refactor, and the
claim that the existing tests prove equivalence has to be checked rather than assumed.

Its existing tests (`a_unit_leaving_this_month_does_not_count` at `:5714`, the ENTER mirror at
`:5695-5711`, `a_unit_leaving_this_month_is_unloaded_weight` at `:5203`) each hold **one** kind of
order, so all three must still pass untouched. If any of them holds both, it encodes the old rule
and is to be rewritten with the rest of them - say so in the PR rather than quietly adjusting it. Keep `is_aboard`'s doc comment where it is; move
nothing else. **Leave `could_captain` (`:1648-1656`) alone** — it deliberately counts a unit that
also LEAVEs, because the server reads its SAIL line first, and its comment says so.

### `check_magic_study` (`:1496-1581`)

Replace `:1546-1551`:

```rust
        let standing_in = ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref().map(|id| {
            hex.region.structures.iter().find(|structure| structure.structure_id == id)
        });
```

with the intent-aware lookup:

```rust
        let standing_in = structure_after_orders(ordered).map(|id| {
            hex.region.structures.iter().find(|structure| structure.structure_id == id)
        });
```

and nothing else in the function changes. The three-armed `match` at `:1552-1566` keeps its exact
meaning, and each arm keeps being right for the new question:

- `None` — in nothing when the study happens, whether it started that way or LEFT. Not sheltered.
- `Some(None)` — the structure it ends in is not in this region's report. `continue`, silent, as
  now: nothing can be said about a structure that is not there to look at. This now also covers
  `ENTER 999` naming a structure the report does not list, which is the same doubt.
- `Some(Some(structure))` — the unfinished rule and `mage_capacity(&structure.kind) >= 1` apply to
  the structure it ends in.

The deliberate exception the navigator settled on 2026-08-17 — an unfinished building shelters
nobody, so the player *is* told — is untouched, and its comment at `:1502-1505` stays as written.

### `check_building` (`:1408`)

Replace:

```rust
        let Some(structure_id) = &worker.unit.structure_id else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(structure) = hex
            .region
            .structures
            .iter()
            .find(|structure| &structure.structure_id == structure_id)
```

with `structure_after_orders(worker)` as the source of `structure_id`, keeping the two `else {
continue; }` arms and the `structure.needs.is_some()` guard (`:1418-1420`) exactly as they are.
Note it is `worker`, not `ordered`: when the BUILD is a `HELP`, the structure that matters is the
**helped** unit's, and `worker` is already whichever of the two that is (`:1396-1405`). The helped
unit's own ENTER/LEAVE intents are in its own `Ordered`, so passing `worker` gets that right for
free.

Mind the borrow: the current code binds `&String` and compares `&structure.structure_id ==
structure_id`; the helper hands back `&str`, so the comparison becomes
`structure.structure_id == structure_id`. That is a compile error away from being noticed, not a
silent change.

### Where state lives

Nowhere new. Both checks stay pure functions over `Hex`, the ruleset and `CheckOptions`; no
caching, no new field on any struct, nothing crosses a boundary.

### Layer

`crates/core` only. Nothing in `packages/`, no generated file, no shell.

## Increments

**1. The helper, proved through `is_aboard`.** Add `structure_after_orders` with the
LEAVE-before-ENTER rule and rewrite `is_aboard` over it. Its RED is one new test, because the rule
itself is what failed verification:

- `a_unit_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_aboard` (beside the `check_sailing` tests at `:5695-5714`) —
  a unit with `ENTER <fleet>` and `LEAVE` in one block, in either written order, is aboard. It fails
  today, and it is the fleet-side statement of the same correction.

Then the existing `a_unit_leaving_this_month_does_not_count` (`:5714`), its ENTER mirror
(`:5695-5711`) and `a_unit_leaving_this_month_is_unloaded_weight` (`:5203`) must stay green
untouched — each holds one kind of order, so the corrected rule does not move them. **If one of them
does move, do not adjust it**: it means it holds both kinds and encodes the rule this bead is
removing, which is exactly how the defect reached the navigator the first time. Say so, rewrite it
deliberately, and name it in the PR. Commit this increment on its own.

**2. The magic-study check.** Failing tests first, in the magic-study section of `mod tests`
(marked at `:4161`, running to about `:4325`), in this file's sentence style. The report fixture is
unchanged from the tests already there; the whole difference is the orders string:

- `a_mage_that_leaves_the_building_this_month_is_warned` — a Castle via
  `finished_of_kind("1", "Castle")`, `in_structure(mage(2), "1")`, orders
  `"unit 5\nLEAVE\nSTUDY FORC\n"`, expecting the one `magic-study-outside-building` finding. Copy
  `magic_studied_inside_a_castle_is_silent` (`:4197-4209`) and add the LEAVE.
- `a_mage_that_enters_a_building_this_month_is_silent` — the same Castle in the region but the mage
  **not** `in_structure`, orders `"unit 5\nENTER 1\nSTUDY FORC\n"`, expecting `vec![]`. This is the
  false warning, and it fails today.
- `a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_sheltered` — **this replaces
  `a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_judged_on_the_last_order`, which asserted the wrong rule and
  is what let this bead reach the navigator.** Orders `"unit 5\nLEAVE\nENTER 1\nSTUDY FORC\n"`
  expecting `vec![]`, **and the reverse order `"unit 5\nENTER 1\nLEAVE\nSTUDY FORC\n"` expecting
  `vec![]` as well** — that second case is verification case A4, the one that failed, and the whole
  point is that the two orderings answer the same. Delete the old test rather than editing it: its
  name states the rule that is being removed.
- `a_mage_that_leaves_twice_is_outside` — `"unit 5\nLEAVE\nLEAVE\nSTUDY FORC\n"` from inside a
  Castle, expecting the warning. Pins that the no-ENTER branch still ends in nothing.
- `a_mage_entering_a_structure_the_report_does_not_list_is_not_judged` — `ENTER 999`, expecting
  `vec![]`, which pins the `Some(None)` arm for the new input.
- `a_mage_entering_a_tower_is_still_halved` — `ENTER` a `finished_of_kind("1", "Tower")` while
  standing outside, expecting the warning: entering shelters it, but a Tower seats zero
  (`BuildingEntry::mages`, `movement/rules.rs:330-332`).

Then make the one-line change at `:1546`. The existing twelve tests in that section must all stay
green — in particular `magic_studied_inside_a_castle_is_silent`, which has no ENTER or LEAVE and
must be unaffected.

**3. The already-built check.** Failing tests first, in `check_building`'s own test section (find it
by searching for `already-built` / `ALREADY_BUILT` in `mod tests`), following the fixtures that
section already uses:

- `a_builder_that_leaves_this_month_is_not_told_the_structure_is_finished` — a unit
  `in_structure` a finished structure, orders `"unit 5\nLEAVE\nBUILD\n"`, expecting `vec![]`
  (it ends the month in nothing, so the `None` arm's `continue` covers it).
- `a_builder_that_enters_a_finished_structure_this_month_is_told_so` — the unit standing outside,
  orders `"unit 5\nENTER 1\nBUILD\n"` with `1` finished, expecting the `already-built` finding.
- `a_helper_that_enters_this_month_is_judged_on_where_it_ends` — the HELP form, where the *helped*
  unit carries the ENTER. This is the one that proves `worker` rather than `ordered` was passed.

Then make the change at `:1408`.

## The test plan

| Suite | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` `mod tests`, magic-study section (`:4161`) | LEAVE warns, ENTER is silent, **an ENTER wins over a LEAVE in either written order** (verification case A4), two LEAVEs still end outside, an unlisted structure is still doubt, a Tower still halves; and the twelve existing tests are unmoved |
| the same file, the `already-built` section | LEAVE silences, ENTER warns, and a HELP is judged on the helped unit's orders |
| the same file, `check_sailing` tests (`:5203`, `:5695`, `:5714`) | `is_aboard` still means exactly what it meant, after being rewritten over the helper |

All of it is `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`. No browser suite and no TS suite is involved:
nothing on screen changes, and no advisory code is added or removed.

Fixtures to reuse rather than reinvent, all already in `mod tests` (opens at `:2267`):
`check(regions, orders)` (`:2404`), `region(units)` (`:2279`), `unit(id)` (`:2301`),
`in_structure(unit, structure_id)` (`:3938`), `studying_unit(id, tag, level)` (`:4081`),
`mage(level)` (`:4183`), `finished_of_kind(structure_id, kind)` / `unfinished_of_kind` (`:4163`),
`only(findings)` (`:2446`), `codes(&findings)` (`:2434`), `ruleset()` (`:2273`).

## User-facing decisions

None. No message text changes — `check_magic_study`'s wording
(`"half of this month's study of {} is wasted outside a building that houses mages"`, `:1574-1577`)
and `check_building`'s two messages (`:1424-1428`) are untouched, as the bead's own *Out of scope*
requires. Both warnings stay advisory and never block an export. What changes is only *when* an
existing sentence appears.

The one decision this bead settles is a scoping one and it is the planner's, not the navigator's:
**`check_building` is fixed here too**, because it is the same defect reached through the same
helper and the bead asked for the grep that found it.

**One rule of the game was settled by the navigator on 2026-08-18**, after the verification failed
on it, and it is not to be re-opened or re-derived from the rules page:

> **Every LEAVE is processed before any ENTER — always**, regardless of the order the lines were
> typed in.

They were asked directly whether this is absolute or conditional and answered *always*, with
certainty rather than hedging. Two consequences follow and both are already written into the helper
above: a block containing an ENTER can never end outside a structure, and document order matters
only among ENTERs.

This changes no message and no wording — only *when* an existing sentence appears, which is what the
whole bead is about.

## Out of scope

- **The message wording, the level threshold, and which skills count as magic.** The bead says so,
  and nothing here touches them.
- **Counting mages against a building's capacity.** A Fort seats one; two mages in one Fort is
  still unhandled and is its own bead. `mage_capacity(...) >= 1` keeps its present meaning.
- **ah-9js's buildings reference and its source**, verified and passing.
- **The two movement-layer readers** that ask the same question from the report alone —
  `movement/mode.rs:286` (`crew_sailing_levels`, which counts crew for a fleet's sailing skill
  without reading ENTER/LEAVE) and `movement/fleet.rs:89`. They sit below the orders layer, where
  intents are not in hand, so fixing them is a different shape of change; filed as its own bead.
- **`could_captain` (`:1648`)**, which deliberately counts a unit that also LEAVEs.
- **`check_sailing`'s `reported` load (`:1887`)**, which is intentionally the static before-picture
  for a before/after message; its comment at `:1874` says so.
- **`orders/effects.rs`.** Its `"enter"`/`"leave"` handling (`:569-575`) is the authoritative model
  of this rule and is already right; it is a second template, not a thing to change.

## Validation

```bash
git pull                                 # check_magic_study is on origin/main (72c6cb8), PR #393
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast                      # fmt, clippy and the rest of the gate
```

**Case A4 must be re-run by hand — it is the one that failed.** Load
`neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f62-t17.rep`, find unit 1657 in mountain (43,81), and give it:

```
@study fire
ENTER 5
LEAVE
```

Building [5] is a Hermits hut, which seats one mage. **Expect silence**: the LEAVE runs first, the
ENTER puts the mage back inside, and it studies sheltered. Then swap the two lines and expect
silence again — the whole correction is that the two orderings answer the same.

Then the five cases that already passed, to show none of them moved: study alone unsheltered
(warns); study + `ENTER` a Hermits hut (silent); study + `ENTER` an unfinished Stockade (still
warns); a sheltered mage studying (silent); a sheltered mage + `LEAVE` (warns).

Nothing else is visible: no surface changes, and both warnings already appear in the region panel's
*Problems* section wherever findings appear.

## Known traps

- **Your checkout may predate the function.** `check_magic_study` landed in PR #393 and is on
  `origin/main` at `72c6cb8`; a tree older than that has no such function and every line number
  here will miss. Pull first.
- **The function is `check_magic_study`.** `check_magic_study_outside_building` is the *code*
  string, `magic-study-outside-building`, not the function's name — the bead's description says the
  longer one.
- **Every LEAVE runs before any ENTER.** This is the rule the first attempt got wrong, and it is
  the whole reason the bead came back. "Last ENTER/LEAVE in document order wins" is not a
  near-miss — under the real rule a block containing an ENTER can never end outside a structure, so
  that branch has no correct use. If the code you are writing folds ENTER and LEAVE into one
  running value, it is the old shape wearing new names.
- **A test can encode the wrong rule and pass.** `a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_judged_on_the_last_order`
  did exactly that, which is why this reached the navigator. Delete it rather than adjusting it, and
  treat any other test whose *name* states an ordering rule with the same suspicion.
- **`is_aboard` changes for a unit with both orders, and that is intended.** It is used by
  `check_sailing` for overloading and crew, so read increment 1's note before touching it: blocks
  with one kind of order are unaffected, blocks with both now answer "aboard", and that is the same
  correction applied to fleets. What must not change is any answer for a block holding one kind.
- **Document order is slice order, and it now decides only which ENTER wins.**
  `read_intents` (`intents.rs:145`) walks the document top to bottom and pushes as it goes, so
  walking `ordered.intents` in slice order is walking in document order. Do not sort, and do not
  reach for `.rev().find(...)` — a unit written in two blocks has both concatenated (`OrderedUnits`,
  `:252-271`), and the walk keeps that right. What slice order must **not** decide is ENTER against
  LEAVE.
- **`Some(None)` is not `None`.** The check's three-armed match distinguishes "in nothing" from "in
  something this report does not list", and only the second is doubt. Flattening them with `??` or
  `.flatten()` turns a silence into a warning about every unit standing in an unlisted structure.

  (`movement/rules.rs:635-646`): the catalogue cannot say, versus the building seats nobody. The
  existing `is_some_and(|seats| seats >= 1)` already honours that; do not simplify it to
  `unwrap_or(0)`.
- **`codes::ALL` is ordered new-last** because `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` copies the order

Correction to the description: one line of the quoted doc comment lost a word to shell interpretation when this bead was filed. The comment on is_aboard (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1636) reads, in full:

    /// Whether the unit is aboard `fleet_id` once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run: the
    /// report's own structure first, then the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document
    /// order - which is the order the server itself would apply them in.

The missing word was the parameter name, `fleet_id`.
Verification failed (2026-08-18, at origin/main 43d1b73), navigator at the app.

Case A4 of the verification matrix: unit 1657 (unsheltered, force 3 / fire 2) in mountain (43,81) of
neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f62-t17.rep, given:

    @study fire
    ENTER 5
    LEAVE

Building [5] is a Hermits hut, which seats one mage.

The navigator's finding, verbatim: "Even though ENTER 5 comes before LEAVE in the order, they are
processed the other way around. I.e. LEAVE comes first and then ENTER 5. This means that the mage
will be sheltered during study. However, the warning is shown which means that ENTER and LEAVE in
the same order does not work."

So the expected result is SILENCE - the mage ends the phase inside Building [5] - and the warning is
shown instead.

## What is wrong, precisely

structure_after_orders (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs) walks the unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in
DOCUMENT order and lets the last one win. Its own doc comment states the assumption:

    the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document order - which is
    the order the server itself would apply them in

That clause is false. The engine runs every LEAVE before any ENTER, so a block containing both ends
with the unit inside the ENTERed structure regardless of which line was typed first. The unit test
a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_judged_on_the_last_order encodes the same wrong rule and passes,
which is why this reached the navigator.

Note the practical consequence: with LEAVE-before-ENTER, a block containing an ENTER can never end
outside a structure, so the "last order wins" branch has no correct use at all - the rule is not
merely mis-ordered, it is the wrong shape.

## What was verified as correct in the same sitting

Cases A1 (study alone, unsheltered, warns), A2 (study + ENTER a Hermits hut, silent - the mirror bug
this bead fixed), A3 (study + ENTER an unfinished Stockade, still warns), B5 (sheltered mage studying,
silent) and B6 (sheltered mage + LEAVE, warns - the bug this bead was filed for) all behaved as
intended. The generalisation into structure_after_orders and its second reader (the BUILD /
already-built check) are sound; only the ordering rule inside it is wrong.

The BUILD check shares structure_after_orders, so it inherits the same defect and needs the same fix
and its own case.
## The rule, from the navigator (2026-08-18), to be planned against

Asked directly whether LEAVE-before-ENTER is absolute or conditional, the navigator answered:
ALWAYS - every LEAVE is processed, then every ENTER, regardless of the order the lines were typed in.

Two consequences the revised plan should state outright:

1. A block containing an ENTER can never end with the unit outside a structure. So the "last
   ENTER/LEAVE in document order wins" branch is not merely mis-ordered - it has no correct use at
   all, and the rule is the wrong shape rather than the wrong direction.
2. structure_after_orders wants: if the block has any ENTER, the unit ends in the LAST ENTERed
   structure; otherwise, if it has any LEAVE, it ends in nothing; otherwise it stays where the
   report found it. Document order matters only among ENTERs.

The doc comment on structure_after_orders and the unit test
a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_judged_on_the_last_order both assert the wrong rule and must be
rewritten, not merely adjusted - a test asserting the old behaviour is what let this reach the
navigator.

The navigator was certain rather than hedging, so this does not need re-confirming against the rules
page before work starts.

title: Warn when a fleet is too heavy or too short-crewed to sail
description:
A fleet ordered to `SAIL` that is over its capacity, or crewed by too few sailors, does not sail. The
turn is lost and nothing warned about it beforehand.

Both failures are arithmetic the checker could do: what is aboard against what the ship can carry,
and the sailing skill aboard against what the ship needs.

## What exists, and the gap

- **Unit weight and capacity are in the report.** Unit lines carry `Weight: 10. Capacity:
  0/0/15/0.`, already parsed for movement (`movement/request.rs`).
- **Skills are parsed** — `ReportUnit.skills` — so a unit's SAIL level is available.
- **`MovementMode::Sail` exists** and `SAIL` is a known movement order.
- **Ships are not.** `Structure` carries `structure_id`, `name`, `kind`, `description` and `needs` —
  **no capacity, no crew requirement**. So the one number the check needs most is not modelled.

That is the real work in this bead, and it should be established before anything else: whether a
ship's capacity and required sailors can be read from the report at all, or must come from the
ruleset by `kind`, or are absent and this check cannot be built as asked.

## What "aboard" means

Everything the check counts is a question about which units are in the ship, and the report says who
is in a structure. Two things to settle rather than assume: whether a unit's own `Capacity` figure
should be added to the ship's (units can carry), and whether the men whose sailing skill counts are
only those aboard.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Where a ship's capacity and crew requirement come from**, per above. If neither the report nor
  the ruleset carries them, say so in the bead rather than hard-coding a table that is right for one
  ruleset and quietly wrong for the next.
- **One warning or two.** Overloaded and undercrewed are different mistakes with different fixes;
  separate codes let the Warnings tab turn one off and keep the other.
- **How close to the limit is worth saying.** Exactly at capacity sails; the interesting case may be
  "this is within a man of not sailing", which is a different check and probably a later one.

## Validation

A fleet loaded past its capacity and ordered to `SAIL`: warned, naming what is over. The same fleet
one unit lighter: silent. A fleet with too few sailors aboard: warned. A fleet that will sail
perfectly well: silent, including when its units carry cargo of their own.

A fleet ordered to `SAIL` that is over its capacity, or short of sailing skill, does not sail; the
turn is lost and nothing warned. Two facts the check needs already exist (verified 2026-08-16,
`origin/main` at `90e2ff4`):

- **The report states a fleet's numbers for your own ships**: `+ Ship [329] : Longship; Load:
  110/150; Sailors: 4/4; MaxSpeed: 4.` (`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t41.rep`)
  — parsed into `Structure { structure_id, name, kind, description: Some("Load: 110/150; Sailors:
  4/4; MaxSpeed: 4."), needs }` (`crates/core/src/report/region.rs:135–168`). A fleet's `kind` is
  a bare hull (`"Longship"`) or `"Fleet, 8 Corsairs"` / `"Fleet, 4 Galleons, 1 Balloon"`. Foreign
  ships state no numbers.
- **The ruleset carries every hull's capacity and crew**: `config/public/ruleset.json` `items[*]`
  with `kind: "ship"` have `cargoCapacity` and `sailingSkill` (Longship 150/4, Raft 450/2, Cog
  750/6, Galleon 2700/15, Galley 1200/12, Corsair 1500/15, Balloon 100/3, Airship 800/10,
  Cloudship 1500/15) → `ItemEntry.cargo_capacity: Option<i64>`, `sailing_skill: Option<i64>`
  (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:178–195`), found by `Ruleset::find_item(name)` (`:551`, which
  strips plurals).
- **`crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs` already reads them for the planner** (ah-2vy.2):
  `parse_fleet_kind(kind) -> Option<Vec<(hull, count)>>` (`:116`), `stated_field` /
  `stated_sailing_requirement` (`:137–146`, private), `sailing_requirement(fleet: &Structure,
  ruleset: &Ruleset) -> Option<i64>` (`:161`, stated first, ruleset second, `None` when neither),
  `crew_sailing_levels(units, structure_id) -> i64` (`:220`), `fleet_of` (`:96`, over a `KnownHex`).
  Callers: `movement/plan.rs:38, 240`, `movement/trace.rs:16, 61`.
- **The report gives each own unit its `Weight:`** (`ReportUnit.weight: Option<i64>`,
  `report/model.rs`) and its skills (`skills: Vec<Skill { tag, level: u32, … }>`); which structure
  it stands in is `structure_id`. Nothing lightens a unit for the ship: the ship carries the total
  weight of what is aboard, and a unit's own `Capacity` is about the unit walking, not the hull.
- **The checks** live in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` (`check_turn :142`, `Hex`/`Ordered`
  `:186–265`, `Ordered::finding(hex, code, message, at)` `:324`, `codes` `:64–90`, the per-code fixture
  table `:2065–2130`, helpers `region(units)`, `unit(id)`, `check`, `codes`, `only` `:1084–1200`).
  Intents (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`): `SAIL <route>` is read as `Intent::Move { steps }`
  and a bare `SAIL` as `Intent::MonthLong("SAIL")` (`:210–219`); `ENTER`/`LEAVE` are grammar
  commands (`grammar.rs:187, 257`) that produce no intent. `MoveStep` is `Go(Direction) | In(Option<String>) | Out`
  (`movement/orders.rs:19–27`).
- **The Warnings tab and vocabulary**: `codes::ALL` → `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs` →
  `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts`; `WARNING_GROUPS` in
  `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx:290–345`; `SettingsDialog.test.tsx:34–80` lists
  the titles by hand. `ah-yk7` (planned, may land first) adds a group *Orders* the same way — the
  patterns are identical; if it has merged, `ALL` is already `[Code; 10]` and this makes it 12.

**Decision (navigator, 2026-08-16, mockup `docs/ui/fleet-cannot-sail.html`, PR #338).** Scope
**B**: the units aboard are the report's own units in the fleet, plus those ordered `ENTER <fleet>`
this month, minus those ordered `LEAVE`; their **report** weights and sailing levels are summed;
capacity and crew requirement come from the report's stated `Load: H/N` / `Sailors: H/N`, else the
ruleset. **Two codes**, `fleet-overloaded` and `fleet-undercrewed`, one finding each on the
captain's `SAIL` line, in a new Warnings-tab group **Sailing**, both on by default. Scope C —
re-weighing units for this month's `GIVE`/`TAKE` — is **`ah-eet`**, filed today, related to this
bead; its seam is `fleet_load` below. Accept on doubt, exactly as `semantics.rs:1–17` says: a
number the report and the ruleset cannot supply, a unit whose weight is unstated, a foreign unit
aboard, or a `MOVE` that touches the fleet (whose ordering against the sail the server does not
promise) silences the check for that fleet rather than guessing.

Design choices that are mine: `SAIL` becomes its own intent (`Intent::Sail { steps }`, bare SAIL
included) because the check has to tell a fleet order from a unit walking off; `ENTER`/`LEAVE`
become intents (`Intent::Enter { structure }`, `Intent::Leave`) because they change who is aboard
and are instant orders that the server runs before movement; `sailing_requirement` in `mode.rs`
learns to work without a ruleset (stated numbers still count) and gains a sibling `cargo_capacity`;
the check itself is `check_sailing` in `semantics.rs`, next to the other three.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`

`Intent` gains three variants (documented in the style of the others):

```rust
    /// `SAIL`, with or without a route: the fleet this unit stands in is being told to move. Bare
    /// SAIL - the turn 71 template's form - has no steps.
    Sail { steps: Vec<MoveStep> },
    /// `ENTER n`: the unit boards structure `n` this month, before anything moves.
    Enter { structure: String },
    /// `LEAVE`: the unit steps out of whatever it is in, before anything moves.
    Leave,
```

`read_order` (`:199–219`): replace the two `SAIL` arms with

```rust
        "SAIL" if arguments.is_empty() => Some(Intent::Sail { steps: Vec::new() }),
        "SAIL" => Some(Intent::Sail { steps: forms::read_move_line(command, arguments)? }),
        "ENTER" => Some(Intent::Enter { structure: forms::read_only_number(arguments)?.to_string() }),
        "LEAVE" if arguments.is_empty() => Some(Intent::Leave),
```

before the `is_movement_command` arm (which would otherwise take SAIL). `forms::read_only_number`
returns the number as `i64` (`:200` uses it for CLAIM) — `.to_string()` gives the structure id
as the report spells it. Tests: `:552–569` (`SAIL N` → `Intent::Sail { steps: parse_move("SAIL N") }`;
bare `SAIL` → `Intent::Sail { steps: vec![] }`), plus `an_enter_names_its_structure` and
`a_leave_is_recorded`.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the existing predicates

- `spends_the_month` (`:276–287`): add `| Intent::Sail { .. }`.
- `leaves_the_hex` (`:249–253`): `Intent::Move { steps } | Intent::Sail { steps } => steps.iter().any(Go)`.
- `apply` (`:464–471`): `Intent::Sail { .. } | Intent::Enter { .. } | Intent::Leave => {}` beside
  `Move`/`MonthLong`.
- The guard test at `:1707–1716` ("A guard that sails away drops the guard … SAIL N") must still
  pass — it does through `leaves_the_hex`.

### `crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs`

`sailing_requirement` takes `ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>`: the stated number first; without a
ruleset and without a stated number, `None`. Callers `plan.rs:240–247` and `trace.rs:61` (via
`fleet_sailing`) pass `Some(ruleset)`. New, beside it:

```rust
/// `"Load: 110/150"` states have and need; this reads the second number, the weight a fleet carries.
fn stated_cargo_capacity(description: &str) -> Option<i64>

/// How much weight a fleet can carry. Stated `Load: H/N` first; else the ruleset's
/// `cargoCapacity` per hull, times the count; `None` when neither can say - an unknown hull, no
/// ruleset - which callers treat as "cannot be priced" rather than a guess.
#[must_use]
pub fn cargo_capacity(fleet: &Structure, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) -> Option<i64>

/// How a fleet is named to the player: `Longship [329]` for one hull, `Fleet [988] (8 Corsairs)`
/// for several - the kind after `Fleet, `, verbatim.
#[must_use]
pub fn fleet_label(fleet: &Structure) -> String
```

from the ruleset for `"Fleet, 2 Galleons"` (5400), `None` for `"Fleet, 2 Barges"` with the ruleset
and for a bare hull with none; `fleet_label` for `Longship`/`329` and `Fleet, 8 Corsairs`/`988`
(exactly `Longship [329]` and `Fleet [988] (8 Corsairs)`); `sailing_requirement(fleet, None)` reads
the stated `Sailors: 4/4` and is `None` unstated.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the check

- `codes`: `pub const FLEET_OVERLOADED: Code = Code("fleet-overloaded");`
  `pub const FLEET_UNDERCREWED: Code = Code("fleet-undercrewed");`, appended to `ALL` in that order
  (after `form-alias-reused` if `ah-yk7` has landed).
- `check_turn`: `check_sailing(&hex, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);` after `check_teaching`.
- The check, one fleet at a time:

```rust
/// Every fleet in the hex that one of our units orders to SAIL: is what is aboard within what the
/// hull carries, and is enough sailing skill aboard to sail it? Aboard means the report's units in
/// the fleet, plus those that ENTER it this month, minus those that LEAVE - the instant orders the
/// server runs before anything moves. Weights and skills are the report's (ah-eet prices this
/// month's GIVEs). Anything the report or the ruleset cannot price silences the fleet - never a guess.
fn check_sailing(hex: &Hex<'_>, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>, options: &CheckOptions, findings: &mut Vec<Finding>)
```

For each `fleet` in `hex.region.structures` with `parse_fleet_kind(&fleet.kind).is_some()`:

1. **Captain**: among `hex.units` (own units) with `unit.structure_id == Some(fleet.structure_id)`
   or an `Intent::Enter { structure == fleet.structure_id }`, the one with the lowest-line
   `Intent::Sail` placement. None → next fleet.
2. **Aboard after**: own units with `structure_id == fleet` and no `Intent::Leave`, plus own units
   with `Intent::Enter { structure == fleet }`. (A unit that both ENTERs and LEAVEs: last order
   wins, as it would on the server — walk its intents in order.)
3. **Doubt** — skip both findings for this fleet if any of: an aboard-after unit has an
   `Intent::Move { .. }` at all, or any own unit's `Intent::Move` steps contain `In(Some(id))` with
   `id == fleet.structure_id`; a unit in the region (any faction) with `structure_id == fleet` is
   not `own`; an aboard-after unit's `weight` is `None` (load side only — the crew side still runs).
4. **Load**: `let load: i64 = aboard.iter().map(|u| u.weight.unwrap()).sum()`;
   `capacity = cargo_capacity(fleet, ruleset)`; if `Some(capacity)` and `load > capacity` and

   overloaded: {load} aboard on a capacity of {capacity}, so it will not sail"), Some(sail_placement))`.
5. **Crew**: `levels = aboard.iter().flat_map(skills).filter(tag == "SAIL").map(level).sum()`

   helper `sailing_levels(units: &[&ReportUnit]) -> i64` in the check, do not call
   `crew_sailing_levels`, which filters by the report's `structure_id`); `required =
   sailing_requirement(fleet, ruleset)`; if `Some(required)` and `levels < required` and
   `options.emits(FLEET_UNDERCREWED)` → `format!("{label} is short of sailors: {levels} sailing
   levels aboard, it needs {required}, so it will not sail")`.

```rust
/// The sailing levels one unit supplies once this month's transfers of men have run.
///
/// A unit's skill level is held by each of its men - "the number of skill levels of the Sailing
/// skill that must be aboard the ship" - so men leaving take levels with them. Read from the
/// ledger for the same reason `weight_after_orders` is: the server runs every GIVE and TAKE
/// (phase 4) before it moves anybody (phase 9), so giving a gnoll away and sailing in the same
/// month is one turn, not two.
///
/// `None` - cannot say, so the caller silences the crew check for this fleet - when men arrive
/// rather than leave. The game merges given men into the receiving unit and recomputes its skill,
/// which this application does not model; counting them at the receiver's own level would turn two
/// unskilled gnolls into two sailors, and a warning that is wrong is worse than one that is missing
/// (this module's header, and the navigator's own answer on the amendment).
fn sailing_levels_after_orders(
    ordered: &Ordered<'_>,
    ledger: &Ledger<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
) -> Option<i64> {
    let level: i64 = ordered
        .unit
        .skills
        .iter()
        .filter(|skill| skill.tag.eq_ignore_ascii_case("SAIL"))
        .map(|skill| i64::from(skill.level))
        .sum();

    // Without a catalogue there is no telling which tags name people, so no delta can be computed.
    let ruleset = ruleset?;

    let mut men_moved: i64 = 0;
    for ((unit_id, tag), balance) in &ledger.balance {
        if unit_id != &ordered.unit.unit_id || !ruleset.is_man(tag) {
            continue;
        }
        men_moved = men_moved.saturating_add(balance - ordered.holding(tag));
    }

    if men_moved > 0 {
        return None;                       // men arrived: the merged skill is unknowable
    }

    let men = ordered.unit.men.saturating_add(men_moved).max(0);
    Some(level.saturating_mul(men))
}
```

`ReportUnit.men` is `i64` (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:142`), so no conversion is needed — only
`skill.level` is a `u32` and wants `i64::from`, exactly as `crew_sailing_levels`
(`movement/mode.rs:294`) already writes it.

Then, in `check_sailing`, replace the inline `levels` sum (`semantics.rs:1730-1741`) with two figures
and the doubt:

```rust
// What the report printed, which is the "before" the message compares against.
let reported_levels: i64 = aboard
    .iter()
    .flat_map(|ordered| { /* the existing per-man sum, unchanged */ })
    .sum();

// The same after this month's transfers of men. `None` from any unit aboard silences the crew
// check for the whole fleet - one unknowable unit makes the fleet's total unknowable.
let levels: Option<i64> = aboard
    .iter()
    .map(|ordered| sailing_levels_after_orders(ordered, ledger, ruleset))
    .sum();
```

`Option<i64>: Sum<Option<i64>>` short-circuits to `None` on the first `None`, which is exactly the
rule wanted and is the same idiom the load side already uses for `sailing` (`:1698-1701`) and
`reported` (`:1689-1696`).

Also consult the ledger's own doubt — a unit whose sums cannot be trusted cannot price its crew
either:

```rust
let doubted_aboard = aboard
    .iter()
    .any(|ordered| ledger.doubted.contains(&ordered.unit.unit_id));
```

**Guard the crew finding with it, and only the crew finding — do not add it to the fleet-wide
`continue`.** `ledger.doubted` is read today only inside `check_resources` (`semantics.rs:940`, `:954`,
`:1047`); `check_sailing` never consults it, on the load side or the crew side. Putting
`doubted_aboard` into the `continue` beside `move_touches_fleet || aboard_unit_moves ||
foreign_aboard` would therefore silence overload warnings that ship today, which is a regression this
amendment must not introduce. So it joins `!headcount_is_doubtful` in the crew `if`, and the load
half is left exactly as it is.

Finally the message, mirroring the overload `match` (`:1705-1716`) arm for arm:

```rust
if let (Some(levels), Some(required)) = (levels, sailing_requirement(fleet, ruleset)) {
    if !headcount_is_doubtful && levels < required && options.emits(codes::FLEET_UNDERCREWED) {
        let crew = match levels - reported_levels {
            change if change < 0 => format!(
                "{reported_levels} sailing levels aboard less {} given away this month, \
                 it needs {required}",
                -change
            ),
            // Unchanged, and the sentence ah-j0e already shipped: the crew did not move this
            // month, so there is no before-and-after to draw. A positive change cannot occur -
            // men arriving returns None above.
            _ => format!("{levels} sailing levels aboard, it needs {required}"),
        };
        findings.push(captain.finding(
            hex,
            codes::FLEET_UNDERCREWED,
            format!("{label} is short of sailors: {crew}, so it will not sail"),
            Some(sail_placement),
        ));
    }
}
```

The two sentences, **quoted verbatim and asserted verbatim in the tests**:

- crew changed this month —
  `Raft [218] is short of sailors: 2 sailing levels aboard less 1 given away this month, it needs 2, so it will not sail`
- crew unchanged (as shipped today, byte for byte) —
  `Raft [218] is short of sailors: 1 sailing levels aboard, it needs 2, so it will not sail`

`levels` and `reported_levels` are plain integers, no thousands separators, and `sailing levels`
stays plural at 1 — that is what ships today and changing it is not this amendment's business.

**Then re-run the verification's four cases** (they are in the notes on this bead): the false
positive must stay silent, the `give 0 1 GNOL` case must warn, the `ENTER 235` overload must still
warn, and the *Sailing* group must still show two working toggles.

### The delivered increments, for the record

1. **RED**: the per-code fixture rows → the two codes and `ALL` (compile) → fixture test fails
   because nothing emits. Intents: RED the four intents tests → the three variants and arms; fix
   the predicates and `apply` (compile). `mode.rs`: RED its five tests → `cargo_capacity`,
   `fleet_label`, `sailing_requirement(Option)`, callers updated. Then RED the sailing tests →
   `check_sailing`. `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`; regenerate the vocabulary; clippy.
2. **Warnings tab**: RED the settings test → the group. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`.
3. `pnpm run check:fast`. Look once: load `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t41.rep` (Longship [329],
   `Load: 110/150; Sailors: 4/4`), give unit 11125 `SAIL N` — silent; add `unit 12590\nLEAVE\n`
   (a sailor) — *Undercrewed fleets* appears on 11125's SAIL line; the Warnings tab shows *Sailing*.

## The test plan

**Added by the 2026-08-17 amendment — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`, `mod tests`.** All against
a Raft fleet `Structure { structure_id: "218", name: "Ship", kind: "Raft", description: Some("Load:
70/450; Sailors: 2/2; MaxSpeed: 2."), needs: None }`, whose aboard unit is `men: 2`, `items: [2 GNOL]`,
`skills: [sail(1)]` — the shape of `neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep`'s `Ship [218]`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `giving_a_sailor_away_this_month_is_short_of_sailors` | The failure: `give 0 1 GNOL` + `sail N` warns, with M2's before-and-after sentence asserted verbatim |
| `giving_a_sailor_to_a_unit_in_the_hex_is_short_of_sailors` | `give 9509 1 GNOL` to a unit **not** aboard warns the same way — the men left the hull, wherever they went |
| `a_full_crew_that_gives_nothing_away_still_sails` | The first failure's case, unchanged: no transfer, 2 levels of 2, silent. This is the regression that must not come back |
| `men_given_into_a_unit_aboard_silence_the_crew_check` | R1's doubt: an overloaded-and-undercrewed fleet receiving `give 9508 2 GNOL` emits **no** `fleet-undercrewed` — and **still emits `fleet-overloaded`**, because the load half is untouched |
| `men_taken_aboard_silence_the_crew_check` | The same for `take 9509 2 GNOL` |
| `a_give_of_equipment_does_not_touch_the_crew` | `give 0 1 SWOR` changes the load and leaves the levels alone — `is_man` is doing its job |
| `no_ruleset_silences_the_crew_check` | `ruleset: None`: no catalogue, so no man tags, so `None` — silent, not a guess |
| `a_doubted_unit_aboard_silences_the_crew_but_not_the_load` | `doubted_aboard` guards the crew finding only, per *Increments* |
| `giving_every_man_away_is_short_of_sailors` | `give 0 2 GNOL` → 0 levels, message `…2 sailing levels aboard less 2 given away this month…`; the `.max(0)` clamp holds |

- Rust: intents ×4, mode ×5, semantics ×14 + two fixture rows; `generated_ts` regenerated;
  everything existing (`a_guard_that_sails_away…`, the planner's `CrewCannotSail` tests) unchanged.
  Plus the nine above; `ALL` and the per-code fixture table are **unchanged** by the amendment — it
  adds no code.
- TS: `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` as edited. `pnpm run check:fast`.
- Smoke: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:941, 1011, 1019` toggle two existing codes by test id;
  nothing enumerates the tab — no change.

## User-facing decisions

Asked with a mockup (`docs/ui/fleet-cannot-sail.html`, PR #338) on 2026-08-16; the navigator chose:

1. **Scope B** — this month's `ENTER`/`LEAVE` counted at report weights and skills; **scope C**
   (`GIVE`/`TAKE` re-weighing) is `ah-eet`. Rejected: A (report state only — silent on this
   month's boarding), C in this bead (bigger, and B is a strict subset that ships first).
2. **Two codes** — `Overloaded fleets` and `Undercrewed fleets` — each its own toggle and line.
   Rejected: one "Fleets that cannot sail" code.
3. **Messages, verbatim**: `Longship [329] is overloaded: 190 aboard on a capacity of 150, so it
   will not sail` and `Longship [329] is short of sailors: 2 sailing levels aboard, it needs 4, so
   it will not sail`; several hulls read `Fleet [988] (8 Corsairs)`. Rejected: the terser
   `Longship [329]: 190/150 aboard, will not sail`.
4. **Settings**: new group **Sailing**, titles/descriptions as above, both **on by default**.
   Rejected: filing them under *Orders*.
5. States accepted as drawn: the line goes to the first own unit aboard giving `SAIL`; exactly at
   the limit sails; unknown hull / foreign ship / no report → silent; a unit's own capacity does
   not lighten the ship; a bare `SAIL` counts.

**Asked again on 2026-08-17 after the second verification failure**, with the mockup
`docs/ui/ah-j0e-crew-after-gives.html`, which shows the failing case in the problems pane and both
candidate sentences as they would ship. Items 1–5 above were **not** reopened; only these two were put,
and the navigator chose:

6. **The sailors count follows this month's `GIVE`/`TAKE` of men — men out exactly, men in silences.**
   Variant **R1**. Men leaving a unit reduce its sailing levels in proportion, because a level is held
   by each of a unit's men; men arriving into a unit aboard make the fleet's crew check silent for the
   month, because the game merges given men and recomputes the receiving unit's skill and this
   application does not model that.
   *Rejected: **R2**, counting both directions at the receiving unit's own level* — one rule with no
   exceptions, but two unskilled gnolls given to a sailor would become two sailors, so it invents
   skill the merged unit will not have. That is the wrong direction of error for a warning check, and
   this module's header refuses it.
   *Rejected: **R3**, any `GIVE`/`TAKE` of men silencing the crew check* — it can never warn wrongly,
   and it does not fix what verification failed on: the raft still sails away unwarned. An implementer
   tempted to reach for R3 as "the safe option" is re-opening a decision the navigator took against
   exactly that argument.

7. **The message says when the crew changed this month**, symmetric with the overload message
   `ah-eet` already ships. Variant **M2**, both sentences quoted verbatim in *Increments*: when men
   moved, `…is short of sailors: 2 sailing levels aboard less 1 given away this month, it needs 2, so
   it will not sail`; when they did not, the sentence agreed in item 3 above, byte for byte unchanged.
   *Rejected: **M1**, one number however it was arrived at* — no new string and a shorter line in a
   narrow pane, but it does not point at the `give` that caused the shortfall, so the player is told
   the fleet will not sail without being told what to undo.

## Out of scope

- Re-weighing units for `GIVE`/`TAKE`/`BUY` — delivered by `ah-eet` (closed). The amendment reads the
  ledger `ah-eet` built and **changes nothing on the load side**: `weight_after_orders`, the overload
  message and its `match` arms are all left exactly as they are.
- "Within a man of not sailing".
- A `SAIL` by a unit in no fleet, or by a unit not the owner — other checks.
- Whether the route itself is sailable (`plan_route` already refuses `CrewCannotSail`).
- Fleet speed.
- **Modelling what a merged unit knows.** R1 answers "men given into a unit aboard" with silence
  precisely so that nobody has to. Working out the receiving unit's skill after a merge is a piece of
  engine behaviour this application does not model anywhere, and it is not to be attempted here — if
  it is ever wanted it is a bead of its own.
- **`movement::mode::crew_sailing_levels`** (`movement/mode.rs:286`). It sums the report's figures for
  the route planner and is correct for that: the planner asks what a fleet can do now, not what this
  month's orders would leave it. Do not point it at the ledger, and do not make `check_sailing` call
  it — the amended check needs the aboard-after set, which `crew_sailing_levels` cannot see.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx
pnpm run check:fast
```

And the look in increment 3.

**Re-verification, after the amendment (increment 0) — all four of Psylocke's cases, in this order.**
The bead has failed twice, so the whole set is re-run rather than the one case that broke; the notes on
this bead carry them, and they are repeated here so the implementer can check its own work before
handing back. Fixture `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep`, `Ship [218]` (Raft,
`Load: 70/450; Sailors: 2/2`), unit `Drones (9508)` = 2 gnolls at `SAIL 1`:

1. `unit 9508` + `sail N` alone → **silent.** (The first failure. 2 levels aboard, 2 needed.)
2. `unit 9508` + `give 0 1 GNOL` + `sail N` → **warns** `fleet-undercrewed` on the `sail` line, with
   the before-and-after sentence from item 7 of *User-facing decisions*. (The second failure, and what
   increment 0 is for.)
3. `unit 8333` + `ENTER 235` with a heavy load → **still warns** `fleet-overloaded`. (The load half must
   be undisturbed.)
4. The Warnings tab still shows the **Sailing** group with both toggles, on by default, and each one
   still silences its own code.

A human runs these — it is the point of verification — but the implementer should reproduce 1 and 2 as
unit tests before it opens a PR, which the test plan above requires anyway.

## Known traps

- **`ALL`'s length is a type** — count what is there when you arrive (`ah-yk7` may have added
  one) and add two.
- **`SAIL N` was an `Intent::Move`**; anything that matched `Move` to mean "goes away" needs `Sail`
  too — `leaves_the_hex` and `spends_the_month` are listed above; grep for `Intent::Move` before
  finishing.
- **`crew_sailing_levels` filters by the report's `structure_id`**, so a unit that ENTERs this month
  is invisible to it; sum over the aboard-after set yourself.
- **Doubt silences, never guesses**: an unknown hull with no stated numbers, a `None` weight, a
  foreign unit aboard, a `MOVE` touching the fleet — each is a `continue`, not a default.
- **`sailing_requirement`'s signature changes** (`Option<&Ruleset>`); the two callers in
  `movement/plan.rs` and `movement/trace.rs` pass `Some(ruleset)`.
- **The messages are asserted verbatim**; `label` comes from `fleet_label`, numbers are plain
  integers, no thousands separators.

Added by the 2026-08-17 amendment:

- **This bead has failed verification twice, and the two failures are opposite.** The first was a
  **false positive** (a fleet that sails, warned) and the second a **false negative** (a fleet that
  will not sail, silent). Every test in the amendment's list is there because one of those two
  directions was got wrong, so run the whole sailing test set and read the names — not just the new
  ones. `a_full_crew_that_gives_nothing_away_still_sails` is the first failure's regression and is the
  single most important assertion in the file.
- **`Option<i64>` summed over the aboard set is the doubt mechanism, and it must stay an `Option`.**
  `.sum::<Option<i64>>()` short-circuits to `None` on the first `None`, which is what makes one
  unknowable unit silence the whole fleet. Unwrapping early, or defaulting a `None` to `0`, turns R1's
  doubt into a claim that the fleet has no sailors — a false positive, and the failure mode this bead
  has already been sent back for once.
- **`ledger.doubted` guards the crew finding alone.** `check_sailing` does not consult it today
  (`semantics.rs:940`, `:954`, `:1047` are all inside `check_resources`), so adding it to the
  fleet-wide `continue` would silence overload warnings that currently ship. See *Increments*.
- **`Ruleset::is_man` is what decides a tag names people** (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:598`).
  Do not hard-code race tags: `GNOL`, `LEAD`, `CTAU` and the rest are one ruleset's list, and a
  centaur is both a race and a mount — the catalogue settles that when it is scraped, as `is_man`'s
  own docstring says.
- **A `GIVE` of men to a unit outside the hull still reduces the crew.** The men have left the ship
  whether they went to another unit in the hex or to `0`. Only men arriving *into* a unit aboard is
  the doubt case, so the test is the sign of `men_moved` for the aboard unit, never who the
  counterparty was.
- **`men_estimated` doubt already exists and stays.** `headcount_is_doubtful` (`semantics.rs:1744`)
  came from a review comment on the original PR; the amendment adds `doubted_aboard` beside it rather
  than replacing it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) codes fleet-overloaded and fleet-undercrewed in codes::ALL; Intent::Sail/Enter/Leave recorded; mode.rs has cargo_capacity, fleet_label, sailing_requirement(Option<&Ruleset>); check_sailing emits one finding per code on the captain's SAIL line with the verbatim messages, counting report units aboard ± ENTER/LEAVE at report weights and sailing levels, silent on doubt (unknown hull, unstated weight, foreign unit aboard, MOVE touching the fleet). 2) The 14 semantics tests, 4 intents tests, 5 mode tests and two fixture rows pass; vocabulary regenerated. 3) Warnings tab group Sailing with 'Overloaded fleets' / 'Undercrewed fleets', on by default; SettingsDialog.test.tsx pins it. 4) pnpm run check:fast green. 5) ah-eet (scope C) exists and is not built here. AMENDED 2026-08-17 (second verification failure, plan at fault) — 6) sailing_levels_after_orders reads the ledger: men leaving a unit aboard reduce its sailing levels (level x men-after), men arriving into a unit aboard return None and silence that fleet's crew check for the month; Ruleset::is_man decides which tags are men and ruleset None silences it. 7) The aboard set is summed as Option<i64> so one unknowable unit silences the whole fleet's crew check; a None is never defaulted to 0. 8) ledger.doubted guards the crew finding alone, never the fleet-wide continue, so overload warnings that ship today are undisturbed. 9) The crew message says when the crew changed this month, verbatim: 'Raft [218] is short of sailors: 2 sailing levels aboard less 1 given away this month, it needs 2, so it will not sail'; unchanged crews keep the shipped sentence byte for byte. 10) The nine new semantics tests pass, a_full_crew_that_gives_nothing_away_still_sails included — that is the first failure's regression. 11) All four of Psylocke's verification cases re-run and pass: sail alone silent, give 0 1 GNOL warns undercrewed, ENTER 235 still warns overloaded, the Sailing group still toggles both codes. 12) The load half of check_sailing is unchanged.
notes:
Verification failed (2026-08-17, at origin/main cd092e6): case 3 of the verification, the silent case, warns. Fixture tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep, Ship [218] at ocean (38,44), stated 'Load: 70/450; Sailors: 2/2'. Drones (9508) aboard is 2 gnolls with sailing [SAIL] 1; ordering it SAIL produces 'Raft [218] is short of sailors: 1 sailing levels aboard, it needs 2, so it will not sail'. The fleet sails perfectly well and the bead's own validation requires silence here.

Cause: crew_sailing_levels (crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs:267) sums each unit's SAIL skill level once per unit and ignores the number of men in the unit. Atlantis counts sailing levels as level x men, which is what the report's own 'Sailors: H/N' H figure states - here 2, not 1. Any fleet crewed by multi-man units of low skill is warned about wrongly, and a false positive on a warning check is worse than a miss.

Note the function predates this bead (ah-2vy.2 wrote it for the movement planner); ah-j0e is what turned it into a warning a player sees, and the planner's speed reckoning is likely wrong in the same way. Fixing it needs the men count per unit available alongside the skill.
Second evidence, from ah-paj (filed by Beast while planning ah-eet, closed as superseded by this bead on the navigator's decision 2026-08-17). Same defect, a different fixture, plus the rules quote and why it went unnoticed:

Found while planning ah-eet, on a real fixture report, not from reading the code.

The 'fleet-undercrewed' check sums each aboard unit's sailing skill *level*, once per unit
(crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs, check_sailing: '.flat_map(|ordered| ordered.unit.skills.iter())
.filter(tag == SAIL).map(level).sum()'). The engine counts a level per *man*: a unit of 2 gnolls at
sailing 1 supplies 2 sailing levels, not 1.

Evidence, tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t24.rep:1359-1362 --

    + Ship [235] : Raft; Load: 220/450; Sailors: 2/2; MaxSpeed: 2.
      * Drones (10575), ... 2 gnolls [GNOL], 2180 silver [SILV]. Weight: 20.
        Skills: sailing [SAIL] 1 (30).
      * Drones (10594), ... 20 gnolls [GNOL]. Weight: 200. Skills: fishing [FISH] 1 (30).

The server states Sailors: 2/2 -- two levels aboard, two needed, so this Raft sails, and it does
sail in that turn's own orders template (line 2353, 'sail se ne'). Our sum is 1, so we warn
'Raft [235] is short of sailors: 1 sailing levels aboard, it needs 2, so it will not sail'. That is
a false warning on a committed fixture, against a fleet that sailed.

The rules agree with the server: 'The sailors are the number of skill levels of the Sailing skill
that must be aboard the ship' (tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html:3747-3752), and a
unit's skill level is held by each of its men.

Why it went unnoticed: every unit in the Longship fixture ah-j0e was built against holds exactly
one man (neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t41.rep:2018-2025 -- one centaur at SAIL 2, one centaur at SAIL 2,
Sailors: 4/4), where per-unit and per-man agree. Every unit fixture in the semantics tests has
men: 1 for the same reason.

The fix is one multiplication -- level * unit.men -- plus a test with a multi-man crew, and the
same question should be asked of movement/mode.rs:220 crew_sailing_levels, which the route planner
uses and which sums the same way. Direction of the defect: false warnings, on every fleet crewed by
units of more than one man, which is most of them.

Not ah-eet's scope: that bead is the load half of this check, and touches nothing on the crew side.
Navigator at verification 2026-08-17: the build is wrong, not the plan - 'planned' stays and this goes straight back to the fleet as an ordinary P0. Cases 1, 2 and 4 of the verification all passed: ship 235 warned as undercrewed, ENTER 235 by unit 8333 warned as overloaded, and the Sailing group with its two toggles was present, on by default and working. Only the false positive in case 3 is at fault; re-verify all four after the fix.
Verification failed (2026-08-17, at origin/main 0ed5814): case 2, the genuinely-undercrewed case, is silent when the crew is reduced by an order given this month.

Fixture tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep, Ship [218] (Raft) at ocean (38,44), stated 'Load: 70/450; Sailors: 2/2'. Unit Drones (9508) aboard is 2 gnolls at SAIL 1. Orders:

  give 0 1 GNOL
  sail N

After the GIVE the raft has 1 sailing level aboard against the 2 it needs, so it will not sail — and nothing warns. Case 1 (the previous failure, the false positive on the same ship) now passes: the per-man count from 8404597 is correct and is not what is wrong here.

Cause, and why it is the plan rather than the build: ah-j0e's own acceptance says the check counts 'report units aboard +/- ENTER/LEAVE at report weights and sailing levels' — a GIVE of men is not in that set, so the code matches its plan. ah-eet (scope C) then priced this month's GIVE/TAKE into each unit's *weight* and said in as many words that 'its sailors are still judged' on the report figures. So the crew side of a GIVE is covered by neither bead's design. The hole is in the plan, not in either implementation.

Navigator's call, 2026-08-17: plan wrong. For the amended plan to settle: whether the sailors count should follow this month's GIVE/TAKE of men the same way ah-eet made the load follow GIVE/TAKE of cargo (the symmetric answer, and the ledger ah-eet reused already tracks per-unit per-tag balances including men), and what 'silent on doubt' means here — a GIVE to a faction whose men have no known sailing level, or a TAKE bringing unknown men aboard. GIVE 0 (discarding men) is the case actually seen.
Verification passed 2026-08-17 at origin/main ec82563, on the third attempt. Both earlier failures re-checked and gone: the per-unit sailing count (fixed 8404597) and the crew unchanged by a GIVE of men (fixed ec82563, after Xavier amended the plan). The amended plan's answer - the sailors follow this month's GIVE/TAKE the way ah-eet made the load follow them - is what the message now states in as many words.

title: Beads wait ~7 minutes in a local gate CI repeats, and again on every BEHIND
description:
## Problem

Getting a bead from "implemented" to "merged" costs much more wall-clock than the actual build.
Measured on ah-k6i.4 (PR #284, a clean run with no rebase conflicts and zero review comments):

- Local `pnpm run check` before opening the PR: ~7 minutes wall clock, almost all of it the smoke
  suite (5.9m) plus build/pwa/rust/native on top. Lint/typecheck/unit were seconds.
- CI on the PR: ~3 minutes wall clock — the *same* suite, but parallelised across ~11 GitHub jobs.
- Review wait: ~2 minutes, running concurrently with CI since both start at PR-open.

So on a clean run, the single biggest cost is a local gate that duplicates work CI is about to do
anyway and is the thing that actually gates the merge — the local run only buys "catch it before a
human/reviewer sees it," which isn't worth ~7 minutes serialized on every bead.

It gets worse under fleet contention. `implement-bead`'s *Merging* section requires, on every
BEHIND: rebase locally, re-run the full local gate, wait for CI again — and the local gate takes a
machine-wide lock (the browser suites), so N implementers running concurrently queue behind each
other's local runs on top of paying the cost N times. With several implementers finishing near each
other, BEHIND keeps re-triggering and this cycle can repeat more than once per bead.

## Proposed changes (implement-bead skill + CI, for Xavier to plan and the navigator to decide)

1. **Stop running the full local `pnpm run check` before opening a PR.** Run only the fast, targeted
   checks locally (lint, typecheck, the touched package's unit tests) and let CI's parallel jobs do
   full verification — it's the thing that gates the merge regardless. Removes ~7 minutes and the
   local machine-wide lock's contention from every bead.

2. **Skip the local re-gate after a rebase when it's provably safe**, instead of always re-running
   the full local gate: if `git diff --stat <old-head>..<new-head> -- <touched files>` shows main's
   new commits didn't touch anything the bead's diff touches, push straight to CI rather than
   re-verifying locally first.

3. **Catch a BEHIND branch up on GitHub instead of locally.** Use the PR update-branch endpoint
