- The regression test from increment 3 — failing before, passing after; its level depends on the
  fault, and the plan above names the harness for each candidate.
- The status-line messages from increment 5 pinned by a unit test if shell-testable, else asserted
  in the smoke test.
- Everything existing stays green: comparison smoke tests (both projects), adapter parity suite,
  `cargo test --workspace` if the Rust side is touched.
- Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`, plus `pnpm run test:native` if the fix touches
  the Tauri path (and it likely does); full `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None taken here. Two standing instructions from the bead: any user-visible change beyond making the
existing design work goes to the navigator first; and if the investigation concludes
"discoverability" rather than "defect", the bead goes back to the navigator rather than being
decided by the implementer (park with `needs-ui-decision` + `human` per `beads-workflow`). The new
status-line failure messages follow the established idiom and are error reporting, not design.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the diff reports or how `ChangesDialog` presents it — wrong *contents* are a second
  bead, per the bead itself.
- Redesigning the comparison interaction.
- The web build, unless increment 2 finds it faulty too.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run test:native   # if the Tauri path was touched
pnpm run check
```

Human (navigator, and this one is the acceptance): on a desktop build, import two turns of one
faction, pick the older in the Turn picker — the chip shows `71 ⇄ 70`, the Changes chip appears,
and the dialog opens with differences matching the two reports.

## Known traps

- **`desktop-shell` smoke is the WASM core in Chrome, not Tauri.** Green smoke on both projects
  proves nothing about the desktop backend. Do not "reproduce" there and conclude the bug is gone;
  the native path is `pnpm run test:native` or a real desktop build.
- **The two clearing effects fire on their dependencies, not on intent** — `applyReport` clears the
  comparison on a new working turn and `enterGame` on a game switch (by design, from ah-jg6.3's
  plan); when instrumenting, distinguish "cleared by design after X" from "cleared in the same
  render it was set".
- **Instrumentation must not land.** The temporary logging from increment 1 is removed in
  increment 6; a `console.log` in `AppShell` will trip nothing automatic and live forever.
- **A `null` from `loadImportedTurn` has two different meanings** — genuinely absent row versus a
  wire-shape/argument mismatch swallowed by normalization. The parity harness with a hand-written
  snake_case payload is how to tell them apart without a desktop build in the loop.
- **`bd heartbeat` before the native suite** — wdio runs are long, and a claim's lease is five
  minutes.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — branch from `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: With two imported turns of one faction on the desktop build, picking another turn to compare against shows the comparison on the Turn chip, shows the Changes chip, and opens a dialog listing the unit, region and order differences between the two turns; the same works in the web build; a regression test covers the fault found and fails without the fix.
notes:
Investigation (increment 1-2), findings before any fix:

Ruled OUT:
- Wire-shape/casing mismatch between core-client's Tauri adapter and core-tauri's DTOs: verified
  matching exactly (rename_all = "snake_case" on the Rust #[tauri::command] args, "camelCase" on
  the DTOs, and normalizeImportedTurnRecord in core-client/src/index.ts handles both cases).
- The two comparison-clearing effects (AppShell.tsx ~836 new-working-turn, ~1533 game-change):
  both are one-shot imperative calls inside unrelated handlers (applyReport-style flow, enterGame),
  not live effects keyed on anything handleSelectComparisonTurn touches. Not reachable from the
  turn-picker click path.
- Rust/persistence layer defect: wrote and ran a throwaway Rust test in core-tauri importing two
  turns (March=2, April=3) then loading the OLDER one (2) via command_load_imported_turn while the
  "working" turn would be 3 - passed cleanly. The existing Rust test only ever loaded the
  just-committed turn, so this scenario (load a turn OTHER than the latest) was untested but is not
  broken.
- Could not run the actual native (Tauri/WebKitGTK) suite in this environment - `test:native` is
  Linux-only per wdio.conf.ts's own comment (WKWebView on macOS exposes no automation endpoint), and
  this session is on macOS. No real desktop GUI available to click through by hand either.

CONFIRMED, real code defects (both are "silent dead end" bugs per the bead's own candidate #1 and
plan increment 5, matching "no dialog at all" exactly):
1. packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx handleSelectComparisonTurn (~2145-2179): zero
   try/catch around `await client.loadImportedTurn(...)` and the subsequent `await parse(...)`, and
   its only caller does `void handleSelectComparisonTurn(turnNumber)` (~2419). Any thrown/rejected
   error - IPC failure, JSON deserialize failure, whatever - becomes an unhandled promise rejection:
   nothing shown to the user, exactly the reported symptom. The `record === null` branch (~2167-2169)
   is the same failure mode already spelled out in the bead.
2. packages/core-client/src/index.ts `loadImportedTurn` (~1818-1824) checks only `value === null`,
   NOT `undefined` - inconsistent with the very next function, `loadLatestImportedTurn`
   (~1825-1829), whose comment explains serde_wasm_bindgen can emit either for Rust's None. If the
   adapter ever returns undefined here, normalizeImportedTurnRecord(undefined) throws, which (via
   defect #1 above) vanishes silently.

Web build (increment 2): the desktop-shell Playwright project runs the built web bundle against the
WASM core in Chrome (not the Tauri path) and already has two passing smoke tests exercising this
exact flow end-to-end ("a second turn can be compared and dismissed", "the changes dialog reads a
real pair" in tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts) - web is not reproducing the bug today.

Decision: could not get a live desktop-only repro (no macOS Tauri automation, no GUI in this
environment) beyond the two confirmed defects above, which are real, present, and match "no dialog,
not even an empty one" exactly. Proceeding per plan increment 5: fix both defects (error handling +
status-line message on every silent exit in handleSelectComparisonTurn, undefined-vs-null fix in
loadImportedTurn), with regression tests pinning each. Not a "discoverability" finding, so not
escalating to the navigator.

title: Orders export on the desktop offers no save dialog
description:
# Summary

Exporting orders from the desktop app opens no save dialog. The player picks "Export orders" (or the
long-format variant), nothing is asked, and either no file appears or one appears somewhere the
player was never told about. The orders file is the one file the whole application exists to produce
— it has to be found again and mailed to the game server — so a save the player cannot locate makes
the desktop build unusable for its main purpose without going hunting in the downloads folder.

# Cause

The machinery for this already exists and the orders export simply does not use it.
`packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts` defines a `TextFileSaver` port — "a shell that can put a file
where the player asks and say where that was" — which the desktop implements with a native dialog in
`apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts` and hands to `AppShell` as the `saveTextFile` prop
(`apps/desktop/src/App.tsx:23`). Only the **map** export uses it: `exportMap` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx:1976-1987` calls `saveTextFile` when the shell offers one
and falls back to `downloadTextFile` otherwise.

`exportOrders` (`AppShell.tsx:1911`) and `exportOrdersLong` (`AppShell.tsx:1924`) call
`downloadTextFile` unconditionally — an anchor download, which is all a browser can do but which on
the desktop reports no path and lands wherever the embedded webview puts it.

The game backup at `AppShell.tsx:1594` has the same shape and is worth deciding on in passing; the
bug as reported is the orders export.

# Scope

- Route both orders exports through `saveTextFile` when the shell provides one, falling back to
  `downloadTextFile` when it does not — the same pattern `exportMap` already uses.
- The dialog is pre-filled with the existing name, `orders-turn-<n>.txt`, and the player may change
  the name and the directory.
- A cancelled dialog writes nothing and leaves the workspace exactly as it was — no error, no
  "exported" feedback.
- The web build is unchanged: it keeps the browser download.

# Out of scope

- Changing the generated orders text, the file name scheme, or the long/plain distinction.
- Remembering the last-used directory between exports.
- The game backup export, unless it falls out for free — if it is worth doing, split a child bead.

# Validation

- `pnpm test` (or the repo's usual gate) green, with new unit coverage on `AppShell` proving the
  orders export calls the injected `saveTextFile` when present and `downloadTextFile` when absent,
  and that a cancelled save (`null`) writes nothing.
- Manual on a desktop build: load a report, edit an order, export both plain and long orders — a
  native save dialog appears each time, the chosen file exists at the chosen path with the expected
  content, and cancelling leaves no file behind.
design:
## Context

Navigator-filed P0. On the desktop, "Export orders" (plain and long) opens no save dialog: both
callbacks call `downloadTextFile` unconditionally (`AppShell.tsx`, `exportOrders` and
`exportOrdersLong`, currently near :1912 and :1925), which in the embedded webview reports no path
and lands the file wherever the webview puts it. The orders file is the artifact the whole
application exists to produce, and the machinery already exists: the `TextFileSaver` port
(`packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts:21`), implemented by the desktop with a native dialog
(`apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts`, `save` + `writeTextFile`, `null` on cancel) and handed to
`AppShell` as the `saveTextFile` prop — used today by the **map export alone** (`exportMap`,
AppShell.tsx:1976-1992: saver when present, `downloadTextFile` otherwise, cancel returns quietly).

The fix is to make the orders exports take the same fork — and to extract that fork into one shared
helper so a fourth exporter cannot get it wrong again.

Verified against the code on main at planning time; all three files read as the bead describes.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts`** — the reusable fork, beside the port it uses:

  ```ts
  /** Saves through the shell's saver when there is one, else the browser download.
   *  Resolves with the path written, "" for a browser download, or null when cancelled. */
  export async function deliverTextFile(
    saver: TextFileSaver | undefined,
    fileName: string,
    text: string,
    mimeType: string,
    download: typeof downloadTextFile = downloadTextFile
  ): Promise<string | null>
  ```

  The `download` parameter exists for the tests (vitest runs without a DOM; `downloadTextFile`
  touches `document`) and defaults to the real one — callers never pass it.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** — three edits:
  - `exportOrders` and `exportOrdersLong` become async and call
    `deliverTextFile(saveTextFile, name, text, "text/plain")`. A cancelled save resolves `null` and
    nothing else happens — no error, no feedback, the workspace untouched (the bead's requirement).
    A failed native write is caught and logged (`console.error`); richer failure surfacing is out of
    scope and matches the download path, which has no failure signal either.
  - `exportMap` swaps its inline fork for the same helper — behaviour identical: `null` leaves the
    export dialog standing, a path (or `""` from the download branch) closes it. Its existing
    comment block moves to the helper.
  - The file name stays `orders-turn-<n>.txt` for both orders exports (same name on purpose — the
    doc comment at `exportOrdersLong` explains why; do not "fix" it).
- **Nothing changes in `apps/desktop/`** — `desktopTextFileSaver` already pre-fills
  `defaultPath: fileName` and lets the player change name and directory, and already returns `null`
  on cancel without writing.
- **The web build is unchanged by construction**: `saveTextFile` is `undefined` there, so
  `deliverTextFile` takes the download branch.

## Increments

1. **The fork, alone.** Opening failing test: `downloadFile.test.ts` (new) › "delivers through the
   saver when there is one" — injected saver resolves a path, injected download must not be called;
   siblings: "falls back to the download without a saver" (download called once with name, text,
   mime; resolves `""`), "a cancelled save downloads nothing" (saver resolves `null`, download not
   called, result `null`). GREEN: `deliverTextFile`.
2. **The orders exports take it.** Opening failing test: in the AppShell test suite
   (`AppShell.test.ts`, or a focused new file following its pattern) › "the orders export saves
   through the shell's saver when present" and "…downloads in a browser shell" — render the shell
   with/without a stubbed `saveTextFile` prop, trigger the export, assert which path ran and that a
   `null` (cancel) leaves no other observable effect. GREEN: the two callbacks rewritten.
3. **The map export reuses it.** No new behaviour — opening check is the existing map-export tests
   staying green after the swap, plus one assertion that a cancelled save still leaves the export
   dialog open (pin it if no existing test does).

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, `packages/shared`):
- `downloadFile.test.ts` — the three fork cases above, plus "a saver that throws rejects into the
  caller's catch" so increment 2's logging path is honest.
- The AppShell-level export tests from increment 2; every existing export/menu test stays green.

Smoke (Playwright): none new — the suite runs the web build, where behaviour is unchanged; the
existing export-menu smoke coverage is the regression net.

Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke` (unchanged, must stay green); full `pnpm run check`
before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None to ask: the dialog is the OS's own, the pre-filled name, cancel behaviour and web fallback are
all specified in the navigator's own bug report (gh-issue-shaped bead description), and no new
surface is added. The navigator ranked this P0 on 2026-08-14.

Decided in passing, as the bead invites: the **game backup export** (`AppShell.tsx:1594`, same
shape) is *not* folded in — it is split out as its own unranked bead (see Out of scope) so this fix
stays exactly the reported defect.

## Out of scope

- The game backup export — split to bead `ah-7pa`'s sibling created at P4 during planning (titled
  "Game backup export bypasses the desktop save dialog"); it will reuse `deliverTextFile` and is
  trivial once this lands.
- Changing the orders text, the name scheme, or the long/plain distinction.
- Remembering the last-used directory between exports.
- Any new failure UI for a failed disk write.
- Automating the native dialog in tests — the OS dialog cannot be driven by the suites; the manual
  check below covers it.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check   # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, on a desktop build — the part no suite can reach): load a report, export
orders plain and long — a native dialog appears each time, pre-filled `orders-turn-<n>.txt`, the
chosen file exists at the chosen path with the expected content; cancel leaves no file and no
message; the web build still plainly downloads.

## Known traps

- **`downloadTextFile` touches `document`** — a node-env vitest test that lets the real fallback
  run dies on it; the injected `download` parameter exists precisely so tests never do. Do not
  switch the suite to jsdom for this.
- **The two orders callbacks become async** — they are wired into `ExportMenu` handlers; fire-and-
  forget is fine, but an unhandled rejection is not: the catch in increment 2 is load-bearing, and
  the "saver that throws" unit test keeps it from being simplified away.
- **A cancelled map save must keep the export dialog open** (the comment in `exportMap` says why);
  when swapping in the helper, preserve the `null → return` before `setExportOpen(false)`.
- **Do not deliver the orders export through a new name** — plain and long share
  `orders-turn-<n>.txt` deliberately (`exportOrdersLong`'s doc comment).
- **The desktop bundle also runs as a plain web page** (dev server, smoke preview) —
  `desktopTextFileSaver` returns `undefined` without a Tauri runtime, so never gate on "is the
  desktop build" — gate on the saver's presence, as `exportMap` does.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree; branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: Exporting orders (plain or long) in the desktop app opens a native save dialog pre-filled with orders-turn-<n>.txt; the player can change name and directory; the file is written where they chose; cancelling writes nothing and shows no error; the web build still downloads as before.

title: Status bar wraps and faction dropdown resizes to avoid clipped content
description:
The top status bar (import/export buttons etc.) can get wider than the window, and currently just overflows/gets clipped instead of adapting. Similarly, the faction info dropdown (opened by clicking the faction name) is a fixed, short height that forces scrolling to see all faction details.

Reported by rmstdope (Henrik Kurelid) in GitHub issue #188.
design:
## Context

GitHub issue #188 (the navigator's own report) names two defects in shipped UI, and the navigator
ranked this bead P0. First: the top status bar (`AppHeader`) is a single fixed-height flex row with
`whitespace-nowrap` and no wrapping or shrinking anywhere, so on a window narrower than its content
the right-hand end — the Export button, the settings gear — is simply clipped off-screen. Second: the
faction view's scroll body is capped at `max-h-[40vh]`, so with a real faction (32 declared attitudes
in the turn-71 fixture) it always scrolls, even when the window below it is mostly empty.

The navigator chose the treatments, mockup at `docs/ui/status-bar-wrap.html` (merged via PR #190):

1. **Grouped wrap.** The header becomes two groups — game state on the left (wordmark, game
   indicator, turn, faction, merged/import-status/messages/problems/battles chips), actions on the
   right (Import, Export, settings gear). When the window is too narrow, the actions group drops to a
   second row **as one unit and stays right-aligned**; the game-state group may also wrap internally
   on very narrow windows. One row whenever everything fits, exactly as today.
2. **Popovers grow to the window.** The fixed-percentage caps go: a popover body's ceiling becomes
   the viewport height minus a small fixed allowance, so it scrolls only when genuinely out of room.
   The navigator chose to apply this to **all four capped header popovers**: FactionPanel (40vh),
   MergedFactionsPanel (40vh), ProblemsPanel (50vh), TurnMessagesPanel (60vh).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx` — the whole change to the bar lives here. Today the
  root (line ~213) is `flex h-9 flex-none items-center gap-3.5 border-b border-edge bg-panel px-3
  text-[11.5px] whitespace-nowrap` with a `<span className="flex-1" />` spacer (line ~409) splitting
  left from right. Restructure: root becomes wrapping (`flex flex-wrap`, `min-h-9` instead of `h-9`,
  keep `flex-none items-center gap-x-3.5 ... whitespace-nowrap`); the elements up to and including the
  battles chip go into a game-state group (`flex h-9 flex-wrap items-center gap-3.5 min-w-0`); the
  hidden file input, Import, Export wrapper and settings wrapper go into an actions group
  (`ml-auto flex h-9 items-center gap-3.5`). `ml-auto` replaces the `flex-1` spacer — it right-aligns
  the group on a shared row *and* after wrapping to its own row; delete the spacer. Give the actions
  group `data-testid="header-actions"`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/GameGate.tsx` (line ~46) — duplicates the header class string
  verbatim for the no-game screen. Mirror the root-class change (`h-9` → `min-h-9`, add `flex-wrap`)
  so the two headers cannot drift; it has no actions group to build.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/FactionPanel.tsx` (line ~92, `max-h-[40vh] overflow-y-auto p-2`),
  `MergedFactionsPanel.tsx` (line ~80), `ProblemsPanel.tsx` (line ~86), `TurnMessagesPanel.tsx`
  (line ~117) — replace each cap with the shared clamp described below.
- **The clamp**: add `export const POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H = "max-h-[calc(100vh-6rem)]"` to
  `packages/shared/src/workspace/primitives.tsx` (the existing shared-primitives home) and use it in
  all four panels. `6rem` = up to two 36px header rows plus the `mt-1` anchor gap plus ~20px of
  breathing room at the window's bottom edge — a pure-CSS clamp, no JS measurement. Tailwind v4 scans
  source text for class literals (`@source` in `theme.css`), so the literal must appear in the
  constant's definition (it does) — do not build the class name by string concatenation.
- **Reuse, don't invent**: the popovers' anchoring (`absolute left-0 top-full z-20 mt-1 ...`),
  dismissal effects and drag-propagation guards are all untouched. No new popover component, no
  collision arithmetic (`unitTooltip.ts` stays where it is), no breakpoint utilities.

## Increments

1. **The header wraps as two groups.** Opening failing test:
   `AppHeader.test.tsx` › "the header wraps and keeps the actions grouped right" — render via the
   existing `draw()` helper, assert the root's class contains `flex-wrap` and `min-h-9` and no longer
   contains bare `h-9` on the root, and that a `header-actions` element carrying `ml-auto` contains
   the Export menu trigger. Then restructure `AppHeader.tsx`, mirror the root class in `GameGate.tsx`
   (assert its markup too — it renders standalone, cheap to snapshot the class), run the full
   AppHeader/GameGate unit suites green.
2. **Narrow-window smoke.** Opening failing test: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` › "a narrow window
   wraps the header instead of clipping it" — `page.setViewportSize({ width: 520, height: 720 })`,
   then assert `export-menu` and `settings-indicator` have bounding boxes fully inside the viewport
   (x + width ≤ 520), and that `app-header`'s bounding-box height is greater than one row (> 40px),
   proving the wrap rather than a shrink. This should go green with increment 1's code; if it does
   not, the code is wrong, not the test.
3. **Popover bodies grow to the window.** Opening failing test: `FactionPanel.test.tsx` › "the body
   is clamped to the window, not to 40vh" — assert the rendered body class contains
   `max-h-[calc(100vh-6rem)]` and not `max-h-[40vh]`. Add the `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H` constant, apply to
   all four panels, with matching one-line class assertions in the other three panels' test files
   (create a minimal test file where one does not exist).
4. **Faction-view height smoke.** Opening failing test: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` › "the
   faction view uses the window before it scrolls" — at the default 1280×720 viewport open the
   faction chip (the existing test at :230 shows how), and assert the panel's footnote line
   ("⌂ marks a faction…", give it a testid if it lacks one) is in the viewport via
   `toBeInViewport()` — with 32 attitudes that line sits below the old 40vh cap, so this fails
   against the old clamp and passes with the new one. Also assert the panel's bounding-box bottom
   ≤ 720, pinning "grows but never past the window".

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, SSR string assertions — the house style in these files):
- `AppHeader.test.tsx`: the new wrap/grouping test above; the two existing faction-chip tests must
  stay green (the chip markup is untouched).
- `GameGate` class-parity assertion (in its existing test file if present, else a new minimal one).
- `FactionPanel.test.tsx`: the clamp test; all 11 existing content tests stay green.
- Class assertions for `MergedFactionsPanel`, `ProblemsPanel`, `TurnMessagesPanel`.

Smoke (Playwright, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, both `web` and `desktop-shell` projects):
- The two new tests from increments 2 and 4.
- The existing faction-view tests (:230–:300) and every header-text assertion must stay green — the
  header's *content* and testids are unchanged, only its layout containers move.

Suites to run: `pnpm run test` (unit) and `pnpm run test:smoke` at minimum; full gate before PR.

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator, 2026-08-14; mockup committed at `docs/ui/status-bar-wrap.html`
(PR #190):
- Wrap treatment: **B, grouped wrap** — actions drop as one right-aligned unit — over A, free flow.
- Panel height: **grow to the window** with a small bottom margin, over merely raising the cap.
- Scope of the height fix: **all four capped header popovers**, not the faction view alone.

## Out of scope

- `ExportMenu`, `GamePicker`, `BadgeMenu` — short fixed menus with no vh cap; they don't scroll today
  and gain nothing from the clamp.
- Truncating or abbreviating long faction/game names (`truncate`/`min-w-0` ellipsis work): the chosen
  fix is wrapping, not shrinking.
- Any collision/flip logic for popovers near the window's right edge (the `w-80` panels can still
  clip horizontally on very narrow windows — a separate defect if the navigator ever reports it).
- `ShortcutHelp`, `UnitTooltip`, and the workspace dock panels — already viewport-aware or unaffected.
- Mobile breakpoints/responsive work anywhere else in the app.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run lint
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check        # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, post-merge is fine): drag the window narrow — the Import/Export/⚙ group drops
to a second right-aligned row and nothing clips; open the faction view on the turn-71 fixture — all
five attitude levels visible without scrolling on a 720px-tall window.

## Known traps

- **The `<header>` is the file drop target** (`onDragOver`/`onDrop` on the root). The new group
  wrappers must not swallow or stop those events; the popovers already `stopPropagation` deliberately
  — leave that alone.
- **Popover dismissal keys off `panelRef.current.parentElement`** (comment at AppHeader.tsx:254–259):
  each chip's own `relative` wrapper must remain its popover's *direct* parent. Wrapping a new flex
  group *around* those wrappers is safe; merging or re-parenting them breaks outside-press dismissal
  for both faction popovers.
- **`GameGate.tsx:46` duplicates the header class string.** Change it in step with AppHeader or the
  no-game screen keeps the old fixed-height bar.
- **`AppHeader.test.tsx`'s `draw()` hand-builds the full ~30-prop object**, so any new AppHeader prop
  breaks that file — this plan adds none, and none should be needed.
- **No narrow-viewport Playwright project exists** (both projects are Desktop Chrome 1280×720): the
  narrow test must call `page.setViewportSize` itself and must not assume other tests' viewport.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled** — a `test:pwa` run
  straight after a smoke run fails with worker timeouts that look real; run `pnpm run check`'s order
  or rebuild between.
- **Tailwind v4, no config file**: class literals must appear verbatim in scanned source
  (`@source` globs in `theme.css`). Keep `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H` a single literal; never assemble
  `max-h-[calc(...)]` from pieces.
acceptance_criteria:
- When the status bar's contents (import/export buttons, faction info, etc.) exceed the available window width, it wraps to a second row instead of overflowing or requiring the window to be resized.
- The faction info dropdown (opened by clicking the faction name) extends further downward to show more/all of its content before falling back to internal scrolling.
- Both behaviours verified at a few window sizes, including a narrow one that currently triggers the clipping.

title: Battles view: unscrollable side lists, empty assassinations, split routs
description:
# Summary

The battles view (`BattlesDialog`, delivered by ah-1is.2 in PR #173) has five defects that make
larger and unusual battles unreadable. Reported by the navigator from a real turn report.

# The defects

1. **The ATTACKERS and DEFENDERS lists do not scroll.** Past roughly ten entries per side the rows
   are compressed on top of each other instead of the list scrolling, and the side becomes
   unreadable. Each list needs its own scroll region with a sane minimum row height.

2. **Outcome is below the rounds.** The outcome section should come *before* the round-by-round
   detail — it is what the reader wants first, and the rounds are the supporting detail.

3. **Assassinations render almost empty.** An assassination shows no attackers and no defenders,
   and the outcome shows only the bare word "Casualties" with nothing after it. Expected:
   - Attackers: when the assassin is unknown (as it is for the victim's faction), show `?`.
   - Defenders: show the assassinated unit.
   - Outcome: the actual casualties, not a bare heading.

4. **The right-hand panel keeps its scroll position across battles.** Switching to another battle in
   the list should always start the detail panel back at the top; today it stays wherever the
   previous battle was scrolled to, so a new battle can open mid-way down.

5. **A rout is parsed as a separate battle.** When a side is routed the rout appears as its own
   entry in the battle list instead of being folded into the battle it came from. The rout belongs
   to the originating battle.

# Scope

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/BattlesDialog.tsx` — 1, 2, 3 (rendering), 4
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.ts` — 3 (assassination shape), 5 (rout grouping)
- `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` — only if the assassination/rout defects turn out to originate
  in the parser rather than in the TS layer; check before changing it.

# Out of scope

- Any redesign of the battles view beyond these five fixes.
- New battle information not already present in the report.

# Validation

- `pnpm test` (or the workspace's test task) covering `battles.test.ts` and `BattlesDialog.test.tsx`
- Manual: open a turn report containing (a) a battle with more than ten units per side,
  (b) an assassination, (c) a battle ending in a rout; confirm each renders as described above.
design:
## Context

The battles view (`BattlesDialog`, ah-1is.2, PR #173) fails on real turn reports in five ways the
navigator reported from play: side rosters compress instead of scrolling, the outcome sits below the
round-by-round detail, assassinations render as empty sections, the detail panel keeps its scroll
position when switching battles, and a rout is split off as a battle of its own. When this lands,
large battles, assassinations and routs all read correctly from the fixtures we already have.

Root causes, confirmed by reading the code and fixtures:

1. **Unscrollable rosters** — the roster `<ul>` (BattlesDialog.tsx ~line 286) is a bounded flex
   column (`flex max-h-48 ... overflow-y-auto`) and each `<li>` has `overflow-hidden`, so flexbox
   *shrinks the rows* to fit `max-h-48` instead of overflowing into the scroll. Rows need
   `shrink-0`.
2. **Outcome below rounds** — plain ordering of blocks in `BattleDetail`.
3. **Empty assassinations** — a victim-side assassination is a one-line battle,
   `L Arslan (1446) is assassinated in forest (43,79) in Utso!` (fixture
   `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f39-t17.rep` line 113; also `g7-f62-t20` line 34,
   `g3-f42-t82` line 277). `parse_headline` in `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` only knows the
   `attacks` form, so every structured field is `None` and the view renders empty ATTACKERS,
   DEFENDERS and a bare "Casualties" heading.
4. **Sticky scroll** — `BattleDetail` is one component reused across selections; its scroll
   container is never reset. Remounting it per battle (React `key`) resets scrollTop for free.
5. **Split routs** — `opens_a_battle` treats any indent-0 line ending in `!` (except
   `is destroyed!`) as a new headline. `Informator (1470) is routed!` appears mid-battle (same
   fixture, line 71), followed by `The Explorers (6363) gets a free round of attacks.`, a losses
   line, and a `Free round statistics:` block — all of which currently become a nonsense second
   battle.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` — the parser fixes (defects 3 and 5).
  - Reuse `split_trailing_id` and `parse_coordinate` (already imported) for the assassination
    headline; the location tail `in <terrain> (<x>,<y>) in <province>` has the same shape the
    `attacks` arm already parses — factor that tail parse out of `parse_headline` and share it.
  - Add `pub assassination: bool` to `Battle` with `#[serde(default)]`.
  - In `opens_a_battle`, exclude `is routed!` the same way `is destroyed!` is excluded.
  - In `parse_one_battle`, a body ending in `is routed!` closes the current round and opens a new
    `BattleRound { number: None, .. }` (phase `Round`) with the rout line as its first `lines`
    entry; the label `Free round statistics` switches to `Phase::RoundStatistics` (extend the
    `strip_suffix(" statistics")` arm: `"Free round"` is valid alongside `Round N`).
- `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` — mirror the new field on the `Battle` type (~line 492):
  `assassination?: boolean` (optional, because stored `parsedPayloadJson` from imports made before
  this change lacks the key). No other TS layer touches the wire shape — `crates/core-wasm`
  serializes `ParsedReport` generically via `serde_json`, so nothing there changes.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.ts` — the view logic, kept DOM-free per this file's own
  doc comment:
  - `roundLabel(round, index): string` — `"Free round"` when `number` is null, else
    `` `Round ${number}` `` (fall back to `index + 1` as today when null but the battle is not
    following the rout shape is unnecessary: after this change the only `number: null` rounds the
    parser produces are free rounds, so null ⇒ "Free round").
  - `assassinationView(battle): { attackers: string[]; defenders: string[]; casualtyText: string } | null` —
    null unless `battle.assassination`; otherwise attackers `["?"]`, defenders
    `["<name> (<id>)"]` from `battle.defender`, and casualty text `"<name> (<id>) is assassinated"`.
    (Shape at your discretion; keep it a pure function so it tests without a DOM.)
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/BattlesDialog.tsx` — the rendering (defects 1, 2, 3, 4):
  - `shrink-0` on the roster `<li>` rows; the `max-h-48` (~10 rows) cap stays, per the navigator.
  - Move the Outcome `<div>` (and, judgement call: the battle-level `StatisticsDisclosure` can
    stay last) above the Rounds block.
  - `key` the `<BattleDetail>` in `BattlesDialog` by the selected battle (e.g. `key={selectedIndex}`)
    so switching battles remounts the scroll container at the top.
  - When `assassinationView` returns non-null, render its attacker/defender strings as the roster
    rows (the `Roster` component takes `BattleUnit[]`; either synthesize minimal entries or render
    plain rows — but do not print "faction not shown" after `?`), and its `casualtyText` as the
    Casualties `<dd>`.
  - Round headings and the round statistics disclosure use `roundLabel` (a free round's disclosure
    reads "Free round statistics", matching the report).

Existing tests to build on: `battle.rs`'s `mod tests` (string fixtures via `unwrap_lines`),
`battles.test.ts`, and `BattlesDialog.test.tsx` (renders with `renderToStaticMarkup` — there is no
jsdom in this repo, so assert on markup strings and order, and keep decisions in `battles.ts` where
they test directly).

## Increments

Work test-first; each increment opens with its failing test.

1. **Parser: rout stays in its battle.** Failing test
   `folds_a_rout_into_the_battle_it_came_from` in `battle.rs`: a fixture-shaped string (crib lines
   40–90 of `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f39-t17.rep`) parses to **one** battle whose last round has
   `number: None`, whose `lines` start with the rout line and include the free-round narrative,
   whose `losses` carry the post-rout casualty, and whose `statistics` hold the
   `Free round statistics` block.
2. **Parser: assassination headline recognised.** Failing test
   `reads_the_assassination_headline`: `L Arslan (1446) is assassinated in forest (43,79) in Utso!`
   yields `assassination: true`, `defender: Some(L Arslan/1446)`, `attacker: None`,
   terrain/coordinate/province filled. Companion assertion: a normal `attacks` battle has
   `assassination: false`, and `keeps_a_headline_it_does_not_recognise` still passes.
3. **Type mirror + view logic.** Failing tests in `battles.test.ts`: `roundLabel` (numbered and
   free rounds), `assassinationView` (the three strings above; null for a normal battle), and
   `summarise` of an assassination battle now yields a `hex` (coordinate is parsed).
4. **Dialog: outcome first, assassination rendering, round labels.** Failing tests in
   `BattlesDialog.test.tsx` (static markup): the Outcome heading appears **before** "Rounds" in the
   markup string (`indexOf` comparison); an assassination battle's markup contains `?` in the
   attackers list, the victim in the defenders list, and
   `L Arslan (1446) is assassinated` in the Casualties row; a free round renders the heading
   `Free round`.
5. **Dialog: roster rows scroll, detail resets.** Failing test: roster `<li>` markup carries
   `shrink-0`. The `key`-remount for scroll reset is not observable in static markup — implement
   it in the same increment and cover it under Validation's manual check.

## The test plan

- **Rust unit** (`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`): the two new parser tests above plus the
  existing `battle.rs` suite unchanged — especially `keeps_a_headline_it_does_not_recognise`
  (an *unrecognised* `!` line must still open a battle) and `records_the_line_span_of_each_battle`.
- **TS unit** (`pnpm test`, which runs the workspace suites): `battles.test.ts` additions pin the
  pure view logic; `BattlesDialog.test.tsx` additions pin markup order and assassination/rout
  rendering. All existing cases keep passing.
- **Browser/smoke**: no new smoke test — the dialog already has coverage and the new behaviour is
  markup-level; the scroll behaviours are checked manually (below).

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator on 2026-08-14 (question tool; no mockup needed — these are
fixes to a dialog whose layout the navigator already chose in `docs/ui/battles-view.html`):

- **Free-round heading: "Free round"**, matching the report's own wording; its statistics
  disclosure reads "Free round statistics".
- **Assassination casualties row: `L Arslan (1446) is assassinated`** — the fact the report
  states, without repeating the location already shown in the panel header. No invented numbers.
- **Roster list height: keep the ~10-row cap** (`max-h-48`) with each list scrolling within
  itself.
- Already specified in the bead by the navigator: attackers show `?` when the assassin is unknown,
  defenders show the assassinated unit, and Outcome renders above the rounds.

## Out of scope

- The assassin-side wording (`X attempts to assassinate Y ...`) — no fixture contains it; the
  parser's unrecognised-headline fallback still applies to it, and it can get its own bead if it
  ever shows up rendered poorly.
- Any redesign of the battles view beyond the five fixes; new battle information not in the report.
- Modelling round/battle statistics field-by-field; they stay verbatim text.
- Backfilling stored imports: an already-imported turn keeps its stored parsed payload until
  re-imported. (`assassination` is optional on the TS side precisely so old payloads still render —
  as today, i.e. with the defect, until re-import.)

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm test
pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck
cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Manual, before the PR (the two scroll behaviours cannot be pinned without a DOM): import
`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` (large battles + an assassination) and
`g7-f39-t17.rep` (rout + assassination), open Battles, and confirm: (a) a side with >10 units
scrolls inside its list; (b) the assassination shows `?` / victim / `... is assassinated`; (c) the
rout battle is one entry whose detail ends with a "Free round"; (d) Outcome renders above Rounds;
(e) scrolling battle A down and clicking battle B opens B at the top.

## Known traps

- **`keeps_a_headline_it_does_not_recognise` is load-bearing.** The `!`-heuristic exists so that
  *unrecognised* headlines still open battles. Exclude exactly `is routed!` (suffix match, like
  `is destroyed!`); do not tighten the heuristic to recognised forms only.
- **`number: null` already means something in the UI.** Today `Round {round.number ?? index + 1}`
  invents a number for null; after this change null means "free round" and must render as such —
  update both the round heading and `StatisticsDisclosure` (its `data-testid` is built from
  `number`, so give the free round a stable testid, e.g. `round-statistics-free`).
- **Old stored payloads lack the new field.** `parsed_payload_json` is persisted per imported turn
  (SQLite / browser storage) and compared as a string; a payload written before this change has no
  `assassination` key. Rust: `#[serde(default)]`. TS: `assassination?: boolean` and truthy checks.
  Also expect `parsedChanged: true` on re-import of an unchanged report — that is the diff working,
  not a bug.
- **No jsdom.** `BattlesDialog.test.tsx` renders with `renderToStaticMarkup`: effects do not run
  and scroll state does not exist. Scroll reset must be the `key`-remount (an effect would neither
  run in tests nor be simpler), and scrolling assertions belong in the manual check.
- **`bd show`'s pretty renderer mangles Markdown** — read this plan back with
  `bd show ah-r12 --json`.
- **Shared checkout.** Verify the branch before every commit (other sessions move HEAD), branch
  from `origin/main` (`git checkout main` fails while another worktree holds it), and put the bead
  id in the commit subject (`fix(ah-r12): ...`).
acceptance_criteria: Attacker and defender lists scroll independently and stay readable past ten entries; the outcome section renders above the rounds; an assassination shows ? for an unknown attacker, the assassinated unit as defender, and real casualties in the outcome; selecting another battle resets the detail panel to the top; a rout appears inside its originating battle rather than as a separate battle

title: Skip CI for docs-only PRs
description:
PRs that only touch files under docs/ currently trigger the full CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) — wasm build, JS checks, Rust checks, Playwright smoke/pwa suites, and the native Tauri e2e job. None of these depend on documentation content, so a docs-only PR waits on the same ~10+ minute pipeline as a code change before it can be merged, even though nothing it changed can affect the outcome.

This bead is about making docs-only PRs quickly mergeable: when a PR's diff is confined to docs/, CI should not need to run (or should complete near-instantly) to satisfy branch protection.
design:
## Context

A PR that touches only `docs/` waits on the whole of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the wasm build,
the JS checks, the Rust job, four sharded Playwright runs, the PWA run, a macOS compile and the
Linux native end-to-end suite — before it can merge. Nothing in it can be affected by a documentation
change. The planning role produces such PRs routinely (the mockup PRs, #152 and #153), so this is
paid several times a week.

The `main` ruleset requires ten status checks by name, and they are:

    checks · rust · wasm · pwa · native · desktop-shell
    smoke (web, 1, 2) · smoke (web, 2, 2) · smoke (desktop-shell, 1, 2) · smoke (desktop-shell, 2, 2)

with `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, so the branch must also be up to date with main.
All ten must report; the ruleset is not to be edited by this bead.

**The mechanism is documented, and the two cases are opposite.** GitHub's *Troubleshooting required
status checks*:

> If a workflow is skipped due to path filtering, branch filtering or a commit message, then checks
> associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those
> checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.
>
> If, however, a job within a workflow is skipped due to a conditional, it will report its status as
> "Success".

and successful statuses are `success`, `skipped` and `neutral`. So the workflow must keep running on
every pull request, and the *jobs* inside it are what a docs-only diff skips. `paths-ignore` is the
trap, not the tool.

When this lands: a docs-only PR is mergeable in about a minute, and everything else runs exactly as
it does today.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - `on: pull_request` keeps **no** `paths` or `paths-ignore`. That is load-bearing; see the quote
    above.
  - A new first job, `changes`, whose single output `code` says whether anything outside `docs/`
    was touched. It needs no checkout and no toolchain: `gh api
    repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}/files --paginate --jq
    '.[].filename'`, and `code=true` unless every line begins `docs/`. `gh` is preinstalled on the
    runners; `GITHUB_TOKEN` goes in the step's env.
  - On anything that is not a `pull_request` — the push to main — `code` is `true` without asking.
  - `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'` on `wasm`, `checks`, `rust`, `smoke`, `pwa`,
    `desktop-shell` and `native`, adding `changes` to each `needs` (the three that already have
    `needs: wasm` become `needs: [changes, wasm]`).
  - The workflow has no `permissions:` block, so it takes the repository default. If that default is
    not enough for `pulls: read`, add `permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: read }` at the
    workflow level rather than widening anything.
- **`scripts/ciDocsGate.test.ts`** — new, under `test:tooling`. This repository already tests its own
  configuration this way: `scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` reads `.cargo/config.toml` and asserts
  the properties that would break elsewhere. Same shape here, over `ci.yml`.
- **`README.md`**, the CI section if it describes the workflow's jobs — one sentence that a docs-only
  PR skips them.

**No new dependency.** `dorny/paths-filter` is the usual answer and is named in the bead as an
example; `gh api` needs no third-party action to audit or pin, and the rule it implements is three
lines of shell. Nothing else in this workflow uses a third-party action beyond the official
`actions/*`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, `Swatinem/rust-cache` and `pnpm/action-setup` it already has.

## Increments

1. **The invariant, before the change.** RED: `scripts/ciDocsGate.test.ts` —
   `every required job is gated on the docs check` fails, because no job is. GREEN: the `changes`
   job and the seven `if:` lines.
2. **The trap, pinned.** RED: `the pull request trigger carries no path filter`. It passes the
   moment it is written, which is the point — it exists so a later "simplification" to `paths-ignore`
   fails here instead of silently leaving every required check Pending for ever. Say so in the
   commit; do not manufacture a failing state for it.
3. **The real thing.** Verified on GitHub, not in a test. See Validation.

## The test plan

Suite: `pnpm run test:tooling`. Nothing else can reach a workflow file.

`scripts/ciDocsGate.test.ts`, reading `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as text:
- `every required job is gated on the docs check` — for each of `wasm`, `checks`, `rust`, `smoke`,
  `pwa`, `desktop-shell`, `native`, that job's block carries
  `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`. This is the test that catches the eighth job somebody
  adds next year and forgets to gate.
- `the gate job is not one of the required checks` — `changes` is not in the required list, so it
  must not be gated on itself and must not be renamed to collide with a required context.
- `the pull request trigger carries no path filter` — no `paths:` or `paths-ignore:` under
  `on.pull_request`.
- `the gate runs everything when the diff cannot be read` — assert the shell in the job defaults to
  `code=true`, by asserting the fallback is present rather than by running it. The direction matters
  more than the mechanism: a gate that fails closed skips CI, which is the one outcome worse than
  slow CI.

Parse by scanning lines rather than by adding a YAML dependency — the file is uniformly two-space
indented and the job ids sit at exactly two spaces. Keep the assertions few and specific; see the
traps.

## User-facing decisions

None. This is CI configuration; the application has no part in it, and nothing a player sees
changes.

Two judgements taken here rather than left open: the gate is `gh api` rather than a third-party
paths-filter action (no dependency to pin, three lines of shell), and the ten required contexts in
the `main` ruleset are left exactly as they are — the whole design exists so that they keep
reporting.

## Out of scope

- Editing the `main` ruleset, or the set of required checks.
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and `release.yml`. A docs merge to main will still deploy; whether
  it should is a separate question with a different risk attached.
- Widening the rule beyond `docs/` — root `*.md`, `.beads/issues.jsonl`, `LICENSE`. The bead says
  `docs/`, and each addition is a place where a real change could slip through ungated. If the
  navigator wants more later, it is a one-line change with its own conversation.
- Speeding up CI for code PRs.
- The `strict` policy that requires a branch to be up to date with main.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test:tooling
pnpm run check
```

Then on GitHub, which is the only place this can actually be proved. The bead's own PR touches
`.github/` and `scripts/`, so it must show the **full** suite running — that is half the acceptance
criteria, free.

For the other half, open a throwaway PR from a branch that changes one line of a file under `docs/`
and confirm:

- all ten required contexts report, none stays Pending, and the merge box goes green in about a
  minute;
- **the four matrix contexts appear** — `smoke (web, 1, 2)` and its three siblings. This is the one
  part that documentation does not settle (see the traps), and it is the reason this trial is
  mandatory rather than a nicety;
- then push a code change onto the same branch and confirm every job runs, proving a mixed diff is
  not skipped.

Close the throwaway PR without merging. Do not merge this bead until that trial has been run and its
result stated in the PR description.

## Known traps

- **`paths-ignore` is the failure mode, not the fix.** A workflow skipped by path filtering leaves
  its required checks Pending for ever and blocks the PR — GitHub documents exactly this. The
  workflow must keep triggering on every pull request; only its jobs are conditional. The test in
  increment 2 exists to keep that from being "tidied up" later.
- **Four of the ten contexts are generated by the matrix.** A skipped matrix job is expected to
  still produce one skipped check run per combination, but that is the piece the documentation does
  not state outright. If the trial PR shows those four staying Pending, the fallback is a twin job
  with the *same* `name:` and the *same* matrix, gated the other way
  (`if: needs.changes.outputs.code != 'true'`) and doing nothing but `echo`. Take that route only if
  the trial demands it — two check runs with one name is a wrinkle worth avoiding when it is not
  needed.
- **A job cannot read `needs.changes.outputs` unless `changes` is in its `needs`.** The three jobs
  that already declare `needs: wasm` are the easy ones to get wrong, and the failure is quiet: an
  unresolvable `needs.*` expression evaluates to empty, the `if` is false, and the job silently
  never runs on any PR at all.
- **Fail open, always.** If the API call fails, the diff cannot be read, or the event is anything
  other than a pull request, `code` must be `true`. A gate that fails closed turns an API blip into
  a merged, untested change.
- **The gate job must not be named after a required context**, and must not be added to the ruleset.
  It reports its own check named `changes`, which nothing requires.
- **`strict_required_status_checks_policy` is on**, so a docs PR that has fallen behind main still
  needs updating from main before it merges. That is a push, so the gate re-runs — cheaply. Do not
  try to solve that here.
- **Line-scanning a YAML file is brittle.** Assert on the few properties that matter and anchor them
  to the two-space job indentation; a test that tries to reimplement YAML will fail on the next
  comment reflow and be deleted by whoever it annoys.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. Branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria:
- A PR whose diff touches only files under docs/ can be merged without waiting on the full CI job matrix (wasm/checks/rust/smoke/pwa/desktop-shell/native).
- Branch protection's required status checks still pass for docs-only PRs — i.e. this is not accomplished by making checks optional, since GitHub does not satisfy a required check that never ran. Use path filtering that still reports a (fast/no-op) success status for the required check names, e.g. via dorny/paths-filter with a lightweight fallback job, rather than relying on paths-ignore alone.
- A PR that touches docs/ together with any non-docs file still runs the full CI suite as today.
- Existing CI behavior for non-docs PRs is unchanged (same jobs, same triggers, same required checks).

title: A unit fishing from a boat that sails away is wrongly told it cannot fish here
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #679 by a player running real turns.

Setup: fishermen and sailors board a boat while the shipbuilders leave it; the fishermen promote the sailors. The fishermen issue PRODUCE fish; the sailors issue SAIL out to the ocean, and the HUD does draw the dashed projected-movement arrow for them. The fishermen are nevertheless flagged with an error saying they cannot fish where they are.

The HUD appears to validate the PRODUCE order against the unit's region as of the start of the month, while the boat — and everyone aboard it, including the fishermen — will be in ocean by the time production resolves. Both are month-long orders and the interaction between them is what the check is missing.

Note that the HUD already models the projected destination well enough to draw the arrow, so this is expected to be about which position the terrain check consults, rather than about building new movement projection.

The user-visible effect is a false error on a perfectly legal and quite ordinary fishing-fleet setup, which teaches players to distrust the order errors generally.
design:
## Context

Reported in **GitHub issue #679** by a player running real turns. Fishermen and sailors board a
boat, the shipbuilders leave it, the fishermen promote the sailors; the sailors issue `SAIL` out to
the ocean and the fishermen issue `PRODUCE fish`. The HUD draws the dashed projected-movement arrow
for the boat — and still flags the fishermen with `cannot produce fish here: this region produces …`.

The reporter's own words for the cost, and the reason this is ranked P1:

> *"a false error on a perfectly legal and quite ordinary fishing-fleet setup, which teaches players
> to distrust the order errors generally."*

**The order really does resolve at the destination**, and the codebase says so itself.
`weight_after_orders` (`semantics.rs:4277-4280`) records the server's phase order:

> *"GIVE and TAKE in phase 4, SELL and BUY in phase 7, movement in phase 9. … PRODUCE, BUILD and
> WORK are phase 10, after the fleet has gone."*

So a passenger's `PRODUCE` is settled **after** the boat has moved, against a region the check never
looks at: `check_production` (`semantics.rs:3905`) reads `hex.region.products` — the hex the unit is
standing in now.

### The report can follow the boat on its own, and that is what makes this small

**The order checks are given no map.** `validate_orders_state` (`core-wasm/src/lib.rs:593`) takes
`raw_orders`, `ruleset_json`, `raw_report` and `disabled_codes`; the arrow is drawn by
`trace_move_orders_state` (`:518`), which is additionally given `map_json` and `remembered_json`.
That difference is real and is not being changed here.

**It is also not needed.** The parsed report already carries everything a short sail needs:

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| every region's own `products` | `report/model.rs:246` |
| every region's `exits`, each with a `direction` and the neighbour's `coordinate` | `model.rs:249`, `Exit` at `:77-83` |
| the region's own `coordinate` | `model.rs:234` |
| a `SAIL`'s steps as typed directions — `MoveStep::Go(Direction)` | `movement/orders.rs:19-26` |
| the idiom for turning an exit's text into a `Direction` | `movement/graph.rs:391`, `Direction::parse` at `:101` |

So the destination is reached by walking the captain's `Go` steps from exit to exit through the
report's own regions. **No map, no remembered regions, no new input to `validate_orders_state`.**
The one limit is the report's horizon: a sail that leaves the regions the faction can see runs out
of exits, and there the answer is silence.

**This corrects a premise in this plan's first draft.** That draft rejected checking the destination
because it believed the map was required, and settled on staying silent for every passenger. The
navigator answered the same question again in a second interview and chose to follow the `SAIL`; the
check above confirms that is the cheaper option as well as the better one. Both answers, and why the
first was wrong, are recorded under *User-facing decisions*.

When this lands: a passenger is judged against the region the vessel reaches, and told nothing at
all only where the report cannot say where that is.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**One file**, `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`, and its tests. No wasm signature changes, no
TypeScript, nothing generated.

### Who is aboard a departing vessel — assemble, do not invent

`check_sailing` (`semantics.rs:4495`) already works out which fleets in the hex one of our units
orders to `SAIL`, and which units are aboard each. Its doc comment defines *aboard* precisely, and
that definition is the one to use:

> *"Aboard means the report's units in the fleet, plus those that ENTER it this month, minus those
> that LEAVE — the instant orders the server runs before anything moves."*

Three pieces, all present, all reused unchanged:

- **`parse_fleet_kind(&structure.kind)`** — whether a structure is a hull or a fleet at all (`:4502`).
- **`could_captain(ordered, fleet_id)`** (`:4266`) — whether a unit could give this fleet its `SAIL`,
  already accounting for boarding orders through `boarding_of`.
- **`is_aboard(ordered, fleet_id)`** (`:4526`) — the *aboard* definition above.

```rust
/// The `SAIL` that will carry this unit out of the hex, if one will.
///
/// `PRODUCE` is phase 10 and movement is phase 9 (`weight_after_orders`), so a passenger produces
/// in the region the vessel reaches (`ah-jk9h`, `gh-679`).
///
/// Returns the captain's placed `SAIL`, because the caller needs its steps. Assembled from
/// `check_sailing`'s own three pieces rather than re-derived.
fn carried_away<'a>(hex: &'a Hex<'a>, ordered: &Ordered<'_>) -> Option<&'a PlacedIntent>;
```

### Following the sail — the report's own regions

```rust
/// Where a sail from `from` ends, as far as the report can say.
///
/// Walks the `Go` steps through each region's own `exits`, looking the neighbour up by coordinate
/// in `regions`. `In` and `Out` steps move a unit within a hex and are skipped.
///
/// `None` the moment the report cannot follow: an exit the region does not list (the coast the
/// player is sailing off), or a neighbour the report does not carry (beyond what the faction can
/// see). **`None` is "cannot say", never "did not move"** - the caller must stay silent for it,
/// which is the whole reason this returns an `Option` rather than the last region it managed to
/// reach.
fn sail_destination<'a>(
    from: &'a ReportRegion,
    steps: &[MoveStep],
    regions: &BTreeMap<Coordinate, &'a ReportRegion>,
) -> Option<&'a ReportRegion>;
```

`Direction::parse(&exit.direction)` is how an exit's text becomes a `Direction`, exactly as
`graph.rs:391` does it — **reuse that, do not match on strings.** `DIRECTIONS`
(`report/region.rs:31`) is the parser's own list and is not the thing to compare against here.

**A sail with no `Go` steps at all ends where it started**, which is the region already being
checked — so the ordinary finding applies and nothing changes for it.

### The region index — built once, and only when it is needed

`review_turn` (`semantics.rs:268`) already has this exact pattern for `where_the_report_shows_each_unit`
(`:228`), built only when the check that reads it is enabled, with the reason written at `:275-278`:
*"`validate_turn` runs this on every keystroke once typing settles, so the lookup is built only when
the check that reads it is actually enabled."*

Follow it precisely:

```rust
    let by_coordinate = if options.emits(codes::PRODUCE_NOT_HERE) {
        report.regions.iter().map(|region| (region.coordinate, region)).collect()
    } else {
        BTreeMap::new()
    };
```

and thread it to `check_production` as one more argument, as `located` is threaded to
`check_transfer_targets`.

### `check_production` — one of its two codes learns where the unit will be

In the `for ordered in &hex.units` loop (`:3844`), the `produce-not-here` block (`:3905`) reads its
products from the destination instead of from `hex.region`:

```rust
        if says_here && recipe.inputs.is_empty() {
            // A passenger produces where the vessel arrives. Silent where the report cannot follow
            // the sail - a guess about a region nobody can see is worse than no mark (`ah-jk9h`).
            let where_it_produces = match carried_away(hex, ordered) {
                None => Some(hex.region),
                Some(sail) => match &sail.intent {
                    Intent::Sail { steps } => sail_destination(hex.region, steps, &by_coordinate),
                    _ => Some(hex.region),
                },
            };
            let Some(region) = where_it_produces else { continue };
            …the existing products test, against `region` rather than `hex.region`…
        }
```

**The message names the place.** Where the unit stays put it is unchanged, verbatim:

> `cannot produce {label} here: this region produces {has}`

and where it will have sailed:

> `cannot produce {label} there: the region this vessel is sailing to produces {has}`

Both ship verbatim; see *User-facing decisions*.

**`PRODUCE_WITHOUT_SKILL` is untouched.** Whether the unit has the skill is a fact about the unit,
not about the region, and `check_production`'s own doc comment argues at length that suppressing one
of its two codes must never hide the other.

**Nothing else changes, and the phase order is why.** Market orders (`not-traded-here`) are phase 7
and settle **before** movement in phase 9, so they resolve in the hex the unit started in and are
correct as they stand.

## Increments

1. **Who is carried away.**
   RED, in `semantics.rs`'s tests: `a unit aboard a fleet whose captain sails is carried away`;
   `a unit aboard a fleet nobody sails is not`; `a unit in the hex but not aboard is not`;
   `a unit aboard an ordinary building is not` (`parse_fleet_kind` is what says so);
   `a unit that ENTERs the fleet this month is carried away`; `a unit that LEAVEs it is not`.
   GREEN: `carried_away`.

2. **Following the sail.**
   RED: `a one-step sail lands in the neighbour the exit names`;
   `a two-step sail follows both`;
   `a sail through an exit the region does not list cannot be followed` (`None`);
   `a sail into a region the report does not carry cannot be followed` (`None`);
   `a sail with no steps stays where it is`;
   `IN and OUT steps do not move the boat between hexes`.
   GREEN: `sail_destination`.

3. **The reported case, and everything it must not break.**
   RED, in `check_production`'s tests:
   - `a passenger is judged where the vessel is sailing to` — **`gh-679`**: fisherman aboard, sailor
     with `SAIL`, start region without fish, destination region **with** fish. No finding.
   - `a passenger sailing somewhere that cannot make it is told so` — the same setup, `PRODUCE wood`,
     destination produces fish. The finding fires with the **`there`** wording, verbatim.
   - `a passenger whose sail cannot be followed is told nothing` — destination outside the report.
   - `a unit that is going nowhere is still told` — no fleet; message unchanged, **`here`** wording.
   - `a passenger without the skill is still told` — `produce-without-skill` fires for a passenger.
     **This is the test that stops the change being written on the unit instead of the code.**
   GREEN: the index, the threading, and the rewritten block.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the six `carried_away` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | who is aboard, including ENTER and LEAVE |
| the six `sail_destination` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | the walk, and both ways it can fail to follow |
| `a passenger is judged where the vessel is sailing to` | `orders/semantics.rs` | **`gh-679`** |
| `a passenger sailing somewhere that cannot make it is told so` | `orders/semantics.rs` | the case "stay silent" would have missed |
| `a passenger whose sail cannot be followed is told nothing` | `orders/semantics.rs` | silence beyond the horizon |
| `a unit that is going nowhere is still told` | `orders/semantics.rs` | no over-suppression, wording unchanged |
| `a passenger without the skill is still told` | `orders/semantics.rs` | only one of the two codes changed |
| the existing `check_production` and `check_sailing` tests | `orders/semantics.rs` | **unedited** |

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

`pnpm run check:generated` is not needed: no type crosses the boundary.

**Watch `validate_real_orders.rs`.** Its `EXPECTED` table counts findings over a committed turn; a
producing passenger on a sailing fleet moves a `produce-not-here` row. **Read the finding before
touching the table** — the table's own doc comment records twice that a moved row was the bead
proving itself.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-25. Mockup, as chosen and committed:
`docs/ui/ah-jk9h-sailing-produce.html`.

**The navigator answered this question twice, and the second answer stands.** The first interview
(mine) settled on *staying silent for every passenger*, having rejected checking the destination on
the belief that it required threading the map onto the keystroke path. A second interview, minutes
later, chose *following the `SAIL` using the report's own regions* — and the premise behind the
first rejection turned out to be wrong: the report carries every region's exits, coordinates and
products, so no map is needed. **The later answer is both better and cheaper.** Recorded here in
full so nobody re-opens it from the older note.

**What the HUD checks.**
Chosen: **follow the captain's `SAIL` through the report's own regions** and judge the `PRODUCE`
against the destination's products; fall back to silence only where the report cannot follow.

*Rejected — stay silent for every passenger.* The false error goes and nothing new reaches the
checks, but a genuinely impossible `PRODUCE` goes unwarned even when the report plainly shows where
the boat is going.
*Rejected — say the check cannot judge it* (`this unit is aboard a vessel that is leaving, so where
it will produce is not checked`). It tells the player the HUD looked, at the cost of a new advisory
on every producing passenger, including the many whose order is fine.
*Rejected — thread the map into `validate_orders_state`.* Unnecessary once the report is enough, and
it would put new work on a path that runs as the player types.

**The two messages, shipping verbatim:**

| Case | Sentence |
|---|---|
| the unit stays put | `cannot produce fish here: this region produces wood, furs and herbs` *(unchanged)* |
| the unit sails first | `cannot produce wood there: the region this vessel is sailing to produces fish` |

**What the reporter is told.** The plan records what changed and what did not, so Moira's `PLANNED`
comment on `gh-679` can be accurate. For that comment:

- the false error on a fishing fleet is gone, which is exactly what was reported;
- the HUD now checks the region the boat is sailing to, using the regions the report itself carries;
- where the sail leaves the map the faction can see, the HUD says nothing rather than guessing;
- **her earlier comment said the fix would consult the projected region — that is now accurate**,
  which it would not have been under the rejected first answer.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** a `SAIL` that
`check_sailing` separately says will fail is still followed, because the player is already being
told the sail fails and a second finding true only *because* of the first is the wrong one to act
on; a sail with no `Go` steps is treated as staying put; and only `produce-not-here` changes.

## Out of scope

- **`BUILD` and `WORK`**, also phase 10 and open to the same argument. Neither was reported and
  neither has a region-products check of this shape. **Worth filing if anybody wants them.**
- **Market checks** (`not-traded-here`). Phase 7, before movement — correct as they stand.
- **Threading the map into the order checks.** Unnecessary; see above.
- **Movement cost, weather, or whether the fleet can actually reach the destination.**
  `check_sailing` owns that and keeps owning it. This bead reads where the orders *say* it goes.
- **The arrow and `trace_move_orders_state`.**

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, and `validate_real_orders.rs`'s `EXPECTED` untouched unless a moved row has been read and
understood.

**Then, by eye — this is the reported case, so it is the one that matters.** Build `gh-679`'s setup
in a report with a coastal region whose ocean neighbour the report carries: a fisherman and a sailor
aboard a boat, the sailor given `SAIL`, the fisherman `PRODUCE fish`, in a start region whose
products exclude fish.

- the fisherman's `PRODUCE` line carries **no error**;
- change it to `PRODUCE wood` and it reads
  `cannot produce wood there: the region this vessel is sailing to produces fish`;
- remove the `SAIL`, and the original **`here`** error returns, word for word;
- sail somewhere the report does not carry, and there is **no** error either way;
- the dashed projected-movement arrow is unchanged throughout.

**A human must confirm the first two**, because they are what the reporter will check.

## Known traps

- **`None` from `sail_destination` means "cannot say", not "did not move".** Returning the last
  region reached, or falling back to the starting hex, would put a confident error on a unit the
  HUD cannot locate — worse than the bug being fixed. There is a test named for it.
- **Change the code, not the unit.** Only the `produce-not-here` block learns about the sail;
  skipping the unit would silence `produce-without-skill` too, which
  `check_production`'s doc comment argues against at length.
- **Use `is_aboard`, not `unit.structure_id`.** *Aboard* includes units that `ENTER` this month and
  excludes those that `LEAVE`. Two of the six `carried_away` tests exist for this, and a raw
  `structure_id` test passes the other four.
- **`parse_fleet_kind` is what makes a structure a vessel.** Without it every unit inside a fort
  stops being checked.
- **Use `Direction::parse` on the exit's text**, as `graph.rs:391` does. Comparing strings against
  `DIRECTIONS` is the parser's job, not this walk's, and abbreviations would slip through.
- **Build the coordinate index only when `produce-not-here` is enabled**, exactly as `located` is
  built only for `give-target-not-here`. This runs on every keystroke and the reason is written at
  `semantics.rs:275-278`.
- **`validate_real_orders.rs`'s `EXPECTED` may move.** Read the finding first.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**: none of the five apply — core only, no browser suite, no persisted
  setting, no `packages/shared` test.
acceptance_criteria:
- A unit aboard a boat whose SAIL order takes it to ocean is not flagged for a PRODUCE fish order.
- Terrain-dependent production checks consult the unit's projected end-of-month region when the unit is aboard a structure that is moving, and its current region otherwise.
- A unit that genuinely cannot produce in either its current or its projected region is still flagged.
- Regression tests cover: fish aboard a sailing boat, fish aboard a stationary boat in a land region (still an error), and a normal land production order (unaffected).
