title: A unit that gains pack animals this month is wrongly called overloaded
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #677 by a player running real turns.

A unit with 1 man, 17 horses and 15 grain is reported by the HUD as overloaded: "this unit is overloaded: it carries 935 and the most it can move with is 85, so it will not move".

The carried weight (935) appears to include the full weight of the 17 horses, while the capacity (85) looks as though it were derived without crediting the capacity the horses themselves provide. In Atlantis, horses are mounts/pack animals: they carry weight as well as having weight, and a unit's movement capacity is the sum of the capacities contributed by every item in it, per movement mode (walk / ride / fly / swim). The current calculation seems to count only one side of that.

The user-visible effect is that ordinary, perfectly mobile caravan units are flagged as immobile, which makes the overload warning untrustworthy exactly where it should be most useful.
design:
## Context

**User-reported** (GitHub issue #677, `external_ref` `gh-677`), by a player running real turns. A
unit of 1 man, 17 horses and 15 grain was told:

> this unit is overloaded: it carries 935 and the most it can move with is 85, so it will not move

The unit is not overloaded. It can carry 1,205 walking.

### What is actually wrong — not what the bead's description says

The bead says capacity *"looks as though it were derived without crediting the capacity the horses
themselves provide"*. That is not it, and an implementer following it would look in the wrong place.
**The capacity is not ignorant; it is stale.**

`check_movement` (`semantics.rs:4613`) pairs two numbers that are computed at different moments:

```rust
let (Some(allowance), Some(weight)) = (
    best_allowance(ordered.unit),                      // the REPORT's printed Capacity line
    weight_after_orders(ordered, ledger, ruleset),     // repriced for this month's transfers
)
```

`weight_after_orders` (`:4286`) walks the ledger and adds the weight of everything gained or lost
this month. `best_allowance` (`movement/mode.rs:98`) parses the `Capacity:` line the server printed
*before* those orders ran. A unit that **acquires** pack animals this month therefore gains their
weight and none of their capacity.

The reporter's numbers say exactly that, and the arithmetic is exact rather than approximate. From
the committed ruleset — `LEAD` weight 10 / walk capacity 5, `HORS` weight 50 / walk capacity 20 /
self-mobile walking, `GRAI` weight 5 / no capacity:

| | |
|---|---|
| weight after orders | 10 + 17×50 + 15×5 = **935** — exactly what they were shown |
| true walk capacity | 15 + 17×70 = **1205** |
| capacity they were shown | **85** — precisely one man and **one** horse |

So the unit held one horse when the report was printed and acquired sixteen more this month. The
weight followed; the allowance did not.

**The code already knows about this gap and gets its direction half right** (`:4606`):

> *"The allowance is the report's own, unrepriced. A unit that gives away the horses it was riding
> loses ride capacity as well as weight, and this does not follow that — the error runs towards
> saying nothing rather than towards a warning that is wrong."*

True for **giving away**: weight falls, capacity does not, so a real overload can go unwarned. For
**acquiring** it inverts, and produces this false warning. Both directions are fixed here — the
navigator's decision at planning.

### The capacity rule, derived and then validated

```
capacity(mode) = Σ over items:  count × ( item.capacity[mode] + (item.self_mobile[mode] ? item.weight : 0) )
```

A self-mobile item carries **itself**, so its own weight joins its capacity — which is what
`SelfMobility`'s own doc comment says: *"Which modes an item can carry itself in"*
(`movement/rules.rs:206`).

Validated against `WoodsmenY (15189)` in `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, 1 wood elf + 1 horse,
printed `Weight: 60. Capacity: 0/70/85/0`:

| mode | derived | the server printed |
|---|---|---|
| walk | man (5 + 10) + horse (20 + 50) = **85** | 85 |
| ride | man 0 (not self-mobile riding) + horse (20 + 50) = **70** | 70 |

Two independent confirmations — the fixture's own printed line, and the reporter's figures. The
navigator confirmed the rule at planning.

**When this lands, a unit that buys or is given pack animals is judged on the capacity it will
actually have, and one that gives them away is too.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs` — a new `capacities_from_items`, beside `best_allowance`.
- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `check_movement` uses it; one new helper next to
  `weight_after_orders`.

No TypeScript, no message change, no new finding code, no Settings row. The warning's wording is
unchanged — only the numbers in it become right.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `Capacities { fly, ride, walk, swim }` (`mode.rs:18`) — the return type. **The printed string is
  `fly/ride/walk/swim` in that order** (`parse_capacities`, `:41-58`); the struct's field order is
  different, so build it by name, never positionally.
- `best_allowance(unit) -> Option<i64>` (`mode.rs:98`) — `fly.max(ride).max(walk)`. **Swimming is
  deliberately excluded**, for the reason `mobility` excludes it; keep that.
- `ItemEntry { weight, capacity: ItemCapacity, self_mobile: SelfMobility, .. }`
  (`movement/rules.rs:257-263`), `ItemCapacity { walk, ride, fly, swim }` (`:199`),
  `SelfMobility { walk, ride, fly, swim }` (`:214`). All already scraped; **add no ruleset field.**
- `Ruleset::find_item(tag)` — how a tag becomes an `ItemEntry`.
- `weight_after_orders(ordered, ledger, ruleset)` (`semantics.rs:4286`) — **the shape to copy.** It
  starts from the report's figure and applies `balance - ordered.holding(tag)` per tag from the
  ledger. The new capacity helper walks the same ledger the same way.
- `Ordered::holding(tag)` — what the report printed of one tag.

### The design of the code

**1. The rule, in `movement/mode.rs`, next to `best_allowance`:**

```rust
/// What a bag of items can carry, per movement mode.
///
/// A self-mobile item carries **itself**, so its own weight joins its capacity - which is what
/// `SelfMobility` means ("which modes an item can carry itself in"). A horse walking contributes
/// its 20 of capacity plus the 50 it no longer makes anybody else carry; a man contributes 5 plus
/// his own 10; a sack of grain contributes nothing and must be carried.
///
/// Derived rather than read off the report's `Capacity:` line because that line is printed before
/// this month's orders run, so a unit that buys pack animals is judged against a capacity it has
/// already outgrown (`ah-titf`, GitHub #677).
///
/// Reproduces the server's own line: 1 wood elf + 1 horse gives `walk 85, ride 70`, which is what
/// `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` prints for WoodsmenY (15189).
#[must_use]
pub fn capacities_from_items(items: &[(&str, i64)], ruleset: &Ruleset) -> Option<Capacities>;
```

`items` is `(tag, count)`. **Returns `None` if any tag is absent from the ruleset**, because a
partial sum understates capacity and understating it is what produces a false warning — the exact
failure being fixed. Silence is the correct answer when the catalogue cannot price everything.

**2. The after-orders view, in `semantics.rs`, immediately after `weight_after_orders`:**

```rust
/// This unit's carrying capacity once the month's transfers have run, as `weight_after_orders` does
/// for the other side of the same comparison.
///
/// The two must be computed at the same moment or the check compares a repriced load against a
/// stale allowance - which warned a real player that a perfectly mobile caravan would not move
/// (`ah-titf`, GitHub #677). `None` with no ruleset, or when any tag the unit holds is not in it;
/// the caller then falls back to the report's own line.
fn capacity_after_orders(
    ordered: &Ordered<'_>,
    ledger: &Ledger<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
) -> Option<Capacities>;
```

It builds the tag/count list from the unit's printed items adjusted by
`balance - ordered.holding(tag)` for every ledger entry belonging to this unit — the same walk
`weight_after_orders` makes — then calls `capacities_from_items`.

**3. `check_movement` prefers the computed allowance and falls back:**

```rust
let allowance = capacity_after_orders(ordered, ledger, ruleset)
    .map(|c| c.fly.max(c.ride).max(c.walk))
    .or_else(|| best_allowance(ordered.unit));
let (Some(allowance), Some(weight)) = (allowance, weight_after_orders(ordered, ledger, ruleset))
else { continue };
```

**The fallback is what keeps every existing test green and every foreign unit silent.** With no
ruleset — or with an item the catalogue does not carry — behaviour is exactly what it is today.

**Both directions change, and that is the decision taken.** A unit that gives its horses away now
loses their capacity too, so a genuine overload that is silent today will warn. That is a *new*
warning on input where none appeared before, and it is deliberate: it is the gap `:4606` already
admits to. Increment 3 pins it.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new. Two pure functions and one changed local. No `Ledger` field, no
new type, no ruleset field, no wire change.

## Increments

**Increment 1 — the rule.**
Failing test: `derives_the_capacity_the_server_prints`, in `movement/mode.rs`'s tests beside the
existing `best_allowance` cases (`:363-380`):

```rust
// 1 wood elf + 1 horse - what neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep prints for WoodsmenY (15189)
let c = capacities_from_items(&[("WELF", 1), ("HORS", 1)], &ruleset()).unwrap();
assert_eq!((c.walk, c.ride), (85, 70));
// grain is cargo: weight, no capacity, not self-mobile
let c = capacities_from_items(&[("LEAD", 1), ("HORS", 17), ("GRAI", 15)], &ruleset()).unwrap();
assert_eq!(c.walk, 1205);
// an item the catalogue does not carry gives no answer at all
assert!(capacities_from_items(&[("HORS", 1), ("ZZZZ", 1)], &ruleset()).is_none());
```

Read `mode.rs`'s existing tests for how they obtain a `Ruleset` before writing `ruleset()`. Then add
`capacities_from_items`.

**Increment 2 — the false warning goes.**
Failing test: `a_unit_that_buys_pack_animals_is_not_called_overloaded`, in `semantics.rs`'s test
module. A unit printed with 1 leader, 1 horse and 15 grain — `Capacity: 0/70/85/0` — ordered to
`BUY 16 horse` and `MOVE N`, with silver enough. Assert **no** `unit-overloaded` finding. On `main`
this fails with the reporter's own message. Then add `capacity_after_orders` and the `check_movement`
change.

**Increment 3 — the other direction, which is a new warning.**
Failing test: `a_unit_that_gives_its_horses_away_loses_their_capacity`. A unit whose printed capacity
covers its load only because of horses it then gives away, ordered to `MOVE`: assert
`unit-overloaded` **does** fire. This is behaviour that changes on input where the check is silent
today, and it is the half `semantics.rs:4606` admits to.

**Increment 4 — the fallback stays silent.**
Failing test: `a_unit_is_judged_by_the_printed_capacity_when_the_ruleset_cannot_price_it`. The same
overloaded unit with `ruleset: None`, and a second case holding a tag the ruleset does not carry:
both must behave exactly as they do on `main`. This is what protects every existing test and every
foreign unit.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `derives_the_capacity_the_server_prints` | `mode.rs` | the rule, against the server's own line; the reporter's 1205; the unknown-tag `None` |
| `a_unit_that_buys_pack_animals_is_not_called_overloaded` | `semantics.rs` | the reported bug |
| `a_unit_that_gives_its_horses_away_loses_their_capacity` | `semantics.rs` | the deliberate new warning |
| `a_unit_is_judged_by_the_printed_capacity_when_the_ruleset_cannot_price_it` | `semantics.rs` | the fallback |

**The regression net:** the two existing overload-message tests (`semantics.rs:15844`, `:15959`) and
every `best_allowance` / `mobility` test in `mode.rs`, **all unedited**. If one moves, either the
fallback is wrong or the derived rule disagrees with the server — and the second would mean the rule
is wrong, not the test.

**Also run the whole corpus:** `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`. Every committed report is parsed by
some test, and a rule that disagrees with the server on any real unit is worth knowing about before
this ships rather than after.

## User-facing decisions

Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-25. **No mockup**: nothing about the interface changes — same
message, same code, same Settings row. What changes is which units it fires on.

1. **The capacity rule** — `Σ count × (capacity[mode] + weight if self-mobile[mode])`. The planner
   derived it and validated it twice (the fixture's printed line; the reporter's figures) and the
   navigator confirmed it.
2. **Scope: reprice in both directions.** *Rejected:* using the computed capacity only where it
   **exceeds** the printed one — strictly safer, since it could only ever remove warnings, but it
   leaves the give-away gap the code already knows about. *Also rejected:* deriving capacity from the
   printed item list while ignoring orders, which would not fix this bug at all, because the
   reporter's unit acquired its horses this month.
3. **The reporter is to be told the real cause.** Moira's `CREATED` comment said the HUD *"is not
   counting the weight your horses are able to carry"*, which is not quite right — the capacity was
   correct and out of date. The navigator asked that the `PLANNED` comment correct it. **That is
   Moira's to post, not this bead's**, and it is recorded here so it is not lost: the honest sentence
   is that the HUD was checking the load your unit will have against the capacity it had *before*
   this month's orders, so buying pack animals made it look immobile.

## Out of scope

- **Any change to the ruleset schema.** `capacity` and `self_mobile` already carry everything needed.
- **`mobility`** (`mode.rs:67`) and the map's movement planning, which answer from the report's
  printed weight on purpose. Only `check_movement` is repaired here.
- **Swimming.** `best_allowance` excludes it deliberately and continues to.
- **Fleets and `SAIL`.** A passenger says `SAIL`, which is its own intent and is already passed over
  (`:4610`).
- **`cargo_capacity`** on `ItemEntry`. That is a ship's hold, not a unit's carrying capacity.
- **Posting to GitHub #677.** Moira owns the thread; see *User-facing decisions* item 3.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core          # after each increment
pnpm run check:fast                      # before the PR
```

**The human check, and this bead has earned one because a real player is waiting:** load
`neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, find a unit with one horse, order it to buy a dozen more and
`MOVE`, and confirm no overload warning appears. Then give the horses away instead and confirm one
does. Say in the PR description what both showed.

## Known traps

- **The printed order is `fly/ride/walk/swim`; the `Capacities` struct's fields are declared
  `fly, ride, walk, swim` but must be set by name.** `parse_capacities` (`mode.rs:41-58`) is the only
  place the string order is known; do not re-derive it, and never build a `Capacities` positionally.
- **A self-mobile item's own weight joins its capacity.** Omitting that gives walk 25 instead of 85
  for the fixture unit, and the first test catches it.
- **Return `None`, not a partial sum, for an unpriceable tag.** A partial sum understates capacity,
  and understating capacity is exactly what produces the false warning this bead exists to remove.
- **Keep the fallback to `best_allowance`.** Without it every foreign unit — which prints no
  capacities — and every ruleset-free test changes behaviour.
- **`weight_after_orders` starts from `ordered.unit.weight?`**, the report's own figure, and applies
  deltas. The capacity helper must start from the report's *item list* instead, because there is no
  single printed number to start from. Do not try to add deltas to the parsed `Capacity:` line — the
  printed line is a sum whose composition is not recoverable.
- **This bead adds a warning as well as removing one** (increment 3). Say so in the PR description;
  a reviewer seeing a new `unit-overloaded` on an existing fixture should find it explained.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.
acceptance_criteria:
- A unit of 1 man + 17 horses + 15 grain is not reported as overloaded.
- Movement capacity is computed per movement mode as the sum of the capacities each item contributes, and compared against total carried weight for that mode.
- The warning text reports the same capacity figure that the calculation used.
- Regression tests cover: a unit with mounts under capacity, one genuinely over capacity, and a unit with no capacity-bearing items.

title: An open bead handed back as nothing-to-build reaches no role at all
description:
Found by Beast on 2026-08-24, tracing why ah-t2pn.3 had not moved since 00:04:50Z.

## The gap

ah-tjaz identified three states that share one set of labels. The third - 'nothing to do,
re-verify' - is reached when an implementer picks up a verification:failed bead, finds nothing to
build, and hands it back by removing 'planned'. That is exactly what Storm did to ah-t2pn.3 on
2026-08-23, correctly, and what implement-bead's hand-back recipe tells it to do.

The bead is then open, carries verification:failed, and carries neither planned nor plan:revise.
Nobody can move it:

  implementers  skip it - no 'planned' label
  planners      skip it - verification:failed without plan:revise is not a planner candidate
  the verifier  cannot see it - her work list is work-beads, which defaults to --status closed,
                and this bead is open

Verified: 'work-beads | <her steady-state query>' returns ten ids and ah-t2pn.3 is not among them;
'work-beads --status open | jq "select(.id==\"ah-t2pn.3\")"' returns it.

## Why the existing open arm does not catch it

ah-e0kf added an open-bead query to the verifier's pass and its own comment names this failure -
'a bead that reached no role at all because the list it was meant to arrive on was built from
closed beads'. But that arm selects verdict:stale only, and a handed-back bead carries
verification:failed.

## The assumption that hid it

ah-t2pn.3's notes say, from Xavier with the navigator: 'it still carries verification:failed, which
is what puts it back on Psylocke's list'. That is stated and never checked, and it is false.

## What a fix would change

A second arm on the verifier's open-bead query for an open verification:failed bead, taken in the
same pass and for the same reason as verdict:stale. Worth considering alongside it: whether
implement-bead's hand-back should set a label that says 'handed back, needs a second look' rather
than relying on an absence, which is the ambiguity ah-tjaz was filed about.

This bead lives in the cerebro submodule (agents/verifier.md, and possibly
skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md).

Unranked at P4.
design:
## Context

`ah-tjaz` identified three states that share one set of labels on a `verification:failed` bead. Two
have a positive label and a role that reads it:

| State | Label | Who takes it |
|---|---|---|
| the **plan** was wrong | `plan:revise` | a planner |
| the **build** was wrong | `planned` | an implementer |
| **nothing left to build** | *neither* | **nobody** |

The third is reached exactly as `implement-bead`'s hand-back block tells an implementer to reach it
(`SKILL.md:347`): read the failure notes, find the surface already there or carried by another bead,
`bd update <id> --remove-label planned`, `bd unclaim`. Storm did that to `ah-t2pn.3` on 2026-08-23,
correctly. The bead was then open, carrying `verification:failed` and neither of the other two
labels, and **no role could see it**:

- implementers skip it — no `planned`;
- planners skip it — `verification:failed` without `plan:revise` is not a planner candidate;
- the verifier cannot see it — her work list is `work-beads`, which **defaults to `--status closed`**
  (`scripts/work-beads:52`), and this bead is `open`.

It sat from 00:04 until Beast traced it on 2026-08-24 — and it is not a hypothetical: `ah-t2pn.3` was
unstuck by hand while this bead was being planned.

**`ah-e0kf` already added an open-bead arm to the verifier's pass** (`agents/verifier.md:140`) and its
own comment names this failure — *"a bead that reached no role at all because the list it was meant
to arrive on was built from closed beads"*. But that arm selects `verdict:stale` only, and a
handed-back bead carries `verification:failed`. The lesson was learnt one state too narrowly.

**Two documents state the false assumption, and both must be fixed.**

1. `agents/verifier.md` — the query that does not match.
2. `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:352`, in the hand-back block:
   *"`verification:failed` is what builds Psylocke's list, and a failed verification with nothing
   left to build wants her second look"*. That sentence is why the hand-back looks safe. It is
   wrong: `verification:failed` builds her list **only among closed beads**.

The same false claim was also written by Xavier into `ah-t2pn.3`'s notes and repeated to the
navigator for a dozen passes. It was stated and never checked. That is the shape of this bug, and it
is why the fix below puts the query somewhere a test can reach it.

**When this lands, a bead handed back as nothing-to-build arrives on the verifier's list in the next
pass, and a test fails if it ever stops doing so.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything is inside the **`.claude/cerebro` submodule**. Nothing in the consumer's application code
changes.

- **New:** `scripts/second-look-beads` — the open-bead query, as a script.
- **New:** `tests/second-look-beads.sh` — its test.
- `agents/verifier.md` — call the script instead of carrying the `jq` in prose.
- `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` — correct the false sentence at `:352`.
- `tests/gate` picks up `tests/*.sh` automatically; no runner change.

### The worktree

`implement-bead`'s *"A bead whose diff is inside `.claude/cerebro`"* section (`SKILL.md:421`) is the
whole recipe and it must be followed exactly: run `prepare-worktree` as normal, work in
`<tree>/.claude/cerebro`, and **fetch and branch inside the submodule first**, because it arrives
detached at the pinned sha:

```bash
git -C <tree>/.claude/cerebro fetch origin
git -C <tree>/.claude/cerebro checkout -b ah-zuhs-second-look origin/main
```

**Never `git -C .claude/cerebro worktree add`**, and never clone cerebro to a sibling directory —
both are called out there, and four retrospectives paid for the second.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `scripts/work-beads` — the one place the harness asks "which beads are real work", owning three bd
  quirks (closed-by-default, epics as bookkeeping, bd's own `event` beads). `--status open` is
  already supported (`:52-57`). **Call it; do not query `bd` directly**, or the epic and event
  exclusions are lost.
- `scripts/consumer-root --shared` — the shared checkout, as `work-beads` resolves it.
- `tests/work-beads.sh` — the shape to copy: plain bash, `set -euo pipefail`, `fail`/`pass` helpers,
  no framework, run as `bash tests/second-look-beads.sh` from the submodule root.
- `tests/gate` — the runner; it loops `tests/*.sh` (and is deliberately not named `gate.sh`).

### The design of the code

**Why a script rather than another `jq` block in the markdown.** The bug being fixed *is* an untested
query living only in prose. `work-beads` exists for exactly this reason — its header records that its
three quirks "were each learnt separately by three different readers and fixed three times in two
days (ah-cg1)". Adding a second untested `jq` to `verifier.md` repeats the mistake in the same file
that already has it once.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The open beads that need the verifier's second look, and the one place that question is answered.
#
# Two states reach her here, and neither can arrive on `work-beads` unaided: that defaults to
# --status closed, and both of these are OPEN. ah-e0kf learnt this for the first of them and
# ah-zuhs for the second, which sat unreachable for eleven hours.
#
#   verdict:stale             a failed verdict formed against a commit main has moved past.
#   handed back               `verification:failed`, and neither `planned` nor `plan:revise`.
#                             An implementer read the failure, found nothing left to build, and
#                             handed it back (implement-bead's hand-back block). The state is an
#                             ABSENCE of the other two labels, deliberately: `plan:revise` means a
#                             planner has it and `planned` means an implementer has it, so "neither"
#                             is exactly "nobody", and acting on the bead clears it with no cleanup
#                             step anybody has to remember.
#
#     scripts/second-look-beads          # ids, one per line
#
set -euo pipefail

script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

"$script_dir/work-beads" --status open | jq -r '
  .[]
  | select(
      ([.labels[]?] | index("verdict:stale"))
      or (
        ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed"))
        and ([.labels[]?] | index("planned") | not)
        and ([.labels[]?] | index("plan:revise") | not)
      )
    )
  | .id'
```

**Three details that decide whether it works, each of which fails silently if wrong:**

- **`index(...) | not` is the right negation.** `index` returns `null` when absent and a number when
  present; in `jq` only `null` and `false` are falsy, so a label at position **0** yields `0`, which
  is truthy, and `0 | not` is `false`. A `has`/`contains` spelling would not behave this way. The
  test pins a bead whose first label is `planned`.
- **`--status open` excludes `in_progress`.** A bead an implementer is currently building has status
  `in_progress`, not `open`, so it cannot appear here — which is why no extra assignee test is
  needed. Do not "fix" this by adding `in_progress` to the status list.
- **The two arms may overlap.** A bead carrying both `verdict:stale` and a handed-back shape is one
  bead and must be listed **once**; `select` with an `or` does that naturally. Do not write two
  queries and concatenate.

**`agents/verifier.md`** replaces the inline `jq` at `:140` with the script, and its surrounding
prose gains the second state. The existing instruction — *run it first in the pass, and take what it
returns before anything on the closed list* — covers both, unchanged, and the reason it gives
(the bead is out of every other queue while it waits) is now more true rather than less.

**What she does with a handed-back bead** is the existing `failed` recipe, and it needs no new
outcome. An implementer has already reported that nothing is left to build, so the second look is:
re-read the finding against current main and either pass it, close it naming the sibling that
delivered it, or take it to the navigator as *plan or build* — which is what sets `plan:revise` or
re-adds `planned`. **Acting on it in any of those ways removes it from this list**, because the
state is the absence of both labels. Say that in the doc; it is the property that makes the
absence-based state safe.

**`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:352`** — replace the false sentence. The hand-back itself is
correct and does not change; only its justification does:

> `verification:failed` on an **open** bead, with neither `planned` nor `plan:revise`, is what puts
> it on Psylocke's second-look list (`scripts/second-look-beads`) — her main list is built from
> closed beads and would never show it. Adding `human` instead parks it in front of a person who has
> nothing to decide.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new. No label is added, no bead field is written, and no state file
changes. The fix is a query and two documents.

### The alternative that was considered and rejected

A **positive label** set by the hand-back — `verification:recheck` or similar — instead of inferring
from two absences. `ah-zuhs` raises it, and it reads more explicitly.

Rejected, for this bead: it is a new thing an implementer must remember at exactly the moment it is
handing work away, and forgetting it strands the bead again with no net. The absence *is* already
well-defined — `plan:revise` means a planner has it, `planned` means an implementer has it, so
neither means nobody — and nothing has to be added or cleaned up. If a future bead shows implementers
reaching a fourth state this cannot distinguish, revisit it then; do not add the label here.

## Increments

Run `bash tests/second-look-beads.sh` from `<tree>/.claude/cerebro` after each, and `bash tests/gate`
before the PR.

**Increment 1 — the test, against a fixture.**
Failing test: `tests/second-look-beads.sh`, which must not need a live database. Follow
`tests/work-beads.sh`'s shape, and drive the `jq` against a hand-written JSON array by putting a stub
`work-beads` earlier on `PATH` (or by factoring the `jq` into a variable the test can pipe into —
whichever `tests/work-beads.sh`'s existing style makes cleaner; read it first). Cover all six states:

| Fixture bead | Expected |
|---|---|
| open, `verdict:stale` | listed |
| open, `verification:failed`, no other labels | listed |
| open, `verification:failed` + `planned` | **not** listed |
| open, `verification:failed` + `plan:revise` | **not** listed |
| open, `verification:failed` + both `verdict:stale` and `planned` | listed **once**, by the stale arm |
| open, `["planned","verification:failed"]` — `planned` **first** | **not** listed |

That last row is the `index(...) | not` trap, and a test that omits it passes with a broken query.

**Increment 2 — the script.**
Add `scripts/second-look-beads`, `chmod +x`, and make increment 1 pass.

**Increment 3 — the verifier's pass.**
Replace the inline `jq` in `agents/verifier.md:140` with the script, and extend the prose above and
below it to name both states and what she does with each. No test; this is documentation, and the
behaviour it describes is what increments 1 and 2 pin.

**Increment 4 — the false sentence.**
Rewrite `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:352` as quoted above. Leave the hand-back commands exactly as
they are — they were never wrong.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/second-look-beads.sh` | cerebro submodule | all six states above, including the `index` trap and the no-double-listing case |

**The regression net:** `bash tests/gate` — it runs every `tests/*.sh`, so `tests/work-beads.sh` and
the rest must stay green. `tests/project-facts.sh` asserts the gate and CI still agree; if it fails,
the new test file has not been picked up the way the others are.

**A live check as well as the fixture, because this bug was a query that matched nothing:** from a
worktree, run `scripts/second-look-beads` against the real database and confirm it exits 0 and prints
either nothing or ids that genuinely are in that state. An empty result is expected — `ah-t2pn.3` was
unstuck by hand — so the fixture test is what proves the query works, and this run only proves it
executes.

## User-facing decisions

None. Nothing here reaches the application: two markdown documents and one script inside the harness
submodule. No message, no setting, no interface. The audience cannot observe this bead.

The one judgement worth recording is the planner's, not the navigator's: **the absence-based state
was kept and a positive label rejected** — see *Files to change*. It is an architecture decision, and
it is reversible in one bead if it proves wrong.

## Out of scope

- **Adding a `verification:recheck` label**, and any change to `implement-bead`'s hand-back
  *commands*. Only the sentence explaining them changes.
- **`ah-t2pn.3` itself.** Already unstuck by hand, and it now carries `plan:revise`, which makes it
  a planner's. This bead stops the next one being stranded; it does not rescue that one.
- **`work-beads`' own behaviour.** `--status open` already works. Do not change its default, which
  three readers have already learnt the hard way.
- **The verdict sweep (`sweep-verdicts.sh`)** and how `verdict:stale` gets set. Untouched.
- **`ah-tjaz`'s wider question** about the three states sharing one label set. This bead makes the
  third state reachable; whether the whole scheme wants redesigning is a separate conversation.

## Validation

```bash
# from <tree>/.claude/cerebro
bash tests/second-look-beads.sh     # after each increment
bash tests/gate                     # before the PR
scripts/second-look-beads           # a live run: exits 0, prints ids or nothing
```

The consumer's `pnpm run check:fast` is **not** the gate for this bead — nothing outside
`.claude/cerebro` changes — but the PR is against the **cerebro** repository, and the consumer then
needs a `chore(ah-zuhs): bump cerebro` commit to pin the new submodule sha. `implement-bead`'s
submodule section covers the two-PR shape.

**The human check:** read the rewritten sentence in `implement-bead/SKILL.md` and satisfy yourself it
is true, because the last one was false and nobody noticed for a day.

## Known traps

- **`work-beads` defaults to `--status closed`** (`scripts/work-beads:52`). That default is correct
  and is the whole reason this bead exists; the fix is a second call with `--status open`, never a
  change to the default.
- **`index(...) | not` versus a label at position 0.** Covered above and pinned by a fixture row. A
  query that gets this wrong lists a `planned` bead and sends the verifier to a bead an implementer
  is about to build.
- **A cerebro-only bead needs no worktree of the submodule** — `prepare-worktree` on the consumer
  already initialises it, and `git -C .claude/cerebro worktree add` makes a tree that the janitor
  historically never saw (`implement-bead/SKILL.md:421`, and four retrospectives).
- **The submodule tree arrives detached at the pinned sha.** Fetch and branch from `origin/main`
  inside it, or the PR is based on a commit behind cerebro's main.
- **`tests/gate` is not `tests/gate.sh`** — its own header explains that naming it so would make the
  suite loop run the gate from inside the gate.
- **This bead's own failure mode is believing a query without running it.** The live run in
  *Validation* is there for that reason; do not skip it because the fixture test is green.

title: A flagged taxer given a month-long order is still paid and warned for tax
description:
Found by adversarial review during ah-leeg (2026-08-24).

## The rule

**Taxing is a month-long order, and an explicit month-long order takes precedence over the autotax
flag.** A unit carrying the flag that is also ordered MOVE, STUDY or any other month-long order does
not tax at all - not in the hex it left, and not in the hex it arrives in, because the explicit order
consumed its month. Stated by the navigator on 2026-08-24, and it settles the attribution question an
earlier version of this description asked about: the answer is nowhere.

## The defect

`taxes(flags, intents)` (crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:1930) asks only whether the unit has a TAX
intent or a taxing flag. It never asks what else the unit is doing, so a flagged unit whose orders are
`MOVE N` is treated as taxing by everything downstream:

- the ledger credits it with this hex's tax income, so the Silver column shows money it will never
  earn;
- check_pillaged_tax marks its block 'a unit is pillaging this hex, so this TAX will collect nothing'
  (ah-fvzu);
- check_guarded_tax marks its block 'a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect
  nothing' (ah-leeg).

The two marks are false warnings about a hex the unit is leaving, and semantics.rs's own policy
(:13-17) is that a false warning costs the player confidence in every other line on the screen.

## What the fix is

One predicate. `taxes()` returns true for an explicit TAX order as it does today; the *flag* half
becomes conditional on nothing else claiming the month.

`spends_the_month(intent)` (crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:481) already answers that, and is
written as an exhaustive match on purpose so the compiler refuses a new Intent variant until somebody
has said which side of the line it falls on (ah-90w). `is_set_to_work` (silver.rs:1920), three lines
above `taxes()`, already composes in exactly this shape: `works_by_default(intents) && !taxes(...)`.

The ledger, check_pillaged_tax and check_guarded_tax all read `taxes()`, so all three become correct
together and cannot drift apart - which is why this is one fix rather than the three the earlier
description implied.

## Not a user-facing decision

The earlier description told its planner to decide the attribution first and treated it as a design
question. It is not: the rules decide it. Nothing here needs a mockup or an interview.
design:
## Context

**The rule, from the navigator on 2026-08-24:** taxing is a month-long order, and an explicit
month-long order takes precedence over the autotax flag. A unit carrying the flag that is also
ordered `MOVE`, `STUDY` or any other month-long order **does not tax at all** — not in the hex it
left, and not in the hex it arrives in, because the explicit order consumed its month.

`taxes(flags, intents)` (`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:1930`) does not know that. It asks only
whether the unit has a `TAX` intent or a taxing flag, and never what else the unit is doing:

```rust
intents.iter().any(|placed| matches!(placed.intent, Intent::Tax))
    || flags.iter().any(|flag| TAXING_FLAGS.iter().any(|known| flag.eq_ignore_ascii_case(known)))
```

So a flagged unit whose orders are `MOVE N` is treated as taxing by **every** surface downstream —
which is the good news, because they all read this one predicate and all become correct together.

**The fix is one predicate**, and the piece it needs already exists.
`works_by_default(intents)` (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:530`) is exactly
`!intents.iter().any(|placed| spends_the_month(&placed.intent))`, and `spends_the_month`
(`intents.rs:481`) is an exhaustive `match` written that way on purpose so the compiler refuses a
new `Intent` variant until somebody has said which side of the line it falls on (ah-90w).
`is_set_to_work` (`silver.rs:1920`), three lines above `taxes`, already composes in this shape.

**No user-facing decision.** An earlier version of this bead's description told its planner to decide
the attribution first — this hex, the destination hex, or nowhere — and treated it as a design
question. The rule settles it: nowhere. The description has been rewritten accordingly.

**When this lands, a flagged unit given a month-long order is not credited tax income it will never
earn, and is not warned about a hex it is leaving.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

One function body in `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`, plus tests. **No other production file
changes** — every consumer below reads `taxes()` and needs no edit.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `works_by_default(intents: &[PlacedIntent]) -> bool` (`intents.rs:530`) — already imported into
  `silver.rs` (`:19`). Use it; do not write `!intents.iter().any(spends_the_month)` by hand, and do
  not reach for `spends_the_month` directly.
- `spends_the_month(intent: &Intent) -> bool` (`intents.rs:481`) — the exhaustive match. Untouched.
- `TAXING_FLAGS: [&str; 2] = ["taxing", "autotax"]` (`silver.rs:108`) — both spellings. Untouched.
- `is_set_to_work` (`silver.rs:1920`) — the composition to copy, and a consumer to check (below).

### The design of the code

`taxes`'s signature, doc comment intent and both flag spellings are unchanged. Only the flag half
becomes conditional:

```rust
/// Whether this unit will tax this month - by an explicit `TAX` order, or because it carries the
/// taxing flag, which taxes every turn without one (`ah-fvzu`).
///
/// **A predicate, not a count.** A unit carrying the flag *and* given a `TAX` this turn still
/// taxes once, and this returns `true` for it exactly as for either alone.
///
/// **The flag only taxes a free month.** Taxing is itself a month-long order, and an explicit
/// month-long order takes precedence over the flag - so a flagged unit ordered `MOVE` or `STUDY`
/// taxes nowhere: not here, because it leaves, and not where it arrives, because the explicit
/// order spent its month (`ah-v8zh`). An explicit `TAX` is tested first and is unaffected: it is
/// itself a month-long order, so `works_by_default` is false for it.
#[must_use]
pub fn taxes(flags: &[String], intents: &[PlacedIntent]) -> bool {
    if intents.iter().any(|placed| matches!(placed.intent, Intent::Tax)) {
        return true;
    }
    works_by_default(intents)
        && flags.iter().any(|flag| {
            TAXING_FLAGS
                .iter()
                .any(|known| flag.eq_ignore_ascii_case(known))
        })
}
```

**The early return is load-bearing.** `spends_the_month(&Intent::Tax)` is `true`, so
`works_by_default` is `false` for a unit with an explicit `TAX`. Folding the two halves into one
`&&` would stop every explicit `TAX` order from taxing — the largest regression this bead could
produce, and the existing test `a_unit_with_a_tax_order_taxes` (`silver.rs:2515`) is what catches it.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere. `taxes` is a pure predicate over two borrowed slices and stays one.

### What changes downstream, and why none of it needs an edit

All seven live consumers read `taxes()`. Three are the reported defect; two more change as a
consequence and are **also** corrections; two do not change at all. The implementer must know which
is which before running the suite, because two of these will move test expectations.

| Consumer | Effect for a flagged unit with a month-long order |
|---|---|
| `credit_tax` (`semantics.rs:1607`) | **Reported.** Stops crediting the ledger with income it will not earn. |
| `check_pillaged_tax` (`semantics.rs:1486`, call at `:1512`) | **Reported.** The false ah-fvzu mark stops firing. |
| `check_guarded_tax` (`semantics.rs:1537`, call at `:1571`) | **Reported.** The false ah-leeg mark stops firing. |
| `price_tax` via `forecast_unit` (`silver.rs:790`) | **Reported.** The Silver column stops showing the income. |
| `pool_wants` (`silver.rs:398`) | **Consequential, and correct.** The unit stops contending for the region's tax base, so every *other* taxer's settled share gets larger. `region-pool-oversubscribed` findings may change. |
| `check_trade_regions` (`semantics.rs:4374`, call at `:4397`) | **Consequential, and correct.** The origin region stops counting against the trade allowance for a unit that will not tax it. `too-many-trade-regions` findings may change. |
| `taxes_by_flag` on `UnitSilver` (`silver.rs:1138`) | **Consequential, and correct.** The hover sentence *"This unit is set to tax every turn, so it taxes without an order."* (`packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts:573`) stops appearing — it exists to explain income that is no longer there. **No wording change**; the sentence is right whenever it now shows. |
| `is_set_to_work` (`silver.rs:1920`) | **No change.** `works_by_default(intents) && !taxes(..)` — `works_by_default` is already `false` for a unit with a month-long order, so the result was `false` before and is `false` after. |
| `check_idle_units` (`semantics.rs:3808`, call at `:3832`) | **No change.** The `taxes()` exemption is immediately followed by `if ordered.intents().any(spends_the_month) { continue; }` (`:3834`), which already exempts a moving unit. A flagged unit with *no* orders — the case that exemption exists for (`ah-fvzu`) — still has `works_by_default == true`, so it still taxes and is still exempt. |

That last row is the one regression risk worth naming explicitly: if the change accidentally made a
flagged, orderless unit stop taxing, it would newly be reported as `unit-does-nothing`. It does not,
and increment 1's second test pins it.

## Increments

**Increment 1 — the predicate.**
Failing test: `a_flagged_unit_given_a_month_long_order_does_not_tax`, in `silver.rs`'s `mod tests`,
beside the existing `a_unit_with_the_taxing_flag_taxes` (`:2520`):

```rust
// `Intent::Study { skill: String }` (`intents.rs:39`) is the cheapest month-long order to build;
// `Intent::Move { steps: Vec<MoveStep> }` (`intents.rs:80`) needs a `MoveStep` and an empty
// `steps` vec is enough, since `spends_the_month` matches the variant and never reads the field.
assert!(!taxes(&flags(&["taxing"]), &[placed(Intent::Move { steps: Vec::new() })]));
assert!(!taxes(&flags(&["autotax"]), &[placed(Intent::Study { skill: "COMB".to_string() })]));
// the flag still taxes a free month, in both spellings
assert!(taxes(&flags(&["taxing"]), &[]));
assert!(taxes(&flags(&["autotax"]), &[]));
// and an explicit TAX is unaffected, whatever else the unit carries
assert!(taxes(&[], &[placed(Intent::Tax)]));
assert!(taxes(&flags(&["taxing"]), &[placed(Intent::Tax)]));
```

`flags(&[..])` (`silver.rs:2510`) and `placed(..)` (`silver.rs:2377`) are the file's existing
helpers, already used by the three tests at `:2515-2528`. Then make the change.

**Increment 2 — the three reported surfaces, together.**
Failing test: `a_flagged_taxer_that_moves_is_not_credited_or_warned`, in `semantics.rs`'s test module.
One hex, pillaged or foreign-guarded so both marks would otherwise fire, holding one own unit with
the `taxing` flag whose only order is a `MOVE`. Assert `codes(&check(..))` contains neither
`taxed-a-pillaged-hex` nor `taxed-a-guarded-hex`, and that the unit's ledger silver is not credited
the region's tax base. Then add a sibling asserting the same unit **without** the `MOVE` still gets
both — so the test cannot pass by the checks having been disabled.

This test should already be green after increment 1. If it is not, one of the three surfaces does not
in fact read `taxes()`, and that is a finding to report before going further.

**Increment 3 — the two consequential consumers.**
Failing test: `a_flagged_taxer_that_moves_does_not_contend_for_the_region` — a hex with two own
units, both flagged, one of them ordered `MOVE`, and a `tax_base` too small for both. Assert the
staying unit's settled tax share is the full ask rather than a split, and that
`region-pool-oversubscribed` does not fire. This is a behaviour change nobody asked for that follows
from the rule, and it must be pinned deliberately rather than discovered as a moved expectation.

Then run the full suite and **read every failure before changing anything**. Any existing test that
now fails is either (a) one of the two consequential consumers above, in which case update its
expectation and say in the commit message which and why, or (b) a genuine regression. Do not update
an expectation without deciding which it is.

**Increment 4 — the corpus cross-check.**
No new test. Run
`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning` on its own and confirm green.
Both surfaces read `taxes()`, so they move together and this should hold — but this is the test that
exists to catch exactly the case where they do not, and it is worth one deliberate run.

## The test plan

Rust only. Nothing in `packages/` changes and no browser suite is touched.

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `a_flagged_unit_given_a_month_long_order_does_not_tax` | `silver.rs` tests | the rule, and that explicit `TAX` survives |
| `a_flagged_taxer_that_moves_is_not_credited_or_warned` | `semantics.rs` tests | the ledger and both marks, together |
| its sibling without the `MOVE` | `semantics.rs` tests | the test is not vacuous |
| `a_flagged_taxer_that_moves_does_not_contend_for_the_region` | `semantics.rs` tests | the consequential pool change |

**Existing tests that must stay green untouched**, and which each guard a specific way of getting
this wrong:

- `a_unit_with_a_tax_order_taxes` (`silver.rs:2515`) — the early return.
- `a_unit_with_the_taxing_flag_taxes` (`:2520`) and `a_unit_with_the_autotax_spelling_taxes` (`:2525`)
  — the flag still taxes a free month, in both spellings.
- `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — the two surfaces over 26 real turns.
- `semantics.rs`'s `codes::ALL` fixture sweep — every code still reachable.

## User-facing decisions

None, and this is a bead where that statement needs its reason stated.

The change *is* visible — a moving flagged unit's Silver figure drops, two warnings stop appearing,
and a hover sentence stops showing — but none of it is a choice. Each surface becomes correct
according to a game rule the navigator stated, and every string involved already exists and keeps its
wording. The one thing that looked like a design question in the bead's original description — where
a moving taxer's income is attributed — is answered by the rules, not by preference.

No mockup was made and none was needed.

## Out of scope

- **Changing any message.** `taxed-a-pillaged-hex`, `taxed-a-guarded-hex` and the
  `"This unit is set to tax every turn, so it taxes without an order."` hover sentence all keep their
  exact wording. They fire less often; they do not say anything new.
- **A unit given both an explicit `TAX` and another month-long order.** Two month-long orders is a
  conflict the engine resolves its own way, and `taxes()` returns `true` for it today and after this
  bead. If it deserves a warning of its own, that is a new bead and a question for the navigator.
- **`is_set_to_work` and `check_idle_units`.** Neither changes; the table in *Files to change* says
  why. Do not "align" them.
- **`works_by_default` and `spends_the_month`.** Both are correct and are reused as they stand.
- **`ah-lu0f.2`, `.3` and `.4`** — the rest of the silver double-pricing epic. This bead touches
  `taxes()` only, not the pricing seam `ah-lu0f.1` established.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core                                        # after each increment
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning  # increment 4, on its own
pnpm run check:fast                                                    # before the PR
```

**The human check:** load `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, find an own unit carrying the `taxing`
or `autotax` flag, give it a `MOVE`, and confirm its Silver figure loses the tax income and its block
loses any tax warning — and that removing the `MOVE` brings all of it back. Worth doing because this
bead's whole claim is about what the player sees.

## Known traps

- **Test the explicit `TAX` before the flag, and return early.** `spends_the_month(&Intent::Tax)` is
  `true`, so a single `works_by_default(..) && (tax_order || flag)` would stop every explicit `TAX`
  from taxing. This is the one way to get this change badly wrong.
- **Two consumers change that the bead does not mention** — `pool_wants` (`silver.rs:398`) and
  `check_trade_regions` (`semantics.rs:4374`). Both move in the correct direction, but they will move
  existing expectations. Increment 3 exists so they are pinned rather than discovered.
- **`TAXING_FLAGS` has two spellings** (`silver.rs:108`), `"taxing"` and `"autotax"`, matched
  case-insensitively. A test using only one proves half the rule.
- **`check_idle_units`' `taxes()` exemption is for a flagged unit with no orders at all**
  (`semantics.rs:3828-3833`, `ah-fvzu`). That case keeps `works_by_default == true` and is unaffected
  — but if it ever were, the unit would newly be told it "has no order that spends the month", which
  is exactly the unfollowable advice `ah-udff` removed.
- **The corpus test is the cross-surface gate** (`silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs`, and the reason
  ah-ycuj and ah-8l9a exist). Both surfaces read `taxes()`, so it should stay green; if it does not,
  something reads the flag directly instead of through the predicate.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, since nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: An overdrawn gift in a sharing hex is warned about the hex, not the line
description:
Closed as correct behaviour on 2026-08-24, after Xavier probed it against the real fixture.

`validate_turn` was run against neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep for WoodsmenY (15189) at (36,4),
which holds one horse:

  GIVE 0 20000 HORS       -> not-enough-items, "the units in this hex are short 19155 horses
                             between them: they can have 845 and their orders spend 20000"
  GIVE NEW 1 20000 HORS   -> the same finding, identically
  GIVE 16435 5 HORS       -> nothing
  GIVE 0 5 HORS           -> nothing

The discard IS called short. The finding is hex-anchored (unit_id and line both null), because
hex (36,4) holds three sharing units - Carpenters (12881), Workers (6567), ArmorerA (5671) -
so HORS pools and `report_shortfalls` judges the pool rather than the unit. It reaches the player
through `findingsForHex` in the region panel; `orderLint.ts:31` and `orderEditor.ts:171` both drop
a finding with no line, which is why nothing marks the order line itself.

The 5-horse gift to a real unit is silent for the same reason and is likewise correct: the hex's
sharers pool 845 horses, which covers a claim of 4.

`party_id` is not implicated. Party::Discard, Party::New and Party::Foreign behave identically
here, and in a hex with no sharing units all four party kinds produce the ordinary per-unit
`not-enough-items` finding on the line. `transfer` charges the giver in every case.

The navigator judged this correct behaviour rather than a defect. The related structural concern -
that `report_shortfalls` answers three ways and says which to nobody - is ah-3ddq (P2).
close_reason: Not a defect. Probed against neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82: GIVE 0 20000 HORS does produce not-enough-items, hex-anchored because hex (36,4) has three sharing units and HORS pools. Party::Discard, New and Foreign behave identically; party_id is not implicated. Navigator judged the behaviour correct on 2026-08-24.

title: An open bead carrying a stale assignee is skipped by every implementer
description:
Found by Xavier on 2026-08-23, by reading bd ready by hand rather than by any check.

ah-fjty was reopened at P0 by a failed verification. It came back with status=open (no lease) but still naming assignee=Cyclops. It then sat at the top of bd ready for 32 minutes while implementers took lower-priority beads - Cyclops itself picked up ah-gjq4 (P1) in that window while still named on the P0.

So an open bead that carries an assignee appears to be skipped by 'bd ready --claim'. The bead is visible in bd ready and looks perfectly healthy; it is simply never taken. The navigator approved clearing the assignee by hand, which unstranded it.

## Why this is worth catching rather than noticing

Nothing in the fleet looks for it. Cerebro already sweeps two neighbouring shapes - a bead left in_progress whose work is already on main (a delivered bead whose implementer died), and an epic left open under a full set of closed children. Both are 'a field says something no live session backs up'. This is the third of that family and the most damaging, because it strands the highest-priority work specifically: a P0 at the top of the queue that every implementer walks past.

It reached P0 through the reopen path, which is exactly where it hurts most - a bead Psylocke sends back is by definition urgent.

## What to check

An open bead whose assignee names no live session, or names a session demonstrably working a different bead. The liveness evidence is the same one every other sweep uses: .cerebro/state/<name>.state.json plus scripts/agent-alive, and that file's own 'bead' field says what the session is actually on.

Worth confirming first whether the skip really is 'bd ready --claim' refusing an assigned bead, or something upstream of it - the observation is behavioural, not read out of bd's source.
design:
## Context

A bead reopened by a failed verification comes back `status=open` — **no lease** — but still naming
its old assignee. Every implementer then walks past it: an open bead carrying an assignee is not
picked up by `bd ready --claim`.

Twice on 2026-08-23, within half an hour, and both times a **P0**:

| Bead | Assignee on file | What that session was actually doing |
|---|---|---|
| `ah-fjty` | `Cyclops` | building `ah-gjq4` |
| `ah-t2pn.3` | `Wolverine` | building `ah-1ad6.1` |

`ah-fjty` sat 32 minutes at the top of `bd ready` while Cyclops finished a bead and took a **P1**
below it. Both were found only because a planner read `bd ready` by hand, and both were cleared by
hand with the navigator's approval.

**This strands the highest-priority work specifically**, because the reopen path is where it happens
and a reopened bead is P0 by definition (`agents/verifier.md`). Nothing in the fleet looks for it.

**It is the fifth of a family the fleet view already has four of** — see `agents/orchestrator.md`:
*Beads that finished without being closed* (`:340`), *Epics left open under closed children* (`:481`),
*Claims held by a session that has stopped moving* (`:535`), and the worktree prune (`:281`). Every
one is *"a field says something no live session backs up"*, and this is the same shape.

**This bead lives in the `cerebro` submodule**, not in `atlantis-hud`. See *Files to change*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**Everything is in `.claude/cerebro/`, a git submodule of its own
(`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git`, branch `main`).** The work is a PR **in that
repository**, followed by a submodule-pointer bump in `atlantis-hud` — the consumer's history already
carries `chore: bump cerebro` commits doing exactly that. Branch in a worktree named with the
`-cerebro` suffix the existing ones use (`.cerebro/worktrees/<id>-cerebro`), which keeps it distinct
from a consumer-side worktree for the same bead.

**Copy `scripts/sweep-stalled.sh` + `cerebro--stalled-finding` as a pair.** They are the newest of
the four and the closest in shape: a read-only script that gathers facts, and a *pure* elisp function
that turns them into a decision.

### The invariant this must not break

`scripts/sweep-claims.sh`'s header states it, and it is why the design is checkable at a glance:

> *This script never mutates anything — no `bd close`, no `bd reclaim`, no git write of any kind …
> Keeping this script read-only is what makes that guarantee checkable at a glance: the only way to
> reach a `bd close` or `bd reclaim` invocation is through the confirmed path in `cerebro.el`.*

And `cerebro--finding-command` is documented as *"the complete list of destructive commands the fleet
view can run"*. **The new sweep obeys both**: the script reads, the finding function is pure, and the
`bd update` runs only from `cerebro--finding-command`, on confirmation.

### `scripts/sweep-assignees.sh` — new, read-only

```
.claude/cerebro/scripts/sweep-assignees.sh --json
```

One object per bead with `status=open` **and** a non-empty `assignee`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | the bead id |
| `assignee` | whatever `bd` has on file |
| `title` | for the confirmation prompt |
| `priority` | the integer, so the fleet view can shout for a `0` |
| `age_min` | minutes since `updated_at` |

`in_progress` beads are **not** emitted at all: a live claim is the claims and stalled sweeps'
business, and emitting it here would put two lines in front of the navigator for one bead — the
reason `cerebro--stalled-finding` gives for its own first guard.

**`age_min` comes from `updated_at`, and an edit resets it. That is correct, not a compromise**: a
bead somebody has just touched is one somebody is attending to, and waiting another cycle before
offering it is right. It is also the only clock available — an open bead has no lease, so there is no
`lease_expires_at` to measure from as `sweep-claims.sh` does.

Model the argument parsing, the `--json` contract and the header comment on `sweep-stalled.sh`.

### `emacs/cerebro.el` — one read, three derivations

`cerebro--live-session-states` (`:746`) returns `(NAME . STATE)` and its docstring records the
pattern: *"`cerebro--findings-from` derives both from one call to this."* This sweep needs a third
fact — **which bead each live session is on** — which is the `bead` key of the same state file it
already parses.

**Refactor rather than read the files twice:**

```elisp
(defun cerebro--live-sessions (repo-root)
  "(NAME STATE BEAD) for every implementer with a live session in REPO-ROOT.
The single read the three derivations below share; a name is present exactly
when its state file parses and its pid is alive, whatever that file says."
  ...)

(defun cerebro--live-session-states (repo-root) ...)   ; (NAME . STATE), as today
(defun cerebro--live-session-beads  (repo-root) ...)   ; (NAME . BEAD), new
```

`cerebro--live-session-states` and `cerebro--live-implementer-names` keep their exact present
signatures and return values, so `cerebro--claim-finding` and `cerebro--stalled-finding` are
untouched. **Liveness stays `cerebro--session-alive-p`**, which checks the pid's own `--name`; a bare
pid check makes a recycled pid look like a live session.

### `emacs/cerebro.el` — the finding

```elisp
(defun cerebro--assignee-finding (candidate live-beads roster now)
  "Pure. What the assignee sweep should offer for CANDIDATE, or nil.

CANDIDATE is one parsed object from `sweep-assignees.sh --json'. LIVE-BEADS is
an alist of (NAME . BEAD) for sessions whose pid is alive. ROSTER is the
implementer roster. NOW is unused, taken for symmetry with the other findings.

Returns nil or (unassign ID). Nil covers four cases: the assignee is not a
roster name, so it was assigned by hand and is not ours to undo; the session
is alive and on this very bead, so it is about to claim it; the bead was
touched inside the grace period, so somebody may be attending to it; or there
is no age to judge."
  (ignore now)
  (let-alist candidate
    (cond
     ((not (member .assignee roster)) nil)
     ((equal (cdr (assoc .assignee live-beads)) .id) nil)
     ((null .age_min) nil)
     ((< .age_min cerebro-stale-assignee-minutes) nil)
     (t (list 'unassign .id)))))
```

Note what is **absent**: there is no "the session is not alive" arm, because that case falls through
to `(unassign ID)` and should. A roster session that is not running cannot be about to claim
anything.

```elisp
(defcustom cerebro-stale-assignee-minutes 10
  "How long an open bead may carry an assignee no live session is on before the
sweep offers to clear it. Ten minutes is one sweep cycle, so a bead is seen
twice before it is offered - long enough that a claim in flight is never
interrupted, short enough that a stranded P0 surfaces on the next pass."
  :type 'integer :group 'cerebro)
```

### The label — `cerebro--sweep-label` (`:638`)

One arm, matching the shipped shape exactly (verb, id, em dash, reason):

```elisp
(`(unassign ,id)
 (format "unassign %s — %s is %s" id .assignee
         (if .assignee_bead (format "on %s" .assignee_bead) "not running")))
```

`.assignee_bead` is **not** a field of the script's output — the script reads `bd`, not the state
files, and cannot know it. **Enrich the candidate in `cerebro--findings-from` before labelling**, so
`cerebro--sweep-label` keeps its two-argument shape and stays a pure formatter like its other three
arms.

Shipped examples, for the shape to match:

```
close ah-xxxx — delivered by Storm, on main 14m
reclaim ah-xxxx — Rogue gone, not on main
unclaim ah-xxxx — Gambit stalled, no commit for 71m
unassign ah-fjty — Cyclops is on ah-gjq4
unassign ah-fjty — Cyclops is not running
```

### Shouting for a P0 — `cerebro--sweep-line` (`:657`)

A stranded **P0** renders its Sweeps line in the `warning` face — the same face `cerebro.el:281`
gives an `asking` session's `?` marker, which is the fleet view's existing way of saying *this one
needs you*. Every other priority renders as the other sweep lines do.

**Reuse the face; do not invent a new one, a new glyph, a popup or a sound.** The escalation is that
a P0 line is visibly different from the rest of the section, nothing more.

### The command — `cerebro--finding-command`

One arm:

```elisp
(`(unassign ,id) (list "bd" "update" id "--assignee" ""))
```

This is the **only** place the write may live, per the invariant above.

### Registration — `cerebro--sweep-scripts` (`:875`)

```elisp
(sweep-assignees . "sweep-assignees.sh")
```

appended last, and `cerebro--findings-from` gains the matching argument in the same position — its
docstring records that the parsed outputs arrive *"as arguments in this same order"*.

### `agents/orchestrator.md`

A new section after *Claims held by a session that has stopped moving* (`:535`), in the voice of its
neighbours: what the sweep looks for, the evidence (both P0s of 2026-08-23, named), the four guards
and why each is a case it must stay out of, and what clearing an assignee does and does not buy —
**it makes the bead pickable; it does not answer why the assignee was left behind.**

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el`

Tests for `cerebro--assignee-finding`, one per guard. It is pure, which is what makes that possible
and is why the guards live there rather than in the script.

## Increments

1. **The script reports the facts, and writes nothing.**
   RED: no elisp yet. Run `scripts/sweep-assignees.sh --json` against a `bd` state containing an open
   bead with an assignee and confirm the object's five fields. Then
   `grep -n "bd update\|bd close\|bd reclaim\|git " scripts/sweep-assignees.sh` and confirm **no
   match** — the invariant, checked the way its own header says it should be.
   GREEN: `scripts/sweep-assignees.sh`.

2. **The finding is pure, and its guards hold.**
   RED: `emacs/cerebro-test.el` — five cases, each asserting the return value:
   `an-assignee-off-the-roster-is-left-alone` (nil),
   `a-session-alive-on-this-bead-is-left-alone` (nil),
   `a-bead-touched-inside-the-grace-period-is-left-alone` (nil),
   `a-session-alive-on-another-bead-is-offered` (`(unassign "ah-fjty")`),
   `a-session-that-is-not-running-is-offered` (`(unassign "ah-fjty")`).
   GREEN: `cerebro--assignee-finding` and the `defcustom`.

3. **The live read gains the bead, and nothing else moves.**
   RED: a test asserting `cerebro--live-session-states` returns exactly what it returns today for a
   given set of state files, and a new one for `cerebro--live-session-beads`.
   GREEN: `cerebro--live-sessions` and the two derivations. **`cerebro--claim-finding` and
   `cerebro--stalled-finding` must not be edited**; if they need editing, the refactor changed a
   signature it should not have.

4. **The line reads right, and a P0 shouts.**
   RED: tests asserting the two label strings verbatim, and that a `priority` of `0` produces a line
   carrying the `warning` face while a `2` does not.
   GREEN: the `cerebro--sweep-label` arm and the `cerebro--sweep-line` face.

5. **The command is the only write.**
   RED: a test asserting `cerebro--finding-command` returns
   `("bd" "update" "ah-fjty" "--assignee" "")` for `(unassign "ah-fjty")`.
   GREEN: the arm.

6. **Wire it in.** `cerebro--sweep-scripts`, `cerebro--findings-from`, and the candidate enrichment
   that gives the label the assignee's current bead. Run the fleet view against a repository in the
   stranded state and confirm the line appears and the key clears it.

7. **The prose.** The `agents/orchestrator.md` section.

8. **Bump the consumer.** A `chore: bump cerebro` commit in `atlantis-hud` moving the submodule
   pointer, once the cerebro PR is merged.

## The test plan

**Elisp, `emacs/cerebro-test.el`** — every test named in *Increments*. The guards are tested through
`cerebro--assignee-finding` because it is pure; that purity is the point of the split and must be
preserved.

**The script has no test harness in this repository**, which is why increment 1's check is a `grep`
for mutating commands and a manual `--json` read. **Say so in the PR** rather than implying coverage
that does not exist.

**What must not move:** `cerebro--claim-finding`, `cerebro--stalled-finding`, `cerebro--epic-finding`
and their tests. The refactor in increment 3 is behaviour-preserving by construction, and their tests
passing unchanged is the proof.

**Run the whole elisp suite**, however this repository runs it — check `cerebro`'s own README or CI
configuration for the command; it is not `pnpm run check:fast`, which is the consumer's.

**No consumer-side tests**: `atlantis-hud` gains one `chore: bump cerebro` commit and nothing else.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23 against `docs/ui/ah-kjfm-sweep.html`. **The fleet view
is the navigator's own surface**, so all three of these are theirs.

**Does the sweep act, or ask?**
**Chosen: confirm like the other four, but shout for a P0.** A stranded P0's Sweeps line renders in
the `warning` face, the same face an `asking` session's marker already uses.
*Rejected — confirm exactly like the other four*: the invariant stays perfectly simple and every
destructive path stays in one auditable list — but the failure this bead exists to fix is that
**nobody was looking**, and a line nobody presses strands the P0 just as silently.
*Rejected — clear it automatically and report*: nothing is destroyed, since the lease is already gone
and no work is taken off anyone, so it is closer to tidying than to `bd close` — rejected because it
would make this the one sweep that writes without asking, and that invariant is what makes the fleet
view's safety checkable at a glance.

**The Sweeps line, shipping verbatim:**

> `unassign ah-fjty — Cyclops is on ah-gjq4`
> `unassign ah-fjty — Cyclops is not running`

*Rejected — leading with the cost* (`unassign ah-fjty — P0 stranded, Cyclops is on ah-gjq4`): puts
the damage first, but only this sweep would carry a priority in its label, breaking the family's
symmetry — and the `warning` face already carries that signal.
*Rejected — naming the fault rather than the bead* (`Cyclops holds it but is not on it`): shorter and
it cannot go stale if the session moves again, but it tells the navigator less.

**The grace period.**
**Chosen: 10 minutes**, as `cerebro-stale-assignee-minutes`. The sweeps run ten-minutely, so a bead
is effectively seen twice before it is offered — long enough that a re-claim in flight is never
interrupted, short enough that a stranded P0 surfaces on the next pass.
*Rejected — 5 minutes*: surfaces on the very next cycle, at some risk of offering a bead an
implementer is a moment from claiming. *Rejected — 30 minutes*: conservative and in the spirit of the
60-minute stalled threshold, but `ah-fjty` sat 32 minutes and would only just have been caught.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** an `in_progress`
bead is never emitted by this sweep, because a live claim belongs to the claims and stalled sweeps;
an assignee that is not a roster name is never offered, because it was assigned by hand and is not
ours to undo; a session alive **on the bead itself** is never offered, because it is about to claim
it; and `age_min` is measured from `updated_at`, so an edit resets the clock — which is right, since
a bead somebody just touched is one somebody is attending to.

## Out of scope

- **Why the assignee is left behind in the first place.** This sweep cleans up after it; finding out
  whether `bd`, the reopen path in `agents/verifier.md`, or an implementer's own exit leaves the
  field set is a separate investigation and a better fix. **Worth filing** — a sweep is a net, not a
  cure.
- **Confirming that `bd ready --claim` really refuses an assigned bead.** The observation is
  behavioural — two P0s skipped for 32 minutes and then taken immediately once cleared — not read out
  of `bd`'s source. The sweep is worth having either way, since an open bead naming a session that is
  elsewhere is wrong regardless of what skips it.
- **Any change to the other four sweeps**, beyond the behaviour-preserving refactor in increment 3.
- **Anything in `atlantis-hud`** except the one `chore: bump cerebro` commit.

## Validation

In the `cerebro` repository:

```
scripts/sweep-assignees.sh --json          # reads; prints one object per open assigned bead
grep -n "bd update\|bd close\|bd reclaim\|git " scripts/sweep-assignees.sh   # must print nothing
```

plus the elisp test suite, run however this repository runs it.

**Checkable only by a human, and worth doing before opening the PR**: put a repository into the
stranded state — an open bead at P0 whose assignee names a roster session working something else —
open the fleet view, and confirm three things: the Sweeps line appears with the wording above, it is
visibly distinct from a non-P0 line, and the key clears the assignee so the bead becomes pickable.

## Known traps

- **The scripts never mutate.** `sweep-claims.sh`'s header states it and gives the reason: it is what
  makes "the only path to a destructive command is the confirmed one" checkable by reading a single
  file. A `bd update` in `sweep-assignees.sh` would pass every test in this plan and quietly destroy
  that guarantee. Increment 1's `grep` exists for this.
- **`cerebro--assignee-finding` must stay pure.** The guards are testable only because the other
  findings are pure; reaching into the filesystem from it would make this the one that cannot be
  tested.
- **Do not edit `cerebro--claim-finding` or `cerebro--stalled-finding`.** The increment-3 refactor
  preserves `cerebro--live-session-states`' signature precisely so they need no change; if they do,
  the refactor went further than it should.
- **This is a submodule.** The work is a PR in `rmstdope/cerebro`, then a pointer bump in
  `atlantis-hud`. A change made in `.claude/cerebro/` from a consumer worktree without committing it
  in the submodule's own repository is lost on the next `git submodule update`.
- **Liveness is `cerebro--session-alive-p`, never a bare pid check.** Pids are recycled, and a
  recycled pid makes a dead session look alive — which here would suppress a real finding.
- **`bd ready` lists a bead it will not let anyone claim.** That is the whole defect, and it makes the
  problem invisible from the queue: the bead looks perfectly healthy and is simply never taken. Do
  not expect `bd ready` to reveal anything; the state files are the evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Cerebro's sweep reports, and clears, an open bead whose assignee names no live session or names one working a different bead - alongside the stranded-claim and open-epic sweeps it already runs. It says which bead and what the assignee was, rather than clearing silently. A bead genuinely in_progress with a live heartbeat is never touched.
