title: An idle unit is warned it will starve, though it will work and earn wages
description:
Found during verification of the silver family (2026-08-23, at dd3f67bd).

A unit with no month-long order issued automatically WORKs, and work pays the region's wage. The forecast prices only an explicit Intent::Work, so an idle unit is shown earning nothing - and, since its upkeep is still charged, it can be shown short of money or starving when the wages it will actually earn would have paid for it.

That last part is why this matters beyond a wrong number: it is the same false-alarm class as ah-fjty, ah-eacd, ah-e66j and ah-tdsi, all four of which warned about a unit something was going to pay for. An idle unit is probably the most common unit in a real turn, so this may be the widest remaining source of spurious not-enough-silver warnings.

Where it goes: wages are already priced for the explicit order - late_income in crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs (~348), which correctly treats work as arriving in the turn's last phase and therefore unable to fund this month's orders. A defaulted WORK should be priced through exactly that same path, not a new one. The ledger in crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs needs the matching arm so the two surfaces agree, per ah-ycuj's corpus-wide test.

Open questions for planning:

  - what counts as a month-long order, precisely - the set that suppresses the default (STUDY, MOVE, BUILD, PRODUCE, TAX, PILLAGE, ENTERTAIN, TEACH and so on), and which of those the parsed model already distinguishes
  - whether a unit that is on guard, or in a structure, or has no men, is excluded
  - whether the forecast should state a defaulted WORK visibly, so the player can see why the silver appeared, rather than crediting it silently
design:
## Context

A unit with no month-long order automatically `WORK`s, and work pays the region's wage. The forecast
prices only an **explicit** `Intent::Work` (`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:396-415`,
`late_income`), so an idle unit is shown earning nothing — while its upkeep is still charged. It can
be shown short of money, or starving, when the wages it will really earn would have paid.

That is the same false-alarm class as `ah-fjty`, `ah-eacd`, `ah-e66j` and `ah-tdsi`, all four of
which warned about a unit something was going to pay for — **and it is the widest of them**, because
an idle unit is probably the commonest unit in a real turn.

**The definition this bead needs is already shipped.** `spends_the_month` (`semantics.rs:714`) is an
exhaustive `match` over `Intent`, written that way on purpose: its own comment records that
`is_busy` was once a `matches!` with a fixed list, and *"a variant missing from such a list returns
`false` silently — the failure `ah-90w` had to write a regression test against when `BUILD` gained a
shape."* It already places `GUARD` (a flag, not a month's work), `CAST` (the rules leave the month
free), `IDLE` and `ANNIHILATE` on the right sides. **This bead defines nothing and reuses it**, which
answers the bead's first open question outright.

**One change covers both surfaces.** The ledger's `apply` credits nothing for `Intent::Work`
(`semantics.rs:1370`) — wages reach the model only through `late_income`, which `forecast_unit` and
`charge_upkeep` share on purpose (`ah-uwa3`). So teaching `late_income` about the default teaches
both, and **`ah-ycuj`'s corpus agreement test is safe by construction** rather than by care.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs` — move `spends_the_month` here

`late_income` lives in `silver.rs`, which is *"arithmetic over values"*; `spends_the_month` lives in
`semantics.rs`, the orchestrator that already depends on `silver`. Calling upward from `silver` into
`semantics` inverts that. **Move the function** — it is a pure function of `Intent`, and `Intent` is
defined here:

```rust
/// Whether this order consumes the unit's month.
/// ...(keep the existing doc comment verbatim, including the `ah-90w` rationale)...
#[must_use]
pub fn spends_the_month(intent: &Intent) -> bool { /* body unchanged */ }

/// Whether a unit with these orders will be set to work by default.
///
/// A unit that spends its month on nothing is made to `WORK`, and work pays the region's wage. The
/// same predicate the `unit-does-nothing` advisory uses, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about
/// which units are idle (`ah-gjq4`).
#[must_use]
pub fn works_by_default(intents: &[PlacedIntent]) -> bool {
    !intents.iter().any(|placed| spends_the_month(&placed.intent))
}
```

A pure move: update the callers at `semantics.rs:893` (`is_busy`) and `semantics.rs:3184`
(`check_idle_units`), and the tests at `semantics.rs:5066-5101`, which may stay where they are or
move with the function — **but they must not be deleted**, since they are the record of where each
order falls.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — `late_income` prices the default

`late_income` (`silver.rs:396`) gains one term, after its loop:

```rust
    // A unit that spends its month on nothing is set to work, and work pays the region's wage
    // exactly as an explicit `WORK` does (`ah-gjq4`). Priced here rather than beside the explicit
    // arm so it is unmistakably a default and not a second `Intent::Work`, and priced through this
    // function so `semantics::charge_upkeep` sees it too - wages arrive in the turn's last phase,
    // which is why they pay upkeep and cannot fund this month's orders.
    if works_by_default(facts.intents) {
        let earned = facts.men.saturating_mul(region.wage_centis.unwrap_or(0)) / 100;
        late = late.saturating_add(earned.min(region.max_wages.unwrap_or(i64::MAX)));
    }
```

**The expression is identical to the `Intent::Work` arm's, and that is deliberate**: they are the
same rule. If `ah-t2pn.2` has landed, that arm reads `shares.wages` instead — see *Known traps*, and
mirror whatever it does.

**A unit with no men earns nothing without a special case**: `men` is `0`, so `earned` is `0`. Do not
add a guard; `check_idle_units`'s `men == 0` exemption exists to avoid unfollowable *advice*, which
is a different question from arithmetic.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the estimated-headcount gate

**This is the change most likely to be missed, and it ships a wrong number if it is.** The
short-circuit at `silver.rs:537` is *conditional*:

```rust
if men_estimated && intents.iter().any(moves_silver_per_man) {
```

`moves_silver_per_man` (`silver.rs:1566`) lists `Tax`, `Work`, `Study`, `Entertain`, `Produce` — all
per-man rules. **An idle unit has no intents at all**, so the condition is false, the short-circuit
does not fire, and a defaulted wage would be multiplied out of a headcount that is a guess — the
precise defect that gate exists to prevent. It becomes:

```rust
if men_estimated && (intents.iter().any(moves_silver_per_man) || works_by_default(intents)) {
```

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — one new field

On `UnitSilver`, so the hover can explain income the player never ordered:

```rust
/// Whether this unit has no month-long order and will therefore be set to work, earning the
/// region's wage. `false` for every unit that spends its month on something (`ah-gjq4`).
///
/// Carried so the hover can say where the silver came from: income arriving from an order nobody
/// wrote reads as a defect until something says why - the same reason `own_food_covered` and
/// `unclaimed_covered` are carried.
pub works_by_default: bool,
```

Set in **both** constructors — the estimated-headcount early return (`silver.rs:538`) and the main
return — as `ah-eacd` and `ah-e66j` each had to. `packages/core-client/src/generated/UnitSilver.ts`
is regenerated, never hand-edited.

### `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts`

One entry in `silverNote`'s one-note-wins table, verbatim:

```
This unit has no month-long order, so it will work and earn wages.
```

Gated on `silver.worksByDefault`. **Not gated on `countUpkeep`** — it explains the `In` row, which is
on show whatever the upkeep setting says, unlike the food and fund notes which explain `Upkeep`.

**Placed last of the informational notes**, after the food and unclaimed-fund lines. Those exist
because a **zero** in a row reads as a defect, which is a sharper surprise than a positive income
figure that the `In too late to spend` row already half-explains; and each of them is the rarer,
more specific fact. The cost is stated rather than hidden: an idle unit that faction food also fed
shows the food note and not this one.

### Nothing else moves

No new `codes::ALL` entry, no new `SilverDoubt`, no change to the ledger's `apply`, no Settings row.

## Increments

1. **The predicate moves, and nothing changes.**
   RED: none — this is a pure move. Run `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` before and after and
   confirm the same tests pass, including `teaching_spends_the_month`,
   `idling_spends_the_month`, `annihilating_spends_the_month` and the two `CAST` tests.
   GREEN: `spends_the_month` and `works_by_default` in `intents.rs`, callers updated.

2. **An idle unit earns the region's wage.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`, `fn a_unit_with_no_month_long_order_works_by_default` —
   a 6-man unit with no intents in a region paying `$12.0` asserts `late_income == Some(72)`,
   `income == Some(72)` and `works_by_default == true`.
   Then `fn a_unit_that_spends_its_month_does_not_also_work` — the same unit ordered `STUDY` asserts
   `late_income == Some(0)` and `works_by_default == false`.
   Then `fn guarding_is_not_spending_the_month` — a unit ordered only `GUARD` asserts it works,
   because `spends_the_month` already says `GUARD` is a flag and a guard can tax as well.
   GREEN: the `late_income` term and the field.

3. **The upkeep charge sees it too.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn an_idle_units_wages_pay_its_upkeep` — a 6-man unit holding nothing, no orders, owing $60 in a
   region paying `$12.0` a man: asserts **no** `not-enough-silver` finding, where today it is
   warned. **This is the bead's headline and the reason it is a P1.**
   Then `fn an_idle_unit_whose_wages_fall_short_is_still_warned` — the same unit in a region paying
   `$1.0`, asserting the warning still fires and names the real shortfall.
   GREEN: nothing further — `charge_upkeep` reads the same `late_income`. If it does not pass, the
   term was added somewhere other than `late_income` and must be moved.

4. **A guessed headcount is not multiplied out.**
   RED: `silver.rs`, `fn an_idle_unit_with_an_estimated_headcount_is_doubted` — a unit with
   `men_estimated` and no intents asserts `income == None` and `doubt ==
   Some(SilverDoubt::EstimatedMen)`.
   **Write this test before the gate change and watch it fail**, producing a number: that failure is
   the evidence the conditional short-circuit was the trap it looks like.
   GREEN: `|| works_by_default(intents)` in the gate.

5. **Regenerate the TypeScript.** `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
   --test generated_ts`, then `pnpm run check:generated`.

6. **The hover.**
   RED: `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts`,
   `fn the_note_says_an_idle_unit_will_work` — asserts the sentence verbatim, and asserts it appears
   with `countUpkeep` **off** as well as on.
   Then a test asserting an idle unit that faction food also fed shows the **food** note, pinning
   the ordering decided above.
   GREEN: the entry in `silverNote`.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core`** — every test named in *Increments*, plus:

- `fn an_idle_units_wages_cannot_fund_its_purchases` — an idle unit ordered `BUY` it can only afford
  out of the defaulted wages asserts `short_for_orders > 0`. Wages arrive in the turn's last phase
  (`ah-uwa3`), and routing the default through `late_income` is what preserves that; a term added to
  `income` directly would pass increment 2 and fail this.
- `fn a_region_with_no_wage_line_pays_an_idle_unit_nothing` — `wage_centis` is `None`, so `earned` is
  0. Guards against a defaulted wage inventing income in a region that pays none.
- `fn a_unit_ordered_only_to_cast_still_works` — `CAST` leaves the month free, which
  `spends_the_month` already encodes; this pins that the default follows it rather than a fresh list.
- `fn an_unread_order_line_does_not_stop_the_default` — see *User-facing decisions*; the navigator
  chose to credit wages regardless, so this is the test that records it deliberately.

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`** will move, and probably a great deal: idle units are
common, and several will stop being warned. **That is the bead working.** Read the diff and expect
the `EXPECTED` counts to fall.

**`ah-ycuj`'s corpus agreement test must stay green untouched.** Both surfaces read the one
`late_income`, so it cannot legitimately move; if it does, the term was added in the wrong place.

**TypeScript** — `unitTooltip.test.ts` and `unitTable.test.ts` (an idle unit's column figure). Both
pure modules; the traps file's no-jsdom rule is respected and no effect-level test is asked for.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `pnpm run check:generated`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23 against `docs/ui/ah-gjq4-idle.html`.

**Does `unit-does-nothing` change?** Because both use the same `spends_the_month`, the units this
bead starts paying wages to are **exactly** the units that check flags — so it now says *"has no
order that spends the month"* about a unit the column shows earning.
**Chosen: leave it exactly as it is.** It is literally true — there is no order — and still worth
saying, because working is usually the worst thing a unit could do with its month. The two surfaces
say different things about the same unit and both are correct.
*Rejected — rewording it to "has no order, so it will work for wages"*: says what will actually
happen rather than implying the month is wasted, and the column would then agree with the warning —
at the cost of changing a shipped string that users have already read.
**Do not touch `check_idle_units` or its message in this bead.**

**Does the hover say where the money came from?**
**Chosen: yes**, verbatim:

> `This unit has no month-long order, so it will work and earn wages.`

Income arriving from an order nobody wrote reads as a defect; this is the same shape as the food and
unclaimed-fund notes, which exist for exactly that reason.
*Rejected — crediting it silently*: the `In too late to spend` row already signals wages, and the
hover's one-note-wins table means a new entry competes with the food and fund notes for one slot.

**A unit with an order line the parser could not read.** `check_idle_units` declines to judge these
— *"silence is the price of never being wrong"* — because an unrecognised line may well be a month's
work, such as `ASSASSINATE`.
**Chosen: credit the wages anyway.** The planner recommended matching the shipped posture and
crediting nothing; the navigator chose the common case instead.
*Rejected — credit nothing*: consistent with the advisory, understating in a rare case, which is the
safe direction. *Rejected — doubt the income*: the `ah-1wcw.1` doctrine, but it turns an unreadable
line into an unpriceable month, a large consequence for a rare parse gap.
**The accepted cost, stated plainly: a unit whose only order is one we could not read is paid wages
it may not earn** — a unit that is actually assassinating someone shows phantom income. It also
means the column and `unit-does-nothing` deliberately disagree about unread units: the check stays
silent, the column credits. `fn an_unread_order_line_does_not_stop_the_default` records that this
was chosen and not overlooked.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** a unit with no men
needs no special case, because `men * wage` is already zero; a unit on guard **does** work, because
`spends_the_month` already places `GUARD` as a flag rather than a month's work; the note is not
gated on `countUpkeep`, because it explains `In` rather than `Upkeep`; and the note sorts **after**
the food and fund notes, so an idle unit that faction food also fed shows the food note instead.

## Out of scope

- **Changing `unit-does-nothing`**, its message, or `check_idle_units`. Decided above.
- **Redefining what spends a month.** `spends_the_month` moves and is otherwise untouched — its
  contents are `ah-dwk6`'s, `ah-udff`'s and `ah-90w`'s work, and a change there is a change to three
  shipped behaviours.
- **`ah-fvzu`** — the taxing flag (`AUTOTAX`) earning nothing. The same *shape* of defect, a
  persistent flag the forecast does not price, but a different flag, a different pool and its own
  bead. Nothing here anticipates it.
- **Entertainment.** There is no defaulted `ENTERTAIN`; work is the only default.
- **Whether the player should be told in the orders document** rather than the hover. The advisory
  that would carry it already exists and is deliberately unchanged.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (inside `check:fast`).

Checkable by looking, once, before opening the PR: load a fixture, find a unit with no orders in a
region that prints a wage, and confirm its **In** row now shows the wage, its **In too late to
spend** row shows the same figure, the hover carries the new sentence, and any
`not-enough-silver` mark it used to have is gone.

## Known traps

- **The estimated-headcount short-circuit is conditional, and an idle unit slips through it.**
  `silver.rs:537` fires only when some intent `moves_silver_per_man`; a unit with **no** intents has
  none, so without the `|| works_by_default(intents)` clause a defaulted wage is multiplied out of a
  guessed headcount — the exact defect that gate exists to prevent. Increment 4 is written to fail
  first for this reason.
- **Price it in `late_income`, nowhere else.** Wages arrive in the turn's last phase, so they pay
  upkeep and cannot fund this month's orders (`ah-uwa3`), and `charge_upkeep` shares that function
  on purpose. A term added straight to `income` passes the obvious test, breaks `short_for_orders`,
  and makes the two surfaces disagree.
- **`ah-t2pn.2` is landing in parallel and touches the same arm.** It settles the wage pool between
  own units in a hex, reading `shares.wages`. **A defaulted worker must contend for that pool too** —
  its `pool_wants` gathers units with an explicit `Intent::Work`, which a defaulted worker does not
  have. Whichever of the two lands second must make `pool_wants` count defaulted workers, or a hex
  full of idle units will each be promised the whole wage pool. Read `ah-t2pn.2`'s plan before
  starting (`bd show ah-t2pn.2 --json`; the command returns an array), and say in the PR which order
  they landed in.
- **Moving `spends_the_month` must not lose its tests.** `semantics.rs:5066-5101` records where each
  order falls, including the two `CAST` cases the rules turn on. Move them or leave them, but do not
  drop them.
- **`UnitSilver` has two constructors.** The estimated-headcount early return is easy to miss and
  fails to compile only if the field has no default — set it in both.
- **Expect `validate_real_orders.rs` to move a lot**, downward. Idle units are common and many stop
  being warned; read the diff rather than narrowing anything.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (`ah-nass`, and the traps file). `unitTooltip.ts` is a pure
  module; do not add an effect-level test.

title: PILLAGE earns nothing without the combat ready men to take it
description: Found by Psylocke verifying ah-abwx at 54dd0824. Both surfaces credit PILLAGE with twice the region's tax base and neither checks whether the faction may pillage at all: 'To do this requires the faction to have enough combat ready men in the region to tax half of the available money in the region.' A taxer collects 50, so the threshold is ceil(tax_base/100) men. Observed: neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep, The Lost One (683), one leader, credited the full 17,926 in a hex whose tax base is 8,963 and which needs 90 men. Uses the weapon data from ah-1ad6.1 to count, and adds one advisory code.
design:
## Context

Found by **Psylocke** verifying `ah-abwx` on 2026-08-23, at `54dd0824`.

`ah-abwx` correctly taught the Silver column to credit `PILLAGE` with twice the region's tax base,
mirroring the ledger. **Neither surface checks whether the faction may pillage at all:**

> "To do this requires the faction to have enough combat ready men in the region to tax half of the
> available money in the region."
> "Only combat-ready units may issue this order."

A taxer collects $50, so half of a tax base needs `ceil(tax_base / 100)` men.

**Observed:** `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep`, unit *The Lost One (683)* -
a single leader, flagged `avoiding, behind` - standing in mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra, tax base
**$8,963**. Ordered `PILLAGE`, the forecast credits the full **$17,926**. The hex needs **90** men;
the faction has one. In the real game that order earns nothing.

So the column promises silver the turn will not deliver - the same class of defect `ah-abwx` just
fixed, only overstating instead of understating.

Two facts shaped the interview and belong here:

- **The rules page never defines "combat ready".** It uses the phrase three times and explains it
  nowhere. `ah-1ad6.1` is the answer: it scrapes each weapon's wield clause, so a man with a weapon
  he can use is countable.
- **There are zero `PILLAGE` orders in any committed turn** in the whole corpus. Psylocke found
  this by writing one during verification. The defect is real and has never yet been hit in
  committed play - which the navigator weighed and chose the thorough route anyway.

**`ah-1ad6.1` blocks this and must land first.** Every count below reads
`ItemEntry.weapon` (`{ needs: string | null }`), which does not exist until it does.

When this lands: a faction without the men is shown earning nothing from `PILLAGE`, and told why on
the order line.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` - the count, shared by both surfaces

Two new public functions. Both surfaces call them, which is what stops the pair drifting - the
failure `ah-ycuj`'s corpus test exists to catch, and the very failure `ah-abwx` was filed for.

```rust
/// How many of one unit's men are combat ready, in the sense `PILLAGE` needs.
///
/// The rules page never defines the phrase (it uses it three times and explains it nowhere), so
/// this is the navigator's reading, settled 2026-08-23: **a man is combat ready when he has a
/// weapon he can wield**, and a unit set to avoid combat has none who are.
///
/// - `avoiding` in `flags` - zero, whatever the unit holds.
/// - otherwise `min(men, weapons the unit can wield)`, where a weapon needing a skill counts only
///   for a unit that has that skill at level 1 or better.
///
/// `behind` is not consulted: a unit in the back rank still fights.
///
/// `None` when `men_estimated` - a guessed headcount cannot be compared against a threshold.
#[must_use]
pub fn combat_ready(facts: &UnitFacts<'_>, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) -> Option<i64>;

/// Combat ready men a faction needs in a region before it may pillage it.
///
/// "enough combat ready men in the region to tax half of the available money" - a taxer collects
/// [`TAX_PER_MAN`], so this is `ceil(tax_base / 2 / 50)`, computed as `ceil(tax_base / 100)` in
/// integers with no float anywhere.
#[must_use]
pub fn pillage_threshold(tax_base: i64) -> i64 {
    (tax_base.max(0) + 99) / 100
}
```

`combat_ready`'s weapon test, exactly:

```
if facts.men_estimated: return None
if facts.flags contains "avoiding" (case-insensitively): return Some(0)
let Some(ruleset) = ruleset else { return None };   // nothing can be told without the catalogue
armed = 0
for each item the unit holds:
    let Some(weapon) = ruleset.items[tag].weapon else { continue };   // not a weapon
    match weapon.needs {
        None            => armed += amount,                   // wieldable by anyone
        Some(skill_tag) => if skill_level(facts.skills, skill_tag) >= 1 { armed += amount },
    }
return Some(min(facts.men, armed))
```

Reuse `skill_level` (`silver.rs:~1020`), which already answers "what level does this unit have in
this skill, or 0". `is_consuming` (`silver.rs:~910`) is the pattern for a case-insensitive flag
test; write `is_avoiding` beside it rather than inlining the comparison.

**A `None` from `combat_ready` for *any* own unit in the hex makes the whole hex's total `None`.**
One guessed headcount is enough to make the comparison unanswerable, and it is unanswerable in the
direction that matters: the estimate might be what carries the faction over the threshold.

One new field on `RegionWages` (`silver.rs:396`), beside `pillaged`:

```rust
/// Combat ready men this faction has in the hex, summed over its own units - or `None` when a
/// headcount in the hex is a guess, or there is no ruleset to read weapons from.
///
/// Like `pillaged` above, this is not a property of the region as the report prints it. It
/// belongs here for the same reason that field does: it is exactly what the `PILLAGE` arm needs,
/// and nothing else in this module has a view of the hex (`ah-1ad6.2`).
pub combat_ready: Option<i64>,
```

The `Intent::Pillage` arm (`silver.rs:648`) becomes:

```rust
Intent::Pillage => match (region.tax_base, region.combat_ready) {
    // No tax base: unchanged, and the older doubt wins - what the region holds is unknown
    // before the question of who may take it arises.
    (None, _) => income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase)),
    // A guessed headcount somewhere in the hex: the threshold cannot be tested at all.
    (Some(_), None) => income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::EstimatedMen)),
    (Some(base), Some(ready)) if ready >= pillage_threshold(base) =>
        income = income.saturating_add(base.saturating_mul(2)),
    // Short of the threshold: the order earns nothing, exactly.
    (Some(_), Some(_)) => {}
},
```

**`EstimatedMen` is reused rather than a new variant added.** It already means "a headcount that is
itself a guess, so nothing per-man can be multiplied out" and its interface sentence -
"This unit's headcount is an estimate, so its month cannot be priced." - is close enough to stay
true. Do not add a variant for this.

**`moves_silver_per_man` (`silver.rs:~1030`) is left alone.** `PILLAGE` is still not priced per
man - its *income* is twice the tax base whatever the headcount - and adding it there would doubt
every pillager whose own headcount is estimated even where the hex plainly qualifies. The hex-wide
estimate is handled above instead, which is the narrower and correct place.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` - the ledger, the total, and the mark

**Building the total.** `forecast_hex` (line ~333) and `charge_upkeep` (line ~975) each build a
`RegionWages`; both gain the new field. Because the sum is needed by both and by the check, put it
in one function beside `hex_facts`:

```rust
/// Combat ready men this faction has in one hex. `None` when any own unit's headcount is a guess,
/// or there is no ruleset - see `silver::combat_ready`.
fn combat_ready_in(hex: &Hex<'_>, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) -> Option<i64>;
```

It walks `hex.units`, builds each `UnitFacts` the way `hex_facts` already does, and sums
`combat_ready`, short-circuiting to `None` on the first `None`.

**The ledger.** `apply`'s `Intent::Pillage` arm (line 1353) gets the same three-way test.
**Compute the sum once per hex and store it on the `Ledger`**, not inside `apply`: `apply` runs per
intent, and a hex of forty units would rebuild the sum forty times on a path that runs per
keystroke. A local in `ledger_for` will not do - `apply` takes `&mut Ledger`, `hex`, `ordered` and
`placed`, so a local cannot reach it. Add:

```rust
/// Combat ready men this faction has in this hex, summed once because `apply` runs per intent and
/// this path runs per keystroke. `None` when a headcount here is a guess (`ah-1ad6.2`).
combat_ready: Option<i64>,
```

to `Ledger` (`semantics.rs:~867`), filled in `ledger_for` (line ~799) before the intent loop.

**The mark.** One new code in `mod codes` (line 81), appended to `ALL`, whose length in the type
goes up by exactly one. **Read the current value rather than assuming it**: `ah-wbr9` adds two
codes to the same array and may land before or after this bead, so the number in `[Code; N]` is not
knowable from here - only that it grows by one.

```rust
pub const PILLAGE_WITHOUT_MEN: Code = Code("pillage-without-men");
```

**A new code is three edits, not one** - `ah-wbr9`'s plan met the same trap: `mod codes`, the `ALL`
array whose length is in its type, and a `Case` fixture in the table ending at `semantics.rs:~9604`,
whose assertion is `cases.len() == codes::ALL.len()` with the message *"every code in codes::ALL
needs a fixture here, or a silenced one would go unnoticed"*. The third lives 9,000 lines from the
first. `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs:21` also asserts the generated TypeScript lists codes in
`ALL`'s order, which is why it is appended and not inserted.

A new check, dispatched beside the others at `semantics.rs:~330`:

```rust
/// A `PILLAGE` by a faction without the combat ready men the region needs.
fn check_pillage_men(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
);
```

It gates on the option, needs `Some(tax_base)` and `Some(ready)` (silence for either `None` - the
column already shows `?` and a mark would be a second, louder claim about something unknown), and
emits **one finding per pillaging unit** on that unit's `PILLAGE` line. Per unit and not per hex,
because the finding hangs on an order and each pillaging unit wrote its own.

The message, verbatim:

```
cannot pillage here: needs 90 combat ready men, this faction has 1
```

Shaped as `needs X, has Y`, the same shape `build-without-skill` and `ah-wbr9`'s
`produce-without-skill` use, so the three read as one family.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx` - one toggle

Into the existing **Orders** group (heading at line ~522), in its neighbours' shape:

```tsx
{
  code: "pillage-without-men",
  title: "Pillaging without the men",
  description:
    "A PILLAGE order where the faction has too few combat ready men in the region to take the money."
}
```

`SettingsDialog.test.tsx:100` holds a hardcoded list of every toggle title and **no cross-check
against `codes::ALL`**, so nothing fails if the entry is forgotten and the advisory would ship
un-toggleable. Add the title to that list deliberately.

## Increments

1. **`pillage_threshold`.** Opening test in `silver.rs`:
   `a_region_needs_a_hundredth_of_its_tax_base_in_men` - 8963 → 90; 100 → 1; 101 → 2; 0 → 0.
   Pure arithmetic, no report.

2. **`combat_ready`, unarmed and armed.** `a_unit_with_no_weapons_is_not_combat_ready` - 50 orcs,
   no items → `Some(0)`. `a_unit_counts_one_man_per_weapon` - 50 orcs, 10 swords → `Some(10)`.
   `weapons_beyond_the_headcount_do_not_add_men` - 5 orcs, 10 swords → `Some(5)`.

3. **Weapons that need a skill.** `a_crossbow_counts_only_for_a_unit_that_can_use_it` - 10 men, 10
   crossbows, no crossbow skill → `Some(0)`; the same unit with crossbow 1 → `Some(10)`.
   `a_double_bow_needs_longbow_not_its_own_tag` - 10 `DBOW`, longbow 1 → `Some(10)`; with crossbow
   1 instead → `Some(0)`. **That last one is the test that catches reading `needs` as the item's
   own tag**, which is the mistake `ah-1ad6.1`'s data invites.

4. **`avoiding` and estimates.** `an_avoiding_unit_has_no_combat_ready_men` - 50 orcs, 50 swords,
   flag `avoiding` → `Some(0)`. `a_behind_unit_still_counts` - the same with `behind` → `Some(50)`.
   `a_guessed_headcount_cannot_be_counted` - `men_estimated` → `None`.

5. **The forecast.** `semantics.rs`: `a_faction_without_the_men_earns_nothing_from_pillage` - the
   observed case rebuilt: one leader, tax base 8963 → `income == Some(0)`, no doubt.
   `a_faction_with_the_men_is_credited_in_full` - 90 armed men → `income == Some(17926)`.
   `a_guessed_headcount_in_the_hex_doubts_the_pillage` - → `doubt == Some(EstimatedMen)`.
   `the_men_are_counted_across_the_hex_not_the_unit` - a lone leader ordering `PILLAGE` beside a
   faction-mate of 90 armed men that orders nothing: credited in full. **This is the navigator's
   round-1 answer and it must be pinned.**

6. **The ledger and the corpus test.** `the_ledger_and_the_column_agree_about_pillage` - the same
   hexes, asserting the `not-enough-silver` picture matches. Then run
   `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` (`ah-ycuj`): it must stay green, and it is
   the guard over exactly this pair of surfaces.

7. **The mark.** `a_faction_without_the_men_is_told_so` - one `pillage-without-men` finding with
   the exact message, on the `PILLAGE` line.
   `a_faction_with_the_men_is_not_marked`.
   `an_unknown_tax_base_is_not_marked` - silence, not a mark.
   Plus the `Case` fixture in the `ALL` coverage table.

8. **The toggle**, and `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`'s title list.

9. **The corpus.** `validate_real_orders.rs`'s `EXPECTED` table (line ~62) is over turn 71, which
   contains **no `PILLAGE` order at all** - nor does any other committed template - so this table
   should not move. If it does, something is wrong with the check rather than with the table.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `a_region_needs_a_hundredth_of_its_tax_base_in_men` | `silver.rs` | the threshold, in integers |
| `a_unit_with_no_weapons_is_not_combat_ready` | `silver.rs` | unarmed men do not count |
| `a_unit_counts_one_man_per_weapon` | `silver.rs` | the navigator's counting rule |
| `weapons_beyond_the_headcount_do_not_add_men` | `silver.rs` | the `min` |
| `a_crossbow_counts_only_for_a_unit_that_can_use_it` | `silver.rs` | the skill gate |
| `a_double_bow_needs_longbow_not_its_own_tag` | `silver.rs` | `needs` is a skill tag |
| `an_avoiding_unit_has_no_combat_ready_men` | `silver.rs` | the `avoiding` reading |
| `a_behind_unit_still_counts` | `silver.rs` | `behind` is not consulted |
| `a_guessed_headcount_cannot_be_counted` | `silver.rs` | `None`, not 0 |
| `a_faction_without_the_men_earns_nothing_from_pillage` | `semantics.rs` | the reported defect |
| `a_faction_with_the_men_is_credited_in_full` | `semantics.rs` | no regression on `ah-abwx` |
| `the_men_are_counted_across_the_hex_not_the_unit` | `semantics.rs` | the faction-wide reading |
| `a_guessed_headcount_in_the_hex_doubts_the_pillage` | `semantics.rs` | `EstimatedMen` |
| `the_ledger_and_the_column_agree_about_pillage` | `semantics.rs` | the two surfaces |
| the three `pillage-without-men` tests | `semantics.rs` | the mark and its message |
| `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` | `tests/` | corpus-wide agreement |

Suites: `cargo test -p atlantis-core`, `pnpm run check:generated`, `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23, in two rounds. Mockups:
`docs/ui/ah-1ad6-pillage.html`, `docs/ui/ah-1ad6-counting.html`.

**Round 1 - what to do above the headcount threshold.** Below it the faction certainly cannot
pillage - combat ready men are a subset of men - so every option fixed the reported case; the
question was the rest.
Chosen: **scrape weapons first and count properly**, which produced `ah-1ad6.1`.
Rejected: *crediting a sufficient headcount in full*, the smallest change, which fixes the reported
defect exactly and overstates whenever the men are unarmed. Rejected: *showing `?` above the
threshold*, the most honest, which would put a question mark on every workable `PILLAGE` for ever.
The navigator took the thorough route knowing there are **zero** `PILLAGE` orders in the committed
corpus.

**Round 1 - what the player sees when it earns nothing.**
Chosen: **the figure and a mark** - income 0 *and* a `pillage-without-men` advisory on the order
line, because it is a wasted month like the `PRODUCE` checks.
Rejected: *the figure and a hover sentence alone*, which needs no new advisory machinery.

**Round 1 - whose men count.**
Chosen: **every own unit in the hex.** The rule says "the faction to have enough combat ready men
in the region", so a lone leader ordering `PILLAGE` beside an army of 90 qualifies and the army
need issue no order.
Rejected: *the pillaging unit alone*, simpler and wrong by the rules.

**Round 2 - how many of a unit's men are combat ready.** A unit of 50 orcs holding 10 swords.
Chosen: **10 - one weapon per man**, capped by weapons held, with a skill-needing weapon counting
only for a unit that has the skill.
Rejected: *the whole unit counts if it holds any usable weapon* (50), reading "combat ready" as a
property of the unit as the rules do elsewhere - "only combat-ready **units** may issue this order".
Rejected: *every man, armed or not*, which is the one-sided headcount test and misses the faction of
200 unarmed peasants - the case the weapon scrape was chosen to catch.

**Round 2 - does an `avoiding` unit count?**
Chosen: **no.** A unit set to run from every fight is not ready for combat in any ordinary sense.
The rules do not say so, so this is an inference - and it errs toward not promising silver, which
is this module's stated safe direction.
Rejected: *counting them*, on the reading that `avoiding` decides whether a unit is drawn into a
battle rather than whether it could fight. **`behind` is not consulted either way**: a behind unit
fights, from the back rank.

**Round 2 - the message.**
Chosen, verbatim:
> `cannot pillage here: needs 90 combat ready men, this faction has 1`

Rejected: *naming the money* ("90 combat ready men are needed to tax half of $8,963"), which
explains where the 90 comes from at the cost of length, with the tax base already on screen.
Rejected: *leading with the shortfall* ("89 short of the 90 needed"), which diverges from the
`needs X, has Y` shape the other two skill checks use.

**Decided here, not asked**, because it follows from the above: the toggle lives in the existing
**Orders** group and reads "Pillaging without the men". This was stated in the round-2 mockup and
drew no objection; it is recorded as a decision rather than an answer so that a later reader knows
which it was. A group of its own would hold one entry, and the `Building`/`Producing` groups exist
because each holds several.

## Out of scope

- **Sharing the pillaged money between several pillaging units.** "The total amount of money that
  can be pillaged will then be shared out between every combat ready unit that issues the PILLAGE
  order" - that is the same shape of question as `ah-t2pn`'s tax pool and belongs with it.
- **`TAX` and combat readiness.** The rules attach the phrase to `PILLAGE`'s threshold and to who
  may issue it; whether a taxer must also be armed is a separate question this bead does not open.
- **Guarding units blocking a `PILLAGE`** - `ah-g7ts`, a separate ranked bead.
- **`PILLAGE` by a unit that is itself not combat ready**, where the faction as a whole qualifies.
  "Only combat-ready units may issue this order" is a second, per-unit rule; the navigator was asked
  about the faction threshold and this bead implements that. File it if it matters.
- **Anything about armor, mounts, or a weapon's attack bonus.** `ah-1ad6.1` scrapes only the wield
  clause.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, no `#[ignore]`. `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` in particular.

Then, by eye, loading `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep` and writing `PILLAGE` for unit **683**:

- its income shows **0**, not 17,926.
- the order line carries `cannot pillage here: needs 90 combat ready men, this faction has 1`.
- the settings tab's **Orders** group has a "Pillaging without the men" toggle, and turning it off
  removes the mark while leaving the income at 0.

**A human must confirm the first two**, because this is exactly the check Psylocke ran when she
found the defect, and the fix is only proved by re-running it.

## Known traps

- **`ah-1ad6.1` must land first.** `ItemEntry.weapon` does not exist until it does. If every item
  answers "not a weapon", regenerate the ruleset before diagnosing anything else.
- **Both surfaces must call the same functions.** Pricing `PILLAGE` twice is precisely how the
  column and the warning drifted apart before (`ah-abwx`), and `ah-ycuj`'s corpus test exists to
  catch it. `combat_ready` and `pillage_threshold` have one implementation and two callers.
- **`combat_ready_in` must be computed once per hex**, not once per pillaging unit inside `apply` -
  that path runs per keystroke and a city holds a great many units.
- **`needs` is a *skill* tag, not the item's own.** `DBOW` needs `LBOW`; `XBOW` the item needs
  `XBOW` the skill, which is a coincidence that makes the wrong implementation look right. The
  `DBOW` test is what separates them.
- **One `None` poisons the hex total.** A single unit with `men_estimated` makes the comparison
  unanswerable, because the estimate might be what carries the faction over. Do not treat an
  estimated unit as contributing zero and carry on.
- **A new code is three edits**: `mod codes`, the `ALL` array (its length is in its type), and a
  `Case` fixture in the table ending at `semantics.rs:~9604` whose assertion is
  `cases.len() == codes::ALL.len()`. The third is 9,000 lines away.
- **Nothing makes the settings tab fail when a toggle is missing.** `SettingsDialog.test.tsx:100`'s
  title list is hardcoded and never compared against `codes::ALL`, so a forgotten entry ships as an
  advisory the player cannot turn off.
- **Reuse `SilverDoubt::EstimatedMen`; do not add a variant.** Its sentence stays true, and every
  new variant is a new string in the interface.
- **The corpus contains no `PILLAGE` order.** So `validate_real_orders.rs`'s table should not move.
  If it does, suspect the check, not the table.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`: no effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`
  is a `renderToStaticMarkup` test; extend it in that style.

title: Scrape which items are weapons, and what skill each needs, into the ruleset
description: ah-1ad6 needs to count a faction's combat ready men, and nothing in the ruleset says which items are weapons: ItemEntry has no weapon field, and the scraped 'combat' block is on monsters only. The data page does say it, in each weapon's description - 'This is a slashing weapon and each attack deals 1 damage. No skill is needed to wield this weapon.' Sixteen items carry a wield clause, every one kind=equipment, in exactly three forms: no skill needed (12), crossbow [XBOW] needed (XBOW, MXBO), longbow [LBOW] needed (LBOW, DBOW). Four further items mention 'weapon' in passing and are races (kind=man), excluded on kind. No counting and no checks - that is ah-1ad6.2.
design:
## Context

`ah-1ad6.2` must count a faction's **combat ready men** in a region, and nothing in the ruleset
says which items are weapons. `ItemEntry` (`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:40`,
`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:178`) has no weapon field, and the scraped `combat` block
(`rules.rs:187`) is `MonsterCombat` - present only for monsters, and `null` on every weapon.

**The data page does say it**, in each weapon's own description:

> `This is a slashing weapon and each attack deals 1 damage. No skill is needed to wield this
> weapon. This weapon grants a bonus of 2 on attack and defence.`

Measured over the committed fixture page, and the numbers are small enough to state completely:

- **16 items carry a wield clause**, and every one is `kind: "equipment"`:
  `SWOR MSWO RUNE PICK SPEA AXE HAMM BAXE ASWR JAVE PIKE FSWO` need no skill (12);
  `XBOW` and `MXBO` need crossbow `[XBOW]`; `LBOW` and `DBOW` need longbow `[LBOW]`.
- **Exactly three wield sentences exist**, whole:
  - `No skill is needed to wield this weapon.`
  - `Knowledge of crossbow [XBOW] is needed to wield this weapon.`
  - `Knowledge of longbow [LBOW] is needed to wield this weapon.`
- **Four further items mention "weapon" and are not weapons**: `IDWA`, `HDWA`, `UDWA`, `GBLN` -
  races whose description lists weaponsmith among the skills they may study. All are
  `kind: "man"`, which is what excludes them.

**This bead is the data half only.** No counting, no checks, nothing user-visible - that is
`ah-1ad6.2`, which this blocks. It is deliberately the same shape as `ah-19l2.1`, which does the
same job for production recipes; read that bead's plan and its implementation for the pattern
before starting.

When this lands: the ruleset can answer "is this a weapon, and what does wielding it need?", and
`ah-1ad6.2` can count.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` - the parse

Reuse the shape of `withdrawOf` (line 342), which is the closest existing parser: a small function
taking the item's paragraph and returning either `{}` or a one-key object, spread into the entry by
the caller. Weapons work the same way.

```ts
/** What wielding a weapon needs: a skill tag, or nothing at all. */
export type WeaponSkill = { tag: string } | null;

/**
 * A weapon, as the data page describes one.
 *
 * Absent from every item that is not a weapon - including the four races whose description lists
 * weaponsmith among the skills they may study, which is why `kind` is checked and not just the
 * word "weapon" (`ah-1ad6.1`).
 */
export type Weapon = {
  /**
   * The skill needed to wield it, or `null` for the twelve that need none. `null` and not an
   * absent field: "no skill is needed" is a thing the page states, and an absence would be
   * indistinguishable from a weapon whose clause this parser failed to read.
   */
  needs: WeaponSkill;
};
```

and on `ItemEntry`, after `withdrawCost` (line 89) and before `description`:

```ts
/** Present only for weapons - an item whose description states how it is wielded. */
weapon?: Weapon;
```

The parser, beside `withdrawOf`:

```ts
/** `No skill is needed to wield this weapon.` / `Knowledge of crossbow [XBOW] is needed to …` */
const WIELD_NONE = /No skill is needed to wield this weapon\./i;
const WIELD_SKILL = /Knowledge of [a-z ]+ \[([A-Z]{2,6})\] is needed to wield this weapon\./i;

function weaponOf(kind: ItemKind, paragraph: string): { weapon?: Weapon };
```

`ItemKind` is `"man" | "mount" | "monster" | "ship" | "equipment"` (`data.ts:16`); the exclusion
below tests `kind === "man"` against that union, so a typo will not compile.

- `kind === "man"` returns `{}` before any matching - the race exclusion, stated once and in the
  one place it can be forgotten.
- `WIELD_NONE` matches → `{ weapon: { needs: null } }`.
- `WIELD_SKILL` matches → `{ weapon: { needs: { tag } } }`.
- Neither matches → `{}`.
- **Both matching is impossible on today's page and must throw** `RulesetScrapeError`, the posture
  `readProduction` takes at `data.ts:549` and every other parser here takes: a page that has changed
  shape stops the scrape rather than being half-read.

**Match on the wield clause, never on the word "weapon".** That word appears in armor descriptions
("versus slashing attacks"), in race descriptions, and in the weaponsmith skill's own text. The
wield sentence is what only a weapon has.

**`XBOW` is both an item tag and a skill tag**, and so is `LBOW`. `data.ts`'s own comment at the top
of the skill types warns about exactly this pair ("FISH is fishing and also fish, HERB is herb lore
and also herbs"). The tag captured here is a **skill** tag, to be looked up in `skills`, and the
crossbow *item* `XBOW` needing the crossbow *skill* `XBOW` is a genuine coincidence and not a bug.
Say so in a comment, because it looks like one.

### `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` - the mirror

`ItemEntry` carries `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]` (line 176), **so
adding the field to the JSON breaks Rust deserialisation of every ruleset until this struct matches**.
One change, one commit - exactly as `ah-19l2.1` had to do for `Production`.

```rust
/// What wielding a weapon needs. `None` for the twelve weapons that need no skill.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Weapon {
    /// The skill tag needed to wield it, or `None` where the page says none is needed.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub needs: Option<String>,
}
```

and on `ItemEntry`, beside its siblings:

```rust
/// Present only for weapons - an item whose page description states how it is wielded. `None`
/// for everything else, and for a ruleset cached before `ah-1ad6.1`.
#[serde(default)]
pub weapon: Option<Weapon>,
```

**`Weapon.needs` is `Option<String>` and the TypeScript is `{ tag } | null`.** Those are the same
JSON - `null` or `{"tag":"XBOW"}` - only if the TypeScript is flattened to a bare tag. **Flatten
it**: make the TypeScript `needs: string | null` carrying the tag directly, and drop the
`WeaponSkill` wrapper type above. A one-field object buys nothing and costs an exact
correspondence between the two declarations, which `deny_unknown_fields` will otherwise turn into a
load failure. Amend the TypeScript accordingly:

```ts
export type Weapon = {
  /** The skill tag needed to wield it, or `null` for the twelve that need none. */
  needs: string | null;
};
```

### `config/public/ruleset.json` - regenerated, never edited

```
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- \
  --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html \
  --data tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html
```

`committed.test.ts:24` holds the file exactly equal to the scraper's output from the committed
pages; a hand edit fails there, which is the guard working.

## Increments

1. **The parser.** Add `Weapon`, the field, and `weaponOf`, and spread it into the entry literal at
   **`data.ts:397`**, beside `...withdrawOf(paragraph)`, `...cargoOf(kind, paragraph)` and
   `...sailingOf(kind, paragraph)`. Those last two already take `kind` as their first argument, so
   `weaponOf(kind, paragraph)` is the established signature here rather than a new one.
   Opening test in `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`, beside the `withdrawCost` tests at line 75:
   `reads a weapon that needs no skill` - `items.SWOR.weapon` is `{ needs: null }`.
   Then `reads a weapon that needs a skill` - `items.XBOW.weapon` is `{ needs: "XBOW" }` and
   `items.DBOW.weapon` is `{ needs: "LBOW" }`.
   Then `leaves everything that is not a weapon alone` - `items.PARM`, `items.HORS` and
   `items.GRAI` have no `weapon` property, using `not.toHaveProperty` as line 82 already does.
   Then `does not mistake a race for a weapon` - `items.IDWA`, `HDWA`, `UDWA` and `GBLN` have no
   `weapon` property. **This is the test that pins the `kind` check** and the one most likely to be
   lost in a refactor.
   Then `refuses a wield clause it cannot read` - a doctored paragraph matching both forms throws
   `RulesetScrapeError`.
   Run: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test`.

2. **The Rust mirror.** Add `Weapon` and the field. Opening test in `rules.rs`'s test module:
   `a_ruleset_without_weapons_still_loads` - deserialise an `ItemEntry` JSON object with no
   `weapon` key and assert it is `None`. That is what `#[serde(default)]` is for, and it is the
   assertion that proves `deny_unknown_fields` was handled the right way round.
   Then `a_weapon_needing_no_skill_round_trips` - `{"needs":null}` deserialises to
   `Weapon { needs: None }`.

3. **Regenerate, and pin the catalogue.** Run the scrape, then add to `committed.test.ts`'s
   existing `describe` block, in the style of its five neighbours:
   `carries every weapon the data page describes` - from the **committed** file, assert the set of
   tags with a `weapon` key is exactly the sixteen named in *Context*, and that exactly four of
   them (`XBOW`, `MXBO`, `LBOW`, `DBOW`) name a skill. A set equality, not a count: a count accepts
   one weapon dropped and another gained.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `reads a weapon that needs no skill` | `data.test.ts` | the twelve-of-sixteen case |
| `reads a weapon that needs a skill` | `data.test.ts` | the tag is captured, and `DBOW` needs `LBOW` rather than its own tag |
| `leaves everything that is not a weapon alone` | `data.test.ts` | armor, mounts and food gain no field |
| `does not mistake a race for a weapon` | `data.test.ts` | the `kind: "man"` exclusion |
| `refuses a wield clause it cannot read` | `data.test.ts` | the scrape stops rather than guessing |
| `a_ruleset_without_weapons_still_loads` | `rules.rs` | `deny_unknown_fields` + `#[serde(default)]` |
| `a_weapon_needing_no_skill_round_trips` | `rules.rs` | the two declarations describe the same JSON |
| `carries every weapon the data page describes` | `committed.test.ts` | the whole catalogue, as a set, from the committed file |

Suites: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test`, `cargo test -p atlantis-core`,
`pnpm run check:fast` (which carries `check:generated`).

## User-facing decisions

**None.** This bead adds one field to a scraped data file and to the Rust struct that mirrors it.
Nothing is shown, no message changes, no setting appears.

The decision that produced it was `ah-1ad6`'s, on 2026-08-23: the navigator chose to **scrape
weapons first** rather than credit a sufficient headcount in full or show `?` above the threshold,
having been shown that there are zero `PILLAGE` orders in any committed turn and that the rules page
never defines "combat ready". That reasoning belongs to `ah-1ad6.2` and is recorded in full there;
it is named here only so this bead's existence is not a mystery.

## Out of scope

- **Counting anything.** No combat-ready arithmetic, no threshold, no advisory. `ah-1ad6.2`.
- **Armor, mounts and shields.** They have their own description grammars and nothing needs them.
  Only the wield clause is read.
- **A weapon's attack and defence bonuses**, its damage, and whether it is ranged or
  armor-piercing. All stated in the same descriptions and none of it needed to answer "may this
  faction pillage". Adding it now would be scraping on speculation.
- **`MonsterCombat`** (`rules.rs:187`), which is a different thing about different items and is not
  touched.
- **Re-fetching the pages.** The committed fixtures are the input; `source.fetchedAt` does not move.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- \
  --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html \
  --data tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green. Then, by eye against the regenerated `config/public/ruleset.json`:

- `items.SWOR.weapon` is `{"needs": null}`; `items.XBOW.weapon` is `{"needs": "XBOW"}`;
  `items.DBOW.weapon` is `{"needs": "LBOW"}`.
- `items.PARM`, `items.HORS`, `items.IDWA` and `items.GBLN` carry no `weapon` key at all.
- exactly sixteen items carry one.

**A human need confirm nothing on screen.** Nothing in this bead is visible to a player; the check
is the diff and the regenerated file.

## Known traps

- **`deny_unknown_fields` on `ItemEntry` (`rules.rs:176`) makes this one change, not two.**
  Regenerating the JSON with a new key and leaving the Rust struct alone fails deserialisation of
  *every* ruleset, and the failure surfaces far from the edit. `ah-19l2.1` met the same trap on
  `Production`; increment 2 exists to force it.
- **The two declarations must describe the same JSON.** `needs: string | null` in TypeScript and
  `needs: Option<String>` in Rust agree; a `{ tag: string } | null` wrapper does not. This is why
  the wrapper is flattened - see *Files to change*.
- **Four races mention "weapon".** `IDWA`, `HDWA`, `UDWA`, `GBLN` list weaponsmith among the skills
  they may study. Matching on the word rather than the wield clause makes four races into weapons,
  and `ah-1ad6.2` would then count a unit as armed because of what its men *are*. The `kind: "man"`
  check and its test are what stop that.
- **`XBOW` and `LBOW` are each an item tag and a skill tag.** The captured tag is the **skill**;
  the crossbow item needing the crossbow skill is a coincidence, not a self-reference. `DBOW` is
  the case that shows the difference - a double bow needs `LBOW`, not `DBOW` - so keep that test.
- **The scraper throws rather than guesses.** A page shape this parser cannot read must stop the
  scrape (`RulesetScrapeError`, as at `data.ts:549`); a scraper that silently reads a new wield
  form as "not a weapon" would make a faction look unable to pillage when it can.
- **`config/public/ruleset.json` is generated.** Hand-editing it to add the field fails
  `committed.test.ts:24`. Run the scrape.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`** has nothing that bites here: no rendering, no persisted default,
  no smoke suite. `packages/ruleset`'s tests read files and assert on JSON.

title: The README sends a would-be player to rustup instead of to the download
description:
The navigator's words, 2026-08-23:

  "The README.md only describes how to compile from source. It should also describe how to install
  the pre-built releases. This section should come before the developer section that describes how
  to install and build from source."

## What the README does today

After the opening line and 'Where your games are kept', it goes straight to 'Requirements' (Node 20+,
pnpm 9+, Rust with the wasm32 target, wasm-pack) and then 'Install' (git submodule update, pnpm
install). Every route into the application is a developer route. Somebody who simply wants to play
has to read past a rustup invocation to discover there is nothing for them, and in fact there is:
they can just download it.

## What is actually available to install

Every release publishes four assets - v0.11.0 has:

  Atlantis.HUD_0.11.0_universal.dmg        macOS, universal
  Atlantis.HUD_0.11.0_x64-setup.exe        Windows installer
  Atlantis.HUD_0.11.0_amd64.AppImage       Linux
  atlantis-hud-web-v0.11.0.tar.gz          the built web app, for self-hosting

And there is a hosted instance needing no installation at all: https://atlantis-hud.kurelid.se
(deploy.yml:175, and the README's own 'Ship it' section names it at line 185). That is almost
certainly the first thing most readers want, and today it appears only in a section about how
releases are deployed.

## Why the ordering matters

It is not presentation. The current order tells a player that this is a project you compile, which
is false, and the people best placed to report bugs are the ones most likely to give up at
'cargo install wasm-pack'.
design:
## Context

The navigator's words, 2026-08-23:

> *"The README.md only describes how to compile from source. It should also describe how to install
> the pre-built releases. This section should come before the developer section that describes how
> to install and build from source."*

`README.md` runs: title and a one-line description (`:1-3`) → **Where your games are kept**
(`:5-66`, some sixty lines on how browser storage can lose a game) → **Requirements** (`:68`, Node,
pnpm, rustup, `wasm-pack`) → **Install** (`:85`, submodule and `pnpm install`) → Run / Check and
test / Ship it / Rulesets / agents.

**Every route into the application is a developer route**, and that is false: there is a hosted
instance needing no installation, and every release publishes a build for each platform. Somebody
who wants to play has to read past `cargo install wasm-pack` to discover there is nothing for them.
The people best placed to report bugs are the ones most likely to give up there.

**The prose already exists and is shipped.** `.github/workflows/release.yml:403-441` is the
release-notes body, and it carries a tested *Installing* section covering all four routes — including
the two that matter most and are easy to omit: the macOS build is **not notarized**
(`release.yml:8-10`), so Gatekeeper says it is damaged, and Windows SmartScreen warns of an unknown
publisher. **Nothing new is being written here.** This bead moves that prose into the README, in an
order the navigator chose, and marks the two copies as a pair.

The four assets are real; `gh release view` on `v0.11.0` lists exactly:
`Atlantis.HUD_0.11.0_universal.dmg`, `Atlantis.HUD_0.11.0_x64-setup.exe`,
`Atlantis.HUD_0.11.0_amd64.AppImage`, `atlantis-hud-web-v0.11.0.tar.gz`. The hosted instance is
`https://atlantis-hud.kurelid.se` (`README.md:185`, `deploy.yml:175`).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**Two files. No code, no tests, no generated anything.**

> **A note on reading this section.** The fenced blocks below contain **README content**, quoted
> verbatim. The `##` and `###` lines inside them are headings of `README.md`, **not** sections of
> this plan. This plan's own eight sections are `Context`, `Files to change, and what to reuse`,
> `Increments`, `The test plan`, `User-facing decisions`, `Out of scope`, `Validation` and
> `Known traps`, and nothing inside a fence belongs to them.

### `README.md`

**1. Insert a new `## Getting Atlantis HUD` immediately after the one-line description at `:3`**, so
it sits before `## Where your games are kept`. Verbatim — this is the section itself, not a
description of one. Copy the whole fenced block into `README.md`, without the fence:

~~~markdown
<!-- The install instructions here and the "Installing" section of the release-notes body in
     .github/workflows/release.yml are a matched pair. Change both, or neither. -->

## Getting Atlantis HUD

You do not need to build anything. There are four ways to run it.

### Use it in your browser

Open **<https://atlantis-hud.kurelid.se>**. There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for.

Your games are kept by your browser, on that device — [Where your games are kept](#where-your-games-are-kept),
just below, is worth two minutes before you start a long game.

**If you use Safari, install it** — Share → Add to Home Screen, or Add to Dock. Safari deletes an
uninstalled site's data after seven days without a visit, and a week between turns is perfectly
ordinary in a play-by-email game.

### Download the app

Each release publishes a build for every platform on the
[latest release page](https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/releases/latest). The desktop app
keeps each game as an ordinary file in your user folder, so your usual backups pick it up.

**macOS** — download the `.dmg`, open it, and drag **Atlantis HUD** to Applications. There is one
macOS download and it runs on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

This build is **not signed by Apple**, so macOS will refuse to open it the first time and say it is
damaged. It is not. Clear the quarantine flag once:

```
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Atlantis HUD.app"
```

**Windows** — download the `.exe` installer and run it. Windows SmartScreen may warn that the
application is from an unknown publisher. Click **More info** → **Run anyway** to proceed.

**Linux** — download the `.AppImage`, mark it executable, and run it:

```
chmod +x Atlantis\ HUD_*.AppImage
./Atlantis\ HUD_*.AppImage
```

### Host the web app yourself

Download `atlantis-hud-web-v<version>.tar.gz` from the same page, unpack it, and serve the `site/`
directory from the root of an HTTPS domain. The README inside covers the server requirements, with
nginx and Apache samples.
~~~

**2. Add a `## Building from source` heading immediately before the present `## Requirements`
(`:68`)**, with this lead, verbatim — again, copy the fenced block's contents, not the fence:

~~~markdown
## Building from source

Everything below is for working *on* Atlantis HUD. If you only want to play, the section above is
all you need.
~~~

**3. Demote `## Requirements` (`:68`) and `## Install` (`:85`) to `###`**, so they sit under it.
**Nothing in either is deleted or reworded.** GitHub derives heading anchors from the text, not the
level, so `#requirements` and `#install` keep working and no existing link breaks.

**Leave every other section exactly as it is** — `Run the app`, `Check and test`, `Ship it`,
`Rulesets`, `Working on it with agents`. They already follow the developer lead-in and already read
as developer sections. **Do not restructure further**: the acceptance asks that nothing be deleted,
and a wider reshuffle is a different bead.

### `.github/workflows/release.yml`

One YAML comment, immediately above `body:` at `:403`:

```yaml
      # The "Installing" section below and README.md's "Getting Atlantis HUD" are a matched pair.
      # Change both, or neither - the Gatekeeper story here is the same one a README reader needs,
      # and it changes the day this build is notarized (ah-m0cj).
```

A YAML `#` comment, **not** an HTML comment inside the body: the body is a block scalar rendered as
the release notes, so anything put inside it reaches the reader.

**Do not change the release-notes prose itself.** It is shipped, and the README copy is derived from
it rather than the other way round.

## Increments

This bead is two text edits and has no red-green loop; there is no behaviour to test-drive, and
inventing a test for prose would be a test that asserts a string nobody would notice changing. The
work is ordered rather than incremental.

1. **The new section.** Insert `## Getting Atlantis HUD` after `:3`, exactly as quoted above,
   including the paired-copy HTML comment.
2. **The developer lead-in.** Insert `## Building from source` before `## Requirements`, and demote
   those two headings to `###`.
3. **The pair marker.** Add the YAML comment above `body:` in `release.yml`.
4. **Read it as a stranger.** Open the rendered README on the branch — GitHub renders it in the PR's
   *Files changed* tab — and check the four things under *Validation*.

## The test plan

**None, and that is the honest answer for a documentation change.** There is no unit, no browser and
no corpus test that would fail if this section were wrong, and adding one would only pin the exact
bytes of a paragraph a person is meant to be free to improve.

What replaces a test is the reading under *Validation*, which is a human check because the thing
being verified — *does a stranger now know how to get this?* — is not machine-checkable.

**What must still pass, unchanged:** `pnpm run check:fast`. Nothing here touches code, so a failure
means something outside this bead's scope was edited.

**Markdown link checking:** the repository runs none, so the `releases/latest` link and the
`#where-your-games-are-kept` anchor are checked by clicking them in the rendered preview.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23 against `docs/ui/ah-m0cj-readme.html`. **This bead is
entirely user-facing** — every line of it is prose an outsider reads — so the section is quoted
verbatim above rather than described.

**Where the new section goes.**
**Chosen: A — getting it first.** Title → *Getting Atlantis HUD* → *Where your games are kept* →
*Building from source*. The storage caveats then land when they are actionable: the reader has
chosen browser or desktop by then, so the Safari warning is advice about a choice already made.
*Rejected — B, caveats first as today*: everyone would read the data-loss warnings, which matters
because the browser is the easiest way in and the most fragile — at the cost of sixty lines of *here
is how you can lose your game* before the reader learns how to get it at all.

**Which route leads.**
**Chosen: 1 — the hosted instance first.** *"Open `https://atlantis-hud.kurelid.se`. There is nothing
to install and nothing to sign up for."* Lowest friction; a reader is playing in one click.
*Rejected — 2, desktop first*: the desktop app keeps games as ordinary files that backups pick up,
which is the durable choice, but it front-loads the unsigned-binary friction onto exactly the readers
least likely to tolerate it.
*Rejected — 3, a table of all four*: even-handed and scannable, and it commits to no recommendation,
which for a first-time reader is itself a cost.
**The known cost of this choice is paid in the same breath**, which is why the browser subsection
carries both the pointer to *Where your games are kept* and the Safari line rather than leaving them
to be discovered.

**Two copies of the install prose.**
**Chosen: c — copy it, and mark the two as a pair.** An HTML comment in the README and a YAML comment
in `release.yml`, each naming the other.
*Rejected — a, just copy it*: two places to fix with nothing pointing between them, and the
Gatekeeper story changes the day this build is notarized.
*Rejected — b, the README as the single copy with the notes linking to it*: one source of truth, but
a release-notes reader would have to click through to GitHub for the step that makes their download
open at all.
**This is a reminder, not a mechanism, and is recorded as such** — nothing enforces it.

**Fixed regardless, and agreed:** links point at
`https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/releases/latest`, never a versioned asset path, so they do
not go stale; the macOS unsigned warning sits **with** the macOS download rather than in a footnote,
because a reader who is not told will conclude the app is broken; and nothing in the existing
developer sections is deleted.

## Out of scope

- **Notarizing the macOS build.** It needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership
  (`release.yml:8-10`). This bead documents the consequence; it does not remove it.
- **Rewriting *Where your games are kept***. It moves down and is otherwise untouched.
- **Restructuring *Run the app*, *Check and test*, *Ship it*, *Rulesets* or the agents section.**
  They stay where they are, under the developer lead-in.
- **A screenshot or any image.** None exists in the README today and adding one is a different
  decision.
- **Any link checker or docs CI.** None exists; adding one is its own bead.
- **The release-notes prose itself.** Shipped, and the source this copy derives from.

## Validation

```
pnpm run check:fast
```

Green — and it should be untouched by this bead, since nothing here is code.

**The real validation is a reading, and it is a human one.** On the PR branch, open the *Files
changed* tab, view `README.md` rendered, and check four things:

1. **A stranger who wants to play finds the hosted URL without scrolling past anything technical.**
2. **The four links resolve** — the hosted instance, `releases/latest`, and the
   `#where-your-games-are-kept` anchor from the browser subsection.
3. **The macOS paragraph is impossible to miss** if you are reading the macOS instructions, and the
   `xattr` line is inside a code block that copies cleanly.
4. **`## Building from source` makes the audience switch obvious**, and `Requirements` and `Install`
   now read as its subsections rather than as the way in.

## Known traps

- **The macOS build is not notarized, and omitting that line breaks the download for most readers.**
  Gatekeeper reports it as *damaged*, which reads as a corrupt file rather than a signing policy.
  This is the single most important sentence in the new section.
- **The release-notes body is a YAML block scalar.** An HTML comment placed inside it is rendered
  into the published release notes; the pair marker there must be a YAML `#` comment above `body:`.
- **Do not pin a download link to a version.** `v0.11.0` asset paths go stale on the next release —
  `releases/latest` does not. This is in the bead's own acceptance.
- **Demoting a heading does not break its anchor.** GitHub derives anchors from heading text, so
  `#requirements` survives `##` → `###`. Changing the *words* would break it, which is why the two
  headings are demoted and not renamed.
- **`README.md` is not `docs/`.** A change to it is an ordinary reviewed PR under the Four Eye
  Principle — it is **not** the `docs(<bead>): mockup` exception, which covers only a chosen mockup
  committed to `docs/ui/`.
- **Resist improving the prose in passing.** It is shipped text that has been read by users; this
  bead moves it. An improvement is welcome as its own bead, where the navigator can see it as a
  change rather than as part of a move.

- The developer sections are retitled or introduced so it is unambiguous which audience each is for; nothing in them is deleted.

title: PILLAGE must be earned, not assumed
description:
Found during verification of ah-abwx (2026-08-23, at 54dd0824).

ah-abwx correctly taught the silver column to credit PILLAGE with twice the region's tax base, mirroring the ledger. But neither surface checks whether the faction may pillage at all.

The rules: "To do this requires the faction to have enough combat ready men in the region to tax half of the available money in the region."

Observed: fixture neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep, unit The Lost One (683) - a single leader, no combat-ready force behind it - standing in mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra, tax base $8,963. Ordered PILLAGE, the forecast credits the full $17,926. One man cannot tax half of $8,963, so in the real game this order earns nothing.

The column therefore promises silver the turn will not deliver, which is the same class of defect ah-abwx just fixed - a surface disagreeing with what the engine will do - only now it overstates rather than understates.

Both surfaces are involved: crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs (the ledger's Intent::Pillage arm, ~1046) and crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs (the new forecast arm, ~472). Whatever the answer is, they must price it the same way, per the reasoning in ah-abwx's design and the corpus-wide agreement test in ah-ycuj.

Open question for planning: what counts as 'combat ready men' from a report alone, and whether an uncertain case should raise a SilverDoubt rather than a flat credit or a flat zero.
