title: Silver a unit CLAIMs counts toward what it will have at month end
description:
In the units-in-hex list, the Silver column does not count silver a unit CLAIMs as income. A unit whose month is funded by a CLAIM therefore reads as though it will end the month short, when in fact the claimed silver covers it.

CLAIM draws from the faction's unclaimed pool into the unit, so it is income to that unit for the month exactly as selling or entertaining is — and those are already counted (ah-1wcw.2). This looks like a gap in the same family rather than a new idea: the ah-1wcw epic and all six of its children are closed, and ah-1wcw.1, .2, .3, .4 and .6 all carry verification:passed, so the column is delivered and in the navigator's hands with this hole in it.

Worth ranking against the fact that the column's whole promise is telling a player whether a unit is paying for itself this month. A unit funded by CLAIM is the ordinary case for a new or idle unit, so the number is wrong on a common shape of unit and wrong in the alarming direction.

Reported by the navigator on 2026-08-23.
design:
## Context

The Silver column prices eight kinds of order and **`CLAIM` is not one of them**. `forecast_unit`
(`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:301`) has arms for `Tax`, `Work`, `Entertain`, `Sell`, `Study`,
`Cast`, `Buy`, `Give` and `Withdraw`. There is no `Intent::Claim` arm at all, so silver a unit claims
from the faction's purse is simply not counted.

A unit funded by a claim therefore reads as ending the month short when the claim covers it — and
that is the ordinary shape of a new or idle unit, so the figure is wrong on a common unit and wrong
in the alarming direction. The navigator reported it on 2026-08-23 against the delivered column: the
`ah-1wcw` epic and all six children are closed, five of them carrying `verification:passed`.

**The shipped order-check ledger already credits `CLAIM`** (`semantics.rs:701`,
`Intent::Claim(amount) => credit(ledger, who, SILVER, *amount)`), so this bead brings the column into
line with the warning rather than moving it away.

**Most of this needs no decision.** The hover's rows are generic — `Held now`, `In`, `Out`,
`At month end` — so a claim makes `In` bigger and nothing else. No new row, no new string, no new
colour. The mockup, `docs/ui/ah-bumi-claim.html`, shows exactly that.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the arm, and what caps it

**The purse is faction-wide**, which nothing in this function's inputs currently carries:
`RegionWages` is regional by name and by contract, and `UnitFacts` is per unit. So a fifth parameter,
in the same shape as `RegionWages` and for the same reason — values, not a report:

```rust
/// What the faction holds that any of its units may draw on.
///
/// Faction-wide, unlike [`RegionWages`]: one purse for the whole report, not one per hex.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct FactionPurse {
    /// `Unclaimed silver: $N` from the report header, or `None` where the report does not say.
    pub unclaimed: Option<i64>,
}
```

`forecast_unit` becomes `forecast_unit(facts, region, purse, lookups, ruleset)`, and the arm is:

```rust
Intent::Claim(amount) => {
    // Capped at what the faction actually holds, and never divided between units that claim in
    // the same turn - exactly as `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` treat their regional pools.
    income = income.saturating_add(match purse.unclaimed {
        Some(held) => (*amount).min(held),
        None => *amount,
    });
}
```

**`None` counts the claim as written, and raises no doubt.** That looks inconsistent with `TAX`,
which doubts when `tax_base` is absent, so the difference is worth stating: `TAX`'s *amount* is
derived (`men × 50`, capped), so without the cap the amount itself is unknown. A claim's amount is
**stated outright in the order**; the purse only limits it. An unstated purse leaves the amount known
and only the limit unknown, so counting the stated figure is not a guess in the way an uncapped tax
would be. **Do not add a `SilverDoubt` variant for this**; it would need a verbatim string the
navigator has not been asked for, and it would be caution about the wrong thing.

`saturating_add` and `.min` throughout, matching every other arm in the function.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — passing the purse

`review_turn` already has the whole `ParsedReport`, so the purse is
`FactionPurse { unclaimed: report.header.unclaimed_silver }` (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:57`),
built **once before the region loop** and passed to every `forecast_unit` call. It is faction-wide;
building it per hex would be the same value computed many times and would invite somebody to make it
per-hex later.

### Nothing else

No TypeScript, no regenerated bindings (`UnitSilver` is unchanged — `income` simply gets bigger), no
Settings entry, no advisory code, no hover string, and no change to `unitTooltip.ts`. **If you find
yourself editing anything under `packages/`, stop** — either the change belongs in `silver.rs` or
something has been misunderstood.

## Increments

**1. A claim is income.**
Failing test: `a_claiming_unit_counts_what_it_claims` in `silver.rs`'s test module — a unit with no
silver and `CLAIM 500` against a purse of 4935 has `income == Some(500)` and
`at_month_end == Some(500)`. That fails today with `income == Some(0)`.
Then, each its own test:
`a_claim_is_capped_by_what_the_faction_holds` (claim 9000, purse 4935 → 4935),
`a_claim_with_no_stated_purse_counts_what_was_claimed` (purse `None` → 500, `doubt` `None`),
`two_units_claiming_are_each_capped_at_the_whole_purse` — the accepted overstatement, pinned
deliberately so nobody "fixes" it into contention modelling,
`a_claim_of_nothing_changes_nothing`,
`a_claim_alongside_other_income_adds_to_it` (claim plus tax, so the arm cannot be written as an
assignment instead of an addition).

**2. The purse reaches the forecast.**
Failing test: `a_review_passes_the_factions_unclaimed_silver` in `semantics.rs`'s test module — a
report whose header states unclaimed silver and a unit claiming more than it, asserting the unit's
`income` is the capped figure. This is the test that proves the plumbing, and it is the one that
would fail if the purse were built but never passed.

**3. The real turn is unmoved, except where it should move.**
Extend `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` with
`the_committed_turns_claims_are_counted`. Assert `EXPECTED`'s finding counts are **unchanged** — this
bead adds no check — and pin the forecast of one unit in the committed turn that carries a `CLAIM`,
by id and figure.
**If no unit in the committed turn claims**, say so in the test's doc comment and assert that no
unit's `income` differs from what the epic left it. An absence stated is worth more than a test
quietly covering nothing.

## The test plan

| Suite | Pins |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` | increments 1 and 2, every rule above |
| `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` | the committed turn, and that no check was added |

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm run check:fast
```

**No new smoke spec.** This bead adds no interface; the column, the cell and the panel are the epic's
and are untouched. Do not add one to "cover" it.

The `ah-1wcw` family's existing `silver.rs` tests must pass **unedited** — the new parameter is the
only signature change, so a test that needs rewriting means the arm has been written into an existing
one rather than beside it.

## User-facing decisions

Taken by the navigator on 2026-08-23. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-bumi-claim.html`.

**Counting the claim needs no interface decision at all** — the hover's rows are generic, so `In`
gets bigger and nothing else changes. That was shown and agreed rather than assumed.

**The purse is capped per unit and never divided.** This was a real choice, because the epic had
already answered the shared-pool question **twice, differently**: `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` cap each
unit at the whole regional pool and never doubt (`ah-1wcw.1`, `ah-1wcw.2`), while faction food pools
and shows `?` when it cannot cover everyone (`ah-7cdt`). Offered as (A) cap with no contention,
(B) pool and doubt when short, (C) uncapped as the ledger does. **A chosen.**
*B rejected*: unlike food, silver has no waste, so a shortfall could be shared exactly and a `?` is
more caution than the case needs — and it would make a third behaviour for a shared pool.
*C rejected*: a unit claiming 9000 from a purse of 4935 would read as though it got 9000, and
overstating income is the direction that makes a player commit orders that fail.
**The accepted cost is stated**: two units can together read more than the purse holds.

**That cost is not left standing.** The navigator's answer was *"A, but file a new bead to introduce
a warning if the total CLAIM in all hexes exceeds the unclaimed silver."* Filed as **`ah-wur4`**,
unranked, and it is the other half of this decision — the same shape as `ah-1wcw.2`, where an
unsellable sale earns 0 and the shipped `not-traded-here` check is what tells the player why. **This
bead adds no warning**; that one does.

**An unstated purse counts the claim as written.** Decided here rather than asked, and the reasoning
is in *Files to change*: a claim's amount is stated in the order, so an unknown purse leaves only the
limit unknown — unlike `TAX`, whose amount is itself derived from the missing figure. Recorded
because it looks like an inconsistency until the difference is spelled out.

## Out of scope

- **Any warning about over-claiming.** `ah-wur4`, filed for it, faction-wide, and needing its own
  code, toggle and wording.
- **Contention between units claiming in one turn.** Deliberately not modelled; see above.
- **Changing `semantics.rs`'s ledger**, which credits `CLAIM` uncapped. It drives the shipped
  `not-enough-silver` check and its findings are pinned in `EXPECTED`; capping it would move them.
  The column and the ⚠ answering slightly differently was settled in `ah-1wcw.1`.
- **Anything under `packages/`.** No TypeScript changes at all.
- **The `Withdraw` arm** and every other intent already handled.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm run check:fast
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. A unit with no silver ordered `CLAIM 500` shows **500** at month end, not −100.
2. `git diff` touches `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`, `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` and
   test files, and **nothing under `packages/`**.
3. `validate_real_orders.rs` passes with `EXPECTED` **unedited**.
4. The existing `silver.rs` tests are unedited apart from the new parameter.

**Only a human can check** the thing the navigator actually reported: load a report, find a unit whose
month is funded by a claim, and confirm the Silver cell is no longer red. Psylocke's pass.

## Known traps

- **The purse is faction-wide, not regional.** Putting `unclaimed` on `RegionWages` would compile,
  pass every test in this bead, and be wrong the moment anybody reads the struct's own doc comment —
  which says "everything about the region".
- **Build the purse once, outside the region loop.** `review_turn` runs on every keystroke once
  typing settles (`crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs:53-55`); rebuilding a constant per hex is waste, and
  more importantly it makes the value look per-hex to the next reader.
- **`income` is accumulated, not assigned.** Every arm in `forecast_unit` adds to a running total
  seeded from `receipts.silver`. An arm written as `income = ...` silently discards gifts and every
  earlier order, and the single-order tests would all still pass — which is why increment 1 has
  `a_claim_alongside_other_income_adds_to_it`.
- **`Intent::Claim` carries an `i64` directly** (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:46`), not a
  struct — `Intent::Claim(amount)` and `*amount`, unlike the braced variants either side of it.
- **`ah-1wcw.1`'s *Known traps* apply here unchanged**, including that rounding is always downward
  and that `men_estimated` doubts the whole forecast before anything else is computed.
- **`corpus_errors` compares against a committed generated table.** Nothing here should change it; if
  it goes red, stop and work out why rather than running `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1` at it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A unit with a CLAIM order has that amount counted as income in the Silver column, so its month-end figure matches what the game will actually give it.
- The faction's unclaimed pool is respected: whatever the existing code does about a claim the faction cannot fund is stated and tested, not left implicit.
- A regression test covers a unit whose month-end Silver is non-negative only because of its CLAIM.

title: The map form refuses wrapping that an odd map size cannot support
description:
Asked for by the navigator on 2026-08-22 while planning ah-brgo: "We should not allow odd width and x wrap. The same for odd height and wrap y."

A hex lattice only holds positions where x + y is even. A map 72 wide joins cleanly, because x and x+72 have the same parity. A map 71 wide does not: the rows on one side of the seam sit half a hex above those on the other, so the two edges genuinely do not meet and a drawn seam would be a lie. The same argument applies to an odd height with wrapY.

So the combination should be refused where it is entered rather than handled where it is drawn - the map form on the create screen and under Settings > Per game (see docs/ui/ah-0w7w-map-size.html).

Its own bead for two reasons: those forms are ah-0w7w's, which is in_progress and carrying a failed verification, so this must not collide with Storm; and refusing input is a different kind of change from drawing a map, with its own wording to settle with the navigator.

Note that ah-brgo.1 must still cope defensively: a game saved before this validation exists may already carry an odd width with wrap set, and the view treats that as non-wrapping rather than drawing a seam that does not join.

FOR THE PLANNER: the wording of the refusal, whether it blocks saving or warns, and what happens to a game that already has the bad combination, are all undecided and are the navigator's.
design:
## Context

A hex lattice only holds positions where `x + y` is even. A map **72** wide joins cleanly across the
east-west seam, because `x` and `x + 72` have the same parity, so the column past the eastern edge
really is the column at the western edge. A map **71** wide does not: the rows on one side of the
seam sit half a hex above those on the other, and the two edges genuinely do not meet. The same
argument applies to an odd **height** with north-south wrap.

`ah-0w7w` added the map form - width, height, and the two wrap flags - to the create screen and to
Settings > Per game, and it has merged (commit `1755c70`). Neither form validates anything about the
combination, so a player can state a 71-wide map that wraps east-west, and the drawing code then has
to make the best of a shape that cannot exist.

This bead refuses the combination **where it is entered**, which is the navigator's own framing:
*"We should not allow odd width and x wrap. The same for odd height and wrap y."*

**It does not change how anything is drawn.** `ah-brgo.1` still has to cope defensively with a game
saved before this validation existed, and that is its business, not this bead's.

**No dependency on `ah-brgo.1` or `ah-brgo.2`**, which are Xavier's and touch the map view rather
than the forms. **`ah-0w7w` has merged**, so the collision its own description warned about is gone;
it is still marked `in_progress` with a failed verification, so **do not touch the files it owns
beyond the two forms named below**, and expect Storm to be working in the same tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The rule, as a pure predicate

**`packages/shared/src/mapShape.ts`** - the natural home: it already owns `MapDraft`,
`mapFromDraft` and `positiveWhole` (`:53-106`). The precedent to follow is `canSave` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/regionNotesState.ts:26-28`, a pure predicate in a non-React module
that a component uses to disable a button and re-checks in its own save path
(`RegionNotes.tsx:88` and `:261`).

```ts
/** Which axis a map shape's parity problem is on, and what to say about it. */
export type MapShapeProblem = {
  axis: "x" | "y";
  /** The sentence shown under the Wraps row, ready to render. */
  message: string;
};

/**
 * Why this draft's wrapping cannot be drawn, if it cannot.
 *
 * A hex lattice only holds positions where `x + y` is even, so a seam joins only at an even span:
 * at an odd one the rows on the two sides sit half a hex out of step and the edges do not meet.
 *
 * Empty for every draft that is fine, **including one whose dimensions cannot be read at all** -
 * an unreadable width states no map (`mapFromDraft` returns `null`), and a map nobody stated wraps
 * nowhere, so there is nothing to refuse. Reporting a parity problem about a field the player has
 * cleared would be an error about an absence.
 *
 * Both axes are reported when both are wrong; the navigator chose two lines over one.
 */
export function mapShapeProblems(draft: MapDraft): MapShapeProblem[];
```

The message text is in *User-facing decisions* and ships verbatim, with the width or height
interpolated.

**`mapFromDraft` is not changed.** Its doc comment (`:84-89`) records a deliberate decision that an
unreadable dimension is silently "no map stated" rather than an error, and that decision is not this
bead's to revisit. `mapShapeProblems` is a second, separate question asked of the same draft.

### The create screen

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/GameForm.tsx`.** The map fieldset is `:74-127`; the inputs are
`game-map-width`, `game-map-height`, `game-map-wrap-x`, `game-map-wrap-y`.

- Compute `const problems = mapShapeProblems(map);` from the existing draft state (`:30`).
- Render one line per problem directly under the Wraps row, before the fieldset closes, each
  `role="alert"` and `data-testid={`game-map-problem-${problem.axis}`}`, styled `text-danger` -
  the same treatment `game-form-error` already gets at `:129-133`.
- The submit button (`:135-141`) becomes `disabled={busy || problems.length > 0}`.
- **Re-check in `submit` (`:37-40`)** and return without calling `onCreate` if there are problems,
  exactly as `RegionNotes.tsx:88` re-checks `canSave`. A disabled button is not a guarantee; Enter
  in a text field submits a form.

### Settings > Per game

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`**, `GameMapSettings` (`:710-816`).

This form has **no Save button**: width and height commit on blur (`:758-780`), and the wrap
checkboxes commit immediately in `onChange` (`:784-811`, whose comment explains why - "A checkbox
has no half-typed state"). So the refusal takes a different shape here, and the navigator chose it
deliberately:

- `commit` (`:735`) becomes conditional. **When `mapShapeProblems(next)` is non-empty, do not call
  `onChangeMap` at all** - the game keeps the map it had.
- **The draft keeps what the player typed.** Do not revert the field and do not un-tick the box.
  The existing resync effect (`:726-733`) must not undo the invalid draft, or the message would
  appear and vanish; it resyncs on a change to `map`, and `map` does not change while nothing is
  committed, so read it and confirm rather than assuming.
- Render the same lines, `data-testid={`settings-map-problem-${problem.axis}`}`, in the same place
  relative to the Wraps row, beside the existing informational paragraph at `:740-754`.

The player can then fix either field, in either order, and the commit happens on whichever edit
makes the pair valid.

### A game that already carries the combination

Corrected **where the shape is read**, in `mapShapeOfGame`
(`packages/shared/src/mapShape.ts:34-39`) - the one choke point both the interface and the core go
through (`AppShell.tsx:566-576` builds `mapJson` from it, and `SettingsDialog` renders
`presentation.map` from it):

```ts
export function mapShapeOfGame(rulesetId: string, recorded: MapShape | undefined): GameMapShape {
  if (recorded !== undefined) {
    return { map: withDrawableWrapping(recorded), stated: true };
  }
  return { map: defaultMapFor(rulesetId), stated: false };
}

/**
 * The same shape with any wrapping that cannot be drawn turned off - an odd width cannot wrap
 * east-west, an odd height cannot wrap north-south.
 *
 * Games saved before `ah-teg0` may carry either combination, and the map is drawn without that
 * seam whatever the manifest says. Applying it here rather than at each reader means the interface
 * and the core cannot disagree about it.
 */
function withDrawableWrapping(map: MapShape): MapShape;
```

**The stored manifest is not rewritten**, and that is my decision rather than the navigator's, so it
is stated plainly: they chose "silently correct it on open", and every visible consequence of that
is delivered here - the form shows the wrap unticked, and the map draws without a seam. What is not
done is a write to the game file on open. A save is a side effect on a game the player may have
opened only to look at, it cannot be undone, and it would race the very backup and manifest paths
`ah-0w7w` has just finished changing. The stored flag is corrected the next time the player commits
anything in that form, which is the first moment they are actually editing the game.

`defaultMapFor` is not passed through `withDrawableWrapping`: a ruleset's own declared map is a
fact about the ruleset, and one that failed this test would be a bug to fix in
`packages/shared/src/rulesets.ts:52`, not to paper over per game.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test. `pnpm run check:fast` at the end of each.

**1. The rule.**
Failing test: `an_odd_width_cannot_wrap_east_west` in `packages/shared/src/mapShape.test.ts`,
asserting `mapShapeProblems` returns one problem on axis `x` with the exact message. Then
`an_odd_height_cannot_wrap_north_south`, `an_even_span_is_fine`,
`wrapping_that_is_off_is_never_a_problem` (71 wide, `wrapX: false` → none),
`both_axes_are_reported_when_both_are_wrong` (two problems), and
`a_draft_whose_dimensions_cannot_be_read_has_no_problem` (`width: "abc"`, `wrapX: true` → none).

**2. The create screen refuses it.**
Failing test: `does not create a game whose map cannot wrap` in
**`packages/shared/src/workspace/GameForm.test.tsx`, which does not exist and must be created** -
`GameForm` has no tests at all today, and no smoke coverage either. Assert that the submit button's
markup carries `disabled` and that the problem line is rendered with its message. Then
`submitting anyway creates nothing`, driving the `submit` handler directly rather than through a
click, because this harness fires no events.

Follow `packages/shared/src/testing/README.md` for the shape of a component test here, and keep the
file to what this bead adds: it is not the place to backfill coverage for the rest of the form.

**3. Settings keeps the typing and stores nothing.**
Failing test: `does not commit a map whose wrapping cannot be drawn` in
`SettingsDialog.test.tsx` - `onChangeMap` is not called, and the problem line is rendered.

**4. An existing game is read as drawable.**
Failing test: `a_recorded_odd_width_is_read_without_east_west_wrap` in `mapShape.test.ts`, and its
north-south twin. Then `a_recorded_shape_that_is_fine_is_returned_unchanged`, and
`the_manifest_is_not_rewritten` - `mapShapeOfGame` is pure and returns a new object, leaving its
argument alone.

## The test plan

| Suite | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `pnpm vitest packages/shared` | the rule, both forms' refusals, and the defensive read |
| `pnpm run check:fast` | lint, types, and the above |

Both component tests render with `renderToStaticMarkup` - see *Known traps*. That is enough for
what this bead adds: a `disabled` attribute and a rendered line are both in the markup. **Do not
write a test that clicks the checkbox and expects a re-render**; that harness cannot do it, and the
failure will not name the harness as the cause.

`GameForm.test.tsx` is a **new file**. `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` and `mapShape.test.ts` exist.

No smoke spec. Neither form has smoke coverage today, and adding some is a bead of its own rather
than a rider on this one.

## User-facing decisions

Taken by the navigator during planning on 2026-08-23. Mockups:
`.cerebro/scratchpad/beast/ah-teg0-odd-width.html` and
`.cerebro/scratchpad/beast/ah-teg0-settings.html`.

**The create screen refuses it: the button is disabled and the message is shown, and nothing is
stored.** Rejected: turning the wrap off for the player (it silently changes a value they set, and
if the width was the typo it has corrected the wrong one), and warning while allowing it (which
would store a combination the app then permanently ignores).

**The message ships verbatim**, with the number interpolated:

```
A 71-wide map cannot wrap east-west: the eastern and western edges would sit half a hex out of
step. Use an even width, or turn off east-west wrap.
```

and its exact twin for the other axis:

```
A 71-high map cannot wrap north-south: the northern and southern edges would sit half a hex out of
step. Use an even height, or turn off north-south wrap.
```

Rejected: three shorter phrasings. The chosen one names the number, says *why* in terms of the
hexes rather than as an arbitrary rule, and states **both** ways out - which matters, because the
app cannot know which of the two values was the mistake.

**Both messages show when both axes are wrong.** Offered against reporting only the first; the
navigator chose both.

**Settings > Per game keeps what was typed and stores nothing.** Asked separately, because that form
has no button to disable. Rejected: snapping the offending control back (undoes the player's typing
in front of them and forces an order of operations), disabling the wrap checkbox at an odd width
(rejected already for the create screen, and would make two identical-looking forms behave
differently), and making the create screen match by never disabling its button.

**A game that already carries the combination is corrected silently when it is opened**, rather than
being flagged as a problem to fix or left alone. See *Files to change* for the one part of that the
planner decided rather than the navigator: the correction is applied where the shape is read, and
the stored manifest is not rewritten on open.

**The rule is symmetric.** Height and north-south wrap behave identically, with identical wording.

## Out of scope

- **How the map is drawn**, at the seam or anywhere else. `ah-brgo.1` and `ah-brgo.2`, both Xavier's.
- **Any other validation of the map fields.** An unreadable or non-positive dimension keeps today's
  deliberate behaviour - it states no map - and `mapFromDraft`'s comment records why. No upper bound
  is added either.
- **Rewriting a stored manifest on open.** Settled above.
- **Validating a ruleset's own declared map.** If one ever failed this test it is a bug in
  `rulesets.ts`, not a per-game correction.
- **Smoke coverage for these forms**, which have none today.
- **The backup and persistence paths** (`crates/core/src/backup.rs`, `core-persistence`). Nothing
  here reaches them.

## Validation

```
pnpm run check:fast
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. On the create screen, typing width 71 with east-west wrap ticked disables **Create game** and
   shows the message; unticking the wrap re-enables it, and so does changing the width to 72.
2. Doing the same in Settings > Per game leaves 71 in the field, shows the message, and leaves the
   game's stored width unchanged; fixing either field commits.
3. Setting height 95 with north-south wrap does the same, with the other message.
4. Doing both at once shows two lines.
5. Opening a game whose manifest says `{"width":71,...,"wrapX":true}` shows east-west wrap
   **unticked**, and the game file on disk is unchanged.
6. Clearing the width entirely still creates the game, with no map stated and no message - today's
   behaviour, deliberately kept.

**Only a human can check** that two stacked messages do not make the fieldset feel cramped -
Psylocke's pass.

## Known traps

- **Never ask for an effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** That package has no jsdom by decision
  (`ah-nass`): component tests render with `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects, attaches
  no refs and fires no timers. The rule lives in `mapShapeProblems`, a pure function, for exactly
  this reason. `packages/shared/src/testing/README.md` has the pattern.
- **A disabled button is not a guarantee.** Enter in a text field submits a form, so `submit` must
  re-check - the same belt-and-braces `RegionNotes.tsx` uses at `:88` alongside `:261`.
- **An unreadable dimension must not produce a parity message.** `mapFromDraft` returns `null` for
  it, meaning no map is stated, and a map nobody stated wraps nowhere. Reporting a problem there
  would be an error about an absence, and it would newly block creating a game with the fields
  cleared - which the existing comment says is an ordinary thing to do.
- **Settings commits on blur for numbers and immediately for checkboxes** (`SettingsDialog.tsx:758`,
  `:784-796`). Both paths go through `commit`, so guard `commit` rather than each handler.
- **`GameMapSettings` resyncs its draft from `map`** (`:726-733`). Read that effect before changing
  `commit`: if a rejected edit somehow still changed `map`, the resync would wipe the invalid draft
  and the message with it.
- **`ah-0w7w` is still `in_progress` with `verification:failed` and Storm assigned**, though its code
  has merged. Both forms are files it owns. Rebase often, keep the diff to what this plan names, and
  do not tidy anything else in them.
- **`bd show <id> --json` returns an array**, so the design field is `.[0].design`.

title: Ruler labels and arrow keys speak the map's real coordinates
description:
The coordinate half of ah-brgo, split from it because it is independent of the drawing and testable on its own.

Two places still speak in unwrapped coordinates once the map repeats:

  - The ruler. rulerTicks (mapViewport.ts:326-348) emits raw indices, so panning east labels 70, 71, 72, 73. A label naming a hex nobody has is worse than no label; it should read 70, 71, 0, 1.
  - Arrow keys. neighbour (mapViewport.ts:302-316) walks from x=71 to x=72 with no clamp and no modulo, so keyboard movement disagrees with the movement planner, which already wraps via MapGeometry::wrap (crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs:134-158).

Both fold modulo the map width (and height for wrapY), and both need the map shape, which ah-brgo.1 threads into the view.

Navigator chose to fold both on 2026-08-22, over folding only the ruler and over leaving both alone.
design:
## Context

Once `ah-brgo.1` makes the map repeat, two things in the view still speak in coordinates the map does
not have.

**The ruler keeps counting.** `rulerTicks` (`mapViewport.ts:326-348`) emits raw lattice indices, so
panning east past the seam labels `70, 71, 72, 73`. On a map 72 wide there is no hex 72; the label
names something nobody has, which is worse than no label — and with `ah-brgo.1` landed it sits
directly above a ghost copy of hex `0`, so the picture and the number disagree in the same glance.

**Arrow keys walk off the edge.** `neighbour` (`mapViewport.ts:302-316`) is four lines of
unconditional arithmetic with no clamp and no modulo, so `ArrowRight` from `x=71` gives `x=72`. The
movement planner already wraps here — `MapGeometry::wrap`
(`crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs:134-158`) — so today the keyboard cursor and the route planner
disagree about what lies east of the seam.

Both fold modulo the map's extent, and both need the map's shape, which **`ah-brgo.1` threads into
the view**. That is why this bead is blocked on it rather than merely sequenced after it.

The navigator settled both on 2026-08-22, in the interview recorded on `docs/ui/ah-brgo-map-wrap.html`.
No new question is opened here.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The seam `ah-brgo.1` leaves

`ah-brgo.1` adds to `mapViewport.ts`:

```ts
export function wrapSpans(shape: MapShape | null): { x: number | null; y: number | null };
export function foldCoordinate(coordinate: Coordinate, shape: MapShape | null): Coordinate;
```

`foldCoordinate` already mirrors `MapGeometry::wrap`'s `rem_euclid`, and already applies the
even-extent guard through `wrapSpans` — an odd width does not fold, because the lattice does not
join. **Reuse it for both halves of this bead.** Do not write a second modulo; the whole value of
that function is that the view has exactly one answer to "which hex is this really".

If `ah-brgo.1` has not merged, stop and wait.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts` — the ruler

`Tick` (`:318`) is `{ index: number; offset: number }` today. It gains a third field rather than
changing either existing one:

```ts
/**
 * One ruler mark: where it sits, and what it is called.
 *
 * `index` is the lattice position and stays unique across the whole panned range, which is what
 * makes it usable as a React key when the map repeats. `label` is what the player reads, folded
 * into the map's own range - so panning east past a 72-wide seam reads `70, 71, 0, 1` while the two
 * ticks called `0` remain different ticks.
 */
export type Tick = { index: number; offset: number; label: number };
```

**`index` must stay unfolded, and this is the trap.** `MapCanvas.tsx:1526` uses `key={tick.index}`;
folding it would give two ticks the same key the moment a second repeat is on screen, and React
would drop one of them. Add `label`, change nothing else.

`rulerTicks` gains a trailing optional parameter so its one caller per axis can say what the extent
is:

```ts
export function rulerTicks(
  axis: "x" | "y",
  viewport: Viewport,
  size: number,
  minPixels: number,
  /** The map's extent on this axis, when it repeats; `null` when it does not. */
  extent: number | null = null
): Tick[];
```

`label` is `index` when `extent` is `null` or not positive, and `((index % extent) + extent) % extent`
otherwise — the same positive-modulo shape `ah-brgo.1` needed for the camera, and for the same
reason: panning west gives negative indices, and `-1 % 72` is `-1` in JavaScript.

Trailing and defaulted, so **every existing call and every existing test compiles and behaves
unchanged**. `mapViewport.test.ts`'s `ruler ticks` suite keeps passing without an edit, which is the
evidence that a non-wrapping map is untouched.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts` — arrow keys

`neighbour` gains the same shape of optional parameter:

```ts
export function neighbour(coordinate: Coordinate, key: ArrowKey, shape: MapShape | null = null): Coordinate;
```

Body unchanged except that the computed coordinate is returned through
`foldCoordinate(stepped, shape)`. With the default `null` that is the identity, so the ten existing
assertions at `mapViewport.test.ts:344-365` — including the two that pin that opposite arrow keys
undo each other — stay green untouched.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — two call sites, one line each

- **The ruler.** `rulerTicks` is called once per axis, at `:796` and `:808`. Pass the extent from the
  `shape` prop `ah-brgo.1` added: `shape?.wrapX ? shape.width : null` for x, and the `wrapY`/`height`
  pair for y. Then render `{tick.label}` in place of `{tick.index}` at the four text nodes
  (`:1527`, `:1530`, `:1541`, `:1548`) — both edges of both rulers, and it is easy to change two and
  leave two.
- **Arrow keys.** One caller, `:746`: `neighbour(from, event.key as ArrowKey)` becomes
  `neighbour(from, event.key as ArrowKey, shape ?? null)`.

**Nothing else in the component changes**, and no new prop is added — `shape` arrives with
`ah-brgo.1`.

## Increments

**1. The ruler knows what to call itself.**
Failing test: `labels_fold_into_the_maps_own_range` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.test.ts` — for a 72-wide extent, a tick at index `72`
carries `label: 0` and one at `73` carries `label: 1`, while their `index` values stay `72` and `73`.
Then `labels_west_of_the_origin_fold_forwards` (index `-1` gives `label: 71`, the negative-modulo
case), and `labels_are_the_index_when_the_map_does_not_repeat` (extent `null` leaves every label
equal to its index — the existing behaviour, pinned).

**2. The ruler reads them.**
Failing test: `renders_the_folded_label_on_both_edges_of_both_rulers` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.test.tsx`, rendered with `renderToStaticMarkup`: for a
wrapping game panned past the seam, the x ruler's markup contains `0` where the index is `72`, and it
does so **twice** — top and bottom. Same for the y ruler when `wrapY` is set.

**3. Arrow keys stay on the map.**
Failing test: `stepping_east_from_the_last_column_arrives_at_the_first` in `mapViewport.test.ts` —
`neighbour(at(71, 40), "ArrowRight", shape)` is `x: 0`; `neighbour(at(0, 40), "ArrowLeft", shape)` is
`x: 71`. Then `stepping_is_unchanged_without_a_shape`, re-asserting one of the existing cases with
the third argument omitted, and `an_odd_width_does_not_fold` — the defensive guard `ah-brgo.1`
established.

**4. It works in the browser.**
Failing test: `the_arrow_keys_cross_the_seam` in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`. Load a wrapping
game, put the map cursor on a hex in the last column, press `ArrowRight`, and assert the focused hex
is in the first column. This is the one thing the unit tests cannot show: that the cursor actually
lands on a hex that exists and can be focused.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `labels_fold_into_the_maps_own_range` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the label, and that `index` does not move |
| `labels_west_of_the_origin_fold_forwards` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | negative modulo |
| `labels_are_the_index_when_the_map_does_not_repeat` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the unchanged case |
| `renders_the_folded_label_on_both_edges_of_both_rulers` | `MapCanvas.test.tsx` | all four text nodes |
| `stepping_east_from_the_last_column_arrives_at_the_first` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the fold, both directions |
| `stepping_is_unchanged_without_a_shape` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the default argument |
| `an_odd_width_does_not_fold` | `mapViewport.test.ts` | the even-extent guard |
| `the_arrow_keys_cross_the_seam` | `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` | a real focusable hex |

The existing `ruler ticks` and `arrow keys` suites in `mapViewport.test.ts` must pass **without being
edited**. If either needs a change, the optional parameters are not defaulting the way this plan
says, and that is a fault in the change rather than in the tests.

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web
```

## User-facing decisions

Settled by the navigator on 2026-08-22 as part of `ah-brgo`'s interview; mockup
`docs/ui/ah-brgo-map-wrap.html`. **Nothing is reopened here.**

**Both the ruler and the arrow keys fold.** Offered as (i) fold both, (ii) fold the ruler only and
leave the arrow keys, since the movement planner's territory was in flux, and (iii) neither — keep
the bead to panning alone. **Fold both chosen.**
*(ii) rejected* because the keyboard cursor would keep disagreeing with the route planner about what
lies east of `x=71`, and the two are read together.
*(iii) rejected* because a ruler labelling a hex nobody has is worse than no label — and with the map
repeating it sits directly over a ghost of hex `0`.

**The label folds; the tick does not.** Not a question put to the navigator — an implementation
consequence recorded here because it is visible: the two ticks reading `0` on screen are genuinely
different ticks, and they must stay distinguishable to React.

No new string is added anywhere. The ruler shows numbers, and the numbers become correct.

## Out of scope

- **Drawing the repeats.** `ah-brgo.1`, which blocks this bead.
- **Refusing an odd width with wrap where it is entered.** `ah-teg0`.
- **Marquee selection across the seam.** Still not representable; still deliberately unfiled.
- **The y ruler's behaviour on a map that does not wrap north-south**, which is the default —
  unchanged, because `extent` is `null` and every label is its index.
- **`coordinateAt`.** `ah-brgo.1` already folds it at its call site; this bead adds no second fold.
- **Anything in `crates/`.** View layer only, no regenerated bindings.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=web
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts --project=desktop-shell
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. `git diff` touches `mapViewport.ts`, `MapCanvas.tsx` and test files, and nothing else.
2. The existing `ruler ticks` and `arrow keys` suites are **unedited** and green.
3. On a wrapping game panned east past the seam, the ruler reads `… 70, 71, 0, 1 …` on both the top
   and bottom edges.
4. On a non-wrapping game the ruler is exactly as it is today.

**Only a human can check** that the ruler reads naturally across the seam rather than looking like a
glitch — Psylocke's pass, on the same game that failed `ah-0w7w`'s verification.

## Known traps

- **`tick.index` is a React key** (`MapCanvas.tsx:1526`). Folding it gives two ticks the same key as
  soon as a second repeat is on screen, and React drops one — a ruler that loses a label
  intermittently, which is a horrible thing to debug. Add `label`; leave `index` alone.
- **`-1 % 72` is `-1` in JavaScript.** Panning west of the origin produces negative indices
  immediately, so the naive modulo prints `-1` where the map says `71`. Same shape as the camera fold
  in `ah-brgo.1`.
- **Four text nodes, not two.** Both rulers draw their labels at both edges (`:1527`, `:1530`,
  `:1541`, `:1548`). Changing two and leaving two produces a map whose top ruler disagrees with its
  bottom one, and increment 2 asserts both deliberately.
- **Keep the new parameters trailing and defaulted.** That is what lets the ten existing `neighbour`
  assertions and the whole `ruler ticks` suite stand unedited — and an unedited suite is the evidence
  that a non-wrapping map is untouched. If you find yourself editing them, stop and reconsider the
  signature.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom, by decision (ah-nass).** `MapCanvas.test.tsx` renders with
  `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects — fine for increment 2, which asserts on markup, and
  the reason increment 4 is a smoke test.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a PWA run straight
  afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker.

title: The map view does not wrap east-west, even when the game says it does
description:
Verification of ah-0w7w (2026-08-23) found that a game with wrapX set still scrolls past x=0 to the left and past x=71 to the right: the flag is recorded and honoured by the movement graph, but the map VIEW has never seen it.

Established while fixing the other two verification failures:

- Panning is unbounded by design. packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts owns the transform (Viewport = {tx,ty,step}); nothing computes world bounds or clamps tx/ty. fitTo and centreOn only derive tx at framing time.
- MapCanvas.tsx never receives a MapShape at all. wrapX today reaches only crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs via AppShell.tsx:571.
- The renderer is favourable: hexes are a plain list drawn at worldOf(coordinate) (x = coordinate.x * COLUMN_PITCH), nothing is clipped to data extents, and fog is already an infinite pattern - so ghost copies at x +/- width*COLUMN_PITCH are straightforward.

Medium change. Touches: threading MapShape from AppShell into MapCanvas; worldOf or a wrapping wrapper; MapCanvas's hex/route/note/region render passes emitting 1 or 3 copies; fitTo, centreOn, isOffScreen; rulerTicks (x labels modulo width); and coordinateAt (mapViewport.ts:143-181), which must normalise x modulo width or a click in a ghost copy returns x=73. mapMarquee.ts and mapViewport's neighbour() need seam handling if selection may span the seam.

FOR THE PLANNER - real user-facing questions here:
- Does panning wrap infinitely, or does it stop at the seam with the map repeating once either side?
- Do the ruler's x labels repeat (0..71, 0..71) or keep counting?
- May a marquee selection span the seam?
- What does wrapY do to the view - the same, or nothing (an Atlantis map has poles)?
- Odd map widths shift row parity across the seam; refuse, or handle?
acceptance_criteria:
- With a game whose map wraps east-west, scrolling east past the last column shows column 0 rather than empty ground, and the same to the west.
- Clicking a hex in a wrapped region selects the real hex (coordinateAt normalises modulo width), not a coordinate off the map.
- A game with no map, or one that does not wrap, pans exactly as it does today.
- wrapY behaves as the navigator decides during planning.
notes: Created at P4 per CLAUDE.md (priority is the navigator's to set), although it comes from a P0 verification failure of ah-0w7w — worth ranking early.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-brgo.1, delivered in PR #582

title: Withdrawal prices are read from the game data
description:
Split from ah-1wcw during the planning of ah-1wcw.3 (2026-08-22, Beast), on the navigator's own observation that the withdraw prices are in the game data and can be scraped.

The data page states a withdrawal price per item, in the same clause the scraper already reads past:

  grain [GRAI], weight 5, costs 37 silver to withdraw.
  chain armor [CARM], weight 1, costs 150 silver to withdraw.

Thirty such entries in the committed data fixture. packages/ruleset/src/data.ts already matches that preamble - its own doc comment quotes it - but keeps only the weight and the prose, so the number is thrown away. ItemEntry (crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:178) has no field for it.

Two consequences, and the second is a change to shipped behaviour the navigator approved deliberately:

- ah-1wcw.3 can price a WITHDRAW order instead of showing ? for the whole unit.
- not-enough-silver stops declining to judge a unit that withdraws. It only ever declined because the price was unknown (semantics.rs:773-776), and once it is known the reason is gone. The committed turn-71 template has no WITHDRAW orders, so nothing there changes.

Blocks ah-1wcw.3.
design:
## Context

The game data page states a withdrawal price for every basic item, in the same clause the scraper
already reads past:

```
grain [GRAI], weight 5, costs 37 silver to withdraw.
chain armor [CARM], weight 1, costs 150 silver to withdraw.
```

Thirty such entries in the committed data fixture. `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` matches that
preamble - its own doc comment quotes it (`data.ts:83-89`) - but keeps only the weight and the
prose, so the number is thrown away. `ItemEntry` (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:178-199`) has
no field for it, and `Intent::Withdraw` (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:55`) is a **bare
variant** that discards the order's arguments entirely.

This bead carries the price end to end: scraped, stored, parsed, and charged. Two things then become
possible, and the second is a deliberate change to shipped behaviour:

1. **`ah-1wcw.3` can price a `WITHDRAW`** instead of showing `?` for the whole unit. That is why
   this bead exists and why it blocks `.3`.
2. **`not-enough-silver` stops declining to judge a unit that withdraws.** It declines today only
   because the price was unknown - "The ruleset carries no withdrawal prices. Spending an amount
   nobody can count is exactly the case for declining to judge the unit" (`semantics.rs:773-776`).
   Once the price is known that reason is gone. The navigator was asked directly and chose to let it
   judge them.

Split from `ah-1wcw` during the planning of `ah-1wcw.3` on the navigator's own observation that the
prices are in the game data. **Blocks `ah-1wcw.3`.**

**No interface at all.** Nothing new is drawn, worded or configured.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The scraper

**`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`.** `ItemEntry` (`:30-91`) gains one optional field, documented in
the file's own idiom:

```ts
  /**
   * What WITHDRAW costs per unit of this item, in silver - `costs 37 silver to withdraw`.
   *
   * Absent for anything the page states no price for, which is every item that is not a basic one:
   * "If you do not have sufficient unclaimed, or if you try withdraw any other than a basic item,
   * an error will be given." Absent, never zero - a zero would claim the page had said so.
   */
  withdrawCost?: number;
```

Read it exactly as `weight` is read, through the existing `readNumber` helper
(`parseItemReference`, `data.ts:346`), and add it as a **spreadable** field so an entry with no
price carries no key - the idiom `conditionOf`, `cargoOf`, `sailingOf` and `descriptionOf` already
follow (`data.ts:300-304` for the shape):

```ts
/** The withdrawal price, as a spreadable field so an item with none carries no key. */
function withdrawOf(paragraph: string): { withdrawCost?: number } {
  const cost = readNumber(paragraph, /costs (\d+) silver to withdraw/i);
  return cost === undefined ? {} : { withdrawCost: cost };
}
```

spread into the `entry` literal at `data.ts:342-357` beside `...conditionOf(paragraph)`.

### The ruleset type

**`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`**, `ItemEntry`:

```rust
    /// What WITHDRAW costs per unit of this item, in silver. `None` for an item the page prices
    /// nowhere - anything that is not a basic item - and for a ruleset cached before `ah-1wcw.6`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub withdraw_cost: Option<i64>,
```

**`ItemEntry` carries `deny_unknown_fields` (`rules.rs:177`), so the order of work matters**: a
regenerated `ruleset.json` containing `withdrawCost` will fail to deserialise against a build
without this field. Add the Rust field **before** regenerating, and keep both in one commit. See
*Known traps*.

### The committed ruleset

`config/public/ruleset.json` is regenerated, not hand-edited. `committed.test.ts:13-15` prints the
command, and it is the only correct one:

```
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html --data tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html
```

That test holds the committed file equal to the scraper's output, so it fails until the file is
regenerated - which is the forcing function, not a nuisance.

### The order

**`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`.** `Intent::Withdraw` gains what the order actually said,
shaped like `Buy`:

```rust
    /// `WITHDRAW [number] <item>`, drawing goods against the faction's unclaimed silver.
    ///
    /// Carried in full since `ah-1wcw.6`; it was a bare variant while the ruleset held no
    /// withdrawal prices and nothing could be done with the arguments.
    Withdraw {
        count: i64,
        item: String,
    },
```

Built at `intents.rs:364`. The grammar's forms are `[Number, Item]` and `[Item]`
(`grammar.rs:396-399`), so **there is no `ALL` form** - a plain count, defaulting to 1 when the
number is omitted. Do not reach for `forms::read_amount`, which exists for `BUY`/`SELL`'s
`Amount::All`; read the number and the item directly, and return `None` if the shape is anything
else, exactly as the neighbouring arms do.

Every `match` on `Intent` must now bind the fields. The compiler will find them; the ones that
exist today are in `semantics.rs` (`apply` at `:668`, `spends_the_month` at `:261`) and
`intents.rs`'s own tests.

### The check

**`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`**, `apply`'s `Intent::Withdraw` arm (`:772-776`). Replace
the doubt with a charge:

- resolve the item through the existing `resolve_item(text, hex, actor, ledger.ruleset)`
  (used by `transfer` at `:773`), which is how every other order turns an item argument into a tag;
- look the tag up in the ruleset's items and read `withdraw_cost`;
- **priced** → `charge(ledger, who, SILVER, count * cost, placed)`;
- **unpriced, unresolvable, or no ruleset at all** → `ledger.doubted.insert(who)`, exactly as today.

The `doubted` path stays and stays reachable: a cached ruleset from before this bead has no
withdrawal prices at all, and the old behaviour is precisely the right one for it.

Update the comment at `:773-774`, which will otherwise state the opposite of what the code does.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test. `pnpm run check:fast` at the end of each.

**1. The scraper keeps the price.**
Failing test: `reads the withdrawal price` in `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`, against the
line the file already quotes at `:67` - `grain [GRAI], weight 5, costs 37 silver to withdraw.` -
asserting `withdrawCost === 37`. Then `an item the page prices nowhere carries no withdrawal price`,
asserting the key is **absent**, not zero.

**2. The core reads it, and the committed file carries it.**
Failing test: `committed.test.ts`'s existing
`is exactly what the scraper produces from the committed fixture pages`, which goes red the moment
increment 1 lands and green when the file is regenerated. Add the Rust field in the same increment,
and a Rust test `a_ruleset_without_withdrawal_prices_still_loads` deserialising an `ItemEntry` JSON
with no `withdrawCost`, which is what `#[serde(default)]` is for.

**3. The order keeps its arguments.**
Failing test: `a_withdrawal_carries_what_it_withdraws` in `intents.rs`'s test module, replacing
`a_withdrawal_is_recorded_even_though_its_price_is_unknown` (`intents.rs:799`) - whose name is now
false. Assert `WITHDRAW 5 stone` reads as `Withdraw { count: 5, item: "stone" }` and `WITHDRAW iron`
as `count: 1`.

**4. A withdrawal is charged.**
Failing test: `a_withdrawing_unit_is_charged_the_rulesets_price` in `semantics.rs`, asserting the
ledger falls by `count * withdraw_cost`. Then
`a_withdrawing_unit_that_cannot_pay_is_warned_about` - the behaviour change the navigator approved,
producing a `not-enough-silver` finding where today there is silence - and
`a_withdrawal_the_ruleset_cannot_price_is_still_doubted`, which pins the old path for cached
rulesets.

**5. The real turn is unmoved.**
Failing test: `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` passes with `EXPECTED` **unedited**. The
committed turn-71 template contains **no `WITHDRAW` orders at all**, so nothing there may change; if
a count moves, increment 4 has charged something it should not have.

## The test plan

| Suite | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `pnpm vitest packages/ruleset` | the price is scraped, and absent where the page states none |
| `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts` | `config/public/ruleset.json` really was regenerated |
| `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` | the field loads, the order carries its arguments, the charge is right, and an unpriced withdrawal is still doubted |
| `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` | the committed turn is **unchanged** |

Must run before the PR: `pnpm run check:fast`. No smoke spec: this bead draws nothing.

## User-facing decisions

**One, and it is a change to shipped behaviour rather than to an interface.**

**`not-enough-silver` will start judging units that withdraw.** Put to the navigator during the
planning of `ah-1wcw.3` on 2026-08-22, with the note that it is a default-on warning that has
never spoken about withdrawals. **Chosen: let it judge them** - the check declined only because the
price was unknown, and once it is known the reason is gone. Rejected: keeping the check declining
while the new Silver column uses the prices, which would give two behaviours from one fact and read
as a bug to whoever found it next.

No message, label, colour or setting changes: a withdrawing unit that cannot pay produces the
existing `not-enough-silver` finding, with its existing wording and its existing Settings toggle.

**No new interface.** Nothing is drawn, worded or configured by this bead.

## Out of scope

- **Using the price in the Silver column.** That is `ah-1wcw.3`, which this bead blocks.
- **Any new advisory code.** Settled for the whole epic in `ah-1wcw.1`.
- **Withdrawal's other rules** - that it cannot be used in the Nexus, and that only basic items may
  be withdrawn. Both are real, both are stated in the rules page, and both are checks rather than
  prices. If they are worth having, they are their own bead; do not smuggle them in here.
- **Whether the faction can afford the withdrawal at all**, which draws on faction-wide unclaimed
  silver rather than on the unit's purse. Different quantity, different check.
- **Re-scraping from the live site.** The committed fixture pages are the input.

## Validation

```
pnpm run check:fast
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. `jq '.items.GRAI.withdrawCost' config/public/ruleset.json` prints `37`.
2. `jq '[.items[] | select(.withdrawCost)] | length' config/public/ruleset.json` prints `30`.
   That figure was counted from the committed data page while planning, over the same paragraph
   shape `parseItemReference` matches. A different number is not a licence to edit this line: it
   means the scraper is splitting the page differently from the page, and that is the bug.
3. `jq '.items.LONG.withdrawCost' config/public/ruleset.json` prints `null` - a ship is not a basic
   item and the page prices none.
4. `committed.test.ts` passes, which is the proof the file was regenerated rather than edited.
5. `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` passes with `EXPECTED` unedited.
6. A constructed fixture in which a unit withdraws more than it can pay for produces a
   `not-enough-silver` finding.

**Nothing here needs a human to look at it** - there is no interface. Psylocke may reasonably mark
this bead as not requiring verification.

## Known traps

- **`ItemEntry` carries `deny_unknown_fields`** (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:177`). A
  regenerated `ruleset.json` with `withdrawCost` in it will fail to deserialise against a build that
  has not yet gained the Rust field, and the failure surfaces as every item in the catalogue
  vanishing rather than as anything naming the field. Add the Rust field first, and keep the field
  and the regenerated file in one commit.
- **`config/public/ruleset.json` is generated, never hand-edited.** `committed.test.ts` holds it
  equal to the scraper's output and prints the exact regeneration command. Two stale copies exist at
  `apps/web/dist/ruleset.json` and `apps/desktop/dist/ruleset.json`; those are build output and are
  not edited either.
- **Absent, never zero.** An item the page prices nowhere must carry no key at all - the scraper's
  spreadable-field idiom exists for exactly this, and `committed.test.ts` uses `toEqual` rather than
  `toStrictEqual` precisely so an absent optional and a missing key are the same thing. A `0` would
  claim the page said the withdrawal was free.
- **`Intent::Withdraw` becoming a struct variant breaks every `match` on `Intent`.** That is the
  point - `spends_the_month` (`semantics.rs:261-301`) is written as an exhaustive match on purpose,
  "so the compiler refuses a new `Intent` variant until somebody has said which side of this line it
  falls on". Bind the fields; do not add a `_ =>` arm anywhere.
- **The grammar gives `WITHDRAW` no `ALL` form** (`grammar.rs:396-399`), unlike `BUY` and `SELL`.
  Reaching for `forms::read_amount` would accept an order the server will reject.
- **The committed turn has no `WITHDRAW` orders**, so a green `validate_real_orders.rs` proves
  nothing broke rather than that anything works. The constructed fixtures in increment 4 are what
  prove the rule.
- **A cached ruleset predates this field**, so the `doubted` path must stay reachable and tested.
  Deleting it would make every withdrawal free for anyone who has not re-scraped.
- **`bd show <id> --json` returns an array**, so the design field is `.[0].design`.

title: Warn when a unit is told to buy or sell something this market does not trade
description:
Asked for by the navigator on 2026-08-22 while planning ah-1wcw.2, and split out of it: "we should add a warning for trying to sell or buy something no wanted or on sale."

A SELL of goods the region's market does not list under Wanted cannot happen, and a BUY of goods not listed under For Sale cannot happen either. Both are silent today - the order is written, the month is spent, and nothing arrives.

ah-1wcw.2 settled the forecast side of this: an impossible sale earns 0 and an impossible purchase costs 0, with no doubt raised, precisely BECAUSE this warning is what tells the player. So the two beads are halves of one answer, and this one carries the part the player actually reads.

## Why it is its own bead

ah-1wcw.1 decided deliberately that the Silver column adds no new advisory code and no new Settings entry. This is a new advisory check and reverses none of that - it is a different claim about a different thing (an order that cannot execute, rather than a unit that runs out of money). But it needs everything a check needs: a code, a message, an anchor line, expected findings pinned in the committed turn-71 template, and its own toggle under Settings then Warnings. ah-dwk6 is the pattern to follow.

## For the planner

The market resolution already exists and should be reused rather than rebuilt: the market function at crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:972, over market_answer at :945 and resolve_item at :990, which already distinguishes NotTraded from Unknown - that distinction is exactly this check's subject, and an Unknown item must NOT warn, or every unrecognised item name becomes a false positive.

Interview the navigator on the message wording, whether it is one code or two (buy and sell), and whether it is on by default - none of that was decided when the bead was split.
close_reason: Already delivered. The warning this bead was created for ships as not-traded-here (check_markets, crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:641-686): it reports a BUY of what the hex does not sell and a SELL of what it does not want, is on by default, carries a Settings > Warnings toggle, and reads 'this hex does not want furs - its market wants ...'. It keys off MarketAnswer::NotTraded, the same distinction ah-1wcw.2's selling rule turns on, so the column and the warning agree by construction. Found while planning; the navigator confirmed the close on 2026-08-22. ah-1wcw.2's plan was corrected to cite the shipped check rather than this bead.

title: A unit whose name contains an unclosed bracket vanishes from the report
description:
Found while planning ah-w544.1, and deliberately left out of it.

split_top_level tracks bracket depth. An unmatched CLOSING bracket is harmless - depth goes negative and the 'depth <= 0' guard still splits. An unmatched OPENING one is not: for

  * Smiley :( (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN].

depth never returns to 0, so nothing splits and the whole head is one field. split_trailing_id then takes the LAST parenthesised number, so the unit is read with the FACTION's id (29) and a name of 'Smiley :( (100), Wanderers'. Silent mis-parse rather than a drop.

ah-w544.1 fixes the comma class and pins the close-unbalanced case; this one needs a different mechanism (a re-scan treating an unmatched '(' as a literal, or a depth clamp with a fallback), so it was scoped out to keep the P0 shippable.

Unknown whether the engine even permits parentheses in player-chosen names - worth checking before building anything.
design:
## Context

A unit whose name contains an **unclosed bracket** is dropped from the report entirely. `Smiley :(`
is the shape that provoked this; so is any name with a stray `(` or `[`.

`split_leading_id` (`crates/core/src/report/scan.rs`) finds the unit's identifier by scanning for the
first parenthesised group **at bracket depth zero**. An unmatched opener pushes the depth up and
nothing ever brings it back, so no candidate group is ever accepted and the function returns `None`.
`parse_unit` returns `None` on that (`unit.rs:127`), and the unit is gone.

Verified against the merged algorithm rather than assumed:

| Head | `split_leading_id` |
|---|---|
| `Smiley :( (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN]` | **`None`** — dropped |
| `Bob [x (100), Wanderers (29)` | **`None`** — dropped |
| `Smiley :) (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN]` | `("Smiley :)", "100", …)` — fine |
| `Three of Five (793), Borg (73), behind` | `("Three of Five", "793", …)` — fine |

**An unmatched *closing* bracket is already handled and must stay handled.** `split_top_level` and
`split_leading_id` both test `depth <= 0` rather than `depth == 0`, deliberately, which is what makes
a trailing `:)` harmless. This bead fixes only the opening case; do not touch that guard.

**This bead's own description is out of date and the notes record why.** It was filed while
`ah-w544.1` was still being planned, and describes the *old* symptom — a silent mis-parse in which
the unit took its faction's id via `split_trailing_id`'s `rfind('(')`. `ah-w544.1` (#561) replaced
that scan, so the symptom is now a clean drop; and `ah-w544.2` (#563) shipped the *Lines that could
not be read* panel, which **lists this line with its raw text**. So the loss announces itself, which
is why the navigator re-ranked this from P1 to P2 on 2026-08-22. Read the bead's notes before the
description.

The navigator also folded in the square-bracket case in the same breath: one depth counter, one fix,
one set of tests.

**Still unknown, and worth ten minutes before building:** whether the engine permits parentheses in
player-chosen names at all. If it does not, this is unreachable in practice and worth saying so on
the bead rather than building. It costs nothing to check the rules page first.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/report/scan.rs` — the whole change

`split_leading_id` keeps its signature and its current scan **byte for byte**. What it gains is a
fallback that only runs when the current scan finds nothing:

```rust
/// The byte indices of brackets that never close (or never open).
///
/// A name may contain a stray bracket - `Smiley :(` is a real one - and a depth counter cannot tell
/// that from a nesting that has not finished yet. Matching the brackets first says exactly which
/// ones are noise, so the scan can step over them instead of being derailed by them.
///
/// Empty for well-formed input, which is what makes the fallback below free on every real report.
fn unmatched_brackets(input: &str) -> BTreeSet<usize>;

/// The existing scan, with a set of positions to treat as ordinary characters.
fn scan_leading_id<'a>(input: &'a str, ignore: &BTreeSet<usize>) -> Option<(String, String, &'a str)>;
```

and `split_leading_id` becomes:

```rust
pub fn split_leading_id(input: &str) -> Option<(String, String, &str)> {
    if let Some(found) = scan_leading_id(input, &BTreeSet::new()) {
        return Some(found);
    }
    let stray = unmatched_brackets(input);
    if stray.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    scan_leading_id(input, &stray)
}
```

**This shape is the point of the design and it is not negotiable.** The first call is the current
function with an empty ignore-set, so it computes exactly what it computes today, for every input
that works today. The fallback runs **only where the answer is currently `None`** — that is, only
where a unit is currently being lost. The regression risk against a 25-report corpus is therefore
not "small", it is structurally zero, and that is worth more here than a tidier single-pass rewrite.
Do not "simplify" this into one scan that always consults the ignore-set.

`unmatched_brackets` is the ordinary stack algorithm: push the index of every `(` and `[`; on `)` or
`]`, pop if the stack is non-empty, otherwise record **this** index as an unmatched closer. Whatever
remains on the stack at the end is an unmatched opener. Both kinds go in the returned set. `(` may
close against `[` and vice versa — the existing scanners already treat the two kinds
interchangeably (`'(' | '['` increments, `')' | ']'` decrements), so this must not start
distinguishing them or it will disagree with `split_top_level` about the same string.

`scan_leading_id` is today's loop with one added line at the top of the match: a character whose
index is in `ignore` falls through to the `_ => {}` arm, changing no depth and opening no candidate.

**Nothing else in `scan.rs` changes.** `split_top_level`, `next_top_level_field` and
`split_trailing_id` keep their current behaviour exactly.

### `crates/core/src/report/unit.rs` — no changes at all

Both the unit's own identifier (`unit.rs:127`) and its faction's (`unit.rs:166`) go through
`split_leading_id`, so the fallback fixes both without a line being edited here. Confirm by reading
those two lines; do not edit the file.

**One known limit stays**, and it is deliberate: the faction branch rejects a candidate whose name
contains `[` (`unit.rs:167`), because that is how an item or a skill is told from a faction. So a
*faction* named with an unmatched `[` is still not recognised. Leave it — removing that guard lets
the greedy faction scan swallow the item list, which is the failure `ah-w544.1` added it to prevent.

## Increments

**1. Matching the brackets.**
Failing test: `finds_the_brackets_that_never_close` in `scan.rs`'s `mod tests`.
`unmatched_brackets("Smiley :( (100)")` is the index of the first `(` and nothing else;
`unmatched_brackets("Bob [x (100)")` is the index of the `[`;
`unmatched_brackets("Three of Five (793)")` is empty;
`unmatched_brackets("Smiley :) (100)")` is the index of the stray `)`.
No caller changes this increment.

**2. The fallback.**
Failing test: `reads_a_name_containing_an_unclosed_bracket` —
`split_leading_id("Smiley :( (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN]")` is
`Some(("Smiley :(", "100", "Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN]"))`, and
`split_leading_id("Bob [x (100), Wanderers (29)")` is `Some(("Bob [x", "100", "Wanderers (29)"))`.
Then `an_unclosed_bracket_does_not_change_a_line_that_already_read` — the four rows of the *Context*
table that already work, asserted unchanged, which is what proves the first scan is untouched.

**3. The unit survives, end to end.**
Failing test: `keeps_a_unit_whose_name_contains_an_unclosed_bracket` in `unit.rs`'s `mod tests`.
`parse_unit("* Smiley :( (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN].", true, "1:7,53", None)` is `Some`,
with `name == "Smiley :("`, `unit_id == "100"`, `faction_name == Some("Wanderers")` and `men == 10`.
A second case for the square bracket, and a third pinning the faction: a unit whose *faction* name
carries an unclosed `(` is read.
**No production code changes in this increment** — it exists to prove increment 2 reached the caller,
and if it fails, the fault is in increment 2.

**4. It no longer reaches the unreadable-lines panel.**
Failing test: `a_name_with_an_unclosed_bracket_is_no_longer_unreadable` in `report/mod.rs`'s
`mod tests`. Parse a small report containing such a unit and assert both that the unit is present
**and** that `parsed.unreadable_lines` is empty. `ah-w544.2` shipped that field; this is the test
that ties the two beads together, and it is the one a reader will most want to see.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `finds_the_brackets_that_never_close` | `scan.rs` | the matcher, both kinds, and the empty case |
| `reads_a_name_containing_an_unclosed_bracket` | `scan.rs` | the fix |
| `an_unclosed_bracket_does_not_change_a_line_that_already_read` | `scan.rs` | that nothing else moved |
| `keeps_a_unit_whose_name_contains_an_unclosed_bracket` | `unit.rs` | the unit, its faction and its men survive |
| `a_name_with_an_unclosed_bracket_is_no_longer_unreadable` | `report/mod.rs` | the panel stops listing it |

Existing suites that are the real regression net, all reading the whole committed corpus:
`parse_real_reports`, `corpus_errors`, `unwrap_real_report`, `unit_composition`, `merge_reports`.

**`ah-w544.2` added `every_committed_report_is_read_completely`** to `parse_real_reports`, asserting
every committed fixture yields zero unreadable lines. That is now the sharpest possible check that
this bead breaks nothing: if the fallback ever fires wrongly on a real report, a unit changes and
that test or `parse_real_reports`' hand-counted figures will say so.

No new `.rep` fixture: `crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs` names every file on disk and
`every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` fails when the two disagree (ah-v2l), and an inline line does
this job.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** Nothing here is visible except that a unit which used to vanish now appears, which is the
only correct outcome and was never in question. No string is added or changed, and the
*Lines that could not be read* panel needs no work — it simply stops having this line to list.

The two decisions the navigator did take about this bead were about **scope and rank**, not
interface, and are recorded in *Context*: square brackets folded into the same bead, and the
priority moved from P1 to P2 once the symptom turned out to be an announced loss rather than silent
corruption.

## Out of scope

- **`split_top_level`, `next_top_level_field` and `split_trailing_id`.** Unchanged. They have the
  same depth counter and the same theoretical weakness, but no reported loss goes through them once
  `split_leading_id` recovers the identifier, and widening the change widens the regression surface
  against the corpus for no evidence.
- **A faction whose name contains an unclosed `[`.** Still unrecognised, by the deliberate guard at
  `unit.rs:167` — see *Files to change*.
- **`parse_item_amount`, `parse_skill`, `parse_settlement`.** All use `rfind`/`find` on a single
  bracket pair and have no depth counter, so this class does not reach them.
- **Deciding what a genuinely ambiguous name means.** `Legion (2), Bob (100)` is a name that
  contains its own parenthesised number; the leftmost group wins, as it does today. Not this bead's
  question and not changed by it.
- **Anything in the shells.** This is entirely inside `crates/core`; no TypeScript is regenerated,
  because no type changes.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm run check:fast
```

Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking:

1. `git diff` touches `crates/core/src/report/scan.rs` and **nothing else** outside test modules.
2. `parse_real_reports` and `corpus_errors` pass with no committed file regenerated — in particular
   `docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md` is **unedited**.
3. The four rows of the *Context* table behave as that table says.

Nothing here needs a human to look at anything.

**Before any of it**, spend ten minutes on the open question in *Context*: check the Atlantis rules
at https://atlantis-pbem.com/rules for whether a unit name may contain a parenthesis. If it plainly
cannot, stop, say so on the bead, and let the navigator decide whether to close it — building a fix
for an unreachable input is worse than not building one.

## Known traps

- **`depth <= 0`, not `depth == 0`.** Both existing scanners use it and it is what makes an unmatched
  *closing* bracket harmless today. Increment 2's second test pins that; if you find yourself
  changing the comparison, you are fixing the wrong half of this bug.
- **`(` and `[` are interchangeable to the existing scanners** — `'(' | '['` increments and
  `')' | ']'` decrements, so `[x)` balances. `unmatched_brackets` must match that convention exactly.
  Making it type-aware is more correct in the abstract and would make it disagree with
  `split_top_level` about the same string, which is worse.
- **The corpus is the net, not the unit tests.** `parse_real_reports` and `corpus_errors` read every
  committed report. `corpus_errors` compares against a committed generated table; if it goes red,
  **stop and work out why** rather than running `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1`. This bead should
  change no real report's parse at all — every committed fixture is well-formed, so the fallback
  should never fire on one.
- **This bead's description predates the fix that changed its symptom.** The notes carry the
  correction and the verified behaviour table. If the description and the notes disagree, the notes
  are right.
- The project traps file (`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`) is about the web and native suites; none of its
  entries touch this bead, which is Rust-only.
notes:
Xavier 2026-08-22, CORRECTION after ah-w544.1 (#561) and ah-w544.2 (#563) merged.

This bead was filed while ah-w544.1 was still being planned, and describes the OLD behaviour. Both have now shipped and the symptom has changed:

  BEFORE (split_trailing_id, rfind): an unmatched opening bracket meant nothing split, and the LAST parenthesised number won - so the unit was read with its FACTION's id and a mangled name. A silent mis-parse.

  NOW (split_leading_id, scan.rs): the depth counter never returns to zero, no candidate group is ever accepted, and the function returns None. parse_unit returns None and the unit is DROPPED.

Verified against the merged algorithm:
  "Smiley :( (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN]"  -> None      (dropped)
  "Smiley :) (100), Wanderers (29), 10 humans [HUMN]"  -> ok        (unmatched CLOSE still fine)
  "Bob [x (100), Wanderers (29)"                       -> None      (unmatched [ also drops - not previously noted)

Two consequences:

1. It is no longer silent. ah-w544.2 shipped the "Lines that could not be read" panel, and a `*` or `-` line that parse_unit rejects is exactly what it lists - so the player is now shown the raw line and told nothing on it reached the map. The bead's claim that the panel "will not even detect it" was true when filed and is now false.

2. It is no longer data CORRUPTION, it is data LOSS that announces itself. Strictly better, and a good deal less urgent than when the navigator ranked it P1 on the mis-parse framing.

Still a real bug: a unit with a legitimate name is lost from the player's own report. The fix direction is unchanged - a re-scan treating an unmatched '(' as a literal, or a depth clamp with a fallback - and it should cover an unmatched '[' too.

Still unknown, and worth settling before building: whether the engine permits parentheses in player-chosen names at all.

title: Monthly upkeep counts against a unit's Silver, switchable in Settings
description:
Split from ah-1wcw. Depends on ah-1wcw.1.

The navigator's words: "It should be configurable if upkeep is to be included in the calculation."

Two parts, and the second is the user-facing one:
- model upkeep at all, which the codebase does not do anywhere today
- a setting deciding whether it counts toward the Silver column's balance, which is a navigator decision: where the setting lives, what it is called, and what the default is.

Worth settling with them whether "configurable" means a global setting (Settings > Global, where ah-l9mp put the display preferences) or something per-unit.
design:
## Context

The last child of `ah-1wcw`, and the one the navigator's original words singled out: *"It should be
configurable if upkeep is to be included in the calculation."*

Every character owes a maintenance fee each month - **10 silver for an ordinary character, 50 for a
leader** - and a unit that ends the month without it has a one-in-three chance of starving. Nothing
