title: A Silver column showing what each unit will have left at month end
description:
First child of ah-1wcw, split so the navigator sees a real number early rather than after the whole economy lands.

## Why this shape
ah-1wcw asks for a Silver column computing "all probable incomes and expenses". Checked before filing: there is NO upkeep, maintenance or starvation modelling anywhere in the codebase, and no income or expense notion at all - the only silver arithmetic is crates/core/src/trade.rs, which computes carrying margins, a different question. So the epic BUILDS an economic model rather than surfacing one.

This child builds the SEAM and proves it with one or two sources, so every later child is an addition rather than a redesign:

- the column itself in units-in-hex, its width, its place in the order, and how it reads
- the negative-balance warning the navigator asked for
- ONE OR TWO income sources modelled end to end - taxing and work are the obvious pair: both are ordered explicitly (TAX, WORK), both have a rate the region reports, and neither needs a market
- a number the navigator can check against their own turn by hand

## Deliberately NOT here
Selling, buying, receiving, giving, entertainment, magic and studying (ah-1wcw.2 and .3), and upkeep with its configurability (ah-1wcw.4). Each is its own rule with its own edge cases.

## For the planner
The column is user-facing: its heading, its format (is a negative shown as -12 or (12)?), where it sits by default, and whether the warning is a colour, an icon or a problems-panel line are all the navigator's. The units table is resizable and reorderable (ah-1owr.2, ah-1owr.3) and DEFAULT_COLUMN_SHARES promises "a player who never drags must see no difference at all" - so adding a column has to be weighed against that promise.
design:
## Context The units-in-hex table says what every unit is, holds and has been told to do, but nothing anywhere says whether a unit is paying for itself. This bead adds a tenth column, **Silver**, showing what each of your own units is expected to hold when the month ends: what it holds now, plus what its orders earn, less what they spend. It is the first child of epic `ah-1wcw`, and it exists to build **the seam** rather than the whole economy. Three sources are modelled end to end - `TAX`, `WORK` and `STUDY`. Selling, buying, receiving, giving, entertainment and magic follow in `ah-1wcw.2` and `ah-1wcw.3`; upkeep and its setting in `ah-1wcw.4`. Each of those is another term in the same arithmetic, added to one function. **Two things the epic's own description gets wrong, discovered while planning, that change the shape of this work:** 1. The epic says "there is no income or expense notion at all". There is. `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` already carries a per-unit, per-tag silver ledger built from a hex's orders (`Ledger` at `semantics.rs:528`, `ledger_for` at `semantics.rs:547`), which already models `TAX` (`TAX_PER_MAN = 50` at `semantics.rs:43`, capped by `region.tax_base`), `CLAIM`, `BUY`, `SELL`, `STUDY`, `CAST`, `GIVE` and `TAKE`, and already carries a `doubted` set for the "cannot be priced honestly" case. What it does **not** model is `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN`, deliberately - see *Known traps*. 2. The epic assumes a new advisory check. **This bead adds none.** The warning the navigator asked for ("if negative, this should also be a warning") is already `not-enough-silver`: it counts what a unit holds, what its orders earn and spend, and pools the result across every same-faction unit in the hex flagged `sharing`, exactly as the engine's `GetSharedNum` rule does (`report_shortfalls`, `semantics.rs:1071`). It is on by default and in the Resources group of Settings -> Warnings. The number was missing; the warning was not. **Blocks `ah-1wcw.2`, `.3` and `.4`.** All three are written against the seam this bead creates, so its public surface below is a promise they will be planned against. ## Files to change, and what to reuse ### The arithmetic: a new pure module in the Rust core **New file `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`**, registered in `crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs` beside the existing `pub mod semantics;`. Pure arithmetic over values, with no dependency on `semantics.rs`'s private `Hex`/`Ordered` types, so it is unit-testable without building a report. ```rust /// What one unit's month is expected to do to its silver. /// /// Every field is silver. `None` anywhere means a term could not be priced and the whole forecast /// is untrustworthy - never a number that might be wrong. See `SilverDoubt`. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct UnitSilver { pub unit_id: String, pub region_id: String, /// Silver the unit holds now, from its `SILV` item. Always known. pub held: i64, /// What this month's orders are expected to earn. `None` when a term could not be priced. pub income: Option, /// What this month's orders are expected to spend. `None` when a term could not be priced. pub expense: Option, /// `held + income - expense`, or `None` when either side is `None`. pub at_month_end: Option, /// Why a term could not be priced, for the hover to explain. `None` when nothing was doubted. pub doubt: Option, } /// Why a unit's month could not be priced. One variant per sentence the interface shows. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))] #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")] pub enum SilverDoubt { /// `TAX` where the report stated no tax base for the region. UnknownTaxBase, /// A headcount that is itself a guess, so nothing per-man can be multiplied out. EstimatedMen, /// `STUDY` of a skill the ruleset prices nowhere, or no ruleset at all. UnpricedSkill, } /// Everything about the region that the arithmetic needs, lifted out so the function takes values. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)] pub struct RegionWages { pub tax_base: Option, /// The region's wage rate in hundredths of a silver, parsed from `ReportRegion::wages`. pub wage_centis: Option, pub max_wages: Option, } /// The wage rate the report prints, as hundredths of a silver. /// /// `ReportRegion::wages` is a *string* the parser stores verbatim - `"$24.1"`, `"$0"`, `"$12.0"` /// (`crates/core/src/report/region.rs:180-186`) - so it has to be read here rather than used. /// Hundredths rather than a float because the forecast is compared against zero to decide whether /// a cell is red, and a float makes that comparison depend on rounding. /// /// Returns `None` for anything it cannot read, which the caller treats as "this region pays no /// wages" rather than as doubt: a region with no wages line genuinely pays none. #[must_use] pub fn parse_wage_centis(wages: Option<&str>) -> Option; /// What one unit's month does to its silver. /// /// `intents` is the unit's orders exactly as `semantics` already holds them - `PlacedIntent` is /// public (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:106`), so the slice is passed straight through with /// no clone on a path that runs per keystroke. `held`, `men` and `men_estimated` come straight off /// the report unit; `held` is 0 for a unit carrying no `SILV` item. #[must_use] pub fn forecast_unit( unit_id: &str, region_id: &str, held: i64, men: i64, men_estimated: bool, region: RegionWages, intents: &[PlacedIntent], ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>, ) -> UnitSilver; ``` **Which side goes `None`, and which doubt wins.** `income` and `expense` are doubted independently, so the hover can show `?` against the side that is actually unknown; `at_month_end` is `None` when either is. When more than one term is doubted, `doubt` reports the **first match in this order**, which is also the order of increasing scope: | Doubt | `income` | `expense` | |---|---|---| | `EstimatedMen` | `None` | `None` | | `UnknownTaxBase` | `None` | unaffected | | `UnpricedSkill` | unaffected | `None` | `EstimatedMen` is checked first and short-circuits: nothing per-man can be multiplied out, so neither side survives. The three rules `forecast_unit` implements, and where each comes from: | Order | Rule | Source to copy | |---|---|---| | `TAX` | `men * 50`, capped at `region.tax_base`. No tax base at all -> `UnknownTaxBase`. | `semantics.rs:704-713`, `TAX_PER_MAN` at `:43` | | `WORK` | `floor(men * wage_centis / 100)`, capped at `max_wages`. No wage -> earns 0, no doubt. | new; `ReportRegion::wages`/`max_wages`, `crates/core/src/report/model.rs:209-211` | | `STUDY` | `ruleset.find_skill(skill).cost * men`. Unpriced or no ruleset -> `UnpricedSkill`. | `fn study`, `semantics.rs:851-879` - copy its posture exactly | `men_estimated` doubts the whole forecast before any of the above, exactly as `study` does at `semantics.rs:863`: a headcount that is a guess cannot multiply anything out. **Rounding is always downward** (`floor`), and deliberately: a forecast that overstates income is the dangerous direction for a column whose negatives are what a player acts on. ### Carrying it out of the core `semantics.rs` already walks every region and every own unit once per validation, on a path the module's own comment says runs "on every keystroke once typing settles" (`crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs:53-55`). Do not walk it a second time. **In `semantics.rs`:** ```rust /// A whole turn read once: everything wrong with it, and what its units' months cost. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct TurnReview { pub findings: Vec, pub silver: Vec, } /// Checks a whole turn's orders against the report they were written for, and forecasts each /// unit's silver in the same pass. #[must_use] pub fn review_turn( report: &ParsedReport, source: &str, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>, options: CheckOptions, ) -> TurnReview; ``` **`check_turn` keeps its exact signature and becomes a one-line wrapper** - `review_turn(report, source, ruleset, options).findings`. That is load-bearing: `check_turn` has about thirty call sites in `semantics.rs`'s own tests and seven in `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`, and changing its return type would churn all of them for nothing. Inside `review_turn`, the forecast is collected in the existing `for region in &report.regions` loop (`semantics.rs:226-251`), from `hex.units` - which `Hex::read` has already filtered to `unit.own` (`semantics.rs:369-383`), so foreign units produce no forecast and their cell is blank for free. Use `Ordered::holding(SILVER)` (`semantics.rs:481`) for `held`, and `ordered.intents.iter().map(|placed| &placed.intent)` for the intents. **In `crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs`:** `validate_turn` (`:57-77`) calls `review_turn` instead of `check_turn` and puts the forecast on the result. **In `crates/core/src/lib.rs:93-97`:** ```rust pub struct OrderValidationResult { pub diagnostics: Vec, /// One entry per own unit the report shows, whether or not it has orders. `ah-1wcw.1`. #[serde(default)] pub silver: Vec, } ``` `#[serde(default)]` so a cached or older payload deserialises to an empty list rather than failing. `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:497-506` and `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:554-563` serialise this struct whole and need **no signature change** - confirm by reading them, do not assume. ### Generated bindings `UnitSilver`, `SilverDoubt` and the extended `OrderValidationResult` are ts-rs exports. Regenerate and commit: ``` ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core ``` Then export the two new types from `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`, beside the existing `export type { OrderValidationResult } from "./generated/OrderValidationResult";` at `:41`. ### The column **`packages/shared/src/unitTable.ts`:** - `UNIT_COLUMNS` (`:42-54`) gains `"silver"` **last**, after `"longOrder"`. - `COLUMN_LABELS` (`:63-72`) gains `silver: "Silver"`. This is also what a screen reader hears for the resize and reorder handles, which read the same map (`ColumnSplitter.tsx:192`, `ColumnReorderHandle.tsx:76,157`). - `SortColumn` (`:34`) gains `| "silver"`, and `valueOf` (`:172-192`) a `case "silver":`. That `switch` has no `default`, so the compiler will demand it. - `DEFAULT_COLUMN_SHARES` (`:306-316`) gains `silver: 96 / NOMINAL_TABLE_PX` and **`NOMINAL_TABLE_PX` becomes `1440`** (`:304`). The nine current numerators sum to exactly 1344; 96 more is 1440. `unitTable.test.ts:371` asserts the shares sum to one and will catch any slip. Update the doc comment's list of widths at `:298-302` to include `silver 96`. **Sorting.** Return `at_month_end` from `valueOf`, i.e. `number | null`. **`null` already sorts last in either direction** without any work: `compareValues` (`unitTable.ts:155-169`) returns `{ settled: 1 }` for a null left-hand side, and `sortUnits` (`:276`) applies `direction` only to `compare`, never to `settled`. So a doubted forecast and a foreign unit both fall to the bottom whichever way the column is sorted. Do not invent a sentinel number. Both `valueOf` (`:172-178`) and `sortUnits` (`:257-263`) need the figures threaded in. `sortUnits` already takes its extras as trailing defaulted parameters, so append one in the same shape: ```ts /** Each own unit's forecast silver at month end, for the column that sorts on it. */ silver: ReadonlyMap = new Map() ``` `UnitTableDock` builds that map **only when `sort.column === "silver"`**, mirroring what it already does for long orders at `:132-137`, so an unsorted table pays nothing for it. **`packages/shared/src/workspace/UnitTableDock.tsx`:** - `SORTABLE_COLUMNS` (`:52-59`) gains `"silver"`. - **Two** new optional props beside `getLongOrder` (`:83`) - the same injection pattern, and for the same reason: neither the forecast nor the diagnostics are on `ReportUnit`. ```ts /** Each own unit's silver forecast, or null where there is none. `ah-1wcw.1`. */ getSilver?: (unitId: string) => UnitSilver | null; /** The unit-anchored `not-enough-silver` findings, by unit id. */ silverWarnings?: ReadonlySet; /** Selects a unit and opens its orders. Absent means the cell is not clickable. */ onSelectUnit?: (unitId: string) => void; ``` `UnitTableDock` has **no** `onSelectUnit` prop today (checked: zero occurrences in the file), so this is a new one, optional so the component's existing tests keep constructing it unchanged. - `cellsByColumn` (`:709-807`) gains a `silver` entry rendering the cell described under *User-facing decisions*. **Only a cell carrying the warning is a ` ``` `SeverityMark` (`primitives.tsx:31-43`) already hides the glyph from assistive technology and announces the word "warning" beside it. **`UNIT_LINK_CLASS` is currently a private `const` at `primitives.tsx:58` - export it** in the same edit; it is the class `ProblemWho` uses at `:96` and `:165`, and a second copy of it is exactly the drift to avoid. **Do not write a new glyph or a new `aria-label`** - see *Known traps* on `ah-bkjd`. - `const COLUMNS = UNIT_COLUMNS.length;` (`:49`) is used for spacer `colSpan` and needs no change, but check the spacer rows still span the full table after the column is added. **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`:** - `validated` (`:330`) becomes `{ text, diagnostics, silver }`; both `setValidated` call sites (`:2062`, `:2079`) update. `ValidatedOrders` is declared at `packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts:120` and gains `silver: UnitSilver[]`. - A `getSilver` callback beside `getLongOrder` (`:308-311`), memoised on `validated.silver` and built through a `Map` so the lookup is not linear per row. - `silverWarnings` is built from `validated.diagnostics`: the ids of every diagnostic whose `code === "not-enough-silver"` **and** whose `unitId` is not null. Memoise it on `validated.diagnostics` beside `problemsByHex` (`:2103`). - All three passed to `` at `:3376-3380`, with `onSelectUnit={(unitId) => goToUnit(unitId, null)}` - the same call `RegionPanel` is already given at `:3256`. `goToUnit` is declared at `:727`. ### The hover **`packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts`** - `UnitSummary` (`:27-33`) gains: ```ts /** The silver section of the panel: the working, and one line explaining it where it needs one. */ export type SilverSummary = { rows: TooltipEntry[]; note: string | null }; ``` and `summariseUnit` (`:47`) takes a second argument `silver: UnitSilver | null` and returns `silver: SilverSummary | null` - `null` when there is no forecast, which is every foreign unit. **All the wording lives in this pure function**, which is what makes it testable; see *Known traps* on why it must not live in the component. **`packages/shared/src/workspace/UnitTooltip.tsx`** gains a third `
` after Items, rendering `rows` through the existing `Row` primitive and the note as a dim line. The component takes the forecast as a prop; `UnitTableDock.tsx:490` passes it from `getSilver`. ## Increments Each opens with the named failing test. Run `pnpm run check:fast` at the end of every one. **1. The wage string becomes a number.** Failing test: `parses_the_wage_the_report_prints` in `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`, asserting `parse_wage_centis(Some("$24.1")) == Some(2410)`, `Some("$0") == Some(0)`, `Some("$12.0") == Some(1200)`, and that `None`, `""` and `"nonsense"` all give `None`. **2. One unit's month, priced.** Failing test: `a_taxing_unit_earns_fifty_a_man` in the same module - eight men, no tax base limit, `income == Some(400)`. Then, in the same increment and each as its own test: `a_taxing_unit_is_capped_by_the_regions_tax_base`, `a_taxing_unit_with_no_tax_base_is_doubted` (`doubt == Some(SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase)`), `a_working_unit_earns_the_regions_wage` (12 men at `$12.0` -> 144), `a_working_unit_is_capped_by_the_regions_maximum`, `a_working_unit_in_a_hex_with_no_wages_earns_nothing` (income `Some(0)`, `doubt` `None`), `a_fractional_wage_rounds_down` (3 men at `$12.5` -> 37, not 38), `a_studying_unit_pays_the_rulesets_cost_per_man`, `a_studying_unit_the_ruleset_cannot_price_is_doubted`, `a_unit_whose_headcount_is_a_guess_is_doubted`, `a_unit_with_no_orders_ends_the_month_holding_what_it_started_with`. **3. The forecast rides out of the core with the findings.** Failing test: `a_review_forecasts_every_own_unit` in `semantics.rs`'s test module - a two-unit hex, one own and one foreign, asserting `review_turn(...).silver` has exactly one entry and that `check_turn` still returns what it returned before. Then extend `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` with `the_committed_turn_forecasts_every_own_unit_and_none_of_the_others`, asserting 27 entries - the number of own unit blocks in that template - and that the `EXPECTED` finding counts are **unchanged**, which is the claim that this bead adds no warning. **4. The column exists and sorts.** Failing test: `the_table_has_a_silver_column` in `packages/shared/src/unitTable.test.ts`, asserting `UNIT_COLUMNS` ends with `"silver"`, `COLUMN_LABELS.silver === "Silver"`, and that the default shares still sum to one. Then `sorts_by_silver_with_unknown_forecasts_last`. **5. The cell reads as agreed.** Failing test: `a_unit_that_runs_out_shows_a_red_warned_figure` in `packages/shared/src/workspace/UnitTableDock.test.tsx`, and one test per row of the states table in *User-facing decisions*. These are `renderToStaticMarkup` tests - see *Known traps*. **6. The hover explains it.** Failing test: `the_silver_section_says_what_made_the_number` in `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts`, asserting the four rows and each of the four notes verbatim. Pure-function tests only. **7. The cell jumps to the unit.** Failing test: a smoke spec `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` - `silver column warns and jumps`: load the committed turn, find a unit with a `not-enough-silver` finding, click its Silver cell, assert the orders pane shows that unit. ## The test plan | Suite | What it pins | |---|---| | `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` | every rule in increments 1-3, and the ts-rs bindings | | `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` | 27 forecasts on the real turn, and **no change** to the `EXPECTED` finding counts | | `pnpm vitest packages/shared` | columns, sorting, share arithmetic, cell markup, hover wording | | `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` | the column appears, sorts, and its cell jumps to the unit | Must run before the PR: `pnpm run check:fast`. Run `pnpm run test:smoke` by hand for increment 7 - CI gates it, but this bead adds a smoke spec and a red one is worth finding locally. **No fixture counts change.** If `EXPECTED` in `validate_real_orders.rs` needs a new row, something has gone wrong: this bead emits no findings. Say so rather than editing the table. ## User-facing decisions Every decision below was the navigator's, taken during planning on 2026-08-22, most of them against measurements of the committed turn-71 template. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-1wcw.1-silver-column.html`. **The column shows an end-of-month amount, not a change.** Asked as "one number, working on hover" (A) / "working on the face of it" (B) / "a warning, not just a red number" (C); **C chosen**. B was rejected as too wide - about 150px against Long order's 144 - and for making the column stop scanning as a stack of aligned numbers. A was rejected for giving a surprising number nothing to act on. *Mid-planning the navigator added: "it also needs to count the silver the unit had to start with", which turned the figure from a signed delta into an amount.* **Heading: `Silver`.** Rejected: `Balance`, `Net silver`, `This month`, `At month end`, `Silver left`, `Projected silver`. It reads as the unit's silver, which - once the starting balance is counted - is what it now is. **Position: last, after `Long order`.** Rejected: after `Men` (pushes four columns right for everybody, and sits far from the order that explains the figure) and between `Structure` and `Long order`. Accepted cost: last is first to be clipped in a narrow dock. **Sortable, numerically.** Rejected: unsortable like Skills and Items; and making it the default sort, which would override the shipped default of name-ascending, own units first. **The cell, exactly:** | Situation | Cell | Colour | |---|---|---| | Forecast known, `at_month_end >= 0` | the figure, e.g. `800` | default ink | | Forecast known, `at_month_end < 0` | the figure, e.g. `-140` | red | | ...and this unit carries a `not-enough-silver` finding | `⚠ -140`, clickable | red | | Positive, but carries a `not-enough-silver` finding | `⚠ 44`, clickable | default ink | | Forecast unknown (`doubt` set) | `?` | dim | | Value is `0` | `0` | dim | | Foreign unit (no forecast) | empty | - | **Red and ⚠ mean different things, deliberately.** Red is this unit, counted on its own, ending below zero. ⚠ is the existing `not-enough-silver` finding, which pools across the hex's `sharing` units. Measured on turn 71: **17 of 27 units are red, and 0 carry ⚠** - most of that faction's mages hold no silver at all and are funded from a purse unit beside them. The navigator was shown this and chose to keep both signals ("column counts the unit alone, warning counts sharing"), over making both count sharing and over making both count the unit alone. **A ⚠ may appear on a positive figure.** The column counts what `WORK` earns; `not-enough-silver` deliberately does not, because wages are paid in the turn's last phase. Both are true about different moments. **Chosen: show the ⚠ anyway and explain it in the hover.** Rejected: suppressing the ⚠ on a positive figure (would hide a real finding and disagree with the Problems panel), and dropping `WORK` income from the column (would leave a working unit showing no income at all). **Clicking a warned cell selects the unit and opens its orders** - `goToUnit(unitId, null)`. Rejected: not clickable, and select-without-opening. **No new advisory code, no new Settings entry.** Asked directly once the overlap with `not-enough-silver` was found; **chosen: no second code**. Rejected: adding `silver-runs-out` anyway, and teaching `not-enough-silver` about wages (which would make it less correct). *Earlier in the interview the navigator chose a per-unit warning on by default over the planner's recommendation of off-by-default, and chose message and Settings wording for a new check. Those choices are superseded by the no-new-code decision above and must not be revived: the strings they named do not ship, because no new check ships.* **The hover.** A `Silver` section joins the panel the table already opens on row rest, after Skills and Items. Rejected: Silver first (reorders a panel people know, for every unit), and a separate panel on the Silver cell (two panels competing for one pointer, and rebuilds all the placement machinery for one cell - the planner initially and wrongly priced this as the cheap option). Four rows, labelled and quoted exactly: ``` Held now 60 In 0 Out 200 -------------------- At month end -140 ``` Then **one** note line, dim - the **first** row of this table that applies, and no more than one. These strings ship verbatim: | When | Line | |---|---| | red, but the hex's `sharing` units cover it | `Shared silver in this hex covers the shortfall.` | | `doubt == UnknownTaxBase` | `The report never said what this region's tax base is.` | | `doubt == UnpricedSkill` | `The ruleset does not say what studying this skill costs.` | | `doubt == EstimatedMen` | `This unit's headcount is an estimate, so its month cannot be priced.` | | `⚠` on a positive figure | `Wages arrive at the end of the month, too late to pay for this month's orders.` | | income and expense both `0` | `Nothing this unit is ordered to do moves silver.` | | none of the above | no line | A doubted row shows `?` in place of its figure, and `At month end` shows `?`. **The stored column order is discarded, silently, and that is accepted.** `columnOrderFromStorage` (`unitTable.ts:417-437`) rejects a stored order whole when its length no longer matches `UNIT_COLUMNS`, so every player who has ever dragged a column loses their order and gets the shipped one back. Widths survive, rescaled. The navigator was offered a fix (accept a short stored order and append the new columns), a one-time notice, and filing it separately, and **chose to accept the loss silently**. Do not fix it in this bead, and do not add a notice. ## Out of scope - **Every other silver source**: selling, buying, receiving, giving, entertainment, and magic that earns or costs. `ah-1wcw.2` and `ah-1wcw.3`. - **Upkeep**, and the setting deciding whether it counts. `ah-1wcw.4`. Nothing in this bead should anticipate that setting's shape. - **Any new advisory check, code, message or Settings toggle.** Settled above. - **Fixing the discarded column order.** Settled above. - **Contention between units.** `WORK` is capped at the region's `max_wages` per unit, and no attempt is made to divide that pool between the units drawing on it - we cannot see other factions' orders. Same for taxing against `tax_base`. - **A faction-wide total.** Discussed and not chosen; the column is per unit. - **Making the forecast available anywhere but the units table and its hover.** ## Validation ``` pnpm run check:fast cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core pnpm run test:smoke ``` Acceptance, each checkable by running or looking: 1. `bd show ah-1wcw.1` design's states table matches what the app draws for a loaded turn-71 report. 2. `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` passes with `EXPECTED` **unedited**. 3. The new test asserts exactly 27 forecasts for the committed turn. 4. `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` is unchanged - `git diff` on `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` is empty. 5. Loading the committed turn and opening a hex with studying mages shows red figures and **no** ⚠ on them, and the region panel shows no silver finding. 6. Sorting by Silver ascending puts the most negative unit first and `?` rows last. 7. Resting on a row shows the Silver section with the four rows and the right note. **Only a human can check** that the column reads well at a narrow dock width and that the hover panel does not become unwieldy - Psylocke's pass. ## Known traps - **Never ask for an effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** That package has no jsdom by decision (`ah-nass`): component tests render with `renderToStaticMarkup`, which runs no effects, attaches no refs and fires no timers. `UnitTooltip` is placed by a `useLayoutEffect` (`UnitTooltip.tsx:24-35`), so **its placement cannot be tested there**. That is exactly why all the hover wording is specified into `summariseUnit`, a pure function - test the strings there, and let the smoke suite cover that the panel appears at all. `packages/shared/src/testing/README.md` has the pattern. - **`ReportRegion::wages` is a `String`, not a number** - `"$24.1"`, stored verbatim including the `$` (`crates/core/src/report/region.rs:180-186`, `model.rs:209`). Wages are fractional in this ruleset. Parse it; never coerce it. - **`max_wages` is the region's whole pool, contended by other factions.** Capping a single unit at it is honest; dividing it is not, and must not be attempted. - **`not-enough-silver` counts `TAX` but not `WORK`**, on purpose: "Wages and takings from entertaining are paid in the last phase of the turn, after study has been paid for, so they can fund nothing this month" (`semantics.rs:731-733`). Do not "fix" this, and do not make the new forecast match it - the disagreement is specified behaviour here. - **In a hex with `sharing` units, `not-enough-silver` is anchored to the hex, not to a unit** (`report_shortfalls`, `semantics.rs:1071-1210`): `unit_id` is `None`, so no row gets a ⚠. This is deliberate - "blaming one of several would be as wrong as blaming the treasurer for holding the purse". Match a ⚠ to a row **only** on `diagnostic.unitId === unit.unitId`; never fall back to the region. - **`bd show --json` returns an array**, so the design field is `.[0].design`. - **`check_turn` must keep its signature.** About thirty test call sites depend on it; `review_turn` is the new entry point and `check_turn` the wrapper. - **`valueOf` in `unitTable.ts` has no `default` arm**, deliberately, so adding a `SortColumn` is a compile error until the case is written. Let it be. - **`DEFAULT_COLUMN_SHARES` numerators must sum to `NOMINAL_TABLE_PX`.** They currently sum to exactly 1344; `unitTable.test.ts:371` asserts the shares sum to one, so the divisor must move to 1440 in the same edit that adds the column. - **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a PWA run straight afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker. - **`vite preview` without `--strictPort`** silently serves somebody else's bundle. - **WebKit's driver answers `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a Chromium assertion on the Silver cell can pass while the native shell shows nothing. `native` is the job that tells you - and this column is the last one, so it is the one most likely to be clipped.

title: Nothing tells a player whether a unit is paying for itself this month
description:
The navigator's words, 2026-08-22:

  "In units in hex, I would like to have a columns for 'Silver'. This column
  shall calculate all probably incomes and expenses and calculate the
  difference. If negative, this should also be a warning. Incomes should be
  selling, receiving, taxing, magic, entertainment, work, etc. Expenses should
  be buying, studying, giving, magic, etc. It should be configurable if upkeep
  is to be included in the calculation."

## This builds an economic model; it does not surface one

Checked before filing, and worth knowing up front:

  - There is NO upkeep, maintenance or starvation modelling anywhere in the
    codebase. Zero hits across crates and packages.
  - There is no income or expense notion at all. The only silver arithmetic is
    crates/core/src/trade.rs, which computes margins for carrying goods between
    hexes -- a different question entirely.
  - The INPUTS are parsed and available: region wages ("Wages: $12.0 (Max:
    $300)"), entertainment, market buy/sell prices and quantities, skill study
    cost per man per month (SkillEntry.cost in movement/rules.rs), silver as an
    item (SILV), and "Unclaimed silver" from the report header.

So every ingredient exists and none of the cooking does.

## Almost certainly larger than one increment

Not splitting it here -- that is planning's call -- but the seams are visible,
and each source the navigator listed is its own calculation with its own rules
and its own test:

  income    selling, receiving (GIVE to this unit), taxing, magic,
            entertainment, work
  expense   buying, studying, giving, magic
  optional  upkeep, behind a setting

Taxing depends on the region's tax base and which men may tax; work is wages
times men against a regional maximum that other units also draw from;
entertainment draws on a shared regional pool; studying is cost per man per
month; giving and receiving are order-derived rather than report-derived. Some
of these are per-unit and some are contended between units in the same hex,
which is the hard part and worth settling early.

The word "probably" in the request is doing real work: these are predictions of
what the month will produce, not facts the report states.

## The two halves have established patterns to follow

THE COLUMN. Units-in-hex columns became data in ah-1owr.1, resizable in
ah-1owr.2 and reorderable in ah-1owr.3, all shipped in v0.10.0. A new column
follows that seam rather than inventing one.

THE WARNING. A negative balance raising a warning is a new advisory check, and
ah-dwk6 set the pattern: a message, an anchor line, a named code, expected
findings pinned in the committed turn-71 template, and its own toggle under
Settings -> Warnings. The upkeep switch the navigator asks for is a second
setting and may belong beside it.

## For the planner

Worth putting to the navigator early, because it shapes everything:

  - How exact must "probably" be? A best-effort estimate that is sometimes
    wrong is a different product from a conservative bound that is never
    optimistic -- and a silver warning that cries wolf is worse than none.
  - What happens where the app cannot know? A unit ordered to SELL into a market
    whose price the player has not seen, or taxing a hex whose tax base is
    unknown, has no honest number. Blank, a range, or an excluded term.
  - Does the column show the net difference only, or is the breakdown reachable?
    A single signed number is unarguable but unactionable when it surprises you.

title: A project using this fleet has nowhere to record what it has already paid for
description:
Split from ah-qled.10 (upstream cerebro#58 §3). Two things a consumer must supply and currently has nowhere to put.

## Traps that are pure atlantis-hud

skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:660-671 ("Traps this repository has already paid for") and skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:878-886 are four Playwright/PWA/WebKit/Vite facts each. In a shared submodule these are one project's scar tissue carried into every consumer's agent session.

**These should be EMPTY in cerebro and sourced from a consumer file** - <consumer>/.cerebro/traps.md, read at the top of Building - which also gives the retrospective loop somewhere to feed. That last part is the real prize: today a retrospective's "prevent by" has nowhere to land except a human's memory.

Note the path: .cerebro/ is the git-ignored personal directory. Consider whether traps are personal (ignored) or a fact every clone needs (tracked, beside cerebro-project.conf) - scripts/project-conf's own header argues the latter for anything every clone needs, and a trap the whole team has paid for is exactly that. Settle it in planning and say why.

## A consumer CLAUDE.md that cerebro requires but does not ship

cerebro currently REQUIRES the consumer to have written a section called "Four Eye Principle" by that exact name - skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:25-27, skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:672, CLAUDE.md:126-128 - with no template offered.

Ship templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md. And make those references say plainly that they mean the CONSUMER'S ROOT CLAUDE.md: from inside a submodule with two files of that name, "governs this repository" is ambiguous.
design:
## Context

Split from `ah-qled.10` by this planning session; upstream cerebro#58 §3.
**Worked in the cerebro submodule** (`.claude/cerebro/` = `rmstdope/cerebro`), plus one file in the
application. See *Known traps*.

Two things a project using this harness must supply and currently has nowhere to put.

**Traps.** `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:676-695` ("Traps this repository has already paid for")
and `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:878-886` carry hard-won facts. In a shared submodule some of those are
one project's scar tissue carried into every consumer's agent session.

**A required document nobody ships.** cerebro *requires* the consumer to have written a section
called **"Four Eye Principle"** by that exact name — `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:18,25`,
`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:672`, `CLAUDE.md:127` — and offers no template for it. A new consumer
discovers the requirement by an agent refusing to merge.

### A correction to the bead, which changes the work

The bead says the traps blocks *"should be **empty** in cerebro and sourced from a consumer file"*.
**They should not be empty.** Read at HEAD, most of `implement-bead`'s block is already written
generically and is genuinely universal:

- *"Where two of a project's suites build the same artefact differently, running them in the wrong
  order fails the second one for a reason that is not a defect."*
- *"A leftover preview server. Without `CI=1`, a browser runner reuses an existing server — including
  your own dying one from the previous run."* (Cost: a "65 passed" and a "40 passed" run of a
  138-test suite.)
- *"`--` forwarded into a test runner … looks exactly like a hang rather than a mistake."*
- *"A stale lease is not an abandoned agent."*
- *"A CI wait against a conflicted head."*

Only two entries are actually this project's: **WebKit's driver** answering `""` for clipped text,
and the job named **`native`**. `plan-bead:878-886` is the opposite — its four examples are all
this project's (WebKit, the PWA/service-worker rebuild, a persisted setting's default, `vite preview
--strictPort`) and it says so in its own words: *"Examples this repository has actually paid for"*.

**So the work is a split, not a deletion.** Emptying the blocks would throw away knowledge every
consumer needs, and would be a bigger regression than the coupling it fixes.

### Two facts settled by reading rather than by asking

**The traps file is tracked, not under `.cerebro/`.** The bead leaves this open. `.cerebro/` is
git-ignored (`.gitignore:49`), and `scripts/project-conf`'s own header gives the rule:

> `.cerebro/models.conf` is a personal preference and rightly git-ignored; how a project installs
> itself and what its gate is called are facts EVERY clone needs. A file under the ignored
> `.cerebro/` vanishes on a fresh clone, and every new machine then silently skips the step.

A trap the whole team has already paid for is exactly such a fact. So: **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**,
tracked, beside `cerebro-project.conf` and `cerebro-roster`.

**The feed is uniform and large.** Every one of the **138** retrospectives in this repository has a
`**Prevent by.**` section — 138 of 138. That is what makes the curation question real: the supply is
not the problem, the filter is.

## Files to change and what to reuse

In cerebro (`.claude/cerebro/`):

- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:676-695`** — keep the universal traps, move the two
  project-specific ones out, add the read.
- **`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:878-886`** — all four examples are this project's; the section keeps
  its *instruction* and loses its examples, and gains the read.
- **`agents/architect.md`** — Forge gains one output. Its findings section is at line ~21 and its
  per-session procedure at ~52; the report template is at ~123.
- **New: `templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md`.**
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:18,25`, `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:672`, `CLAUDE.md:127`** — say
  plainly that they mean the **consumer's root** `CLAUDE.md`, and point at the template.
- **New or extended: `tests/consumer-traps.sh`**, or a case in an existing suite.

In the application:

- **New: `.claude/cerebro-traps.md`** — this project's own two traps, plus `plan-bead`'s four.

Reuse:

- **`scripts/project-conf`'s header** — the tracked-versus-ignored rule, quoted above. Do not
  re-derive it.
- **`.claude/cerebro-roster`'s precedent** (`ah-qled.5.1`, merged) — a tracked consumer file at
  `.claude/cerebro-<thing>`, found by path arithmetic from the script's own location, absent meaning
  a documented fallback. **Read `scripts/roster:68-110` before deciding how the traps file is
  found.**
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:422`'s idiom** — the established way for prose to tell an agent
  to read a project fact: *"run `.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf prewarm` and run what it
  names, now."*

## Increments

### 1 — Split the traps

**`implement-bead`'s block keeps every universal entry, in place and unedited.** Move out only:

- the **WebKit** entry (`WebKit's driver answers "" for text it considers clipped … native is the
  job that tells you`), which names both a browser engine and a job this project has;
- any other entry naming a tool, job or path a consumer need not have. **Judge each one on that
  test, not on this list** — the list is what one reading found.

**`plan-bead`'s section keeps its instruction and loses its examples.** The instruction —
*"The last section is where hard-won knowledge goes, and it is worth real effort … If the bead
touches one of those, say so and say what to do about it"* — is the valuable part and is already
generic. The four examples after *"Examples this repository has actually paid for:"* go.

Both sections then end with the read, in the house idiom:

> Read `<consumer>/.claude/cerebro-traps.md` if it exists — the traps this project has already paid
> for. It is a list of facts, not rules: if the bead touches one, say so and say what to do about it.

**Absent is an ordinary state**, not an error. A consumer with no traps file has paid for nothing
yet, which is where every project starts.

### 2 — The consumer's file

In the application, `.claude/cerebro-traps.md`, carrying what increment 1 moved out plus
`plan-bead`'s four:

- WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped, so a Chromium-only assertion passes
  while the native shell is broken — `native` is the job that tells you.
- The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled, so a PWA run straight
  afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker.
- A persisted setting's old default must be migrated rather than clamped.
- `vite preview` without `--strictPort` silently serves somebody else's bundle.

**Copy the wording across rather than rewriting it.** These sentences were paid for; a paraphrase
loses the specificity that makes them useful.

A header saying what the file is, who adds to it, and that it is tracked on purpose.

### 3 — Forge proposes; the navigator decides

The navigator chose **A**: Forge proposes a traps entry during its sweep, and nothing lands without
them.

Forge already reads every new retrospective (`agents/architect.md:79`, and it delegates the reading
to subagents at :90-95 because the corpus is too large for one context). It gains **one more output**,
and the shape must match what is already there:

- **Only from a retrospective's `**Prevent by.**`**, and only when that names something **the next
  agent could act on before starting** — not a fix, not a principle. This is the same bar Forge
  already applies to findings (`:21-35`: a cost already being paid, never a bare principle).
- **Never files it and never edits the file.** Forge *"never edits code and never sets a priority
  itself"*; adding to a tracked file is the same kind of act. It **proposes**, in its report, quoting
  the retrospective and naming its section — and the navigator says yes or no.
- **A proposal is not a finding.** It goes in a section of its own in the report so it cannot be
  mistaken for a bead being filed. Match the existing report template at `:123-127`.
- **Nothing to propose is the normal case** and must be silent. 138 of 138 retrospectives have a
  `Prevent by`; a sweep that proposes one every time is a sweep nobody reads. Say this in Forge's own
  file, with the number, so the bar is calibrated rather than left to taste.

### 4 — `templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md`

The navigator chose **ii**: a working default meant to be edited, not a form to fill in.

Its "Four Eye Principle" section, generalised from this project's:

> ## Four Eye Principle
>
> Nothing merges unreviewed and nothing merges red.
>
> For a change built by an agent, an automated reviewer counts as the second pair of eyes when all of
> these hold: exactly one review is requested as the pull request opens; every comment it leaves is
> answered, by a change or by a posted reply saying why not; and every check is green.
>
> Everything else needs a person.

Plus the other sections cerebro reads or assumes, each as a working default with a line saying what
the fleet does with it. **Derive that list from the files rather than from memory**: grep the skills
and agents for references to the consumer's `CLAUDE.md` and include every section named.

**Say at the top that it is a starting point and expected to be edited.** The navigator accepted that
a default policy is one people may adopt without deciding; the mitigation is that the document says
so about itself.

### 5 — Say which `CLAUDE.md` is meant

`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:18,25`, `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:672` and `CLAUDE.md:127` say
"CLAUDE.md's Four Eye Principle". **From inside a submodule with two files of that name, that is
ambiguous** — and an agent reading cerebro's own `CLAUDE.md` finds no such section.

Each becomes "the **consumer's root** `CLAUDE.md`", and at least one of them points at
`templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md` so a project without one knows where to start.

### 6 — A test

The read is prose and cannot be tested. What can:

- `templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md` **exists and contains a `## Four Eye Principle` heading** — the
  exact string the skills require. If the template and the requirement ever disagree, this is what
  says so.
- Every skill or agent that names the required section **also names it as the consumer's root file**
  — grep for the phrase and assert none of the hits is bare.

Put these wherever the existing frontmatter-and-file assertions live (`tests/launchers.sh` has a
cluster of them near line 598), or a new `tests/consumer-contract.sh`. Either is fine; **do not add a
fifth wide `cp -R` fixture** — these assertions read cerebro's own files and need no consumer.

## The test plan

cerebro's suites are shell: `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done`. CI runs all of them plus ERT
on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1. Increment 6's assertions are the only new ones and are written first.

Most of this bead is prose, and the real verification is a **read-through as a consumer with no traps
file**: every step still actionable, nothing pointing at a file that does not exist, nothing telling
the reader about WebKit.

`pnpm run check:fast` before the application PR.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-22 (`docs/ui/consumer-traps.html`). **Decided; raise
disagreements through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Who decides what goes in the consumer's traps file? | **A — Forge proposes in its sweep, the navigator accepts or declines.** Curated by the one role that reads the whole corpus, and nothing lands unasked |
| 2 | What does `templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md` contain? | **ii — a working default meant to be edited.** It works on day one and makes the fleet's expectations visible, rather than being a form to fill in |

**Option B (the implementer appends its own) was declined**, and the reason constrains increment 3:
138 of 138 retrospectives have a `Prevent by`, so an implementer appending its own would add noise
most days — and an implementer is the worst judge of whether its own pain generalises.

**Option C (only ever by hand) was declined** because it depends on the navigator remembering, which
is the thing the retrospective loop exists to fix.

**Option i for the template (shape only) was declined**: a blank is harder to fill than an example is
to edit, and two consumers would answer it in shapes the fleet reads differently.

## Out of scope

- **Emptying the traps blocks.** See the correction in *Context*: most entries are universal and stay.
- **Rewriting any universal trap.** They are moved or kept, never reworded.
- **`ah-qled.10.1` / `.10.2` / `.10.3` / `.10.4`** — frontmatter, Moira's public line, `audience_noun`,
  and worked examples. This bead touches none of their sites.
- **Making Forge file or edit anything.** It proposes. `agents/architect.md:177` ("What Forge never
  does") is the boundary and it does not move.
- **A `traps` key in `cerebro-project.conf`.** The file is found by path, exactly as
  `.claude/cerebro-roster` is; a key pointing at a file whose location is already conventional is a
  second source of truth.
- **Any change to how retrospectives are written.** `**Prevent by.**` already exists in all 138 and
  is the feed as it stands.

## Validation

1. Every `tests/*.sh` passes; cerebro's CI is green. `pnpm run check:fast` passes in the application.
2. `grep -rn "WebKit\|vite preview\|service worker" skills/ agents/` in cerebro returns **nothing**.
3. `grep -rn "preview server\|stale lease\|conflicted head" skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` still
   returns the universal traps — they were **kept**, not moved.
4. `.claude/cerebro-traps.md` exists in the application and carries all six moved traps, **in their
   original wording**.
5. `templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md` exists and contains a `## Four Eye Principle` heading matching the
   string the skills require.
6. `grep -rn "CLAUDE.md's Four Eye Principle" skills/ agents/ CLAUDE.md` returns no hit that fails to
   say **whose** `CLAUDE.md`.
7. **Read `implement-bead` and `plan-bead` end to end as a consumer with no traps file.** Nothing
   refers to a file that does not exist as though it must; nothing mentions a tool the consumer may
   not have.
8. `agents/architect.md` says Forge **proposes** and never writes the traps file, and names the
   138-of-138 figure so the bar is calibrated.

## Known traps

- **Do not empty the traps blocks.** The bead says to; the blocks say otherwise. Increment 1 is a
  split and validation item 3 is the guard.
- **`plan-bead`'s section and `implement-bead`'s are not the same shape.** One is mostly universal
  with two project entries; the other is an instruction followed by four project examples. Treat them
  separately.
- **The traps file is tracked, at `.claude/cerebro-traps.md`, not under `.cerebro/`.** Putting it in
  the git-ignored directory means it vanishes on a fresh clone and every new machine silently loses
  the traps — `project-conf`'s header makes exactly this argument about exactly this mistake.
- **Forge proposes and never writes.** `agents/architect.md:177` is a boundary with its own section;
  a "helpful" auto-append crosses it and turns a curated file into a log.
- **A proposal every sweep is a proposal nobody reads.** 138 of 138 retrospectives have a
  `Prevent by`; the bar is "the next agent could act on this before starting", and it must be written
  into Forge's file rather than assumed.
- **Two repositories.** Increments 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 are a cerebro PR; increment 2 is an application PR
  with the pointer bump. Do not bump before the cerebro PR merges — and note that increment 1 removes
  the WebKit trap from the prompts while increment 2 adds it to the consumer's file, so **between the
  two merges this project has lost it**. Land them close together and say so in both PR bodies.
- **Copy trap wording verbatim.** These sentences were paid for in CI cycles; a paraphrase loses the
  specificity that makes them actionable.
- **`templates/` may not exist yet** in cerebro. Check before assuming, and if it is new, say in the
  PR that a new top-level directory was added.

## The cost

The prompts teach with THIS project's examples, so a consumer's agent reads worked examples about a game it is not building, and citations it cannot resolve.

- agents/reviewer.md:135-139 - "no rule of the game decided in a React component", "the ruleset owning the vocabulary the UI merely displays"
- agents/reviewer.md:164 - "a wasm bundle that grew"
- skills/release-notes/SKILL.md:128-133 - a hardcoded glossary: "Hexes, units, orders, turns, provinces and factions are the game's language and belong"
- skills/release-notes/SKILL.md:98-114 - a whole worked example headed "What's new for you in Atlantis HUD"
- skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:127,619,805 - "reaches a player", "a game switch and a new turn"
- skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md:200 - .rep files

**Worked examples using real bead ids and titles:**
- skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md:180-181 (feat(ah-t65): load multiple reports), :209-210, :372-373
- agents/orchestrator.md:357,361-367
- skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:136,646,804 (hexMapModel), :812-821
- agents/user-feedback.md:365-372 (a real feature and ah-7pa)
- emacs/README.md:69-113 - a whole sample panel of real beads

Write these as <bead-id> / <parent>.<n> and neutral titles.

**Bead ids as citations, roughly 40 across the prompts** - orchestrator.md alone has ~20, plus verifier.md, user-feedback.md, architect.md, planner.md.

The upstream issue's §5 recommends leaving the ~379 in the ELISP AND TESTS alone, and that is right: they are load-bearing reasons in code comments. But an id carried into every agent session is different - it costs context and credibility for a reference the consumer cannot resolve. **Keep the rule in the prompt, move the provenance to a cerebro-side docs/decisions.md the prompt does not carry.**

## The trap

A citation is often the only thing making a rule believable ("this cost three implementers a cycle each"). Stripping the id must not strip the evidence: the prompt keeps the claim and the cost, and docs/decisions.md carries which bead established it.
design:
## Context

The prompts **teach with this project's examples**, so a consumer's agent reads worked examples about
a game it is not building, and citations it cannot resolve.

**Measured on `origin/main`** — bead ids carried in agent prose:

```
agents/orchestrator.md   27
agents/user-feedback.md   7
agents/verifier.md        5
agents/architect.md       1
agents/planner.md         1
agents/reviewer.md        1
                         42 total
elisp + tests           475   ← deliberately NOT touched
```

**Three distinct couplings**, and they are not fixed the same way:

1. **Domain vocabulary as worked examples** — `reviewer.md:170` (*"this runs per hex per turn; have
   you measured it on a 200-hex report?"*), `:135-139`, `:164` (*"a wasm bundle that grew"*);
   `plan-bead/SKILL.md:127,619,805`; `beads-workflow/SKILL.md:200` (`.rep` files).
2. **Worked examples using real bead ids and titles** — `beads-workflow/SKILL.md:180-181`
   (`feat(ah-t65): load multiple reports`), `:209-210`, `:372-373`; `orchestrator.md:357,361-367`;
   `plan-bead/SKILL.md:136,646,804` (`hexMapModel`), `:812-821`;
   `user-feedback.md:365-372`; `emacs/README.md:69-113` (a whole sample panel of real beads).
3. **Bead ids as citations** — the 42 above.

**The elisp and tests keep their ~475.** Upstream §5 is right: those are load-bearing reasons in code
comments, read by whoever is editing that line. **An id carried into every agent session is
different.**

### Being honest about the size of the win

42 ids is a few hundred bytes. **This is not a context saving and the plan should not pretend it is.**
It is **credibility**: a consumer's agent reading *"(ah-v09e)"* sees a citation it cannot check, in a
document telling it what to do.

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. 🔴 `release-notes/SKILL.md` stays concrete — the whole file

The navigator decided on 2026-08-22, extending the decision they made for `audience_noun` an hour
earlier (**ah-qled.10.3**): **the exception covers the vocabulary and the worked example too, not just
the audience noun.**

So **`:98-114`'s worked example** (*"What's new for you in Atlantis HUD"*), **`:128-133`'s glossary**
(*"Hexes, units, orders, turns, provinces and factions are the game's language and belong"*) and its
concrete phrasing (*"Right-click a hex to…"*) **all stay exactly as they are.**

The reasoning, worth keeping in the file so nobody genericises it later: **the file's job is teaching
someone to write good notes, and a worked example about hexes and turns teaches better than one about
widgets and things.** A consumer forks the file or ignores the examples — which is what they would do
with generic ones anyway.

**`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md` should barely appear in this bead's diff.** If it does, check it
against this decision first.

### 2. Domain vocabulary elsewhere becomes neutral

`reviewer.md` and `plan-bead/SKILL.md` are internal instructions with no public output, so the
exception does not reach them:

- *"this runs per hex per turn; have you measured it on a 200-hex report?"* → the same question about
  a large input, with **the cost claim intact**. The rule is *"a per-item cost on a large input"*, and
  it survives without hexes.
- *"no rule of the game decided in a React component"* → the rule is *"domain logic decided in a view
  component"*.
- *"a wasm bundle that grew"* → *"a bundle that grew"*.
- `beads-workflow/SKILL.md:200`'s `.rep` files → a neutral file extension or none.

**Keep every rule's force.** These examples exist because an abstract rule is unmemorable; a neutral
example must still be an example, not a definition.

### 3. Worked examples lose the real ids and titles

`<bead-id>`, `<parent>.<n>`, and neutral titles:

```
feat(ah-t65): load multiple reports      →   feat(<bead-id>): <a short description of the work>
```

**`emacs/README.md:69-113` is a whole sample panel of real beads** and is the largest single item
here. It must still *look like* a panel — the point is showing the shape — so replace the ids and
titles and **keep the column widths and the layout intact.**

### 4. The citations move to `docs/decisions.md`

**The prompt keeps the rule and the cost; only the parenthetical id moves.**

```
before:  …twelve smoke tests' worth, from the orders editor to the region panel (ah-v09e).
after:   …twelve smoke tests' worth, from the orders editor to the region panel.
```

and `docs/decisions.md`, cerebro-side and **not carried into any session**, records `ah-v09e` →
the rule it established.

**🔴 The trap the bead names, and it is the acceptance:** *"a citation is often the only thing making
a rule believable"*. **Stripping the id must not strip the evidence.** Where a sentence reads
*"this cost three implementers a cycle each (ah-9ess)"*, the claim and the cost **stay in the
prompt** — a rule that loses its evidence becomes an assertion, and an agent weighing whether to
follow it has less to go on than before.

**Read each of the 42 in its sentence.** Where removing the id leaves a bare assertion, **the sentence
needs the cost written into it** before the id goes.

### 5. Not touched

`emacs/` and `tests/`'s ~475 ids, `release-notes/SKILL.md`, and every rule's substance.

## Increments

1. **The decisions file exists and is not carried.**
   RED: `tests/` — `docs/decisions.md` exists; **no agent file or skill loads it.**
   GREEN: the file, seeded from the first ids moved.
2. **Citations move, evidence stays.**
   RED: per file — no bare `ah-…` remains in the prose, **and** each sentence that carried one still
   states its claim and cost.
   GREEN: `orchestrator.md` (27) first, as the largest; then the other five.
3. **Worked examples are neutral.**
   RED: `grep -n "ah-t65\|hexMapModel\|ah-7pa"` returns nothing in `skills/` or `agents/`.
   GREEN: the placeholders, and `emacs/README.md`'s panel with its layout intact.
4. **Domain vocabulary outside release-notes is neutral.**
   RED: `grep -ni "hex\|wasm\|\.rep\b" agents/ skills/` returns only `release-notes/SKILL.md`.
   GREEN: `reviewer.md`, `plan-bead/SKILL.md`, `beads-workflow/SKILL.md`.
5. **release-notes is untouched.**
   RED: none. **GREEN**: nothing — and the diff proves it.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the submodule pin bump. Nothing else.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **no bead id remains in agent prose or skills** | `tests/` | the bead |
| **every sentence that carried one still states its cost** | reading | 🔴 the trap |
| `docs/decisions.md` exists and is loaded by nothing | `tests/` | §4 |
| no real bead id or title in a worked example | same | §3 |
| **`emacs/README.md`'s panel still looks like a panel** | reading | §3 |
| domain vocabulary is gone outside release-notes | same | §2 |
| **`release-notes/SKILL.md` is unchanged** | the diff | §1 — the navigator's decision |
| the elisp and tests keep their ~475 | same | deliberately untouched |
| every existing test | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `for t in tests/*.sh`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-22.

**Q1 — how far the release-notes exception reaches.** Chosen: **the whole file stays concrete** — the
vocabulary and the worked example as well as the audience noun. A worked example about hexes and
turns teaches better than one about widgets and things, and a consumer forks the file or ignores the
examples either way. Accepted cost: release-notes stays visibly this project's. Rejected: **holding
the exception to the audience noun alone** (the worked example gets markedly worse as teaching, and
*"the game's language"* has no neutral form that still says anything) and **a `domain_nouns` key**
(a fourth key and a list to maintain, for a file one role reads).

**Q2 — the 42 citations.** Chosen: **move them, keep every claim and cost in place.** Accepted after I
put the honest version: this is credibility, not a context saving. Rejected: **leaving them** (compact,
and they resolve for *this* project — but the epic's whole promise is that the prose stops naming it)
and **moving only the pure-provenance ones** (a judgement call at 42 sites and two conventions in one
file).

## Out of scope

- **`release-notes/SKILL.md`** — see §1.
- **The ~475 ids in `emacs/` and `tests/`.**
- **ah-qled.10.3's `audience_noun`** and **ah-qled.10.2's `project_name`** — planned; coordinate if
  the same line is touched.
- **Any rule's substance.**

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rnoE '\bah-[a-z0-9]{3,}(\.[0-9]+)*\b' agents/ skills/ docs/agent-workflow.md   # nothing
grep -rnoE '\bah-[a-z0-9]{3,}' emacs/ tests/ | wc -l                                  # still ~475
git diff --stat -- skills/release-notes/SKILL.md                                       # empty
```

Then by hand — **and the reading is the real test**:

1. **Read the six files as a consumer's agent would**, with no access to this bead database. Does any
   sentence now assert something with no reason given? **That is the failure this bead can cause**,
   and it is worse than the coupling it removes.
2. Pick three rules that carried a citation and check the **cost survived** — *"twelve smoke tests'
   worth"*, *"three implementers a cycle each"*. If the number went with the id, put it back.
3. Read `emacs/README.md`'s sample panel: does it still teach the **shape** of the panel?
4. Read `reviewer.md`'s performance question without hexes: is it still a **question a reviewer can
   act on**, or has it become a platitude?
5. Confirm `docs/decisions.md` is **loaded by nothing** — grep the agent files and skills for it.
6. Confirm `release-notes/SKILL.md` shows **no diff at all**.

## Known traps

- **🔴 Stripping the id must not strip the evidence.** A citation is often the only thing making a
  rule believable. The claim and the cost stay in the prompt; only the id moves. Read each of the 42
  **in its sentence**, and write the cost in before removing the id where it is missing.
- **🔴 `release-notes/SKILL.md` is exempt in full**, by a decision made twice — once for
  `audience_noun` (ah-qled.10.3) and once for the whole file here. Genericising it is the most likely
  wrong turn in this bead.
- **A neutral example must still be an example.** These exist because an abstract rule is
  unmemorable; replacing *"200-hex report"* with *"a large input"* is fine, replacing it with nothing
  is not.
- **Leave the elisp and tests alone.** Their ~475 ids are load-bearing reasons read by whoever edits
  that line.
- **`emacs/README.md`'s panel must still look like a panel** — the ids change, the layout does not.
- **`docs/decisions.md` must not be loaded by any prompt**, or the context it was meant to save comes
  straight back with worse structure.
- **Do not claim a context saving.** A few hundred bytes; the argument is credibility, and overstating
  it in the commit message invites a reviewer to reject the whole bead on arithmetic.

title: The fleet's own prose calls its reader a player, in a harness for projects that are not games
description:
Split from ah-qled.10 (upstream cerebro#58 §4).

## The cost

"player" is the assumed reader of the fleet's own prose, in a harness meant to be used by projects that are not games:

- skills/release-notes/SKILL.md - 13 occurrences, and its whole audience section is written for a game
- agents/planner.md:81,86,129
- agents/reviewer.md:141,178,180,191
- agents/verifier.md:202,206,259
- agents/orchestrator.md:743
- docs/agent-workflow.md:163,532

## The mechanism already exists

audience_noun is ALREADY a declared key - .claude/cerebro-project.conf:18 carries `audience_noun  player` today, put there by ah-qled.1. scripts/project-conf reads it and never fails on absence, so a default of "user" is one argument.

So this bead is not building anything: it is one key, already declared and already read, applied to about twenty sentences.

## The property to preserve

Every rule that currently uses the word must survive the substitution intact. A sentence like "would a player notice this?" becomes a sentence about whatever the consumer's audience is called, and must still read as English for "user", "operator" or "reader". A sentence that only makes sense about a game is domain vocabulary and belongs to ah-qled.10.4, not here.
design:
## Context

**"player" is the assumed reader of the fleet's own prose**, in a harness meant to be mounted by
projects that are not games. Counted on `origin/main` — **30 occurrences across six files**:

```
skills/release-notes/SKILL.md   13   — its whole audience section is written for a game
agents/reviewer.md               5
agents/planner.md                3
agents/verifier.md               3
docs/agent-workflow.md           4
agents/orchestrator.md           2
```

**This bead builds nothing.** `audience_noun` is **already a declared key** —
`.claude/cerebro-project.conf:18` carries `audience_noun  player`, put there by ah-qled.1 — and
`scripts/project-conf` already reads it and never fails on absence. So this is **one existing key
applied to about thirty sentences**, with `user` as the default when unset.

**The property that must survive**: every rule using the word must still read as English for
`user`, `operator` or `reader`. *"Would a player notice this?"* becomes a sentence about whatever the
consumer's audience is called, and must not become a sentence a reader has to decode.

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. Two treatments, not one — the navigator's decision of 2026-08-22

**This section was rewritten after the plan was first published.** The navigator settled a question
Beast put to them, and it postdates and supersedes what stood here.

**Six of the seven files get neutral prose with no substitution at all:**

> *"Anything **the audience** will see is theirs to decide"*, *"nothing **the audience** could ever
> see"*

`agents/planner.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`, `agents/verifier.md`, `agents/orchestrator.md`,
`docs/agent-workflow.md` and `agents/user-feedback.md` therefore **read no key and perform no
substitution.** They stop naming a player because they stop naming anyone in particular.

**`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md` alone stays concrete.** It reads the key at the top and then uses
the literal word throughout:

> *"First, read `project-conf audience_noun` — this project's word for the people who use what you
> build. It is "player". Use that word, not "user", throughout the notes."*

and its body keeps *"Dropping what a player cannot see"*, *"A player thinks 'what is different when
I…'"*.

**Why the split, and it is the reason not to flatten it later:** release-notes produces **the
navigator's public output**. *"What a player would say where they were"* is doing real work that
*"what the audience would say"* loses. The other six are internal instructions to agents, where a
neutral noun costs nothing.

### 1a. The grammar cases — now only inside release-notes

Counted across the whole repository: **2 plural (`players`) and 2 possessive (`player's`) sites.**
Under the split above, **only those falling inside `release-notes/SKILL.md` need forming from the
key**; any in the other six files are rewritten to neutral prose and need no machinery.

Where forming is needed: **singular key, `+s` and `+'s` from it.** That works for `player`, `user`,
`operator`, `reader`. **State the irregular-plural limitation rather than adding a second key** — the
handful of sites does not justify `audience_noun_plural`.

### 2. 🔴 The verb at `user-feedback.md:138` — claimed here, deliberately

> *"feedback from people actually **playing** with Atlantis HUD"*

**`playing` occurs exactly once in the whole repository** (verified), and it sits in the one sentence
**ah-qled.10.2 also edits** — that bead takes the *name*, and its plan says the verb is this bead's.

**This bead takes it**, and must, because otherwise it belongs to nobody: `audience_noun` is a noun
and has no verb form, while **ah-qled.10.4** is *domain examples*, not grammar. The sentence would
fall between all three.

**Reword to avoid a verb entirely** rather than inventing an `audience_verb` key for one site:

> *"feedback from the people actually using it"*

**Coordinate with ah-qled.10.2**: it changes the name in the same line. **Whichever lands second
rebases**, and neither rewrites the whole sentence.

### 3. A sentence that only works for a game is not this bead's

`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md` holds **13** of the 30, and the bead notes *"its whole audience
section is written for a game"*. **Substitute the noun; leave anything that only makes sense about a
game to ah-qled.10.4** — and **list in the PR which sentences were left and why**, so the sibling has
a starting point rather than a re-read.

The test is simple and should be applied per sentence: **swap in `operator` and read it aloud.** If it
still says what it meant, it was the noun. If it now says something absurd, the sentence is about a
game and is not this bead's.

### 4. Where the key is read — one file, not seven

There is no renderer; this is prose an agent follows. **Only `release-notes/SKILL.md` instructs its
reader to run `project-conf audience_noun`**, and it does so once, at the top, before the notes are
written.

**The other six files instruct nothing** — they simply say *the audience*. That is the whole
simplification the navigator's decision buys: six files with no placeholder to explain, no key to
resolve, and nothing that can be half-substituted.

**Default `user` when unset**, inside release-notes only, so a consumer that declared no key still
gets readable notes.

### 5. What must not change

Every rule's *substance*. This bead changes one word, thirty times; if a rule's meaning shifts, the
sentence was rewritten rather than substituted.

## Increments

1. **The noun substitutes, and reads.**
   RED: `tests/` — with `audience_noun operator`, the affected prose resolves to `operator`; with the
   key absent, to `user`.
   GREEN: the prose, file by file.
2. **Plural and possessive.**
   RED: the two `players` and two `player's` sites form correctly from the key.
   GREEN: the `+s` / `+'s` rule, stated where the key is documented.
3. **The verb site.**
   RED: `grep -rn "playing" .` returns nothing.
   GREEN: `user-feedback.md:138`, reworded — **coordinated with ah-qled.10.2**.
4. **Nothing is left, and what was left is named.**
   RED: `grep -rni "player" skills/ agents/ docs/` returns only sentences deliberately left for
   ah-qled.10.4.
   GREEN: the remainder, and the PR's list of what was left and why.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the submodule pin bump. **`audience_noun player` is already in the
conf**, so nothing else is needed — this is the one bead in the family whose key is already declared.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `audience_noun` resolves and is used | `tests/` | the bead |
| **absent key defaults to `user`** | same | the fallback |
| the two plural sites form `+s` | same | §1 |
| the two possessive sites form `+'s` | same | §1 |
| **`grep -rn "playing"` returns nothing** | same | §2 |
| **remaining `player` sites are only the ones left for ah-qled.10.4** | same | §3 |
| every existing test | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `for t in tests/*.sh`.

## User-facing decisions

**Q (added 2026-08-22, after first publication).** Beast put the substitution question to the
navigator while this bead briefly carried two `planning` labels, and the answer changes §1, §1a and
§4 above. Chosen: **generic everywhere, concrete in release-notes.** Rejected: **substituting
`audience_noun` in all seven files**, which is what this plan originally specified — it was rejected
because release-notes produces the navigator's public output, and *"what a player would say where
they were"* does work that *"what the audience would say"* loses.

**Recorded rather than quietly folded in**, because the plan said something different when it was
first published and an implementer may have read the earlier version.


**None, and none to ask for.** This is prose the fleet's own agents read; nothing reaches a player —
or a user, or an operator. The navigator ranked the ah-qled family P1.

**Decided here** (architecture): **a singular key with `+s` and `+'s` formed from it**, with the
irregular-plural limitation stated rather than a second key added for two sites; **this bead claiming
the one verb site** and rewording it to avoid needing a verb key at all; and **the read-it-aloud test**
as the boundary with ah-qled.10.4.

## Out of scope

- **Sentences that only make sense about a game** — **ah-qled.10.4**, and this bead's PR lists which
  were left.
- **`project_name` in the same `:138` sentence** — **ah-qled.10.2**, which is planned; coordinate.
- **An `audience_noun_plural` or `audience_verb` key.**
- **The substance of any rule.**

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rni "player" skills/ agents/ docs/     # only what was deliberately left
grep -rn "playing" .                          # nothing
```

Then by hand — **and the real test is reading, not grepping**:

1. Set `audience_noun operator` and **read the affected sentences aloud.** *"Anything the operator
   will see is theirs to decide"*, *"backwards-compatible for an operator who upgrades?"* — each must
   still say what it meant. **This is the acceptance**, and it is a judgement rather than an
   assertion.
2. Remove the key and confirm the default reads as `user` everywhere, equally naturally.
3. Put `player` back and confirm **this project's prose is word-for-word what it is today**.
4. Check the two plural sites and the two possessive sites specifically — those are where a naive
   substitution produces `operators's` or `operator s`.
5. Read `user-feedback.md:138` after both this bead and ah-qled.10.2 have landed: **one sentence, both
   halves fixed, still natural.**
6. Read the PR's list of sentences left for ah-qled.10.4 and check each really is about a game rather
   than merely mentioning the audience.

## Known traps

- **🔴 Do not genericise `release-notes/SKILL.md`.** It is the one file that keeps the literal
  word, on the navigator's explicit decision, because it produces public output. Flattening all seven
  to *"the audience"* is the plan as originally written and is **no longer what was agreed.**
- **🔴 The other six substitute nothing.** They are neutral prose. Adding a `project-conf`
  read to `planner.md` or `verifier.md` reintroduces machinery the decision removed.
- **🔴 The verb `playing` occurs exactly once and belongs to nobody by default.** `audience_noun` has
  no verb form and ah-qled.10.4 is about examples. **This bead takes it**, by rewording rather than by
  inventing a key.
- **🔴 `user-feedback.md:138` is edited by two beads.** ah-qled.10.2 takes the name, this one takes
  the verb. Whichever lands second rebases; neither rewrites the whole sentence.
- **Read it aloud with `operator`.** That is the whole test for whether a sentence was about the noun
  or about a game, and it is the boundary with ah-qled.10.4.
- **Plural and possessive are 2 sites each** and are where a blind find-and-replace produces nonsense.
- **`release-notes/SKILL.md` holds 13 of the 30** and is the file most likely to contain
  game-only sentences. Do not force them; list them.
- **Explain where the value comes from.** A placeholder in a document with no instruction to resolve
  it is worse than the hardcoded word.
- **Substance must not move.** One word, thirty times.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first** — and the consumer's key is already declared, so PR two is the pin alone.
