title: Finishing a nested block leaves END sitting one level too deep
description:
Found during verification of ah-2tj8 (2026-08-21, origin/main ac663c0). That bead passed - indentation on typing, on opening a unit and on paste; closers aligned with their openers; the setting off means off; and no spurious save - and this is the follow-up filed alongside the pass.

## What the player sees

The navigator's words: "when i have typed END or ENDTURN and press enter, that line should be automatically indented to the right one (one level in)".

Every other line Enter opens is indented to the depth it belongs at. After a closer it is not, so a player who has just finished a nested block has to indent the next order by hand - in a setting whose whole promise is that they never have to.

## Where the rule lives

`packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx:203`, the `Enter` binding. It asks `lineDepths` for the depth of a hypothetical empty line appended after the caret:

    const depth = lineDepths(`${editor.state.doc.sliceString(0, from)}\n`).at(-1) ?? 0;
    const insert = `\n${" ".repeat(depth)}`;

and `orderIndent.ts:28` records the property that makes closers align with their openers:

    a closer reports the depth *outside* the block it closes, which is what puts `END` under `FORM`

Those two interact, and the interaction is what wants examining: the depth reported *for* the closer line is the depth outside the block, and the depth wanted *after* it is the depth of whatever still encloses it. Whether `lineDepths` distinguishes those two when the closer is the last line of the text handed to it is the question - it is one function answering "where does this line sit" and "where does the next line sit" from the same walk.

## What is NOT settled, and why this is not simply a bug

ah-2tj8's ten decisions cover when indentation is applied (Q1), where closers sit (Q2) and what happens to an unclosed block (Q4). **None of them says where the caret goes on the line after a closer.** So there is a genuine question here rather than only an arithmetic slip, and it should be put to the navigator rather than assumed:

- After `END` closing a `FORM` nested in a `TURN`, the next line is presumably at the `TURN`'s content depth - the same column the `END` itself sits at. That is what "one level in" reads as, and it is the common case.
- After `ENDTURN` at the outermost level there is no enclosing block, so depth 0 is correct and nothing should change. A fix that indents unconditionally would be wrong here.
- After a **stray** closer with no opener, Q4's spirit ("indent by the running depth anyway, the runaway is the signal") suggests doing whatever the running depth says rather than special-casing, but that follows from Q4 rather than being stated by it.

Worth confirming the behaviour is the same for `END` and `ENDTURN`, since the navigator named both.

## Acceptance

With Order OCD on, pressing Enter at the end of a closer line puts the caret at the depth of the block that still encloses it - the same column as the closer for a nested block, and column 0 after an outermost `ENDTURN`. One Ctrl+Z still takes back the newline and its indent together, as it does for every other Enter.
design:
## Context

Found by Psylocke verifying **ah-2tj8** (which passed). The navigator's words:

> *"when i have typed END or ENDTURN and press enter, that line should be automatically indented to
> the right one (one level in)"*

**The bead reads this as the line Enter *opens*; the navigator confirmed on 2026-08-21 that it is the
`END`/`ENDTURN` line *itself*** — *"not the line after end/endturn. the actual end/endturn line as
soon as I press enter on that line to move to next"*. **This plan is written to the navigator's
reading**, and it is a different defect from the one the bead describes.

**The asymmetry, in one function.** `OrdersEditor.tsx:202-246`'s Enter binding already **re-processes
the line you just finished** — `keywordJustFinished` uppercases `end` to `END` in the same
transaction (`:220-236`). **It does not re-indent it.**

So:

```
        you type                on Enter, today          wanted
TURN                        TURN                     TURN
 FORM 1                      FORM 1                   FORM 1
  MOVE N                      MOVE N                   MOVE N
  end                         END      <- cased,       END     <- cased AND dedented
                                          not moved     |
```

The line was opened at the **inner** depth, because at that moment it was inside the block. Typing
`end` turns it into a closer, whose depth is the one **outside** the block it closes
(`orderIndent.ts:24-29`) — so **the common correction is a dedent, not an indent.** The navigator
confirmed that explicitly.

**ah-2tj8's ten decisions do not cover this.** Q1 (when indentation is applied), Q2 (closers align
with their openers) and Q4 (an unclosed block) say nothing about the line you are leaving. Psylocke
was right to flag it as a question rather than an arithmetic slip.

Branch from `origin/main`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. One more change in the transaction Enter already dispatches

`lineDepths` answers both questions from **the same walk, one character apart** — the existing code
already relies on this:

```ts
lineDepths(`${doc.sliceString(0, from)}\n`).at(-1)   // the NEXT line's depth  (today, :214)
lineDepths(   doc.sliceString(0, from)     ).at(-1)   // THIS line's own depth  (what this bead needs)
```

Without the appended `\n`, the last entry is the current line's own depth, **computed from the text
including the `end` that was just typed**. That is the whole arithmetic; no new function is needed.

Then replace the current line's leading whitespace:

```ts
const indent = line.text.length - line.text.trimStart().length;
// … a change over [line.from, line.from + indent] inserting " ".repeat(ownDepth)
```

**Make it general, not closer-specific.** Re-indent the current line to its own depth whatever that
is; for a line whose depth did not change it is a no-op, so a special case for `END`/`ENDTURN` buys
nothing and would miss any other line whose depth moved as it was typed.

**Skip the change entirely when the indentation is already right.** A no-op change still makes a
history entry, and one Ctrl+Z would then give back nothing visible.

### 2. 🔴 The caret must be mapped, not arithmetic

`:239` sets `selection: { anchor: from + insert.length }`. **`from` is a position in the *old*
document, and a dedent deletes characters before it.** A transaction's `selection` is interpreted
against the **new** document, so the obvious implementation leaves the caret one column off per level
removed — and it would look almost right, which is worse.

Compute the anchor from the change set (`ChangeSet.mapPos`), or add the indent delta explicitly. **Do
not leave `from + insert.length` unchanged.**

### 3. Change order

CodeMirror requires `changes` in ascending, non-overlapping order. The re-indent covers
`[line.from, line.from + indent]`; the case fix sits at `line.from + finished.from`, **after** the
whitespace. **So the re-indent must be listed first**, ahead of the existing case entry at `:228-236`.

### 4. One transaction, one undo

Keep `userEvent: "input"` and the single `dispatch`, so **one Ctrl+Z still hands the line back exactly
as it was typed** — the promise `:241-243` already makes, now covering the indent too.

### 5. Unchanged

The next line's depth and its indent (`:214-215`), the completion popup's higher-precedence Enter,
the `orderOcd` guard at `:205`, and everything `lineDepths` does.

## Increments

1. **The line you leave is indented correctly.**
   RED: `OrdersEditor` tests — with `orderOcd` on, Enter on a line reading `  end` inside
   `TURN`/`FORM` leaves `END` at the closer's depth. **Assert the dedent**, which is the case the
   bead got backwards.
   GREEN: the own-depth read and the re-indent change.
2. **The caret is where the player left it.**
   RED: after a dedent, the caret is at the start of the **new** line, not offset by the removed
   spaces. **This fails against the naive implementation**, which is the point.
   GREEN: a mapped anchor.
3. **Nothing else moved.**
   RED: the next line still opens at its own depth; a line whose indentation is already right
   produces **no** change; `ENDTURN` at the margin stays at the margin; the case fix still fires.
   GREEN: the guards.
4. **One undo.**
   RED: Ctrl+Z after Enter restores the line exactly as typed, indentation included, in one step.
   GREEN: nothing — the single transaction already does this if increments 1–3 kept it.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **Enter on `  end` dedents it to the closer's depth** | `OrdersEditor` tests | the bead |
| `endturn` at the outermost level stays at column 0 | same | no over-indent |
| a line already correctly indented produces no change | same | no empty history entry |
| **the caret lands correctly after a dedent** | same | 🔴 the mapping |
| the case fix still uppercases `end` → `END` | same | **unchanged** |
| the next line still opens at its own depth | same | **unchanged** |
| `orderOcd` off changes nothing | same | the setting means off |
| **one Ctrl+Z restores the line as typed** | smoke | the single-transaction promise |
| a stray closer with no opener | same | Q4's spirit — the running depth, no crash |
| ah-2tj8's existing indentation tests | its own | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. Anything asserting the caret's screen position is a Playwright
test — **there is no jsdom in this repository**.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-21. No mockup: this is whitespace, and worked text made the
difference clearer than a picture would.

**Q1 — which line.** The navigator **corrected the bead**: the `END`/`ENDTURN` line **itself**, as
Enter is pressed on it, not the line Enter opens. Recorded because the bead, and Psylocke's analysis
of it, are written to the other reading.

**Q2 — the rule.** Chosen: **on Enter, fix the current line's indentation as well as its case**,
accepting that the common correction is a **dedent**. Symmetric with what Enter already does for the
word you just finished, one rule for indent and dedent alike, and no special case for `ENDTURN` at the
margin. Rejected: **only ever adding indentation**, which would leave a closer at the block's inner
depth and contradict ah-2tj8's Q2, where the navigator chose that closers align with their openers.

## Out of scope

- **The line Enter opens.** Its depth is already right (`:214-215`) and this bead does not touch it.
- **Re-indenting on any key other than Enter.** ah-2tj8 settled when indentation is applied.
- **`lineDepths` itself**, and ah-2tj8's ten decisions.
- **A closer-specific rule.** The general one covers it.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm exec playwright test --project=web
```

Then by hand, with **Order OCD on**:

1. Type `TURN`, Enter, `FORM 1`, Enter, `MOVE N`, Enter, then `end` — and press **Enter**. The `END`
   must **move left** to line up under its `FORM`, and uppercase. **This is the acceptance.**
2. Watch the **caret**: it must be at the start of the new line, not a couple of columns adrift.
   That is the bug the obvious implementation introduces.
3. Type `endturn` at the outermost level and press Enter: it stays at the left margin.
4. Press **Ctrl+Z once**: the line comes back exactly as you typed it — lowercase and at the old
   indentation — in a single step.
5. Press Enter on a line that is already correctly indented: nothing moves, and Ctrl+Z does not eat
   an invisible step.
6. **Turn Order OCD off** and repeat step 1: nothing is re-indented and nothing is uppercased.
7. Type a stray `end` with no opener and press Enter: it does something sane and does not crash.

## Known traps

- **🔴 It is the line you are leaving, not the line you are opening.** The bead and its analysis are
  written to the other reading; the navigator corrected it explicitly. Building the bead as written
  fixes something nobody reported.
- **🔴 The caret must be mapped through the change set.** `from + insert.length` is arithmetic on the
  *old* document, and a dedent removes characters before `from`. The result looks almost right, which
  is how it ships.
- **The common correction is a DEDENT.** "Indented one level in" describes the destination, not the
  direction — an implementation that only ever adds spaces fixes nothing here.
- **Change order matters.** The re-indent covers the leading whitespace and must be listed before the
  case fix, or CodeMirror rejects the out-of-order set.
- **One transaction, one undo.** Splitting the re-indent into its own dispatch costs the
  single-Ctrl+Z promise `:241-243` makes.
- **Skip a no-op re-indent** — an empty change still consumes an undo step.
- **`lineDepths` with and without the trailing `\n`** answers two different questions. They differ by
  one character and it is easy to read the wrong one.
- **No jsdom here.** Caret position is a Playwright assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
- IT IS THE END/ENDTURN LINE ITSELF that is re-indented, as Enter is pressed on it - NOT the line Enter opens. The navigator corrected the bead's reading on 2026-08-21: "not the line after end/endturn. the actual end/endturn line as soon as I press enter on that line to move to next".
- On Enter with Order OCD on, the current line's indentation is corrected to its own depth, in the SAME transaction that already corrects the finished keyword's case. The common correction is a DEDENT: a line opened at the block's inner depth becomes a closer belonging one level out.
- The rule is general - re-indent the current line to its own depth, whatever it is - not a special case for END/ENDTURN. For a line whose depth did not change it is a no-op.
- A no-op re-indent produces NO change, so it does not consume an undo step.
- THE CARET IS MAPPED THROUGH THE CHANGE SET, not computed as `from + insert.length`: `from` is a position in the OLD document and a dedent deletes characters before it. The naive version leaves the caret a column adrift per level removed.
- The re-indent change is listed BEFORE the existing case-fix change - CodeMirror requires ascending, non-overlapping changes, and the re-indent covers the leading whitespace.
- One transaction, so ONE Ctrl+Z restores the line exactly as typed, indentation and case together.
- ENDTURN at the outermost level stays at column 0. A stray closer with no opener behaves sanely and does not crash.
- The next line's depth (:214-215), the completion popup's Enter, the orderOcd guard and lineDepths are unchanged. Order OCD off changes nothing.
- Caret-position assertions are Playwright tests; no jsdom is added.
- `pnpm run check:fast` and the smoke suite pass.

title: Cutting a release tells you to watch a build that only this project has
description:
Split from ah-qled.7.

`agents/orchestrator.md:767,789` names `pnpm run release <bump>` and describes the gate as "lint, typecheck, unit tests, rustfmt, clippy, rust tests"; `:798-804` describes a GitHub Actions workflow literally named `Release` producing a macOS bundle.

`release_cmd` becomes a project key (already on ah-qled.1's designed list). The post-tag watch must be OPTIONAL - "there is a build to watch after tagging" is an assumption, not a fact, and a consumer with no release workflow should not be told to watch one.

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58 §2
design:
## Context

Split from `ah-qled.7`, itself under the epic `ah-qled`, "Cerebro runs in a project that is not
atlantis-hud". Upstream: <https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58> §2.

**Worked in the cerebro submodule**, `.claude/cerebro/` = `rmstdope/cerebro`. See *Known traps* for
the two-repository dance.

`agents/orchestrator.md`'s release procedure is shared by every project using this harness, and three
passages in it are about **Atlantis HUD specifically**:

1. **Line 768 and line 790** run `pnpm run release <bump>`.
2. **Line 790** describes the gate as *"lint, typecheck, unit tests, rustfmt, clippy, rust tests"* —
   half of it Rust, which most consumers will not have.
3. **Lines 798–804** say the tag push *"starts the `Release` workflow that builds the macOS bundle"*
   and give a `gh run watch` command hardcoding `--workflow Release`.

There is a fourth, which the bead does not name and which was found while planning: **line 779 names
`--allow-any-branch` and `--dry-run`**, flags of *this* project's release script that another
project's release command need not have.

**The mechanism this bead needs already exists and the key is already declared.** `ah-qled.1` is
closed; it built `scripts/project-conf` and `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`, and that file carries
`release_cmd  pnpm run release` **today, on main**. So decision 1 of the bead's own description
("`release_cmd` becomes a project key, already on `ah-qled.1`'s designed list") needs no new
mechanism — only prose that reads it.

Read `scripts/project-conf`'s header before writing anything. Three of its properties shape every
increment below:

- **It never fails on absence.** A missing file, a missing key and an unreadable file all exit 0 with
  the default, because callers run under `set -euo pipefail`. Only a missing `<key>` *argument* exits
  non-zero.
- **A value runs to the end of the line**, and can never contain `#`.
- **Which branch it took goes to stderr, never stdout**, so `x="$(project-conf release_cmd)"` gets the
  value and nothing else.

The prose idiom is already established, once, in `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:422`:

> run `.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf prewarm` and run what it names, now.

Follow it. Do not invent a second way for a `.md` file to tell an agent to read a project fact.

## Files to change and what to reuse

All paths relative to `.claude/cerebro/`.

**`agents/orchestrator.md`** — the release section, roughly lines 755–815. This is the whole of the
bead's substance.

**`scripts/project-conf`** — **unchanged as code.** Its comment lists which keys are *detected*
rather than declared (`install`), and `release_watch` is not one of them; nothing there needs
editing. **Do not add `release_watch` to the detection table**: a guessed workflow name is exactly
the failure mode decision A was chosen to avoid.

**`tests/project-conf.sh`** — one new case for `release_watch` (increment 2).

**In the application repository, `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`** — one new line,
`release_watch  Release`. This is the consumer's own declaration and belongs in the *second* PR, with
the submodule bump.

Reuse:

- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:422`** — the one existing example of prose telling an agent to
  read a project key. Match its phrasing and its full path form.
- **The conf's existing comment block** — it documents the file's shape for a reader adding a key.
  A new key needs no new commentary there unless its meaning is not obvious from its name; this one
  is not obvious (absent means "do not watch"), so it does need a line. See increment 3.

## Increments

Increments 1–3 are one PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`; increment 4 is the consumer's declaration and
the submodule bump.

### 1 — The release command comes from the project

Both occurrences of `pnpm run release <bump>` (lines 768 and 790) become the key. At line 768, inside
the fenced command block:

```bash
git pull --ff-only origin main    # if behind; --ff-only, never a merge commit
"$(.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf release_cmd)" <bump>
```

**That line is wrong as written and must not be shipped that way** — `release_cmd` is
`pnpm run release`, three words, and quoting it as one command looks for a binary called
`pnpm run release`. Write the block so the value is *word-split*, or — better, and consistent with
how `prewarm` is handled — **make it an instruction rather than a substitution**:

```bash
git pull --ff-only origin main    # if behind; --ff-only, never a merge commit
```

Then, in prose: *"Run what `.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf release_cmd` names, with the bump as
its argument."* `implement-bead`'s `prewarm` line does exactly this, and for exactly this reason: an
agent reading a `.md` file is not a shell, and telling it to run what a command *names* is both
safer and clearer than handing it a substitution to get right.

At line 790, `` `pnpm run release <bump>` runs the same gate CI does `` becomes *"The release command
runs the project's full gate…"* — see increment 2, which changes the rest of that sentence anyway.

**The paragraph about `--allow-any-branch` and `--dry-run`** (line 779) becomes:

> A project's release command may offer a rehearsal — a run that does all the reading and the whole
> gate and stops before writing anything. If it does, that is a fine thing to offer when the
> navigator asks for one, and never something to reach for unprompted. Find out what it offers by
> asking it, not by assuming these flags exist.

The rule the original states — *neither is yours to reach for unprompted* — is the part that must
survive verbatim in meaning. Only the assumption that the flags exist goes.

**Everything else in that section stays exactly as it is.** The pre-flight checks (behind, ahead,
dirty tree, not on main), what each failure means, "a failing gate is not yours to repair", the two
things to say out loud, and the stranded-release recovery paragraph are all project-neutral already
and are the substance of the procedure. **Do not rewrite prose that is already generic** — a
diff that touches them is a diff that has to be re-reviewed for meaning it did not need to change.

### 2 — The gate is described by what it is for

Line 790's enumeration goes. The navigator chose **i**: say what it is for, not what it contains.

> The release command runs the project's full gate before it touches either manifest, so **expect it
> to take several minutes** and give it a generous timeout. Nothing is written until every check
> passes, so a gate failure leaves the version untouched and the repository exactly as it was.

Note what is preserved and why: *"expect it to take several minutes"* is the sentence that stops an
agent killing the release on a timeout, and *"nothing is written until every check passes"* is what
makes a gate failure safe to report rather than recover from. **Both must survive.** The list of
check names is the only thing being removed.

"either manifest" is itself mildly project-specific (this project has `package.json` and
`Cargo.toml`). Leave it: it is describing what a release command generally does, it is not a command
anyone runs, and widening it further costs clarity for no consumer benefit. Noted here so the next
reader does not file it as an oversight.

### 3 — The post-tag watch becomes optional, and declared

The navigator chose **A**: a declared `release_watch` key naming the workflow, **absent meaning there
is nothing to watch.**

Lines 798–804 become:

> On success it commits the version, pushes it to main, then pushes the tag. **Whether anything
> happens after that is the project's own business**, so ask it:
> `.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf release_watch`.
>
> If it names a workflow, that workflow was started by the tag push and the build takes minutes
> more:
>
> ```bash
> gh run watch "$(gh run list --workflow "$(.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf release_watch)" --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')"
> ```
>
> If it names nothing, the tag push was the last step. Say the version went out and stop — **do not
> go looking for a build to watch.** A project with no release workflow is an ordinary project, not
> a misconfigured one.

Then, unchanged: the two things to say out loud, and the stranded-release paragraph.

**"builds the macOS bundle" goes and does not come back in any form.** What the workflow produces is
the consumer's business and Cerebro has no need to know it.

`tests/project-conf.sh` gains one case, following the file's existing shape:

- `project-conf release_watch` with no such key in the conf **exits 0 and prints nothing**. That is
  the property the whole "absent means do not watch" rule rests on, and `project-conf`'s
  never-fail-on-absence promise is what makes it true — pin it explicitly rather than assuming it,
  because a future change to the reader that made an unknown key non-zero would silently turn every
  consumer's release into a failure.
- `project-conf release_watch` with `release_watch  Release` in the conf prints `Release`.

The conf's own comment block gains one line, because this key's meaning is not obvious from its name:

```
# release_watch  — the GitHub Actions workflow the tag push starts, if there is one. ABSENT means
#                  there is nothing to watch after tagging, which is an ordinary state.
```

### 4 — The consumer declares its workflow

In the **application** repository, `.claude/cerebro-project.conf` gains:

```
release_watch  Release
```

placed with the other keys, in the file's existing style (key, whitespace, value to end of line).
Verify the name against the workflow that actually exists — `ls .github/workflows/` and read the
`name:` field — rather than trusting the old prose, which is the thing being replaced.

This goes in the same PR as the submodule pointer bump. **If this line is forgotten, this project
silently stops watching its own release build** — which is the one real cost of decision A, and
validation item 4 is what catches it.

## The test plan

cerebro's suites are shell: `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` from the submodule root. CI
runs every `tests/*.sh` plus ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1.

Increments 1 and 2 change **prose only** — there is nothing to unit-test and nothing should be
invented to test them. Increment 3's two cases in `tests/project-conf.sh` are the only new
assertions.

**The real verification is reading the section end to end** as a consumer with no release workflow,
and asking at every paragraph: *does this still tell me what to do?* That is validation item 5, and
for a bead that is almost entirely prose it matters more than the test suite.

Run the whole shell suite anyway; `project-conf` is called by other tests' fixtures.

`pnpm run check:fast` before the second PR, since it gates the merge in the application.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21 (`docs/ui/release-in-any-project.html`). **Decided; raise
disagreements through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | How does Cerebro know whether there is a build to watch after tagging? | **A — a declared `release_watch` key.** Absent means nothing to watch and the release is done at the tag. Explicit, and the same pattern as every other project fact |
| 2 | The gate description | **i — say what it is for, not what it contains.** True in every project, still explains why it is slow, and nothing to keep in step when a gate changes |

**Option B (look and see what started) was declined**, and the reason constrains the implementation:
a slow-starting workflow would look like no workflow, which is a timing guess inside a release. So
increment 3 must **not** fall back to probing `gh run list` when `release_watch` is absent — absence
is an answer, not a gap to fill.

**Option C (ask the navigator) was declined** because Cerebro relays a release rather than conducting
an interview during one. Do not add a confirmation prompt.

## Out of scope

- **`scripts/project-conf` as code.** The reader is `ah-qled.1`, closed, and works. Adding a
  key requires no change to it.
- **Detection of `release_watch`.** Explicitly rejected — see *User-facing decisions*.
- **The rest of `ah-qled.7`.** `ah-qled.7.1` (the gate command an implementer runs) and `ah-qled.7.2`
  (harness scripts invoked through the consumer's package manager) are separate beads.
- **The pre-flight checks and everything about how a release is *decided*.** Already project-neutral.
- **Anything about the actual release script** in the application (`pnpm run release`). Not touched.
- **`ah-90gu`**, the disk-floor bead named in `ah-qled.7.2`'s notes. Different sibling, different
  bead.
- **Any other agent file.** `orchestrator.md` alone.

## Validation

1. Every `tests/*.sh` in the submodule passes; cerebro's CI is green.
2. `grep -n "pnpm\|macOS\|rustfmt\|clippy\|--dry-run\|--allow-any-branch" agents/orchestrator.md`
   returns nothing in the release section.
3. `grep -n "workflow Release" agents/orchestrator.md` returns nothing — the literal workflow name is
   gone.
4. In the application, `.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf release_watch` prints `Release`, and the
   name matches the `name:` of a workflow that actually exists in `.github/workflows/`.
5. **Read the whole release section as a consumer with no `release_watch` declared.** Every step is
   actionable, nothing tells you to watch a build, and nothing reads as though something is missing.
   This is a manual read and it is the point of the bead.
6. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/project-conf release_watch` in a checkout with no such key exits **0**
   and prints nothing.
7. The next real release cut by Cerebro still watches this project's build and still reports the
   version that went out. This is the one thing decision A can silently break; it is checked at the
   next release rather than gating the bead.

## Known traps

- **This is two repositories.** Branch and PR **inside `.claude/cerebro`**, merge there, then a
  second commit in the application bumps the submodule pointer *and* adds the `release_watch` line.
  Do not bump the pointer before the cerebro PR merges.
- **The bead's line numbers may be stale**, as they were for `ah-qled.5.2` and `ah-qled.5.3` in the
  same file family. `:767,789` in the bead are `:768,790` at HEAD. **Find every passage by content.**
- **`release_cmd` is three words.** `"$(project-conf release_cmd)" <bump>` looks for a binary named
  `pnpm run release`. Increment 1 says to make it an instruction rather than a substitution, which is
  what `implement-bead` already does for `prewarm` — follow that, do not get clever with word
  splitting inside a `.md` file an agent will copy verbatim.
- **Do not probe for a workflow when `release_watch` is absent.** Option B was declined by name; a
  helpful fallback added "just in case" reintroduces exactly the timing guess it was declined for.
- **`project-conf` prints its provenance to stderr.** A caller that captures both streams gets
  `project-conf: release_watch unset -> the default` in its value. The existing callers get this
  right; a new one written from memory may not.
- **Do not rewrite the generic prose.** Most of the release section is already project-neutral and
  is load-bearing (the four pre-flight failures, "a failing gate is not yours to repair", the
  stranded-release recovery). A large diff there costs a careful re-read for no gain.
- **Two sentences in the gate paragraph must survive the rewrite**: *"expect it to take several
  minutes"* stops an agent killing the release on a timeout, and *"nothing is written until every
  check passes"* is what makes a gate failure safe to report. Only the list of check names goes.
- **Forgetting increment 4 breaks this project quietly.** Nothing fails; Cerebro simply stops
  watching the build and says the release is done at the tag. Validation item 4 is the guard.
- **Disk space.** Eleven of the application's retrospectives name `scripts/diskPreflight.ts` refusing
  to start a bead below its 8 GB floor. It applies to `pnpm run check:fast` before the second PR.
  Safe offline reclaims: `~/.cargo/registry/src`, `target/debug/incremental`,
  `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache`.

title: The fleet's disk check and its retrospective sweep only work in this one project
description:
Split from ah-qled.7.

Two pieces of harness functionality live in the consumer and are invoked through its package manager:

- `agents/orchestrator.md:41,133-141` calls `pnpm sightings`, which resolves to `tsx scripts/retroSightings.ts` in ATLANTIS-HUD's package.json, not cerebro's. Move retroSightings.ts into `.claude/cerebro/scripts/` and call it by path, as work-beads, roster and prepare-worktree already are.
- `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:363` calls `pnpm exec tsx scripts/diskPreflight.ts` - a consumer-side TypeScript file invoked through pnpm. Either a language-neutral `.claude/cerebro/scripts/disk-preflight`, or an optional consumer preflight hook skipped when absent.

Note ah-90gu also touches the disk story (it changes when prune-worktrees reclaims a cold target, and reuses diskPreflight's FREE_SPACE_FLOOR_GB). Sequence rather than run in parallel, and do not move the floor's definition without checking ah-90gu has landed.

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58 §2
design:
## Context

Split from `ah-qled.7`, under the epic `ah-qled`, "Cerebro runs in a project that is not
atlantis-hud". Upstream: <https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58> §2.

**Worked in the cerebro submodule** (`.claude/cerebro/` = `rmstdope/cerebro`) *and* in the
application. See *Known traps*.

Two pieces of harness functionality are **cerebro's job** but live in **this project's** `scripts/`
and are reached through **this project's** package manager, so a consumer adopting the fleet gets an
agent instruction that cannot run:

- **`agents/orchestrator.md:41,133-141`** calls `pnpm sightings`, which resolves through
  atlantis-hud's `package.json:11` to `tsx scripts/retroSightings.ts`.
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:363`** calls `pnpm exec tsx scripts/diskPreflight.ts`.

Both are genuinely cerebro concepts. Retrospectives are the fleet's own practice — the conf already
declares `retro_dir  docs/retrospectives` — and the disk floor is what stops an implementer starting
a bead it cannot build.

**The bead's sequencing note is discharged: `ah-90gu` is closed**, delivered in `rmstdope/cerebro#71`
and PR #523. But it made the coupling sharper rather than looser, and this is the fact that shapes
the whole bead:

> `prune-worktrees.sh:160` — `sed -n 's/.*FREE_SPACE_FLOOR_GB *= *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p'
> "$repo_root/scripts/diskPreflight.ts"`

**A shared submodule greps a consumer's TypeScript source for a number.** Its own comment explains
why it does that — a threshold of its own would drift from the one that refuses to start beads — and
the reasoning is right; only the mechanism is wrong.

**What cerebro already allows itself**, counted rather than assumed, because it decides section 1:

| tool | cerebro scripts using it |
|---|---|
| `jq` | 13 |
| `awk` | 8 — `roster`, `launch`, `sweep-claims.sh`, `prune-worktrees.sh`, `sweep-stalled.sh` |
| `grep` | 7 |
| `sed` | 2 |
| **`node`** | **0** |

`awk` is ordinary here; `node` is a dependency cerebro does not have anywhere. The "Bash 3.2,
builtins only … no `awk`" rule applies to exactly **two** scripts — `roster:32` and
`default-branch:22` — for a stated reason: `tests/launchers.sh` narrows `PATH` to `dirname` and
`bash` to prove the *launch* path survives a broken environment. **A reporting script Cerebro runs on
demand is nowhere near that path and is not under that constraint.**

And `retroSightings.ts` already shells out to `git` (line 288) and `bd` (line 348), so it was never
pure Node.

## Files to change and what to reuse

**In cerebro** (`.claude/cerebro/`):

- **New: `scripts/retro-sightings`** — bash + awk, the port.
- **New: `tests/retro-sightings.sh`** — its tests, written first.
- **New: `scripts/disk-preflight`** — bash, the port.
- **New: `tests/disk-preflight.sh`** — its tests.
- **`scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`** — the floor comes from `project-conf`, not from a `sed` of a
  TypeScript file. Lines ~150–163.
- **`scripts/project-conf`** — **unchanged as code.** Its comment gains the new keys' meanings.
- **`agents/orchestrator.md:41,133-141`** — `pnpm sightings` becomes the script by path.
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:363`** — likewise.
- **`tests/project-conf.sh`** — a case for `disk_floor_gb`.

**In the application:**

- **`.claude/cerebro-project.conf`** — gains `disk_floor_gb  8`.
- **`package.json:11`** — the `sightings` script points at the new path, or goes.
- **`scripts/retroSightings.ts`, `scripts/retroSightings.test.ts`** — deleted.
- **`scripts/diskPreflight.ts`, `scripts/diskPreflight.test.ts`** — deleted.

Reuse, and do not re-implement:

- **`scripts/project-conf`** — never fails on absence, value runs to end of line, provenance to
  stderr. Its header is required reading.
- **`retro_dir`** — already declared. `retro-sightings` reads it rather than hardcoding
  `docs/retrospectives`.
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:422`'s idiom** — the one established way for prose to tell an
  agent to read a project fact. Match it.
- **`scripts/retroSightings.ts` and its 272-line test file** — **the specification for the port.**
  Read both before writing a line of awk.

## Increments

### 1 — `tests/retro-sightings.sh`, before any port exists

The Vitest suite pins twelve behaviours across five functions. **Port the tests first**, in cerebro's
own `tests/*.sh` style (plain bash, `set -euo pipefail`, `fail`/`pass`, exit non-zero on first
failure — copy the header and helpers from `tests/project-conf.sh`).

The suite must cover **at least** these, each of which is a real trap the TypeScript version already
handles:

| behaviour | why it is not obvious |
|---|---|
| A `Seen before` paragraph that **wraps across six lines** is read whole | The label is at column 0 but the payload wraps |
| A paragraph **stops at the next bold run-in** rather than swallowing it | |
| **One paragraph per finding** when a file holds two sections | |
| **A `None found` paragraph cites nothing, even when it names beads** | The single subtlest case: nine files name bead ids as *counter-examples*, and reading them as citations silently merges unrelated findings |
| **A qualified `None found`** still cites nothing | |
| A bead id is read **however it is written** — bare, backticked, or as a path | |
| A **sub-bead suffix** (`ah-k6i.5`) is kept, not read as a sentence end | |
| **A chain of five beads about one cause is one finding of five** | The connected-components property |
| **A citation naming ids the cited bead already names does not inflate the count** | Transitivity |
| **A cited bead that wrote no retrospective of its own is still counted** | |
| A cause **sighted twice stays below the threshold** | |
| A finding is **named by the oldest sighting's own headline**, and has no name when none exists | |
| **Biggest finding first, then most recent** | |

Feed each case a fixture directory of small `.md` files written by the test, not the real corpus.
The real corpus changes daily; a test that reads it asserts today's fleet history rather than the
parser.

**These tests must fail** (no script yet) before increment 2 begins. That is the point of doing them
first: the port is then a matter of making a specification pass, not of reproducing behaviour from
memory.

### 2 — `scripts/retro-sightings`

Bash for the file walking and the reporting; **one awk program** for the parsing and the graph.

- Read `retro_dir` from `project-conf` (default `docs/retrospectives`), walk `*.md` in it.
- Extract `Seen before` paragraphs, then citations, per the rules the tests now pin.
- **Union-find over the citations**, which is what awk's associative arrays make straightforward:
  a `parent[]` array, `find()` with path compression, `union()` on every citation edge. Each
  connected component is one finding, whatever the chain length. This is the property that turns ten
  bead ids about one full disk into one finding of ten rather than ten findings — do not replace it
  with grouping by pair.
- Threshold default 3, matching `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`.
- `--dismiss <bead>` silences the component containing that bead, permanently. The TypeScript stores
  this through `bd remember`/`bd recall` (line 348); keep that, and keep the key name, so an existing
  dismissal survives the port.
- Output format: one line per finding, **count first**, and how many retrospectives are new since
  the last sweep — `agents/orchestrator.md:140-141` documents both and that prose is not changing.

**Do not port `formatReport`'s exact bytes.** Port its shape: count, name, last-seen bead. The tests
should assert the count and the ids, not the column alignment, or every cosmetic change becomes a
test failure.

### 3 — `tests/disk-preflight.sh`, then `scripts/disk-preflight`

Same order. `scripts/diskPreflight.ts` and its 187-line test are the specification.

The script:

- Floor from `project-conf disk_floor_gb`. **A consumer that declares none gets no preflight**: exit
  0 silently. `project-conf` never fails on absence, which is what makes that a one-line branch.
- Free space at the repository root. The TypeScript uses `statfs`; bash uses `df`. **Parse `df -k`,
  not `df -h`** — `-h` rounds and its unit suffix varies by platform.
- Report in the shape the existing one does: how many GB free, the floor, and **what is reclaimable
  and where**. That last part is what makes the message actionable; eleven retrospectives complain
  the current advice sends the reader to a script that reclaims nothing, so **name the offline
  reclaims explicitly** — `~/.cargo/registry/src`, `target/debug/incremental`,
  `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache` — rather than pointing at `prune-worktrees.sh`.
- **Exit non-zero below the floor**, zero above. `implement-bead` reads the exit status.
- The comparison is **strictly greater than the floor**, matching `hasHeadroom`
  (`freeGb > FREE_SPACE_FLOOR_GB`) and `prune-worktrees.sh:229`'s note that the two must never
  disagree. An `>=` here reintroduces exactly the drift this bead removes.

### 4 — `prune-worktrees.sh` reads the declaration

Lines ~150–163. The `sed` of `diskPreflight.ts` goes; the floor comes from
`project-conf disk_floor_gb`.

Keep the existing precedence and the existing absence behaviour, both of which are deliberate:

- `FREE_SPACE_FLOOR_GB` **in the environment still wins** (line 156).
- **No declared floor disables the pressure path entirely** — only the outer bound applies. The
  comment says it well already: *"rather than a number this script made up."* Keep that sentence;
  only what it points at changes.

Rewrite the comment at lines 60–64 so it names the conf key rather than the TypeScript file.

### 5 — The call sites

- **`agents/orchestrator.md:41`**: `pnpm sightings` → `.claude/cerebro/scripts/retro-sightings`.
- **`agents/orchestrator.md:133`**: *"`pnpm sightings`, run from the atlantis-hud checkout"* — the
  named project goes with the command.
- **`agents/orchestrator.md:140-141`**: both example lines take the new path.
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:363`**: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/diskPreflight.ts` →
  `.claude/cerebro/scripts/disk-preflight`, keeping the trailing comment
  *"prints what it found; non-zero means do not start"*, which is the contract.

`project-conf`'s comment block gains two lines:

```
# disk_floor_gb  — GB of free disk below which a bead must not start. ABSENT means no disk preflight
#                  runs at all, and prune-worktrees.sh loses its pressure path.
```

### 6 — The application lets go

Second PR, in the application, with the submodule pointer bump:

- `.claude/cerebro-project.conf` gains `disk_floor_gb  8` — **8, matching
  `FREE_SPACE_FLOOR_GB` exactly.** Read it from the file rather than from this plan.
- Delete `scripts/retroSightings.ts`, `scripts/retroSightings.test.ts`, `scripts/diskPreflight.ts`,
  `scripts/diskPreflight.test.ts`.
- `package.json:11`'s `"sightings"` script: point it at the new path
  (`.claude/cerebro/scripts/retro-sightings`) so muscle memory survives, **or** delete it. Either is
  fine; pointing it is kinder and costs one line.
- **Grep for every other caller** before deleting: `grep -rn "diskPreflight\|retroSightings\|pnpm sightings" --exclude-dir=.git .`
  Expect hits in `docs/retrospectives/` — **leave those, they are history** — and in
  `.github/workflows/` or `tsconfig.tooling.json`, which are not.

## The test plan

cerebro's suites are shell: `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done`. CI runs every `tests/*.sh`
plus ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1.

**Increments 1 and 3 are written before the scripts they test and must be seen to fail.** For a port
this is not ceremony: the parser has at least three cases (`None found` counter-examples, wrapped
paragraphs, sub-bead suffixes) that a reimplementation-from-description silently loses, and the
existing Vitest suite is the only place they are written down.

**One extra check, worth its cost once:** run the old `pnpm sightings` and the new
`retro-sightings` against the **real corpus** and diff the findings. Same components, same counts.
Do this before deleting the TypeScript, and say in the PR what the diff showed. Fixture tests prove
the rules; this proves the port on the data that actually exists.

`pnpm run check:fast` before the application PR. Deleting the two test files reduces
`test:tooling`'s set — expected, and worth stating in the PR body so it does not read as coverage
quietly lost.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21 (`docs/ui/harness-scripts.html`), over two rounds.
**Decided; raise disagreements through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Where does `retroSightings.ts` go? | **Ported to bash + awk in cerebro**, as `scripts/retro-sightings` |
| 1a | Port first or test first? | **Tests ported first**, so the subtle parser cases are pinned before anything is rewritten |
| 2 | The disk preflight and the shared floor | **cerebro owns the check; the project declares the floor.** A bash `disk-preflight`, and `disk_floor_gb` as a project key that both it and `prune-worktrees.sh` read |

The navigator asked directly whether a bash/elisp migration was possible; the answer that decided it
was the dependency count above — **`awk` appears in 8 cerebro scripts and `node` in none** — so the
port adds no new dependency, while moving the file as JavaScript would have.

**Elisp was considered and rejected**, and the reason is worth keeping: Cerebro runs in a terminal,
and requiring `emacs --batch` for a CLI report would put an Emacs dependency on a path that has none.
The fleet view is the only thing that legitimately needs Emacs.

**Option ii for section 2 (an optional `preflight_cmd` hook) was declined.** A new consumer would get
no disk check unless they wrote one, and the disk floor is the most-cited cost in this repository's
history — eleven retrospectives name it.

## Out of scope

- **Changing the floor's value**, or when `prune-worktrees.sh` reclaims. That was `ah-90gu`, closed.
- **`scripts/project-conf` as code.** Adding keys needs no change to it.
- **The rest of `ah-qled.7`.** `.7.1` and `.7.3` are separate, planned beads.
- **Any other script in the application's `scripts/`.** Thirteen other tooling files live there and
  are genuinely this project's.
- **Changing what the sightings report says**, beyond what the port requires. The prose in
  `orchestrator.md:133-141` describing the output is not being rewritten.
- **`bd remember` / `bd recall`** as a mechanism, or the dismissal key's name.

## Validation

1. Every `tests/*.sh` in the submodule passes; cerebro's CI is green.
2. `pnpm run check:fast` passes in the application.
3. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/retro-sightings` run from the application prints the same findings, with
   the same counts, as `pnpm sightings` did before the change. **Diff them and record the result.**
4. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/retro-sightings --dismiss <bead>` silences that finding, and a dismissal
   made before the port is still in force after it.
5. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/disk-preflight` prints free space, the floor, and what is reclaimable;
   exits non-zero below the floor and zero above. Check both by temporarily overriding the floor.
6. In a checkout with no `disk_floor_gb` declared, `disk-preflight` exits **0** and prints nothing,
   and `prune-worktrees.sh` still runs with only its outer bound.
7. `grep -rn "diskPreflight\|retroSightings" --exclude-dir=.git .` returns only files under
   `docs/retrospectives/`.
8. `grep -rn "pnpm sightings" --exclude-dir=.git .claude/` returns nothing.
9. `prune-worktrees.sh` and `disk-preflight` agree on the boundary: at exactly the floor, both treat
   the disk as **too full**.

## Known traps

- **Two repositories, two PRs.** Branch and PR inside `.claude/cerebro`, merge, then the application
  PR bumps the pointer *and* does increment 6. **Do not delete the TypeScript before the cerebro PR
  merges** — validation item 3 needs both versions present to diff.
- **The `None found` trap is the single most losable behaviour in the port.** Nine files in the real
  corpus name bead ids inside a `None found` paragraph as *counter-examples*. Reading those as
  citations merges unrelated findings and the report quietly becomes wrong rather than failing.
  Increment 1's test for it is not optional.
- **Union-find, not pairwise grouping.** Citations are transitive; a chain of five beads about one
  cause must be one finding of five. Grouping by citation pair gives four findings and looks
  plausible.
- **`df -k`, never `df -h`.** `-h` rounds and its suffix varies by platform.
- **Strictly greater than the floor.** `hasHeadroom` is `freeGb > FREE_SPACE_FLOOR_GB` and
  `prune-worktrees.sh:229` explicitly notes the two must make the same test. Validation item 9 is the
  guard.
- **`roster`'s "no awk" rule is `roster`'s alone.** It exists because a test narrows `PATH` for the
  launch path. Do not generalise it to these two scripts — and equally, do not add `awk` to `roster`
  or `default-branch`.
- **The bead's line numbers may be stale**, as they were for `ah-qled.5.2`, `.5.3` and `.7.3` in this
  same file family. Find every passage by content.
- **`retroSightings.ts` shells out to `git` and `bd`.** The port must too; a pure-text
  reimplementation loses the dates and the dismissal state.
- **Deleting the two `.test.ts` files shrinks `test:tooling`.** Say so in the PR body. A silently
  smaller suite reads as coverage lost even when the coverage moved.
- **Disk space, with a sharp edge here.** Eleven retrospectives name the 8 GB floor. This bead
  rewrites the very thing that refuses to start a bead, so a mistake in `disk-preflight` either
  blocks every bead or lets one start on a disk that cannot build it. Safe offline reclaims:
  `~/.cargo/registry/src`, `target/debug/incremental`, `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every `tests/*.sh` in the submodule passes; cerebro's CI is green. `pnpm run check:fast` passes in the application.
- `.claude/cerebro/scripts/retro-sightings` prints the same findings, with the same counts, as `pnpm sightings` did before the change. The two are diffed against the real corpus and the result is recorded in the PR.
- `retro-sightings --dismiss <bead>` silences that finding, and a dismissal made before the port is still in force after it.
- `.claude/cerebro/scripts/disk-preflight` prints free space, the floor and what is reclaimable; exits non-zero below the floor and zero above. Both checked by overriding the floor.
- In a checkout with no `disk_floor_gb` declared, `disk-preflight` exits 0 and prints nothing, and `prune-worktrees.sh` still runs with only its outer bound.
- `grep -rn "diskPreflight\|retroSightings" --exclude-dir=.git .` returns only files under `docs/retrospectives/`.
- `grep -rn "pnpm sightings" --exclude-dir=.git .claude/` returns nothing.
- `prune-worktrees.sh` and `disk-preflight` agree on the boundary: at exactly the floor, both treat the disk as too full.
