title: An implementer in another project is told to run a command that does not exist
description:
The highest-impact single failure in the upstream audit (cerebro#58 §2), split out of ah-qled.7.

skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md names `pnpm run check:fast` as an imperative with NO FALLBACK. An implementer in a Python project runs it, fails, and has no instruction for what to do instead. 17 pnpm occurrences plus cargo fmt and cargo clippy in that one file: :85, :363, :405-421, :423-426, :518.

## Two keys, not two hook files
ah-qled.7 proposes executable hooks at `<consumer>/.cerebro/gate-fast` and `.cerebro/gate-full`. VERIFIED: `.gitignore:40` ignores `.cerebro/`, so those files vanish on a fresh clone and every agent on a new machine has no gate - the same failure ah-qled.1 rejects for project facts, and the third time this pattern has appeared in this epic.

Use `gate_fast` and `gate_full` keys in the TRACKED `.claude/cerebro-project.conf` that ah-qled.1 introduced, alongside `install` and `prewarm`. Same contract - exit 0 is green - with no new file, no executable bit and no PATH question. A consumer whose gate needs real logic points the key at a script, exactly as ah-qled.2 decided for `install`.

## What changes
- `gate_fast` / `gate_full` read through project-conf.
- The skill says "run the fast gate" and carries NO command. This alone removes every pnpm and cargo occurrence from implement-bead.
- launch-preflight refuses to start an IMPLEMENTER when no fast gate is configured or detectable - a loud immediate failure instead of an agent improvising. It already refuses on a missing agent file, so it is the natural place.
- Detection (package.json scripts, Makefile targets, cargo presence) is a convenience fallback only, NEVER a guess that runs unannounced - ah-qled.1's "detect, never guess" rule.
- :423-426 writes out atlantis-hud's entire CI path filter; that is `app_paths`, already a planned key.

atlantis-hud's own conf gains gate_fast and gate_full in the consumer PR.

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58 §2
design:
## Context

**The highest-impact single failure in the upstream audit** (`cerebro#58 §2`), split out of
ah-qled.7.

`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` names **`pnpm run check:fast` as an imperative with no fallback**.
An implementer in a Python project runs it, fails, and **has no instruction for what to do instead** —
so it improvises, which is the worst outcome available to an unattended agent.

**17 `pnpm` occurrences plus `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` in that one file**, concentrated at:

- `:85` — the state table, *"Building, before `pnpm run check:fast`"*
- `:363` — `pnpm exec tsx scripts/diskPreflight.ts` (**ah-qled.7.2's**, not this bead's)
- `:405-421` — *"Run **`pnpm run check:fast`** before opening the PR — lint, typecheck, the touched
  packages' unit tests, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`… not the browser suites"*
- `:423-426` — atlantis-hud's entire CI path filter, written out
- `:518` — `pnpm run test:smoke`, `test:pwa`, `test:native`

### 🔴 Two keys, not two hook files — the third time this trap has appeared

ah-qled.7 proposes executable hooks at `<consumer>/.cerebro/gate-fast` and `.cerebro/gate-full`.
**Verified: `.gitignore:40` ignores `.cerebro/`**, so those files vanish on a fresh clone and every
agent on a new machine has **no gate at all** — the same failure ah-qled.1 rejects for project facts,
and the third time this epic has proposed putting a project fact somewhere ignored (after ah-qled.5's
roster).

Use **`gate_fast` and `gate_full` keys in the tracked `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`** that ah-qled.1
introduced, beside `install` and `prewarm`. **The contract is identical — exit 0 is green** — with no
new file, no executable bit and no question about how the hook is found. A consumer whose gate needs
real logic **points the key at a script**, exactly as ah-qled.2 decided for `install`.

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. Two keys, read through the existing seam

```bash
gate_fast="$(project-conf gate_fast)"
gate_full="$(project-conf gate_full)"
```

The value is a **command line**, expanded unquoted at the point of use, with the same reasoning and
the same stated limitation ah-qled.2 established for `install` (`project-conf:42-45`). **Do not
reimplement that; follow it.**

### 2. Detection is a fallback, and never a silent one

`package.json` scripts, a `Makefile` target, `cargo` presence — **a convenience only**. ah-qled.1's
rule holds: *"Detect, never guess… Whichever branch is taken is printed."* A gate that was detected
rather than declared must **say so on stderr**, because an agent about to trust a green result should
know the harness chose the command.

### 3. The skill carries no command at all

`implement-bead/SKILL.md` says **"run the fast gate"** and **"run the full gate"**, and names neither
`pnpm` nor `cargo`. **This alone removes every `pnpm` and `cargo` occurrence from the file** except
`:363`, which is ah-qled.7.2's.

Two of the sites need more than a swap:

- **`:405-421` enumerates what the fast gate contains** — *"lint, typecheck, the touched packages'
  unit tests, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`. It is not the browser suites"*. That distinction —
  **a fast gate that is not everything, and a full gate that is** — is real and worth keeping, but it
  must be stated as *what the project declared each gate to be*, not as this project's contents.
- **`:423-426` writes out atlantis-hud's CI path filter.** That is **`app_paths`**, already on
  ah-qled.1's designed key list. Use it.
- **`:518`'s `test:smoke` / `test:pwa` / `test:native`** are for reproducing a flake. There is no
  third key for them; the honest move is to phrase it as *the full gate, or the project's own suite
  for the surface in question* rather than inventing `gate_smoke`.

### 4. A missing gate is a refusal, not an improvisation

`scripts/launch-preflight` already refuses to start a session on a missing agent file, and its
three-case block (`:88-100`) is the shape to follow: it distinguishes *a consumer-only role*, *a role
the consumer's roster declares but has no file for*, and *the submodule is behind* — and says which.

**Refuse to start an implementer when no fast gate is configured and none can be detected.** A loud,
immediate failure beats an agent improvising a gate and reporting green.

**Only an implementer.** A planner, a verifier or the orchestrator has no gate to run, and refusing
them would take the whole fleet down over a key that does not concern them. `roster --entry <Name>`
gives the kind.

### 5. atlantis-hud's own conf

The consumer PR adds `gate_fast pnpm run check:fast` and `gate_full pnpm run check` — **load-bearing,
not decorative**: without them this fleet's implementers would be refused at launch.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):**

1. **The gate is declared.**
   RED: `tests/` — a fabricated consumer with `gate_fast` set; the value is read whole, arguments
   included.
   GREEN: the reads.
2. **Detection is announced.**
   RED: with no key but a `package.json` carrying the script, the gate is detected **and a line says
   so**; with neither, nothing is returned.
   GREEN: the fallback.
3. **A missing gate refuses an implementer, and only an implementer.**
   RED: preflight refuses an implementer with no gate, **naming that as the cause**; it starts a
   planner unaffected.
   GREEN: the guard, following `:88-100`'s shape.
4. **The skill names no tool.**
   RED: `grep -nE "pnpm|cargo" skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` returns only `:363`.
   GREEN: the prose, including `app_paths` at `:423-426`.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the pin bump **and** `gate_fast` / `gate_full` in
`.claude/cerebro-project.conf`. **PR one merges first** — and note that **this pair must land
together**: a bumped submodule without the keys refuses every implementer at launch.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| a configured `gate_fast` is read whole | `tests/` | §1 |
| a detected gate **says it was detected** | same | ah-qled.1's rule |
| neither configured nor detectable → nothing | same | the refusal's input |
| **preflight refuses an implementer with no gate** | `tests/launch-preflight.sh` | §4 |
| **a planner with no gate still starts** | same | the kind guard |
| the refusal names the gate, not the submodule | same | ah-qled.5.1's lesson |
| **`grep -nE "pnpm\|cargo"` on the skill returns only `:363`** | same | the bead |
| every existing test | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `for t in tests/*.sh`.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing reaches a player. The navigator ranked the ah-qled family P1
on 2026-08-21.

**Decided here** (architecture): **two tracked keys rather than two hook files under the ignored
`.cerebro/`**, overriding the bead on ah-qled.1's own reasoning; **refusing only implementers**;
keeping the fast/full distinction as a declared property rather than an enumerated list of this
project's tools; and **not** inventing a third key for the smoke suites.

## Out of scope

- **`:363`'s disk preflight** and `retroSightings.ts` — **ah-qled.7.2**.
- **`release_cmd` and the orchestrator's release prose** — **ah-qled.7.3**.
- **What atlantis-hud's gates contain.** This bead makes them declarable.
- **A `gate_smoke` key.**

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -nE "pnpm|cargo" skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md    # only :363 may remain
```

Then by hand:

1. With `gate_fast` set in this repo's conf, start an implementer: it launches exactly as today.
   **This is the acceptance for the consumer we have.**
2. **Remove `gate_fast` and try to start an implementer.** It must be refused, with a message naming
   the missing gate — not the submodule, and not silence.
3. **With `gate_fast` still removed, start a planner.** It must launch. Put the key back.
4. In a scratch repo with a `package.json` but no conf, confirm the gate is **detected** and that a
   line on stderr says so.
5. Read `implement-bead/SKILL.md` as a stranger in a Python project: does it tell you what to run
   **without naming a tool you do not have?** If not, the prose is not fixed.
6. Confirm the fast/full distinction survives — the skill still says the fast gate is not everything
   and the full gate is.

## Known traps

- **🔴 Not under `.cerebro/`.** It is git-ignored; a gate hook there vanishes on a fresh clone and
  every agent on a new machine has none. This is the third time this epic has proposed it, and the
  third time the answer is the tracked conf.
- **The two PRs must land together in effect.** A bumped submodule in a consumer with no `gate_fast`
  **refuses every implementer at launch**. Say so in the PR, and add the keys in the same consumer PR
  as the bump.
- **Refuse implementers only.** A planner or verifier has no gate; refusing them takes the fleet down
  over a key that does not concern them.
- **A detected gate must announce itself.** An agent about to trust a green result should know the
  harness chose the command.
- **Expand the value unquoted**, as ah-qled.2 established — a gate is a command line, not a program.
- **Do not enumerate this project's tools in the new prose.** Replacing "pnpm run check:fast" with
  "the fast gate — lint, typecheck, cargo clippy…" fixes the command and keeps the coupling.
- **`:423-426` is `app_paths`**, a key ah-qled.1 already designed. Do not write a second one.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**
acceptance_criteria:
- `gate_fast` and `gate_full` are keys in the TRACKED .claude/cerebro-project.conf, NOT executable hooks under the git-ignored .cerebro/. The contract is exit 0 is green. A consumer needing logic points the key at a script, as ah-qled.2 decided for `install`.
- The values are command lines, expanded unquoted at the point of use, following ah-qled.2's reasoning and stated limitation (project-conf:42-45) rather than reimplementing it.
- Detection (package.json scripts, Makefile target, cargo presence) is a fallback only and ANNOUNCES ITSELF on stderr - ah-qled.1's "detect, never guess ... whichever branch is taken is printed".
- skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md says "run the fast gate" / "run the full gate" and names NO tool. `grep -nE "pnpm|cargo" skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` returns only :363, which is ah-qled.7.2's.
- The fast/full distinction survives, stated as what the project DECLARED each gate to be, not as an enumeration of this project's tools.
- :423-426's CI path filter uses the `app_paths` key ah-qled.1 already designed; no second key is written.
- No `gate_smoke` key is invented for :518.
- launch-preflight REFUSES to start an IMPLEMENTER when no fast gate is configured or detectable, naming the missing gate as the cause - following the three-case shape at :88-100. A planner, verifier or orchestrator with no gate still starts.
- The consumer PR adds `gate_fast pnpm run check:fast` and `gate_full pnpm run check` IN THE SAME PR as the pin bump - a bumped submodule without them refuses every implementer at launch.
- cerebro's suites pass.

title: Every agent starts the same way, and the docs stop naming a launcher that does not exist
description:
Split from ah-qled.5. Independent tidy-up; no consumer-facing behaviour depends on it.

- Seven run-* shims each hardcode one name. Generate them from the roster, or drop them for `launch <Name>`.
- scripts/run-implementer:25-33 still carries the Bishop -> Forge rename courtesy.
- scripts/implementer-state is a rename shim whose stated removal condition is a release of atlantis-hud - check whether that condition has now been met before removing it.
- tests/launchers.sh:127 asserts the literal name Forge is not an implementer; :210-219 hardcodes opus where the file's own model_of helper would answer; :454-481 pins `roster --entry Cypher` to an exact row, agents/reviewer.md to model: opus, and agents/architect.md to model: opus + effort: xhigh. Assert invariants, not values.

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58
design:
## Context

Split from the epic `ah-qled.5`, "A consumer can declare its own fleet, and the tests stop pinning
ours". Upstream: <https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58>.

**This bead is worked in the cerebro submodule, not in the application.** Every file it touches lives
under `.claude/cerebro/` (which is `rmstdope/cerebro`), except the documentation sweep in increment 4.
See *Known traps* for the two-repository dance that implies — it is not the usual one-PR cycle.

Four separate tidy-ups, all of them "this shared script still knows one fleet's names":

1. **Seven `run-*` shims**, each a single `exec launch <Name>` line, each explaining in its own
   comment that it exists *"because the docs and the navigator's fingers know it"*.
2. **`scripts/run-implementer:25-33`**, a courtesy message for the retired name Bishop.
3. **`scripts/implementer-state`**, a rename shim whose stated removal condition is "a release of
   atlantis-hud".
4. **`tests/launchers.sh`**, which pins this fleet's specific names and models where it means to
   assert a rule.

**Two facts found while planning changed the shape of the answer, and both are load-bearing:**

**The Emacs fleet view already does not use the shims.** `emacs/cerebro.el:1171-1174`:

```elisp
(defun cerebro--launch-command (agent)
  "The command that launches AGENT: `scripts/launch' and the agent's name,
for every kind - a role's launcher is no longer a fact this file knows."
  (list (cerebro--script "launch") (cerebro-agent-name agent)))
```

So the navigator's primary tool launches every agent by name through `launch`. The shims are only
ever typed by hand.

**And the documentation has already drifted off them.** `CLAUDE.md` tells the reader to run
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-bishop`, at **lines 176 and 189** — and that shim **does not exist**.
The architect was renamed Bishop → Forge and the shim became `run-forge`; the documentation never
followed. The shims are kept *so that the docs and the navigator's fingers keep working*, and the
docs stopped working a rename ago without anyone noticing.

That is the argument the navigator acted on, and it is a better one than "seven copies of one line".

**The removal condition for `implementer-state` is met**, verified rather than assumed: the rename
landed in cerebro on **2026-08-15** (`4b5b312`, `chore(ah-2n3.1)`), and atlantis-hud has since
tagged **v0.9.0** and **v0.10.0**. Nothing calls it anywhere except the test that exists to test it
(`tests/agent-state.sh:28,39,212`) and one line of `CLAUDE.md` prose describing it.

## Files to change and what to reuse

All paths are relative to `.claude/cerebro/` unless said otherwise.

**Deleted:** `scripts/run-beast`, `scripts/run-cypher`, `scripts/run-forge`,
`scripts/run-implementer`, `scripts/run-orchestrator`, `scripts/run-planner`,
`scripts/run-psylocke`, `scripts/run-user-feedback`, `scripts/implementer-state`.

**`scripts/launch`** — must answer everything the shims answered. It already takes an agent name and
is already what the fleet view calls; read it before changing anything, and change as little as
possible.

**`scripts/roster`** — **unchanged.** It is already the single table, and `--implementers`,
`--role` and `--entry` already answer everything the deleted shims asked it. Do not add a column,
and in particular do not add a "was" column for retired names — the navigator chose to drop the
Bishop courtesy rather than carry it forward.

**`tests/launchers.sh`** — the assertions in increment 3, and the removal of every test of a deleted
shim.

**`tests/agent-state.sh:28,39,212`** — the `implementer-state` symlink and its case go with the
script.

**`CLAUDE.md`** (cerebro's own) — the prose describing `implementer-state` and any launcher lines.

**In the application repository:** `CLAUDE.md` (7 launcher references, two of them the dead
`run-bishop`), `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (5), and the `.claude/agents/*.md` files that name a
`scripts/run-*` command — `architect.md`, `implementer.md`, `orchestrator.md`, `reviewer.md`,
`user-feedback.md`, `verifier.md`. **`.claude/agents/*.md` are symlinks into the submodule**
(`sync-symlinks.sh` maintains them), so edit the file in `.claude/cerebro/agents/` and the consumer's
link follows. Check with `readlink` before editing; do not write through a symlink into the wrong
repository.

## Increments

Each is a commit. Increments 1–3 are one PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`; increment 4 is a second PR
against the application. See *Known traps*.

### 1 — The shims go; `launch` answers for them

Delete the eight `scripts/run-*` files. Then make sure `launch` still answers the two questions
`run-implementer` answered:

- **`run-implementer --roster`** printed the implementer names. It did that by `exec`ing
  `roster --implementers`, which still exists and is what every caller should now use. Nothing to
  add to `launch`; just update the callers (`tests/launchers.sh`).
- **A name that is not on the roster.** `launch` must fail clearly, exit non-zero, and print the
  names that *are* available — read `roster` for them rather than listing any name in `launch`
  itself. If `launch` already does this, leave it alone and pin it with a test.

**Deliberately not carried forward** (both navigator decisions):

- **The Bishop → Forge courtesy.** `launch Bishop` now says Bishop is not on the roster, with the
  list of names that are. The rename was 2026-08-15 and the shim carrying the courtesy was already
  unreachable from the documentation.
- **`run-implementer`'s guard against `run-implementer Forge`.** That guard exists because
  `run-implementer` *promises* an implementer and Forge is not one. `launch Forge` promises Forge and
  delivers Forge, so there is no broken promise left to guard. Removing it is the point, not an
  oversight — do not reintroduce it in `launch` as a "kind" check.

### 2 — `implementer-state` goes

Delete `scripts/implementer-state`. Remove its symlink and its case from `tests/agent-state.sh`
(lines 28, 39 and 212 at the time of writing — **find them by content**, see *Known traps*). Remove
the sentence in cerebro's `CLAUDE.md` describing the shim's existence and its removal condition.

Before deleting, re-run the check rather than trusting this plan:

```bash
git -C .claude/cerebro log -1 --format=%ci $(git -C .claude/cerebro log --format=%H -- scripts/implementer-state | tail -1)
git tag --sort=-creatordate | head -3          # in the application repository
grep -rn "implementer-state" --exclude-dir=.git .
```

The condition is "a release of atlantis-hud after the rename". If the first command shows a date
before the newest tag's, it is met. It was met when this plan was written; confirm it still is.

### 3 — The tests assert rules, not this fleet's values

`tests/launchers.sh`. In each case the assertion stays and only what it compares against changes:
**derive the expected value from the roster or the agent file, so a consumer with a different fleet
passes the same suite.**

| what it does today | what it should assert |
|---|---|
| `roster --implementers` output is grepped for the literal `Forge` and fails if present | No name whose roster **role is not `implementer`** appears in `--implementers`. Derive the interactive names from `roster` itself, exactly as the two assertions immediately above it already derive `expected_implementers` with `awk` |
| `roster --entry Cypher` compared to the literal `Cypher\treviewer\tinteractive` | For **whatever name the roster gives for the `reviewer` role**, `--entry <name>` returns three tab-separated fields whose second is `reviewer` and whose third is the kind `kind_of` would give. The invariant is the shape and the derivation, not the name |
| `agents/reviewer.md` grepped for the literal line `model: opus` | The file exists and declares **a** `model:` line with a non-empty value |
| `agents/architect.md` grepped for `model: opus` and `effort: xhigh` | The file exists and declares a non-empty `model:` and a non-empty `effort:` |

**Do not use the existing `model_of` helper for the last two.** `model_of` reads the agent file, so
asserting the file's model *through* it is circular and asserts nothing. `model_of` is the right tool
where the test compares a *launched* flag against the declared value (it is already used that way);
it is the wrong tool for "the file declares one at all".

Delete every test of a deleted shim — the `run-implementer Cyclops` / `storm` / `bishop` / `Forge` /
`--roster` cases. Where one of them was testing something real that only `run-implementer` exposed,
**re-express it against `launch`** rather than dropping the coverage:

- `run-implementer Cyclops sets BEADS_ACTOR=Cyclops` → `launch Cyclops` sets it. This is a real
  invariant and must survive.
- The lower-case-name cases (`run-implementer storm`) tested name handling; keep the equivalent
  against `launch` if `launch` has an opinion about case, and drop them if it does not.

Add one new case: **`launch` with a name that is not on the roster exits non-zero and names the
roster's own names.** That is increment 1's contract, and nothing tests it today.

### 4 — The documentation stops naming scripts that do not exist

A second PR, against the **application** repository.

- **`CLAUDE.md`**: the seven launcher lines (46, 68, 103, 121, 152, 176, 189) become
  `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch <Name>`. **Lines 176 and 189 say `run-bishop`, which has never
  existed since the rename** — they become `launch Forge`. The navigator chose to fix this here
  rather than as its own bead, because this sweep touches those lines regardless.
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`**: the same five commands.
- **`agents/*.md` in the submodule**: `architect.md`, `implementer.md`, `orchestrator.md`,
  `reviewer.md`, `user-feedback.md`, `verifier.md` each name a `scripts/run-*` in their "Started by"
  line. These belong to increment 1's PR, not this one — they are submodule files. Listed here only
  so the sweep is complete; **do not edit them through the consumer's symlinks.**
- Grep for stragglers before finishing:
  `grep -rn "scripts/run-" --exclude-dir=.git .` in both repositories. **Retrospectives under
  `docs/retrospectives/` are history and are left exactly as they are** — they describe what was true
  when they were written.

## The test plan

cerebro's suites are shell: `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` from the submodule root, or
`bash tests/launchers.sh` for one. CI runs every `tests/*.sh` plus ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1.

**Run the whole suite, not only `launchers.sh`** — increment 2 touches `agent-state.sh` and
increment 1 deletes files other suites may reference.

`tests/launchers.sh` builds fabricated consumer repositories in temp directories (see the block at
its line ~455). The changed assertions in increment 3 must pass against **both** the built-in roster
and a fabricated consumer roster; the file already has a consumer fixture with `Ada`, `Grace`,
`Hopper`, `Turing`, `Lovelace` — **use it**, because a test that only passes against the X-Men is the
exact defect this bead exists to remove.

Nothing in the application's own suites is affected, but run `pnpm run check:fast` before the second
PR anyway: it is what gates the merge.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21 (`docs/ui/launchers.html`). **Decided; raise disagreements
through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What replaces the seven shims? | **Drop them — `launch <Name>` only.** The roster becomes the single place a fleet is declared, and a consumer adds a role by adding one roster line |
| 2 | Naming: `run-planner` starts Xavier, not Beast | **Everything by agent name.** Under decision 1 this comes free: `launch` takes agent names only, so the role/agent inconsistency disappears rather than being maintained |
| 3 | The Bishop → Forge courtesy message | **Dropped.** `launch Bishop` says Bishop is not on the roster, with the names that are |
| 4 | `CLAUDE.md` documents `run-bishop`, which does not exist | **Fixed in this bead**, as part of the sweep that rewrites those lines anyway |

The navigator's own framing, worth keeping in view while doing it: *"the different names that can be
used is defined in the roster so that scripts keep as generic as possible."* Anything this bead adds
that names an agent, a role or a model outside `scripts/roster` and `agents/*.md` is going the wrong
way.

## Out of scope

- **`scripts/roster` itself.** Making the table overridable is `ah-qled.5.1`, which is planned and
  separate. This bead consumes the roster; it does not change it.
- **`scripts/agent-state`'s closed phase vocabulary.** That is `ah-qled.5.2`.
- **The `emacs/` fleet view.** It already calls `launch` and needs no change. If it turns out to
  reference a deleted shim anywhere, that is in scope — but the launch path does not.
- **Adding a `was`/alias column to the roster.** Considered and declined (decision 3).
- **Any new guard in `launch` about agent kind.** Declined deliberately (increment 1).
- **Retrospectives under `docs/retrospectives/`.** History, left alone.
- **Renaming any agent or role.**

## Validation

1. Every `tests/*.sh` in the submodule passes, and cerebro's CI is green.
2. `pnpm run check:fast` passes in the application.
3. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch Xavier` starts Xavier; `launch Cyclops` starts Cyclops;
   `launch Forge` starts Forge as the architect.
4. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch Bishop` exits non-zero and prints the roster's names.
5. `ls .claude/cerebro/scripts/run-*` finds nothing, and `scripts/implementer-state` is gone.
6. Starting an implementer from the Emacs fleet view (`s`) still works — **check this by hand**; it
   is the navigator's primary tool and no automated test covers the vterm path.
7. `grep -rn "scripts/run-" --exclude-dir=.git .` in both repositories returns only files under
   `docs/retrospectives/`.
8. `grep -rn "run-bishop" --exclude-dir=.git .` returns only files under `docs/retrospectives/`.
9. `tests/launchers.sh` passes against the fabricated consumer roster as well as the built-in one —
   i.e. no assertion in it names an X-Man.

## Known traps

- **This is two repositories and two PRs.** The submodule is `rmstdope/cerebro`; the application is
  `rmstdope/atlantis-hud`. Increments 1–3 are a branch and PR **inside `.claude/cerebro`**, reviewed
  and merged there first. Only then does the application get a second commit bumping the submodule
  pointer (`chore: bump cerebro`) together with increment 4's documentation sweep. **Do not commit a
  submodule pointer bump before the cerebro PR is merged** — it would point the application at a
  branch that may not survive review.
- **The bead's line numbers are from a specific commit and may already be stale.** `run-implementer:25-33`,
  `tests/launchers.sh:127`, `:210-219`, `:454-481` — **find each by content**, not by number. One of
  them (`:210-219`, described as hardcoding `opus`) does not match what is at those lines today,
  which is the consumer-roster fixture; the `opus`/`xhigh` pins are near line 598 and 616. Trust the
  descriptions, not the addresses.
- **`.claude/agents/*.md` are symlinks into the submodule.** `readlink` before editing. Writing
  through one puts a submodule change in the application's diff, where it will be lost at the next
  `sync-symlinks.sh`.
- **`launch` is what the Emacs fleet view calls.** A regression here does not break a script, it
  breaks the navigator's window onto the whole fleet, and no test covers the vterm path. Validation
  item 6 is manual on purpose.
- **`roster` is bash 3.2, builtins only** — no `awk`, `grep`, `cut`, `tr`, no `declare -A`; its own
  header says so, and one test deliberately narrows `PATH` to `dirname` and `bash`. **`launch` may
  have the same constraint**: read its header before adding a command to it. The *tests* may use
  `awk` freely — they already do.
- **Do not assert a fleet's values through `model_of`.** It reads the agent file, so using it to
  check the agent file asserts nothing. Increment 3 says where it is and is not the right tool.
- **`BEADS_ACTOR` is real coverage.** It is currently tested only through `run-implementer`. Deleting
  that test without re-expressing it against `launch` silently drops the guarantee that an
  implementer's bead writes are attributed to it.
- **Deleting a shim is easy to under-grep.** A shim name appears in prose, in tests, in agent
  definitions and in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Validation items 7 and 8 are the sweep;
  run them in **both** repositories.

title: A fleet's own extra role cannot report what it is doing at all
description:
Split from ah-qled.5.

scripts/agent-state:22-29 fixes the phase vocabulary as a closed union naming roles by agent name ("triage plan (a planner: Xavier, Beast)", "daily weekly (Forge)"), enforced at :108 as a literal case that EXITS 2 on an unknown phase. A consumer-added role therefore cannot report state at all. The comment at :30-32 already concedes the vocabulary is not checked per role, so the whitelist buys little and costs extensibility.

Either drop the whitelist to a shape check, or read it from the same consumer source ah-qled.5.1 introduces.

## cerebro--phases is NOT dead - checked
ah-qled.5 speculates it "may simply be dead, in which case delete it". Verified: it is defined at emacs/cerebro.el:326 and used nowhere else in the elisp - but tests/launchers.sh:471 asserts every phase a shipped agent file uses appears in it. So it is unused CODE but a live CHECK, keeping agent-state's vocabulary and the elisp in step. Deleting it silently removes that guard. Whatever happens to the whitelist, cerebro--phases must move with it (tests/launchers.sh:466-472 already pins the two together).

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58
design:
## Context

Split from the epic `ah-qled.5`, "A consumer can declare its own fleet, and the tests stop pinning
ours". Upstream: <https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58>. Depends on `ah-qled.5.1`, which is
**closed** — its consumer-roster mechanism is already on `main` and is described below because this
bead was asked to consider following it.

**This bead is worked in the cerebro submodule, not in the application.** Every file it touches lives
under `.claude/cerebro/` (which is `rmstdope/cerebro`). See *Known traps* for the two-repository
dance.

Every agent reports what it is doing with `scripts/agent-state <Name> working --phase <word>`, and
the fleet view shows that word in its **State** column. Two places hold the vocabulary:

- **`scripts/agent-state`** — eighteen words in a literal `case`, which **exits 2** on anything else.
- **`emacs/cerebro.el`** — the same eighteen in `defconst cerebro--phases`.

and `tests/launchers.sh` asserts they agree.

**The cost.** A consumer of cerebro that adds a role of its own invents a phase word for it, and that
role **cannot report state at all**: every `agent-state` call exits 2, so it never appears as working
in the fleet view. A shared submodule refusing to record a consumer's own role is the reuse blocker
the epic is about.

**What the closed list actually buys, which is less than it looks.** `agent-state`'s own comment
concedes it:

> The vocabulary is not checked per-role — any of the words above is accepted from any name, the
> same trade cerebro.el's `cerebro--phases` makes: a wrong word in the State column is not worth a
> per-role table in bash.

So an implementer may report `weekly` and a planner `merge`, and nothing complains. The only thing
the refusal catches is a **typo** — `--phase plna`. That is the whole of what is being weighed
against a consumer role being able to report at all, and the navigator weighed it (decision 1).

**`cerebro--phases` is not dead, and the bead is right to say so** — verified at the current HEAD
rather than taken on trust. It is defined at `emacs/cerebro.el:344` and read by no other elisp, but
`tests/launchers.sh` (near line 604) asserts a set of phase words appears both in `agent-state`'s
`case` and in `cerebro--phases`. It is unused *code* holding a live *check*.

## What A and i mean together, and what the guard becomes

The navigator chose **A** (drop the refusal to a shape check) and **i** (keep the guard). Taken
literally those pull against each other, and the mockup said so: once `agent-state` accepts any
lower-case word, "every phase a shipped agent uses is one `agent-state` accepts" is vacuous.

**The guard therefore changes what it asserts, and this is the central design decision of the bead.**
It stops being a legality check and becomes a **documentation-completeness check**:

> Every phase word any shipped agent definition or skill actually instructs an agent to use appears
> in `cerebro--phases`.

That is not vacuous, it is what the check was really buying, and it now bites on the failure that can
still happen: **an agent starts using a new phase word and nobody writes it down**, so the fleet
view's reference list and the fleet's actual behaviour drift apart.

Two facts make it implementable and generic, both verified:

- The words are **derivable from the shipped files**. `grep -oh -- "--phase [a-z][a-z-]*" agents/*.md
  skills/*/SKILL.md | sort -u` returns exactly eighteen words at HEAD — `build check ci daily gate
  merge plan prepare read rebase release report review sweep triage verify walk weekly` — which is
  precisely the list in both places.
- The current test **hardcodes four of them** (`read check walk report`, Cypher's). Deriving them
  instead is the epic's own instruction, "assert invariants, not values", applied here.

`cerebro--phases` survives as **the reference list**, in one place, with `agent-state`'s comment
pointing at it rather than restating it.

## Files to change and what to reuse

All paths relative to `.claude/cerebro/`.

**`scripts/agent-state`** — the `case` at ~line 108 becomes a shape check; the comment block at
~lines 22–32 stops being the vocabulary's home and points at `cerebro--phases`.

**`emacs/cerebro.el`** — `cerebro--phases` (line 344) **stays**, and its docstring gains one sentence
saying it is now the reference list rather than a mirror of an enforced one. **Do not delete it** and
do not let its by-role reference paragraph go: it is the only prose anywhere saying which words
belong to which role.

**`tests/launchers.sh`** — the phases case (near line 604) rewritten per *Increments*.

**`tests/agent-state.sh`** — gains the new acceptance and rejection cases. The existing
`an-implementer-name-can-use-a-role-phase-word-too` case (near line 268) **stays exactly as it is**;
it pins the union-not-per-role trade, which this bead does not change.

Reuse, and do not re-implement:

- **`scripts/roster`'s consumer-file pattern** — read it (lines ~68–110) before deciding anything.
  It is the shape a consumer-declared vocabulary would have taken. **This bead deliberately does not
  use it** (decision 1 chose A over C); it is named here so the implementer does not reinvent option
  C on the grounds that it looks consistent.
- **`agent-state`'s existing `case` for `state`** (idle|working|asking|waiting|done) — **unchanged.**
  Only the *phase* vocabulary opens up. The state vocabulary is a closed set that `cerebro.el`
  genuinely switches on, and opening it would break the fleet view's rendering.

## Increments

Each is a commit; all three are one PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`.

### 1 — `agent-state` accepts any well-formed phase

Replace the eighteen-way `case` with a shape check. The shape, exactly:

- One or more characters, all of `a-z`, `0-9` or `-`.
- Must start with a letter `a-z`.
- Must not end with `-`.

```bash
case "$phase" in
  [a-z]*[!a-z0-9-]*|*-) bad=1 ;;
  [a-z]|[a-z]*)         bad=0 ;;
  *)                    bad=1 ;;
esac
```

**Write it however is clearest in bash 3.2 with builtins only** — the sketch above is a shape, not a
prescription, and a `[[ "$phase" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ ]]` is fine if `agent-state` is not under
`roster`'s no-external-commands constraint (check its header; `roster`'s constraint is `roster`'s).
What matters is the rule and the message:

```
agent-state: phase 'Plan Bead' is not a phase word (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; see cerebro--phases in emacs/cerebro.el for the ones this fleet uses)
```

Exit 2, as today, for a **malformed** word. A well-formed unknown word is accepted silently — no
warning, because the navigator chose A over B precisely so that a consumer's own role does not warn
on every call forever.

The comment block at ~22–32 loses its list and gains a pointer:

```bash
# <phase>, only meaningful with `working` or `asking`, is any lower-case word: letters, digits and
# hyphens, starting with a letter. It is NOT a closed set - a consumer that adds a role of its own
# invents a word for it and this script must record it, which is what the old eighteen-way case
# prevented (ah-qled.5.2).
#
# The words THIS fleet uses are listed once, in `cerebro--phases' (emacs/cerebro.el), together with
# which role each belongs to. That list is a reference rather than a gate: the vocabulary is not
# checked per role - any word is accepted from any name - so a wrong word in the State column is
# still not worth a per-role table in bash.
```

**Do not restate the eighteen words here.** One reference list is the point; two is what this bead
is undoing.

Tests, in `tests/agent-state.sh`:

- `--phase index` (a word cerebro does not ship) is accepted and lands in the file as `index`. This
  is the bead's whole promise — write it first, red.
- `--phase plan` still works, and `--phase triage` from an implementer name still works (the
  existing case).
- `--phase 'Plan Bead'`, `--phase Plan`, `--phase -plan`, `--phase plan-`, `--phase ''` and
  `--phase 2plan` each exit 2.
- `--phase deep-clean` (hyphenated, well-formed) is accepted.
- `--phase` with any `state` other than `working`/`asking` still exits 2 — unchanged behaviour, worth
  re-pinning since the surrounding code moves.

### 2 — `cerebro--phases` becomes the reference list

`emacs/cerebro.el:344`. The list itself does not change. The docstring's first paragraph changes from
describing a mirror to describing a reference:

> The phase vocabulary this fleet uses.
>
> `scripts/agent-state` no longer enforces it — any lower-case word is accepted, so that a consumer
> adding a role of its own can report state at all (ah-qled.5.2). This list is what *these* agents
> use, kept in step with them by `tests/launchers.sh`, and it is the only place saying which words
> belong to which role.

Keep the by-role paragraph exactly as it is.

**Nothing in the elisp switches on this list**, before or after — the State column renders whatever
word the state file carries. So a consumer's `index` shows up correctly in the fleet view with no
elisp change at all. **Verify that claim** rather than trusting it: grep for `cerebro--phases` and
confirm the only reader is the test.

### 3 — The guard, rewritten to derive rather than pin

`tests/launchers.sh`, replacing the case near line 604 that hardcodes `read check walk report`.

```bash
# Every phase word a shipped agent or skill actually tells an agent to use must be in the fleet
# view's reference list. `agent-state` no longer refuses an unknown word (ah-qled.5.2), so this is
# no longer a legality check - it is a drift check, and the drift it catches is real: an agent that
# starts using a new phase and never says so leaves `cerebro--phases' describing a fleet that has
# moved on, and that list is the only prose saying which words belong to which role.
used="$(grep -oh -- '--phase [a-z][a-z0-9-]*' "$repo_root"/agents/*.md "$repo_root"/skills/*/SKILL.md \
        | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u)"
[[ -n "$used" ]] || fail "phase drift: found no --phase words at all - the grep has stopped matching"
while IFS= read -r phase; do
  grep -q "\"$phase\"" "$repo_root/emacs/cerebro.el" \
    || fail "emacs/cerebro.el: phase '$phase' is used by an agent file but missing from cerebro--phases"
done <<<"$used"
pass "every phase a shipped agent uses is in cerebro--phases"
```

Three things about that:

- **The `[[ -n "$used" ]]` guard is not decoration.** A test that greps for something and asserts a
  property of every hit passes silently and forever the day the grep stops matching — which is how
  this rewrite could quietly become worthless. It must fail loudly instead.
- **`grep -q "\"$phase\""` is the existing test's own matching** and is deliberately loose: it finds
  the word anywhere in the elisp, not only in the list. That was acceptable when it was one of two
  checks and it is acceptable now; tightening it to the `defconst` block is optional and needs the
  block located without a multi-line regex in bash 3.2. Leave it loose rather than getting clever.
- **`skills/*/SKILL.md` must be in the glob.** Several phase words appear only in skill files, not in
  `agents/*.md`. A glob that misses them shrinks the derived set and weakens the check without
  failing.

**Drop the half of the old case that greps `agent-state` for `|$phase|`.** It asserted the word was
in the `case` that increment 1 deletes; there is no `case` to be in, and keeping a grep against a
removed construct would fail for the right reason at the wrong time.

Add one new case, which is what stops the shape check silently widening:

- `agent-state`'s rejection message and the shape rule are pinned by `tests/agent-state.sh`
  (increment 1). `launchers.sh` additionally asserts **`cerebro--phases` still exists and is
  non-empty** — under A there is nothing forcing it to, and an empty reference list would pass every
  other assertion in this file.

## The test plan

cerebro's suites are shell: `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` from the submodule root, or one
at a time. CI runs every `tests/*.sh` plus ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1.

**Run the whole suite**, not only the two files changed — `agent-state` is called by every launcher
test fixture.

`tests/agent-state.sh` builds fabricated consumer roots (`new_fixture`, `run_state`, `state_file`);
increment 1's cases go there and use those helpers rather than new machinery.

The elisp change is a docstring, so ERT has nothing new to assert — but run it anyway, because a
malformed docstring is a byte-compile warning and CI treats those seriously.

Nothing in the application's own suites is affected.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21 (`docs/ui/phase-vocabulary.html`). **Decided; raise
disagreements through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What replaces the closed list of eighteen words? | **A — a shape check.** Any lower-case word is accepted. A consumer's role works the day it is written, with nothing to declare. The cost, accepted: a typo reaches the State column instead of failing at the call |
| 2 | `cerebro--phases`, unused elisp holding a live test | **i — keep the guard, rewritten.** It stops asserting legality and starts asserting that the reference list has not drifted from what the shipped agents actually use |

**Option B (warn, do not refuse) was declined**, and the reason matters to the implementation: a
consumer's own role would warn on every single call, forever. So increment 1 accepts an unknown
well-formed word **silently**. Do not add a "helpful" warning back.

**Option C (a consumer file, like the roster) was declined** even though it matches
`ah-qled.5.1`'s pattern. Consistency was not judged worth a second config file for eighteen words,
plus an elisp reader for it.

## Out of scope

- **`scripts/roster`** and the consumer-roster mechanism. That was `ah-qled.5.1`, closed.
- **The `run-*` launcher shims.** That is `ah-qled.5.3`, planned separately.
- **`agent-state`'s `state` vocabulary** (idle|working|asking|waiting|done). Closed on purpose —
  `cerebro.el` switches on these — and untouched.
- **Per-role phase checking.** Explicitly rejected by the existing design and not revisited here; the
  union-not-per-role test stays.
- **A consumer-declared phase list**, in any form. Declined (decision 1).
- **Deleting `cerebro--phases`.** Declined (decision 2).
- **Any change to how the fleet view renders the State column.**

## Validation

1. Every `tests/*.sh` in the submodule passes, and cerebro's CI is green (shell suites plus ERT on
   both Emacs versions).
2. `scripts/agent-state Archivist working --phase index --pid $$` succeeds and writes
   `"phase": "index"` into the state file — the bead's whole point, checked by hand once.
3. `scripts/agent-state Xavier working --phase 'Plan Bead' --pid $$` exits 2 with a message naming
   the shape rule and pointing at `cerebro--phases`.
4. `scripts/agent-state Xavier working --phase plan --pid $$` still works, and Xavier still shows as
   `plan` in the fleet view.
5. An agent whose state file carries a phase cerebro does not ship renders that word in the fleet
   view's State column without complaint.
6. `grep -c '"' ` on the `cerebro--phases` block still finds eighteen words — the list was not
   accidentally emptied while its enforcement was removed.
7. Adding `--phase index` to a shipped agent file makes `tests/launchers.sh` **fail** until `index`
   is added to `cerebro--phases`. Check this by hand, then revert: it is the only proof the rewritten
   guard actually bites, and increment 3 is worthless without it.

## Known traps

- **This is two repositories.** The submodule is `rmstdope/cerebro`; branch and PR **inside
  `.claude/cerebro`**, get it merged there, and only then bump the submodule pointer in the
  application with a `chore: bump cerebro` commit. Do not commit a pointer bump before the cerebro PR
  merges.
- **The bead's line numbers are stale.** `agent-state:22-29`, `:108`, `:30-32`,
  `emacs/cerebro.el:326`, `tests/launchers.sh:466-472` and `:471` were taken at an earlier commit;
  `cerebro--phases` is at **344** today and the phases test is near **604**. **Find everything by
  content.** `ah-qled.5.3`'s plan hit the same problem in the same file.
- **A guard that greps must fail when the grep stops matching.** Increment 3's `[[ -n "$used" ]]` is
  the whole difference between a drift check and a test that passes forever having asserted nothing.
- **`skills/*/SKILL.md` carries phase words that `agents/*.md` does not.** Verified: the eighteen only
  come out complete when both globs are searched.
- **Do not restate the vocabulary in `agent-state`'s comment.** Two lists is what this bead removes;
  the pointer to `cerebro--phases` is the replacement, not a supplement.
- **Do not add a warning for an unknown phase.** Option B was declined for a stated reason
  (*User-facing decisions*), and a warning is exactly what B was.
- **`agent-state` may be under a no-external-commands constraint.** `roster`'s header states one, and
  `tests/launchers.sh` narrows `PATH` to `dirname` and `bash` for a launcher test. **Read
  `agent-state`'s own header before reaching for `grep` or `sed`** in it; the tests may use `awk` and
  `grep` freely, and increment 3 does.
- **The `state` case sits next to the `phase` case.** They look alike and only one of them opens up.
  Changing both would let `agent-state` write a state the fleet view cannot render.
- **Disk space.** Eleven of the application's retrospectives name `scripts/diskPreflight.ts` refusing
  to start a bead below its 8 GB floor. It does not apply to the submodule's shell suites, but it
  will apply to `pnpm run check:fast` before the pointer-bump PR. Safe offline reclaims:
  `~/.cargo/registry/src`, `target/debug/incremental`, `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache`.
close_reason: Delivered in rmstdope/cerebro#77, pointer bumped in PR #530

title: A consumer cannot name its own fleet without editing a shared submodule
description:
The core reuse blocker of ah-qled.5, split out because that bead is several passes of work.

## What
scripts/roster keeps its TABLE= heredoc as the fallback and gains a consumer source. Agent files resolve from the consumer first with the submodule as fallback, and launch-preflight stops misdiagnosing a consumer-supplied role as "the submodule is behind" (launch-preflight:87).

## The location is NOT what ah-qled.5 proposed
ah-qled.5 says `<consumer>/.cerebro/roster`. Verified: `.gitignore:40` ignores `.cerebro/`, so that file VANISHES ON A FRESH CLONE and every new machine silently falls back to cerebro's X-Men - the exact failure ah-qled.1 rejects for project facts ("how a project installs itself ... are facts every clone needs"). Which agents exist is a project fact, not a personal preference; how many are running is already measured from live pids and is not in this file.

So: a TRACKED path, beside ah-qled.1's `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`. Same TSV shape as the built-in TABLE.

## Tests move with it
tests/launchers.sh:260-261 duplicates the roster as two parallel arrays - the drift scripts/roster exists to prevent, reintroduced in its own suite. Rewrite to invariants: every roster row has an agent file whose frontmatter parses; names come from `roster --implementers | head -n N` rather than being spelled out. tests/launchers.sh:101-110 already demonstrates the pattern. Also tests/agent-alive.sh:107-119 (needs Beast present and Beastly absent) and tests/agent-state.sh:387 (ten specific implementer names).

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58
design:
## Context

**Split out of ah-qled.5**, which was several passes of work in one bead. This is its core reuse
blocker; `.5.2` (the phase vocabulary, blocked on this) and `.5.3` (the launcher shims) are the rest.

`scripts/roster` holds the whole fleet as a `TABLE=` heredoc **inside the submodule** (`:39-59`). A
consumer wanting different names, more implementers, or a role cerebro does not ship must edit a file
shared with every other consumer. That is exactly the problem `.cerebro/models.conf` was created to
solve for models.

The roster is generic in *content* — the X-Men are cerebro's branding — but **not overridable**,
which is the blocker.

### Two corrections to ah-qled.5, both checked

**🔴 The location it proposes does not survive a clone.** ah-qled.5 says
`<consumer>/.cerebro/roster`. Verified: `.gitignore:40` ignores `.cerebro/`, so that file is
**git-ignored**, vanishes on a fresh clone, and every new machine silently falls back to cerebro's
X-Men with nothing said. That is precisely the failure **ah-qled.1** rejects for project facts —
*"how a project installs itself … are facts every clone needs"*. **Which agents exist is a project
fact.** How many are *running* is measured from live pids and is not in this file at all.

So: a **tracked** path, beside ah-qled.1's `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`.

**The agent-file half is nearly done already.** `<consumer>/.claude/agents/` exists, is **tracked**,
and its entries are symlinks into the submodule:

```
.claude/agents/planner.md -> ../cerebro/agents/planner.md
```

So resolving agent files from the consumer's directory handles shipped roles **and** consumer roles
with no fallback logic: a shipped role is a symlink that lands in the submodule, a consumer role is a
real file.

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. `scripts/roster` reads a consumer file — with no new dependencies

```
<consumer>/.claude/cerebro-roster
```

Same shape as the built-in `TABLE`: `NAME  ROLE` per line, `#` comments and blank lines ignored,
`KIND` still derived by `kind_of`. `print_all` (`:70-82`) already parses exactly that with pure
builtins — **feed it the file's contents instead of `$TABLE` when the file exists and is non-empty.**

**It replaces the table; it does not merge with it.** File order is load-bearing — `plan-bead` gives
the P4 triage pass to *the first planner listed*, and Cerebro picks the next unused implementer name
in file order — and a merge makes that order ambiguous.

**🔴 The constraint that decides how the path is found.** `roster` today needs **no external command
at all**, and `tests/launchers.sh:412-422` runs a launcher with `PATH` containing only `dirname` and
`bash`, because that is *"the one external command a launcher needs before it even"* reaches
`claude`. **So `roster` must not start calling `consumer-root`**, which shells out to `git`.

Resolve the consumer root by **path arithmetic** instead. `roster` lives at
`<consumer>/.claude/cerebro/scripts/roster`, so:

```bash
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
consumer="$(cd "$here/../../.." && pwd)"
```

`dirname` and `cd` only — allowed by that test, and no `git`. **Say in a comment that this is
deliberately not `consumer-root`**, and why, or the next reader will "tidy" it into the seam and
break the narrowed-PATH test with no idea what they broke.

### 2. Agent files resolve from the consumer — `scripts/launch:77-79`

```bash
agents_dir="$here/../agents"     # the submodule, today
```

Prefer `<consumer>/.claude/agents/$role.md` and fall back to the submodule's. Because the shipped
roles are already symlinks there, **the consumer path alone answers both cases** — but keep the
fallback for a consumer whose symlinks have not been synced.

`launch` may use `awk` here; it is past the point the narrowed-PATH test covers.

### 3. Preflight stops misdiagnosing — `scripts/launch-preflight:87`

It currently refuses a consumer-supplied role with *"the submodule is behind"*, which names the wrong
cause. Distinguish **"cerebro does not ship this role, and the consumer has no
`.claude/agents/<role>.md` either"** from **"the submodule is behind"**, and say which.

### 4. The tests assert invariants, not this fleet

- **`tests/launchers.sh:260-261` duplicates the roster as two parallel arrays** — the drift
  `scripts/roster` exists to prevent, reintroduced inside its own suite. Derive from
  `roster --implementers` instead.
- `tests/agent-alive.sh:107-119` needs `Beast` present *and* `Beastly` absent — take a name from
  `roster --role planner | head -n 1` and append a suffix for the absent one.
- `tests/agent-state.sh:387` needs ten specific implementer names — `roster --implementers | head -n 10`.

**`tests/launchers.sh:101-110` already demonstrates the pattern**; follow it rather than inventing
one.

**New tests**: a consumer roster replaces the built-in; a missing one falls back; `#` and blank lines
are ignored; **file order is preserved**; and **`roster` still works with `PATH` narrowed to
`dirname` and `bash`**.

### 5. Not in this bead

`agent-state`'s phase whitelist (**ah-qled.5.2**), and the run-* shims, the Bishop courtesy and
`implementer-state` (**ah-qled.5.3**).

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):**

1. **A consumer roster is read.**
   RED: `tests/launchers.sh` — a fabricated consumer with `.claude/cerebro-roster` gets its own names
   from bare `roster`, `--implementers`, `--entry` and `--role`.
   GREEN: the file source in `print_all`.
2. **Nothing else changed.**
   RED: with no consumer file, every existing roster assertion passes untouched.
   GREEN: the `-s` guard.
3. **No new dependency.**
   RED: **`roster` under `PATH` of `dirname` and `bash` only** still prints the table.
   GREEN: path arithmetic, not `consumer-root`. **If this is red, `git` crept in.**
4. **The awkward lines and the order.**
   RED: comments, blank lines, and **file order preserved** — first planner first, implementers in
   order.
   GREEN: reuse `print_all`'s existing parse.
5. **A consumer role launches.**
   RED: a role with no submodule agent file but a real `.claude/agents/<role>.md` passes preflight and
   resolves its model; preflight's refusal for a genuinely absent role **names the right cause**.
   GREEN: the resolution order and the message.
6. **The suite stops pinning this fleet.**
   RED: the three files above, rewritten to derive names.
   GREEN: nothing — they should pass once derived.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the submodule pin bump. **No `.claude/cerebro-roster` is added** —
this consumer wants the built-in fleet, and shipping a file that merely restates it is a second copy
to drift. **PR one merges first.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **a consumer roster replaces the built-in** | `tests/launchers.sh` | the bead |
| all four modes read the consumer file | same | the whole surface |
| a missing consumer file falls back | same | no regression |
| **file order is preserved** | same | first-planner-triages, implementer pick order |
| comments and blank lines are ignored | same | the format |
| **`roster` works with `PATH` of `dirname` and `bash`** | same | 🔴 no `git` |
| a consumer-only role launches | same | §2, §3 |
| preflight names the right cause | same | §3 |
| `tests/launchers.sh:260-261` derived, not duplicated | same | the drift |
| `agent-alive.sh:107-119`, `agent-state.sh:387` derived | those files | same |
| every existing test | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `for t in tests/*.sh` and the ERT suite.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing reaches a player: a config file and a bash reader in the fleet
harness. The navigator ranked the ah-qled family P1 on 2026-08-21.

**Decided here** (architecture): the **tracked** `.claude/cerebro-roster` rather than ah-qled.5's
git-ignored `.cerebro/roster`, on ah-qled.1's own reasoning; **replace rather than merge**, because
file order is load-bearing; **path arithmetic rather than `consumer-root`**, to keep `roster`
dependency-free; resolving agent files from the consumer's already-tracked `.claude/agents/`; and
**not** shipping a roster file for atlantis-hud.

## Out of scope

- **ah-qled.5.2** (phase vocabulary, blocked on this) and **ah-qled.5.3** (shims).
- **`models.conf`**, which stays personal and ignored.
- **Changing the X-Men names**, or atlantis-hud's fleet.
- **`sync-symlinks.sh`** — see the trap below; its behaviour is not changed here.
- **The rest of the ah-qled audit.**

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
emacs -Q --batch -l emacs/cerebro.el -l emacs/cerebro-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

Then by hand, from the consumer root:

1. `scripts/roster` — unchanged output, the X-Men in file order. **Nothing about this checkout moves.**
2. Write a `.claude/cerebro-roster` with two names and run `scripts/roster`, `--implementers`,
   `--entry` and `--role` — **all four** must answer from it. Then delete it and confirm the built-in
   returns.
3. **The dependency check**: `PATH="$(dirname "$(command -v dirname)")" bash scripts/roster` still
   prints the table. If it fails, `git` has crept in and the launcher's narrowed-PATH guarantee is
   gone.
4. Confirm **file order** survives: the first planner in your file is the first row out.
5. Add `.claude/agents/<some-new-role>.md` and a roster row for it, and launch that name. It must
   start — and a role with **no** file anywhere must be refused with a message naming *that*, not
   "the submodule is behind".
6. Confirm `git check-ignore .claude/cerebro-roster` says **nothing** — it must be trackable.

## Known traps

- **🔴 Do not call `consumer-root` from `roster`.** It shells out to `git`, and
  `tests/launchers.sh:412-422` runs a launcher with `PATH` containing only `dirname` and `bash`.
  Use path arithmetic and comment that it is deliberate.
- **🔴 Tracked, not `.cerebro/`.** ah-qled.5 proposes `.cerebro/roster`; `.gitignore:40` ignores it,
  so it disappears on a fresh clone and the fleet silently reverts. This plan overrides the bead on
  purpose.
- **Replace, do not merge.** File order decides which planner triages and which implementer name is
  taken next; a merged order is nobody's decision.
- **`sync-symlinks.sh:85` uses `ln -sfn`, which replaces a real file.** A consumer role cerebro does
  **not** ship is safe — the script iterates the submodule's items — but a consumer *override* of a
  shipped role would be clobbered on the next sync. Worth knowing; **not fixed here**.
- **`KIND` stays derived.** `kind_of` is the one place that rule lives; a consumer file must not be
  allowed to state a third column and contradict it.
- **Keep `print_all`'s parse.** It is pure-builtin and already handles comments, blanks and short
  rows. Writing a second parser for the consumer file is how the two shapes drift.
- **Do not ship a roster for atlantis-hud.** It wants the built-in; a file restating it is a copy to
  drift.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**
acceptance_criteria:
- `<consumer>/.claude/cerebro-roster` (TRACKED, NOT the git-ignored .cerebro/) supplies the fleet when present, in the same NAME ROLE shape as the built-in TABLE, with `#` comments and blank lines ignored and KIND still derived by kind_of.
- All four roster modes read it: bare, --implementers, --entry <Name>, --role <role>.
- It REPLACES the built-in table rather than merging with it - file order is load-bearing (plan-bead gives P4 triage to the first planner listed; Cerebro takes implementer names in file order).
- A missing or empty consumer file falls back to the built-in TABLE, and every existing roster assertion passes untouched.
- `roster` STILL NEEDS NO EXTERNAL COMMAND BEYOND `dirname`: it must not call consumer-root (which shells out to git). The consumer root is found by path arithmetic, with a comment saying that is deliberate. `PATH` of only dirname and bash must still work - tests/launchers.sh:412-422 depends on it.
- Agent files resolve from `<consumer>/.claude/agents/<role>.md` first (already tracked, already symlinked to the submodule for shipped roles) with the submodule as fallback, so a consumer-only role launches.
- launch-preflight:87 distinguishes "cerebro does not ship this role and the consumer has no agent file either" from "the submodule is behind", and says which.
- The suite stops pinning this fleet: tests/launchers.sh:260-261 derives from `roster --implementers` instead of duplicating it as parallel arrays; tests/agent-alive.sh:107-119 and tests/agent-state.sh:387 derive their names too. Follow the pattern at tests/launchers.sh:101-110.
- NO .claude/cerebro-roster is added to atlantis-hud - it wants the built-in fleet, and a file restating it is a second copy to drift.
- Out of scope: agent-state's phase whitelist (ah-qled.5.2) and the run-* shims, Bishop courtesy and implementer-state (ah-qled.5.3).
- cerebro's suites pass; the submodule pin is bumped in a second PR after the cerebro PR merges.

title: Cerebro's public tests and prose name one person instead of stating the rule
description:
## What

Small, independent of the rest of the epic, and worth doing whether or not the split proceeds.
Cerebro is a public repository, so anyone who clones or forks it takes these with them.

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el:1437` — `(cerebro-test--bead "ah-13o" 1 "Resizable split" "henrik@kurelid.se")`
  is the bead-owner fixture, and `:1438` asserts on the string `"henrik"`. The test only proves the
  owner column is hidden for one particular person.
- `emacs/cerebro-test.el:2325,2331,2334` — `"Henrik Kurelid"` is the "a claim held by hand" fixture,
  and the docstring names him as the reason the guard exists.
- `agents/orchestrator.md:391-394` — "`assignee: Henrik Kurelid` (or any name off the roster) now
  specifically means a claim made by hand … Two of the navigator's own beads were found stale this
  way on 2026-08-14 — `ah-r2e` and `ah-52b`". This one is carried into every orchestrator session.

## What changes

Neutral fixtures — `owner@example.com` matched on `example.com`, and `"A Human"` — and in the
orchestrator prompt, the rule stated as it actually is: **a name that is not on `scripts/roster`**.
That is what the code means, it is what a consumer needs, and it stops depending on one person's
name being recognisable.

## While here

Two documented paths that do not resolve, both found in the same read:

- `agents/orchestrator.md:317-319` says "**Never `.claude/worktrees/psylocke`**" where every other
  reference in the repository says `.cerebro/worktrees/psylocke` — and `.claude/worktrees/` exists as
  a separate directory, so the never-delete instruction currently names the wrong tree.
- The same line points at `docs/cerebro-jobs.md`, which from a consumer root resolves to nothing; the
  file is at `.claude/cerebro/docs/cerebro-jobs.md`.

And a latent rename bug: `agents/architect.md:59-60,150-151` still keys its memory on
`bishop-watermark` / `bishop-weekly` after the Bishop→Forge rename (cerebro #38). Harmless today,
invisible to anyone grepping for `forge-watermark`. `docs/agent-workflow.md:418-425` documents it as
a known trap, so it is a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight — but it belongs on a list.
design:
## Context

Cerebro is a **public repository** (`rmstdope/cerebro`, verified), so anyone who clones or forks it
takes its fixtures with them. Three places hardcode the navigator:

- **`emacs/cerebro-test.el:1437`** — `(cerebro-test--bead "ah-13o" 1 "Resizable split"
  "henrik@kurelid.se")`, with `:1438` asserting `(should-not (string-match-p "henrik" line))`.
  **The test only proves the owner column is hidden for one particular person.**
- **`emacs/cerebro-test.el:2323-2336`** — `"Henrik Kurelid"` is the *claim held by hand* fixture, and
  the docstring names him as the reason the guard exists.
- **`agents/orchestrator.md:389-394`** — *"`assignee: Henrik Kurelid` (or any name off the roster)
  now specifically means a claim made by hand…"*, naming two of the navigator's own beads. **This one
  is carried into every orchestrator session.**

**Being straight about the exposure:** the address is already public via every commit in
`rmstdope/atlantis-hud`, which is also public, so removing it from cerebro changes little about who
can find it. **The better argument is that these are weak constructions**: a test that asserts on one
person's name proves only that the owner column hides *that person*, and a rule stated as a name is a
rule a consumer cannot apply.

**Standalone.** The navigator detached this from ah-qled on 2026-08-21 and ranked it separately: the
bead's own text says it is *"small, independent of the rest of the epic, and worth doing whether or
not the split proceeds"*.

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. Neutral fixtures — `emacs/cerebro-test.el`

- **`:1437-1438`** — `"owner@example.com"`, with the assertion matched on **`example.com`**. Matching
  the domain rather than a name is what makes the test prove the *column* is hidden rather than one
  string being absent by luck.
- **`:2323-2336`** — `"A Human"` as the claim-held-by-hand fixture, and **the docstring rewritten to
  state the rule rather than the person**: an assignee that is *not on `scripts/roster`* is a live
  claim held by hand exactly as often as it is a crashed session, and only the lease tells the two
  apart.

The docstring's substance — *"which is the bug this test was written to catch"* — stays. Only the
person goes.

### 2. The rule as it actually is — `agents/orchestrator.md:389-394`

State it as **a name that is not on `scripts/roster`**. That is what
`cerebro--claim-finding` actually does (`cerebro.el:947` tests `(member .assignee live-names)`), it is
what a consumer needs, and it stops the rule depending on one person's name being recognisable.

**Keep the evidence, drop the identification.** The 2026-08-14 incident is why the guard exists and is
worth keeping — as *two beads held under a human name*, with the bead ids, without whose name it was.

### 3. While here — two documented paths that do not resolve

Both were named in the bead and **I checked both. One of them is not what the bead says**, and
following the bead literally would make it worse.

#### 🔴 `orchestrator.md:317-319` is incomplete, not wrong

The bead says the never-delete instruction *"names the wrong tree"*. It does not. **Both trees
exist** — verified with `git worktree list`:

```
/…/atlantis-hud/.cerebro/worktrees/psylocke   (detached HEAD)
/…/atlantis-hud/.claude/worktrees/psylocke    (detached HEAD)
```

and `prune-worktrees.sh` protects psylocke at **either** path, deliberately and in those words:

```
:31   One named exception, at **either** path: `psylocke` is kept by name, unconditionally
:149      "$repo_root"/.cerebro/worktrees/*) ;;
:150      "$repo_root"/.claude/worktrees/*) ;;
:157    if [ "$name" = "psylocke" ]; then
```

The name is matched, not the path. So **the prose naming only `.claude/worktrees/psylocke` is
incomplete**, and the obvious fix — swapping it for `.cerebro/worktrees/psylocke` — **makes it wrong
in the other direction.** Say *at either path*, matching the script's own wording.

#### `docs/cerebro-jobs.md` resolves from the wrong root

The file exists at `.claude/cerebro/docs/cerebro-jobs.md`; the consumer's `docs/` has no such file
(checked). The reference is correct from inside cerebro and broken from a consumer root — **which is
where an orchestrator session actually runs**. Make it unambiguous: `.claude/cerebro/docs/…`, or
whatever form the surrounding prose uses for a path inside the submodule.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):**

1. **No person in the fixtures.**
   RED: the two ERT tests, edited to the neutral values, still pass and still fail if the owner column
   leaks — flip the production behaviour once to confirm the assertion still catches it.
   GREEN: the fixtures and the docstring.
2. **The rule reads as a rule.** `orchestrator.md:389-394`.
3. **The two paths resolve.** `:317-319` — *at either path*, and the unambiguous doc reference.
4. **Nobody is left.**
   `grep -rn "Henrik\|henrik@\|kurelid" .` in the cerebro tree returns nothing outside git history.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the submodule pin bump, nothing else. **PR one merges first.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `the owner column is hidden` (`:1437`) | `cerebro-test.el` | **unchanged in intent**, matched on `example.com` |
| `claim-finding leaves a lease not yet stale` (`:2323`) | same | unchanged in intent, `"A Human"` |
| **the owner assertion still fails when the column leaks** | same | that the neutral fixture did not weaken it |
| every other ERT test | same | **unchanged** |
| the bash suite | `tests/*.sh` | **unchanged — no script changes here** |

**Suites:** the ERT suite and `for t in tests/*.sh`.

**No production behaviour changes in this bead.** If `cerebro.el` appears in the diff outside a
docstring, scope has slipped.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing here reaches a player: two test fixtures and three paragraphs
of agent prose in the fleet harness.

The one decision this bead carried — whether it should ride at the epic's priority or be ranked on
its own — **the navigator took on 2026-08-21**, choosing to detach it. They also chose its priority
knowing the honest version of the exposure.

**Decided here** (architecture): `owner@example.com` matched on the domain rather than the local
part; `"A Human"` for the by-hand fixture; and stating the roster rule rather than swapping one name
for another neutral one.

## Out of scope

- **Every other child of ah-qled**, and the epic's portability work.
- **`cerebro--claim-finding`'s behaviour.** The rule is being *stated* correctly, not changed.
- **Git history.** Rewriting authorship is not on the table and would not help — the address is public
  via commits in this repository regardless.
- **`prune-worktrees.sh`.** Its either-path handling is correct; only the prose describing it is
  incomplete.
- **The `.claude/worktrees` / `.cerebro/worktrees` duplication itself.** Two psylocke trees exist and
  that may deserve a bead; this one only fixes the sentence.

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
emacs -Q --batch -l emacs/cerebro.el -l emacs/cerebro-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rni "henrik\|kurelid" --exclude-dir=.git .   # must return nothing
```

Then:

1. **Break the owner column on purpose** — make the bead line include the owner — and confirm the
   `:1437` test **goes red**. This is the point: a neutral fixture must not be a weaker test. Put it
   back.
2. Read `orchestrator.md:389-394` as a stranger: does it tell you what to do **without knowing who
   Henrik is**? If it still needs that, it has not been fixed.
3. Read `:317-319`: it must say psylocke is never deleted **at either path**, and the doc reference
   must resolve from a consumer root.
4. `git worktree list` and confirm **both** psylocke trees are still there after
   `prune-worktrees.sh --dry-run` — the prose changed, the behaviour did not.

## Known traps

- **🔴 Do not swap `.claude/worktrees/psylocke` for `.cerebro/worktrees/psylocke`.** That is the
  obvious reading of the bead and it is wrong: **both trees exist**, and `prune-worktrees.sh` protects
  psylocke **by name at either path** (`:31`, `:149-150`, `:157`). Swapping makes the prose wrong in
  the other direction. Say *at either path*.
- **Match the neutral email on `example.com`, not on the local part.** Matching `owner` could pass by
  accident against unrelated text and would quietly weaken the test.
- **State the rule, do not merely rename the person.** `"A Human"` in the fixture is fine;
  `"A Human"` in the prose as the thing to look for reproduces the original defect with a different
  string. The rule is *not on `scripts/roster`*.
- **Keep the 2026-08-14 evidence.** It is why the guard exists; only the identification goes.
- **`docs/cerebro-jobs.md` exists** — inside cerebro. It is a wrong *relative* path from a consumer
  root, not a missing file, and an implementer who "fixes" it by deleting the reference removes a real
  document.
- **No production behaviour changes.** Docstrings and fixtures only.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**
acceptance_criteria:
- No occurrence of "Henrik", "henrik@" or "kurelid" remains anywhere in the cerebro tree outside git history.
- cerebro-test.el:1437 uses "owner@example.com" and its assertion matches on `example.com` (the domain, not the local part), so the test still proves the OWNER COLUMN is hidden rather than one string being absent by luck. Breaking the column on purpose must still turn the test red.
- cerebro-test.el:2323-2336 uses "A Human" as the claim-held-by-hand fixture, and its docstring states the rule - an assignee NOT ON scripts/roster is a live claim held by hand exactly as often as a crashed session, and only the lease tells them apart - rather than naming a person.
- agents/orchestrator.md:389-394 states the rule as "a name that is not on scripts/roster", which is what cerebro--claim-finding actually tests. The 2026-08-14 evidence and the bead ids stay; the identification goes.
- agents/orchestrator.md:317-319 says psylocke is never deleted AT EITHER PATH. It must NOT be changed to name .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke instead: both trees exist and prune-worktrees.sh protects psylocke by NAME at either path (:31, :149-150, :157).
- The docs/cerebro-jobs.md reference resolves from a consumer root, not only from inside cerebro.
- No production behaviour changes: cerebro.el is untouched outside a docstring, prune-worktrees.sh is untouched, and both psylocke worktrees survive a --dry-run unchanged.
- The ERT suite and every tests/*.sh pass; the submodule pin is bumped in a second PR after the cerebro PR merges.
