title: Nothing checks that the fleet works anywhere but here
description:
## Why

This is what makes the epic's definition of done enforceable rather than aspirational, and it is why
none of the coupling in the sibling beads was noticed: **nothing anywhere exercises cerebro as a
consumer's submodule.**

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` is itself clean — byte-compile plus ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1, then every
`tests/*.sh` on ubuntu-latest, with no checkout of another repository, no `bd`, no `gh`, no pnpm and
no cargo. But it only ever runs cerebro *in place*. The mount point, the `bd` program name, the
default branch and the pnpm install are all invisible to it.

The bash suites do build fabricated consumers already (ah-dy4x, `tests/launchers.sh`,
`tests/launch-preflight.sh`, `tests/consumer-root.sh`), and `cerebro-test/fleet-reads-the-roster-script`
(`emacs/cerebro-test.el:344-364`) builds a temp dir with `.claude/cerebro` symlinked to cerebro's own
root. Generalising that is the missing fixture, not a new invention.

## What to build

One CI job that stands up a consumer deliberately unlike atlantis-hud and drives the fleet against it:

- **no JavaScript at all** — no `package.json`, no lockfile, so `prepare-worktree` must take its
  no-install branch and say so
- **a default branch that is not `main`** — `trunk`, which catches the 15 hardcoded `origin/main`
  occurrences
- **a `cerebro-project.conf` of its own** — its own `app_paths`, its own `gate-fast` that exits 0,
  its own `audience_noun`
- **a roster of its own** with names that are not X-Men, and a role cerebro does not ship, which
  catches the roster table and the `agent-state` phase whitelist
- **a stub `bd`** on `PATH` answering fixed JSON, so the fleet view and the sweeps can be driven
  without a real tracker
- **mounted somewhere other than `.claude/cerebro`** in at least one case, to catch the two
  hardcoded mount-point sites

Then assert what the epic promises: `sync-symlinks.sh` links everything, `launch-preflight` passes
for every role, `prepare-worktree --dry-run` prints the right commands and no others, the sweeps
return clean rather than erroring, and `agent-state` accepts the consumer's own phase words.

## Note on the fixtures

`tests/launch-preflight.sh:67` and `tests/launchers.sh:62,321,438` copy the whole submodule with
`cp -R "$repo_root"`, which drags in any `.cerebro/` or build output present at the time. Copy only
`scripts/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `hooks/` so the fixture is hermetic and cheap.

Depends on the other children in the sense that each one's assertions land here — but the fixture
itself can be built first, red, and turned green as they land. That is the better order: it makes
every sibling's definition of done mechanical.
design:
## Context

A child of the epic `ah-qled`, "Cerebro runs in a project that is not atlantis-hud".
Upstream: <https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58>.

**Worked in the cerebro submodule** (`.claude/cerebro/` = `rmstdope/cerebro`). Nothing in the
application changes.

**Nothing anywhere exercises cerebro as a consumer's submodule.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is
itself clean — byte-compile plus ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1, then every `tests/*.sh` on
`ubuntu-latest`, with no checkout of another repository and no `bd`, `gh`, `pnpm` or `cargo` — but it
only ever runs cerebro **in place**. The mount point, the tracker's program name, the default branch
and the install step are all invisible to it. That is why none of the coupling the sibling beads
found was noticed by CI: there is no CI that could have noticed it.

This bead builds the missing fixture: one job that stands up a consumer deliberately unlike this
project and drives the fleet against it.

**Two findings from reading the tree, both of which make the bead smaller than it reads:**

**The fixture is mostly built already.** `tests/launch-preflight.sh` fabricates a consumer under
`mktemp -d` with its **own bare `origin`** and its **own branch name** (`git init -q --bare -b
"$branch"`, line 64), and `tests/launchers.sh`, `tests/consumer-root.sh` do similar. On the elisp
side `cerebro-test/fleet-reads-the-roster-script` (`emacs/cerebro-test.el:344`) builds a temp
directory with `.claude/cerebro` **symlinked** to cerebro's own root. This is generalising four
existing fixtures, not inventing one.

**The bead's numbers are stale in the good direction.** It cites *"the 15 hardcoded `origin/main`
occurrences"*; at HEAD there is **one**, in `scripts/prepare-worktree`. `ah-qled.3` has been eating
them. **Re-count before writing an assertion around that number** — see *Known traps*.

## The decision that shapes everything: green by construction

The bead recommends building the job **red** and turning it green as siblings land, *"because it
makes every sibling's definition of done mechanical"*.

**That cannot be done as written.** Nothing merges red, so a failing job blocks every pull request in
the repository until the last sibling lands — the whole fleet stopped for days to gain a checklist.
The navigator chose **B, green by construction**: the fixture is built now and asserts **only what
passes today**; each sibling adds its own assertion as part of its own work.

B has one weakness, stated plainly when it was chosen: *a sibling can land without adding its
assertion.* **Increment 5 closes it rather than leaving it**, and by the time this plan was finished most of the
weakness had evaporated on its own: three of the four siblings have already landed, so their
assertions go in green immediately and only one is deferred.

## Files to change and what to reuse

All paths relative to `.claude/cerebro/`.

- **New: `tests/consumer-fixture.sh`** — the fabricated consumer and the assertions.
- **New or extended: a shared fixture helper.** Four suites already build consumers by hand. Either
  add `tests/lib/consumer.sh` sourced by all of them, or keep the new suite self-contained and leave
  the others alone. **Prefer self-contained**: refactoring four working suites is a second bead's
  worth of risk inside this one, and the epic's point is coverage, not tidiness. If a helper does
  emerge, it must not change what the existing four assert.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — one new job.
- **`tests/launch-preflight.sh:73,271` and `tests/launchers.sh:62,321,438`** — the `cp -R "$repo_root"`
  narrowing described in increment 4.

Reuse, and read before writing:

- **`tests/launch-preflight.sh:30-80`** — the closest thing to the wanted fixture: temp dirs, a bare
  origin, a named branch, `cp -R` of the submodule, `.claude/` layout.
- **`emacs/cerebro-test.el:344-364`** — the symlink-mount pattern, and the shape of a
  fleet-reads-the-roster assertion.
- **`scripts/project-conf`** — how a consumer declares facts, and its never-fail-on-absence contract.
- **`scripts/roster`'s consumer-roster support** (`ah-qled.5.1`, merged) — `.claude/cerebro-roster`,
  tracked, replacing the built-in table.

## Increments

### 1 — The fixture: a consumer deliberately unlike this project

`tests/consumer-fixture.sh`, in cerebro's own suite style (plain bash, `set -euo pipefail`,
`fail`/`pass`, exit non-zero on the first failure — copy the header from `tests/launch-preflight.sh`).

Build, under `mktemp -d`, a consumer with **every axis different from atlantis-hud**:

| axis | this project | the fixture | what it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| language | pnpm, TypeScript, Rust | **no `package.json`, no lockfile, nothing** | `prepare-worktree` must take its no-install branch **and say so** |
| default branch | `main` | **`trunk`** | every hardcoded `origin/main` |
| project facts | `.claude/cerebro-project.conf` | **its own**: own `app_paths`, own `audience_noun`, a gate command that exits 0 | anything reading this project's values |
| fleet | X-Men | **its own roster**, names that are not X-Men, **plus a role cerebro does not ship** | the roster table, and `agent-state`'s phase whitelist |
| tracker | real `bd` | **a stub `bd` on `PATH`** answering fixed JSON | the sweeps and the fleet view, driven without a tracker |
| mount point | `.claude/cerebro` | **`.claude/cerebro` in most cases, and somewhere else in at least one** | the two hardcoded mount-point sites |

The stub `bd` is a shell script on a `PATH` the test controls, printing fixed JSON per subcommand and
exiting 0. Keep it in the fixture, not in `scripts/` — it is a test double, not a shipped thing.

**The consumer's `cerebro-roster` must include a role cerebro does not ship** (say `archivist`), and
the fixture must then also provide `agents/archivist.md`, or assert the specific error for a role
with no agent file. Decide which by reading `launch-preflight`; do not guess.

### 2 — Assert only what passes today

Every assertion goes in **green**. Run each one before committing it; if it fails, it belongs to a
sibling bead and **is not written here**.

Start from these, and keep whichever pass at the time of writing:

- `sync-symlinks.sh` links every `agents/*.md` and `skills/*` into the consumer's `.claude/`, as
  relative links.
- `launch-preflight` passes for **every role on the consumer's own roster**, derived from
  `roster`, not listed.
- `roster`, `roster --implementers`, `roster --role <role>` and `roster --entry <name>` all answer
  from the consumer's file, and **no X-Man name appears in any of them**.
- `consumer-root` and `consumer-root --shared` resolve to the fixture, from inside it and from a
  worktree of it.
- `agent-state` accepts the consumer's own phase words and writes them into
  `.cerebro/state/<Name>.state.json`. *(Passes only once `ah-qled.5.2` lands — so at the time of
  writing, this is that bead's assertion to add, not this one's.)*
- `project-conf` returns the consumer's values, and its declared default for an absent key.
- `prepare-worktree --dry-run` prints the no-install branch and **does not print an install command**.
- The sweeps (`sweep-claims.sh`, `sweep-epics.sh`, `sweep-stalled.sh`, `prune-worktrees.sh`) exit 0
  against the stub `bd` and an empty fleet — **clean, not erroring**.

**Each assertion that does not pass yet gets a commented-out stub with the sibling's bead id beside
it**, so the file itself lists what is still missing. That recovers most of what option A promised,
at no cost:

```bash
# ah-qled.5.2 — agent-state accepts a consumer's own phase word.
# run_state "$c" Archivist working --phase index --pid 1
# [[ "$(jq -r .phase "$(state_file "$c" Archivist)")" == index ]] || fail "consumer phase word"
```

### 3 — The CI job

One job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, alongside the two that exist:

```yaml
  consumer-fixture:
    name: Consumer fixture (ubuntu-latest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Drive the fleet against a fabricated consumer
        shell: bash
        run: bash tests/consumer-fixture.sh
```

**No `continue-on-error`.** The navigator chose B precisely so that this job is honest from its first
run; an advisory flag is option C and was declined.

**Do not add it to the existing `bash-tests` loop.** `tests/*.sh` is globbed there, so a file placed
in `tests/` would run in both jobs. Either name the new suite so the glob misses it (put it in
`tests/consumer/` and glob `tests/*.sh` unchanged), **or** let it run only in `bash-tests` and skip
the separate job entirely. **Prefer the second**: one job, no duplication, and the existing loop
already reports per-suite groups and errors. The separate job is only worth it if the fixture needs
setup the other suites must not pay for — which, with no `bd`, no `pnpm` and no `gh`, it does not.

**Decide this by reading, not by guessing**, and say which was chosen in the PR body. If the suite
simply joins `tests/*.sh`, increment 3 is one sentence and the workflow does not change at all —
which is the better outcome.

### 4 — Hermetic, cheap fixtures

`tests/launch-preflight.sh:73,271` and `tests/launchers.sh:62,321,438` do
`cp -R "$repo_root" .../cerebro`, which drags in whatever is present at the time — a local
`.cerebro/`, an `.git/`, byte-compiled elisp, editor droppings. Narrow every one of them to the
directories the fixture actually needs:

```bash
mkdir -p "$dest"
for d in scripts agents skills hooks; do
  [ -d "$repo_root/$d" ] && cp -R "$repo_root/$d" "$dest/"
done
```

**Run the two suites before and after** and confirm they still pass unchanged. If narrowing breaks
one, that suite was depending on something in the copy nobody declared — **report it rather than
widening the list back**; that is a finding, not an obstacle.

`emacs/` is deliberately absent: no bash suite needs it, and it is the largest thing in the tree.

### 5 — The siblings, most of which have already landed

**Check the siblings' state before doing anything here — it moved while this bead was being
planned**, and it is the difference between writing an assertion and deferring it.

At the time of writing:

| sibling | state | its assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `ah-qled.5.2` | **closed** (cerebro#77, pointer bumped in #530) | `agent-state` accepts the consumer's own phase word — **write it green, now** |
| `ah-qled.5.3` | **closed** (cerebro#72, atlantis-hud#524) | `launch <Name>` starts every role on the consumer's roster, and no `run-*` shim exists — **write it green, now** |
| `ah-qled.7.3` | **closed** (#531, cerebro#79) | the release procedure reads `release_cmd`, and `release_watch` absent means nothing is watched — **write it green, now** |
| `ah-qled.7.2` | **in progress**, claimed by Storm | `disk-preflight` and `retro-sightings` run against the consumer, reading its `disk_floor_gb` and `retro_dir` — **commented-out stub, with the bead id** |

This is B working exactly as intended: three of the four behaviours already exist, so three of the
four assertions go in green on the first commit, and only one is deferred.

**Re-run that check yourself** (`bd show <id>` for each) rather than trusting this table. If
`ah-qled.7.2` has landed by the time you start, write its assertion green too and there is nothing
deferred at all.

**Do not amend `ah-qled.7.2`'s design.** It is claimed, and changing a plan under a running
implementer is how a plan and a build come to disagree. Its stub carries the bead id and that is
enough; if it lands without uncommenting the stub, this bead's own suite still names what is missing.

For any sibling planned **after** this bead: its plan should carry a line requiring it to make its
stub pass. That is the planner's job rather than the implementer's, and it is written here so the
next planner sees it.

## The test plan

This bead **is** a test. There is nothing to unit-test about it and nothing should be invented.

What must be verified instead:

1. **Every assertion written passes**, locally, before it is committed. An assertion committed red is
   option A by accident.
2. **The existing suites still pass** after increment 4's narrowing — `tests/launch-preflight.sh` and
   `tests/launchers.sh` specifically, run before and after.
3. **The whole suite runs in CI**, on `ubuntu-latest`, with no `bd`, `gh`, `pnpm` or `cargo`
   available. If any assertion needs one of those, it is wrong: the stub `bd` exists so that it does
   not.
4. `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` from the submodule root, plus ERT on both Emacs
   versions.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21 (`docs/ui/consumer-ci.html`). **Decided; raise
disagreements through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | How does the job behave while its siblings are still landing? | **B — green by construction.** The fixture asserts only what passes today; each sibling adds its own assertion as part of its own work |

**Option A (red and blocking), which is what the bead's own description recommends, was declined
because it cannot work**: nothing merges red, so the job would block every pull request in the
repository until the last sibling landed.

**Option C (red but `continue-on-error`) was declined** because an advisory check is one nobody has
to act on, and removing the flag afterwards is a step no bead but this one would remember.

Increment 2's commented-out stubs and increment 5's amendments exist to recover what option A
promised — a mechanical definition of done per sibling — without the blockage.

## Out of scope

- **Fixing any coupling the fixture reveals.** If an assertion fails, it belongs to a sibling bead —
  write it commented-out with the bead id, or file a new bead. **Do not fix application or harness
  behaviour in this bead**; it is the ruler, not the correction.
- **Refactoring the four existing consumer fixtures into a shared helper**, beyond increment 4's
  narrowing.
- **`emacs/cerebro-test.el`.** The ERT side already has its consumer test and is not extended here.
- **Adding `bd`, `gh`, `pnpm` or `cargo` to CI.** The stub exists so none is needed, and cerebro's CI
  being free of them is a property worth keeping.
- **Any change in the application repository.**

## Validation

1. `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` passes from the submodule root; cerebro's CI is green,
   including the new coverage.
2. `tests/launch-preflight.sh` and `tests/launchers.sh` pass unchanged after increment 4.
3. The fixture's consumer has **no `package.json`**, a default branch of **`trunk`**, its own
   `cerebro-project.conf`, its own roster with **no X-Man name**, and a role cerebro does not ship.
   Read the fixture and confirm all five.
4. `grep -rn "Xavier\|Cyclops\|Psylocke\|Forge\|Moira\|Cerebro\|Cypher" tests/consumer-fixture.sh`
   returns nothing. A fixture that names this fleet is not testing what it claims to.
5. Every commented-out assertion carries a sibling bead id.
6. The assertions for every **closed** sibling are present and green; every **open or claimed**
   sibling has a commented-out stub naming its bead id. Nothing is both missing and unnamed.
7. The suite runs with `PATH` holding no `bd`, `gh`, `pnpm` or `cargo` beyond the stub.

## Known traps

- **Do not commit a failing assertion.** The navigator declined red-and-blocking by name; one
  assertion committed red turns the whole repository's CI into option A.
- **`tests/*.sh` is globbed by the existing `bash-tests` job.** A new file in `tests/` runs there
  automatically — which is probably what you want, and means the separate job in increment 3 may be
  unnecessary. Decide deliberately and say which in the PR body; do not end up running the suite
  twice.
- **The bead's counts are stale.** *"15 hardcoded `origin/main` occurrences"* is **one** at HEAD.
  Re-count before asserting anything about that number, and prefer asserting **behaviour on a
  `trunk` branch** over counting occurrences in source — a count is a test that fails on a refactor
  that changed nothing.
- **Narrowing `cp -R` can break a suite in a way that is a finding.** If `tests/launchers.sh` needs
  something outside `scripts/ agents/ skills/ hooks/`, report it. Widening the list back hides it.
- **The stub `bd` must exit 0 and print valid JSON**, or the sweeps will fail for the stub's reasons
  rather than cerebro's, and the assertion will look like a real failure.
- **A role cerebro does not ship needs an agent file, or a defined error.** `launch-preflight` has an
  opinion about this; read it rather than assuming which.
- **Amending a sibling's design under a running implementer** makes the plan and the build disagree.
  Check `bd show <id>` for a claim before every edit in increment 5.
- **This bead is a ruler, not a repair.** The temptation to fix the first thing the fixture catches
  is strong and must be refused; that is a sibling's work, and mixing them makes both unreviewable.

title: The prose stops naming this project and its players
description:
## The coupling

Upstream §3 and §4. This does not break the harness — it breaks the *reading*, and in one place it
reaches strangers.

**The project name, in 11 files.** `atlantis-hud` is in the `description:` frontmatter of all seven
roles and all four skills. That frontmatter is what Claude Code matches against when choosing an
agent or skill, so in another project every one of them reads as inapplicable.

**The product name reaches users.** `agents/user-feedback.md:136,153,363` mandates, and declares
exact, the first line of every comment Moira posts to a public issue:
`_Written by **Moira**, an AI agent that triages issues for Atlantis HUD._` `:138` adds "feedback
from people actually playing with Atlantis HUD"; `:174` builds its own long-line rule out of the name
("a wrap that lands mid-name gives them \"Atlantis\" on one line and \"HUD\" on the next"). The
*requirement to disclose* is product and stays; the name must come from `project_name`.

**"player" is the assumed reader**, 13 times in `skills/release-notes/SKILL.md` alone (whose entire
audience section is written for a game), plus `planner.md:81,86,129`, `reviewer.md:141,178,180,191`,
`verifier.md:202,206,259`, `orchestrator.md:743`, `docs/agent-workflow.md:163,532`. One
`audience_noun` key defaulting to "user" fixes every one, and every rule using it survives the
rename intact.

**Domain vocabulary as worked examples.** `reviewer.md:170` — "this runs per hex per turn; have you
measured it on a 200-hex report?"; `:135-139` — "no rule of the game decided in a React component",
"the ruleset owning the vocabulary the UI merely displays"; `:164` — "a wasm bundle that grew";
`release-notes:128-133` — a hardcoded glossary ("Hexes, units, orders, turns, provinces and factions
are the game's language and belong"); `:98-114` — a whole worked example headed "What's new for you
in **Atlantis HUD**"; `plan-bead:127,619,805` — "reaches a **player**", "a game switch and a new
turn"; `beads-workflow:200` — `.rep` files.

**Traps that are pure atlantis-hud.** `implement-bead:660-671` ("Traps this repository has already
paid for") and `plan-bead:878-886` are four Playwright/PWA/WebKit/Vite facts each. These should be
**empty in cerebro** and sourced from a consumer file — `<consumer>/.cerebro/traps.md`, read at the
top of Building — which also gives the retrospective loop somewhere to feed.

**Bead ids as citations, roughly 40 across the prompts** — `orchestrator.md` alone has ~20, plus
`verifier.md`, `user-feedback.md`, `architect.md`, `planner.md`. The upstream issue's §5 recommends
leaving the ~379 in the *elisp and tests* alone, and that is right: they are load-bearing reasons in
code comments. But an id carried into every agent session is different — it costs context and
credibility for a reference the consumer cannot resolve. Keep the rule in the prompt, move the
provenance to a cerebro-side `docs/decisions.md` the prompt does not carry.

**Worked examples using real ids and titles**: `beads-workflow:180-181` (`feat(ah-t65): load
multiple reports`), `:209-210`, `:372-373`; `orchestrator.md:357,361-367`; `plan-bead:136,646,804`
(`hexMapModel`), `:812-821`; `user-feedback.md:365-372` (a real feature and `ah-7pa`);
`emacs/README.md:69-113` (a whole sample panel of real beads). Write these as `<bead-id>` /
`<parent>.<n>` and neutral titles.

## Also

`README.md:128-131` — "as it is by beads in atlantis-hud" should generalise to "whenever another tool
— beads, husky, lefthook — already owns `core.hooksPath`". `docs/cerebro-jobs.md:7,18-24` declares
itself one bead's acceptance artifact and tabulates PR numbers from two different repositories; it
should become a dated ADR or leave the consumer-facing set.

`.claude/cerebro/CLAUDE.md:11-14` is the anchor: the line admitting the coupling should become the
pointer to the contract — "every project-specific fact is read from
`<consumer>/.claude/cerebro-project.conf`".

Ship a `templates/consumer-CLAUDE.md` too: cerebro currently *requires* the consumer to have written
a section called "Four Eye Principle" by that exact name (`implement-bead:25-27`,
`plan-bead:672`, `CLAUDE.md:126-128`) with no template offered. Those references should also say
plainly that they mean the **consumer's root** CLAUDE.md — from inside a submodule with two files of
that name, "governs this repository" is ambiguous.

Do last: the wording depends on what the earlier children settle.

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58 §3, §4
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-qled.10.5, delivered in PR #548

title: The fleet view's project-shaped facts are constants a consumer cannot set
description:
## The coupling

Not in the upstream issue, which says `emacs/cerebro.el` "carries no project knowledge". Its
*structure* is genuinely excellent — the roster is read from `scripts/roster`, launcher dispatch is
name-driven, window height is derived from the agent count, and no agent name or role→kind mapping is
duplicated in elisp. But the project-shaped facts landed on the wrong side of the customisation line:
**18 `defconst` against 5 `defcustom`.**

- **`bd` is a bare literal in 7 argv positions** — `:899` (`bd dolt push`, which additionally assumes
  the Dolt backend), `:1307-1313` (`close`, `reclaim --older-than 10m`, `epic-close`, `unclaim`),
  `:1835` (`bd list --status … --json --brief`), `:1866` (`bd show`), `:1974` (`bd update`). A
  consumer tracking work anywhere else gets a permanently empty panel with no configuration point.
- **The label and type vocabulary is `defconst`** — `verification:passed`, `verification:failed`,
  `verification:not-needed` (`:502`), `planned`, `planning`, issue types `epic`/`event`
  (`:1880-1891, 1902-1907, 1946-1947`) and `cerebro-priority-floor 4` (`:1959`). The five buckets only
  partition correctly for a project using exactly these.
- **The mount point is hardcoded twice** — `defconst cerebro--script-directory
  ".claude/cerebro/scripts"` (`:1074`) and `locate-dominating-file … ".claude/cerebro"` (`:1324`).
  Mounted at `vendor/cerebro`, `M-x cerebro` simply errors. `githooks/sync-if-changed.sh:12` has the
  same assumption and silently no-ops instead.
- **`cerebro--stalled-minutes 60`** (`:1259-1266`) is a `defconst` justified from atlantis-hud's own
  telemetry — "across the 72 hours to 2026-08-20 every one of the 36 beads that ran cleanly made its
  first commit 6 to 36 minutes after being claimed". A consumer whose builds take an hour gets false
  stalled findings with no knob. `cerebro--sweep-stale-minutes 10` (`:1196`) is the same shape.
- **`cerebro-wake-intervals` defaults to `'(("Psylocke" . 300))`** (`:941`) — a fleet-specific policy
  keyed on an agent name that need not exist. Key it on **role** instead; role comes from the roster.
- **`cerebro-list-width 59`** and `tabulated-list-format`'s five fixed column widths (`:48-61, 2854`)
  assume short single-word names and cerebro's role words; the Bead column is sized at 10 from the
  real id `ah-dzj.1.1.1.1` (`:425`).
- **`cerebro.el:1348`** documents the state path as "mirroring `statePath' in runImplementer.ts" — a
  TypeScript file that exists in neither repository. A dangling reference implying a Node consumer.
- **`cerebro.el:2850`** — the `cerebro-mode` docstring, which `C-h m` shows every user, reads
  "Major mode listing the atlantis-hud agent fleet."
- **`cerebro--nudge-message` (`:1692-1700`)** types `label it 'human', release your claim … the
  hand-back in the implement-bead skill` into a live session — a beads label and a cerebro skill name
  in the words sent to an agent.

## What changes

Promote each project-shaped constant to `defcustom` under the existing `cerebro` group: a
`cerebro-bd-program` (properly, a small `cerebro-bd-commands` table so the whole panel is one
indirection from a different tracker), the label and type vocabulary, `cerebro-stalled-minutes`,
`cerebro-sweep-stale-minutes`, `cerebro-submodule-path` feeding both mount-point sites, and the
column widths — or compute those from the roster's longest name. Note
`cerebro-skipped-issue-types` is cross-checked against `scripts/work-beads` by `:2258-2272`, so both
sides move together.

Fix the docstring, drop the `runImplementer.ts` reference, and key `cerebro-wake-intervals` on role.

Related bug found while reading: **`scripts/work-beads:67` invokes `bd` with no `-C`**, unlike
`sweep-claims.sh:72` and `sweep-epics.sh:44,56` which both pass `-C "$repo_root"`. Run from a
worktree it reads a different or empty database — and the script's own header says an empty array
that really means "the query broke" is the worst possible answer.
design:
## Context

`emacs/cerebro.el`'s **structure** is genuinely good and the upstream issue is right that it carries
no project knowledge in its shape: the roster is read from `scripts/roster`, launcher dispatch is
name-driven, window height derives from the agent count, and no agent name or role→kind mapping is
duplicated in elisp.

**The project-shaped facts landed on the wrong side of the customisation line.** Measured on
`origin/main` (submodule at `e1e64dd`, current): **18 `defconst` against 5 `defcustom`.**

Verified, each one:

| What | Where | Why it blocks a consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `bd` as a bare literal in **7 argv positions** | `:899`, `:1307-1313`, `:1835`, `:1866`, `:1974` | a differently-installed or wrapped `bd` cannot be reached |
| Label and type vocabulary | `:502`, `:1880-1891`, `:1902-1907`, `:1946-1947` | the five panel buckets only partition for these labels |
| `cerebro-priority-floor` 4 | `:1959` | a consumer whose backlog floor differs |
| **Mount point, hardcoded twice** | `:1074` `".claude/cerebro/scripts"`, `:1324` `".claude/cerebro"` | mounted at `vendor/cerebro`, `M-x cerebro` simply errors |
| `cerebro--stalled-minutes` 60 | `:1259-1266` | justified from **atlantis-hud's own telemetry**; a consumer whose builds take an hour gets false findings |
| `cerebro--sweep-stale-minutes` 10 | `:1196` | same shape |
| `cerebro-wake-intervals` `'(("Psylocke" . 300))` | `:941` | keyed on an **agent name that need not exist** |
| Column widths | `:48-61`, `:2854`, Bead at 10 from `ah-dzj.1.1.1.1` (`:425`) | assume short names and this project's ids |
| `"mirroring `statePath' in runImplementer.ts"` | `:1348` | **a file in neither repository**, implying a Node consumer |
| `"Major mode listing the atlantis-hud agent fleet."` | `:2850` | `C-h m` shows every user |
| `cerebro--nudge-message` | `:1692-1700` | names the `human` label and the `implement-bead` skill in words sent to a live session |

`githooks/sync-if-changed.sh:12` shares the mount-point assumption and **silently no-ops** rather
than erroring.

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. `bd`: one program, not a command table

The bead proposes *"a small `cerebro-bd-commands` table so the whole panel is one indirection from a
different tracker"*. **I am specifying `cerebro-bd-program` instead, and the reasoning matters.**

This epic is *"Cerebro runs in a project that is not atlantis-hud"* — **not a tracker that is not
beads**. Beads is cerebro's own work-tracking assumption, baked into `scripts/work-beads`,
`sweep-claims.sh`, `sweep-epics.sh` and every agent document; a command table in the elisp would
abstract one of a dozen call sites and leave the rest, buying nothing real while adding a layer.
CLAUDE.md is explicit: *"Always prefer simple design solutions. Avoid over-engineering."*

```elisp
(defcustom cerebro-bd-program "bd"
  "The beads executable…  A consumer may install it under another name, or
behind a wrapper.  This is the program, not the command language: cerebro
speaks beads, and a different tracker is a larger change than a defcustom."
  :type 'string :group 'cerebro)
```

and every one of the seven argv positions takes it. **Say in the docstring that a non-beads tracker
is out of scope**, so the next reader does not take the absence of a table as an oversight.

**`:899` additionally assumes the Dolt backend** (`bd dolt push`). Leave that as is — it is a beads
feature, not a project fact — but note it.

### 2. The vocabulary and the thresholds become settings

`defcustom` under the existing `cerebro` group, keeping every current value as the default so
**nothing about this checkout changes**:

- the verification labels (`:502`), `planned` / `planning` (`:1880-1891`), the skipped issue types
  (`:1902-1907`, `:1946-1947`), and `cerebro-priority-floor` (`:1959`);
- `cerebro-stalled-minutes` and `cerebro-sweep-stale-minutes` — **and each docstring must keep the
  measurement that justified its default** while saying it is this project's, not a universal.

**`cerebro-skipped-issue-types` is cross-checked against `scripts/work-beads` by
`cerebro-test.el:2258-2272`** — *"The two owners of 'which issue types are not work' cannot drift
apart."* **Both sides move together, and that test must keep passing.** It is the guard that makes
this promotion safe.

### 3. One mount point

`cerebro-submodule-path`, defaulting to `".claude/cerebro"`, feeding **both** `:1074` (which appends
`/scripts`) and `:1324`'s `locate-dominating-file`. And `githooks/sync-if-changed.sh:12` — **make it
say something when it cannot find the mount** rather than no-opping, which is how this class of
breakage stays invisible.

### 4. Wake intervals keyed on role

`'(("Psylocke" . 300))` becomes a **role** key — `verifier` — because role comes from the roster and
a consumer's verifier may be called anything. The lookup should still prefer a name if one is given,
the way `models.conf` resolves most-specific-first (`scripts/launch:123-140`), so an existing
name-keyed entry keeps working.

### 5. Column widths: compute, do not configure

The Bead column is 10 because of `ah-dzj.1.1.1.1`, and the name columns assume short single words.
**Derive them from the data** — the roster's longest name, the longest id actually being shown —
rather than adding four more knobs. Data-driven beats configuration, and it is one fewer thing for a
consumer to discover.

### 6. Prose

`:2850`'s docstring stops naming atlantis-hud; `:1348` drops the `runImplementer.ts` reference; and
`cerebro--nudge-message` (`:1692-1700`) stops naming the `human` label and the `implement-bead`
skill in words typed at a live session.

### 7. Not here

**`scripts/work-beads:67` invoking `bd` with no `-C`** — a real defect, filed separately as
**ah-il8j**. It is a bug, not a customisation, and it must not ride along inside a promotion pass.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):** one increment per group, each **defaulting to today's value so the
suite stays green throughout** — that is what makes this safe to do in one bead.

1. **`cerebro-bd-program`** through all seven argv positions.
2. **Vocabulary and thresholds** — and `cerebro-test.el:2258-2272` still passing.
3. **`cerebro-submodule-path`**, both sites, plus the githook saying something.
4. **Wake intervals on role**, name still honoured.
5. **Widths derived** from roster and ids.
6. **Prose** — docstring, dangling reference, nudge message.
7. **The audit closes**: `defconst` count is down to the ones that are genuinely internal, and each
   remaining one is internal on purpose.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the submodule pin bump. **No settings are set** — every default is
already this project's value. **PR one merges first.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **every default equals today's literal** | ERT | nothing about this checkout moves |
| a changed `cerebro-bd-program` reaches all seven call sites | ERT | §1 |
| **`the-panel-skips-exactly-what-work-beads-excludes` (`:2258`)** | ERT | **must still pass** — the anti-drift guard |
| a changed submodule path reaches both mount sites | ERT | §3 |
| wake intervals resolve by role, and by name when given | ERT | §4 |
| widths grow for a long name and a long id | ERT | §5 |
| **no docstring names atlantis-hud** | ERT or grep | §6 |
| the nudge message names no label or skill | ERT | §6 |
| every existing ERT and `tests/*.sh` | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** the ERT suite and `for t in tests/*.sh`.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing here reaches a player: elisp constants and docstrings in the
navigator's own fleet view. The navigator ranked the ah-qled family P1 on 2026-08-21.

**Decided here** (architecture): **`cerebro-bd-program` rather than a `cerebro-bd-commands` table**,
overriding the bead — the epic is about a different project, not a different tracker, and beads is
assumed by a dozen shell call sites the table would not reach; **computing** column widths rather
than configuring them; keying wake intervals on role while still honouring a name; and splitting the
`work-beads` `-C` defect out as **ah-il8j**.

## Out of scope

- **ah-il8j**, the `work-beads` `-C` bug.
- **Supporting a non-beads tracker.** `bd dolt push` at `:899` stays.
- **The rest of the ah-qled audit**, including `scripts/roster` (**ah-qled.5.1**) and the phase
  vocabulary (**ah-qled.5.2**).
- **Changing any default.** Every value stays exactly what it is today.
- **Restructuring the panel.**

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
emacs -Q --batch -l emacs/cerebro.el -l emacs/cerebro-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rn "atlantis-hud" emacs/cerebro.el          # must return nothing
grep -rn "runImplementer" .                        # must return nothing
```

Then by hand:

1. **`M-x cerebro` and confirm nothing has changed** — same rows, same columns, same sweeps, same
   widths. **This is the acceptance**: a promotion pass that alters behaviour has gone wrong.
2. `C-h v cerebro-bd-program` — it exists, is customisable, and reads `"bd"`.
3. `C-h m` in the fleet view: the mode docstring **does not say atlantis-hud**.
4. Set `cerebro-bd-program` to a wrapper script that logs and delegates, then reopen the panel:
   **all seven call sites go through it**. That is the only way to prove none was missed.
5. Set `cerebro-submodule-path` to something wrong and confirm the failure **says so** rather than
   erroring obscurely; put it back.
6. Add a roster name much longer than any current one and confirm the column **grows** rather than
   truncating.
7. Confirm a `Psylocke`-keyed `cerebro-wake-intervals` entry still works, and that a `verifier`-keyed
   one does too.

## Known traps

- **Every default must equal today's literal.** This bead changes *where a value can be set*, not
  what it is. A default that differs is a behaviour change hiding inside a refactor.
- **`cerebro-test.el:2258-2272` is the anti-drift guard** between the elisp and `scripts/work-beads`.
  Both sides of the issue-type list move together, and that test staying green is what proves it.
- **Do not build a tracker abstraction.** A `cerebro-bd-commands` table abstracts the elisp's call
  sites and leaves `work-beads`, `sweep-claims.sh`, `sweep-epics.sh` and every agent document still
  speaking beads. Say in the docstring that this is the program, not the command language.
- **The mount point is hardcoded in three places**, not two: `:1074`, `:1324`, and
  `githooks/sync-if-changed.sh:12` — and the githook **no-ops silently**, so it will not tell you it
  was missed.
- **Keep the measurements in the docstrings.** `cerebro--stalled-minutes` is 60 because of a real
  observation; a defcustom with a bare number loses the reason it was ever right.
- **Do not fix `work-beads`'s missing `-C` here.** It is **ah-il8j**.
- **`defconst` is not always wrong.** Some of the 18 are genuinely internal; the goal is that each
  remaining one is internal *on purpose*, not that the count reaches zero.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**

- A `cerebro-bd-commands` table is deliberately NOT built: this epic is about a different project, not a different tracker, and beads is assumed by work-beads, sweep-claims.sh, sweep-epics.sh and every agent document. The docstring says so.

title: A verifier in another project has to invent a command to start the app
description:
## The coupling

`agents/verifier.md:263-270` is the single most project-specific passage in all seven role files:

- "Web: `(cd .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke && pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev)` (vite, default port 5173)"
- "Desktop: `… pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev --features desktop-runtime` (Tauri v2;
  its own `beforeDevCommand` starts vite on 4174 with `--strictPort`). Without
  `--features desktop-runtime` this builds the stub `main`, which exits at once"
- "Both need the wasm build warm"

pnpm, Vite, Tauri v2, wasm, two `@atlantis/*` package names and a cargo feature flag, in the one
place a role has to actually start the application.

Ports are duplicated: `verifier.md:238-245` and `reviewer.md:205-206` both spell
`lsof -nP -iTCP:5173` (web) and `4174` (desktop), and `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:391-397` adds a
third set — `4173`, `SMOKE_PORT_BASE=4183`, `lsof -i :4183 -i :4184 -i :4185`.

`reviewer.md:202` warms the build with `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core build:wasm`.
`verifier.md:271` reads `tests/fixtures/reports/README.md` for "the consecutive-turn report pairs".
`docs/agent-workflow.md:361,383` assumes two shells and a fixture report; `:516-518` assumes port
blocks at 4173/4183/4193.

## What changes

A `launch_targets` section in the project file: a list of `{name, command, port, notes}` the consumer
writes once. The prompt iterates it, and **when none are declared it asks the navigator how to run
the app** rather than improvising a command.

`dev_ports` as name→port pairs replaces the six hardcoded `lsof` lines; `port_base` and
`port_block_size` replace the smoke-port arithmetic. The generic rule that survives is "give each
session its own block of ports and check before claiming one".

`warm_build_cmd` (optional) replaces `--with-wasm` at both call sites, matching the `--prewarm`
rename in the prepare-worktree child. `fixtures_doc` (optional) replaces the reports README, with the
step skipped when unset.

The rules all survive untouched: check the port before starting a server, refuse rather than reuse
what is already listening, build after the reset never before, and pick the fixture that exercises
what the bead changed.

Blocked by the project-file child and the prepare-worktree child.

Upstream: https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/58 §2
design:
## Context

**`agents/verifier.md:263-270` is the single most project-specific passage in all seven role files** —
the one place a role has to actually start the application:

> *"Web: `(cd .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke && pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev)` (vite, default port
> 5173)… Desktop: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev --features desktop-runtime` (Tauri
> v2; its own `beforeDevCommand` starts vite on 4174 with `--strictPort`). Without
> `--features desktop-runtime` this builds the stub main, which exits at once… Both need the wasm
> build warm"*

**pnpm, Vite, Tauri v2, wasm, two `@atlantis/*` package names and a cargo feature flag**, in six
lines. A consumer's verifier reads that, cannot run any of it, and **improvises a command** — the
worst outcome for a role whose whole job is to launch the real application in front of the navigator.

**The ports are written out six times**, verified on `origin/main`:

```
agents/reviewer.md:207                 lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 … (web)
agents/verifier.md:249-250             5173 (web) / 4174 (desktop's vite)
skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:395-396 lsof -i :4183 -i :4184 -i :4185, SMOKE_PORT_BASE=4183
docs/agent-workflow.md:514             blocks of three — 4173, 4183, 4193
```

**Blocked by ah-qled.1** (the project file, merged) **and ah-qled.2** (the `--prewarm` rename).
Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. 🔴 `launch_targets` cannot be a list of records — and does not need to be

The bead asks for *"a list of `{name, command, port, notes}`"*. **`project-conf` is `key value`, one
per line, value to end of line** — it cannot express a list of records, and `lookup` returns only the
**first** matching key, so repeated lines will not work either.

**The established answer for tabular data in this epic is a separate tracked file** — that is what
`.claude/cerebro-roster` is (**ah-qled.5.1**). But a third config file and a third parser for **two
launch targets** is not worth it. **Use flat keys with an index**, which the existing format expresses
exactly:

```
launch_targets       web desktop

launch_web           pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev
launch_web_port      5173

# Without --features desktop-runtime this builds the stub main, which exits at once.
launch_desktop       pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev --features desktop-runtime
launch_desktop_port  4174
```

`launch_targets` is the index the prompt iterates; `launch_<name>` and `launch_<name>_port` carry the
rest. **The `notes` field becomes a comment line** — `project-conf` strips from any `#`, so a note on
its own line is free, and it lands where the person editing the file will read it. **No new file, no
new parser, and nothing added to `project-conf`.**

### 2. 🔴 No targets declared means asking, not improvising

The bead is right and it is the most important behaviour here: **when nothing is declared, the role
asks the navigator how to run the application.** It must not guess a command, and it must not skip the
verification silently — which is exactly the failure mode **ah-qled.6** is about, in the same family.

### 3. The ports come from the same place

`launch_<name>_port` replaces the six hardcoded `lsof` lines at `reviewer.md:207`,
`verifier.md:249-250`, and the prose in `docs/agent-workflow.md:514`.

`port_base` and `port_block_size` replace the smoke-port arithmetic at
`implement-bead/SKILL.md:395-396`.

**The generic rule survives untouched and must be stated in exactly those words**: *"give each session
its own block of ports and check before claiming one."* That is the part that is true of every
project, and it is what the numbers were only ever an example of.

### 4. Two optional keys

- **`warm_build_cmd`** replaces `--with-wasm` at both call sites. **This must match ah-qled.2's
  `--prewarm` rename** — the two beads are renaming the same thing from opposite ends. **Check which
  has merged and follow it**; do not introduce a third spelling.
- **`fixtures_doc`** replaces `verifier.md:271`'s `tests/fixtures/reports/README.md`, with **the step
  skipped when unset** rather than pointing at nothing.

### 5. The rules that must survive

Stated in the bead and worth repeating as acceptance, because they are the substance and the commands
were only ever the illustration:

- check the port before starting a server;
- **refuse rather than reuse** what is already listening;
- **build after the reset, never before** (`verifier.md:246`);
- pick the fixture that exercises what the bead changed.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):**

1. **The targets are declared and iterated.**
   RED: `tests/` — a consumer declaring `launch_targets web desktop` yields both, with commands and
   ports; an unknown name in the index yields nothing for that name rather than an error.
   GREEN: the reads.
2. **Nothing declared means ask.**
   RED: with no `launch_targets`, the resolver reports **that there are none** — distinctly from
   "none matched".
   GREEN: the guard. **The prose change that turns this into "ask the navigator" is increment 4.**
3. **The ports come from the keys.**
   RED: `port_base` and `port_block_size` produce the block the smoke prose describes.
   GREEN: the arithmetic.
4. **No role names a tool.**
   RED: `grep -nE "pnpm|tauri|vite|@atlantis|5173|4174|4183" agents/ skills/ docs/` returns nothing.
   GREEN: `verifier.md`, `reviewer.md`, `implement-bead/SKILL.md`, `docs/agent-workflow.md`.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the pin bump **and** the launch keys, `port_base`, `port_block_size`,
`warm_build_cmd` and `fixtures_doc` in the conf. **These must land together** — a bumped submodule
with no launch targets means **every verification stops and asks the navigator how to run the app.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| declared targets resolve with command and port | `tests/` | §1 |
| **no `launch_targets` is reported as "none declared"** | same | §2 — the ask |
| a name in the index with no `launch_<name>` is reported, not silently dropped | same | a half-written conf |
| `port_base` / `port_block_size` produce the block | same | §3 |
| `warm_build_cmd` and `fixtures_doc` absent → their steps are skipped | same | §4 |
| **no role file names pnpm, tauri, vite, @atlantis or a port number** | same | the bead |
| **the four surviving rules are still stated** | same | §5 — the substance |
| every existing test | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `for t in tests/*.sh`.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing reaches a player: agent prose and a config file. The navigator
ranked the ah-qled family P1 on 2026-08-21.

**Decided here** (architecture): **flat keys plus a `launch_targets` index rather than a list of
records**, because `project-conf` cannot express records and a third config file for two targets is
not worth a third parser; **`notes` as a comment line**, which the format gives free; and **not**
adding structure to `project-conf` for this.

## Out of scope

- **Adding list or record support to `project-conf`.**
- **ah-qled.7.1's gate keys** and **ah-qled.7.3's release keys** — different keys, same file.
- **What atlantis-hud's launch commands are.** This declares them.
- **The verification workflow itself.** Only how the app is started becomes declarable.

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rnE "pnpm|tauri|vite|@atlantis|5173|4174|4183" agents/ skills/ docs/   # nothing
```

Then by hand — **and the real test is a verification, not a grep**:

1. With the keys in this repo's conf, **run a real verification**: Psylocke must start the web app and
   the desktop app exactly as it does today. **This is the acceptance.**
2. Confirm the **desktop** target still carries `--features desktop-runtime`. Without it the stub main
   exits at once, and a lost flag would look like a broken app rather than a lost flag.
3. **Remove `launch_targets` and start a verification.** It must **ask you how to run the
   application** — not guess, and not skip. Put the keys back.
4. Confirm the port checks still refuse a port that is already listening.
5. Confirm the smoke port block still works from `port_base` / `port_block_size`.
6. Read `verifier.md` as a stranger in a Python project: does it tell you how to launch the app
   **without naming a tool you do not have?**
7. Confirm `warm_build_cmd` agrees with whatever ah-qled.2 settled — one spelling, not two.

## Known traps

- **🔴 `project-conf` cannot hold a list of records**, and `lookup` returns only the first match, so
  repeated `launch_target` lines silently give you one. Flat keys plus an index, or a separate file —
  not repeated keys.
- **🔴 No targets must mean *ask*, not guess or skip.** A verifier that improvises a command, or
  quietly reports nothing to verify, is the ah-qled.6 failure in a new place.
- **`--features desktop-runtime` is load-bearing.** Dropping it builds the stub main, which exits at
  once — and the symptom looks like a broken application.
- **`warm_build_cmd` and ah-qled.2's `--prewarm` are the same rename from two ends.** Check which
  merged; a third spelling is worse than either.
- **Keep the four rules.** The ports and commands were illustrations; *"check before claiming"*,
  *"refuse rather than reuse"*, *"build after the reset"* and *"pick the fixture that exercises what
  changed"* are the actual content.
- **The consumer PR must carry the keys**, or every verification stops and asks.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**
acceptance_criteria:
- Launch targets are declared as FLAT KEYS plus an index - `launch_targets web desktop`, `launch_web`, `launch_web_port` - NOT as a list of {name, command, port, notes}. project-conf is key/value with the value running to end of line, and its lookup returns only the FIRST match, so records and repeated keys are both unexpressible. `notes` become comment lines, which the format gives free.
- NOTHING is added to project-conf's format, and no third config file is introduced.
- WITH NO launch_targets DECLARED, THE ROLE ASKS THE NAVIGATOR how to run the application. It must not guess a command and must not skip the verification silently.
- A name in the index with no matching launch_<name> is reported, not silently dropped.
- launch_<name>_port replaces the six hardcoded lsof lines at reviewer.md:207, verifier.md:249-250 and docs/agent-workflow.md:514. port_base and port_block_size replace the smoke arithmetic at implement-bead/SKILL.md:395-396.
- warm_build_cmd (optional) replaces --with-wasm at both call sites AND AGREES WITH ah-qled.2's --prewarm rename - one spelling, not a third. fixtures_doc (optional) replaces verifier.md:271's README, with the step SKIPPED when unset.
- The desktop target keeps `--features desktop-runtime`; without it the stub main exits at once and the symptom looks like a broken app.
- `grep -rnE "pnpm|tauri|vite|@atlantis|5173|4174|4183" agents/ skills/ docs/` returns nothing.
- The four rules survive, stated as rules: check the port before starting a server; refuse rather than reuse what is already listening; build after the reset never before; pick the fixture that exercises what the bead changed.
- The consumer PR adds the launch keys, port_base, port_block_size, warm_build_cmd and fixtures_doc IN THE SAME PR as the pin bump - without them every verification stops and asks.
- cerebro's suites pass.

title: An agent runs the project's gate without knowing what it is called
description:
## The coupling

The upstream issue calls this the highest-impact single failure, and the re-audit agrees:
`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` names `pnpm run check:fast` as an imperative with no fallback. An
implementer in a Python project runs it, fails, and has no instruction for what to do instead.

17 `pnpm` occurrences plus `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` in that one file, concentrated at:

- `:85, :405-421` — "lint, typecheck, the touched packages' unit tests, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo clippy`. It is not the browser suites: `test:smoke`, `build:web` and `test:pwa`… Run the
  full `pnpm run check`… run `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core build:wasm`"
- `:363` — `pnpm exec tsx scripts/diskPreflight.ts`, a consumer-side TypeScript file invoked
  through pnpm
- `:423-426` — atlantis-hud's entire CI path filter, written out
- `:518` — `pnpm run test:smoke`, `test:pwa`, `test:native` for reproducing a flake

And in `agents/orchestrator.md`: `:41,133-141` `pnpm sightings` (which resolves to
`tsx scripts/retroSightings.ts` in **atlantis-hud's** `package.json`, not cerebro's), `:767,789`
`pnpm run release <bump>` and a gate described as "lint, typecheck, unit tests, rustfmt, clippy,
rust tests", `:798-804` a GitHub Actions workflow literally named `Release` producing a macOS bundle.

## What changes

Two executable consumer hooks, `<consumer>/.cerebro/gate-fast` and `.cerebro/gate-full` — exit 0 is
green, and that is the whole contract. The skill then says "run the fast gate" and carries no command
at all. This alone removes every `pnpm` and `cargo` occurrence from `implement-bead`.

`scripts/launch-preflight` already refuses to start a session on a missing agent file and is the
natural place to refuse an implementer when `gate-fast` is missing — a loud, immediate failure
instead of an agent improvising.

Detection (`package.json` scripts, `Makefile` targets, `cargo` presence) is a convenience fallback
only, never a guess that runs.

`retroSightings.ts` should move into `.claude/cerebro/scripts/` and be called by path, as
`work-beads`, `roster` and `prepare-worktree` already are — it is harness functionality that
happens to live in the consumer. Same for the disk check: a language-neutral
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/disk-preflight`, or an optional `.cerebro/preflight` hook skipped when
absent.

`release_cmd` and an optional post-tag watch become project keys; "there is a build to watch after
tagging" must be optional, not assumed.

Blocked by the project-file child.

title: In another project every bead looks invisible, so nothing is verified and release notes come out empty
description:
## The coupling

The upstream issue names this as §2's first job and counts four copies. There are **seven, across six
files**, and they serve two different rules:

The app-touching test, as a regex:
- `agents/reviewer.md:195` — "user-experience-touching iff some changed path matches `^(packages|crates|apps)/`"
- `agents/verifier.md:202` — "**application-touching** iff some changed path matches `^(packages|crates|apps)/`"
- `skills/release-notes/SKILL.md:51` — "**Application-touching iff some changed path matches `^(packages|crates|apps)/`.**"

The never-edit rule, as prose:
- `agents/architect.md:179` — "If you are in `packages/`, `crates/`, `apps/` or `emacs/`"
- `agents/verifier.md:443` — "If you are editing `packages/`, `crates/` or `apps/`"
- `agents/planner.md:123-124` — "If you are editing `packages/` or `crates/`"
- `agents/user-feedback.md:521` — "you do not touch `packages/` or `crates/`"
- and `.claude/cerebro/CLAUDE.md:144`

Plus `agents/architect.md:87-92`, which is a verbatim map of atlantis-hud's workspace members:
`packages/shared`, `packages/core-client`, `packages/browser-core`, `packages/ruleset`,
`crates/core`, `crates/core-persistence`, `crates/core-tauri`, `crates/core-wasm`, `apps/desktop`,
`apps/web`.

## Why this one matters most

It is the **quietest** failure in the epic. A consumer with `src/` or `lib/` gets no error: every
bead is classified as invisible, so release notes come out empty and every verification is skipped,
with no signal that anything is wrong. Every other coupling at least fails loudly.

The seven copies also drift by construction — a consumer must edit six files consistently to
re-point them.

## What changes

One `app_paths` key in the project file, quoted by all seven call sites. The roles then say "the
app-touching test is `app_paths`" and "never edit the project's source directories" rather than
naming directories.

For `architect.md`'s weekly fan-out, replace the literal member list with a probe — read the
workspace manifest, or `git ls-files` grouped by top-level path — so the list cannot go stale.

Two fixes while here: `architect.md:179`'s `emacs/` is simply wrong (cerebro's elisp is at
`.claude/cerebro/emacs`, and atlantis-hud has no top-level `emacs/`), and `orchestrator.md`'s three
bare `emacs/cerebro.el` references should carry the `.claude/cerebro/` prefix, since a bare `emacs/`
reads as a consumer directory.

Blocked by the project-file child.

design:
## Context

**The quietest failure in the epic**, and that is why it matters most. A consumer with `src/` or
`lib/` gets **no error at all**: every bead is classified as invisible, so **release notes come out
empty and every verification is skipped**, with nothing on stderr. Every other coupling in this epic
at least fails loudly.

Where the application lives is written out **seven times across six files**, and the upstream issue
counts four.

### 🔴 The seven copies are two different rules, and they do not agree with each other

I read all seven. **The app-touching regex is consistent:**

| Site | Says |
|---|---|
| `agents/reviewer.md:195` | `^(packages\|crates\|apps)/` |
| `agents/verifier.md:202` | `^(packages\|crates\|apps)/` |
| `skills/release-notes/SKILL.md:51` | `^(packages\|crates\|apps)/` |

**The never-edit rule is not.** Three different lists:

| Site | `packages/` | `crates/` | `apps/` | `emacs/` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agents/architect.md:179` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **✓** |
| `.claude/cerebro/CLAUDE.md:144` (Forge) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **✓** |
| `agents/verifier.md:443` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `agents/planner.md:123` | ✓ | ✓ | **—** | — |
| `agents/user-feedback.md:521` | ✓ | ✓ | **—** | — |

**`emacs/` is not the consumer's application — it is cerebro's own source.** So the architect's and
Forge's rule is genuinely *"do not edit application code **or the harness's elisp**"*, which is two
clauses, not one. **Folding `emacs/` into `app_paths` would be wrong** in every consumer: it would
declare cerebro's own source part of the consumer's application.

**`apps/` missing from the planner's and user-feedback's rule is drift**, not a decision — nothing
explains why those two roles may edit `apps/` when the verifier may not. Unifying them **changes
behaviour**: a planner is newly told not to edit `apps/`. That is a correction, and it should be
stated as one rather than slipped in.

Plus **`agents/architect.md:87-92`**, a verbatim map of atlantis-hud's workspace members
(`packages/shared`, `packages/core-client`, `packages/browser-core`, `packages/ruleset`,
`crates/core`, `crates/core-persistence`, `crates/core-tauri`, `crates/core-wasm`, `apps/desktop`,
`apps/web`).

**`ah-qled.1` has merged**, and `app_paths` is already on its designed key list. Cerebro change, so
**two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. One declaration

`app_paths` in the tracked `.claude/cerebro-project.conf`, defaulting — when the key is absent — to
**nothing matching**, not to a guess.

**🔴 Absent must not mean "everything is application code", and must not mean silence either.** The
whole defect is a silent misclassification; replacing one silent default with another achieves
nothing. When no `app_paths` is declared and a classification is asked for, **say so** — the roles
that consume it (the verifier deciding whether to check a bead, release-notes deciding whether to
mention it) would otherwise repeat exactly today's failure in a new place.

Value for this repository: `^(packages|crates|apps)/`. **It contains no `#`**, so it is expressible —
worth checking, since `project-conf` cannot carry one.

### 2. The three regex sites read it

`reviewer.md:195`, `verifier.md:202`, `release-notes/SKILL.md:51` say *"matches the project's
application paths"* and stop quoting a regex. Each of those is prose an agent follows, so it must also
say **how to get the value** — `project-conf app_paths` — rather than leaving the agent to guess.

### 3. The never-edit rule, unified — with `emacs/` kept separate

All five become *"if you are editing the project's application paths, you have taken the wrong job"*,
**plus**, for `architect.md:179` and `CLAUDE.md:144` only, a second clause naming **`emacs/`** as
cerebro's own source.

**Say in the commit message that `apps/` is newly included for the planner and user-feedback**, and
why: nothing distinguished those two roles, and the omission was drift.

### 4. `architect.md:87-92`

A verbatim workspace map of one repository. **Delete it, or replace it with how to find the answer**
(`app_paths`, or the project's own workspace manifest). It is the single most project-specific block
in the agent prose and it teaches every consumer's Forge the wrong layout.

### 5. Not here

`agents/orchestrator.md`'s release prose (**ah-qled.7.3**), the gate (**ah-qled.7.1**), and
`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:423-426`'s CI path filter — **which is also `app_paths`** and is
ah-qled.7.1's to change. **Coordinate**: both beads want the same key, and neither should invent a
second one.

## Increments

1. **The key is read and its absence is loud.**
   RED: `tests/` — `project-conf app_paths` returns the configured value; **with no key, a
   classification helper reports that it cannot classify** rather than returning "no match".
   GREEN: the read and the guard.
2. **The three regex copies go.**
   RED: `grep -n "packages|crates|apps" agents/ skills/` finds none of the three.
   GREEN: the prose, each naming `project-conf app_paths`.
3. **The never-edit rule is one rule, and `emacs/` survives.**
   RED: all five sites read the same way; **`emacs/` still appears in exactly `architect.md` and
   `CLAUDE.md`** and in neither of the other three.
   GREEN: the prose.
4. **The workspace map goes.**
   RED: `grep -n "core-persistence\|core-wasm\|apps/desktop" agents/` returns nothing.
   GREEN: `architect.md:87-92`.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** the pin bump **and `app_paths ^(packages|crates|apps)/` in the conf**.
**These must land together**: a bumped submodule with no `app_paths` makes every bead unclassifiable,
which is this bead's own failure mode arriving by the front door.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `app_paths` is read whole, regex intact | `tests/` | §1 |
| **an absent `app_paths` is reported, not silently "no match"** | same | the quiet failure |
| **no `^(packages\|crates\|apps)/` remains in `agents/` or `skills/`** | same | §2 |
| the never-edit rule reads identically in all five | same | §3 |
| **`emacs/` appears in exactly two files** | same | the clause that must not be folded in |
| the workspace map is gone | same | §4 |
| every existing test | all | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `for t in tests/*.sh`.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing reaches a player. The navigator ranked the ah-qled family P1
on 2026-08-21.

**Decided here** (architecture): **keeping `emacs/` out of `app_paths`** and as its own clause, since
it is cerebro's source rather than the consumer's application; **unifying `apps/` into the planner's
and user-feedback's rule** as a correction of drift, stated in the commit message; and **making an
absent `app_paths` loud** rather than defaulting either way.

## Out of scope

- **ah-qled.7.1's** `:423-426` CI path filter, **which is the same key** — coordinate, do not
  duplicate.
- **ah-qled.7.3's** release prose.
- **Deciding atlantis-hud's application paths.** They are what they are; this bead declares them.
- **The workspace members themselves.**

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rn "packages|crates|apps" agents/ skills/ CLAUDE.md      # nothing
grep -rn "emacs/" agents/ CLAUDE.md                            # architect.md and CLAUDE.md only
grep -rn "core-persistence\|core-wasm\|apps/desktop" agents/   # nothing
```

Then by hand:

1. `scripts/project-conf app_paths` → `^(packages|crates|apps)/`, the regex **intact** — no
   truncation at a metacharacter.
2. Read `verifier.md` as a stranger: does it tell you how to decide whether a bead is
   application-touching **without naming a directory this project happens to have?**
3. **Remove `app_paths` and ask for a classification.** It must **say it cannot classify**. If it
   quietly answers "not application-touching", the bead's own defect has been reproduced.
4. Restore it, and confirm a real bead classifies as it does today — **nothing about this
   repository's behaviour may change**.
5. Confirm `architect.md` still forbids `emacs/` and that `verifier.md`, `planner.md` and
   `user-feedback.md` do **not** newly forbid it.
6. Confirm `planner.md` and `user-feedback.md` **now include `apps/`**, which they did not before —
   the intended correction.

## Known traps

- **🔴 `emacs/` is not application code.** It is cerebro's own source. Folding it into `app_paths`
  declares the harness part of every consumer's application; dropping it lets Forge and the architect
  edit the elisp they are forbidden.
- **🔴 An absent key must be loud.** The defect is a silent misclassification; a default of "matches
  nothing" reproduces it exactly, and a default of "matches everything" verifies every docs change.
- **The five never-edit copies do not agree today.** Unifying them **adds `apps/`** for the planner
  and user-feedback. That is a correction, not an accident — say so, or it looks like a mistake in
  review.
- **ah-qled.7.1 wants the same key** for `implement-bead:423-426`. Two keys for one fact is the thing
  this bead exists to end.
- **The value is a regex in a `key value` file.** `project-conf` strips from any `#`, so a pattern
  containing one cannot be expressed. `^(packages|crates|apps)/` is safe; check anything else.
- **The workspace map at `architect.md:87-92`** is prose, not code, and greps for `packages|crates`
  will not find it. Look for the member names.
- **Two PRs, and the consumer PR must carry `app_paths`.**
acceptance_criteria:
- `app_paths` is declared once in the tracked .claude/cerebro-project.conf and read through project-conf. Value here: ^(packages|crates|apps)/ - checked to contain no `#`, which project-conf cannot carry.
- AN ABSENT app_paths IS LOUD: a classification request with no key SAYS IT CANNOT CLASSIFY. It must not quietly answer "not application-touching" (which reproduces this bead's own defect) nor "everything matches" (which verifies every docs change).
- The three regex copies are gone: agents/reviewer.md:195, agents/verifier.md:202, skills/release-notes/SKILL.md:51 name the project's application paths and say how to get them, not a regex.
- The five never-edit copies read identically: agents/architect.md:179, .claude/cerebro/CLAUDE.md:144, agents/verifier.md:443, agents/planner.md:123, agents/user-feedback.md:521.
- `emacs/` IS NOT FOLDED INTO app_paths - it is cerebro's own source, not the consumer's application. It survives as a SECOND CLAUSE in exactly architect.md and CLAUDE.md, and appears in none of the other three.
- planner.md and user-feedback.md NEWLY INCLUDE apps/, which they omitted. This is a correction of drift, not an accident, and the commit message says so.
- agents/architect.md:87-92's verbatim map of atlantis-hud's workspace members is gone or replaced by how to find the answer.
- ah-qled.7.1 wants the same key for implement-bead:423-426; coordinate rather than writing a second one.
- The consumer PR adds `app_paths` IN THE SAME PR as the pin bump - a bumped submodule without it makes every bead unclassifiable, which is this bead's failure arriving by the front door.
- This repository's behaviour is unchanged: a real bead classifies exactly as it does today.
- cerebro's suites pass.

title: A consumer can declare its own fleet, and the tests stop pinning ours
description:
## The coupling

Not in the upstream issue, which calls the roster already generic. It is generic in *content* — the
X-Men are cerebro's branding, not atlantis-hud's — but it is **not overridable**, which is the reuse
blocker.

- `scripts/roster:39-59` holds the whole fleet as a `TABLE=` heredoc inside the submodule. A consumer
  wanting different names, more implementers, or a role cerebro does not ship must edit a file shared
  with every other consumer. This is precisely the problem `.cerebro/models.conf` was created to
  solve for models.
- `scripts/agent-state:22-29` fixes the phase vocabulary as a closed union naming roles by agent name
  (`triage plan (a planner: Xavier, Beast)`, `daily weekly (Forge)` …), enforced at `:108` as a
  literal `case` that **exits 2 on an unknown phase**. A consumer-added role therefore cannot report
  state at all. The comment at `:30-32` already concedes the vocabulary is not checked per role, so
  the whitelist buys little and costs extensibility.
- `scripts/launch:78-79` reads model and effort from `agents/<role>.md` inside the submodule, and
  `launch-preflight:87` then refuses a consumer-supplied role with `the submodule is behind`, which
  misdiagnoses the cause.
- Seven `run-*` shims each hardcode one name; `scripts/run-implementer:25-33` still carries the
  Bishop→Forge rename courtesy; `scripts/implementer-state` is a rename shim whose removal condition
  is a release of atlantis-hud.

## The tests are the hidden cost

They will go red on any consumer-supplied roster, and this is the part the upstream issue's half-day
estimate does not account for:

- `tests/launchers.sh:260-261` duplicates the roster as two parallel arrays — exactly the drift
  `scripts/roster` was created to prevent, reintroduced in its own suite.
- `tests/launchers.sh:454-481` pins `roster --entry Cypher` to an exact row, `agents/reviewer.md` to
  `model: opus`, `agents/architect.md` to `model: opus` + `effort: xhigh`, and Forge's phase words in
  both `agent-state` and `emacs/cerebro.el`.
- `tests/launchers.sh:127` asserts the literal name `Forge` is not an implementer; `:210-219`
  hardcodes `opus` where the file's own `model_of` helper would answer.
- `tests/agent-alive.sh:107-119` needs `Beast` present *and* `Beastly` absent.
- `tests/agent-state.sh:387` needs ten specific implementer names.

## What changes

`scripts/roster` stays the single reader and gains a source: `<consumer>/.cerebro/roster`, same TSV
shape, when present; the built-in TABLE as fallback. Every existing caller keeps working unchanged.
Agent files resolve from `<consumer>/.cerebro/agents/` with the submodule as fallback, and
preflight's message distinguishes "not shipped by cerebro" from "submodule behind".

Open the phase vocabulary — either drop the whitelist to a shape check, or read it from the same
consumer source. `emacs/cerebro--phases` must move with it; `tests/launchers.sh:466-472` already
pins the two together. (Note `cerebro--phases` is referenced nowhere in the elisp — it may simply be
dead, in which case delete it.)

Rewrite the tests to assert **invariants** rather than values: every roster row has an agent file
whose frontmatter parses; every phase a shipped agent file uses is in the vocabulary; names come from
`roster --implementers | head -n N` rather than being spelled out. `tests/launchers.sh:101-110`
already demonstrates the pattern.

Delete `scripts/implementer-state` and the Bishop courtesy; generate the `run-*` shims from the
roster or drop them for `launch <Name>`.

title: The janitor deletes a directory called target and trusts GitHub to say what merged
description:
## The coupling

Not in the upstream issue. Three sweeps encode atlantis-hud's build layout and git conventions.

**`scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` — destructive and Cargo-specific.**

- `:115` `target="$tree/target"` in `reclaim_cold_target`. A Node consumer's `node_modules/` is never
  reclaimed, a Python consumer's `.venv/` never, and a consumer whose *source* lives in `target/`
  loses it. The justification at `:46-48` names a tracked `.cargo/config.toml`, a precondition only
  atlantis-hud satisfies, so on any other consumer the reclaim logic's premise is silently false.
- `:157` `if [ "$name" = "psylocke" ]; then` — one roster agent's name, lowercased, as a literal in
  the control flow of a destructive script. A consumer that renames or drops the verifier loses the
  exception and has its verification tree deleted mid-verification; one with a second such tree
  cannot express it.
- `:150` still sweeps `"$repo_root"/.claude/worktrees/*`, the pre-`.cerebro/` location. No new
  consumer has ever had that directory; it is a permanent extra target in a destructive script.
- `:88-92` the two-test `landed_on_main` design is only safe because this repository merges with
  `--squash`; the `-d`-then-`-D` force-delete fallback at `:192-195` does more than its comment
  claims under a rebase or merge-commit consumer.
- `:105` `gh pr list --head "$branch" --state merged` — GitHub via `gh` is the only recognised
  authority on whether work landed. A GitLab or PR-less consumer always reads "not merged", so
  squash-merged worktrees are kept for ever and the janitor never reclaims anything.

**`scripts/sweep-claims.sh` — atlantis-hud's commit conventions.**

- `:96` detects delivery with `--grep "($id):"`, a Conventional-Commits scope equal to the bead id.
  A consumer that does not put its work-item id in a `type(scope):` subject gets `on_main:false` for
  every bead, so nothing is ever swept and the cleanup silently does nothing.
- `:97` excludes the literal `docs($id): mockup` — the `plan-bead` convention, in a sweep.

**`scripts/sweep-stalled.sh:86`** — `if [[ "$wt_branch" == "$id-"* ]]`. A consumer naming branches
`feature/PROJ-123` gets `branch:null` and every claim measured from claim time instead of real
commits, so live work reads as stalled.

## What changes

Project keys with safe defaults: `reclaim_dirs` (default empty, so the destructive behaviour is
opt-in), `commit_ref_pattern` (default `({id}):`, substituted not concatenated),
`non_delivery_commit_pattern` (default empty), `branch_pattern` (default `{id}-*`),
`merged_check` (`gh|none|<command>`; with `none`, fall back to the `rev-list` test plus the
staleness bound).

The `psylocke` exception comes from the roster — a `keep-worktree` column, or `roster --role
verifier` — not from a name in an `if`. Drop the `.claude/worktrees` legacy path.

Also fix, while here: `agents/orchestrator.md:317` says `.claude/worktrees/psylocke` where every
other reference says `.cerebro/worktrees/psylocke`, and `.claude/worktrees/` exists in this checkout
as a separate directory — so the never-delete instruction currently names the wrong tree.

### 🔴 Two corrections before anything is built

**1. `.claude/worktrees/` is not vestigial here.** The bead calls `:150` *"the pre-`.cerebro/`
location. No new consumer has ever had that directory"* and says **"Drop the `.claude/worktrees`
