design:
## Context

Every interactive role schedules itself. `agents/user-feedback.md:86-91`:

```bash
for i in $(seq 5); do sleep 60; echo "Moira idle, ${i}/5 of this half"; done
```

Ten minutes in two halves, because a single ten-minute silent `Bash` call is rejected outright.
`plan-bead/SKILL.md:326` says the same thing again in its own words, and every interactive role
carries a *"Sleeping without dying"* section that exists **only** to work around the tool.

What that costs: it is **opaque** (an agent inside `sleep` is indistinguishable from one that has
hung — the fleet view sees `idle` for both), **unstoppable** (a stop flag cannot land on a session
mid-sleep), **unreliable** (`scripts/agent-asking` exists as a PreToolUse hook precisely because
state-writing was an instruction and agents forgot — cadence is the same class of problem), and
**rigid** (changing a cadence means editing prose and restarting a session; in elisp it is a
`defcustom`).

**The inversion: the monitor owns cadence, the agent still owns policy.** The fleet view decides
*when* a role resumes; the role's own skill still decides *what* to do on waking — Xavier still
counts its buffer, Moira still walks the issues oldest first. This removes the timer, not the
judgement.

Blocked on **ah-hiib.1** (the log) and **ah-hiib.2** (reading it), deliberately: the intervals must
come from measured idle frequency, not from the ten minutes in today's prose, which has never been
checked against anything. Also depends on **ah-4xm4** — see the trap about that below, because **the
bead's own note about it is now out of date.**

Cerebro change, so **two PRs**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. A fourth state: `waiting` — `scripts/agent-state`

The epic's second constraint is explicit: **do not add a third meaning to `idle`.** For an
implementer `idle` means "safe to retire" and the fleet view ends it within a poll of a stop flag;
for an interactive role it already means "sleeping, will wake myself". A third meaning collides with
the race `agents/orchestrator.md` records — an implementer between beads writes `idle`, claims its
next bead, and only then writes `working`, so a flag landing in that gap ends a session holding a
fresh claim.

So a distinct state:

```
scripts/agent-state <name> waiting --wake-in <seconds> --pid <pid>
```

- Writes `state: "waiting"` and **`wake_at`**, an ISO timestamp computed from `--wake-in`.
- **Interactive names only.** `waiting` is refused from an implementer exactly as `done` is refused
  from an interactive name (`agent-state:75-86`) — an implementer is replaced between beads and has
  no cadence of its own. The roster check at `:68-73` already distinguishes them.
- `--wake-in` is **required** with `waiting` and invalid without it, in the manner `--phase` is
  already validated against state at `:97-102`.
- The existing `since` / `phase_since` rules are untouched, and `waiting` appends to the ah-hiib.1
  log like any other state — which is what makes the cadence itself measurable afterwards.

### 2. The decision — a `waiting` arm in `cerebro--supervise-action`

`cerebro--supervise-action` (`cerebro.el:773-783`) currently guards on
`(eq (cerebro-agent-kind agent) 'implementer)`, which excludes every interactive role. **That guard
has to become per-arm rather than wrapping the whole body**: `restart`, `retire` and `nudge` stay
implementer-only for the reasons its docstring gives at length, and the new arm is interactive-only.
The docstring already warns that *"any future unification of this function must keep excluding them
explicitly rather than by accident"* — this is that moment, and the exclusion must stay explicit.

```elisp
('waiting
 (cond
  (stop-flag-p 'retire)          ; nothing is in flight; the flag lands cleanly
  ((cerebro--wake-due-p agent now) 'poke)
  (t nil)))
```

**`waiting` + stop flag is `retire`, and that is an acceptance criterion in itself**: a waiting role
holds no bead, no claim and no worktree, so ending it now strands nothing. It is the same reasoning
`idle` + stop flag already uses for an implementer (`:777`), and it is what makes a stop flag land
cleanly instead of racing a `sleep`.

`cerebro--wake-due-p` is pure, takes `wake_at` and `now`, and gets its own ERT tests.

### 3. The poke — and why the fragile channel is safe here

The epic's third constraint: *"typing into a vterm is a fragile primary API… keystrokes arriving
while an agent is mid-tool-call is a real failure mode."* True — **and it is exactly the failure this
design removes.**

`cerebro--nudge` (`:1358-1364`) types into the session's vterm buffer, and **cerebro has no other
channel: there is no message API in the codebase today.** But the danger in typing at an agent has
always been *typing at a busy one*. A role in `waiting` has, by construction, **ended its turn and is
sitting at the prompt** — that is what `waiting` means and it is the whole point of the state. So the
new state converts the fragile channel into a safe one, rather than needing a new channel to be
invented.

Reuse `cerebro--nudge`'s mechanism with a wake message of its own (`cerebro--wake-message`).

**It must not silently fail**, which is the remaining acceptance criterion. The acknowledgement is
free: **a poked role writes its next transition**, so the log and the state file both show it leaving
`waiting`. So —

- after a poke, record when it was sent;
- if the role is **still `waiting` with the same `wake_at`** after a grace period (60 seconds is
  ample for a session that is genuinely at the prompt), **poke once more**;
- if it is still there after the second, **stop poking and show it in the fleet view** as a role that
  did not answer. A line the navigator can see beats a poke repeated every tick for ever, and it is
  the same judgement `cerebro--supervise-action` already makes about a `nudge`.

**A session cerebro did not start cannot be poked**: `cerebro--nudge` resolves a buffer via
`cerebro--session`, and an external session has none. Treat it as the existing code does — the
`cerebro-agent-external` check — and say so, or a role in somebody's own terminal looks broken.

### 4. Cadence is configuration — a `defcustom`

One per role, or one alist keyed by role, with **defaults taken from ah-hiib.2's measured idle
distribution rather than from the ten minutes in today's prose.** Whoever builds this should run
`scripts/fleet-history --summary`, read the `idle`/`waiting` rows, and **say in the PR what the
measurement was** — that is the entire reason this bead sits third in its family.

The role passes `--wake-in`, so the number must reach the agent: the simplest honest answer is that
**the role asks for its own interval and the monitor is free to poke earlier**, which keeps `agent-state`
ignorant of policy. A monitor that pokes before `wake_at` is not a bug — cadence is its to own.

### 5. The prose goes — every role document

**Delete "Sleeping without dying" from every role it appears in**, and replace it with the new
instruction: finish the pass, write `waiting` with an interval, **end the turn**. At least
`agents/user-feedback.md`, `agents/orchestrator.md`, `agents/verifier.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`,
`agents/architect.md` and `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:326` — **grep for it rather than working from
this list**, and leave none behind. A role still carrying the old prose will sleep *and* be poked.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):**

1. **A role can say it is waiting.**
   RED: `tests/agent-state.sh` — `waiting records a wake_at`; `waiting is refused from an
   implementer`; `waiting without --wake-in is refused`; `--wake-in is refused without waiting`.
   GREEN: the new state.
2. **The monitor knows when to wake it.**
   RED: ERT on `cerebro--wake-due-p` — before, after, and a missing `wake_at`.
   GREEN: the predicate.
3. **The arm decides.**
   RED: ERT — `a waiting role past its wake is poked`; `a waiting role before it is left alone`;
   **`a waiting role under a stop flag retires`**; `an implementer never reaches the waiting arm`;
   `an interactive role is still never restarted or nudged`.
   GREEN: the `waiting` arm and the per-arm kind guards.
4. **The poke is sent, and confirmed.**
   RED: ERT with `cerebro--nudge` stubbed — sent once; **re-sent once after the grace period**;
   **not sent a third time, and surfaced instead**; never sent to an external session.
   GREEN: the poke and its bookkeeping.
5. **Cadence is configuration.** RED: ERT that the interval comes from the custom variable.
6. **The prose is gone.** `grep -r "Sleeping without dying"` returns nothing; each role document
   carries the new instruction.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** bump the submodule pin. **PR one merges first.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `waiting records a wake_at` | `tests/agent-state.sh` | the state |
| **`waiting is refused from an implementer`** | same | constraint 2 |
| `waiting without --wake-in is refused` | same | validation |
| `--wake-in is refused without waiting` | same | validation |
| every existing agent-state test | same | **unchanged** |
| `cerebro--wake-due-p` before / after / missing | ERT | the predicate |
| `a waiting role past its wake is poked` | ERT | the bead |
| **`a waiting role under a stop flag retires`** | ERT | the clean stop |
| `an implementer never reaches the waiting arm` | ERT | constraint 2 |
| `an interactive role is never restarted or nudged` | ERT | the docstring's warning |
| **`a poke is re-sent once, then surfaced`** | ERT | no silent failure |
| `an external session is never poked` | ERT | no buffer to type into |
| `the interval comes from the custom variable` | ERT | configurability |
| every existing supervise-action test | ERT | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** cerebro's `for t in tests/*.sh`, and ERT.

## User-facing decisions

**None to ask for.** Nothing here reaches a player; this is how the navigator's own fleet is
operated. The three constraints that *would* have been questions were settled by the navigator with
Cerebro on 2026-08-20 and are recorded in the bead's design: **a poke does not reset context**;
**no third meaning for `idle`**; **weigh the vterm channel rather than assuming it**.

**Decided here, inside those constraints** (architecture): a distinct `waiting` state carrying
`wake_at`, rather than a flag on `idle`; the vterm poke kept — because a `waiting` role is at the
prompt by construction, which is what made the channel fragile in the first place, and cerebro has no
other channel today; acknowledgement by the role's own next transition, with one retry and then a
visible line; and cadence as a `defcustom` seeded from ah-hiib.2's measurements.

**Explicitly not done:** restarting a role per pass. The epic forbids it — a planner holds a mockup
conversation with the navigator across several turns, and restarting mid-conversation destroys it.

## Out of scope

- **Bounding an interactive role's context.** Named and rejected in the epic; a poke is the same
  session and its context still grows.
- **Implementers.** They are replaced between beads and have no cadence.
- **Writing or reading the log** — ah-hiib.1 and ah-hiib.2.
- **The stalled-claim sweep** — ah-4xm4, which is about implementers that stopped moving.
- **A new message channel to `claude` sessions.** Considered, does not exist in cerebro today, and
  inventing one is a bead of its own — the `waiting` state is what makes the existing channel
  sufficient.
- **What a role does on waking.** Policy stays in each role's skill.

## Validation

```bash
bash tests/agent-state.sh
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
grep -rn "Sleeping without dying" . && echo "STILL THERE - increment 6 is not done"
```

Then by hand, with the fleet view open — this is a change to how the fleet is operated and cannot be
signed off from tests:

1. Let an interactive role (Moira or a planner) finish a pass. It writes **`waiting`** and **ends its
   turn** — confirm in its terminal that it is at the prompt, **not** counting out sleep halves.
2. The fleet view shows it as **waiting, with when it will wake** — visibly different from `idle` and
   from a hung session. That distinction is an acceptance criterion; look at it properly.
3. Wait for the interval and confirm it **resumes on its own**, and that its next pass behaves
   normally.
4. **Set a stop flag on a waiting role.** It must retire **promptly and cleanly** — this is the
   behaviour that is impossible today.
5. Change the cadence `defcustom` **without restarting anything** and confirm the next wake honours
   it.
6. `scripts/fleet-history --summary` and confirm `waiting` intervals now appear — the cadence is
   measurable by the same tool that set it.
7. Poke-failure path: with a role waiting, make the poke fail (kill the vterm buffer) and confirm the
   fleet view **says so** rather than retrying for ever.
8. Confirm an implementer is completely unaffected: still `working`/`done`/`idle`, still restarted
   between beads.

## Known traps

- **The bead's note that ah-4xm4 "adds a `working` arm to the same function" is out of date.**
  ah-4xm4 was planned as a **confirmed Sweeps finding**, on the navigator's recorded decision, and
  deliberately leaves `cerebro--supervise-action` alone. So the two do **not** collide there — but
  ah-4xm4 is still a declared dependency and still merges first. Do not go looking for a `working`
  arm to merge with, and do not add one.
- **Do not overload `idle`.** The race is real: an implementer between beads is `idle` while holding
  a fresh claim, and a flag landing in that gap ends a session mid-claim.
- **The kind guard must become per-arm, explicitly.** `restart`, `retire` and `nudge` stay
  implementer-only; the docstring warns against unifying by accident, and dropping the outer guard
  without replacing it per-arm would let an interactive role be restarted — destroying exactly the
  mockup conversation the epic protects.
- **Poke only a `waiting` role.** That is what makes vterm typing safe; poking a `working` one is the
  mid-tool-call failure the epic warns about.
- **An external session has no buffer.** Poking one silently does nothing; exclude it and say so.
- **Bound the retries.** One re-send, then a visible line. A poke repeated every tick is an infinite
  loop nobody sees.
- **Leave no role behind.** Grep for the prose; a role that still sleeps *and* gets poked is worse
  than either.
- **Set the interval from ah-hiib.2's numbers, and say what they were.** Copying the existing ten
  minutes forward would waste the whole reason this bead is third in its family.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**
acceptance_criteria:
- An interactive role finishes a pass, writes `waiting` with an interval, and ENDS ITS TURN - it does not sleep inside its own session. The monitor resumes it.
- `scripts/agent-state <name> waiting --wake-in <seconds>` writes state "waiting" and a `wake_at` timestamp. It is refused from an implementer, and --wake-in is required with it and invalid without it.
- The "Sleeping without dying" prose is gone from every role document and skill it currently appears in; `grep -r "Sleeping without dying"` returns nothing.
- A stop flag lands cleanly on a waiting role: `waiting` + stop flag retires it, holding no bead, claim or worktree.
- `idle` gains no third meaning - a distinct state is used, so the implementer's idle-then-claim race is untouched.
- Cadence is a defcustom, changeable without editing an agent document or restarting a session, with defaults taken from ah-hiib.2's measured idle distribution (and the measurement stated in the PR).
- A waiting role is distinguishable in the fleet view from one that has hung and from an implementer that is idle-and-safe-to-retire, and shows when it will wake.
- The poke does not silently fail: acknowledgement is the role's own next transition; one re-send after a grace period, then it is surfaced in the fleet view rather than retried for ever.
- Only a `waiting` role is ever poked (it is at the prompt by construction), and a session cerebro did not start is never poked.
- `cerebro--supervise-action`'s kind guard becomes per-arm: restart/retire/nudge stay implementer-only, the waiting arm is interactive-only. An interactive role is never restarted - a planner's mockup conversation must survive.
- A poke does not reset context; roles are not restarted per pass.
- Existing agent-state and supervise-action behaviour and tests are unchanged.
- cerebro's suites pass; the submodule pin is bumped in a second PR after the cerebro PR merges.

title: Nobody can ask how long the fleet's work actually takes
description:
Once the transition log exists (ah-hiib.1) the fleet's behaviour is recorded but
still not readable. This bead makes it answerable.

The questions that went unanswered on 2026-08-20, each of which this should turn
into one command or one panel:

  - How long does an implementer typically hold a bead, and how is that split
    between building, waiting for review, and getting to main?
  - How long do agents actually wait at `asking` before the navigator answers?
    The 900-second nudge threshold in cerebro.el:726 has never been checked
    against a measured distribution.
  - How often does a role go idle, and how long does it stay there? This is the
    number the wake cadence in ah-hiib.3 must be tuned against.
  - Which agent is the outlier this week? A per-implementer comparison today
    needs a GitHub API crawl; Wolverine was found spending three times as long
    addressing reviews as Cyclops or Storm, and only because someone went
    looking by hand.
  - Did anything stall, and for how long? Four beads were found parked for a
    combined 21.7 hours and none of them surfaced while it was happening.

Elisp and bash only, per the navigator. The fleet view already renders a bead
panel and a Sweeps section, so a view over the log fits where the reader already
looks; a bash query is what Cerebro and the navigator reach for from a terminal.
Both are wanted -- the panel for the fleet as it stands, the query for a
question nobody anticipated.
design:
## Context

ah-hiib.1 makes the fleet write down what it did. This bead makes that **answerable**, and it is the
reading side only: **no agent gains behaviour and no cadence changes here.**

The questions that went unanswered on 2026-08-20, each of which this turns into one command or one
panel line:

- How long does an implementer hold a bead, split between building, waiting for review, and getting
  to main?
- **How long do agents actually wait at `asking`?** `cerebro-answer-timeout` is 900 seconds
  (`cerebro.el:726`) and has never been checked against a measured distribution.
- How often does a role go idle, and for how long? — the number **ah-hiib.3** must tune its cadence
  against.
- Which agent is the outlier this week? Wolverine was found spending three times as long addressing
  reviews as Cyclops or Storm, and only because somebody went looking by hand.
- Did anything stall, and for how long? Four beads sat parked for a combined 21.7 hours and none
  surfaced while it was happening.

**Both readers are wanted**, and the bead says so: a bash query for a question nobody anticipated,
and a panel where the navigator already looks.

**Blocked on ah-hiib.1**, whose log this reads. Bash and elisp only. This is a cerebro change, so
**two PRs** — see *Increments*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. The aggregation is bash — `scripts/fleet-history`

**All the computation lives here, and elisp only renders it.** That is the decisive split: it keeps
the fleet view's 5-second tick cheap by construction, and it means the panel and a terminal question
can never disagree, because they are the same code.

`scripts/work-beads` is the house example to follow — one job, `--json` on stdout, and a header
explaining what it excludes and why. Match its manners exactly, including **failing loudly**:
non-zero, a message on stderr, nothing on stdout, when the log is unreadable or a line will not
parse. An empty array that really means "the query broke" is the worst possible answer for a reader
deciding whether anything stalled.

```
scripts/fleet-history --json [--since <when>] [--agent <name>]
scripts/fleet-history --summary [--since <when>] [--agent <name>]
```

**`--json` emits intervals** — the log is transitions, and every question above is about *durations*,
so pairing is the script's whole job:

```json
{"agent":"Cyclops","state":"working","phase":"review","bead":"ah-gfzu",
 "from_ts":"2026-08-20T17:04:11Z","to_ts":"2026-08-20T17:26:02Z","minutes":21.8,"open":false}
```

**The last interval for each agent has no successor**, and it is the one that answers "is anything
stalled *right now*". Emit it with `"open":true`, `to_ts` null, and `minutes` measured to now — and
say in the header that an open interval is still running, so a reader does not average it in
unknowingly.

**`--summary` aggregates** per agent and state — `count`, `total_min`, `median_min`, `max_min`. That
one mode answers four of the five questions above; `median` rather than mean, because a single 9-hour
park would otherwise swallow the typical case, and the typical case is what a threshold is set from.

**Pairing rule.** Sort by `ts`, group by agent, and pair each line with the next one from the same
agent. Use `changed:false` lines as **evidence the agent is still reporting** — they do not end an
interval, they extend confidence in it. A `from` of null (a fresh session, per ah-hiib.1) **ends the
previous interval** rather than continuing it: the session restarted, and time before it belongs to
the old session.

### 2. Reading the log, both generations

ah-hiib.1 rotates on size to `transitions.1.jsonl`, keeping one generation. **Read
`transitions.1.jsonl` first, then `transitions.jsonl`**, or every window that reaches back past a
rotation silently loses its older half — and it will look like an agent simply was not running.

`--since` accepts an ISO timestamp or a plain `24h` / `7d`; **default `7d`**, which is the window the
questions above are asked over. Filter after the pairing, not before, so an interval that *starts*
before the window is still reported with its true length rather than truncated to look shorter.

### 3. The panel is a renderer, on its own cadence

A **History section** in the fleet view, beside the Sweeps section it should imitate in every way
(`cerebro--sweep-section`, `cerebro.el:529-541`):

- Built from `scripts/fleet-history --summary` through **`cerebro--run-async`** (`:568`), exactly as
  `cerebro--request-sweeps` runs its scripts — so a large log can never block the tick.
- Gated by **`cerebro--due-p`** (`:2110`) with an interval of its own — **300 seconds** is ample for a
  distribution that moves slowly, and the tick is 5. The bead is explicit that recomputing on every
  tick would be wrong, and `cerebro--system-args-cache` (`:1082-1087`) is the caching shape already
  in the file.
- **Cached and rendered from the cache**, so a redraw between refreshes costs nothing.
- A pure function turning parsed summary rows into lines, with ERT tests — the same division
  `cerebro--sweep-label` and `cerebro--sweep-section` already keep. **Nothing in the renderer shells
  out.**

The section shows, per live agent, its current state with how long it has been there, and — the point
of the whole family — **marks an interval that has run past what is typical for that state.** It is
the same information Sweeps gives about claims, for agents.

Follow `cerebro--sweep-section`'s judgement about emptiness: **no header and nothing at all when
there is nothing to say.** A History section printing "(none)" every five minutes is exactly the
noise `orchestrator.md` warns against.

### 4. The schema is documented for hand queries

An acceptance criterion in its own right: *"a question the views did not anticipate can still be
answered by reading the log directly."* So the header carries the field list, **two or three worked
`jq` one-liners** against the real log (longest `asking` wait; time-in-state for one agent; every
open interval over an hour), and a pointer to `agent-state`'s own header for where the fields come
from. Somebody at a terminal at 2am is the reader.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one):**

1. **Transitions become intervals.**
   RED: `tests/fleet-history.sh` over a fabricated log — two transitions become one interval with the
   right minutes.
   GREEN: the pairing.
2. **The edges are right.**
   RED: `the last interval is open`; `a null from ends the previous interval`;
   `a changed-false line does not end an interval`; `an interval starting before the window keeps its
   true length`.
   GREEN: the pairing rules.
3. **Both generations are read.**
   RED: `a rotated log is read oldest first`.
   GREEN: read `transitions.1.jsonl` then `transitions.jsonl`.
4. **It summarises.**
   RED: `--summary counts, totals and takes a median per agent and state`.
   GREEN: the aggregation.
5. **It fails loudly.**
   RED: `a corrupt line exits non-zero with nothing on stdout`; `a missing log exits non-zero`.
   GREEN: the guards.
6. **The panel renders it without shelling out.**
   RED: ERT over the pure row-to-lines function, including the empty case rendering nothing.
   GREEN: the renderer.
7. **The panel refreshes on its own cadence.**
   RED: ERT that a second call inside the interval does not re-run, and one past it does
   (`cerebro--due-p`, stubbed clock).
   GREEN: the cache and the async call.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** bump the submodule pin. **PR one merges first.**

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **`two transitions become one interval`** | `tests/fleet-history.sh` | the core |
| `the last interval is open` | same | "is anything stalled now" |
| **`a null from ends the previous interval`** | same | a restarted session |
| `a changed-false line does not end an interval` | same | ah-hiib.1's heartbeat |
| `an interval starting before the window keeps its true length` | same | filter after pairing |
| **`a rotated log is read oldest first`** | same | the rotation trap |
| `--summary counts, totals and takes a median` | same | the aggregate |
| `--agent filters to one agent` | same | the outlier question |
| **`a corrupt line exits non-zero with nothing on stdout`** | same | loud failure |
| `a missing log exits non-zero` | same | same |
| `summary rows render as lines` | ERT | the pure renderer |
| `an empty history renders nothing at all` | ERT | no "(none)" noise |
| **`the panel does not recompute inside its interval`** | ERT | the tick stays cheap |
| every existing test | both | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** cerebro's CI runs `for t in tests/*.sh`, so a new file needs no registration. ERT as the
`emacs/` README documents.

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing here reaches a player: it is a bash script and a section of
the navigator's own fleet view. The one split the bead flagged for the planner — what belongs in the
panel and what in a script — is an architecture decision, settled above: **all computation in bash,
the panel a cached async renderer on a 300-second cadence**, following the sweeps' existing shape.

**Decided here** (all architecture): a script emitting intervals with a `--summary` mode; median
rather than mean; open intervals reported rather than dropped; `--since` defaulting to `7d` and
filtering after pairing; reading both log generations; and the panel showing current state with
elapsed time and marking what has run long.

## Out of scope

- **Writing the log** — ah-hiib.1's, and this bead must not add a field to it. If it needs one, that
  is a change to ah-hiib.1's contract and its tests.
- **The wake cadence** — ah-hiib.3. This bead *provides* the number; it does not act on it.
- **Acting on anything.** No `bd` call, no unclaim, no nudge. A stalled claim already has a confirmed
  Sweeps finding (**ah-4xm4**); this is a view, and if the diff reaches a destructive command the two
  beads have been conflated.
- **The GitHub API.** The entire point is answering these without it.
- **Retrospective findings** — a different corpus and a different bead (**ah-x7gr**).
- **Charts, or any rendering beyond text lines.**

## Validation

```bash
bash tests/fleet-history.sh
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
```

Then by hand, against a real log with a few days in it:

1. `scripts/fleet-history --json | jq length` — intervals, plausible in number.
2. `scripts/fleet-history --summary` and check the **`asking`** row: that median is the evidence
   `cerebro-answer-timeout`'s 900 seconds has never been checked against. **Say what it turns out to
   be** — it may well argue for changing the constant, which would be a new bead, not this one.
3. `--agent <name>` for two implementers and compare: this is the outlier question that previously
   needed an API crawl.
4. `jq` the log **by hand**, using a one-liner from the script's own header, and confirm the header is
   good enough to work from without reading the script.
5. Confirm the **open interval** for a running agent grows between two calls a minute apart.
6. Open the fleet view: the History section appears, and **the panel does not stutter** — the tick is
   5 seconds and this must not be doing work on it.
7. Watch for five minutes and confirm the section refreshes **once**, not sixty times.
8. Rotate the log by hand (`mv transitions.jsonl transitions.1.jsonl`), write a new transition, and
   confirm a `7d` window still shows the older intervals.
9. Corrupt one line and confirm the script **fails loudly** and the panel simply shows nothing rather
   than a wrong number.

## Known traps

- **Read `transitions.1.jsonl` before `transitions.jsonl`.** Miss the rotated generation and a window
  reaching past a rotation loses its older half — which reads as an agent that was not running, the
  most misleading possible answer for a tool built to measure absence.
- **Filter by `--since` after pairing, never before.** Dropping the opening transition truncates the
  interval and makes long waits look short — the exact bias this bead exists to remove.
- **The open interval must be reported.** The stalled bead you most want to know about is the one
  still stalling, and it is the one with no closing transition.
- **`changed:false` extends, it does not end.** Treating a heartbeat as a transition turns one long
  interval into a run of tiny ones and makes every stall disappear.
- **A null `from` ends the previous interval.** It means a fresh session; carrying the interval
  across it invents time an agent never spent in that state.
- **Median, not mean.** One 9h43m park (ah-rpnb) moves a mean far enough to make a threshold set from
  it useless.
- **Nothing expensive on the tick.** `cerebro--due-p` plus `cerebro--run-async`, cached, exactly as
  the sweeps do it. A synchronous read of a large log on a 5-second tick makes the whole fleet view
  stutter, and it will be blamed on Emacs.
- **The renderer must be pure and must not shell out.** It is the half that is ERT-tested; a
  `call-process` inside it is untestable and lands on the tick.
- **Fail loudly, like `work-beads`.** Nothing on stdout on failure — a caller deciding whether
  anything stalled must not read a broken query as "all clear".
- **Do not add a field to the log to make a question easier.** That is ah-hiib.1's contract.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**
acceptance_criteria:
- Time-in-state per agent over a chosen window is answerable without touching the GitHub API, via `scripts/fleet-history --summary [--since <when>] [--agent <name>]`.
- The distribution of `asking` waits is answerable, so cerebro-answer-timeout's 900 seconds can be judged against evidence.
- Idle frequency and duration per role is answerable - the input ah-hiib.3 needs.
- `--json` emits paired intervals: agent, state, phase, bead, from_ts, to_ts, minutes, open.
- The last interval per agent is emitted with open:true and minutes measured to now, so a stall still in progress is visible.
- A `changed:false` heartbeat line does not end an interval; a null `from` (fresh session) does.
- An interval starting before the window keeps its true length - the window filters after pairing, never before.
- Both log generations are read, transitions.1.jsonl before transitions.jsonl.
- Summary uses median as well as total and max, so one long park cannot swallow the typical case.
- The script fails loudly like scripts/work-beads: non-zero, stderr, nothing on stdout, on a corrupt or missing log.
- The script header documents the schema and carries worked jq one-liners, so an unanticipated question can be answered by hand.
- A History section appears in the fleet view, rendered by a pure ERT-tested function that never shells out, fed asynchronously and gated by cerebro--due-p on its own interval - reading the log never blocks or slows the 5-second tick, however large the log.
- The section renders nothing at all when there is nothing to say.
- No agent gains behaviour, no cadence changes, and nothing destructive is ever run.
- cerebro's suites pass; the submodule pin is bumped in a second PR after the cerebro PR merges.

title: The fleet overwrites its own history, so nothing can be asked about what it did
description:
scripts/agent-state overwrites .cerebro/state/<name>.state.json on every
transition. The previous state is gone. Nothing anywhere in cerebro keeps an
append-only record.

The consequence, concretely: on 2026-08-20 Cerebro was asked whether any
interactive agent had ever sat at `asking` long enough to matter, and could not
answer -- not "no", but "the evidence no longer exists". In the same session it
reconstructed 72 hours of fleet timing by walking the GitHub API PR by PR,
because the fleet keeps no record of its own behaviour. Every question of the
form "how long does X usually take" is currently answered by a twenty-minute
API crawl or not at all.

This is the foundation of the family: the two beads behind it both read this
log, and the wake cadence in particular is meant to be tuned from measured
time-in-state rather than guessed.

WHY IT IS CHEAP. agent-state already has every field at the moment of writing --
the name, the new state, the phase, the bead, the pid, the timestamp. It already
knows the old state, because it reads the file before replacing it. Appending
one line is a few lines of bash and no new dependency.
design:
## Context

`scripts/agent-state` writes `.cerebro/state/<name>.state.json` and nothing else — **current state
only, overwritten on every transition**. There is no append-only record anywhere in cerebro.

The consequence, concretely: on 2026-08-20 Cerebro was asked whether any interactive agent had ever
sat at `asking` long enough to matter, and could not answer — not "no", but *the evidence no longer
exists*. In the same session it reconstructed 72 hours of fleet timing by walking the GitHub API PR
by PR. Every question of the form "how long does X usually take" is currently answered by a
twenty-minute API crawl, or not at all.

**This is the foundation of its family.** ah-hiib.2 (asking the fleet what it has been doing) and
ah-hiib.3 (replacing every role's hand-rolled sleep loop) both read this log, and the wake cadence in
particular is meant to be tuned from *measured* time-in-state rather than guessed. Both are blocked
on this bead.

**It is cheap because `agent-state` already holds every field at the moment of writing** — the name,
the new state, the phase, the bead, the pid, the timestamp — and it **already reads the old file
before replacing it** (`agent-state:125-131`), so the previous state is in hand too.

**This is a cerebro change**, in the submodule's own repository (`rmstdope/cerebro`), so it takes
**two pull requests** — see *Increments*. Bash only; this bead adds no elisp.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. One shared log — `.cerebro/state/transitions.jsonl`

**Shared, not one file per agent.** The questions this family exists to answer are fleet-wide and
time-ordered — "what was the fleet doing at 14:00", "how long does a bead sit in `review`" — and a
shared log answers them in one pass, where per-agent files would need a merge sort before any
question could be asked at all. The bead's own reasoning, and it is right.

One JSON object per line:

```json
{"ts":"2026-08-20T17:04:11Z","agent":"Cyclops","from":"idle","to":"working","phase":"build","bead":"ah-gfzu","pid":5219,"changed":true}
```

`from` is `null` on an agent's very first write, where there is no previous file — that is a real
distinction (a fresh session, not a transition) and must not be flattened to `"idle"`.

**`.cerebro/` is git-ignored** (`.gitignore:40`), so this log is local to the machine and is never
committed. That is correct — it is an operational record, not project history — but it must be
**said in the header**, because "the fleet keeps a history" invites the assumption that the history
survives a fresh clone. It does not.

### 2. Every call is logged, including one that changes nothing

The acceptance requires the reader to tell *"still working"* from *"no longer reporting"*. So:
**append on every invocation**, and carry `changed` — true when `state` or `bead` differs from the
file, false when the call repeated what was already there.

That single field is what makes both questions answerable: time-in-state comes from the `changed:
true` lines, and liveness — an agent still calling in — comes from the last line of any kind. It also
gives ah-hiib.3 exactly what it needs to tune a cadence, since a long run of `changed:false` lines
*is* a sleep loop, measured rather than described.

### 3. The append — after the state file, and never fatal

Two rules, and they are the whole of the risk in this bead.

**It must come after `mv -f "$tmp_file" "$out_file"` (`agent-state:163`)**, so the state file — the
thing the fleet view actually reads — is already in place before anything else is attempted.

**It must not be able to fail the script.** `agent-state` runs under `set -euo pipefail`
(`:34`), so an unwritable path or a full disk would abort it — and if the append were placed before
the `mv`, that would take the state file with it. Guard it explicitly:

```bash
# The transition log (ah-hiib.1). Deliberately last, and deliberately unable to fail: the state
# file above is what the fleet view reads, and an agent must never be brought down by a full disk
# or an unwritable log. `|| true` under `set -e` is the point, not an oversight.
{
  printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$log_file"
} 2>/dev/null || true
```

**Atomicity.** A shell `>>` redirect opens the file with `O_APPEND`, so every write is positioned at
the current end of file by the kernel rather than by a remembered offset — two agents appending at
once cannot overwrite one another. A single short line is written by a single `write(2)`, so it
cannot be split by another writer's line on a local filesystem. **Say this in the header, with its
limit**: it holds for the local disk the fleet runs on, and is not a promise about NFS. Build the
line with `jq -c -n` (one line by construction, and correctly escaped) and append it with one
`printf`, never with several `echo`s that could be split.

### 4. A bounded size story

At roughly 150 bytes a line, eight agents, and a call every few minutes while running, the log grows
on the order of **a few hundred kilobytes a day** — tens of megabytes a year. That is acceptable, but
"acceptable" is not the same as unbounded, so **rotate on size**: when the log exceeds a documented
ceiling (5 MB is ample), `mv` it to `transitions.1.jsonl`, replacing any previous one, and start a new
file. One generation kept, no dependency on `logrotate`, and a reader that wants the full window
reads the two in order.

Check the size **before** appending, and let the rotation fail as harmlessly as the append does.

### 5. Nothing else moves

Every existing behaviour of `agent-state` — validation, the roster check, the `done` refusal, the
`since` / `phase_since` rules, the atomic tmp-and-`mv` write — is **unchanged**, and its tests in
`tests/agent-state.sh` (301 lines) must pass untouched. If any of them needs editing, the state
file's contract has been changed, which this bead does not do.

## Increments

**In `.claude/cerebro` (PR one, against `rmstdope/cerebro`):**

1. **A transition is recorded.**
   RED: in `tests/agent-state.sh` — `a transition appends one line to the log`, asserting the file
   exists, holds one line, and parses as JSON with the seven fields.
   GREEN: build the line with `jq -c -n` and append after the `mv`.
2. **The line says what happened.**
   RED: `the first write records a null from`; `a state change records both states`;
   `a repeat records changed false`.
   GREEN: read `from` out of the `prev_*` variables already parsed at `:127-131`; compute `changed`
   from the same comparison `since` already makes at `:133`.
3. **The log cannot break an agent.**
   RED: `an unwritable log still writes the state file` — point the log at a path that cannot be
   created, and assert `agent-state` exits zero and the state file is correct.
   GREEN: the `|| true` guard, and its placement after the `mv`.
4. **Two writers do not interleave.**
   RED: `concurrent writes leave whole lines` — run many `agent-state` calls in parallel and assert
   every line of the log parses as JSON and the count matches.
   GREEN: nothing, if increment 1 was built with one `printf`. **If this fails, the line is being
   written in more than one write** — fix that rather than adding a lock.
5. **It does not grow for ever.**
   RED: `an oversized log is rotated, once`.
   GREEN: the size check and the single-generation `mv`.

**In `atlantis-hud` (PR two):** bump the submodule pin to the merged cerebro commit, nothing else.
**PR one merges first** — a pin to an unmerged commit pins something that may be rebased away.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| **`a transition appends one line to the log`** | `tests/agent-state.sh` | the bead |
| `the first write records a null from` | same | a fresh session is not a transition |
| `a state change records both states` | same | `from`/`to` |
| **`a repeat records changed false`** | same | "still working" vs "no longer reporting" |
| `a phase-only change is recorded` | same | phase transitions, which `since` deliberately ignores |
| **`an unwritable log still writes the state file`** | same | the never-fatal rule |
| **`concurrent writes leave whole lines`** | same | atomicity |
| `an oversized log is rotated, once` | same | the size ceiling |
| every existing test in the file | same | **unchanged** — the state file's contract does not move |

**Suites:** cerebro's CI runs `for t in tests/*.sh`, so extending the existing file needs no
registration. Run it as its own header says: `bash tests/agent-state.sh` from the submodule root.

The fixture tree the file already builds (its own `scripts/` of symlinks, its own git repo, so
`consumer-root --shared` resolves inside the fixture) is exactly what these tests need — **reuse it,
do not build a second one.**

## User-facing decisions

**None, and none to ask for.** Nothing in this bead is visible to a player: it writes a log file
under `.cerebro/`, read only by other agents and by the navigator through the fleet view. The one
question the bead itself flagged as "worth deciding early" — one shared log or one per agent — is an
architecture decision, not an interface one, and is settled above in favour of **shared**, on the
bead's own reasoning that the questions this family answers are fleet-wide and time-ordered.

**Decided here** (all architecture): logging every call rather than only changes, with a `changed`
flag; `from` being null on a first write; rotation on size with one generation kept; the append
placed after the `mv` and guarded so it can never be fatal; and building the line with `jq -c -n`.

## Out of scope

- **Reading the log.** Answering "what has the fleet been doing" is **ah-hiib.2**, and this bead must
  not grow a query interface — it writes, and stops there.
- **The wake cadence.** **ah-hiib.3**, which is also blocked by ah-4xm4.
- **Any elisp.** The fleet view is not changed; it keeps reading the state file exactly as it does.
- **Changing the state file's schema or `agent-state`'s existing behaviour.** Its tests must pass
  untouched.
- **Committing the log, or sharing it between machines.** `.cerebro/` is git-ignored and stays so.
- **A lock, or any concurrency mechanism beyond `O_APPEND`.** If one line ever needs more than one
  `write`, the line is too big or is being built wrong.

## Validation

In `.claude/cerebro`:

```bash
bash tests/agent-state.sh
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t" || echo "FAILED: $t"; done
```

Then by hand, against the real fleet:

1. `scripts/agent-state <yourname> idle --pid $$`, then look at
   `.cerebro/state/transitions.jsonl` — **one new line**, valid JSON, with the right agent and `to`.
2. Run the same command **again unchanged**: a second line, with **`"changed":false`**.
3. Change the state (`working --phase plan --bead ah-x`): a line with `from` naming the previous
   state and **`"changed":true`**.
4. Confirm `.cerebro/state/<name>.state.json` is **exactly as it was before this bead** — same
   fields, same `since` semantics. This is the regression that matters.
5. `chmod a-w` the log (or point it at an unwritable path) and run `agent-state` again: it **exits
   zero**, the state file is updated, and nothing is printed to the agent's terminal.
6. Run twenty `agent-state` calls in parallel and confirm `jq -c . transitions.jsonl` parses **every**
   line and the count is right.
7. Confirm the log is **not** in `git status` — it is under an ignored directory.
8. Leave the fleet running for a while and confirm a long idle stretch reads as a run of
   `changed:false` lines — that shape is what ah-hiib.3 will tune a cadence from.

## Known traps

- **The append must come after the `mv`, and must not be able to fail.** `agent-state` runs under
  `set -euo pipefail`; an unguarded append before the `mv` turns an unwritable log into an agent with
  no state file at all, which is far worse than no log. `|| true` here is deliberate.
- **One `write`, one line.** Build the whole line with `jq -c -n` and emit it with a single `printf`.
  Several `echo`s, or a multi-line `jq` output, can interleave with another agent's line and corrupt
  the log for every reader.
- **`from` is null on a first write, not `"idle"`.** A fresh session is not a transition, and
  ah-hiib.2 will need to tell the difference.
- **Log every call, not only changed ones.** The acceptance is explicit that a reader must tell
  "still working" from "no longer reporting"; only logging changes makes those two identical.
- **Do not touch the `since` / `phase_since` logic.** It is subtle (`:133-145`), separately tested,
  and unrelated. Read `changed` off the same comparison rather than reworking it.
- **Do not add a query, a formatter or a fleet-view line.** Those are ah-hiib.2's, and a bead that
  grows into its successor is one nobody can review.
- **The log is git-ignored and per-machine.** Say so in the header; "the fleet keeps a history" reads
  as a promise that it survives a clone, and it does not.
- **Two PRs, cerebro first.**

title: The fleet keeps no history, and every agent runs its own clock
description:
Two gaps that turn out to be one piece of work.

NO HISTORY. scripts/agent-state writes .cerebro/state/<name>.state.json and
nothing else -- current state only, overwritten on every transition. There is no
append-only record anywhere in cerebro. On 2026-08-20 a Cerebro session was asked
whether any interactive agent had ever sat at `asking` and could not answer:
the evidence had been overwritten. The same session had to reconstruct 72 hours
of fleet timing from the GitHub API, one PR at a time, because the fleet keeps
no record of its own behaviour.

EVERY ROLE RUNS ITS OWN CLOCK. The interactive roles loop inside their own
session. agents/user-feedback.md:86-91 is the shape:

  for i in $(seq 5); do sleep 60; echo "Moira idle, ${i}/5 of this half"; done

Ten minutes, in two halves, because a single ten-minute silent Bash call is
rejected by the tool. Every interactive role carries a "Sleeping without dying"
section that is pure workaround. plan-bead/SKILL.md:326 is the same thing again.

An instruction-based loop is unreliable and opaque. scripts/agent-asking exists
as a PreToolUse hook precisely because an agent kept forgetting to write its own
state (agent-asking:9-15). An agent blocked inside a sleep is indistinguishable
from one that has hung, cannot be stopped cleanly, and its cadence can only be
changed by editing prose and restarting the session.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX. The fleet view already owns a 5-second tick, the state
files, and an ERT culture for its pure functions. Give it the history and the
cadence too: agents report state, the monitor records it and decides when work
resumes. Elisp and bash only -- no new runtime, no daemon beyond what
cerebro--tick already is.

ORDER MATTERS AND IS DELIBERATE (navigator, 2026-08-20): the log lands first and
runs for a day or two, so the wake cadence is designed against measured
time-in-state rather than guessed. You cannot tune a cadence you cannot measure.

CONSTRAINTS THAT APPLY TO THE WHOLE FAMILY

  - A poke does not reset context. The session is the same session and its
    context still grows; it grows on the monitor's schedule instead of its own.
    Bounded context would mean restarting a role per pass, and that is NOT
    wanted here -- planners hold a mockup conversation with the navigator across
    several turns and restarting mid-conversation would destroy it.
  - `idle` is already overloaded. For an implementer it means "safe to retire",
    and the fleet view ends it within about one poll of a stop flag. For an
    interactive role it already means "sleeping, will wake myself". A third
    meaning collides with the race agents/orchestrator.md already records: an
    implementer between beads writes idle, claims its next bead, and only then
    writes working -- a flag landing in that gap ends a session holding a fresh
    claim.
  - Typing into a vterm is a fragile primary API. cerebro--nudge does it as a
    last resort; keystrokes arriving while an agent is mid-tool-call is a real
    failure mode. Interactive sessions are reachable through `claude agents`,
    which is a proper channel.
