title: Jump to a unit by clicking its number in a problem list
description:
The problem lists in the region pane and in the top bar name units by number, but the numbers are inert: seeing a problem tells you which unit has it and then leaves you to find that unit yourself.

Make the unit number a link. Clicking it selects that unit immediately. From the top bar the unit may be in a different hex than the one currently selected, so the selected hex changes to follow it; from the region pane the unit is in the region already.

Raised by the navigator 2026-08-19.
design: ## Context The problem lists name the unit at fault by number, and the number is inert. You read which unit has the problem, then go and find it yourself — in a units table that may be showing three hundred rows, or in a hex that is not the one on screen. **This is worth more now than when it was raised.** Five order warnings landed in the last two days (`ah-vkut`'s two, `ah-dwk6`, and `ah-90w`'s before them), and every one of them names a unit by number. The count of inert numbers in front of the player has gone up sharply. **Almost all of the machinery already exists**, which is the most important thing to know before starting: - **`goToUnit` (`AppShell.tsx:660-679`) already does the whole job.** Given a unit id it finds the region, switches level if the unit is on another one, calls `selectRegion(regionId, unitId)` *and* `selectUnit(unitId)` — the second because `selectRegion` is a no-op when that hex is already selected. It is already wired to the turn-messages panel, the F8 diagnostic walk, the next/prev unit shortcuts, the command palette and the Changes dialog. - **`unitRegions` (`AppShell.tsx:640-648`) is the `unitId → regionId` map**, built from the parsed report and including foreign units, with **`knownUnitIds` (`:651`)** beside it as the set of ids that can be gone to. - **`TurnMessagesPanel`'s `Unit` (`TurnMessagesPanel.tsx:171-207`) is this exact control, already built** — a unit id as a jump button, rendered as plain dimmed text when the report does not describe it. Its doc comment settles the absent-unit case, and this bead follows it rather than re-deciding it. - **`ProblemWho` (`primitives.tsx:47-61`) is shared** by both problem lists, so one component carries the change for both. So this bead is mostly *threading* what exists into two more panels. The new work is: making `ProblemWho` a button, linking the unit numbers **inside** the message text, and giving `RegionPanel` the callbacks it has never had. Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree. ## Files to change, and what to reuse Five files under `packages/shared/src/`, plus two test files and one smoke spec. **No Rust, no core change, no new token, no settings.** ### 1. The shared unit id becomes a link — `workspace/primitives.tsx` `ProblemWho` (`:47-61`) gains two optional props and renders a button when it can: ```tsx /** * Whose problem it is: a unit id, or `hex` for a diagnostic that belongs to the hex and to no unit. * * The id is a way to go and look at the unit, on the same terms `TurnMessagesPanel`'s `Unit` sets * (ah-87he): a button only when the loaded turn actually describes that unit, and plain text * otherwise, because a button that does nothing is worse than plain text saying the same thing. * Without `onSelectUnit` it stays the plain span it has always been, so a caller that has no * selection to offer loses nothing. */ export function ProblemWho({ unitId, known, onSelectUnit }: { unitId: string | null; known?: ReadonlySet; onSelectUnit?: (unitId: string) => void; }) ``` - `unitId === null` → unchanged, the `hex` span and its `sr-only` "the whole hex". **Do not touch this branch**; `ProblemsPanel.test.tsx:95` and `RegionPanel.test.tsx:137` both assert `>hex<`. - `unitId` present, but `onSelectUnit` is absent **or** `known` does not have it → the span exactly as today, including the `sr-only "unit "` prefix. - otherwise → a button carrying the same content: ```tsx ``` `text-brass hover:underline` is `TurnMessagesPanel.tsx:203`'s className, chosen by the navigator so one gesture reads the same everywhere. `shrink-0 tabular-nums` are carried over from the span so the row's layout does not move. The `focus-visible` pair is the house pattern (`CollapsiblePanel.tsx:75`, `UnitTableDock.tsx:358`) — **added deliberately**, because none of the popover panels have any today and this control is now a tab stop. ### 2. The unit numbers inside the message — `workspace/primitives.tsx` The navigator chose to link **every** unit number, including the second unit a message names (`unit 4021 is not building`, `Soggy Saw Mill, which unit 4021 is in, is already finished`, `unit 9002 is not in this hex to be taught`). The messages are plain strings built in Rust (`orders/semantics.rs`), so they have to be parsed: ```tsx /** `unit 4021` as a message writes it. The core's own messages are the only input. */ const UNIT_IN_MESSAGE = /\bunit (\d+)\b/g; /** * A diagnostic's message, with every unit it names turned into a way to go and look at it. * * The messages are prose built in Rust, so the ids have to be read back out of them - which means * this is coupled to their wording, and a message reworded to say "by 4021" rather than "unit 4021" * silently stops linking. That is the accepted cost of ah-87he's "every unit number": the failure * is a link that is not offered, never a wrong one, because every id found is checked against * `known` before it becomes a button. */ export function ProblemMessage({ message, known, onSelectUnit }: { message: string; known?: ReadonlySet; onSelectUnit?: (unitId: string) => void; }) ``` Without `onSelectUnit` or `known` it returns `<>{message}` unchanged. Otherwise it splits the string on `UNIT_IN_MESSAGE` and rebuilds it: the literal text between matches as-is, and each `unit ` as the word `unit `, then either the same button as §1 (when `known.has(id)`) or the plain id. **Keep the word `unit` outside the button** so the button's accessible name matches §1's and a screen reader does not hear "unit unit 4021". Rendered with `key`s from the match index, and `UNIT_IN_MESSAGE` must be created per call or have `lastIndex` reset — a module-level `/g` regex is stateful across calls, and that is the classic way this goes wrong. ### 3. The whole-map panel — `workspace/ProblemsPanel.tsx` Two new props beside the existing four (`:22-28`): ```ts known: ReadonlySet; onSelectUnit: (unitId: string) => void; ``` and the row (`:80-82`) passes them through: ```tsx ``` replacing the bare `{finding.message}` with a `` wrapping `ProblemMessage`, so the message's own colour is unchanged. **The panel closes on the jump**, as the navigator chose — the same thing the card head already does (`:60-63`, `onSelectHex(...)` then `onDismiss()`). Do it in the parent's handler rather than here, so `ProblemsPanel` keeps taking a plain `(unitId) => void`; see §5. ### 4. The region pane — `workspace/RegionPanel.tsx` `Problems` (`:244-269`) takes only `{ problems }` today, and `RegionPanel` itself has no selection props at all. Both gain the same two, threaded from `AppShell` — **not** read from the store inside `RegionPanel`, even though it already reads the store for `regionProblemsShown` (`:245`): the unit lookup lives in `AppShell`'s `unitRegions` memo, not in the store, so there is nothing there to read. No `onDismiss` here: the region pane is not a popover and stays where it is. Its units are in the hex already, so the jump is a selection and nothing else — but it still goes through `goToUnit`, so the one path is exercised everywhere. ### 5. Wiring — `workspace/AppShell.tsx` `goToUnit` (`:660-679`) ends with a hard-coded `closePopover("messages")` (`:676`), written when its only caller was the turn-messages panel. That is wrong for every other caller and would close the wrong popover here. Give it the popover to close: ```ts const goToUnit = useCallback( (unitId: string, closing: HeaderPopoverId | null = "messages") => { … if (closing) { closePopover(closing); } }, […] ); ``` The default keeps all five existing call sites (`:2736`, `:718-734`, `:747-754`, `:809`, `:876`, `:2584-2594`) behaving exactly as they do — check each still compiles without an argument rather than assuming. Then: - `ProblemsPanel` (`:2743-2750`) gets `known={knownUnitIds}` and `onSelectUnit={(unitId) => goToUnit(unitId, "problems")}`. - `RegionPanel` (`:2949-2957`) gets `known={knownUnitIds}` and `onSelectUnit={(unitId) => goToUnit(unitId, null)}`. `knownUnitIds` (`:651`) already exists and is already passed to `TurnMessagesPanel` (`:2737`). **`OrdersPanel` is not changed.** Its `ProblemList` (`:190-222`) shows no unit id, by construction — the list is already scoped to the selected unit (`diagnosticsForUnit`, `:108-114`). Its messages do carry other units' numbers, so `ProblemMessage` could be used there too; that is deliberately out of scope, below. ## Increments 1. **The id is a button when it can be.** RED: `primitives.test.tsx` (`:26-40`, which already has a `describe("ProblemWho")` with two cases) — `a unit id with a way to select it renders as a button`, `a unit id with no handler stays plain text` (the existing callers' behaviour), `a unit the report does not describe stays plain text`, and `a hex-level diagnostic still reads "hex"`. GREEN: §1. 2. **The existing lists keep their markup.** RED: none — this is the check. `ProblemsPanel.test.tsx` and `RegionPanel.test.tsx` must stay green **before** their call sites change, because §1's default path is the old span. If either goes red here, `ProblemWho`'s no-handler branch was altered and that is the bug. 3. **The message's own numbers link too.** RED: `ProblemMessage` tests — `links every unit a message names` (`unit 4021 is not building` → one button), `links both when a message names two` (`Soggy Saw Mill, which unit 4021 is in, is already finished` plus a two-unit case), `leaves a unit the report does not describe as plain text` (`unit 9002 is not in this hex to be taught`), `leaves a message naming no unit alone`, and **`links the second call as well as the first`** — the `lastIndex` trap, written as a test that calls the component twice. GREEN: §2. 4. **Both panels offer it.** RED: `ProblemsPanel.test.tsx` — `the unit id is a button when a handler is given`; and `RegionPanel.test.tsx` — the same. Both assert on `renderToStaticMarkup`, so they check for `data-testid="problem-unit-…"` and `text-brass`, not on clicking. GREEN: §3 and §4, and the `AppShell` wiring in §5. 5. **Clicking actually goes there.** RED: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` — two tests, modelled on `a unit named in a turn message is a way back to it` (`:2613-2624`): - from the top bar: open the problems chip, click a `problem-unit-*` button, expect `problems-panel` to have count 0 and `panel-unit` / `panel-region` to describe that unit and its hex — **choosing a unit in a hex that is not the selected one**, which is the whole point; - from the region pane: click a `problem-unit-*` in `region-problems`, expect `panel-unit` to follow and the region pane to stay open. GREEN: the `closePopover` parameter in §5. ## The test plan **TypeScript unit — `renderToStaticMarkup` only. There is no jsdom in this repository** (`UnitTableDock.test.tsx:8-14` says so), so nothing here can click. Anything that clicks is increment 5. | File | Test | Pins | |---|---|---| | `primitives.test.tsx` (`:26`, existing `describe("ProblemWho")`) | `a unit id with a way to select it renders as a button` | §1's button, `text-brass`, the testid | | | its two existing cases (`:27`, `:34`) | unchanged — they exercise the no-handler path | | | `a unit id with no handler stays plain text` | the existing callers are unaffected | | | `a unit the report does not describe stays plain text` | the `known` rule | | | `a hex-level diagnostic still reads "hex"` | the untouched branch | | | `links every unit a message names` | `ProblemMessage`, one id | | | `links both when a message names two` | two ids in one message | | | `leaves a unit the report does not describe as plain text` | `unit 9002 …` | | | `leaves a message naming no unit alone` | the common case | | | **`links the second call as well as the first`** | the `/g` `lastIndex` trap | | `ProblemsPanel.test.tsx` | `the unit id is a button when a handler is given` | §3 | | | the existing `>hex<` assertion at `:95` | unchanged | | `RegionPanel.test.tsx` | `the unit id is a button when a handler is given` | §4 | | | the existing assertions at `:137-145` (`>hex<`, `>unit <`, `18642`) | unchanged | **Playwright — `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`.** Reuse `loadReport`, and the existing problems-chip test at `:940-958` for how the chip and panel are opened. `warnAboutUnguardedHexes` (`:971-976`) and `silenceIdleUnits` (`:986-991`) control which findings the fixture produces, and `OWN_UNIT = "18642"` (`:60`). **Careful with the baseline counts** at `:949` and `:958` (`"12 problems"`, `"10 problems"`): they are brittle to any change in which checks fire, though not to a rendering change. This bead changes no check, so they must not move — if they do, something else did. **Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast` for the unit tests, and the smoke suite for increment 5 — `pnpm run test:smoke`. This is one of the few beads where the browser suite is the point rather than a formality, because the whole feature is a click. ## User-facing decisions Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-19 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-87he-clickable-units.html`, in two rounds — the second because the research found an existing control the first round did not know about. The chosen mockup is committed to `docs/ui/ah-87he-clickable-units.html`. **Q1 — how the number looks.** First chosen: **A, link blue (`--color-select`)**, over *quiet until hovered* (undiscoverable — a player who never hovers never learns it does anything) and *a shade brighter* (weaker signal, and it stops the number being subordinate to the message). **Q2 — the numbers inside the message.** Chosen: **every unit number, including in the message.** Rejected: *subject only* (safer — the messages are Rust prose and parsing ids out of them is coupled to their wording) and *subject only now, file the rest*. The navigator accepted the fragility; §2 records it in the code, and the `known` check means the failure mode is a link not offered, never a wrong one. **Q3 — the panel after a jump.** Chosen: **close it.** You clicked to go and look at that unit, and a popover covering the workspace is in the way — the same thing the card head's hex-jump already does. Rejected: leaving it open to work down a list. **Q4 — the colour, re-asked.** After Q1, the research found that **`TurnMessagesPanel` already renders exactly this control**, in `text-brass hover:underline`. Put to the navigator that blue would mean the same gesture reading brass in one header panel and blue in the next. Chosen: **brass, matching the existing control** — one colour for "a unit you can jump to", everywhere. Accepted cost: brass is also the hex heading colour in these cards, so the number shares a hue with the title above it. Rejected: keeping blue (distinct from the heading, and matches the units table's `text-select` for own unit ids, but two colours for one gesture) and recolouring turn messages to blue as well (one colour, chosen rather than inherited — but it widens the bead into a panel it is not about). **Q5 — a number naming a unit that is not there.** Chosen: **plain dimmed text, not a button** — which is what `TurnMessagesPanel` already does, for the reason its own comment gives. Rejected: a button that silently does nothing, and a button that explains itself (needs a message and somewhere to put it, in a pane with no room). **Not asked:** the `focus-visible` ring (house pattern, and this control is a new tab stop); parameterising `goToUnit`'s `closePopover` (mechanical); and leaving `OrdersPanel` alone. ## Out of scope - **`OrdersPanel`'s problem list.** It shows no unit id, and its messages' embedded numbers are left as prose. `ProblemMessage` would drop in, and the pane is already scoped to one unit — worth doing, not here, and not filed. - **Making the hex name in a card head anything other than what it is.** The head is already a jump-to-hex button (`ProblemsPanel.tsx:56-71`); this bead does not touch it. - **The turn-messages panel.** It already has this control, and recolouring it was considered and rejected under Q4. - **A shared clickable primitive.** There is none today — every clickable thing in these panes is a hand-rolled `
acceptance_criteria: Every unit number shown in the whole-map problems panel and in the region pane's Problems section is a button that selects that unit when clicked, including the second unit a message names in its text. From the problems panel the selected hex moves to the unit's hex, the level switches when the unit is on another one, and the panel closes; from the region pane the unit is selected and the pane stays open. Both go through AppShell's existing goToUnit, whose hard-coded closePopover("messages") is parameterised so each caller closes its own popover and the five existing call sites are unchanged. A number naming a unit the loaded report does not describe renders as plain dimmed text and is not a button; a hex-level finding still shows "hex" in italics and is inert. The buttons are brass with an underline on hover, matching TurnMessagesPanel's existing jump-to-unit control, carry the house focus-visible brass outline, are reachable by Tab and activate on Enter and Space, and a screen reader hears "unit 4021" once rather than twice. ProblemWho and the new ProblemMessage both fall back to exactly today's plain markup when given no handler, so the existing assertions on ">hex<" and ">unit <" continue to pass. Clicking is covered by the Playwright smoke suite, there being no jsdom in this repository, and the smoke suite's existing problem counts do not move.

title: Sending orders reports only an error count, not which order failed
description:
Found during verification of ah-etb0.2 (2026-08-19, origin/main 5265ba2), on a real send to the live server. ah-etb0.2 passed; this is the follow-up filed alongside the pass.

## What the player sees

Send a turn whose orders contain a mistake. The dialog reports the whole of what went wrong as:

    1 error found!

It never says which order was wrong, or where. The player is told a turn they just submitted has an error and given nothing whatever to find it with — so they must go back to the server's own web interface or their email to learn what the application already received and discarded.

## The cause

packages/shared/src/workspace/ordersUpload.ts, serverErrorReport. It reads only the tail of the echoed <pre>, after the LAST `#end` line. Its comment states the reason, and the reason is sound:

    Only the tail of the echoed `<pre>`, after the **last** `#end` line, and that is what keeps the
    password out of it: the `#atlantis` header is the first line of that block, so a function that
    starts after `#end` can never reach it. It must never be widened to return the whole `<pre>`.

The premise that fails is about the reply's shape, not about the password. The server does not put its errors after `#end`. It echoes the submitted document and annotates it INLINE, immediately above the offending line, like this (document redacted, real password removed):

    #atlantis <faction> "<password>"      <- first line of the block; must never be shown
    unit 803
    FORM 5
      STUDY FORC

    *** Error: xNAME is not a valid order. ***
      xNAME UNIT "..."
      CLAIM 895
    END
    #end

    1 error found!

Everything useful is before `#end`; only the summary count is after it. So the extractor is not merely narrow, it is reading the wrong region — and the naive widening is exactly what the password rule forbids.

## Why this is a planning question, not a patch

The navigator was asked and said the plan is wrong rather than the build. The two constraints have to be satisfied together, and how to do that is a decision:

- the `#atlantis` line is the first line of the echoed block and must never reach the screen, a log, an Error message or storage (ah-etb0.1's known traps);
- the error annotations are interleaved with the player's own orders, so "show the errors" means showing document lines.

Some shapes to weigh, none chosen: show only lines matching the `*** Error: ... ***` marker; show those plus N lines of surrounding context; show the whole echo with the first line dropped unconditionally; show the whole echo with any `#atlantis` line filtered wherever it appears. They differ in how much of the player's document ends up on screen and in how they fail if the server ever reformats. Worth deciding explicitly: whether dropping "the first line" is safe enough on its own, or whether the filter should match the `#atlantis` directive by name so it cannot be defeated by a leading blank line.

Also worth revisiting while here: ah-etb0.2's decision to show the report "only when it is not `No errors found.`" is unaffected and should stay.

## Acceptance

Send a turn with a deliberate bad order. The dialog names the failing order and what was wrong with it. The faction password appears nowhere in the dialog, in any log, or in any stored state, under any server reply shape.
design:
## Context

Send a turn whose orders contain a mistake and the dialog reports the whole of what went wrong as:

```
1 error found!
```

It never says which order, which unit, or what was wrong. The player has just been told the turn they
submitted has an error and given nothing to find it with, so they go back to the server's own web
interface to read what this application already received and discarded. Found by Psylocke on a **real
send to the live server** while verifying `ah-etb0.2`, which passed; filed alongside the pass.

**The extractor is reading the wrong region, not merely too little.** `serverErrorReport`
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/ordersUpload.ts:156-177`) takes only the lines *after the last
`#end`*. The server does not put its errors there — it echoes the submitted document and annotates it
**inline, immediately above the offending line**:

```
#atlantis 95 "swordfish"     <- the password; must never reach the screen
unit 803
FORM 5
  STUDY FORC

*** Error: xNAME is not a valid order. ***
  xNAME UNIT "Scouts"
  CLAIM 895
END
#end
                             <- everything above is discarded today
1 error found!               <- this, alone, is what the player is shown
```

Everything useful is *before* `#end`; only the summary count is after it.

**And the widening the fix needs is exactly what the password rule appears to forbid** — the
`#atlantis` line, carrying the faction password, is the first line of that block, and
`ah-etb0.1`'s traps say it must never reach the screen, a log, an `Error` message or storage.

**That apparent conflict does not survive reading the code, and this is the finding that unlocks the
bead.** The password defence never depended on the region boundary. `serverErrorReport` already
filters every line it emits against `FACTION_HEADER_LINE` — `/^\s*#atlantis\b/` (`:180`) — applied
*positively*, and its own comment (`:170-172`) says why:

> The tail-only rule alone is not enough: a document holding a second faction block, or one missing
> its final `#end`, puts an `#atlantis <id> "<password>"` line after the last `#end`. **Dropping the
> header positively is what actually keeps the password out of what a player sees.**

So the rule is already *match the directive by name, anywhere*, which is what the bead asks the
planner to decide between and is strictly the stronger of the two options — a leading blank line or
indentation cannot defeat it, and neither can position. **Widening the region is safe provided that
same filter is applied to all of it**, and that is the whole of the safety argument.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Two files, both under `packages/shared/src/workspace/`. **No Rust, no core change, no settings, no
new token.**

### 1. Read the annotations, not the tail — `ordersUpload.ts`

`serverErrorReport` (`:156-177`) keeps its signature, its `<pre>` selection and its null contract.
Only what it does with the lines changes:

```ts
/**
 * What the server said about the orders themselves - "No errors found.", or the errors it found.
 *
 * The server annotates the echoed document **inline**, immediately above each offending line, and
 * puts only the summary count after `#end`. Reading the tail alone (which is what shipped, and what
 * ah-58dz was filed against) therefore reports "1 error found!" and nothing a player can act on.
 *
 * Every line returned is filtered against `FACTION_HEADER_LINE`, wherever it appears - that, and
 * not the region boundary, is what keeps the password out of what a player sees. Do not remove the
 * filter on the grounds that the header is "before the errors"; a document with a second faction
 * block puts one anywhere.
 */
export function serverErrorReport(body: string): string | null {
```

The body becomes, after the unchanged `<pre>` selection (`:157-164`) and the unchanged
`decodeEntities(stripTags(pre)).split("\n")` (`:166`):

1. **Filter first, once.** `const safe = lines.filter((line) => !FACTION_HEADER_LINE.test(line));`
   Everything downstream reads `safe`, so no later branch can reintroduce the header.
2. **Split at the last `#end`.** `const end = safe.map((l) => l.trim()).lastIndexOf("#end");` — the
   document is `safe.slice(0, end)`, the summary tail is `safe.slice(end + 1)`. When `end` is `-1`
   the whole thing is the tail, which preserves today's behaviour for a reply with no `#end` in that
   `<pre>` (though the `find` at `:159-161` means one is always present).
3. **Collect an entry per annotation** from the document part, in order. An annotation is a line
   matching `ANNOTATION_LINE`, and each entry carries three strings:
   - the most recent preceding `unit <n>` line, or none if the annotation precedes any;
   - the annotation line itself;
   - **the line immediately after it**, which is the offending order — omitted when that line is
     blank, is itself an annotation, or is `#end`.
4. **Render.** Each entry is its lines joined by `\n`; entries are joined by `\n\n`. **The unit line
   is emitted only when it differs from the one emitted for the previous entry**, so three errors in
   one unit read as one heading and three annotations rather than the heading three times.
5. **Append the summary.** The tail, trimmed, as its own final block after a blank line — so the
   result ends `\n\n1 error found!`. When there are no annotations at all, return the trimmed tail
   exactly as today: that is the `No errors found.` path, which `showsServerReport` then hides.
6. Return `null` when the whole result is empty, as today.

Two new constants beside `END_LINE` and `FACTION_HEADER_LINE` (`:179-180`):

```ts
/**
 * The server's inline annotation marker. Matched on the leading `***` alone rather than on the
 * word "Error", so a reply that says `*** Warning: ... ***` - or reworded errors - is still shown
 * rather than silently dropped. Showing one line too many is the safe direction here; the failure
 * this bead fixes was showing none.
 */
const ANNOTATION_LINE = /^\s*\*\*\*/;
/** The `unit <n>` line an annotation falls under, so the player knows where to look. */
const UNIT_LINE = /^\s*unit\s+\d+/i;
```

**`FACTION_HEADER_LINE` and `END_LINE` are unchanged.** So is `interpretOrdersUploadReply`
(`:110-116`), `refusalReason` (`:135-147`), and every other export in the file.

### 2. The dialog — `SendOrdersDialog.tsx`

**Nothing changes.** The report already renders in a `<pre>` with
`max-h-[7rem] overflow-auto … whitespace-pre-wrap` (`:130-136`), which is exactly right for a
multi-line report: it scrolls rather than pushing **Close** out of reach, and the comment there says
so. The label stays **"The server reported"** (`:129`) — the navigator's choice; it is neutral,
already agreed for `ah-etb0.2`, and still accurate whether the box holds a count or the errors
themselves.

`showsServerReport` (`sendOrdersView.ts:63-65`) is unchanged: the report is shown only when it is
non-empty and is not `No errors found.`, and `ah-etb0.2`'s decision there stands.

## Increments

1. **The errors themselves come through.**
   RED: `ordersUpload.test.ts` — `names the failing order and the unit it belongs to`, against a
   fixture built from the real reply in *Context* (annotation inline, summary after `#end`).
   Expects exactly:
   ```
   unit 803
   *** Error: xNAME is not a valid order. ***
     xNAME UNIT "Scouts"

   1 error found!
   ```
   It fails today with `1 error found!` alone — the reported defect, written as a test.
   GREEN: steps 1–5 above.

2. **The password cannot get out, however the reply is shaped.**
   RED: `never returns an #atlantis line, wherever the reply puts one` — one fixture carrying an
   `#atlantis 95 "swordfish"` line in **four** places at once: first line of the block, after a blank
   line mid-document, indented with leading whitespace, and after the last `#end`. Asserts the result
   contains neither `swordfish` nor `#atlantis`.
   GREEN: nothing, if step 1's filter was applied to `lines` before anything else. **If this passes
   without any change, check it was actually red for the mid-document case first** — it is the one
   assertion in this bead that must not be taken on trust.

3. **Several errors, and several units.**
   RED: `groups each error under the unit it falls in`, `repeats the unit line only when it changes`
   (two annotations in one unit → one `unit 803` line), and
   `an annotation before any unit line is shown without one`.
   GREEN: step 4's rendering rule.

4. **The shapes that must not break.**
   RED: `omits the offending line when the annotation is the last line`,
   `omits it when the next line is another annotation`,
   `omits it when the next line is #end`, and
   `a clean reply is still the tail alone` (`No errors found.` → unchanged, so
   `showsServerReport` still hides it).
   GREEN: step 3's omission rules and step 5's no-annotations path.

5. **The existing contract is intact.**
   RED: none — this is the check. The five existing `serverErrorReport` tests
   (`ordersUpload.test.ts:121-158`) must still pass, in particular
   `takes the pre that holds the echoed document, not merely the first on the page` and
   `strips markup the server wrapped the tail in`.
   GREEN: any of them that needed adjusting, adjusted **to the new truth and not weakened** — a test
   asserting the old tail-only behaviour is asserting the bug.

## The test plan

**TypeScript — `packages/shared/src/workspace/ordersUpload.test.ts`**, `describe("serverErrorReport")`
at `:121`, which already holds five cases and the `ACCEPTED` fixture. `pnpm run check:fast` runs it.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| **`names the failing order and the unit it belongs to`** | the reported defect: the full expected string |
| **`never returns an #atlantis line, wherever the reply puts one`** | first line, mid-document, indented, after `#end` — all four in one fixture |
| `groups each error under the unit it falls in` | two units, two annotations |
| `repeats the unit line only when it changes` | two annotations in one unit → one heading |
| `an annotation before any unit line is shown without one` | faction-level errors |
| `omits the offending line when the annotation is the last line` | no line after the marker |
| `omits it when the next line is another annotation` | two markers in a row |
| `omits it when the next line is #end` | the document boundary |
| `keeps the summary count as the last line` | `1 error found!` after a blank line |
| `a clean reply is still the tail alone` | `No errors found.` unchanged |
| `shows an annotation the server did not word as "Error"` | `*** Warning: … ***` is not dropped |
| the five existing cases at `:121-158` | the `<pre>` selection, markup stripping, the last-`#end` rule |

**`SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx` and `sendOrdersView.test.ts`** need no new cases — neither the dialog
nor `showsServerReport` changes — but both must stay green, and
`SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx:64` (`serverReport: "Unit 1234: unknown order."`) already exercises a
multi-line-capable report box.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. No Rust suite (nothing under `crates/` changes) and no browser
suite — the dialog's markup is untouched.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-19 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-58dz-server-errors.html`. The
chosen mockup is committed to `docs/ui/ah-58dz-server-errors.html`, and its §2 draws each variant in
the dialog at its real 26rem width.

**Q1 — how much of the echoed document to show.** Chosen: **the error, the offending order, and the
unit it falls under**, plus the summary count. That is everything needed to go and fix it, and
several errors read as several small blocks. Rejected: **the whole echo** with `#atlantis` filtered
(simplest rule and robust to the server reformatting, but a real turn is hundreds of lines in a 7rem
box, so finding the one error means scrolling — close to the problem being fixed); **the annotation
lines alone** (smallest exposure, but still does not say which order or which unit, and three
identical mistakes give three identical lines); and **error plus order without the unit line**.

**Q2 — the summary count.** Chosen: **keep it, as the last line.** It is the server's own count and
it tells the player whether the list they are looking at is complete — which matters when the box has
scrolled. Rejected: dropping it as redundant.

**Q3 — the label above the box.** Chosen: **"The server reported", unchanged.** Neutral, already
agreed for `ah-etb0.2`, and accurate whether the box holds a count or the errors. Rejected:
"What the server rejected" (the box only appears when something was wrong, so it says twice what the
box's presence already says) and "Errors in this turn" (drops the attribution — these are the
server's findings, not the app's).

**Not asked, and decided here:** matching the annotation on `***` rather than on the word "Error"
(robustness, and the failure direction is one line too many rather than none); emitting the unit line
only when it changes; and the three cases where the offending line is omitted. Also not asked, and
stated in *Context* rather than put as a question: the bead's own open question about whether
dropping "the first line" is safe enough — the code already matches `#atlantis` by name, which is the
stronger of the two, so there was nothing to choose.

## Out of scope

- **`ah-etb0.2`'s decision to show the report only when it is not `No errors found.`** Unaffected,
  and it stays (`showsServerReport`, `sendOrdersView.ts:63-65`).
- **The dialog's layout, label, sizing and keyboard.** All settled by `ah-etb0.2`; the report box
  already scrolls and already keeps **Close** reachable.
- **Linking an error to the order in the editor** — jumping to the line, or underlining it. A real
  feature, and a different one: the echo's line numbering is the *sent* document's, not the editor's.
  Not filed.
- **Anything about `refusalReason`** or the accepted/refused classification (`ah-etb0.1`'s).
- **Parsing the errors into structured findings** and merging them with the app's own order warnings.
  The server's text is shown verbatim, as `ah-etb0.2` chose.
- **The password's storage on disk**, which is `ah-d7ih`.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by hand, and **this bead cannot be signed off without a real send** — the defect existed because
every unit test passed against a fixture nobody had checked against a live reply:

1. Take a real turn, break one order deliberately (`xNAME UNIT "Scouts"` under some unit is exactly
   the case that was found), and send it to the live server from the dialog.
2. The report box must name **the unit**, **the server's complaint**, and **the offending order
   line**, and end with the server's own count. Read it and satisfy yourself you could go and fix the
   order from that alone — which is the whole acceptance.
3. **Look for the password.** It must not be in the box, and it must not be anywhere else either:
   open the browser console and the network panel and check the reply is not logged; check
   `localStorage` and the game workspace afterwards. The document you sent *does* carry the password
   in its `#atlantis` line, so the reply certainly contains it — the assertion is that nothing this
   application shows or stores does.
4. Break **two** orders in the same unit, and one in a different unit. The first unit's heading
   appears once; the second unit gets its own.
5. Send a **clean** turn. No report box at all — `No errors found.` is still hidden.
6. Both shells, since `SendOrdersDialog` and `ordersUpload` are shared: `apps/web` and
   `apps/desktop`. The desktop build reaches the game host through the Tauri allowlist added by
   `ah-etb0.1`, so a send that works on web and not on desktop is a capability problem rather than
   this bead's.

## Known traps

- **The `#atlantis` filter is the whole safety argument, and it must be applied before anything
  else.** Filter `lines` once, up front, and read only the filtered array afterwards. Filtering at
  render time instead leaves every intermediate value — and any future branch — carrying the
  password.
- **Do not "simplify" the filter to dropping the first line.** The existing comment (`:170-172`)
  records why: a document with a second faction block, or one missing its final `#end`, carries an
  `#atlantis` line anywhere. Position is not a defence; the name is.
- **The errors are before `#end`, not after it.** That inversion is the bug, and it is easy to
  reintroduce while refactoring, because the tail is still needed — for the summary count.
- **The offending order is the line *after* the marker**, not before it. The server annotates
  immediately above the line it objects to.
- **`serverErrorReport` must keep returning `null`, not `""`**, for a reply with nothing to say —
  `showsServerReport` and the dialog both branch on it, and `ah-etb0.2`'s tests assert it.
- **A clean reply must come through unchanged.** `No errors found.` has no annotations, so it must
  take the no-annotations path and return the tail verbatim, or the dialog starts showing a box on
  every successful send.
- **The `<pre>` selection is load-bearing** (`:157-161`): the echo is the `<pre>` carrying `#end`,
  which is not always the first on the page. Leave that alone.
- **`decodeEntities` runs before the line split** (`:166`), so `"` in the echoed password is
  already a real quote by the time `FACTION_HEADER_LINE` sees the line. Keep that order; testing the
  filter against an already-decoded fixture is what the new test does.
acceptance_criteria: Sending a turn whose orders contain a mistake shows, in the send dialog, each of the server's inline annotations together with the offending order line beneath it and the unit line it falls under, followed by the server's own summary count as the last line. The unit line is repeated only when it changes, so several errors in one unit read as one heading. An annotation preceding any unit line is shown without one, and the offending line is omitted when the annotation is the last line, is followed by another annotation, or is followed by #end. A reply with no annotations is unchanged, so "No errors found." still produces a report the dialog hides. The faction password appears nowhere in the dialog, in any log, in any Error message or in any stored state, under any reply shape - specifically including an #atlantis line that is the first line of the block, that sits mid-document after a blank line, that is indented, or that follows the last #end; every line emitted is filtered against /^\s*#atlantis\b/ before anything else reads it, and a single test fixture carrying all four cases pins it. serverErrorReport still returns null rather than an empty string when there is nothing to say, still selects the pre carrying #end rather than the first on the page, and the existing tests for those continue to pass. No change to the dialog's markup, its label, showsServerReport, or the accepted/refused classification.

title: Light theme headings and warnings sit below the readable contrast bar
description:
Split out of ah-v09e, which the navigator scoped to the dark theme. Measured while planning it; every ratio below is the WCAG sRGB formula against the light theme's own tokens in packages/shared/src/theme.css:146-204.

Five light-theme accent tokens fail AA (4.5:1) on an opaque panel (--color-panel #eae6da):

  brass   #9a6f1d  3.61:1  FAILS
  warn    #9a6f1d  3.61:1  FAILS  (same colour as brass)
  ok      #2e7d54  4.03:1  FAILS
  select  #2470a8  4.25:1  FAILS
  danger  #b04a4a  4.29:1  FAILS

Against --color-ground (#f2efe8) they are 3.92 / 3.92 / 4.38 / 4.62 / 4.66, so brass and warn fail on every surface and ok fails on two.

This matters more than the numbers suggest because of where brass is used: every panel title bar (CollapsiblePanel.tsx:75), every section heading (primitives.tsx:77), the app wordmark (AppHeader.tsx:245) and every order warning. In light mode the application's entire heading system is below AA.

Nothing in the app qualifies as WCAG "large text" - the largest size is 13px (--text-pane-lg) and the heaviest weight is 500 - so 4.5:1 is the bar for all of it, not 3:1.

Why this was never caught: theme.test.ts:100-117 does real WCAG maths, but only over INK_TOKENS (ink, ink-soft, ink-dim) against the three surfaces. No accent token is checked in either theme. Dark mode happens to pass anyway; light mode does not.

Also unmeasured by that test, and worse in light than in dark: the floating panes are 10% opaque over the live map (.bg-pane, theme.css:344-350, --pane-transparency default 90). Light ink over a light pane on dark terrain measures 1.09:1. ah-v09e changes the default transparency to 20, which helps both themes; whether that is sufficient for light needs measuring once it lands.

Every colour here is user-facing, so the new values are the navigator's to choose from a mockup, exactly as ah-v09e's were.
design:
## Context

The light theme has contrast failures the dark theme does not, and they were invisible because
nothing tested for them.

**Five accent tokens fail AA (4.5:1) on the light panel `#eae6da`**, which is the darkest of the
three light surfaces and so the worst case:

| Token | ratio | where it is drawn |
|---|---|---|
| `brass` `#9a6f1d` | **3.61** | every panel title (`CollapsiblePanel.tsx:75`), every section heading (`primitives.tsx:77`), the wordmark (`AppHeader.tsx:245`) |
| `warn` `#9a6f1d` | **3.61** | every order warning |
| `ok` `#2e7d54` | **4.03** | success marks |
| `select` `#2470a8` | **4.25** | selection and links |
| `danger` `#b04a4a` | **4.29** | errors |

So in light mode the application's **entire heading system** sits below AA. Nothing here qualifies as
WCAG "large text" — 13px is the largest size and 500 the heaviest weight — so 4.5:1 is the bar for
all of it.

**Why nothing caught it.** `theme.test.ts:100-117` does correct WCAG maths, but only over
`INK_TOKENS` (`ink`, `ink-soft`, `ink-dim`) × three surfaces. **No accent token is checked in either
theme.** Dark happens to pass anyway; light does not. Closing that gap is half this bead.

**And then the map shows through.** `ah-v09e` changes the pane transparency default from 90 to 20, so
a pane is 80% panel over the live map. Light text is *dark*, so a light pane is worst over **dark**
terrain — the mirror image of the dark theme's problem. Measured over volcano at 20%: `ink-soft`
**4.02**, `ink-dim` **3.24**. And lowering transparency does not rescue it — even at 5%, `ink-dim`
reaches only 4.28, because the token is already marginal at 4.64 on an opaque panel. **The tokens have
to move.**

Swept across all fourteen terrain colours, the worst is `terrain-unknown` `#161c24` — unexplored
hexes, which is most of the map early in a game, and nearly black. Over that, at 20% transparency,
**seven of the nine light text tokens fail**, `brass` worst at **3.04**. Darkening brass far enough to
survive would take it to a near-black brown that stops reading as brass at all. Light mode only clears
AA across the whole map at **0% transparency** — fully opaque panes. That is what forces the
per-theme transparency below.

**This bead is blocked by `ah-v09e`** (`bd dep`: `ah-j1xd` blocks-on `ah-v09e`), because every number
here is measured at the transparency default that bead sets, and because it introduces the
pane-composite test shape this bead extends. Read `ah-v09e`'s plan before starting — particularly its
*Known traps*, all of which apply here.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Three files: `packages/shared/src/theme.css`, `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts`, and
`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`, plus their tests. **No other component changes** —
the app compiles to `var()` references, so redefining tokens repaints everything.

### 1. The light palette — `theme.css:146-204`

Seven values change inside `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Every accent keeps its hue and is darkened
the smallest amount that clears 4.5:1; **no token changes what it means or what family it belongs
to.** Ratios are against the new panel `#f0ece2`:

| Token | line | today | new | on panel | worst through a pane |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--color-panel` | `:150` | `#eae6da` | `#f0ece2` | — | — |
| `--color-ink` | `:156` | `#2a3038` | unchanged | 11.28 | 7.47 |
| `--color-ink-soft` | `:157` | `#4f5866` | `#454d59` | 7.24 | 4.79 |
| `--color-ink-dim` | `:158` | `#5e6673` | `#4a5160` | 6.75 | 4.47 |
| `--color-brass` | `:160` | `#9a6f1d` | `#8a6317` | 4.59 | — |
| `--color-warn` | `:170` | `#9a6f1d` | `#8a6317` | 4.59 | — |
| `--color-select` | `:162` | `#2470a8` | `#1f5f8f` | 5.76 | — |
| `--color-ok` | `:169` | `#2e7d54` | `#256b48` | 5.44 | — |
| `--color-danger` | `:171` | `#b04a4a` | `#9c4040` | 5.53 | — |

`--color-brass-bright` `#7d5a15` (5.32) and `--color-gain` `#3f7233` (4.86) already clear AA on every
light surface and are unchanged.

**Lightening the panel is what makes the ink hierarchy fit, and it is the only change here you would
notice as a change rather than as a fix.** Without it, `ink-dim` has to darken to about `#43495a` to
clear AA over dark terrain — which is *darker than `ink-soft` is today*, collapsing or inverting the
three-level hierarchy. With `#f0ece2` there is enough headroom for all three to clear AA and stay
visibly distinct (11.28 / 7.24 / 6.75 on the panel). Panel remains the **darkest** of the three light
surfaces (`ground` `#f2efe8`, `panel-raised` `#f7f4ec`), so the elevation cue is unchanged.

**The "worst through a pane" column is the light theme's own slider setting, not the dark one** —
see §2. At light's default of 0 the panes are opaque and those numbers are the panel column; the
figures shown are at 20%, to record what a light user who moves the slider is choosing.

**The dark theme is not touched.** `ah-v09e` owns every dark value.

### 2. Transparency remembered per theme — `settingsStore.ts`

Today `paneTransparency` is one number (`:72`), one default (`:20`), one clamp (`:173-181`), one
setter (`:280-284`), stamped onto the root by `applyPaneTransparency` (`:183-190`). It becomes one
value **per theme**:

```ts
/** Panes over the map: dark can afford to be see-through, light cannot. See ah-j1xd. */
export const DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY: Record<ThemeName, number> = { dark: 20, light: 0 };
```

and in `SettingsState` (`:72`):

```ts
  paneTransparency: Record<ThemeName, number>;
```

- **`setPaneTransparency(percent)` writes the *active* theme's slot** and stamps it. Its signature
  does not change; the theme comes from `get().theme`.
- **`setTheme` must re-stamp the transparency.** This is the easiest thing in the bead to miss:
  switching to light has to repaint the panes at light's value, and nothing does that today because
  there was only one value. Add `applyPaneTransparency(get().paneTransparency[theme])` to `setTheme`
  beside its existing `applyTheme(theme)`.
- **`applyPersistedSettings` (`:344-357`) stamps the active theme's value**, keeping its existing
  reconciliation: clamp, write back into the store, then stamp. Its doc comment explains why both
  halves are needed; that reasoning is unchanged, it now just applies to a record.
- `clampTransparency` (`:173-181`) is unchanged and still returns `0…95` — **the slider's range is
  the same in both themes, and a light user may still choose a value below AA.** The navigator chose
  freedom over a clamp, in both this bead and `ah-v09e`.

**The migration is the risky part.** `paneTransparency` is persisted (`:132` in the `Persisted` pick,
`:333` in the partialize), so every existing user has a **number** in localStorage where the code now
expects a record. Reconcile on rehydration:

```ts
function reconcilePaneTransparency(stored: unknown): Record<ThemeName, number> {
  // Before ah-j1xd this was a single number shared by both themes. A stored number is a choice the
  // user made, so it is kept - for dark, where see-through panes are affordable. Light takes its
  // new default rather than inheriting a value measured against the wrong theme.
  if (typeof stored === "number" || typeof stored === "string") {
    return { dark: clampTransparency(stored), light: DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY.light };
  }
  if (stored && typeof stored === "object") {
    const record = stored as Partial<Record<ThemeName, unknown>>;
    return {
      dark: record.dark === undefined ? DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY.dark : clampTransparency(record.dark),
      light: record.light === undefined ? DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY.light : clampTransparency(record.light)
    };
  }
  return { ...DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY };
}
```

Called from `applyPersistedSettings`, where the existing clamp-and-write-back happens. Note that
`clampTransparency` already coerces strings deliberately (its comment at `:175-176` says storage is
hand-editable), so the string case above is not paranoia.

`resetSettings` (`:401`) stamps `DEFAULTS.paneTransparency[theme]` for whichever theme is active.

### 3. The slider — `SettingsDialog.tsx:256-277`

It reads and writes the **active theme's** value: `paneTransparency[theme]` rather than
`paneTransparency`. Nothing else about the control changes — same `min 0 max 95 step 5`, same
`data-testid="pane-transparency"`.

Its hint gains a sentence, exactly as the navigator worded it:

> Makes the panes see-through so the map shows behind them. Remembered separately for the dark and
> light themes.

### 4. The test that closes the gap — `theme.test.ts`

The navigator asked for **every text token, both themes, on every surface and through a pane**. Reuse
the existing `relativeLuminance()` / `contrast()` (`:85-98`) and `AA_SMALL_TEXT` (`:74`), and widen
`INK_TOKENS` into a full list:

```ts
/**
 * Every token the application draws text in. The old list held only the three `ink` tokens, and
 * that gap is why five light accents sat below AA unnoticed - `brass` at 3.61:1, carrying every
 * panel title, every section heading and every order warning in the app (ah-j1xd).
 */
const TEXT_TOKENS = [
  "--color-ink", "--color-ink-soft", "--color-ink-dim",
  "--color-brass", "--color-brass-bright", "--color-select",
  "--color-ok", "--color-warn", "--color-danger", "--color-gain"
] as const;
```

Two assertions, each over `TEXT_TOKENS` × both themes:

1. **On every surface** — `ground`, `panel`, `panel-raised` — clears `AA_SMALL_TEXT`. This is the
   existing assertion at `:100-117` with a wider token list; keep its shape.
2. **Through a pane over every terrain** — composite `panel` over each `--color-terrain-*` at **that
   theme's own default transparency** and clear `AA_SMALL_TEXT`. `ah-v09e` introduces this assertion
   for dark; this bead generalises it to both themes by reading
   `DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY[theme]` rather than a single constant.

Assertion 2 is why light's default must be 0: at 0 the composite *is* the panel, so it reduces to
assertion 1 and passes. **Read the defaults from `settingsStore.ts`, never hard-code them** — that is
what makes a future change to either default either keep the app readable or fail this test, which is
the whole value of it.

Compositing is `t * a + b * (1 - a)` per channel in sRGB with `a = (100 - transparency) / 100`,
matching `color-mix(in srgb, …)`, which is what `.bg-pane` uses.

The existing dark/light parity check (`:119-128`) and the no-hex-literals check (`:37-60`) are
unchanged and must stay green.

## Increments

1. **The test learns about accents, and light goes red.**
   RED: widen `INK_TOKENS` to `TEXT_TOKENS` in the existing surface assertion. It fails immediately,
   naming light `brass` at 3.61 and four others. **Do not fix anything yet** — read the failure and
   check it names exactly the five tokens in *Context*. If it names a sixth, or names a dark token,
   stop and work out why before going on.
   GREEN: the five accent values in §1 (`brass`, `warn`, `select`, `ok`, `danger`).

2. **Transparency is remembered per theme.**
   RED: `settingsStore.test.ts` — `pane transparency is kept per theme` (set 40 in dark, switch to
   light, expect light's default and not 40, switch back, expect 40), and
   `switching theme repaints the panes` (asserting `--pane-transparency` on the root element changes
   with the theme). Both fail to compile against a `number`.
   GREEN: the record, the theme-aware setter, `setTheme` re-stamping, and
   `applyPersistedSettings`.

3. **Nobody's stored setting is lost or misread.**
   RED: `a stored number becomes the dark value` (localStorage holding `paneTransparency: 65` →
   `{ dark: 65, light: 0 }`), `a stored string is coerced`, `a half-written record is completed`
   (`{ dark: 40 }` → light takes its default), and `nonsense falls back to both defaults`.
   GREEN: `reconcilePaneTransparency`.

4. **The light ink hierarchy fits.**
   RED: the pane-composite assertion from §4, generalised to both themes and reading each theme's
   default. Light fails on `ink-soft` and `ink-dim` while light's default is still whatever
   increment 2 left it.
   GREEN: `panel` `#f0ece2`, `ink-soft` `#454d59`, `ink-dim` `#4a5160`, and light's default
   transparency of 0.

5. **The slider says what it now does.**
   RED: `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` — `the transparency slider shows the active theme's value` and a
   check for the new hint text.
   GREEN: reading `paneTransparency[theme]`, and the hint string quoted in §3.

## The test plan

**TypeScript — three files**, all run by `pnpm run check:fast`.

`packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| **`every text token clears AA on every surface`** | `TEXT_TOKENS` × 3 surfaces × both themes — the widened assertion, and the one that catches this whole class |
| **`every text token clears AA through a pane over every terrain`** | × 14 terrains × both themes, at each theme's own default transparency |
| the existing parity check (`:119-128`) | unchanged |
| the existing no-hex-literals check (`:37-60`) | unchanged |

`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.test.ts` (which already iterates `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` at `:73`,
so the file and its helpers exist):

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `pane transparency is kept per theme` | 40 in dark, light untouched, 40 still there on switching back |
| `switching theme repaints the panes` | `setTheme` re-stamps `--pane-transparency` — the easiest thing here to forget |
| `a stored number becomes the dark value` | the migration: `65` → `{ dark: 65, light: 0 }` |
| `a stored string is coerced` | `"65"` likewise |
| `a half-written record is completed` | `{ dark: 40 }` → light defaults |
| `nonsense falls back to both defaults` | `null`, `[]`, `"x"` |
| `resetting settings stamps the active theme's default` | `resetSettings` |

`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `the transparency slider shows the active theme's value` | reads `paneTransparency[theme]` |
| `the transparency hint names both themes` | the exact hint string |

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`, plus the browser suites by choice — the light theme is not the
default, so a smoke test is unlikely to be looking at it, but the panel colour moves and a screenshot
comparison would notice.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-18 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-j1xd-light.html`. The chosen
mockup is committed to `docs/ui/ah-j1xd-light.html`.

**Q1 — the light ink hierarchy squeeze.** To clear AA over dark terrain, `ink-dim` must darken past
where `ink-soft` sits today, collapsing or inverting the three-level hierarchy. Chosen: **lighten the
light panel** from `#eae6da` to `#f0ece2`, which buys enough headroom for all three to clear AA and
stay distinct. Rejected: keeping the surfaces and **compressing the hierarchy** so secondary and
dimmed text end up nearly the same colour; keeping the surfaces and **letting dimmed text sit below
AA** as a documented exception on the grounds that it is genuinely tertiary; and **a per-theme
transparency floor alone**, which was measured and does not work by itself — even at 5% transparency
`ink-dim` reaches only 4.28.

**Q2 — the accent values.** Chosen: **as proposed** — each keeps its hue and is darkened the smallest
amount that clears 4.5:1. `brass`/`warn` `#9a6f1d`→`#8a6317`, `select` `#2470a8`→`#1f5f8f`, `ok`
`#2e7d54`→`#256b48`, `danger` `#b04a4a`→`#9c4040`. `brass` at 4.59 is deliberately the tightest, to
stay as close to today's colour as the bar allows. Rejected: darkening further for margin (roughly
5.5–6:1, visibly darker, especially brass) and drawing brass alternatives to choose from.

**Q3 — how far the new tests reach.** Chosen: **every text token, both themes, on every surface and
through a pane.** Rejected: adding the accents but skipping the through-pane check for light; and
simply matching whatever `ah-v09e` does.

**Q4 — light mode and the map showing through.** Raised by me after Q3, when the terrain sweep showed
that Q3's own answer is unachievable for light at `ah-v09e`'s default: over `terrain-unknown`
`#161c24`, seven of nine light tokens fail at 20% transparency, `brass` at 3.04. Chosen: **transparency
is remembered per theme**, defaulting to 20 in dark and **0 in light**, both freely adjustable.
Rejected: **pinning light to opaque** with no slider (guarantees AA, takes the choice away);
**asserting light on opaque surfaces only** and documenting the gap; and **clamping light to 5%** with
`brass` pushed to about `#7a5713`, which moves two colours further than Q2 agreed.

**Q5 — the slider's hint.** Chosen, verbatim: **"Makes the panes see-through so the map shows behind
them. Remembered separately for the dark and light themes."** Rejected: the terser "Set per theme."
and leaving the hint unchanged.

## Out of scope

- **The dark theme.** Every dark value is `ah-v09e`'s. This bead changes none of them, and the
  widened test must find them already passing — if it does not, `ah-v09e` did not land correctly and
  that is the bug to chase.
- **The map.** Terrain, fog, unit, settlement, selection, note and risk tokens are untouched, and so
  is `mapThemes/**`. `ah-v09e` adds `--color-map-label-halo` and `--color-map-region-name` precisely
  so a chrome palette change cannot move the map; this bead relies on that and adds nothing.
- **Clamping either theme's slider** so a user cannot choose a below-AA value. Considered in both
  beads and rejected in both.
- **`--color-selection-ring` and `--color-selection-casing`**, which are deliberately inverted between
  themes (`theme.css:166-167`) and are map chrome.
- **`--color-note` and `--color-note-ink`**, identical in both themes by design (`theme.css:194`).
- **A high-contrast mode or a `prefers-contrast` query.** Neither exists; neither is added.
- **The light theme's type scale.** Shared with dark, and `ah-v09e` raises it.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye, in the running app — and **in the light theme**, which is the whole point:

1. Switch to **Light**. Every panel title and section heading should read comfortably against the
   panel; those are the `brass` 3.61:1 headings the bead is about. Compare with `git stash`ed main
   side by side if in any doubt — the difference is meant to be noticeable.
2. Find a hex with an order warning (the fixtures produce several) and read it in light. That is
   `warn`, the same failing colour.
3. **Panes are opaque in light by default.** Confirm the map does not show through, then drag the
   transparency slider up and confirm it does, then switch to **Dark** and confirm the slider snaps
   back to dark's own value and the panes are see-through again. Switch back to light: your light
   value is remembered.
4. **The migration.** With a profile that has a pre-existing `paneTransparency` number in
   localStorage, confirm the dark theme keeps that number and light starts at 0.
5. Read the slider's hint and check it matches the wording in §3 exactly.
6. **The dark theme is unchanged.** Switch to dark and compare against main-after-`ah-v09e`; nothing
   should have moved.
7. **The map is unchanged in both themes** — terrain, fog, unit dots, labels and region names.

## Known traps

- **`setTheme` must re-stamp `--pane-transparency`.** Nothing does this today because there was one
  value for both themes. Miss it and switching to light leaves the panes painted at dark's
  transparency until something else happens to re-stamp — which looks like the setting being ignored,
  intermittently. `switching theme repaints the panes` is the guard.
- **`paneTransparency` is persisted, so every existing user has a number where the code now wants a
  record.** Without `reconcilePaneTransparency`, `paneTransparency[theme]` on a number is `undefined`,
  `String(undefined)` reaches the CSS custom property, and `.bg-pane`'s `calc()` produces an invalid
  value — panes render with no background at all. This is the failure that reaches users rather than
  tests, because a fresh profile never hits it.
- **`clampTransparency` deliberately coerces strings** (`:175-176`); keep that behaviour when reusing
  it inside the record reconciler.
- **The widened test will fail for light before anything is fixed, and that is increment 1.** Read
  the failure rather than fixing forward from it — it should name exactly five tokens, all light.
- **Light's worst terrain is `terrain-unknown` `#161c24`, not a colourful one.** Unexplored hexes are
  most of an early map. Any reasoning that samples only "interesting" terrain will conclude the light
  theme is fine when it is not.
- **`theme.test.ts:37-60` forbids `#rrggbb` literals** in non-test `.ts`/`.tsx` under
  `packages/shared/src`. Every colour here belongs in `theme.css`.
- **Dark/light parity is enforced** (`:119-128`). This bead adds no tokens, so it should not fire —
  if it does, something was added to one block only.
- **`--color-brass-bright` is *darker* than `--color-brass` in light** (`#7d5a15` vs `#9a6f1d`,
  becoming `#8a6317`). The name inverts its meaning in this theme. That is pre-existing, it is not a
  mistake, and it is not this bead's to tidy.
- **`ah-v09e` must be merged first.** This bead's pane-composite test generalises the one that bead
  introduces, and its numbers assume that bead's transparency default. Starting before it lands means
  writing the assertion twice.

The light palette moves: panel #eae6da to #f0ece2, ink-soft #4f5866 to #454d59, ink-dim #5e6673 to #4a5160, brass and warn #9a6f1d to #8a6317, select #2470a8 to #1f5f8f, ok #2e7d54 to #256b48, danger #b04a4a to #9c4040; every accent keeps its hue and panel stays the darkest of the three light surfaces.
