title: Warn when a BUILD order has nothing to build
description:
A unit with the Building skill can write `BUILD` or `BUILD COMPLETE` while it is not inside a
structure. Neither form names what to build, so both only make sense for a unit that is already in
the structure it is working on - from outside, the order does nothing and the month is wasted. The
other forms (`BUILD <name>`, `BUILD <name> COMPLETE`, `BUILD HELP <unit>`) each say what to work on
and are fine from outside.

This should be a warning, not an error: the report is a snapshot, and a unit that enters a structure
earlier in the same month may be inside by the time the order runs.

Both pieces already exist:

- `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:271` parses the BUILD forms. The bare form and the `COMPLETE`
  form both yield `Intent::Build { founding: None, helping: None }`, which is exactly the pair to
  warn on - the other forms carry a `founding` or a `helping`.
- `crates/core/src/report/model.rs:159` has `pub structure_id: Option<String>`, documented as "Set
  when the unit sits inside a structure". `None` is the outside case.

So the rule is: warn when `Intent::Build` has neither `founding` nor `helping` and the unit's
`structure_id` is `None`.

For the planner:

- Whether the entering-a-structure case (`ENTER` earlier in the same month's orders) should suppress
  the warning, or whether the warning is worth having even then.
- Which warning category this joins, and whether it belongs behind one of the warning toggles.
design:
## Context

A unit with the Building skill can write `BUILD` or `BUILD COMPLETE` while standing in no structure
at all. Neither form names what to work on, so from outside the order does nothing and the unit's
whole month is spent for nothing. The same waste happens a second way: `BUILD HELP 4021` when 4021
is one of our own units that has no BUILD order of its own — there is nothing to help with, so the
helper's month goes too.

Both are warnings rather than errors: the report is a snapshot, and the orders can move a unit
before the BUILD runs.

**This is the sibling of `ah-90w`, which is merged.** That bead landed everything this one builds
on — the `Intent::Build { founding, helping }` shape (`intents.rs:90-101`), the `check_building`
function, `structure_after_orders`, and the **Building** group in the Warnings tab. It deliberately
went silent on a unit in no structure, calling that in its own plan *"a different mistake and not
this bead's"* — `semantics.rs:1408-1410` is the `continue` where it does so. This bead is that
different mistake.

**The bead grew by one check during the interview.** Its filed acceptance criteria said the HELP
forms raise nothing "whether or not the unit is inside a structure". The navigator kept that for the
*outside-a-structure* rule but added a second, different rule about HELP: warn when the helped unit
is one of ours and is not building at all. The acceptance criteria below supersede the filed ones.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Two new codes — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

Append to `mod codes` (`:73-124`), beside `ALREADY_BUILT` at `:91`:

```rust
    pub const BUILD_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE: Code = Code("build-outside-structure");
    pub const BUILD_HELP_NOT_BUILDING: Code = Code("build-help-not-building");
```

and append both to `ALL`, **last, in that order**, bumping its length: `pub const ALL: [Code; 20]`
(`:104`) becomes `[Code; 22]`. The array's own doc comment (`:97-103`) states the rule this follows:
new-*here*-last regardless of where the codes land in the settings UI, because the generated
TypeScript copies this array's order.

### Two new checks — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

**Two functions, not one, and not an extension of `check_building`.** `check_building` early-returns
on `!options.emits(codes::ALREADY_BUILT)` at `:1374`, so anything hosted inside it would be silently
switched off by the *"Building what is built"* toggle. Each check gates on its own code. (Navigator
confirmed, round two.)

Register both in `check_turn`'s per-hex call list (`:221-232`), immediately after the existing
`check_building(&hex, &options, &mut findings);` at `:226`:

```rust
        check_building_outside(&hex, &options, &mut findings);
        check_build_help(&hex, &options, &mut findings);
```

Findings are sorted within the hex by line afterwards (`:237`), so the call order does not decide the
displayed order.

#### `check_building_outside`

```rust
/// Every own unit whose bare `BUILD` or `BUILD COMPLETE` is written from inside no structure at
/// all. Neither form names what to work on, so from outside the order does nothing.
fn check_building_outside(hex: &Hex<'_>, options: &CheckOptions, findings: &mut Vec<Finding>)
```

For each `ordered` in `hex.units` (own units only — `Hex::read` filters `unit.own`, `:286`):

1. The **first** `Intent::Build` in the block, exactly as `check_building` does at `:1379-1385`
   (`ordered.intents.iter().find(...)`); none, `continue`. One warning per unit, on the first BUILD —
   navigator confirmed.
2. `founding.is_some()` → `continue`. `BUILD Tower` names what to found and is fine from outside.
3. `helping.is_some()` → `continue`. The HELP forms name whose structure to work on; they are the
   other check's business, and they are silent here whether or not either unit is in a structure.
4. `structure_after_orders(ordered)` (`:1656`) — `Some(_)` → `continue`; `None` → warn.
5. `findings.push(ordered.finding(hex, codes::BUILD_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE,
   "is in no structure to build in".to_string(), Some(placed)))`.

The message is a fixed string — it names nothing variable — but it is still built at the point of
emission like every other one, and it carries no trailing full stop and no leading capital, matching
`"Soggy Saw Mill is already finished"` (`:1426`).

**Step 4 is the whole of the ENTER/LEAVE behaviour, and it is deliberate.** `structure_after_orders`
answers "what is this unit standing in when its orders happen", and its doc comment (`:1640-1656`)
says every such check wants it rather than `unit.structure_id`. So `ENTER 4` then `BUILD` is silent —
the unit is inside 4 by the time BUILD runs, which is the normal correct way to write it — and
`LEAVE` then `BUILD` warns even though the report shows the unit safely inside a structure. **The
navigator was shown that consequence and accepted it**; the two cannot be separated, since reading
`unit.structure_id` instead would warn on the common `ENTER`/`BUILD` pattern.

#### `check_build_help`

```rust
/// Every own unit whose `BUILD HELP` names one of our own units in this hex that has no BUILD
/// order of its own. There is nothing to help with, so the helper's month is spent for nothing.
fn check_build_help(hex: &Hex<'_>, options: &CheckOptions, findings: &mut Vec<Finding>)
```

For each `ordered` in `hex.units`:

1. The first `Intent::Build` in the block; none, `continue`.
2. `helping` is `Some(Party::Unit(id))` — anything else (`None`, `Party::New`, `Party::Foreign`,
   `Party::Discard`) → `continue`. `Party` is `crates/core/src/orders/forms.rs:43-52`; the same
   match `check_building` uses at `:1397-1406`.
3. `hex.find(id)` (`:299`) — `None` → `continue`. A unit the report does not show in this hex, or
   one forming this month with no number yet, cannot be judged. `hex.units` holds own units only, so
   this also enforces "one of our own units".
4. Does the helped unit build? `helped.intents.iter().any(|placed| matches!(placed.intent,
   Intent::Build { .. }))` — `true` → `continue`. **Any** BUILD counts, `BUILD Tower` included:
   founding is building, so there is work to help with. Whether that unit's own BUILD is any good is
   judged on that unit's own line, by `check_building` or by `check_building_outside`.
5. `false` → warn: `format!("unit {id} is not building")`, pushed with
   `ordered.finding(hex, codes::BUILD_HELP_NOT_BUILDING, message, Some(placed))`.

**One mistake is marked once, where it was made.** A helper whose target *is* building but is
itself in no structure stays silent — the target's own line carries that warning. Navigator chose
this over marking every helper, explicitly accepting that it differs from `ah-90w`'s helper
behaviour: six units helping one builder produce one warning here, not seven.

### The settings tab — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

Two entries appended to the existing **Building** group (`:437-446`, which today holds only
`already-built` at `:443-447`), keeping its `heading: "Building"` unchanged:

```tsx
      {
        code: "build-outside-structure",
        title: "Building outside a structure",
        description: "A bare BUILD or BUILD COMPLETE by a unit that is in no structure."
      },
      {
        code: "build-help-not-building",
        title: "Helping a unit that is not building",
        description: "A BUILD HELP naming a unit with no BUILD order of its own."
      }
```

All four strings are the navigator's, chosen as drawn in the mockup. **Two toggles, not one** — two
genuinely different mistakes, each switchable alone, as every other group in the tab does it.

**Nothing to change in `settingsStore.ts`.** `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS`
(`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:26-35`) derives its defaults as `code !== "hex-unguarded"`, so
both new codes are **on by default** with no edit. `reconcileAdvisoryChecks` (`:42`) folds them into
settings saved before this bead. Nor is there anything to change at the two call sites that compute
the disabled list, `AppShell.tsx:1902` and `:2079` — both filter over `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`.

### The generated vocabulary

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` mirrors `codes::ALL` (`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`,
`:5-25`). Regenerate rather than hand-edit:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

## Increments

1. **A BUILD from nowhere warns.**
   RED: `semantics.rs` tests — `a_bare_build_outside_any_structure_warns`, a hex with one own unit
   whose `structure_id` is `None` ordering `BUILD`, expecting one finding with code
   `build-outside-structure`, `unit_id` `Some("4021")`, `line` `Some(2)` and message
   `is in no structure to build in`. Fails: no such code, no such check.
   GREEN: `codes::BUILD_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE`, `ALL` at `[Code; 21]`, `check_building_outside`, and its
   call in `check_turn`.

2. **BUILD COMPLETE is the same mistake, and the named forms are not.**
   RED: `build_complete_outside_any_structure_warns`, `founding_a_structure_from_outside_is_silent`
   (`BUILD Tower`), `a_unit_inside_a_structure_is_not_told_it_is_outside` (`in_structure(unit("4021"),
   "1")` with an unfinished building, ordering `BUILD`), and
   `a_foreign_unit_building_outside_is_not_warned_about`,
   `a_build_help_is_not_told_it_is_outside_a_structure` (`BUILD HELP 4021` from outside → nothing
   from this check, whatever `check_build_help` later says), and
   `only_the_first_build_in_a_block_is_warned_about` (a block with two bare `BUILD` lines → one
   finding, on line 2).
   GREEN: the `founding.is_some()`, `helping.is_some()` and `structure_after_orders` branches, and
   the `.find(...)` that takes only the first intent. `BUILD COMPLETE` needs no code of its own —
   `intents.rs:271-274` already gives it `founding: None, helping: None`.

3. **ENTER and LEAVE decide where the unit is.**
   RED: `a_unit_that_enters_a_structure_this_month_is_not_told_it_is_outside` (`ENTER 1` then
   `BUILD`, unit outside per the report → silent) and
   `a_unit_that_leaves_its_structure_this_month_is_told_it_is_outside` (`LEAVE` then `BUILD`, unit
   inside per the report → warns). The second is the navigator's accepted consequence and must be
   pinned, or a later reader will "fix" it.
   GREEN: nothing, if increment 1 used `structure_after_orders`. If either fails, that is the bug
   this increment exists to catch.

4. **Helping somebody who is not building.**
   RED: `helping_a_unit_that_is_not_building_warns` — a hex with own units 4021 (ordering `WORK`)
   and 4117 (ordering `BUILD HELP 4021`), expecting exactly one finding, on 4117, code
   `build-help-not-building`, message `unit 4021 is not building`.
   GREEN: `codes::BUILD_HELP_NOT_BUILDING`, `ALL` at `[Code; 22]`, `check_build_help`, and its call.

5. **Every silence the HELP check owes.**
   RED: `helping_a_unit_that_is_building_is_silent`, `helping_a_unit_that_is_founding_is_silent`
   (`BUILD Tower`), `helping_a_unit_not_in_this_hex_is_silent` (`BUILD HELP 9999`),
   `helping_a_new_unit_is_silent` (`BUILD HELP NEW 1`),
   `a_helper_whose_target_builds_from_outside_is_not_warned_too` — the double-marking case: 4021
   outside a structure ordering `BUILD`, 4117 ordering `BUILD HELP 4021`, expecting exactly **one**
   finding, on 4021.
   GREEN: the `Party` match and the `any(Intent::Build)` branch.

6. **Both toggles switch their own check off, and only their own.**
   RED: `the_build_outside_check_can_be_turned_off` and `the_build_help_check_can_be_turned_off`,
   using the existing `disabling(code)` helper (`:4775`); plus the disable table these tests sit
   beside gaining a row for each code.
   GREEN: nothing, if the gates were written as specified. This pins that neither check hid behind
   `ALREADY_BUILT`'s gate.

7. **The vocabulary and the tab.**
   RED: `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts` fails
   (`core_client_vocabulary_matches_the_core`, `generated_ts.rs:52`), and
   `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`'s first case fails on its hard-coded `titles` array.
   GREEN: regenerate the vocabulary; add the two `WARNING_GROUPS` entries; add both titles to the
   `titles` array at `SettingsDialog.test.tsx:67-85`, positioned to match the rendered order.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`, `mod tests` at `:2292`.** Naming convention is a
full sentence in snake_case with no `test_` prefix. Reuse the existing fixtures rather than writing
new ones: `region(units)` `:2305`, `unit(id)` `:2327`, `in_structure(unit, id)` `:3963`,
`unfinished_building(id)` `:3954`, `finished_mill(id)` `:3931`; drivers `check(regions, orders)`
`:2430`, `only(findings)` `:2472`, `codes(&findings)` `:2455`, `disabling(code)` `:4775`. A unit is
outside a structure by default — `unit(id)` leaves `structure_id` as `None` — so the warning case
needs no fixture at all beyond `region(vec![unit("4021")])`.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `a_bare_build_outside_any_structure_warns` | code, unit, line 2, `is in no structure to build in` |
| `build_complete_outside_any_structure_warns` | `BUILD COMPLETE` is the same mistake |
| `founding_a_structure_from_outside_is_silent` | `BUILD Tower` → nothing |
| `a_unit_inside_a_structure_is_not_told_it_is_outside` | the ordinary correct case |
| `a_foreign_unit_building_outside_is_not_warned_about` | own units only |
| `a_unit_that_enters_a_structure_this_month_is_not_told_it_is_outside` | `ENTER 1` / `BUILD` → nothing |
| **`a_unit_that_leaves_its_structure_this_month_is_told_it_is_outside`** | `LEAVE` / `BUILD` → warns. The navigator's accepted consequence |
| `only_the_first_build_in_a_block_is_warned_about` | two bare BUILDs → one finding |
| `helping_a_unit_that_is_not_building_warns` | `unit 4021 is not building`, on the helper |
| `helping_a_unit_that_is_building_is_silent` | there is work to help with |
| `helping_a_unit_that_is_founding_is_silent` | `BUILD Tower` counts as building |
| `helping_a_unit_not_in_this_hex_is_silent` | `BUILD HELP 9999` → nothing, no panic |
| `helping_a_new_unit_is_silent` | `BUILD HELP NEW 1` → nothing |
| **`a_helper_whose_target_builds_from_outside_is_not_warned_too`** | exactly one finding, on the target |
| `a_build_help_is_not_told_it_is_outside_a_structure` | the HELP form never raises `build-outside-structure` |
| `the_build_outside_check_can_be_turned_off` | its own gate |
| `the_build_help_check_can_be_turned_off` | its own gate, independent of `already-built` |
| the disable table at `:~4775` | a row for each new code |

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` must be run and must stay green.** It asserts the
turn-71 template produces an exact finding list (`:204-216`); a new check that fires on real,
server-accepted orders breaks it, and correctly so. **It will not fire here** — the committed
template (`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep`) contains no BUILD order of any
form; verified by `grep -inE "^[[:space:]]*build"` returning nothing. If it does break, the check is
wrong, not the fixture.

**TypeScript — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`.** Its first case (`:56`)
hard-codes a `titles` array (`:67-85`) that must gain **"Building outside a structure"** and
**"Helping a unit that is not building"**, then loops over `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` asserting a
`settings-warning-${code}` toggle exists — so a Rust code without a UI entry fails here by design.
Its second case (`:98`) asserts every code but `hex-unguarded` starts checked, and both new codes
must satisfy it. `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.test.ts` (`:73`) iterates the same list and needs
no edit.

**Suites:** `cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite — nothing here
changes rendering, only a checkbox row and a message string.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-18 over
`.cerebro/scratch/ah-vkut-build-outside.html`, in two rounds. The chosen mockup is committed to
`docs/ui/ah-vkut-build-outside.html`.

**Q1 — the wording of the outside-a-structure warning.** Chosen: **`is in no structure to build in`**
(rendered as `4102  is in no structure to build in`). The same message covers bare `BUILD` and
`BUILD COMPLETE`; the navigator was asked whether they should differ and said no.
Rejected: `is in no structure, so BUILD works on nothing` — the consequence clause `ah-90w`
deliberately dropped, and it wraps at panel width; and `orders BUILD from outside any structure` — an
"orders X" construction no other message uses, and redundant with the line the finding sits on.

**Q2 — the Warnings tab entry.** Chosen: title **"Building outside a structure"**, description
**"A bare BUILD or BUILD COMPLETE by a unit that is in no structure."** Rejected: "Building nothing"
/ "A BUILD that names no structure, by a unit standing in none." — a neater pair with "Building what
is built", but it says the effect where the player wants to know the situation.

**Q3 — ENTER and LEAVE.** Chosen: **read where the unit stands after its own orders**, via
`structure_after_orders`. `ENTER 4` / `BUILD` is silent; **`LEAVE` / `BUILD` warns**, about a unit the
report shows inside a structure. The navigator was shown that consequence in a table and accepted it
explicitly. Rejected: reading `unit.structure_id` (would warn on the common `ENTER`/`BUILD`
pattern — the two cannot be separated); and going silent whenever the block holds any ENTER or LEAVE
(misses the real LEAVE mistake and diverges from the house rule).

**Q4 — the HELP form.** The bead as filed said the HELP forms raise nothing. The navigator **kept
that for the outside-a-structure rule and added a different check**: `BUILD HELP <unit>` warns when
the named unit is one of our own and **has no BUILD order at all** — you cannot help someone who is
not building. Rejected: my proposal to warn when the helped unit is outside a structure; and leaving
HELP entirely alone.

**Q5 — the HELP wording.** Chosen: **`unit 4021 is not building`**. Rejected:
`unit 4021 is not building, so there is nothing to help with` (longer, wraps in the region pane) and
`unit 4021, which it would help, is not building` (mirrors `ah-90w`'s helper line, but the clause
does less work here since HELP already named the unit).

**Q6 — double-marking.** Chosen: **silent**. When the helped unit is building but is itself in no
structure, only that unit is warned; the helper is not. One mistake, marked once, where it was made.
Rejected: warning the helper too — which is what `ah-90w` does for its own helper case — because six
units helping one builder would produce seven warnings about one mistake. **This is a deliberate
divergence from `ah-90w`; do not "fix" it into consistency.**

**Q7 — one toggle or two.** Chosen: **two**, both in the existing Building group. Rejected: a single
"BUILD orders that build nothing" toggle covering both — fewer rows, but one could not be silenced
without the other.

**Q8 — repeated BUILDs.** Chosen: **one warning per unit, on the first BUILD in the block**,
mirroring `check_building`. Rejected: one per BUILD order.

## Out of scope

- **Whether the materials or the skill are there.** A unit with no Building skill, or nothing to
  build with, is a different check and is not filed.
- **`BUILD HELP` naming a unit outside a structure.** Deliberately silent (Q6). Not filed as a
  follow-up — the navigator judged the target's own warning sufficient.
- **The other BUILD forms' correctness.** `BUILD Tower` is never questioned here; whether the type
  exists in the ruleset, and whether the hex allows it, are not this bead's.
- **A structure founded by this turn's own orders.** `BUILD Tower` earlier in the same block does not
  put the unit inside anything as far as `structure_after_orders` is concerned, and nothing here
  pretends otherwise.
- **`crate::movement::fleet::OrderedUnits::structure_of`**, the second model of "where is this unit"
  that `structure_after_orders`'s doc comment names. Unifying them is `ah-ssd`. **Nothing in this
  bead changes `structure_after_orders`, so nothing here needs to touch that second model.**
- **Severity.** Every finding this repository emits is a warning (`orders/mod.rs:78-90` maps them all
  to `OrderDiagnosticSeverity::Warning`); no error path is added.

## Validation

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye, in the running app:

1. Load any turn. Pick a unit the report shows **outside** any structure, order it `BUILD`, and check
   the problems list reads exactly `is in no structure to build in` against that unit's number.
   Change it to `BUILD COMPLETE` — same warning. Change it to `BUILD Tower` — silent.
2. Pick a unit the report shows **inside** a structure, order it `BUILD` — silent (or `already-built`
   if that structure is finished, which is `ah-90w`'s check, not this one). Add `LEAVE` above the
   `BUILD` — it now warns. Replace the `LEAVE` with `ENTER <that structure's number>` on a unit that
   starts outside — silent.
3. Two units in one hex: order one `WORK` and the other `BUILD HELP <the first>` — one warning,
   `unit <n> is not building`, on the helper. Give the first `BUILD` as well — the helper goes
   silent.
4. Settings → Warnings → **Building** shows three rows. Untick "Building outside a structure": the
   §1 warnings go, the HELP warning stays. Untick "Helping a unit that is not building": that one
   goes. Untick "Building what is built": neither of the new ones is affected.

## Known traps

- **`codes::ALL` has its length in its type** (`semantics.rs:104`) and the generated TypeScript
  copies its order. Two codes means `[Code; 22]`, **appended last**, and a regeneration. Inserting
  them next to `ALREADY_BUILT` in `ALL` compiles and silently reorders the generated file.
- **Do not host either check inside `check_building`.** It early-returns on
  `!options.emits(codes::ALREADY_BUILT)` at `:1374`, so switching off "Building what is built" would
  silently switch off whatever shares that function. Increment 6 exists to catch this.
- **`structure_after_orders`, never `unit.structure_id`.** Its doc comment (`:1640-1656`) records
  that every LEAVE is processed before any ENTER — the engine's own order, confirmed by the
  navigator on 2026-08-18 *after a verification failed on exactly this point*. Reading the report's
  field instead makes `ENTER`/`BUILD` warn falsely, which is the whole false-positive failure mode.
- **`LEAVE` then `BUILD` warning is intended, not a bug.** It warns about a unit the report shows
  inside a structure. It is pinned by a named test and was accepted by the navigator; do not soften
  it.
- **The helper case deliberately differs from `ah-90w`.** That check warns the helper about the
  structure it would work on; this one does not double-mark. Two adjacent checks, two different
  answers, both deliberate.
- **`[name]` in the BUILD parse matches any single token that is not `COMPLETE` or `HELP`**
  (`intents.rs:277-280`), so a misspelt keyword lands in `founding` and both new checks go silent on
  it. That is the syntax checker's business, not theirs.
- **`read_intents` drops `TURN` blocks and `FORM` blocks** (`intents.rs:140-143`). A `BUILD` inside a
  `TURN` block is next month's and is not seen here at all — do not try to make it visible.
- **`SettingsDialog.test.tsx` hard-codes its `titles` array** (`:67-85`). Adding a code in Rust
  without adding both the `WARNING_GROUPS` entry and the title here fails the TS suite, and the
  failure names the count rather than the missing title.
- **`validate_real_orders.rs` is the false-positive bar**, asserting an exact finding list against
  orders a real server accepted. The turn-71 template has no BUILD orders, so it should stay green;
  if it does not, the check is wrong.
- **`hex.units` is own units only** (`Hex::read`, `:286`), which is what makes `hex.find` answer
  "one of our own units in this hex" in a single call. Do not reach past it to `region.units`.
acceptance_criteria: A unit that is in no structure once its own ENTER/LEAVE orders have run, and orders bare BUILD or BUILD COMPLETE, raises a warning reading exactly "is in no structure to build in". A unit inside a structure raises none. BUILD <name>, BUILD <name> COMPLETE and BUILD HELP <unit> raise none from this check, whether or not the unit is inside a structure. Separately, a BUILD HELP naming one of our own units in the hex that has no BUILD order of its own raises "unit <n> is not building" against the helper; if the named unit has any BUILD order, or is not one of ours in this hex, none is raised. Each of the two checks has its own toggle in Settings -> Warnings -> Building, on by default, and each can be switched off without affecting the other or "Building what is built". The committed turn-71 template still produces no findings.

title: Order OCD leaves existing orders alone until you switch units and back
description:
Found by the navigator on 2026-08-18 while verifying ah-bn6.2 (origin/main 890bbf8). That bead passed - cases 1 to 6 of the verification all behaved as designed - and this is the follow-up filed alongside the pass.

## What the reader sees

With Order OCD on, opening a unit whose orders were written before the setting was turned on leaves them untouched. Selecting a different unit and then selecting the first one again tidies them. The navigator's words: "the orders are not updated when i select a unit, but if i then select another unit and back to the first again, it has been transformed to upper case."

So decision E3 - "orders already written are tidied when the unit is next opened" - does not happen on the unit the player actually opened. E1, never touching existing text, was explicitly rejected during planning because "a half-written turn stays mixed, which is what the OCD player minds most"; on the first unit of a session the shipped behaviour is E1.

## The cause, and the code already names it

packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx, in the editor-construction effect (the block that dispatches the tidied document, around line 311). Its own comment says:

    // A block written before the setting was on is tidied the first time its unit is opened with
    // the setting on (the navigator's E3). Not External: it is a real edit to the draft and must
    // be saved. Kept out of the history - the player did not type it. An empty vocabulary (the
    // call still in flight) makes this a no-op, and the block is tidied at the next open.

The last sentence is the defect, written down and accepted. The effect's dependency list is [unitId], and it reads latest.current.vocabulary at mount time. The vocabulary is fetched asynchronously from the core (orderVocabulary, published by ah-bn6.1), so on the first editor mount after a page load the set is still empty, uppercaseKeywords returns the document unchanged, and nothing re-runs when the vocabulary later arrives. Remounting the editor - which is what selecting away and back does - picks up the by-then-populated vocabulary.

This also means the miss is not limited to the very first unit in the strictest sense: any editor that mounts before the vocabulary resolves is affected. In practice that is the first unit opened after a load, which is exactly the one the player is looking at when they form their first impression of the setting.

## Shape of a fix

Make the tidy run when the vocabulary becomes available as well as when the unit changes - the vocabulary belongs in the dependencies, or a small effect of its own tidies the current document once the set is non-empty. Whatever shape is chosen must keep the three properties the original block was careful about: the edit is a real change to the draft and must be saved (not annotated External), it stays out of the undo history because the player did not type it, and it must not fight the caret if the player has already started typing in that block.

Worth deciding at planning: whether a document the player has already edited in this session should still be tidied when the vocabulary arrives late, or left alone as their own text.

## Acceptance

With Order OCD on and a unit whose orders are lower case, opening that unit as the first unit after a page load tidies its block. Everything ah-bn6.2 delivered still holds: quoted names and comments untouched, one Ctrl+Z undoing both the typed word and the uppercasing, the setting off by default, uppercasing on the space that ends a word.

## Out of scope

Everything else in ah-bn6.2, all verified passing. The vocabulary itself (ah-bn6.1). Uppercasing on import, which is deliberately not done.
design:
## Context

With **Order OCD** on, a unit's existing orders are supposed to be tidied the first time that unit
is opened with the setting on — decision **E3** of `ah-bn6.2`. On the first unit opened after a page
load they are not: selecting a second unit and coming back tidies them, which is what the navigator
saw while verifying `ah-bn6.2` (origin/main `890bbf8`).

The cause is in `packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx`. The editor-construction
`useLayoutEffect` has the dependency list `[unitId]` and reads `latest.current.vocabulary` at mount
time. The vocabulary is fetched asynchronously from the core (`client.orderVocabulary`, published by
`ah-bn6.1`, fetched by the effect at `AppShell.tsx:1316`), so on the first mount after a page load the set is
still empty, `uppercaseKeywords` returns the document unchanged, and **nothing re-runs when the
vocabulary later arrives**. The block's own comment already admits this: "An empty vocabulary (the
call still in flight) makes this a no-op, and the block is tidied at the next open."

The same dependency list hides a second face of the same defect, and the navigator asked for it in
scope here (Q5): `orderOcd` is not a dependency either, so **turning the setting on while a unit is
already open does nothing** until the player switches units.

When this lands, the tidy stops being a mount-time event and becomes something that runs whenever it
*can* run: the block on screen is tidied as soon as the word list is available, as soon as the
setting is turned on, and again when a ruleset switch brings a new catalogue.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/orderCase.ts` — the pure half (new export)

Everything decidable moves here, because **this repository has no jsdom** (see *Known traps*): a
React effect wrapped round CodeMirror cannot be unit tested at all, so anything left inside the
component is only ever pinned by the smoke suite.

Add, beside the existing `uppercaseKeywords`:

```ts
/** One keyword to shout, in whole-block offsets. `insert` is always the same length as the span. */
export interface CaseChange {
  readonly from: number;
  readonly to: number;
  readonly insert: string;
}

/**
 * Every keyword span of a whole block that is not already upper case, in block offsets.
 *
 * `protect`, when it is a number, is a block offset whose word is left alone — the caret, so a
 * word still being typed is not shouted at under the cursor. `null` protects nothing.
 */
export function keywordCaseChanges(
  text: string,
  vocabulary: Vocabulary,
  protect: number | null
): CaseChange[];
```

Build it from what is already there rather than from scratch: split on `"\n"` exactly as
`uppercaseKeywords` does, keep a running line-start offset, and per line use the existing
`bareWords(line)` and `isKeyword(word.text, vocabulary)`. A word is emitted when
`word.text.toUpperCase() !== word.text` (already-upper words are not changes) and when it is not
protected. **Protected means `protect !== null && protect >= from && protect <= to`, in block
offsets, inclusive at both ends** — inclusive because the caret sitting immediately after the last
character of `move` is exactly the "still typing it" case this rule exists for, and inclusive at
`from` so a caret at the head of the word counts too.

Then **reimplement `uppercaseKeywords` on top of it**, so there is one description of what a keyword
span is:

```ts
export function uppercaseKeywords(text: string, vocabulary: Vocabulary): string {
  let result = text;
  const changes = keywordCaseChanges(text, vocabulary, null);
  for (let i = changes.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
    const change = changes[i] as CaseChange;
    result = result.slice(0, change.from) + change.insert + result.slice(change.to);
  }
  return result;
}
```

Its existing tests in `packages/shared/src/orderCase.test.ts` must keep passing untouched — that is
the check that the refactor changed nothing. `uppercaseLine` stays exported and unchanged; nothing
else in the module moves.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx` — the wiring

**Delete** the tidy block at the end of the creation `useLayoutEffect` (currently around line 305,
the `if (latest.current.orderOcd) { ... }` after `view.current = created;`, together with its
four-line comment). Its work moves to the effect below, which also covers the mount case: effects
run after layout effects, so on mount `view.current` is already set.

**Add**, immediately after that layout effect and before the `externalRevision` effect:

```tsx
// The tidy E3 promises, run whenever it *can* run rather than only at mount. The vocabulary
// arrives from the core asynchronously, so the first editor created after a page load is built
// against an empty set and would otherwise never be tidied (ah-1znc). Keyed on the vocabulary and
// the setting as well as the unit, so the same effect catches the setting being turned on with a
// unit already open, and a ruleset switch bringing a new catalogue.
useEffect(() => {
  const editor = view.current;
  if (!editor || !orderOcd || vocabulary.size === 0) {
    return;
  }
  // The word the caret is inside is left as typed: while typing, this setting only shouts a word
  // as the space ends it, and a late tidy must not break that promise. Unfocused there is no
  // caret to protect - and selecting a unit row does not focus the editor, so that is the common
  // case, not the exotic one.
  const protect = editor.hasFocus ? editor.state.selection.main.head : null;
  const changes = keywordCaseChanges(editor.state.doc.toString(), vocabulary, protect);
  if (changes.length === 0) {
    return;
  }
  editor.dispatch({
    changes,
    // Every replacement is exactly as long as what it replaces, so every offset still means what
    // it meant. Restated anyway when there is a caret, because CodeMirror maps a position sitting
    // on a replacement boundary to the far side of it. Left untouched when unfocused: writing a
    // selection there would paint one on an editor nobody is in.
    ...(protect === null ? {} : { selection: editor.state.selection }),
    // Deliberately not External: this is a real edit to the draft, it must reach `onChange` and be
    // saved. Deliberately out of the history: the player did not type it, exactly as the tidy this
    // replaces was. And deliberately no `userEvent`, which is what history groups typing under.
    annotations: [Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)]
  });
}, [unitId, orderOcd, vocabulary]);
```

Import `keywordCaseChanges` alongside the existing
`import { buildVocabulary, keywordJustFinished, uppercaseKeywords } from "../orderCase";` — and
**drop `uppercaseKeywords` from that import**, since the block that used it is gone and
`--max-warnings=0` fails on an unused import.

Where state lives, and why the dependency list is the whole fix:

- `orderVocabulary` lives in `AppShell` (`AppShell.tsx:294`), fetched by the effect that calls
  `client.orderVocabulary(rulesetText)` at `AppShell.tsx:1316`, and passed down through
  `OrdersPanel.tsx:145`.
- `orderOcd` lives in the settings store (`settingsStore.ts:257`, default `false`) and is read in
  `OrdersPanel.tsx:96`.
- `vocabulary` is the `useMemo(() => buildVocabulary(orderVocabulary), [orderVocabulary])` already
  at `OrdersEditor.tsx:120`. Its identity moves only when the `orderVocabulary` array does, which
  is only when `setOrderVocabulary` runs — so it is a safe effect dependency and will not re-fire
  per render. **Use the props `orderOcd` and `vocabulary` directly in this effect, not
  `latest.current`**: the whole point is that the effect re-runs when they change, and reading them
  through the ref would freeze it at mount all over again.

Nothing changes in `OrdersPanel.tsx`, `AppShell.tsx` or `settingsStore.ts`.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test. Run `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test` for the first two and the
smoke command in *Validation* for the rest.

**1 — `keywordCaseChanges` exists and finds the spans.** RED: in
`packages/shared/src/orderCase.test.ts`, `describe("keywordCaseChanges")` with
`it("returns a span per keyword that is not already upper case")` —
`keywordCaseChanges("move n\nstudy combat", buildVocabulary(["MOVE", "N", "STUDY", "COMBAT"]), null)`
returns four changes, and asserts the second line's offsets are block offsets and not line offsets
(`STUDY` at `from: 7`). A second case, `it("returns nothing when the block is already upper case")`,
asserts `[]` for `"MOVE N"`. GREEN: implement it.

**2 — the caret's word is protected, and `uppercaseKeywords` is unchanged.** RED:
`it("leaves the word the caret is inside alone")` — for `"study combat\nmove"` with the caret at the
end of the block (offset 17, just after `move`), the returned changes cover `study` and `combat` and
not `move`; and `it("protects a caret at the head of a word")` for offset 0 of `"move n"`. GREEN:
add the `protect` test to the emit condition, then reimplement `uppercaseKeywords` on top of
`keywordCaseChanges` and confirm every pre-existing `uppercaseKeywords` and `uppercaseLine` test in
that file still passes untouched.

**3 — the reported bug.** RED: a new test in `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts` (see *The test
plan*) that writes lower-case orders, turns the setting on, reloads the page, opens that unit first,
and expects the block upper case. It fails against today's code. GREEN: delete the tidy from the
creation layout effect and add the new effect above.

**4 — the setting turned on with a unit already open.** A second smoke test — no reload, orders
written with the setting off, then Order OCD ticked while the unit is on screen, expecting the block
to tidy without a unit switch. **Expect it to pass the moment it is written**, because increment 3
already put `orderOcd` in the dependency list; that is the intended outcome, not a skipped RED, so
keep the test as the pin on that dependency and say so in the commit message. If it fails, the
dependency list of the new effect is not `[unitId, orderOcd, vocabulary]` — make it so.

**5 — nothing else moved.** No new test. Run the whole `orders-editor.spec.ts` file plus
`persistence.spec.ts` in both projects and confirm the `ah-bn6.2` walks — the as-you-type
uppercasing, the quoted name, the single Ctrl+Z — are still green.

## The test plan

**Unit — `packages/shared/src/orderCase.test.ts`** (vitest, `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test`).
Four new cases under `describe("keywordCaseChanges")`, exactly as named in increments 1 and 2:
`returns a span per keyword that is not already upper case`,
`returns nothing when the block is already upper case`,
`leaves the word the caret is inside alone`,
`protects a caret at the head of a word`. Every existing case in the file must still pass with no
edit — that is what pins the `uppercaseKeywords` refactor.

**Smoke — `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`** (Playwright, both `web` and `desktop-shell`
projects). Two new tests, written with the helpers already imported at the top of that file
(`clearGames`, `createGame`, `expectOrders`, `fillOrders`, `ordersInput`) and its local
`loadReport`, `selectUnit` and `enableOrderOcd`:

1. `"orders written before the setting was on are tidied on the first unit opened after a reload"`
   — `loadReport(page)`, which already ends by selecting `OWN_UNIT`, so **do not select it again**;
   `fillOrders(page, "move n\nstudy combat")`;
   wait for the write to land with
   `await expect(page.getByTestId("orders-status")).toContainText(/saved \d/u, { timeout: 20_000 })`
   (the idiom and the timeout are `persistence.spec.ts:229`'s); `enableOrderOcd(page)`;
   `await page.reload()`; then `selectHex(page, "1:7,53")` and `selectUnit(page, OWN_UNIT)` so this
   is the **first** editor mounted since the load; finally
   `await expectOrders(page, /^MOVE N\nSTUDY COMBAT/)`. `expectOrders` polls, so a tidy that arrives
   a few hundred milliseconds after the mount passes without a sleep — and against today's code it
   fails on the poll timeout, which is the RED.
2. `"turning Order OCD on tidies the unit already on screen"` — `loadReport(page)`;
   `fillOrders(page, "move n\nstudy combat")`; `enableOrderOcd(page)`; **no reload and no unit
   switch**; `await expectOrders(page, /^MOVE N\nSTUDY COMBAT/)`.

   Prove this test can fail before trusting it: with the fix in place, temporarily drop `orderOcd`
   from the new effect's dependency list and confirm test 2 goes red. If it stays green, opening the
   settings dialog is remounting the editor, so the test is passing on the remount rather than on
   the dependency. **Keep it anyway** — it still pins the player-visible behaviour — and say in the
   PR body that it is a weak pin for that reason. Do not chase a stronger one; there is no jsdom to
   build it with.

Both must run in both projects — the fix is in shared component code, and the desktop shell mounts
the same editor. Suites that must run: `pnpm run check:fast` (which covers the unit half) and the
smoke command in *Validation*.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-18 over two mockups, both drawn in the app's own theme
with all four cases side by side. **Option A was chosen**;
`docs/ui/order-ocd-late-vocabulary.html` (merged as PR #422) is the chosen mockup and records every
answer in its header.

**Q1 — when the word list arrives late and the player has already typed into that block, does the
tidy still run?** → **A, always tidy.** The block is tidied the moment the list lands, whatever has
happened meanwhile; it is the on-open tidy, late. *Rejected: B, standing aside once the player has
typed* — it leaves the block the player is actually looking at mixed for the rest of the session,
which is this bead's complaint only narrower, and makes the behaviour depend on whether they
happened to type inside the first half-second, which is neither visible nor predictable. The
navigator's reason for A is the one recorded against `ah-bn6.2`'s E1: "a half-written turn stays
mixed, which is what the OCD player minds most."

**Q2 — the word the caret is inside.** → **2-i, leave it alone.** While typing, a keyword shouts on
the space that ends it and never while it is still being written; the late tidy keeps that rule, so
nothing changes under the cursor. *Rejected: 2-ii, tidy it too* — the word under the cursor would
change while the player is still writing it.

**Q3 — undo.** → **The tidy is not in the history.** `Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)`, the same
as the tidy it replaces. Ctrl+Z undoes the player's last typing and the uppercasing stays.
*Rejected: one undoable step* — it would differ from the on-open tidy, so the same edit would be
undoable or not depending on how fast the fetch happened to be.

**Q4 — does anything announce it?** → **Nothing.** No status line, no toast, no marker. The player
asked for this by turning the setting on. *Rejected: a header notice tone* — noise for something
that was requested.

**Q5 — scope.** → **Fix both faces of the defect in this bead.** The effect is keyed on the unit,
the setting and the vocabulary, so turning Order OCD on with a unit already open tidies that block
immediately. *Rejected: fixing only the late word list and filing the other as a separate P4* —
same cause, same three lines, same test harness.

**Q6 — the editor is not focused when the list arrives** (the common case: selecting a unit row does
not focus the editor). → **Tidy everything.** No caret is showing, so there is no word to protect.
*Rejected: protecting the last internal caret position anyway* — it would leave one stray lower-case
word in an otherwise tidied block for no reason the player can see.

**Q7 — a ruleset switch mid-session**, which clears the vocabulary and refetches it. → **Tidy the
open block again against the new catalogue.** A word that is a keyword under the new ruleset and was
not under the old one shouts like any other; nothing is ever un-shouted, since an already-upper-case
word is never a change. *Rejected: tidying once per unit open* — needs extra state and leaves the
block stale against the ruleset on screen.

**Q8 — saving.** → **The tidy is a real edit and is saved**, so a clean block becomes dirty and
autosaves with no keystroke behind it, exactly as the on-open tidy already does. *Rejected: showing
it without saving until the player types* — what is on screen would not be what is stored, and a
reload would throw the tidy away, which is how this looked broken in the first place.

No strings are added or changed by this bead; there is nothing new for the player to read.

## Out of scope

- **Uppercasing on import.** Deliberately not done, and untouched here. The `externalRevision`
  effect splices imported text in without tidying it, and stays that way.
- **The vocabulary fetch itself** (`ah-bn6.1`, `client.orderVocabulary`). Its timing, its caching
  and its failure path are not this bead's; a fetch that never resolves still leaves the block
  untidied, silently, as today.
- **Tidying units other than the one on screen.** `E3` is "tidied when next opened", and one editor
  holds one unit; nothing here walks the faction.
- **Un-shouting.** A word already upper case is never lowered, under any ruleset.
- **Everything else `ah-bn6.2` delivered** — the as-you-type rule, quoted names, comments, the
  single Ctrl+Z, the setting's default — all verified passing and only regression-checked here.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts
```

The two smoke runs cover both the `web` and `desktop-shell` projects; CI runs them as separate jobs
and is what actually gates the merge. `check:fast` covers the `orderCase` unit tests, lint,
typecheck and the Rust gates.

Acceptance, checkable by running the app: with Order OCD on and a unit whose orders are lower case,
opening that unit **as the first unit after a page load** tidies its block, with no unit switch. And
with a unit already on screen and its orders lower case, ticking Order OCD in settings tidies that
block immediately. Everything `ah-bn6.2` delivered still holds: quoted names and comments untouched,
one Ctrl+Z undoing both the typed word and the uppercasing, the setting off by default, uppercasing
on the space that ends a word.

## Known traps

- **This repository has no jsdom.** There is no `@testing-library/react`, no DOM environment and no
  test anywhere that mounts CodeMirror — `OrdersEditor.tsx` has no unit test and cannot be given
  one. Every component test in `packages/shared` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` and asserts on markup
  (`OrdersImportPrompt.test.tsx` is the pattern), which cannot see an effect at all. That is why
  `keywordCaseChanges` is a pure export and why the regression pin is a smoke test. **Do not spend
  the bead adding jsdom.**
- **`data-commands-ready` is about the wrong list.** The attribute on `orders-input`
  (`OrdersEditor.tsx`, the returned `<div>`) reads `commands.length > 0` — the *completion* command
  list, fetched by a different effect (`setOrderCommands` at `AppShell.tsx:1299`, not
  `setOrderVocabulary` at `AppShell.tsx:1314`). It says nothing
  about `orderVocabulary` and must not be used to wait for it. `expectOrders`, which polls, is the
  right wait.
- **The vocabulary is cleared to `[]` before every refetch** (`AppShell.tsx:1314`, "Cleared first: the
  words are the open ruleset's"). So the effect sees `size === 0` on a ruleset switch and must
  no-op rather than "tidy against nothing" — the guard is not defensive padding, it fires in normal
  use.
- **Not `External`, or nothing is saved.** The update listener skips any transaction whose every
  annotation is `External`, so annotating this one would keep the tidy off `onChange` and out of the
  document — and the next reload would show lower case again, which is the shape of the bug being
  fixed.
- **No `userEvent: "input"` on the transaction.** That is what CodeMirror's history groups runs of
  typing under; the as-you-type handler already omits it deliberately, for the same reason, and its
  comment explains the cost.
- **Uppercasing never changes a length**, which is what makes the caret safe here and is worth not
  breaking: if a future change makes a `CaseChange` a different length from its span, the
  `selection: editor.state.selection` restatement becomes wrong rather than redundant.
- **The smoke test must wait for the save before reloading.** `page.reload()` before the autosave
  has landed proves nothing — the draft is simply not there. `persistence.spec.ts:229` is the idiom:
  `expect(page.getByTestId("orders-status")).toContainText(/saved \d/u, { timeout: 20_000 })`, and
  the long timeout is deliberate.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a Chromium-only assertion can
  pass while the native shell is broken. `ordersText` in `gameSetup.ts` reads `.cm-line`
  `textContent` through `evaluate`, which is not affected — but keep assertions on text through that
  helper and off geometry.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**, so a `test:pwa` run
  straight afterwards fails with timeouts that look like a broken worker. Not this bead's concern
  unless a PWA failure appears out of nowhere.

title: A planner gets a bead ranked before planning it
description:
Found by the navigator on 2026-08-17, watching Beast pick up ah-mjy (P4) minutes after Psylocke
filed it and before Xavier had triaged it.

## What happened

`plan-bead`'s candidate query is

    bd list --exclude-label planned --exclude-label planning --exclude-label human \
            --exclude-type epic --sort priority --json

and the skill says to take the highest-priority candidate. That treats **P4 as a rank** when the
whole point of P4 in this repository is that it means *unranked* - the skill says so itself, two
sections earlier, when it explains why triage comes first.

So when the backlog holds nothing but unranked beads, the rule "plan the highest-priority
candidate" resolves to "plan an unranked one", and the planner does, immediately.

## Why it is systematic rather than a slip

Three things line up:

- **Triage happens once per session at the start**, and thereafter only on the triaging planner's
  own wake-ups, which are ten minutes apart.
- **Only the first planner on the roster triages.** The second planner never asks for a ranking and
  has no instruction to wait for one.
- **A drained backlog makes the race certain.** With candidates queued, an unranked bead sits at the
  bottom of the sort and is never reached; with the queue empty - the state the fleet reaches
  whenever it builds faster than beads are filed - the unranked tail is the *only* thing to plan,
  and the second planner takes it within seconds of it being filed.

Observed: ah-mjy was filed by Psylocke as a verification follow-up, and Beast had labelled it
`planning` before Xavier's next wake-up came round.

## The cost being paid

Not the ordering - a P4 planned early only means it is built early. The cost is that **the
navigator is never asked**. Triage is the one point where they can say "close this", "this is
actually a P0", or "this belongs behind the other thing", and a bead that is planned before it is
ranked skips that decision entirely. It also spends a planning session, and the navigator's time in
its interview, on work whose place in the queue nobody has agreed.

It contradicts the skill's own standing rule, "Never set a priority the navigator did not choose" -
not in the letter, since no priority was set, but squarely in the spirit: planning order is what
priority is *for*, and taking an unranked bead decides it by default.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **What a planner does when every candidate is unranked.** Report "nothing rankable to plan, N
  beads waiting on triage" and sleep, which puts the pressure on triage where it belongs; or plan
  it anyway and say so; or something between.
- **Whether the second planner may ask.** Both planners are interactive sessions with the navigator
  sitting there. The cheapest fix may simply be that any planner meeting an unranked candidate asks
  for that one bead's priority before taking it - one question, answered in seconds - rather than
  waiting for the other session's triage cycle. The reason triage is one planner's job is to stop
  the navigator being walked through the whole backlog twice; asking about a single new bead is not
  that.
- **Whether the triaging planner should triage on every wake-up** rather than once per session.
  The skill already says only beads arrived since the last pass need asking about, so this may be a
  wording fix rather than a behaviour change.

## Where the fix goes

`.claude/skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`, in *Choosing what to plan* and *Then: triage the P4 backlog*.
Possibly also the candidate query itself, if the answer is that P4 is excluded from it outright.
Agent instructions only - no application code.

## Acceptance

A planner that finds only unranked candidates does not silently plan one: it either gets a ranking
from the navigator first, or reports the backlog as untriaged and sleeps. Two planners still do not
walk the navigator through the same backlog twice. The behaviour is written into `plan-bead` where
the candidate is chosen, not only in the triage section.

## Context

Found by the navigator on 2026-08-17, watching Beast pick up `ah-mjy` (P4) minutes after Psylocke
filed it and before Xavier had triaged it. **Xavier did the same thing twice the same day**
(`ah-6qp`, `ah-3ox`), so this is systematic and not one session's slip.

`plan-bead`'s candidate query sorts by priority and the skill says to take the highest-priority
candidate. That treats **P4 as a rank**, when the whole point of P4 in this repository is that it
means *unranked* — the skill says so itself, two sections earlier, when it explains why triage comes
first. So when the backlog holds nothing but unranked beads, "plan the highest-priority candidate"
resolves to "plan an unranked one", and the planner does, immediately.

Three things line it up:

- **Triage happens once per session, at the start** (`SKILL.md:189`), and thereafter only on the
  triaging planner's own wake-ups.
- **Only the first planner on the roster triages**, so the second planner never asks for a ranking at
  all and has no instruction to wait for one.
- **The candidate query does not distinguish unranked from lowest-ranked**, so nothing in the moment
  of choosing says "this has never been weighed".

No rule is broken in the letter — no priority is set by the planner — but squarely in the spirit:
planning order is what priority is *for*, and taking an unranked bead decides it by default.

All of the work is in the **`.claude/cerebro` submodule** (`rmstdope/cerebro`), in
`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`. Agent instructions only; no application code, no script, no elisp.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

The navigator settled all four questions the bead raises (2026-08-17). The fix is three edits, and it
is deliberately **not** a change to the candidate query: an unranked bead stays a candidate, and what
changes is that the planner gets it ranked before taking it.

### 1. `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` — *Choosing what to plan*, after "Highest priority first" (line 482)

The rule, where the candidate is actually chosen:

> **A P4 candidate is unranked, not lowest-ranked — ask before you take it.** P4 means nobody has
> weighed this bead yet, so "highest priority first" cannot order it against anything; taking it
> decides the navigator's ordering by default, which is the one thing triage exists to prevent
> (ah-2g7). When the candidate you are about to take is P4, ask for that one bead's priority first —
> the question tool, one bead, your recommendation and a reason, exactly as the triage pass does it —
> then apply the answer and plan it at the rank you were given.
>
> ```bash
> bd update <id> --priority=<n>
> bd dolt push
> ```
>
> **This is not triage** and it is not the triaging planner's alone: either planner asks, about the
> one bead in front of it. The reason triage belongs to one session is to stop the navigator being
> walked through the whole backlog twice; asking about a single bead you are about to spend an hour
> on is not that.
>
> **If the ask goes unanswered, plan it anyway** — an idle fleet is the more expensive error — and
> **lead your next report with it**: name every bead you planned unranked, so the navigator can
> correct the order at a glance. Do not park it with `human`: if it was your only candidate, parking
> it empties the queue outright.

### 2. `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` — *Then: triage the P4 backlog*, line 189

```
Triage runs **once per session, at the start**. On later wake-ups, only beads that have arrived at P4
since the last pass need asking about — a bead the navigator already ranked is settled, and a bead
they declined to rank is not worth asking about twice.
```

becomes:

> Triage runs **at the start of the session and again on every wake-up** — new arrivals only. A bead
> the navigator already ranked is settled, and one they declined to rank is not worth asking about
> twice, so most wake-ups have nothing to ask and cost nothing. Ten minutes is then the longest a
> newly filed bead waits for a ranking, which is what keeps the buffer from filling with work nobody
> has weighed (ah-2g7).

The old wording is not wrong so much as read as a prohibition — "once per session" sounds like *do
not do this again* — and that reading is half of how this bug survives.

### 3. `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` — the "only the first planner triages" paragraph

One sentence, so the second planner is not left inferring it:

> **The second planner still asks about a single bead it is about to plan.** Skipping triage means
> not walking the backlog; it does not mean planning work the navigator has never ranked. See
> *Choosing what to plan*.

### Nothing else

- **The candidate query is unchanged.** Excluding P4 outright was considered and is not what the
  navigator chose: an unranked bead is still work, and the answer is to rank it, not to hide it.
- **No change to the buffer, the P0 pre-emption, or the `planning` label.**
- **`agents/planner.md` is not edited.** It points at the skill for all of this, and two copies of a
  rule is what `ah-3ox` was about.

## Increments

One. There is no test harness for `skills/*/SKILL.md`, and the cerebro repo's CI covers elisp and
`tests/*.sh`.

**What stands in for a test** is the read-through in *Validation*, and the PR body should say which
three sections changed and quote the new rule — the same discipline `ah-cg1`, `ah-60w` and `ah-3ox`
used for the same kind of change.

## The test plan

No automated test.

| Check | How | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| The rule is where the decision is | Read *Choosing what to plan* start to finish | A planner choosing a candidate meets the unranked rule in the same breath as "highest priority first", not three sections away |
| Both planners are covered | Read the "only the first planner triages" paragraph | It says plainly that skipping triage does not mean planning unranked work |
| The cadence reads as an instruction, not a prohibition | Read line 189's replacement | "at the start and again on every wake-up" cannot be read as "once, ever" |
| Nothing else moved | `git diff --stat` | One file, three hunks |

## User-facing decisions

Fleet tooling — nothing a player sees — but it changes how both planners behave and how often the
navigator is asked, so they settled it (2026-08-17):

1. **A planner meeting an unranked candidate asks for that one bead's priority, then plans it at the
   rank it is given.** *Rejected: reporting "nothing rankable to plan" and sleeping* — it puts the
   pressure on triage where it belongs and never plans against an order the navigator did not set,
   and it idles the implementers whenever they are away. *Rejected: planning it anyway and saying so
   loudly* — the fleet never starves, but it still decides the ordering by default, which is the
   defect.
2. **If the ask goes unanswered, plan it and lead the next report with it.** Three idle implementers
   is the expensive error; an unranked bead planned in the wrong order costs a re-rank. *Rejected:
   leaving it and sleeping* (the fleet stops for as long as the navigator is away); *rejected: parking
   it with `human`* (there may be no next candidate, and parking empties the queue).
3. **Either planner may ask about a single bead.** *Rejected: only the first planner asks* — one voice
   for priorities, at the cost of the second planner idling while rankable work sits there.
4. **The triaging planner sweeps for new arrivals on every wake-up**, not once per session.
   *Rejected: keeping it once per session* — fewer interruptions, and a bead filed after the session
   started waits for the next planner session, which on 2026-08-17 would have been hours.

## Out of scope

- **Excluding P4 from the candidate query.** Considered, not chosen.
- **The buffer's size, the P0 rule, the `planning` label, and the split rules.**
- **`ah-mjy`, `ah-6qp` and `ah-3ox`**, the beads that exposed this. All three are planned; re-rank
  them if their order is wrong, which is the point of the report line this bead adds.
- **Whether Bishop/Forge, Psylocke and Moira should file at something other than P4.** They should
  not — P4-on-create is the rule that makes triage meaningful, and this bead is about what the planner
  does with it.

## Validation

```bash
cd .claude/cerebro
git diff --stat            # one file, three hunks
```

Then the check only a person can make, and it is the whole of the bead: read *Choosing what to plan*
as a planner who has just run the candidate query and found one P4 bead. The instruction to ask must
be impossible to miss at that moment — if it reads as an aside, it will be skipped exactly as the
current wording is.

## Known traps

- **This bead lives in another git repository.** Branch, commit and PR **inside the submodule**, then
  a second small PR in `atlantis-hud` bumps the pointer (`chore(ah-2g7): bump cerebro to …`,
  precedent `d014de2`).
- **The instructions are the runtime.** There is no code to make this true — a planner does what the
  skill says. Vagueness here is the defect, and the rule has to survive being read in a hurry by a
  session that has just found its only candidate.
- **Do not turn the single-bead ask into a second triage pass.** One bead, the one being taken. A
  planner that starts walking the backlog is the duplication the one-triager rule exists to stop, and
  the navigator answering the same questions in two windows is exactly what it costs.
- **`plan-bead/SKILL.md` is edited by several beads at once** — `ah-bqi`, `ah-cg1` and `ah-3ox` all
  touched this repository within a day. Rebase before opening the PR.
- **Keep the P0 rule above this one.** An unplanned P0 is planned immediately and is never unranked by
  definition, so nothing here applies to it; a reader must not come away thinking a P0 waits for an
  ask.

title: A bead offered for verification and never answered is offered again
description:
Found by the navigator on 2026-08-17, who saw ah-wxk.2 and ah-164.1 listed as merged-and-unverified in the fleet view while Psylocke's own sweep reported nothing to do. Both had sat at verification:pending since 2026-08-16, invisible to the verifier for a day.

## The defect

verifier.md's work-list query (the 'The work list' section) selects a closed bead only when it carries NO verification:* label at all, or carries verification:failed:

    select(([.labels[]? | select(startswith("verification:"))] | length == 0)
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed")))

verification:pending is therefore excluded by construction. That is deliberate within one session - 'pending waits, it does not escalate', and it is what stops the same bead being re-offered every five minutes - but pending is written to the bead database, not to session memory, so it outlives the session that wrote it. A verifier session that sets pending and then ends (the navigator says later, the session is restarted, the machine sleeps) leaves the bead in a state no future sweep can see. The bead is never verified and never marked not-needed; it simply stops existing as far as the role is concerned.

Two beads reached that state within one day of the role existing, so this is the normal outcome of an ordinary interruption rather than a rare race.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

Simply adding pending to the query makes every pass re-offer every pending bead, which is the churn the exclusion exists to prevent. The distinction that matters is *whose* pending it is: one this session set is waiting on an answer, one an earlier session set is abandoned.

## Sketch of a fix, for the planner to settle with the navigator

Options seen from here, none chosen:

- Have the sweep pick up a pending bead whose pending predates the current session's start, and treat it as an ordinary candidate. Needs the session start time, which the session has, and the label's write time, which bd records on the event bead the set-state wrote.
- Have the verifier clear pending back to unlabelled when a pass ends with the bead unresolved, so the next session sees an ordinary candidate. Simplest, and loses the information that it was already offered once.
- Give the state a distinct name for 'offered and not answered' vs 'in flight now'.

Whichever is chosen, verifier.md's 'The work list' section and its 'Asking whether they are ready' section both need updating, since the second is where pending is written and where the 're-offered at most once per pass' rule lives.

## Acceptance

A bead set verification:pending by a verifier session that then ends is picked up by the next session's sweep. A bead set pending by the session currently running is still not re-offered within that session more than once per pass. verifier.md documents whichever rule is chosen.

## Out of scope

ah-wxk.2 and ah-164.1 themselves, both resolved as verification:not-needed on 2026-08-17 with the navigator's agreement.
design:
## Context

Found by the navigator on 2026-08-17, who saw `ah-wxk.2` and `ah-164.1` listed as merged-and-unverified
in the fleet view while Psylocke's own sweep reported nothing to do. Both had sat at
`verification:pending` since 2026-08-16 — **invisible to the verifier for a day**.

`verifier.md`'s work list asks for closed work beads carrying **no** `verification:*` label or
`verification:failed`. `verification:pending` is therefore excluded by construction. That is right
*within* one session — "pending waits, it does not escalate", and it is what stops a bead being
re-offered every five minutes — but **pending is written to the bead database, not to session
memory, so it outlives the session that wrote it**. A verifier that offers a bead, hears "later", and
then ends (the machine sleeps, the session is restarted) leaves the bead in a state no future sweep
can see. It is never verified and never marked not-needed; it stops existing as far as the role is
concerned.

Two beads reached that state within one day of the role existing, so this is the normal outcome of an
ordinary interruption rather than a rare race.

**The obvious fix is wrong**: simply including pending in the query re-offers every pending bead on
every pass, which is the churn the exclusion exists to prevent. The distinction that matters is
*whose* pending it is — one this session set is waiting on an answer, one an earlier session set is
abandoned.

All of the work is in the **`.claude/cerebro` submodule** (`rmstdope/cerebro`), in `agents/verifier.md`.
See *Known traps*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

The navigator chose (2026-08-17): **the query stops excluding pending, and the running session skips
what it has already offered — because it is the session that offered it, and it remembers.**

### `agents/verifier.md` — "The work list"

The `jq` filter (in the section quoted below, on top of `work-beads` since ah-cg1) gains
`verification:pending` alongside the two states it already accepts:

```bash
.claude/cerebro/scripts/work-beads | jq -r '.[]
  | select(([.labels[]? | select(startswith("verification:"))] | length == 0)
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed"))
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:pending")))
  | .id'
```

and gains the paragraph that makes it safe — written as a rule about *this* session, since that is
where the memory lives:

> **`verification:pending` is in the list, and this pass's own offers are what you leave out.**
> Pending means "offered to the navigator and not yet answered". Within a pass you know which of
> those you offered, because you offered them — skip those, and offer each of them at most once per
> pass, exactly as before. What you must **not** do is trust the label to mean it: pending is written
> to the bead database and outlives the session that wrote it, so a bead a previous session offered
> and never heard back about is an ordinary candidate again and must be picked up (ah-60w). Two beads
> sat unverifiable for a day because the query excluded pending outright.

### `agents/verifier.md` — "Asking whether they are ready"

The sentence *"the bead simply stays `verification:pending` (set it the moment you select a candidate)
and is **re-offered at most once per pass**"* stays true and stays as it is. One clause is added after
it, so the two sections cannot drift:

> A later session will see that pending bead in its work list and offer it again — which is what
> should happen, and is not the churn this rule prevents: that rule is about one pass, and a session
> that has ended is asking nobody anything.

`bd set-state <id> verification=pending` and the `bd dolt push` beside it are unchanged.

### Nothing else

- **`scripts/work-beads` is untouched.** It answers "which closed beads are real work"; which of that
  work still wants a verdict is the caller's `jq`, and the header says so.
- **No new label, no new state name, no timestamp read.** All three were considered and rejected —
  see *User-facing decisions*.
- **`agents/orchestrator.md`'s merged-but-unverified query** already counts a pending bead as
  unverified (it excludes only `passed` and `not-needed`), which is exactly why the fleet view showed
  these two and Psylocke did not. It is right and stays.
- **`emacs/cerebro.el`** likewise: its Verified bucket keys on `cerebro-verification-settled`
  (`passed` / `not-needed`), so a pending bead already shows as merged-unverified. That agreement is
  what surfaced the bug, and it needs no change.

## Increments

One — this is a documentation change to an agent's own instructions, and the agent is the runtime.

RED: none available; `agents/*.md` has no test harness and the cerebro repo's suites cover elisp and
scripts. GREEN: the two edits above.

**What stands in for a test** is the check in *Validation*: run the corrected query against the live
backlog and confirm it returns the pending beads that the current query hides. Paste both outputs into
the PR body — that comparison is the evidence, and it is the same discipline ah-cg1's plan used for
the same kind of change.

## The test plan

No automated test. The cerebro repo's CI runs `emacs --batch … ert` and every `tests/*.sh`, and this
bead adds neither elisp nor a script.

| Check | How | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| The pending beads are visible again | Run the new `jq` against the live backlog and diff it against the old one | The two lists differ by exactly the beads carrying `verification:pending` |
| Nothing else changed | The same comparison | No bead carrying `passed` or `not-needed` appears in either |
| Both sections agree | Read them | "The work list" and "Asking whether they are ready" state the same rule from their two ends, and neither claims pending is excluded |

## User-facing decisions

Fleet tooling, so nothing a player sees — but it changes how often the navigator is asked, so they
chose it (2026-08-17):

> **The session remembers what it offered.** The query stops excluding pending; the running session
> skips the beads it has already offered in this pass. A pending bead from an ended session is an
> ordinary candidate again, with no timestamps and no new label, and "later" still means later for as
> long as that session lives.

*Rejected: clearing pending when a pass ends unresolved* — simplest on paper, but a session killed
mid-pass never runs the clearing step and the bead strands exactly as it does today, which is the
failure being fixed. *Rejected: comparing the label's write time to the session's start* — precise and
it survives a killed session, but it depends on reading a timestamp off bd's own audit event, which
is a fiddly thing for an agent's instructions to rest on. *Rejected: a second state name for "offered,
not answered"* — clearest to read on the bead, at the cost of a new state every reader of
verification labels has to learn (`orchestrator.md`, `user-feedback.md`, `cerebro.el`).

## Out of scope

- **`ah-wxk.2` and `ah-164.1`**, both already resolved as `verification:not-needed` on 2026-08-17 with
  the navigator's agreement.
- **The verdicts themselves** — passed, follow-up, failed — and everything about how a verification is
  prepared or run.
- **`work-beads`**, and every other reader of closed beads.
- **Making `pending` visible in the fleet view as its own bucket.** It already shows as
  merged-unverified, which is true.

## Validation

From the submodule, against the live backlog:

```bash
cd .claude/cerebro
# what the sweep sees today
.claude/cerebro/scripts/work-beads | jq -r '.[]
  | select(([.labels[]? | select(startswith("verification:"))] | length == 0)
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed"))) | .id' | sort > /tmp/before
# what it sees after
.claude/cerebro/scripts/work-beads | jq -r '.[]
  | select(([.labels[]? | select(startswith("verification:"))] | length == 0)
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed"))
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:pending"))) | .id' | sort > /tmp/after
comm -13 /tmp/before /tmp/after      # exactly the pending beads, and nothing else
```

Both files and that diff belong in the PR body. Then the check only a person can make: read the two
edited sections end to end and satisfy yourself that a verifier following them would offer a bead an
earlier session abandoned, and would not offer the same bead twice in one pass.

## Known traps

- **This bead lives in another git repository.** `.claude/cerebro` is a submodule of
  `rmstdope/cerebro`: branch, commit and open the PR **inside the submodule**, with the bead id in the
  subject, and let its own CI run. Then a second small PR in `atlantis-hud` bumps the pointer —
  `chore(ah-60w): bump cerebro to …`, precedent `d014de2` (#380).
- **The instructions *are* the runtime.** There is no code to make this true — a verifier session does
  what `verifier.md` says. So the wording carries the whole fix, and vagueness here is a defect, not a
  style problem. State the rule twice, from both sections, deliberately.
- **Do not make the session's memory a file.** It is one pass's list of offers, held by the session
  that made them; writing it to disk recreates the very problem — state that outlives the session that
  understands it.
- **`work-beads` already excludes epics and bd's own `event` beads** (ah-cg1). Do not re-add those
  guards to the `jq`; the only clause that changes is the label filter.
- **A `verification:failed` bead is already in the list and stays there.** Adding pending must not
  disturb that: a bead reopened by a failed verdict closes again still carrying `failed`, and being a
  candidate a second time is what that state is for.

title: Problems are grouped into a card per hex, with a mark for warning or error
description:
The problems list mixes two kinds of line — the hex a problem is in, and the problem itself — and
reads as one undifferentiated run. A player scanning it cannot tell at a glance which lines are
locations and which are things wrong, so the list is slower to use than the information in it
deserves.

**The request:** redesign the list so the two are obviously different.

**It appears twice and the design must serve both.** The header dropdown (`problemsPanel`, with its
`problemCount`) lists the whole turn's problems across hexes; `RegionPanel` lists one region's, via
the same `Problems` component and the same `OrderDiagnostic` shape. One design applied in both places
— which is why this is one bead rather than two, and why the region list is the constraint: it is
narrow, and already inside a panel with its own heading, so a hex label there may be redundant where
in the dropdown it is essential.

## What the list has to work with

`OrderDiagnostic` carries `code`, `message`, `severity` (`warning` or `error`), `regionId`, `unitId`
and a line/column span. So the design can lean on more than indentation: severity distinguishes a
malformed order from an advisory one, `unitId` says whose problem it is, and a diagnostic with a line
can be clicked into the editor while one belonging to a hex cannot.

Note some diagnostics belong to a hex and to no unit or line at all — "nobody is guarding this hex" is
nobody's line, as the model's own comment says. Those are the ones most likely to be mistaken for a
