title: Importing your own report sets which faction the game reopens as
description:
Third child of ah-do8. Wires the remembered faction to the flows that decide it.

The remembered faction changes only when the player says so at an import: the first report loaded into a game, 'Switch faction' on a foreign report, and the batch import's 'which faction is yours' answer. A merge never changes it, and a report stored for history (an older turn) never changes it.

Depends on ah-do8.1 for the stored field and ah-do8.2 for the rule that reads it.
design:
## Context

Third and last child of the epic ah-do8. **Read the epic's `design` field first** — it carries the
navigator's decision in their own words, with the alternatives that were rejected.

ah-do8.1 gave a game a remembered faction (`GameMetadata.activeFactionId`) and a `setActiveFaction`
path on both platforms. ah-do8.2 made reopening use it: the remembered faction's highest-numbered
turn, falling back to the game's highest turn when that faction holds none. Nothing yet sets it from
the import flows, so today every game still reopens through the fallback and settles on whatever the
adopt in `restoreLatestTurn` happened to find.

This bead closes it: **the faction the player chose becomes the faction the game remembers**, and the
navigator's rule — *"that should only change if the user say so during an import"* — is finally
literally true.

The three moments the player says so all end in the same place, which is what makes this small:

| The player does | The path |
|---|---|
| Imports the first report into a new game | `routeReport` → `{ kind: "load" }` → `applyReport` → `loadTurn` |
| Presses **Switch faction** on somebody else's report | the foreign-report prompt → `applyReport` → `loadTurn` |
| Answers "which faction is yours" in a batch | `walkBatch` → `applyReport(…, committed)` → `loadTurn` |

And the two moments the player does **not**:

| The player does | The path | Why it must not move |
|---|---|---|
| Presses **Merge** on an ally's report | `AppShell.mergeReport` (line 1011) — never reaches `loadTurn` | "Merge adds everywhere they went to your map and leaves you playing *you*" (`foreignReport.ts`) |
| Opens an older report | `routeReport` → `{ kind: "storeOnly" }` → `storeOlderTurn` (`reportLoad.ts:186`) | It is filed for history and never becomes the working turn (gh-208) |

So there is exactly one place to write it: `loadTurn`. Putting it there rather than in `AppShell`
means all three player paths are covered by one edit, and it is a plain function
`reportLoad.test.ts` can test without a DOM.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts`

`LoadedTurn` (line 59) gains one field:

```ts
  /**
   * The game's manifest, rewritten because this report changed which faction the game remembers,
   * or `null` when it did not. The shell puts it back into its `game` state so the in-memory
   * manifest does not lag the file.
   */
  manifest: GameManifest | null;
```

`loadTurn` (line 85) writes it after the memory and the document have been read — last, because it is
the least important of the three and must not stand between a failure and the report reaching the
screen:

```ts
  // The faction the player chose is the faction the game remembers (ah-do8). Only the paths that
  // make a report the working turn reach here - a merge and an older report stored for history
  // both stop short of it - which is exactly the navigator's rule: it changes only when the player
  // says so at an import.
  //
  // A failure is a warning, like `rememberTurn`'s and `documentFor`'s: the report in front of the
  // player parsed perfectly well, and refusing to show it over a manifest that would not write
  // would be a worse answer than reopening on the wrong faction once.
  let manifest: GameManifest | null = null;
  let rememberWarning: string | null = null;
  const factionId = report.header.factionId;
  if (game && factionId && factionId !== game.manifest.metadata.activeFactionId) {
    try {
      manifest = await client.setActiveFaction(game.manifest.metadata.gameId, factionId);
    } catch (error: unknown) {
      rememberWarning = `which faction this game reopens as could not be remembered: ${detail(error)}`;
    }
  }
```

and the existing `const message = memory.warning ?? chosen.warning;` becomes
`memory.warning ?? chosen.warning ?? rememberWarning` — last in the chain, since the two existing
warnings are about the turn the player is looking at and this one is about the next time they open
the game.

`detail(error)` is `gameMemory.ts:40`'s, and it is **not exported** — it is a module-private
`error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)`. Write the same one-liner privately in
`reportLoad.ts` rather than exporting the other one: two three-line copies of that expression already
exist in this package, and un-privatising a helper across module boundaries to save one of them is a
worse trade than the duplication. If you disagree strongly enough to export it, that is a refactoring
for Forge to file, not a change to slip into this bead.

`report.header.factionId` is `string | null`. It cannot be null on this path — `decideReportLoad`
(`reportLoadDecision.ts:78`) rejects a report naming no faction before routing reaches `load` — but
the guard above costs one `&&` and means this function does not depend on that being true for ever.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

`applyLoadedTurn` (line 844) puts the rewritten manifest back into the `game` state
(`const [game, setGame] = useState<OpenedGame | null>(null)`, line 301 — `changeRuleset` and
`renameGame` already call `setGame` directly, per the comment at line 305):

```ts
      // The manifest was rewritten because this report changed which faction the game remembers.
      // Putting it back keeps the in-memory copy level with the file, so the next report loaded in
      // this session can tell whether anything actually changed.
      if (loaded.manifest) {
        setGame((current) => (current ? { ...current, manifest: loaded.manifest } : current));
      }
```

`setGame` is a `useState` setter and stable, so `applyLoadedTurn`'s dependency list (line 875) does
not change.

### Nothing else

`batchImport.ts` needs no edit: the batch's own commits are `walkBatch`'s, and the viewer's turn
reaches the screen through `applyReport` like any other. `storeOlderTurn`, `mergeReport` and
`reportLoadDecision.ts` are all deliberately untouched — see the second table above.

## Increments

1. **The write, and when it must not happen.** RED: the first four tests in the table below, in
   `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.test.ts`. GREEN: the `loadTurn` change and the new `LoadedTurn`
   field.
2. **The shell keeps its manifest level.** RED: `storeOlderTurn` and the "no game" cases (the last two
   rows) — they pin that nothing writes on the paths that must not. GREEN: nothing new if increment 1
   is right; then wire `applyLoadedTurn`, which is a typecheck-driven edit (`LoadedTurn.manifest` is
   not optional).

## The test plan

All in `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.test.ts` unless said otherwise; that file already builds a
`CoreClient` stub, so extend it with `setActiveFaction` rather than starting a new fixture.

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `remembers the faction whose report became the working turn` | `setActiveFaction` called once with the game id and the report's faction; the returned manifest comes back as `LoadedTurn.manifest` |
| `does not rewrite the remembered faction when it is already this one` | Manifest already carrying `activeFactionId: "95"`, report of 95 → not called, `manifest` is `null` |
| `remembers the faction on the batch path too, where the turn was already committed` | Same as the first, with `committed` supplied — the commit is skipped, the remembering is not |
| `a manifest that will not write becomes a warning, not a failed load` | `setActiveFaction` rejects → `LoadedTurn` still carries the parsed report, and `status` is the warning; the existing memory/draft warnings still win over it |
| `remembers nothing when there is no open game` | `game === null` → not called |
| `an older report stored for history does not change which faction the game remembers` | `storeOlderTurn` (line 186) → `setActiveFaction` not called |

Not unit-testable, and named here so nobody goes looking: **merging** never reaches `loadTurn`
(`AppShell.mergeReport`, line 1011), and the Playwright test `merging leaves the orders and the
selection where they were` (`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:771`) is what pins that the workspace stays
on the viewer's faction across a merge.

Suites: `pnpm -r run test`. No Rust in this bead. `pnpm run test:smoke` is not required, but CI runs
it and the merge test above is the one to read if it goes red.

## User-facing decisions

The rule is the navigator's, settled 2026-08-17 and recorded in full — with the rejected
alternatives — in the epic ah-do8's `design` field. The line this bead implements:

> "we should always have an 'active faction' and that should only change if the user say so during an
> import"

Nothing on screen changes: no control, no wording, no message. The player sees the effect only the
next time they open the game. No mockup, and nothing to ask.

**Do not** add a confirmation, a status line or a toast saying the faction was remembered. The player
already answered a question to get here — "Switch faction", or "which faction is yours" — and telling
them again about the consequence of their own answer was not asked for.

## Out of scope

- **The reopen rule itself** — ah-do8.2, which this depends on. Do not touch `reopen.rs`.
- **`restoreLatestTurn`'s adopt** (added by ah-do8.2). It writes the same field on the reopen path and
  leaves the in-memory manifest stale on purpose; the first report loaded in that session then writes
  the same value once more, which is one redundant manifest write and no defect. Do not add a second
  refresh path to tidy it.
- **Making a merge or an older report change the remembered faction.** Both are explicitly excluded.
- **Offering the player a way to change it directly** — a faction picker in the This game panel, say.
  A reasonable idea, a separate bead, and the navigator's to ask for.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

The human check, which is the epic's own and Psylocke's to run: in a game holding two factions, press
**Switch faction** on the other faction's report, reload — the game comes back on the faction you
switched to. Then import an *older* report of the first faction and reload again — it comes back on
the faction you switched to, on its highest turn, not on the report you just imported.

## Known traps

- **`loadTurn` is the only place this may be written.** Putting it in `AppShell` next to the
  foreign-report prompt would cover the switch and miss the first import and the batch — the three
  paths were deliberately funnelled through `applyReport` (see its doc comment at line 878: "a report
  the player reached by pressing 'Switch faction' must land exactly as one they simply opened"), and
  this bead is spending that.
- **Write it last inside `loadTurn`.** The function's contract is that nothing reaches the screen
  until it resolves; an early `await` on a manifest write adds a failure mode between the commit and
  the document read for no benefit.
- **`committed` means the batch already committed the turn — it does not mean the faction is already
  remembered.** Do not put the new write inside the `committed ?? …` branch.
- **`LoadedTurn.manifest` is required, not optional.** Making it optional would let the
  `applyLoadedTurn` edit be forgotten with nothing to catch it; as written, the typecheck names every
  construction site.
- **`@atlantis/shared` runs vitest in Node** — there is no DOM, so `AppShell` has no unit test. The
  `applyLoadedTurn` edit is proved by the typecheck and by the smoke suite, and that is the honest
  extent of it.

title: Reopening a game never goes back to an older turn
description:
Second child of ah-do8, and the one that fixes the reported defect.

Reopening ranks turns by which was touched most recently, so importing turn 23 into a game that already holds turn 25 reopens on 23 - you can go back in time by importing. The rule becomes: the remembered faction's highest-numbered imported turn; when that faction holds none (every game upgraded from today's version), the highest-numbered turn in the game whichever faction holds it, and the shell adopts that faction as the remembered one.

Depends on ah-do8.1 for the stored field. Valuable on its own even before ah-do8.3 sets it: with no remembered faction the fallback alone already fixes the reported case.
design:
## Context

Second child of the epic ah-do8, and the one that fixes the reported defect. **Read the epic's
`design` field first** — it carries the navigator's decision, quoted, with the four alternatives that
were rejected. Do not re-open any of it.

Today a game reopens on the turn *touched* most recently, with the turn number only a tiebreak
(`crates/core/src/reopen.rs:42`). Import turn 25 into a fresh game and then import turn 23, and the
game reopens on 23 — you can go back in time by importing. Reported by the navigator at ah-8m0.3's
verification, 2026-08-17. Not a regression: ah-8m0.3 moved that rule into the core unchanged from the
SQL that predates it.

After this bead the rule is: **the remembered faction's highest-numbered imported turn; and when that
faction holds none, the highest-numbered turn in the game, whichever faction holds it.** The stamps
stop deciding anything, so `TurnTouch`, the draft input and the second SQL query all go.

**ah-do8.1 is a blocker and must be built first.** It adds `GameMetadata.activeFactionId` and
`setActiveFaction` across both platforms; this bead reads that field and never writes it, except for
the one adopt described below. Nothing sets it from the import flows until ah-do8.3, so when this bead
lands *every* reopen takes the fallback path on its first run and adopts from it — which is exactly
the reported case, and fixes it on its own.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` — the rule

`TurnTouch` is **deleted**, and with it the `drafts` parameter, the `updated_at` field, the
`HashMap` of edited drafts and the string comparison of ISO stamps. The whole public surface becomes:

```rust
/// One turn a game holds, and the turn it reopens on: the same three-word shape either way.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct TurnRef {
    pub faction_id: String,
    pub turn_number: u32,
}

/// The turn a game reopens on, or `None` when it holds no imported turns.
///
/// The remembered faction's highest-numbered turn. When that faction holds none - a game whose
/// manifest predates `activeFactionId`, or one whose only turn of that faction was removed - the
/// highest-numbered turn in the game, whichever faction holds it; a game that holds a turn always
/// reopens on a turn. Ties on the turn number in that fallback go to the lower `faction_id` as
/// text, which only ever decides between two factions that both hold the game's highest turn and
/// neither of which is remembered.
///
/// Nothing here reads a timestamp. Which faction is the player's is remembered
/// (`GameMetadata::active_faction_id`, ah-do8.1) rather than inferred from what was touched last,
/// which is what let an older report imported later take the game back in time.
#[must_use]
pub fn latest_turn(turns: &[TurnRef], active_faction_id: Option<&str>) -> Option<TurnRef>
```

The body, for the avoidance of doubt: build the pool as the turns of `active_faction_id` when there
is at least one, and as all the turns otherwise; then `max_by` on
`a.turn_number.cmp(&b.turn_number).then(b.faction_id.cmp(&a.faction_id))` — turn number ascending so
`max_by` yields the highest, faction id reversed so `max_by` yields the lowest. `.cloned()` the
winner. Keep the module doc-comment at the top of the file rewritten to the new rule; the one that is
there now describes the rule this bead removes.

`TurnRef` keeps its `ts(export)`, so `packages/core-client/src/generated/TurnRef.ts` is rewritten by
`cargo test`. `packages/core-client/src/generated/TurnTouch.ts` must be **deleted by hand** —
see *Known traps* — along with its re-export at `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:7`.

### `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` — the desktop read path

`load_latest_imported_turn` (line 944) gains the remembered faction as a parameter rather than
reading the manifest itself: the manifest is the caller's, on both platforms, and this function is
given a database path, not a game home.

```rust
pub fn load_latest_imported_turn(
    database_path: &Path,
    game_id: &str,
    active_faction_id: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Option<ImportedTurnRecord>, PersistenceError>
```

`touches` (line 981) is replaced by one query over one table, which also removes the `format!`-built
SQL and the comment explaining why it was safe:

```rust
/// Every `(faction, turn)` this game's `imported_turns` table holds, for `latest_turn` to rank.
fn imported_turn_refs(
    connection: &Connection,
    game_id: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<TurnRef>, PersistenceError>
```

with `"SELECT faction_id, turn_number FROM imported_turns WHERE game_id = ?1"` as a plain literal.
The `order_drafts` read goes entirely. Rewrite the function's doc comment (lines 933–943): "worked on"
and the paragraph about writing the first faction's orders all evening describe the rule being
removed.

### `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs` — the web read path

`latest_turn_state` (line 262) loses its drafts argument and gains the faction:

```rust
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn latest_turn_state(
    turns_json: String,
    active_faction_id: Option<String>,
) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue>
```

`turns_json` is `[{ factionId, turnNumber }]` now — two fields, not three. Update the doc comment
above it and the module header's mention at line 6.

### `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` — the command surface

`command_load_latest_imported_turn` (line 681) gains `active_faction_id: Option<String>` as its third
parameter and passes `active_faction_id.as_deref()` down. `Option<String>` rather than `Option<&str>`
because Tauri deserialises the argument and a missing or `null` argument must arrive as `None`.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` and `tauriCommands.ts`

- `CoreAdapter.loadLatestImportedTurn` (line 581) becomes:

```ts
  loadLatestImportedTurn(
    databasePath: string,
    gameId: string,
    activeFactionId: string | null
  ): Promise<ImportedTurnRecord | null>;
```

- `TurnTouch`'s re-export (line 7) is removed.
- `tauriCommands.ts:75` becomes
  `loadLatestImportedTurn: ["load_latest_imported_turn", "database_path", "game_id", "active_faction_id"],`
  — the type holds each row to its method's arity, so this and the interface change together.

### `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`

- `CoreWasmModule.latest_turn_state` (line 109) becomes
  `latest_turn_state(turnsJson: string, activeFactionId: string | null): TurnRef | null;`
- `loadLatestImportedTurn` (line 820) takes the third parameter, stops calling
  `store.getOrderDrafts`, drops the `touch` mapper and the `TurnTouch` import (line 25), and hands
  over `JSON.stringify(turns.map(({ factionId, turnNumber }) => ({ factionId, turnNumber })))`. Keep
  the `Promise.all` only if something else still needs it — with the drafts read gone it is one
  await. Keep the "the core named a turn the store does not hold" guard exactly as it is.

### `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.ts` — the caller, and the adopt

`restoreLatestTurn` (line 320) is the only production caller. It has the manifest already:

```ts
  const remembered = game.manifest.metadata.activeFactionId ?? null;
  const stored = await client.loadLatestImportedTurn(game.databasePath, gameId, remembered);
```

and after a turn is found, when the game reopened on a faction it was not remembering, it adopts that
faction — the navigator's answer to "what happens to a game upgraded from today's version": *fall back
to the highest turn in the game, and adopt that faction as the remembered one*.

```ts
  // A game reopened by the fallback has now settled on a faction; remembering it is what stops the
  // next import of somebody else's report deciding the question by accident. A failure here is a
  // warning, not a failed restore - the turn on screen is right either way.
  if (factionId !== remembered) {
    try {
      await client.setActiveFaction(gameId, factionId);
    } catch (error: unknown) {
      warning = warning ?? `which faction this game reopens as could not be remembered: ${detail(error)}`;
    }
  }
```

placed beside the existing `loadRegionSightings` try/catch, which is the pattern it follows (`detail`
and the `warning` variable are already in scope). The write is to the manifest, not to a turn, so the
module's standing promise — *"Nothing is committed … re-committing would move its `updated_at`"* —
still holds; say so in a line where the comment above it lives, since a reader who knows that
paragraph will stop at this call.

## Increments

1. **The core rule.** RED: rewrite `crates/core/src/reopen.rs`'s test module to the tests named in
   the table below — they will not compile against today's signature, which is the RED. GREEN: the
   new `latest_turn` and the deletion of `TurnTouch`.
2. **The desktop read path.** RED: `reopening_never_goes_back_to_an_older_turn` in
   `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs`. GREEN: the new parameter and `imported_turn_refs`; the
   existing test `the_turn_most_recently_edited_wins_over_the_one_most_recently_imported` (line 2327)
   is **replaced**, not repaired — it pins the rule being removed.
3. **The wasm entry point and the Tauri command.** RED: `cargo test --workspace` will not compile
   until both callers are updated; add the tauri test named below. GREEN: both signatures.
4. **The transport rows.** RED: change `TAURI_COMMANDS`'s row — `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` goes
   red naming `main.rs` and the sweep. GREEN: `tests/native/sweep.ts:186` gains
   `active_faction_id: null`; `main.rs` needs no change, since this command is registered directly
   rather than through a games-root wrapper (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:154`).
5. **The browser adapter.** RED: the `fakeWasm` stand-in and the routing test in
   `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` (lines 171 and 668) no longer typecheck. GREEN:
   the adapter change, the stand-in rewritten to the new rule, and the routing test renamed to
   `hands every turn and the remembered faction to the core, two fields each`.
6. **The rule across the real WebAssembly boundary.** RED: rewrite
   `packages/browser-core/src/reopen.wasm.test.ts`'s first test — it asserts today's rule (a draft
   edit sends you back to turn 70) and must become the navigator's reported case. GREEN: nothing, if
   the earlier increments are right; if this needs code, the rule is in the wrong place.
7. **The caller and the adopt.** RED: the two tests named below in
   `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.test.ts`. GREEN: the `restoreLatestTurn` change.

## The test plan

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `the_remembered_factions_highest_turn_reopens` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | Faction "95" holding 70 and 71, faction "73" holding 71 → 95/71 |
| `a_higher_turn_of_another_faction_does_not_win` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | Remembered "95" holds 70, "73" holds 71 → 95/70 |
| `an_older_turn_imported_later_does_not_win` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | The reported case, at unit level: turns 25 and 23 of one faction → 25 |
| `with_no_remembered_faction_the_highest_turn_in_the_game_reopens` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | `None` → the highest turn, whichever faction |
| `a_remembered_faction_holding_no_turns_falls_back_to_the_game` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | `Some("42")` with no turns of 42 → the highest turn in the game |
| `a_tie_on_turn_number_in_the_fallback_goes_to_the_lower_faction_id` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | "73" and "95" both at 71, none remembered → 73 |
| `a_game_with_no_turns_reopens_on_nothing` | `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` | Kept from today, with the new signature |
| `reopening_never_goes_back_to_an_older_turn` | `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` | Seed turn 25 then turn 23 via `turn_at` (line 2405), a draft on 23, `None` remembered → 25. Replaces `the_turn_most_recently_edited_wins_over_the_one_most_recently_imported` |
| `the_remembered_faction_decides_which_turn_reopens` | `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` | Two factions at the same turn, `Some("18")` → 18 |
| `a_game_with_no_imports_has_no_latest_turn` | `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` | Kept, third argument `None` |
| `one_games_latest_turn_is_invisible_to_another` | `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` | Kept, third argument `None` |
| `the_remembered_faction_reaches_the_query` | `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` | The command passes it through: two factions, one remembered, the other returned when it is the one named |
| `hands every turn and the remembered faction to the core, two fields each` | `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` | No draft read, no `updatedAt` in the payload, the faction passed as given |
| `reopens on the highest turn, not the one imported last` | `packages/browser-core/src/reopen.wasm.test.ts` | The real wasm core: commit `g7f95t71` then `g7f95t70`, remembered `null` → turn 71. Replaces `reopens on the turn last edited rather than the one last imported` |
| `reopens as the remembered faction even when another holds the same turn` | `packages/browser-core/src/reopen.wasm.test.ts` | Commit `g7f95t71` as "95" and `g8f73t71` as "73", remembered `"95"` → 95/71; `"73"` → 73/71 |
| `a game holding no imports reopens on nothing` | `packages/browser-core/src/reopen.wasm.test.ts` | Kept |
| `passes the remembered faction from the manifest` | `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.test.ts` | `restoreLatestTurn` reads `metadata.activeFactionId`, and passes `null` when it is absent |
| `remembers the faction a fallback reopen settled on` | `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.test.ts` | `setActiveFaction` called once with the restored turn's faction when the manifest remembered none, and not called when it already matches; a rejection becomes a warning, not a failure |

Suites: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm -r run test`, `pnpm run test:tooling` — all three are
`pnpm test`. The Playwright suite is not required, but note that
`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:1648` ("a folded panel is still folded after a reload") asserts
`restored turn 71` after a reload and now exercises the fallback-and-adopt path; it must still pass,
and CI runs it.

## User-facing decisions

The rule is the navigator's, settled in the interview of 2026-08-17 and recorded **in full, with the
rejected alternatives, in the epic ah-do8's `design` field**. The two lines that govern this bead:

> "What I tried to tell Psylocke was about never going back in time (making earlier turns the current
> one)."

> "we should always have an 'active faction' and that should only change if the user say so during an
> import"

Nothing on screen changes: no control, no wording, no new state. What changes is which turn is
already there when a game opens. There is no mockup because there is nothing to look at.

Do not re-open with the navigator: whether the tiebreak is numeric or textual (there is no tiebreak in
the intended state — a game always has a remembered faction once ah-do8.3 lands, and the textual
comparison in the fallback is unchanged from today), whether editing orders should count as
attention (it no longer counts for anything), and whether reopening should ask the player which
faction to continue as (rejected).

## Out of scope

- **Setting `activeFactionId` from the import flows** — ah-do8.3. The only write this bead adds is the
  adopt in `restoreLatestTurn`.
- **Anything that happens during a session.** `decideReportLoad`
  (`packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts:78`) already refuses to make an older report the working
  turn and already asks before switching faction; leave it alone.
- **`updated_at` itself.** The column stays and keeps its other readers (import stamps, the turn
  diff); it merely stops deciding which turn reopens.
- **The two comments about merging putting an ally's turn "at the top of `load_latest_imported_turn`"**
  (`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:759`, `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts:1349`). Still
  true under the new rule and still worth having; do not rewrite them, and do not change what merging
  stores.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run typecheck           # rebuilds the wasm module - see the trap below - before anything reads it
pnpm run check:fast
```

`check:fast` is the gate; it runs typecheck first, which is what keeps the wasm module fresh.

A human check the navigator has already named, and the one this bead exists for: create a fresh game,
import turn 25, then import turn 23, reload — the game must come back on **turn 25**. Psylocke will run
exactly that.

## Known traps

- **`cargo test` rewrites the generated bindings but never deletes one.**
  `packages/core-client/src/generated/TurnTouch.ts` will still be sitting there, tracked and
  unchanged, after `TurnTouch` is gone from Rust — and `pnpm run check:generated` only looks for a
  *dirty* generated directory, so it will not notice. Remove it explicitly
  (`git rm packages/core-client/src/generated/TurnTouch.ts`) and remove its re-export at
  `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:7`; the removed export is what makes the typecheck agree.
- **The wasm module is not rebuilt by the test suites.** `scripts/ensure-wasm.mjs` runs from
  browser-core's `pretypecheck` only. After changing any crate, `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test`
  runs `reopen.wasm.test.ts` against the *old* module — which, for this bead, is a test of the exact
  rule you just removed, failing or passing for reasons that have nothing to do with the code in front
  of you. Run `pnpm run typecheck` (or `node scripts/ensure-wasm.mjs`) first, every time.
- **`bd show --json` on the epic is where the decision lives.** Do not reconstruct the rule from this
  section list.
- **`fakeWasm`'s `latest_turn_state` is a stand-in, not the rule**
  (`packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts:171`). It only has to agree with itself so the
  routing tests read true — keep it as simple as the new rule allows (highest turn number of the
  named faction, else highest overall) and resist reimplementing the tiebreaks there. The rule itself
  is pinned in `reopen.rs` and against the real module in `reopen.wasm.test.ts`.
- **`TAURI_COMMANDS` rows are arity-checked by the type**, and `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` holds
  the command to `main.rs` and to `tests/native/sweep.ts` as well as to the Rust parameter names.
  Changing the interface without the row (or the row without the sweep) fails the tooling suite; that
  is increment 4's RED.
- **Every `load_latest_imported_turn` call site must be found, including test-only ones.** There are
  five in `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` alone (lines 2317, 2350, 2370, 2394, 2399) and one in
  `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:1845`; the compiler finds them, but expect the diff to be wider than
  the production change suggests.

title: A game remembers which faction is yours
description:
First child of ah-do8. Adds the storage only - no behaviour change yet.

A game has no record of which faction the player is; the workspace infers it from whichever turn happened to reopen, which is the defect ah-do8 describes. This child gives GameMetadata an optional activeFactionId and a setActiveFaction path on both platforms, following set_game_name/setGameName exactly. Nothing reads it yet: ah-do8.2 makes reopening use it, ah-do8.3 sets it from the import flows.

Navigator, 2026-08-17 (interview on ah-do8): 'we should always have an active faction and that should only change if the user says so during an import'.
design:
## Context

First child of the epic ah-do8, whose `design` field carries the decision this family is built
against — read it first, and do not re-open anything it settles.

A game has no record of which faction is the player's. The workspace infers it from whichever turn
happened to reopen, which is the defect ah-do8 describes: import an older report and the game reopens
on it, silently changing whose eyes you are looking through. The fix is for a game to remember its
faction; this child adds that memory and nothing else.

**Nothing reads the field when this bead is done, and no behaviour changes.** ah-do8.2 makes reopening
use it; ah-do8.3 sets it from the import flows. That is deliberate — the storage crosses four layers
and both platforms, and it is a whole increment on its own.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**`set_game_name` is the template for every layer of this.** It is the same shape of change — one
scalar on the manifest, settable after creation — and it is already wired end to end. Copy its
structure, its doc-comment habits and its tests rather than inventing a second pattern.

The manifest JSON file on disk is the source of truth on the desktop; the `game_metadata` SQLite table
is a snapshot rewritten on every open (`persist_game_snapshot`, `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:1190`)
and is read back only for `ruleset_id`/`game_name` in tests. `export_game`
(`crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:459`) reads the manifest file, not the table. **So this bead needs
no SQL migration and no new column** — see *Known traps*.

### `crates/core/src/backup.rs`

`GameMetadata` (line 17) gains one field:

```rust
pub struct GameMetadata {
    pub game_id: String,
    pub game_name: String,
    pub ruleset_id: String,
    /// Which faction in this game is the player's, or `None` for a game that has never had a report
    /// imported - and for every game written before this field existed, whose manifest simply has no
    /// such key. Set only when the player says so at an import (ah-do8.3); read when the game is
    /// reopened (ah-do8.2).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub active_faction_id: Option<String>,
}
```

`#[serde(default)]` and no `skip_serializing_if`: a manifest written before this change has no key and
must still load, and one written after it always carries the key — as `null` when unset — so the JSON
shape is the same whichever way it was produced. `CURRENT_MANIFEST_VERSION` (`backup.rs:15`) stays at
`1`; see *Known traps*.

`GameMetadata` is **not** a ts-rs type. `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:64` declares the
TypeScript `GameMetadata` by hand and it must be edited by hand to match.

### `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs`

One new public function, modelled line for line on `set_game_name` (line 364):

```rust
/// Records which faction in this game is the player's, after creation.
///
/// The id is stored as the report names it, opaque to this crate, exactly as `confirmed_faction_id`
/// reaches `commit_report_import`. Which faction that is - and when it may change - is the shell's
/// decision (ah-do8.3), never this crate's.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns an error when no game exists under this id, when its manifest cannot be read, or when the
/// database cannot be opened or migrated.
pub fn set_active_faction(
    games_root: &Path,
    game_id: &str,
    faction_id: &str,
) -> Result<GameManifest, PersistenceError>
```

Body identical to `set_game_name`'s, assigning `manifest.metadata.active_faction_id = Some(faction_id.to_string())`
— including the database-then-manifest write order and the comment that says why it is that way.

### `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`

- `GameMetadataDto` (line 34) gains `pub active_faction_id: Option<String>`, with `#[serde(default)]`
  for the same reason.
- Both `From` impls between `GameMetadata` and `GameMetadataDto` (around lines 165 and 195) carry it.
- `test_support::manifest_dto` (line 1379) sets it to `None`.
- One new command, modelled on `command_set_game_name` (line 1115):

```rust
pub fn command_set_active_faction(
    games_root: &str,
    game_id: &str,
    faction_id: &str,
) -> Result<GameManifestDto, String>
```

### `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`

A games-root wrapper beside `set_game_name` (line 116), and the same two edits its neighbours have:
the `use atlantis_hud_core_tauri::{…}` list (line 5) and the `tauri::generate_handler![…]` list
(line 139).

```rust
#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]
fn set_active_faction(
    app: tauri::AppHandle,
    game_id: String,
    faction_id: String,
) -> Result<GameManifestDto, String> {
    command_set_active_faction(&games_root(&app)?, &game_id, &faction_id)
}
```

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

- `GameMetadata` (line 64) gains:

```ts
  /**
   * Which faction in this game is the player's, if one has been chosen yet.
   *
   * Optional rather than `string | null` because it is genuinely absent on a game created before
   * this field existed: the browser stores the manifest object as it stands, so an old record has no
   * such key at all.
   */
  activeFactionId?: string | null;
```

- `CoreAdapter` (line 480) gains, beside `setGameName` (line 489):

```ts
  setActiveFaction(gameId: string, factionId: string): Promise<GameManifest>;
```

`CoreClient` (line 636) is `Omit<CoreAdapter, …>` and `createCoreClient` (line 688) spreads the
adapter, so nothing else is needed for it to reach the shells.

### `packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts`

One row beside `setGameName` (line 32):

```ts
  setActiveFaction: ["set_active_faction", "game_id", "faction_id"],
```

### `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`

One method, copied from `setGameName` (line 574) including its comment about the registry's copy of
the manifest being what every later open reads:

```ts
    async setActiveFaction(gameId: string, factionId: string) {
      const game = await store.getGame(gameId);
      if (!game) {
        throw new Error(`no game with id ${gameId}`);
      }
      const manifest = {
        ...(game.manifest as GameManifest),
        metadata: { ...(game.manifest as GameManifest).metadata, activeFactionId: factionId }
      };
      await store.putGame({ ...game, manifest });
      return manifest;
    },
```

### `tests/native/sweep.ts`

One row beside `set_game_name` (line 72):

```ts
  { command: "set_active_faction", args: () => ({ game_id: GAME_ID, faction_id: "95" }) },
```

### `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`

The adapter stub gains one line directly beside `setGameName` (line 84), using the same value its two
neighbours already use:

```ts
    setActiveFaction: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(gameManifest),
```

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test. Follow the `test-driven-development` skill.

1. **The field exists and survives a manifest that never had it.**
   RED: in `crates/core/src/backup.rs`'s test module,
   `a_manifest_metadata_without_an_active_faction_reads_as_none` — `serde_json::from_str::<GameMetadata>`
   on `{"gameId":"g","gameName":"G","rulesetId":"neworigins"}` yields `active_faction_id: None`.
   GREEN: add the field with `#[serde(default)]`.

2. **A backup carries it both ways.**
   RED: `an_active_faction_survives_the_backup_round_trip` in `backup.rs` — encode a document whose
   manifest metadata has `Some("95")`, decode it, assert `Some("95")`; and a second assertion that a
   document encoded with `None` decodes as `None`. GREEN: nothing beyond increment 1 if the field is
   in the right struct — if this test needs new code, the field went in the wrong place.

3. **The desktop remembers it across a reopen.**
   RED: `the_active_faction_is_remembered_across_reopening` in `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs`'s
   tests — `create_game`, then `set_active_faction(root, GAME_ID, "95")` returns a manifest whose
   `metadata.active_faction_id == Some("95")`, then `open_game` reads it back off disk as `Some("95")`.
   Plus `setting_the_active_faction_of_a_game_that_does_not_exist_is_an_error`, asserting
   `PersistenceError::GameNotFound`, mirroring `set_game_ruleset`'s error test (line 1770).
   GREEN: `set_active_faction`.

4. **The Tauri surface carries it.**
   RED: `setting_the_active_faction_returns_the_updated_manifest` in `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`,
   modelled on `renaming_a_game_returns_the_updated_manifest` (line 1438) — create, set, assert on the
   returned DTO, then assert it stuck by listing the games again.
   GREEN: the DTO field, both `From` impls, and `command_set_active_faction`.

5. **The desktop transport is wired.**
   RED: add the `TAURI_COMMANDS` row first — `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` holds every row to the
   Rust parameter names, to `main.rs` and to the native sweep, so it goes red naming exactly what is
   missing. GREEN: the `main.rs` wrapper and its two list entries, and the `sweep.ts` row. Add the
   `CoreAdapter` method and the `index.test.ts` stub entry in the same increment — typecheck fails
   until both exist.

6. **The browser remembers it across a reopen.**
   RED: in `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts`, beside the existing game-manifest
   tests, `remembers which faction is yours, and hands it back on the next open` — `createGame`,
   `setActiveFaction(gameId, "95")`, then `openGame` and assert
   `manifest.metadata.activeFactionId === "95"`. GREEN: the adapter method.

## The test plan

Unit, and no browser suite: this bead adds no surface a Playwright test could see.

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `a_manifest_metadata_without_an_active_faction_reads_as_none` | `crates/core/src/backup.rs` | A manifest written before this field still loads |
| `an_active_faction_survives_the_backup_round_trip` | `crates/core/src/backup.rs` | Export/import does not drop it |
| `the_active_faction_is_remembered_across_reopening` | `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` | It reaches the manifest file and comes back |
| `setting_the_active_faction_of_a_game_that_does_not_exist_is_an_error` | `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` | `GameNotFound`, like its neighbours |
| `setting_the_active_faction_returns_the_updated_manifest` | `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` | The command surface returns what the shell needs, no second round trip |
| `remembers which faction is yours, and hands it back on the next open` | `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` | The web's counterpart of the manifest rewrite |
| (existing) `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` | unchanged | Command name, parameter names, `main.rs` and the sweep all agree |
| (existing) `createCoreClient` "is the adapter's methods, plus nothing" | `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts:371` | The new method reaches `CoreClient` |

Suites that must run: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm -r run test`, `pnpm run test:tooling` — all
three are `pnpm test` (`scripts/runSuites.ts`). Then `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

**None in this child** — it stores a field nothing reads yet, and adds no control, wording or visible
behaviour.

The decision it is built for was taken by the navigator on 2026-08-17 and is recorded in full, with
the four rejected alternatives, in the epic ah-do8's `design` field. Read it, do not re-open it, and
do not ask the navigator anything this bead could decide for itself: the one line that governs this
child is *"we should always have an 'active faction' and that should only change if the user say so
during an import"*.

## Out of scope

- **Reading the field when a game reopens** — ah-do8.2. Nothing in this bead may change which turn
  reopens; the existing reopen tests must still pass unchanged.
- **Setting it from the import flows** — ah-do8.3. `set_active_faction` gains no caller in this bead
  beyond its own tests.
- **A SQL migration or a `game_metadata` column.** See *Known traps*.
- **Validating the faction id** against the turns the game holds. The id is opaque here, exactly as
  `ruleset_id` is.
- **Bumping `CURRENT_MANIFEST_VERSION`.**

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast          # lint, typecheck, all three test suites, check:generated, fmt, clippy
```

`check:fast` is the gate. The browser suites (`test:smoke`, `build:web`, `test:pwa`) and the native
suite are CI's job and are not needed locally for this bead — it renders nothing.

Nothing here needs a human to look at it: the field is invisible until ah-do8.2 and ah-do8.3 land.

## Known traps

- **Do not add a SQL migration or a `game_metadata` column.** The manifest JSON file is the truth on
  the desktop; `persist_game_snapshot` (line 1190) rewrites that table wholesale on every open and
  `export_game` (line 459) reads the manifest file rather than the table. A column would be a second
  copy to fall out of step, for no reader.
- **Do not bump `CURRENT_MANIFEST_VERSION` (`crates/core/src/backup.rs:15`).**
  `ensure_supported_manifest_version` (`core-persistence:1073`) refuses a manifest whose version is
  *higher* than the build supports, so bumping it would make every game touched by a new build
  unreadable by an older one — to announce a field that is optional in both directions.
- **`GameMetadata` is not generated.** There is no ts-rs `#[ts(export)]` on it and there must not be:
  `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:64` declares the TypeScript shape by hand. Edit both, or the two
  drift with nothing to catch it. If you do add a ts-rs export by reflex, `pnpm run check:generated`
  fails with an uncommitted file under `packages/core-client/src/generated/` — the fix is to remove
  the export, not to commit the file.
- **`activeFactionId` is optional in TypeScript (`?: string | null`), `Option<String>` with
  `#[serde(default)]` in Rust.** Making it required in TS would force `activeFactionId: null` into
  every manifest literal in the repository and would still be a lie about what the browser store
  actually holds for an old game.
- **The wasm module is not rebuilt by the test suites.** `scripts/ensure-wasm.mjs` runs from
  browser-core's `pretypecheck` only, so `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test` straight after a
  Rust change runs against a stale `packages/browser-core/src/wasm/`. Run `pnpm run typecheck` (or
  `node scripts/ensure-wasm.mjs`) after touching any crate and before believing a browser-core test.
- **Adding a `TAURI_COMMANDS` row is a three-place commitment.** `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`
  checks the command against `main.rs` and `tests/native/sweep.ts` as well as the Rust parameter
  names, so a row added alone fails the tooling suite. That failure is increment 5's RED, not a
  problem to route around.

title: A game reopens on its latest turn, never an earlier one
description:
Reported by the navigator at verification of ah-8m0.3 on 2026-08-17.

## What happens now

A game reopens on the turn touched most recently, with the turn number only a tiebreak (crates/core/src/reopen.rs:42, latest_turn: rank by the later of the turn's own updated_at and its draft's, then higher turn_number, then lower faction_id). Import turn 25 into a fresh game and then import turn 23, and the game reopens on 23 - the older report was touched last.

This is not a regression: ah-8m0.3 moved the rule into the core unchanged from the SQL that predates it (ORDER BY MAX(t.updated_at, COALESCE(d.updated_at, '')) DESC, t.turn_number DESC in load_latest_imported_turn), and the web store's reduce ranked the same way. ah-8m0.3 is verified passed.

## What the navigator wants instead

Reopen on the game's latest turn, always. An older report imported later is history to look back at, never somewhere the application returns you to - you should not be able to go back in time by importing.

Navigator at verification 2026-08-17, on the two-faction case: the latest turn is the highest turn number in the game, whichever faction holds it, with a fixed tiebreak (lowest faction id) when two factions both have it. Reopening does not follow the faction you last worked.

## Shape of the change

latest_turn's rank becomes turn_number first, then faction_id, and the updated_at stamps stop deciding it. Both stores already hand it every turn's and every draft's (faction, turn, updated_at), so no store change is needed and the draft stamps may become unused input - worth deciding whether to keep taking them. crates/core/src/reopen.rs carries the rule and its tests; packages/browser-core/src/reopen.wasm.test.ts pins the web side.

## Validation

A fresh game with turn 25 imported and then turn 23 imported reopens on 25. A game whose only turn is 23 reopens on 23. A game where two factions both hold turn 25 reopens on the same one every time.
design:
## Context

An epic: split into ah-do8.1, ah-do8.2 and ah-do8.3, in that order. This field records the decision
the three children are built against, so none of them re-opens it.

The defect that started it (navigator, at ah-8m0.3's verification, 2026-08-17): import turn 25 into a
fresh game and then import turn 23, and the game reopens on 23. Reopening ranks turns by which was
*touched* most recently (`crates/core/src/reopen.rs:42`), with the turn number only a tiebreak, so an
older report imported later wins. Not a regression — ah-8m0.3 moved that rule into the core unchanged
from the SQL that predates it.

## The rule, as the navigator settled it (interview, 2026-08-17)

The first framing — "highest turn number, lowest faction id" — was wrong, and the navigator corrected
it twice during the interview. Quoted, because the wording is the decision:

> "What I tried to tell Psylocke was about never going back in time (making earlier turns the current
> one). The faction should always be the last one I worked on unless the user decides something else
> (there is a question about switching factions when an ally report of the current turn is imported)."

> "we should always have an 'active faction' and that should only change if the user say so during an
> import"

So the model is **a remembered faction per game**, not a ranking over stamps:

1. A game remembers which faction is the player's (`activeFactionId`).
2. It changes only when the player says so at an import: the first report loaded into a game, the
   batch import's "which faction is yours" answer, and "Switch faction" on a foreign report. Merging
   an ally's report never changes it; storing an older report for history never changes it.
3. Reopening loads **that faction's highest-numbered imported turn**. Never a lower-numbered turn,
   whatever was touched last — "you should not be able to go back in time by importing".
4. When the remembered faction holds no imported turns — every game upgraded from today's version,
   until its next import — reopening falls back to **the highest-numbered turn in the game, whichever
   faction holds it**, and the shell adopts that faction as the remembered one. A game that holds a
   turn always reopens on a turn.

Rejected during the interview, and not to be re-proposed:

- **Rank by highest turn number, then by which was touched most recently** (no stored faction). The
  cheap fix; rejected because importing another faction's turn 26 would still silently move the
  player to that faction.
- **Lowest faction id as the tiebreak**, numeric or as text. Rejected: the navigator was never asking
  for a tiebreak, and a game always has an active faction, so there is nothing to break a tie
  between.
- **Remembered faction, but their most recently touched turn.** Rejected: that can still be an older
  turn, which is the whole defect.
- **Asking the player which faction to continue as at reopen.** Rejected: no new surface.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Per child; each child's own plan carries its paths and signatures.

- ah-do8.1 — `GameMetadata.activeFactionId` and a `setActiveFaction` path on both platforms. Storage
  only, no behaviour change.
- ah-do8.2 — the reopen rule reads it: `crates/core/src/reopen.rs`, `crates/core-persistence`,
  `crates/core-wasm`, `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`,

description:
## The cost being paid
Two questions about a fleet session — "is it still alive" and "what does ending it have to remove" — are each answered in several hand-kept places, and every fix has reached only the sites its author looked at:
- Ending a session. `cerebro--supervise`'s `retire` and `restart` branches, `cerebro--end-session`, and `k`'s `cerebro--kill-session-buffer` each list by hand which per-session artifacts go (buffer, `cerebro--sessions` entry, stop flag, state file). The same omission was fixed twice in the same two branches: 7496a8e (ah-kgc, #21) added stop-flag removal to `retire` and to `s` after a retired name inherited an instruction and was retired again at once; 7bd5962 (#43) added state-file removal to `retire` and `restart` after Rogue's `done` file outlived its session by ten hours and a recycled pid lit the row green. `k` still removes neither.
- Is this pid still that session. #43 also replaced a bare pid check in elisp with `cerebro--session-alive-p` (pid and `--name` in its args — "pids are recycled, so a bare number is not an identity"). The same afternoon e90224f (#47) added a second bare `kill -0 "$pid"` in plan-bead's label-reclaim loop as the test for whether a `planning` label is held (:395), beside the one already sizing the buffer from running implementers (:294, 054bc34). Both are the pre-#43 shape; a recycled pid there makes a dead planner look alive, which is exactly the stranded-label failure #47 exists to fix, and inflates the count the buffer is sized from. ah-5pp's retrospective is the same split seen from the ownership side (a liveness predicate that over-pruned, found only by review, +15 minutes).

## Evidence
- 7496a8e "fix(ah-kgc): a stop flag is removed when it retires an implementer, and when the name is started again (#21)"
- 7bd5962 "fix(fleet view): a state file dies with its session, and a pid must still be that session (#43)" — "Two independent faults, so two fixes"
- e90224f "fix(plan-bead): an abandoned planning label is freed, not left for nobody (#47)"; 054bc34 "docs(ah-4hr): the planning buffer follows the number of running implementers (#14)"
- docs/retrospectives/ah-5pp.md §"The plan's own pruning rule for the ownership table was subtly wrong, and only the Copilot review caught it"
- .claude/cerebro @ bbfa374: emacs/cerebro.el:1042-1058 (`cerebro--session-alive-p`), :1382-1414 (`cerebro--supervise` retire/restart), :1363 (`cerebro--end-session`), :2189 (`cerebro--kill-session-buffer`), :2244/:2264 (`cerebro--delete-state-file`, `cerebro--clear-stop-flag`); skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:294, :395

## Where
.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el; .claude/cerebro/skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md; .claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state (the natural home for a shell-side "is this state file's session alive")

## What a refactoring would change
One owner for a session's end (a single function every branch and `k` call, that removes buffer, table entry, stop flag and state file) and one owner for a session's liveness — in elisp `cerebro--session-alive-p`, and on the shell side an `agent-state … alive <Name>` (or similar) that plan-bead's two loops call instead of a bare `kill -0`, so the pid-plus-name rule lives once. Not a plan: a planner plans it.

design:
## Context

Two questions about a fleet session are each answered in several hand-kept places, and every fix so
far has reached only the sites its author looked at.

**"What does ending a session have to remove?"** Four artifacts belong to a session: its vterm
buffer, its entry in `cerebro--sessions`, its stop flag and its state file. Three call sites end a
session and each lists by hand which of the four it removes:

| Site | buffer + table | state file | stop flag |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cerebro--supervise` `'restart` (cerebro.el:1409) | yes | yes | no (correct — a restart means no flag was set) |
| `cerebro--supervise` `'retire` (cerebro.el:1414) | yes | yes | yes |
| `cerebro--kill-session-buffer` — the `k` key (cerebro.el:2189) | yes | **no** | no |

The same omission has been fixed twice, both times in the two `supervise` branches only: 7496a8e
(ah-kgc, cerebro#21) added stop-flag removal after a retired name inherited an instruction; 7bd5962
(cerebro#43) added state-file removal after Rogue's `done` file outlived its session by ten hours and
a recycled pid lit the row green. **`k` still leaks a state file**, which is the live bug: kill a
session with `k` and the fleet view keeps reading its file, so the row keeps showing `working` on a
bead nobody is building, and once the operating system reuses that pid the row goes green for an
unrelated daemon.

**"Is this pid still that session?"** cerebro#43 established the rule in elisp — a pid alone is not
an identity, so `cerebro--session-alive-p` (cerebro.el:1042) requires the process's own args to carry
`--name <Name>`. The same afternoon e90224f (cerebro#47) added a *second* bare `kill -0 "$pid"` in
`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md:395`, as the test for whether a `planning` label is held, beside the one
already sizing the buffer at `:294`. Both are the pre-#43 shape. A recycled pid there makes a dead
planner look alive — which strands exactly the label cerebro#47 exists to free — and inflates the
count the planning buffer is sized from, so both planners sleep over a short queue.

When this lands: `k` becomes a full session-end (one function owns all four artifacts, so a fourth
site cannot be added half-right), and the shell has one liveness predicate that both plan-bead loops
call, so the pid-plus-name rule lives in exactly two places — once in elisp, once in bash — instead
of four.

**This bead is almost entirely inside the `.claude/cerebro` submodule** (`rmstdope/cerebro`), plus a
one-line gitlink bump in `atlantis-hud`. See *Known traps*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

All paths are relative to the submodule root, `.claude/cerebro/`, unless marked otherwise.

### `emacs/cerebro.el` — one owner for ending a session

Today's `cerebro--end-session (agent)` (cerebro.el:1363) kills the buffer and drops the
`cerebro--sessions` entry, and nothing more; `cerebro--kill-session-buffer` (cerebro.el:2189)
duplicates that body verbatim and then reverts the view. **Split the name from the job**: the partial
operation gets a name that says it is partial, and `cerebro--end-session` becomes the total one.

```elisp
;; Renamed from today's `cerebro--end-session'. Body, docstring and the
;; `cerebro--recorded-buffer' / query-on-exit-flag reasoning move across unchanged.
;; Called only by `cerebro--end-session' below.
(defun cerebro--forget-session (agent)
  "Kill AGENT's session buffer, if any, and forget it in `cerebro--sessions'.")

;; The one owner. Every artifact a session leaves is removed here or nowhere.
(defun cerebro--end-session (agent repo-root &optional clear-stop-flag)
  "End AGENT's session and remove every per-session artifact it leaves behind.

Buffer and `cerebro--sessions' entry always; the state file always, because a
file naming a session that has been ended is a claim about a pid that no longer
exists and pids are recycled (`cerebro--session-alive-p'); the stop flag only
when CLEAR-STOP-FLAG, since only a retire has finished with the instruction.")
```

Its body is exactly three forms — `cerebro--forget-session`, `cerebro--delete-state-file`, and a
`when`-guarded `cerebro--clear-stop-flag`. Reuse those two helpers as they stand (cerebro.el:2244 and
:2264); both already delete unconditionally and catch `file-missing`, which is what makes them safe
to call from a timer with demoted errors. `cerebro--state-file-path` (cerebro.el:1017) and
`cerebro--stop-flag-path` (cerebro.el:1337) stay where they are; nothing here needs them directly.

**The `clear-stop-flag` argument stays explicit rather than being inferred.** `cerebro--supervise`
chose `'restart` *because* there was no flag, so clearing one there would be a no-op today — but a
flag written between that decision and this call is the navigator pressing `f`, and swallowing it is
the ah-kgc failure with the sign reversed.

The three call sites become:

```elisp
;; cerebro--supervise, 'restart branch (cerebro.el:1409) — deletion still precedes the launch,
;; which is what `cerebro-test/restart-removes-the-state-file-before-launching' pins.
('restart (let ((watching (cerebro--detail-showing-p agent)))
            (cerebro--end-session agent repo-root)
            (cerebro--launch agent)
            (when watching (cerebro--show-detail agent))))

;; 'retire branch (cerebro.el:1414)
('retire (cerebro--end-session agent repo-root 'clear-stop-flag))
```

```elisp
;; cerebro--kill-session-buffer (cerebro.el:2189) — takes repo-root now, and its body is three lines.
(defun cerebro--kill-session-buffer (agent repo-root)
  "End AGENT's session (`k'), then refresh the view and the detail window.

`cerebro-kill' has already confirmed this exact kill via `y-or-n-p', so
`cerebro--end-session' clears the process's query-on-exit flag rather than
prompting a second time. The stop flag is left alone: `k' is not a retire, and
a flag set with `f' means this name stays down until `s' clears it and says so."
  (cerebro--end-session agent repo-root)
  (revert-buffer)
  (cerebro--show-detail agent))
```

`repo-root` is **passed in, not fetched here** — `cerebro-kill` (cerebro.el:2212) computes
`(cerebro--repo-root)` once and hands it to all three of its `kill`/`kill-working` branches. That
keeps `cerebro--repo-root` (cerebro.el:988, buffer-local `default-directory` work) out of the unit
under test, exactly as `cerebro--supervise` already takes its root as a parameter.

Nothing else in `cerebro.el` calls `cerebro--end-session` — confirmed by
`grep -n 'cerebro--end-session\|cerebro--kill-session-buffer' emacs/cerebro.el`, which returns only
the definitions and the sites listed above. Run that grep again after the rename and expect no
stragglers.

### `scripts/agent-alive` (new) — one owner for shell liveness

A predicate, not a writer, so it is its own script rather than a mode of `scripts/agent-state`
(which requires `--pid` and exists to write a file). Same one-job shape as `scripts/roster`,
`scripts/consumer-root` and `scripts/agent-asking`.

```
usage: agent-alive <Name>

exit 0   <Name>'s state file names a pid that is running AND whose command line
         carries `--name <Name>` — so it is still that session, not a recycled pid
exit 1   not alive: no state file, no pid in it, the pid is gone, or the pid is
         alive but is somebody else's process
exit 2   usage error, or <Name> is not on scripts/roster
```

Mirror the four pieces already in the tree rather than inventing any of them:

- **The roster check** — copy `scripts/agent-state`:67-70 verbatim
  (`"$script_dir/roster" --entry "$name"`, message `agent-alive: $name is not on the roster`,
  exit 2). A typo must not read as "dead".
- **The state file's path** — `repo_root="$("$script_dir/consumer-root" --shared)"`, then
  `"$repo_root/.cerebro/state/$name.state.json"`, as `scripts/agent-state`:116-119 does. `--shared`
  and never bare `consumer-root`: from a bead worktree's own submodule copy the bare answer is the
  worktree, not the checkout the fleet writes state into (ah-e0w).
- **The pid** — `jq -r '.pid // empty'`, the same expression both skill loops already use.
- **The identity test** — the bash counterpart of `cerebro--name-in-args-p` (cerebro.el:106), whose
  needle is `--name[ \t]+<Name>` on a word boundary:

  ```bash
  args="$(ps -o args= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null)" || exit 1
  [[ -n "$args" ]] || exit 1
  grep -Eq -- "--name[[:space:]]+${name}([[:space:]]|\$)" <<<"$args" || exit 1
  ```

  `ps -o args= -p <pid>` is the portable form (BSD and GNU alike) and CI is ubuntu-latest, so the
  suite must pass there as well as on macOS. `-o args=` with the trailing `=` suppresses the header;
  without it the header line alone makes `-n "$args"` true for a dead pid. The trailing
  `([[:space:]]|$)` is the word boundary — without it `--name Beast` would match a hypothetical
  `Beastly`.
- **`set -euo pipefail`** as every script here has, with the `grep`/`ps` non-zero exits handled by
  the explicit `|| exit 1` above rather than left to `-e`.

Emit nothing on stdout in the 0/1 cases. It is called in a loop per agent on every planner pass, so
its output would be noise; exit status is the whole answer.

### `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` — both loops call it

Two `kill -0` sites, and no others in the tree
(`grep -rn 'kill -0' .` returns exactly these two).

At **`:294`**, inside *You keep a buffer sized to the fleet*, the loop that counts running
implementers:

```bash
  [ -e ".cerebro/state/$name.stop" ] && continue
  .claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-alive "$name" && n=$((n+1))
```

replacing `pid="$(jq -r '.pid // empty' "$f" 2>/dev/null)"` and the `kill -0` line that follows it —
the `pid` variable has no other reader in that loop.

At **`:395`**, inside *Reclaiming a label nobody is holding*, the loop that lists each live planner's
bead:

```bash
  f=".cerebro/state/$name.state.json"
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  .claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-alive "$name" || continue   # a dead session holds nothing
  jq -r '.bead // empty' "$f"
```

The `jq` for the bead stays — `agent-alive` answers liveness and nothing else, and the loop still
needs the bead name.

Add one sentence to each loop's surrounding prose saying that liveness is `agent-alive`'s to answer
and why a bare `kill -0` is wrong there: *"pids are recycled, so a bare `kill -0` makes a dead
planner look alive — `agent-alive` checks the pid's own `--name`, the rule
`cerebro--session-alive-p` follows in elisp."* That sentence is the durable half of this bead: it is
what stops a third bare `kill -0` being added by the next author.

`.claude/skills/plan-bead` in the consumer is a directory symlink into the submodule
(`readlink` → `../cerebro/skills/plan-bead`), so the edit is live for a running planner with no
re-sync. Do **not** run `sync-symlinks.sh` for this — the links already exist and nothing new is
added under `skills/` or `agents/`.

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` and `tests/agent-alive.sh` (new)

See *The test plan*.

## Increments

Four increments, in this order. Increments 1–3 are one PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`; increment 4 is
a separate one-line PR against `atlantis-hud`.

### 1. `k` removes the state file

**RED — `emacs/cerebro-test.el`, `cerebro-test/kill-removes-the-state-file`.** The bug, stated as a
test. Build an agent with `cerebro-test--agent "Cyclops" "implementer" 'implementer 'working` (the
helper the tests at :899 and :917 already use), write a state file at
`(cerebro--state-file-path root "Cyclops")` containing `{"state":"working","pid":42}`, stub
`revert-buffer` and `cerebro--show-detail` with `#'ignore` as
`cerebro-test/kill-session-buffer-kills-a-buffer-whose-process-already-exited` (:913) does, call
`(cerebro--kill-session-buffer agent root)`, and `should-not (file-exists-p path)`. It fails today at
the arity, and would fail on the assertion once the arity is right — write it against the new
signature.

GREEN, in this order:

1. Rename `cerebro--end-session` → `cerebro--forget-session` (definition at :1363 and every caller),
   with no behaviour change.
2. Add the new `cerebro--end-session (agent repo-root &optional clear-stop-flag)`.
3. Point `'restart`, `'retire` and `cerebro--kill-session-buffer` at it, and give

4. **Migrate the nine existing test sites.** `grep -n 'cerebro--end-session\|cerebro--kill-session-buffer' emacs/cerebro-test.el`

   - A test whose subject is the buffer/table cleanup (the direct calls at 890 and 908) calls
     `cerebro--forget-session` instead. Rename the test at :895 to
     `cerebro-test/forget-session-kills-a-buffer-whose-process-already-exited` so its name still
     names its subject.
   - A test that **stubs it out to avoid killing a real buffer** while asserting on the flag or the
     file (1225, 1240, 1255, 2996, 3014) must now stub `cerebro--forget-session` — stubbing
     `cerebro--end-session` would stub out the very removal the test asserts, and the test would go
     green for the wrong reason. This is the one place in the migration where a careless edit passes.
   - A test that **records the call for its ordering** (1140, 1158, 1196) stubs
     `cerebro--forget-session` too, and its stub takes `(lambda (a) ...)` unchanged since
     `forget-session` keeps the one-argument signature.
   - The `k`-path test at :913 gets `root` threaded through, like the RED test above.

   No stub of the new `cerebro--end-session` should remain anywhere: `grep -n "'cerebro--end-session" emacs/cerebro-test.el`
   must return nothing after this increment.

### 2. The owner's contract, and `k` leaves the flag

**RED — three tests in `emacs/cerebro-test.el`**, all following the
`(make-temp-file "cerebro-test-" t)` + `unwind-protect` + `delete-directory` shape the file uses
throughout (see :1216):

- `cerebro-test/end-session-removes-the-state-file` — buffer, `cerebro--sessions` entry and state

- `cerebro-test/end-session-leaves-the-stop-flag-unless-asked` — write a flag with

Plus the navigator's decision, as its own test:

- `cerebro-test/kill-leaves-the-stop-flag` — flag written, `(cerebro--kill-session-buffer agent root)`,

  gone; `s` is what clears a stale flag, and it says so when it does.*

GREEN: satisfied by increment 1's implementation if it was written correctly. **If these all pass
without a single edit, that is the expected outcome** — they are the contract being pinned, not new
behaviour. Do not manufacture a failure to make the loop look right; note in the commit that they
were regression pins.

The existing `cerebro-test/retire-removes-the-stop-flag` (:1216),
`cerebro-test/restart-leaves-no-flag-to-remove` (:1232),
`cerebro-test/retire-removes-the-state-file` (:2986) and
`cerebro-test/restart-removes-the-state-file-before-launching` (:3003) must all still pass, on their
stubs migrated in increment 1. They are the proof the two `supervise` branches did not regress.

### 3. `scripts/agent-alive`, and the two loops that call it

**RED — `tests/agent-alive.sh` (new).** Plain bash, no framework, `set -euo pipefail`, exiting
non-zero at the first failed assertion, with the `fail`/`pass`/`new_fixture` helpers copied from

`consumer-root` and `agent-alive` — and the same `git init -q` (`consumer-root --shared` asks git for
the main `.git`). Six cases, in this order:

1. `dead-for-a-live-pid-that-is-not-that-session` — **the pid-recycling case, and the reason the
   script exists.** Write `Cyclops`'s state file with `pid` set to the test shell's own `$$`, which

Then edit `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` at both loops as specified in *Files to change*, and add the
one-sentence justification to each. No test covers a Markdown file; the check is that the two loops
