### 4. The bump, in `atlantis-hud`

Once the cerebro PR is merged: `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin && git -C .claude/cerebro checkout <merge sha>`,
then commit the one-line gitlink move as `chore(ah-bqi): bump cerebro to one owner for ending a
session`. `git log --oneline -- .claude/cerebro` shows this shape a dozen times (3621c84, db719aa,
d802e01). It touches nothing else, so `pnpm run check:fast` is the whole gate.

## The test plan

**ERT — `emacs/cerebro-test.el`.** Run both matrix versions' worth locally with one command:

```bash
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

New tests, and what each pins:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `kill-removes-the-state-file` | The live bug: `k` no longer leaves a file that keeps the row alive |
| `kill-leaves-the-stop-flag` | The navigator's decision — `k` is not a retire |
| `end-session-removes-the-state-file` | The owner removes buffer, table entry and file together |
| `end-session-leaves-the-stop-flag-unless-asked` | The flag is opt-in, so a flag written mid-poll is not swallowed |
| `end-session-clears-the-stop-flag-when-asked` | Retire's half of the same contract |
| `forget-session-kills-a-buffer-whose-process-already-exited` | The renamed partial keeps its own guarantee (was `end-session-…`) |

Unchanged and load-bearing as regressions: `retire-removes-the-stop-flag`,
`retire-removes-the-state-file`, `restart-removes-the-state-file-before-launching`,
`restart-leaves-no-flag-to-remove`, `supervise-retire-kills-without-launching`,
`supervise-restart-kills-then-launches`, `restart-shows-the-session-only-where-it-was-watched`,
`supervise-ends-an-idle-session-under-stop`,
`kill-session-buffer-kills-a-buffer-whose-process-already-exited`.

**Bash — `tests/agent-alive.sh`**, the six cases above plus usage. Run the whole set, since the
rename touches nothing else in `scripts/` but the suites are cheap:

```bash
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done
```

**Byte-compile**, because CI does and a rename is exactly what leaves a stale reference:

```bash
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
```

A warning naming `cerebro--end-session` called with the wrong number of arguments is a real finding
here, not noise. Remove the `.elc` afterwards if one is produced in the tree
(`git status` must be clean of it — `emacs/cerebro.elc` is a build artifact).

**No suite covers the Markdown.** The two skill loops are checked by hand, per *Validation*.

## User-facing decisions

The fleet view is the navigator's own interface, so one question in this bead was theirs.

**Asked: `k` is becoming a full session-end. What should it do to a stop flag set earlier with `f`?**

- **Chosen — leave the flag.** `f` then `k` reads as "finish; no, stop now, and stay gone". The row
  reads `dead` with the flag still shown, and the name does not come back until the navigator presses
  `s`, which already clears a stale flag and reports `"%s: cleared a stale stop flag"`
  (cerebro.el:2185). No new message is needed anywhere.
- **Rejected — clear the flag, as `retire` does.** It would make `k` a clean slate, but it silently
  discards an instruction the navigator gave deliberately: a name they meant to keep down would look
  ordinary again, with nothing on the row to say the flag had been dropped. This is ah-kgc's failure
  with the sign reversed, and an implementer meeting this fork must not re-decide it — the
  `clear-stop-flag` argument is deliberately opt-in for exactly this reason.

No mockup: the surface is two keypresses and a row that already exists, with no layout, wording or
new string in it. **No user-visible string is added or changed by this bead** — the only message in
the changed paths is the existing "cleared a stale stop flag", quoted above and left alone.

One behaviour the navigator will notice and which follows from the fix rather than being a choice:
**after `k`, the row reads `dead` immediately** instead of holding whatever the dead session last
wrote. That is the bug being fixed, and the alternative is the phantom row the bead was filed for.

## Out of scope

- **The stranded claim, worktree and open PR** that `cerebro-kill`'s `kill-working` prompt warns
  about (cerebro.el:2225). Killing mid-bead still leaves all three for the navigator; this bead
  removes the *state file*, not the bead's claim. Do not add a `bd unclaim` here.
- **`cerebro--session-alive-p` itself** (cerebro.el:1042). It is already the right shape and is the
  rule the new script mirrors; leave it, its docstring and its tests untouched.
- **Any other liveness check.** `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`, `scripts/sweep-claims.sh` and
  `scripts/sweep-epics.sh` contain no pid check at all (`grep -rn 'kill -0' .` finds only the two
  skill sites), so nothing there needs converting and nothing there should be reorganised on the way
  past.
- **The other five skills and the six agent definitions.** Only `plan-bead` reads a pid.
- **A `--json` or verbose mode on `agent-alive`.** Exit status is the whole interface; the loops that
  need the bead read it with `jq` themselves.
- **Retiring `scripts/implementer-state`**, the deprecation shim. It is exercised by
  `tests/agent-state.sh` and is not this bead's business.

## Validation

From the submodule root, `.claude/cerebro/`:

```bash
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el   # no new warnings
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done
grep -rn 'kill -0' . | grep -v '^./.git'                        # must print nothing
grep -n "'cerebro--end-session" emacs/cerebro-test.el           # must print nothing
```

From the `atlantis-hud` worktree root, for increment 4:

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
git diff --stat HEAD~1     # one line, .claude/cerebro only
```

**The one check only a person can make**, and it is worth doing because no test drives real vterm
sessions: in the Emacs fleet view, with an implementer up —

1. Press `f` on it, confirm the row shows the stop instruction.
2. Press `k` and confirm the kill. The row must go to `dead`, **the stop flag must still be shown**,
   and `.cerebro/state/<Name>.state.json` must be gone (`ls .cerebro/state/`).
3. Press `s` on the same row. It must report `"<Name>: cleared a stale stop flag"` and launch.
4. With a planner running, `bash -c 'source the two loops from skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md'` — or
   simply run the loop bodies by hand — and confirm `n` counts the live planner and the abandoned-label
   check lists nothing held by a dead one.

Steps 1–3 are the whole of the navigator's decision, exercised end to end. Ask them for it; do not
mark the bead done on the suites alone.

## Known traps

- **Two repositories.** `emacs/`, `scripts/` and `skills/` are the `cerebro` submodule
  (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git`); only the gitlink bump is `atlantis-hud`. A commit in
  the wrong one looks right locally and does not exist for anybody else. Branch inside
  `<your worktree>/.claude/cerebro` for increments 1–3, open the PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`, and
  only then make the bump commit in the outer tree. ah-gdp's plan and db719aa/ba6510b are the
  precedent for the pair.
- **Both PRs need the second pair of eyes, and neither request is automatic.** Request Copilot on the
  `cerebro` PR the moment it opens (`gh pr edit <n> --repo rmstdope/cerebro --add-reviewer @copilot`)
  and on the `atlantis-hud` bump PR likewise — one request each, never re-requested after a fix or a
  rebase. `--add-reviewer Copilot` without the `@` errors with "Could not resolve user". Merge each
  with `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`, never `--auto`.
- **The stub migration in increment 1 is where this bead can go green while broken.** Five existing
  tests stub the session-ender out in order to assert on the flag or the state file. If those stubs
  are pointed at the *new* `cerebro--end-session`, the removal under test is stubbed away and the
  assertion passes vacuously. They must stub `cerebro--forget-session`. The grep in *Validation*
  (`'cerebro--end-session` in the test file) is the mechanical guard.
- **`ps -o args=` needs the trailing `=`.** Without it `ps` prints a header, so `args` is non-empty
  even for a pid that does not exist, and every dead session reads alive. CI runs the bash suites on
  ubuntu-latest while you develop on macOS — `ps -o args= -p <pid>` is correct on both, but
  `ps -p <pid> -o command` and `pgrep`-based variants are not portable here. A suite that only
  passes on macOS is a red PR (submodule `CLAUDE.md`).
- **The word boundary in the args match is not optional.** `cerebro--name-in-args-p` uses `\_>` for
  it; bash has no equivalent, hence the explicit `([[:space:]]|$)`. Without it, one roster name that
  is a prefix of another silently reads as alive.
- **`consumer-root --shared`, never bare `consumer-root`.** From a bead worktree's own submodule copy
  the bare answer is the worktree, so the script would look for state files in a directory the fleet
  never writes to and report every agent dead (ah-e0w). `scripts/agent-state`:113-116 has the comment
  to copy.
- **`grep` under `set -e`.** A non-matching `grep` exits 1 and would abort the script before the
  intended `exit 1`, which is the same status by luck rather than by design — and would be the wrong
  status if the logic ever grows. Guard every `grep`/`ps` with an explicit `|| exit 1`.
- **`chmod +x scripts/agent-alive`.** The suite invokes it through a symlink under `bash`, which
  works either way; the skill's loop invokes it directly, which does not. Check
  `git ls-files -s scripts/agent-alive` shows mode `100755`.
- **The deletion must stay before the launch in the `'restart` branch.** The comment at
  cerebro.el:1400-1408 explains why, and `cerebro-test/restart-removes-the-state-file-before-launching`
  pins it. Folding four artifacts into one call makes it easy to move that call after
  `cerebro--launch` while reading; do not.
- **Do not commit `emacs/cerebro.elc`.** The byte-compile in *Validation* produces one in the tree.
- **`.claude/skills/plan-bead` is a directory symlink into the submodule.** Editing
  `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` in the submodule is immediately live for a running planner — including
  the two planners reading it while you work. That is fine and intended; it also means there is no
  `sync-symlinks.sh` step, and running one would be a no-op that dirties nothing but time.
acceptance_criteria: 1. cerebro--end-session is the only site that removes a session's artifacts, and k (cerebro--kill-session-buffer) goes through it: grep finds no other caller of cerebro--delete-state-file or cerebro--clear-stop-flag outside it. 2. Pressing k removes the state file (ERT: kill-removes-the-state-file) and leaves a stop flag set with f (ERT: kill-leaves-the-stop-flag). 3. retire still clears both; restart still deletes the state file before launching — existing ERT tests unchanged and green. 4. scripts/agent-alive exists, mode 100755, and returns 1 for a live pid whose args do not name the agent (tests/agent-alive.sh). 5. grep -rn 'kill -0' over the submodule prints nothing; both plan-bead loops call agent-alive. 6. Byte-compile clean, all ERT green on the suite, every tests/*.sh green. 7. The submodule gitlink is bumped in atlantis-hud in its own chore(ah-bqi) commit. 8. Navigator has run f then k then s in the fleet view and confirmed the flag survived the kill.

title: One script prepares a worktree, so the missing submodule step has an owner
description:
## The cost being paid
Preparing a fresh worktree and launching the desktop shell are written per role in the harness, and the copies disagree with each other and with the call sites — so implementers keep paying for a step another role's text already has:
- `git worktree add` does not initialise the `.claude/cerebro` submodule. Five implementers in five beads hit it (ah-4ao 5 min, ah-aao 10 min plus a detached superproject HEAD, ah-axj 5 min, ah-30t 2 min, ah-brd 2 min — where the first `agent-state` write failed "No such file or directory" because the empty submodule has no scripts at all), and each retrospective recommends the same one line, `git submodule update --init --recursive`, in implement-bead's *Workspace* section. On bbfa374 that section is still `fetch` / `worktree add` / `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; `agents/verifier.md:212` (Psylocke's own worktree block) already has the line.
- A fresh worktree has no wasm build, and the first `test:smoke` fails on `Could not resolve "./wasm/atlantis_core.js"` (ah-o1t.3, 5 min). verifier.md:233 and :253-255 warm `build:wasm`; implement-bead §Workspace does not name it.
- verifier.md:251's desktop launch, `pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev`, lacks `--features desktop-runtime`, which every other call site that builds the real binary passes (ci.yml, release.yml); followed exactly, it builds the stub `main` that exits at once — one cold Tauri build thrown away and the navigator summoned to look at nothing (ah-wxk.1-verifier).
Roughly 30 minutes across six retrospectives, and each was told "record it again" rather than fixed, because no role owns the shared procedure.

## Evidence
- docs/retrospectives/ah-4ao.md §"A fresh implementer worktree does not carry an initialized submodule"; ah-aao.md §"A fresh worktree's submodule checkout silently operated on the wrong repo again"; ah-axj.md §"A fresh implementer worktree still does not carry an initialized submodule"; ah-30t.md §"A fresh implementer worktree leaves `.claude/cerebro` uninitialized, again"; ah-brd.md §"A fresh worktree's uninitialized `.claude/cerebro` submodule broke the first `agent-state` write"
- docs/retrospectives/ah-o1t.3.md §"A fresh worktree has no wasm build, and `test:smoke` fails with an error that reads unrelated"
- docs/retrospectives/ah-wxk.1-verifier.md §"Launching the desktop dev build without `--features desktop-runtime` runs the stub `main`"
- .claude/cerebro @ bbfa374: skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md §Workspace (the `worktree add` / `pnpm install` block); agents/verifier.md:212, :233, :251-255

## Where
.claude/cerebro/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md §Workspace; .claude/cerebro/agents/verifier.md §Preparing; (possibly) .claude/cerebro/scripts — a `prepare-worktree` step the roles share

## What a refactoring would change
One workspace-preparation procedure — a script under `.claude/cerebro/scripts` (worktree add, submodule init, `pnpm install`, `build:wasm` when the browser suites will run) that implement-bead and verifier.md both call, or at minimum one section both texts point at; and one desktop launch line, with the feature flag, wherever the desktop shell is started by a role. Then a retrospective's "add this line to the skill" has one place to land. Not a plan: a planner plans it.

Filed by Forge, daily sweep of 2026-08-17, range b2188b2..a19f579 (harness 8bee269..bbfa374).
design:
## Context

Preparing a worktree is written out per role, and the copies disagree. Five implementers in five
beads lost 2–10 minutes each to the same missing line — `git worktree add` does not initialise the
`.claude/cerebro` submodule, so the first `agent-state` write fails with *"No such file or
directory"* and the scripts the role needs are simply absent — and every retrospective recommended
the same fix to `implement-bead`'s *Workspace* section, which still does not have it. Psylocke's
`agents/verifier.md:212` has had the line for some time. Roughly 30 minutes across six
retrospectives, each answered with "record it again" because no role owns the shared procedure.

This bead gives it an owner: **one script both roles call.**

**All of it lives in the `.claude/cerebro` submodule**, which is its own repository
(`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git`). Nothing in `atlantis-hud` changes except the submodule
pointer. See *The two repositories* below — getting that wrong is the one way this bead can waste an
afternoon.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The script — `scripts/prepare-worktree` (new, in the cerebro repo)

`scripts/launch-preflight` is the model for style: `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, a
header comment saying what it owns and why, a `usage:` block, and `exit 2` with one line on stderr
for a usage error.

```
usage: prepare-worktree --path <dir> [--branch <name>] [--from <ref>] [--with-wasm]
```

- `--path <dir>` — where the worktree goes. Required. Must be under `.cerebro/worktrees/`; refuse
  anything else with the reason (`bd` and cargo walk up for their configuration, so a worktree
  outside the repository silently gets its own empty bead database and its own multi-gigabyte build
  directory).
- `--branch <name>` — **a fresh per-bead tree**, which is what an implementer wants:
  `git worktree add -b <name> <path> <ref>`. If `<path>` already exists, **fail** rather than reuse
  it: an implementer reusing another bead's tree is how work gets lost.
- no `--branch` — **the reusable detached tree**, which is what Psylocke wants. Create it with
  `git worktree add --detach <path> <ref>` when absent; when present, bring it to `<ref>` the way
  `verifier.md:209-211` already does: `fetch`, `reset --hard`, `clean -fd`. **Only in this mode**,
  and only when the tree is detached — a `reset --hard` on a branch worktree would destroy an
  implementer's bead, so check `git -C <path> symbolic-ref -q HEAD` and refuse if it names a branch.
- `--from <ref>` — defaults to `origin/main`. The script always `git fetch origin main` first.

Then, in **both** modes and in this order:

1. `git -C <path> submodule update --init --recursive` — the missing line, and the whole reason this
   bead exists.
2. `(cd <path> && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)` — a fresh worktree has no `node_modules`, so the
   first `pnpm run lint` otherwise fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the bead.
3. `--with-wasm` only: `(cd <path> && pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core build:wasm)`.

Finally print, on stdout, the path and `git -C <path> rev-parse --short HEAD` — the sha is what
Psylocke's text already tells her to say out loud, and an implementer wants to know what it branched
from.

**`--with-wasm` is a flag rather than always-on** (the navigator's decision): most beads never run
the browser suites, and a wasm build is minutes of cold cache to pay on every worktree. The flag is
named where it is needed — beside the smoke instructions — rather than in the general procedure.

### `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md` — the *Workspace* section

Replace the `fetch` / `worktree add` / `pnpm install` block with one call:

```bash
.claude/cerebro/scripts/prepare-worktree --path .cerebro/worktrees/<id> --branch <id>-short-description
cd .cerebro/worktrees/<id>
```

and keep, unchanged, everything around it that is not about creating the tree: the disk preflight,
the "never check out main" reasoning, the rule that worktrees live under `.cerebro/worktrees/`, the
`pwd` warning, and the port block. The prose that explained *why* `pnpm install` is not optional
becomes a sentence about what the script does, not an instruction to run it — the reason is still
worth knowing when it fails.

In the same file's smoke/browser-suite instructions, name `--with-wasm`: *"a fresh worktree has no
wasm build and the first `test:smoke` fails on `Could not resolve "./wasm/atlantis_core.js"` — pass
`--with-wasm` when you prepared the tree, or run `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core build:wasm`
now."*

### `agents/verifier.md` — the *Preparing* section

The "once" block and the "before EVERY verification" block (`:205-214`) both become:

```bash
.claude/cerebro/scripts/prepare-worktree --path .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke --with-wasm
```

which creates the tree when it is missing and resets it when it is not — which is exactly what those
two blocks say in eleven lines today. `--with-wasm` because a verification always ends in a running
application, and `:233` and `:251-255` already insist the warm build happen *after* the reset: the
script does them in that order, which is what makes the warm build the right build.

**And the desktop launch line at `:251`** — `pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev` — gains
the feature every other call site passes:

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev --features desktop-runtime
```

Without it the stub `main` is built, which exits at once: one cold Tauri build thrown away and the
navigator summoned to look at nothing (`ah-wxk.1-verifier`). `release.yml:114`, `:194` and `:241`
all pass `--features desktop-runtime`, and `ci.yml:419` explains why. The navigator chose not to
wrap the desktop launch in a script of its own, so this is a one-line correction in place.

### Nothing else calls it

`run-implementer`, `run-psylocke` and the other launchers start sessions; they do not make
worktrees, and none of them changes.

## The two repositories

This is the part to get right before writing any code:

1. **The work is a PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`**, the submodule's own repository — the script, both
   role texts, all of it. Branch from that repo's `main`, inside `.claude/cerebro`.
2. **Then `atlantis-hud` gets a submodule bump**: `.claude/cerebro` moves to the new sha and is
   committed on its own. The convention is already established — `git log --oneline -- .claude/cerebro`
   shows `chore: bump cerebro` three times, each a one-line diff touching nothing else.
3. The bead is done when both have merged. A bumped pointer to an unmerged branch is a checkout
   nobody else can reproduce.

Check `pwd` constantly here: `git` inside `.claude/cerebro` is one repository and one directory up is
another.

## Increments

1. **The script exists and makes a fresh tree.**
   RED: run it by hand in a scratch path with `--branch`, and confirm the tree appears with
   `.claude/cerebro/scripts/` populated and `node_modules` present — the two things whose absence
   cost the five retrospectives. There is no test harness for these scripts; the check is running it.
   GREEN: the script, through step 2.

2. **It resets the reusable tree and refuses to reset a branch.**
   RED: run it twice without `--branch` on the same path and confirm the second run resets rather
   than fails; then run it without `--branch` against a path holding a branch worktree and confirm it
   **refuses**, naming the branch.
   GREEN: the detached-only guard.

3. **It refuses what it should.**
   RED: a path outside `.cerebro/worktrees/`; `--branch` onto an existing path; no `--path`. Each
   exits 2 with one line on stderr.
   GREEN: the argument checks.

4. **`--with-wasm` warms the build.**
   RED: a tree prepared without it fails `test:smoke` on `Could not resolve "./wasm/atlantis_core.js"`;
   with it, that resolution succeeds.
   GREEN: step 3.

5. **The two role texts call it**, and the desktop line gains its feature flag.

6. **The bump.** Merge the cerebro PR, then bump `.claude/cerebro` in `atlantis-hud`.

## The test plan

**There is no automated suite for `.claude/cerebro/scripts`** — `launch-preflight`,
`prune-worktrees.sh` and the rest are covered by being run. So the test plan is a walk, and it must
actually be walked:

| Walk | Expect |
|---|---|
| `--path .cerebro/worktrees/zzz-test --branch zzz-test` | tree created on `origin/main`; `zzz-test/.claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state` exists and runs; `node_modules` present |
| the same command again | fails, naming the existing path |
| `--path .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke` twice | first creates detached, second fetches, resets and cleans; a file touched in between is gone after the second |
| the same, against a branch worktree | refuses, naming the branch, and **leaves the tree untouched** |
| `--path /tmp/elsewhere --branch x` | exits 2, says worktrees live under `.cerebro/worktrees/` |
| no arguments | exits 2 with the usage line |
| `--with-wasm`, then `pnpm run test:smoke` in that tree | no `Could not resolve "./wasm/atlantis_core.js"` |
| `tauri dev --features desktop-runtime` in a prepared tree | a window opens and stays open, rather than the stub exiting at once |

Remove the scratch worktrees afterwards (`git worktree remove --force`, then `git worktree prune`).

**In `atlantis-hud` itself**: nothing to run. The superproject change is a submodule pointer, and
`pnpm run check:fast` there is unaffected — but run it once after the bump anyway, because a bump is
the one change that can alter what every agent's tooling does.

## User-facing decisions

**None a player sees.** This is harness text and a script; no application code changes and nothing
reaches the interface.

Two **workflow** decisions were the navigator's, since CLAUDE.md reserves changes to the workflow
itself to them, and both were taken on 2026-08-17:

- **A script the roles call**, rather than one shared section both texts point at. The reason for the
  script over the prose: a retrospective's "add this step" then has exactly one place to land and
  cannot drift, which is the finding. Rejected: the shared section (still hand-run, still
  copyable-wrong — how the copies drifted in the first place); and additionally scripting the
  desktop launch, which stays a one-line fix in `verifier.md`.
- **`--with-wasm` is a flag**, not always-on. Rejected: always warming it (a slow build on every
  worktree, including the many that only touch Rust or docs) and leaving it out entirely (the trap
  stays one step further away).

## Out of scope

- **The disk preflight**, the port block and the `pwd` warning in `implement-bead`. They are about
  starting work, not about making a tree, and they stay as prose.
- **`prune-worktrees.sh`**, which removes trees and is already shared.
- **Any launcher.** `run-implementer` and friends start sessions and do not make worktrees.
- **A script for the desktop launch**, explicitly declined by the navigator.
- **The wasm build's own speed.** It is slow; that is a different bead if it is a bead at all.
- **`ah-gdp`'s disk finding**, which is about `target/` trees and is its own bead.

## Validation

The walks in *The test plan*, run in order, and then:

```bash
# in .claude/cerebro
git status                # the PR's diff: one new script, two edited texts
# in atlantis-hud, after the cerebro PR merges
git submodule update --remote .claude/cerebro
git add .claude/cerebro && git commit -m "chore: bump cerebro"
pnpm run check:fast
```

The check a human must make: **start one real implementer against a real bead** and watch its first
`agent-state` write succeed. That single write failing is what five retrospectives describe, and it
is the only proof that matters.

## Known traps

- **Two repositories.** The script and the texts are a PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`; `atlantis-hud`
  only moves a pointer. A `git commit` in the wrong one produces a change that looks right locally
  and does not exist for anybody else.
- **`reset --hard` must never touch a branch worktree.** Psylocke's tree is detached and reusable;
  an implementer's carries a bead's work. The mode without `--branch` is the resetting one, and it
  must refuse a tree whose HEAD is a branch. Getting this wrong destroys work with no warning.
- **A script cannot `cd` its caller.** `prepare-worktree` prints the path; the role's text still says
  `cd` on the next line.
- **The submodule is empty in a fresh worktree** — that is the whole bug, and it means the script
  cannot rely on anything under `<path>/.claude/cerebro` existing before step 1 runs.
- **`--frozen-lockfile` is not optional** and neither is running `pnpm install` from inside the
  worktree; running it from the superproject installs into the wrong tree.
- **`tauri dev` without `--features desktop-runtime` builds a stub that exits at once**, and the cold
  build before it is minutes. `release.yml:114` is the call site to copy.
- **`launch-preflight` already checks the submodule for launchers** and is a good read before
  starting: it shows the house style for exit codes and stderr, and what a role expects to be there.
close_reason: Delivered in rmstdope/cerebro#49 (scripts/prepare-worktree, both role texts updated) and rmstdope/atlantis-hud#369 (submodule bump).

title: SAIL orders preview like MOVE, carrying the fleet's passengers and hull
description:
## The cost being paid
ah-p1p was filed because "the movement-order words" were spelt in five places and a SAIL added in four of them (962fbe4) left the fifth reader disagreeing with the trace. Its delivery, e69f586, made `MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS` / `is_movement_command` the one list and fixed the reader Bishop cited (intents.rs) — and did not touch `crates/core/src/orders/effects.rs`, whose `read_order` still spells `command.is("move") || command.is("advance")` by hand. So on origin/main the consolidation left the same concept in two places, and the leftover copy carries the divergence the bead was filed for: a unit ordered `SAIL` is counted as leaving by `semantics::leaves_the_hex` (`Intent::Sail`) and drawn leaving by the tracer, but previewed as `Present` rather than `Departing` by the unit preview effects.rs produces for the panel. Cost paid: the ah-p1p bead itself (a five-reader walk and one reader missed); the sixth reader is the same shape, unpaid only because nobody has yet reported the preview.

## Evidence

- e69f586 refactor(ah-p1p): advisory codes and movement words come from core; a SAIL order counts as leaving (#322) — 16 files, effects.rs absent

title: Refactoring: one function decides whether a saved unit's orders end in a newline
description:
## The cost being paid
The unit editor mishandling its own trailing newline is the same defect fixed four times. Bishop's ah-vfr named three (9420c54, 949c6a6, 279bffd — one of them visible only as a CI flake) and was delivered as 0f0fc3e; inside that very PR the Copilot review found the fourth: the tidy effect that re-adds the newline after a save re-ran only on `savedAt`/`unitId`, so an external write (an import, a route) landing while the document was saved spliced in an untidied block, and a fixup commit put `externalRevision` in its dependency list. What remains on origin/main is the compensator ah-vfr did not remove: `writeUnitOrders` drops the trailing blank line from the block (`withoutTrailingBlankLines`), and the editor puts it back with a `useEffect` keyed on `[savedAt, externalRevision, unitId]` whose comment relies on declaration order ("Effects run in the order they are declared, so the reload above has already applied by the time this one reads the doc"). The document and the editor disagree about whether a saved unit's text ends in a newline, and every path that writes the document from outside the editor has to remember to poke the tidy.

## Evidence
- 0f0fc3e refactor(ah-vfr): the orders editor is never handed its own text back (#311) — body ("fixed three times in three days, once visible only as a CI flake") and its fixup "fix(ah-vfr): re-tidy the trailing newline on any external write while saved"
- bead ah-vfr §Evidence: 9420c54 fix(#37) ("a newline typed at the end of a block was swallowed"), 949c6a6 feat(orders): end a saved unit draft with a trailing newline, 279bffd feat(#89) sub-commits
- origin/main: packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx:247-270 (the tidy effect and its comment); packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts:84-90 (`draftAfterSave`); packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:103-114 (`writeUnitOrders` → `withoutTrailingBlankLines`)

## Where
packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts; packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts; packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx (reload and tidy effects)

## What a refactoring would change
One answer to "does a unit's saved text end in a newline" that the document and the editor share — either the block boundary carries it, or the editor's view of a block is derived from the document by one function on every path (reload and save alike) rather than by a second effect that must run after the first. Then the tidy effect and its dependency list go, and the four fixes have nowhere left to recur. Not a plan: a planner plans it.

design:
## Context

Whether a saved unit's orders end in a newline is answered in two places that must agree, and keeping
them in step has now been fixed four times.

The document deliberately does **not** carry it: `writeUnitOrders`
(`packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:102`) drops trailing blank lines through
`withoutTrailingBlankLines`, because a blank line written into a block would sit above the next write
instead of being replaced by it, and every line the player opened would leave one behind for good.
The editor **does** show it, once a save has landed — `draftAfterSave`
(`packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts:88`), applied by a `useEffect` in `OrdersEditor.tsx:258` keyed on
`[savedAt, externalRevision, unitId]`.

That effect is the compensator. It has to name `externalRevision` because an import or a route landing
while the document is already saved splices the block in untidied (the fourth fix, a Copilot finding
inside ah-vfr's own PR), and its comment then rests on a rule nobody can see from the call site:
*"Effects run in the order they are declared, so the reload above has already applied by the time this
one reads the doc."* Every future path that writes the document from outside has to remember to poke
it, and the ordering it depends on is invisible to whoever reorders the effects.

After this bead **one function** answers the question, every path that puts text into the editor goes
through it, and the tidy effect no longer depends on another effect having run first. Behaviour is
unchanged — this is a refactoring, and the two Playwright tests named below are the proof.

Fixes so far, for the record: 9420c54 (#37), 949c6a6, 279bffd (#89), and 0f0fc3e (ah-vfr, #311) with
its fixup "re-tidy the trailing newline on any external write while saved".

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts`

`draftAfterSave` (line 88) is **replaced** by the one function that owns the answer. One exported
name, not two:

```ts
/**
 * The text the editor should show for a unit: its block as the document holds it, ended with the
 * newline an orders file ends with once the document has landed on disk.
 *
 * The single answer to "does a saved unit's text end in a newline". The document's block boundary
 * neither holds nor needs it - `writeUnitOrders` (ordersDocument.ts:102) drops trailing blank lines
 * so an opened line cannot accumulate - so the editor is the only place the two differ, and every
 * path that puts text into the editor goes through here. That is what replaced a second effect
 * which had to run after the reload and had to be told about every source of an external write.
 *
 * Idempotent, and safe on the editor's own document: text already ending in a newline comes back
 * unchanged, an unsaved unit comes back unchanged, and an empty draft stays empty rather than
 * gaining a blank line the player never opened.
 */
export function shownUnitText(text: string, savedAt: string | null): string {
  if (savedAt === null || text === "" || text.endsWith("\n")) {
    return text;
  }
  return `${text}\n`;
}
```

`savedAt` is `string | null`, matching `OrdersEditorProps.savedAt`
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx:43`) — not a number.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx`

Four edits, and the deletion of a paragraph:

1. **The `latest` ref** (lines 106–107) gains `savedAt`, so both effects and the creation path can read
   the current value without adding it to a dependency list:
   `useRef({ text, ariaLabel, savedAt, commands, … })`, and the same on the assignment line below it.
2. **Creation** (line 118): `doc: shownUnitText(latest.current.text, latest.current.savedAt)`. A saved
   unit browsed to now opens tidied, instead of opening untidied and being fixed by an effect a moment
   later.
3. **The external-write effect** (lines 231–243): the target becomes
   `shownUnitText(latest.current.text, latest.current.savedAt)` — everything else, including
   `minimalChange`, the `External`/`addToHistory` annotations and the dependency list
   `[externalRevision, unitId]`, is untouched. Add one sentence to its comment: the text it splices in
   is already what the editor should show, so nothing runs after it to finish the job.
4. **The tidy effect** (lines 258–270): the dependency list becomes `[savedAt, unitId]`, and the body
   measures its own document through the same function:

```ts
  // Once a save has landed, the shown text ends with the newline an orders file ends with. In the
  // editor only: the block boundary neither holds nor needs it, so the document is not written
  // (External, and not history either). An append at the end never moves a caret that is anywhere
  // else - what persistence.spec pins.
  useEffect(() => {
    const editor = view.current;
    if (!editor) {
      return;
    }
    const current = editor.state.doc.toString();
    const wanted = shownUnitText(current, savedAt);
    if (wanted !== current) {
      editor.dispatch({
        changes: { from: current.length, to: current.length, insert: "\n" },
        annotations: [External.of(true), Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)]
      });
    }
  }, [savedAt, unitId]);
```

   **Delete the whole `externalRevision`/declaration-order paragraph** (lines 251–257). It is the thing
   this bead exists to remove: an external write while saved is now tidied by the effect that applies
   it, so this one has nothing to say about ordering and must not imply that it does.

5. The `savedAt` prop's doc comment (line 41) names `draftAfterSave`; it becomes `shownUnitText`.

### What must not change

`writeUnitOrders` and `withoutTrailingBlankLines` (`packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:102–114`)
stay exactly as they are, comment included. Making the document carry the newline is the other shape
this could take and it is **rejected**: the block boundary is a line range, and a trailing blank line
inside it is what the comment there describes going wrong.

## Increments

1. **The one function.**
   RED: in `packages/shared/src/orderEditor.test.ts`, rewrite the `describe("tidying the draft after
   a save")` block (lines 97–109) to the four tests named below — they will not compile against
   `draftAfterSave`'s one-argument signature.
   GREEN: `shownUnitText` replaces `draftAfterSave`; the only other reference is
   `OrdersEditor.tsx:9`'s import.
2. **The editor goes through it, everywhere.**
   RED: none available at unit level — `OrdersEditor` is CodeMirror and needs a DOM, and this package
   runs in Node (see *Known traps*). The safety net is the two Playwright tests named below, which
   already pin both halves of the behaviour; run them for this increment rather than adding new ones.
   GREEN: the four edits above and the deleted paragraph.

## The test plan

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `appends the missing newline once the document has been saved` | `packages/shared/src/orderEditor.test.ts` | `shownUnitText("@work\n@study combat", "2026-08-17T…")` ends with `\n` |
| `leaves text already ending in a newline alone` | same | Idempotent, which is what makes it safe on the editor's own doc |
| `leaves an unsaved unit alone, however it ends` | same | `savedAt === null` returns the text unchanged — the case `draftAfterSave` could not express, and the reason the caller used to need an `if` |
| `leaves an empty draft empty rather than opening a blank line` | same | Kept from today |
| (existing) `a saved draft gains its missing trailing newline without moving the cursor` | `tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts:212` | The save path, and the caret — the regression net for edits 2 and 4 |
| (existing) `merging leaves the orders and the selection where they were` | `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:771` | **The fourth fix's own scenario**: an external write landing while the document is saved, asserting `/^@study obse\n@work\n$/u` afterwards. This is what proves the ordering dependency was removable rather than merely hidden |

Suites: `pnpm -r run test` for the unit change, and **the Playwright suite must be run for this bead**
even though `check:fast` does not include it —

```bash
pnpm run test:smoke
```

That is not optional here: the only proof that behaviour is unchanged lives in those two specs.

## User-facing decisions

**None**, and that is a decision in itself. The editor's trailing newline after a save is behaviour
the navigator already has (949c6a6, and `persistence.spec.ts:212` pins it); **this bead must not
change what the player sees**. If the refactoring appears to want the newline to go away, or to appear
before a save lands, stop — that is a user-facing change, it belongs to the navigator, and it is not
this bead.

No mockup; nothing on screen moves.

## Out of scope

- **Making the document carry the trailing newline.** Rejected above, with the reason.
- **When a save lands**, the autosave interval, or `shouldTriggerAutosave` / `shouldSaveOnBlur`.
- **`OrdersOrigin` and the `externalRevision` contract** (`orderEditor.ts:100`). The editor is still
  never handed its own text back; the external-write effect keeps its exact dependency list. Widening
  it would re-open #89, where a lagging copy rewound the text under the player.
- **The unit-description stripping** below `writeUnitOrders` in the same file.
- **Adding a DOM test environment to `@atlantis/shared`** so `OrdersEditor` could be unit-tested. A
  fair idea, a separate bead, and not a refactoring.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke      # required for this bead: it is where the behaviour is pinned
```

Then one read, which is the point of the whole bead: `git grep -n "draftAfterSave"` returns nothing,
and `git grep -n "shownUnitText"` returns `orderEditor.ts`, its test, and exactly three call sites in
`OrdersEditor.tsx` — creation, the external-write effect, the save effect. Any fourth path into the
editor that does not go through it is the defect coming back.

## Known traps

- **`@atlantis/shared` runs vitest in Node with no config**, so there is no DOM and `OrdersEditor`
  cannot be unit-tested at all. Do not go looking for a component test to change, and do not add jsdom
  to get one — the Playwright specs are the net here, by design.
- **`pnpm run check:fast` does not run Playwright.** For most beads that is right; for this one it
  would mean merging a behaviour change with nothing that could have caught it. Run `test:smoke`.
- **`savedAt` is a `string | null`, not a number** (`OrdersEditor.tsx:43`). A signature taking `number`
  compiles against a truthiness check and then quietly never tidies.
- **The tidy effect dispatches an append at `current.length`, never a whole-document replacement.**
  `persistence.spec.ts:212` parks the caret mid-word specifically to catch a replacement; keep the
  `changes: { from: current.length, to: current.length, insert: "\n" }` shape even though
  `shownUnitText` now hands you the wanted string.
- **Reading `savedAt` through `latest.current` in the external-write effect is deliberate.** Putting it
  in that effect's dependency list would make a save re-splice the document's copy over the editor's
  own newer text — the rewind #89 fixed. The ref is how the effect sees the current value without
  being triggered by it.
- **`smoke` and `pwa` share a gate lock** (`scripts/withGateLock.ts`); run them one at a time.

title: Refactoring: a test helper lets a static render see non-default store state
description:
## The cost being paid
`renderToStaticMarkup` (the only renderer this project's tests have) reads a zustand store through `getInitialState()`, not `getState()`, so a test cannot show a component with anything but the store's defaults. That trap has been rediscovered per test file and solved two different ways: a `vi.mock` of the store hook (4107920 ah-3cs in UnitTableDock.test.tsx, copied by 581dabc ah-m9q.2 into SettingsDialog.test.tsx, removed again from UnitTableDock by 3d44bf1 ah-2r3), then, unaware of those, a test-only seam in a production module — `setHexNotesStateForTest` in hexNotesStore.ts mutates the object `getInitialState()` returns (7ee0aa5 ah-o1t.2). ah-o1t.2's retrospective prices the rediscovery at ~20 minutes and records "Seen before: None found", although two test files had already worked around it that week. SettingsDialog.test.tsx:9-10 still says "see `UnitTableDock.test.tsx` for the same trap" — a file that no longer carries it. Thirty test files render with `renderToStaticMarkup`; every next component that reads a store in a non-default state pays this again, in whichever of the two ways its author finds first.

## Evidence
- docs/retrospectives/ah-o1t.2.md §"`renderToStaticMarkup` can never see a zustand store's non-default state via `.setState(...)`" (Cost: ~20 minutes; Prevent by: the seam now on file)
- 4107920 feat(ah-3cs) (#236) — `vi.mock("../settingsStore", …)` added to UnitTableDock.test.tsx; 581dabc feat(ah-m9q.2) (#255) — same mock copied into SettingsDialog.test.tsx; 3d44bf1 feat(ah-2r3) (#265) — removed from UnitTableDock.test.tsx; 7ee0aa5 feat(ah-o1t.2) (#272) — `setHexNotesStateForTest` in hexNotesStore.ts
- origin/main: packages/shared/src/hexNotesStore.ts:130-147; packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx:6-24 (the dangling cross-reference)

## Where
packages/shared/src/hexNotesStore.ts; packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx; packages/shared/src/workspace/RegionNotes.test.tsx; every zustand store under packages/shared/src (workspaceStore, settingsStore, hexNotesStore) and the tests that render against them

## What a refactoring would change
One test helper, in one place, that renders a component against a store in a given state under `renderToStaticMarkup` — whether by writing through both `setState` and `getInitialState()` for any store, or by a `renderWithStore` that mocks the hook — so no production module carries a test seam and no test file re-derives the trap. Replace the two existing workarounds with it and fix the cross-reference. Not a plan: a planner plans it.
