## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-16 against three mockups; the chosen state is committed as
`docs/ui/order-argument-completion.html` (PR #344).

**Q1 — which argument positions get a popup.** Chosen: **everything the ruleset closes, in two
beads** — closed keyword lists, directions and the 22 item classes here; the ruleset's 171 items and
96 skills in `ah-bai.2`. Rejected: closed keyword lists only (leaves `MOVE`, the most typed order in
the game, unhelped); keywords and directions but no item classes (they are already in the grammar and
cost nothing); everything in one bead (too big for one increment, and the catalogue needs a loaded
ruleset where none of this does).

**Q2 — when the popup opens.** Chosen: **quiet until a letter is typed**, with
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd> summoning it on an empty position — the same rule the command
position already follows. Rejected: opening as soon as the space after the command is typed; it
teaches the shape of an order without being asked, at the price of a panel over the line at every
space, in a rail that is often 150px wide.

**Q3 — nothing matches what is typed** (`NAME XY`). Chosen: **silence**. The checker underlines the
line a moment later in the margin and the diagnostics strip, and the popup adds nothing to that.
Rejected: listing every keyword valid at the position as a correction — it leaves a popup hanging
over a line that is being typed rather than fixed.

**Q4 — what accepts an entry.** Chosen: **<kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unchanged** — one rule
across the editor, accepting the known cost that with a popup open the first <kbd>Enter</kbd> takes
the entry instead of ending the line (most noticeable on `MOVE N`, where the text inserted is the
text already typed and the keystroke is simply eaten). Rejected: <kbd>Tab</kbd>-only in argument
positions (two accept keys in one editor); <kbd>Tab</kbd>-only everywhere (changes the command
position too, for a problem the command position does not have).

**Q5 — what accepting leaves on the line.** Chosen: **the word and a trailing space, everywhere** —
`NAME U` + <kbd>Enter</kbd> gives `NAME UNIT `, and accepting a command now gives `STUDY ` where it
gave `STUDY`. Rejected: the bare word; a trailing space in argument positions only, which would have
left the editor with two rules. Accepted consequence: completing a word in the middle of a line can
leave two spaces, which the lexer skips (`lexer.rs:111`) so the orders file means exactly the same
thing.

**Q6 — the order entries sit in.** Chosen: **the ruleset's own order**, kept with `sortText`: `MOVE`
offers `N NE SE S SW NW IN OUT`, clockwise from north as a report writes its exits; `NAME` offers
`UNIT FACTION OBJECT CITY` as the rules page lists them. Rejected: alphabetical, which is
CodeMirror's default tie-break and puts the compass out of order (`IN N NE NW OUT S SE SW`). Typing
still wins over declared order — `MOVE S` puts `S` first either way.

**Q7 — what an entry shows.** Chosen: **the bare word, with `type: "keyword"`** — the same icon a
command gets, no `detail`. An argument popup and a command popup never appear in the same position,
so looking alike costs nothing. Rejected: a hint naming the form the entry belongs to
(`ALL — ALL [item]`), which needs a hand-written line per keyword in the grammar table and a wider
popup.

**Q8 — where an item class and an item are both valid** (`GIVE 4573 ALL `). Chosen: **one flat list,
classes first**, which is what this bead produces on its own and what `ah-bai.2` must preserve when
it appends the catalogue. Rejected: two labelled CodeMirror sections (chrome in an already tall
popup, and a heading that shows when its group has filtered down to nothing); holding the catalogue
back until two letters are typed (a rule the player has to discover).

**Q9 — the item classes' own order.** Chosen: **alphabetical**, the single exception to Q6: 22
unfamiliar words is past the point where a list in an unfamiliar order can be scanned. Rejected:
the rules page's order (`NORMAL, ADVANCED, TRADE, MAN, MEN, MONSTER…`), which keeps singular beside
plural but is unscannable at that length.

No string is added to the interface by this bead: every word the popup shows is a keyword out of the
ruleset, and there is no label, message or empty state to write.

## Out of scope

- **Items, skills and spells.** `PRODUCE 5 SI` offers nothing here. That is `ah-bai.2`, which is
  blocked on this bead and will widen `order_argument_completions` and the same completion source.
- **Flags.** `GUARD ` offers nothing, deliberately (Q1's mockup, "what stays quiet").
- **Unit numbers from the report.** `GIVE ` will not offer the units in the hex. The core function
  answers from the grammar alone and takes no report; a completion that knows what is standing here
  is a different feature and is not filed.
- **Anything after `CAST`.** The grammar says `Arg::Skill, Arg::Tail` because the arguments depend on
  the spell, and accept-on-doubt means it stays that way.
- **Changing what the checker accepts.** This bead adds a reader of `GRAMMAR` and edits no entry in
  it. If a keyword looks wrong while implementing, file a bead; do not fix it here.
- **The snippet source.** Untouched, including by Q5's trailing space.
- **`docs/adapter-api.md`'s per-command reference list.** The five-step checklist at `:77-87` is to
  be followed; no prose entry is owed, since `order_commands` has none.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast     # lint, typecheck, package + tooling + cargo suites, fmt, clippy
pnpm run test:smoke     # a smoke spec changed
```

Then, by eye in the running app (`pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev`, load the g7f95t71 fixture, select
a unit):

- `NAME U` offers `UNIT`; <kbd>Enter</kbd> leaves `NAME UNIT ` with the caret after the space.
- `MOVE ` then <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd> lists `N NE SE S SW NW IN OUT` in that order.
- `MOVE N` shows `N NE NW`; <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it and leaves the text alone.
- `GIVE 4573 ` then <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd> lists `UNIT ALL`.
- `NAME XY` shows nothing; `MOVE N ; go h` shows nothing.
- Accepting `stu` in the command position leaves `STUDY ` — the changed behaviour.

## Known traps

- **`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts:249` pins the command count.** `expect(renames.size).toBe(24)`
  becomes `25` in the same commit as the new `#[cfg_attr(..., tauri::command(...))]`, or the tooling
  suite fails with a number rather than a name.
- **The wasm boundary is checked by string parsing, both ways.** `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts:261`
  holds `CoreWasmModule`'s members equal to `crates/core-wasm`'s `#[wasm_bindgen]` exports by name
  and arity, reading `webCoreAdapter.ts`'s `export type CoreWasmModule = {` block literally. Keep the
  block's shape, and give the member the same name and one parameter.
- **Two fakes are complete by construction and will not compile without the new method:**
  `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts:30` (`fakeAdapter`) and
  `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts:39` (`fakeWasm`). Every other stub client in the
  repo is a `Partial<...> as unknown as CoreClient` and needs nothing.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array**, if the bead is read back with `jq`: index `.[0]`.
- **CodeMirror's default tie-break is alphabetical**, via
  `compareCompletions: (a, b) => (a.sortText || a.label).localeCompare(b.sortText || b.label)`.
  Without `sortText` the declared order is silently lost, and no test that only checks membership
  will notice — which is why the order test asserts the array, not a set.
- **`acceptCompletion` ignores <kbd>Enter</kbd> for 75ms after the popup opens** (its
  `interactionDelay`). The existing smoke test waits 150ms for exactly this reason
  (`tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:135-138`); a new one that types and presses Enter immediately
  will flake.
- **Assert the popup's *selected* option**, `li[aria-selected]`, not merely a listed one: Enter falls
  through to a plain newline until the popup has made a selection, and a test asserting on the list
  alone races it. That comment is at `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:131-134` and cost a flake
  once already.
- **Do not assert trailing whitespace through the DOM.** `ordersText` (`tests/smoke/gameSetup.ts:139`)
  reads rendered line elements; how a trailing space survives that is a CodeMirror detail and differs
  between engines. The unit test on `apply` is where the space is pinned.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped**, so a Chromium-only assertion can
  pass while the native shell is broken. Nothing here should depend on reading text out of a
  narrow popup.
- **`match_arg` takes `&mut Vec<UnknownItem>`** and pushes to it for `Arg::Item` when a ruleset is
  passed. Pass `None` and ignore the vector; do not thread a ruleset into this path, or the answer
  starts depending on a file the desktop may not have loaded.
- **`Arg::Rest` is assumed to be a form's last argument.** True of every entry in `GRAMMAR` today,
  asserted by `every_form_keeps_its_rest_last`, and `debug_assert`ed in `next_argument`. A future
  form with an argument after a `Rest` needs that walk revisited, not a quick patch.

title: The editor helps with the whole order line, not just its first word
description:
Typing `NAME U` offers nothing. The completion popup only ever fires in the command position, so every word after the order name is on the player to remember and spell — including the ones the ruleset fixes to a short closed list, like `NAME UNIT|FACTION|OBJECT|CITY`.

Reported by the navigator: `NAME U` should offer `UNIT`.

This deliberately reverses a limit `orderCompletion.ts` states in its own header ("Only there. Everything after the command is arguments - directions, item names, quantities - and offering TAX inside a half-typed direction would be noise"). That reasoning still holds for open-ended arguments — a unit number, a quantity, a faction's chosen name — and the ask is narrower than the comment assumes: complete the argument positions the ruleset *closes*, and stay silent on the rest.

Where the vocabulary already lives: `crates/core/src/orders/grammar.rs` models argument positions per order (`Arg::OneOf(NAMEABLE)` for NAME, `Arg::Kw("ALL")`, `Arg::OneOf(DESCRIBABLE)` for DESCRIBE, `SPOILS` for the spoils types, and so on). So the closed sets exist and are already the ruleset's own; what is missing is a way to ask the core "what may stand at position n of this order", the way `order_commands()` answers the command position today, and a second CodeMirror completion source beside `orderCommandCompletions`. Keeping the answer on the core side is what stops the popup drifting from the ruleset, which is the reason the first-word vocabulary is fetched rather than hard-coded.

Open, for the navigator to decide when this is planned:
- Which argument kinds are worth completing. Closed keyword lists (`Arg::OneOf`, `Arg::Kw`) are the obvious yes; directions are a small closed set too. Items, skills and spells are large but finite and may deserve their own answer; unit numbers, quantities and free text are clearly no.
- Whether the popup opens on an empty argument position, or only once a letter is typed — the command position stays quiet unless summoned, and the same choice arises here per position.
- Whether a wrong-but-typed argument still offers alternatives, or the popup gives up once what is typed matches nothing.

Acceptance should include the reported case end to end: with the vocabulary loaded, typing `NAME U` in the orders editor offers `UNIT`, and accepting it leaves `NAME UNIT `.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-bai.2, delivered in PR #351

title: Warn when the same FORM number is used twice in a hex this month
description:
Reusing a FORM number inside one unit's order block is accepted silently today. Reported by the navigator, who hit it while writing orders by hand.

What the checker accepts now, without a word:

    FORM 1
      STUDY FORC
    END
    FORM 1
      STUDY FORC
    END
    FORM 1
      STUDY FORC
    END
    FORM 1
      STUDY FORC
    END
    FORM 1
      STUDY FORC
    END

Each FORM n opens a new temporary unit under the issuing unit, and n is the handle the rest of the turn refers to that unit by. Two blocks sharing a number means later references are ambiguous and the orders almost certainly do not do what the player meant - typically a copy-paste of a block whose number was never edited, as above. Nothing in the current checks looks at the numbers as a set, so the mistake reaches the server.

Expected: the order checks notice a FORM number that has already been used by the same unit this turn and say so, naming the number and pointing at the repeated blocks.

Open, for the navigator to decide when this is planned:
- Warning or error? Every existing check in this area warns (see "Warn when a mage cannot pay for the spell it is ordered to cast", "Warn when a fleet is too heavy or too short-crewed to sail"), which argues for a warning - but this one is closer to a certain mistake than to a risky choice.
- What the message says, and whether it names every repeat or only the first.
- Scope: numbers repeated within one unit's orders is the reported case. Whether the same number used by two *different* units is also worth flagging (it is legal - the number is scoped to the issuing unit) is a separate question, and the answer may well be no.
design:
## Context

Reusing a FORM number is accepted silently today. The rules (https://atlantis-pbem.com/rules, the
FORM order): *"pick an alias number (the only restriction on this is that it must be at least 1,
and you should not create two units in the same region in the same month, with the same alias
numbers)"* — the alias is scoped **per region**, and the server refuses the second FORM and its
whole block; every later `NEW n` then means the first unit. The checker's own preview already
models this (`crates/core/src/orders/effects.rs:267–269, 375–379`: aliases keyed by
`(region id, alias)`, a taken alias's block "swallowed rather than applied"), so the truth is in
the codebase and nothing surfaces it. The navigator hit the copy-paste case by hand (five
`FORM 1` blocks under one unit).

Where the pieces are (verified 2026-08-16, `origin/main` at `c120515`):

- **The walk** (`crates/core/src/orders/walk.rs`) reports every `FORM` as `Event::Open { line,
  kind: BlockKind::Form, depth }`, `depth` being the depth *before* it opens (`:60–65, :81–86`);
  the alias is `line.arguments.first()` (a `TokenKind::Number`).
- **The intents** (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`): `read_intents` (`:108–145`) records only
  `Event::Order` at `Depth::default()` into `UnitIntents.intents` as `PlacedIntent { intent, line,
  column_start, column_end }` (`:69–77`); every other event falls to `_ => {}` (`:142`). `Intent`
  (`:19–66`) has no variant for FORM. Only `intents.rs` and `semantics.rs` match on `Intent`.
- **The checks** (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`): `check_turn` (`:142–172`) reads
  `OrderedUnits` once, then per hex builds `Hex { region, units: Vec<Ordered> }` (`:186–232`) and
  runs `check_resources`, `check_guard`, `check_teaching`; findings within a hex are sorted by
  line. `Ordered::finding(hex, code, message, at: Option<&PlacedIntent>)` (`:324–340`) makes a
  finding with the unit, the line and the keyword's columns. Codes live in `codes` (`:64–90`,
  `ALL: [Code; 9]`); `CheckOptions::emits(code)` (`:98–104`) is the on/off. The test module has
  `region(units)`, `unit(id)`, `check(regions, orders)`, `codes(findings)`, `only(findings)`
  (`:1084–1200`), a per-code fixture table asserted against `codes::ALL.len()` (`:2065–2130`) and
  `default_options_disable_only_the_broad_guard_check` (`:1755–1770`).
- **The TypeScript vocabulary** is generated from `codes::ALL` by `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs`
  into `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` (`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`); the settings
  store defaults every code on except `hex-unguarded` and reconciles a stored blob against the
  current list (`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:30–49`, so an existing installation gets the
  new code **on** without a migration); the Warnings tab is `WARNING_GROUPS` in
  `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx:290–345` (groups Teaching / Resources /
  Guarding, each entry `{ code, title, description }`), tested by
  `SettingsDialog.test.tsx:34–80` (every code has a toggle; the titles are listed by hand).
- Two policies every check obeys (`semantics.rs:1–17`): never blocking, accept on doubt.

**Decision.** A new advisory code, `form-alias-reused`, checked per hex in `semantics.rs` from a
new `Intent::Form { alias }` that `read_intents` records for every `FORM` opened outside a TURN
block. One finding **per repeat, on the repeat** (Option A of the mockup), naming the first use;
the first FORM is left alone. Wording, settings group and default as the navigator chose (see
*User-facing decisions*). Chosen mockup: `docs/ui/form-alias-reused.html` (PR #335).

Why semantic and not a parser diagnostic: the scope is the hex, which only the report knows; a
parser-level check would catch one unit's copy-paste and miss the two-units case the rules
name, and would be an *error* in a panel where every judgement about the turn is a warning. The
cost is that with no report loaded nothing is said — the same as every other check.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`

`Intent` gains a variant, documented:

```rust
    /// `FORM n` at this month's depth: the unit is asking for a new unit under alias `n`. Recorded
    /// on the forming unit (the enclosing `unit` block), nested FORMs included, so a check can see
    /// every alias a hex hands out this month. A FORM inside a TURN block is next month's and is
    /// not recorded.
    Form { alias: String },
```

`read_intents` gets one more arm before `_ => {}` (`:142`):

```rust
        Event::Open { line, kind: walk::BlockKind::Form, depth } if depth.turn == 0 => {
            if let (Some(unit), Some(alias)) = (
                units.last_mut(),
                line.arguments.first().filter(|alias| alias.kind == TokenKind::Number),
            ) {
                unit.intents.push(PlacedIntent {
                    intent: Intent::Form { alias: alias.text.clone() },
                    line: line.number,
                    column_start: line.command.column_start,
                    column_end: line.command.column_end,
                });
            }
        }
```

(`use super::walk::{self, Depth, Event}` is already there; `BlockKind` reached as `walk::BlockKind`.
The existing `Event::Order` arm's `depth == Depth::default()` guard is untouched: orders inside a
FORM block still belong to nobody here.) A `FORM` with no numeric alias records nothing — the
syntax checker owns that line.

Tests, in the module's existing style: `a_form_at_this_months_depth_is_recorded_on_the_forming_unit`
(`"unit 5\nFORM 1\nBUY 5 Plainsmen\nEND\n"` → unit 5's intents are exactly
`[Form { alias: "1" }]` at line 2 — the BUY inside the block still is not the unit's, which the
existing test at `:627` already pins); `a_form_inside_a_turn_block_is_not_recorded`
(`"unit 5\nTURN\nFORM 1\nEND\nENDTURN\n"` → no intents); `a_nested_form_is_recorded_too`
(`"unit 5\nFORM 1\nFORM 2\nEND\nEND\n"` → `Form{"1"}`, `Form{"2"}`).

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

- `codes`: `pub const FORM_ALIAS_REUSED: Code = Code("form-alias-reused");` and `ALL: [Code; 10]`
  with it **appended last** (the generated TypeScript copies this order; the settings tab lists the
  new group last).
- `check_turn`: after `check_teaching(...)`, `check_forms(&hex, &options, &mut findings);`.
- The check:

```rust
/// Every FORM in the hex, in document order; each alias after its first use is a block the server
/// will refuse (the alias is per region for the month — see the rules on FORM), and says so on
/// its own line, naming the first use. The first FORM is the one that will exist and is left alone.
fn check_forms(hex: &Hex<'_>, options: &CheckOptions, findings: &mut Vec<Finding>) {
    if !options.emits(codes::FORM_ALIAS_REUSED) {
        return;
    }
    // (alias, forming unit, the FORM's placement), every FORM in the hex, by line.
    let mut forms: Vec<(&str, &Ordered<'_>, &PlacedIntent)> = hex
        .units
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|ordered| {
            ordered.intents.iter().filter_map(move |placed| match &placed.intent {
                Intent::Form { alias } => Some((alias.as_str(), ordered, placed)),
                _ => None,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    forms.sort_by_key(|(_, _, placed)| placed.line);

    let mut first_use: BTreeMap<&str, (&Ordered<'_>, &PlacedIntent)> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (alias, ordered, placed) in forms {
        match first_use.get(alias) {
            None => {
                first_use.insert(alias, (ordered, placed));
            }
            Some((first_unit, first)) => {
                let where_ = if first_unit.unit.unit_id == ordered.unit.unit_id {
                    format!("line {}", first.line)
                } else {
                    format!("unit {} (line {})", first_unit.unit.unit_id, first.line)
                };
                findings.push(ordered.finding(
                    hex,
                    codes::FORM_ALIAS_REUSED,
                    format!("FORM {alias} again: {where_} already forms NEW {alias} in this hex, so this block is refused"),
                    Some(placed),
                ));
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`Ordered.intents` is `&[PlacedIntent]` (`:202–205`); `BTreeMap` is already imported (`:19`). Two hexes are two `Hex`es, so
the same alias in two hexes never meets.

Tests (the module's `check`/`region`/`unit`/`only`/`codes` helpers; `unit("5")` and `unit("7")`
in one `region(...)`; expected messages **verbatim**):

- `a_form_number_used_twice_by_one_unit_warns_on_the_second`:
  `"unit 5\nFORM 1\nSTUDY FORC\nEND\nFORM 1\nSTUDY FORC\nEND\n"` → `only(...)`: code
  `form-alias-reused`, `unit_id == Some("5")`, `line == Some(5)`, message
  `FORM 1 again: line 2 already forms NEW 1 in this hex, so this block is refused`.
- `three_copies_give_two_warnings_each_naming_the_first`: three blocks → two findings, lines 5 and
  8, both messages name `line 2`.
- `two_units_in_one_hex_forming_the_same_number_warn_on_the_second_and_name_the_first_unit`:
  `"unit 5\nFORM 1\nEND\nunit 7\nFORM 1\nEND\n"` → one finding, `unit_id == Some("7")`, `line ==
  Some(5)`, message `FORM 1 again: unit 5 (line 2) already forms NEW 1 in this hex, so this block is refused`.
- `the_same_number_in_two_hexes_is_fine`: two regions (`region(vec![unit("5")])`,
  `region(vec![unit("7")])` — the helper puts every region at (7,53); give the second a different
  `region_id`/`coordinate` the way `a_recipient_outside_the_hex…` at `:1275` does) → `codes(...)`
  is empty.
- `a_form_inside_a_turn_block_is_next_months_and_not_counted`:
  `"unit 5\nFORM 1\nEND\nTURN\nFORM 1\nEND\nENDTURN\n"` → empty.
- `distinct_numbers_are_silent`: `"unit 5\nFORM 1\nEND\nFORM 2\nEND\n"` → empty.
- `a_nested_form_that_repeats_the_outer_alias_is_a_repeat`: `"unit 5\nFORM 1\nFORM 1\nEND\nEND\n"`
  → one finding at line 3 naming line 2.
- The per-code fixture table (`:2065–2130`) gains
  `(codes::FORM_ALIAS_REUSED, vec![region(vec![unit("5")])], "unit 5\nFORM 1\nEND\nFORM 1\nEND\n")`
  — the `cases.len() == codes::ALL.len()` assertion is the RED that opens the bead.
- `default_options_disable_only_the_broad_guard_check` passes unchanged (new code is on).

### `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts`

Regenerated: `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts`.
`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` gains `"form-alias-reused"` last. Never edited by hand.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

`WARNING_GROUPS` (`:290`) gains a fourth group, last:

```ts
  {
    heading: "Orders",
    entries: [
      {
        code: "form-alias-reused",
        title: "Reused FORM numbers",
        description: "Two units formed in the same hex this month with the same NEW number."
      }
    ]
  }
```

The doc comment above it ("grouped Teaching / Resources / Guarding") becomes "… / Guarding / Orders".

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`

`:39` test renamed `"renders one toggle per advisory code, grouped Teaching / Resources / Guarding / Orders"`;
`expect(html).toContain("Orders")`; `"Reused FORM numbers"` appended to `titles`. The
"one toggle per code" loop and the "starts every check on" test cover the new code without edits.

### `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts`, `AppShell.tsx`

Nothing: they iterate `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`. `settingsStore.test.ts:70–98` passes unchanged.

### `docs/ui/README.md`

Already carries the row for `form-alias-reused.html` (PR #335).

## Increments

1. **RED in Rust.** Add the per-code fixture case; `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` fails on
   `codes::FORM_ALIAS_REUSED` not existing (compile) — add the const and `ALL: [Code; 10]`; now the
   fixture test fails because nothing emits it. Add the intents tests (RED) → the `Intent::Form`
   variant and the arm (GREEN). Add the seven semantics tests (RED) → `check_forms` (GREEN).
   `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` — the `generated_ts` test now fails, saying the vocabulary is
   stale: regenerate. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
2. **The Warnings tab.** RED: the renamed settings test with `"Orders"` and the new title; GREEN:
   the group. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`.
3. `pnpm run check:fast`. Then look once: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev` (or the desktop),
   load `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep`, paste the navigator's five
   `FORM 1` blocks under one of your units, and see four warnings on lines 5, 8, 11 and 14 of the
   block, each naming the first; the Warnings tab shows *Orders › Reused FORM numbers*, on.

## The test plan

- Rust (`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`): three intents tests; seven `check_forms` tests; the
  per-code fixture row; `generated_ts` (regenerated); every existing semantics test unchanged.
- TS (`pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test`): `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` as edited;
  `settingsStore.test.ts` unchanged.
- `pnpm run check:fast`. The smoke suite has no settings-tab title assertion (grep
  `tests/smoke` for `Reused` / `Unguarded hexes` before assuming — if one lists every toggle,
  add the new one).

## User-facing decisions

Asked with a mockup (`docs/ui/form-alias-reused.html`, PR #335) on 2026-08-16; the navigator chose:

1. **Anchoring — Option A**: one warning per repeat, underlined on the repeated `FORM` line,
   naming the first use; the first FORM carries nothing. Rejected: B, one warning per number on the
   first use listing the repeats — it underlines the FORM that is fine and leaves the ones to delete
   unmarked, and attributes a second unit's slip to the first unit.
2. **Scope — per hex**, as the rules say: two different units in one hex forming the same number
   are warned about (on the later one). Rejected: same-unit only.
3. **Message**, verbatim: `FORM 1 again: line 11 already forms NEW 1 in this hex, so this block is refused`,
   and when the first use is another unit's: `FORM 1 again: unit 5 (line 11) already forms NEW 1 in this hex, so this block is refused`.
   Rejected: `NEW 1 was already formed on line 11; the server will refuse this FORM` and
   `duplicate FORM 1 (first used on line 11)`.
4. **Warnings tab**: a new group **Orders**, toggle title **Reused FORM numbers**, description
   **Two units formed in the same hex this month with the same NEW number.**, **on by default**.
   Rejected: filing it under an existing group; no toggle.
5. States accepted as drawn: a FORM inside a TURN block is not counted; with no report loaded
   nothing is said; the same number in two different hexes is fine.

## Out of scope

- A parser-level (report-less) duplicate check.
- Warning about the same number used in two different hexes (legal).
- Any change to how the preview (`effects.rs`) treats a taken alias — it already refuses it.
- `NEW n` references to an alias nobody forms — a different check, not filed here.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx
pnpm run check:fast
git status --porcelain packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts   # committed, not dirty
```

And the look in increment 3.

## Known traps

- **`ALL`'s length is a type**: `[Code; 10]`, or the array literal will not compile.
- **The generated vocabulary is a test, not a build step**: `generated_ts` fails until you run it
  with `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1`; commit the regenerated file.
- **Do not put the FORM alias in the `Event::Order` arm** — a FORM is `Event::Open`, and the
  `depth.turn == 0` guard (not `depth == Depth::default()`) is what keeps nested FORMs while
  dropping TURN-block ones.
- **Sort by line before deciding "first"**: `hex.units` is in report order, not document order,
  and the unit that comes first in the report may have written its FORM later.
- **The message strings are quoted verbatim above**; the tests assert them exactly. `line N` when
  the first use is the same unit's, `unit U (line N)` otherwise — nothing else varies.
- **The settings test lists titles by hand**; forgetting the new title passes the loop and fails
  nothing — the renamed test's `"Reused FORM numbers"` line is the pin.
acceptance_criteria: 1) codes::FORM_ALIAS_REUSED ("form-alias-reused") is in codes::ALL; Intent::Form is recorded for FORMs outside TURN blocks; check_forms emits one finding per repeat, on the repeat, with the exact messages from the plan; the seven semantics tests, three intents tests and the per-code fixture row pass. 2) coreVocabulary.generated.ts regenerated. 3) Warnings tab has group Orders with 'Reused FORM numbers' — 'Two units formed in the same hex this month with the same NEW number.', on by default; SettingsDialog.test.tsx pins it. 4) pnpm run check:fast green.

title: Mine the report corpus for errors the order checks could have caught
description:
The order checks were written from the outside in — somebody noticed a mistake worth catching and
wrote a check for it. Meanwhile 26 turn reports sit in `tests/fixtures/reports/`, and every one of
them records what the engine actually rejected. That is a list of real mistakes real players made,
and nobody has read it.

**The request:** mine the corpus for engine errors, work out which could have been caught from the
orders before the turn was run, and file beads for the checks worth having.

This is an investigation whose output is beads, not code.

## There is plenty there

Engine errors appear against the unit that made them, in a consistent shape — `UNIT (id): ORDER:
message`. A sample from the corpus:

    Builders (11619): MOVE: Unit is overloaded and cannot move.
    Drone (8548): STUDY: Not enough funds.
    Drone (11852): PRODUCE: Faction can't produce in that many regions.
    Advisor (10989): STUDY: Can't have another quartermaster.
    a Workers (7308): BUY: Can't buy that.
    DECLARE: Can't declare towards your own faction.

Enough regularity to extract and count mechanically, which is the first step: **every distinct
message, with how often it occurs and across how many turns**. Frequency is the whole point —
"Not enough funds" appearing in twenty turns is a different proposition from a message appearing
once in one.

## Then the judgement, per message

Sort each into one of three:

- **Catchable from the orders and the report** — everything needed was on the player's screen before
  they submitted. `Unit is overloaded and cannot move` is the clearest example, and is close kin to
  the fleet-sailing bead.
- **Catchable only with rules the client does not have** — faction-wide production limits, quartermaster
  restrictions. Worth recording as blocked on the rules rather than dismissed.
- **Not catchable** — it depended on what another faction did, or on a die roll. These should be
  named as such so nobody re-investigates them next year.

For the first group, one bead each, sized by how often the message actually occurs.

## Watch for

- **The corpus is one ruleset.** All 26 files are `neworigins-3.0.0`, and several are the same game
  at different turns, so counts are not independent samples. Two players' mistakes are not
  everybody's — say so in whatever the investigation concludes.
- **Existing checks should show up as already-solved.** If a message appears that `not-enough-silver`
  or `not-enough-items` would now catch, that is evidence those checks work, and worth noting rather
  than filing again.
- **A missing message is also a finding.** A check that exists but whose error never appears in 26
  turns is a check nobody needed.

## Validation

The investigation is done when there is a table of every distinct engine error in the corpus with
its frequency, each sorted into the three groups with a reason, and a bead filed for each catchable
one that does not already have a check.
design:
## Context

An investigation whose output is a table, a findings document and beads — not a feature. The 26
reports in `tests/fixtures/reports/` (games g2, g3 ×5, g4, g5 ×5, g7 ×10, g8 ×3, all
`neworigins-3.0.0`) each carry an `Errors during turn:` section: what the engine refused, one line
per refusal, in the shape `Name (id): ORDER: message` for a unit's order or `ORDER: message` for a
faction-level one. Nobody has read those against the order checks we have. The navigator filed
this with the backlog empty; its beads are next month's fleet work, so the filing is as much the
deliverable as the analysis.

What exists to build on (verified 2026-08-16):

- **The parser already collects the errors, unwrapped.** `crates/core/src/report/header.rs:249–310`
  reads `Errors during turn` into `ReportHeader.errors: Vec<String>` (`:49`), one logical line per
  error — the report wraps long lines and `unwrap_lines` rejoins them, so a grep over the raw text
  ("insufficient movement points; remaining" and "insufficient movement points;" as two messages)
  is wrong and the parser is right. `parse_report_full(text).header.errors` is the whole extraction.
- **The corpus is named once**: `atlantis_hud_fixtures::ALL` (`crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs`), each
  with `.name`, `.file`, `.text`. `parse_real_reports.rs` already reads fixtures through it, and `crates/core/Cargo.toml:16` has it as a dev-dependency.
- **The checks we have**: the nine advisory codes in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:64–90`
  (`not-enough-silver`, `not-enough-items`, `guard-dropped`, `hex-unguarded`, `taught-not-here`,
  `taught-not-studying`, `teacher-cannot-teach`, `teaching-oversubscribed`,
  `teacher-has-free-slots`) plus the parser's syntax diagnostics (`unknown-command`,
  `unclosed-block`, … in `orders/parser.rs`). The module doc at `semantics.rs:1–17` states the two
  policies — never blocking, accept on doubt — that any proposed check must respect.
- **A generator-and-gate pattern**: `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs` renders a file from the
  core and fails when the committed copy is stale unless `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1` rewrites it.
- **Beads already in flight that some messages will map to**: `ah-j0e` (fleet too heavy/short-crewed
  to `SAIL`), `ah-j2w` (item shortfalls count GIVEs and shares), `ah-dbb` (mage cannot pay for a
  spell). Check `bd list --status open` before filing anything.

A raw sample (grep, wrapped lines and all): `MOVE: Unit has insufficient movement points…` ~26,
`STUDY: Maximum level for skill reached.` 11, `STUDY: Not enough funds.` 7, `PRODUCE: Faction can't
produce in that many regions.` 5, `BUY: Can't buy that.` 3, `MOVE: Unit is overloaded and cannot
move.` 2, `GIVE: Nonexistant target (N).` 5, `TEACH: X (N) is not studying a skill you can teach` 3,
and a tail of ones. Expect twenty-odd distinct messages once normalised.

**Decision.** Three deliverables in one PR: (1) `crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs`, a
generator-and-gate in the `generated_ts.rs` mould that renders
`docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md` — every distinct normalised message with its order
keyword, occurrences, turns (files) and games — so the table cannot rot as the corpus grows;
(2) `docs/order-checks/README.md`, the hand-written findings: each message classified into one of
the three groups with a reason, mapped to an existing check or a bead id, plus the caveats and the
"missing message" finding; (3) one bead per catchable, uncovered message, filed at P4 with the
evidence in its body and `relates-to` this bead. Messages catchable only with rules the client
lacks are recorded in the findings, not filed — a bead blocked on a rules source nobody has named
rots; the finding names what source would unblock it, and a bead is filed the day that source
exists.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs` — new

```rust
//! Every engine error in the committed report corpus, counted, as
//! `docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md`. Fails when the committed table no longer
//! matches the corpus (a fixture added, a message changed) unless `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1`
//! rewrites it — the same gate as `generated_ts.rs`. The judgement about which errors an order
//! check could have caught is not here; it is `docs/order-checks/README.md`.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use atlantis_hud_core::report::parse_report_full;
use atlantis_hud_fixtures::ALL;

const RELATIVE_PATH: &str = "../../docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md";
const REGENERATE: &str = "ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test corpus_errors";

/// One engine error, reduced to what repeats: the order keyword and the message with the unit
/// prefix stripped and every number replaced by `N`.
///
/// `Builders (11619): MOVE: Unit is overloaded and cannot move.` → (`MOVE`, `Unit is overloaded and cannot move.`)
/// `GIVE: Nonexistant target (7233).` → (`GIVE`, `Nonexistant target (N).`)
/// `Drone (8548): STUDY: Not enough funds.` → (`STUDY`, `Not enough funds.`)
/// A line with no `ORDER:` keyword (none in the corpus today) keeps its whole text under `-`.
pub fn normalise(line: &str) -> (String, String)

/// (order, message) → (occurrences, turns, games), where a turn is one fixture file and a game
/// is the `gN` in its name.
pub fn tally() -> BTreeMap<(String, String), Tally>

pub struct Tally { pub occurrences: usize, pub turns: usize, pub games: usize }

fn render() -> String   // the markdown table, sorted by occurrences desc, then order, then message
```

`normalise`: strip a leading `<anything> (<digits>): ` if present (the unit prefix — match the
*first* `(\d+): ` since a unit name is not followed by another; do it by hand with `find` on
`"): "` and a check that what precedes the `)` is digits and a `(`, no regex crate); split the
rest at the first `: ` into keyword and message; replace every maximal digit run in the message
with `N`; trim. Games: the fixture's `.file` is `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep` — the game is
the `g…` segment; count distinct. Turns: distinct `.file`s.

The rendered file:

```markdown
# Engine errors in the report corpus

GENERATED by crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs from tests/fixtures/reports/. Do not edit by hand.
Regenerate with: ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test corpus_errors

26 reports, 6 games (g2, g3, g4, g5, g7, g8), all neworigins-3.0.0. Numbers in messages are `N`.
Turns of one game are not independent samples; see README.md.

| Order | Message | Occurrences | Turns | Games |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MOVE | Unit has insufficient movement points; remaining moves queued. | … | … | … |
…
```

(The exact counts and rows come from running it — the header line's report/game counts are
computed too, from `ALL`.) `#[test] fn corpus_error_table_matches_the_corpus()` is
`generated_ts.rs:45–70` verbatim with the new path, message and `render()`.

Unit tests in the same file, on `normalise`: the three doc-comment examples, plus
`"DECLARE: Can't declare towards your own faction."` → (`DECLARE`, unchanged) and a message with
two numbers → both `N`.

`crates/core/Cargo.toml` already has `atlantis-hud-fixtures` under `[dev-dependencies]`
(`generated_ts.rs`/`parse_real_reports.rs` use it); nothing to add.

### `docs/order-checks/README.md` — new, hand-written

Structure, in this order:

1. **What this is** — two paragraphs: the corpus, the method (parser, `header.errors`, the
   generated table beside it), and the two caveats from the bead verbatim in substance: one
   ruleset (`neworigins-3.0.0`), and several turns of the same game are one player's habits, so
   the counts rank *how often it bit these players*, not everybody.
2. **The classification** — one table, every row of the generated table in the same order:
   `| Order | Message | Occurrences | Group | Reason | Covered by |`. `Group` is exactly one of
   **Catchable from the orders and the report**, **Catchable only with rules the client lacks**,
   **Not catchable**. `Reason` is one sentence naming what the check would need and whether the
   report/orders carry it. `Covered by` is an existing code (`not-enough-silver`, …), an existing
   bead (`ah-j0e`, `ah-j2w`, `ah-dbb`), the bead filed by this investigation (`ah-…`), the rules
   source that would unblock it (group 2), or `—` (group 3).
3. **What was filed** — the beads, one line each: id, title, message, occurrences.
4. **Checks nobody needed** — for each of the nine codes and the parser's diagnostics: whether an
   engine error it would have prevented appears in the corpus, and how often. A code whose error
   never appears is named as such (the bead's "a missing message is also a finding"); this is a
   list, not a proposal to remove anything.
5. **Already solved** — messages an existing check would now catch, as evidence the check works
   (the bead's second "watch for").

**The classification criteria — apply them, do not re-derive them:**

- **Group 1 (catchable)** if everything the check needs was in the player's own report and orders
  before submission: the unit's own items, silver, men, skills, weight, capacity, movement points
  (the movement planner already computes them — `crates/core/src/movement/{rules,plan,trace}.rs`), the hex's exits and terrain,
  the units in the hex, the orders text. `Unit is overloaded and cannot move`, `Unit has
  insufficient movement points`, `Not enough funds`, `Nonexistant target (N)` (a `GIVE` to an id
  not in the report), `X is not studying a skill you can teach` are group 1. Where an existing
  code already covers it, `Covered by` names the code; where an open bead does, the bead id.
- **Group 2 (rules the client lacks)** if the refusal depends on a rule the client does not model
  and the report does not state: faction-wide production/region limits (`Faction can't produce in
  that many regions` — needs faction type points), quartermaster rules, skill maximums (`Maximum
  level for skill reached` — needs the skill table's max per race), what a market sells (`Can't buy
  that` — the market list is in the report, so check whether it is group 1 before settling on 2).
  Name the source: the ruleset (`config/public/ruleset.json` — read what it carries), the rules
  text at https://atlantis-pbem.com/rules, or "unknown".
- **Group 3 (not catchable)** if it depended on another faction's orders, a battle, a die roll,
  or state the report of the previous turn cannot show (`ATTACK: Non-existent unit` when the target
  left; `TRANSPORT: Target does not own a transport structure` may be either — reason it out from
  the report line: is the target's structure visible in the player's report?).

When a message could be either of two groups, choose the more conservative (2 over 1, 3 over 2)
and say why in `Reason`; the point of the reason column is that the next reader can disagree.

### The beads

For every group-1 message not covered by an existing code or an open bead, one bead:

```bash
bd create "<title>" --type feature -p 4 --body-file /tmp/<id>.md
bd dep add <new-id> ah-v25 --type relates-to
```

Title: the symptom in player terms, ~70 chars, no engine jargon — "Warn when a MOVE order needs
more movement points than the unit has this turn", not "insufficient movement points check".
Body:

```markdown
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`<ORDER>: <message>` — N occurrences across T turns of G games in tests/fixtures/reports/
(docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). <One sentence on what the player did wrong.>

## What the check would need
<From the report: which fields. From the orders: which order. Which existing module computes it
today, if any (e.g. crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs and plan.rs for movement points).>

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1–17). <The specific doubt for
this check — e.g. terrain unknown along the path.>

## Validation
<Two sentences: the case that warns, the case that stays silent.>
```

Group the near-duplicates: `insufficient movement points; remaining moves queued` and any variant
without the tail are one bead; the five `Nonexistant target (N)` lines are one bead. Before each
`bd create`, `bd search "<key words>"` and read the open list, so `ah-j0e`/`ah-j2w`/`ah-dbb` and
anything filed since are cited rather than duplicated. **P4, always** — the navigator ranks them at
the next triage; argue the frequency in the body. Then `bd dolt push`.

List every filed id in the README's section 3 and in the PR body.

## Increments

1. **`normalise`.** RED: the five unit tests in `corpus_errors.rs`; GREEN: the function.
2. **The table.** `tally`, `render`, the gate test; `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p
   atlantis-hud-core --test corpus_errors` writes the file; a plain `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
   --test corpus_errors` then passes. Read the table: if a row looks like a wrapped-line fragment
   or a unit name survived, `normalise` is wrong — fix it, regenerate.
3. **The findings and the beads.** README as above, then the beads, then their ids into the README.
4. `pnpm run check:fast` (the new test runs inside `cargo test`; `cargo clippy --all-targets`
   sees the file — `-D warnings`, so no dead code).

## The test plan

- `crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs`: `normalise` ×5; `corpus_error_table_matches_the_corpus`
  (the gate — it is what makes the table trustworthy next year).
- No TypeScript, no browser suite. `pnpm run check:fast`.
- The classification is reviewed by reading: the PR body links `docs/order-checks/README.md`, and
  Copilot's review is the second pair of eyes as for any bead.

## User-facing decisions

None. Documents and beads; nothing a player sees changes.

## Out of scope

- Building any check. Every check is its own bead, filed here at P4 and ranked by the navigator.
- Reading `Events during turn` (`header.events`) — events are what happened, not what was refused;
  if a refusal turns out to live there in some fixture, note it in the README and leave it.
- Any change to the parser or the fixtures crate.
- Extending the corpus.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test corpus_errors
pnpm run check:fast
test -s docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md && test -s docs/order-checks/README.md
bd list --status open --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.dependencies // [] | any(.depends_on_id=="ah-v25")) | .id'   # the filed beads
```

And a read: every generated-table row has a README row with a group, a reason and a `Covered by`
entry that is a code, a bead id, a source or `—`.

## Known traps

- **Grep is wrong here.** The report wraps at ~70 columns; only the parser's `header.errors` gives
  whole messages. The sample in *Context* came from grep and double-counts the wrapped `MOVE`
  message for exactly that reason.
- **The gate fails on a fresh corpus, by design.** Adding a fixture later means regenerating; the
  failure message says how. Do not weaken the assertion to a subset check.
- **Numbers become `N` — but not the unit id in the prefix**, which is stripped, not replaced. If a
  message keeps a `(N)` that is a *target*, that is right (`Nonexistant target (N)`).
- **`-D warnings` on `--all-targets`**: `Tally` and `normalise` are used by the test; a helper you
  write and stop using fails clippy.
- **`bd create` defaults to P2.** `-p 4`, explicitly, on every bead. And `bd dolt push` after,
  or the beads exist only on this machine.
- **Do not classify by how easy the check is to build.** The groups are about whether the
  information existed on the player's screen; difficulty goes in the bead's body.
acceptance_criteria: 1) crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs exists: normalise (5 unit tests) and the generated/gated table docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md listing every distinct engine error with order, occurrences, turns, games. 2) docs/order-checks/README.md classifies every row into one of the three groups with a reason and a 'Covered by' (code, bead id, rules source or —), lists the beads filed, the checks whose error never appears, and the messages existing checks already cover. 3) One P4 bead per catchable, uncovered message, related to ah-v25 by bd dep --type relates-to, each with the evidence/what-it-needs/must-not/validation body. 4) pnpm run check:fast green.

title: Item shortfalls count what sharing units in the hex hold, and any unit may borrow, as the engine does
description:
Silver already gets the full treatment: `GIVE` orders inside the hex are credited to the receiving
unit (`silver_given_inside_the_hex_is_credited_to_the_unit_receiving_it`), and units carrying the
`sharing` flag have their purses pooled — added after turn 71, where sixteen units of one fleet each
reported a shortfall for a study the game paid for without complaint.

**Items get neither.** The pooled purse in `semantics.rs` is silver by construction:

    let purse: i64 = sharers.iter().map(|o| balance_of(ledger, &o.unit.unit_id, SILVER)).sum();

`SILVER` is hard-coded, so a hex where one unit holds the herbs and its neighbour is ordered to use
them warns about a shortfall the game will resolve by borrowing, exactly as it used to for silver.

**The request:** `not-enough-items` should count what a unit can actually reach — its own holdings,
what other units in the hex `GIVE` it this turn, and what sharing units in the hex hold.

## What to reuse rather than rebuild

The silver path already establishes the shape and the traps:

- **The ledger** tracks a running balance per unit and tag, so incoming gives are already expressible
  per item — `balance_of(ledger, unit, tag)` takes a tag.
- **`doubted`** exists because a pool is only as trustworthy as its members: if any sharer's own sums
  cannot be trusted, the whole pool is skipped rather than reported wrongly. Items need the same
  restraint.
- **`shares()`** reads the `sharing` flag and needs no change.

A false shortfall is worse than a missed one here. The warning's job is to catch a turn that will not
run as intended; one that cries wolf on every hex with a shared stock trains the navigator to ignore
the panel, which is what the sharing work fixed for silver.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Which items pool.** Silver is fungible and the flag says "resources"; whether the check treats
  every tag alike, or only consumables, is a rules question worth confirming against the engine.
- Whether a shortfall against a pool should read differently from one against a unit's own holdings
  — "the hex is short" is a different sentence from "this unit is short".

## Validation

A hex where one unit holds a stock, a second is ordered to spend it, and either a `GIVE` or a
`sharing` flag covers it: no warning. The same hex without either: warned. A hex where the pool is
genuinely short: warned once, about the pool.
design:
## Context

Filed by the navigator on 2026-08-16; planned by Beast the same day. Blocks ah-dbb (spell reagents),
which is the second consumer of "what can this unit actually reach".

Today `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` models the `sharing` flag for **silver only**:
`report_shared_purse` (:783) sums the silver of the units that share, and a sharing unit's own
silver shortfall is skipped (:735). Two things are wrong against the game itself, and I checked
them in the engine's source rather than the rules page (which does not describe SHARE at all):

- **Items are never pooled.** `SILVER` is hard-coded into the purse, so a hex where one sharing
  unit holds the swords and its neighbour is ordered to give or sell them warns about a shortfall
  the game will not have. (`GIVE`s inside the hex *are* already credited to the receiver for every
  tag — `transfer` at :488 is tag-generic and `items_given_between_units_in_the_hex_go_round`
  pins it. What is missing is the sharing half.)
- **The borrower need not share.** `Unit::GetSharedNum(item)` in the engine's `unit.cpp` counts
  *the unit itself, plus every unit of the same faction in the region carrying `FLAG_SHARING`* —
  the calling unit's own flag is not consulted. `DoGiveOrder` and `DoSell` (`runorders.cpp`)
  check and consume through it for items, `DoBuy` and `Do1StudyOrder` (`monthorders.cpp`)
  through `GetSharedMoney`, `Run1BuildOrder`/`consume_production_inputs` for materials; the one
  exception is `IT_MAN` (men are never borrowed). So a non-sharing unit studying next to a sharing
  treasurer is paid for by the game and warned about by the HUD — the test
  `a_unit_that_does_not_share_cannot_borrow_from_one_that_does` (:1389) pins the wrong behaviour.

**After this bead** there is one rule for every tag, and it is the engine's: what a unit can reach
is its own balance plus the balances of the units in the hex that share. When a hex has sharers, a
tag's shortfall is judged for the hex as one pool (the sharers' net balances against the overdrafts
of the units that must borrow from them) and reported once, against the hex — because the engine
drains sharers in order, so which borrower "went short" is genuinely undeterminable. When a hex has
no sharers, per-unit findings stay exactly as they are. Silver stops being special: the purse code
becomes the general pooled path, and a non-sharer may draw on it as the engine allows.

The navigator decided the three user-visible points on 2026-08-16 (see *User-facing decisions*).

For ah-dbb: nothing new is needed at the seam — a spell that consumes reagents will `charge()` the
mage's balance for the reagent tag, and this bead's `report_shortfalls` pools it like any item.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the only code file

**Delete `report_shared_purse` (:783–826)** and fold its job into `report_shortfalls` (:706), which
becomes:

```rust
fn report_shortfalls(ledger, hex, ruleset, options, findings) {
    // The units whose stock the engine lets everyone in the hex draw on (`FLAG_SHARING`).
    let sharers: Vec<&Ordered<'_>> = hex.units.iter().filter(|o| o.shares()).collect();
    // A pool is only as trustworthy as its members (the existing rule, kept): one doubted sharer
    // silences every pooled tag in the hex.
    let pool_trusted = !sharers.iter().any(|o| ledger.doubted.contains(&o.unit.unit_id));
    // Men are the engine's one exception (`IT_MAN` in GetSharedNum): never borrowed. Without a
    // ruleset every tag pools.
    let pooled = |tag: &str| !sharers.is_empty() && !ruleset.is_some_and(|r| r.is_man(tag));

    // tag → the overdrafts of the units that must borrow it (non-sharers, not doubted, balance < 0)
    let mut claims: BTreeMap<String, i64> = BTreeMap::new();
    // every pooled tag any unit is short of (a sharer's own overdraft is inside the pool sum)
    let mut pooled_tags: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();

    for ordered in &hex.units {
        if doubted → continue;
        for (tag, balance) in <this unit's negative balances, the existing range() scan :721–727> {
            if pooled(tag) {
                pooled_tags.insert(tag.clone());
                if !ordered.shares() { *claims.entry(tag.clone()).or_insert(0) += -balance; }
                continue;
            }
            <the existing per-unit finding, :737–768, unchanged except the item verb (below)>
        }
    }

    if !pool_trusted { return; }
    for tag in pooled_tags {
        let code = if tag == SILVER { NOT_ENOUGH_SILVER } else { NOT_ENOUGH_ITEMS };
        if !options.emits(code) { continue; }
        let pool: i64 = sharers.iter().map(|o| balance_of(ledger, &o.unit.unit_id, &tag)).sum();
        let short = claims.get(&tag).copied().unwrap_or(0) - pool;
        if short <= 0 { continue; }
        // What the pool's members and its borrowers actually hold, so the message can say
        // "they can have X and their orders spend Y" the way the per-unit one does.
        let held: i64 = hex.units.iter()
            .filter(|o| o.shares() || (!ledger.doubted.contains(&o.unit.unit_id) && balance_of(ledger, &o.unit.unit_id, &tag) < 0))
            .map(|o| o.holding(&tag)).sum();
        findings.push(hex.finding(code, <message, below>));
    }
}
```

`Ruleset::is_man(tag)` exists (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:540`) and takes the uppercase
tag the ledger keys by. `Hex::finding` (:228, used by the old purse; `Ordered::finding` at :324 is the per-unit form) is unchanged. `Ordered::holding`
(:317) and `balance_of` (:679) are the existing helpers. Delete the `if tag == SILVER && ordered.shares() { continue; }` at :735 —
it is subsumed by `pooled(tag)`. Keep the `range()` scan comment (:721–724).

**Messages** (every string quoted from *User-facing decisions*; the per-unit silver one is unchanged):

- per-unit item (:761–767): `format!("short {short} {name}: this unit can have {} and its orders give away or sell {}", ordered.holding(tag), ordered.holding(tag) + short)`
- hex-level silver: `format!("the units in this hex are short ${short} between them: they can have ${held} and their orders spend ${}", held + short)`
- hex-level item: `format!("the units in this hex are short {short} {name} between them: they can have {held} and their orders give away or sell {}", held + short)` with `name = item_name(&tag, hex, ruleset)` — **change `item_name` (:826) to drop its `ordered` parameter** and search the hex's inventories only (it already chains them after the unit's own); update its one existing caller at the per-unit message.

**Docs in the file:** the module header's "Accept on doubt" paragraph stands. Replace the doc on
`report_shared_purse` (:779–782, "Sixteen units of turn 71…") with a doc on `report_shortfalls`
that says the engine rule (`GetSharedNum`: own + same-faction sharers in the region, borrower's
own flag irrelevant, men excepted) and why the pooled case is reported against the hex. Update
`Ordered::shares`' doc (:305–308) — "puts its stock, silver included, at the disposal of the
others in the hex".

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — tests (`mod tests`, helpers at :1084–1201: `region`, `unit`, `with_silver`, `with_item`, `with_men`, `sharing` (:1369), `check`, `codes`, `only`)

Add, after the sharing tests:

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx:335`

`SettingsDialog.test.tsx` asserts the title "Overdrawn items" (:54) and never the description —
no test change.

### `crates/core-wasm`, `crates/core-tauri`, `packages/core-client` — untouched

`Finding` and the codes are unchanged; only messages and which findings are emitted differ.

## Increments

Rust: `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core semantics`. Each opens with the named failing test.

4. **Men are the exception.** RED: `men_are_never_borrowed_from_a_sharing_unit`; add the

5. **Settings text.** `SettingsDialog.tsx`; `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test`.
6. **Gate.** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`;
