title: State files written from a bead worktree land in the worktree, so the fleet view reads stale state
description:
## The cost being paid
The consumer root is derived from the script's own location, five different ways in seven files (`$script_dir/../../..`; `git -C $script_dir rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` with a --git-common-dir fallback, three copies; `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, two copies), so every script answers a different root depending on which copy of the submodule — the main checkout's or a bead worktree's — it was invoked through. Being paid right now: Storm's state file in the main checkout says phase build since 16:55:48Z, the copy under .claude/worktrees/ah-o1t.2/ says gate since 17:07:15Z (checked 17:23Z), and the fleet list reads the former — because the implementer followed the remedy three retrospectives prescribe (init the submodule in the worktree), the skill's relative invocation `.claude/cerebro/scripts/implementer-state` resolved into the worktree copy, and `../../..` answered the worktree. The same defect class has been paid twice before.

## Evidence
- .claude/implementers/Storm.state.json vs .claude/worktrees/ah-o1t.2/.claude/implementers/Storm.state.json on 2026-08-15 17:23Z; cerebro.el:776–801 (cerebro--repo-root, state file path)
- .claude/cerebro/scripts/implementer-state:101–106 — comment says it avoids --show-toplevel because "from a bead worktree [it] is the worktree", then fails the identical way via ../../..
- cerebro 1ecb5c7 review commit "fix the worktree sweep, which the move quietly broke": --git-common-dir from inside the submodule made prune-worktrees.sh sweep the wrong directory — "every sweep would have reported nothing to do, for ever, without an error"
- atlantis-hud cbe52ec fix(ah-vek): cargoTargetDir.test.ts derived the worktree, not the repo — same class
- docs/retrospectives/ah-4ao.md §2, ah-axj.md, ah-aao.md — the init-in-worktree remedy that creates the second copy
- `git -C .claude/worktrees/ah-o1t.2/.claude/cerebro rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` prints the worktree, so sweep-claims.sh, sweep-epics.sh and prune-worktrees.sh share the dependency on being invoked from the main checkout's copy

## Where
.claude/cerebro/scripts/implementer-state (:101–106); prune-worktrees.sh (:67–81); sweep-claims.sh (:52–63); sweep-epics.sh (:27–38); sync-symlinks.sh (:11–13); .claude/cerebro/githooks/install.sh (:10), sync-if-changed.sh (:14)

## What a refactoring would change
One answer to "where is the consumer root", written once — a shared shell function (or a CEREBRO_ROOT the launchers export) that resolves the shared checkout regardless of which submodule copy runs, used by every script and hook — so a state file, a sweep or a symlink can only ever land in the checkout the fleet view reads.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

Every cerebro script derives "the consumer repository root" from its own location, and they do it
five ways in seven files (`git grep -n 'rev-parse\|\.\./\.\./\.\.' scripts githooks` on cerebro
`origin/main` `7cea8fa`): `agent-state:136` climbs `../../..`; `prune-worktrees.sh:69-81`,
`sweep-claims.sh:54-63`, `sweep-epics.sh:29-38` ask `--show-superproject-working-tree` with a
`--git-common-dir` fallback; `sync-symlinks.sh:13` climbs; `launch-preflight:35-40` climbs and
checks `--show-toplevel`; the two hooks use `--show-toplevel` from cwd. Each answers a *different*
root depending on which copy of the submodule ran — the main checkout's or a bead worktree's — and
the cost is live: an implementer that inits the submodule in its worktree (the remedy three
retrospectives prescribe: ah-4ao, ah-axj, ah-aao) then calls
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state` *relative to the worktree*, `../../..` answers the worktree,
and its state file lands in `.claude/worktrees/<bead>/.claude/agents-state/` while the fleet view
reads the main checkout's stale copy (Storm, 2026-08-15: `build` on screen, `gate` in the worktree).
The same misroute is waiting in the three sweeps: `--show-superproject-working-tree` from a
worktree's submodule copy is the worktree, so a sweep run from there sweeps the wrong root.

There are two legitimate roots, and that is why five derivations grew: the **enclosing** tree —
the working tree this copy sits in (main checkout or worktree), right for anything that acts on
*this* tree: syncing its symlinks, finding its agent files before a launch, a git hook — and the
**shared** tree — the main working tree that every worktree of the repository shares, right for
anything the fleet view reads or that reasons about the whole repository: state files, stop flags,
the worktree/claims/epics sweeps. This bead writes **one resolver that answers both**, and makes
every script ask it. The shared answer is `dirname "$(git -C <enclosing> rev-parse
--path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"` — the main `.git` from anywhere, asked from the consumer
tree and never from inside the submodule (from there it names the submodule's own git dir, the trap
`prune-worktrees.sh:62-67` documents). Verified on this machine: from `.claude/worktrees/ah-k6i.1`
it prints `/Users/henrikku/repos/atlantis-hud/.git`; git here is 2.54 (`--path-format` needs ≥2.31).

Rejected: a `CEREBRO_ROOT` the launchers export — a script the navigator runs by hand, or Cerebro
runs from its own session, would not have it, and the git answer needs no environment.

**Where the code lives.** cerebro submodule (`scripts/`, `tests/`, `CLAUDE.md`), PR 1 to
`rmstdope/cerebro`; PR 2 the atlantis-hud pointer bump. Line numbers against cerebro `origin/main`
at **`7cea8fa`**.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `scripts/consumer-root` (bash, `+x`)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The consumer repository root this copy of cerebro serves. Two answers, on purpose:
#
#   consumer-root            the enclosing working tree - the main checkout, or a bead worktree
#                            when this copy is the worktree's own submodule. Right for anything
#                            that acts on THIS tree: its symlinks, its agent files, its hooks.
#   consumer-root --shared   the main working tree every worktree of the repository shares -
#                            where the fleet view reads state files and stop flags and where the
#                            sweeps look. Right for anything the fleet reads or that reasons about
#                            the whole repository. From the main checkout both answers are equal.
#
# Exit 1 with a message when this checkout is not mounted at <consumer>/.claude/cerebro (a
# standalone clone of cerebro has no consumer), or when --shared is asked outside a git tree.
set -euo pipefail
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
enclosing="$(cd "$script_dir/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || enclosing=""
if [[ -z "$enclosing" || "$(cd "$enclosing/.claude/cerebro" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" != "$(cd "$script_dir/.." && pwd -P)" ]]; then
  echo "consumer-root: $script_dir is not <consumer>/.claude/cerebro/scripts" >&2
  exit 1
fi
case "${1:-}" in
  "") printf '%s\n' "$enclosing" ;;
  --shared)
    # Asked from the consumer tree, never from inside the submodule: from here --git-common-dir
    # would name the submodule's own git directory. From a linked worktree it names the main
    # repository's .git, whose parent is the shared working tree.
    common="$(git -C "$enclosing" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" \
      || { echo "consumer-root: $enclosing is not inside a git working tree" >&2; exit 1; }
    printf '%s\n' "$(cd "$(dirname "$common")" && pwd -P)" ;;
  *) echo "usage: consumer-root [--shared]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
```

`pwd -P` throughout: git prints physical paths, and macOS `mktemp` lives under a symlink
(`/var` → `/private/var`), the same reason `launch-preflight:38-40` gives.

### The callers

- `scripts/agent-state` (:132-137): `repo_root="$("$script_dir/consumer-root" --shared)"` — the
  fix. Replace the comment with why `--shared`: a state file written from a worktree's copy must
  land where the fleet view reads (ah-e0w). `out_dir` and everything below unchanged.
- `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` (:58-81), `scripts/sweep-claims.sh` (:50-63),
  `scripts/sweep-epics.sh` (:26-38): replace each two-question block with
  `repo_root="$("$script_dir/consumer-root" --shared)"` and one comment line pointing at the
  resolver's header for the reasoning. The "not a submodule / vendored" fallback goes: the resolver
  requires the `<consumer>/.claude/cerebro` mount and refuses otherwise, which is what these
  scripts' README says the layout is.
- `scripts/sync-symlinks.sh` (:10-24): `CLAUDE_ROOT="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/consumer-root")/.claude"`
  (enclosing — a worktree syncs its own links; that is what lets a bump PR commit them, ah-cuc);
  the two guards at :15-24 collapse to the resolver's exit 1 (keep the message text the existing
  `tests/sync-symlinks.sh` asserts on — check `grep -n "must run from\|Required directory"
  tests/sync-symlinks.sh` and either keep printing that line before exiting or update the
  assertion; prefer keeping the line).
- `scripts/launch-preflight` (:34-40): `consumer="$("$script_dir/consumer-root" 2>/dev/null)" || exit 0`
  replaces the `parent`/`basename` test; keep the `--show-toplevel == consumer` line (it is what
  makes a clone at `~/.claude/cerebro` do nothing), and `parent="$consumer/.claude"`.
- `githooks/install.sh:10` and `githooks/sync-if-changed.sh:14`: **unchanged** — a git hook runs
  with cwd in the tree it fires in, and `--show-toplevel` there is the enclosing tree by
  definition; say so in a one-line comment at each site so the next sweep does not count them.
- `scripts/implementer-state` (the shim) and the six `run-*` launchers: unchanged.

### Tests

- New `tests/consumer-root.sh` (plain bash, `fail`/`pass` as `tests/launchers.sh:14-21`), under
  `mktemp -d`:
  1. A consumer: `T/repo` (`git init -q`, `git -C T/repo commit -q --allow-empty -m init`),
     `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/scripts/consumer-root` symlinked to the real script → both modes print
     the physical `T/repo`.
  2. A linked worktree of it: `git -C T/repo worktree add -q T/repo/.claude/worktrees/wt`, the same
     symlink under `T/repo/.claude/worktrees/wt/.claude/cerebro/scripts/` → plain prints the
     worktree, `--shared` prints `T/repo`.
  3. Standalone: `T/x/cerebro/scripts/consumer-root` → exit 1, stderr contains
     `is not <consumer>/.claude/cerebro/scripts`, stdout empty.
  4. Consumer layout that is not a git tree (`T/plain/.claude/cerebro/scripts/`) → plain prints

- `tests/agent-state.sh`: `new_fixture` (:29-37) gains `git init -q "$tmp"` and a symlink for
  `consumer-root`; every existing case keeps passing (the shared root of a plain repo is itself).
  Add **`from-a-worktree-copy-writes-to-the-shared-checkout`**: build fixture 2 above (worktree
  with its own scripts symlinks incl. `agent-state`, `run-implementer`, `consumer-root`), run
  `wt/.claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state Cyclops working --bead ah-f9c --pid 42`, assert
  `T/repo/.claude/agents-state/Cyclops.state.json` exists and `wt/.claude/agents-state` does not.
- `tests/sync-symlinks.sh` and `tests/launchers.sh`: keep passing (their fixtures already `git init`
  and copy/symlink scripts — add `consumer-root` beside `sync-symlinks.sh` wherever they copy it:
  `tests/sync-symlinks.sh:37` and `:78`, and the launcher tests' consumer layout).

### Docs

- cerebro `CLAUDE.md` *Gotchas* (:141-149): rewrite the first bullet — every script asks
  `scripts/consumer-root` for the consumer root, enclosing or `--shared`, and why there are two;
  `.claude/cerebro/scripts` stays a load-bearing location because the resolver climbs from it.
- `README.md` *Sync Script* section: one sentence that the sync targets the enclosing tree.
- The comment blocks removed from the three sweeps are replaced by the resolver's header; nothing
  else.

## Increments

1. RED: `tests/consumer-root.sh` cases 1-4. GREEN: `scripts/consumer-root`.
2. RED: the new `agent-state` worktree case (and `new_fixture`'s `git init` + symlink). GREEN:
   `agent-state` through `--shared`.
3. The three sweeps, `sync-symlinks.sh`, `launch-preflight` through the resolver; the four
   existing bash suites green; the two hook comments; docs.
4. PR 1 `fix(ah-e0w): one resolver for the consumer root, and state files land in the shared
   checkout from a worktree copy`; `@copilot`; CI (ERT only — paste the bash suites' output);
   squash. PR 2 the bump. **Then, on this machine**: `find .claude/worktrees -path
   '*/.claude/agents-state/*' -o -path '*/.claude/implementers/*'` and say in the PR what stale
   worktree-local state files exist; do not delete them (they belong to live worktrees).

## The test plan

- `bash tests/consumer-root.sh` (new), `bash tests/agent-state.sh` (extended),
  `bash tests/sync-symlinks.sh`, `bash tests/launchers.sh` — from the cerebro worktree root.
- ERT and byte-compile untouched; run anyway.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator: P1 at triage (2026-08-15), no design questions — the fleet view's
behaviour is unchanged; it simply reads the file the implementer actually wrote.

## Out of scope

- `cerebro--repo-root` in `emacs/cerebro.el` (`locate-dominating-file … ".claude/cerebro"`): a
  fleet view opened with `default-directory` inside a worktree would read that worktree — the same
  class, but Emacs is opened from the main checkout by every documented path; file a follow-up if
  it bites.
- The two git hooks (see above), the launchers, `implementer-state`.
- Cleaning up stale `.claude/agents-state` directories inside existing worktrees.
- atlantis-hud's own `scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` root logic (ah-vek fixed it; ah-efj covers
  its remaining defect).

## Validation

```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<cerebro worktree>
bash tests/consumer-root.sh && bash tests/agent-state.sh && bash tests/sync-symlinks.sh && bash tests/launchers.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

Human check (after PR 2 and `git submodule update` in the main checkout): from a bead worktree
with its submodule initialised, run `.claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state Wolverine idle --pid $$`
inside the worktree — the file appears under the main checkout's `.claude/agents-state/`, and the
fleet view shows it within five seconds. `.claude/cerebro/scripts/consumer-root --shared` from that
worktree prints the main checkout. Psylocke marks this not-needed.

## Known traps

- **Never ask git from inside the submodule** (`git -C "$script_dir" …`): `--git-common-dir` then
  names the submodule's git directory and `--show-superproject-working-tree` names whichever tree
  holds this copy — both wrong for `--shared`. Ask from `$enclosing`.
- **`pwd -P` everywhere in the resolver and the tests**, or `/var/folders/…` never equals
  `/private/var/folders/…` (`launch-preflight:38-40`).
- **`tests/agent-state.sh`'s fixture is not a git repo today** — without `git init` every case fails
  under `--shared` with "not inside a git working tree"; add it in the same increment as the switch.
- **A worktree needs a commit to be added** (`git worktree add` refuses in an unborn repo) — the
  `--allow-empty` commit in fixture 1.
- **Do not branch inside the shared `.claude/cerebro`**; cerebro worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`
  with an absolute path (ah-3bl's retrospective), then the atlantis-hud bump from a worktree.
- **The stale copies already on disk** (`.claude/worktrees/*/.claude/agents-state/*`) are not
  removed by this bead; a live worktree's copy is harmless once nothing writes there.

title: One session's scratch worktree outside the repository fails every other session's gate
description:
## The cost being paid
scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts's "keeps the worktrees inside the repository" runs `git worktree list --porcelain` and expects no worktree outside .claude/worktrees/ — a per-branch unit test whose verdict depends on the state of the shared machine, not the branch under test. It has failed three separate beads' gates: twice because the anchor was wrong from a worktree (fixed by cbe52ec), then again two days later because another session's worktree sat outside .claude/worktrees/, which is the normal state of this fleet (the navigator's own scratch worktrees). `pnpm run check` is still an && chain that stops at that link, so each time the remaining gate was run by hand, step by step.

## Evidence
- bead ah-vek (P1 bug): "Hit while merging ah-ebv (#144); the whole remaining gate had to be run by hand, step by step"; notes: "Raised to P1 … after hitting it a second time, while gating ah-ctf (#149) … an agent … has silently skipped the entire Rust suite while believing the gate covered it"
- cbe52ec fix(ah-vek): let the worktree check ask the same question wherever it runs (#154) — root anchored in git, runSuites.ts made pnpm test exhaustive
- docs/retrospectives/ah-sup.md §"pnpm run check's tooling suite fails on any live sibling worktree, not just my own" — "another live session's worktree sitting outside .claude/worktrees/ (/private/tmp/…/scratchpad/pr-epic) … About five minutes … running the remaining steps manually since the script stops at the first failure … Worth a project-level decision"
- scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts:50–59 today; package.json "check" still lint && typecheck && test && test:smoke && …

## Where
scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts; scripts/cargoTargetDir.ts; package.json (check)

## What a refactoring would change
Keep the pure strayWorktrees() unit table; move the live "no worktree outside the repo" property out of the per-branch gate into a place that owns the machine's worktrees — the implementer's workspace preflight for its own worktree, or Cerebro's prune sweep — so one session's scratch worktree cannot redden another session's check.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

`scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` (atlantis-hud `origin/main` `deb434a`, :50-63) asserts, on every
run of the tooling suite, that **no worktree on the machine** sits outside the repository —
`git worktree list --porcelain` from the repository root, `strayWorktrees(listed, REPO)` must be
empty. The property it protects is real (a worktree elsewhere compiles into its own `target/` and
finds its own empty bead database), but it is a property of *this* worktree, and the test asks about
every worktree the machine has. So one session's scratch worktree — the navigator's, another agent's
`/private/tmp/…/scratchpad/pr-epic` — reddens every other session's `pnpm run check`, and because
`check` is an `&&` chain the rest of the gate is then run by hand, step by step. Three beads have
paid it (ah-vek twice, then ah-sup's retrospective two days after the fix), and ah-k6i's six plans
each carry a trap paragraph about it.

The fix keeps the assertion honest and per-branch: **the worktree the suite is running in must be
inside the repository** — the repository root itself, or under `<root>/.claude/`. That is exactly the
build-dir/bead-db hazard for the branch under test, it cannot be reddened by anybody else's tree, and
it still fails — rightly — for a PR gated from a stray worktree. `strayWorktrees` (pure, its own
table at :77-101) is kept and reused: fed one worktree instead of the machine's list. Nothing about
Cerebro's prune sweep changes (it already confines itself to `.claude/worktrees/`, and a scratch
worktree of the navigator's is not something to nag about).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts`

Replace the `it("keeps the worktrees inside the repository, …")` case (:50-63) with:

```ts
it("runs from a worktree inside the repository, where the config and the bead database are shared", () => {
  // Asked of THIS worktree only. The machine's other worktrees are other sessions' business - a
  // scratch tree elsewhere used to redden every session's gate (ah-efj). What matters for the
  // branch under test is that its own tree finds the repository's cargo config and bead database.
  const here = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], { cwd: HERE, encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
  expect(strayWorktrees(`worktree ${here}\n`, REPO)).toEqual([]);
});
```

`HERE`, `REPO`, `execFileSync`, `strayWorktrees`, `normalize` are already imported/defined (:1-30).
The second `expect(listed).toContain(…)` guard (:60-62) goes with the listing it guarded. Update the
file's head comment (:9-26) — one sentence: the check is per-worktree, on purpose. Everything else
in the file (the pure `strayWorktrees` table, `repositoryRoot`, the temp-repo cases) is unchanged.

### `scripts/cargoTargetDir.ts`

Unchanged. (`strayWorktrees`'s doc comment (:35-40) can gain "— or a single worktree, as the tooling
suite asks about its own"; optional.)

### The six ah-k6i plans' *Known traps*

Nothing to edit — they say "if it fails, that is the machine"; after this bead it does not fail
for that reason. Mention in the PR body that the trap paragraphs are now moot.

## Increments

1. RED: run `pnpm run test:tooling` from a worktree while a scratch worktree exists outside the
   repository (`git worktree add /tmp/ah-efj-stray origin/main`; **remove it after** with
   `git worktree remove --force /tmp/ah-efj-stray && git worktree prune`) — today's test fails on
   the stray. Rewrite the case; GREEN with the stray still present. Then remove the stray. (This
   RED is a manual demonstration; the case itself is the regression test from now on.)
2. `pnpm run check`; PR `fix(ah-efj): the tooling gate asks whether its own worktree is inside the
   repository, not the machine's` — `@copilot`, CI, squash. Close.

## The test plan

- `pnpm run test:tooling` — the rewritten case green from the main checkout and from an agent
  worktree, with and without a stray scratch worktree present on the machine.
- `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator: P1 at triage (2026-08-15); no design question.

## Out of scope

- A machine-wide stray report in Cerebro's `prune-worktrees.sh` (Bishop's other option): a
  navigator's scratch worktree is legitimate, and nothing acts on the report.
- Making `pnpm run check` continue past a failed step (Bishop's aside about the `&&` chain — failing
  fast is the point of a gate).
- The implementer's own worktree location, which `implement-bead` already fixes to
  `.claude/worktrees/`.

## Validation

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/ah-efj-stray origin/main
pnpm run test:tooling            # green with the stray present
git worktree remove --force /tmp/ah-efj-stray && git worktree prune
pnpm run check
```

Human check: none — tooling only; Psylocke marks not-needed.

## Known traps

- **Do not leave the demonstration stray behind** — it is exactly the thing that used to redden
  everyone else's gate until this merges; remove it in the same shell.
- **`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints the physical path** (`/private/tmp` for `/tmp` on macOS);
  `strayWorktrees` normalizes both sides through `resolve`, and `REPO` comes from
  `repositoryRoot`, also physical — but if the assertion is red for the main checkout, compare
  `here` and `normalize(REPO)` by eye before assuming the test is wrong.
- **The tooling suite runs from the repository root** (`vitest.tooling.config.ts`); `HERE` is the
  file's own directory, and `cwd: HERE` is what makes the answer the *current* worktree when the
  suite runs inside one.

title: The desktop-shell smoke suite is a second web run, so desktop-only export defects arrive green
description:
## The cost being paid
The desktop bundle silently becomes the web app when there is no Tauri runtime (desktopCore.ts hasTauriRuntime → WASM fallback), so the "desktop-shell" Playwright project — two of the four smoke CI jobs — drives the WASM core in Chrome with saveTextFile undefined and appUpdate unsupported: a second web run. The real IPC path is reachable only through WebKitGTK on Linux CI, and the desktop's file save calls @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog directly with nothing to inject in its place. Three desktop-only defects reached the navigator with that project green; one P0 was fixed blind; one P0 spent two commits trying to cover the desktop export in the native suite and gave up.

## Evidence
- Bead ah-6l2 (P0) notes: "Could not run the actual native (Tauri/WebKitGTK) suite in this environment - test:native is Linux-only … this session is on macOS. No real desktop GUI available … Decision: could not get a live desktop-only repro"; design "Known traps": "desktop-shell smoke is the WASM core in Chrome, not Tauri. Green smoke on both projects proves nothing about the desktop backend"
- 4573b49 fix(ah-7pa) sub-commits: "native orders-export test follows the new save dialog … an OS window WebDriver cannot see or drive", then "drop the undriveable native export assertion … Tauri defines invoke via Object.defineProperty with no writable/configurable, so the WebDriver-injected override never took"; bead ah-7pa design "Out of scope": "Automating the native dialog in tests"
- ah-7pa (P0) and ah-jfx (P1), both desktop-only save-dialog defects, reached the navigator with the desktop-shell project green

## Where
apps/desktop/src/desktopCore.ts; apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts; playwright.config.ts (desktop-shell project); tests/native/*; .github/workflows/ci.yml (native job)

## What a refactoring would change
A seam between the shell and the Tauri plugins (dialog, fs, updater) that a test can stand in for — an injected saver/updater port at the desktop entry, or a fake __TAURI_INTERNALS__ installed before Tauri's own — so a desktop-path test can run in Chrome, and the desktop-shell project asserts something the web project does not.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

The desktop bundle becomes the web app when there is no Tauri runtime: `apps/desktop/src/desktopCore.ts`
(`hasTauriRuntime()`, :17-27) falls back to the WASM core, `saveTextFile.ts:44-49` returns no
saver, `updateCheck.ts:46` reports updates unsupported. So the Playwright **`desktop-shell`**
project — two of the four smoke CI jobs — is a second web run: it drives the WASM core in Chrome
with `saveTextFile` undefined, and asserts nothing the `web` project does not. Three desktop-only
defects reached the navigator with it green (ah-7pa P0, ah-jfx P1 — exports not using the native
save dialog; ah-6l2 P0, fixed blind), and ah-7pa spent two commits trying to drive the OS dialog
from the native WebKitGTK suite and gave up: it is an OS window WebDriver cannot see, and Tauri
defines `invoke` non-writable so an injected override never took.

The seam this bead adds is small and honest: **the desktop shell reaches its plugins through one
port, and a test can install a stand-in for that port before the bundle loads.** The core transport
is untouched (`hasTauriRuntime()` still decides IPC vs WASM; the native suite covers IPC), and the
port only carries what the shell calls on plugins today: the dialog's `save` and the fs's
`writeTextFile`. With a fake port installed by `page.addInitScript`, the `desktop-shell` project can
assert exactly the class of defect that slipped through three times: **each export goes through the
save dialog, with the right file name and filter, writes what the dialog answered, and a cancelled
dialog writes nothing and closes nothing.** Those tests are skipped on the `web` project, which is
what makes the two projects finally differ.

Rejected (mine): a fake `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` — it would flip `hasTauriRuntime()` and send every
core command to a fake that would have to be a whole core; and a Playwright-level dialog driver —
there is none for a native dialog. Line numbers against atlantis-hud `origin/main` after #282.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `apps/desktop/src/desktopPlugins.ts`

```ts
/** What the shell asks of Tauri's plugins - the whole of it, so a stand-in is two functions. */
export type DesktopPlugins = {
  save(options: { defaultPath?: string; filters?: { name: string; extensions: string[] }[] }): Promise<string | null>;
  writeTextFile(path: string, text: string): Promise<void>;
};

declare global {
  interface Window {
    /** A test's stand-in, installed before the bundle loads (Playwright addInitScript). Never set in production. */
    __ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__?: DesktopPlugins;
  }
}

/**
 * The plugins this build can reach: a stand-in when a test installed one, else Tauri's own when the
 * runtime is there, else nothing - which is what the preview server and the web-style smoke run see.
 */
export function desktopPlugins(): DesktopPlugins | undefined {
  if (typeof window !== "undefined" && window.__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__) {
    return window.__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__;
  }
  if (!hasTauriRuntime()) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return { save, writeTextFile };   // the real @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog / plugin-fs imports
}
```

Imports: `save` from `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`, `writeTextFile` from `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs`,
`hasTauriRuntime` from `./desktopCore` — the same three `saveTextFile.ts` imports today (:13-16);
they move here. Module doc: why the port exists (ah-9lv, the three defects), why the core is not
behind it, and that the global is read at call time so an init script that runs before the bundle
is always seen.

### `apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts`

`desktopTextFileSaver(plugins: DesktopPlugins | undefined = desktopPlugins()): TextFileSaver | undefined`
— `undefined` when `plugins` is; else today's body (:50-62) through `plugins.save` / `plugins.writeTextFile`.
`filterFor` unchanged. Drop the direct plugin imports and the `hasTauriRuntime` import; keep the
doc comment, plus one line: the plugins come through the port so a test can stand in for them.
`App.tsx` is unchanged (`saveTextFile={desktopTextFileSaver()}`).

### `apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.test.ts` (extend)

- `desktopTextFileSaver(undefined)` → `undefined`.
- With a fake `{ save: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue("/chosen/orders-turn-71.txt"), writeTextFile: vi.fn() }`:
  the saver calls `save({ defaultPath: "orders-turn-71.txt", filters: [{ name: "Text", extensions: ["txt"] }] })`,
  then `writeTextFile("/chosen/orders-turn-71.txt", "unit 1 : work")`, and resolves the path.
- `save` resolving `null` → resolves `null` and `writeTextFile` is never called.
- New `desktopPlugins.test.ts`: with `window.__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__` set (vitest `jsdom`? —
  check `apps/desktop`'s vitest environment first; if it is `node`, set `globalThis.window = { __ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__: fake }`
  in the test and delete it after) → returns the fake; without it and without a runtime → `undefined`.

### New: `tests/smoke/desktop-shell.spec.ts`

Skipped on every project but `desktop-shell`:

```ts
test.skip(({}, testInfo) => testInfo.project.name !== "desktop-shell", "desktop wiring: the port is only there in the desktop bundle");
test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const calls: unknown[][] = [];
    (window as any).__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_CALLS__ = calls;
    (window as any).__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__ = {
      async save(options: { defaultPath?: string }) {
        calls.push(["save", options]);
        return (window as any).__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_CANCEL__ ? null : `/fake/${options.defaultPath ?? "file"}`;
      },
      async writeTextFile(path: string, text: string) { calls.push(["write", path, text.length]); }
    };
  });
});
```

   before clicking `export-game`; `save` called, no `write`, `game-picker` still visible.
