title: Export gate stands aside off main
description:
scripts/beadsExportGate.ts writes the whole bead database into .beads/issues.jsonl on every branch it runs on. Two agents' PRs therefore carry complete backlog snapshots taken at different moments, and whichever merges last silently reverts every close, claim, label and plan recorded in between. Git usually will not even conflict, because each side rewrote a different subset of the one-line-per-bead file.

The gate becomes a main-only obligation: on any other branch it stands aside, exactly as it already does when bd is missing or node_modules are absent. main is refreshed by the planner's own pushes and by a post-merge refresh.

This is the highest-probability silent-wrong-result in the harness, and it gets worse once plans live in the design field.
acceptance_criteria:
runGate proceeds without exporting when the current branch is not main.
The existing stand-aside idiom and its tests are followed rather than a new mechanism.
Two branches, each pushed after a bead change and merged in turn, leave the first branch's bead state intact - demonstrated, not assumed.

title: Planner and implementer agent harness
description:
A planning session turns unplanned beads into fully specified ones and owns every UI decision with the navigator; one or more implementation sessions pick up a planned bead, implement it under TDD, get it reviewed by Copilot, merged, and loop.

The split only works if the plan is a real contract and if the agents cannot corrupt each other. A stress test against this repository found five ways the obvious design breaks or silently produces wrong results; the infrastructure children below are those fixes, and they must land before more than one implementation agent runs.

Full design, including the twenty decisions taken with the navigator, is in the children's plans and in the harness skills themselves.
acceptance_criteria:
One planner session and one implementer session carry a real bead from unplanned to merged, with no navigator action beyond the UI discussion during planning.
Two agents can run the smoke and PWA suites at once without testing each other's bundles.
Concurrent PRs no longer overwrite each other's bead state.
close_reason: All 11 children delivered; validated by a live trial on 2026-08-13 in which Cyclops took ah-5jm from claim to merge unattended under scripts/run-implementer

title: Stop agents colliding on a bead someone already claimed
description:
## Summary

Two agents keep starting work on the same bead. The cause is not carelessness — it is that a claim
looks abandoned within minutes of being taken.

`bd update <id> --claim` takes a **lease** with a short TTL, kept alive only by `bd heartbeat`.
Neither `CLAUDE.md` nor the `beads-workflow` skill mentions `bd heartbeat` at all, so no agent here
has ever sent one. A work cycle in this repo — RED, GREEN, REFACTOR, a full local gate, CI — runs an
hour or more against a TTL of roughly five minutes.

Observed, on a bead an agent had claimed ten minutes earlier and was demonstrably still working
(it had already wired a dependency from it):

```
◐ ah-xde · Remove the Classic map theme   [P2 · IN_PROGRESS]
Lease: expires in 1 min (heartbeat 3 mins ago)
```

`bd reclaim` is the reaper: it finds in_progress issues whose lease expired, **clears the assignee
and sets them back to open** so another worker can claim them. `bd update --force` documents itself
as being for "abandoned claims — crashed agent, expired lease". With nobody heartbeating, every live
claim in this repository matches that description exactly.

Three contributing findings:

- **The selection window.** The loop claims before branching, but exploration and planning happen
  first — one bead was planned for ten minutes before it was claimed. Selected-but-unclaimed work is
  invisible to every other agent.
- **Worktrees are not the problem.** All three worktrees resolve to the same Dolt database, so a
  claim is visible locally the moment it is written.
- **Cross-machine is.** Leases are node-local and write no Dolt commit; only status and assignee
  commit, and those travel only on `bd dolt push`/`bd dolt pull`. The skill says to push at session
  end, so a claim can stay invisible to another machine for an entire session.

`claim.ttl` is not a documented config key — `bd config get claim.ttl` reports "not set", and the
skill already records that `bd config set` accepts unknown keys silently — so lengthening the TTL is
not a reliable lever. The fix belongs in the instructions.

## Scope

Update `.claude/skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (the symlink to
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) with four rules, agreed with the navigator:

1. **Claim first.** `bd update <id> --claim` is the first action after choosing a bead — before
   exploring, planning or asking questions, not merely before branching. A failed claim means
   somebody else won; pick another bead.
2. **Heartbeat while working.** `bd heartbeat <id>` at every phase gate and before any long wait (a
   full smoke run, a CI watch). Heartbeats write no Dolt commit and no history, so the cadence is
   free.
3. **Never take over a claim unasked.** `in_progress` with an assignee is authoritative whatever the
   lease says. No `bd reclaim`, no `bd update --force`, no reassignment over a live claim without
   the navigator saying so — an expired lease here means "nobody heartbeated", not "the worker
   died".
4. **Push the claim immediately.** `bd dolt push` right after claiming, not only at session end, so
   another machine can see it. Keep the session-end push as well.

Record the lease behaviour itself in the skill's Traps section, so an agent that meets a stale lease
recognises it rather than reasoning from `--force`'s help text.

## Out of scope

- Changing `claim.ttl` or any beads configuration; the key is not part of the documented surface.
- A supervisor process running `bd reclaim` on a timer. That is the upstream design for dead-worker
  recovery, and it is exactly what must not run here while nothing heartbeats.

## Validation

- `bd heartbeat <id>` on a bead this session holds, confirming the lease moves forward — the one
  claim in the four rules that has never actually been exercised here.
- Re-read both documents end to end: the daily loop, the checklist and CLAUDE.md's work-package
  rules must agree with each other, since all three currently describe claiming.
- No code changes, so the gate is `pnpm run lint` for the markdown-adjacent tooling only.
acceptance_criteria:
The beads-workflow skill and CLAUDE.md both say to claim before exploring or planning, not merely before branching.
Both say to heartbeat during long work, naming bd heartbeat.
Both forbid bd reclaim, bd update --force and reassignment over a live claim without the navigator's approval.
Both say to bd dolt push straight after claiming, in addition to at session end.
The skill's Traps section explains the lease TTL and why an expired lease here does not mean an abandoned worker.

title: Cutting a release lives in one place, and publishes the notes it wrote
description:
Cutting a release and writing its notes live in the cerebro submodule today, split across two places that do not know about each other: orchestrator.md's 'Cutting a release' section (clean main, run the release script, watch the workflow) and the release-notes skill (collect the shipped beads, drop what a player cannot see, write the notes). Neither publishes anything.

CORRECTION, 2026-08-25 (Xavier, checked before planning). This bead originally said the handwritten
notes "never reach the GitHub release, whose body is GitHub's own generate_release_notes commit
dump". That is false. Checked against the five most recent releases:

  v0.11.1  handwritten notes
  v0.11.0  handwritten notes
  v0.10.0  handwritten notes
  v0.9.0   predates docs/releases/ entirely
  v0.8.0   predates docs/releases/ entirely

So the upload IS happening - by hand, from memory, every time, with nothing written down that says
to do it. That is a better argument for this bead rather than a worse one: the step is undocumented,
not missing, and an undocumented step survives only as long as the person who remembers it. What the
flag does cause is a WINDOW: the release is born with the machine commit list and carries it publicly
until the notes are uploaded.

Atlantis HUD's release is a project concern, not a fleet concern, so it should be a skill in this repository rather than something every consumer of cerebro inherits. This bead creates that skill; ah-<cerebro side> strips the submodule.

The skill is role-neutral: any session can load it, Cerebro is simply the usual caller.

The sequence it teaches, in order:
1. Clean and current main, in the primary checkout (the checks orchestrator.md 876-899 carries today).
2. Ask which bump if the navigator did not say; run 'pnpm run release <bump>'. The script owns the version arithmetic, the gate, the two manifests, the commit and the tag push - do not duplicate any of it here.
3. The tag push starts the Release workflow, which builds the bundles and creates the GitHub release. Start watching it.
4. WHILE it builds, write the notes from the beads in the range - this is the whole of the current release-notes skill, moved in and made concrete about this project: notes live at docs/releases/v<version>.md, and v0.11.0.md and v0.11.1.md are the worked examples.
5. When the workflow finishes, upload the notes: gh release edit v<version> --notes-file docs/releases/v<version>.md.
6. Commit the notes file to main.

Note that release.yml's publish job currently sets generate_release_notes: true, so the release is born with a machine-generated commit list as its body until step 5 overwrites it. Decide whether that flag should go.
design:
## Context

Cutting a release and writing its notes live in the cerebro submodule, split across two documents
that do not know about each other: `agents/orchestrator.md`'s *"Cutting a release"* (clean main, run
the release script, watch the workflow) and the `release-notes` skill (collect the shipped beads,
drop what a player cannot see, write the notes). **Neither says to publish anything.**

**One claim in the bead was wrong and the planner checked it first.** It said the written notes
*"never reach the GitHub release"*. They do — `v0.11.1`, `v0.11.0` and `v0.10.0` all carry the
handwritten page; only `v0.9.0` and `v0.8.0`, which predate `docs/releases/` entirely, do not. **The
upload is happening from memory, every time, with nothing written down that says to do it.** The
bead's description now records that, and it is a better argument for this work rather than a worse
one: an undocumented step survives exactly as long as the person who remembers it.

What the flag *does* cause is a **window**. `release.yml:402` sets `generate_release_notes: true`, so
the release is born with GitHub's machine commit list — bead ids, refactorings, everything the
release-notes skill exists to strip — and carries it publicly until the notes are uploaded.

**Releases are this project's concern, not the fleet's.** Every consumer of cerebro inherits
`orchestrator.md` and the `release-notes` skill today; a project-owned skill is the right home, and
this bead creates it. A separate cerebro-side change strips the submodule afterwards.

**When this lands, one document carries the whole sequence, and a release is never publicly described
by a commit dump.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **New:** `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md` — the whole sequence.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — drop `generate_release_notes: true` (`:402`).
- **Nothing in `.claude/cerebro`.** The submodule is stripped by its own bead, later; touching it here
  turns a one-PR change into two while the skill it replaces still works.

### The structural fact that shapes this

**`.claude/skills/` is currently four symlinks into the submodule** and nothing else:

```
beads-workflow -> ../cerebro/skills/beads-workflow
implement-bead -> ../cerebro/skills/implement-bead
plan-bead      -> ../cerebro/skills/plan-bead
release-notes  -> ../cerebro/skills/release-notes
```

So this is **the repository's first skill of its own**. It goes in as a real directory beside them —
the navigator's choice — and `.gitignore:33` already carries `!.claude/skills/`, so it is tracked
with no ignore change. **Do not add a fifth symlink, and do not disturb the four.**

### What already exists and must be reused

- **`.claude/cerebro/agents/orchestrator.md:876-899`** — the clean-and-current-main checks, including
  the `cd "$(git worktree list --porcelain | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2)"` step and *why* it matters
  (*"one `cd` into an implementer's worktree sends every later git command there, where a release
  would be cut from somebody's feature branch"*). **Move this text; do not rewrite it.**
- **`.claude/cerebro/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`** — 178 lines, the whole of steps 4's content:
  the range, the beads that shipped, dropping what a player cannot see, what each surviving bead did,
  writing it, and the *Before you hand it over* checks. **Move it in and make it concrete about this
  project**, which mostly means resolving one lookup: it currently reads the audience noun from
  `project-conf audience_noun` and then says *"Here it is **player**"*. In a project-owned skill the
  lookup is unnecessary — write `player` throughout and drop the paragraph explaining the key.
- **`pnpm run release <bump>`** (`package.json:8` → `scripts/release.ts`), which
  `project-conf release_cmd` names. **It owns the version arithmetic, the gate, the two manifests,
  the commit and the tag push.** The skill must say so and duplicate none of it.
- **`docs/releases/v0.11.0.md` and `v0.11.1.md`** — the worked examples the skill points at.
- **`gh release edit v<version> --notes-file docs/releases/v<version>.md`** — the publish step.

### The design of the document

`.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`, with the usual frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: release
description: Cut a release of Atlantis HUD, write its notes while the workflow builds, publish them to the GitHub release, and commit the file. Use when the navigator asks for a release, or asks what would go out in one.
---
```

**Role-neutral.** Any session can load it; Cerebro is simply the usual caller. Say that in the
opening, because the text it absorbs from `orchestrator.md` is written to one role and must stop
being.

**Six steps, in order, with the ordering itself argued** — the notes are written *while* the workflow
builds, which is what makes the sequence worth writing down rather than obvious:

1. **A clean and current main, in the primary checkout.** The `orchestrator.md` block verbatim,
   including the `pwd` warning.
2. **Ask which bump if the navigator did not say**, then `pnpm run release <bump>`. State plainly
   that the script owns everything from version arithmetic to the tag push, and that this document
   must never duplicate it — a second copy of the release arithmetic is the failure this bead exists
   to prevent, one level up.
3. **The tag push starts the Release workflow.** Start watching it.
4. **While it builds, write the notes** — the release-notes content, moved in. They live at
   `docs/releases/v<version>.md`.
5. **When the workflow finishes, publish:**
   `gh release edit v<version> --notes-file docs/releases/v<version>.md`. **This is the step nobody
   wrote down**, and the skill should say so in a line, so the next reader understands why a document
   exists for something that has always worked.
6. **Commit the notes file to main.**

**The workflow change.** Drop `generate_release_notes: true` from `release.yml:402`, so the release
is born with an empty body and step 5 fills it. The navigator's reasoning, recorded because the diff
is one line and the reason is not obvious: *an empty body reads as "not written yet"; a commit dump
reads as "this is the changelog", and it is the wrong thing to show a player.* Leave the comment
below that line — the *Installing* / README matched pair — exactly where it is.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere: a document and a one-line workflow change. No code, no tests, no
schema.

## Increments

**1. The skill.**
Create `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md` with all six steps, moving the two sources in rather than
paraphrasing them. Confirm it is a real file and tracked:

```bash
ls -l .claude/skills/          # release/ is a directory, the other four still symlinks
git status --short             # the new file appears, i.e. .gitignore does not swallow it
```

**2. The workflow.**
Remove `generate_release_notes: true` (`release.yml:402`). Nothing else in that step changes.

**3. Read it back as the caller.**
Follow the skill from the top **without running it**, checking that every command it names exists and
every path it cites resolves — `pnpm run release`, `gh release edit`, `docs/releases/`, the two
worked examples. This is a document whose whole value is being followed unattended; a stale path in
it is the same defect as a stale citation in a plan.

## The test plan

**There is no test to write, and saying so is better than inventing one.** This bead produces a
markdown document and deletes one line of YAML. The repository has no harness that exercises a skill,
and `release.yml` is only exercised by cutting a real release.

What stands in for tests:

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| the skill is tracked, not ignored | `git status --short` shows it; `.gitignore:33` is `!.claude/skills/` |
| the four symlinks are undisturbed | `ls -l .claude/skills/` |
| every path and command the skill cites exists | increment 3, by hand |
| the workflow file still parses | `pnpm run check:fast` includes the CI-shape gates |
| nothing else changed in `release.yml` | read the diff — it must be exactly one line |

**The real proof is the next release**, and the skill should be followed rather than remembered when
it comes.

## User-facing decisions

Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-25. **No mockup**: the only audience-visible surface is the
GitHub release page, and the change to it is the absence of a machine-generated list.

1. **The release is born with an empty body.** `generate_release_notes: true` goes.
   *Rejected — keep the flag*, on the ground that something is better than nothing in the window: the
   machine list names beads and refactorings a player cannot act on, which is exactly the material
   the notes exist to strip out.
   *Rejected — seed a placeholder line* (*"Release notes are being written and will appear here
   shortly"*): honest about the window, but it is a string to maintain and a stale one if an upload
   ever fails.
2. **The skill is a real directory at `.claude/skills/release/`**, beside the four symlinks.
   *Rejected — source it elsewhere and symlink it in*, keeping `.claude/skills/` purely symlinks:
   indirection with no second consumer to justify it.
   *Rejected — leave it in cerebro*: every consumer would inherit this project's release shape, which
   is what the bead argues against.

## Out of scope

- **`.claude/cerebro` in any form**, including deleting the `release-notes` symlink or stripping
  `orchestrator.md`'s section. That is the paired cerebro-side bead, and doing it here would leave
  this repository depending on a submodule bump to be coherent.
- **`scripts/release.ts`.** The skill describes it and changes nothing in it.
- **The wording of the notes themselves**, and `docs/releases/`'s existing pages.
- **Automating the upload** in `release.yml`. The notes are written by a session while the workflow
  runs, so the workflow cannot have them; a later bead could invert that, and this one does not.
- **The `Installing` section** of the publish step, which is a matched pair with README.md and is
  called out as such in the file.

## Validation

```bash
ls -l .claude/skills/                 # release/ real, the four symlinks intact
git status --short                    # the new file is tracked
git diff .github/workflows/release.yml # exactly one line removed
pnpm run check:fast
```

**The human check:** read the skill end to end as somebody who has never cut a release here, and ask
whether they could do it from this document alone — including the step that has only ever existed in
somebody's head. That is the whole point of the bead, and it cannot be tested any other way.

## Known traps

- **`.claude/skills/` is four symlinks today.** Add a real directory; do not convert the others, and
  do not add a fifth symlink. `.gitignore:33`'s `!.claude/skills/` already tracks what you add.
- **Do not duplicate `scripts/release.ts`.** It owns the version arithmetic, the gate, the two
  manifests, the commit and the tag push. A second copy of any of that in prose is the same class of
  defect this project has spent several beads removing from its code.
- **The primary-checkout check is load-bearing.** `orchestrator.md` explains that a `cd` into an
  implementer's worktree persists, and a release cut from there comes off somebody's feature branch.
  Move that paragraph with its reasoning, not just its commands.
- **The audience noun is `player`, and in a project-owned skill it is written, not looked up.** The
  cerebro skill reads `project-conf audience_noun` because it serves every consumer; this one does
  not need to, and carrying the lookup across would be copying machinery that has lost its purpose.
- **Touching the submodule turns this into two PRs.** See *Out of scope*.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, nothing is rendered, but named because it is
  the trap most beads in this repository meet.
acceptance_criteria:
A skill in this repository (not the submodule) that a session can load and follow to take a release from 'cut a minor release' to a published GitHub release carrying the handwritten notes.

The notes have TWO destinations, and both are required - neither substitutes for the other:
 - committed to main at docs/releases/v<version>.md, which is the durable record and matches the existing v0.11.0.md and v0.11.1.md;
 - uploaded as the GitHub release body once the Release workflow has finished, via gh release edit v<version> --notes-file docs/releases/v<version>.md, replacing the machine-generated commit list the workflow's generate_release_notes flag puts there.

It absorbs everything the cerebro release-notes skill taught about choosing and phrasing what a player can see, including the audience-noun handling, since the submodule copy is being deleted.
It absorbs orchestrator.md's clean-main checks and its never-force rules.
It does not restate what scripts/release.ts already does.
Nothing in it is specific to the fleet - no Cerebro, no state files, no phases.
notes: Inventory of what is being moved: release-notes/SKILL.md (178 lines, in full); orchestrator.md 849-956 plus the phase-table line at 22-23; the docs/releases/ convention, which exists only as two files on disk. Depends on nothing; ah-<cerebro side> depends on this one landing first so the submodule is not stripped before the replacement exists.

title: Picking a unit in the hex already selected does not bring the map to it
description:
Found by the navigator on 2026-08-25 while verifying ah-z31p at origin/main a81d1b45.

## What happens

Clicking a unit in the Problems list, when that unit's hex is not currently visible on the map,
leaves the map where it is. The selection ring is somewhere the player cannot see, which is the
exact situation the travel rule exists to prevent.

The same jump from the COMMAND PALETTE does travel, correctly. So this is not the travel machinery
being broken - it is some Problems entries not reaching it.

## What is already known, so nobody re-derives it

The rule, at packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewState.ts:137, names this case in terms:

  "It should [travel] whenever the player picks a hex from somewhere other than the map - the units
   table, A PROBLEM IN THE PANEL - because a selection ring nobody can see is no answer."

Both surfaces call the same function. AppShell.tsx:3195 wires the Problems panel as
onSelectUnit={(unitId) => goToUnit(unitId, "problems")}, and the palette calls goToUnit(unitId) at
:1011. goToUnit (:836) switches level if needed and then calls selectRegion(regionId, unitId).

The travel itself is decided by travelsToSelection (mapViewState.ts:191), which fires only when
selectedRegionId or restoredRegionId CHANGES. That is deliberate: a hex clicked on the map is already
visible, and a hex the player panned away from before quitting is left alone on restore.

## The most likely cause, stated as a hypothesis and not a diagnosis

There is more than one Problems surface. The header's Problems panel (AppShell.tsx:3189-3195) lists
findings across the faction; the region panel's list (:3430, :3556, both goToUnit(unitId, null)) is
scoped to the hex already selected. For the hex-scoped one, the unit is in the SELECTED hex, so
selectedRegionId does not change, travelsToSelection returns false, and the map deliberately stays -
even if the player has panned that hex off screen.

If that is what the navigator hit, then the question this bead has to answer is a DESIGN one and
belongs to a planner: should picking a unit from a list bring the map back to a selection the player
has panned away from? travelsToSelection's own doc comment currently says no, for the restore case,
and the two cases may want different answers.

If instead the header Problems panel fails to travel for a unit in a genuinely different hex, that is
a straightforward defect in that path and no interview is needed.

WHICH OF THE TWO IT IS SHOULD BE ESTABLISHED FIRST, on a real report, before any code is written.

## Not caused by ah-z31p

ah-z31p passed verification at a81d1b45. It moved this arithmetic out of MapCanvas so it could be
tested at all; it did not write the rule, and the palette path proves the extracted machinery works.

## Reproduction

tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep, any hex with findings. Select a hex, pan the
map until it is off screen, then click a unit in the Problems list. Compare with the same unit
reached from the command palette.
design:
## Context

Clicking a unit in the region panel's Problems list leaves the map where it is when the selected hex
has been panned off screen. The rule at `mapViewState.ts:137` names that case in terms — the map
should travel *"whenever the player picks a hex from somewhere other than the map — the units table,
a problem in the panel — because a selection ring nobody can see is no answer."*

**The bead's framing is wrong, and the planner established that before planning.** It supposes some
Problems entries fail to reach the travel machinery while the command palette reaches it correctly.
They reach the same machinery, and the palette fails identically on the same input:

| fact | where |
|---|---|
| the palette runs `goToUnit(unitId)` | `AppShell.tsx:1011` |
| the Problems panel runs `goToUnit(unitId, "problems")` | `:3195` |
| the region panel's lists run `goToUnit(unitId, null)` | `:3430`, `:3556` |
| `travelsToSelection` fires **only when `selectedRegionId` changes** | `mapViewState.ts:191` |
| `selectRegion` is a **complete no-op** for the hex already selected | `workspaceStore.ts:412` |
| the region panel's Problems list is **hex-scoped** — `findingsForHex(diagnostics, hex?.regionId)` | `AppShell.tsx:3425` |

So the failing condition is **"the target is in the hex already selected"**, not "the click came from
Problems". The region panel's list is scoped to the selected hex, so *every* unit in it is same-hex
and that surface never travels; the header Problems panel spans the faction and usually does. The
original comparison was a same-hex click against a different-hex click, not two surfaces.

**Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-25: travel because the player asked, not because of
geometry.** See *User-facing decisions*, including why the obvious alternative is dangerous.

**When this lands, picking a unit or hex from any list brings the map to it — even when that hex is
already selected and has been panned away from — and nothing else moves the map that did not before.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.ts` — a pick epoch, and `selectRegion` learning about picks.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewState.ts` — `FollowedSelection` and `travelsToSelection`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — read the epoch into the effect's `current`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — `goToUnit` marks its calls as picks.

### What already exists and must be reused

- **`selectionEpoch`** (`workspaceStore.ts:116`, bumped at `:413`) — the precedent for a counter that
  exists purely to make a repeat *observable*. It is **not** the right one to reuse: it drives a CSS
  remount (`key={selectionEpoch}` in `MapCanvas.tsx`, documented at `theme.css:244`), so bumping it
  on every pick would restart the selection-ring animation for a hex that did not change. Add a
  second counter rather than overloading this one.
- **`travelsToSelection(current, last)`** (`mapViewState.ts:191`) and **`FollowedSelection`**
  (`:173`) — the comparison already takes a `last` snapshot, so a third field is a natural extension.
- **`shouldFollowSelection`** (`:142`) — the restore exemption. **It must also learn about picks**;
  see the trap below.
- **`mapViewSelectionChanged`** (`:67`) — ends the restore exemption when the selection moves off the
  restored hex. It is called from `selectRegion`, which same-hex picks never reach.
- **`followViewport`** (`mapFraming.ts:89`) — takes `travels` as a parameter, *"computed by the
  caller"*. Unchanged: this bead only changes what that boolean says.
- **`lastFollowed` ref** (`MapCanvas.tsx:546`) — the effect's own memory of the last pair.

### The design of the code

**1. A pick epoch on the store**, beside `selectionEpoch` and deliberately separate from it:

```ts
/**
 * Bumped every time the player picks a hex or unit from somewhere OTHER than the map - a list, the
 * palette, a problem in the panel. It exists so that picking the hex that is already selected is
 * still observable: `selectRegion` short-circuits for an unchanged region, and the map would
 * otherwise never learn the player asked to be taken there (`ah-lqct`).
 *
 * Separate from `selectionEpoch`, which drives the selection ring's remount: bumping that one for
 * an unchanged hex would restart the ring's animation for no visible reason.
 */
pickEpoch: number;
```

`selectRegion` gains an options argument rather than a fourth positional:

```ts
selectRegion: (
  regionId: string | null,
  defaultUnitId?: string | null,
  options?: { picked?: boolean }
) => void;
```

and its body keeps its short-circuit for the ordinary case while letting a pick through:

```ts
selectRegion: (regionId, defaultUnitId = null, options) =>
  set((state) => {
    if (state.selectedRegionId === regionId) {
      // The hex is already selected. Nothing about the selection changes - but if the player
      // ASKED for it, the map still owes them a look at it.
      return options?.picked
        ? {
            pickEpoch: state.pickEpoch + 1,
            // An explicit pick ends the restore exemption too: the player has asked for this hex
            // by name, which the restore rule's "leave it where they left it" no longer covers.
            mapView: { ...state.mapView, restoredRegionId: null }
          }
        : state;
    }
    return {
      selectedRegionId: regionId,
      selectedUnitId: defaultUnitId,
      selectionEpoch: state.selectionEpoch + 1,
      pickEpoch: options?.picked ? state.pickEpoch + 1 : state.pickEpoch,
      mapView: mapViewSelectionChanged(state.mapView, regionId)
    };
  }),
```

**2. `FollowedSelection` and the predicate:**

```ts
export type FollowedSelection = {
  selectedRegionId: string | null;
  restoredRegionId: string | null;
  /** `pickEpoch` from the store - see its doc comment. */
  pickEpoch: number;
};

export function travelsToSelection(current: FollowedSelection, last: FollowedSelection): boolean {
  if (!shouldFollowSelection(current.selectedRegionId, current.restoredRegionId)) {
    return false;
  }
  return (
    current.selectedRegionId !== last.selectedRegionId ||
    current.restoredRegionId !== last.restoredRegionId ||
    // The player picked a hex from a list. A repeat pick of the hex already selected changes
    // neither id, and is exactly the case this bead exists for.
    current.pickEpoch !== last.pickEpoch
  );
}
```

**3. `MapCanvas` reads it into `current`** (`:553`) and seeds `lastFollowed` with `pickEpoch: 0`.
Nothing else in that effect changes — in particular it still depends on `size` and `insets`, and a
container resize with no pick still computes `travels === false`, which is what four earlier fixes
were about.

**4. `goToUnit` marks its calls as picks.** Every one of its eight call sites
(`AppShell.tsx:922, 954, 1011, 2405, 3013, 3195, 3430, 3556`) is a list, a palette entry or a panel —
none is a click on the map — so `goToUnit` passes `{ picked: true }` on the *inside* rather than each
caller opting in:

```ts
selectRegion(regionId, unitId, { picked: true });
```

**Do not make the callers pass it.** Eight call sites that must all remember a flag is eight chances
to forget one, and the fact that makes them all picks — none of them is the map — is a property of
`goToUnit`, not of its callers.

**Where state lives.** One integer on the workspace store, one field on a type that already exists,
and one ref seed. No new component, no new effect, nothing persisted — `pickEpoch` is session state
like `selectionEpoch` and must not be written to the saved view.

## Increments

**1. The predicate.**
Failing test in `mapViewState.test.ts`: `travels_when_the_player_picks_the_hex_already_selected` —
same `selectedRegionId` and `restoredRegionId`, `pickEpoch` incremented → `true`. Plus
`does_not_travel_when_nothing_changed` (identical snapshots → `false`, the resize case) and
`does_not_travel_for_the_restored_hex_without_a_pick`. Then add the field and the clause.

**2. The store.**
Failing tests in `workspaceStore.test.ts`: `a_pick_of_the_selected_hex_bumps_the_pick_epoch`;
`an_ordinary_reselect_of_the_same_hex_changes_nothing` (no `picked` → state identity unchanged,
which is what keeps the short-circuit honest); `a_pick_of_the_selected_hex_does_not_bump_the_selection_epoch`
— **the ring must not re-animate**; `a_pick_ends_the_restore_exemption`. Then add `pickEpoch` and the
options argument.

**3. The wiring.**
No new test of its own; increments 1 and 2 pin the behaviour and the existing `MapCanvas` and
`AppShell` suites must stay green. Read `pickEpoch` into `current`, seed `lastFollowed`, and pass
`{ picked: true }` from inside `goToUnit`.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `travels_when_the_player_picks_the_hex_already_selected` | `mapViewState.test.ts` | the bug |
| `does_not_travel_when_nothing_changed` | `mapViewState.test.ts` | the resize case four fixes paid for |
| `does_not_travel_for_the_restored_hex_without_a_pick` | `mapViewState.test.ts` | the restore exemption survives |
| `a_pick_of_the_selected_hex_bumps_the_pick_epoch` | `workspaceStore.test.ts` | the signal exists |
| `an_ordinary_reselect_of_the_same_hex_changes_nothing` | `workspaceStore.test.ts` | the short-circuit is intact |
| `a_pick_of_the_selected_hex_does_not_bump_the_selection_epoch` | `workspaceStore.test.ts` | the ring does not re-animate |
| `a_pick_ends_the_restore_exemption` | `workspaceStore.test.ts` | `shouldFollowSelection` cannot block a pick |

**The regression net:** every existing `mapViewState`, `workspaceStore`, `MapCanvas` and `AppShell`
test, **unedited**. `mapViewState`'s suite in particular encodes the four fixes about the map moving
under a landed turn; if one of those moves, this bead has reopened exactly what it must not.

**`packages/shared` has no jsdom**, so none of this is tested by rendering. Every test above is on a
pure function or the store — which is why the design puts the whole rule in those two places and
leaves `MapCanvas` as three lines of wiring.

## User-facing decisions

Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-25. **No mockup**: nothing about the interface changes — no
message, no control, no layout. What changes is when the map moves, which a static page cannot show.

1. **Travel because the player asked, not because of geometry.** An explicit "the player picked this"
   signal forces the travel even when the region is unchanged.
   *Rejected — travel when the selection is off screen.* Simpler and needs no new signal, but
   `travelsToSelection`'s own comment records that re-running against `size` and `insets` with
   nothing about the selection changed *"is what moved the map under a landed turn, four fixes
   running"*. A geometry test reopens that door; an intent test cannot, because a resize is not a
   pick.
   *Rejected — fix only the region panel's Problems list.* It is the surface the navigator hit, but
   the palette and the units table fail identically for a same-hex unit, so the rule would stay
   inconsistent and the next report would be the same bug from a different list.
   *Rejected — leave it*, on the ground that a selected hex has already been navigated to. It
   contradicts `mapViewState.ts:137`, which the navigator wrote.
2. **The code evidence was accepted in place of a live reproduction.** The bead asks for the fork to
   be established on a real report first; the planner established it from the call graph — one
   function, one predicate, one hex-scoped list — and the navigator judged that sufficient.

## Out of scope

- **The `selectionEpoch` ring animation.** Deliberately untouched; a pick of the same hex must not
  restart it.
- **The restore-on-load behaviour.** A restore is not a pick and stays exempt.
- **Map clicks.** They already travel or need not; `goToUnit` is not on that path.
- **Whether the region panel's Problems list should be hex-scoped at all.** It is, by design; this
  bead makes picking from it work rather than changing what it lists.
- **`followViewport` and the framing arithmetic** (`mapFraming.ts`), including `ah-z31p`'s
  extraction. Only the `travels` boolean handed to it changes.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm vitest run packages/shared        # after each increment
pnpm run check:fast                    # before the PR
```

**The human check, and this bead needs one because the whole subject is movement:** load
`neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, select a hex with findings, pan until it is off screen, then click
a unit in the region panel's Problems list — the map should come back to it. Then repeat with the
command palette on a unit in that same hex, which fails the same way today and must also be fixed.
Finally, open and close a pane while a hex is selected and confirm the map does **not** move.

## Known traps

- **A same-hex `selectRegion` is a complete no-op today** (`workspaceStore.ts:412`). That is why no
  epoch bumps and why the map never learns. Preserving the short-circuit for the *unpicked* case is
  what keeps every other caller's behaviour identical.
- **Do not reuse `selectionEpoch`.** It drives the selection ring's remount (`theme.css:244`);
  bumping it for an unchanged hex restarts an animation for no visible reason. A test pins this.
- **A pick must end the restore exemption**, or `shouldFollowSelection` returns `false` and the pick
  is swallowed for exactly the hex a restore put back — which is a hex the player is especially
  likely to have panned away from.
- **Geometry must not decide travel.** The effect still depends on `size` and `insets`; a resize with
  no pick must still compute `travels === false`. Four earlier fixes are about this.
- **Put `{ picked: true }` inside `goToUnit`, not at its eight call sites.** They are all lists,
  panels and palette entries; none is the map.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (ah-nass) — test the pure function and the store, never by
  rendering `MapCanvas`.
acceptance_criteria:
Picking a unit from the Problems list puts its hex on screen, or the navigator has decided at triage that a hex the player panned away from is deliberately left alone and that decision is recorded beside travelsToSelection.

The command palette's behaviour is unchanged.

A hex clicked on the map still does not make the view jump.

Whichever answer is chosen is covered by a test in mapViewState.test.ts or mapFraming.test.ts - both are now reachable without a browser, which is what ah-z31p delivered.

title: A combat mage's men are not counted toward the pillage threshold
description:
Found by Xavier on 2026-08-25 while revising ah-cw75, and kept out of that bead by the navigator so a
P0 a player is waiting on is not delayed.

## The gap

The rules give four ways a unit can tax, and the pillage threshold counts those same taxing
characters (tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html):

  "A unit may TAX if it has Combat skill of at least level 1, has a weapon and the appropriate skill
  to use it, has a mount and sufficient skill to ride it in combat or is a mage who knows a spell
  which damages enemies."

ah-cw75 implements the first three. This bead is the fourth.

## CORRECTION, 2026-08-25

An earlier version of this description said the fourth way was not answerable from the ruleset -
"no damage marker, and skills carry no descriptions at all". THAT WAS WRONG, and it was wrong in a
way worth recording: the planner queried a top-level `description` field, found none, and concluded
the text was absent.

The text is there. It lives under levels[] as { level, description }, one entry per level, written
by parseSkillReference in packages/ruleset/src/data.ts. COMB's own level-1 entry reads "This skill
gives the unit a bonus in hand to hand combat. Also, a unit with this skill may TAX or PILLAGE."

This is the failure mode filed as https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/150 - checking that a
name resolves rather than what it means - committed by the planner who filed it, hours later.

## What the data supports

Of 70 magic skills, 18 mention battle. Testing the pattern "deals N damage" against each level-1
description selects exactly eight:

  FIRE  EQUA  STOR  CALL  SBLA  BUND  BDEM  DISP

with no false positives:

  the four shields (FSHI, ESHI, SSHI and the fourth) say "shield against all ranged attacks" and
  match no damage pattern;
  the four summons (DRAG, SUSK, RAIS, SULI) say the summoned creatures "aid in battle" and likewise
  do not.

A naive match on "attack" or "battle" would have caught both groups. The navigator confirmed the
eight on 2026-08-25.

Deliberately excluded: FEAR (cause fear) and SSTO (summon storm), which are cast at enemies but
state no damage. That under-counts, which produces a missing warning rather than a false one - the
direction crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs always errs in. Included, deliberately: BUND, BDEM and
DISP, which damage only undead, demons and illusions respectively; they do damage enemies when those
enemies are present, and the rules draw no distinction.

## The effect while it is missing

A combat mage's men are not counted toward a region's pillage threshold, so a faction that could
legally pillage may be told it has too few combat ready men.

## DO NOT hard-code a spell list

A per-tag allowlist in core that nothing links back to the ruleset is exactly the failure ah-v9p2
was filed and fixed for: upkeep-exceeds-unclaimed shipped correct, tested and invisible because its
properties lived in a hand-maintained list. Derive it.
design:
## Context

The rules give four ways a unit can tax, and the pillage threshold counts those same taxing
characters (`tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html`):

> *"A unit may TAX if it has Combat skill of at least level 1, has a weapon and the appropriate skill
> to use it, has a mount and sufficient skill to ride it in combat **or is a mage who knows a spell
> which damages enemies**."*

`ah-cw75` (P0) implements the first three. This bead is the fourth, kept separate by the navigator so
that P0 is not delayed.

While a combat mage is uncounted, a faction that could legally pillage may be told it has too few
combat ready men — an under-count, so a **missing** warning rather than a false one, which is the
direction `semantics.rs` always errs in. That is why it was safe to ship `ah-cw75` without it.

**Two things this bead's own description got wrong, both corrected there and repeated here because
they change the cost:**

1. **The skill text is in the ruleset.** It lives under `levels[]` as `{ level, description }`, one
   entry per level. Only a *top-level* `description` field is absent, and that is what the planner
   queried before wrongly concluding the data could not answer this
   (https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro/issues/150 is about exactly that habit).
2. **The schema is no longer mirrored by hand.** `ah-gdfe` shipped as `4b22714d` (#656),
   *"generate the ruleset schema from Rust"*. `packages/ruleset/src/generated/SkillEntry.ts` now
   opens *"generated by ts-rs. Do not edit this file manually."* So adding a field is a Rust struct
   change, a scraper change and a regeneration — **not** the seven-to-eight files kept in step by
   hand that this bead originally cited as the cost.

**And there is a direct precedent for the whole shape.** `SkillEntry::magic` is a boolean the data
page *"marks nowhere and the scraper therefore reads from the skill's own description"*
(`rules.rs:501-506`), derived by `MAGIC_WORDS.test(paragraph)` at `data.ts:621`. This bead adds a
second field of exactly that kind.

**When this lands, a mage who knows a damaging spell counts toward the pillage threshold like any
other taxing character.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` — one field on `SkillEntry`.
- `packages/ruleset/src/generated/SkillEntry.ts` — regenerated, never hand-edited.
- `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` — the scraper derives it.
- `config/public/ruleset.json` — re-scraped, or the field defaults false.
- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — `readiness` reads it.

### What already exists and must be reused

- **`SkillEntry::magic`** (`rules.rs:506`) and its derivation (`data.ts:393` `MAGIC_WORDS`, applied
  at `:619-621`). **This is the model**: a `#[serde(default)]` boolean on the Rust struct, derived
  from the level-1 paragraph by a named regex with a doc comment explaining what it must and must
  not match.
- **`parseSkillReference`** (`data.ts:580`) and its per-level `appendLevel`, which is what puts the
  paragraph text in `levels[]` in the first place.
- **`skill_level(facts.skills, tag)`** in `silver.rs` — how a unit's own skill level is read.
- **`readiness`** (`silver.rs:1853`) as `ah-cw75` leaves it. **This bead is written against
  `ah-cw75`'s result, not against `main`** — see *Out of scope*.
- **`#[serde(default)]`**, so a ruleset scraped before this field exists still deserialises. `magic`
  does the same and says why.

### The design of the code

**1. The derivation, in `data.ts` beside `MAGIC_WORDS`:**

```ts
/**
 * Whether a spell damages enemies, which is one of the four ways the rules let a unit TAX - and so
 * one of the ways its men count toward PILLAGE's threshold. The data page marks it nowhere, so it
 * is read from the skill's own description, exactly as `magic` is.
 *
 * "deals N damage" is the discriminator, and it is chosen because it separates cleanly on the
 * committed fixture where looser patterns do not:
 *
 *   matches 8 - FIRE, EQUA, STOR, CALL, SBLA, BUND, BDEM, DISP
 *   the four shields say "shield against all ranged ATTACKS" and match nothing here
 *   the four summons say the creatures "aid in BATTLE" and match nothing here
 *
 * A pattern on `attack` or `battle` would have caught both groups. Deliberately excluded: FEAR and
 * SSTO, cast at enemies but stating no damage - under-counting, which costs a missing warning
 * rather than a false one. Deliberately included: BUND, BDEM and DISP, which damage only undead,
 * demons and illusions; they damage enemies when those enemies are present, and the rules draw no
 * distinction.
 */
const DAMAGES_ENEMIES = /\bdeals? \d+ damage\b/i;
```

applied in `parseSkillReference` in the same shape as `magic` — level-1 only, `||`-accumulated so
paragraph order does not matter and a later level cannot unset it:

```ts
damagesEnemies:
  (existing?.damagesEnemies ?? false) ||
  (Number.parseInt(level, 10) === 1 && DAMAGES_ENEMIES.test(paragraph)),
```

**2. The field, in `rules.rs` beside `magic`:**

```rust
/// Whether casting this skill damages enemies, which is one of the four ways the rules let a unit
/// TAX - and so one of the ways its men count toward `PILLAGE`'s threshold. The data page marks it
/// nowhere and the scraper reads it from the skill's own description, exactly as `magic` is read.
/// `false` for a ruleset scraped before this was added, which under-counts rather than over-counts.
#[serde(default)]
pub damages_enemies: bool,
```

**3. `readiness` gains one clause.** `ah-cw75` establishes:

```rust
let all_men_count = skill_level(facts.skills, "COMB") >= 1;
```

This bead widens it:

```rust
// The rules' fourth way: "or is a mage who knows a spell which damages enemies" (`ah-v585`).
// Any level of the skill will do - the rules ask whether the mage KNOWS the spell, not how well.
let knows_a_damaging_spell = facts.skills.iter().any(|held| {
    ruleset
        .find_skill(&held.tag)
        .is_some_and(|entry| entry.damages_enemies)
        && held.level >= 1
});
let all_men_count = skill_level(facts.skills, "COMB") >= 1 || knows_a_damaging_spell;
```

**Read the real shape of a held skill before writing that** — `facts.skills` is `&[Skill]` and the
field names are the report's, not invented here; `skill_level` is the existing accessor and may be
the cleaner route.

**Any level counts, and that is a decision.** The rules say *"knows a spell which damages enemies"*
with no level qualifier, unlike Combat's explicit *"of at least level 1"*. A skill the unit holds at
all is one it knows.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new: one scraped boolean on a catalogue entry, read at the point of
use. No new type crosses the wire beyond the regenerated `SkillEntry`.

## Increments

**1. The derivation.**
Failing test in `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`: `reads_which_spells_damage_enemies`, against the
committed data-page fixture the other scraper tests use. Assert the **eight** by tag, and assert
`false` for a shield (`FSHI`), a summon (`DRAG`), `FEAR`, `SSTO` and a mundane skill (`COMB`). The
negative cases are the point: the false positives a looser pattern produces are what this test is
for. Then add `DAMAGES_ENEMIES` and the field to the scraper's output.

**2. The schema.**
Add `damages_enemies` to `SkillEntry` in `rules.rs`, regenerate, and commit the regenerated
`SkillEntry.ts`. **Do not hand-edit it.** `pnpm run check:generated` is the gate.

**3. The catalogue.**
Re-scrape `config/public/ruleset.json` so the committed ruleset carries the field. Read the diff:
exactly eight skills should gain `damagesEnemies: true` and nothing else should change. **A diff that
touches anything else means the scrape is not reproducible and is a finding in its own right.**

**4. The count.**
Failing test in `silver.rs`: `a_mage_who_knows_a_damaging_spell_makes_every_man_count` — a unit with
`FIRE` at level 1 and no weapons, asserting `ready == men`; and
`a_mage_with_only_a_shield_spell_does_not` — `FSHI` at level 1, asserting `ready == 0`. Then widen
`all_men_count`.

**5. The region sum.**
No new code. `semantics.rs:690` sums `combat_ready`, so thresholds get easier to meet again and
`pillage-without-men` findings may disappear. Run the corpus and read what moved before editing any
expectation.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `reads_which_spells_damage_enemies` | `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts` | the eight, **and the shields, summons, FEAR, SSTO and COMB that must not match** |
| `a_mage_who_knows_a_damaging_spell_makes_every_man_count` | `silver.rs` | the rule reaches the count |
| `a_mage_with_only_a_shield_spell_does_not` | `silver.rs` | the discriminator matters at the point of use, not only in the scraper |
| the existing `parseSkillReference` tests | `data.test.ts` | **unedited** — the new field must not disturb `magic`, `cost`, `produces` or `requires` |
| `pnpm run check:generated` | gate | the regenerated type is committed and in step |

**The regression net:** every existing `readiness` test from `ah-cw75`, the corpus, and
`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`, whose `EXPECTED` table counts findings over committed
turns and may move as thresholds become easier to meet.

## User-facing decisions

**No new string, no new code, no new setting.** This bead changes *which units are counted*, and the
sentences `ah-cw75` ships are unchanged.

**Which spells count — decided with the navigator on 2026-08-25.** Chosen: the eight that state
`deals N damage` — `FIRE`, `EQUA`, `STOR`, `CALL`, `SBLA`, `BUND`, `BDEM`, `DISP`.

- *Rejected — those eight plus `FEAR` and `SSTO`*, on the ground that any spell cast at enemies
  counts. It makes *"damages"* stop meaning damage, and it over-counts.
- *Rejected — excluding `BUND`, `BDEM` and `DISP`* because they damage only undead, demons and
  illusions. They damage enemies when those enemies are present, and the rules draw no distinction.
- *Rejected — not deriving it from prose at all*, and recording the fact by hand instead. Prose is
  where the data page puts it, `magic` already does this, and a hand-kept list is the `ah-v9p2`
  failure class.

**Any level of the skill counts** — the planner's reading of *"knows a spell"* against Combat's
explicit *"of at least level 1"*. Flagged here rather than buried: if the navigator wants a level
floor, it is one line.

## Out of scope

- **`ah-cw75`'s three ways.** This bead is written **against `ah-cw75`'s result** and must be built
  after it. If `readiness` still has an `avoiding` field when you pick this up, `ah-cw75` has not
  landed — stop and check.
- **Rewriting the scrape pipeline**, or adding any other derived field.
- **`FEAR` and `SSTO`.** Excluded deliberately; see above. If a player reports a mage of that kind
  being uncounted, that is a new bead and a new decision.
- **Whether a *monster's* combat skill counts**, and anything about combat itself. This is the tax
  and pillage threshold only.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test          # increment 1
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core               # increments 2 and 4
pnpm run check:generated                      # increment 2 - the gate on the regenerated type
pnpm run check:fast                           # before the PR
```

**Re-scraping the catalogue needs the data page.** `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape` takes the
source HTML; see `packages/ruleset/src/cli.ts:4` for the invocation. If the page is not to hand,
`#[serde(default)]` means the committed ruleset simply reports `false` for every skill and the
feature is inert rather than broken — say so in the PR rather than hand-editing the JSON.

**The human check:** find a fixture unit with a mage skill, order it to `PILLAGE` in a region whose
threshold it now meets, and confirm the `pillage-without-men` warning no longer fires.

## Known traps

- **`SkillEntry.ts` is generated by ts-rs.** Its first line says so. Regenerate; never hand-edit.
- **The skill's text is under `levels[]`, not a top-level `description`.** The planner got this
  wrong first time and wrote it into two beads; do not repeat it. `COMB`'s own entry is the quick
  check — it should read *"a unit with this skill may TAX or PILLAGE."*
- **A looser pattern than `deals N damage` produces false positives that matter.** Shields say
  *"shield against all ranged attacks"* and summons say *"aid in battle"*; matching `attack` or
  `battle` counts eight units that cannot tax. Over-counting is the direction this module never errs
  in.
- **Level-1 paragraph only, and `||`-accumulated**, exactly as `magic` is — higher levels describe
  what the skill does at that level and mention things incidentally.
- **`#[serde(default)]` is required**, or every ruleset scraped before this bead fails to
  deserialise — the `deny_unknown_fields` shape makes that abrupt.
- **Do not hard-code a spell list** (`ah-v9p2`).
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, nothing renders, but named because it is the
  trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: An order that overdraws a shared hex leaves its own line unmarked
description:
Found by the navigator during verification of ah-3ddq (2026-08-24, at origin/main 53b45720).

## What happened

Given GIVE 0 20000 HORS on WoodsmenY (15189) in mountain (36,4) of
tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep, the navigator looked at the order line and
saw nothing at all. The finding does exist — in the region panel:

  "the units in this hex are short 19155 horses between them: they can have 845 and their orders
  spend 20000"

— but the line that caused it carries no mark, so a player writing that order gets no signal where
they are looking.

## Why it happens

Hex (36,4) holds three sharing units, so HORS pools and report_shortfalls judges the pool rather
than the unit. A pooled finding is hex-anchored: unit_id and line are both null. orderLint.ts:31 and
orderEditor.ts:171 both drop a finding with no line, so nothing reaches the editor. It surfaces only
through findingsForHex in the region panel.

## History, and why this is filed again

ah-sdda asked this exact question and was closed on 2026-08-24 as correct behaviour, after Xavier
probed it: the pool genuinely is not that one line's fault, and the finding is accurate as written.
That reasoning stands. What is new is evidence of the cost: the navigator — who knows this system —
went looking for the message on the line, did not find it, and initially read it as a regression in
ah-3ddq. A player with less context has no reason to look at the region panel at all.

So this is not a claim that the *finding* is wrong. It is that the player is not told, at the place
they are typing, that something about this line is being reported elsewhere.

## Possible shapes, none chosen

Deliberately left open for the planner and the navigator:

- mark the line with a pointer rather than the finding itself — something that says 'this hex has a
  shortfall involving this order' and sends the reader to the region panel;
- anchor a pooled finding to every contributing line as well as to the hex, worded so it is clearly
  about the pool and not about that line alone;
- surface hex findings in the editor's gutter for whichever hex the cursor's unit is in;
- do nothing, and instead make the region panel's findings more discoverable.

Whether this is worth solving at all is the navigator's call at triage. Unranked at P4.

## Related

- ah-sdda — closed as correct behaviour; this bead is the follow-on question, not a contradiction.
- ah-3ddq — the refactoring being verified when this surfaced; it passed, and did not cause this.
design:
## Context

A pooled shortfall is hex-anchored. `report_shortfalls`'s second pass emits it through
`Hex::finding` (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`), which sets `unit_id: None` and `line: None` —
correctly, because the pool is genuinely not one line's fault. `orderLint.ts:31` and
`orderEditor.ts:171` both drop a diagnostic with no line, so **nothing reaches the editor** and the
finding surfaces only through `findingsForHex` in the region panel.

The cost is not that the finding is wrong. **ah-sdda settled that it is right**, after a probe, and
this bead does not reopen it. The cost is that the player is not told, where they are typing, that
something about this line is being reported elsewhere — and the evidence is that the navigator, who
knows this system, went looking for the mark on `GIVE 0 20000 HORS` in hex (36,4), did not find it,
and initially read it as a regression in `ah-3ddq` (which had passed).

**The contributing line is already knowable, which is what makes this cheap.**
`ledger.charged_at.get(&(unit_id, tag))` holds the `PlacedIntent` — line and columns — and the
per-unit shortfall path already uses exactly that as its `at` argument. The pooled path throws it
away. Nothing new has to be computed.

**When this lands, every order line that contributes to a pooled shortfall carries a warning saying
so, with a keyboard-reachable button that opens the hex's Problems section.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — one new code; `report_shortfalls` records contributors and
  emits a pointer per contributor.
- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — nothing.
- `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` — regenerated (the code joins `codes::ALL`).
- `packages/shared/src/orderLint.ts` — the lint action.
- `packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts` — exclude the new code from `findingsForHex`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx` — one entry in the **Resources** group.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `ledger.charged_at: BTreeMap<(String, String), PlacedIntent>` — keyed by `(unit_id, tag)`; the
  per-unit path reads it as `let at = ledger.charged_at.get(&(unit_id.clone(), tag.clone()));`.
- `Ordered::finding(&self, hex, code, message, at: Option<&PlacedIntent>) -> Finding` — sets
  `unit_id`, `line`, `column_start`, `column_end`. **This is what makes the pointer reach the editor.**
- `Hex::finding(code, message)` — the pooled finding itself, unchanged.
- The pooled pass's existing accumulators: `claims: BTreeMap<String, i64>` and
  `pooled_tags: BTreeSet<String>`, and `sharing.pool(..)` / `Sharing::reading(..)` from `ah-3ddq`.
- `plurals.get(&tag.to_ascii_uppercase()).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| item_name(tag, hex, ruleset))` —
  the plural item name **without** a count. `counted_item` requires a count and is the wrong helper
  here; this is the expression it uses internally.
- `codes::ALL` and the generator `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs`.
- `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` and `settingsStore.ts:45`, which defaults every code **on** except
  `hex-unguarded`.
- CodeMirror's `Diagnostic.actions?: readonly Action[]`
  (`@codemirror/lint@6.9.7`, `dist/index.d.ts:45`) — an `{ name, apply }` pair rendered as a button
  in the lint tooltip and reachable by keyboard. **Use this, not an `<a>` in the message**: an anchor
  inside a tooltip is not keyboard-reachable, which is why the shape was chosen this way.

### The design of the code

**Rust — one code, and a record of who contributed.**

```rust
// in `mod codes`, appended to the list and to `ALL` (which becomes `[Code; 34]`)
pub const PART_OF_HEX_SHORTFALL: Code = Code("part-of-hex-shortfall");
```

In `report_shortfalls`'s **per-unit** pass, where a non-sharer's overdraft is already added to
`claims`, also record the contributor — the unit, and the line it was charged at:

```rust
/// A unit whose overdraft claims against a pooled tag, and the order line that charged it.
/// Kept so the second pass can point at the line once it knows the pool is actually short.
struct Contributor<'a> {
    ordered: &'a Ordered<'a>,
    tag: String,
    at: Option<&'a PlacedIntent>,
}
```

**Record only where a claim is recorded.** That is the same `if !ordered.shares()` branch — a
sharer's stock is inside the pool's sum and claims nothing against it, so its line is **not** marked.
That was decided with the navigator and it matches the arithmetic the finding is computed from.

In the **pooled** pass, after `let short = claims… - pool;` and the `if short <= 0 { continue; }`
guard — so a pool that covers its claims marks nothing — emit one pointer per contributor of that
tag, in `hex.units` order:

```rust
for contributor in contributors.iter().filter(|c| c.tag == tag) {
    findings.push(contributor.ordered.finding(
        hex,
        codes::PART_OF_HEX_SHORTFALL,
        format!("This hex is short of {name} between its units. See Problems for the hex."),
        contributor.at,
    ));
}
```

where `name` is the plural item name with no count, by the expression named above.

**Gate it on `options.emits(codes::PART_OF_HEX_SHORTFALL)` separately** from the pooled finding's own
gate: a player who turns this off must still get the hex finding, and one who turns the hex finding
off must not silently keep the pointers. Two independent tests, both against the same `short > 0`.

**Ordering.** The pointers are pushed immediately after the hex finding for that tag, inside the
existing `for tag in pooled_tags` loop. `validate_turn` sorts by line with line-less findings last
(`orders/mod.rs:75`), so the pointers sort to their lines and the hex finding stays at the end;
nothing else moves.

**One order, two shortfalls** produces two pointers on the same line — one per tag — which is what
was chosen, so the editor's mark count and the panel's finding count agree one-to-one. Do not merge
them into one sentence.

**TypeScript — the action, and keeping the pointer out of the panel.**

`orderLint.ts`, in `toEditorDiagnostics`, attaches the action to this code only:

```ts
actions:
  problem.code === "part-of-hex-shortfall"
    ? [{ name: "Show problems", apply: () => showRegionProblems() }]
    : undefined
```

`apply` must switch the Problems section **on** if it is off and leave it on if it is already on —
the whole point of the button is that the pointer lands even when the player has collapsed the
section. `useWorkspaceStore`'s `regionProblemsShown` / `toggleRegionProblems`
(`workspaceStore.ts:235` and `:486`; used at `RegionPanel.tsx:278-279`) is the state; **do not call `toggleRegionProblems` blindly**, or clicking
the button while the section is open closes it. Add a `showRegionProblems` setter beside the toggle
rather than reading-then-toggling at the call site.

`orderEditor.ts`'s `findingsForHex` (`:194`) must **exclude** this code, or every pointer appears in
the region panel as well and the Problems count doubles:

```ts
return diagnostics.filter(
  (diagnostic) =>
    diagnostic.regionId === regionId && diagnostic.code !== "part-of-hex-shortfall"
);
```

`diagnosticsForUnit` needs no change: the pointer carries a `unitId`, so its existing
`diagnostic.unitId === unitId` branch routes it to the right editor tab already.

**Settings** — one entry in the **Resources** group, beside *Overspent silver* and *Overdrawn items*:

```ts
{
  code: "part-of-hex-shortfall",
  title: "Orders in a hex that is short between its units",
  description:
    "Marks each order line contributing to a shortfall that is reported against the whole hex rather than one unit."
}
```

Default **on**, which needs no code: `settingsStore.ts:45` defaults everything except
`hex-unguarded`.

**Where state lives.** One `Vec<Contributor>` local to `report_shortfalls`, borrowed from the hex and
dropped at the end of the call. One new setter on the workspace store. No new persisted setting
beyond the advisory toggle every code already gets.

## Increments

**Increment 1 — the code and the contributors.**
Failing test: `points_at_every_line_that_claims_against_a_short_pool`, in `semantics.rs`'s test
module. A hex with a sharer, and two non-sharing units each overdrawing the same pooled tag from one
order line: assert two `part-of-hex-shortfall` findings, each carrying the right `unit_id` and the
right `line`, plus the one hex-anchored `not-enough-items`. Add
`a_pool_that_covers_its_claims_points_at_nothing` (no pointers when `short <= 0`) and
`a_sharers_own_overdraft_is_not_pointed_at`. Then add the code, `Contributor`, and the emission.
`codes::ALL` becomes `[Code; 33]` (it is `[Code; 32]` today, `semantics.rs:125`); the fixture sweep at the end of `semantics.rs` needs its new case.

**Increment 2 — the message.**
Failing test: `says_which_goods_the_hex_is_short_of`, asserting the exact string
`"This hex is short of horses between its units. See Problems for the hex."` and, for silver,
`"This hex is short of silver between its units. See Problems for the hex."` Use the plural
expression named in *Files to change*; a test that only covers silver would not notice
`counted_item` being reached for by mistake.

**Increment 3 — the generated boundary and Settings.**
`ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts`, commit the
regenerated `coreVocabulary.generated.ts`, then add the Settings entry. `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`'s
`lists_every_advisory_check_code` (shipped by `ah-v9p2`) fails until the entry exists — that is the
gate working, and it is why no separate test is named here.

**Increment 4 — the editor.**
Failing test: in `orderLint.test.ts`, `attaches_a_show_problems_action_to_a_hex_shortfall_pointer` —
a diagnostic with that code gets exactly one action named `"Show problems"`, and a diagnostic with
any other code gets none. Then add the action.

**Increment 5 — the button opens rather than toggles.**
Failing test: in the workspace store's test file, `show_region_problems_is_idempotent` — calling
`showRegionProblems()` with the section already shown leaves it shown. This is the trap the plan
exists to prevent; write it before the setter.

**Increment 6 — keep the pointer out of the panel.**
Failing test: in `orderEditor.test.ts`, `hex_findings_exclude_the_editor_only_pointer` — a
`part-of-hex-shortfall` diagnostic with a matching `regionId` is **not** returned by
`findingsForHex`, while the hex's own `not-enough-items` is. Then add the filter.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `points_at_every_line_that_claims_against_a_short_pool` | `semantics.rs` | one pointer per contributor, with unit and line |
| `a_pool_that_covers_its_claims_points_at_nothing` | `semantics.rs` | nothing is marked when the pool covers |
| `a_sharers_own_overdraft_is_not_pointed_at` | `semantics.rs` | the sharer rule |
| `says_which_goods_the_hex_is_short_of` | `semantics.rs` | both shipped strings, plural and silver |
| `lists_every_advisory_check_code` (existing) | `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` | the Settings entry exists |
| `attaches_a_show_problems_action_to_a_hex_shortfall_pointer` | `orderLint.test.ts` | the action, and only on this code |
| `show_region_problems_is_idempotent` | workspace store tests | the button opens, never closes |
| `hex_findings_exclude_the_editor_only_pointer` | `orderEditor.test.ts` | the panel does not double-count |

**The regression net:** every existing `report_shortfalls` test — especially the message tests that
pin the three pooled wordings — unedited; `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs`;
`semantics.rs`'s `codes::ALL` fixture sweep; and `pnpm run check:generated`.

**A pointer must never change an existing message or count.** If a pooled-shortfall message test
moves, the emission is in the wrong place.

## User-facing decisions

Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-24 over three rounds. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-eurs-pooled-mark.html`.

**Round 1 — the shape.**

1. **Chosen: A, a pointer on the line** — the line is marked, the message does not accuse it, and the
   pooled finding stays hex-anchored exactly as it is. *Rejected:* **B**, anchoring the whole finding
   to every contributing line (long in a tooltip, repeats per line, and reads as an accusation — it
   also contradicts what ah-sdda settled); **C**, a strip under the editor listing line-less findings
   (a second findings list duplicating the region panel, in a pane short of vertical space);
   **D**, leaving the editor alone and forcing the Problems chip open (does nothing for a reader whose
   eyes are on the editor, which is the complaint).
2. **Every contributing line is marked**, not just the largest or first contributor. *Rejected:*
   marking one line, because a player who fixes it is still short and the warning stays.
3. **A sharer's line is not marked.** Its stock is inside the pool's sum, so it claims nothing
   against it. *Rejected:* marking any line that overdraws, which contradicts the arithmetic the
   finding is computed from.

**Round 2 — the words.**

4. **Chosen: W1** — `This hex is short of horses between its units. See Problems for the hex.`
   *Rejected:* **W2** `This order is part of a horse shortfall across this hex — see Problems.`
   ("part of" is vaguer about what to do); **W3**, the bare first sentence (never tells the reader the
   numbers exist elsewhere, which is the complaint); **W4**, carrying the figure
   (`short 19,155 horses`) — halfway to shape B, and it starts reading as this line's debt.
5. **One mark per shortfall**, so a line contributing to two short pools carries two. *Rejected:*
   one mark naming both goods, which makes the editor's mark count and the panel's finding count
   disagree.
6. **The pointer is a working control**, not plain text — it must land even when the player has
   collapsed the Problems section. *Rejected:* plain words, which send a reader with Problems
   switched off somewhere that shows nothing.

**Round 3 — the strings that ship.**

7. **The action is labelled `Show problems`.** *Rejected:* "Show the hex's problems" (long for a
   button), "Open Problems". The planner chose CodeMirror's `actions` over an inline `<a>` because an
   anchor in a tooltip is not keyboard-reachable — that is an implementation decision, but it is
   what makes the button a button.
8. **Settings entry**, in the Resources group — title
   `Orders in a hex that is short between its units`, description
   `Marks each order line contributing to a shortfall that is reported against the whole hex rather than one unit.`
   *Rejected:* "Part of a hex-wide shortfall"; "Pooled shortfall pointers" ("pooled" is our word, not
   the rules').
9. **Default on.** *Rejected:* off — it exists because the information was unreachable, and shipping
   it off would leave the complaint unfixed for anyone who never opens Settings.

Every string above is final and quoted verbatim in *The design of the code*.

## Out of scope

- **Changing the pooled finding itself** — its wording, its anchoring, or the rule that produces it.
  ah-sdda settled that it is correct; this bead adds a pointer beside it and touches nothing else.
- **Making the Problems section open by default** (shape D). Rejected in round 1.
- **The map-wide findings list and the header chip.** Neither changes; the new code is excluded from
  `findingsForHex`, so counts elsewhere stay as they are.
- **Per-unit (non-pooled) shortfalls.** They already carry their own line and need no pointer.
- **`region-pool-oversubscribed`** and the other hex-anchored codes. If they deserve pointers too,
  that is a follow-on bead once this one has been seen in use — do not generalise it here.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core                                              # increments 1-2
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts   # increment 3
pnpm vitest run packages/shared packages/core-client                         # increments 3-6
pnpm run check:fast                                                          # before the PR
```

**The human check, and this bead is entirely about it:** load
`neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, open WoodsmenY (15189) in mountain (36,4), type
`GIVE 0 20000 HORS`, and confirm the line is marked with
`This hex is short of horses between its units. See Problems for the hex.` Then collapse the
Problems section, click **Show problems** in the tooltip, and confirm it opens. Then reach the same
button with the keyboard alone.

## Known traps

- **`toggleRegionProblems` is a toggle.** Calling it from the button closes the section when it is
  already open, which is the opposite of what the button is for. Add a `showRegionProblems` setter;
  increment 5 pins it.
- **An `<a>` inside a CodeMirror lint tooltip is not keyboard-reachable.** `Diagnostic.actions` is,
  and it is why the design uses it.
- **`findingsForHex` filters by `regionId` only** (`orderEditor.ts:194`). Without the code exclusion,
  every pointer also lands in the region panel and the Problems count doubles.
- **A new code with no Settings entry now fails a test** (`lists_every_advisory_check_code`, shipped
  by `ah-v9p2`) — that gate is deliberate and is the reason this bead cannot ship half-done. Do not
  weaken it.
- **`codes::ALL` is a fixed-size array**; its length and the fixture sweep at the end of
  `semantics.rs` both need the new case, and the sweep asserts the count and the distinctness.
- **Use the plural name without a count**, not `counted_item` — the sentence has no number in it.
- **Gate the pointer independently of the hex finding.** Two `options.emits` tests, not one.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (ah-nass). Increments 4-6 test pure functions and the store, as
  the existing tests do; nothing renders.
acceptance_criteria:
A player writing an order that overdraws a shared hex is told so at the point they wrote it, or the navigator has decided at triage that the region panel is sufficient and this bead is closed with that reasoning recorded.

If a change is made: the pooled finding is still worded as being about the hex's pool rather than about one line, and is not duplicated once per contributing line in the region panel.

title: Price transfers once for both silver surfaces, and drop the mirror comments
description:
Fourth and last child of ah-lu0f, after ah-lu0f.3.

Moves GIVE and TAKE onto 'price_order' as far as they can go, and retires the hand-written 'Mirrors forecast_unit's arm exactly - two surfaces reading one order must not price it two ways' comments at semantics.rs:1607 and :1621 and their siblings, which exist only because the mirroring was manual.

The least shareable pair, and the plan must say honestly how far it goes: forecast_unit prices only the silver a transfer moves, while the ledger moves arbitrary item tags between units in the hex (transfer, semantics.rs:1689). If the shared seam cannot cover the item half, the plan scopes that out explicitly rather than forcing it.

Closes the family: once this lands, crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs guards an invariant rather than standing in for a missing one.
design:
## Context

Fourth and last child of the ah-lu0f epic (P2), after `ah-lu0f.3`. It moves `GIVE` onto the `Priced`
seam and closes the family.

**It is the smallest of the four, and the honest reason is that most of what the bead's description
expected is already done or cannot be shared.**

- **The "Mirrors `forecast_unit`'s arm exactly" comments are gone.** `ah-lu0f.1` and `ah-lu0f.2`
  removed each as they moved its arm. One stale relic remains, at `silver.rs:817`: *"Mirrors
  `semantics::apply`'s own arm exactly, down to the doubt"*, on the `PILLAGE` term — which since
  `ah-lu0f.1` does not mirror anything, because both surfaces call `price_pillage`. Increment 3
  rewrites it.
- **`GIVE`'s `Amount::All` cannot be shared, and forcing it would be wrong.** The column has no
  running balance and defers it to a second pass (`Deferred::GiveAllSilver`, `silver.rs:1000-1003`);
  the ledger reads `balance_of(ledger, who, &tag) - except` directly (`semantics::transfer`). Those
  are two different questions about *what the unit has*, not two copies of one answer. The bead's own
  description anticipated this: *"If the shared seam cannot cover the item half, the plan scopes that
  out explicitly rather than forcing it."*
- **`WITHDRAW` was settled in `ah-lu0f.2`.** The fund pays, not the unit (`ah-tdsi`); the ledger does
