  nothing and the column sets a hover flag. No shared arithmetic exists.

What **is** shared, and is worth one function, is the part that has to agree: **which shapes of
`GIVE` are priceable at all**. Both surfaces classify the `Selector` and both raise
`SilverDoubt::GivesAWholeClass` for a class or the whole unit (`silver.rs:981-984`,
`semantics::transfer`'s `let Selector::Item(text) = what else`). That classification is the thing a
future `Selector` variant would break in two places at once.

### A finding this child deliberately does not fix

**The Silver column does not model `TAKE` at all.** `Intent::Take` appears nowhere in `silver.rs`; it
falls through to `_ => {}` at `:1013`. The ledger credits it (`semantics.rs`'s `Intent::Take` arm,
which grants a stated quantity outright — *"the order says how much, and optimism grants it"*). So a
unit ordered `TAKE FROM 17 100 SILV` has that $100 in the ledger and not in the column, and the
column understates what it will hold.

That is a real gap and the mirror image of `ah-lu0f.2`'s finding — but fixing it **adds a term to a
user-facing figure**, which is a change to what the column says rather than a reconciliation of two
readings of one rule. It is filed separately for the navigator to rank. **Do not fix it here.**

**When this child lands, the epic is closed:** every order kind that moves silver is priced by one
function both surfaces call, or is explicitly and documentedly not shareable.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — one new enum and function; the `Intent::Give` arm calls it;
  the stale comment at `:817`.
- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `transfer` calls it.
- The epic parent `ah-lu0f` is closed by the implementer as it closes this last child (see
  `implement-bead`).

### What already exists and must be reused

- `Selector::{Item, Class, WholeUnit}` and `Amount::{Exact, All}` (`crates/core/src/orders/forms.rs`).
- `SilverDoubt::GivesAWholeClass` (`silver.rs:300`) — its doc already says *"what leaves depends on
  classifying everything the unit holds, which is not modelled"*. **Add no variant.**
- `Deferred::GiveAllSilver { except, to_nobody }` (`silver.rs:1000`) — the column's second pass.
  Untouched.
- `semantics::transfer` (`semantics.rs:1733`) — charges the giver and credits a recipient in the
  hex, for any tag. Its item half is not this bead's business.
- `Priced` (`silver.rs:274`) — **not used by this bead**, and that is deliberate; see below.

### The design of the code

`Priced` is the wrong return type here, and using it anyway would be the mistake this plan exists to
prevent. A `GIVE`'s cost is not a number both surfaces can compute from the same inputs — one of the
three shapes is genuinely caller-resolved. So the shared function returns the **classification**, and
each surface prices from it:

```rust
/// What shape of transfer a `GIVE` or `TAKE` names, once the selector and the amount are read.
///
/// The two surfaces price a transfer from different information - the column has no running balance
/// and the ledger does - so what they must agree on is not the number but *which* of these three
/// cases they are in. A new `Selector` variant lands here once instead of in two arms that would
/// silently disagree.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TransferShape {
    /// A whole class of goods, or the unit itself. What leaves depends on classifying everything
    /// the unit holds, which neither surface models: the column doubts, the ledger doubts.
    Unpriceable,
    /// A stated quantity of one item. The one shape both surfaces price identically.
    Exact(i64),
    /// `ALL`, less a reserve. Each surface resolves it against its own notion of what the unit has:
    /// the column defers to its running total (`Deferred::GiveAllSilver`), the ledger reads
    /// `balance_of`. Deliberately **not** resolved here.
    All { except: i64 },
}

/// Reads a transfer's selector and amount into the shape both surfaces must agree about.
#[must_use]
pub fn transfer_shape(what: &Selector, amount: &Amount) -> TransferShape {
    match what {
        Selector::Class(_) | Selector::WholeUnit => TransferShape::Unpriceable,
        Selector::Item(_) => match amount {
            Amount::Exact(count) => TransferShape::Exact(*count),
            Amount::All { except } => TransferShape::All { except: *except },
        },
    }
}
```

**How each surface consumes it.**

`forecast_unit`'s `Intent::Give` arm (`silver.rs:975-1005`) keeps every line it has — the
silver-tag test at `:986`, `to_nobody`, `given_to_nobody`, `spent_on` — and replaces its two nested
`match`es with one `match transfer_shape(what, amount)`. Note the ordering the current code has and
must keep: the `Selector` is classified **before** the silver-tag test, so
`GIVE 1 ALL` of a whole class doubts even though no tag was resolved.

`semantics::transfer` replaces its `let Selector::Item(text) = what else { ..doubt.. }` and its
`quantity` match with the same call, resolving `All { except }` to
`(balance_of(ledger, &from, &tag) - except).max(0)` exactly as it does today.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere. `TransferShape` is a `Copy` value read and discarded at each call
site; no `Ledger` field, no new parameter threaded anywhere.

## Increments

**Increment 1 — the shape.**
Failing test: `reads_the_shape_of_a_transfer`, in `silver.rs`'s `mod tests`:

```rust
assert_eq!(transfer_shape(&Selector::WholeUnit, &Amount::Exact(5)), TransferShape::Unpriceable);
assert_eq!(transfer_shape(&Selector::Class("men".into()), &Amount::All { except: 0 }),
           TransferShape::Unpriceable);
assert_eq!(transfer_shape(&Selector::Item("SILV".into()), &Amount::Exact(100)),
           TransferShape::Exact(100));
assert_eq!(transfer_shape(&Selector::Item("SILV".into()), &Amount::All { except: 20 }),
           TransferShape::All { except: 20 });
```

Read `Selector::Class`'s actual payload from `forms.rs` before writing that second line. Then add the
enum and the function, and point `forecast_unit`'s arm at it. **Every existing `forecast_unit` test
must stay green unedited.**

**Increment 2 — the ledger.**
No new test; behaviour-identical, proven by the existing suites and the corpus cross-check. Rewrite
`semantics::transfer`'s selector and amount handling over `transfer_shape`.

**Increment 3 — the stale comment.**
No test. Rewrite `silver.rs:817-819`. It currently claims the `PILLAGE` term *"Mirrors
`semantics::apply`'s own arm exactly, down to the doubt: two surfaces reading one order must not
price it two ways"*. Since `ah-lu0f.1` both surfaces call `price_pillage`, so say that instead — the
rule is now enforced by the code rather than by a comment asking somebody to remember it. Name
`ah-lu0f`. This is the sentence the whole epic existed to be able to delete.

**Increment 4 — close the epic.**
`ah-lu0f` is an epic whose children are now all closed. Close it as the last child closes, per
`implement-bead`; Cerebro's sweep is the net under that, not a substitute.

## The test plan

Rust only. Nothing in `packages/` changes, no message changes, no browser suite is touched.

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `reads_the_shape_of_a_transfer` | `silver.rs` tests | all four shapes, including both unpriceable selectors |

One new test, because this child adds one function with four branches and changes no behaviour. **The
real net is the existing suites**, and this is the child where "unedited" is the whole proof:

- Every existing `forecast_unit` test in `silver.rs`, and every `transfer` / `GIVE` / `TAKE` test in
  `semantics.rs` — **unedited**.
- `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — green, and by now it should be guarding an
  invariant rather than standing in for a missing one, which is what the epic set out to achieve.
- `semantics.rs`'s `codes::ALL` fixture sweep.

**If any existing test needs editing, this child has changed behaviour and is wrong.**

## User-facing decisions

None. No message, no number, no column and no warning changes: this child moves a classification into
one function and rewrites a comment.

The one thing that *would* have been user-facing — modelling `TAKE` in the Silver column — is
deliberately not here. See *Context*; it is filed for the navigator to rank.

## Out of scope

- **Modelling `TAKE` in the Silver column.** Filed separately. Do not add it, however obviously
  correct it looks while you are in this arm.
- **`GIVE`'s `Amount::All` on either surface.** Named in *Files to change* as unshareable by design;
  `Deferred::GiveAllSilver` and `balance_of` both stay.
- **`semantics::transfer`'s item half** — charging and crediting non-silver tags between units. The
  column does not model it and this bead does not change it.
- **`WITHDRAW`** — settled in `ah-lu0f.2`.
- **`gather_receipts`** (`semantics.rs:887`), which credits a recipient from the *giver's* orders.
  Untouched.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core                                        # after each increment
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning  # the epic's gate, one last time
pnpm run check:fast                                                    # before the PR
```

**The human check is the diff**: no message string and no number may differ from `main`. There is
nothing new to look at in a running app.

## Known traps

- **Classify the `Selector` before testing for silver.** `silver.rs:976-988` does it in that order,
  so `GIVE 1 ALL` of a whole class raises `GivesAWholeClass` even though no tag was resolved.
  Reversing it silently loses that doubt.
- **`Amount::All { except }` can go negative**, which is why both surfaces end with `.max(0)`.
  `transfer_shape` deliberately does **not** clamp — it has no holding to clamp against — so each
  caller keeps its own `.max(0)`.
- **Do not return `Priced` from `transfer_shape`.** Two of its three shapes have no number, and
  inventing a zero for them would make an unpriceable gift look free.
- **`to_nobody` / `given_to_nobody`** (`silver.rs:989`, `:996-998`) are column-only, for the hover
  sentence about a discard. They stay at the call site.
- **Closing the last child closes the epic** — `ah-lu0f` has no plan of its own and must not be left
  open under a full set of closed children.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, since nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: Price PRODUCE, STUDY and CAST once for both silver surfaces
description:
Third child of ah-lu0f, after ah-lu0f.2.

Moves PRODUCE (silver.rs:880, semantics.rs produce), STUDY (silver.rs:900, semantics.rs study) and CAST (silver.rs:915, semantics.rs cast) onto 'price_order'.

plan_production (silver.rs:1961) is already the shared recipe reader and must stay the only one; its doc comment records why it caps against the report's holdings rather than a running balance, and that decision is load-bearing for keeping the two surfaces in step (ah-ycuj).
design:
## Context

Third child of the ah-lu0f epic (P2), after `ah-lu0f.2` moved the market orders and `CLAIM` onto the
`Priced` seam. This child moves `PRODUCE`, `STUDY` and `CAST`.

**`ah-lu0f.2` has not merged when this is written.** It is planned and in progress (Storm), and it
adds `pub spends: i64` to `Priced` (`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:274`). Everything below assumes
that field exists — see *Files to change* for what to do if it does not yet.

**Researching this child found the third false-warning class in a row, and it is the largest.**

`ah-lu0f.1` found the ledger's deliberate tax optimism (preserved). `ah-lu0f.2` found that a decision
of 2026-08-23 reached the column and not the ledger (fixed there). This one:

> **The ledger never credits the two earning spells.** `PHANTASMAL` and `EARTH_LORE` appear nowhere
> in `semantics.rs`. `forecast_unit` credits both (`silver.rs:908-928`) — Phantasmal Entertainment at
> `skill_level × 600`, capped by the region's entertainment pool; Earth Lore at
> `skill_level × 2 × wage_centis / 100` — and the column's own comment says why they belong in the
> month's spendable money: *"Both earning spells arrive in time to be spent: `CAST` resolves before
> every spend order, so neither is `late_income`'s business."*

So a mage that casts Earth Lore or Phantasmal Entertainment and then spends the proceeds is shown the
income in the Silver column and is **not** credited it in the ledger — and may be warned
`not-enough-silver` for money it will have. In the committed corpus that is a real unit: turn 82 shows
*"Ivanhoe, son of Cedric (683): Casts Phantasmal Entertainment, raising 1200 silver."* A false warning
of $1,200, against a module whose stated policy is that *"a false warning costs the player their
confidence in every other line on the screen"* (`semantics.rs:13-17`).

The other two arms are closer to honest duplication:

- **`PRODUCE` already shares its arithmetic** through `plan_production` (`silver.rs:2052`, ah-ycuj's
  doing) and both sides charge `plan.silver`. What is written twice is the
  *resolve → recipe → plan* chain: `silver.rs:866-869` against `semantics.rs:1816-1819`.
- **`STUDY` is `cost × men` on both sides** (`silver.rs:886-897`, `semantics.rs:1871-1888`), each with
  its own `find_skill(..).cost` lookup and its own doubt on an unpriced skill.

**When this child lands, all three are priced by one function each, and the ledger stops warning
about money a mage will have.**

### This child changes behaviour, in one place

Only `CAST`, and only by *adding* income to the ledger. `not-enough-silver` will stop firing for
mages who cast an earning spell and spend the proceeds. That is the same shape as `ah-lu0f.2`'s
`BUY` fix: the column has behaved this way since it shipped, and the ledger is being brought into
line with it, not the other way round.

`PRODUCE` and `STUDY` must come out **behaviour-identical**; if either moves a test, the extraction
is wrong.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — three new pricing functions; `forecast_unit`'s three arms call
  them.
- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `produce`, `study` and `cast` call them; `ledger_for` gains
  `RegionWages`.

No other file. No message changes.

**If `ah-lu0f.2` has not merged when you pick this up:** `Priced` will not have `spends`. Do not add
it here and do not work around it — rebase onto `main` once `ah-lu0f.2` lands, or if it has been
abandoned, add the field exactly as `ah-lu0f.2`'s plan specifies (it is the same field, and two
definitions of it is the very drift this epic exists to remove). Say which you did in the PR.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `plan_production(recipe: &Production, men: i64, held: &[ItemAmount]) -> Option<ProductionPlan>`
  (`silver.rs:2052`). **The one recipe reader**, and its doc comment records why it caps against the
  report's holdings rather than a running balance — *"capping against one would give the two surfaces
  different answers for the same order - which is exactly the drift `ah-ycuj`'s corpus test exists to
  catch"*. Do not touch it, and do not add a second caller-side cap.
- `recipe_for(ruleset, tag)` — used by both sides already.
- `SkillEntry` (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:484`), with `cost: Option<i64>` (`:489`) and
  `cast: Option<CastCost>` (`:495`); `Ruleset::find_skill(text) -> Option<&SkillEntry>` (`:944`).
- `skill_level(skills: &[Skill], tag: &str) -> i64` (`silver.rs:1962`) — **private, and it stays
  private**: the new `price_cast` lives in the same module and calls it.
- `PHANTASMAL_TAG` (`silver.rs:44`), `PHANTASMAL_PER_LEVEL = 600` (`:33`), `EARTH_LORE_TAG` (`:49`),
  `EARTH_LORE_PER_LEVEL_PER_WAGE = 2` (`:57`), `SILVER_TAG`. All already in `silver.rs`.
- `RegionWages` (`silver.rs:532`), with `wage_centis: Option<i64>` (`:535`) and
  `entertainment: Option<i64>` (`:540`).
- `region_wages(hex, ruleset) -> RegionWages` (`semantics.rs:647`) — **already exists in the ledger's
  own module**, which is what makes the `CAST` fix cheap. `ledger_for` calls it; nothing new is
  written.
- `SilverDoubt::UnpricedSkill` and `UnpricedProduction`. **Add no variant.**

### The design of the code

```rust
/// What a `STUDY` costs: the ruleset's price for the skill, once per man.
///
/// `cost` is `None` where the ruleset prices the skill nowhere - or where there is no ruleset, or
/// where the headcount is a guess and nothing per-man can be multiplied out. Resolving which of
/// those is the caller's, because the two surfaces reach the ruleset differently; what they must
/// not do twice is the arithmetic and the doubt.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_study(cost: Option<i64>, men: i64) -> Priced {
    match cost {
        Some(cost) => Priced { spends: cost.saturating_mul(men), ..Priced::default() },
        None => Priced { doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::UnpricedSkill), ..Priced::default() },
    }
}

/// What a `PRODUCE` costs, and the run it describes.
///
/// Returns the plan as well as the price because the two surfaces need different parts of it: the
/// ledger charges `plan.materials` tag by tag, and the column names what is made. `None` for the
/// plan means the ruleset prices it nowhere - an unknown item, an item no skill makes, a recipe of
/// alternatives rather than requirements - which is a doubt on both surfaces.
///
/// The caller resolves the item to a recipe, because the column has a `Lookups` closure and the
/// ledger has the hex; `plan_production` is the shared part and stays the only recipe reader.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_production(
    recipe: Option<&Production>,
    men: i64,
    held: &[ItemAmount],
) -> (Priced, Option<ProductionPlan>) {
    match recipe.and_then(|recipe| plan_production(recipe, men, held)) {
        Some(plan) => (Priced { spends: plan.silver, ..Priced::default() }, Some(plan)),
        None => (
            Priced { doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::UnpricedProduction), ..Priced::default() },
            None,
        ),
    }
}

/// What a `CAST` earns and costs.
///
/// **Two spells earn**, and both arrive in time to be spent: `CAST` resolves before every spend
/// order, so neither is [`late_income`]'s business. Phantasmal Entertainment pays
/// `level × PHANTASMAL_PER_LEVEL`, capped by what the region's entertainment pool holds; Earth Lore
/// pays `level × EARTH_LORE_PER_LEVEL_PER_WAGE × W`, where W is the region's wage - carried in
/// hundredths, so the multiplication comes before the division by 100 and a fractional wage is not
/// lost. A hex stating no wage pays nothing and raises no doubt, exactly as `WORK` treats one.
///
/// **Every spell may cost.** Only the `SILV` entries of the cast cost move silver here; item costs
/// and the whole `transmute` map are the item ledger's business and are not this function's.
///
/// A spell the ruleset does not know, or knows no cost for, earns nothing, costs nothing and doubts
/// nothing - which is the truth about most spells.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_cast(spell: Option<&SkillEntry>, skills: &[Skill], region: RegionWages) -> Priced;
```

**`price_cast` returns both halves in one `Priced`** — `earns` from the two spells, `spends` from the
`SILV` cost entries — which is the one place in this epic where a single order does both. That is
exactly why `ah-lu0f.2` made `spends` a separate field rather than a signed `earns`.

**How each surface consumes them.**

`forecast_unit` keeps `spent_on`, `doubt_subject`, `income_doubt`, `expense_doubt` and the
`production` bookkeeping exactly where they are, set from the returned values. In particular
`doubt_subject` for an unpriced production is still `item.to_lowercase()` at the call site — it is
the order's own text, which the pricing function never sees.

`semantics::produce` (`:1807`) resolves the tag with `resolve_item` as it does today, calls
`price_production`, charges `priced.spends` of `SILVER`, then charges each `plan.materials` entry —
the item half stays in the ledger, since the column does not model it.

`semantics::cast` (`:1893`) keeps its whole `transmute` block and its item charges unchanged, and
gains the earning half: `credit(ledger, who, SILVER, price_cast(..).earns)`. **Charge silver through
`price_cast(..).spends` rather than through the existing `for input in &cost.costs` loop for the
`SILV` entries**, or silver is charged twice — once by the loop and once by the shared function. The
loop must skip `SILV` and keep charging every other tag.

**`ledger_for` gains `RegionWages`.** `region_wages(hex, ruleset)` (`semantics.rs:647`) already
exists; call it once in `ledger_for` and thread it to `apply` and on to `cast`, the same way
`ah-lu0f.2` threads the market shares. Do not compute it per intent — `find_skill` walks the
catalogue and this runs per keystroke.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new. One more borrowed value threaded through `ledger_for` → `apply` →
`cast`; `Priced` and `ProductionPlan` are owned values built and dropped at each call site.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test. `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` after each.

**Increment 1 — `price_study` and `price_production`.**
Failing test: `prices_a_study_and_a_production`, in `silver.rs`'s `mod tests`:

```rust
assert_eq!(price_study(Some(30), 10), Priced { spends: 300, ..Priced::default() });
assert_eq!(price_study(None, 10),
           Priced { doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::UnpricedSkill), ..Priced::default() });
let (priced, plan) = price_production(None, 5, &[]);
assert_eq!(priced, Priced { doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::UnpricedProduction), ..Priced::default() });
assert!(plan.is_none());
```

Add a positive `price_production` case using the committed ruleset's catapult recipe — `silver.rs`'s
tests already build one (`ruleset()` at `:2515` and the recipe named in `plan_production`'s own
tests). Then add both functions and point `forecast_unit`'s `Intent::Study` (`:886`) and
`Intent::Produce` (`:865`) at them. **Every existing `forecast_unit` test must stay green unedited.**

**Increment 2 — the ledger's study and produce.**
No new test; behaviour-identical, proven by the existing suites. Rewrite `semantics::study`
(`:1867`) and `semantics::produce` (`:1807`) over the two functions, keeping `study`'s
`.filter(|_| !actor.unit.men_estimated)` at the call site — it is how the ledger says "a guessed
headcount cannot price a study", and it belongs with the ruleset lookup, not in the arithmetic.

**Increment 3 — `price_cast`, and the column.**
Failing test: `prices_a_cast_that_earns_and_one_that_costs`, in `silver.rs`. Cover: Phantasmal
Entertainment capped by the entertainment pool; Phantasmal with **no** pool stated, earning nothing;
Earth Lore with a fractional wage, proving the multiply-before-divide; a spell with a `SILV` cast
cost, giving `spends`; and an unknown spell giving `Priced::default()`. Then add `price_cast` and
point `forecast_unit`'s `Intent::Cast` arm (`:900`) at it. Existing tests stay green unedited.

**Increment 4 — the ledger credits the earning spells.**
Failing test: `a_mage_casting_an_earning_spell_can_spend_what_it_raises`, in `semantics.rs`'s test
module. One hex with an entertainment pool, one own unit holding $0 with Phantasmal Entertainment at
a level worth $1,200, ordered `CAST Phantasmal Entertainment` and then to `BUY` something costing
less than that. Assert **no** `not-enough-silver`. On `main` it fails — the ledger credits nothing.

Then thread `region_wages` through `ledger_for` and `apply`, and rewrite `cast` (`:1893`): credit
`price_cast(..).earns`, charge `price_cast(..).spends` of silver, and **narrow the existing
`for input in &cost.costs` loop to skip `SILV`** so silver is not charged twice. Leave the
`transmute` block alone.

**Increment 5 — the corpus.**
Run `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning` on its own. Turn 82's
Ivanhoe (683) is a live Phantasmal caster, so this is the increment most likely to move it — and it
should move *toward* agreement. If it fails, report the fixture and unit rather than adjusting the
test.

## The test plan

Rust only. Nothing in `packages/` changes and no browser suite is touched.

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `prices_a_study_and_a_production` | `silver.rs` tests | both arms and both doubts |
| `prices_a_cast_that_earns_and_one_that_costs` | `silver.rs` tests | both spells, the pool cap, the fractional wage, the `SILV` cost |
| `a_mage_casting_an_earning_spell_can_spend_what_it_raises` | `semantics.rs` tests | the false warning goes |
| `a_cast_is_not_charged_twice_for_its_silver` | `semantics.rs` tests | the double-charge trap in increment 4 — a unit whose cast costs `SILV` ends the month with exactly that much less |

That last test is not optional: narrowing the cost loop and adding a shared charge is precisely the
edit where silver gets charged twice, and no existing test would notice a doubled cast cost.

**The regression net:**

- Every existing `forecast_unit` test in `silver.rs` — unedited, which is increments 1 and 3's proof.
- `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — see increment 5.
- `semantics.rs`'s `codes::ALL` fixture sweep, and `plan_production`'s own tests.

## User-facing decisions

**None to take, one to report.** `not-enough-silver` stops firing for a mage who casts an earning
spell and spends the proceeds. No message changes and no code is added or removed; the ledger simply
counts money the column has always counted. Say so in the PR description so whoever verifies it knows
the warning count moved and why.

If the navigator would rather the ledger kept ignoring cast income, that is a decision they have
never been asked for and it is theirs — stop and ask rather than guessing.

## Out of scope

- **`GIVE`, `TAKE`, and retiring the "Mirrors `forecast_unit`'s arm exactly" comments** — `ah-lu0f.4`,
  which this child blocks.
- **The `transmute` map and every non-`SILV` cast cost** (`semantics.rs:1915-1935`). Item movement is
  the ledger's alone; the column does not model it and this bead does not change it.
- **`plan_production`'s holdings cap.** Deliberate, documented, and the reason the two surfaces agree
  about production at all (`ah-ycuj`).
- **Whether `PHANTASMAL_PER_LEVEL` and `EARTH_LORE_PER_LEVEL_PER_WAGE` are the right numbers.**
  `silver.rs:47` records that the rules page gives no arithmetic for Earth Lore and that the constant
  is the only source. Wrong constants would be a separate bug; this bead only makes both surfaces use
  the same ones.
- **`late_income`.** `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` were already shared before this epic began (`ah-lu0f.1`,
  increment 4).

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core                                        # after each increment
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning  # increment 5, on its own
pnpm run check:fast                                                    # before the PR
```

**The human check:** load `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`, find Ivanhoe, son of Cedric (683) —
the report shows it casting Phantasmal Entertainment and raising 1,200 silver — order it to spend
some of that, and confirm the Silver column and the warning now agree. Before this bead they do not.

## Known traps

- **Silver can be charged twice for a cast.** `semantics::cast`'s existing loop charges *every* input
  tag including `SILV`. Adding `price_cast(..).spends` without narrowing that loop doubles the cost,
  and nothing existing would catch it — hence the fourth test.
- **`region.wage_centis` is in hundredths.** Multiply before dividing by 100, exactly as
  `silver.rs:920-924` already does, or a fractional wage is lost.
- **A hex stating no entertainment pool pays nothing and raises no doubt** — `unwrap_or(0)`, not a
  doubt. Same for no wage. Copy the column's treatment.
- **`price_cast` needs `RegionWages`, so `ledger_for` must build it once**, not per intent:
  `find_skill` walks the catalogue and this runs on every keystroke.
- **`study`'s `men_estimated` filter belongs at the call site**, not inside `price_study`. The column
  handles a guessed headcount by short-circuiting the whole of `forecast_unit` near its top; the two
  surfaces reach the same answer by different routes and must keep doing so.
- **`skill_level` is private and stays private.** `price_cast` lives in the same module.
- **`ah-lu0f.2` must land first.** It adds `Priced::spends`. See *Files to change*.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, since nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: Price the market orders and CLAIM once for both silver surfaces
description:
Second child of ah-lu0f, after ah-lu0f.1 establishes the seam.

Moves BUY (silver.rs:959, semantics.rs buy), SELL (silver.rs:846, semantics.rs sell), CLAIM (silver.rs:806, semantics.rs:1633) and WITHDRAW (silver.rs:1027) onto 'price_order'.

The market arms are the awkward ones: forecast_unit reaches the market through the 'sale' and 'purchase' lookups in Lookups, while the ledger reads hex.region's market lines directly. The shared function must take what both can supply. ah-t2pn.3 and ah-t2pn.4 both concern how a contended market pool is split, and that logic must not be duplicated a third time.
design:
## Context

Second child of the ah-lu0f epic (P2), after `ah-lu0f.1` established the `Priced` seam
(`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:274`, `price_tax` at `:1830`, `price_pillage` at `:1876`, merged
as #647). This child moves `BUY`, `SELL`, `CLAIM` and `WITHDRAW` onto it.

**Researching it turned up something bigger than a duplication: a decision the navigator took on
2026-08-23 was implemented in one surface and never in the other.**

`ah-t2pn.3`'s own design records it:

> *"The navigator settled on 2026-08-23 that the settlement should fix both: it applies whenever
> **anyone** buys or sells, not only when two units contend"* … *"so a lone over-buyer is charged
> only for goods that exist."*

That landed in `forecast_unit` — the Silver column consults `lookups.market_share`
(`silver.rs:950` for `BUY`, `:844` for `SELL`). It never landed in the ledger:

| | Column (`forecast_unit`) | Ledger (`semantics.rs`) |
|---|---|---|
| `BUY 200 HORS`, market has 100 | charges for **100** (`silver.rs:950-953`) | charges for **200** (`buy`, `:1790-1796`) |
| `SELL 100 GRAI`, market wants 20 | earns **20 × price** (`silver.rs:844-847`) | credits **100 × price** (`sell`, `:1856-1857`) |

So today a lone over-buyer is charged in the ledger for goods that do not exist, which produces a
**false `not-enough-silver` warning** — against a module whose stated policy is that *"a false warning
costs the player their confidence in every other line on the screen"* (`semantics.rs:13-17`). And a
lone over-seller is credited income it will not receive, which **suppresses a warning that should
fire**. The two surfaces are wrong in opposite directions from the same missing settlement.

**The ledger already computes the settlement it does not use.** `market_shares_for`
(`semantics.rs:543`) exists and is called at `:700`, in the silver-column pass. `ledger_for`
(`:1288`) — the pass that runs `buy` and `sell` — never receives it.

**When this child lands, `BUY`, `SELL` and `CLAIM` are each priced by one function both surfaces
call, and the navigator's 2026-08-23 decision is finally true of both.**

### This child changes behaviour, deliberately, and that is new for this epic

`ah-lu0f.1` was strictly behaviour-preserving. This one is not, and the difference must be
understood before a line is written:

- **`BUY` and `SELL` in the ledger change.** That is not a tidy-up smuggled into a refactoring — it
  is applying a decision the navigator already took and recorded, exactly as `ah-hlqc` applies
  `ah-lt0o`'s rule to the scanners that missed it. Expect `not-enough-silver` findings to
  **disappear** for over-buyers and to **appear** for over-sellers.
- **`CLAIM` does not change**, and the divergence there is preserved on purpose. See below.
- The corpus cross-check `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` should get
  **closer** to agreement, not further. If it goes red, read it as evidence about which surface was
  wrong rather than as something to silence.

### The one divergence that stays

`CLAIM` is capped at `purse.unclaimed` in the column (`silver.rs:801-812`) and uncapped in the ledger
(`semantics.rs:1683`, `credit(ledger, who, SILVER, *amount)`). **Keep it.** The column is showing what
the unit will actually have; the ledger is deliberately generous, because the overrun has its own
finding — `claims-exceed-unclaimed` (`ah-wur4`), computed faction-wide at `semantics.rs:4627` — and
warning twice about one mistake is worse than warning once. `ah-bumi` settled the purse the other way
from the regional pools on purpose. This is the same shape as `price_tax`'s `share` parameter from
`ah-lu0f.1`: the arithmetic is shared, the policy is the caller's.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — `Priced` gains one field; three new pricing functions;
  `forecast_unit`'s four arms call them.
- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `ledger_for` gains the settled market shares; `buy`, `sell`
  and the `Intent::Claim` arm call the same functions.

No other file, and no change to any message.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `Priced` (`silver.rs:274`) — `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]`. It stays
  `Copy`; see the design note below about what must **not** be added to it.
- `SilverDoubt` (`silver.rs:285`) — `UnknownGoods` (`:292`) and `MarketDoesNotSell` are this child's
  two. **Add no variant.**
- `market_shares_for(hex, ruleset, overruns) -> BTreeMap<(String, MarketSide), Vec<i64>>`
  (`semantics.rs:543`) — the settlement, already written. Do not write a second one.
- `MarketSide::{Buying, Selling}` (`silver.rs:438`) — buying and selling the same goods draw on two
  separate pools, so the side is part of the key.
- `SaleAnswer` (`silver.rs:476`) and `PurchaseAnswer` (`silver.rs:430`) — the column's market answers.
  Unchanged.
- `market(lines, item, hex, actor, ruleset)` (`semantics.rs`, used at `buy:1779` and `sell:1842`) —
  the ledger's market lookup. Unchanged.
- `resolve_item` — how a tag is found from an order's text, in `market_shares_for` already.

### The design of the code

**1. `Priced` gains `spends`.** Three of this child's four arms cost silver rather than earning it,
and `ah-lu0f.1` deliberately left the field out because `TAX` and `PILLAGE` only earn.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Priced {
    /// Silver the order earns. Never negative.
    pub earns: i64,
    /// Silver the order spends. Never negative. An order does not both earn and spend, but the
    /// field is separate rather than a signed `earns` so a caller that tracks the two totals apart
    /// - which `forecast_unit` does, as `income` and `expense` - needs no sign convention.
    pub spends: i64,
    /// Why it could not be priced, or `None`.
    pub doubt: Option<SilverDoubt>,
}
```

**`price_tax` and `price_pillage` will stop compiling, and that is intended.** Both construct
`Priced` naming every field — `silver.rs:1832`, `:1840`, `:1844`, and the four arms of
`price_pillage` at `:1878` onward. Fix each by replacing the explicit `doubt: None` / `earns: 0`
pairs with `..Priced::default()` where that reads better, so the *next* field added to `Priced` by
`ah-lu0f.3` does not break them a second time. Do not add `spends: 0` by hand to seven call sites.

**Do not add `spent_on` or `doubt_subject` to `Priced`.** `forecast_unit` tracks
`spent_on: Option<SilverSpender>` and `doubt_subject: Option<String>` for the column's sentences.
They are presentation, the ledger has no use for them, and `doubt_subject` is a `String`, which would
cost `Priced` its `Copy`. They stay in `forecast_unit`, set beside the call from the same inputs.

**2. Three pricing functions, and two quantity helpers.** The ledger needs the *quantity* as well as
the silver — it charges and credits item tags, which the column never does.

```rust
/// How many of the goods a `BUY` actually takes: what was asked, capped by what the settlement
/// leaves this unit of the market's line.
///
/// `allowed` is the settled share, or the asked count where the hex could not be settled - which is
/// what `Lookups::market_share` returning `None` means, and is the behaviour before `ah-t2pn.3`.
#[must_use]
pub fn quantity_bought(count: i64, allowed: i64) -> i64 {
    count.min(allowed).max(0)
}

/// What a `BUY` costs.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_purchase(count: i64, price: i64, allowed: i64) -> Priced {
    Priced {
        spends: quantity_bought(count, allowed).saturating_mul(price),
        ..Priced::default()
    }
}

/// How many of the goods a `SELL` actually moves: what was asked, capped by the settled share and
/// by what the unit holds. The three caps are applied in this order and the `max(0)` last, because
/// `Amount::All { except }` can make `asked` negative.
#[must_use]
pub fn quantity_sold(asked: i64, unit_holds: i64, allowed: i64) -> i64 {
    asked.min(allowed).min(unit_holds).max(0)
}

/// What a `SELL` earns.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_sale(asked: i64, unit_holds: i64, price: i64, allowed: i64) -> Priced {
    Priced {
        earns: quantity_sold(asked, unit_holds, allowed).saturating_mul(price),
        ..Priced::default()
    }
}

/// What a `CLAIM` earns.
///
/// `unclaimed` is the caller's policy about the faction purse, and the two surfaces differ on
/// purpose. The Silver column passes `purse.unclaimed`, because it shows what the unit will actually
/// have. The ledger passes `None`: the overrun has its own finding, `claims-exceed-unclaimed`
/// (`ah-wur4`), computed faction-wide, and warning twice about one mistake is worse than once
/// (`ah-bumi` settled the purse the other way from the regional pools). A purse the report does not
/// state also arrives as `None`, and means the same thing here - the limit is unknown, the stated
/// figure is counted, nothing is doubted.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_claim(amount: i64, unclaimed: Option<i64>) -> Priced {
    Priced {
        earns: match unclaimed {
            Some(available) => amount.min(available),
            None => amount,
        },
        ..Priced::default()
    }
}
```

**`WITHDRAW` gets no function.** The ledger already does nothing for it — *"The fund pays, not the
unit (`ah-tdsi`)"*, `semantics.rs:1706` — and the column only sets a `withdrawing` flag for a hover
sentence. There is no shared arithmetic, so inventing a `price_withdrawal` returning
`Priced::default()` would be a function that exists to make a list look complete. Increment 5 records
that instead.

**3. Threading the settlement into the ledger.** `ledger_for(hex, ruleset)` (`semantics.rs:1288`)
must obtain the same shares the column uses, so `buy` and `sell` can pass `allowed`.

```rust
// In `ledger_for`, before the intent walk. The overruns are discarded: the silver pass at `:700`
// already records them, and emitting them twice would duplicate every
// `region-pool-oversubscribed` finding.
let market_shares = market_shares_for(hex, ruleset, &mut Vec::new());
```

Thread it to `apply` and on to `buy`/`sell` as a `&BTreeMap<(String, MarketSide), Vec<i64>>`, and
resolve a unit's share from it exactly as the column's `Lookups::market_share` closure does — **read
that closure (built around `semantics.rs:700-760`) and mirror it; do not re-derive the indexing
rule.** The share is per unit *and* per item *and* per side, and getting the unit index wrong gives
one unit another's allowance.

This computes the settlement twice per hex, which is accepted rather than overlooked: the two passes
are separate entry points, `market_shares_for` is O(units × intents) over one hex, and threading one
computation between them means restructuring `check_hex` and the silver pass together — a bigger
change than this child, and one that would make the diff unreadable. If it ever shows up in a
profile, that is its own bead.

**Where state lives.** One new borrowed map threaded through `ledger_for` → `apply` → `buy`/`sell`.
Nothing is stored on `Ledger`, and `Priced` stays a `Copy` value built and dropped at each call site.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test. `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` after each.

**Increment 1 — `Priced::spends`, and the three functions.**
Failing test: `prices_a_purchase_a_sale_and_a_claim`, in `silver.rs`'s `mod tests`, beside
`ah-lu0f.1`'s `price_tax` tests:

```rust
// a lone over-buyer is charged only for goods that exist (`ah-t2pn.3`)
assert_eq!(price_purchase(200, 5, 100), Priced { spends: 500, ..Priced::default() });
assert_eq!(price_purchase(50, 5, 100), Priced { spends: 250, ..Priced::default() });
// a sale is capped by the share and by what the unit holds
assert_eq!(price_sale(100, 100, 3, 20), Priced { earns: 60, ..Priced::default() });
assert_eq!(price_sale(100, 10, 3, 100), Priced { earns: 30, ..Priced::default() });
// `Amount::All { except }` can ask for a negative amount
assert_eq!(quantity_sold(-5, 10, 100), 0);
// the claim policy is the caller's
assert_eq!(price_claim(500, Some(120)), Priced { earns: 120, ..Priced::default() });
assert_eq!(price_claim(500, None), Priced { earns: 500, ..Priced::default() });
```

Then add the `spends` field and the five functions, and repair `price_tax`'s and `price_pillage`'s
constructors as described above — the compiler will list every one. Nothing calls the new functions
yet.

**Increment 2 — the column calls them.**
No new test; every existing `forecast_unit` test must stay green **unedited**, which is what proves
the functions reproduce the column's arithmetic exactly. Replace the bodies of `Intent::Buy`
(`silver.rs:944-974`), `Intent::Sell` (`:832-861`) and `Intent::Claim` (`:801-812`) with calls,
keeping every surrounding line — `spent_on`, `doubt_subject`, `income_doubt`, `expense_doubt` and
the `Deferred::BuyAll` push — exactly where it is. If any existing test needs editing here, the
extraction is wrong.

**Increment 3 — the ledger gets the settlement.**
Failing test: `a_lone_over_buyer_is_not_charged_for_goods_that_do_not_exist`, in `semantics.rs`'s
test module. One hex, one own unit, a `For Sale` line of 100 horses at $5, and
`unit 1\nBUY 200 HORS\n` with the unit holding $500. Assert **no** `not-enough-silver` finding: the
unit can afford the 100 that exist. On `main` this fails, because the ledger charges $1,000.

Then thread `market_shares_for` through `ledger_for` and `apply`, and rewrite `buy`
(`semantics.rs:1769-1798`) to charge `price_purchase(...).spends` and credit
`quantity_bought(...)` of the tag.

**Increment 4 — the ledger's sale.**
Failing test: `an_over_seller_is_credited_only_for_what_the_market_takes`. One hex, one own unit
holding 100 grain, a `Wanted` line of 20 grain at $3, `unit 1\nSELL 100 GRAI\nBUY 60 HORS\n` with a
`For Sale` line of 60 horses at $5 and the unit holding $0. The sale earns $60, the purchase costs
$300, so `not-enough-silver` **must** fire. On `main` it does not, because the ledger credits $300
for the sale. Then rewrite `sell` (`:1832-1858`) to charge `quantity_sold(...)` of the tag and credit
`price_sale(...).earns`.

**Increment 5 — `CLAIM`, and saying why `WITHDRAW` is not here.**
Replace `semantics.rs:1683` with `credit(ledger, who, SILVER, price_claim(*amount, None).earns)` —
behaviour-identical, and the `None` is now documented at `price_claim` rather than implied by
absence. Then extend the `Intent::Withdraw { .. } => {}` comment (`:1703-1706`) with one line naming
`ah-lu0f.2`: there is no shared arithmetic because the fund pays and the unit is charged nothing, so
this arm is deliberately not part of the seam.

**Increment 6 — the corpus, read rather than obeyed.**
Run `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning` on its own. It should
pass, and pass *more* convincingly than before. **If it fails, do not adjust it**: report which
fixture and which unit, because that is a real disagreement between two surfaces this bead was
supposed to reconcile, and knowing which one is wrong is worth more than a green run.

## The test plan

Rust only. Nothing in `packages/` changes, no message changes, no browser suite is touched.

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `prices_a_purchase_a_sale_and_a_claim` | `silver.rs` tests | all five functions, including the negative-`asked` edge |
| `a_lone_over_buyer_is_not_charged_for_goods_that_do_not_exist` | `semantics.rs` tests | the false warning goes |
| `an_over_seller_is_credited_only_for_what_the_market_takes` | `semantics.rs` tests | the missing warning arrives |
| `a_claim_is_still_uncapped_in_the_ledger` | `semantics.rs` tests | the preserved divergence — a unit claiming more than the faction holds gets **no** `not-enough-silver` from the claim itself |

That last test matters as much as the other three: it is what stops a later reader "finishing the
job" by capping the ledger's claim and producing the double warning `ah-wur4` exists to avoid.

**The regression net:**

- Every existing `forecast_unit` test in `silver.rs` — unedited, which is increment 2's whole proof.
- `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — see increment 6.
- `semantics.rs`'s `codes::ALL` fixture sweep.
- `ah-t2pn.3` and `ah-t2pn.4`'s own tests, which pin the settlement itself.

**Existing tests that assert the *old* ledger behaviour will fail, and that is the finding.** If a
test says a lone over-buyer is warned, it is pinning the defect. Update it, and **say so explicitly
in the commit message and the PR description**, naming the test and quoting `ah-t2pn.3`'s recorded
decision. Do not update one silently.

## User-facing decisions

**None to take — but one to report, because the player will see it.**

Warnings change: `not-enough-silver` stops firing for a unit that ordered more than the market sells,
and starts firing for a unit whose income depended on selling more than the market wants. No message
is reworded and no code is added or removed; the same findings fire on a more accurate reading.

This is not a new decision. The navigator settled it on 2026-08-23 — *"it applies whenever anyone
buys or sells, not only when two units contend"* — and the column has behaved this way since
`ah-t2pn.3` shipped. This child makes the ledger agree. **Say in the PR description that the warning
counts move and why**, so the change is visible to whoever verifies it rather than arriving as a
surprise.

If the navigator wants the ledger to keep its old reading, that is a change to the 2026-08-23
decision and it is theirs to make — stop and ask rather than guessing.

## Out of scope

- **`PRODUCE`, `STUDY`, `CAST`** — `ah-lu0f.3`, which this child blocks.
- **`GIVE`, `TAKE`, and retiring the "Mirrors `forecast_unit`'s arm exactly" comments** —
  `ah-lu0f.4`.
- **Computing the market settlement once instead of twice per hex.** Named in *Files to change* as a
  deliberate acceptance; a separate bead if it ever matters.
- **`Deferred::BuyAll`** (`silver.rs:962-966`). `BUY ALL` waits for the running total and is
  column-only — the ledger returns early for it (`semantics.rs:1784-1788`, *"BUY ALL takes as many as
  the unit can pay for, so it cannot overdraw"*). Leave both alone.
- **`claims-exceed-unclaimed`** and the faction-wide claim total (`semantics.rs:4627`). Untouched;
  it is why the ledger's claim stays uncapped.
- **Adding a `SilverDoubt` variant**, changing any message, or touching `UnitSilver`.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core                                        # after each increment
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning  # increment 6, on its own
pnpm run check:fast                                                    # before the PR
```

**The human check, and this bead earns one:** load a fixture, find a hex with a `For Sale` line, order
a unit to `BUY` more than the line holds, and confirm the Silver column and the warning now agree
about the cost. Before this bead they disagree by the difference. Worth doing because the whole child
is about two surfaces telling the player different things.

## Known traps

- **The ledger is charging against a decision the navigator already took.** Read *Context* before
  treating any of increments 3 or 4 as a behaviour change to be avoided. The failing tests there are
  meant to fail on `main`.
- **`market_shares_for` needs an `overruns` sink and the ledger must discard it**
  (`&mut Vec::new()`), or every `region-pool-oversubscribed` finding is emitted twice.
- **The share is per unit, per item, *and* per side** (`MarketSide`, `silver.rs:438`): a unit selling
  horses and buying horses draws on two different pools. Mirror the column's existing closure rather
  than re-deriving the lookup, and be careful with the unit index — the wrong one silently gives a
  unit another's allowance.
- **`Amount::All { except }` can make `asked` negative**, which is why `quantity_sold` ends in
  `.max(0)` and why the order of the caps matters. `silver.rs:840` is where the existing arm does it.
- **`Priced` must stay `Copy`.** Do not put `doubt_subject: Option<String>` on it.
- **A doubt and a non-zero figure never occur together** — `Priced`'s own doc says so. The market
  arms raise `UnknownGoods` / `MarketDoesNotSell` in `forecast_unit`, outside these functions, which
  is why none of the five sets `doubt` at all.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, since nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: Price TAX, PILLAGE, WORK and ENTERTAIN once for both silver surfaces
description:
First child of ah-lu0f. Introduces the shared pricing seam and moves the four arms onto it that the corpus cross-check has already caught drifting.

Establishes 'Priced' and 'price_order' in crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs, consulted by both forecast_unit (silver.rs:676) and apply (semantics.rs:1586). The two PILLAGE arms - silver.rs:828 and semantics.rs:1638 - are already structurally identical and differ only in how they express doubt (a typed SilverDoubt variant against ledger.doubted.insert), and pillage_threshold (silver.rs:1829) is already shared between them. TAX is credited once per unit on both sides (credit_tax, semantics.rs:1569, and its mirror in forecast_unit), and both carry a hand-written 'Mirrors forecast_unit's arm exactly' comment saying so.

ah-abwx (54dd0824) and ah-cxxa each fixed a divergence in exactly these arms. The plan for this child is written by Xavier before it is built.
design:
## Context

First child of the ah-lu0f epic (P2). It establishes the shared pricing seam that ah-lu0f.2, .3 and
.4 will move the remaining order kinds onto, and moves the arms that have already been caught
drifting.

The month's silver is computed twice from the same orders. `silver::forecast_unit`
(`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:676`) produces the Silver column, one entry per own unit counting
that unit alone; `semantics::apply` (`:1586`) and `semantics::credit_tax` (`:1569`) produce the
`not-enough-silver` finding, a hex-wide balance with sharing pooled. Each has a separate arm per
order kind, so every order must be priced identically in two places by hand. Four `fix` commits
landed on 2026-08-23 alone, each one a divergence, and two whole beads (ah-ycuj, ah-8l9a) were spent
building nothing but a cross-check between them
(`crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs`). The code carries hand-written
*"Mirrors `forecast_unit`'s arm exactly - two surfaces reading one order must not price it two
ways"* comments at `semantics.rs:1607` and `:1621`, which is the smell stating itself.

**Two of this child's four order kinds are already shared, and the plan must not invent work for
them.** That is the first finding of the research and it halves the bead:

- **`WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` are done.** `silver::late_income` (`silver.rs:612`) prices both, and
  `semantics::charge_upkeep` already calls it — `semantics.rs:1386`,
  `(owed - late_income(facts, region, *shares)).max(0)`. Its doc comment says so outright:
  *"[`forecast_unit`] and `semantics::charge_upkeep` must be handed **the same** shares, for the
  reason this function exists at all."* Both `Intent::Work | Intent::Entertain => {}` arms are
  therefore already empty on purpose. **Leave them alone.**
- **`TAX`'s *rule* is shared and its *arithmetic* is not.** `taxes(flags, intents)` (`silver.rs:1850`)
  and `TAX_PER_MAN` (`silver.rs:23`) are both consulted by `credit_tax`, so *whether* a unit taxes is
  decided once. But `men.saturating_mul(TAX_PER_MAN).min(base)` is written at `silver.rs:784` and
  again at `semantics.rs:1582`.

So the real scope is **`PILLAGE` entirely, and `TAX`'s arithmetic** — plus the `Priced` seam itself,
which is the child's actual product.

### The divergence that must survive, and must not be "fixed"

`forecast_unit`'s tax term runs through `shares.tax`, the ah-t2pn settlement of a regional pool
between own units (`silver.rs:781-798`). `credit_tax` does not: it caps at
`hex.region.tax_base.unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` and its comment says why — *"optimistically, none of what
is left goes to any foreign unit"*.

**That difference is deliberate and load-bearing.** `semantics.rs`'s module doc (`:13-17`) states the
policy: *"Accept on doubt. Income the report cannot pin down is estimated at its most generous …
so a shortfall is reported only when the unit is short even in the best case. A false warning costs
the player their confidence in every other line on the screen."* The column has no such duty and
shows the settled figure.

An implementer that unifies TAX naively will make the ledger adopt the settlement, and the result is
false `not-enough-silver` warnings in every contended tax hex — the exact failure the module was
built to avoid. **The seam must share the arithmetic and leave the optimism a parameter.** See the
design below; this is the single most important sentence in this plan.

**When this child lands, `PILLAGE` and `TAX` are each priced by one function that both surfaces call,
and the next order kind has somewhere to move to.**

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — new `Priced`, `price_pillage`, `price_tax`; `forecast_unit`
  calls them.
- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `apply`'s `Intent::Pillage` arm and `credit_tax` call them.

No other file. No public API is removed; `Priced` and the two functions are new `pub` items in
`silver`, which `semantics` already imports from heavily (`semantics.rs:35`).

### What already exists and must be reused

- `SilverDoubt` (`silver.rs:271`) — the typed reasons. `UnknownTaxBase` (`:273`) and `EstimatedMen`
  (`:275`) are the two this child produces. **Add no variant**; the existing comment at
  `silver.rs:833` records that `EstimatedMen` is deliberately reused for a guessed headcount
  elsewhere in the hex rather than a new variant being added, and that stays true.
- `pillage_threshold(tax_base: i64) -> i64` (`silver.rs:1829`) — already `pub` and already called by
  both sides. It is the precedent this child generalises.
- `taxes(flags: &[String], intents: &[PlacedIntent]) -> bool` (`silver.rs:1850`) and
  `TAX_PER_MAN` (`silver.rs:23`) — already shared. Do not move or duplicate either.
- `PoolShare` / `PoolShares` (`silver.rs:~300`) — the ah-t2pn settlement, `Uncontended`,
  `Share(i64)`, `Unknowable`.
- `late_income` (`silver.rs:612`) — untouched, and the model for what "shared" looks like here.
- `credit(ledger, who, SILVER, amount)` and `ledger.doubted.insert(..)` in `semantics.rs` — how the
  ledger consumes a price. Unchanged.

### The design of the code

```rust
/// What one order does to a unit's silver this month, before either surface decides what to do
/// about it.
///
/// The two surfaces differ in how they *react* — the column shows a reason, the ledger stops
/// trusting the unit's sums — but never in the number. Adding a field here is how a new order kind
/// joins the seam (ah-lu0f.2, .3, .4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Priced {
    /// Silver the order earns. Never negative.
    pub earns: i64,
    /// Why it could not be priced, or `None`. A doubt and a non-zero `earns` never occur together.
    pub doubt: Option<SilverDoubt>,
}

/// What a `PILLAGE` earns: twice the region's available tax money, and nothing at all where the
/// faction is short of the combat-ready threshold.
///
/// "The amount of money collected is equal to twice the available tax money", and "this requires
/// the faction to have enough combat ready men in the region to tax half of the available money"
/// (`ah-1ad6.2`). Short of that the order earns a *certain* zero, so the unit is not doubted.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_pillage(tax_base: Option<i64>, combat_ready: Option<i64>) -> Priced;

/// What a unit's taxing earns this month: `men * TAX_PER_MAN`, capped.
///
/// **A unit-level term, not a per-line one** — the taxing flag makes a unit tax with no `TAX` order
/// at all, and a unit carrying both taxes once (`ah-fvzu`). Call it once per unit, never inside an
/// intent loop.
///
/// `share` is the caller's policy about a contended regional pool, and it is a parameter precisely
/// because **the two surfaces disagree about it on purpose**:
///
/// - The Silver column passes the ah-t2pn settlement (`shares.tax`), because it is showing the
///   player what this unit will actually collect.
/// - The ledger passes [`PoolShare::Uncontended`], because `semantics`' policy is *accept on doubt*
///   (`semantics.rs:13-17`): a shortfall is reported only when the unit is short even in the best
///   case, and "no other faction competes" is that best case. Passing the settlement here would
///   produce a false `not-enough-silver` in every contended tax hex.
///
/// `pillaged` is a certain zero and never a doubt: a pillage empties the hex whatever the base was,
/// so this collects nothing even where the base itself is unknown (`ah-cxxa`). It is tested before
/// `share`, or a hex with no stated base would raise `UnknownTaxBase` where the certain zero is the
/// better answer.
#[must_use]
pub fn price_tax(men: i64, tax_base: Option<i64>, pillaged: bool, share: PoolShare) -> Priced;
```

**How each surface consumes it.**

`forecast_unit`, replacing `silver.rs:771-800`:

```rust
if taxes(unit_flags, intents) {
    let priced = price_tax(men, region.tax_base, region.pillaged, shares.tax);
    income = income.saturating_add(priced.earns);
    income_doubt = income_doubt.or(priced.doubt);
}
```

`income_doubt.or(...)` preserves *"a tax doubt wins over a later order's, whichever line the player
typed first"* (`silver.rs:769-770`), which is deliberate and tested. Keep the term before the intent
loop, for the same reason it is there now.

`semantics::credit_tax`, replacing `semantics.rs:1569-1593`:

```rust
fn credit_tax(ledger: &mut Ledger<'_>, hex: &Hex<'_>, actor: &Ordered<'_>, pillaged: bool) {
    if !taxes(&actor.unit.flags, actor.intents) {
        return;
    }
    // `PoolShare::Uncontended` is this module's *accept on doubt* policy, not an oversight —
    // see `price_tax`'s doc comment.
    let priced = price_tax(actor.unit.men, hex.region.tax_base, pillaged, PoolShare::Uncontended);
    credit(ledger, &actor.unit.unit_id, SILVER, priced.earns);
    // A tax doubt is not the ledger's to raise: an unknown tax base credits nothing, which is
    // already the pessimistic direction for a shortfall. Behaviour on `main` today.
}
```

**Check that last claim against `main` before relying on it.** `credit_tax` today does not touch
`ledger.doubted` at all, so discarding `priced.doubt` preserves behaviour — but confirm it with the
test named in increment 3 rather than taking this plan's word for it.

`semantics::apply`'s `Intent::Pillage` arm, replacing `semantics.rs:1638-1653`:

```rust
Intent::Pillage => {
    let priced = price_pillage(hex.region.tax_base, hex_combat_ready);
    if priced.doubt.is_some() {
        ledger.doubted.insert(who.clone());
    } else {
        credit(ledger, who, SILVER, priced.earns);
    }
}
```

That is exactly the present three-arm match: `(None, _)` and `(Some(_), None)` doubt,
`(Some(_), Some(_))` short of the threshold credits zero without doubting.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere new. `Priced` is a `Copy` value built and dropped at each call site;
both functions are pure and take no `Ledger`, no `Hex` and no `UnitFacts`. That purity is the point —
it is what lets two callers with entirely different context share one rule.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test. Run `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` for each.

**Increment 1 — `Priced` and `price_pillage`.**
Failing test: `prices_a_pillage_from_the_base_and_the_threshold`, in `silver.rs`'s `mod tests`:

```rust
assert_eq!(price_pillage(None, Some(100)),
           Priced { earns: 0, doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase) });
assert_eq!(price_pillage(Some(8963), None),
           Priced { earns: 0, doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::EstimatedMen) });
assert_eq!(price_pillage(Some(100), Some(0)), Priced { earns: 0, doubt: None });
let base = 100;
assert_eq!(price_pillage(Some(base), Some(pillage_threshold(base))),
           Priced { earns: 200, doubt: None });
```

Then add `Priced` and `price_pillage`, and point `forecast_unit`'s arm (`silver.rs:828`) at it.
`semantics` is untouched in this increment.

**Increment 2 — the ledger's pillage arm.**
No new unit test; the increment is proven by the existing suites staying green and by the corpus
cross-check. Replace `semantics.rs:1638-1653` with the call above. If
`crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` goes red here, the two arms were **not**
identical on `main` and that is a finding to report, not to paper over.

**Increment 3 — `price_tax`, and the optimism made explicit.**
Failing test: `prices_a_units_tax_once_and_leaves_the_pool_policy_to_the_caller`, in `silver.rs`:

```rust
assert_eq!(price_tax(10, Some(8963), false, PoolShare::Uncontended),
           Priced { earns: 500, doubt: None });
// capped by the base
assert_eq!(price_tax(10, Some(200), false, PoolShare::Uncontended),
           Priced { earns: 200, doubt: None });
// a pillaged hex is a certain zero even with no stated base (`ah-cxxa`)
assert_eq!(price_tax(10, None, true, PoolShare::Uncontended),
           Priced { earns: 0, doubt: None });
// no base, not pillaged
assert_eq!(price_tax(10, None, false, PoolShare::Uncontended),
           Priced { earns: 0, doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase) });
// the settlement wins where the caller passes one
assert_eq!(price_tax(10, Some(8963), false, PoolShare::Share(120)),
           Priced { earns: 120, doubt: None });
assert_eq!(price_tax(10, Some(8963), false, PoolShare::Unknowable),
           Priced { earns: 0, doubt: Some(SilverDoubt::ContestedRegionPool) });
```

Add a second test, `the_ledger_stays_optimistic_about_a_contended_tax_pool`, in `semantics.rs`'s test
module: a hex where two own units both `TAX` and contend for the pool, asserting that **no**
`not-enough-silver` finding fires for a unit that the settled figure would have made short. This is
the regression guard for the divergence described in *Context*, and on `main` it must pass unchanged.
Write it and see it pass **before** touching `credit_tax`.

Then add `price_tax` and point both `silver.rs:771-800` and `credit_tax` at it.

**Increment 4 — say that WORK and ENTERTAIN are already done.**
No code change and no test. `late_income`'s doc comment (`silver.rs:596`) already says the important
half — *"The one place that decides which earnings arrive too late to be spent. [`forecast_unit`] and
`semantics::charge_upkeep` both read it, because two copies of this rule is exactly the drift that
`ah-uwa3` was filed to remove."* Add one sentence to it naming **ah-lu0f**: this function is already
the shared pricing seam for `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN`, so the empty
`Intent::Work | Intent::Entertain => {}` arms on both sides are that sharing rather than an omission.
The point is to stop a later child of this epic, or a later Forge sweep, re-filing work that is
already done — ah-lu0f's own description lists `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` as outstanding, and they are
not.

## The test plan

Rust only. Nothing in `packages/` changes and no browser suite is touched.

| Test | Where | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `prices_a_pillage_from_the_base_and_the_threshold` | `silver.rs` tests | all four `price_pillage` branches |
| `prices_a_units_tax_once_and_leaves_the_pool_policy_to_the_caller` | `silver.rs` tests | all six `price_tax` branches |
| `the_ledger_stays_optimistic_about_a_contended_tax_pool` | `semantics.rs` tests | the deliberate divergence; green on `main` |

**The regression net, none of which may be edited:**

- `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` — the two surfaces held to each other over
  26 real turns. **This is the gate for this whole epic.** It is why ah-ycuj and ah-8l9a exist.
- `the_column_and_the_warning_agree_about_a_taxer_in_a_pillaged_hex` (`semantics.rs:6193`) — the
  ah-abwx/ah-cxxa pair, and the one test that fails when a single-surface fix is attempted.
- `semantics.rs`'s `codes::ALL` fixture sweep (`:12803`).
- Every existing `forecast_unit` test in `silver.rs`.

**If any of those needs editing, this child has changed behaviour and is wrong.** The whole epic is
predicated on the numbers not moving.

## User-facing decisions

None.

Nothing here changes a message, a number, a column or a warning: both surfaces must produce
byte-identical output to `main`, which is the acceptance criterion above. The one place where a
user-visible choice *could* have been smuggled in — making the ledger adopt the column's pool
settlement — is explicitly forbidden by *Context* and guarded by
`the_ledger_stays_optimistic_about_a_contended_tax_pool`. If a later bead wants to revisit that,
it is a question for the navigator and a bead of its own.

## Out of scope

- **`BUY`, `SELL`, `CLAIM`, `WITHDRAW`** — ah-lu0f.2, which this child blocks.
- **`PRODUCE`, `STUDY`, `CAST`** — ah-lu0f.3.
- **`GIVE`, `TAKE`, and retiring the "Mirrors `forecast_unit`'s arm exactly" comments** — ah-lu0f.4.
  Leave those comments in place; they are still true of the arms this child does not touch.
- **`late_income`, `pool_wants`, `unit_upkeep`, `own_unit_pillages`.** Already shared. Increment 4
  documents `late_income` and changes no code in any of them.
- **Making the ledger use the ah-t2pn tax settlement.** See *Context*. Not a tidy-up; a behaviour
  change the navigator has not been asked about.
- **Any change to `SilverDoubt`'s variants**, to `UnitSilver`, or to the `not-enough-silver` message.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core                                  # after each increment
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning   # the epic's gate
pnpm run check:fast                                              # before the PR
```

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` runs inside `check:fast`. A `pub` item in
`silver.rs` that nothing calls yet will not trip it (the crate is a library), but an unused import in
`semantics.rs` will.

**The human check is the diff.** No message string and no number may differ from `main`. The
corpus cross-check is the machine half of that, and it is genuinely load-bearing here rather than
ceremonial: it is the only thing comparing the two surfaces at all.

## Known traps

- **The ledger is deliberately optimistic and the column is not** (`semantics.rs:13-17`). This is the
  trap this bead exists next to, and the one an implementer is most likely to fall into. Read
  *Context* before writing a line of `credit_tax`.
- **TAX is a unit-level term, not a per-line one** (`ah-fvzu`). A unit taxes by its flag with no
  `TAX` order at all, and one carrying both taxes once. `price_tax` must be called once per unit,
  outside any intent loop — both surfaces already do this and both say so in comments.
- **`region.pillaged` is tested before the pool settlement** (`silver.rs:772-777`), and the comment
  there says why: a pillaged hex with no stated base would otherwise raise `UnknownTaxBase` where a
  certain zero is the better answer (`ah-cxxa`). Preserve that order inside `price_tax`.
- **`income_doubt.or(...)`, never `= Some(...)`.** The first doubt wins, whichever line the player
  typed first (`silver.rs:769-770`), and that is tested.
- **A vacuously-true corpus assertion is this repository's known failure mode** (ah-ycuj: true for
  758 of 1,392 units, caught only by a reviewer). If
  `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` stays green through a change you expected to break it, check
  that it is actually exercising the case before believing it.
- **`plan_production` caps against the report's holdings, not a running balance** (`silver.rs:1961`),
  precisely so the two surfaces agree. Not this child's business, but it is the shape of decision
  ah-lu0f.3 will meet.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** — irrelevant here, since nothing leaves `crates/core`, but named
  because it is the trap most beads in this repository meet.

title: Refactoring: a command's arguments are agreed in four places and checked in CI
description:
## The cost being paid

One core capability reaches the app only by being written out again along a ladder of hand-maintained
files — the Tauri command, the wasm export, the persistence call, the client index, `tauriCommands.ts`,
`webCoreAdapter.ts`, `main.rs`, `gameActions.ts` and the native IPC sweep. The local lockstep gate
compares command *names* only, so a missing or renamed argument passes every local check and fails in
CI's Linux-only `native` job.

## Evidence

- docs/retrospectives/ah-0w7w.md §"Adding a parameter to an existing Tauri command passes every local
  check and fails `native` in CI" — `check:fast` fully green including the live lockstep test, then four
  `native` specs failed with `missing required key map_json`; **one CI cycle, ~25 minutes**. The retro
  names the structural reason and defers the fix: "extending it to compare those parameters against each
  sweep entry's `args` keys would move this whole class of failure from CI to the local gate. That is a
  change to a shared test rather than to this bead."
- docs/retrospectives/ah-o1t.1.md §"A new Tauri command needs a matching entry in the native binding
  sweep, and the plan did not name it" — one CI cycle ~7 minutes plus a rebase (PR #268).
- `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts:257-261` states the gap in its own comment — "The sweep names only real
  parameters (it may omit an Option; it may not invent one)" — beside a hand-pinned
  `expect(renames.size).toBe(28)`.
- Ladder size, by `git show --stat`: `1755c70c` 33 files for one concept; `632673ce` (ah-do8.1) and
  `00a2a13b` (ah-58n.1) 11 files each.

## Where

- `packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts`, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`,
  `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `tests/native/sweep.ts`, `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`

## What a refactoring would change

Derive the command surface from one declaration instead of agreeing it in four — or, at least, extend
the existing lockstep test to compare argument names in both directions, which is what ah-0w7w says
would move this whole class from CI to the local gate. The hand-pinned count of 28 becomes unnecessary
once the list has a single source.

Filed by Forge, weekly sweep of 2026-08-24, range 440b51fb..origin/main.
design:
## Context

A Tauri command's argument list is agreed in several places — the Rust `fn`, `TAURI_COMMANDS` in
`packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts`, and the driving entry in `tests/native/sweep.ts` — and
the local gate does not compare all of them. ah-0w7w's retrospective states the cost exactly:
`check:fast` fully green **including the live lockstep test**, then four `native` specs failing in CI
with `missing required key map_json`. **One CI cycle, ~25 minutes.** ah-o1t.1 paid another ~7 minutes
plus a rebase (PR #268).

**The hole is narrower than the bead states, and naming it precisely is most of the work.**
`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` already closes three of the four sides:

- `lockstep(registered, swept)` (`:235`) — what `main.rs` registers and what the sweep drives are the
  same set, both ways. So **every registered command has a sweep entry**; nothing is unswept.
- `expect(Object.keys(table).sort()).toEqual([...registered].sort())` (`:240`) — the adapter's table
  names the same commands.
- `expect(keys, command).toEqual(parameters[command])` (`:252`) — every `TAURI_COMMANDS` row's keys
  are the Rust parameter names, **in order**.

What is *not* checked is the sweep's own arguments, and the existing loop says so in its own comment
(`:255`): *"The sweep names only real parameters (it may omit an Option; it may not invent one)"*. It
asserts one direction only — every key the sweep sends is a real parameter — and nothing asserts that
every **required** parameter is sent. That is precisely `missing required key map_json`.

It cannot assert the other direction today because `commandParameters` (`scripts/tauriCommands.ts:102`)
throws the type away: `param.split(":")[0].trim()`. Names survive; `Option<…>` does not. So the test
has no way to tell a parameter a caller may omit from one it may not.

**When this lands, a required argument missing from the sweep fails `pnpm run check:fast` in seconds
instead of failing CI's Linux-only `native` job 25 minutes later.** That is the whole of the cost the
bead names, and it is closed completely.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Two files, both tooling. **No application code, no Rust, no `packages/` change.**

- `scripts/tauriCommands.ts` — `commandParameters` learns about `Option<…>`.
- `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` — its unit tests follow the new return type, and the lockstep test
  gains one assertion.

### What already exists and must be reused

- `splitTopLevel(text: string): string[]` (`tauriCommands.ts:70`) — splits a parameter list on
  top-level commas, respecting `<>`, `()`, `[]` and `{}`. `disabled_codes: Option<Vec<String>>`
  depends on it. Do not write a second splitter.
- `commandRenames(coreTauriLibRs)` (`:54`) — `command_x` → wire name.
- `lockstep(registered, swept)` — already proves the sweep covers every registered command, which is
  what makes the new assertion exhaustive by construction rather than by a second sweep of its own.
- `SWEEP: SweepEntry[]` (`tests/native/sweep.ts:57`), where `SweepEntry` is
  `{ command: string; args: () => Record<string, unknown> }` (`:48-49`).

### The design of the code

One exported interface and one changed return type.

```ts
/** One wire parameter of a Tauri command. */
export interface CommandParameter {
  /** The wire name, exactly as a caller must send it. */
  name: string;
  /**
   * False when the Rust type is `Option<…>`, which Tauri lets a caller omit; true otherwise.
   *
   * A required parameter that nothing sends is `missing required key <name>` at runtime, and
   * before ah-enik that was only ever seen in CI's Linux-only `native` job (ah-0w7w).
   */
  required: boolean;
}

/**
 * The wire parameters of every Tauri command, in declaration order, keyed by wire name.
 *
 * Was `Record<string, string[]>`; the name alone could not say whether a caller may omit the
 * parameter, which is the one thing the sweep needed to be checked against.
 */
export function commandParameters(
  mainRs: string,
  coreTauriLibRs: string
): Record<string, CommandParameter[]>;
```

**The requiredness rule, stated once.** For a parameter piece `name: Type`, split on the **first**
`:` only — `Option<Vec<String>>` contains none, but splitting on all of them would still be wrong for
a future `Foo::Bar` — then:

```ts
const required = !type.trim().startsWith("Option<");
```

`&str`, `u32`, `bool`, `Vec<String>` and `String` are all required; `Option<&str>`,
`Option<String>` and `Option<Vec<String>>` are not. These are the live cases —
`command_order_vocabulary(ruleset_json: Option<&str>)` (`core-tauri/src/lib.rs:478`),
`command_validate_orders`'s three optionals (`:555`) and
`command_commit_report_import(… ruleset_json: Option<&str> …)` (`:362`).

**Read the parameter list only, never the return type.** `command_load_order_draft` (`:625`) returns
`Result<Option<OrderDraftRecordDto>, String>` and takes four required parameters; a rule that looked
for `Option<` anywhere in the signature would call it optional. The existing regexes already capture
only what is inside the parentheses (`\(([^)]*)\)`), so this holds as long as the capture is not
widened — do not widen it.

**Where state lives.** Nowhere. Both functions are pure string-in, value-out and are called once by
one test.

**The two existing call sites become name comparisons**, and nothing else about them changes:

```ts
// tauriCommands.test.ts:252
expect(keys, command).toEqual(parameters[command].map((parameter) => parameter.name));
```

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test in `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`. Run
`pnpm vitest run scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` for each.

**Increment 1 — the parser learns requiredness.**
Failing test: `reads_whether_each_parameter_may_be_omitted`, added to the existing
`describe("commandParameters")` block (`:108`). Against a small inline `coreTauriLibRs` fixture in
the shape the existing tests at `:119` and `:133` already use:

```ts
expect(commandParameters("", coreTauriLibRs)).toEqual({
  order_vocabulary: [{ name: "ruleset_json", required: false }],
  set_game_map: [
    { name: "game_id", required: true },
    { name: "map_json", required: true }
  ]
});
```

Then add `CommandParameter` and change `commandParameters` to return it. Update the three existing
`commandParameters` unit tests (`:119`, `:133`, `:148`) to the new shape — they are expressing the
same facts, so change only the literals.

**Increment 2 — the existing lockstep assertions follow the type.**
No new test; the suite must simply go green again. Change `:252` to compare
`parameters[command].map((p) => p.name)`, and `:257` (the "may not invent one" loop) to test against
the same mapped names. Nothing about what those two assert changes.

**Increment 3 — the assertion that closes the hole.**
Failing test: prove it fails before it passes. Temporarily delete `map_json` from `set_game_map`'s
`args()` in `tests/native/sweep.ts:78`, confirm the new assertion goes red with a message naming
`set_game_map.map_json`, then put it back. Add, inside the lockstep test beside the existing sweep
loop:

```ts
// Every required parameter is supplied. An Option may be omitted; a required one may not, and
// omitting one is `missing required key <name>` in CI's native job 25 minutes later (ah-0w7w).
// `lockstep` above has already proved SWEEP covers every registered command, so this is
// exhaustive: there is no command it can skip.
for (const entry of SWEEP) {
  const supplied = new Set(Object.keys(entry.args()));
  for (const parameter of parameters[entry.command] ?? []) {
    if (parameter.required) {
      expect([...supplied], `${entry.command}.${parameter.name}`).toContain(parameter.name);
    }
  }
}
```

**Increment 4 — a guard against the assertion going vacuous.**
Failing test: `the_required_and_optional_parameter_sets_are_both_populated`. ah-ycuj's retrospective
records a corpus assertion that was vacuously true for 758 of 1,392 units and passed for a year; the
loop above would pass identically if the requiredness rule ever started returning `false` for
