## Known traps

- **This is a submodule.** The work is a PR in `rmstdope/cerebro`, then a `chore: bump cerebro`
  pointer commit in `atlantis-hud`. `.claude/agents/*` and `.claude/skills/*` are **symlinks** into
  it: editing them from the consumer checkout writes into the submodule working tree and shows as a
  dirty submodule, and a change not committed in the submodule's own repository is **lost** on the
  next `git submodule update`.
- **`.metadata` is absent, not empty, when a bead has none.** Verified by probe on 2026-08-24. Every
  reader must be `.metadata // {} | .verified_at`; `.metadata.verified_at` on a bead without any
  metadata errors out in `jq` rather than returning null.
- **The scripts never mutate.** `sweep-claims.sh`'s header states it and gives the reason: it is what
  makes "the only path to a destructive command is the confirmed one" checkable by reading a single
  file. A `bd set-state` inside `sweep-verdicts.sh` would pass every test in this plan and quietly
  destroy that guarantee. Increment 2's `grep` exists for this.
- **`cerebro--verdict-finding` must stay pure.** The guards are testable only because the family's
  findings are pure; reaching into the filesystem or calling `git` from it would make this the one
  that cannot be tested.
- **`verification:` is a bd dimension and `bd set-state` replaces it.** `--add-label
  verification:stale` would leave two labels in one dimension, and `set-state verification=stale`
  would erase the verdict. That is why the dimension is `verdict`, and it is not a naming
  preference.
- **`1 merges since`.** The chosen threshold is one, so the singular case is the common one. There is
  a test named for it.
- **All three consumer queries, or none.** `implement-bead`, `plan-bead` (several copies of the
  query — grep `plan:revise`) and `verifier.md`. A bead skipped by implementers but still taken by
  planners is the original failure with an extra label on it.
- **A stale bead is `open`, and Psylocke's work-list selects closed beads.** Adding
  `verdict:stale` to her query is not a tidy-up; without it the flagged bead reaches nobody at all,
  which is strictly worse than today.
- **Liveness, wherever this bead touches it, is `cerebro--session-alive-p`** — but note this sweep
  needs none, which is why `cerebro--verdict-finding` takes one argument. Do not add a roster or a
  `now` parameter for symmetry.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**: none of the five recorded traps apply. This bead touches no
  application code, no browser suite and no persisted setting.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict carries the commit it was formed against in a field, not only in prose. Before a failed bead is offered to an implementer or a planner, that commit is compared to the head of the default branch, and a verdict formed against an older commit is flagged for a second look rather than acted on. The three cases above would each have been caught.

title: A unit that taxes without an order is not warned about a foreign guard
description:
Split out of ah-fvzu (implementation, 2026-08-23).

ah-g7ts marks a TAX in a hex a foreign unit guards - one finding per order line, 'a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing'. It landed after ah-fvzu was planned, and ah-fvzu put it explicitly out of scope.

A unit that taxes by its taxing flag (ah-fvzu) collects nothing in a guarded hex for exactly the same reason, but has no TAX line to hang the mark on, so it is silently unwarned. The fix mirrors what ah-fvzu did for the pillaged-hex mark: keep the per-line finding for units with a TAX, and add a block-level one (semantics::finding_at_block) for a flagged unit without one, in crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs's check_taxed_guarded_hex.

This is a new user-visible warning on a unit, which is why the implementer did not decide it alone.

The same question applies to ah-1ad6's combat-ready threshold if it ever gates TAX the way it gates PILLAGE.
design:
## Context

`ah-g7ts` warns when we tax or pillage a hex a **foreign unit is guarding**: one finding per order
line, `taxed-a-guarded-hex`, saying *may* rather than *will* because whether the guard actually
blocks us turns on that faction's declared attitude, which our report does not state.

`ah-fvzu` then made a unit that carries the **taxing** flag (`AUTOTAX`) tax without any `TAX` line
in this month's orders, and routed the flagged case through the same code as an explicit `TAX`
everywhere it could. It could not do so here: `check_guarded_tax` walks `ordered.intents`, so a
flagged unit with no `TAX` line is never reached. `ah-fvzu` put this explicitly out of scope and
split this bead out of its implementation on 2026-08-23.

So today a flagged unit in a foreign-guarded hex collects nothing for exactly the same reason as
its neighbour with a `TAX` line, and is **silently unwarned**. `ah-fvzu` already solved the shape of
this problem for the pillaged-hex mark, in `check_pillaged_tax` — keep the per-line finding for
units that have a `TAX`, add a block-level one (`Ordered::finding_at_block`) for a flagged unit
without one — and this bead applies that same treatment to `check_guarded_tax`.

The corpus has one such unit of ours and it is not small: `City Guards (13303)`, 800 orcs, taxing,
in `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`.

When this lands: a unit that taxes by its flag is warned about a foreign guard exactly as a unit
with a `TAX` line is, in the same words.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**One function changes. There is no TypeScript in this bead, and no new finding code** —
`codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX` (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:114`) already exists, is already
registered, and already has its own toggle in `CheckOptions`. Nothing has to be listed by hand
anywhere.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `check_guarded_tax` (line 1518)

It reads today:

```rust
fn check_guarded_tax(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    guarded: bool,
    pillaged: bool,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
) {
    if !guarded || !options.emits(codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX) {
        return;
    }

    for ordered in &hex.units {
        for placed in ordered.intents {
            let order = match placed.intent {
                Intent::Tax if !pillaged => "TAX",
                Intent::Pillage => "PILLAGE",
                _ => continue,
            };
            findings.push(ordered.finding(
                hex,
                codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX,
                format!("a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this {order} may collect nothing"),
                Some(placed),
            ));
        }
    }
}
```

The change is confined to the body of the outer `for ordered` loop, and mirrors
`check_pillaged_tax` (line 1471-1504) line for line:

```rust
    for ordered in &hex.units {
        let mut ordered_to_tax = false;
        for placed in ordered.intents {
            let order = match placed.intent {
                Intent::Tax if !pillaged => "TAX",
                Intent::Pillage => "PILLAGE",
                _ => continue,
            };
            if matches!(placed.intent, Intent::Tax) {
                ordered_to_tax = true;
            }
            findings.push(ordered.finding(
                hex,
                codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX,
                format!("a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this {order} may collect nothing"),
                Some(placed),
            ));
        }
        // A unit that taxes by its flag collects nothing here either, and has no line to hang the
        // mark on - so it hangs on the block, which is what `finding_at_block` is for (`ah-fvzu`).
        // Suppressed in a pillaged hex for the same reason the `TAX` line is: `taxed-a-pillaged-hex`
        // already says the money is certainly gone, and `check_pillaged_tax` marks this same block
        // with it (`ah-cxxa`).
        if !pillaged && !ordered_to_tax && taxes(&ordered.unit.flags, ordered.intents) {
            findings.push(ordered.finding_at_block(
                hex,
                codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX,
                "a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing".to_string(),
            ));
        }
    }
```

**The `ordered_to_tax` flag must be set on `Intent::Tax` itself, not on the `match` succeeding.**
The `match` arm is `Intent::Tax if !pillaged`, so in a pillaged hex a `TAX` line falls through to
`continue` and would leave the flag false — but the whole block-level branch is then suppressed by
`!pillaged` anyway, so the two guards agree. Writing `ordered_to_tax = true` inside the `Tax` arm of
the match instead would be wrong in a pillaged hex and is only saved by the outer guard; set it on
the intent, as written above, so the reason is local.

What to reuse, all of it already present in this file and verified:

- **`taxes(flags, intents)`** — `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`, already imported into
  `semantics.rs` at line 29 and already called at lines 1498, 1572, 3619 and 4184. It is a
  predicate, true for an explicit `TAX`, for either flag spelling (`taxing`, `autotax`), and for
  both together. Do not re-derive it and do not test flags by hand.
- **`Ordered::finding_at_block(&self, hex, code, message)`** — `semantics.rs:1146`. Sets
  `unit_id: Some(...)`, `line: self.block_line`, and **no columns**: *"a finding against the unit's
  block rather than against one order in it, for a check whose subject is the absence of an
  order."*
  Note that `block_line` is `None` when the unit has no orders block in the document at all — see
  *User-facing decisions*; that case is intended and must not be guarded against.
- **`foreign_unit_guards(hex)`** (`semantics.rs:1242`) and **`own_unit_pillages(hex)`**
  (`semantics.rs:1259`) — the caller at `semantics.rs:345` already computes both and passes them in.
  The call site does not change.
- **`check_pillaged_tax`** (`semantics.rs:1471`) — the shape being copied. Read it before writing.

**No state moves and no layer boundary is crossed.** This is a pure function over one hex,
producing findings the existing pipeline already sorts (`semantics.rs:368`: within a hex, line-anchored
findings first in line order, block-level ones last).

Update the doc comment on `check_guarded_tax` (lines 1507-1516) to say that a flagged unit without a
`TAX` line is marked on its block, and cite `ah-leeg` — the comment currently says "one finding per
affected order line", which stops being the whole truth.

## Increments

Both increments are in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s test module, beside the existing
`taxed-a-guarded-hex` fixtures (from `fn foreign_guard` at line 6636). Reuse `foreign_guard`,
`guarded_hex(own)`, `with_silver`, `unit` and **`taxing_by_flag(unit)`** (line 6046), which pushes
the `"taxing"` flag.

1. **The block-level mark.** Opening failing test —
   `a_flagged_taxer_in_a_guarded_hex_is_marked_on_its_block`, modelled on
   `a_flagged_taxer_in_a_pillaged_hex_is_marked_on_its_block` (line 6126):

   ```rust
   /// A flagged unit has no `TAX` line to hang the mark on, so it hangs on its block
   /// (`semantics::finding_at_block`) - `ah-leeg`, mirroring what `ah-fvzu` did for the
   /// pillaged-hex mark.
   #[test]
   fn a_flagged_taxer_in_a_guarded_hex_is_marked_on_its_block() {
       let region = guarded_hex(vec![with_silver(taxing_by_flag(unit("683")), 0)]);
       let ordered = OrderedUnits::read("");
       let hex = Hex::read(&region, &ordered);
       let mut findings = Vec::new();
       check_guarded_tax(&hex, true, false, &CheckOptions::default(), &mut findings);

       assert_eq!(findings.len(), 1, "{findings:?}");
       assert_eq!(
           findings[0].message,
           "a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing"
       );
       assert_eq!(findings[0].unit_id.as_deref(), Some("683"));
       assert_eq!(findings[0].column_start, None);
       assert_eq!(findings[0].column_end, None);
   }
   ```

   Then, in the same increment, the three tests that pin what must **not** change:

   - `a_flagged_taxer_with_a_tax_order_is_marked_only_on_its_line` — same hex, orders
     `"unit 683\nTAX\n"`, unit carries the flag as well. Exactly one finding, and
     `column_start.is_some()`. This is the test that catches the obvious wrong implementation,
     which marks the block as well and shows the same sentence twice on one unit.
   - `a_flagged_taxer_in_a_pillaged_and_guarded_hex_is_not_told_twice` — `guarded_hex` holding
     `armed_to_pillage(with_silver(unit("1"), 0), 8963)` and
     `with_silver(taxing_by_flag(unit("2")), 0)`, orders `"unit 1\nPILLAGE\n"`, called with
     `pillaged = true`. **No** `TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX` finding for unit 2 at all; the block-level
     `taxed-a-pillaged-hex` mark that `ah-fvzu` added is the one it gets. Assert on the codes
     carried by findings whose `unit_id` is `Some("2")`, as
     `a_pillaged_and_guarded_hex_warns_once_about_tax` (line 6770) does for the line case.
   - `an_unflagged_unit_without_orders_is_not_marked` — the same hex with a plain
     `with_silver(unit("683"), 0)` and no orders. Nothing at all: the mark is about taxing, not
     about standing in a guarded hex.

2. **The whole pipeline, and the toggle.** These go through `review_turn` rather than calling the
   check directly, beside `taxing_a_hex_a_foreigner_guards_is_flagged` (line 6702):

   - `a_flagged_taxer_is_warned_through_review_turn` — `review_turn(&report(vec![guarded_hex(...)]),
     "", Some(&ruleset()), CheckOptions::default())` with the flagged unit and **empty orders text**.
     Exactly one `TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX` finding, carrying the agreed message. This is the
     no-orders-block case the navigator chose to keep (see *User-facing decisions*), and asserting
     it end to end is the only way to prove the hex's other checks do not suppress it.
   - `the_guarded_hex_toggle_silences_the_flagged_case_too` — the same call with
     `CheckOptions` that disables `taxed-a-guarded-hex`, asserting no finding of that code. One
     code, one toggle; a second path that ignored `options.emits` would be a real defect and the
     early return already prevents it, so this test pins it rather than driving it.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `a_flagged_taxer_in_a_guarded_hex_is_marked_on_its_block` | `orders/semantics.rs` | the defect: the mark exists, with the agreed message, on the block, with no columns |
| `a_flagged_taxer_with_a_tax_order_is_marked_only_on_its_line` | `orders/semantics.rs` | no double warning for a unit carrying both |
| `a_flagged_taxer_in_a_pillaged_and_guarded_hex_is_not_told_twice` | `orders/semantics.rs` | the weaker "may" stays suppressed where the pillage mark already speaks |
| `an_unflagged_unit_without_orders_is_not_marked` | `orders/semantics.rs` | the mark is about taxing, not about being present |
| `a_flagged_taxer_is_warned_through_review_turn` | `orders/semantics.rs` | the no-orders-block case survives the full pipeline |
| `the_guarded_hex_toggle_silences_the_flagged_case_too` | `orders/semantics.rs` | one code, one toggle |
| `validate_real_orders.rs` (existing) | `crates/core/tests/` | the corpus expectations table does not move |

Suites that must run: `cargo test -p atlantis-core`, then `pnpm run check:fast`.

**The corpus table is expected not to move.** `validate_real_orders.rs` reads
`atlantis_hud_fixtures::G7_F95_T71` (line 15) — turn 71 of g7/f95 — while the one flagged own unit
in the corpus is in the g3/f42 turn-82 fixture, a different report entirely. `EXPECTED` (line 60)
lists `magic-study-outside-building`, `not-enough-items`, `study-at-maximum` and `unit-does-nothing`
and no guard code at all. If it does move, **read the finding before touching the table** — the
table's own doc comment records twice that a moved row was the bead proving itself, and twice that
it was worth understanding first.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-24. Mockup, as chosen and committed:
`docs/ui/ah-leeg-guarded-flag-tax.html` (PR #641, merged). Three variants were put side by side,
each showing the same three states — the unit with orders, the unit with no orders at all, and the
hex also being pillaged.

**What the warning says on a unit with no `TAX` line.**
Chosen: **reuse the existing sentence, unchanged and verbatim**:

> `a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing`

The same string the `TAX` line already carries, and the same treatment `ah-fvzu` gave the
block-level pillage mark. One unit never sees two spellings of one idea. The accepted cost: it says
*this TAX* where there is no `TAX` on screen to point at.

Rejected: *naming the flag instead* — `this unit taxes every turn, and a foreign unit is guarding
this hex, so it may collect nothing`. More accurate about a unit with no order, and it would tell a
player who did not know the flag was set why the unit is being warned at all; rejected because the
same unit's pillaged-hex mark would still say *this TAX*, so the two marks on one unit would
disagree in wording.

Rejected: *keeping the shape and adding the flag as a clause* — `a foreign unit is guarding this
hex, so this unit's automatic TAX may collect nothing`. Rejected as a third spelling in a family
that already has one, and because it would leave `ah-fvzu`'s pillage mark wanting the same
treatment later.

**A flagged unit with no orders block in the document at all.** This is the common case and the
real corpus one: `City Guards (13303)` has 800 men, the taxing flag, and not a line of orders. With
no block, `finding_at_block` produces `line: None`, and `orderLint.ts:32` drops a diagnostic whose
`lineStart` is null — so the mark shows in the **Problems panel**, grouped under its hex and named
by unit (`workspace/ProblemsPanel.tsx`), and nowhere in the editor.
Chosen: **warn anyway, always.** The money is at risk whether or not the unit has orders, and this
is precisely the unit the bead exists for.

Rejected: *warning only where the unit has a block*, so the mark can always be seen beside the
orders being typed. Quieter, and it never produces a warning invisible in the editor — rejected
because it would silence the largest taxing unit in the corpus, which is the whole case.

**Decided here, not asked**, each following from the two answers above:

- **A unit carrying the flag *and* an explicit `TAX` gets one mark, on its line.** The message is
  the same either way, so a block-level mark beside it would show one sentence twice on one unit.
  Same rule `ah-fvzu` applied.
- **In a hex one of our own units is pillaging, the flagged unit gets no guarded mark at all.**
  `taxed-a-pillaged-hex` is the stronger fact — the money is certainly gone, not *may* be — and
  `check_pillaged_tax` already marks that same block with it. This is the existing `TAX`-line rule
  (`semantics.rs:1509-1514`) applied to the block, and the navigator saw it as state 3 of the
  mockup.
- **The flagged case rides the existing `taxed-a-guarded-hex` toggle.** One code, one switch; a
  player who has turned this advisory off has turned it off.
- **Nothing is added to the unit hover.** `ah-fvzu`'s
  `This unit is set to tax every turn, so it taxes without an order.` already explains where the
  income came from; that the income may be blocked is a finding, and findings live in the problems
  panel and the editor.

## Out of scope

- **`ah-1ad6`'s combat-ready threshold.** The bead's description notes the same question will arise
  if that threshold ever gates `TAX` the way it gates `PILLAGE`. It does not today, and nothing
  here anticipates it.
- **Whether a foreign guard actually blocks us.** It depends on that faction's declared attitude,
  which the report does not state — which is why `ah-g7ts` chose *may* and why this bead keeps it.
- **Our own unit being on guard.** `City Guards` is itself on guard; that has never exempted it
  from this check and does not now. `foreign_unit_guards` (`semantics.rs:1242`) tests
  `!unit.own && unit.on_guard`, and is not touched.
- **The pillaged-hex mark's wording.** Unchanged, and the reason option C was rejected.
- **Any change to `orderLint.ts` or the problems panel** to surface line-less findings differently.
  The navigator chose the existing behaviour knowingly.
- **Foreign units' taxing flags.** `Hex::read` filters foreign units out before any of this.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, no `#[ignore]`. `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` in particular must stay green
with `EXPECTED` untouched.

Then, by eye — **a human must confirm this**, because no assertion over hand-built fixtures proves
it of a real report: load `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` with its
committed orders template and find the hex holding `City Guards (13303)`. If a foreign unit is on
guard there, the problems panel shows one row against unit 13303 reading
`a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing`, and no other unit's findings
have changed. **If no foreign unit guards that hex, there is nothing to see in the corpus** — say so
in the PR rather than hunting for a report that shows it; the constructed fixtures are what prove
this bead, and the corpus check here is only that nothing else moved.

## Known traps

- **`ordered_to_tax` must be set on the intent, not on the `match` arm succeeding.** The arm is
  `Intent::Tax if !pillaged`, so in a pillaged hex a real `TAX` line does not reach it. Setting the
  flag inside that arm is wrong there and only survives because the block-level branch is guarded by
  `!pillaged` as well. Set it on `matches!(placed.intent, Intent::Tax)`, so the two guards do not
  have to be read together to see that the code is right.
- **Do not test the flags by hand.** `taxes(&ordered.unit.flags, ordered.intents)` is the predicate,
  it is already imported (`semantics.rs:29`), and it handles both spellings — `taxing` and
  `autotax`, both in the parser's `KNOWN_FLAGS` (`report/unit.rs:18`). Matching only one silently
  halves the fix, which is a trap `ah-fvzu` recorded and this bead inherits.
- **`finding_at_block` gives `line: None` when the unit has no orders block**, and `orderLint.ts`
  drops such a diagnostic from the editor. That is expected and chosen; do not "fix" it by
  inventing a `PlacedIntent` or by falling back to the hex's own line.
- **Do not invent a `PlacedIntent`** to reuse `Ordered::finding`. `finding_at_block`
  (`semantics.rs:1146`) exists for exactly the absence of an order.
- **No new finding code, and no expectations row.** `TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX` already exists at
  `semantics.rs:114` with its own toggle. Nothing needs listing by hand, and `EXPECTED` in
  `validate_real_orders.rs` is over a different fixture and should not move.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**: none of the five recorded traps apply. This bead touches no
  persisted setting, no browser suite and no `packages/shared` code — it is one Rust function and
  its unit tests.

title: A bead awaiting re-verification looks exactly like one whose plan was judged wrong
description:
Found by Xavier on 2026-08-23, twice in two passes, on ah-t2pn.3.

## The ambiguity

skills/plan-bead and agents/planner tell a planner that a reopened bead reaching them with its 'planned' label REMOVED means the plan itself was judged wrong, and is to be amended in place. That reading is asserted, not checked:

  A reopened bead that reaches you with its planned label removed (the plan itself was
  judged wrong, not just the build) is a P0 with an existing design and a recorded
  failure to read - amend it in place.

But 'planned' also comes off for a completely different reason. On ah-t2pn.3, Storm picked the bead up, established from its notes that there was nothing to implement, and removed 'planned' so no implementer would claim it again - which was correct, and which agents/implement-bead's hand-back recipe tells it to do. The bead then carried P0 + verification:failed + no planned, which is character for character what a plan-judged-wrong bead looks like.

## What it costs

A planner's P0 check returns it every pass. Twice now Xavier has had to reason from the notes to decide not to act; a planner that trusted the label rule would have rewritten a sound plan, and the interview that produced it, against a verification finding the plan had already scoped out deliberately.

It also parks the bead: the same hand-back adds 'human', which routes it to the navigator's queue when what it needs is Psylocke. That half was fixed by hand on 2026-08-23 (remove 'human', keep 'verification:failed') but nothing stops the next one.

## The shape of the gap

Three states share one set of labels:

  build was wrong          -> implementers      planned kept, verification:failed
  plan was wrong           -> a planner         planned removed, verification:failed
  nothing to do, re-verify -> Psylocke          planned removed, verification:failed

The second and third are indistinguishable, and they route to different roles.
design:
## Context

When Psylocke fails a bead she asks the navigator one question — **is the plan wrong, or is the build
wrong?** — and records the answer by *removing* `planned`, or not
(`agents/verifier.md:388-400`):

- **build wrong** → `planned` stays → back to `bd ready` for implementers;
- **plan wrong** → `bd update <id> --remove-label planned` → *"a P0 pre-emption for the planners"*.

That much works. **The gap is downstream.** An implementer handing a bead back also removes
`planned` — `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:323` and `skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md:96` both say to,
and both are right for the case they were written for. So a bead the navigator judged **build wrong**
can arrive at a planner wearing the labels of **plan wrong**, and the answer they gave is overwritten
by a recipe that never knew about it.

**Observed twice on `ah-t2pn.3`, 2026-08-23.** Psylocke failed it; the navigator said *build wrong*,
so `planned` stayed. Storm then picked it up, found from the notes that there was nothing to build
(its sibling `ah-t2pn.4` carried the surface the verification asked for), and handed it back —
removing `planned` and adding `human`. The planner's P0 check then returned it as *plan wrong*, on
two consecutive passes. **A planner that trusted the label rule would have rewritten a sound plan,
and the interview behind it, against a finding that plan had deliberately scoped out.**

Nothing here was anyone's mistake. Psylocke asked the right question, Storm followed the right
recipe, and three states cannot be carried by one label's presence.

| State | Who should have it | Labels today |
|---|---|---|
| build was wrong | implementers | `planned`, `verification:failed` |
| plan was wrong | a planner | `verification:failed` |
| nothing to build, re-verify | Psylocke | `verification:failed` |

The last two are indistinguishable.

**This bead is documentation and label convention, not code, and it lives in the `cerebro`
submodule** — every `.claude/agents/*.md` and `.claude/skills/*` in the consumer is a symlink into
`.claude/cerebro/`. See *Files to change*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**All five files are in `.claude/cerebro/`, a git submodule of its own
(`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git`, `main`).** The work is a PR **in that repository**,
followed by a `chore: bump cerebro` pointer commit in `atlantis-hud` — the consumer's history
already carries such commits. Branch in a worktree named `.cerebro/worktrees/<id>-cerebro`, the
suffix the existing cerebro worktrees use.

**No code, no tests, no generated files, and nothing in `atlantis-hud` but the bump.**

### The design: say it positively

The planner's rule reads the state from an **absence**, and an absence cannot say why it is absent.
Replace it with a label the verifier sets deliberately:

```
plan:revise
```

Set by Psylocke, and **only** by Psylocke, on the branch where the navigator answered *plan wrong*.
Then `planned`'s removal means only what it says — *not ready for an implementer* — and every future
reason to remove it is harmless instead of a fresh collision with the planners.

The name matches the existing `verification:failed` shape (namespace, colon, verb) and says what the
planner should **do** rather than what went wrong.

### 1. `agents/verifier.md` — set the label

At the *Plan wrong* branch (`:395-400`), the command becomes:

```bash
bd update <id> --remove-label planned --add-label plan:revise
```

Extend the prose immediately below it — which already says *"This is a P0 pre-emption for the
planners"* — to say that **`plan:revise` is what a planner looks for**, and that removing `planned`
alone no longer means anything to them. One or two sentences, in the voice of the surrounding text.

Add, to the *Build wrong* branch: a planner never picks up a build-wrong bead, and nothing in that
branch should ever add `plan:revise`.

### 2. `agents/planner.md:133` — read the label, not the absence

Today:

> A reopened bead that reaches you with its `planned` label removed (the plan itself was judged
> wrong, not just the build) is a P0 with an existing design and a recorded failure to read — amend
> it in place; `plan-bead` has the detail.

Becomes a rule about `plan:revise`, and **says why the old wording was wrong** so nobody reinstates
it: `planned` comes off for more than one reason, and an implementer handing back a bead with
nothing to build removes it too.

### 3. `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md` — the P0 query and the reopened-bead section

**The query at `:455-459`** must stop returning a bead that is merely awaiting re-verification. A
bead with no `planned` is a candidate **unless** it is a failed verification that has not been
handed to the planners:

```bash
bd list --status open --exclude-label planned --exclude-label human \
        --exclude-type epic --json \
  | jq -r '.[] | select((.labels // []) | any(. == "planning" or startswith("planning:")) | not)
              | select((.labels // []) | (index("verification:failed") | not)
                                         or (index("plan:revise") != null))
              | select(.priority==0) | "\(.id)\t\(.title)"'
```

Read as: **a failed verification is a candidate only when it carries `plan:revise`.** A brand-new
P0 that was never planned carries neither label and is unaffected — which is why the test is on
`verification:failed` rather than on `planned`.

The same filter belongs on the ordinary candidate query in *Choosing what to plan*, which has the
same shape and the same blind spot.

**The reopened-bead section (`:494`)** currently states the false inference outright:

> It reached you unplanned because the navigator judged the *plan* wrong, not just the build (a
> build-only failure never leaves `planned`, and never reaches you at all — see
> `agents/verifier.md`).

The parenthetical is exactly what `ah-t2pn.3` disproved. Rewrite it to key on `plan:revise`, and
**keep the sentence's job**: it is telling a planner why this bead is different from new work.

Add one short paragraph: **a `verification:failed` bead without `plan:revise` is not yours.** It is
waiting for Psylocke's second look, and the right action is to leave it alone — naming `ah-t2pn.3`
as the case that produced the rule, in the way this skill already names beads for its other hard-won
rules.

**Remove `plan:revise` when the amended plan is marked `planned` again**, in the same `bd update`.
The section already ends *"Then re-add `planned` as usual"*; that line becomes:

```bash
bd update <id> --add-label planned --remove-label plan:revise --remove-label planning:<your-name>
```

Leaving it on would make the bead a permanent planner candidate.

### 4. `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:323` — the hand-back stops misrouting

Today the recipe is unconditional:

```bash
bd update <id> --remove-label planned --add-label human --append-notes "<the section that is missing>"
```

**A bead already carrying `verification:failed` must not gain `human`.** `verification:failed` is
what builds Psylocke's list; `human` is what parks it in the navigator's. On `ah-t2pn.3` the bead
needed her, not them, and was moved by hand.

Split the recipe in two, with the reason stated:

- **An ordinary bead** — a missing plan section, an unanswerable question — keeps today's line
  exactly.
- **A bead carrying `verification:failed`, handed back because there is nothing to implement** —
  `--remove-label planned` and the notes, and **no `human`**. It goes back to Psylocke, which is
  where a failed verification with nothing left to build belongs.

The implementer must also **not** add `plan:revise`: whether the plan was wrong is the navigator's
answer to Psylocke's question, not an implementer's to assert.

### 5. `skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md:96`

Carries the same recipe and needs the same split, or a pointer to `implement-bead`'s. **Whichever
is chosen, the two must not disagree** — two copies of a recipe that differ is how this bead's own
defect arrived.

### Nothing to migrate

The beads open today are already in the right state under the new scheme, and this is worth checking
rather than assuming:

- `ah-fjty` — `planned`, `verification:failed`: build wrong, implementers. Correct, untouched.
- `ah-t2pn.3` — `verification:failed`, no `planned`, no `plan:revise`: awaiting re-verification.
  Correct under the new rule, and **no longer a planner candidate**, which is the bug being fixed.

**Do not add `plan:revise` to any existing bead.** No open bead was judged plan-wrong.

## Increments

Documentation, so there is no red-green loop and none should be invented — a test asserting the bytes
of a paragraph pins prose a person should be free to improve. The work is ordered instead, and
**each step is checked by re-reading the changed file as the role it addresses**.

1. **The verifier sets it.** `agents/verifier.md`'s *Plan wrong* branch and its prose. Read the
   section back as Psylocke: is it unambiguous which branch adds `plan:revise`, and that the build-
   wrong branch never does?

2. **The planner reads it.** `agents/planner.md:133` and `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`'s reopened-bead
   section. Read them back as a planner meeting a reopened bead for the first time: can they tell,
   from labels alone, whether it is theirs?

3. **The query stops returning it.** The two queries in `skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`. **Run both
   against the live backlog** — this is the one step with a checkable answer:
   - `ah-t2pn.3` (P0, `verification:failed`, no `plan:revise`) **must not** appear;
   - a bead given `plan:revise` by hand **must** appear;
   - `ah-fjty` (`planned`) must not appear, as today.
   Undo any label used for that check.

4. **The hand-back stops misrouting.** `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:323` and
   `skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md:96`. Read back as an implementer that has just found nothing to
   build: is it obvious which of the two lines applies?

5. **Bump the consumer.** A `chore: bump cerebro` commit in `atlantis-hud` moving the submodule
   pointer, once the cerebro PR is merged.

## The test plan

**None, and that is the honest answer for a change to documentation and a label convention.** There
is no suite in either repository that would fail if this were wrong.

What replaces it is increment 3, which is genuinely checkable: the corrected queries are run against
the live backlog and must return the right beads. Everything else is the four readings named in
*Increments*, each done as the role the file addresses.

**What must still pass, unchanged:** `pnpm run check:fast` in the consumer, which nothing here
touches. If it moves, something outside this bead's scope was edited.

**Say in the PR that there is no automated coverage**, rather than implying any.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23 against `docs/ui/ah-tjaz-labels.html`. **The audience
here is the navigator and the agents themselves** — these labels decide which role picks work up, and
one of them decides when the navigator is interrupted — so all three are theirs.

**How the state is carried.**
**Chosen: A — say it positively.** Psylocke adds a label on the *plan wrong* branch, and the planner
looks for that rather than for an absence. Removing `planned` then means only "not ready for an
implementer", and every future reason to remove it becomes harmless.
*Rejected — B, label the third state* (`verification:ready` on the hand-back, planners skip it): a
smaller change that fixes today's case exactly, and leaves the next new reason to drop `planned` to
collide again.
*Rejected — C, no new label, change the rule* (planners must read the notes): nothing to build, and
it puts a judgement call in the path of every reopened P0 for ever.

**The name.**
**Chosen: `plan:revise`.** Matches `verification:failed`'s shape — namespace, colon, verb — and says
what the planner should do rather than what went wrong.
*Rejected — `verification:replan`*: keeps the whole reopen story in one namespace so every label a
failed verification can produce sorts together. *Rejected — `needs-replan`*: matches the older flat
style (`needs-ui-decision`, `human`) rather than the newer namespaced one.

**Where a handed-back failed verification goes.**
**Chosen: 1 — no `human` when the bead already carries `verification:failed`.** It returns to
Psylocke, whose list that label already builds, and the navigator stops being asked about something
nobody needs them to decide.
*Rejected — 2, keep `human` always*: the safe default and how it works today, at the cost of a queue
carrying items that would route themselves.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** only Psylocke ever
sets `plan:revise`, because whether the plan was wrong is the navigator's answer to her question and
not an implementer's to assert; the planner removes it in the same `bd update` that re-adds
`planned`, or the bead becomes a permanent candidate; and no existing bead is migrated, because none
was judged plan-wrong.

## Out of scope

- **Why an implementer keeps re-claiming a bead with nothing to build.** Storm stopped the loop by
  removing `planned`, which is what created the ambiguity. A better answer might be that a
  `verification:failed` bead without `planned` is simply never in `bd ready` — that is a change to
  what implementers pick up and is its own bead.
- **`ah-kjfm`** — the stale-assignee sweep. A neighbouring symptom of the same reopen path, already
  planned, and nothing here changes it.
- **Any change to Psylocke's verdict question.** Asking the navigator *plan or build* is right and
  stays exactly as it is; this bead only changes how the answer is recorded.
- **Retro-labelling closed beads.**
- **Anything in `atlantis-hud`** except the one `chore: bump cerebro` commit.

## Validation

In the `cerebro` repository, and then from the consumer:

```bash
# increment 3, the one checkable step - run from the consumer, against the live backlog
bd list --status open --exclude-label planned --exclude-label human --exclude-type epic --json \
  | jq -r '.[] | select((.labels // []) | any(. == "planning" or startswith("planning:")) | not)
              | select((.labels // []) | (index("verification:failed") | not)
                                         or (index("plan:revise") != null))
              | select(.priority==0) | "\(.id)\t\(.title)"'
```

`ah-t2pn.3` must **not** be listed while it lacks `plan:revise`, and must appear if the label is
added by hand. Remove any label added for that check.

```
pnpm run check:fast          # in the consumer; untouched by this bead
```

**Checkable only by a person, and the point of the bead:** read `agents/planner.md` and
`skills/plan-bead`'s reopened-bead section as a planner who has never seen `ah-t2pn.3`, and confirm
they can tell from labels alone whether a reopened bead is theirs. If they still have to read the
notes to find out, the change has not worked.

## Known traps

- **`planned` comes off for more than one reason, and always will.** That is the whole defect. Any
  rule that infers intent from its absence will fail again the next time somebody has a good reason
  to remove it — which is why the chosen design puts the meaning in a label somebody sets on purpose.
- **Only Psylocke sets `plan:revise`.** An implementer that adds it is asserting the navigator's
  answer to a question the navigator was never asked.
- **Remove it when the plan is re-marked `planned`.** Otherwise the bead is a planner candidate for
  ever, which is the same class of bug pointing the other way.
- **Two copies of the hand-back recipe** exist, at `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:323` and
  `skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md:96`. They must not disagree — two copies of a recipe drifting apart
  is how this defect arrived.
- **These files are symlinks in the consumer.** Editing `.claude/agents/planner.md` from an
  `atlantis-hud` worktree writes into the submodule's working tree; unless it is committed in
  `rmstdope/cerebro` and the pointer bumped, it is lost on the next `git submodule update`.
- **`--exclude-label` matches one exact string** and cannot express "either of these", which is why
  the query change is in `jq` — the same reason `plan-bead` already filters `planning` there.
acceptance_criteria: A bead that is waiting for a second look is distinguishable from one whose plan was judged wrong, without reading its notes. A planner's P0 check does not return the former; Psylocke's list does. The three roles' docs agree on which labels mean what, and the hand-back recipe in agents/implement-bead sets whichever is correct for 'nothing to implement, re-verify'.

title: A unit that taxes by its flag earns nothing in the forecast
description:
Found during verification of the silver family (2026-08-23, at dd3f67bd).

A unit's taxing flag (the AUTOTAX order) makes it tax every turn without an explicit TAX order in that turn's orders. The forecast only prices the explicit Intent::Tax, so a unit that carries the flag and issues no TAX is shown earning nothing, and its month-end silver is understated by the whole tax take.

This is the same defect ah-abwx fixed for PILLAGE - an order that earns, priced by one surface and not the other - except here the trigger is a persistent unit flag rather than a line in this month's orders.

What the flag should count for, everywhere the TAX order already counts:

  - income in the silver column, capped by the region's tax base exactly as Intent::Tax is (crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:463)
  - the ledger's own credit (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs)
  - the taxed-a-pillaged-hex conflict just landed by ah-cxxa: a flagged taxer in a hex one of your units is pillaging gets nothing, same as an explicit taxer does

Both surfaces must price it the same way, per ah-ycuj's corpus-wide agreement test.

Open questions for planning: where the flag is read from the parsed report (the unit line's flag list), whether a unit carrying the flag AND an explicit TAX should be counted once rather than twice, and whether the prospective follow-ups about who may tax at all - ah-1ad6 (enough combat-ready men) and ah-g7ts (a guarding foreign unit blocks it) - apply to the flagged case identically. They almost certainly do.
design:
## Context

The `AUTOTAX` order sets a unit's **taxing** flag, and it then taxes every turn without a `TAX`
line in that turn's orders. Every surface here prices only the explicit `Intent::Tax`, so a flagged
unit is shown earning **nothing** and its month-end silver is understated by the whole tax take.

Found during verification of the silver family on 2026-08-23, at `dd3f67bd`. It is the same defect
`ah-abwx` fixed for `PILLAGE` - an order that earns, priced by one surface and not the other -
except the trigger is a persistent unit flag rather than a line in this month's orders.

**The corpus has one such unit of ours, and it is not small:**

```
* City Guards (13303), on guard, The Disinherited Knights (42), revealing faction, holding,
  taxing, sharing, 800 orcs [ORC], 2 catapults [CATP], 2049 swords [SWOR], ...
```

(`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep`.) Eight hundred men taxing is **$40,000**
before the region's cap; the column shows **0**.

**The same unit carries a second, false mark.** It has no orders at all, so `check_idle_units`
(`semantics.rs:3268`) gives it `has no order that spends the month` - which is wrong, it spends the
month taxing, and there is no order the player could add to satisfy the advice. The navigator chose
on 2026-08-23 to fix both here: they are one unit on one screen.

**Everything about how a tax is priced is already settled and must be reused, not re-derived.** The
`Intent::Tax` arm (`silver.rs:623`) already carries `ah-cxxa`'s pillage branch and `ah-t2pn`'s
`PoolShare` split. A flagged taxer joins that identical path.

When this lands: a unit that taxes by flag earns what it will earn, on both surfaces, and is not
told it is idle.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` - one predicate, and tax leaves the intent loop

```rust
/// The flags the game prints for a unit that taxes every turn without an order.
///
/// Two spellings, both already in the report parser's `KNOWN_FLAGS`
/// (`crates/core/src/report/unit.rs:19-38`): reports print `taxing`, and `autotax` is the order's
/// own name. Match both, because the parser accepts both.
const TAXING_FLAGS: [&str; 2] = ["taxing", "autotax"];

/// Whether this unit will tax this month - by an explicit `TAX` order, or because it carries the
/// taxing flag, which taxes every turn without one (`ah-fvzu`).
///
/// **A predicate, not a count.** A unit carrying the flag *and* given a `TAX` this turn still
/// taxes once, and this returns `true` for it exactly as for either alone.
#[must_use]
pub fn taxes(flags: &[String], intents: &[PlacedIntent]) -> bool {
    intents.iter().any(|placed| matches!(placed.intent, Intent::Tax))
        || flags.iter().any(|flag| {
            TAXING_FLAGS.iter().any(|known| flag.eq_ignore_ascii_case(known))
        })
}
```

Write it beside `is_consuming` (`silver.rs:1576`), whose case-insensitive flag test is the pattern.

**`Intent::Tax` stops being an arm of the intent loop and becomes a unit-level term.** That is the
whole of the design and it is not optional: leaving the arm in place and adding a second path for
the flagged case gives two computations of one number, which is exactly how the column and the
warning drifted apart before (`ah-abwx`, and `ah-ycuj` exists to catch it).

In `forecast_unit`:

- **Before** the `for placed in facts.intents` loop (`silver.rs:495`), run the tax term:
  `if taxes(facts.flags, facts.intents) { …the existing arm's body, verbatim… }` - the `pillaged`
  branch, the `shares.tax` match, the cap, and both doubts, moved and not rewritten.
- In the loop, `Intent::Tax => {}` with a comment saying the term is computed once above and why.

**Placing it before the loop changes doubt precedence, deliberately.** `income_doubt.or(...)` keeps
the first `Some`, so today a unit with an unpriceable `TAX` and an unpriceable `SELL` shows
whichever sentence its *earlier order line* produced. After this change the tax doubt always wins.
That is an improvement rather than a regression - the same unit no longer shows a different
sentence depending on which line the player happened to type first - and it needs a test saying so,
because it is a behaviour change nobody asked for and a later reader will wonder.

One new field on `UnitSilver` (`silver.rs:107`), beside the other explanatory flags:

```rust
/// Whether this unit's tax income comes from its taxing flag rather than from a `TAX` order in
/// this month's orders. Drives the hover's note and nothing else: the income is the same either
/// way (`ah-fvzu`).
pub taxes_by_flag: bool,
```

`true` when `taxes(...)` holds **and** no `Intent::Tax` is present - the flag is what is
noteworthy, and a unit with both has an order on screen that explains itself. Initialise it in both
constructors, as `ah-eacd` and `ah-1ad6.2` had to.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` - five sites, all the same predicate

Every one of these currently asks "does this unit have `Intent::Tax`", and every one must ask "does
this unit tax". **All five, or the change is worse than not making it** - a flagged unit counted in
one place and not another produces exactly the disagreements this family keeps fixing.

1. **The tax pool split** (`semantics.rs:529`) - the `taxers` list feeding `tax_shares_for`. A
   flagged taxer contends for the region's tax base like any other, so leaving it out makes every
   *other* taxer's share too large (`ah-t2pn.1`).
2. **`spends_the_month`** (`semantics.rs:817`) - see below; this one cannot use the predicate as
   written, because it takes an `&Intent`.
3. **The pillaged-hex mark** (`semantics.rs:1361`) - `TAXED_A_PILLAGED_HEX`. See below; a flagged
   unit has no line to mark.
4. **`apply`'s credit** (`semantics.rs:1440`) - the ledger's own tax income. It runs per intent, so
   a flagged unit with no `TAX` is never reached. Credit it in `ledger_for` (line ~799) alongside
   the intent loop, once per unit, guarded by `taxes(...)` - and **remove the credit from the
   `Intent::Tax` arm** so a unit with both is not credited twice. Same reasoning as the forecast.
5. **`check_trade_regions`** (`semantics.rs:3826`, the `taxing` set at line 3861) - the count of
   regions this faction taxes or produces in, against its Martial allowance
   (`too-many-trade-regions`). A flagged unit taxes its region, so the region counts. Missing this
   under-counts the faction's regions and silences a real warning.

**`spends_the_month` (site 2) takes an `&Intent` and a flagged unit has no intent at all**, so the
exemption belongs in its caller. In `check_idle_units` (line 3268), beside the two exemptions it
already has and in their style:

```rust
// A unit set to tax every turn spends its month doing so, with no order in this turn's orders
// to say it - and no order the player could add would satisfy this advice, since a `TAX` would
// be redundant (`ah-fvzu`). The same reasoning `ah-udff` used for a unit with no men.
if taxes(&ordered.unit.flags, ordered.intents) {
    continue;
}
```

Placed **after** the `unread` and `men == 0` guards and **before** the `spends_the_month` scan, so
the cheapest tests still come first.

**The pillaged-hex mark (site 3) has no line to hang on.** Today it emits one finding per `TAX`
line, via `ordered.finding(..., Some(placed))`. A flagged unit has no such line, so use
`finding_at_block` (`semantics.rs:1042`), which exists for exactly this - *"a finding against the
unit's block rather than against one order in it, for a check whose subject is the absence of an
order. No columns: there is no token to underline."* Keep the existing per-line finding for units
that do have a `TAX`; add the block-level one only for a flagged unit without one. The message is
unchanged in both cases:

```
a unit is pillaging this hex, so this TAX will collect nothing
```

### `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts` - one sentence

One new branch, placed **immediately before** the `received` branch (`unitTooltip.ts:307`,
`Includes N given by …`). Both explain where money in the figure came from, and a gift is the more
specific of the two:

```ts
if (silver.taxesByFlag) {
  return "This unit is set to tax every turn, so it taxes without an order.";
}
```

Quoted exactly as agreed. It takes no number: the income is already in the figure.

## Increments

1. **The predicate.** Add `TAXING_FLAGS` and `taxes`. Opening test in `silver.rs`:
   `a_unit_with_a_tax_order_taxes`; `a_unit_with_the_taxing_flag_taxes`;
   `a_unit_with_the_autotax_spelling_taxes`; `a_unit_with_both_taxes_once` (the predicate is
   `true`, asserted alongside the income test in increment 2); `a_unit_with_neither_does_not`.
   Nothing else changes yet.

2. **Tax leaves the intent loop.** Move the arm to a unit-level term guarded by `taxes(...)`.
   Opening test: `a_flagged_unit_earns_its_tax_without_an_order` - 800 men, flag, no orders, tax
   base 40000 → `income == Some(40000)`.
   Then `a_flagged_unit_with_a_tax_order_is_not_counted_twice` - the same unit *with* `TAX` →
   the same `Some(40000)`. **This is the test that catches the obvious wrong implementation.**
   Then `a_flagged_unit_is_capped_by_the_tax_base`, `a_flagged_unit_in_a_pillaged_hex_earns_nothing`
   and `a_flagged_unit_contends_for_the_pool_like_any_other` - each asserting the moved body still
   behaves, since it was moved and not rewritten.
   Then `a_taxing_doubt_no_longer_depends_on_which_line_came_first` - a unit with an unpriceable
   `TAX` and an unpriceable `SELL`, in both orders, showing the same doubt.

3. **`taxes_by_flag` and the hover.** The field, then
   `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts`: `says_when_a_unit_taxes_by_its_flag`, and
   `a_unit_with_a_tax_order_says_nothing_extra` - `taxesByFlag` false when an explicit `TAX` is
   present, even with the flag set.

4. **The ledger.** Credit in `ledger_for`, remove it from the `Intent::Tax` arm.
   `the_ledger_credits_a_flagged_taxer`; `the_ledger_does_not_credit_a_flagged_taxer_twice`.
   Then run `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` (`ah-ycuj`) - it must stay green,
   and it is the guard over exactly this pair of surfaces.

5. **The pool split.** `semantics.rs:529`.
   `a_flagged_taxer_contends_for_the_tax_base` - one explicit taxer and one flagged, one hex: each
   gets its share, not the whole base.

6. **The idle mark.** `a_flagged_unit_is_not_told_it_does_nothing`, and
   `a_unit_without_the_flag_still_is`.

7. **The pillaged-hex mark.** `a_flagged_taxer_in_a_pillaged_hex_is_marked_on_its_block` - the
   finding exists, carries the same message, and has **no** line or columns.
   `a_unit_with_a_tax_order_is_still_marked_on_its_line`.

8. **The trade-regions count.** `a_flagged_taxer_counts_toward_the_taxed_regions`.

9. **The corpus.** `validate_real_orders.rs`'s `EXPECTED` table (line ~62) is over turn 71; the one
   flagged own unit is in turn **82**, a different fixture, so the table should not move. Run it. If
   it does move, read the finding before touching the table.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the five `taxes` predicate tests | `silver.rs` | both flag spellings, both triggers, and neither |
| `a_flagged_unit_earns_its_tax_without_an_order` | `silver.rs` | the reported defect |
| `a_flagged_unit_with_a_tax_order_is_not_counted_twice` | `silver.rs` | the obvious wrong implementation |
| the three moved-body tests | `silver.rs` | the cap, the pillage branch and the pool share survive the move |
| `a_taxing_doubt_no_longer_depends_on_which_line_came_first` | `silver.rs` | the deliberate precedence change |
| `says_when_a_unit_taxes_by_its_flag` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | the sentence |
| `a_unit_with_a_tax_order_says_nothing_extra` | `unitTooltip.test.ts` | `taxesByFlag` is about the flag alone |
| the two ledger tests | `semantics.rs` | the second surface, and no double credit |
| `a_flagged_taxer_contends_for_the_tax_base` | `semantics.rs` | the pool split |
| the two idle tests | `semantics.rs` | the false mark, and no over-exemption |
| the two pillaged-hex tests | `semantics.rs` | a block finding where there is no line |
| `a_flagged_taxer_counts_toward_the_taxed_regions` | `semantics.rs` | the Martial allowance |
| `silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` | `tests/` | corpus-wide agreement |

Suites: `cargo test -p atlantis-core`, `pnpm run check:generated`, `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23. Mockup: `docs/ui/ah-fvzu-autotax.html`.

**Where the money appears to come from.** Every other income in the column is answered by a line in
the orders; this one is answered by a flag set in some earlier turn and invisible in this turn's.
Chosen: **say it**, verbatim:
> `This unit is set to tax every turn, so it taxes without an order.`

Rejected: *saying nothing* - consistent with every other unit and cheapest, and it leaves a player
who did not set the flag themselves, or set it twenty turns ago, with $40,000 appearing from
nowhere and no way to find out why from this screen.

**Is a flagged unit "doing nothing"?** It carries `has no order that spends the month` today, which
is false, and no order the player could add would satisfy it.
Chosen: **exempt it, in this bead.** The two defects are the same unit on the same screen, and the
fix is one condition beside the two `check_idle_units` already has.
Rejected: *filing it separately*, which would keep this bead to the silver column as its title says
and leave a false mark on the affected unit until a second bead was planned and built.

**The flag and an explicit `TAX` together.** A unit may carry both and still taxes once.
Chosen: **count once, silently.** The income is the same either way and the redundant order is
harmless.
Rejected: *marking the redundant `TAX`* ("this unit already taxes every turn"), which would catch a
player who does not realise the flag is set, at the cost of a new advisory code, its own toggle and
its own row in the expectations table.

**Decided here, not asked**, because each follows from the above: the note sits immediately before
the `Includes N given by …` branch, since both explain where money in the figure came from and a
gift is the more specific; `taxes_by_flag` is `false` for a unit that also has an explicit `TAX`,
because that unit has an order on screen that explains itself; and the pillaged-hex mark on a
flagged unit hangs on its block rather than a line, because there is no line.

## Out of scope

- **Whether a flagged unit may tax at all.** `ah-1ad6` (enough combat ready men) and `ah-g7ts` (a
  guarding foreign unit blocks it) both narrow who may tax. They will apply to the flagged case
  identically **because this bead routes it through the same code**, which is the point of the
  single predicate - but neither is implemented here and neither is waited for.
- **Marking a redundant `TAX` on a flagged unit.** Settled above.
- **`AUTOTAX` as an order in this turn's orders**, setting or clearing the flag. The flag this bead
  reads is the one the *report* prints, which is the state at the start of the month; an `AUTOTAX`
  issued this turn changes next month's report and not this month's income.
- **Foreign units' taxing flags.** `Hex::read` filters foreign units out before any of this, and
  nothing here forecasts them.
- **Showing the flag in the unit table.** The hover carries it; the table is not touched.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, no `#[ignore]`. `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` in particular.

Then, by eye, loading `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` with its committed orders template:

- **City Guards (13303)** shows a large tax income where it showed 0, capped by its region's base.
- its hover reads `This unit is set to tax every turn, so it taxes without an order.`
- it no longer carries `has no order that spends the month`.
- every other unit in that turn is unchanged.

**A human must confirm the last of those.** Lifting tax out of the intent loop touches the income of
every taxing unit in the game, and no assertion over hand-built fixtures proves that a real turn's
other twenty-six units did not move.

## Known traps

- **All five `Intent::Tax` sites, or none.** `semantics.rs` lines 529, 1361, 1440 and 3861, plus
  `check_idle_units` at 3268. A flagged unit counted in one place and not another is the
  disagreement this whole family of beads keeps fixing. Grep `Intent::Tax` before opening the PR
  and account for every hit.
- **Do not leave the `Intent::Tax` arm in place and add a second path for the flag.** Two
  computations of one number is how the column and the warning drifted apart (`ah-abwx`), and
  `ah-ycuj`'s corpus test is what will catch it - after the interview, the build and the review.
- **A unit with both the flag and a `TAX` must be credited once.** The predicate makes this easy to
  get right and the "obvious" implementation - keep the arm, add a flag branch - gets it wrong by
  doubling. There is a test named for it.
- **`spends_the_month` takes an `&Intent`**, and a flagged unit has no intent. The exemption cannot
  go there; it goes in `check_idle_units`.
- **The pillaged-hex check has no line to mark** on a flagged unit. `finding_at_block`
  (`semantics.rs:1042`) exists for this; do not invent a `PlacedIntent`.
- **Doubt precedence changes** for a unit with an unpriceable `TAX` and another unpriceable order.
  That is deliberate and tested; do not "restore" it by moving the term back inside the loop.
- **Both flag spellings.** `taxing` and `autotax` are both in `KNOWN_FLAGS`
  (`report/unit.rs:19-38`). Matching only one silently halves the fix.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`: no effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** The hover work is pure
  and belongs in `unitTooltip.test.ts`.

title: Taxing a hex another faction guards is forecast as if nothing could stop it
description:
Found during verification of ah-abwx (2026-08-23, at 54dd0824).

The rules: "Units which have the Guard flag set (using the GUARD order) will block TAX orders issued by other factions in the same region, unless you have declared the faction in question Friendly."

Observed: fixture neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep, mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra. The hex contains

  - City Guard (14), on guard, The Guardsmen (1), 120 leaders, 120 swords

a foreign unit of faction 1, on guard. Our unit The Lost One (683) ordering PILLAGE (or TAX) there is liable to be blocked outright and earn nothing, yet the forecast credits the full amount with no hint of it.

The point is that we cannot know the outcome from the report: the blocking rule turns on our declared attitude to the guarding faction, and a report does not always state it. So the honest answer is almost certainly a doubt, not a number - the same shape as SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase (crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:167), which already exists for 'the report does not say enough to price this'. A flat credit asserts something we have not established; a flat zero would assert the opposite just as wrongly.

Applies to both TAX and PILLAGE, and to both surfaces - crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs (the ledger, Intent::Tax / Intent::Pillage) and crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs (the forecast arms, ~463 and ~472) - which must agree, per ah-ycuj's corpus-wide agreement test.

Open questions for planning: where a faction's attitude to another is read from (the report's declared attitudes block, if present, and what to do when it is absent or Unfriendly/Neutral), and whether guard detection needs anything the parsed model does not already carry - the 'on guard' flag on a foreign unit in the same hex.
design:
## Context

The rules: *"Units which have the Guard flag set (using the GUARD order) will block TAX orders
issued by other factions in the same region, unless you have declared the faction in question
Friendly."*

Found during Psylocke's verification of `ah-abwx` (2026-08-23, at `54dd0824`). In
`neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep`, mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra holds a foreign **City Guard (14)**
of The Guardsmen (1), on guard, 120 leaders. Our unit The Lost One (683) ordering `TAX` or `PILLAGE`
there is credited in full, with nothing on screen about the guard.

**The navigator settled the rule's ambiguity on 2026-08-23, and it decides the whole design.** The
sentence's *"you"* is **the guarding faction, not us**: the guard blocks unless *its owner* has
declared *us* Friendly. Their declaration toward us is **not in our report and never will be** — our
`Declared Attitudes` block states our attitudes toward them, which is the other direction.

Two consequences, and both are why this bead is small:

- **`DeclaredAttitudes` is not read at all.** The bead's open question — *"where a faction's attitude
  to another is read from"* — has the answer **nowhere**. `header.attitudes`
  (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:61`) is the wrong direction and must not be consulted; a plan
  that reaches for it has adopted the rejected reading. Nor does it matter whether the guard conceals
  its faction (`ReportUnit.faction_id: Option<String>`): unknowable is unknowable either way.
- **Neither surface's arithmetic changes.** The navigator chose a finding alone: the column keeps its
  optimistic figure and a warning carries the uncertainty — the shape `ah-bumi` and `ah-wur4` settled
  for the faction purse. So `forecast_unit` and the ledger are untouched, and **`ah-ycuj`'s
  corpus agreement test cannot move**, because nothing either surface computes is different.

The data the check does need is already parsed: `ReportUnit.on_guard`
(`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:133`) and `ReportUnit.own` (`:132`), and `Hex` carries
`region: &'a ReportRegion` (`semantics.rs:797-800`), whose `units` include foreign ones — the same
route `check_claims` uses when it filters on `own`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**`ah-cxxa` shipped this exact shape a few hours ago and is the model in every respect** — a hex
predicate, a per-order finding, a code, a Settings row in the **Orders** group. Read
`check_pillaged_tax` (`semantics.rs:1241-1264`) before writing anything; this is its sibling.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the predicate

Beside `own_unit_pillages` (`semantics.rs:1030`):

```rust
/// Whether any *foreign* unit in this hex is on guard.
///
/// A guard blocks another faction's `TAX` unless the guarding faction has declared that faction
/// Friendly - **its** declaration, not ours, which our report does not carry and never will
/// (`ah-g7ts`). So this is deliberately a bare "is anyone guarding", with no reference to
/// `header.attitudes`: that block states our attitudes toward them, which is the other direction
/// and would answer a question nobody asked.
///
/// Foreign units are read from `hex.region.units` rather than `hex.units`, which `Hex::read` has
/// already filtered down to our own.
fn foreign_unit_guards(hex: &Hex<'_>) -> bool {
    hex.region.units.iter().any(|unit| !unit.own && unit.on_guard)
}
```

Computed **once per hex** in `review_turn`'s per-hex block and passed to the check, exactly as
`own_unit_pillages(hex)` is at `semantics.rs:322`. Do not call it inside a per-unit or per-intent
loop.

### The code

```rust
pub const TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX: Code = Code("taxed-a-guarded-hex");
```

Appended **last** to `codes::ALL`, whose length literal goes `[Code; 27]` → `[Code; 28]`
(`semantics.rs:117`). The array's own doc comment states that new-here-last rule and why — the
generated TypeScript copies this order.

### The check

Called from `review_turn`'s per-hex block, immediately after `check_pillaged_tax`
(`semantics.rs:322`):

```rust
/// Our units taxing or pillaging a hex a foreign unit is guarding.
///
/// One finding per affected order line, like its sibling `check_pillaged_tax`. It says **may**
/// rather than **will**: whether the guard actually blocks us turns on that faction's declared
/// attitude toward ours, which our report does not state (`ah-g7ts`).
fn check_guarded_tax(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    guarded: bool,
    pillaged: bool,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
);
```

Returns immediately unless `guarded` and `options.emits(codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX)`. Then, for each
own unit and each placed intent:

- `Intent::Tax` → **skip when `pillaged`.** See *the two-warning rule* below.
- `Intent::Pillage` → always emitted while `guarded`.
- anything else → skipped.

Built with `ordered.finding(hex, code, message, Some(placed))`, the same call
`check_pillaged_tax` makes, so the finding lands on that order's own line.

### The two-warning rule — decided, and load-bearing

A hex can be both pillaged by one of our own units (`ah-cxxa`) and guarded by a foreigner. On a
**`TAX` line** `ah-cxxa`'s finding already says the money is gone — *"will collect nothing"*, which
is certain — so adding *"may collect nothing"* beside it is a weaker restatement of a stronger fact.
**Suppress this bead's finding on a `TAX` line whenever `own_unit_pillages(hex)`**, which is why
`check_guarded_tax` takes `pillaged`.

On a **`PILLAGE` line** both still fire, and correctly: our own pillage does not stop our own
pillager, but the guard may. `ah-cxxa` emits nothing on a `PILLAGE` line, so there is no overlap
there in any case.

### The messages — verbatim

| Order | Line |
|---|---|
| `TAX` | `a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing` |
| `PILLAGE` | `a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this PILLAGE may collect nothing` |

**`may`, not `will`** — that single word is the difference between this bead and `ah-cxxa`, and it is
the whole of what the R2 reading buys the player. The guarding faction is **not named**: see
*User-facing decisions*.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

A new entry in the **Orders** group, directly beneath `taxed-a-pillaged-hex` (`:550-554`) — the same
shape exactly, a legal order that may do nothing.

- title: `Taxing a hex someone else guards`
- description: `TAX and PILLAGE orders in a hex where another faction has a unit on guard, which can block them.`

On by default through `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS`' existing "everything except `hex-unguarded`" rule
(`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:43`); `reconcileAdvisoryChecks` (`:51`) gives an existing
user's stored settings the new code at that default. **No migration is needed and none must be
written.**

### Generated TypeScript

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` moves. Regenerate, never hand-edit:

```
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

`UnitSilver` gains no field, so `generated/UnitSilver.ts` does not move.

### Nothing else moves

**No change to `forecast_unit`, to the ledger's `Intent::Tax` or `Intent::Pillage` arms, to
`RegionWages`, or to any `SilverDoubt`.** The figures are deliberately left as they are.

## Increments

1. **The predicate sees a foreign guard, and only a foreign one.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn a_foreign_unit_on_guard_is_seen` — a hex with one own unit and one foreign unit with
   `on_guard` asserts the predicate is true.
   Then `fn our_own_guard_is_not_a_foreign_guard` — a hex where **our** unit is on guard and no
   foreign unit is asserts false. Guarding our own hex must not warn us about our own tax; this is
   the test that catches the missing `!unit.own`.
   Then `fn a_foreign_unit_not_on_guard_is_not_a_guard`.
   GREEN: `foreign_unit_guards`.

2. **Taxing a guarded hex is flagged.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn taxing_a_hex_a_foreigner_guards_is_flagged` — asserts one
   `taxed-a-guarded-hex` finding on the `TAX` line reading
   `a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing`.
   Then `fn an_unguarded_hex_says_nothing`.
   Then a case in the shipped `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` fixture test, which every new
   code must join.
   GREEN: `codes::TAXED_A_GUARDED_HEX`, `codes::ALL` at 28, `check_guarded_tax`, the `TAX` arm.

3. **Pillaging a guarded hex is flagged too.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn pillaging_a_hex_a_foreigner_guards_is_flagged`, asserting the `PILLAGE`
   wording verbatim.
   GREEN: the `Pillage` arm.

4. **One warning, not two, on a tax line.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_pillaged_and_guarded_hex_warns_once_about_tax` — a hex with a foreign
   guard **and** one of our units pillaging: asserts the `TAX` line carries exactly one finding,
   `taxed-a-pillaged-hex`, and **no** `taxed-a-guarded-hex`.
   Then `fn a_pillaged_and_guarded_hex_still_warns_the_pillager` — asserts the `PILLAGE` line does
   carry `taxed-a-guarded-hex`.
   GREEN: the `pillaged` parameter and the `Intent::Tax` skip.

5. **The figures do not move.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_guarded_hex_does_not_change_what_tax_earns` — asserts the taxing
   unit's forecast `income` and the ledger's credit are exactly what they are without the guard.
   GREEN: nothing. This is the regression net under the navigator's decision that the column keeps
   its optimistic figure, and it fails loudly if someone "helpfully" zeroes or doubts it.

6. **Regenerate the TypeScript.** `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
   --test generated_ts`, then `pnpm run check:generated`.

7. **The settings row.**
   RED: `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, asserting the title and description
   verbatim in the **Orders** group.
   GREEN: the entry in `SettingsDialog.tsx`.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core`** — every test named in *Increments*, plus:

- `fn the_attitudes_block_is_not_consulted` — the same guarded hex, run twice: once with the guard's
  faction declared `Friendly` in `header.attitudes` and once with no attitudes block at all;
  asserts **the same finding both times**. This is the test that pins the navigator's reading of the
  rule, and without it the next reader will "fix" the check by consulting attitudes.
- `fn a_hex_with_several_foreign_guards_warns_once_per_order_line` — the finding is per order, not
  per guard.
- `fn a_unit_doing_neither_is_not_warned` — a third unit ordered `MOVE` in the guarded hex gets
  nothing.

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`** — a new code that fires on the committed corpus needs
a row in its `EXPECTED` table. **Expect this to fire widely and budget for it**: City Guards are on
guard by definition, so every city hex the corpus taxes will carry it. Read the diff rather than
suppressing the code — a large number here is the bead working, and `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep`
is the fixture the defect was found in.

**`ah-ycuj`'s corpus agreement test must stay green untouched, and cannot legitimately move.** This
bead changes no figure on either surface. If it goes red, something outside this bead's scope was
edited.

**TypeScript** — `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` only. The traps file's no-jsdom rule is respected: that is
a static render, and no effect-level test is asked for.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `pnpm run check:generated`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23 against `docs/ui/ah-g7ts-guard.html`.

**Whose declaration blocks — the rule's ambiguity, and the decision the bead turns on.**
The rules say a guard blocks *"unless **you** have declared the faction in question Friendly"*, and
the two readings give opposite designs.
**Chosen: R2 — "you" is the guarding faction, not us.** Their attitude toward us is not in our report
and never will be, so whether we are blocked is **unknowable**, always.
*Rejected — R1, "you" is us*: our own `Declared Attitudes` block states exactly our attitudes toward
them, so we could have given an exact answer in the common case — a certain `0` when blocked, like
`ah-cxxa`'s pillaged hex, with a doubt only where the guard conceals its faction or the report
carries no attitudes block. That is a much more informative design, and it was rejected because it is
not what the rule says. **The navigator plays this game; this was their call to make and not the
planner's.**

**What the player sees.**
**Chosen: A — a finding on the order line, and the figure left alone.** The column keeps its
optimistic credit and the warning carries the uncertainty — the shape `ah-bumi` settled and
`ah-wur4` shipped for the faction purse.
*Rejected — B, a doubt only*: no new code and no Settings row, but under R2 it would put `?` on
nearly every city tax order every turn, and a `?` you cannot act on is worse than a number with a
warning beside it.
*Rejected — C, both*: the most informative and the noisiest; under R2 it would mark most taxing
orders in the game.

**Whether `PILLAGE` is covered.** The bead was filed as covering both, by Psylocke; the rule quoted
names only `TAX`.
**Chosen: both, as filed.** A guarded hex is hostile ground either way, and a player pillaging into a
standing guard wants telling; if the engine resolves it as combat rather than a block, the warning is
still pointing at something real.
*Rejected — `TAX` only*: ship exactly what the rule says, on the ground that pillaging a guarded hex
is a different interaction we have not established.
*Rejected — both, with the `PILLAGE` half filed separately.*

**The messages, shipping verbatim:**

> `a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this TAX may collect nothing`
> `a foreign unit is guarding this hex, so this PILLAGE may collect nothing`

*Rejected — naming the faction* (`The Guardsmen (1) is guarding this hex, and may block this TAX`):
lets a player see who it is and whether they might negotiate, but it is longer and needs a fallback
for a guard that conceals its faction.
*Rejected — stating the rule* (`this hex is guarded by another faction; your TAX will be blocked
unless they count you Friendly`): teaches the mechanic rather than just the risk, at the cost of
putting a rules lesson in a warning line.

**The Settings row**, verbatim, in the **Orders** group beside "Taxing a hex you are pillaging":

- title: `Taxing a hex someone else guards`
- description: `TAX and PILLAGE orders in a hex where another faction has a unit on guard, which can block them.`

*Rejected — Resources*: what is at stake is income, but nothing here is short of money — the order
simply may not work. *Rejected — the Guarding group*: it is about our own guards, and this would
widen what that group means.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** our own unit being
on guard is never a reason to warn us; the finding is one per affected order line rather than one per
guard; a hex both pillaged by us and guarded emits only `ah-cxxa`'s stronger warning on a `TAX` line,
but both on a `PILLAGE` line; and the check is on by default through the existing rule, with no
migration.

## Out of scope

- **Reading `header.attitudes`.** Under the chosen reading it answers the wrong direction. This is
  the single most likely wrong turn; there is a test against it.
- **Any change to what `TAX` or `PILLAGE` earns**, on either surface. The figure is deliberately left
  optimistic.
- **Whether a guard triggers combat rather than a block.** Not established, which is exactly why the
  message says *may*.
- **`ah-1ad6`** — PILLAGE credited to a faction with too few combat-ready men, being planned by Beast
  from the same verification. **It also reaches for the `PILLAGE` line**, so a hex could carry both
  findings. They say different things and both may be true, so nothing here suppresses it; **whichever
  of the two is built second should look at the other's shipped behaviour and decide whether the pair
  reads sensibly**, and file a follow-up if not. Do not try to pre-empt it.
- **Friendly-faction detection of any kind**, including a future report format that might carry
  their attitudes toward us. If that ever exists, this bead's `may` becomes a `will` or a silence,
  and that is a new bead.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (inside `check:fast`).

Checkable by looking, once, before opening the PR: load
`neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t1.rep`, order The Lost One (683) to `TAX` in mountain (36,4), and confirm
