the line is marked with the new sentence while the Silver figure is unchanged — that combination is
the whole bead. Then turn the row off in Settings → Orders and confirm the mark disappears.

## Known traps

- **`header.attitudes` is the wrong direction.** It states our attitudes toward other factions; the
  blocking rule turns on theirs toward us. Consulting it produces a check that looks thorough and
  answers a different question. `fn the_attitudes_block_is_not_consulted` exists to stop that.
- **Foreign units are in `hex.region.units`, not `hex.units`.** `Hex::read` filters `hex.units` down
  to our own, so a predicate written against it finds nothing and the check silently never fires.
- **`!unit.own` is load-bearing.** Without it, guarding our own hex warns us about our own tax
  orders — on most turns, for most factions. Increment 1's second test is the net.
- **Expect `validate_real_orders.rs` to move a lot.** City Guards are on guard by definition, so this
  fires on every city hex the corpus taxes. That is the bead working; read the diff and add the
  `EXPECTED` rows rather than narrowing the check.
- **A new code needs four things and the compiler catches only one**: the constant, the `codes::ALL`
  entry **and its length literal** (27 → 28), a case in `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced`, and a
  row in `validate_real_orders.rs`'s `EXPECTED`.
- **Do not zero or doubt the figure.** It is tempting, it is what `ah-cxxa` does, and it is the
  opposite of what was decided here — because there the money is certainly gone and here it may not
  be. Increment 5 fails if it is done.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (`ah-nass`, and the traps file). `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` is a
  static render; do not add an effect-level test.

title: The corpus guard over the hex-level silver warning passes without comparing anything
description:
`ah-e66j` made maintenance sharing automatic, so every hex holding more than one own unit now lends silver between its units at step 4 of the payment order. The lender's row shows nothing of the loan (the navigator's round-2 decision on `ah-e66j`), and in the contended branch - where the hex cannot cover every claimant - neither the lender's nor the borrower's row records anything, by design.

`crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` reconstructs each sharing hex's purse from the Silver column and holds it against the pooled `not-enough-silver` finding. That reconstruction is no longer possible: three attempts during ah-e66j's implementation each agreed with production on most of the corpus and diverged on a hex where step 4 had moved silver invisibly.

So `the_column_and_the_warning_agree_on_every_sharing_hex_in_the_corpus` now skips every hex with more than one own unit, which is every sharing hex in the corpus - the test is dormant. That is exactly the vacuity Copilot caught on #602, reintroduced deliberately and with the navigator's agreement rather than by accident.

Restore it. The likely shape is a signal the test can read - a per-unit `shared_silver_lent`, or a hex-level 'step 4 pooled here' flag - so the guard can subtract what step 4 moved instead of guessing. Whether that field is also shown to the player is a separate, user-facing question.
design:
## Context

`crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` holds the Silver column and the
`not-enough-silver` finding to each other over 26 real turns. Its hex-level half,
`the_column_and_the_warning_agree_on_every_sharing_hex_in_the_corpus` (`:340`), reconstructs each
sharing hex's purse from the column and asserts the pooled finding fires exactly when that purse
cannot cover the claims on it.

`ah-e66j` makes maintenance sharing automatic: every hex with more than one own unit now lends
silver between its units at **step 4** of the payment order, `SHARE` flag or not. The lender's row
shows nothing of the loan (`ah-e66j`'s round-2 decision, taken with the navigator), so the column no
longer reconstructs the purse the way that test does — and rather than ship a wrong assertion, the
test now **skips every hex with more than one own unit**, which is every sharing hex in the corpus.

**The test is dormant.** That is exactly the vacuity Copilot caught on #602, reintroduced knowingly
rather than by accident, and a dormant test is worse than an absent one because it reads as coverage.

**The bead's own guess at the fix is wrong, and following it would add a production field for
nothing.** It suggests *"a per-unit `shared_silver_lent`, or a hex-level 'step 4 pooled here' flag"*.
Neither is needed. The reconstruction can be made **invariant under step 4** instead, using only
fields `ah-e66j` already ships — the argument is under *Files to change*. **No production code
changes in this bead**: `crates/core/tests/` and nothing else.

**Blocked on `ah-e66j`**, which is planned and in flight; the edge is wired. Everything below is
written against `ah-e66j`'s plan, which is committed to its `design` field — read it first
(`bd show ah-e66j --json`, and note the command returns an array).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**`crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs`, and nothing else.**

### Why step 4 breaks the present reconstruction

The test builds each hex's position from two helpers:

- `balance_before_maintenance` (`:218`) — `held + income - late_income - expense`. **Step 4 touches
  none of those four terms**, so this is already invariant under the lending.
- `upkeep_drawn_from_silver` (`:231`) — `max(0, upkeep - late_income)`. `UnitSilver::upkeep` is
  *"already net of every relief"*, and after `ah-e66j` that includes what a faction-mate lent.

So the borrower's claim shrinks while the lender's balance shows no debit, and the hex reads richer
than it is. That asymmetry — not the split by `sharing` flag — is the whole defect.

### The fix: add the loan back, and pool over the whole hex

Two changes to the reconstruction, both inside the test file.

**1. A step-4-aware claim.** A new helper beside the two above:

```rust
/// What maintenance draws off a unit's own silver **before step 4 moves anything**.
///
/// `upkeep_drawn_from_silver` is the figure the column shows, which is net of every relief - and
/// after `ah-e66j` that includes silver a faction-mate in the same hex lent at step 4. Steps 2 and
/// 7 are paid from *outside* the hex (faction food, the unclaimed fund) and must stay subtracted;
/// step 4 is paid from *inside* it, by a unit this very sum is about to count as a lender, so
/// leaving it subtracted would count the same silver twice - once as the lender's spare and once
/// as a claim that no longer exists.
fn upkeep_before_hex_sharing(silver: &UnitSilver) -> i64 {
    let late = silver.late_income.unwrap_or(0);
    (silver.upkeep.unwrap_or(0) + silver.shared_silver_covered - late).max(0)
}
```

`shared_silver_covered` is the field `ah-e66j` adds to `UnitSilver`, placed between
`faction_food_covered` and `own_food_covered`.

**This works in both of `ah-e66j`'s branches, and that is the load-bearing claim of this plan:**

- **The hex covers everybody.** `shared_silver_covered` carries what each fed unit received, so
  adding it back restores the pre-step-4 claim exactly. The reconstructed pool then satisfies
  `pool >= needed` and no maintenance finding is expected — which is what production did.
- **The hex falls short.** `ah-e66j` records nothing in that branch: *"record nothing in the
  returned map — no unit's figure drops."* So `upkeep` is **not** reduced and
  `shared_silver_covered` is `0`, and the claim is already the pre-step-4 one. Adding zero is
  correct. The reconstruction gives `pool < needed`, and the hex-level finding is expected — which
  is again what production did.

The two branches need no distinguishing in the test, and therefore no flag to distinguish them
with. **That is why neither field the bead proposes is required.**

**2. Pool over every non-doubted unit, not over the sharers.** The present body splits the hex by
`case.shares` into a `pool` of sharers' balances and `claims` from non-sharers (`:377-381`). After
`ah-e66j` that split no longer describes maintenance at all: the pool is automatic and every own
unit is in it. Replace it with:

```
pool   = Σ over non-doubted own units of  max(0, balance)
needed = Σ over non-doubted own units of  max(0, upkeep_before_hex_sharing - max(0, balance))
```

and assert `hex.warned == (pool < needed)`.

That is `ah-e66j`'s own step-4 condition (`pool >= needed`), restated from the column — which is
what makes it a guard on the two surfaces agreeing rather than a re-derivation of one of them.

Keep unchanged: the `untrusted` short-circuit (`:368`, `:390`), which still skips a hex holding a
doubted sharer, since production emits no pooled finding there; the `Doubted` handling (`:372-375`);
and the failure message, which already names the fixture, the hex, both figures and every unit in
the purse. Extend the message to print `needed` alongside `pool`, since the two are now separate
sums rather than a subtraction.

**Delete the skip** over hexes with more than one own unit. It is the whole point.

### The floor assertion the acceptance names

A test that compares nothing passes. Add, after the per-hex loop:

```rust
assert!(
    warned_sharing_hexes > 0,
    "no sharing hex in the corpus produced a pooled finding, so this test compared nothing - \
     either the corpus changed or the reconstruction is silently exempting every hex"
);
```

counting hexes where `hex.warned` was true and the hex was actually judged (not `untrusted`). This
is the guard against exactly the failure mode that produced this bead, and it must count **judged**
hexes rather than merely present ones — a floor over hexes that were all skipped is the same
vacuity in a new place.

## Increments

1. **Prove the test is dormant before changing it.**
   RED: add the floor assertion above, alone, and run the test. It **fails** on today's tree, with
   the message naming zero. Do not proceed until it has failed for that reason — a floor that passes
   before the fix is measuring something other than what this bead is about.
   GREEN: nothing yet. The failure is the evidence.

2. **The claim is step-4 aware.**
   RED: `fn upkeep_before_hex_sharing_adds_back_what_a_neighbour_lent` — a hand-built `UnitSilver`
   with `upkeep: Some(20)`, `shared_silver_covered: 40`, `late_income: Some(0)` asserts `60`; and a
   second with `shared_silver_covered: 0` asserts it agrees with `upkeep_drawn_from_silver`.
   Build it with the file's existing `forecast({...})` helper rather than a fresh literal.
   GREEN: the helper.

3. **The pool covers the whole hex, and the skip goes.**
   RED: remove the skip and switch the reconstruction to the two sums above. The corpus test now
   runs over every sharing hex and the floor assertion from increment 1 passes.
   GREEN: the rewritten body.
   **Expect this to fail first on a real hex and read the message before touching either side** — a
   divergence here is either this reconstruction being wrong or `ah-e66j` genuinely disagreeing with
   itself, and the two want opposite responses. If it is the latter, stop and hand the bead back
   rather than loosening the assertion; that is the finding this test exists to produce.

4. **A regression fixture for the branch the corpus may not contain.**
   RED: `fn a_hex_that_cannot_cover_its_own_upkeep_is_warned_once_for_the_hex` — a hand-built
   two-unit hex, one broke unit owing upkeep and one faction-mate too poor to cover it, asserting a
   hex-level finding and no per-unit one. If the corpus contains no short-sharing hex, this is the
   only cover the contended branch gets, and the floor assertion cannot see that gap.
   GREEN: nothing — production is already correct; this is coverage the corpus does not guarantee.

## The test plan

This bead **is** a test, so the plan above is the test plan. Beyond it:

- `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning` is the suite that matters,
  and it must be run **twice**: once at increment 1 to watch the floor fail, once at the end.
- `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` must stay green **untouched**. If it moves, production
  changed, and this bead changes no production code.
- No TypeScript, no generated files, no `codes::ALL`, no `UnitSilver` field. `pnpm run
  check:generated` should have nothing to do; if it complains, something outside this bead's scope
  was edited.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

**None.**

This bead changes one file under `crates/core/tests/` and nothing a player can see — no string, no
figure, no finding, no setting. The one user-facing question in this area was raised by the bead
itself (*"Whether that field is also shown to the player is a separate, user-facing question"*) and
**does not arise**, because no field is added: the reconstruction is made invariant under step 4
instead. `ah-e66j`'s round-2 decision that the lender's row shows nothing therefore stands
untouched and unreopened.

## Out of scope

- **Any production change.** Not a field, not a flag, not a comment in `silver.rs` or
  `semantics.rs`. If the fix appears to need one, the argument in *Files to change* is wrong and the
  bead should come back rather than growing.
- **The `SHARE` pool for *orders*.** `report_shortfalls` pools every tag across a hex's `sharing`
  units, and after `ah-e66j` it does so over `silver_balance`, which carries `upkeep_relieved` and
  `upkeep_lent` — neither of which reaches the column. **That half stays unguarded by this test, and
  saying so is deliberate**: this bead restores the maintenance guard, which is what `ah-e66j` broke.
  A guard over the orders pool would need the lending exposed, which is the field this plan argues
  against adding for the maintenance case. File it if it is wanted.
- **The per-unit half of the file** (`the_column_and_the_warning_agree_on_every_unit_in_the_corpus`
  and its `Exempt` rules). Untouched.
- **Widening the corpus.** Same 26 turns.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Checkable by looking, and the one check that actually proves this bead: run
`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning -- --nocapture` and confirm
the floor assertion's count is **greater than zero**. A passing suite is not evidence here; a
non-zero count is.

## Known traps

- **A dormant test passes.** This bead exists because one did. Increment 1 makes the floor fail
  *first*, deliberately; skipping that step and writing the fix straight through leaves no evidence
  that the guard was ever off.
- **The floor must count hexes that were judged**, not hexes that exist. `untrusted` hexes are
  short-circuited before the assertion and must not count toward it, or the same vacuity returns in
  a new place.
- **Do not add back `faction_food_covered` or `unclaimed_covered`.** The helper's shipped doc
  comment at `:225-227` warns against exactly that, and it is still right: steps 2 and 7 are paid
  from outside the hex. **Only** step 4's `shared_silver_covered` is added back, and only because
  the lender is inside the sum.
- **`shared_silver_covered` is `0` in the contended branch by design**, not by omission
  (`ah-e66j`'s round-2 decision). A reader who assumes it always carries the loan will conclude the
  reconstruction is broken and add the field the bead suggested. It is not, and the two-branch
  argument in *Files to change* is why.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array**, and `ah-e66j`'s plan is worth reading in full before
  starting: this bead is written against a seam that does not exist on `main` yet.
- **If the corpus disagrees, that may be the point.** A real divergence between the two surfaces is
  the finding this file was built to produce. Read the failure message — it names the fixture, the
  hex, both sums and every unit — before assuming the reconstruction is at fault.
acceptance_criteria: the_column_and_the_warning_agree_on_every_sharing_hex_in_the_corpus compares real sharing hexes again (its floor assertion for warned sharing hexes is non-zero and passes), over the same 26-turn corpus, with step 4's lending accounted for rather than assumed away.

title: A warning when your units in one hex are promised more of a region's pool than it holds
description:
Road A, fourth piece: the advisory check.

With the column corrected by the three sibling beads, a unit earns less than its men could collect alone and nothing on screen says why. The navigator chose on 2026-08-23 to have a finding as well as the corrected figure: one code, region-pool-oversubscribed, one finding per contending unit, wording mirroring the shipped claims-exceed-unclaimed.
design:
## Context

`ah-t2pn.1`, `.2` and `.3` correct the Silver column: own units in a hex now split the region's tax
base, wage pool, entertainment demand and market stock between them, in proportion to what each
asked for. With the column corrected, **a unit earns less than its men could collect alone and
nothing on screen says why** — a 50-man taxer showing $2,083 instead of $2,500 looks like a defect
until something explains it.

The navigator chose a finding as well as the corrected figure (2026-08-23): one code,
`region-pool-oversubscribed`, one finding per contending unit on its own order line, wording
mirroring the shipped `claims-exceed-unclaimed`. The planner's recommendation — a hover note only,
now that the column is right — was rejected. Agreed design:
`docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html` and `docs/ui/ah-t2pn4-warning.html`.

**Last of four, and blocked on `ah-t2pn.1`**; that edge is wired. **It also needs `.2` and `.3` in
practice** — the wage, entertainment and market pools it reports are settled there — but no edge is
wired to either, deliberately: this bead is buildable and useful with only `.1` landed, reporting
tax alone, and the other pools' arms drop in as their beads land. **If `.2` or `.3` has not landed
when you pick this up, implement only the pools that exist and say so in the PR.** Do not stub the
others.

**Everything below naming `split_pool`, `PoolShare`, `PoolShares`, `pool_shares_for`,
`pool_wants`, `market_shares_for` or `MarketSide` is a promise from a sibling's plan, not a fact in
the tree.** Read `ah-t2pn.1`'s, `.2`'s and `.3`'s designs before you start
(`bd show ah-t2pn.1 --json`; the command returns an array). Where what landed differs, it is right
and this plan is stale.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

`check_claims` (`semantics.rs`) is the model in every respect except scope: it names **every**
participant with a message stating the total, for the stated reason that none is more at fault than
the others, and anchors each finding on that unit's own order line. Read it before writing anything.
This bead is the same shape at hex scope.

### The settlement must surface what it settled

`pool_shares_for` (`ah-t2pn.2`) and `market_shares_for` (`ah-t2pn.3`) currently compute the totals
they need and throw them away. **Do not recompute them here** — a second derivation of "what did
these units ask for" is exactly the drift this family's own `ah-ycuj` guard exists to catch. Have
each return its overruns alongside its shares:

```rust
/// Which of a region's contended pools an order draws on. `Market` carries the goods and the side,
/// because a hex has one such pool per item per side.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ContendedPool {
    Tax,
    Wages,
    Entertainment,
    Market { tag: String, side: MarketSide },
}

/// One pool that the hex's own units asked more of than it holds.
///
/// Produced by the settlement rather than recomputed, so the sentence a player reads and the shares
/// their column shows can never disagree about what was asked for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PoolOverrun {
    pub pool: ContendedPool,
    /// What the hex's own units asked for between them, before any split.
    pub wanted: i64,
    /// What the pool holds.
    pub available: i64,
    /// Indices into `hex.units` of the units that asked, in `hex.units` order.
    pub claimants: Vec<usize>,
}
```

An overrun is recorded **only when `wanted > available`**. A pool that covers every claim is not
oversubscribed, nothing was divided, and nothing is said.

**A pool the settlement could not judge produces no overrun.** Where `ah-t2pn.1`'s rule 2 gives
`PoolShare::Unknowable` — a contender's headcount is a guess — `wanted` is not a number, so there is
nothing to put in the sentence. The affected units already carry the `ContestedRegionPool` doubt and
its hover line, which is the right thing to show and is `ah-t2pn.1`'s.

### The code — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

```rust
pub const REGION_POOL_OVERSUBSCRIBED: Code = Code("region-pool-oversubscribed");
```

Appended **last** to `codes::ALL`, its length literal bumped. The array's own doc comment states that
rule and why (the generated TypeScript copies the order).

### The check

Called from `review_turn`'s per-hex block, beside `check_markets`:

```rust
/// Own units in one hex promised more of a region's pool than it holds.
///
/// Per hex, because the pools are: a tax base, a wage pool, an entertainment demand and each market
/// line belong to the region, unlike the faction purse `claims-exceed-unclaimed` guards.
///
/// Every claimant is named, on its own order line, each carrying the same total - `ah-wur4`'s
/// reasoning, and its words: none of them is more at fault than the others, and a message stating
/// the total means a unit reading it is not being blamed for the overrun on its own.
fn check_region_pools(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    overruns: &[PoolOverrun],
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
);
```

For each overrun, one finding per index in `claimants`, anchored on **that unit's own order line for
that pool** — the `TAX` line for a tax overrun, the `BUY` line for a market one. The unit may have
several such lines; anchor on the first placement of the relevant intent, which is what
`check_claims` does per placement and what makes the finding clickable.

Build the `Finding` with `Ordered::finding` (`semantics.rs:749`), the per-hex helper the other
per-unit checks use.

### The sentences — verbatim, and which is used when

`claimants.len() >= 2` — the plural form:

| Pool | Line |
|---|---|
| `Tax` | `your units here tax for ${wanted} between them and this region has ${available}` |
| `Wages` | `your units here work for ${wanted} between them and this region pays ${available}` |
| `Entertainment` | `your units here entertain for ${wanted} between them and this region pays ${available}` |
| `Market{Selling}` | `your units here sell {wanted} {goods} between them and this market wants {available}` |
| `Market{Buying}` | `your units here buy {wanted} {goods} between them and this market has {available}` |

`claimants.len() == 1` — the singular form. **Markets only**: `ah-t2pn.1`'s rule 1 leaves a lone
claimant `Uncontended` for tax, wages and entertainment, so those three can never produce a
one-claimant overrun. `ah-t2pn.3` deliberately settles markets for a lone trader too, which is what
caps a unit ordering `BUY 200` where 100 exist — and that is the case these two sentences are for.

| Pool | Line |
|---|---|
| `Market{Selling}` | `this unit sells {wanted} {goods} and this market wants {available}` |
| `Market{Buying}` | `this unit buys {wanted} {goods} and this market has {available}` |

**A one-claimant overrun on a silver pool is unreachable, and must be treated as a bug rather than
formatted.** `debug_assert!` it and emit nothing in release — inventing a singular tax sentence would
hide a real defect in the settlement behind a plausible message.

`{goods}` is the item's catalogue name where the ruleset has one and the tag otherwise, through the
existing `item_name` helper (`semantics.rs`), which every other market message uses. Silver figures
carry a literal `$` as `claims-exceed-unclaimed` does; goods counts do not.

### Settings — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

A new entry in the **Resources** group, beside `claims-exceed-unclaimed` — the same
pool-runs-out shape, one hex-scope and one faction-scope. **Not the Orders group**: every order here
is legal, there is simply not enough to go round.

- title: `Promised more than the region has`
- description: `Your units in one hex ordered to tax, work, entertain or trade for more than the region or its market can supply between them.`

On by default through `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS`' existing "everything except `hex-unguarded`" rule
(`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:43`); `reconcileAdvisoryChecks` (`:51`) gives an existing
user's stored settings the new code at that default. **No migration is needed and none must be
written.**

### Generated TypeScript

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` moves. Regenerate, never hand-edit:

```
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

`UnitSilver` gains no field, so `generated/UnitSilver.ts` does not move.

## Increments

1. **The settlement reports what it settled.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn the_settlement_reports_an_oversubscribed_tax_base` — a 10-man and a 50-man unit taxing a
   $2,500 region assert one `PoolOverrun { pool: Tax, wanted: 3000, available: 2500, claimants: [0, 1] }`.
   Then `fn a_pool_that_covers_everybody_reports_no_overrun`.
   Then `fn an_unjudgeable_pool_reports_no_overrun` — one contender with `men_estimated`; asserts the
   overruns are empty and the units still carry `ContestedRegionPool`.
   GREEN: `ContendedPool`, `PoolOverrun`, and `pool_shares_for` returning them.

2. **Every claimant is told, on its own line.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn every_taxer_is_told_the_region_cannot_pay_them_all` — the same hex
   asserts two `region-pool-oversubscribed` findings, one anchored on each unit's `TAX` line, both
   reading `your units here tax for $3,000 between them and this region has $2,500`.
   Then `fn a_unit_not_drawing_on_the_pool_is_not_told` — a third unit ordered `MOVE` gets nothing.
   Then a case in the shipped `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` fixture test, which every new
   code must join.
   GREEN: `codes::REGION_POOL_OVERSUBSCRIBED`, `codes::ALL` bumped, `check_region_pools`, the tax
   sentence.

3. **Wages and entertainment.** *(Only if `ah-t2pn.2` has landed.)*
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn every_worker_is_told_the_region_cannot_pay_them_all` and
   `fn every_entertainer_is_told_the_region_cannot_pay_them_all`, asserting the two sentences
   verbatim — note **`pays`**, not `has`.
   GREEN: those two arms.

4. **Markets, in goods, plural.** *(Only if `ah-t2pn.3` has landed.)*
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn every_seller_is_told_the_market_will_not_take_it_all` — two units each
   selling 60 horses into a `Wanted` line of 100 assert
   `your units here sell 120 horses between them and this market wants 100`, named in goods and with
   no `$`.
   Then the buying equivalent, asserting `this market has`.
   GREEN: the two market arms and `item_name`.

5. **The lone trader, singular.** *(Only if `ah-t2pn.3` has landed.)*
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_lone_buyer_asking_for_more_than_the_market_has_is_told_so` — one unit
   ordering `BUY 200 HORS` against a line of 100, nobody else trading; asserts exactly one finding
   reading `this unit buys 200 horses and this market has 100` — **not** the plural form.
   Then the selling equivalent.
   Then `fn a_lone_taxer_never_produces_an_overrun` — asserts no finding and, in debug, that no
   one-claimant silver overrun was produced.
   GREEN: the singular arms and the `debug_assert!`.

6. **Regenerate the TypeScript.** `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
   --test generated_ts`, then `pnpm run check:generated`.

7. **The settings row.**
   RED: `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, asserting the title and description
   verbatim in the **Resources** group.
   GREEN: the entry in `SettingsDialog.tsx`.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core`** — every test named in *Increments*, plus:

- `fn two_pools_in_one_hex_produce_two_findings_per_unit` — a unit that both taxes and works in a hex
  where both pools are oversubscribed is told about each, on its own line for each. One code, two
  facts; nothing here deduplicates by unit.
- `fn different_goods_produce_different_findings` — sellers of horses and sellers of swords in one
  hex, only the horses oversubscribed; asserts one sentence naming horses and nothing about swords.
- `fn the_totals_in_the_sentence_match_the_column` — the `wanted` in the message equals the sum of
  what the units' own columns would have shown before the split. This is the guard that the sentence
  and the figures come from one computation, which is the whole reason `PoolOverrun` is returned by
  the settlement instead of recomputed here.

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`** — a new code that fires on the committed corpus needs
a row in its `EXPECTED` table. A city with several taxing or working units is the normal case, so
**expect this to fire and budget for it**; read the diff rather than suppressing the code.

**`ah-ycuj`'s corpus agreement test** must stay green untouched. This bead adds a finding and moves
no figure, so it should not move at all; if it does, something outside this bead's scope changed.

**TypeScript** — `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` only. The traps file's no-jsdom rule is respected: that is
a static render, and no effect-level test is asked for.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `pnpm run check:generated`.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-23, across the family interview
(`docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html`) and this bead's own
(`docs/ui/ah-t2pn4-warning.html`).

**A finding as well as the corrected column.**
**Chosen: yes** — one code, one finding per contending unit, on its own order line.
*Rejected — a hover note only*, which was the planner's recommendation once the column was correct:
it explains the figure where it appears but puts nothing in the Problems panel, which is where a
player goes to fix orders.
*Rejected — neither*, which would leave a taxer earning under $50 a man unexplained.
*Rejected — one finding for the hex*: quiet and it scales, but a hex-scope finding has no line to
point at, so nothing marks the units in the orders being edited.

**One code, not four.**
**Chosen: `region-pool-oversubscribed`**, one Settings row, the message naming which pool.
*Rejected — four codes* (`tax-` / `wages-` / `entertainment-` / `market-oversubscribed`), each
separately silenceable and matching the single-purpose shipped neighbours — but four rows for one
idea is the largest single addition the Resources group has had.

**The five plural sentences, shipping verbatim**, as tabled in *Files to change*. The verb follows
what the report line itself prints: a region **has** a tax base and **pays** wages and entertainment;
a market **wants** what it will buy and **has** what it will sell. Markets are named in goods, not
silver, because that is what the market line states — and because the shipped `not-traded-here`
already speaks about a market in its own terms.
*Rejected — one noun throughout ("has" everywhere)*: fewer variants to keep true, at the cost of
saying a region "has" wages, which it does not.

**The lone trader.** Raised by this bead, because `ah-t2pn.3` settles markets whenever anyone trades
— which is what caps a unit ordering `BUY 200` where 100 exist — so a single unit can oversubscribe
a pool by itself and the plural sentence would say "your units … between them" of one unit.
**Chosen: a second, singular sentence** for buying and selling, as tabled above.
*Rejected — fire only with two or more units*: one sentence per pool, and the code stays about
contention as its name says, but the lone case would then be silently corrected with nothing saying
why.
*Rejected — keep the plural sentence*: no new string, and it reads wrong on the commonest
single-unit mistake there is.

**The Settings row**, verbatim, in the **Resources** group beside "Claiming more than the faction
has":

- title: `Promised more than the region has`
- description: `Your units in one hex ordered to tax, work, entertain or trade for more than the region or its market can supply between them.`

*Rejected — "Sharing a region's pool"* with a description naming the situation rather than the fault:
less alarming for something often deliberate, but it does not say what is wrong.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** an overrun is
recorded only when the pool is genuinely short, so a hex whose pool covers everybody says nothing; a
pool the settlement could not judge produces no finding, because `wanted` is not a number and the
affected units already carry `ah-t2pn.1`'s `ContestedRegionPool` doubt; a unit drawing on two
oversubscribed pools is told about each; and the check is on by default through the existing rule,
with no migration.

## Out of scope

- **The column arithmetic.** `ah-t2pn.1`, `.2` and `.3`. This bead moves no figure and adds no
  `UnitSilver` field — it reports what they settled.
- **`CLAIM` against the faction purse.** `ah-bumi` settled its column and `ah-wur4` shipped
  `claims-exceed-unclaimed`; both stand, and this code is its hex-scope counterpart, not its
  replacement.
- **`PILLAGE` emptying the tax base** — `ah-cxxa`, which has its own `taxed-a-pillaged-hex` finding.
  A pillaged hex yields nothing to any taxer, so there is no pool to oversubscribe and the two
  findings do not both fire.
- **Foreign units.** Permanently out: their orders are unknowable, so they are neither counted into
  `wanted` nor named.
- **Any hover note.** The finding is on the line; a note would repeat it.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (inside `check:fast`).

Checkable by looking, once, before opening the PR: load a fixture with a city hex, order two units of
different sizes to `TAX`, and confirm both `TAX` lines are marked with one sentence naming the same
total — then turn the new row off in Settings → Resources and confirm both marks disappear while the
Silver figures stay split.

## Known traps

- **Do not recompute the totals.** `wanted` and `available` must come from the settlement that
  produced the shares, or the sentence and the column can disagree about the same hex — the exact
  class of defect `ah-ycuj` was built to catch, in a family that has already produced two of them.
- **A new code needs four things, and the compiler catches only one**: the constant, the
  `codes::ALL` entry **and its length literal**, a case in the shipped
  `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` fixture test, and a row in `validate_real_orders.rs`'s
  `EXPECTED` if it fires on the corpus. Only the length literal fails to compile.
- **A one-claimant overrun on tax, wages or entertainment is unreachable.** `debug_assert!` rather
  than inventing a singular sentence: formatting it would hide a real settlement defect behind a
  plausible message.
- **Anchor on the order line, not the unit block.** A finding with no line sorts to the end of the
  hex and cannot be clicked to the order it is about; `check_claims` anchors on the placement and so
  must this.
- **`ah-t2pn.2` and `.3` may not have landed.** Implement the pools that exist, and say so in the
  PR. Do not stub the arms — a sentence for a pool nothing settles is a string nobody can reach and
  a test nobody can write.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (`ah-nass`, and the traps file). `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` is a
  static render; do not add an effect-level test.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array**, and three sibling plans are worth reading before you start.

title: Own units buying or selling the same goods in one hex split what the market will trade
description:
Road A, third piece: markets, which are the one pool the rules are explicit about.

'Oversupply and oversubscription split up in proportion to the number each unit tried to sell / in proportion to the amount each buyer attempted to buy.'

Unlike the other three pools this one is a quantity, not silver: market_takes for a SELL, market_has for a BUY. Two units each selling 60 horses into a market that wants 100 sell 50 each, and the silver follows from that.
design:
## Context

A market's stock is shared, and the rules say what happens when it is oversubscribed: oversupply and
oversubscription *"split up in proportion to the number each unit tried to sell"* / *"in proportion
to the amount each buyer attempted to buy"*. This is the one contended pool the rulebook is explicit
about.

The forecast re-reads the market fresh for every unit. `forecast_hex` (`semantics.rs:354`) builds a
`sale` and a `purchase` closure per unit, each answering from `hex.region.wanted` /
`hex.region.for_sale`, so two units each selling 60 horses into a market that wants 100 are both
shown the silver for 60.

**A second defect lives in the same arm.** The `Buy` arm (`silver.rs:617`) charges
`count * price` for an `Amount::Exact` and **never consults `market_has`** — only `BUY ALL` does
(`silver.rs:~660`, the `Deferred::BuyAll` pass). So one unit ordering `BUY 200 HORS` where 100 exist
is charged for 200. The navigator settled on 2026-08-23 that the settlement should fix both: it
applies whenever **anyone** buys or sells, not only when two units contend, because `split_pool`
caps a lone claimant exactly as it caps five. See *User-facing decisions*.

`Sell` has no equivalent surprise: it is already capped by `asked.min(market_takes).min(unit_holds)`.

**Third of four, blocked on `ah-t2pn.1`**, which builds `split_pool`; that edge is wired. Agreed
design: `docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html`.

**`ah-t2pn.1` and `ah-t2pn.2` may not have landed when you pick this up.** Everything below naming
`split_pool`, `PoolShare` or `PoolShares` is **a promise from `ah-t2pn.1`'s plan, not a fact in the
tree** — read it first (`bd show ah-t2pn.1 --json`; the command returns an array). If what landed
differs, it is right and this plan is stale.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Markets are per goods, so the share is a lookup, not a field

Tax, wages and entertainment are one pool each per hex, which is why `ah-t2pn.1` carries them as
fields on `PoolShares`. A market is **one pool per item per side**: a unit may sell horses and buy
swords in the same hex, contending with different faction-mates for each. So the share cannot be a
field and must be resolved per item name — which is precisely what `Lookups<'a>` (`silver.rs:207`)
exists for. Its three members are already closures that resolve an order's item text with
`semantics`' help.

**Do not add a market field to `PoolShares`.** Add a fourth closure:

```rust
/// Which side of the market an order is on, for [`Lookups::market_share`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MarketSide { Buying, Selling }

pub struct Lookups<'a> {
    pub sale: &'a dyn Fn(&str) -> SaleAnswer,
    pub purchase: &'a dyn Fn(&str) -> PurchaseAnswer,
    pub item_tag: &'a dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
    /// How much of the goods an order names this unit may trade, once its faction-mates in the same
    /// hex have been settled against it (`ah-t2pn.3`).
    ///
    /// `None` means nothing was settled - the goods are not traded here, nothing could identify
    /// them, or the hex could not be settled at all - and the arm falls back to what the market
    /// line itself says, which is today's behaviour.
    pub market_share: &'a dyn Fn(&str, MarketSide) -> Option<i64>,
}
```

**`SaleAnswer` and `PurchaseAnswer` keep their present meaning.** `market_takes` and `market_has`
go on being what the market line states. Repurposing them to carry a share would give the same field
two meanings depending on caller, which is the drift `ah-t2pn.1`'s plan refuses for `RegionWages` and
which this codebase keeps a traps file about.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the three arms

**`Sell`** (`silver.rs:532-545`), one more `min`:

```rust
let allowed = (lookups.market_share)(item, MarketSide::Selling).unwrap_or(market_takes);
let sold = asked.min(allowed).min(unit_holds).max(0);
```

**`Buy`, `Amount::Exact`** (`silver.rs:617-625`) — this is where the second defect is fixed:

```rust
let allowed = (lookups.market_share)(item, MarketSide::Buying).unwrap_or(*count);
let bought = (*count).min(allowed);
let charged = bought.saturating_mul(price);
```

`unwrap_or(*count)` is what preserves today's behaviour when nothing was settled — the arm charges
for what was asked. When the settlement did run, `allowed` is already capped by what the market has,
so a lone over-buyer is charged only for goods that exist.

**`Buy`, `Amount::All`** — `Deferred::BuyAll { price, market_has }` (`silver.rs:721`) already caps at
`market_has` in the deferred pass. Capture the settled figure at the point the intent is read, so
the deferred pass needs no knowledge of the settlement:

```rust
Amount::All { .. } => deferred.push(Deferred::BuyAll {
    price,
    market_has: (lookups.market_share)(item, MarketSide::Buying).unwrap_or(market_has),
}),
```

**`SaleAnswer::NotWanted`, `SaleAnswer::Unknown` and `PurchaseAnswer`'s non-`ForSale` variants are
untouched.** Goods the market does not trade still earn nothing and are still explained by the
shipped `not-traded-here` finding; goods nothing could identify are still doubted with
`UnknownGoods` and its subject. The settlement never sees either — there is no pool to divide.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — settling the market

In `forecast_hex`, before the per-unit loop, build the settlement and close over it:

```rust
/// Every own unit's claim on each of the hex's market lines, settled.
///
/// Keyed by canonical item tag **and side**: a unit selling horses and a unit buying horses draw on
/// two different pools (`Wanted` and `For Sale`), which the report prints as two lines.
fn market_shares_for(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
) -> BTreeMap<(String, MarketSide), Vec<i64>>;
```

Each vector is index-aligned with `hex.units`, as `ah-t2pn.1`'s shares are and as
`feed_from_faction_food` is, so two units carrying the same id cannot be merged.

Per `(tag, side)`:

- **The pool** is the market line's amount — `market_takes` for `Selling` (the `Wanted` list),
  `market_has` for `Buying` (the `For Sale` list). A tag neither list carries has no pool and no
  entry.
- **The wants**, per unit:
  - `Selling`, `Amount::Exact(n)` → `n.min(unit_holds)`. A unit cannot sell what it does not hold,
    so asking for more is not a larger claim on the market.
  - `Selling`, `Amount::All { except }` → `(unit_holds - except).max(0)`, the same expression the arm
    uses.
  - `Buying`, `Amount::Exact(n)` → `n`.
  - `Buying`, `Amount::All { .. }` → **the whole pool**. An unbounded order attempts to buy
    everything there is, so that is what it contends for. Stated rather than derived, because the
    amount a `BUY ALL` can actually afford is not known until the deferred pass and cannot be fed
    back into a settlement that must run before it.
- **A zero want is not a claim** and takes no share.
- **The split** is `ah-t2pn.1`'s `split_pool(&wants, pool)`, unchanged. It returns the wants intact
  when the pool covers them, and a proportional, rounded-down share when it does not — which is the
  rules' own words for this pool.
- **A wanting unit with `men_estimated` does not make a market pool unknowable.** A market claim is
  counted in goods and does not multiply out by headcount, so a guessed headcount tells us nothing
  about it. **`PoolShare::Unknowable` does not arise here**, which is why `market_share` returns a
  plain `Option<i64>` and not a `PoolShare`.

Then the closure handed to each unit resolves the order's item text to a tag with the same
`item_tag` lookup the other closures use, and reads its own index out of the vector.

**`check_markets` (`semantics.rs:~440`) is untouched.** It asks whether the hex trades the goods at
all, which is a different question from how much of them, and it already has its own finding.

### Nothing else moves

No `UnitSilver` field, no `codes::ALL` entry — the finding is `ah-t2pn.4`. No new string, no new
settings row, no generated TypeScript beyond whatever `ah-t2pn.1` already regenerated.

## Increments

1. **Two sellers split what the market wants.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn two_sellers_split_what_the_market_will_take` — two units each holding 60 horses and ordered
   `SELL 60 HORS` into a `Wanted` line of 100; asserts each is credited for 50 and the two sum to no
   more than 100.
   Then `fn two_sellers_the_market_can_take_from_are_not_divided` — 30 each into the same line, both
   credited in full.
   GREEN: `MarketSide`, `Lookups::market_share`, `market_shares_for`, the `Sell` arm.

2. **A lone buyer is charged only for goods that exist.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_buyer_asking_for_more_than_the_market_has_is_charged_for_what_it_gets`
   — one unit ordering `BUY 200 HORS` against a `For Sale` line of 100 at $60; asserts `expense ==
   Some(6000)`, not `12_000`. **This is the navigator's decision and the change most likely to be
   read as out of scope; the test is what records that it was chosen.**
   GREEN: the `Buy`/`Exact` arm.

3. **Two buyers split what the market has.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn two_buyers_split_what_the_market_has` — two units each ordering
   `BUY 60 HORS` against a line of 100; asserts each is charged for 50.
   GREEN: the `Buying` side of `market_shares_for`.

4. **`BUY ALL` contends for the whole line.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_buy_all_contends_for_everything_the_market_has` — one `BUY ALL HORS`
   and one `BUY 50 HORS` against a line of 100; asserts the exact buyer is charged for its
   proportional share rather than its full 50, and that the two together buy no more than 100.
   Then `fn a_lone_buy_all_is_unchanged` — a single `BUY ALL` still buys what it can afford up to
   the whole line, exactly as today.
   GREEN: the `Amount::All` want, and capturing the share into `Deferred::BuyAll`.

5. **Different goods and different sides do not contend.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn selling_horses_does_not_contend_with_selling_swords`, and
   `fn buying_horses_does_not_contend_with_selling_horses` — the second asserts the two draw on the
   `For Sale` and `Wanted` lines separately.
   GREEN: the `(tag, side)` key.

6. **The untraded and unidentifiable cases are untouched.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn goods_this_market_does_not_want_still_earn_nothing` and
   `fn goods_nothing_could_identify_are_still_doubted` — assert `income` and `doubt` exactly as
   today, with two units ordering them so the settlement is live.
   GREEN: nothing — the settlement never sees a tag with no market line. These are the regression net.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core`** — every test named in *Increments*, plus:

- `fn a_sellers_claim_is_capped_by_what_it_holds` — a unit ordering `SELL 200 HORS` while holding 10
  contends for 10, not 200, so a faction-mate is not squeezed by an order that could never run.
- `fn a_guessed_headcount_does_not_doubt_a_market_share` — a hex where a trading unit has
  `men_estimated`; asserts both traders still get exact market figures. Markets are counted in goods,
  and this is the test that stops `ah-t2pn.1`'s `Unknowable` rule being copied here on autopilot.
- `fn a_market_split_never_sells_more_than_the_line` — a property test over several ask/pool
  combinations asserting the shares sum to no more than the pool.

**`ah-ycuj`'s corpus agreement test must stay green untouched.** The ledger prices `BUY` and `SELL`
through `semantics::buy`/`sell`, **not** through `forecast_unit` — so this bead changes the column and
not the ledger, and `ah-ycuj` compares the two. **Read *Known traps* before starting: this is the
one place in the family where the two surfaces are genuinely separate implementations.**

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`** will move if any fixture trades. Read the diff.

**TypeScript: none.**

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-23. Family design: `docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html`; this
bead's own question: `docs/ui/ah-t2pn3-markets.html`.

**How markets divide.** Settled in the family interview: **in proportion to what each unit tried to
buy or sell**, which for this pool is the rules' own wording rather than a rule of ours. Named in
goods rather than silver, because that is what the market line states.
*Rejected in that interview — road B*, leaving the column and adding only a warning;
*rejected — splitting evenly*; *rejected — `?` on every contending unit*.

**Whether the settlement applies to a lone trader.** Raised by this bead, because the `BUY` arm
never consults `market_has` for an exact amount, so a unit ordering `BUY 200` where 100 exist is
charged for 200 — a defect with nothing to do with contention, which the settlement fixes for free.
**Chosen: A — settle whenever anyone buys or sells**, not only when two units contend. One rule
covers both, and `split_pool` does not treat a lone claimant as a special case.
*Rejected — B, two or more units only*: consistent with tax and wages, where contention needs two,
and strictly in scope — but it would cap two units asking 200 between them at 100 while charging one
unit asking 200 alone for 200, two answers about one market.
*Rejected — C, do B now and file the lone over-buyer separately*: nothing decided unasked, at the
cost of leaving that inconsistency on screen until a new bead is ranked and built.

**This makes markets deliberately unlike the other three pools**, where `ah-t2pn.1`'s rule 1 leaves a
lone claimant `Uncontended`. That is the navigator's choice and must not be "corrected" for
consistency: for tax and wages a lone claimant is already capped correctly by the existing arms, so
settling it would change nothing; for `BUY` it is not, which is the whole point.

**No new user-facing surface.** No finding — that is `ah-t2pn.4`. No new string, no new setting, no
new doubt. The only things a player sees change are figures that were already wrong.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** a `BUY ALL` contends
for the whole market line, because what it can afford is not known until after the settlement must
run; a seller's claim is capped by what it holds; a guessed headcount never makes a market share
unknowable, because a market claim is counted in goods and does not multiply out by headcount; and
buying and selling the same goods draw on two separate pools, because the report prints two lines.

## Out of scope

- **Tax, wages and entertainment** — `ah-t2pn.1` and `ah-t2pn.2`.
- **The `region-pool-oversubscribed` finding** — `ah-t2pn.4`. This bead emits no finding.
- **`check_markets`.** Whether the hex trades the goods at all is a different question and already
  has its own check.
- **The ledger's `buy`/`sell`.** See *Known traps* — this is a deliberate, named gap, not an
  oversight.
- **Foreign units.** Permanently out.
- **Prices moving as stock is drawn down.** Atlantis prices a line at one figure; nothing here
  models a market that gets dearer as it empties.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (inside `check:fast`).
The corpus agreement suite is called out separately because it is the one most likely to move here —
see *Known traps*.

Checkable by looking, once, before opening the PR: load a fixture with a market hex, order two units
to sell more of one good than the `Wanted` line will take, and confirm their two **In** figures now
add up to no more than that line — then order a single unit to `BUY` more than the `For Sale` line
holds and confirm its **Out** is charged only for what exists.

## Known traps

- **The ledger prices `BUY` and `SELL` through its own `buy`/`sell` functions
  (`semantics.rs`), not through `forecast_unit`.** Unlike tax, wages and upkeep, the two surfaces are
  genuinely separate implementations here. **This bead changes the column only**, so the ledger goes
  on crediting a seller for goods the market will not take. `ah-ycuj`'s corpus test compares the two
  on `SILV` — **run it early**, and if it goes red the ledger must be brought along in the same PR
  rather than the assertion being loosened. If that turns out to be more than a mirrored `min`, stop
  and hand the bead back: a second divergence is a bead, not a patch.
- **`unwrap_or` preserves today's behaviour and must not be `unwrap_or(0)`.** `Sell` falls back to
  `market_takes`, `Buy` to the asked `count`. A zero fallback silently stops every trade in any hex
  the settlement did not cover.
- **`PoolShare::Unknowable` does not apply to markets.** Copying `ah-t2pn.1`'s estimated-headcount
  rule here would doubt traders for a reason that cannot affect them.
- **`BUY ALL`'s share is captured when the intent is read, not in the deferred pass.** The deferred
  pass runs after the settlement and has no `Lookups`; pushing the settled figure into
  `Deferred::BuyAll` is what keeps it out of there.
- **Two units may carry the same unit id.** The share vectors are index-aligned with `hex.units` for
  the reason `feed_from_faction_food`'s comment gives; a map keyed by unit id merges them silently.
- **`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` will move.** Expected; read the diff.
- **`ah-t2pn.1` may have landed differently.** `split_pool`, `PoolShare` and `PoolShares` are
  promises from its plan. Read what is in the tree first.
