title: Own units working or entertaining in one hex split the region's pay between them
description:
Road A, second piece: WORK and ENTERTAIN.

The rules print a wage pool (Wages: $12.0 (Max: $1200)) and an entertainment demand, and say they run out - but never say how they are divided. The navigator settled on 2026-08-23 that both split in proportion to what each unit asked for, borrowing the rule the rulebook does state for markets rather than inventing one whole.

The delicate part: WORK and ENTERTAIN are priced by late_income, which forecast_unit and semantics::charge_upkeep share on purpose (ah-uwa3). Contention must not make those two disagree.
design:
## Context

A region prints a wage pool (`Wages: $12.0 (Max: $1200)`) and an entertainment demand, and the rules
say both run out. The forecast gives every unit the whole of each.

`late_income` (`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:396-415`) prices both, capping each unit at the
**region's** figure:

```rust
Intent::Work => {
    let earned = facts.men.saturating_mul(region.wage_centis.unwrap_or(0)) / 100;
    late = late.saturating_add(earned.min(region.max_wages.unwrap_or(i64::MAX)));
}
Intent::Entertain => {
    let earned = facts.men
        .saturating_mul(skill_level(facts.skills, ENTERTAIN_TAG))
        .saturating_mul(ENTERTAIN_PER_MAN_PER_LEVEL);
    late = late.saturating_add(earned.min(region.entertainment.unwrap_or(0)));
}
```

So a 50-man and a 60-man unit ordered `WORK` in a region whose pool is $1,200 are shown $600 and
$720 — $1,320 promised where $1,200 exists.

**The navigator chose to model the contention** (2026-08-23), and settled that wages and
entertainment split **in proportion to what each unit asked for** — borrowing the split the rulebook
states outright for markets, since it states none for these two. The whole interview, including the
roads not taken, is under *User-facing decisions*; the agreed design is
`docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html`.

**This bead is the second of four and is blocked on `ah-t2pn.1`**, which builds the shared
settlement. That edge is wired.

**`ah-t2pn.1` is planned but not yet built at the time of writing**, so everything below that names
`split_pool`, `PoolShare` or `PoolShares` is **a promise, not a fact** — read `ah-t2pn.1`'s plan
before you start (`bd show ah-t2pn.1 --json`; note the command returns an array). If those types have
landed and differ from what is described here, they are right and this plan is stale: build against
what is in the tree and say so in the PR.

**The delicate part, and the reason this is its own bead.** `late_income` is read by
`forecast_unit` **and** by `semantics::charge_upkeep`, deliberately — its doc comment says *"because
two copies of this rule is exactly the drift that `ah-uwa3` was filed to remove"*. Contention must
reach both, from one computation. A worker whose wages are cut by contention also covers less of its
own upkeep, and if only the column learns that, the Silver column and the `not-enough-silver` warning
disagree — which `ah-ycuj`'s corpus test will catch and which is the exact defect `ah-abwx` was filed
for.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — two more shares

`ah-t2pn.1`'s `PoolShares` gains two fields, both the same `PoolShare` enum:

```rust
pub struct PoolShares {
    pub tax: PoolShare,
    /// This unit's share of the region's wage pool (`Max:` on the `Wages:` line).
    pub wages: PoolShare,
    /// This unit's share of the region's entertainment demand.
    pub entertainment: PoolShare,
}
```

`PoolShares` derives `Default` and `PoolShare::Uncontended` is its default, so every existing
construction keeps compiling as today's behaviour.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — `late_income` takes the shares

```rust
/// ...
/// `shares` is what this unit may draw from each pool once its faction-mates in the same hex have
/// been settled against it (`ah-t2pn`). It is a parameter rather than something derived here
/// because the settlement needs the whole hex, and this function is deliberately per unit and
/// pure - and because `forecast_unit` and `semantics::charge_upkeep` must be handed **the same**
/// shares, for the reason this function exists at all.
#[must_use]
pub fn late_income(facts: &UnitFacts<'_>, region: RegionWages, shares: PoolShares) -> i64
```

The two arms become:

```rust
Intent::Work => {
    let earned = facts.men.saturating_mul(region.wage_centis.unwrap_or(0)) / 100;
    late = late.saturating_add(match shares.wages {
        PoolShare::Uncontended => earned.min(region.max_wages.unwrap_or(i64::MAX)),
        PoolShare::Share(share) => share,
        PoolShare::Unknowable => 0,
    });
}
Intent::Entertain => {
    let earned = facts.men
        .saturating_mul(skill_level(facts.skills, ENTERTAIN_TAG))
        .saturating_mul(ENTERTAIN_PER_MAN_PER_LEVEL);
    late = late.saturating_add(match shares.entertainment {
        PoolShare::Uncontended => earned.min(region.entertainment.unwrap_or(0)),
        PoolShare::Share(share) => share,
        PoolShare::Unknowable => 0,
    });
}
```

**Note the asymmetry in the two `unwrap_or`s, and keep it.** A region with no `Max:` figure pays
wages without a stated ceiling (`i64::MAX`); a region with no entertainment line pays entertainers
**nothing** (`0`). `RegionWages`'s own doc comment states the second. Neither is a bug and neither
is this bead's to change.

**`Unknowable` returns `0` here, and the doubt is raised by `forecast_unit`, not by
`late_income`.** `late_income` returns a plain `i64` and has nowhere to put a doubt; giving it an
`Option` would ripple into `charge_upkeep`, which has no doubt to raise either — a unit whose share
cannot be told is charged its full fee, which is the pessimistic direction and the one every other
contended case in this codebase takes. `forecast_unit` sets `income_doubt` separately, below.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — `forecast_unit` raises the doubt

`forecast_unit` already receives `shares` (from `ah-t2pn.1`). After its intent loop, where it calls
`late_income`, it must also doubt the income when either pool is unknowable:

```rust
// A pool this unit draws on is contended by a faction-mate whose headcount is a guess, so its
// share is not a number. `late_income` returned 0 for it; the figure the column shows must say so
// rather than quietly understating (`ah-t2pn.2`).
for placed in facts.intents {
    match &placed.intent {
        Intent::Work if shares.wages == PoolShare::Unknowable => {
            income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::ContestedRegionPool));
        }
        Intent::Entertain if shares.entertainment == PoolShare::Unknowable => {
            income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::ContestedRegionPool));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

`SilverDoubt::ContestedRegionPool` and its hover sentence are `ah-t2pn.1`'s and are **reused
unchanged**. No new variant, no new string, and `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts` is not touched.

**`late_income` on `UnitSilver` becomes a doubted term too.** `UnitSilver::late_income` is documented
as *"Always `Some` where `income` is: it is a subset of the same sum, computed in the same pass."*
That invariant must hold: where `income` becomes `None` through this doubt, `late_income` must be
`None` as well. Check the existing construction does that for `UnknownTaxBase` and follow it exactly.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — one settlement, two readers

`ah-t2pn.1` introduces `tax_shares_for(hex, taxers, tax_base)`. **Generalise it** rather than adding
two siblings beside it:

```rust
/// One `PoolShares` per unit in `hex.units`, index-aligned, for every contended regional pool.
///
/// Computed **once per hex** and handed to both `forecast_hex` and `charge_upkeep`: they price
/// `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` through the same `late_income`, so two settlements would be two answers
/// to one question - the drift `ah-uwa3` removed and `ah-ycuj` now guards.
fn pool_shares_for(hex: &Hex<'_>, region: RegionWages) -> Vec<PoolShares>;
```

Per pool, the same three rules `ah-t2pn.1` established for tax:

1. **Fewer than two units want the pool** → every unit `Uncontended`. One worker is exactly today's
   case and must keep today's arithmetic, including the two `unwrap_or` defaults above.
2. **Any wanting unit has `men_estimated`** → every **wanting** unit gets `Unknowable`; every other
   unit in the hex stays `Uncontended` for that pool. A unit not drawing on a pool is never doubted
   by somebody else's contention for it.
3. **Otherwise** → `split_pool(&wants, pool)`, and each wanting unit gets `Share(shares[i])`.

The pools and the wants:

| Pool | The pool is | A unit's want is |
|---|---|---|
| wages | `region.max_wages` — **`None` means no ceiling, so not contended** | `men * wage_centis / 100` |
| entertainment | `region.entertainment` — **`None` means the region pays nothing** | `men * skill_level(ENTE) * 30` |

**`max_wages == None` must be `Uncontended`, never a pool of zero.** Today that case means
"unlimited", and turning it into a split would pay every worker nothing — the opposite of the
current behaviour and a far worse bug than the one being fixed.

**`entertainment == None`** is a pool the region genuinely does not have. Leave it `Uncontended`:
today's `min(earned, 0)` already yields zero for every entertainer, so there is nothing to divide and
no reason to doubt.

`skill_level` (`silver.rs:1322`) and `ENTERTAIN_PER_MAN_PER_LEVEL` (`:28`) / `ENTERTAIN_TAG` (`:35`)
are in `silver.rs`. **Do not re-derive an entertainer's want in `semantics.rs`** — that is a second
copy of the arithmetic `late_income` owns. Export a small helper from `silver.rs` instead:

```rust
/// What one unit's orders ask of each of its region's contended pools, before any settlement.
/// The single place the wants are derived, so `late_income` and the settlement cannot disagree.
#[must_use]
pub fn pool_wants(facts: &UnitFacts<'_>, region: RegionWages) -> PoolWants;

pub struct PoolWants { pub tax: i64, pub wages: i64, pub entertainment: i64 }
```

A unit not ordered to do the thing wants `0`, and a zero want is not a claim on the pool — so a hex
with one worker and four idle units has one wanting unit and is `Uncontended`, by rule 1.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — both callers

- **`forecast_hex`** (`semantics.rs:354`): already builds `RegionWages`; replace `ah-t2pn.1`'s
  tax-only call with `pool_shares_for(hex, region)` and pass each unit its entry, as it already does.
- **`charge_upkeep`** (`semantics.rs:975`): builds its own `RegionWages` at `:982` and calls
  `late_income` per unit. It must call `pool_shares_for` on the same hex with the same region and
  pass each unit the same entry.

**Those two `RegionWages` literals are already identical and must stay so.** If it is cheap, lift
both into one `fn region_wages(hex: &Hex<'_>) -> RegionWages` — two copies of the same literal are
two things to keep in step, and this bead is about exactly that class of drift. Do not restructure
further than that.

### The stale comment

`silver.rs:507-510`, the `CLAIM` arm, reads:

> *"Capped at what the faction actually holds, and never divided between units that claim in the same
> turn — exactly as `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` treat their regional pools."*

After this bead the comparison is false: `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` now **are** divided. **Correct the
second half and leave the behaviour alone.** `CLAIM` draws on the faction purse, not a regional pool;
`ah-bumi` settled its column and `ah-wur4` shipped its warning, and both stand. Suggested:

> *"Capped at what the faction actually holds, and never divided between units that claim in the same
> turn — unlike the regional pools, which `ah-t2pn` settles between own units. The purse is
> faction-wide and `ah-bumi` settled it deliberately the other way; `claims-exceed-unclaimed`
> (`ah-wur4`) is what carries the overrun. A purse the report does not state leaves only the limit
> unknown, not the amount, so the stated figure is counted and nothing is doubted."*

`two_units_claiming_are_each_capped_at_the_whole_purse` (`silver.rs:1104`) and its *"do not 'fix'
this into contention modelling"* body **stay exactly as they are.**

### Nothing else moves

No new `codes::ALL` entry — the finding is `ah-t2pn.4`. No `UnitSilver` field. No new string. No
generated TypeScript, unless `ah-t2pn.1` has not yet landed `ContestedRegionPool`, in which case that
is `.1`'s to add and not this bead's.

## Increments

1. **Wages split when the pool is short.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn two_workers_split_a_wage_pool_that_cannot_cover_both` — a 50-man and a 60-man unit ordered
   `WORK` in a region at `$12.0` with `Max: $1200`; asserts late income of `545` and `655`, and that
   the two sum to no more than `1200`.
   Then `fn two_workers_a_pool_can_cover_are_not_divided` — the same units with `Max: $2000`, each
   getting its full `600` and `720`.
   GREEN: `PoolShares`' two fields, `late_income`'s parameter, `pool_wants`, `pool_shares_for`, and
   both callers.

2. **A region with no stated ceiling is untouched.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn two_workers_in_a_region_with_no_wage_ceiling_are_not_divided` —
   `max_wages: None`; asserts each gets its full `earned`. This is the test that catches the single
   most damaging mistake available here: treating `None` as a pool of zero.
   GREEN: rule 1's `None` handling.

3. **Entertainers split their own pool, and do not contend with workers.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn two_entertainers_split_the_regions_demand`, and
   `fn a_worker_and_an_entertainer_do_not_contend` — a hex with one of each asserts both
   `Uncontended` and both figures unchanged.
   GREEN: the entertainment arm.

4. **Upkeep learns it too — the bead's real risk.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn contended_wages_leave_less_to_cover_upkeep` — two workers contending, one
   of whom relied on its full wages to pay its fee; asserts a `not-enough-silver` finding that does
   **not** fire today, and asserts the Silver column shows the same unit short.
   The two assertions together are the point: one alone passes on a surface that learned about
   contention while the other did not.
   GREEN: `charge_upkeep` reading `pool_shares_for`.

5. **A guessed headcount doubts the pool's users.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_workers_estimated_headcount_doubts_every_worker_in_the_hex` — two
   workers, one with `men_estimated`; asserts both carry `ContestedRegionPool`, `income == None` and
   `late_income == None`, and that an entertainer in the same hex keeps an exact figure.
   Then `fn a_contested_wage_pool_still_prices_what_the_unit_spends` — the same unit with a `BUY`,
   asserting `expense` is `Some(_)`.
   GREEN: `forecast_unit`'s doubt loop, and the `late_income`/`income` invariant.

6. **The stale comment.** No test. Correct `silver.rs:507-510` and leave the `CLAIM` behaviour and
   its pinning test untouched.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core`** — every test named in *Increments*, plus:

- `fn claiming_is_still_never_divided` — if `ah-t2pn.1` added it, extend rather than duplicate it;
  otherwise add it here. Two units each `CLAIM 4000` against a `$4,935` purse still read `4000`
  each.
- `fn a_lone_worker_still_earns_the_whole_pool` — the regression net under rule 1.
- `fn wages_and_upkeep_agree_about_one_contended_worker` — the same unit's `late_income` from the
  column and the fee `charge_upkeep` nets it against are the same number. This is the one-computation
  invariant stated as a test, and it is what stops the two `RegionWages` literals drifting.

**`ah-ycuj`'s corpus agreement test must stay green untouched.** It is the net under this bead: the
column and the ledger must learn about contention in the same PR.

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`** will move — a city with several working units is the
normal case. Read the diff; do not loosen the assertion.

**TypeScript: none.** No string, no field, no generated file.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-23 in the `ah-t2pn` family interview, against
`docs/ui/ah-t2pn-a-contention.html`, `ah-t2pn-b-warnings.html` and `ah-t2pn-roadA-splits.html`.
The agreed design is `docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html`.

**The road.** **Chosen: model the contention** rather than leave the column and warn about it.
*Rejected — road B*, which was the planner's recommendation: it would have extended `ah-wur4`,
needs no invented rule and reverses nothing. Rejected because a wage column that promises $1,320
where $1,200 exists is wrong on the surface a player reads first.

**How wages and entertainment divide — the question this bead exists to answer.** The rules state a
split for tax (evenly) and markets (proportionally) and **none at all** for these two.
**Chosen: in proportion to what each unit asked for** — $545 and $655 for a 50-man and a 60-man unit
against a $1,200 pool. Our rule rather than the rulebook's, but borrowed from the split the rulebook
does state for markets rather than invented whole.
*Rejected — evenly*: $600 each, which pays a 60-man unit what a 50-man unit gets, understating the
larger and overstating the smaller — the same defect this family removes, in a new place.
*Rejected — `?` on every contending unit*: the doctrine `ah-1wcw.1` and `ah-7cdt` both applied,
*never a number that might be wrong*. Rejected because a city where several units work is the normal
case, so it would be `?` on many units every turn.

**The doubt sentence** when a contender's headcount is a guess is `ah-t2pn.1`'s, chosen in the same
interview and **reused here verbatim and unchanged**:

> `Another of your units here draws on the same pool and its headcount is an estimate, so this unit's share cannot be worked out.`

**No new user-facing surface is added by this bead.** No finding — that is `ah-t2pn.4`. No new
string, no new setting. The only thing a player sees change is two figures that were already wrong.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** a region with no
`Max:` wage figure is **not** contended, because `None` there means "no ceiling" and not "no money";
a region with no entertainment line stays `Uncontended` because today's arithmetic already yields
zero for every entertainer; a unit whose share is `Unknowable` is charged its **full** upkeep fee,
the pessimistic direction, because `charge_upkeep` has nowhere to raise a doubt; and workers and
entertainers never contend with each other.

## Out of scope

- **Tax** — `ah-t2pn.1`, which this bead is blocked on and whose `split_pool` it reuses unchanged.
- **Markets** — `ah-t2pn.3`. `PoolShares` gains no market field here.
- **The `region-pool-oversubscribed` finding and its Settings row** — `ah-t2pn.4`. This bead emits no
  finding and adds nothing to `codes::ALL`.
- **`CLAIM` against the faction purse.** Only the stale half of its comment changes; the behaviour,
  the arm and its pinning test do not.
- **The two `unwrap_or` defaults in `late_income`.** `i64::MAX` for an absent wage ceiling and `0`
  for an absent entertainment line are both deliberate and both stay.
- **Foreign units.** Permanently out.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

Both green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Checkable by looking, once, before opening the PR: load a fixture with a city hex, order two units of
different sizes to `WORK`, and confirm the two **In** figures now add up to no more than the
region's stated `Max:` — where before each showed its own full wage.

## Known traps

- **`late_income` is shared by two callers on purpose** (`ah-uwa3`). Wiring contention into
  `forecast_hex` and forgetting `charge_upkeep` makes the column and the `not-enough-silver` warning
  disagree about the same worker. Increment 4 is built to fail in exactly that case, and `ah-ycuj`'s
  corpus test is the net under it.
- **`max_wages: None` means *no ceiling*, not *no money*.** Treating it as a pool of zero pays every
  worker nothing. Increment 2 exists for this and nothing else.
- **`entertainment: None` means the region pays entertainers nothing** — the opposite default, in
  the same struct, two lines apart. Both are documented on `RegionWages`; keep both.
- **Do not re-derive an entertainer's want in `semantics.rs`.** `skill_level`,
  `ENTERTAIN_PER_MAN_PER_LEVEL` and the `/100` wage arithmetic all live in `silver.rs`; export
  `pool_wants` and use it, or you have written a second copy of the rule this file exists to keep
  single.
- **`UnitSilver::late_income` must be `None` wherever `income` is.** Its doc comment states the
  invariant; a doubt that sets one and not the other breaks it silently.
- **`ah-t2pn.1` may have landed differently.** Everything here naming `split_pool`, `PoolShare` or
  `PoolShares` is a promise from its plan, not a fact in the tree. Read what is there first.
- **`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` will move.** Expected; read the diff.

title: Own units taxing one hex split its tax base instead of each being promised all of it
description:
Road A, first piece: the shared settlement helper, applied to TAX.

The rules say tax income is 'split evenly among all taxers'. The navigator settled on 2026-08-23 that 'evenly' means per man - which for TAX is arithmetically identical to 'in proportion to what each unit asked for', because a taxer's ask is men * 50. That makes one rule serve all four pools, and this bead builds it and wires TAX to it.

Today forecast_hex builds one RegionWages and hands the same copy to every unit, so two 50-man units in a $2500 region are each shown $2500.
design:
## Context

A region's tax base is shared, and the rules say what happens when it is oversubscribed: tax income
is *"split evenly among all taxers"*. The forecast gives every unit the whole of it.

`forecast_hex` (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:354`) builds **one** `RegionWages` and hands the
same copy to each unit; the only cross-unit accounting in the function is food. So the `TAX` arm at
`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:504-509` prices each unit against the region's whole base:

```rust
Intent::Tax => match region.tax_base {
    Some(base) => income = income.saturating_add(men.saturating_mul(TAX_PER_MAN).min(base)),
    None => income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase)),
},
```

Two 50-man units in a $2,500 region are each shown $2,500 — $5,000 promised where $2,500 exists.

**The navigator chose to model the contention** rather than warn about it (2026-08-23; the whole
interview and the roads not taken are under *User-facing decisions*). This bead is the first of four:
it builds the shared settlement every contended pool will use, and wires **`TAX`** to it. Its
siblings wire wages and entertaining (`ah-t2pn.2`), the markets (`ah-t2pn.3`), and add the advisory
finding (`ah-t2pn.4`). All three are blocked on this one, and the edges are wired.

**This reverses a shipped decision, deliberately and with the navigator's knowledge.** `ah-1wcw.1`
settled that the Silver column counts each unit alone, `ah-bumi` re-confirmed it for `CLAIM`, and
`silver.rs`'s `CLAIM` arm still carries the comment *"never divided between units that claim in the
same turn — exactly as `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` treat their regional pools"*, pinned by
`two_units_claiming_are_each_capped_at_the_whole_purse` (`silver.rs:1104`), whose body says *"do not
'fix' this into contention modelling."*

**Leave `CLAIM` alone.** That comment and that test stay exactly as they are. `CLAIM` draws on the
faction purse, not a regional pool; `ah-wur4` shipped a warning for it and that decision stands. Only
the sentence in the comment that describes *`WORK` and `ENTERTAIN`* becomes stale, and `ah-t2pn.2`
owns correcting it. Do not touch it here.

**The key arithmetic, and why one rule serves all four pools.** The navigator settled that "evenly
among all taxers" means **per man**, not per unit. For `TAX` that is identical to *in proportion to
what each unit asked for*, because a taxer's ask is exactly `men × 50` — so the proportional split
the rules state outright for markets is the same function. One helper, four pools.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the settlement, new

`feed_from_faction_food` (`silver.rs:852` area) is the precedent: a pure function in `silver.rs`,
index-aligned with the caller's list rather than keyed by unit id, whose doc comment explains why
(*"which is also what keeps two units sharing an id from being confused for one another, as a lookup
by id could not"*). Copy that shape.

```rust
/// Splits a contended regional pool between the units that asked for it.
///
/// Returns one share per claim, **index-aligned with `wants`** - not keyed by unit id, for the
/// reason `feed_from_faction_food` gives: two units in one hex may carry the same id, and a map
/// would silently merge them.
///
/// When the pool covers every claim, each unit gets exactly what it asked for and nothing is
/// divided. When it does not, each gets `pool * wants[i] / total`, **rounded down** - so the shares
/// never add up to more than the pool, and up to `wants.len() - 1` silver of it goes unpromised.
/// Understating by a few silver is the safe direction for a figure whose negatives a player acts
/// on; the alternative is promising money the region does not have, which is the defect this
/// removes.
///
/// The rules state this split for markets outright ("in proportion to the amount each buyer
/// attempted to buy"). For `TAX` it is the same arithmetic as the rules' own "split evenly among
/// all taxers", read per man: a taxer's ask is `men * 50`, so proportional-to-ask *is*
/// proportional-to-men.
#[must_use]
pub fn split_pool(wants: &[i64], pool: i64) -> Vec<i64>;
```

Exhaustive behaviour — every one of these is a test below:

| `wants` | `pool` | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `[]` | anything | `[]` |
| any | `<= 0` | all zeros |
| any, all `<= 0` | any | all zeros (no division by zero) |
| total `<= pool` | | `wants` unchanged — **nothing is divided when nothing is contended** |
| `[500, 2500]` | `2500` | `[416, 2083]` — floor, and 1 silver left unpromised |
| `[2500]` | `2500` | `[2500]` — one unit is not a special case |
| `[3000]` | `2500` | `[2500]` — identical to today's `min(men*50, base)` |

A negative individual `want` is clamped to 0 before the total is taken; it cannot arise from `TAX`
(`men` is never negative) and clamping is cheaper than a precondition nobody can violate.

Use `i128` for the `pool * wants[i]` product, or `saturating_mul` before the divide. A $2,500 base
against a large ask cannot overflow `i64`, but `split_pool` is about to be handed market quantities
by `ah-t2pn.3` and the file's settled habit is `saturating_*` throughout.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — what a unit may draw

```rust
/// What one unit may draw from one contended regional pool, once its faction-mates in the same hex
/// have been settled against it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum PoolShare {
    /// Nothing to settle: this unit is the only one in the hex wanting the pool, or the region
    /// states no pool at all. The arithmetic falls back to `RegionWages` and behaves exactly as it
    /// does today.
    #[default]
    Uncontended,
    /// What `split_pool` gave this unit.
    Share(i64),
    /// The hex cannot be settled: some unit contending for this pool has a headcount that is
    /// itself a guess, so no unit's share is a number - including units whose own count is exact.
    Unknowable,
}

/// What one unit may draw from each of its region's contended pools.
///
/// One field per pool. `ah-t2pn.2` adds `wages` and `entertainment`, `ah-t2pn.3` adds the market
/// quantities; each is `Uncontended` until its own bead lands, which is exactly today's behaviour.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct PoolShares {
    pub tax: PoolShare,
}
```

**`forecast_unit` (`silver.rs:422`) gains one parameter**, `shares: PoolShares`, after `region`.
`RegionWages` keeps its present meaning — the region's own figures — and is **not** repurposed to
carry a share. A field that means "the region's tax base" from one caller and "this unit's slice of
it" from another is the kind of drift this codebase has a traps file about.

The `TAX` arm becomes:

```rust
Intent::Tax => match shares.tax {
    // Today's behaviour, unchanged, for a unit nobody contends with.
    PoolShare::Uncontended => match region.tax_base {
        Some(base) => {
            income = income.saturating_add(men.saturating_mul(TAX_PER_MAN).min(base))
        }
        None => income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase)),
    },
    // Already capped by the settlement, and already no larger than this unit's own ask.
    PoolShare::Share(share) => income = income.saturating_add(share),
    PoolShare::Unknowable => {
        income_doubt = income_doubt.or(Some(SilverDoubt::ContestedRegionPool))
    }
},
```

**`PoolShare::Unknowable` sets `income_doubt`; it must not take the whole-unit early return** at
`silver.rs:445-470`. That return exists for a unit whose *own* headcount is a guess, where nothing
per-man can be multiplied out at all. Here the unit's own men are known and its expenses are exactly
priceable — only its share of one pool is not — so this behaves like `UnknownTaxBase`: income and
`at_month_end` become `None`, expense stays a number.

### `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs` — the new doubt

```rust
/// A regional pool this unit draws on is contended by a faction-mate whose headcount is itself a
/// guess, so no unit's share of it can be worked out - including this one's, whose own count is
/// exact. Distinct from [`SilverDoubt::EstimatedMen`], which is about the unit's own headcount.
ContestedRegionPool,
```

Appended to the `SilverDoubt` enum (`silver.rs:~195-215`). The enum is `#[serde(rename_all =
"kebab-case")]`, so the wire value is `contested-region-pool`, and
`packages/core-client/src/generated/SilverDoubt.ts` is regenerated, not hand-edited.

**Where it sorts.** `forecast_unit`'s doc comment (`silver.rs:419`) says doubts are reported *"in
order of increasing scope — `EstimatedMen` first, which short-circuits"*. `ContestedRegionPool` is
wider than `EstimatedMen` and narrower than nothing else here; it is set through the ordinary
`income_doubt.or(...)`, so an earlier doubt on the same side wins, which is the file's existing rule
and needs no new code.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — settling the hex

`forecast_hex` (`semantics.rs:352`) gains a pre-pass before its unit loop, and passes each unit its
own `PoolShares`:

```rust
// Every own unit ordered to TAX, in `hex.units` order so the shares come back index-aligned.
let taxers: Vec<usize> = hex
    .units
    .iter()
    .enumerate()
    .filter(|(_, o)| o.intents.iter().any(|p| matches!(p.intent, Intent::Tax)))
    .map(|(i, _)| i)
    .collect();

let tax_shares: Vec<PoolShare> = tax_shares_for(hex, &taxers, region.tax_base);
```

with one private helper, whose whole job is the three-way decision:

```rust
/// One `PoolShare` per unit in `hex.units`, for the region's tax base.
///
/// `Uncontended` unless two or more own units in this hex are ordered to tax it: one taxer is
/// exactly today's case and must keep today's arithmetic, including its `UnknownTaxBase` doubt for
/// a region that states no base.
fn tax_shares_for(hex: &Hex<'_>, taxers: &[usize], tax_base: Option<i64>) -> Vec<PoolShare>;
```

Its rules, in order:

1. Fewer than two taxers, or `tax_base` is `None` → every unit `Uncontended`. A region with no
   stated base has no pool to divide, and `Uncontended` keeps the existing `UnknownTaxBase` doubt
   for the taxer, which is the right sentence.
2. Any taxer has `men_estimated` → every **taxer** gets `Unknowable`; every non-taxer stays
   `Uncontended`. A unit not drawing on the base is unaffected, exactly as `ah-7cdt`'s quartermaster
   kept an exact figure while the contending units went to `?`.
3. Otherwise → `split_pool(&wants, base)`, where `wants[i] = men * TAX_PER_MAN` for each taxer, and
   each taxer gets `Share(shares[i])`. Non-taxers stay `Uncontended`.

`TAX_PER_MAN` is `silver.rs:23` and is already `pub(crate)`-visible to `semantics` through the
module; if it is not, export it rather than writing `50` here — a second copy of that constant is
precisely the drift `ah-uwa3` was filed about.

**`charge_upkeep` (`semantics.rs:975`) is not touched by this bead.** It builds its own
`RegionWages` (`semantics.rs:982`) and reads it only through `late_income`, which prices `Work` and
`Entertain` alone — `TAX` is not in it. Keeping those two `RegionWages` literals in step is
`ah-t2pn.2`'s problem, and it is named in that bead.

### Nothing else moves

`UnitSilver` gains no field. `codes::ALL` is untouched — the finding is `ah-t2pn.4`. `unitTable.ts`
and `SettingsDialog.tsx` are untouched.

### `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.ts`

One entry in `silverNote`'s doubt table, beside the shipped `estimated-men` line at
`unitTooltip.ts:203`:

```ts
if (silver.doubt === "contested-region-pool") {
  return "Another of your units here draws on the same pool and its headcount is an estimate, so this unit's share cannot be worked out.";
}
```

Placed with the other doubts, above the informational notes, as they all are.

### Generated TypeScript

`packages/core-client/src/generated/SilverDoubt.ts` moves. Regenerate, never hand-edit:

```
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

`pnpm run check:generated` fails the build if it is stale.

## Increments

1. **The split is a pure function.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs`,
   `fn a_pool_that_covers_every_claim_divides_nothing` — `split_pool(&[500, 1000], 2500)` returns
   `[500, 1000]`.
   Then `fn a_short_pool_is_divided_in_proportion_to_what_each_asked` —
   `split_pool(&[500, 2500], 2500)` returns `[416, 2083]`, and the test asserts the sum is
   `<= 2500`, which is the property that matters more than either figure.
   Then `fn a_pool_is_never_promised_twice` — a table over the seven rows of the behaviour table in
   *Files to change*, including the empty slice, a zero pool and all-zero wants, each asserting the
   sum never exceeds the pool and no panic occurs.
   GREEN: `split_pool`.

2. **One taxer is untouched.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
   `fn a_lone_taxer_still_collects_against_the_whole_base` — one 50-man unit ordered `TAX` in a
   $2,500 region asserts income `2500`; and a sibling asserting a 10-man unit gets `500`. Both pass
   today, and that is the point: they are the regression net under everything below.
   GREEN: nothing — `tax_shares_for` returning `Uncontended` for fewer than two taxers.

3. **Two taxers split the base.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn two_taxers_split_the_base_in_proportion_to_their_men` — a 10-man scout
   and a 50-man garrison in a $2,500 region assert income of `416` and `2083`. This is the bead's
   headline and the case its title names.
   Then `fn two_taxers_the_base_can_cover_are_not_divided` — a 10-man and a 20-man unit in the same
   region assert `500` and `1000`, unchanged.
   GREEN: `PoolShare`, `PoolShares`, the `TAX` arm, `tax_shares_for`, and `forecast_unit`'s new
   parameter.

4. **A guessed headcount makes the hex unsettleable.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn a_taxers_estimated_headcount_doubts_every_taxer_in_the_hex` — two
   taxers, one with `men_estimated`, asserts **both** carry
   `doubt == Some(SilverDoubt::ContestedRegionPool)` and `income == None`, and that a third unit in
   the same hex ordered `MOVE` is untouched with an exact figure.
   Then `fn a_contested_pool_still_prices_what_the_unit_spends` — the same unit with a `BUY`,
   asserting `expense` is `Some(_)` and not `None`. That is what separates this doubt from
   `EstimatedMen`'s whole-unit early return, and without the test the two are easy to conflate.
   GREEN: the `Unknowable` arm and rule 2 of `tax_shares_for`.

5. **A region with no stated base is unchanged.**
   RED: `semantics.rs`, `fn two_taxers_in_a_region_with_no_stated_base_are_doubted_as_before` —
   asserts both carry `SilverDoubt::UnknownTaxBase`, not `ContestedRegionPool`. Absence of a base is
   not contention.
   GREEN: rule 1 of `tax_shares_for`.

6. **Regenerate the TypeScript.** `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
   --test generated_ts`, then `pnpm run check:generated`.

7. **The hover explains the doubt.**
   RED: `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts`,
   `fn the_note_explains_a_pool_contended_by_a_guessed_headcount` — asserts the sentence verbatim.
   GREEN: one entry in `silverNote`.

## The test plan

**Rust, `crates/core`** (`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`) — every test named in *Increments*, plus:

- `fn claiming_is_still_never_divided` — two units each ordered `CLAIM 4000` against a $4,935 purse
  still read `4000` each. `two_units_claiming_are_each_capped_at_the_whole_purse` (`silver.rs:1104`)
  already asserts this and **must not be modified**; add the new test beside it naming this bead, so
  the next reader sees the boundary was deliberate rather than missed.
- `fn working_is_still_never_divided` — two units ordered `WORK` in a region whose `max_wages`
  cannot cover both still read the full amount each. This bead does **not** fix wages, and a test
  saying so is what stops an implementer helpfully wiring `PoolShares.wages` that does not exist yet.
- `fn a_taxer_and_a_worker_do_not_contend` — one unit taxing and one working in the same hex are
  both `Uncontended` for tax. Different pools, no contention.

**Existing tests that will move.** `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` audits every committed
fixture; any fixture with two own units taxing one hex will change. **Read the diff — do not loosen
the assertion.** A moved figure there is this bead working; the corpus is real turn reports, and a
city with several taxing units is the normal case the bead was filed about.

**TypeScript** — `packages/shared/src/unitTooltip.test.ts` only. Note the traps file: `packages/shared`
has no jsdom, so nothing here asks for an effect-level test; `unitTooltip.ts` is a pure module.

**Suites that must run:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `pnpm run check:generated`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-23 over three mockups. The chosen mockup is
`docs/ui/ah-t2pn-shared-pools.html`.

**The road — model the contention, or warn about it?** Two mockups, side by side.
**Chosen: road A — model it.** Own units in a hex split the pool and the column shows what the game
will pay.
*Rejected — road B, leave the column and add a warning*: this was the planner's recommendation and
the navigator chose against it. It would have extended `ah-wur4`, which shipped exactly that shape
for the faction purse and whose design says in terms that it is the *other half* of `ah-bumi`'s
decision to leave the column per-unit; it needs no invented rule and reverses nothing. It was
rejected because a tax column that says $1,500 twice where $2,500 exists is wrong on the surface a
player reads first, and a warning does not make the number right.
*Rejected — road A for tax and markets, road B for wages*: honest to the rules, but two pools in one
hex would then behave in two different ways.

**"Split evenly among all taxers" — evenly between what?** A 10-man scout and a 50-man garrison in a
$2,500 region make the difference stark: $1,250 each, or $417 and $2,083.
**Chosen: per man.** "All taxers" read as the men doing the taxing, which is how the $50 rate is
stated in the first place ("each taxing character collects $50"). Nobody exceeds their own ceiling
and one large unit is not held back by a small one.
*Rejected — evenly per unit*: the literal words, but it promises a 10-man unit $1,250 when 10 men can
collect $500 — the same class of defect this bead removes.
*Rejected — cap each at what it could collect alone, then split the remainder evenly*: nobody is
promised the impossible and the leftover is shared, but it is the most code and it invents a
two-stage rule the rulebook does not describe.

**Wages and entertainment** were settled in the same interview — **in proportion to what each unit
asked**, borrowing the rule the rulebook states for markets. **That is `ah-t2pn.2`'s to build**, and
it is recorded here only so this bead's `split_pool` is known to be the function that will serve it.
*Rejected there — evenly*, and *rejected — `?` on every contending unit*, the doctrine
`ah-1wcw.1` and `ah-7cdt` applied, because a city where several units work is the normal case and
that is `?` on many units every turn.

**Is there a warning as well as the corrected column?**
**Chosen: yes** — one code, `region-pool-oversubscribed`, one finding per contending unit, wording
mirroring the shipped `claims-exceed-unclaimed`. **`ah-t2pn.4` builds it; nothing in this bead emits
a finding.**
*Rejected — a hover note only*, which was the planner's recommendation once the column was correct.
*Rejected — neither*, which would leave a taxer earning less than $50 a man with nothing on screen
saying why.

**The doubt sentence, when a contender's headcount is a guess.** Shipping verbatim:

> `Another of your units here draws on the same pool and its headcount is an estimate, so this unit's share cannot be worked out.`

*Rejected — the shorter "A unit sharing this region's pool has an estimated headcount, so the shares
cannot be worked out."* (same fact, less finger-pointing, fits a narrow hover without wrapping).
*Rejected — reusing `estimated-men`*, whose shipped sentence is "This unit's headcount is an
estimate, so its month cannot be priced" — untrue of a unit whose own count is exact, which is the
whole reason a new variant exists.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** contention needs two
or more units, so a lone taxer is never touched; a unit not ordered to tax is never doubted by
somebody else's tax contention; foreign units are never counted, since `Hex::read` has already
filtered them out and their orders are unknowable; a region stating no tax base keeps today's
`UnknownTaxBase` doubt rather than gaining a contention doubt; and shares are rounded **down**, so a
few silver of a contended pool goes unpromised.

## Out of scope

- **Wages and entertainment** — `ah-t2pn.2`, which also owns correcting the now-stale half of the
  `CLAIM` arm's comment about how `WORK` and `ENTERTAIN` treat their pools.
- **Markets** — `ah-t2pn.3`. `split_pool` is built here to serve them, but no market code is touched
  and `PoolShares` gains no market field in this bead.
- **The `region-pool-oversubscribed` finding and its Settings row** — `ah-t2pn.4`. This bead emits no
  finding and adds nothing to `codes::ALL`.
- **`CLAIM` against the faction purse.** Not a regional pool; `ah-bumi` settled the column and
  `ah-wur4` shipped the warning. Its comment and its pinning test stay exactly as they are.
- **`PILLAGE` emptying the base for your own taxers** — `ah-cxxa` (P3). It is a special case of this
  settlement (the pool becomes zero for taxers once anybody pillages) and will be much cheaper once
  this lands, but nothing here anticipates it.
- **Foreign units.** Permanently out: their orders are not in the document.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
```

All green, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (inside `check:fast`).

Checkable by looking, once, before opening the PR: load a committed fixture with a city hex, give two
units of different sizes a `TAX` order, and confirm the two Silver figures now add up to no more than
the region's stated tax base — where before they each showed the whole of it.

## Known traps

- **`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` will move**, and that is this bead working. Several
  committed fixtures are real turn reports of cities with more than one taxing unit. Read the diff;
  do not loosen the assertion.
- **Do not repurpose `RegionWages`.** It means the region's own figures, and it is read by
  `late_income`, which `forecast_unit` and `charge_upkeep` share on purpose (`ah-uwa3`). Handing one
  caller a "share" through that struct would silently change upkeep as well as the column, in a bead
  that is not supposed to touch wages at all.
- **`PoolShare::Unknowable` is not `EstimatedMen`.** The whole-unit early return at
  `silver.rs:445-470` throws away expense as well as income; this doubt must go through
  `income_doubt` so a contended taxer's spending is still priced. Increment 4's second test is what
  holds that apart.
- **`SilverDoubt` is `#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]` and generated into TypeScript.** Adding a
  variant moves `packages/core-client/src/generated/SilverDoubt.ts`; regenerate with
  `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts`, and never edit
  it by hand — it passes locally and fails `pnpm run check:generated`.
- **`packages/shared` has no jsdom** (`ah-nass`, and the traps file). `unitTooltip.ts` is a pure
  module and is tested as one; do not add an effect-level test there.
- **Integer division, not rounding.** `pool * wants[i] / total` rounded down, deliberately. A
  round-to-nearest would let the shares sum to more than the pool, which is the exact thing this bead
  exists to stop.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array**, if you go reading the sibling beads' plans — and reading
  `ah-t2pn.2`'s before starting is worth the minute, because it inherits `split_pool` from you.

title: A corpus test that the silver column and the not-enough-silver warning agree
description:
The economy is computed twice from the same orders: forecast_unit (crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs) produces the Silver column, and the ledger (semantics.rs, ledger_for/apply/report_shortfalls) produces the not-enough-silver finding. They are separate code with separate arms per order, and they have already drifted apart in at least one place - PILLAGE is credited by the ledger and absent from the forecast, so a pillager can be shown red by one surface and silent by the other.

Both sides are individually well covered: silver.rs carries roughly 1400 lines of unit tests, semantics.rs its own, and crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs audits the whole fixture corpus. What no test does is compare the two. A test that says 'for every unit in every committed fixture, if the column shows the unit ending below zero then the warning fires, and if the warning fires the column is not comfortably positive' would have caught the pillage divergence for free, and would catch the next one.

This is the cheapest guard available against a whole class of defect, and it is the reason several beads filed alongside it exist.
design:
## Context

The economy is computed **twice from the same orders**, by two pieces of code that share nothing but
their inputs:

- `forecast_unit` (`crates/core/src/orders/silver.rs:~600`) produces the **Silver column** - one
  `UnitSilver` per own unit, counting that unit alone.
- the ledger (`semantics.rs`: `ledger_for:799`, `apply:~1000`, `charge_upkeep:914`,
  `report_shortfalls:1609`) produces the **`not-enough-silver` finding** - a hex-wide balance in
  every item tag, with sharing pooled across the hex.

They have separate arms per order and they have already drifted: `PILLAGE` was credited by the
ledger and absent from the forecast, so a pillager could be shown red by one surface and silent by
the other. Both sides are individually well covered - `silver.rs` carries roughly 1,400 lines of
unit tests, `semantics.rs` its own, and `validate_real_orders.rs` audits the whole fixture corpus -
and **nothing compares the two**.

**That pillage divergence has since been fixed**: `ah-abwx` merged as `54dd0824`, *"a pillaging unit
earns in the silver column too"*. The bead's acceptance criterion "the test fails today if the
PILLAGE divergence is still present" is therefore already discharged by another bead, and this test
is expected to pass on the corpus the day it is written. **That is the intended outcome and not a
sign the test is toothless** - see *Known traps* for how to prove it has teeth before merging.

Two more beads in the same family land in this area and both are already planned or in flight:
`ah-eacd` (steps 5-6 of the maintenance payment order) and `ah-fjty` (step 7, merged as `3817339f`).
This test is the guard under all of them.

When this lands: any future change that moves one surface without the other fails a corpus test by
name, with the unit and the two numbers in the message.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**One new file, and nothing else changes.** No production code is touched. If the test as specified
below fails on the corpus, that is a defect in the production code and it is reported to the
navigator rather than fixed here - see *Out of scope*.

```
crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs      (new)
```

Reuse, and copy the shape of, `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`:

- `atlantis_hud_fixtures::ALL` (`crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs:52`) - all 26 committed reports, 25 of
  which carry an orders template.
- `extract_orders_template(report.text)` (`crates/core/src/report/orders.rs:66`), which returns
  `Option<OrdersTemplate>` with a `.text` field. **A fixture without one is not skipped**: run it
  with an empty orders document, because a unit with no orders still holds silver and still owes
  maintenance, and that is exactly the case where the two surfaces are simplest and most likely to
  be assumed rather than checked.
- `review_turn(&parsed, &orders_text, Some(&ruleset), CheckOptions::default())`
  (`semantics.rs:237`), which returns `TurnReview { findings, silver }` - **both surfaces from one
  call**, which is what makes this test cheap. `CheckOptions::default()` emits
  `not-enough-silver`; only `hex-unguarded` is off by default (`semantics.rs:162`).
- `common::ruleset()` (`crates/core/tests/common/mod.rs`) and `mod common;`.
- `parse_report_full` and `classify_units` exactly as `validate_real_orders.rs:11` imports them.

### The predicate - the whole of the bead

The ledger's silver balance is **exactly reconstructible from `UnitSilver`**, and that is what
makes this a precise equality rather than the loose "not comfortably positive" the bead's
description reaches for. Deriving it once here so the test can assert it:

```
B = held + income - late_income - expense        // the ledger's balance before maintenance:
                                                 // it credits TAX but never WORK/ENTERTAIN
                                                 // (`semantics.rs:1072`)
U = max(0, upkeep - late_income)                 // what maintenance actually draws off silver,
                                                 // which is `charge_upkeep`'s own arithmetic
warned  <=>  B - U < 0
```

Every term is a public field of `UnitSilver` (`silver.rs:85-160`): `held`, `income`, `late_income`,
`expense`, `upkeep`. `upkeep` there is already net of every relief - step 2's faction food, and step
7's unclaimed fund, are both subtracted from it before it reaches the column
(`semantics.rs:~470`) - so no relief term is needed.

Two identities worth writing into the test as comments, because they are what a reader will want to
check by hand:

- when `upkeep >= late_income`, `B - U` is exactly `at_month_end - upkeep`, the month-end figure
  with maintenance counted;
- when `upkeep < late_income`, `B - U` is exactly `B`, and `B < 0` is exactly
  `short_for_orders > 0` - which is `short_for_orders`'s own definition (`silver.rs:108`).

So the assertion is one equality, and the test reconstructs nothing the column does not already
publish.

### The exemption table

The acceptance criterion demands that legitimate differences are **enumerated with a reason**, not
absorbed by a loose assertion. Follow `validate_real_orders.rs`'s `EXPECTED` table
(line ~62) in spirit: a table of rows, each carrying its reason in a doc comment, and each
*computed* rather than listed by unit id wherever the reason is a rule rather than an accident.

```rust
/// Why one unit is exempt from the equality, and what is asserted about it instead.
///
/// A rule, never a unit id: a list of ids rots the moment a fixture is added, and it hides a real
/// divergence behind "that one was already failing".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Exempt {
    /// The column cannot be reconstructed at all: a term of it is `None` because something in the
    /// unit's month could not be priced. The check does not judge such a unit either
    /// (`Ledger.doubted`, `semantics.rs:781`), so the assertion becomes "and it is not warned".
    Doubted,
    /// Some own unit in this hex carries the `sharing` flag, so `report_shortfalls` judges the hex
    /// as one purse (`Ordered::shares`, `semantics.rs:778`) while the column counts each unit
    /// alone by decision (`ah-1wcw.1`). The assertion becomes a hex-level one: see below.
    SharedHex,
    /// `food_contended` - a remaining food pool too small to feed every claimant. `ah-eacd` chose
    /// to leave the figure pessimistic and suppress the warning, so the two disagree by design.
    /// **Only exists once `ah-eacd` has landed** - see *Known traps*.
    ContendedFood,
}
```

**`Doubted`** is `silver.income.is_none() || silver.expense.is_none() || silver.late_income.is_none()`.
Assert `!warned`.

**`SharedHex`** is: any own unit whose `region_id` matches this unit's carries the `sharing` flag
in the parsed report. Compute the set of such region ids once per fixture from
`parsed.regions`, filtering to own units the way `classify_units` already marks them. For a unit in
one, assert the **hex-level** statement instead, which is the strongest thing that survives pooling:

> if any unit in the hex is warned, then the hex's units are collectively in trouble - the sum of
> `B - U` over the hex's non-doubted units is negative.

and the converse: if that sum is `>= 0`, no unit in the hex is warned.

**`ContendedFood`** is `silver.food_contended`. Assert `!warned`.

Anything not exempt gets the equality:

```rust
assert_eq!(
    warned,
    b - u < 0,
    "{fixture} unit {unit_id} in {region_id}: the column says {b_minus_u} \
     (held {held} + income {income} - late {late} - expense {expense} - upkeep-drawn {u}) \
     and the warning {}",
    if warned { "fires" } else { "does not fire" },
);
```

The message must carry **the fixture name, the unit, the hex, and every term**, because the whole
value of this test is that a failure tells the next person which of two surfaces moved without
reading either.

### One more assertion, nearly free

A second test in the same file, asserting the corpus is not silently empty:

```rust
/// Guards the guard: a predicate that is never exercised asserts nothing, and a refactor that
/// stopped producing `UnitSilver` entries would make the walk above pass by walking nothing.
#[test]
fn the_corpus_actually_exercises_the_agreement()
```

It asserts, over the whole corpus, that: more than 500 own units were compared; at least one unit
was warned; at least one unit was exempt as `Doubted`; and at least one hex was exempt as
`SharedHex` (17 of the 26 fixture files mention `sharing`). Use `>` bounds with round numbers and a
comment saying they are floors and not measurements, so adding a fixture never renegotiates them.

## Increments

1. **The walk, with no assertion.** New file, `mod common;`, a test that parses every fixture in
   `ALL`, extracts its orders template (empty string where there is none), calls `review_turn`, and
   counts the `UnitSilver` entries and `not-enough-silver` findings it saw. Assert only that the
   count of units is `> 500`. Opening test: `the_corpus_actually_exercises_the_agreement`, which
   fails first on a `todo!()` and then on the count until the walk is right. This increment is
   where fixture plumbing goes wrong, and it is worth having it green on its own.
   Run: `cargo test -p atlantis-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning`.

2. **The equality, doubted units exempt.** Add
   `the_column_and_the_warning_agree_on_every_unit_in_the_corpus`, computing `B` and `U` as above
   and asserting the equality, with only the `Doubted` exemption implemented. **Expect this to fail
   on sharing hexes** - that is the increment's own evidence that the exemption below is needed and
   not theoretical. Record in a comment how many units failed and in which fixtures before adding
   it.

3. **The `SharedHex` exemption and its hex-level assertion.** Add the region-id set, exempt those
   units from the equality, and add the two hex-level assertions. Green.

4. **The `ContendedFood` exemption**, only if `UnitSilver::food_contended` exists - see
   *Known traps*. If it does not, add nothing and leave a comment naming `ah-eacd` and what the row
   will say, so the next reader knows the omission is dated rather than missed.

5. **Finish `the_corpus_actually_exercises_the_agreement`** with its four floors.

## The test plan

Everything in this bead **is** the test; there is no production code to cover. What follows is what
each assertion pins.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `the_column_and_the_warning_agree_on_every_unit_in_the_corpus` | that `forecast_unit` and the ledger price every order the same way, for every own unit of 26 real turns. Fails by name and unit on any future drift. |
| `the_corpus_actually_exercises_the_agreement` | that the walk above walks something: >500 units compared, and at least one each of warned, `Doubted` and `SharedHex`. |

Both live in `crates/core/tests/silver_agrees_with_the_warning.rs` and are pure integration tests
over committed fixtures - no network, no timing, no ordering between them.

Suites that must run: `cargo test -p atlantis-core` and `pnpm run check:fast`. Nothing here touches
TypeScript, a rendered component or a generated binding, so the browser suites are CI's alone.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** This bead adds one integration test file and changes no production code, so nothing about
it reaches the interface: no column moves, no message changes, no setting is added. Nothing was put
to the navigator, and nothing should be.

The one decision the bead's own `design` field asks planning to settle is an **architecture**
question and therefore mine: *is the right end state one computation feeding both surfaces, rather
than two that a test keeps in step?*

**Decided: not here, and not yet.** The two surfaces genuinely answer different questions - the
column counts each unit alone by an explicit decision (`ah-1wcw.1`), while the check pools a hex's
sharing units and tracks every item tag, not just silver. Unifying them is a substantial refactor
of `silver.rs` and `semantics.rs` together, and **doing it without this test first is doing it with
no safety net at all** - which is the argument for this bead's ordering, not against the refactor.
The right sequence is: this test, then the refactor, with this test as its proof.

Filing that refactor is **Forge's**, not mine: it files `Refactoring: ...` beads against costs
already being paid, and after this lands the cost is measurable rather than argued. Do not create
it as part of this bead.

## Out of scope

- **Fixing any divergence the test finds.** If the equality fails on the corpus, the test is right
  and the production code is wrong: report it to the navigator with the fixture, unit and both
  numbers, file it as its own bead, and **do not** loosen the assertion to make this bead green.
  Loosening it is the one way to deliver this bead and have it be worth nothing.
- **Item tags other than silver.** The ledger tracks balances the column cannot show at all - cast
  item costs, transmute inputs - so the assertion is about `SILV` and only `SILV`. The bead's own
  `design` field scoped this out and it stays out.
- **`not-enough-items`.** Same reason.
- **Unifying the two computations.** See *User-facing decisions*.
- **Adding fixtures.** 26 committed reports across 5 games is the corpus; this bead uses it and
  does not grow it.
- **The hex-level assertion being made exact for sharing hexes.** Pooling loses per-unit
  information by design, so the hex-level statement is the strongest available and is deliberately
  weaker than the per-unit one.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-core --test silver_agrees_with_the_warning
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green, with no `#[ignore]`, no `#[should_panic]` and no assertion commented out.

**A human must confirm one thing**, and it cannot be automated: that the test **has teeth**. Before
opening the PR, prove it by breaking the production code on purpose and watching it fail - see the
first entry under *Known traps* for exactly how. Paste the failure message into the PR description.
A test written against a corpus it already passes is otherwise indistinguishable from a test that
asserts nothing.

## Known traps

- **This test passes the day it is written, and that is the trap.** `ah-abwx` (`54dd0824`) already
  fixed the pillage divergence the bead was filed around, so there is no red-to-green transition to
  ride. **Manufacture one**: temporarily delete the `Intent::Pillage` arm of `forecast_unit`'s
  income (or, equivalently, the `Intent::Pillage` credit in `apply`, `semantics.rs:~1046`), run the
  test, confirm it fails naming a real unit in a real fixture, then revert. The TDD skill's
  red-green loop applies here through that deliberate break, not through a naturally failing
  corpus.
- **`UnitSilver::food_contended` may not exist yet.** `ah-eacd` introduces it and was claimed by an
  implementer on 2026-08-23; whether it has merged by the time this is built is not knowable from
  here. Check with `git log --oneline --grep 'ah-eacd'` and by grepping `silver.rs` for
  `food_contended`. Present - add the `ContendedFood` row. Absent - add nothing and leave the
  dated comment increment 4 describes. **Do not add a bead dependency for it**: this test is
  valuable without that row, and blocking on `ah-eacd` would keep the guard off the tree for
  exactly as long as the code most likely to need it is being written.
- **The ledger credits `TAX` but not `WORK`/`ENTERTAIN`** (`semantics.rs:1072`: "Wages and takings
  from entertaining are paid in the last phase of the turn... so they can fund nothing this
  month"). That asymmetry is the whole reason `late_income` appears in `B`. Dropping it makes the
  equality fail on every unit that works, which reads as a drift and is not one.
- **`upkeep` on `UnitSilver` is already net of relief** - step 2's faction food and step 7's
  unclaimed fund are subtracted before it reaches the column (`semantics.rs:~455-470`). Adding
  `unclaimed_covered` or `faction_food_covered` back into `U` double-counts them and fails on every
  unit the fund fed.
- **`upkeep` can be `None`** (`SilverDoubt::ContestedFactionFood`) while `income` and `expense` are
  both `Some`. The ledger charges such a unit nothing at all (`charge_upkeep`'s `Some(None) =>
  continue`), so `U = 0` is right and the unit is **not** `Doubted` for this test's purposes. Treat
  `upkeep: None` as `U = 0`, not as a skip.
- **`Finding::unit_id` is `Option<String>`** (`semantics.rs:184`) - a hex-level finding has none.
  Filter on `code == not-enough-silver` *and* a present `unit_id` before building the warned set.
- **One fixture carries no orders template** (25 of 26 do). `extract_orders_template` returns
  `None` for it; run it with `""` rather than skipping it, or the simplest and most-assumed case
  goes unchecked.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md` applies in full**, though only one entry touches this bead: nothing
  here goes in `packages/shared`, so the jsdom rule is not in play. The others - the WebKit driver,
  the smoke suite's service worker, `vite preview --strictPort`, migrating a persisted default -
  are all about surfaces this bead does not touch.
