what it needs in order to work, or where to report a problem.

The navigator raised this on 2026-08-21 and supplied copy; Cerebro filed the bead with a suggested
revision it explicitly marked as *not* decided. **Both went to the navigator during planning and the
final wording is settled** — see *User-facing decisions*, which is authoritative over anything in the
bead's own description.

One of Cerebro's changes was about accuracy rather than style and is worth restating, because it is
the reason this bead is more than copy-editing. The navigator's original opens *"Atlantis HUD is a
web based client…"*, and that sentence would sit **directly beneath the Build row**, which on a
desktop build reads `Desktop (Windows)`. v0.10.0 shipped macOS, Linux and Windows bundles and
`CLAUDE.md` states the app is deployed both ways. A player on the Windows desktop app would be told
something the line immediately above it contradicts. The chosen copy fixes that.

Two facts found during planning that shape the work:

- **`packages/shared/src/rulesets.ts` already holds the variant names.** `RULESETS` is a list of
  `{ id, label, url, ordersUploadUrl }`, with one entry today labelled `NewOrigins`. Its own doc
  comment says "There is one entry today. Adding a second is a scrape and a line here." So the About
  tab can *read* the supported variants instead of restating them in prose that would silently go
  stale on the day that second line lands. The navigator chose exactly that.
- **The desktop capability already permits the GitHub link.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`
  scopes `opener:allow-open-url` to `https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/*`, so
  `/issues/new` is inside the allowance. **No capability change is needed** — and none should be
  made, since widening that scope is a larger thing to own than this bead.

## Files to change and what to reuse

**`packages/shared/src/rulesets.ts`** — one string. `label: "NewOrigins"` becomes
`label: "New Origins"`. The `id` stays `"neworigins"` and **must not change**: a game records its
ruleset by id (`GameManifest.metadata.rulesetId`), so touching the id would orphan every saved game.
Only the human-readable label moves. Check whether any test asserts the literal `"NewOrigins"` and
update it; `rulesetById` is unaffected.

**New: `packages/shared/src/workspace/openExternal.ts`** — the shell port for opening a link, modelled
on `appUpdate.ts` line for line. Read that file first: it exists because `packages/shared` must never
import `@tauri-apps/api` ("importing `@tauri-apps/api` here would put half a desktop shell in the web
bundle"), and this port exists for the identical reason.

```ts
/** How this shell hands a URL to something that can open it. */
export type OpenExternal = (url: string) => void;

/** The web shell's answer, and the default when no shell supplies one. */
export const OPEN_EXTERNAL_IN_NEW_TAB: OpenExternal = (url) => {
  window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer");
};
```

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** — a new optional prop
`openExternal?: OpenExternal`, defaulted to `OPEN_EXTERNAL_IN_NEW_TAB` in the same destructuring
where `appUpdate = UNSUPPORTED_UPDATES` is defaulted (line 246), declared beside it in the props type
(line 271), and passed down to `SettingsDialog` beside `appUpdate` (line 2789).

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`** — threaded through the same two hops
`platformLabel` and `appUpdate` already take (lines 35/43/142 and 784/787), and the `About` component
body (lines 792–823) rewritten. This is the substance of the bead.

**`apps/desktop/src/App.tsx:25`** — `openExternal={openExternalOnDesktop}`.
**New: a small function in `apps/desktop/src/`** — `openUrl` from `@tauri-apps/plugin-opener`, the
same dynamic `await import(...)` `useDesktopAppUpdate` uses (`updateCheck.ts:34`). It may live in
`updateCheck.ts` beside `RELEASES_URL` or in a file of its own; either is fine, but it must not be
a hook — the port is a plain function.

**`apps/web/src/App.tsx:18`** — nothing to add. The default is already the web behaviour; passing it
explicitly is allowed but not required.

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`** — already renders panels in isolation
(`GlobalSettings` is exported "for `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`"). Export `About` the same way and test
it there.

## Increments

### 1 — The label

`rulesets.ts`: `"NewOrigins"` → `"New Origins"`. Run the unit suites and fix whatever asserts the old
string. Nothing else in this increment.

This is a real user-visible change beyond the About tab: the label is what the **game-settings
ruleset picker** shows. That is intended — the navigator chose one spelling everywhere rather than
two spellings of one thing.

### 2 — The `openExternal` port

`openExternal.ts` as above, exported from the package's index alongside `AppUpdateControl` and
`UNSUPPORTED_UPDATES` (follow whatever `packages/shared/src/index.ts` does for those — do not invent
a different export style).

Threaded through `AppShell` and `SettingsDialog` as described. No behaviour change yet; nothing calls
it.

Test: `OPEN_EXTERNAL_IN_NEW_TAB` calls `window.open` with the url, `"_blank"`, and
`"noopener,noreferrer"`. A plain `vi.fn()` on `window.open` — no DOM library needed.

### 3 — The About tab

Replace the `About` component's body. The wanted result, top to bottom:

1. The existing `<dl>`, now with **three** rows: `Version`, `Build`, and a new `Variants` row whose
   value is `RULESETS.map((ruleset) => ruleset.label).join(", ")`.
2. The existing `border-t border-edge pt-2` rule.
3. **The prose**, three paragraphs (exact text under *User-facing decisions*).
4. Another `border-t border-edge pt-2` rule.
5. The existing update button and status line, unchanged.

That ordering is the navigator's choice **P1**: prose below the rows, above the update control.

The `Variants` row uses the same markup as `Version` and `Build` — `dt` at `text-ink-soft`, `dd` at
`text-ink` — so it needs no new styling. Give it `data-testid="app-variants"`, matching
`data-testid="app-version"`.

The third paragraph carries the link. It is a `<button>` styled as a link, **not an `<a href>`** —
an anchor works in the browser and does nothing useful inside the Tauri webview, which is the whole
reason increment 2 exists:

```tsx
<button
  type="button"
  data-testid="about-issues-link"
  onClick={() => openExternal(ISSUES_URL)}
  className="text-select underline underline-offset-2 hover:text-brass"
>
  project's issue page on GitHub
</button>
```

with, near the top of the file:

```ts
/**
 * Where a player reports a bug or asks for a feature.
 *
 * `/issues/new` rather than `/issues`: the call to action is "describe it", so the form is the
 * right target rather than a list to hunt through. The desktop capability scopes
 * `opener:allow-open-url` to `https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/*`, so this address is
 * already inside the allowance and no capability change is needed - one that drifts outside it
 * would be refused at runtime rather than opened.
 */
const ISSUES_URL = "https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/issues/new";
```

Use the app's own colour tokens, never hex literals — `theme.test.ts` enforces this and the rest of
this file already obeys it.

### 4 — Tests

In `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, rendering `About` in isolation with `renderToStaticMarkup`:

- The three paragraphs appear, asserted on a distinctive phrase from each rather than the whole
  string — `"the play-by-email game"`, `"the particular Atlantis variant"`, `"project's issue page"`.
- The `Variants` row shows `New Origins`, and it is read from `RULESETS` rather than hardcoded:
  assert `screenText` contains `RULESETS.map((r) => r.label).join(", ")`, so the test cannot pass by
  someone typing the name into the JSX.
- **The words "web based" appear nowhere.** This is the accuracy regression the bead exists to fix
  and it is worth pinning explicitly.

A separate unit test, wherever `rulesets.ts` is tested (or a new `rulesets.test.ts`):

- `rulesetById("neworigins")` still resolves. The id survived the label change — this is the test
  that stops a well-meaning rename from orphaning every saved game.

Clicking the link is a behaviour test, and `renderToStaticMarkup` cannot click. **Do not reach for
Testing Library — this repository has neither it nor jsdom.** Cover it with a Playwright test in
`tests/smoke/` instead: open Settings, go to the About tab, and assert
`about-issues-link` is present and carries the right accessible name. Asserting that a *new tab
opens* is not worth the machinery; that the button exists and is reachable is.

### 5 — Copy check

Re-read the three paragraphs against the table in *User-facing decisions*, character for character,
including the closing full stops. This is a copy bead; a typo here is the defect.

## The test plan

Unit tests are `vitest`. Component tests use `renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server` — the
existing `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` shows the shape. **There is no jsdom and no Testing Library in
this repository**; do not add either.

`pnpm run check:fast` before the PR (lint, typecheck, unit/tooling suites, `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy`). No Rust changes, so the native suite is untouched.

One new Playwright test (increment 4). The browser suites are not run locally by default, but this
bead adds a test to them, so run `pnpm run test:smoke` once before opening the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21 over two rounds of mockups
(`docs/ui/about-tab.html`, `docs/ui/about-tab-variant.html`). **These are decided. An implementer who
disagrees raises it through the `human` queue rather than choosing differently — and in particular,
the wording in the bead's own description is superseded by the table below.**

| # | Question | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which copy ships? | **Cerebro's revision**, with its variant sentence deleted (see 4) |
| 2 | Variant names: written, or read from the build? | **Read from `RULESETS`** — it cannot go stale, and there is one spelling of the name everywhere |
| 3 | `NewOrigins` (code) or `New Origin` (the navigator's copy)? | **Neither — `New Origins`**, spaced and plural, changed in `rulesets.ts` so the whole app says it that way |
| 4 | Where does the variant name appear? | **A `Variants` row beside Version and Build.** The prose keeps no sentence about it at all — it is a fact about the build, like the version and the platform, and it grows to any number without touching a word of copy |
| 5 | Where does the prose go? | **Below the Version/Build rows, above the update control** |
| 6 | The GitHub address | **A link on the words** "project's issue page on GitHub", pointing at `/issues/new` — the form, not the list |

**The copy, exact. Three paragraphs, in this order:**

> Atlantis HUD is a client for Atlantis, the play-by-email game. It runs in a browser and as a
> desktop app.

> To work properly it needs the rules and game data for the particular Atlantis variant you are
> playing.

> If you run into a bug or would like a feature added, please describe it on the project's issue
> page on GitHub.

with `project's issue page on GitHub` as the link text in the third, and the full stop **outside**
the link.

The `Variants` row's value is `RULESETS.map((ruleset) => ruleset.label).join(", ")` — today
`New Origins`, and `New Origins, Otherworld` the day a second is added, with no copy change.

## Out of scope

- **Widening `opener:allow-open-url`.** The existing scope already covers `/issues/new`. Its own
  comment explains why it is scoped: "a webview that can ask the operating system to open anything is
  a larger thing to own than that."
- **Changing any ruleset `id`.** `"neworigins"` is what saved games record. Only the `label` moves.
- **Adding a second ruleset**, or any change to how rulesets are fetched or scraped.
- **A links section, a credits list, a licence notice, or a changelog** in the About tab. Three
  paragraphs and one link is the whole of it.
- **Anything about the update button or its status line.** They keep their position and behaviour.
- **Using `openExternal` anywhere else.** The port is added because this link needs it; retrofitting
  other links is a separate bead.
- **Translating or localising the copy.** The app has no i18n and this bead does not start one.

## Validation

1. `pnpm run check:fast` passes.
2. `pnpm run test:smoke` passes, including the new About test.
3. In the **web** build, Settings → About shows Version, Build, **Variants: New Origins**, then the
   three paragraphs, then the update button. Clicking `project's issue page on GitHub` opens
   `https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/issues/new` in a new tab.
4. In the **desktop** build, the same tab shows the same thing, and the link opens the same page in
   the player's browser rather than navigating the app's own window.
5. The words **"web based"** appear nowhere in the application.
6. The game-settings ruleset picker now reads **New Origins**, and an existing saved game still opens
   — its stored `rulesetId` of `"neworigins"` still resolves through `rulesetById`.
7. Running `pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop dev` in a plain browser (no Tauri runtime), the link
   still works via the web fallback rather than throwing.

## Known traps

- **`packages/shared` must never import `@tauri-apps/api` or any Tauri plugin.** This is why
  `appUpdate.ts` and `quitGuard.ts` exist in the shape they do, and it is why the link needs a port
  rather than a direct call. An import added here goes into the web bundle.
- **An `<a href>` is not enough.** It works in the browser and does the wrong thing inside the Tauri
  webview. The button-plus-port is the point of increment 2; replacing it with an anchor "because it
  is simpler" reintroduces exactly the bug this design avoids.
- **Do not change any ruleset `id`.** `label` and `id` sit on the same object one line apart, and
  changing the wrong one orphans every saved game. Validation item 6 is the guard.
- **The label change reaches beyond this tab.** `RULESETS[].label` is what the game-settings ruleset
  picker shows. Expect a test elsewhere to assert `"NewOrigins"`; that assertion is now wrong and
  should be updated, not worked around.
- **`theme.test.ts` scans components for hex colour literals.** The link's styling must use tokens
  (`text-select`, `text-brass`) like everything else in this file.
- **`renderToStaticMarkup` cannot click.** The click path is a smoke test, not a component test, and
  the temptation to install Testing Library to close that gap must be refused — see *The test plan*.
- **The desktop `openUrl` import is dynamic on purpose.** `updateCheck.ts:34` does
  `await import("@tauri-apps/plugin-opener")` inside the handler; copy that, and catch the rejection.
  The ACL can refuse, and there may be no browser to hand the page to.
- **Disk space.** Ten of this repository's retrospectives name `scripts/diskPreflight.ts` refusing to
  start a bead below its 8 GB floor, and it can trip again mid-`check:fast`, where it surfaces as a
  failing *tooling* test that reads like a defect in the diff. If that happens it is a full disk, not
  your change. Safe offline reclaims: `~/.cargo/registry/src`, `target/debug/incremental`,
  `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache`.

title: Clicking a fleet asks the dictionary for a name that cannot exist
description:
Found during verification of ah-3pr9 (2026-08-21, origin/main a003d41). That bead passed - fleets draw as ships, `Fleet, 6 Airships` still works, and the Ships badge counts vessels - and this is the follow-up filed alongside the pass.

## What the player sees

The navigator's words: "When clicking on a fleet, the game data dialog comes up, but the search shown there is for the fleet summary, e.g. 'Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons'. There should be different links for Galleons, Galleys and Balloons."

In the region pane, a structure's kind is a link into the game-data dictionary (`ah-5jkt.2`). For an ordinary structure that is right: `Fort` links to the Fort entry. For a fleet, the whole vessel manifest is one link, so clicking `Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons` asks the dictionary for an entry of that name, which cannot exist. The player is shown a dead end where four real entries were named.

## The cause

`packages/shared/src/workspace/RegionPanel.tsx:239` wraps the entire kind in one link:

    <GameDataLink entryId={buildingEntryId(structure.kind)} onOpen={linkable}>
      {structure.kind}
    </GameDataLink>

The comment above it records the reasoning - "The kind alone is the catalogue entry" - which holds for every structure except a vessel-bearing one, where the kind is a manifest rather than a name. `buildingEntryId()` is also the wrong lookup for these: Galleons and Balloons are **items** (the Ships tab of `ah-5jkt.1`), not buildings.

## The parsing already exists

`ah-3pr9` added `vesselCount()` (`hexView.ts:283`), which splits exactly these segments to total the badge:

    const parts = kind.split(",").slice(1);
    ... /^\s*(\d+)\b/u.exec(part)

So the same split that produces `61` for Frozen Tomb also yields the four names this bead wants linked. Whatever shape is chosen should share that rule rather than write a second one - two parsers disagreeing about a manifest is how the count and the links would drift apart.

## Worth deciding at planning

- **What the leading word is.** In `Galley, 40 Galleons, ...` the first segment is the vessel *kind* of the structure itself, not a counted entry - `vesselCount` deliberately drops it with `.slice(1)`. Whether it should also be a link, and to what, is a real question.
- **Whether the counts stay plain.** Linking `Galleons` while leaving `40` as text is probably right, but it is a decision about what the link text is.
- **The singular/plural mismatch.** The report writes `40 Galleons`; the catalogue entry is presumably singular. Something has to map one to the other, and getting it wrong yields a dead link rather than a wrong one.
- **A vessel the catalogue does not describe.** `ah-5jkt.2` already decided that a structure kind the catalogue lacks still opens the dialog and says so; the same rule presumably applies, but it should be stated rather than assumed.

## Acceptance

Clicking a fleet's manifest in the region pane offers a separate link per named vessel, each opening that vessel's entry in the dictionary. The vessel names come from the same split that `vesselCount` uses. Nothing changes for a structure whose kind is a single name.
design:
## Context

Found by Psylocke verifying **ah-3pr9** (which passed). The navigator's words:

> *"When clicking on a fleet, the game data dialog comes up, but the search shown there is for the
> fleet summary, e.g. 'Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons'. There should be different links
> for Galleons, Galleys and Balloons."*

In the region pane a structure's kind is a link into the dictionary (ah-5jkt.2). For an ordinary
structure that is right — `Fort` links to the Fort entry. For a fleet, **the whole manifest is one
link**, so the dictionary is asked for an entry of that name, which cannot exist.

**Two things are wrong, not one**, and I confirmed both against `origin/main`:

1. **The span.** `RegionPanel.tsx:238-244` wraps the entire `structure.kind` in one `GameDataLink`.
2. **The lookup.** `buildingEntryId(kind)` is `` `building:${kind.toUpperCase()}` ``
   (`gameData.ts:202-204`) — it searches **buildings**, and every vessel is a **ship** entry.

**Every vessel type is in the catalogue, singular, with a tag** — measured from
`config/public/ruleset.json`:

```
Longship LONG   Raft RAFT   Cog COG      Galleon GALL   Galley GLLY
Corsair CORS    Balloon BALL   Airship AIRS   Cloudship CLOU
```

So every name in a manifest has somewhere real to go.

**The same defect reaches beyond fleets.** `Ship [623] : Galley` has no comma and is not a manifest,
but its link also asks for a *building* called Galley and is dead for the same reason. The navigator
chose to fix that here.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. One lookup that answers for any structure kind — `gameData.ts`

`itemEntryId(index, tag)` (`:186-193`) already walks `ITEM_KINDS` looking for `` `${category}:${tag}` ``
— but it takes a **tag**, and a report gives a **name**. Ship ids are keyed by tag
(`ship:GALL`, `:242`) while building ids are keyed by name (`:247`), so **there is no name→entry path
for a vessel today.** That is the gap.

Add one:

```ts
/**
 * The entry a name in a report refers to, or null (ah-t5fk).
 *
 * Ships first, then buildings, because a structure's kind can be either and only the catalogue
 * knows which: `Galley` is a ship, `Fort` is a building, and no hand-kept list of vessel words has
 * to be maintained beside the data. `SHIP_KINDS` in `hexView.ts` is deliberately NOT consulted -
 * ah-lcyn is a whole bead about an enumerated list failing on the kind nobody listed.
 *
 * Plural spellings are tried the way `isKeyword` (`orderCase.ts:33`) does, which mirrors the Rust
 * core's `item_spellings`: the word as written first, then without a trailing `ES`, then without a
 * trailing `S`. A report writes `40 Galleons`; the entry is `Galleon`.
 */
export function structureEntryId(index: GameDataIndex, name: string): string | null
```

**As-written first, then stripped** — that ordering matters: a vessel whose name genuinely ends in
`s` must be found before anything is removed from it.

Lookup by name needs a name→entry search over `index.entries` filtered to `ship` (then the building
id built as today). A linear scan is fine — ~270 entries, a handful of links per pane — but building
a `byName` map at parse time is equally acceptable; **the implementer's call, and worth a comment
either way.**

### 2. The manifest becomes several links — `RegionPanel.tsx:231-247`

Split the kind and render a link per named vessel, **counts left plain**:

```
Frozen Tomb [194] : Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons
                    ^^^^^^     ^^^^^^^^     ^^^^^^^     ^^^^^^^^
```

**Share ah-3pr9's split, do not write a second one.** `vesselCount` (`hexView.ts`) already splits
exactly these segments to total the badge:

```ts
const parts = kind.split(",").slice(1);
… /^\s*(\d+)\b/u.exec(part)
```

Two parsers disagreeing about a manifest is how the count and the links drift apart. **Extract the
segment split into something both call**, rather than copying the regex.

**The leading segment is linked too** (`Galley`), on the navigator's choice: it is a vessel name with
a real entry, every vessel word in the line then behaves the same way, and it is what keeps
`Ship [623] : Galley` clickable. **Note in a comment that `vesselCount` deliberately drops it with
`.slice(1)`** — ah-3pr9 established the leading word is a label, not a vessel (`Cloudship, 14
Cloudships` totals 14, not 15) — **so the two uses of the same split differ on purpose**, and a later
reader must not "fix" one to match the other.

**A name the catalogue lacks is still a link.** ah-5jkt.2 already decided this for structure kinds:
an id the index does not hold still opens the dialog and says the entry is absent —
*"saying so is the whole point of landing there"* (`gameDataDialogState.ts:66-69`).

**The comment at `:233-236` must be rewritten.** It says *"The kind alone is the catalogue entry"*,
which is exactly the assumption this bead disproves.

### 3. Unchanged

The structure's own name and number stay plain (`structureLabelParts(structure).prefix`), `, needs N`
stays plain, and `linkable` still gates the whole thing. **A kind with no comma and no vessel name —
`Fort`, `Mine`, `Stockade` — must resolve to exactly the building entry it does today.**

## Increments

1. **A name resolves to the right entry.**
   RED: `gameData.test.ts` — `Galley` → `ship:GLLY`; `Galleons` → `ship:GALL` (plural);
   `Fort` → `building:FORT`; **`Mine` → `building:MINE`** (unchanged); an unknown name → null.
   GREEN: `structureEntryId`.
2. **The split is shared.**
   RED: a test that the segment split used by the pane and by `vesselCount` is the same function.
   GREEN: extract it.
3. **A manifest is several links.**
   RED: `RegionPanel` tests — `Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons` renders **four** links
   with texts `Galley`, `Galleons`, `Galleys`, `Balloons`, and the counts as plain text.
   GREEN: the render.
4. **Everything else keeps its single link.**
   RED: `Fort` renders one link to `building:FORT`; **`Galley` alone renders one link to `ship:GLLY`**
   (today dead); `Stockade` with `needs` renders one link and the needs stays plain.
   GREEN: nothing new — increment 1 covers it. **If this fails, the comma rule is being used to
   decide ship-vs-building**, which it must not be.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `Galley resolves to the ship entry` | `gameData.test.ts` | the lookup |
| **`Galleons resolves to Galleon`** | same | the plural rule |
| `a name ending in s is tried as written first` | same | the ordering |
| `Fort and Mine still resolve to buildings` | same | **no regression on ordinary structures** |
| an unknown name resolves to null | same | §5's decision |
| **`a fleet manifest renders one link per vessel`** | `RegionPanel` tests | the bead |
| `the counts are not links` | same | the chosen span |
| **`a single-vessel structure links to the ship entry`** | same | the widened scope |
| `a building structure is unchanged` | same | the regression that matters |
| `an unknown vessel is still a link` | same | §5 |
| `the structure's name, number and needs stay plain` | same | unchanged |
| `vesselCount still totals 61 and 18` | `hexView` tests | **ah-3pr9 must not move** |

**Every string from `tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep`.** Synthetic words hid ah-o0d3 and ah-lcyn both.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-21 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-t5fk-fleet-links.html`,
committed to `docs/ui/`.

**Q1 — the link span.** Chosen: **the vessel names only, counts plain.** The link text is exactly what
the link opens, and the count stays the player's rather than the catalogue's. Accepted cost: four
short words in a row, each its own small target. Rejected: **count and name together**, which gives
bigger targets but makes `40 Galleons` open a page about one Galleon — a promise not kept.

**Q2 — the leading word.** Chosen: **link it like any other vessel name.** It has a real entry, every
vessel word behaves alike, and it keeps `Ship [623] : Galley` clickable. Accepted cost: it is not part
of the tally, so linking it may imply one more Galley. Rejected: **leaving it plain**, which would
make the word a player is most likely to click do nothing, and would strip a single-vessel structure
of its link entirely.

**Q3 — a vessel the catalogue lacks.** Chosen: **still a link; the dialog says the entry is absent**,
consistent with ah-5jkt.2. Rejected: plain text, which gives a ragged line with no visible reason and
contradicts a rule already set.

**Q4 — single-vessel structures.** Chosen: **look up ship first, then building, for every structure.**
One data-driven rule, no second list, and the dead `Ship [623] : Galley` link is fixed by the same
code. Accepted cost: every structure's lookup gains a step. Rejected: fixing only comma-bearing kinds
(leaves the same defect for someone to re-file) and **using `SHIP_KINDS`** (a hand-kept word list —
`ah-lcyn` is a whole bead about that shape failing).

## Out of scope

- **`vesselCount` and the Ships badge** — ah-3pr9's, and their numbers must not move.
- **The map's `classify()` and `SHIP_KINDS`** — deliberately not consulted here.
- **The dictionary's contents or its Ships tab** — ah-5jkt.1's.
- **Linking anything else in the region pane** — the structure's own name and number stay plain, by
  ah-5jkt.2's reasoning that *"linking `Odds and Ends` would look right and open nothing"*.
- **Showing a vessel breakdown anywhere else.**

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by hand, with the turn-71 report:

1. Find **`Frozen Tomb [194]`** in the region pane. Its kind shows **four separate links** —
   `Galley`, `Galleons`, `Galleys`, `Balloons` — with `40`, `11` and `10` as plain text.
   **This is the acceptance.**
2. Click **`Galleons`**: the dictionary opens on **Galleon**, on the **Ships** tab. Not a dead end,
   and not a building.
3. Click the leading **`Galley`**: it opens Galley.
4. Find **`Ship [623] : Galley`** (turn-39, game 5) and confirm its single link now opens the
   **Galley ship entry** — it was dead before.
5. Find an ordinary building — a **Fort**, a **Mine**, a **Stockade, needs 20** — and confirm it
   still opens the **building** entry exactly as before, with the needs still plain. **This is the
   regression that matters.**
6. Confirm the **Ships badge still counts 61** for Frozen Tomb — ah-3pr9's number must not have
   moved.
7. Confirm the structure's own name and `[194]` are still plain text.

## Known traps

- **`buildingEntryId` is the wrong lookup for a vessel.** Ship ids are keyed by **tag**
  (`ship:GALL`), building ids by **name** (`building:FORT`). A name→entry search is new work; it does
  not already exist.
- **Do not use the comma to decide ship-vs-building.** `Galley` has no comma and is a ship; `Mine`
  has no comma and is a building. Only the catalogue knows, which is why the lookup asks it.
- **Do not consult `SHIP_KINDS`.** A hand-kept list of vessel words is exactly the shape ah-lcyn
  exists to remove.
- **Share ah-3pr9's split; do not copy the regex.** Two parsers disagreeing about one manifest is how
  the badge count and the links drift apart.
- **`vesselCount` drops the leading segment and this bead links it — on purpose.** ah-3pr9 proved the
  leading word is a label, not a vessel. Say so in a comment, or someone will "fix" the inconsistency
  and break the badge.
- **Try the name as written before stripping a plural.** Strip-first would miss a vessel whose real
  name ends in `s`.
- **Rewrite the comment at `RegionPanel.tsx:233-236`.** *"The kind alone is the catalogue entry"* is
  the assumption this bead disproves.
- **An ordinary building must resolve exactly as it does today.** That is the one way this change can
  do damage, and increment 4 exists for it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fleet's manifest renders one link per named vessel: "Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys, 10 Balloons" gives four links reading Galley, Galleons, Galleys, Balloons, with 40, 11 and 10 as plain text.
- Each link opens that vessel's entry on the Ships tab - Galleons opens Galleon - not a building lookup.
- A new name-to-entry lookup resolves ships first, then buildings, for EVERY structure kind. `SHIP_KINDS` is NOT consulted and no hand-kept list of vessel words is introduced.
- Plural spellings are tried as `isKeyword` does (orderCase.ts:33): the word as written FIRST, then without a trailing ES, then without a trailing S.
- A single-vessel structure ("Ship [623] : Galley") links to the Galley ship entry - it is dead today for the same reason as the fleet.
- An ordinary building (Fort, Mine, "Stockade, needs 20") resolves to exactly the building entry it does today, with `needs` still plain. This is the regression that matters.
- A vessel name the catalogue lacks is still a link; the dialog opens and says the entry is absent, per ah-5jkt.2.
- The segment split is SHARED with ah-3pr9's vesselCount rather than copied - one parser, not two.
- A comment records that vesselCount drops the leading segment while this bead links it, on purpose, so nobody "fixes" the difference and breaks the badge.
- The Ships badge still counts 61 for Frozen Tomb; no ah-3pr9 number moves.
- The structure's own name and number stay plain, and the comment at RegionPanel.tsx:233-236 ("The kind alone is the catalogue entry") is rewritten.
- Every test string comes from tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep.
- `pnpm run check:fast` passes.

title: Order OCD indents nested FORM and TURN blocks and ends each unit's orders with one blank line
description:
Two more things Order OCD should do. The navigator's words, 2026-08-21:

1. "Automatically set one space indentation on every level in a nested FORM and
   TURN."

2. "Ensure there is always one and only one newline at the end of each order, so
   when the user clicks in the order editor below all text, the cursor always
   start on a new line, below the last order."

WHY THE SECOND ONE MATTERS. It is described in terms of the symptom rather than
the rule: clicking in the editor below the last order should put the cursor on a
fresh line ready to type, not at the end of the last order. Today that depends
on whether a trailing newline happens to be there.

CONTEXT. Order OCD already exists and tidies case. ah-1znc (v0.10.0) fixed the
case where the first unit opened in a session kept its untidied orders until the
player clicked away and back, so the "tidied when the unit is next opened"
behaviour is the one these two additions inherit.

FOR THE PLANNER. Worth settling with the navigator: whether the indentation rule
applies to orders the player has already written by hand with different
indentation, given ah-1znc's history of that exact question -- E1 (never touch
existing text) was considered and rejected during that bead's planning because
"a half-written turn stays mixed, which is what the OCD player minds most".
design:
## Context

**Order OCD** is a settings toggle (`settingsStore.orderOcd`, `SettingsDialog.tsx:377`) that today
does exactly one thing: it uppercases the order keywords the player types. It works on two clocks —
as the word ends (an `EditorView.inputHandler` in `OrdersEditor.tsx` that shouts the word in the same
transaction as the space or newline that finished it), and as a **whole-block tidy** that runs
whenever it can (the effect keyed on `[externalRevision, unitId, orderOcd, vocabulary]` near the
bottom of `OrdersEditor.tsx`). That second clock is what `ah-1znc` settled: the tidy runs when a unit
is next opened, when the setting is switched on with a unit already open, when the core's word list
arrives late, and when a draft is restored asynchronously after a reload.

This bead adds two more things to the same setting, in the navigator's words (2026-08-21):

1. *"Automatically set one space indentation on every level in a nested FORM and TURN."*
2. *"Ensure there is always one and only one newline at the end of each order, so when the user
   clicks in the order editor below all text, the cursor always start on a new line, below the last
   order."*

The second is stated as a symptom rather than a rule, and that is the useful framing: clicking in the
empty space below the last order should put the caret on a fresh line ready to type. That happens
when the block's text ends in a newline. **Half of this already exists** — `shownUnitText`
(`orderEditor.ts`) appends a newline to what the editor shows — but only *once a save has landed*
(`savedAt !== null`), and nothing anywhere collapses the extra blank lines a player left behind.

Block structure is already walked once, authoritatively, in Rust: `crates/core/src/orders/walk.rs`.
That module exists because four readers used to keep the walk each and had drifted apart. **This bead
does not call it** — it is a synchronous, per-keystroke need in the editor, and `orderCase.ts` sets
the precedent for exactly this ("All real lexing lives in Rust; this is the small amount of that
knowledge the editor needs"). What it does do is mirror `walk.rs`'s three rules faithfully and say so
in a comment: `END` closes only a `FORM` and `ENDTURN` only a `TURN`; a closer that matches nothing
is stray and changes no depth; a `unit` line or a `#` directive abandons everything still open.

## Files to change and what to reuse

**New: `packages/shared/src/orderIndent.ts`** — the whole of the new logic, as pure string functions.
Nothing in it touches CodeMirror or React.

**New: `packages/shared/src/orderIndent.test.ts`** — its unit tests.

**`packages/shared/src/orderCase.ts`** — unchanged except that `CaseChange` and `bareWords` are now
imported by the new module. Re-export nothing; `orderIndent.ts` imports what it needs.

Reuse, and do not re-implement:

- `bareWords(line)` (`orderCase.ts`) gives a line's words outside quotes and before any `;` comment,
  with `@` stripped from the front. **That `@`-stripping is exactly right here**: `walk.rs`'s own
  test `summarize("@turn\nWORK\nEndturn\n")` shows `@turn` opens a TURN block, and `bareWords` makes
  `@turn` read as `turn`. A line that is only `@;` yields no bare words at all, which is also right.
- `CaseChange` (`orderCase.ts`) — `{ from, to, insert }` in whole-block offsets. Indent edits are
  described in the same shape so the two lists can be merged.
- `keywordCaseChanges(text, vocabulary, protect)` (`orderCase.ts`) — unchanged, still the source of
  the case edits.
- `withoutTrailingBlankLines(text)` (`ordersDocument.ts`) — already drops trailing whitespace-only
  lines. This is the exact primitive the trailing-newline rule needs; use it rather than writing a
  second one.
- `shownUnitText(text, savedAt)` (`orderEditor.ts`) — **leave it alone.** It is the "what the editor
  shows once saved" rule and this bead does not change it. The new rule is stricter and runs on the
  tidy's clock; the two agree wherever both apply, because both end the text in exactly one newline.

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx`** — four changes, all inside the existing
`useLayoutEffect` that builds the editor, plus one to the existing tidy effect. Detailed under
*Increments*.

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx:377-382`** — the `description` string only.

**`tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`** — new tests alongside the three that already cover Order OCD
(they start at line 328 with the `enableOrderOcd` helper; reuse it).

## Increments

Each increment is a commit, tests first.

### 1 — `orderIndent.ts`: the depth walk

```ts
/** How deep each line of a block sits: the number of enclosing TURN and FORM blocks. */
export function lineDepths(text: string): number[];
```

One entry per line of `text.split("\n")`, giving the depth **the line itself should be indented to**
— which for a closer is the depth *outside* the block it closes, and for an opener is the depth
outside the block it opens.

Mirror `walk.rs` exactly, keeping a stack of `"turn" | "form"`:

- Take `bareWords(line)[0]`; if there is none, the line sits at the current depth and nothing changes.
- The raw first token of the line starting with `#`, **or** the first bare word being `unit`
  (case-insensitively): the stack is emptied, the line sits at depth 0. (Neither occurs inside a
  unit's own block, which is all the editor ever holds — mirrored because `walk.rs` does it and
  because a pasted region banner could bring one in.)
- First word `TURN` → the line sits at the current depth, then push `"turn"`.
  First word `FORM` → same, push `"form"`.
- First word `ENDTURN` → if the top of the stack is `"turn"`, pop it and **the line sits at the new,
  shallower depth**. Otherwise it is stray: the line sits at the current depth and the stack is
  untouched. `END` → the same against `"form"`.
- Anything else: the current depth.

All keyword matching is case-insensitive (`toUpperCase()`), and it is a **plain equality test**, not
`isKeyword` — these four words are grammar, and the vocabulary is not consulted.

Tests (`orderIndent.test.ts`), each asserting the whole depth array:

| input | depths |
|---|---|
| `"WORK\nSTUDY COMBAT"` | `[0, 0]` |
| `"TURN\nWORK\nENDTURN"` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| `"TURN\nFORM 1\nWORK\nEND\nMOVE N\nENDTURN\nWORK"` | `[0, 1, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]` |
| `"@turn\nWORK\nEndturn"` | `[0, 1, 0]` — case, and the `@` prefix |
| `"FORM 1\nWORK"` (never closed) | `[0, 1]` |
| `"FORM 1\nWORK\nENDTURN\nMOVE N"` (stray closer, wrong kind) | `[0, 1, 1, 1]` |
| `"WORK\nEND\nSTUDY COMBAT"` (stray closer, nothing open) | `[0, 0, 0]` |
| `"TURN\nunit 42\nWORK"` | `[0, 0, 0]` — `unit` abandons |
| `"TURN\n#end\nWORK"` | `[0, 0, 0]` — a directive abandons |
| `"TURN\n; a note\n\nWORK\nENDTURN"` | `[0, 1, 1, 1, 0]` |
| `'TURN\nNAME UNIT "END of the line"\nENDTURN'` | `[0, 1, 0]` — quoted text is not grammar |
| `"TURN\nWORK ; END\nENDTURN"` | `[0, 1, 0]` — after `;` is not grammar |

### 2 — `orderIndent.ts`: the edits

```ts
/** One space per level: the leading-whitespace replacements, in whole-block offsets. */
export function indentChanges(text: string): CaseChange[];
/** The block with every line indented to its depth. */
export function indentBlock(text: string): string;
```

For each line, the wanted indent is `" ".repeat(depth)` and the span replaced is the line's existing
leading whitespace — `line.length - line.trimStart().length` characters from the line's start. Emit
nothing when the two already agree, and **emit nothing at all for a line whose `trim()` is empty**:
blank lines stay truly empty, so no invisible whitespace is ever written into an orders file
(navigator's decision, section 2 of the second mockup).

`indentBlock` applies them back-to-front, exactly as `uppercaseKeywords` applies case changes.

Tests, at minimum:

- The three-level example above round-trips to
  `"TURN\n NAME UNIT \"Scout\"\n FORM 1\n  NAME UNIT \"New\"\n  STUDY COMBAT\n END\n MOVE N\nENDTURN\nWORK"`.
- A line the player indented with four spaces, or with a tab, is replaced — **all** leading
  whitespace goes, whatever it was.
- An already-correct block yields `indentChanges(...) === []` and `indentBlock(t) === t`. Assert the
  empty array, not just the unchanged string: the editor's "nothing to do, do not dispatch" gate
  hangs off it.
- A blank line inside a nested block gains nothing: `"TURN\nWORK\n\nMOVE N\nENDTURN"` →
  `"TURN\n WORK\n\n MOVE N\nENDTURN"`, with a genuinely empty third line.
- A comment line indents like any other: `"TURN\n; note\nWORK\nENDTURN"` →
  `"TURN\n ; note\n WORK\nENDTURN"`. Same for `@;`.
- An unclosed `FORM` indents everything below it to the running depth (navigator's decision A,
  section 1 of the second mockup): `"TURN\nFORM 1\nWORK\nMOVE N"` →
  `"TURN\n FORM 1\n  WORK\n  MOVE N"`. There is deliberately **no** "leave a broken block alone"
  path; the runaway indent is the signal.

### 3 — `orderIndent.ts`: the trailing newline

```ts
/** The block ending in exactly one newline — and an empty block left empty. */
export function withSingleTrailingNewline(text: string): string;
/** The one edit that achieves it, or null when there is nothing to do. */
export function trailingNewlineChange(text: string): CaseChange | null;
```

`withSingleTrailingNewline`: `withoutTrailingBlankLines(text)` (from `ordersDocument.ts`); if that is
`""` return `""`, otherwise return it with a single `"\n"` appended.

`trailingNewlineChange` describes the same thing as one splice: `from` is the end of the kept text,
`to` is `text.length`, `insert` is `"\n"`. `null` when `withSingleTrailingNewline(text) === text`.

Tests:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `""` | `""` — an empty unit stays empty (navigator's decision, section 3 of the second mockup) |
| `"WORK"` | `"WORK\n"` |
| `"WORK\n"` | `"WORK\n"` — idempotent, and `trailingNewlineChange` is `null` |
| `"WORK\n\n\n"` | `"WORK\n"` |
| `"WORK\n   \n\t\n"` | `"WORK\n"` — whitespace-only lines count as blank |
| `"\n\n"` | `""` — nothing but blank lines is an empty unit |

**Why empty stays empty**: a blank line written into an untouched draft is a line the player never
opened, and it would dirty and save a unit merely because it was looked at. An empty editor already
puts the caret on line one, so the reported symptom cannot arise there.

### 4 — `orderIndent.ts`: the one function the editor calls

```ts
/** Every edit the whole-block tidy wants, in whole-block offsets, ordered by `from`. */
export function tidyChanges(
  text: string,
  vocabulary: Vocabulary,
  protect: number | null
): CaseChange[];
```

`keywordCaseChanges(text, vocabulary, protect)` merged with `indentChanges(text)` and, last,
`trailingNewlineChange(text)` if it is not null. Sort by `from` ascending and return.

**The three kinds can never overlap, and that is what makes merging safe.** A case change covers a
bare word, which by construction starts after the line's leading whitespace; an indent change covers
exactly that leading whitespace; the trailing-newline change covers only the run of blank lines at
the very end, which contains no bare words and (increment 2) is emitted no indent edits. Assert this
directly in a test: a block that wants all three at once yields a strictly ordered,
non-overlapping list.

### 5 — `OrdersEditor.tsx`: the whole-block tidy learns the other two rules

The existing effect keyed `[externalRevision, unitId, orderOcd, vocabulary]` changes in exactly two
places. Do not move it, do not re-key it, and do not touch the comment block above it explaining why
it is declared after the `externalRevision` effect — `ah-1znc`'s retrospective is about precisely
that ordering, and it must survive.

```ts
const changes = tidyChanges(editor.state.doc.toString(), vocabulary, protect);
if (changes.length === 0) {
  return;
}
const lengthPreserving = changes.every((c) => c.insert.length === c.to - c.from);
editor.dispatch({
  changes,
  ...(protect === null || !lengthPreserving ? {} : { selection: editor.state.selection }),
  annotations: [Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)]
});
```

Two things about that:

- **The selection is only restated when every edit is length-preserving.** The existing code restates
  it unconditionally because case edits are exactly as long as what they replace, so a caret sitting
  on a replacement boundary would otherwise map to the far side of it. Indent and newline edits
  change lengths, and restating a stale offset there would move the caret into the wrong column —
  so in that case CodeMirror's own mapping is the correct answer and the selection is left out.
- **Still deliberately not `External`, still out of the history** — unchanged from today, and for the
  same two reasons the existing comment gives. The navigator chose *"Enter is one step; the tidy is
  not undoable"* (section 2 of the third mockup); this line is what implements it, so leave it.

`protect` keeps its current meaning and is passed straight through: the word the caret is inside is
still left as typed. There is deliberately **no** equivalent protection for the caret's *line* —
indentation is not "a word half typed", and with increment 6 in place a focused block's indentation
is already right, so a focused tidy finds little to do.

### 6 — `OrdersEditor.tsx`: Enter indents the new line

A keybinding placed **before** `editingKeymap` in the `keymap.of([...])` array, so it beats
`defaultKeymap`'s `insertNewlineAndIndent`, and after `autocompletion`'s own extension so an open
completion popup still takes Enter first (that ordering is already how the file is built — do not
reorder the extension array).

```ts
{
  key: "Enter",
  run: (editor) => {
    if (!latest.current.orderOcd) return false;
    const { from, to } = editor.state.selection.main;
    const before = editor.state.doc.sliceString(0, from);
    // The depth the *next* line will sit at. `lineDepths` reports an opener at the depth outside
    // its own block, so asking it for a hypothetical empty line appended after the caret is what
    // turns "the caret is on a FORM line" into "the next line is one level deeper".
    const depth = lineDepths(`${before}\n`).at(-1) ?? 0;
    const insert = `\n${" ".repeat(depth)}`;
    editor.dispatch({
      changes: { from, to, insert },
      selection: { anchor: from + insert.length },
      scrollIntoView: true,
      userEvent: "input"
    });
    return true;
  }
}
```

Computing the depth from the text *before the caret only* is deliberate: it is what makes the answer
right while the block below is still being written. Worked examples, all with the caret at the end:
`"TURN"` → depth 1; `"TURN\n FORM 1"` → depth 2; `"TURN\n WORK"` → depth 1; `"TURN\n FOR"` (still
typing the keyword) → depth 1, and the on-open tidy corrects it once the word is finished.

- **One transaction, so one `Ctrl+Z` takes back the newline and its indent together** — the
  navigator's choice, and the same promise the keyword-shouting handler already makes.
- `userEvent: "input"` **is** set here, unlike in the shouting handler: this is ordinary typing and
  history should group a run of it as usual. (The shouting handler omits it for a stated reason that
  does not apply to a plain newline.)
- A non-empty selection is replaced, which is what Enter does everywhere.
- Returning `false` when the setting is off leaves stock behaviour completely untouched.
- **Backspace is not bound.** The navigator chose stock CodeMirror: one press deletes one space
  (section 1 of the third mockup). Nothing to do — just do not be tempted.

### 7 — `OrdersEditor.tsx`: paste is tidied as it lands

`EditorView.domEventHandlers({ paste })`, added to the extension array:

```ts
EditorView.domEventHandlers({
  paste(event, editor) {
    if (!latest.current.orderOcd || latest.current.vocabulary.size === 0) return false;
    const text = event.clipboardData?.getData("text/plain");
    if (!text) return false;
    const { from, to } = editor.state.selection.main;
    const base = lineDepths(editor.state.doc.sliceString(0, from)).at(-1) ?? 0;
    const insert = tidyInsertion(text, base, latest.current.vocabulary);
    event.preventDefault();
    editor.dispatch({
      changes: { from, to, insert },
      selection: { anchor: from + insert.length },
      scrollIntoView: true,
      userEvent: "input.paste"
    });
    return true;
  }
})
```

with, in `orderIndent.ts`:

```ts
/** Pasted text, uppercased and re-indented as if it had been typed at `baseDepth`. */
export function tidyInsertion(text: string, baseDepth: number, vocabulary: Vocabulary): string;
```

`uppercaseKeywords(text, vocabulary)` first; then indent **every line after the first** to
`baseDepth + lineDepths(text)[i]`, leaving the first line's leading whitespace alone — it is
continuing whatever the caret was already on, and re-indenting it would move text the paste is not
responsible for. Blank lines gain nothing, as everywhere else.

Tests for `tidyInsertion`: a flat two-line paste at base 1 gains one space on its second line only;
`"form 1\nstudy combat\nend"` at base 0 becomes `"FORM 1\n STUDY COMBAT\nEND"`; a single-line paste
is uppercased and otherwise untouched at any base.

One transaction again, so one `Ctrl+Z` removes the whole pasted, tidied block. Returning `false` when
the setting is off, when the vocabulary has not arrived, or when there is no plain text means the
browser's own paste happens exactly as it does today.

### 8 — The setting's description

`SettingsDialog.tsx:379`, replaced with the navigator's chosen wording **verbatim**:

> Uppercase the command keywords as you write, indent each level of a nested FORM or TURN by one
> space, and end every unit's orders with a single blank line. Text inside quotes is left alone.

### 9 — Smoke tests

In `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`, after the three existing Order OCD tests, reusing
`enableOrderOcd`, `loadReport`, `selectUnit`, `fillOrders`, `ordersInput` and `expectOrders`:

1. **Enter inside a block opens an indented line.** OCD on, type `TURN`, Enter, `FORM 1`, Enter,
   `work`, and assert the text is `TURN\n FORM 1\n  WORK` — this proves the keyword shouting and the
   auto-indent coexist in one line of typing.
2. **Opening a unit re-indents its whole block.** `fillOrders(page, "turn\nform 1\nstudy combat\nend\nendturn")`
   *before* enabling OCD, then enable it, and assert
   `TURN\n FORM 1\n  STUDY COMBAT\n END\nENDTURN`. Mirrors the existing "turning Order OCD on tidies
   the unit already on screen" test, which is the cheapest way to trigger the tidy.
3. **Trailing blank lines collapse when the tidy runs, and not before.** With OCD on, put the caret
   at the end and press Enter three times; assert the blank lines are still there (Enter is not
   absorbed — the navigator's decision, section 3 of the first mockup). Then switch the setting off
   and on again and assert the block now ends in exactly one newline.
4. **Undo after Enter is one press.** OCD on, in a `TURN` block, `waitForTimeout(700)` to clear
   history's grouping window (the existing test does this, with a comment explaining why), press
   Enter, then `ControlOrMeta+z`, and assert both the newline and its indent are gone.

## The test plan

Unit tests are `vitest` in `packages/shared/src/orderIndent.test.ts`, following
`orderCase.test.ts`'s shape exactly — plain function calls on strings, no DOM, no React. **There is
no jsdom and no Testing Library in this repository**; component tests use
`renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server`, and nothing here needs even that.

Every function in `orderIndent.ts` gets direct tests; the tables under increments 1, 2, 3 and 7 are
the minimum set and are written first, red, before the function exists.

Browser behaviour — the keymap, the paste handler, the tidy effect — is covered by the four
Playwright tests in increment 9 and nowhere else. Do not try to unit-test `OrdersEditor.tsx`.

`pnpm run check:fast` before the PR (lint, typecheck, unit and tooling suites, `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy`). This bead changes editor behaviour, so **also run `pnpm run test:smoke` locally**
before opening the PR rather than leaving it to CI — the four new smoke tests are the only proof
increments 5, 6 and 7 work at all, and a failure there is much cheaper found locally.

No Rust changes, so the native suite is untouched.

## User-facing decisions

All ten settled with the navigator on 2026-08-21, over three rounds of mockups. The mockups are
`docs/ui/order-ocd-indent.html`, `docs/ui/order-ocd-indent-edges.html` and
`docs/ui/order-ocd-indent-keys.html` (committed by the planning session). **These are decided. An
implementer that finds one of them awkward to build raises it through the `human` queue rather than
choosing differently.**

| # | Question | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | When is the indentation applied? | **Both**: Enter indents the new line as you type, *and* the whole block is re-indented when the tidy runs | The indentation is right while you write rather than only after clicking away and back; imports, pastes and hand-typed text all end up the same |
| 2 | Where do `END` and `ENDTURN` sit? | **Aligned with their openers** — only the block's contents are indented | The pair brackets the indented run, so a missing `END` is visible at a glance |
| 3 | How strictly is "exactly one newline" held? | **Fixed up when the tidy runs**, not continuously | Enter still opens as many lines as you press it; Enter silently not working gets reported as broken |
| 4 | An unclosed `FORM`, or a stray closer? | **Indent by the running depth anyway** | The runaway indent is itself the signal that a block was left open; one rule, no special cases |
| 5 | Comment lines? | **Indented like any other line**, `;` and `@;` alike | A note lines up with the orders it is about, and `@;` is an order the server acts on |
| 6 | Blank lines inside a block? | **Left truly empty** | Nothing invisible is ever written into an orders file |
| 7 | A unit with no orders at all? | **Stays empty** | An empty editor already puts the caret on line one; a blank line would dirty and save a draft the player never touched |
| 8 | Backspace on an auto-indented line? | **Stock CodeMirror** — deletes one space | Backspace means the same thing everywhere in the editor; orders rarely nest past two levels |
| 9 | What does `Ctrl+Z` reach? | **Enter is one step; the whole-block tidy is not undoable at all** | Matches the precedent set for keyword shouting; undo never rewinds past something you typed to reach something you did not |
| 10 | Pasted orders? | **Tidied as they land**, in the same transaction | The setting stays true of everything on screen; one `Ctrl+Z` still removes the whole paste |

Wording, exact, for `SettingsDialog.tsx`:

> Uppercase the command keywords as you write, indent each level of a nested FORM or TURN by one
> space, and end every unit's orders with a single blank line. Text inside quotes is left alone.

## Out of scope

- **Any change to `crates/core`.** `walk.rs` is mirrored, not called or altered.
- **Any change to `shownUnitText` or `writeUnitOrders`.** Both keep their current behaviour; see
  *Known traps* for why they interact benignly.
- **Indentation with anything but spaces**, or any width but one per level. The navigator asked for
  one space; there is no setting for it and none is to be added.
- **Re-indenting the faction document as a whole**, or any unit other than the one on screen. The
  editor holds one unit's block and that is all this touches.
- **A format-on-demand command or keyboard shortcut.** The tidy's clock is the one `ah-1znc` settled
  and this bead does not add a fourth.
- **Anything about the case rules.** `orderCase.ts` is unchanged.
- **Turning Order OCD on by default.** It stays `false` in `settingsStore.ts:305`.

## Validation

The bead is done when all of these hold:

1. `pnpm run check:fast` passes.
2. `pnpm run test:smoke` passes, including the four new tests.
3. With Order OCD **on**, in a unit's orders: typing `TURN`, Enter, `FORM 1`, Enter, `work` leaves
   `TURN\n FORM 1\n  WORK` on screen.
4. With Order OCD on, opening a unit whose stored orders are flat and nested leaves every level
   indented one space, with `END` under `FORM` and `ENDTURN` under `TURN`.
5. Clicking in the empty space below the last order, in a unit whose orders have been tidied, puts
   the caret on an empty line below the last order rather than at the end of it.
6. With Order OCD **off**, none of this happens: typing, pasting, Enter, and opening a unit all
   behave exactly as they do on `main` today.
7. Opening a unit with Order OCD on does **not** mark its draft as edited or trigger a save, when the
   only thing the tidy would change is the trailing newline. See *Known traps*.
8. Pasting `form 1\nstudy combat\nend` into an empty block yields `FORM 1\n STUDY COMBAT\nEND`, and
   one `Ctrl+Z` removes all of it.

## Known traps

- **The tidy effect's position in the file is load-bearing.** It is declared *after* the
  `externalRevision` effect and keyed on `externalRevision`, because a draft restored asynchronously
  after a reload is spliced into an editor that mounted empty — tidy it before that and it tidies a
  blank document and never runs again. This is `ah-1znc`'s entire retrospective. Moving the effect,
  or dropping a key from it, reintroduces that bug and the smoke tests may not catch it.
- **`OrdersEditor.tsx` has three asynchronous inputs** — the document (via `externalRevision`), the
  vocabulary, and the setting. `ah-1znc`'s retrospective is explicit that its plan reasoned about two
  of the three and lost a smoke cycle to the third. Anything new that reads a late-arriving value
  must be keyed on all of them.
- **The trailing newline does not survive a round trip through the document, and that is fine.**
  `writeUnitOrders` (`ordersDocument.ts:123`) calls `withoutTrailingBlankLines` on what it writes, so
  the newline the editor holds is stripped on the way into the faction document and put back by
  `shownUnitText` on the way out once saved. **Verify that this does not mark the draft dirty**
  (validation item 7): the tidy fires `onChange`, the shell writes the document, and the document
  comes back byte-identical — so nothing should register as an edit. If the shell's dirty flag is set
  from `onChange` firing rather than from the document actually changing, opening any unit would now
  mark it edited, and that must be fixed here rather than shipped.
- **`bareWords` strips a leading `@` and stops at `;`, and both matter.** `@turn` opens a block
  (`walk.rs`'s own test proves it); `WORK ; END` does not close one. Do not hand-roll the first-token
  extraction — a `split(/\s+/)[0]` gets both of these wrong.
- **`END` inside a quoted name is not grammar.** `NAME UNIT "END of the line"` must not pop the
  stack. `bareWords` already handles this; a regex would not.
- **Do not restate the selection when a length-changing edit is in the batch** (increment 5). The
  existing unconditional restatement is only correct because case edits are exactly as long as what
  they replace.
- **The keymap's order inside the extension array is deliberate.** `autocompletion` must keep Enter
  when its popup is open; the new binding goes ahead of `editingKeymap` but the extension array's own
  ordering is not to be shuffled.
- **`lineDepths` is called on a prefix of the document, once per Enter and once per paste.** It is
  O(document) and the document is one unit's block — a few dozen lines. Do not add memoisation; do
  not put it in a `useMemo` that would go stale.
- **A closer reports the depth *outside* the block it closes.** This is the difference between `END`
  landing under `FORM` (chosen) and under the block's contents (rejected), and it is easy to get
  backwards. The table in increment 1 pins it: `"TURN\nFORM 1\nWORK\nEND\nMOVE N\nENDTURN\nWORK"` →
  `[0, 1, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]`.
- **Disk space.** Ten of this repository's retrospectives name `scripts/diskPreflight.ts` refusing to
  start a bead below its 8 GB floor, and it can trip again mid-`check:fast`, where it surfaces as a
  failing *tooling* test that reads like a defect in the diff. If that happens, it is a full disk and
  not your change. Safe offline reclaims: `~/.cargo/registry/src`, `target/debug/incremental`,
  `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache`.

title: The game data can only be reached by name, so there is no way to browse it
description:
The navigator's words: "It should be possible to bring up the game data both
using keyboard shortcut and through the palette."

Raised by the navigator 2026-08-21.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY. ah-5jkt.1 (v0.10.0) added skills, items and buildings to the
command palette as individual searchable entries, and ah-5jkt.2 made those names
clickable where they appear in a pane. Both routes start from a specific thing:
you search for "Mining" or you click the word "Mining" somewhere.

There is no entry point to the game data itself. A player who wants to browse
what the ruleset contains, or who cannot remember what a thing is called, has
nowhere to start.

FOR THE PLANNER. Two entry points are asked for -- a keyboard shortcut and a
palette command -- and both want a user-facing decision the navigator should be
asked about rather than assumed: which key, and what the dialog shows when it is
opened with nothing chosen. The existing reference dialog from ah-5jkt.1 opens
onto one entry; whether this reuses it, opens it on a list, or is a different
surface is exactly the sort of thing planning settles with the navigator.
design:
## Context

The navigator's words: *"It should be possible to bring up the game data both using keyboard shortcut
and through the palette."*

**What exists today.** ah-5jkt.1 added skills, items and buildings to the command palette as
individual searchable entries; ah-5jkt.2 made those names clickable where they appear in a pane. Both
routes **start from a specific thing** — you search for `Mining`, or you click the word `Mining`
somewhere. A player who wants to browse what the ruleset holds, or who cannot remember what a thing
is called, has nowhere to start.

**This is a door, not a new room, and that is the central finding.**
`openGameDataDialog(index, entryId)` (`workspace/gameDataDialogState.ts:62-77`) **already handles
being opened with nothing named**:

```ts
  const landing = entryId === null ? null : (index.detailOf(entryId)?.entry ?? null);
  const category = landing?.category ?? GAME_DATA_CATEGORIES[0];
  …selectedId: landing?.id ?? (entriesOf(index, category)[0]?.id ?? null),
```

**Nothing has ever called it with `null`.** `GAME_DATA_CATEGORIES[0]` is `"skill"`, so a cold open
already lands on **Skills with its first entry showing** — which is exactly what the navigator chose.
So the dialog behind this door needs **no new state at all**.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. A seventh shortcut — `packages/shared/src/shortcuts.ts`

The file is *"the global keyboard layer's single source of truth… so the help overlay, the palette's
inline hints and the actual dispatch can never disagree"*. Three edits, all in it:

```ts
export type ShortcutId =
  | "palette"
  | "help"
  | "gameData"        // new
  | …
```

```ts
  {
    id: "gameData",
    group: "Navigation",
    description: "Browse the game data - skills, items, buildings and the rest",
    mac: "F2",
    other: "F2"
  },
```

and in `matchShortcut` (`:89-116`), beside the existing `F8` arm:

```ts
  if (event.key === "F2" && noMod && !event.altKey && !event.shiftKey) {
    return "gameData";
  }
```

**`noMod` and no Alt/Shift**, matching how `F8` is guarded at `:111` — a modified F2 is a different
chord and belongs to whatever else may claim it.

**`firesInContext` (`:126-134`) gets `gameData` alongside `palette` and `help`:**

```ts
  if (id === "palette" || id === "help" || id === "gameData") {
    return true;
  }
```

and its doc comment must be updated to say why — **F2 is an unmodified function key that produces no
character**, so unlike an arrow chord it can never be something the player was trying to type, and
looking a thing up mid-sentence while writing orders is exactly when it is wanted.

**The help overlay and the palette's binding hints need nothing**: both read `SHORTCUTS`, which is
the point of the table.

### 2. The palette entry — where the other actions are built

An **action** entry reading **`Browse game data`**, whose `run` opens the dialog cold. It is an
`action`, so it inherits the palette's binding-hint column and will show `F2` beside itself for free.

**It must not exist when the ruleset has not loaded.** `commandPalette.test.ts:256-268`
(`offers no game data when the ruleset has not loaded`) pins that an empty `gameData` yields **no
entries at all**; this action follows the same rule, so the palette never offers a door onto seven
empty tabs.

### 3. Opening, and closing — the dialog's owner

Whoever holds the dialog's open/closed state (the shell that renders `GameDataDialog`) gains:

- a handler for the `gameData` shortcut, and
- the same call behind the palette action: **`openGameDataDialog(index, null)`**.

**F2 is a toggle.** Open when closed; **close when open**, and *without* resetting anything — the
player may have followed a cross-reference deep into Buildings, and F2 must never silently throw that
away. Escape keeps closing it through the dismiss stack exactly as now.

**F2 is a no-op when the ruleset has not loaded**, matching §2.

### 4. Nothing inside the dialog changes

Its tabs, filter, list, detail pane, `goBack` and cross-references are ah-5jkt.1's and are untouched.
**If `gameDataDialogState.ts` appears in the diff, something has been misread** — the cold-open path
already exists and needs no edit.

## Increments

1. **The chord exists and means one thing.**
   RED: `shortcuts.test.ts` — `F2` returns `"gameData"`; a modified F2 (`Shift`, `Alt`, `Mod`)
   returns null; and **`firesInContext("gameData", …)` is true in a foreign text input**.
   GREEN: the id, the `SHORTCUTS` row, the `matchShortcut` arm and the `firesInContext` arm.
2. **The palette offers the door.**
   RED: `commandPalette.test.ts` — an action labelled `Browse game data` is offered; and
   **`offers no game data when the ruleset has not loaded` still returns `[]`**, now with the action
   in the picture.
   GREEN: the entry.
3. **Both doors open the same dialog, cold.**
   RED: smoke — pressing **F2** opens the dialog on **Skills** with its first entry showing;
   choosing **Browse game data** in the palette does the same.
   GREEN: the handler and the action's `run`.
4. **F2 closes it again, without losing your place.**
   RED: smoke — open, **follow a cross-reference into another category**, press F2 (it closes), press
   F2 again. Assert it opens cold on Skills. The point of the test is that closing did not throw
   anything away mid-flight and the second open is a fresh one.
   GREEN: the toggle.
5. **No ruleset, no door.**
   RED: smoke or unit — with no ruleset loaded, the palette offers no `Browse game data`, and F2
   opens nothing.
   GREEN: the guard.

## The test plan

| Test | Where | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| `F2 opens the game data` | `shortcuts.test.ts` | the chord |
| **`a modified F2 is not the game data`** | same | Shift/Alt/Mod all null, as `F8` is guarded |
| **`the game data chord fires inside a text input`** | same | the navigator's choice |
| `Browse game data is offered as an action` | `commandPalette.test.ts` | the palette door |
| **`offers no game data when the ruleset has not loaded`** (`:256`) | same | **must still return `[]`** |
| `F2 opens the dialog on Skills` | smoke | cold open |
| `the palette action opens the same dialog` | smoke | both doors agree |
| **`F2 closes an open dialog`** | smoke | the toggle |
| `F2 while the ruleset is absent does nothing` | smoke | §2 |
| the existing shortcut, palette and dialog tests | all three files | **unchanged** |

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`, plus the smoke suite — anything that presses a key and looks at a
dialog is Playwright, since **there is no jsdom in this repository**.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-21, over two rounds, using
`.cerebro/scratch/ah-u44o-gamedata-door.html`. The mockup is committed to `docs/ui/`.

**Q1 — which key.** Chosen: **F2**. No browser claims it on any platform — the only one of the three
of which that is simply true — it sits with `F8` which the app already owns, and it is the same chord
on every platform. Accepted cost: not mnemonic, and awkward on a Mac laptop where the function row
wants `fn`. Rejected: **⌘⇧K / Ctrl+Shift+K** (reads beautifully as a sibling of ⌘K, but **Firefox
uses Ctrl+Shift+K for its Web Console** on Windows and Linux, and this ships as a web app) and **F1**
(the oldest convention for reference, but the app already has a help key at ⌘/, and two help-shaped
keys meaning different things is worse than one unmemorable key).

**Q2 — what a cold open lands on.** Chosen: **Skills, first entry showing** — already exactly what
the code does, so no new state and no empty pane. Accepted cost: it lands on an arbitrary skill the
player did not ask for. Rejected: **nothing selected with the cursor in the filter**, which is more
honest about having been opened without a subject but needs a new empty state and `selectedId: null`
handled as an opening state rather than only as a bad id.

**Q3 — the palette wording.** Chosen: **`Browse game data`**. The verb says it opens something to
look around in rather than reading as a page *about* game data — which matters because it sits among
~270 dictionary entries that are exactly that. Rejected: `Game data` (shortest, matches the dialog's
name elsewhere, but reads like one of the entries) and `Open the rules reference` (what a player would
call it, but a second name for one thing).

**Q4 — where F2 may fire.** Chosen: **anywhere, like ⌘K and ⌘/**. F2 produces no character, so it can
never be something the player was trying to type, and looking a thing up while writing orders is
exactly the moment. Rejected: following the arrow chords' rule, which would make F2 dead in the unit
filter for no reason a player could infer.

**Q5 — no ruleset loaded.** Chosen: **hide the palette entry and make F2 a no-op**, consistent with
the palette already offering no game data at all in that state. Rejected: opening the dialog to
explain itself (a new empty state, and it would contradict the palette's silence).

**Q6 — F2 at an already-open dialog.** Chosen: **it closes, like a toggle** — one key in, same key
out, and it never destroys where the player had got to. Rejected: doing nothing (Escape already
closes it, but a dead key at an open dialog feels broken) and re-opening cold (which would silently
throw away a followed entry).

## Out of scope

- **The dialog itself.** Its layout, scrolling and keyboard are ah-5jkt.1's, and its two reported
  defects are **ah-vwdi**.
- **`gameDataDialogState.ts`.** The cold-open path already exists.
- **The per-entry palette results and the in-pane links** — ah-5jkt.1 and ah-5jkt.2, both unchanged.
- **Remembering where the dialog was last left.** F2 always opens cold; a "resume where I was"
  behaviour was not asked for and is a decision of its own.
- **Any other new shortcut.**

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm exec playwright test --project=web
```

Then by hand:

1. Press **F2** from the map. The dialog opens on **Skills** with the first skill showing.
   **This is the acceptance.**
2. Press **F2** again: it closes.
3. Open it, **follow a cross-reference** into another category, then **F2** to close and **F2** to
   re-open. It comes back **cold on Skills** — and nothing was lost in a way that mattered, because
   closing was deliberate.
4. Open the palette (**⌘K**), type `game`, and choose **Browse game data**. Same dialog, same cold
   state as F2.
5. Check the palette row shows **F2** in its binding column, and that **⌘/** lists the chord under
   Navigation. Neither should have needed wiring — if either is missing, `SHORTCUTS` was bypassed.
6. **Click into the orders editor and press F2**: it must open. Then try from the **unit filter**:
   also open. This is Q4, and it is the one that would be easy to get wrong.
7. **Escape** still closes the dialog.
8. With **no report and no ruleset loaded**, press F2: nothing happens, and `Browse game data` is not
   in the palette.

## Known traps

- **Do not touch `gameDataDialogState.ts`.** `openGameDataDialog(index, null)` already lands on
  Skills with the first entry. The whole bead is that nobody ever called it that way.
- **Add the chord to `SHORTCUTS`, not just to `matchShortcut`.** The help overlay and the palette's
  hint column both read the table; a chord that works but is listed nowhere is the exact disagreement
  the file's header says it exists to prevent.
- **Guard the modifiers.** Bare F2 only, matching `F8` at `:111`.
- **`firesInContext` needs `gameData` explicitly**, and its comment updated. Left out, F2 dies in the
  unit filter and works in the orders editor, which is the confusing half of both worlds.
- **The no-ruleset guard must cover both doors.** The palette hiding its entry while F2 still opens
  an empty dialog is worse than either alone.
- **F2 must not reset an open dialog** — it closes it. Re-opening cold is right; closing *by*
  re-opening is not.
- **There is no jsdom here.** Anything that presses a key and inspects a dialog is a Playwright test.
acceptance_criteria:
- F2 opens the game data dialog, cold: on Skills with its first entry showing. A modified F2 (Shift, Alt, Mod) does nothing.
- The command palette offers an action labelled "Browse game data" which opens the same dialog in the same cold state.
- The chord is added to the SHORTCUTS table in shortcuts.ts, so the help overlay (Cmd+/) lists it and the palette row shows F2 in its binding column with no extra wiring.
- `firesInContext` returns true for the new id alongside "palette" and "help", so F2 fires from anywhere including the orders editor and the unit filter, and its doc comment says why (an unmodified function key produces no character).
- When the ruleset has not loaded, the palette does NOT offer "Browse game data" and F2 does nothing. The existing test `offers no game data when the ruleset has not loaded` still returns [].
- Pressing F2 while the dialog is open CLOSES it, without resetting or discarding anything. Escape still closes it via the dismiss stack.
- gameDataDialogState.ts is NOT modified - openGameDataDialog(index, null) already lands on Skills with the first entry, and this bead only calls it that way.
- The dialog's tabs, filter, list, detail pane, goBack and cross-references are unchanged.
- Anything that presses a key and inspects a dialog is a Playwright smoke test; no jsdom is added.
- `pnpm run check:fast` and the smoke suite pass.

title: Fleets are drawn as buildings, and the Ships count says one where forty are moored
description:
Found while planning ah-o0d3 (2026-08-21), by simulating classify() over all 100 distinct structure kinds in tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep. Out of scope for ah-o0d3, which is about the trailing clause; this is a separate hole in SHIP_KINDS.

## What is wrong

`SHIP_KINDS` (mapThemes/hexView.ts:57) is galley, raft, cog, clipper, galleon, corsair, balloon. **`fleet` is not in it**, and `isShip()` otherwise only rescues a kind whose text contains "ship" or "boat".

So of the seven Fleet kinds in the fixtures, exactly one draws as a ship, and it does so **by accident**:

    ship      <- Fleet, 6 Airships          <- only because "Airships" contains "ship"
    building  <- Fleet, 8 Corsairs
    building  <- Fleet, 4 Galleons, 1 Balloon
    building  <- Fleet, 3 Corsairs
    building  <- Fleet, 2 Galleons
    building  <- Fleet, 2 Corsairs
    building  <- Fleet, 2 Balloons

This holds both before and after ah-o0d3's comma split - verified against both versions. ah-o0d3 changes seven structures and regresses none, and none of the six above is among them.

## Why it matters

A fleet is a stack of ships sitting in a hex, and it is drawn as an anonymous building. The contents are named right there in the kind - Corsairs, Galleons, Balloons - all of which ARE in SHIP_KINDS individually; only the word that heads the line is missing.

## Shape of a fix

Probably one word: add `fleet` to SHIP_KINDS. Worth checking first whether any non-vessel kind begins with "Fleet" in another ruleset, and worth deciding whether a fleet should draw as a ship or earn a mark of its own - a stack of forty vessels is not the same thing on the map as one galley. That is a navigator question.

Take every test case from tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep. Synthetic bare words are what hid both this and ah-o0d3.
design:
## Context

Found while planning **ah-o0d3**, by simulating `classify()` over all 100 distinct structure kinds in
`tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep`. Two things, and the navigator chose to fix both here.

**1. `fleet` is not in `SHIP_KINDS`.** The set (`mapThemes/hexView.ts:57`) is
`galley, raft, cog, clipper, galleon, corsair, balloon`, and `isShip()` otherwise only rescues a kind
whose text contains `ship` or `boat`. Atlantis writes **the lead vessel's type, or the word `Fleet`
when there is no single lead** — both mean *vessels sitting in this hex*. So of the seven `Fleet`
lines in the fixtures, exactly one draws as a ship, **by accident**:

```
ship      <- Red Squadron [1027] : Fleet, 6 Airships.     only because "Airships" contains "ship"
building  <- Fleet [988]  : Fleet, 8 Corsairs.
building  <- Ship [1121]  : Fleet, 2 Galleons.
building  <- Ship [1176]  : Fleet, 3 Corsairs.
building  <- Ship [386]   : Fleet, 2 Balloons.
building  <- Bradr [797]  : Fleet, 2 Corsairs.
building  <- Ship [697]   : Fleet, 4 Galleons, 1 Balloon.
```

Three of them are *named* `Ship` or `Fleet` by their owner and still draw as buildings. **This holds
both before and after ah-o0d3's comma split** — verified against both versions.

**2. The Ships badge counts structures, not vessels.**
