Its own comment names the both-places rule. - **Do not set a root `font-size`.** It would scale every rem in the app — the rails, the orders pane, the units-pane heights, the map's zoom buttons — and break the drag walks. Scale the tokens. - **`--ui-scale` goes outside the `@theme` block**, beside `--pane-transparency`. `@theme` is Tailwind's utility-generating namespace. - **`ah-46p.1`'s own guard rejects a `calc()`** and will go red the moment `theme.css` changes, in a file nothing else in this bead touches. `theme.test.ts:140`'s regex demands a bare number after the colon. The fix is in *The test plan* and it makes the guard stronger, not weaker — do not reach for `.skip` or delete an assertion. - **`theme.test.ts` also forbids absolute pane px** (`:185-187`), and that guard stays green. A `calc()` is fine; computing a pixel string in JS and stamping it as a font size is not. Never go near that. - **Reset the size at the end of any smoke test that changes it.** `settings.spec.ts:193-222` does this for the transparency slider, and the pixel-exact tests that follow depend on it. - **The default must stay 100%.** Every pixel-exact assertion in the suite holds only there, and `docs/retrospectives/ah-1uj.md` is the record of what it costs when the chrome grows unnoticed.

title: A three-step type scale in rem replaces 67 hard-coded pixel sizes
description:
First half of ah-46p. The panes set type in absolute pixels at 67 sites across 28 files - 31 `text-[10px]`, 19 `text-[11.5px]`, 13 `text-[11px]`, 2 `text-[10.5px]`, 1 each of `text-[9.5px]` and `text-[13px]` - and CSS `px` ignores the browser's font-size preference outright, so a reader who raises theirs sees no change at all.

Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-17 (mockup: docs/ui/pane-type-scale.html): six sizes become **three named rem tokens**, and the floor rises - the smallest pane text goes from 10px to 11px at a 16px root. That is visible to everyone, deliberately.

Nothing else changes: no setting, no control. ah-46p.2 adds the Interface size slider on top, and needs this first because a multiplier cannot reach an absolute pixel.
design:
## Context

The map is resolution-independent by construction — it is SVG, so the browser re-rasterises it at
device resolution. The panes over it are not: they set type in **absolute pixels at 67 sites across
28 files** in `packages/shared/src`, and CSS `px` ignores the browser's font-size preference
outright. A reader who raises their default sees no change at all, because all 67 sites override it.
On a 4K panel at 100% OS scaling — ordinary on Windows and Linux — 10px type is physically about half
the size it is on a 1080p screen, and the only escape is full-page zoom, which also zooms the map
that was perfectly legible.

Counted on `origin/main`, and the numbers below are what
`git grep -o 'text-\[[0-9.]*px\]' -- packages/shared/src | sed 's/.*://' | sort | uniq -c` returns:

| Class | Uses |
|---|---|
| `text-[10px]` | 31 |
| `text-[11.5px]` | 19 |
| `text-[11px]` | 13 |
| `text-[10.5px]` | 2 |
| `text-[9.5px]` | 1 |
| `text-[13px]` | 1 |

This bead replaces all 67 with **three named `rem` tokens**, and raises the floor. `ah-46p.2` then
adds an Interface size setting on top; it is blocked on this one, because a multiplier cannot reach
an absolute pixel.

The mockup the navigator chose from is `docs/ui/pane-type-scale.html`.

Branch from `origin/main`; line numbers are that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The scale — `packages/shared/src/theme.css`

Tailwind v4 generates a font-size utility from every `--text-*` key in the `@theme` block, so the
scale is declared once beside the colours (`:36-110`) and used as a class everywhere:

```css
  /* The panes' type scale. Three steps, in rem so the reader's own font-size preference reaches
     them - `px` does not, which is the whole of ah-46p. The map sets its own sizes and is not on
     this scale. */
  --text-pane-sm: 0.6875rem;   /* 11px at a 16px root */
  --text-pane: 0.75rem;        /* 12px */
  --text-pane-lg: 0.8125rem;   /* 13px */
```

Font sizes only — **do not add `--text-pane--line-height` companions.** The existing markup sets its
own leading with `leading-*` classes where it wants it, and giving these tokens a line-height would
silently re-space every pane in the same commit that changes the sizes, making a layout regression
impossible to attribute.

There is no `--text-*` token in the file today; these are the first. Note they go in the `@theme`
block **only** — unlike a colour, a size has no light-theme counterpart, and `theme.test.ts`'s guard
is specifically about `--color-*` tokens (`theme.test.ts:13`, `colorTokens`), so it neither requires
nor objects to these.

### The mapping — 67 sites, 28 files

| Today | Uses | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `text-[9.5px]`, `text-[10px]`, `text-[10.5px]` | 34 | `text-pane-sm` |
| `text-[11px]`, `text-[11.5px]` | 32 | `text-pane` |
| `text-[13px]` | 1 | `text-pane-lg` |

Mechanical, and the whole of it. Find every site with:

```bash
git grep -n 'text-\[[0-9.]*px\]' -- packages/shared/src
```

**The floor rises**: today's smallest pane text is 10px and becomes 11px at a default root. That is
visible to every reader and is the navigator's deliberate choice — see *User-facing decisions*. Do
not "preserve" it by mapping 10px to 0.625rem.

### The one site that is not a Tailwind class

`packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx` sets the editor's type inside an injected CodeMirror
theme rather than as a class: `"&": { height: "100%", fontSize: "11.5px", … }` (`:147`). It is pane
text read by the same eyes, so it moves too:

```ts
"&": { height: "100%", fontSize: "var(--text-pane)", color: "var(--color-ink)" },
```

Tailwind emits the `@theme` tokens on `:root` (`theme.css:124` says so in as many words), so a
`var()` in an injected style resolves exactly as it does for the colours that file already reads
this way. The file's own comment — *"Tokens, not hex literals: theme.test.ts's rule holds in spirit
for injected styles its component scan cannot see"* (`:144-145`) — is the precedent, and it applies
to sizes for the same reason.

That is a **decision I took rather than the navigator**: they settled that pane text scales, and the
orders editor is a pane. If the monospace editor should keep a fixed size while the panes around it
grow, that is a one-line reversal and worth asking about — but the default that follows from what was
agreed is that it scales.

### The guard — `packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts`

Add a case that the panes carry no absolute type any more, so this cannot come back a site at a time:

```ts
it("sets no pane type in absolute pixels", () => {
  // `px` ignores the reader's font-size preference, which is the whole of ah-46p. The three
  // `--text-pane*` tokens are the scale; a new `text-[13px]` is how 67 of them accumulated.
  expect(sourcesWithAbsoluteType()).toEqual([]);
});
```

reading the same `packages/shared/src` tree the file already reads `theme.css` from, and matching
`/text-\[[0-9.]+px\]/`. Report the offending file paths in the failure, not just a count — the
message is what tells the next author what to do.

## Increments

1. **The scale exists and is proven to reach the DOM.**
   RED: `theme.test.ts` — `the pane type scale is declared`, asserting `--text-pane-sm`, `--text-pane`
   and `--text-pane-lg` are all in the `@theme` block, in rem.
   GREEN: the three tokens.

2. **Nothing sets type in pixels.**
   RED: the `sets no pane type in absolute pixels` case, which fails with 28 file paths.
   GREEN: the mechanical replacement, one size at a time — the 34 smallest first, then the 32, then
   the single `13px`. Run `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run typecheck` between them; a mistyped class name
   is not a type error in Tailwind, so the test above is the only thing that catches a typo in a
   class that silently does nothing.

3. **The editor moves with them.**
   RED: extend the guard to `OrdersEditor.tsx`'s injected theme, or assert directly that the file
   contains no `fontSize: "…px"`.
   GREEN: `var(--text-pane)`.

4. **Nothing is clipped.**
   RED: the smoke walk in *The test plan*.
   GREEN: whatever it turns up — see *Known traps* for the two places most likely to need a
   `min-h`/`min-w` nudge.

## The test plan

**Unit — `packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts`, `pnpm -r run test`.** The two cases above. They are
cheap and they are the whole regression story: a scale that exists, and nothing bypassing it.

**Component — none.** Every changed line is a class name; a component test asserting a class name
pins the implementation rather than the behaviour.

**Browser — `pnpm run test:smoke`.** The existing suite is the safety net for layout, and two of its
walks already measure boxes: `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:169` pins the editor's left edge at
≤6px, and the units-pane drag walks measure heights. Run the whole suite; a type change that breaks
layout shows up there rather than in a unit test.

Add one walk, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, that is the actual point of the bead:

> **the panes grow when the reader's text size does** — set the root font size to 20px
> (`page.addStyleTag({ content: "html { font-size: 20px }" })` before the app renders, or
> `document.documentElement.style.fontSize`), then assert a known pane's computed `font-size` is
> larger than at the default, and that the region panel's own bounding box has not overflowed its
> rail. That is one assertion for "rem reached it" and one for "and it still fits".

**By eye, and this is the case no test covers**: with the browser's default font size raised two
steps, walk the region panel, the unit panel, the unit table dock, the orders panel and the header —
nothing clipped, nothing overlapping, the rails still draggable.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `pnpm run test:smoke`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 over `docs/ui/pane-type-scale.html`, which draws the
same pane at today's sizes, ×1.15 and ×1.3.

**Q1 — how the reader gets control.** Chosen: **rem first, then a UI-scale setting**, as two beads.
The conversion alone already fixes the reported problem for anyone who has set a browser preference,
and rem is what makes a multiplier possible at all, so the first is half of the second either way.
Rejected: rem only (a reader who does not know the browser preference exists gets no help); one bead
doing both (28 files and the settings store at once).

**Q2 — the sizes themselves.** Chosen: **tidied — six sizes become three, and the floor rises to
11px** at a 16px root. Six sizes, three of them within half a pixel of each other, were carried
forward unexamined; a named three-step scale is what the next author needs, and 10px is small by any
measure. Rejected: a faithful translation (zero visual risk, six sizes preserved for the next person
to wonder about); tidying to three steps while keeping the 10px floor.

**Consequence the navigator accepted**: because the floor rises, this bead is *not* invisible. Every
reader's smallest pane text grows by a pixel, and the densest lists — the unit table, the market rows
— are where it shows.

**Taken by me, and flagged**: the orders editor's injected `fontSize: "11.5px"` moves onto the same
token, because it is pane text and the decision was that pane text scales.

## Out of scope

- **The Interface size setting.** `ah-46p.2`, blocked on this.
- **The map.** It sets its own sizes, is SVG, and already scales with the display. Nothing under
  `mapThemes/` or in `MapCanvas`'s SVG text is touched.
- **Line heights and spacing.** No `leading-*`, padding or gap changes: this bead moves font sizes
  and nothing else, so a layout regression has one possible cause.
- **The rails' widths.** They are already in rem (`RAIL_LEFT_DEFAULT_REM = 19`, `panelLayout.ts:35`)
  and grow with the root on their own; a reader who has dragged one keeps their width.
- **`apps/`.** The 67 sites are all in `packages/shared/src`; if the shells carry any of their own,
  they are a separate sweep and not part of the measured cost.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke
```

Then by eye, at the browser's default and again two steps up:

- the region panel, unit panel, unit table dock, orders panel and header all readable and unclipped;
- the orders editor's monospace text grows with them;
- the rails still drag, and a narrow rail still shows its content;
- the map is unchanged at both sizes — that is the point of the bead.

## Known traps

- **A mistyped Tailwind class silently does nothing.** `text-pane-sm` and `text-pane-small` both
  compile; only one has a size. The `sets no pane type in absolute pixels` test catches a leftover
  `text-[10px]`, but nothing catches a typo in the new name, so read the diff — or grep for
  `text-pane` and count 67.
- **`--text-*` in `@theme` is what makes the utility exist.** Declaring the tokens under a plain
  `:root` gives working `var()` references and **no** `text-pane` class, which then falls back to
  inherited size and looks almost right.
- **Do not give the tokens line-height companions.** Tailwind v4 lets `--text-pane--line-height` ride
  along, and it would re-space every pane in the same commit as the size change.
- **`theme.test.ts` guards `--color-*` only** (`:13`). It will not notice a missing size token; the
  new cases are what do.
- **The two dense lists are where the extra pixel shows** — `UnitTableDock` (a virtualised table with
  its own row heights) and the market rows in `RegionPanel`. If a row clips, raise that container's
  `min-h`, do not shrink the type back.
- **The editor's own left-edge budget is pinned at ≤6px** by `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:169`
  and is measured in px against a 2px line padding. Changing the editor's font size changes the
  text's box but not that padding; if the walk fails, read it before adjusting anything — the budget
  is a deliberate agreement (`docs/ui/orders-editor-left-edge.html`).

title: Refactoring: one script answers which closed beads are real work
description:
## The cost being paid
"Closed beads that are work, not bd's own audit records" is a query hand-written independently wherever the harness reads closed beads — the fleet view's bead partition in elisp, Psylocke's work list and first-pass check in verifier.md, Cerebro's shipped-count and merged-but-unverified queries in orchestrator.md — and each copy had to learn bd's `event` beads and its default-to-open listing on its own. The same defect was fixed twice in nineteen hours in two implementations: b0bbfaf (#6, 2026-08-15 01:22) taught the elisp panel to exclude event beads after three "State change: verification -> passed" records sat at the top of Verified as merged work; 7cea8fa (#26, ah-9gm, 20:54 the same day) fixed verifier.md and orchestrator.md after Psylocke's work list grew an event-bead chain "one link per pass, forever". A third fix the next day, 5ccc3b3 (#30): verifier.md's first-pass query lacked `--status closed` and read zero against 118 labelled beads — a trap agents/user-feedback.md had already documented for Moira ("`--all` is load-bearing"). Every reader of closed beads is a place the next bd quirk has to be discovered again.

## Evidence
- b0bbfaf "A bead panel under the agent list, and three fixes it turned up (#6)" — body: "It also holds bd's `event' beads … three of them were sitting at the top of Verified titled 'State change: verification -> passed'"
- 7cea8fa "fix(ah-9gm): closed-bead queries exclude bd's own audit event beads (#26)" — agents/orchestrator.md and agents/verifier.md
- 5ccc3b3 "fix(verifier): first-pass detection must query closed beads (#30)"
- .claude/cerebro @ bbfa374: emacs/cerebro.el:1520 (`(member (alist-get 'issue_type bead) '("epic" "event"))`); agents/verifier.md:123 (`select(.issue_type != "event")`), :152; agents/orchestrator.md:622-626, :649 (`--exclude-type epic,event`)

## Where
.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el (cerebro--partition-beads); .claude/cerebro/agents/verifier.md; .claude/cerebro/agents/orchestrator.md; .claude/cerebro/agents/user-feedback.md

## What a refactoring would change
One place that answers "closed work beads since X" — a small script under `.claude/cerebro/scripts` (or a documented `bd` invocation the roles copy verbatim) that excludes epics and event beads and always passes the status it means — used by the elisp partition and quoted by every agent text instead of each writing its own `bd list … | jq`. Then a bd quirk is learnt once. Not a plan: a planner plans it.

Filed by Forge, daily sweep of 2026-08-17, harness range 8bee269..bbfa374.
design:
## Context

"Closed beads that are work, not bd's own bookkeeping" is a question three agent roles ask, and each
of them hand-wrote its own `bd list … | jq` to ask it. Every copy had to learn bd's quirks on its own,
and the same defect was fixed three times in two days:

- **b0bbfaf** (#6) taught the fleet view's bead panel to exclude `event` beads, after three
  "State change: verification -> passed" records sat at the top of Verified as merged work.
- **7cea8fa** (#26, ah-9gm) fixed `agents/verifier.md` and `agents/orchestrator.md` after Psylocke's
  work list grew an event-bead chain "one link per pass, forever".
- **5ccc3b3** (#30) fixed `agents/verifier.md`'s first-pass query, which lacked `--status closed` and
  read zero against 118 labelled beads — a trap `agents/user-feedback.md` had already documented for
  Moira ("`--all` is load-bearing").

Three quirks, learnt separately by every reader: bd's `event` beads are closed and carry the very
labels these queries key on; an epic closing is bookkeeping rather than delivery; and `bd list`
defaults to open beads, so a closed-bead query without `--status closed` silently reads zero.

After this bead **one script** knows all three, the three roles quote it instead of composing their
own, and the next bd quirk is learnt once.

**All of the work is in the `.claude/cerebro` submodule** — a separate repository
(`rmstdope/cerebro`) with its own CI. See *Known traps* before making a single commit.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `scripts/work-beads` (in the cerebro repo)

Bash, executable, in the style of `scripts/agent-state` and `scripts/roster` — a header comment
saying what it is for, `set -euo pipefail`, arguments parsed by a `while`/`case`, and a loud failure
rather than a silent empty answer.

```
work-beads [--status <list>] [--closed-after <when>] [--print-excluded-types]
```

- **`--status <list>`** — passed straight to `bd list --status`. **Defaults to `closed`**, because
  every caller of this script wants closed beads and the default that bites is bd's own.
- **`--closed-after <when>`** — passed through when given, for the delivery windows.
- **`--print-excluded-types`** — prints the excluded issue types, one per line (`epic`, then `event`),
  and exits. It exists so `emacs/cerebro-test.el` can hold the panel's own exclusion list to this one;
  see increment 4.
- Prints a **JSON array** on stdout, so a caller pipes it into `jq` exactly as it pipes `bd list --json`
  today.
- Excludes epics and events **twice**: `--exclude-type epic,event` on the `bd` call *and*
  `select(.issue_type != "epic" and .issue_type != "event")` in the `jq`. Both on purpose, and the
  comment must say why — the flag does the work, the `jq` guard keeps the answer right under a `bd`
  whose `--exclude-type` does not know `event` (the reasoning already written at
  `agents/verifier.md:123`).
- **Fails loudly**: non-zero exit with a message on stderr when `bd` exits non-zero, or when its
  output does not parse as JSON. A reader of this script's output is deciding what has shipped or what
  needs verifying, and an empty array that means "the query broke" is the worst possible answer.

The doc comment at the top is where the three quirks are written down, once. It is the artefact this
bead is really delivering, so write it for somebody who has never been bitten by any of them.

### `agents/verifier.md`

- **The work list** (lines 118–126): the `bd list --status closed --exclude-type event --json` call
  becomes `.claude/cerebro/scripts/work-beads`. The `jq` that follows keeps its own
  `verification:*` filter unchanged — that is Psylocke's question, not this script's — but loses the
  `select(.issue_type != "event")` line, which the script now owns.
- **The first pass ever** (lines 145–152): same substitution. The `--status closed` paragraph stays,
  rewritten to say the script always passes it — the reason is still worth reading, and it is now a
  fact about the script rather than a rule to remember.
- The "Why the exclusion exists at all" paragraph (lines 128–136) stays: it explains why **never to
  label an event bead**, which is a rule about Psylocke's behaviour, not about the query.

### `agents/orchestrator.md`

- **The three delivery windows** (lines 618–624) become three `work-beads --closed-after "$X"` calls.
  The `WEEK_AGO` line and its BSD/GNU `date` comment stay exactly as they are.
- **Merged but unverified** (lines 645–649): `work-beads` piped into the same `jq`.
- The four bullets below (lines 626–633) explaining `--exclude-type epic`, `event` and
  `--status closed` are **compressed to one** pointing at the script — that is the duplication this
  bead removes. Keep the fourth bullet in full: the release window being the tag's commit date is
  about `git describe`, not about bd.

### `agents/user-feedback.md`

**One cross-reference line only**, beside the existing `--all` paragraph (line 51): the same family of
bd traps is written down in `scripts/work-beads`. Moira's query is `bd list --external-ref gh-<n>
--all --json` — a lookup by external ref across every status, not a closed-work-beads query — so it
does **not** move to the script. See *Out of scope*.

### `emacs/cerebro.el`

**The panel's query does not change.** `cerebro--bd-list-argv` (line 1426) deliberately passes every
status and **no** `--exclude-type`, and `cerebro-test/bd-list-argv-covers-every-status-briefly`
(`emacs/cerebro-test.el:2243`) pins exactly that, with the reason: the partition can only be complete
if the list it partitions is. Routing the panel through a script that pre-excludes would break a
tested, reasoned decision to save nothing — the panel does not compose a bd query per section, which
is the duplication this bead is about.

What it gets instead is one comment on the `'("epic" "event")` clause
(`emacs/cerebro.el:1520`) naming `scripts/work-beads` as the shell-side owner of the same list, and
the test in increment 4 that stops the two drifting.

## Increments

1. **The script.** RED: `tests/work-beads.sh` (new; CI runs every `tests/*.sh` — see *Known traps*),
   with a stub `bd` on `PATH` in the style of `tests/launchers.sh:27–45`. GREEN: `scripts/work-beads`.
2. **Psylocke's two queries.** RED: none available — these are markdown. Instead **run both new
   commands against the real backlog before and after** and paste the two id lists into the PR body;
   they must be identical. GREEN: the `agents/verifier.md` edits.
3. **Cerebro's four queries.** Same shape: run all four before and after, compare, then edit
   `agents/orchestrator.md`.
4. **The elisp and the script cannot drift.** RED: a new ERT test in `emacs/cerebro-test.el` asserting
   that the types the panel skips are exactly what `scripts/work-beads --print-excluded-types` prints
   — `(process-lines "scripts/work-beads" "--print-excluded-types")`, run from the repository root as
   CI runs ERT (`emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`). Write it
   against the constant, so extract the list from the `cond` clause into a `defconst
   cerebro-skipped-issue-types '("epic" "event")` first and have the clause use it. GREEN: the
   `defconst` and the comment.

## The test plan

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `defaults to closed beads` | `tests/work-beads.sh` | The stub `bd` records its argv; `--status closed` is there with no flag given |
| `passes the status it was given` | same | `--status open,closed` reaches `bd` verbatim |
| `passes a closed-after window through, and omits it when absent` | same | The delivery windows |
| `drops epics and events even when bd returns them` | same | The `jq` guard: the stub returns an epic and an event **despite** `--exclude-type`, and neither survives |
| `asks bd to exclude them as well` | same | `--exclude-type epic,event` is on the `bd` call, so the guard is a belt and not the only brace |
| `fails loudly when bd fails` | same | Stub exits 1 → non-zero exit, message on stderr, nothing that looks like an empty array on stdout |
| `fails loudly when bd prints something that is not JSON` | same | The failure mode `cerebro--try-parse-json` already guards against on the elisp side |
| `prints the excluded types for the panel to check itself against` | same | `--print-excluded-types` → `epic\nevent` |
| `cerebro-test/the-panel-skips-exactly-what-work-beads-excludes` | `emacs/cerebro-test.el` | The elisp list and the script's cannot drift |
| (existing) `cerebro-test/bd-list-argv-covers-every-status-briefly` | `emacs/cerebro-test.el:2243` | Unchanged, and must stay green — the panel's query is not touched |
| (existing) `cerebro-test/each-shape-lands-where-it-belongs` | `emacs/cerebro-test.el:2195` | The `defconst` extraction changed no behaviour |

Run in the submodule:

```bash
bash tests/work-beads.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

The before/after id lists from increments 2 and 3 are part of the evidence and belong in the PR body.
There is nothing to run in `atlantis-hud` itself: no application code is touched, so `check:fast`
has nothing to say about this bead.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** Nothing here reaches a player: it is the fleet's own tooling. The navigator does read
Cerebro's delivery line and Psylocke's work list, so the *numbers* must not move — which is what the
before/after comparison in increments 2 and 3 is for, and why it belongs in the PR body rather than in
a commit message nobody re-reads.

## Out of scope

- **Moira's `--external-ref … --all` query.** A lookup by external ref across every status is a
  different question, and folding it in would give the script two shapes and one confusing name.
- **The fleet view's `bd list` argv.** Explained above; it stays, and its ERT test stays green.
- **Any other `bd` invocation in the agent texts** — claiming, labelling, `bd show`. This script
  answers one question.
- **A `bd` alias, a wrapper, or teaching `bd` itself about "work beads".** Upstream is not ours.
- **Changing what any of the four queries returns.** This is a refactoring: identical ids, before and
  after.

## Validation

```bash
cd .claude/cerebro
bash tests/work-beads.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

And the check only a person can make: open `scripts/work-beads`, read its header, and ask whether
somebody who has never seen an `event` bead would now avoid all three traps. If not, the bead has
delivered a script and not the thing it was filed for.

## Known traps

- **This bead lives in another git repository.** `.claude/cerebro` is a submodule of
  `rmstdope/cerebro`. Branch, commit, push and open the PR **inside the submodule**, with the bead id
  in the subject as usual; its own CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the ERT suite on Emacs 28.2
  and 30.1 and every `tests/*.sh`. Request the Copilot review there, exactly as in the main repo.
  Then, once it is merged, a second small PR **in `atlantis-hud`** bumps the submodule pointer —
  `chore(ah-cg1): bump cerebro to pull in work-beads`, precedent 3621c84 (#369). Committing the
  cerebro changes from the atlantis-hud worktree without a PR in the cerebro repo puts unreviewed
  fleet tooling on everyone's machines.
- **`emacs/cerebro.el` is being edited right now by ah-bqi** (Cyclops, in flight), which touches
  `cerebro--session-alive-p` and the supervise/retire branches. This bead's elisp change is one
  `defconst`, one comment and one test, all far from those — but rebase before opening the PR rather
  than after CI goes red.
- **CI runs every `tests/*.sh`**, so a new file there is picked up with no registration and no edit to
  the workflow. It must be runnable from the submodule root (`bash tests/work-beads.sh`) like its
  four neighbours.
- **Stub `bd` on `PATH`, never the real one.** `tests/launchers.sh:27–45` is the pattern: a `mktemp -d`
  ahead of `PATH`, a stub that echoes its argv, and a `trap` to remove it. A test that runs the real
  `bd` reads the machine's own backlog and passes or fails by accident.
- **An ERT test that shells out depends on the working directory.** CI runs
  `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test` from the repository root, so `"scripts/work-beads"` resolves;
  do not write an absolute path, and skip the test gracefully (`ert-skip`) if the script is not found,
  so running the suite from elsewhere fails honestly rather than mysteriously.
- **`jq` is already a dependency** of the sweep scripts, so using it here adds nothing new to install.

title: Refactoring: one set of rules for importing a report, alone or in a batch
description:
## The cost being paid
A report reaches the workspace by two pipelines that decide the same things separately: one file at a time (`decideReportLoad` in reportLoadDecision.ts → `routeReport`/`loadReport` in reportLoad.ts → `loadReport` in AppShell.tsx) and as a batch (`planReportBatch` in reportBatch.ts → `walkBatch` in batchImport.ts → `runBatch` in AppShell.tsx). Whether a report is usable at all, how old is too old, whose faction it is, and how a merge lands are each written on both sides, and the two have now drifted three times in three days:
- ah-brd (P1, found by Psylocke): the batch path had refused a report naming no faction since 4e7c980 (ah-t65); the single-file path accepted it as an empty turn and wiped the map, regions and orders on screen. The fix (e0cbd84) had to thread a new `reject` case through reportLoadDecision.ts, reportLoad.ts and AppShell.tsx and share the reason constant back into reportBatch.ts and gameMemory.ts — five production files — and its second commit says outright "this bead exists to keep the single-file and batch paths from drifting apart".
- ah-u4e.3: a `mergeTurn` signature change was planned against AppShell's caller only; batchImport.ts's caller was found by `tsc`, and the review then found that calling the full `mergeTurn` there was a latent bug (an un-guarded `loadRegionSightings` after a merge that had already landed) — one review round-trip and CI cycle.
- ah-k6i.6: the batch path's null-viewer guard, copied from a plan describing "today's guards", silently changed behaviour; one review round-trip and a second full CI cycle.
Meanwhile the core's own verdict on usability, `ReportParseResultWire.meetsMinimumImportThreshold`, crosses the wire (ah-164.1) and is read by no production TypeScript (grep: only tests and the generated type) — the TS front doors each judge for themselves.

## Evidence
- e0cbd84 fix(ah-brd): refuse a report that names no faction (#327) — file list; second commit "pin routeReport's reject test to the shared reason constant"; bead ah-brd (P1)
- docs/retrospectives/ah-u4e.3.md §"The plan named `mergeTurn`'s consumers, but missed one of the two call sites"
- docs/retrospectives/ah-k6i.6.md §"The plan's own code snippet introduced the regression its bead explicitly forbade"
- packages/shared/src/reportBatch.ts header (the deliberate split: "a batch decides for itself"); crates/core/src/lib.rs `meets_minimum_import_threshold` / `reject_import` unread from TS

## Where
packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts, reportLoad.ts, reportBatch.ts, batchImport.ts, gameMemory.ts (mergeTurn); packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx (loadReport, runBatch)

## What a refactoring would change
The rules — is this report usable, is it older than the screen, is it the viewer's or a foreigner's — written once and consumed by both front doors; the batch keeps its "decide, don't ask" policy as a policy over the same rules rather than a second copy of them. One landing path for a merge (batchImport's `client.mergeReport` and AppShell's `mergeTurn` agree on what a merged step does and guards). Consider reading the core's usability verdict instead of re-deriving it. Not a plan: a planner plans it.

Filed by Forge, daily sweep of 2026-08-17, range b2188b2..a19f579.
design:
## Context

An epic: split into ah-sgn.1 and ah-sgn.2, in that order. This field records the decisions both
children are built against.

A report reaches the workspace by two pipelines that decide the same things separately — one file at
a time (`decideReportLoad` → `routeReport`/`loadReport` → `AppShell.loadReport`) and as a batch
(`planReportBatch` → `walkBatch` → `AppShell.runBatch`) — and the two have drifted three times in
three days (ah-brd, found by Psylocke; ah-u4e.3; ah-k6i.6). Forge filed the cost; the children fix it.

## The rules, and which of them are actually shared

Not everything these two paths decide is duplication, and the split must not flatten what is a
deliberate policy difference. Sorted out during planning, 2026-08-17:

- **"Can this report be imported at all"** — duplicated, and genuinely one rule. ah-sgn.1.
- **"One merge step"** — duplicated in effect, but the divergence is deliberate and documented
  (review of ah-u4e.3, PR #313: a batch reads the map back once at the end, and a read-back failure
  after a merge that landed must not mark the step failed). The fix is to split `mergeTurn` into the
  merge and the read-back, never to make the batch call the whole of it. ah-sgn.2.
- **"Is it older than what is on screen"** and **"whose faction is it"** — **not** duplication, and
  not to be unified. One at a time the player is asked (`decideReportLoad`'s `ask` and `storeOnly`);
  twenty at a time the question is unaskable and the batch decides for itself, with its own ceiling
  rule for how new an ally's report may be. Both modules say so in their headers, at length. Leave
  them alone.

## User-facing decisions (navigator, 2026-08-17)

Sharing the usability rule changes what the single-file path accepts, so all three were settled
before anything was planned:

1. **A report that names no turn is refused on both paths.** Today the batch skips it and a single
   dropped file is accepted as the working turn. The batch's behaviour wins: an unnumbered report
   cannot be filed under a turn, and what is on screen should not be replaced by something that
   cannot be stored properly. Rejected: accepting it on both paths; leaving the two different.
2. **A report with no regions and no units is refused on both paths**, adopting the rule the Rust
   core already has — `meets_minimum_import_threshold` (`crates/core/src/lib.rs:247`): a turn header,
   a faction, and at least one region or unit. Today a single empty file is accepted and wipes a
   populated map. Rejected: accepting it; refusing only in a batch.
3. **A refusal is the red import status line that already exists**, exactly as a report naming no
   faction gets today — `could not read turn-70.rep: <reason>`, and nothing on screen changes.
   Rejected: a dialog (interrupting, and a new surface for an error the status line already carries);
   refusing silently.
4. **The words, exactly**: `the report has no regions or units in it`. Chosen against "the report is
   empty" (untrue of a truncated file the player can see text in) and "the report describes no hexes
   and no units" ("regions" is what the report format calls them). Its two neighbours, unchanged, are
   `the report does not name its faction` and `the report does not name its turn`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Per child.

## Increments

ah-sgn.1, then ah-sgn.2 — wired as a blocker only to keep two beads out of `batchImport.ts` and
`gameMemory.ts` at the same time.

## The test plan

Per child.

## Out of scope

Unifying the age and ownership policies (above). Anything in `AppShell.tsx` beyond what the two
children name.

## Validation

Per child.

## Known traps

Per child. The one that belongs to the family: `packages/shared/src/reportBatch.ts`'s header and
`packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts`'s header both explain why the two paths differ where they
differ. A reader who deletes one of those explanations while sharing a rule has removed the reason
somebody will need in three months.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-sgn.2, delivered in PR #385

title: The build tree is per-worktree, and the sweep reclaims it
description:
## The cost being paid
Four retrospectives in two days (~40 minutes, plus one bead where every Bash call failed with ENOSPC for a minute) blame "the shared `target/` build tree" for tripping the disk floor mid-bead, and each recommends reclaiming that shared tree on a schedule. The tree they describe does not exist. `.cargo/config.toml` is tracked, so every worktree carries its own copy; cargo takes the nearest config and resolves `target-dir = "target"` against the directory holding it — the worktree. Checked read-only on this machine on 2026-08-17: `cargo metadata` from `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-eet` answers `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-eet/target`; five live trees hold 14.4 GB (root 3.5G, ah-bai.2 3.8G, ah-eet 2.5G, .cerebro/worktrees/psylocke 2.5G, .claude/worktrees/psylocke 2.1G — the last an ah-v82 leftover no sweep names). The file's own `[build]` comment claims one tree for every worktree; its `[env]` comment three lines below says the opposite ("a worktree's own root, since the file is tracked and cargo takes the nearest one"). ah-6xq.3's acceptance criterion was "a shared build.target-dir outside the repository"; what shipped is a relative, tracked path that is per-worktree by construction, and the 5 GB floor in `diskPreflight.ts` was sized by rejecting the per-worktree arithmetic that is in fact the case.

The same false premise carries a second cost: `scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` ("keeps the worktrees inside the repository", rationale: a worktree inside the repository finds the repository's cargo config) has been fixed twice for false positives — cbe52ec (ah-vek, root anchored on the test file's path) and 98aa5f4 (ah-efj, machine-wide `git worktree list`) — and cost ah-sup, ah-2n3.1 and ah-k6i.1 minutes before the second fix and ah-mi7/ah-yvf ~30 minutes after it (their own worktree at the old location after the `.cerebro/` move). It guards a location convention for a benefit that is not there, and nothing on the harness side (`prune-worktrees.sh`, `agent-state`, the launcher) sets `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or reclaims any `target/`; `diskPreflight` runs once, at bead start (implement-bead §Workspace).

## Evidence
- bdd2076 feat(ah-6xq.3): one build directory for every worktree (#142); bead ah-6xq.3 acceptance "a shared build.target-dir outside the repository"; `.cargo/config.toml` on origin/main, `[build]` vs `[env]` comments
- docs/retrospectives/ah-s0m.md §"The shared `target/` build tree crossed the disk floor mid-bead, after the initial preflight had already passed"; ah-9lv.md §"The shared `target/` build tree crossed the disk floor mid-bead, again"; ah-9r0.md §"The disk-preflight floor was tripped mid-bead by a cache the documented reclaim doesn't cover" (its own numbers: "three implementer worktrees' builds … had each grown their own `target/`"); ah-8m0.2.md §"Every Bash call failed with ENOSPC mid-bead, self-resolved within a minute"
- cbe52ec fix(ah-vek): let the worktree check ask the same question wherever it runs (#154); 98aa5f4 fix(ah-efj): the tooling gate asks whether its own worktree is inside the repository, not the machine's (#279); docs/retrospectives/ah-sup.md, ah-2n3.1.md, ah-mi7.md, ah-yvf.md (the red gate in each is this test)
- `cargo metadata --no-deps` from `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-eet` → `…/ah-eet/target`; `du -sh` of the five trees, 2026-08-17

## Where
.cargo/config.toml; scripts/diskPreflight.ts, scripts/diskPreflight.test.ts; scripts/cargoTargetDir.ts, scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts; .claude/cerebro/scripts/prune-worktrees.sh and the launcher; .claude/cerebro/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md §Workspace

## What a refactoring would change
Decide once what the build tree is — genuinely shared (an absolute or `$HOME`-relative `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set by the launcher/`launch-preflight`, so CI is untouched) or deliberately per-worktree with the floor and the sweep sized for it — and make the config comment, the preflight floor, `cargoTargetDir.test.ts` and the retrospectives' standing advice say the same thing. Whichever shape, the harness's periodic sweep should own reclaiming stale trees (a removed worktree's `target/`, `target/release`, `~/Library/Caches/Mozilla.sccache`), since four retrospectives now show that leaving it to whichever implementer hits the floor costs the fleet every day. Retire or re-aim the stray-worktree gate once the premise it guards is real.
