title: The fleet view records the sessions it starts and refuses a second one at the source
description:
## The cost being paid
"Which sessions are mine" is derived by regexing vterm buffer names (cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name, cerebro--owned), so any second vterm call for a name yields `*fleet: <name>*<2>` and an agent that is invisible for ever. The code defends that one failure in four separate places instead of at the source, and it still shipped as a real double-session bug when a state added in one guard was missed in another.

## Evidence
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Scope the detail-window override, and stop it hiding the fleet" — condition-case in cerebro--spawn-into-detail
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Make implementers interactive, and let Emacs supervise the one-bead loop" — kill-before-launch in cerebro--supervise
- cerebro 5fe8e83 sub-commit "Address the review: an owned session is alive whatever its file says" — cerebro--derive-implementer owned-but-no-file → idle
- cerebro 1bdfda7 feat(ah-u3i): "folds in a fix for cerebro--alive-p treating asking/done as dead (the `*fleet: <name>*<2>` double-session bug)" — the states added to derive in 5fe8e83 were missed in cerebro--alive-p's allow-list

## Where
.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el (cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name :830, cerebro--owned :839, guards at :123, :643, :936, :1070)

## What a refactoring would change
Own the session handle rather than infer it: the fleet view records the buffer/process it started per name (a table keyed by name), and liveness, ownership and "already running" all read that one table — so a second launch is refused at the source and there is one predicate to keep in step with the state set.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `emacs/cerebro-test.el`;
`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`), delivered the ah-aao/ah-mi7 way: a PR to cerebro, then a
submodule bump PR here. **Blocked by ah-mi7** (`bd dep`): that bead rewrites the spawn in
`cerebro--launch` (one `cerebro--make-session-buffer (name)` that creates the buffer in no window and
returns it; `quiet` gone; the restart branch calls `cerebro--show-detail` itself) and this bead builds
on that shape — read `bd show ah-mi7 --json` and the merged cerebro diff before writing. Line numbers
below are against cerebro `origin/main` at `ec0bfa6` **before** ah-mi7; the functions named will have
moved a little, not changed meaning, except `cerebro--launch`, whose body is ah-mi7's.

"Which sessions are mine" is inferred, not known: `cerebro--owned` (:946-955) regexes every buffer
name against `*fleet: NAME*` (`cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name` :937-944) and requires a live
process; `cerebro--note-exit` (:1154-1174) maps a dying buffer back to its agent the same way; every
lookup of an agent's session is `(get-buffer (cerebro--session-buffer-name agent))` (`--detail-showing-p`
:992, `--show-detail` :1003, `--nudge` :1206, `--end-session` :1217, `--kill-session-buffer` :1910).
So a second `vterm` call for a name yields `*fleet: NAME*<2>`, which the regex never matches, and
that agent is invisible for ever — a failure the code defends in four places (the `condition-case`
in `spawn-into-detail`, gone with ah-mi7; kill-before-launch in `cerebro--supervise` :1232-1238;
owned-but-no-file → `idle` in `cerebro--derive-implementer` :174-186; the `cerebro--alive-p`
allow-list :697-706) and still shipped once (ah-u3i: states added to derive were missed in
`alive-p`). `cerebro--start-action` (:708-717) decides "already up" from the agent's *state* first and
ownership second, which is why every hole in the state derivation became a double session.

This bead **owns the handle instead of inferring it**: `cerebro--launch` records the buffer it made in
one table keyed by agent name, refuses to make a second while the first is live, and every question
about a session — is it ours, is it up, which buffer is it, whose buffer just died — reads that table.
The buffer name stays `*fleet: NAME*` (the navigator sees it, the detail window shows it, the
placeholder scheme `*fleet: NAME (no view)*` is unchanged), but the name is a label now, not the key.
The four defences: the derive rule (owned-but-no-file → `idle`) **stays** — it is a real state, a
fresh session before its first state file — and `cerebro--alive-p` stays as the state predicate; what
changes is that neither is load-bearing for "start a second session" any more, because
`start-action` asks the table first and `launch` refuses at the source. No behaviour the navigator
sees changes.

Verified at `ec0bfa6`:
- `cerebro.el`: `cerebro--session-buffer-name` :693-695, `cerebro--alive-p` :697-706,
  `cerebro--start-action` :708-717, `cerebro--kill-action` :727-738, `cerebro--last-exit` :763,
  `cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name` :937-944, `cerebro--owned` :946-955, `cerebro--detail-showing-p`
  :988-993, `cerebro--show-detail` :995-1008 (uses `(cerebro--owned)` and the name lookup),
  `cerebro--launch` :1076-1120 (ah-mi7 rewrites its spawn; the exit-hook add and `cerebro--last-exit`
  clearing :1096-1101 stay), `cerebro--note-exit` :1154-1174, `cerebro--nudge` :1204-1210,
  `cerebro--end-session` :1212-1220, `cerebro--supervise` restart comment :1232-1238, `cerebro--revert`
  `(owned (cerebro--owned))` :1742, `cerebro-start` :1887, `cerebro--kill-session-buffer` :1899-1914,
  `cerebro-kill` :1923, `cerebro--live-implementer-names` :509-520 (by process, deliberately not by
  `--owned` — leave it), `cerebro--derive-implementer` :165-189, `cerebro--derive` :191+ (`owned` is a
  list of names, threaded through — keep that shape).
- `cerebro-test.el`: `session-buffer-name-shape` :348, `start-action-*` :353-367, `kill-action-*`
  :384-400 and :2239, `note-exit-records-and-forgets` :445-473 (drives `cerebro--note-exit` with a
  buffer named `*fleet: Bishop*`), `owned-buffer-agent-name-*` :594-600, a `cerebro--owned` stub at
  :267 and :614, `derive-owned-implementer-without-a-state-file-is-idle` :1100-1113 (asserts
  `start-action` → `already-up` with `owned` given), `derive-owned-implementer-ignores-a-stale-state-file`
  :1115-1126, the ah-mi7 launch tests (stub `require` and `vterm-mode`).
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:26,29`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el`

**The table**, in the "Launching and killing" section, before `cerebro--launch`:

```elisp
(defvar cerebro--sessions nil
  "The sessions this Emacs started: an alist of (NAME . BUFFER), one per agent.

The one record of ownership (ah-5pp).  It used to be inferred by matching
every buffer's name against `*fleet: NAME*', so a second launch for a name -
which vterm would call `*fleet: NAME*<2>' - made an agent nobody could see,
and four separate guards stood in front of that one failure.  Now
`cerebro--launch' writes here and refuses a second session while the first
is live, and everything that asks whose a session is, whether it is up, or
which buffer holds it reads here.  Global, not buffer-local: sessions
outlive the fleet buffer, and `M-x cerebro' after a `q' must still know
what it started.")

(defun cerebro--session (name)
  "The live session buffer this Emacs started for NAME, or nil.

Live means the buffer exists and its process is running - the same test
`cerebro--owned' has always applied.  A dead entry is dropped on the way
past, so the table never accumulates the sessions of the day."
  (let ((buffer (alist-get name cerebro--sessions nil nil #'equal)))
    (if (and buffer (buffer-live-p buffer) (get-buffer-process buffer))
        buffer
      (when buffer
        (setq cerebro--sessions (assoc-delete-all name cerebro--sessions)))
      nil)))

(defun cerebro--session-name (buffer)
  "The agent name whose session is BUFFER, or nil when it is not one of ours."
  (car (rassq buffer cerebro--sessions)))

(defun cerebro--owned ()
  "Agent names whose sessions this Emacs itself started and which are still up."
  (delq nil (mapcar (lambda (entry) (and (cerebro--session (car entry)) (car entry)))
                    cerebro--sessions)))
```

`cerebro--session-name` reads the raw table (not `cerebro--session`) on purpose: `cerebro--note-exit`
is called by vterm's sentinel *after* the process is gone, and must still find the name.

- **`cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name`** (:937-944) is deleted, with the docstring's naming-scheme
  argument moved into `cerebro--sessions`'s.
- **`cerebro--launch`** (as ah-mi7 leaves it): first line of the body, before `require`:
  `(when (cerebro--session (cerebro-agent-name agent)) (error "cerebro: %s already has a live session" (cerebro-agent-name agent)))`;
  after `(buffer (cerebro--make-session-buffer session-name))`:
  `(setf (alist-get (cerebro-agent-name agent) cerebro--sessions nil nil #'equal) buffer)`.
  Docstring: one sentence — the buffer is recorded in `cerebro--sessions', which is what makes it
  ours; a name with a live session is refused here, whatever the list believes about its state.
- **`cerebro--start-action (agent owned)`** (:708-717) — the order flips, and it is the point of the
  bead:
  ```elisp
  (cond
   ((member (cerebro-agent-name agent) owned) 'already-up)   ; ours and live: nothing else matters
   ((cerebro--alive-p agent) 'external)                      ; up, but not ours
   (t 'launch))
  ```
  Docstring: ownership first, "so no gap in how a state is derived can start a second session over
  one we hold (ah-u3i's double session)". `cerebro--kill-action` (:727-738) is unchanged in logic
  (`dead` before `external` is still right for `k`), and takes `owned` from the table as before.
- **Session lookups**: `cerebro--detail-showing-p` :992, `cerebro--show-detail` :1003 (its
  `(member … (cerebro--owned))` guard becomes `(cerebro--session name)` → that buffer, else the
  placeholder), `cerebro--nudge` :1206, `cerebro--end-session` :1217, `cerebro--kill-session-buffer`
  :1910: `(get-buffer (cerebro--session-buffer-name agent))` becomes `(cerebro--session
  (cerebro-agent-name agent))`. `cerebro--end-session` and `cerebro--kill-session-buffer` also drop the
  entry after killing (`(setq cerebro--sessions (assoc-delete-all name cerebro--sessions))`), so a
  restart's launch sees no session even before the process sentinel has run.
- **`cerebro--note-exit`** (:1154-1174): `name` becomes `(and (buffer-live-p buffer) (cerebro--session-name buffer))`.
  Docstring: "finds the agent through `cerebro--sessions', not by the buffer's name". BUFFER nil and a
  buffer that is not ours still do nothing.
- **`cerebro--session-buffer-name`** stays: it names the buffer at creation and the placeholder scheme
  is derived from it. Its docstring loses "that holds AGENT's live session" — it is the name a
  session is *given*, and `cerebro--sessions` is what holds it.
- **`cerebro--supervise`** restart comment (:1232-1238): reword — kill before launch is still the
  order, and now `cerebro--launch` would refuse rather than make an invisible `<2>` if it were not.
- **`cerebro--derive-implementer`** (:174-186): the comment's second half ("vterm would call it
  `*fleet: <name>*<2>` … invisible for ever") is no longer true; reword to "…`s` would ask to launch
  over a session we hold — `cerebro--start-action` refuses on ownership, and `cerebro--launch`
  refuses again, but the row should not lie in the meantime". The rule (`idle`) stays.
- Grep the file for `owned-buffer-agent-name`, `*<2>` and "invisible for ever"; nothing may survive
  that describes the old failure as current.
- **`emacs/README.md`**: if it explains ownership by buffer name, one line: sessions are recorded
  when started.

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el`

- Delete `owned-buffer-agent-name-*` (:594-600). Every test binds `cerebro--sessions` with `let` around
  what it drives (or `cl-letf` `cerebro--owned`, as :267/:614 already do).
- `cerebro-test/session-table-knows-what-it-started`: with `cerebro--sessions` let-bound to nil, a
  buffer with a live process (`(start-process "cerebro-test" buf "sleep" "30")` — batch Emacs can)
  recorded under `"Cyclops"`: `(cerebro--session "Cyclops")` is that buffer, `(cerebro--owned)` is
  `("Cyclops")`, `(cerebro--session-name buf)` is `"Cyclops"`; kill the process (`delete-process`)
  and wait for it (`(while (process-live-p p) (accept-process-output p 0.1))`) → `cerebro--session`
  is nil and the entry is gone from the table; a buffer killed outright likewise; a name never
  recorded → nil. `unwind-protect` the process and buffer.
- `cerebro-test/launch-records-its-session-and-refuses-a-second` (extends ah-mi7's
  `launch-makes-the-session-in-no-window` stubbing: `require`, `vterm-mode`, `cerebro--repo-root`;
  `cerebro--sessions` let-bound nil; the `vterm-mode` stub **starts a `sleep` process in the current
  buffer** with `start-process`, so liveness is real — a stub that starts nothing reads as dead to
  `cerebro--session`): after `(cerebro--launch agent)`, `(cerebro--session-name <the buffer>)` is the
  agent's name and `(cerebro--owned)` lists it; a second `(cerebro--launch agent)` signals an error
  whose message names the agent, and the table still holds exactly one entry for it. Kill the process
  in `unwind-protect`.
- `cerebro-test/start-action-already-up-beats-any-state`: an agent whose state is `dead` (the
  worst-case derivation) with `owned` = `("Cyclops")` → `already-up`; state `asking`, `done`,
  `unknown` with ownership → `already-up`; state `up` external, not owned → `external`; state `dead`,
  not owned → `launch`. Rewrite the docstring of `start-action-already-up` (:363) to say ownership
  is checked first.
- `note-exit-records-and-forgets` (:445-473): the buffers are no longer found by name — record each
  under `"Bishop"` in a let-bound `cerebro--sessions` before calling `cerebro--note-exit`; the
  `*scratch*` case (a buffer not in the table) still records nothing; a buffer *named* `*fleet:
  Bishop*` but **not** in the table records nothing (new assertion — the name is not the key).
- `derive-owned-implementer-without-a-state-file-is-idle` (:1100-1113): keep; its docstring's second
  sentence rewords as above.
- `cerebro-test/end-session-forgets-the-session`: record a live-process buffer, `cerebro--end-session`
  → the buffer is killed and `(cerebro--session name)` is nil without waiting for a sentinel.
- Grep the test file for `owned-buffer-agent-name` and `*<2>`; update the prose in the two ah-aao
  docstrings (:731, :969) that describe the `<2>` failure as the reason for a guard — the guard's
  reason is now "the launch would refuse", not "an invisible buffer".

Run from the cerebro clone root: byte-compile (warning-free) and the ERT suite in batch.

## Increments

1. RED: `session-table-knows-what-it-started`. GREEN: `cerebro--sessions`, `cerebro--session`,
   `cerebro--session-name`, the new `cerebro--owned`; delete `cerebro--owned-buffer-agent-name` and
   its two tests.
2. RED: `launch-records-its-session-and-refuses-a-second`, `end-session-forgets-the-session`. GREEN:
   `cerebro--launch`'s guard and record; the five lookups; `--end-session`/`--kill-session-buffer`
   forget; `cerebro--note-exit` by table (its rewritten test RED first).
3. RED: `start-action-already-up-beats-any-state`. GREEN: the flipped `cerebro--start-action`.
   Reword the comments/docstrings listed. Byte-compile clean; whole suite green.
4. Delivery, two PRs: cerebro `refactor(ah-5pp): the fleet view records the sessions it starts, and
   refuses a second one at the source`, `@copilot`, CI, squash; atlantis-hud bump `chore(ah-5pp): bump
   cerebro to owned sessions`. Close the bead after the bump merges.

## The test plan

- cerebro ERT in batch: five new/rewritten tests plus the suite; the byte-compile step.
- atlantis-hud: the bump PR's CI only.

## User-facing decisions

None. `s`, `k`, the detail window, the placeholder text and the buffer names are unchanged; a second
`s` on a running agent says "already up" as it does today, only for a better reason. Not asked.

## Out of scope

- ah-mi7 (the spawn — this builds on it) and ah-6uo (render/tick): same file, other functions.
- `cerebro--live-implementer-names` (:509-520): by process on purpose, for the sweeps; leave it.
- Adopting a session the navigator started in their own terminal (an "external" agent stays
  external).
- Persisting `cerebro--sessions` across an Emacs restart: a new Emacs owns nothing, as today.

## Validation

```bash
cd <cerebro clone>
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el       # no warnings
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
grep -n "owned-buffer-agent-name\|\*<2>\|invisible for ever" emacs/cerebro.el emacs/cerebro-test.el   # nothing that describes it as current
```

By hand, after the bump: `M-x cerebro`, `s` an implementer, `s` it again — "already up", one
`*fleet: NAME*` buffer; let it finish a bead — the restart replaces it, still one buffer; `k` it,
then `s` — a fresh session; `q` the fleet buffer, `M-x cerebro` — the running sessions are still
listed as owned (not "outside Emacs").

## Known traps

- **`cerebro--session-name` must read the raw table**, not go through `cerebro--session`: vterm's
  sentinel calls `cerebro--note-exit` after the process has died, when `cerebro--session` would
  already say nil — and would prune the entry before the exit line was recorded.
- **Prune from the sentinel side too?** No: `cerebro--session`'s lazy prune and the explicit forget in
  `--end-session`/`--kill-session-buffer` are enough; a hook in every session buffer would be a
  fifth place to keep in step.
- **Batch tests need a real process for liveness** (`start-process … "sleep" "30"`); kill it in
  `unwind-protect`, and after `delete-process` wait for the sentinel before asserting the entry is
  gone. `get-buffer-process` is what `cerebro--session` reads, so a stubbed `vterm-mode` that starts
  no process reads as *dead* — the ah-mi7 launch tests that only check "no window" are fine with
  that; the ownership tests here are not.
- **`assoc-delete-all` with `#'equal`**: names are strings; `alist-get`'s TESTFN and
  `assoc-delete-all` (which uses `equal` by default) both need string equality — never `assq`.
- **`cerebro--show-detail`'s guard.** It showed the placeholder for an owned name whose buffer had
  gone; with `cerebro--session` returning nil for a dead process the same fallback holds — do not
  drop the `or … placeholder`.
- **Wait for ah-mi7 to merge** and rebase on it; the `cerebro--launch` body you edit is its. Never
  branch inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared checkout; the bump PR here will be `BEHIND` — the
  merge-state check first.

title: Releases push main through a pre-push export gate that aborts, and retry around it
description:
## The cost being paid
The bead export is kept honest by a pre-push hook that commits on main and aborts the push, so everything else that pushes main — the release script above all — has to know the gate's contract and retry around it. Five fix/chore commits landed on the same interaction in three days; two releases were stranded at a bumped manifest with no tag and finished by hand; two release tags point at gate commits; twelve "chore(beads): refresh the issues export" commits sit on first-parent main; and two beads rewrote the same few lines of scripts/release.ts.

## Evidence
- 3293921 chore(ah-601): refresh the beads export at pre-push instead of every commit (#134)
- 6d1f5dc fix(ah-6xq.1): let only main carry the bead export (#141) — feature branches each carried a backlog snapshot and "whichever merged last reverted every close, claim, label and plan"
- 13c29b7 fix(ah-7go): settle the bead export before a release bumps anything (#148) — "meeting that abort after the version commit is what stranded v0.5.2 at a bumped manifest with no tag"
- 1cd99c3 fix(ah-r2e): retry a release push on the export gate's abort (#174) — v0.5.3 "failed exactly as v0.5.2 did and had to be finished by hand"; "tidying merged branches took four attempts"
- db24011 fix(ah-9dg): anchor the release tag to the release commit, not HEAD (#198); bead ah-9dg notes: "Both beads rewrite the same few lines of scripts/release.ts"
- git tag: v0.5.2 → 52ce64c chore(beads): refresh the issues export; v0.5.3 → b757b1d chore(beads): refresh the issues export

## Where
scripts/release.ts; scripts/releaseSupport.ts; scripts/beadsExportGate.ts; .beads/hooks/pre-push

## What a refactoring would change
One place that owns "push main" — the release script and the gate calling the same settle-then-push step, or the export refreshed by a workflow on the remote rather than a hook that fails the pusher — so a release is one push with no retry logic and no tag can land on a gate commit.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

`.beads/issues.jsonl` — the committed, readable export of the bead database — is kept fresh by a
**pre-push hook** (`scripts/beadsExportGate.ts`, run from `.beads/hooks/pre-push:59-68` outside
beads' own markers): on `main`, it exports, compares, and if stale **commits the refresh and aborts
the push** with "run the push again". A hook cannot amend the refs git has computed, so the abort is
inherent to the design — and everything else that pushes `main` has had to learn its contract: the
release script settles the export before bumping (ah-7go, after v0.5.2 was stranded at a bumped
manifest with no tag), retries the push on the gate's abort (ah-r2e, after v0.5.3 was stranded the
same way), and pins the tag's sha (ah-9dg, after v0.5.3's tag landed three commits above its
release). Five fixes on one seam in three days; two tags (`v0.5.2`, `v0.5.3`) point at
`chore(beads)` commits; twelve `chore(beads): refresh` commits on first-parent main; and
`scripts/releaseSupport.ts` grew `settleExport`, `pushWithRetry`, `isGateAbort`, `recoveryAdvice`.

Since squash-merges happen on GitHub, only two things ever push `main` from a machine: the release
script and the navigator's own hand-pushes (`git log --first-parent v0.5.3..` shows exactly those).
Settled with the navigator (2026-08-15): **the committed export is refreshed at release time only,
by the release script, as an ordinary commit before the version bump; the pre-push gate goes.**
Rejected: Cerebro refreshing it on its ten-minute sweep (a `chore(beads)` commit on main whenever the
backlog moved — many a day with four implementers); keeping the gate and only trimming the release
script (the abort-and-retry contract would remain for every hand-push). Between tags bd/Dolt is the
source of truth, as the beads-workflow skill already says ("never read it as truth").

After this bead: one push, no retry, no settle, no abort — the release commit follows the export
commit, the tag is pinned to the release commit as ah-9dg made it, and `releaseSupport.ts` loses the
gate machinery. **Where the code lives.** atlantis-hud (`scripts/`, `.beads/hooks/pre-push`,
`CLAUDE.md` pair, `docs/implementation-plan.md` line) — PR 1; cerebro (`skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md`,
`agents/orchestrator.md`) — PR 2 — plus the bump. Line numbers against atlantis-hud `origin/main`
after #284 and cerebro `origin/main` `d05694b`+.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `scripts/beadsExportGate.ts` → `scripts/beadsExport.ts` (`git mv`)

Keep the two things worth keeping — `stableExport` (:55-103, the volatile-field normalisation, with
its tests) and the export/compare logic — and turn the module from a gate into **an exporter**:

```ts
export type ExportOutcome =
  | { kind: "unchanged" }
  | { kind: "refreshed"; committed: boolean }     // written; committed unless git refused
  | { kind: "skipped"; reason: "no-bd" | "no-beads" | "export-failed" };

/**
 * Refreshes .beads/issues.jsonl from the database and commits it as
 * "chore(beads): refresh the issues export" when it changed. Run by the release script before the
 * version bump (ah-cgk); never from a hook. Any branch: the caller decides where it runs.
 */
export function refreshBeadsExport(root: string): ExportOutcome;
```

- `decideGate`/`GateDecision` (:105-166) become `decideExport(input): { kind: "unchanged" } | { kind: "refresh"; text } | { kind: "skipped"; reason }` — the `detached-head` and `off-main` cases go (the caller, `release.ts`, has already refused a non-main branch at :150-158); the rest as today.
- `runGate` (:222-266) becomes `refreshBeadsExport`: write, `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>`, `git add`/`git commit --no-verify -m <REFRESH_MESSAGE>`; **no `process.exit`, no stderr contract about pushing again**; `PUSH_AGAIN_MESSAGE` deleted. The `invokedDirectly` block (:272-287) becomes a tiny CLI: `pnpm run beads:export` prints the outcome — for the navigator who wants a fresh export by hand (`package.json`: `"beads:export": "tsx scripts/beadsExport.ts"`).
- Header comment rewritten: why the export exists, why it is refreshed at release time only, why no
  branch but main should ever commit it (keep the ah-6xq.1 paragraph :16-20 verbatim), and that
  `export.auto` stays `false` in `.beads/config.yaml` (its comment at :75-77 → "refreshed by the
  release script").
- `scripts/beadsExportGate.test.ts` → `beadsExport.test.ts`: `stableExport` cases unchanged;
  `decideGate` cases → `decideExport` (drop `off-main`/`detached-head`; keep `no-bd`, `no-beads`,
  `export-failed`, `up-to-date`/`unchanged`, `refresh`).

### `.beads/hooks/pre-push`

Delete the block below the `END BEADS INTEGRATION` marker (:59-68). Beads' own section stays byte
for byte. Add nothing.

### `scripts/releaseSupport.ts` and `scripts/release.ts`

- Delete `settleStep`, `settleExport`, `Settlement` (:28-61), `isGateAbort`, `pushWithRetry`,
  `PushResult` (:111-146); `recoveryAdvice`/`ReleaseState` (:148-182) stay only if `finishRelease`
  still uses them for a *failed push* (it should: a push that fails for any reason must still say
  what state the release is in — bumped, tagged, pushed — and how to finish by hand); `finishRelease`
  (:202-…) drops `attempts` and the retry loop: create the tag on the pinned sha, push the branch
  once, push the tag once, report.
- `release.ts`: the *Settling the bead export* step (:207-230) becomes
  `const exported = refreshBeadsExport(root)` before the bump commit; log one line per outcome
  (`refreshed`: "release: refreshed the bead export (committed ahead of the bump)"; `unchanged`:
  nothing; `skipped`: "release: bead export skipped: <reason>" — a skip is not fatal, the release
  is not about the export). `PUSH_ATTEMPTS` (:75-80) and its comment go; the *pinned SHA* comment
  (:249-252) stays (ah-9dg). The header's mention of the gate (:50) is rewritten. `--dry-run` (:203)
  must not export or commit — check the order.
- `scripts/releaseSupport.test.ts`: delete the settle/retry cases; keep/adjust `finishRelease`
  (single push, tag pinned to the given sha, failure advice) and `describeGitFailure`.
- `scripts/releaseWorkflowGate.ts` — read it; if it references the export gate, adjust; probably not.

### Docs

- cerebro `skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md`: *Storage* bullet (:303-307) — "refreshed by the release
  script at every release (`pnpm run release`), or by hand with `pnpm run beads:export` from main;
  never read it as truth"; delete *The export gate* (:315-337) and replace with three lines

title: The map view has one owner, one decision module and one writer
description:
## The cost being paid
"Where the map is" is owned in two places — MapCanvas owns pan/zoom/framing, AppShell owns level and selected hex — both writing one localStorage record, and correctness rests on four refs plus effect definition order ("This effect runs before the frame effect (effects fire in definition order), which is what makes the restore win"). Viewport persistence had to be delivered twice: the first restore was overwritten a moment later by two other effects, the second PR's review found a third defect in the same mechanism, and the storage had to become read-modify-write so the two halves would stop undoing each other.

## Evidence
- bc9957c "Persist map viewport (pan + zoom) per game across sessions (#65)"
- 45b29be feat(ah-ppd): reopen a game on the map view it was left at (#137) — "were then overwritten a moment later, twice over": the selection-follow effect pulled the pan back to the opening hex, and the model-keyed re-frame threw the position away on every import; PR #137 review: "restoredRegionRef outlived the selection it described … keepsRestoredHex now ends the exemption"
- packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewRestore.ts:1–9: "A plain module rather than logic inside the component, because this decision has been wrong twice and neither mistake was visible in anything that renders"
- packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewportStorage.ts:8–11: read-modify-write "because the two halves change at different moments … or each would keep undoing the other's half of the view"

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx (viewRef/framedRef/pendingRestoreRef/restoredRegionRef :168–215, effects :359–449); mapViewRestore.ts; mapViewportStorage.ts; AppShell.tsx (enterGame :1729–1780, saveFocusForGame effect :575–582)

## What a refactoring would change
One owner of the map view (level, pan, zoom, selection) as one piece of state with one persistence step, MapCanvas rendering it rather than holding half of it in refs, so restore-vs-frame-vs-follow is a decision made once in plain code (as mapViewRestore.ts started to do) rather than by effect ordering.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

"Where the map is" is owned in two places. `MapCanvas.tsx` holds pan and zoom in `viewRef`/`view`
(:215) plus three bookkeeping refs — `framedRef` (:210), `pendingRestoreRef` (:235),
`restoredRegionRef` (:239) — and reads the saved record itself in an effect keyed on `gameId`
(:373-384) that must run *before* the frame effect (:386-424) because "effects fire in definition
order"; the follow effect (:426-450) reads and clears the restored hex. `AppShell.tsx` owns level and
selected hex in `workspaceStore`, reads the same record in `enterGame` (:1359-1364) to set them, and
writes them back from an effect (:445-452). Both halves write one localStorage record through
`mapViewportStorage.ts`'s read-modify-write `merge` (:159-172; `saveViewportForGame` :182-188 from
`MapCanvas` `commit` :310-321, `saveFocusForGame` :198-205 from the shell), "or each would keep undoing
the other's half of the view". Viewport persistence shipped twice (bc9957c, then ah-ppd #137) and the
second's review found a third defect in the same mechanism; `mapViewRestore.ts` was the start of
lifting the decision out of the component.

This bead finishes that: **one owner** — the workspace store — holds the whole map view (level, selected
hex, committed viewport, and the restore bookkeeping) as one slice, updated by explicit actions in
the same `set` as the selection changes that affect it; **one pure module** (`mapViewState.ts`, which
absorbs `mapViewRestore.ts`) holds every transition and decision; **one persistence step** in the shell
writes the whole record from that state — no read-modify-write, no second reader, no refs, no
reliance on effect order. `MapCanvas` keeps only what is genuinely the DOM's: the in-flight
`viewRef` for a free drag, `applyView`, size, insets, and the two effects that turn a decision into a
`commit` — and those read the store rather than refs. **No player-visible change**: the three
`tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts` tests (:127-190 — reopen on the left view, per-game views, a landing
turn leaves the map alone) are the acceptance criteria and must pass unchanged. ah-lfo (insets as an
explicit input) is a separate, later bead on the same file and is wired behind this one.

Verified on `origin/main` `6388e88`:
- `MapCanvas.tsx`: imports :28-29; `framedRef` :203-213; `view` state :215; `gameIdRef` :228-231;
  `pendingRestoreRef` :233-235; `restoredRegionRef` :236-239; `applyView` :286; `commit` :310-321;
  `slide` :324-330; `readInsets` :339-353; resize observer :355-370; the game-change effect :373-384;
  the frame effect :386-424; the follow effect :426-450; `view` read at :668 (`zoomBand`), :709-720
  (rulers), :1126-1134 (note pins).
- `mapViewRestore.ts` (87 lines): `MapViewDecision`, `MapViewInput`, `mapViewDecision`,
  `shouldFollowSelection`, `keepsRestoredHex`; `mapViewRestore.test.ts` (three describes).
- `mapViewportStorage.ts`: `SavedMapView` :43-51, `loadSavedView` :140-156, `merge` :159-172,
  `saveViewportForGame` :182-188, `saveFocusForGame` :198-205; its test file (the "keeps the focus /
  keeps the viewport" cases at :73-92 are the read-modify-write pins).
- `workspaceStore.ts`: `WorkspaceGame` :39-44, `level` :71, `openGame` :99/:251-257, `closeGame`
  :259-265, `selectRegion` :271-281, `restoreSelection` :283-284, `setLevel` :289-294,
  `DEFAULT_LEVEL` :161, `partialize` :338-347 (the map view is **not** persisted by the store — the
  per-game record in localStorage is the persistence, and stays so); `workspaceStore.test.ts` (the
  selection describes :35-164).
- `AppShell.tsx`: `import { loadSavedView, saveFocusForGame }` :114; `selectRegion`,
  `restoreSelection`, `level`, `setLevel` store bindings :362-369, `openGameInStore`/`closeGameInStore` :409-411;
  `saveFocusForGame` effect :445-452; the "saved level this game no longer draws" effect :454-462;
  `enterGame` :1316-1370 (`openGameInStore` :1338-1343, `loadSavedView` … `restoreSelection`
  :1359-1364); `<MapCanvas` :2466-2490.
- `MapCanvas.test.tsx` renders with `renderToStaticMarkup` (:48, :81) — no store setup; the store's
  default state must be enough for a static render.
- `mapViewport.ts:40` `Viewport = { tx; ty; step }`, `ORIGIN`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewState.ts` — new; `mapViewRestore.ts` is renamed into it

Everything from `mapViewRestore.ts` moves here unchanged in meaning (`mapViewDecision`,
`shouldFollowSelection`, `keepsRestoredHex` and their docs), plus the state and its transitions:

```ts
import type { Viewport } from "./mapViewport";
import type { SavedMapView } from "./mapViewportStorage";

/**
 * The map view as the workspace store holds it: everything about "where the map is" that is not
 * the level or the selected hex (those are the store's own fields), owned in one place so the
 * decisions below are made from state, not from refs and effect order.
 */
export type MapViewState = {
  /** The game this view belongs to; `null` between games. */
  gameId: string | null;
  /** The pan and zoom last committed by the map, or `null` before the first frame or restore. */
  viewport: Viewport | null;
  /** A saved viewport still waiting for the map to apply it. */
  pendingViewport: Viewport | null;
  /** The level last framed for `gameId`, or `null` when none has been. */
  framedLevel: number | null;
  /** The hex a restore put back, for as long as it is still the one selected. */
  restoredRegionId: string | null;
};

export const NO_MAP_VIEW: MapViewState = { gameId: null, viewport: null, pendingViewport: null, framedLevel: null, restoredRegionId: null };

/** The view for a game just opened, from its saved record (or none). */
export function mapViewOpened(gameId: string, saved: SavedMapView | null): MapViewState;
// { gameId, viewport: null, pendingViewport: saved?.viewport ?? null, framedLevel: null, restoredRegionId: saved?.regionId ?? null }

/** After the map commits VIEWPORT on LEVEL: the pending restore is spent and the level is framed. */
export function mapViewCommitted(state: MapViewState, viewport: Viewport, level: number): MapViewState;
// { ...state, viewport, pendingViewport: null, framedLevel: level }

/** After the selection becomes SELECTED-REGION-ID: the restored hex's exemption ends unless it is still the one selected (`keepsRestoredHex`). */
export function mapViewSelectionChanged(state: MapViewState, selectedRegionId: string | null): MapViewState;
// keepsRestoredHex(selectedRegionId, state.restoredRegionId) ? state : { ...state, restoredRegionId: null }
```

`mapViewDecision`'s input becomes `{ view: MapViewState; gameId: string | null; level; hasHexes }`
and reads `pending: view.pendingViewport` and `framedLevel: view.gameId === gameId ? view.framedLevel
: null` — the same two facts, from state. Its doc's first paragraph (why restore does not wait for
the level) still holds and stays.

### `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.ts` — the owner

- State: `mapView: MapViewState` (initial `NO_MAP_VIEW`), **not** in `partialize` (say so next to it:
  the per-game record is the persistence, `mapViewportStorage.ts`).
- Actions:
  ```ts
  /** Opens GAME on its saved view: level, selected hex and the pending viewport land in one set. */
  openGame: (game: WorkspaceGame, saved: SavedMapView | null) => void;
  // set({ game, level: saved?.level ?? DEFAULT_LEVEL, selectedRegionId: saved?.regionId ?? null,
  //       selectedUnitId: null, selectionEpoch: 0, mapView: mapViewOpened(game.gameId, saved) })
  /** The map committed a view: `mapViewCommitted`. */
  commitMapView: (viewport: Viewport, level: number) => void;
  ```
  `closeGame` also sets `mapView: NO_MAP_VIEW`. `selectRegion`, `restoreSelection` and `setLevel`
  each apply `mapView: mapViewSelectionChanged(state.mapView, <the new selectedRegionId>)` in their
  existing `set` (for `setLevel`, `null`; for `selectRegion` only on the branch that changes the
  selection). `updateGameRuleset`, `selectUnit`, the panels: untouched.
- Doc on `openGame`: "the one place a game's saved view enters the store — the level, the hex and
  the pending viewport arrive together, so no render sees a new game over an old view or the reverse
  (ah-ian)".

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewportStorage.ts` — one writer

- `saveMapView(gameId: string, view: { viewport: Viewport; level: number; regionId: string | null }, storage = optionalStorage()): void`
  writes the whole record `{ tx, ty, step, level, regionId }` with `setItem` — no `merge`, no read.
  Doc: one writer now; the record is written whole whenever any part changes, and only once the map
  has a committed viewport for the game (the shell's rule, below), so there is nothing to preserve
  from a previous write.
- Delete `merge`, `saveViewportForGame`, `saveFocusForGame`. `loadSavedView` and everything it
  reads (`viewportIn`, `levelIn`, `regionIdIn`, `storedView`, `StoredView`) unchanged. Header doc:
  drop the "two writers" paragraph, say the opposite.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — renders the view, owns the drag

- Imports: drop `loadSavedView, saveViewportForGame, SavedMapView` (:28) and `./mapViewRestore`
  (:29); add `import { mapViewDecision, shouldFollowSelection } from "./mapViewState";` and
  `import { useWorkspaceStore } from "../workspaceStore";`.
- Delete `framedRef` (:203-213), `gameIdRef` (:228-231), `pendingRestoreRef` (:233-235),
  `restoredRegionRef` (:236-239), the `view` state (:215), and the game-change effect (:373-384).
- Read from the store: `const mapView = useWorkspaceStore((state) => state.mapView);`
  `const commitMapView = useWorkspaceStore((state) => state.commitMapView);`
  `const view = mapView.viewport ?? ORIGIN;` (what `zoomBand` :668, the rulers :709-720 and the pins
  :1126-1134 read — the same variable name, so those lines do not change).
- `commit` (:310-321): `viewRef.current = next; applyView(); commitMapView(next, level);` — no
  storage call, no `setView`; add `level` and `commitMapView` to its deps (it re-creates on a level
  change; the effects that depend on it re-run and decide "hold"). `slide` unchanged.
- The frame effect (:386-424): the decision from state —
  `mapViewDecision({ view: mapView, gameId, level, hasHexes: onLevel.length > 0 })`; on `restore`:
  `commit(decision.viewport)` (the commit stamps `framedLevel` and spends the pending viewport in the
  store — no ref writes); on `fit`: as today, `commit(fitted)` when `fitTo` returns one. Deps:
  `[gameId, level, onLevel, size, commit, mapView]`. Keep the comments; drop the sentence about
  effect order.
- The follow effect (:426-450): `if (!shouldFollowSelection(selectedRegionId, mapView.restoredRegionId)) return;`
  then as today; the `keepsRestoredHex` branch is gone (the store did it). Deps add `mapView.restoredRegionId`.
- Everything else in the file (drag, wheel, keyboard cursor, marquee, notes, themes) untouched.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — one read, one write

- Import: `import { loadSavedView, saveMapView } from "./mapViewportStorage";` (:114).
- `enterGame` (:1338-1364): `openGameInStore({ …the four fields… }, loadSavedView(opened.manifest.metadata.gameId))`
  replaces the `openGameInStore(...)` call **and** the `loadSavedView`/`setLevel`/`restoreSelection`
  block; the comment about "the level is set whether or not one was saved" moves to the store's
  `openGame`. Drop `setLevel`/`restoreSelection` from `enterGame`'s deps if unused there (`setLevel`
  is still used by the effect at :454-462, which stays).
- The `saveFocusForGame` effect (:445-452) becomes the one writer:
  ```ts
  const mapView = useWorkspaceStore((state) => state.mapView);
  // The whole view, written whenever any part of it changes - once the map has committed a
  // viewport for this game, which is when there is a whole view to write. Before that (a game
  // with nothing to frame yet) nothing is written, and nothing is lost: the level and the hex
  // were read from this same record a moment ago.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (openGameId === null || mapView.gameId !== openGameId || mapView.viewport === null) return;
    saveMapView(openGameId, { viewport: mapView.viewport, level, regionId: selectedRegionId });
  }, [openGameId, mapView, level, selectedRegionId]);
  ```
- Nothing else: `<MapCanvas>` props unchanged.

### Tests

- `mapViewState.test.ts` (rename `mapViewRestore.test.ts`, keep every case, adapt
  `mapViewDecision`'s input shape) plus a `describe("the map view's transitions")`:
  `mapViewOpened` with a full record → pending viewport, restored hex, no frame; with `null` → all
  null but `gameId`; `mapViewCommitted` → viewport set, pending spent, level framed;
  `mapViewSelectionChanged` keeps the exemption on the same hex, ends it on another and on `null`;
  no-op when nothing was restored (`===` the same object).
- `workspaceStore.test.ts`: `openGame(game, saved)` sets `level`, `selectedRegionId`, `selectionEpoch
  0`, `mapView` in one call (assert with `getState()` after one action); `openGame(game, null)` →
  `DEFAULT_LEVEL`, no selection; `selectRegion` to another hex ends the restored exemption;
  `restoreSelection(sameHex)` keeps it; `setLevel` ends it; `commitMapView` sets viewport/framed;
  `closeGame` → `NO_MAP_VIEW`. Existing selection tests stay green (`openGame` gains a second
  argument — update their calls to pass `null`).
- `mapViewportStorage.test.ts`: `saveMapView` round-trips through `loadSavedView`; per-game
  independence; the two "keeps the … when … is saved" cases (:73-92) are replaced by "writes the
  whole record" (a second `saveMapView` with a different level replaces the first entirely). The
  read cases untouched.
- `MapCanvas.test.tsx`: unchanged; it must still render (the store's default `mapView` is
  `NO_MAP_VIEW`, so `view` is `ORIGIN`). A zustand store needs no provider — `useWorkspaceStore`
  reads the module-level store, and its `persist` storage falls back to an in-memory map under Node
  (`workspaceStore.ts:205-217`), so a static render works. `MapCanvas.tsx` reads no store today
  (`grep useWorkspaceStore MapCanvas.tsx` is empty), so this is the first hook into it — but
  `LayerChips.tsx` and `RegionPanel.tsx` read `useWorkspaceStore` and are static-rendered by their
  tests today, so a store read is not a provider problem.
- Smoke: `tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts` (:127-190, three tests) unchanged and green on both
  projects — the acceptance; `tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts` and `workspace.spec.ts` (map recentre,
  drags) unchanged and green.

## Increments

1. RED: `mapViewState.test.ts` (rename + transitions). GREEN: `mapViewState.ts`; delete
   `mapViewRestore.ts`. Point `MapCanvas.tsx`'s import at the new module (no other change yet) so
   the suite compiles.
2. RED: `workspaceStore.test.ts` cases. GREEN: the slice and actions; `enterGame` passes `saved`
   (typecheck forces it).
3. RED: `mapViewportStorage.test.ts` (`saveMapView`, whole-record). GREEN: `saveMapView`; delete
   the three old functions; the shell's writer effect; typecheck.
4. `MapCanvas.tsx`: refs out, store in, effects on state. `pnpm run typecheck && pnpm --filter
   @atlantis/shared test`; then `pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts` locally, both
   projects, and `tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts` (recentre reads the view).
5. `pnpm run check:fast`; PR `refactor(ah-ian): the map view has one owner, one decision module and
   one writer`; `@copilot`; CI; squash. Close the bead.

## The test plan

- Unit: `mapViewState.test.ts`, `workspaceStore.test.ts`, `mapViewportStorage.test.ts`,
  `MapCanvas.test.tsx` (unchanged), the shared suite.
- Browser: `persistence.spec.ts` (3), `shortcuts.spec.ts`, `workspace.spec.ts` — unchanged, both
  projects; the whole smoke suite in CI.

## User-facing decisions

None. Where the map opens, what it remembers, and when it travels to a selection are exactly as
today; the three persistence smoke tests pin it. Not asked.

## Out of scope

- The insets / one-shot fit (ah-lfo, wired behind this bead): `readInsets`, `fitTo`, the resize
  observer and the keyboard path are untouched here.
- Persisting the map view through the store's own `persist` middleware: the per-game localStorage
  record is the format every player already has; keep it.
- Any change to the drag (`slide`, `viewRef`, `applyView`): "panning writes no React state" stands.
- The `selectionEpoch` pulse rules.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts
pnpm run check:fast
grep -rn "mapViewRestore\|saveViewportForGame\|saveFocusForGame\|pendingRestoreRef\|restoredRegionRef\|framedRef\|effects fire in definition order" packages/shared/src   # nothing
```

Human (Psylocke): open a game, pan and zoom, select a hex from the units table, pan away, reload —
same view, same selected hex, no travel; switch to another game and back — each keeps its own view;
import a new turn — the map does not move; change level and back — the level is framed once, then
held.

## Known traps

- **`commit` now depends on `level`.** It is recreated on a level change, and both effects that list
  it re-run — the frame effect decides `hold` unless the new level is unframed (in which case it
  fits, which is right), the follow effect finds nothing selected (`setLevel` clears the selection).
  Do not "stabilise" `commit` with a ref for `level`; the store needs the level the viewport was
  committed on.
- **The follow effect must not re-derive `keepsRestoredHex`.** The store ended the exemption in the
  same `set` that moved the selection; a second clearing in the effect is harmless but a second
  *reading* before clearing (today's order) is the ref-era logic this bead removes. `shouldFollowSelection`
  on the store's `restoredRegionId` is the whole rule.
- **Write only once a viewport is committed.** The writer effect's `mapView.viewport === null` guard
  is what makes whole-record writes safe; without it the first selection change after opening a game
  would write `{level, regionId}` and no viewport, and the reload would fit instead of restore —
  exactly the ah-ppd symptom.
- **`openGame` gains a parameter.** Every caller (`enterGame` only, but grep) and every store test
  that calls `openGame` must pass `saved` (`null` in tests that do not care).
- **`mapView` in the store is *not* persisted.** Adding it to `partialize` would restore game A's
  viewport into game B's first render; the per-game record is keyed correctly and this slice is not.
- **`MapCanvas.test.tsx` renders outside a game**: `mapView.viewport` is `null` there, `view` must
  fall back to `ORIGIN` — keep the `?? ORIGIN`.
- **WebKit / desktop-shell**: `persistence.spec.ts` asserts the exact `transform` string of
  `map-world`; a change in the order commits happen (e.g. fit then restore) shows up as a different
  string. Restore must still win over fit in the same render — that is the decision function's
  first branch, and the "restores a saved view rather than waiting for the level to agree" test.
- **Rebase risk**: ah-u4e.3 rewrites `AppShell.tsx`'s map model wiring (`model`, `memory`) around
  :429-439 and `enterGame` (:1320) — different lines from this bead's, but the same functions; and
  ah-lfo (behind this bead) touches `readInsets`/the frame effect. Rebase textually.

title: The map's visible strip is a measured value the first fit waits for and every path reads
description:
## The cost being paid
MapCanvas's initial fit is computed once from the live DOM boxes of whatever [data-map-overlay] panes are mounted at that instant, then held (framedRef → "hold"); its ResizeObserver watches only the host. So any panel's default footprint silently re-tiers the initial zoom, nothing exposes the "visible strip" to tests, and two plans read the mechanism as continuous when it is one-shot. One implementer paid about two hours when a bigger default units pane pushed the fit from map-mid to map-far and broke two smoke tests that never touch the pane; another paid 25 minutes recomputing the visible centre in a test, and that inset arithmetic is now duplicated in two smoke specs.

## Evidence
- docs/retrospectives/ah-2r3.md §"A bigger default units pane pushed the map's initial fit out a zoom tier, breaking two unrelated smoke tests" — "About two hours"; fixed by explicit zoom/pan in 3d44bf1's tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts hunk
- docs/retrospectives/ah-t2i.md §"A gesture that recentres the view is not idempotent at a fixed screen pixel" — "About 25 minutes … the side panes' insets are asymmetric enough that using box.width/2, box.height/2 picked a point covered by a panel header"; the arithmetic now lives in tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts:222–247 (visibleCentre) and tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:2477–2510
- Two plans misread it the same way: bead ah-3cs design "feeds mapOverlayInsets.ts and re-fits the map"; bead ah-2r3 design "MapCanvas observes every [data-map-overlay] with a ResizeObserver (MapCanvas.tsx:329, 345) and refits the map — dragging the units pane refits continuously" — the observer at :340–353 observes host only; framedRef/hold at :376–404
- bead ah-t2i design "Known traps": "readInsets() matters … the keyboard cursor path does not [pass insets], a known inconsistency — do not copy it" (MapCanvas.tsx:646–647 vs :434, :532, :783, :1032)

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx (readInsets :322–335, observer :340–353, frame effect :372–408, keyboard path :646–647); packages/shared/src/workspace/mapOverlayInsets.ts; packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx (:2889–3025 data-map-overlay markers)

## What a refactoring would change
The visible strip made an explicit input — the shell computes insets from its own layout state (which panes are open and how tall) and passes them to MapCanvas, which fits against that and re-fits when it changes — with the strip exposed for tests, so a pane's default cannot silently move the zoom tier and every pointer path (keyboard included) uses the same insets.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

**Blocked by ah-ian** (`bd dep`): that bead moves the map's view bookkeeping into the workspace store
and its decisions into `mapViewState.ts` (`mapViewDecision({ view, gameId, level, hasHexes })`,
`commit → commitMapView`, refs gone). This plan is written against ah-ian's plan; **read the merged
result before writing** and re-find the lines named below — the functions keep their names.

`MapCanvas` fits the level into "the strip the player can actually see" — the host minus whatever
`[data-map-overlay]` panes cover — but that strip is not an input: `readInsets` (:339-353 on
`origin/main` `6388e88`) reads the live DOM boxes at the moment it is called, the frame effect
(:386-424) calls it once when the level is first framed and then holds, and the `ResizeObserver`
(:355-370) watches only the host. So any pane's *default* footprint at that instant decides the
initial zoom tier (ah-2r3 paid two hours when a taller default units pane pushed two unrelated smoke
tests from map-mid to map-far), nothing exposes the strip to tests (two specs re-derive it from the
overlay boxes: `tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts:222-247` `visibleCentre`, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:2477-2510`),
two plans read the mechanism as continuous when it is one-shot, and the keyboard cursor path
(:663-665) is the one caller that passes no insets at all while the click, context-menu and
selection paths do (:449, :549, :831, :1080).

This bead makes the strip **an explicit, state-held input**: a hook measures the panes into
`insets: Insets | null` (`null` until the first measurement lands), `MapCanvas` reads that value —
never the DOM directly — on every path (fit, follow, recentre, click, keyboard), **the first fit
waits until the strip is known**, and the value is stamped on the map host as `data-map-insets` so
the smoke suite reads it instead of recomputing it. The fit stays one-shot per level (ah-ian's
`framedLevel`): a pane folding later moves nothing, which is the ah-ppd rule; what changes is that
the one fit is against a strip that is a value in state, arrives before the fit runs, and can be
asserted. Measurement stays DOM-based (`ResizeObserver` + `MutationObserver`) rather than being
computed from rem widths in the store: a pane's rendered height depends on its content and its
padding, and rem arithmetic in the shell would be a second, drifting copy of layout. No
player-visible change; the smoke suites are the acceptance.

Verified on `origin/main` `6388e88`:
- `MapCanvas.tsx`: `readInsets` :339-353 (queries `host.parentElement` for `[data-map-overlay]`,
  `overlayInsets(host.getBoundingClientRect(), overlays)`); size observer :355-370; frame effect
  :386-424 (`fitTo(..., readInsets())` :412-417); follow effect :426-450 (`readInsets()` :449);
  recentre `onContextMenu` :540-550 (:549); the keyboard cursor path :660-666 (**no insets**);
  :831 and :1080 (`centreOn(..., readInsets())`); host `<div ref={hostRef} … data-testid="map-canvas">`
  :752.
- `mapOverlayInsets.ts`: `Edge`, `Box`, `OverlayBox`, `overlayInsets(host, overlays)` — pure, tested
  in `mapOverlayInsets.test.ts` (7 cases); `mapViewport.ts`: `Insets` :192, `NO_INSETS` :194,
  `fitTo(coordinates, width, height, insets)` :222, `centreOn` :256, `isOffScreen` :279.
- `AppShell.tsx`: the four markers `data-map-overlay="top|left|right|bottom"` :2517, :2543, :2567,
  :2648 and the comment :2510-2515; the marked elements are always mounted (folding changes their
  class/size, and `overlayInsets` ignores a zero-size box).
- Smoke: `shortcuts.spec.ts:228-260` `visibleCentre(page, map)`; `workspace.spec.ts:2470-2510` the
  same arithmetic inline (`document.querySelectorAll("[data-map-overlay]")` :2487).
- `mapViewRestore.test.ts` (→ `mapViewState.test.ts` after ah-ian) `mapViewDecision` cases.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `packages/shared/src/workspace/useOverlayInsets.ts`

```ts
import { useEffect, useState, type RefObject } from "react";
import { overlayInsets } from "./mapOverlayInsets";
import type { Insets } from "./mapViewport";

/**
 * How much of the map the panes are covering, as state.
 *
 * `null` until the first measurement has landed - the map's first fit waits for it, so a pane's
 * default size can never re-tier the initial zoom by being measured a frame late (ah-2r3), and so
 * the strip is one value every path reads rather than a DOM read at each call site (the keyboard
 * cursor used to skip it). Measured, not computed from the store's rem widths: a pane's height is
 * its content's, and a second copy of the layout arithmetic here would drift.
 *
 * Re-measured when the host resizes, when any marked pane resizes, and when the set of marked
 * panes changes (a `MutationObserver` on the host's parent for `data-map-overlay`). Panes mark
 * themselves with `data-map-overlay="<edge>"`; nothing here knows which panes exist.
 */
export function useOverlayInsets(hostRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>): Insets | null;
```

Implementation shape: `const [insets, setInsets] = useState<Insets | null>(null)`; one effect on
`[]` (the ref is stable): `measure()` = the body of today's `readInsets` (:339-353) → `setInsets`
(a value-equal result keeps the previous object — compare the four numbers, so consumers' deps do
not churn); a `ResizeObserver` observing the host and every current overlay element; a
`MutationObserver` on `host.parentElement` (`{ subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true,
attributeFilter: ["data-map-overlay"] }`) that re-collects the overlays (`observer.disconnect()`,
observe again) and measures; measure once synchronously at effect start; disconnect both on
cleanup. Guard `typeof ResizeObserver === "undefined"` (the static-render tests never run effects,
but be safe) by returning `null`.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewState.ts` (from ah-ian)

`mapViewDecision` gains `stripKnown: boolean` in its input and returns `hold` instead of `fit` while
it is false: "restore needs no strip — a saved viewport is where the player left the map; a fit does,
because it is computed against it. Fitting against a strip not yet measured is exactly the one-shot
that went wrong on ah-2r3." One new test:
`waits for the strip before the first fit, but restores without it` (`stripKnown: false` → `hold` when
a fit would otherwise be due; `restore` regardless).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx`

- `const insets = useOverlayInsets(hostRef);` next to the size state; delete `readInsets`
  (:339-353) and its `overlayInsets`/`OverlayBox` imports (:27) if unused.
- Frame effect: `mapViewDecision({ …, stripKnown: insets !== null })`; `fitTo(coordinates, size.width,
  size.height, insets ?? NO_INSETS)` — the `?? NO_INSETS` is unreachable on the `fit` branch and is
  for the type; add `insets` to the deps (a first measurement arriving triggers the fit that was
  waiting).
- Every `readInsets()` call (:449, :549, :831, :1080) becomes `insets ?? NO_INSETS`; the keyboard
  path (:663-665) **gains** `insets ?? NO_INSETS` on both `isOffScreen` and `centreOn`, and its
  comment says why it is the same value the pointer paths use (ah-t2i's "known inconsistency", now
  gone).
- The host: `<div ref={hostRef} className="absolute inset-0" data-testid="map-canvas"
  data-map-insets={insets ? JSON.stringify(insets) : undefined}>` — absent until measured, then the
  four numbers, e.g. `{"left":320,"right":300,"top":40,"bottom":220}`.
- The component doc (:155-176): add one bullet — **"The fit is one-shot per level, against a
  measured strip."** `useOverlayInsets` is the strip; it arrives before the first fit and is the
  only insets any path reads; a pane changing later moves nothing until the next level or game
  (ah-lfo). This is the sentence two plans needed.

### Smoke — one helper, read not derived

Add to `tests/smoke/gameSetup.ts` (the one helper module every spec imports; `shortcuts.spec.ts:4`):

```ts
/** The strip of the map the player can see, from the value the map itself fits against. */
export async function visibleStrip(page: Page): Promise<{ x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }>;
// box = map-canvas boundingBox; insets = JSON.parse(await page.getByTestId("map-canvas").getAttribute("data-map-insets"))
// (expect.poll until the attribute is present); return { x: box.x + insets.left, y: box.y + insets.top,
//   width: box.width - insets.left - insets.right, height: box.height - insets.top - insets.bottom }
export async function visibleCentre(page: Page): Promise<{ x: number; y: number }>;
```

`shortcuts.spec.ts:228-260` and `workspace.spec.ts:2477-2510` use it and lose their own overlay
arithmetic. Their assertions are unchanged.

New smoke test in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` (the zoom tier is asserted there, `map-far` at
:2522 and :3181): `"the first fit is against the strip the panes leave"`: open a report; read
`data-map-insets` — every inset non-zero (the four panes are there); then `foldPanel(page, "units")`
(the helper the fold test at :1402-1411 uses) — `data-map-insets.bottom` drops, and the `map-world`
`transform` does **not** change (one-shot). Two facts pinned: the strip is exposed and true, and a
later change moves nothing.

### Unit tests

- `useOverlayInsets`: no jsdom, so no hook test; the pure arithmetic is `overlayInsets` (already
  tested). Add to `mapOverlayInsets.test.ts` nothing.
- `mapViewState.test.ts`: the `stripKnown` case above.
- `MapCanvas.test.tsx`: static renders never run effects, so `insets` is `null` and the host has no
  `data-map-insets`; add one assertion in an existing render that the attribute is absent (pins
  "unknown until measured").

## Increments

1. RED: `mapViewState.test.ts` `stripKnown` case. GREEN: the decision.
2. `useOverlayInsets.ts`; `MapCanvas.tsx` reads it everywhere, `readInsets` deleted, the keyboard
   path fixed, the attribute stamped, the doc bullet. `pnpm run typecheck && pnpm --filter
   @atlantis/shared test`.
3. RED: the new smoke test (fails before increment 2 on the missing attribute — run it now to see
   it green, then keep it) and the two specs on `visibleStrip`/`visibleCentre` (`shortcuts.spec.ts`,
   `workspace.spec.ts`). `pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts
   tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts` locally, both projects.
4. `pnpm run check:fast`; PR `refactor(ah-lfo): the map's visible strip is a measured value the first
   fit waits for, and every path reads`; `@copilot`; CI; squash. Close the bead.

## The test plan

- Unit: `mapViewState.test.ts` (+1), `MapCanvas.test.tsx` (+1 assertion), the shared suite.
- Browser: `shortcuts.spec.ts` (recentre idempotence, now on the shared helper), `workspace.spec.ts`
  (+1, and the drag/marquee tests on the helper), `persistence.spec.ts` (restore must still win over
  the waiting fit); the whole smoke suite in CI on both projects.

## User-facing decisions

None. The map opens on the same fit it does today (the panes are measured before the fit either
way; this makes the order a guarantee), and nothing moves that did not move before. Not asked.

## Out of scope

- Re-fitting when a pane folds or resizes: the fit is one-shot per level by design (ah-ppd/ah-ian);
  this bead exposes and stabilises the strip it uses, it does not make framing continuous.
- Computing insets from the store's rem widths.
- The `data-map-overlay` markers in `AppShell.tsx` — unchanged.
- ah-ian's ownership move (this builds on it).

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts
pnpm run check:fast
grep -rn "readInsets\|getBoundingClientRect" packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx   # readInsets gone; the remaining rect reads are the pointer paths' own event bounds
grep -rn "data-map-overlay" tests/smoke/*.spec.ts   # only the new helper (or none)
```

Human (Psylocke): open a game with a report — the map opens framed inside the strip between the
panes at the same zoom as before; drag the units pane taller — the map does not move; press the
arrow keys until the cursor leaves the strip — the map recentres inside the strip, not under a pane.

## Known traps

- **`useOverlayInsets` must measure synchronously once at effect start**, before any observer
  callback — otherwise the first fit waits for a resize that may never come on a static layout.
- **Value equality on `setInsets`**: `overlayInsets` returns a fresh object every time; setting it
  unconditionally re-runs every effect that lists `insets` on every observer tick (and the frame
  effect would then re-decide on each — harmless, `hold`, but noisy). Keep the previous object when
  the four numbers match.
- **The frame effect's deps gain `insets`; the follow and pointer paths read the render's `insets`.**
  A measurement lags a real layout change by one observer tick — same as today's `readInsets` lagged
  nothing but was called at each site; the recentre gesture (`shortcuts.spec.ts`) is idempotent
  either way, which is what its test pins.
- **Restore must not wait for the strip.** `mapViewDecision`'s `restore` branch stays first and
  unconditional; only `fit` checks `stripKnown` — `persistence.spec.ts` asserts the exact restored
  `transform` and would show a fit-then-restore as a different string.
- **The attribute is a string**: `JSON.stringify` on every render is cheap, but stamp `undefined`
  (attribute absent) while `null`, not the string `"null"` — the smoke helper polls for presence.
- **WebKit** (`desktop-shell` project) reports `boundingBox()` in CSS pixels like Chromium; the
  helper's arithmetic is the same on both. Do not `Math.round` the insets on one side only.
- **`MutationObserver` on the host's parent** sees the whole workspace subtree — filter to
  `attributeFilter: ["data-map-overlay"]` and `childList`, and re-collect rather than re-measure on
  every mutation, or a typing session in the orders editor re-measures the map on every keystroke.
- **ah-ian first.** Its `commit` and effect deps change; write this on top of the merged result,
  not on `6388e88`'s line numbers.

title: A new export can still bypass the desktop save dialog, because the saver is optional
description:
## The cost being paid
"The shell saves a file where the player asks" is an optional TextFileSaver prop threaded into AppShell that each export site had to remember to take, while the browser-only downloadTextFile stayed exported from the shared barrel as a callable default. The same defect — a desktop export landing wherever the webview puts it, no dialog, no path — was fixed three times: once when the port was introduced for the map export only, then for the orders exports as a P0, then for the game backup as a P1. After the extraction downloadTextFile is still a public export and saveTextFile still optional.

## Evidence
- ce6150a feat(#113): introduced the port, used for the map export only
- 4573b49 fix(ah-7pa): orders export uses the desktop's native save dialog (#206) — bead ah-7pa (P0): "exportOrders and exportOrdersLong call downloadTextFile unconditionally"; extracted deliverTextFile "so a fourth exporter cannot get it wrong again"
- 7600c20 fix(ah-jfx): game backup export uses the desktop's native save dialog (#209) — bead ah-jfx (P1): "calls downloadTextFile unconditionally, exactly as the orders export did before ah-7pa"; also fixed the saver's hard-coded Text/["txt"] filter that "would fight the .json name or append .txt"; plan: "after this bead the fork's callers are map, orders ×2, and backup; anything new is a new bead"
- packages/shared/src/index.ts:2 still `export *` from downloadFile.ts

## Where
packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts and index.ts; packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx (:183–216 and the export sites); apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts (desktopTextFileSaver, filterFor); apps/desktop/src/App.tsx

## What a refactoring would change
Make the saver the only way to deliver a file — a required port with the browser download as its web implementation, downloadTextFile no longer exported — so a fourth exporter cannot choose the wrong one; the filter derived from the file name.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

"Save this file where the player asks" is an **optional** `TextFileSaver` prop on `AppShell`
(`AppShell.tsx:359`, `saveTextFile?: TextFileSaver`), and every exporter has to remember to route
through `deliverTextFile(saver, …)` (`downloadFile.ts:35-47`) — the fork that picks the shell's saver
when there is one and the browser download when there is not. The desktop bundle passes
`desktopTextFileSaver()` (undefined outside Tauri), the web bundle passes nothing. The same defect —
a desktop export landing wherever the webview puts it, no dialog, no path — was fixed three times
(map export ce6150a, orders ah-7pa P0, backup ah-jfx P1), and after all that `downloadTextFile` is
still a public export of `@atlantis/shared` (`index.ts:2`) that a fourth exporter can call directly,
and `saveTextFile` is still optional.

The fix inverts the default: **the saver is the only way to deliver a file.** `TextFileSaver` takes
the MIME type too and is a **required** prop; the browser download becomes one implementation of it
(`browserTextFileSaver`, the web shell's), the desktop's saver returns the dialog when the plugins
are there and the browser saver otherwise; `deliverTextFile` and the public `downloadTextFile`
disappear. A fourth exporter then has exactly one thing to call, and TypeScript refuses a shell that
forgets to say how files are saved. **No player-visible change** in either shell.

Blocked by (both planned, wired): **ah-k6i.4** — moves the three exporters into
`packages/shared/src/workspace/exportActions.ts`, which is where this bead edits them (its plan
names `deliverMapExport`, `deliverOrdersExport`, `deliverGameBackupExport`, each taking
`saveTextFile: TextFileSaver | undefined` and a `deliver` default) — and **ah-9lv** — gives
`desktopTextFileSaver(plugins = desktopPlugins())` in `apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts`, which
this bead changes to never return `undefined`. Read both plans; line numbers here are against
`origin/main` after #282 for files they do not touch, and against those plans' shapes for the ones
they do. Re-grep everything when you branch.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts`

```ts
/**
 * A shell's way of putting a file where the player asks. Resolves with the path written, `""` when
 * the shell cannot name one (a browser download), or `null` when the player cancelled the save.
 * Required of every shell (ah-150): the fork between "dialog" and "download" used to be per export,
 * and was forgotten three times.
 */
export type TextFileSaver = (fileName: string, text: string, mimeType: string) => Promise<string | null>;

/** The browser's implementation: an anchor download, which reports no path. */
export const browserTextFileSaver: TextFileSaver = async (fileName, text, mimeType) => {
  downloadTextFile(fileName, text, mimeType);
  return "";
};

function downloadTextFile(fileName: string, text: string, mimeType: string): void { … as today :49-58 … }
```

`deliverTextFile` (:35-47) is deleted; `downloadTextFile` becomes module-private. Keep the header
comment (:1-12), reworded: the download is *one saver*, and the desktop's dialog is the other.
`downloadFile.test.ts` (:4-40, four `deliverTextFile` cases) → replaced by two `browserTextFileSaver`
cases with `document`/`URL` stubbed as the file already does for the download (read it first):
resolves `""` and clicks an anchor named `fileName`; the object URL is revoked on a later task.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/exportActions.ts` (as ah-k6i.4 leaves it)

- `deliverOrdersExport(saveTextFile: TextFileSaver, turnNumber, ordersDocument, ordersTemplateText, withDescriptions)`
  — the `deliver` parameter goes; body: `await saveTextFile(fileName, text, "text/plain")` inside
  the same try/catch-and-log.
- `deliverGameBackupExport(saveTextFile: TextFileSaver, gameId, backup)` → `return saveTextFile(fileName, backup, "application/json")`.
- `deliverMapExport(client, saveTextFile: TextFileSaver, …)` → `return saveTextFile(fileName, text, "text/plain")`.
- Header doc: the port is required now; the tests hand in a fake saver directly (no `deliver` seam
  needed any more).
- `exportActions.test.ts`: the "forwards an undefined saver … falls back to downloading" cases
  (from `AppShell.test.ts:34-46` and `:95-107`, moved by .4) are deleted — there is no undefined
  saver; the "forwards the shell's saver" cases assert on the fake saver's calls
  (`(fileName, text, mimeType)`) instead of on `deliver`.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

- Prop `saveTextFile: TextFileSaver` (required; :359 today) — the doc comment says why (three
  defects). Everything else in the shell already passes `saveTextFile` through to the three
  functions.
- `packages/shared/src/index.ts:2` still `export * from "./downloadFile"` — now exporting
  `TextFileSaver` and `browserTextFileSaver` only; `git grep -n downloadTextFile` outside
  `downloadFile.ts` must be empty.

### `apps/web/src/App.tsx` (:14)

`<AppShell client={client} platformLabel="web" appUpdate={useWebAppUpdate()} saveTextFile={browserTextFileSaver} />`
— import from `@atlantis/shared`.

### `apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts` (as ah-9lv leaves it)

`desktopTextFileSaver(plugins = desktopPlugins()): TextFileSaver` — never `undefined`: with plugins,
today's dialog body (ignoring `mimeType`; the filter still comes from `filterFor(fileName)`); without,
`browserTextFileSaver`. Doc: the browser saver is the answer in the preview server and the
web-style smoke run, exactly as an undefined saver used to be. `App.tsx` unchanged
(`saveTextFile={desktopTextFileSaver()}`), now always defined. `saveTextFile.test.ts`: the
"undefined → undefined" case (ah-9lv's) becomes "no plugins → the browser saver" (`toBe(browserTextFileSaver)`).

### `tests/smoke/desktop-shell.spec.ts` (ah-9lv's) — unchanged; it must still pass, and the web
project's export cases (`workspace.spec.ts:747-775` downloads, `backup.spec.ts:121-124`) too.

## Increments

1. RED: `downloadFile.test.ts` rewritten (`browserTextFileSaver`), `exportActions.test.ts` cases on
   the required saver, `saveTextFile.test.ts` no-plugins case. GREEN: `downloadFile.ts`,
   `exportActions.ts`, `saveTextFile.ts`.
2. `AppShell` prop required; `apps/web/src/App.tsx`; typecheck across the workspace
   (`pnpm run typecheck`) — the compiler finds any caller left; `git grep downloadTextFile` empty.
3. `pnpm run check`; PR `refactor(ah-150): saving a file is one required port; the browser download
   is its web implementation`; `@copilot`; CI; squash.

## The test plan

- Unit: `downloadFile.test.ts`, `exportActions.test.ts`, `apps/desktop` `saveTextFile.test.ts`, whole
  shared and desktop suites; workspace typecheck.
- Smoke: web export downloads (`workspace.spec.ts:747-775`, `backup.spec.ts`, `map-export.spec.ts`)
  and the desktop-shell port cases (ah-9lv) all green under `pnpm run check`.

## User-facing decisions

None — both shells save exactly as before. Navigator: P2 at triage (2026-08-15).

## Out of scope

- Any new exporter; the updater/opener ports; `filterFor`.
- The desktop plugin port itself (ah-9lv).

## Validation

```bash
git grep -n 'downloadTextFile\|deliverTextFile' -- packages apps tests   # only downloadFile.ts's private function
pnpm run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test && pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop test
pnpm run check
```

Human check: none needed; Psylocke may spot-check an orders export in the web build (a download)
and on the desktop build (the dialog).

## Known traps

- **Two blockers move the same files** (`exportActions.ts` from .4, `saveTextFile.ts` from ah-9lv);
  branch only after both have merged and read their final shapes, not their plans, for the exact
  signatures.
- **`TextFileSaver` gains a third parameter** — every fake in the tests and the desktop's saver
  must accept it; the desktop ignores it (the dialog's filter comes from the name).
- **Making the prop required is a compile-time change across three packages** — run the workspace
  typecheck, not just `@atlantis/shared`'s.
- **The smoke suites take the machine-wide lock**; run `check` once at the end.

title: Refactoring: the remembered map is built once, in core, and the planner and the screen agree about who is in a hex
description:
## The cost being paid
The map accumulated across turns is built once in Rust for the planner and risk (movement/graph.rs MapKnowledge) and once in TypeScript for display (hexMapModel.ts buildHexMapModel), from the same stored sightings, with every precedence rule — remembered regions bring their exits, only the current report may claim units, a same-turn ally sighting is current — re-derived by hand on the TS side.
