design:
## Context

The rule "which lines are this unit's, this month" — a `TURN…ENDTURN` block is next month, a
`FORM…END` block is another unit's, both nest, `END` and `ENDTURN` are not interchangeable, a `unit`
line or a `#` directive abandons whatever is still open — is written four times and kept in step by
hand: `orders/parser.rs` (`OpenBlock` stack, `track_block` :191-233, `close_open_blocks` :276-293,
`read_line` :73-100), `orders/intents.rs` (`blocks` vec inside `read_intents` :107-163),
`orders/effects.rs` (`turn_depth` counter + `forming` stack in `Working::read_line` :310-347), and
`movement/request.rs` (`last_top_level_move` :197-238, over `split_whitespace` with no lexer at all).
One defect was fixed in three readers in one commit (c6ee017 / #95), the fourth needed its own issue,
and they disagree again today: `effects.rs` returns early on `turn_depth > 0` *before* the `unit`
check (:318-324), so an unclosed `TURN` swallows every later unit, while `intents.rs` (:118-121) and
`parser.rs` (:134-136) say a `unit` line ends everything; `end_does_not_close_a_turn_block` exists
twice (`intents.rs:596`, `tests/movement_trace.rs:157`).

This bead writes the walk **once**: `orders/walk.rs`, a block walker that reads a document line by
line through the lexer and hands each consumer *events* — a directive, a unit line, a block opening
or closing, a stray closer, an abandoned block, an order line with the depths it sits at — and the
four readers fold over those events with only their own semantics left in them. The block rules
become one set of tests, on the walker; the consumers' tests keep what is theirs (which intent a
line is, which unit an effect lands on, which move is last). Where the readers disagree today, the
walker settles it in the parser's favour — the syntax checker is the reader the player sees — and
the plan says so where it changes a consumer's behaviour on malformed input.

Verified on `origin/main` `6388e88`:
- `orders/lexer.rs`: `TokenKind` :21+, `Token { kind, text, column_start, column_end }` :41-49,
  `Token::is` :51-53 (case-insensitive), `LexedLine { repeat, tokens, comment, unterminated_quote }`
  :71-90, `lex_line` :94.
- `orders/parser.rs`: `validate_against` :31-46, `OpenBlock` :49-58, `Document` :61-70, `read_line`
  :73-100 (unterminated quote → error and return, :77-88; directive/unit/order dispatch :94-100),
  `read_directive` :103-132, `read_unit_line` :134-150, `read_order` :152-189 (`track_block` then
  `match_order`), `track_block` :191-233 (the `unexpected-block-end` message), `close_open_blocks`
  :276-293 (`unclosed-block`), `finish` :295-309; tests module :359+ (`end_closes_a_form_block…` :424,
  `a_balanced_turn_block_is_accepted` :579, `a_turn_block_left_open_at_the_next_unit_is_an_error` :599).
- `orders/intents.rs`: `read_intents` :107-163; tests :245+ (`orders_inside_a_turn_block…` :577,
  `end_does_not_close_a_turn_block` :596, `endturn_does_not_close_a_form_block` :612,
  `orders_inside_a_form_block_belong_to_the_unit_being_formed` :629).
- `orders/effects.rs`: `Working { …, current, forming: Vec<Option<usize>>, turn_depth }` :265-278,
  `read_line` :310-347, `active` :350-355, `open_form` :357-408; tests :617+
  (`turn_blocks_are_next_month_and_repeat_orders_are_this_month` :1025).
- `movement/request.rs`: `last_top_level_move` :185-238 (doc :185-196 — the "no ENDFORM" and
  "unmatched opener swallows the rest" rules), tests :270+.
- `crates/core/tests/movement_trace.rs` :108-170 (the four block tests on the trace).
- `orders/mod.rs` :12-20 (`pub mod` list).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `crates/core/src/orders/walk.rs` (`pub mod walk;` in `mod.rs`, alphabetical)

```rust
//! The one walk over an orders document's block structure.
//!
//! Every reader of an orders document has to know which lines are inside a `TURN…ENDTURN` block
//! (next month's orders) or a `FORM…END` block (a unit that does not exist yet), that the two nest,
//! that `END` closes only a FORM and `ENDTURN` only a TURN, and that a `unit` line or a `#`
//! directive abandons whatever is still open. Four readers used to keep that walk each; one defect
//! had to be fixed in three of them at once (c6ee017), and they had drifted apart again by ah-nc7.
//! This module walks once and reports what it passes; what to do about it is each reader's.

use super::lexer::{lex_line, LexedLine, Token};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BlockKind { Turn, Form }

impl BlockKind {
    /// The keyword that opens it, as the messages spell it.
    pub fn opener(self) -> &'static str;      // "TURN" | "FORM"
    /// The keyword that closes it.
    pub fn terminator(self) -> &'static str;  // "ENDTURN" | "END"
}

/// Where a block was opened, for a message about it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Opened { pub kind: BlockKind, pub number: usize, pub column_start: usize, pub column_end: usize }

/// One line, lexed, with its first token split off. `arguments` is everything after `command`.
pub struct Line<'a> {
    pub number: usize,            // 1-based
    pub text: &'a str,
    pub lexed: &'a LexedLine,     // `repeat`, `comment` and the tokens as lexed
    pub command: &'a Token,
    pub arguments: &'a [Token],
}

/// How deep a line sits: `turn` open TURN blocks, `form` open FORM blocks, innermost last is
/// whichever opened last - the walker keeps the stack; readers get the two counts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Depth { pub turn: usize, pub form: usize }

pub enum Event<'a> {
    /// A line the lexer could not finish: an unterminated quote. Nothing about it is classified and
    /// it changes no block. `span` is the quote's `(start, end)`.
    Broken { number: usize, text: &'a str, span: (usize, usize) },
    /// A `#…` line (`#atlantis`, `#end`, or an unknown directive). Every open block was abandoned
    /// first - the `Abandoned` events for them precede this one.
    Directive(Line<'a>),
    /// A `unit …` line. Likewise preceded by `Abandoned` for every block still open.
    Unit(Line<'a>),
    /// `TURN` or `FORM`. `depth` is the depth *before* it opens.
    Open { line: Line<'a>, kind: BlockKind, depth: Depth },
    /// `ENDTURN` or `END` closing the innermost open block, which was of its kind. `depth` is the
    /// depth *after* closing.
    Close { line: Line<'a>, kind: BlockKind, depth: Depth },
    /// `ENDTURN` or `END` that closes nothing: no block open, or the innermost is of the other kind
    /// (`expected` says which, and where it opened). The stack is unchanged.
    Stray { line: Line<'a>, expected: Option<Opened>, depth: Depth },
    /// A block still open when a `unit` line, a `#` directive or the end of the document arrived.
    Abandoned(Opened),
    /// Any other line with a command: an order. `depth` is where it sits.
    Order { line: Line<'a>, depth: Depth },
}

/// Walks SOURCE and calls VISIT once per event, in document order. Blank lines and comment-only
/// lines produce no event. Every reader in this crate goes through here.
pub fn walk(source: &str, mut visit: impl FnMut(Event<'_>));

/// The last line number in SOURCE (0 for an empty document) - what `parser::Document::finish`
/// needs and used to track itself.
pub fn last_line_number(source: &str) -> usize;   // source.lines().count()
```

Rules inside `walk`, in the order applied per line: lex; `unterminated_quote` → `Broken`, done;
no tokens → nothing; command starts with `#` → abandon all (innermost first? — **outermost first**,
the order `close_open_blocks` reports today: `std::mem::take` iterates in push order), then
`Directive`; `unit` → abandon all, then `Unit`; `TURN`/`FORM` (via `Token::is`, so `@TURN` and
`turn` count — the lexer strips `@` and `is` ignores case) → `Open`, push; `ENDTURN`/`END` → if the
innermost open block's terminator is this keyword, pop and `Close`, else `Stray { expected:
innermost }`; anything else → `Order` at the current depth. At end of source: abandon all
(outermost first). A visitor callback rather than an iterator, so the events can borrow the
per-line `LexedLine` without an owned copy per line.

`Depth` is derived from the stack each time (`iter().filter(kind).count()`); the stack is a
`Vec<Opened>`.

### `orders/parser.rs`

`Document` loses `blocks`; `read_line`/`read_directive`/`read_unit_line`/`track_block`/
`close_open_blocks` are replaced by one `visit(&mut self, event: Event<'_>, ruleset)`:
- `Broken` → the `unterminated-quote` error (:80-88);
- `Directive` → the body of `read_directive` (:104-131) minus `close_open_blocks` (the walker's
  `Abandoned` events did it) — `#end` still sets `closed`;
- `Unit` → the `missing-unit-id` check (:139-149);
- `Open`/`Close` → the `match_order` half of `read_order` still runs for the keyword (`TURN`, `FORM`,
  `END`, `ENDTURN` are grammar commands with argument shapes — today `read_order` runs
  `track_block` *and* `match_order` on them; keep `match_order` and `report_mismatch`), no block
  bookkeeping;
- `Stray` → the `unexpected-block-end` error with today's two messages (:212-227), built from
  `expected` (`Opened.kind.opener()`, `.number`, `.kind.terminator()`), plus `match_order` as above;
- `Abandoned(opened)` → the `unclosed-block` error (:278-291) from `opened`;
- `Order` → `find_order` / `unknown-command` / `match_order` / `report_mismatch` (:158-188).
`validate_against`: `walk(source, |event| document.visit(event, ruleset)); document.finish(source)`;
`finish` uses `last_line_number(source)` and no longer calls `close_open_blocks`. Diagnostics still
sorted by line afterwards (:41-44). **Every existing parser test stays green unchanged** — the
messages, codes and columns are the same.

### `orders/intents.rs`

`read_intents` becomes a fold: `Unit` → push a `UnitIntents` when the id is a number (as :123-129);
`Order { depth }` with `depth == Depth::default()` → `read_order` into the last unit (:150-160);
everything else ignored. The `blocks` vec and the four `if command.is(…)` branches go. Tests
:577-650 stay green (they are the consumer's view of the same rules); leave them.

### `orders/effects.rs`

`Working` loses `turn_depth`; `read_line` becomes `visit(&mut self, event)`:
`Directive` → `current = None; forming.clear()`; `Unit` → `forming.clear(); current = …` (:335-339);
`Open { kind: Form, depth }` with `depth.turn == 0` → `open_form(arguments)`; `Close { kind: Form,
depth }` with `depth.turn == 0` → `forming.pop()`; `Open/Close { kind: Turn }` → nothing;
`Order { depth }` with `depth.turn == 0` → `read_order(command, arguments)`; anything at
`depth.turn > 0` → nothing. **One behaviour change, deliberate**: an unclosed `TURN` no longer
swallows the units after it — the walker abandons it at the next `unit` line, as the parser and the
intents reader always did. Add a test `an_unclosed_turn_block_ends_at_the_next_unit` in effects'
tests (:617+): unit A `TURN` `WORK` (no ENDTURN), unit B `WORK` → B's effect is recorded. Say in
`Working`'s doc that the walk is `orders::walk`'s.

### `movement/request.rs`

`last_top_level_move` becomes `walk(orders, |event| if let Event::Order { line, depth } = event {
if depth == Depth::default() { if let Some(steps) = parse_move(line.text) { last = Some(steps) } } })`.
Its docstring keeps the "unmatched opener swallows the rest" sentence **only for the end of the
document** — a `unit` line inside the text (which this function is not given today; it reads one
unit's orders) would now abandon the block, which is the walker's rule and harmless here. The
`split_whitespace` reading and the `@` stripping go (the lexer does both). Tests :270+ stay green.

### Tests — `crates/core/src/orders/walk.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`, the block rules once

Fold `walk` into a `Vec<String>` of event summaries (`"open TURN @1 t0f0"`, `"order @3 t1f0"`,
`"close FORM @5 t0f0"`, `"stray END @6 expects ENDTURN@2"`, `"abandoned TURN@2"`, `"unit @7"`,
`"directive @1"`, `"broken @4"`) and assert the sequence for:
- `a_turn_block_is_next_month`: order inside TURN has `t1`; after ENDTURN `t0`.
- `a_form_block_nests_inside_a_turn`: TURN, FORM, order (`t1f1`), END closes the FORM (`t1f0`),
  ENDTURN closes the TURN.
- `end_does_not_close_a_turn_block` and `endturn_does_not_close_a_form_block` — `Stray` with
  `expected` naming the innermost block; depth unchanged.
- `a_unit_line_abandons_every_open_block` — `Abandoned` ×2 outermost first, then `Unit`.
- `a_directive_abandons_every_open_block` and `the_end_of_the_document_abandons_open_blocks`.
- `a_repeat_prefix_and_case_do_not_matter` (`@turn`, `Endturn`).
- `an_unterminated_quote_is_broken_and_changes_no_block`.
- `blank_and_comment_lines_produce_no_event`.
Then delete the duplicate `end_does_not_close_a_turn_block` from `tests/movement_trace.rs:157-170`
(keep the intents copy — it asserts intents, not the walk — or delete it too if it asserts only the
walk; read it and decide, saying which in the commit).

## Increments

1. RED: the walker tests. GREEN: `walk.rs`, `pub mod walk`.
2. RED: `an_unclosed_turn_block_ends_at_the_next_unit` in effects (fails today). GREEN: effects
   through the walker. Suite green.
3. Parser through the walker (its own tests are the RED/GREEN — run them; every one must pass with
   no assertion changed). Then intents, then request, each with its existing tests as the gate.
4. Delete the duplicated trace test; `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
   -D warnings && cargo test --workspace`; `pnpm run check:fast` (the wasm build); PR
   `refactor(ah-nc7): one walk over the orders document's blocks, four readers fold over it`;
   `@copilot`; CI; squash. Close the bead.

## The test plan

- Rust: `walk.rs` tests (new, ~9), `parser.rs`/`intents.rs`/`effects.rs`/`request.rs` tests
  (unchanged, +1 in effects), `tests/movement_trace.rs`, `tests/orders_preview.rs`,
  `tests/validate_real_orders.rs`, `tests/movement_orders.rs`; the workspace suite; clippy, fmt.
- CI `wasm` (the crate compiles for the web); `pnpm run check:fast`. The smoke suite exercises the
  orders lint and the movement trace and stays green.

## User-facing decisions

None. The one behaviour change (an unclosed `TURN` no longer hides later units from the effects
preview) is a malformed-orders edge already flagged by the syntax checker, resolved toward what the
checker says; not asked.

## Out of scope

- The SAIL divergence (`intents.rs:234` files SAIL as month-long while `parse_move` reads it as
  movement): a classification rule, not the walk — file a follow-up bead if it bites.
- Any change to the grammar (`grammar.rs`), the token readers (`forms.rs`) or the semantics.
- Reading `#atlantis`/`#end` differently in any consumer.
- The TypeScript orders editor's own line reading (`packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts` etc.) — a
  different layer.

## Validation

```bash
cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check:fast
grep -n "blocks: Vec<\|turn_depth\|split_whitespace" crates/core/src/orders/parser.rs crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs crates/core/src/orders/effects.rs crates/core/src/movement/request.rs   # nothing
```

Human: none needed (Psylocke may skip): the orders lint, the movement trace and the effects preview
read the same documents as before.

## Known traps

- **`Abandoned` events come outermost first.** `close_open_blocks` reported in push order
  (`std::mem::take` + `for`), and the parser's diagnostics are sorted by line afterwards anyway —
  but a test on the walker's event order should pin outermost first so a future consumer relying on
  it is not surprised.
- **`TURN`/`FORM`/`END`/`ENDTURN` are still grammar commands.** The parser must keep running
  `match_order` on them (they have argument shapes: `FORM n`, `TURN` takes none) — the walker only
  removes the *block* bookkeeping from `read_order`, not the shape check.
- **`Token::is` is case-insensitive and the lexer strips `@`**: `@turn` opens a block in every reader
  today (request.rs strips `@` by hand); the walker inherits both from the lexer, and the test
  `a_repeat_prefix_and_case_do_not_matter` pins it.
- **The visitor borrows the per-line `LexedLine`.** `Line<'a>` lives for one callback; a consumer that
  needs a token past the callback clones it (intents already clones `id.text`).
- **`Depth` equality**: "top level" is `depth == Depth::default()` (both zero); effects deliberately
  ignores `form` depth (a FORM's orders belong to the formed unit) and reads only `depth.turn`.
- **The unterminated-quote line**: today only the parser stops on it; intents/effects/request read
  whatever tokens the lexer produced before the quote. After this bead none of them classify such a
  line (`Broken`). That is a change on a line the checker already marks as an error; accept it, and
  say so in the PR.
- **`clippy -D warnings`** on a big `match` — keep `visit` methods flat; a `#[allow]` is not the
  answer.

`index.test.ts` that builds a wasm client and a tauri client from fakes and asserts they normalise
alike, which is what makes every persistence bead write both arms (ah-o1t.1: +154 lines of
core-wasm for three notes commands; ah-jg6.1: +59). Bishop asks that the arm's fate be decided.

**Decision (mine): delete it.** The web has had its own store for a week and the sibling bead on
the store's duplication (ah-8m0, P3) is about moving *rules* into core, not about routing the web
through these functions. After this bead a persistence command is a Rust core function, a
`core-tauri` command, a Tauri wrapper, an IndexedDB twin and a `createTauriAdapter` method — one
fewer layer and no stub. Behaviour changes nowhere: nothing called what goes.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs`

- Delete the fifteen native persistence functions (:766-1112) and the fifteen stubs (:1113-1293).
- Delete the DTOs and `From` impls that only they used (:131-416, the `#[cfg(not(target_arch =
  "wasm32"))]` block) — but **let the compiler decide**: remove the functions first, `cargo build -p
  atlantis-hud-core-wasm` on the host and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, then delete whatever is
  now unused (dead-code warnings under `-D warnings` will name them). Some DTOs (e.g. the report
  import/merge ones used by `prepare_report_import_state`, :437) stay; the persistence ones
  (`OpenedGameDto`, `OrderDraftDto`, `HexNoteDto`, …) go.
- Delete the imports at :3-4 (`Path`), :10-11 (`parse_report`, if unused after), :16-24
  (`atlantis_hud_core_persistence::…`), and the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` cases that exercise them
  (:1294-1400: `order_draft_dto_maps_composite_key`, `hex_note_dto_maps_both_ways`,
  `persistence_dto_maps_bidirectionally`, and any other on a deleted DTO; keep
  `dto_maps_core_fields` and the two `order_validation_dto_*`).
- Header comment: say what this crate is now — the core's pure functions for the browser bundle;
  persistence is `core-tauri` (desktop) and `browser-core`'s IndexedDB store (web).

### `crates/core-wasm/Cargo.toml`

Remove the `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies] atlantis-hud-core-persistence`
block and `tempfile` under `[dev-dependencies]` if nothing else uses it (grep the tests). `crate-type`
stays.

### `crates/core-persistence/Cargo.toml`

Its comment "The web app stores through its own adapter instead" (Bishop's *Where*) — reread and
keep or trim; no dependency change.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

- Delete `WasmBindings` (:1195-1299) and `createWasmAdapter` (:2085-2265); `git grep -n
  'WasmBindings\|createWasmAdapter' packages apps docs` must then name nothing but the test and doc
  edited below.
- Any type used only by them (check `TauriInvoke`'s neighbours; the `*WireShape` types are shared
  with the tauri adapter and stay).

### `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`

The parity describe (:11-…) compares `wasmClient` and `tauriClient` method by method. Rewrite each
`await expect(wasmClient.x(...)).resolves.toEqual(await tauriClient.x(...))` as
`await expect(tauriClient.x(...)).resolves.toEqual(<literal>)`, where `<literal>` is what the pair
produces today: run the suite **before** deleting anything with a temporary
`console.log(JSON.stringify(await tauriClient.x(...)))` per case (or `expect(...).toMatchInlineSnapshot()`
once, then convert to `toEqual` literals — inline snapshots are acceptable here if the file already
uses them; check), then delete the wasm side. Cases that exist only for the wasm build (:1060-1068
"refuses to merge through a wasm build with no persistence linked in", :1186 "normalizes the wasm
answer to the same manifest", :1205, :1257 "asks the wasm binding for the same export") are deleted.
The describe's name becomes "core client tauri adapter contract" and its comment says the wasm
transport lives in `browser-core` with its own tests.

### `docs/adapter-api.md:87`

Drop the `createWasmAdapter(bindings)` bullet; one sentence that the browser transport is
`createWebCoreAdapter` in `@atlantis/browser-core`.

## Increments

1. Capture the tauri literals in `index.test.ts` (test still green with both clients), commit that
   rewrite alone (`test(ah-350): pin the tauri adapter's contract directly`).
2. RED is not the shape here — this is deletion; the tests that must stay green are the whole
   `core-client` suite, `browser-core`'s, `cargo test --workspace`, and the wasm build. Delete
   `createWasmAdapter`/`WasmBindings` and the wasm-only cases; typecheck.
3. Delete the Rust arms and DTOs, `Cargo.toml` deps; `cargo build -p atlantis-hud-core-wasm --target
   wasm32-unknown-unknown` (CI's `wasm` job builds this — check `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the
   exact command and run it), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test
   --workspace`; `pnpm run build:web` (the wasm bundle) and the smoke suite via `pnpm run check`.
4. PR `refactor(ah-350): core-wasm carries only the core's pure functions; the unused wasm
   persistence arm and adapter are gone`; `@copilot`; CI (watch `wasm`, `rust`, `checks`); squash.

## The test plan

- `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client test`, `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test`,
  `pnpm run typecheck`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy …`, the wasm target build, `pnpm run check`.

## User-facing decisions

None — nothing that ran is touched. Navigator: P2 at triage (2026-08-15).

## Out of scope

- Unifying the two stores' rules (ah-8m0) or generating the boundary (ah-wxk).
- Any change to `browser-core`, `core-tauri`, `main.rs`, or the native sweep (ah-ga6).

## Validation

```bash
git grep -n 'WasmBindings\|createWasmAdapter\|persistence is not linked' -- packages apps crates docs   # nothing
cargo build -p atlantis-hud-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown && cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check
```

Human check: none; Psylocke marks not-needed (the web and desktop apps behave identically; she may
load a report in each as a smoke).

## Known traps

- **Do the test rewrite first and separately** — once `createWasmAdapter` is gone the literals
  cannot be recovered without `git stash`; the pinned literals are the proof the tauri contract did
  not change.
- **Let `-D warnings` find the dead DTOs** rather than deleting by eye — a DTO used by a kept
  function (the import/merge ones) must stay; a `From` impl left without its DTO will not compile.
- **`crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` and the host build**: `cargo test --workspace` compiles this
  crate for the host, where the deleted arm used to live — after deletion the host build must still
  succeed with `core-persistence` gone from the manifest.
- **The wasm CI job's exact command** — read `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and run the same locally;
  `wasm-pack`/`wasm-bindgen` versions matter for the bundle the smoke suite serves.
- **The smoke suites take the machine-wide lock**; run `check` once at the end.

title: A Tauri command left out of the native sweep is only caught by a red Linux CI job
description:
## The cost being paid
The Tauri command registry is three hand-kept lists — the `generate_handler![…]` in main.rs behind cfg'd wrappers, the SWEEP table in tests/native/binding.spec.ts that must equal it in both directions, and the command names and snake_case argument names in core-client's createTauriAdapter — and the local gate sees none of them (`cargo check --workspace` runs without `desktop-runtime`, so every wrapper is cfg'd out; the native suite is Linux-only). The identical slip, a command in the handler list but not in SWEEP, has been fixed as a follow-up commit in five separate PRs, each after a red native CI job. The retrospective for the fifth prices it at one CI cycle (~7 minutes) plus a rebase, and records "Seen before: none found" — the day after the fourth.

## Evidence
- 82e418e "sweep the export_game and import_game commands main gained" (in 54cc409, PR #25)
- d32cc47 "sweep the new order_commands binding over real IPC" (in 3abf381, PR #84)
- 3849cef "sweep trace_move_orders" (in 6ea7f50, PR #85)
- c1fb9c9 "fix(ah-jg6.1): sweep list_imported_turns in the native IPC binding test" (in 9120935, PR #200)
- 16eb89a "fix(ah-o1t.1): sweep the three hex-note Tauri commands too" (in 78a2aa7, PR #268)
- docs/retrospectives/ah-o1t.1.md §"A new Tauri command needs a matching entry in the native binding sweep, and the plan did not name it"
- Same mirror, earlier: 24779d7 fix(#20) "Every native command was unreachable … all eleven commands failed" (camelCase vs snake_case); c9aa9ce feat(#18) "Three commands existed in core-tauri but were never registered in the Tauri handler"

## Where
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs (wrappers, generate_handler!); tests/native/binding.spec.ts (SWEEP); packages/core-client/src/index.ts (createTauriAdapter)

## What a refactoring would change
Derive the sweep from the handler list (or both from one table) so there is nothing to forget, and give the local gate a way to see the mirror — a check that compiles the desktop-runtime wrappers, or a unit test over the same table — so the first sign is not a red Linux job twenty minutes after the PR opens.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

The Tauri command registry is three hand-kept lists: `generate_handler![…]` in
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` (:485-516 on `origin/main` after #282), the `SWEEP` table in
`tests/native/binding.spec.ts` (:64-258) that must equal it in both directions, and the command
names `createTauriAdapter` invokes in `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` (:2267 onward,
`invoke<…>("command_name", …)`). The lockstep test that holds `SWEEP` equal to the handler list
already exists (`binding.spec.ts:258-289`) — but it lives in the **native suite**, which is
WebDriver + WebKitGTK, Linux-only, and runs only in CI. So the identical slip — a command
registered in `main.rs` and forgotten in `SWEEP` — has been fixed as a follow-up commit in five
separate PRs, each after a red native job (~7 minutes and a rebase each; ah-o1t.1's retrospective
records the fifth), and the local gate (`cargo check --workspace` without `desktop-runtime`, so
the wrappers are cfg'd out) sees none of it.

The fix is not a new check but **running the existing lockstep locally**: the `SWEEP` table moves to
a plain module both suites can import, and the two-way comparison against `main.rs` — plus a third,
new one-way check that every command `createTauriAdapter` invokes is registered (the c9aa9ce class:
"three commands existed in core-tauri but were never registered") — becomes a **tooling unit test**
that `pnpm test` and `pnpm run check` run on every machine. The native suite keeps the per-command
IPC binding tests, which are the part that genuinely needs the runtime. No player-visible change.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `tests/native/sweep.ts`

The `SweepEntry` type and the `SWEEP` array move here verbatim from `binding.spec.ts:52-258`,
together with the constants they read (`GAME_ID`, `ISO`, `REPORT`, `ALLY_REPORT`, `RULESET`, `context`
— check which of :17-50 they close over; move those too and export `context`, since the spec's
`create_game` case writes `context.databasePath`). Header: one table, two readers — the native
binding sweep and the tooling lockstep — and the ordering rule (`create_game` first, `delete_game`
last) from the existing comment (:59-63).

`binding.spec.ts` imports `SWEEP`, `context`, `BINDING_FAILURE` stays; its `describe` keeps the
per-command `it`s (:291-305) and **drops** the lockstep `it` (:258-289) — say in a comment where it
went and why (ah-ga6: the lockstep must run without WebKitGTK).

`tests/native/helpers.ts` is untouched (only the spec calls `invokeNative`).

### New: `scripts/tauriCommands.ts` (pure) and `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`

```ts
/** The commands `generate_handler![…]` registers, from main.rs's text; throws unless exactly one handler list. */
export function registeredCommands(mainRs: string): string[];        // the regex + split at binding.spec.ts:270-283
/** The commands createTauriAdapter invokes: every string literal passed as invoke's first argument. */
export function invokedCommands(coreClientIndex: string): string[];   // /invoke<[^>]*>\(\s*"([a-z_]+)"/g, deduplicated, in order
/** Registered but not swept, and swept but not registered. */
export function lockstep(registered: string[], swept: string[]): { registeredButNotSwept: string[]; sweptButNotRegistered: string[] };
```

`tauriCommands.test.ts` (runs under `vitest.tooling.config.ts` — `scripts/**/*.test.ts`):

- pure cases on small strings: `registeredCommands` parses a two-entry list, throws on zero or two
  handler lists; `invokedCommands` finds `invoke<X>("a", …)` and `invoke<void>("b")` and ignores a
  string that is not invoke's first argument; `lockstep` reports both directions.
- **the live lockstep**: read `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`, `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`
  and import `SWEEP` from `../tests/native/sweep` (path relative to `scripts/`; the tooling
  tsconfig — `tsconfig.tooling.json` — must include `tests/native/sweep.ts`; check and add it) →
  `lockstep(registered, SWEEP.map(e => e.command))` is `{ [], [] }`, and every `invokedCommands(...)`
  entry is in `registered` (`expect(invoked.filter(c => !registered.includes(c))).toEqual([])`).
  Message on failure names the command, as the native test's object shape does.

`sweep.ts` must therefore import nothing from `@wdio/globals` or `./helpers` — only `node:fs`/`node:path`
for the fixtures; keep it that way (a comment says so).

### `package.json` / CI

Nothing: `test:tooling` already runs `scripts/**/*.test.ts` and `pnpm test` (`scripts/runSuites.ts`)
includes it — confirm by running it. The native job is unchanged.

## Increments

1. RED: `tauriCommands.test.ts` pure cases. GREEN: `scripts/tauriCommands.ts`.
2. Move `SWEEP` to `tests/native/sweep.ts`; RED: the live lockstep test (fails only if the lists
   disagree today — they should not; to see it red once, temporarily add a fake name to a copy of
   the handler text in the pure test rather than to `main.rs`). GREEN. Drop the native lockstep
   `it`; `binding.spec.ts` compiles (`pnpm run typecheck:tooling` and whatever typechecks
   `tests/native` — `wdio.conf.ts`'s tsconfig; check).
3. `pnpm run check`; PR `test(ah-ga6): the Tauri command lockstep runs in the local gate, and the
   adapter's commands are checked against the handler list`; `@copilot`; CI — the native job must
   still run every `SWEEP` command; squash.

## The test plan

- `pnpm run test:tooling` (new file), `pnpm test`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run check`.
- CI's `native` job green with the sweep still driving every command over IPC.

## User-facing decisions

None. Navigator: P2 at triage (2026-08-15).

## Out of scope

- Generating the handler list or the adapter from one table (ah-wxk, P3, the boundary refactor).
- Argument-name checking (snake_case) — that needs real IPC and stays native.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test:tooling && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run check
```

Human check: none; Psylocke marks not-needed.

## Known traps

- **`tests/native/sweep.ts` is imported by a vitest test outside the native tsconfig** — it must be
  plain TypeScript with no wdio globals; and `tsconfig.tooling.json`'s `include` must cover it or
  `typecheck:tooling` will not see it (or will fail on it) — check both directions.
- **The native spec's `context` is mutated by the `create_game` case** — export the object, not a
  copy, or the scoped commands lose the database path and every case after `create_game` fails as
  a command (loudly, and misleadingly).
- **The regex for `invoke` must not match `invoke<T>(command, …)` where `command` is a variable** —
  only string literals; if a dynamic call exists (grep `invoke(` without `"` first), list it as
  known-dynamic in the test rather than widening the regex.
- **The tooling worktree test** (ah-efj) is fixed; the smoke lock still applies to `check`.

title: Agent state lives in .claude/agents-state, written by agent-state, for every role
description: First of two passes for ah-2n3. A pure rename, no behaviour change: the per-agent state directory .claude/implementers/ becomes .claude/agents-state/ (state files and stop flags alike) and scripts/implementer-state becomes scripts/agent-state, with a one-release shim at the old script name so an implementer mid-bead keeps writing. Every reader and every doc in the cerebro repo and the consumer (cerebro.el, the launchers, implement-bead, plan-bead, the agent files, README/CLAUDE.md, .gitignore) follows. Decided by the navigator on 2026-08-15 in preference to living with the misnomer.
design:
## Context

First of two passes for **ah-2n3** (interactive agents are invisible when asking). The navigator
decided the fix — every agent writes the same state file implementers do — and, asked on 2026-08-15
whether the directory and script names should follow, chose the **rename**: `.claude/implementers/`
becomes **`.claude/agents-state/`** (state files *and* stop flags) and `scripts/implementer-state`
becomes **`scripts/agent-state`**. This bead is that rename and nothing else: no behaviour changes,
so that ah-2n3.2 (interactive agents writing state) lands on honest names.

A pure rename still has one live-system hazard: an implementer that started before the bump keeps
running the old command from its skill text and writing to the old directory. So the old script
name stays for one release as a **shim** that `exec`s the new one (with a line on stderr), and the
new script writes to the new directory — so a mid-bead implementer's next write lands where the
fleet view now looks. The navigator moves any existing flags by hand once (`mv
.claude/implementers .claude/agents-state`) after the bump and restarts the fleet view; the PR
description says so.

**Where the code lives.** The cerebro submodule (PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro`), then the atlantis-hud
bump PR that also edits `.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md` and its mirror `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
Line numbers are against cerebro `origin/main` at **`8549679`** — check whether ah-p31's PR has
landed first (it edits `agents/verifier.md` and `docs/agent-workflow.md`) and rebase if so; the
sites below are found by `git grep -n "claude/implementers\|implementer-state"`, which must come
back empty at the end (except the two deliberate mentions named below).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Every occurrence is a mechanical replacement; the list is the complete output of that grep today.

### cerebro repo

- **`scripts/agent-state`** — `git mv scripts/implementer-state scripts/agent-state`; inside, every
  `implementer-state` in messages/usage → `agent-state`, the header's path →
  `.claude/agents-state/<name>.state.json`, and the target directory in the write (find
  `.claude/implementers` in the script's body — 11 sites) → `.claude/agents-state`. Nothing else in
  it changes (roster check, states, phases, `since` rules stay exactly as ah-u3i wrote them).
- **`scripts/implementer-state`** (new, the shim, `chmod +x`):

  ```bash
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  # Renamed to agent-state in ah-2n3.1 (the file it writes is every agent's now, not only an
  # implementer's). Kept for one release so an implementer whose session began before the rename
  # keeps writing; remove after the next release tag.
  echo "implementer-state: renamed to agent-state; update the caller" >&2
  exec "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/agent-state" "$@"
  ```

- **`tests/agent-state.sh`** — `git mv tests/implementer-state.sh tests/agent-state.sh`; its
  symlink fixture (line 34) links `agent-state`, the state-file path helper (46) and the two
  `mkdir`/`find` lines (184, 199) use `.claude/agents-state`, the header and the final echo (3, 10,
  204) say `agent-state`. **New assertion**: calling the shim `implementer-state` through the same
  fixture writes the same file under `.claude/agents-state` and prints the renamed line on stderr.
- **`emacs/cerebro.el`** (9 sites): commentary :17; `cerebro--phases` docstring :244; the
  `cerebro--supervise-action` docstring :569; **`cerebro--repo-root` :776-779** — locate the repository by
  **`.claude/cerebro`** (the submodule mount, present in every consumer from clone time) rather than
  by the state directory, which may not exist yet on a fresh machine; error text likewise, and the
  docstring says why (see *Known traps*); `cerebro--state-file-path` :801;
  `cerebro--stop-flag-path` :1022; the docstring at :1756-1757.
- **`emacs/cerebro-test.el`** (2 sites): :376 docstring, :839 expected path
  `/repo/.claude/agents-state/Cyclops.stop`.
- **`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`** (24 sites): every `.claude/cerebro/scripts/implementer-state`
  → `.claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state`; :64 and :160 path → `.claude/agents-state/`.
- **`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`** (3 sites, :212-220): the `n` measurement's `find` and stop-flag
  test → `.claude/agents-state`.
- **`agents/implementer.md`** (:51, :53, :58), **`agents/orchestrator.md`** (11 sites: :77, :104,
  :154-155, :203, :206, :472, :502, :511, :697, :702), **`agents/verifier.md`** (:273),
  **`agents/architect.md`** (:166 — "Nothing under `.claude/agents-state/`"), **`CLAUDE.md`** (:76,
  :119, :122), **`README.md`** (:42), **`emacs/README.md`** (:137, :141),
  **`docs/agent-workflow.md`** (:119, :138), **`scripts/run-orchestrator`** (:13).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** additionally: one sentence under *Gotchas* — the directory was
  `.claude/implementers/` until ah-2n3.1 and a shim `scripts/implementer-state` survives one release.

### atlantis-hud (bump PR)

- `.gitignore` :31 comment → `.claude/agents-state/` stays ignored (the `.claude/*` rule already
  covers it; only the words change).
- `CLAUDE.md` (4 sites: grep `claude/implementers`) → `.claude/agents-state`, and the identical edit
  in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`; `diff` them afterwards.
- `.claude/cerebro` pointer bump.

The two deliberate survivors of the grep: the shim's own comment, and the `CLAUDE.md` gotcha line.

## Increments

1. **Script and its test.** RED: `git mv` the test first, edit its paths and add the shim assertion;
   `bash tests/agent-state.sh` fails (no `agent-state`). GREEN: `git mv` the script, edit, add the
   shim. `bash tests/launchers.sh` still green.
2. **cerebro.el.** RED: edit `cerebro-test.el:839` to the new stop-flag path; ERT fails. GREEN: the
   seven `cerebro.el` edits; byte-compile clean; suite green.
3. **Docs and skills.** The grep, until it prints only the two survivors.
4. **PR 1** `chore(ah-2n3.1): the agent state directory and script are named for every role`;
   `@copilot`; CI; squash. **PR 2** in an atlantis-hud worktree: bump + `.gitignore` + `CLAUDE.md` +
   mirror; the PR body carries the one-time `mv .claude/implementers .claude/agents-state` and
   "restart the fleet view" instruction for the navigator.

## The test plan

- `bash tests/agent-state.sh` (renamed suite plus the shim assertion), `bash tests/launchers.sh`.
- `emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el` and the ERT suite.
- The grep in *Validation*.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. The navigator chose the rename on 2026-08-15 over keeping the names with a
documented misnomer (rejected: zero churn but a directory called implementers holding Xavier's
state) and over renaming only the script (rejected). Names as decided: **`.claude/agents-state/`**
and **`agent-state`**.

## Out of scope

- Any state written by an interactive agent, any change to `cerebro--derive-*`, any new phase
  word — all ah-2n3.2.
- Removing the shim (a later release).
- Migrating a running machine's flags automatically — the PR body tells the navigator the one `mv`.

## Validation

```bash
# cerebro worktree
bash tests/agent-state.sh && bash tests/launchers.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
git grep -n "claude/implementers\|implementer-state" | grep -v "scripts/implementer-state:\|CLAUDE.md:.*ah-2n3.1"   # nothing
# atlantis-hud worktree, after the bump
grep -rn "claude/implementers" CLAUDE.md .github/copilot-instructions.md .gitignore                    # nothing
diff CLAUDE.md .github/copilot-instructions.md                                                        # nothing
```

Human check: after the bump merges and the `mv`, `M-x cerebro` shows the running implementers as
before, `f` writes `.claude/agents-state/<name>.stop`, and an implementer that started before the
bump keeps updating its row (its writes go through the shim). Psylocke marks this bead not-needed.

## Known traps

- **`cerebro--repo-root` locates the repository by the directory's existence** (:778). Renaming the
  path without touching that function makes the fleet view fail to find the repo at all on a machine
  where `.claude/agents-state` does not exist yet. That is why the plan moves the lookup to
  `.claude/cerebro`, which always exists in a consumer; `agent-state` and `cerebro--write-stop-flag`
  both `mkdir -p` the state directory, so nothing else needs it to pre-exist. The ERT test at :376
  keeps passing.
- **The Emacs session has the old `cerebro.el` loaded** until the navigator reloads it — the PR body
  says to restart the fleet view after the bump; the shim keeps writes flowing meanwhile.
- **Two repos, two PRs**; the bead closes when the bump lands. Do not branch inside the shared
  `.claude/cerebro`.
- **`git mv`, not copy** — the tests reference the script by name through a symlink fixture, and a
  leftover real `implementer-state` beside the shim would shadow it.
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md` mirrors `CLAUDE.md`** byte for byte.

title: Interactive agents write state files, and the fleet list shows when one is asking
description: Second of two passes for ah-2n3. Xavier, Cerebro, Moira, Psylocke and Bishop write the same .claude/agents-state/<name>.state.json implementers do — idle / working / asking, with a role phase (Xavier: triage · plan; Psylocke: prepare · verify; Moira: sweep; Cerebro: sweep · release; Bishop: daily · weekly) — and cerebro.el derives their rows from the file when one exists for a live pid, falling back to the process scan otherwise, so an interactive agent waiting on the navigator shows ? and the ah-axj emphasis. done stays implementer-only and supervision keeps its kind guard. Blocked by ah-2n3.1 (the rename).
design:
## Context

Second of two passes for **ah-2n3**. Psylocke asked the navigator a question and the fleet list
said `up`, as it does when she wants nothing: `cerebro--derive-interactive` (cerebro.el:88-104)
knows only `up`/`dead` from a process scan, and the `asking` state — the `?` glyph and the ah-axj
whole-row emphasis — comes only from a state file, which only implementers write. The navigator
decided the fix in the bead: **every agent writes the same state file**, one contract, one
derivation. **ah-2n3.1** (planned; must land first) renamed the file's home to
`.claude/agents-state/` and the writer to `scripts/agent-state`; this bead is written against those
names — if .1 has not merged when you pick this up, `bd ready` will not offer it.

Settled with the navigator (2026-08-15): the shared state vocabulary stays **`idle · working ·
asking · done`** with `done` **implementer-only**; the role-specific part is the **`phase`**, one or
two words per role — **Xavier `triage · plan`, Psylocke `prepare · verify`, Moira `sweep`, Cerebro
`sweep · release`, Bishop `daily · weekly`**; `idle` between passes with no phase; and `asking` is
what every one of them writes the moment it puts a question to the navigator and clears the moment
the answer is in. Liveness is **file first, process scan second**: an interactive session started by
hand that never writes a file still shows `up`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Line numbers against cerebro `origin/main` at `8549679` **before** ah-2n3.1's rename; re-grep after
it (the rename moves no lines in `cerebro.el`'s functions but renames paths in docstrings).

### `scripts/agent-state`

- The name check (today: `run-implementer --roster` only) accepts the roster **or** one of the five
  interactive names. Read them from `cerebro.el`? No — a bash script cannot; keep a literal list in
  the script, `INTERACTIVE=(Xavier Cerebro Moira Psylocke Bishop)`, with a comment that
  `cerebro-interactive-agents` in `emacs/cerebro.el` and the five launchers' `--name` are the other
  two copies and all three must agree; the error becomes
  `agent-state: <name> is neither on the roster nor an interactive agent`.
- The phase check accepts the union: `build|gate|review|ci|rebase|merge|triage|plan|prepare|verify|sweep|release|daily|weekly`;
  usage and the error line list them. `done` from an interactive name is **refused**, exit 2:
  `agent-state: done is an implementer's state; an interactive agent writes idle when it has nothing to do`.
- `tests/agent-state.sh` gains: `Xavier working --phase triage --pid N` writes the file;
  `Psylocke asking --bead ah-xyz --phase verify` writes; `Bishop done` exits 2 with that message;
  `Nobody working` exits 2 with the new wording; `Cyclops working --phase triage` **also passes**
  (the union is deliberately not per-role — the fleet view shows the word, and a wrong word in a
  column is not worth a role table in bash; the docstring of `cerebro--phases` says the same).

### `emacs/cerebro.el`

- `cerebro--phases` (:243-244) becomes the union list, in the order above, docstring saying which
  words belong to whom.
- **`cerebro--derive-interactive`** (:88-104) gains `states` and `pid-alive-p` parameters (same
  shape as `cerebro--derive-implementer`, :106-160) and becomes:
  1. if a state file exists for the name **and** its `pid` is alive → derive exactly as the
     implementer branch does (`state`, `bead`, `since`, `phase`, `phase-since`, `raw`, `external` =
     not owned), but with `:kind 'interactive` and `:role` from the alist; a raw `done` maps to
     `'unknown` (shown in yellow with its raw word — an interactive agent must never write it);
  2. otherwise the three existing branches unchanged (`owned` → up; name in args → up external;
     else dead) — the process scan is the fallback, not the other way round.
  Pull the shared file→struct derivation into `cerebro--derive-from-state (name role kind parsed
  owned-p)` used by both, so there is one mapping of raw states.
- **`cerebro--derive`** (:162-176) passes `states` and `pid-alive-p` through; `cerebro--gather-states`
  (:813-818) is called with `(append (mapcar #'car cerebro-interactive-agents) roster)` at the two
  call sites (`cerebro--tick` and wherever else `cerebro--gather-states` is called — grep).
- **`cerebro--supervise-action`** (:566-…): the `(eq (cerebro-agent-kind agent) 'implementer)` guard
  gains a comment: it is now load-bearing for interactive agents that write `asking`/`working` —
  they are never restarted, retired or nudged from here — and must survive any future unification.
- `cerebro--state-label`/`cerebro--for-column`/`cerebro--glyph`/`cerebro--entry` need **no change**:
  they read the struct, and an interactive agent with a phase now shows it exactly as an
  implementer's row does (State = phase word while `working`, `asking` bold with `?`, Bead/Phase
  times). Check `cerebro--entry`'s external/`—` handling: an interactive agent's row today shows `—`
  in the Bead column when external; with a file it shows the bead — verify the branch at the Bead
  column does not special-case `'interactive`; if it does, remove that case.
- `cerebro--kill-action`/`cerebro--alive-p`: no change (alive is anything but dead).
- Commentary (:8-22): "the interactive five write the same file when they can; their liveness is the
  file when there is one and the process scan when there is not."

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el`

New tests beside `interactive-roster-has-bishop`: `derive-interactive-reads-a-live-state-file`
(state `asking`, phase `verify`, bead `ah-xyz`, alive pid → `'asking`, phase, bead, kind
`'interactive`), `derive-interactive-falls-back-to-the-process-scan` (file with dead pid, name in
args → `'up` external), `derive-interactive-without-a-file-is-unchanged` (the three old branches),
`derive-interactive-treats-done-as-unknown`, `supervise-ignores-an-asking-interactive-agent` (no
nudge/restart), and the 18-row `derive` test passes `states` for an interactive name.

### The five instruction files — the writes

Each gains a short table like `implement-bead`'s (:83-92) — *moment → command* — using
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state <Name> <state> [--bead <id>] [--phase <word>] --pid $PPID`, and
one sentence: **write `asking` immediately before the question tool, and `working` (same bead, same
phase) immediately after the answer arrives — a marker left behind is what makes the signal
untrustworthy.** `idle --pid $PPID` before every sleep loop; `working` when a pass starts.

- **`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`** (Xavier — the cycle lives in the skill, not `agents/planner.md`):
  `working --phase triage` when the triage pass starts; `asking` around each triage question;
  `working --bead <id> --phase plan` on `--add-label planning`; `asking --bead <id> --phase plan`
  around every interview question; `idle` before "Sleeping without dying"; the P0 check keeps
  `working --phase plan`. Table goes beside the *Choosing what to plan* commands and a line under
  *Sleeping without dying*.
- **`agents/verifier.md`** (Psylocke): `working --phase prepare` at the start of a pass; `working
  --bead <id> --phase prepare` on selecting a candidate; `asking --bead <id> --phase verify` around
  "Asking whether they are ready" **and** around "Taking the verdict" (she is waiting on a person in
  both); `working --bead <id> --phase verify` between them (app running, briefing given); `idle`
  before her sleep loop. Her never-list line "Never has a state file" (:266-269 today) is **replaced**
  by the opposite: she writes one like everyone else, and only `done` is not hers.
- **`agents/user-feedback.md`** (Moira): `working --phase sweep` at the top of a pass; `asking`
  around every triage question (*A new issue*, :155; *A closed issue with an open bead*, :386);
  `idle` before sleeping.
- **`agents/orchestrator.md`** (Cerebro): `working --phase sweep` on the startup sequence and any
  sweep it runs; `working --phase release` while cutting a release; `asking` around a question to
  the navigator; `idle` while waiting for the navigator (*Staying alive between questions*, :440).
  The section that today says interactive agents have no state file — grep `state file` — is
  reworded.
- **`agents/architect.md`** (Bishop): `working --phase daily|weekly` after deciding the sweep;
  `asking` around a question if it ever asks one; `idle` after the report (it ends its turn — the
  file must be `idle`, never `done`, and the never-list line "never has a state file" is replaced).
- **`agents/planner.md`**, **`CLAUDE.md`** (cerebro, *Invariants*: "The state file is the contract"
  gains "for every agent; `done` is an implementer's"), **`emacs/README.md`** (:137-141: the states
  and who writes them), **`docs/agent-workflow.md`** (one paragraph under *Your queue* or the fleet
  view section: an agent waiting on you shows `?`, whichever it is).

### atlantis-hud

The bump PR, and `CLAUDE.md` + mirror: the sentence "Interactive agents — Xavier, Cerebro, Moira,
Psylocke — have no state file and never count" in *plan-bead*'s buffer measurement is in the
**skill** (cerebro), not the consumer; grep the consumer for "no state file" and reword any hit;
also the `n` measurement in `plan-bead` must **exclude the interactive names** when counting
implementers (filter `$name` against `run-implementer --roster`), or Xavier's own file inflates `n`.

## Increments

1. **The script.** RED: the five new `tests/agent-state.sh` assertions. GREEN: names, phases, the
   `done` refusal.
2. **Derivation.** RED: the six ERT tests. GREEN: `cerebro--derive-from-state`,
   `cerebro--derive-interactive`, `cerebro--derive`, `cerebro--gather-states` call sites, the
   supervise comment; byte-compile clean.
3. **The five files and docs.** Read each once as its agent: every table entry names a moment that
   exists in that file, and every `asking` has a matching `working` after it.
4. **plan-bead's `n`** excludes interactive names — a one-line change in the loop (`case` on the
   roster).
5. **PR 1** `feat(ah-2n3.2): every agent writes its state, and the fleet list shows who is asking`;
   `@copilot`; CI; squash. **PR 2** the bump (+ any consumer CLAUDE.md wording, mirrored).

## The test plan

- `bash tests/agent-state.sh`, `bash tests/launchers.sh`.
- ERT (28.2 and 30.1 in CI) + byte-compile.
- No atlantis-hud suite.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator's decisions (2026-08-15): the approach (in the bead: one contract,
every agent writes the file); the phase words **`triage · plan / prepare · verify / sweep / sweep ·
release / daily · weekly`** — chosen over one word per role (rejected: repeats the Role column) and
over no phase for interactive agents (rejected: the column would say only working). Everything the
fleet view shows for these rows is what it already shows for implementers.

## Out of scope

- Nudging or timing out an interactive agent's `asking` (implementers keep theirs; interactive
  agents block by design).
- A stop flag for interactive agents; `f` on them stays `not-implementer` (ah-ymn is about `f`).
- Any change to the state file's schema.

## Validation

```bash
bash tests/agent-state.sh && bash tests/launchers.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

Human check (the bead's own): start Psylocke; when she asks whether you are ready, her row shows
`?`, bold, `verify`, and the time waiting; answer — the row returns to `prepare`/`idle` and no mark
remains. Start a session by hand with `claude --name Moira …` and no state file — she still shows
`up`. An implementer's `asking` still nudges after `cerebro-answer-timeout`. Psylocke marks this
bead not-needed.

## Known traps

- **`done` from an interactive agent would be restarted/retired if the kind guard ever went** —
  refuse it in the script *and* map it to `'unknown` in the derivation, so a stray write can only
  mislabel a row.
- **`cerebro--gather-states` reads a file per name on every 5-second tick**; five more reads is
  nothing, but do not read the file inside the pure derivation — pass it in, as the roster's are.
- **The process-scan fallback must stay** — a hand-started session (`claude --name Xavier`) has no
  file, and the ah-2n3 bead names it as a requirement.
- **`$PPID` is the claude process only from a top-level Bash call** — the same rule
  `agent-state`'s header states; the interactive agents' files must say `--pid $PPID` verbatim.
- **plan-bead's `n`** — without the roster filter Xavier counts itself as an implementer and the
  buffer target moves. Test it by hand: with only Xavier running, `n=0`.
- **Two repos; ah-2n3.1 first.** Do not start this from a cerebro main that still has
  `implementer-state`.
acceptance_criteria: agent-state accepts the five interactive names and their phases; a Psylocke asking a question shows ? in the fleet list until answered and nothing afterwards; a session started by hand with no state file still shows up; implementers' asking behaviour and timeout are unchanged; ERT tests cover the derivation.

title: An interactive agent asking a question is invisible in the fleet list
description:
Psylocke put a question to the navigator and the fleet list said nothing. No `?`, no emphasis — the
row read `up`, exactly as it does when she is working through a verification and wants nothing.

It is not a missed edge case. **An interactive agent cannot reach the `asking` state at all.**

## Why

`cerebro--derive-interactive` produces exactly two states, `up` and `dead`, from whether the name
appears in the process list. The `asking` state — and with it the `?` glyph and the whole-row
emphasis from ah-axj — comes only from `.claude/implementers/<name>.state.json`, and only
implementers write one. Their liveness is a file; an interactive agent's is a `pgrep`.

So the signal exists for the one kind of agent that is *least* likely to need it. An implementer
asking a question is rare and comes with a timeout that hands the bead back. The five interactive
agents ask constantly, and it is the whole point of them:

| Agent | Asks about |
|---|---|
| Xavier | every user-facing decision in a plan |
| Psylocke | whether a verification passed — she cannot judge it herself |
| Moira | how to triage each new issue |
| Bishop | which findings are worth a bead |
| Cerebro | what to do when a sweep finds something ambiguous |

Four of those five block until answered. The navigator's own screen is the thing that should say so,
and it is the thing that does not.

## The fix, as the navigator has decided it

**Every agent writes the same `<name>.state.json` the implementers already write.** Not a second
mechanism for the interactive five: one contract, one derivation, and the states of all of them
become visible rather than only their liveness.

That is worth more than the `?` this bead started from. Today an interactive agent is either `up` or
`dead` — the list cannot say that Xavier is triaging, Moira is sweeping issues, Bishop is halfway
through a weekly pass or that any of them is asleep between passes. With a state file each, all of
that is displayable, and the `For` column starts answering "waiting on you for 40 minutes" instead
of nothing.

The `phase` field added by ah-u3i is the natural place for the role-specific part, with the shared
vocabulary staying small: `idle`, `working`, `asking`, `done`.

### What this pulls in

- **The directory name becomes wrong.** `.claude/implementers/` would hold Xavier's and Cerebro's
  state too. Renaming it touches the stop flags, `cerebro--supervise`, the launchers and the docs;
  living with the misnomer is cheaper and uglier. Worth deciding rather than drifting.
- **`done` must stay implementer-only.** `cerebro--supervise-action` already guards on
  `(eq (cerebro-agent-kind agent) 'implementer)` before it restarts or retires anything, which is
  the only reason an interactive agent writing `done` will not get killed and relaunched. That guard
  is now load-bearing for a case it was not written for: say so where it lives, so nobody
  generalises it away while unifying the two derivations.
- **Liveness should not become file-only.** An interactive agent is found today by scanning process
  args for `--name`, which works whether or not it ever writes a file — including a session the
  navigator started by hand outside Emacs. If the file becomes the only evidence, that session
  disappears from the list. Prefer the file when it is there and fall back to the process scan.
- **Five instruction files gain the writes**, and each agent must be told when to clear `asking` as
  precisely as when to set it. A marker left behind is the failure mode that makes the whole signal
  untrustworthy.

## Validation

Have Psylocke ask something and confirm the fleet list marks her row with `?` and the ah-axj
emphasis, from the moment she asks until she has an answer. Confirm no mark is left behind
afterwards, and that an implementer's `asking` behaviour, including its timeout, is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Every agent, interactive or implementer, writes the same <name>.state.json, and the fleet list derives its state from it. An agent waiting on an answer is marked with the ? glyph and the row emphasis, whichever kind it is, and the mark clears when the wait ends. The list shows what an interactive agent is doing rather than only that it is up, and the For column shows how long it has been doing it. An interactive agent found only in the process list, with no state file, still appears. Implementers' behaviour is unchanged: the answer timeout stays theirs alone, and restart and retire still act only on implementers.

title: The fleet view forgets which agent was selected
description:
Move out of the fleet's agent list and back — TAB, or `C-x o` — and point is on the topmost agent
again, even though another one was selected before leaving.

This is `emacs/cerebro.el` in the cerebro submodule, the `*cerebro*` buffer.

## What it probably is

Not established, but the shape is familiar: the agent list reverts every five seconds, and a window
whose buffer is not the selected one keeps its **own** point. Redrawing moves the buffer's point;
the window's stays where it was, or goes back to the top when the buffer is rewritten under it. The
navigator only notices on returning, which is why it looks like a TAB bug rather than a refresh one.

The bead panel had exactly this, found while building it: `cerebro--beads-render` now calls
`set-window-point` for every window showing the buffer, after placing the mark. The agent list has
no equivalent — `tabulated-list-print` can remember position by id, but that restores the buffer's
point, not the window's.

Worth checking before fixing: whether it reproduces without ever leaving the window (wait past a
refresh with an agent selected), which separates "the redraw loses it" from "returning loses it".

## Validation

Select an implementer partway down the list. TAB away and back: same agent selected. Then wait past
a refresh without leaving: still the same agent.
design:
## Context

In the Emacs fleet view (the `*cerebro*` buffer), move out of the agent list — TAB, or `C-x o` —
and back, and point is on the topmost agent again, even though another one was selected before
leaving. The list refreshes every 5 seconds: `cerebro--timer` fires `cerebro--tick`, which calls
`revert-buffer`; tabulated-list's revert re-runs `cerebro--revert` (the entries) and then
`tabulated-list-print` with remember-pos, which restores **the buffer's point** by entry id. But a
window whose buffer is not the selected one keeps its **own** point — so the timer, which almost
always runs while the navigator sits in the detail or beads window, rewrites the list under the
list window and leaves that window's point behind (in practice: back at the top row). The
navigator only notices on returning, which is why it looks like a TAB bug rather than a refresh
one.

The beads panel underneath the list had exactly this and already carries the fix and its
explanation: `cerebro--beads-render` ends by walking `get-buffer-window-list` and calling
`set-window-point` for every window showing the buffer, with a comment saying why ("A window keeps
its own point when its buffer is not the selected one…"). The agent list has no equivalent. This
bead adds it.

**This is the cerebro submodule, not atlantis-hud.** The file is `emacs/cerebro.el` in
`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro` (checked out at `.claude/cerebro`). All line numbers below
are against **cerebro's `origin/main` at `30272fa`** — note the submodule checkout in the main
atlantis-hud tree may be behind that; `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin` first, and read via
`git -C .claude/cerebro show origin/main:emacs/cerebro.el` when in doubt.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` (cerebro repo)

- `cerebro--tick` — lines 1539–1547. Today:

  ```elisp
  (when (buffer-live-p buffer)
    (with-current-buffer buffer
      (revert-buffer)
      (cerebro--supervise cerebro--agents (cerebro--repo-root) (current-time))))
  ```

  After `revert-buffer`, sync every window showing the list to the buffer's freshly-restored
  point. Factor it as a named function so the test can drive it without the repo-state machinery:

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--sync-list-windows ()
    "Give every window showing the current buffer the buffer's own point.
  `tabulated-list-print' restores the buffer's point by id, but a window
  whose buffer is not selected keeps its own point - the timer almost
  always renders from the detail or beads window, so without this the
  list window's selection walks to the top on every refresh. Mirrors the
  set-window-point loop in `cerebro--beads-render'."
    (dolist (window (get-buffer-window-list (current-buffer) nil t))
      (set-window-point window (point))))
  ```

  and call it in `cerebro--tick` between `revert-buffer` and `cerebro--supervise`. Setting the
  selected window's point too is harmless (it already equals the buffer's), so no window filter.

- **Reuse, don't reinvent**: the restore-by-id itself already works — `tabulated-list-print`'s
  remember-pos handles it, and the buffer's point holds the right row because Emacs copies the
  window's point back to the buffer when a window is deselected. The only missing half is the
  window sync, which is why the fix is three lines and not a position-tracking scheme. The model
  is `cerebro--beads-render`'s tail (lines ~1330–1337) and its comment; keep the new docstring's
  cross-reference to it.

- If an agent's row vanished between refreshes (its session ended), remember-pos leaves point on
  the nearest surviving line; the sync then propagates that. That is the same behaviour the beads
  panel accepts (`cerebro--goto-first-bead` fallback) and needs no extra handling here.

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (cerebro repo)

One new ERT test (see Increments). The file's header gives the run command:
`emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` from the cerebro repo
root. Batch Emacs has a real (undisplayed) frame, so `split-window`, `set-window-buffer`,
`set-window-point` and `select-window` all work in it — the existing suite is pure-derivation
only, so this is the file's first window test; keep it self-contained.

### `.claude/cerebro` submodule pointer (atlantis-hud repo)

After the cerebro PR merges, a second, one-line PR in atlantis-hud bumps the submodule to the new
cerebro main — the established pattern (`feat(ah-4ao): bump cerebro to the fleet-driven jobs`
(#238), `feat(ah-rnz): … (#237)`). See Increments 3.

## Increments

1. **The failing test.** In `emacs/cerebro-test.el`:
   `cerebro-test/list-window-keeps-selection-across-refresh` — arrange: a fresh buffer in
   `cerebro-mode`; set `tabulated-list-entries` directly to three fake rows (ids `"A"`, `"B"`,
   `"C"`, each with a vector matching the 5-column `tabulated-list-format`); `tabulated-list-print`;
   show the buffer in one window, `select-window` a second window showing another buffer;
   `set-window-point` the list window to row `"B"` (find it with `goto-char`/`tabulated-list-get-id`
   in the buffer, then point the *window* there). Act: with the *other* window still selected,
   re-run the refresh path — `(with-current-buffer buf (tabulated-list-print t)
   (cerebro--sync-list-windows))` — after first simulating the stale-window state.
   Assert: `(tabulated-list-get-id)` at the list **window's** point (`window-point`) is still
   `"B"`. Written against the current code (no `cerebro--sync-list-windows`, or with the sync call
   absent from the path) this fails; wrap arrange/cleanup in `save-window-excursion` /
   `unwind-protect` so batch runs stay hermetic. Do **not** call `cerebro--tick` in the test — it
   drags in `cerebro--revert` (repo state) and `cerebro--supervise`; the function under test is
   the sync.
2. **The fix.** Add `cerebro--sync-list-windows` and its call in `cerebro--tick` (after
   `revert-buffer`, before `cerebro--supervise`). Test from increment 1 goes green; the whole
   suite (`ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`) stays green.
3. **Delivery, two PRs.**
   a. In a clone/worktree of the **cerebro** repo (not inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared
      checkout — treat it like any shared tree: branch from cerebro's `origin/main` in a worktree
      of that repo), commit `fix(ah-b8o): the fleet list keeps its selected agent across the 5s
      refresh`, open the PR against `rmstdope/cerebro`, request `@copilot` review
      (`gh pr edit <n> --add-reviewer @copilot`), answer every comment, merge on green.
   b. In an **atlantis-hud** worktree: `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin && git -C
      .claude/cerebro checkout <merged-main-sha>` inside that worktree's own submodule checkout,
      commit the pointer as `feat(ah-b8o): bump cerebro to the fleet-list selection fix`, PR,
      Copilot review, merge. The bead closes when the bump lands in atlantis-hud main.

## The test plan

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el`: the new
  `cerebro-test/list-window-keeps-selection-across-refresh` (increment 1), plus the existing suite
  unchanged. Run from the cerebro repo root:
  `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`.
- No atlantis-hud suites are touched by the elisp change; the bump PR runs atlantis-hud CI as
  usual (`pnpm run check` is not needed for a submodule-pointer-only diff, but CI decides).

## User-facing decisions

None. This is the navigator's own fleet tooling, and the change restores behaviour that was
always intended — "the selection stays where I put it" — with no design fork: no layout, wording
or interaction choice exists to make. (The bead's own "worth checking" question — does it
reproduce without leaving the window — is answered by the mechanism: `tabulated-list-print`'s
remember-pos protects the selected-window case, so the loss needs a second window, which is what
the test pins.)

## Out of scope

- The beads panel and detail window — already correct; the fix copies their pattern.
- Any change to `cerebro--follow`, `cerebro--supervise`, refresh cadence, or the layout.
- Preserving selection when the selected agent's row disappears (nearest-line fallback stands).
- Any atlantis-hud application code.

## Validation

- The ERT suite green in batch, before (new test red) and after (all green).
- Human check, in the real fleet view: `M-x cerebro`, move point to an agent partway down, TAB to
  the detail window, wait past a refresh (>5s), TAB back — same agent selected; then stay in the
  list window with an agent selected and wait past a refresh — still selected (the case
  remember-pos already covered, now pinned by eye).

## Known traps

- **The submodule checkout lags.** `.claude/cerebro` in the main atlantis-hud tree may be checked
  out behind cerebro's `origin/main` (it was at `16429b0` when this was planned; main is
  `30272fa`, where the beads-panel precedent lives). Fetch and read `origin/main`, and branch from
  it — a fix written against the stale checkout will conflict with the bead panel and the
  fleet-driven-jobs work.
- **Do not branch inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared checkout** — it is live tooling the
  navigator's Emacs is running from; use a worktree/clone of the cerebro repo, exactly as the main
  repo's worktree rule says.
- **Do not call `cerebro--tick` from the test** — it reads real repo state
  (`cerebro--repo-root`, state files) and runs `cerebro--supervise`, which can touch stop flags.
  Test `cerebro--sync-list-windows` against a hand-built buffer.
- **`get-buffer-window-list`'s third argument must be `t`** (all frames), as the beads-panel loop
  does — the navigator may have the fleet view on another frame.
- **Two-PR delivery**: the bead is not done when the cerebro PR merges — the fleet runs whatever
  the submodule pointer names, so without the bump PR in atlantis-hud the fix is invisible.
  Close the bead only after the bump lands.
acceptance_criteria: With an agent other than the first selected, leaving the fleet window and returning leaves that same agent selected. An automatic refresh while the window is not selected does not move the selection either.

title: Right-clicking a hex centres the map on it without selecting
description:
Bringing a distant hex to the middle of the view is a manual pan today. There is no single gesture
that says "look at this one".

**The request:** right-clicking in a hex centres the map on that hex.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- Does right-click also *select* the hex, or centre only and leave the selection alone?
- Does the map jump or animate to the new centre?
- What does right-click on the map do today, and is that being replaced or is this an addition?
- Right-click outside the map, or on a hex the map cannot centre on (an edge hex, where centring
  would scroll past the boundary) — what happens?

## Validation

Manual: right-click a hex near the edge of the view and confirm the map centres on it.
design:
## Context

Bringing a distant hex to the middle of the view is a manual pan today; there is no single gesture
for "look at this one". Right-click currently does **nothing** in the app — `onPointerDown`
(`MapCanvas.tsx:515-561`) early-returns on `event.button !== 0`, no `contextmenu` handler exists
anywhere in the repository (shared, apps/web, apps/desktop, or the Rust shell), and the browser or
WKWebView shows its native context menu. So this gesture replaces nothing; suppressing the native
menu over the map is part of the work.

Chosen behaviour (all settled with the navigator, mockup at `docs/ui/map-recentre.html`, merged in
PR #245): right-clicking a hex **instantly centres the view on it, without selecting it**;
Ctrl+click on macOS is treated as right-click; the gesture always centres — known hexes and
unexplored ground alike, even when the hex is already visible.

Almost everything needed already exists: `centreOn(...)` in `mapViewport.ts` is a pure function the
selection-follow effect already uses, and `coordinateAt(...)` already resolves an arbitrary point
on the map to a hex. The work is one event handler, a small pure helper, a guide row, and tests.

All line numbers are against `origin/main` (commit `f44e917`, and re-verified below where it
matters); the working tree can lag — verify with `git show origin/main:<path>` if a number looks
off.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts` — nothing to change, everything to reuse

- `centreOn(coordinate, viewport, width, height, insets = NO_INSETS): Viewport` (lines 256–271).
  Pure; keeps `viewport.step`; no bounds clamp, so an edge hex centres with fog around it —
  consistent with the keyboard cursor, and explicitly chosen by the navigator.
- `coordinateAt(x, y, viewport, level)` (lines 154–183) — point → nearest even-parity hex
  coordinate; this is how the unexplored-ground click already resolves (`MapCanvas.tsx:743-763`).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapRecentre.ts` — new, one pure decision helper

The one genuinely new decision is "which pointer events count as the gesture", and it should be
testable without a DOM:

```ts
/**
 * True when the event is the recentre gesture: the secondary button's contextmenu, or a
 * Ctrl+click on macOS (the platform synonym, which would otherwise fall through and select).
 */
export function isRecentreGesture(ev: { button: number; ctrlKey: boolean }, isMac: boolean): boolean;
```

Rules: a `contextmenu` event (any platform) → true. For the click path: `isMac && ctrlKey &&
button === 0` → true. Reuse `isMacPlatform()` from `packages/shared/src/shortcuts.ts` (line 140)
at the call site — pass its result in, keep the helper pure.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — the handler

- Add `onContextMenu` to the root `<svg>` (line 688, next to `onPointerDown`). React attaches
  `contextmenu` normally (it is **not** in React's passive-event set, unlike `wheel` — see the
  comment at lines 436–437), so a React prop works; no manual listener needed. Handler:
  1. `event.preventDefault()` — always, over the whole map surface, so the native menu never
     appears there (this includes the fog rect and the rulers; the navigator chose the gesture, and
     a menu popping on fog but not hexes would be incoherent).
  2. Resolve the hex exactly as the fog-rect click does (lines 743–763): `const bounds =
     event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()`, then `coordinateAt(event.clientX - bounds.left,
     event.clientY - bounds.top, viewRef.current, level)`. This works uniformly for known hexes and
     unexplored ground — no per-polygon handler needed, and the polygons' own `onClick` is not
     involved because `click` does not fire for the secondary button.
  3. `commit(centreOn(coordinate, viewRef.current, size.width, size.height, readInsets()))` —
     the same call shape as the selection-follow effect (lines 413–434), **including
     `readInsets()`**: "centre" means the centre of the map area the panes leave visible, not the
     centre of the window. Unlike selection-follow, no `isOffScreen` gate — the navigator chose
     always-centre. `commit` (lines 291–302) already persists the view via `saveViewportForGame`,
     which is the established behaviour for every view change and stays.
- Ctrl+click on macOS: in the two `onClick` handlers (fog rect at 743–763, hex polygon at
  995–1004), when `isRecentreGesture({button: 0, ctrlKey: event.ctrlKey}, isMacPlatform())`,
  centre (same as step 3) **instead of** selecting, and return. Note macOS Chromium/WebKit
  usually deliver Ctrl+primary-click as a `contextmenu` event already — the click-path check is
  the belt to that suspender; both paths must behave identically, and the no-select rule is the
  point.
- Selection, `selectionEpoch`, the cursor and `mapFocused` are all untouched — centring only.
  Do not set `draggedRef`; a right-click is not a drag and must not suppress a following
  left-click's select.

### `packages/shared/src/navigationGuide.ts` — the guide row

`NAVIGATION_MOVES`, `MAP` group (constant at line 40; entries at 67–131). Insert after `mapPan`
(lines 67–73), before `mapZoom`. Agreed words, verbatim:

```ts
{
  id: "mapCentre",
  group: MAP,
  description: "Bring a hex to the middle of the view",
  mouse: "Right-click it",
  keys: null
}
```

("(or Ctrl+click)" was offered for the mouse text and declined.) `navigationGuide.test.ts:18-31`
requires non-empty description/group, one of mouse/keys non-null, unique ids — all satisfied; add
the id to the fixed id list at `navigationGuide.test.ts:43-49`, which is the idiom. The module's
header contract requires the smoke suite to perform the gesture — increment 3 does.

## Increments

1. **The gesture predicate.** Failing test first: `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapRecentre.test.ts`
   — `describe("isRecentreGesture")`: `"a contextmenu event centres on every platform"`,
   `"Ctrl+click is the gesture on macOS"`, `"Ctrl+click is not the gesture elsewhere"`,
   `"a plain left click never is"`. Then the helper.
2. **The handler.** Failing test in `MapCanvas.test.tsx` (which today has no pointer tests — this
