that fails when a modal sets a max-w/max-h utility the global rule will beat"*. After this change
there is no such utility: the global rule beats nothing, so the class of defect the lint would look
for cannot exist. The one thing worth guarding is that the `:where()` is not removed, and increment
1's assertion does that in a line. **Do not build the lint** — it would encode the old world.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-24. Mockup, as chosen and committed:
`docs/ui/ah-y4zb-dialog-sizing.html` (PR #654, merged). It draws the shortcut help and the wide
dialogs in a 1400×900 window, today against each option, with a per-dialog table.

**What happens to sizing that has been inert all along.**
Chosen: **honour every bit of it.** `ShortcutHelp` caps at 85vh and `calc(100vw − 2rem)` as its
markup and its comment have always said; `BattlesDialog`, `ChangesDialog` and `GameDataDialog`
narrow from 95vw to the 94vw they ask for; the other six are unchanged.

Rejected: *delete the inert utilities so nothing moves at all* — pixel-identical to today, and it
would make this a purely mechanical refactor. Rejected because `ShortcutHelp`'s 85vh is defended by
a comment explaining exactly why the guide needs capping against a short window, and discarding it
throws away the reasoning rather than the bug.

Rejected: *honour only what a comment defends* — `ShortcutHelp`'s sizing, and delete the three bare
`max-w-[94vw]`. Rejected because it decides per dialog on whether somebody happened to write a
comment, which is a rule nobody could apply to the eleventh dialog.

**Whether a dialog that sets no size still gets the cap.**
Chosen: **yes, automatically.** The cap stays on `[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]`, only wrapped
in `:where()` so a component can override it. A new dialog is safe by default and needs to know
nothing — which is `ah-ziv`'s own reason for putting it on the role.

Rejected: *dialogs opt into a class*. Nothing is ever overruled by surprise and the rule is visible
at the call site — rejected because a new dialog that forgets the class runs off the edge of the
window and takes its Close button with it, which is the precise failure `ah-ziv` was filed for.

**Decided by the planner, and stated so the implementer does not re-open them:** `:where()` rather
than a custom property or an opt-in class (argued in *Files to change*); the `!` in
`GameDataDialog` is removed because it becomes redundant and its comment would otherwise explain
something that is not there; and the six dialogs that set no root `max-*` are not touched at all,
including their inner `max-h-*` utilities, which are about scrolling lists and were never in this
rule's way.

## Out of scope

- **`PopoverFrame`** (`workspace/popover.tsx`). It carries `role="dialog"` without
  `aria-modal="true"`, so this rule has never applied to it, and `ah-ziv`'s comment says why it must
  not.
- **The inner `max-h-*` utilities** in the six unaffected dialogs — scrollable lists inside a
  dialog, never in contention with this rule.
- **The values themselves.** 95vw, 90vh, 85vh, 94vw, 80vh all stay exactly as written. This bead
  changes which of them applies, never what any of them is.
- **A lint for inert sizing utilities.** Argued above: the defect class is gone by construction.
- **Any other specificity contest in `theme.css`.** `ah-vwdi`'s retrospective names this one block;
  auditing the stylesheet for others is a separate bead worth filing, not a widening of this one.
- **`ah-ziv`'s original decision** that the viewport is the last word for a dialog that says
  nothing. Reaffirmed by the navigator here, not revisited.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke
```

All green, nothing skipped.

**Then a human must look, and it is the only way these can be checked** — three of the four changes
are one viewport percent, and no assertion in this repository measures a rendered `vh`. In a window
around 1400×900:

- **Getting around** (`?` or the shortcut help): the guide is capped at **85vh**, so there is a
  visible margin above and below it on a short window, and it is **not** flush to 90vh as before.
- **Battles**, **Changes**, **Game data**: each is capped at **94vw** rather than 95vw. Compare
  against `main` in a second window if the difference is hard to see; it is about 14 px at this
  width.
- **Game data** specifically: its 10vh top offset still leaves a real margin **below** it. This is
  `ah-vwdi`'s own acceptance check, and removing the `!` is the change most able to break it.
- **The other six dialogs** — Map export, Command palette, both import summaries, Viewer faction,
  Settings — open and close, sized exactly as before.
- **At 200% UI scale**, open Battles: it must still fit the window with its Close button reachable.
  That is what the cap exists for, and it is the failure this bead must not reintroduce.

## Known traps

- **`:where()` is the entire bead, and it looks like a formatting change.** A later edit that
  "tidies" the selector back out restores the trap in full and silently. Increment 1's assertion is
  the only thing standing between this repository and a third sighting; do not weaken it to a
  substring match on `role="dialog"`.
- **`max-h-[80vh]!` must lose its `!` in the same PR.** Left in, it still works — so nothing fails —
  but the next reader learns the wrong rule from it, and its comment would be describing a
  specificity contest that no longer exists.
- **Do not touch the six dialogs that set nothing**, or their inner `max-h-*` utilities. Those are
  scrolling lists, not dialog sizing, and changing one is a visible regression with no bead behind
  it.
- **`extractBlock` in `theme.test.ts` takes a regex over the raw CSS.** The existing pattern
  `/\[role="dialog"\]\[aria-modal="true"\]/` still matches inside `:where(...)`, so that case needs
  no edit — and if it is "helpfully" updated to include `:where`, the two tests then assert the same
  thing and the guard is gone.
- **Tailwind v4 writes `!` as a suffix** (`max-h-[80vh]!`), not as the v3 prefix (`!max-h-[80vh]`).
  Removing it means deleting the trailing character, and a search for `!max-` finds nothing.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`, two of the five apply.** *The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle
  with the service worker disabled*, so a PWA-shaped failure here is not this bead's; and *no
  effect-level test in `packages/shared`* — which is exactly why the four visible changes are
  checked by eye rather than asserted.

title: Refactoring: the store's rules are still written twice, and have drifted
description:
## The cost being paid

The closed epic ah-8m0 ("the store's rules are written twice, in SQL and TypeScript, and diverge")
moved the backup codec, import stamping and reopen ranking into core. The game-manifest shape and the
read-rule-write sequences were not moved, and stores written since have followed the old pattern.

The two have already drifted. "What a reset keeps" exists as `reset_game` in Rust and `resetGame` in
TypeScript, each carrying its own hand-written warning against a struct spread — and they disagree:
Rust writes `manifest_version: CURRENT_MANIFEST_VERSION` and clears `map`, TypeScript keeps
`previous.manifestVersion` and has no `map` field at all. `webCoreAdapter.ts` still carries about
twenty comments of the form "matching the desktop's ORDER BY" (:400), "The desktop refuses this in the
same words" (:353), "The three steps are the desktop's three steps" (:312) — twinned rules guaranteed
by nothing but a comment.

## Evidence

- `00a2a13b` (ah-58n.1, "a game can be emptied and kept, on both platforms") — one concept across
  **11 files**, +275 lines in `core-persistence/src/lib.rs` and a parallel field-by-field manifest
  rebuild in `webCoreAdapter.ts`.
- `1755c70c` (ah-0w7w) — one optional manifest field written twice with the same reasoning, inside a
  33-file commit.
- The closed bead ah-8m0's own description records what this class already cost: `4e7c980` (the
  browser lacked SQL's `last_seen_turn` guard for four days) and `f153bf3` (one defect present in both,
  fixed across 13 files).
- Live divergence today: `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:543-555` vs
  `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:586-596`.

## Where

- `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` (`reset_game`), `crates/core/src/backup.rs`
- `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts` (`resetGame` and the ~20 "matching the desktop" rules)
- `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` (the manifest shape)

## What a refactoring would change

Finish what ah-8m0's children started: move the manifest shape and each read-rule-write sequence into
core, and leave the two adapters holding only their storage primitives. A rule then has one home and
the platforms cannot disagree about it — starting with the reset, whose two versions disagree now.

title: Refactoring: one new ruleset field must be written into eight files at once
description:
## The cost being paid

The ruleset's TypeScript types are mirrored by hand in Rust under `deny_unknown_fields`, so a new JSON
key that is not added on both sides in the same commit fails deserialisation of every ruleset. The two
can never be split across beads, and one scraped field is a seven-to-eight file change every time.

The project already generates 44 TypeScript types from Rust into `packages/core-client/src/generated/`.
The ruleset schema is the one contract that bypasses that pipeline and is kept in step by hand.

## Evidence

- `03170964` feat(ah-1ad6.1) (#629) — **7 files** for one optional `weapon` field; the commit message
  states the constraint outright: "mirrored in the Rust `ItemEntry` (which carries `deny_unknown_fields`,
  so both must change together)". It also needed a second commit inside the same PR just to add the
  forgotten `index.ts` re-export.
- `4273b298` feat(ah-19l2.1) (#611) — **8 files**: "The Rust `Production` mirror moves in the same
  commit: `deny_unknown_fields` means new JSON keys would otherwise fail deserialisation of every ruleset".
- `41a1558b` feat(ah-1wcw.6) (#566) — **8 files**.

## Where

- `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` (`ItemEntry`, `Production`), `packages/ruleset/src/index.ts`
- `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` (the hand-written mirror, `deny_unknown_fields`)
- `config/public/ruleset.json`, and the two test files that pin both sides

## What a refactoring would change

Put the ruleset schema on the generator the rest of the contract already uses: declare it once in Rust
and emit the TypeScript type, so a new field is one declaration plus the scraper that fills it. The
back-compat test that each of these commits hand-wrote becomes a property of the pipeline rather than
something a plan has to remember.

design:
## Context

The ruleset schema is written twice: once in TypeScript, where the scraper builds it, and once in
Rust, where the core reads it. The Rust mirror carries `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase",
deny_unknown_fields)]` on **25 structs**, so a JSON key added on one side and not the other **fails
deserialisation of every ruleset**. The two therefore can never be split across beads, and one
scraped field is a seven-to-eight file change every time:

| Commit | Cost |
|---|---|
| `03170964 feat(ah-1ad6.1) (#629)` | **7 files** for one optional weapon field. Its message states the constraint outright: *"mirrored in the Rust `ItemEntry` (which carries `deny_unknown_fields`, so both must change together)"*. It needed a **second commit inside the same PR** just to add the forgotten `index.ts` re-export. |
| `4273b298 feat(ah-19l2.1) (#611)` | **8 files**: *"The Rust `Production` mirror moves in the same commit: `deny_unknown_fields` means new JSON keys would otherwise fail deserialisation of every ruleset"*. |
| `41a1558b feat(ah-1wcw.6) (#566)` | **8 files**. |

**This project already generates its cross-language contract.** `crates/core` depends on `ts-rs`
(`Cargo.toml:17`) and exports dozens of types into `packages/core-client/src/generated/`, checked by
`pnpm run check:generated`. The ruleset schema is the one contract that bypasses that pipeline.

What is mirrored, exactly — **23 TypeScript types against 25 Rust structs**:

| TypeScript | Rust (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`) |
|---|---|
| `data.ts:16-125` — `ItemKind`, `ItemCapacity`, `MonsterCombat`, `SelfMobility`, `Weapon`, `ItemEntry`, `ItemReference`, `CastInput`, `CastCost`, `ProductionInput`, `Production` | `:122`, `:149`, `:169`, `:159`, `:179`, `:187`, (a map), `:291`, `:300`, `:308`, `:316` |
| `data.ts:175-231, 807-850` — `SkillRequirement`, `SkillLevel`, `SkillEntry`, `SkillReference`, `BuildingEntry`, `BuildingReference` | the corresponding structs later in the same file |
| `rules.ts:14-76` — `MovementPoints`, `TerrainCosts`, `RoadRule`, `OceanRule`, `SailingRule`, `MovementRules` | `:36`, `:45`, `:61`, `:69`, `:83`, `:106` |
| `build.ts:48` — `Ruleset`, `RiskThresholds`, `Gap` | the envelope, `:221`, `:244` |

When this lands: a new scraped field is **one Rust declaration plus the scraper line that fills it**,
and the back-compat reasoning each of those commits hand-wrote becomes a property of the pipeline.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**Rust owns the schema and TypeScript is generated from it.** That is the direction, and it is not
arbitrary: `deny_unknown_fields` is what makes a mismatch fatal, it lives on the Rust side, and the
Rust structs already carry the richer documentation. The scraper then writes against a type it
cannot silently diverge from.

### Where the generated types go — `packages/ruleset/src/generated/`

**Not `packages/core-client/src/generated/`**, and this is a deliberate departure from where every
other generated type lands. `packages/ruleset` declares **no dependencies at all** (its
`package.json` has no `dependencies` block) and **nothing in the workspace depends on it** — it is a
standalone scraper with a CLI. Making it depend on `@atlantis/core-client` to reach its own schema
would invert that for no gain. `ts-rs`'s `export_to` takes a path and can point anywhere.

So each struct gets `#[ts(export, export_to = "../../../packages/ruleset/src/generated/<Name>.ts")]`
— **verify the relative depth against a real regenerate** rather than trusting this line; `export_to`
is resolved relative to ts-rs's own output root, and the existing exports in `crates/core` use bare
filenames because that root is already `packages/core-client/src/generated`. If a relative path
proves not to work, set the root per-crate with ts-rs's own configuration and say so in the PR —
**do not fall back to putting them in `core-client` and adding a dependency**, which is the decision
this section is making.

### `scripts/checkGenerated.ts` — one directory becomes two

```ts
export const GENERATED_DIRS = [
  "packages/core-client/src/generated",
  "packages/ruleset/src/generated"
];
```

`GENERATED_DIR` (`:10`) is a single string today and `git status --porcelain -- <dir>` (`:23`) takes
it. Pass both paths — `git status` accepts several pathspecs — and update the message. `staleFiles`
(`:12`) is already exported and pure; it needs no change.

### The two attributes the whole bead turns on

Same crux as `ah-8z4y.2`. **Verified against `ts-rs 12.0.1`'s own documentation
(`src/lib.rs:310-313`) on 2026-08-24:**

| Attribute | Generates |
|---|---|
| none | `t: T \| null` |
| `#[ts(optional)]` | `t?: T` |
| `#[ts(optional = nullable)]` | `t?: T \| null` |

**Every `Option<T>` in the ruleset mirror needs `#[ts(optional)]`.** `ItemEntry` alone has seven
(`combat`, `cargo_capacity`, `capacity_condition`, `sailing_skill`, `withdraw_cost`, `weapon`,
`description`), all `#[serde(default)]`, and TypeScript writes every one as `field?: T`
(`data.ts:73` onward). Generating `T | null` instead would make the scraper write `"combat": null`
into `config/public/ruleset.json` for every non-monster — a large, silent data change to a committed
file, which `deny_unknown_fields` would happily accept. **Use `#[ts(optional)]`, not
`optional = nullable`**: the ruleset's absent fields are absent, never null.

### `ItemKind` — the one type that is not a mirror

Rust's enum (`rules.rs:122`) has **six** variants; TypeScript's union (`data.ts:16`) has five. The
sixth is `Unknown`, and `rules.rs:117-119` explains it: *"Deliberately tolerant … a ruleset that
invents a sixth kind should cost the same routes as before rather than refuse to plan at all."* It
has a **hand-written `Deserialize`** (`:132-145`) precisely because `#[serde(other)]` is not allowed
on an untagged enum.

**Generate it as it is, `"unknown"` included, and stop the scraper emitting it with a test.** The
enum already carries `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` (`:121`), which ts-rs reads, so the five
real variants come out as the exact strings TypeScript already uses. The union simply gains a sixth
member.

That is safe here, and it was checked rather than assumed: **no TypeScript anywhere switches
exhaustively on `ItemKind`.** Every use is an equality comparison — `entry.kind === "man"`
(`build.ts:117`), `=== "ship"`, `=== "monster"` (`data.test.ts:171,182,346`) — and a widened union
does not affect those. `packages/ruleset/src/index.ts:6` re-exports the type and nothing else uses
it.

**Do not try to hide the variant with `#[ts(skip)]`.** That attribute is documented for *fields*
(`ts-rs/src/lib.rs:38-39`); whether it applies to an enum variant was not established, and
`#[serde(skip)]` is not an option because it would break Rust's own serialisation of `Unknown`.

### `packages/ruleset/src/{data,rules,build}.ts` and `index.ts`

Each hand-written type is deleted and the generated one re-exported in its place. **No type is
renamed**, so the scraper's own code, `index.ts`'s public surface and every test keep referring to
the same names and need no edit beyond the import.

`ItemReference`, `SkillReference` and `BuildingReference` are `Record<string, T>` aliases with no
Rust struct of their own (Rust uses `HashMap`/`BTreeMap` inline). **Keep those three hand-written**,
one line each, over the generated element type. A generated map alias would add nothing and ts-rs's
map output is a different shape from a plain `Record`.

## Increments

Four, in this order, each green on its own. **One bead rather than four**, because the operation is
identical 23 times and the risk lives entirely in the per-field attributes, which are decided once
above; three more plans would repeat one trap list three times.

1. **The pipeline, proved on the smallest type.** `checkGenerated.ts` takes two directories; add its
   test in `scripts/` beside the existing one for `staleFiles`. Then derive `TS` on **`ItemCapacity`
   alone** (`rules.rs:149`), regenerate, commit the generated file, delete the hand-written
   `data.ts:18-23`, re-export the generated one.
   The assertion is `pnpm run check:generated` passing and `pnpm run typecheck` compiling — if the
   `export_to` path is wrong, this increment is where it is found, on one type instead of
   twenty-three.

2. **The items group.** `ItemKind`, `MonsterCombat`, `SelfMobility`, `Weapon`, `ItemEntry`,
   `CastInput`, `CastCost`, `ProductionInput`, `Production`. Every `Option<T>` gets `#[ts(optional)]`.
   Then, in `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`:

   ```ts
   // `ah-gdfe`: Rust's ItemKind carries a tolerant `Unknown` fallback the scraper must never
   // produce - it means "this build has never heard of this kind" (rules.rs:117-119). The
   // generated union includes it; the scraped data must not.
   it("no scraped item has an unknown kind", () => {
     expect(Object.values(items).filter((entry) => entry.kind === "unknown")).toEqual([]);
   });
   ```

3. **The skills and buildings groups.** `SkillRequirement`, `SkillLevel`, `SkillEntry`,
   `BuildingEntry`, and the three `Record` aliases rewritten over generated element types.

4. **Movement and the envelope.** `MovementPoints`, `TerrainCosts`, `RoadRule`, `OceanRule`,
   `SailingRule`, `MovementRules`, `RiskThresholds`, `Gap`, and `build.ts:48`'s `Ruleset`.
   **`Ruleset` last**, because it names every other type and is the one that will not compile until
   the rest have landed.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the `checkGenerated` test, extended | `scripts/` | both generated directories are checked, not just the first |
| `no scraped item has an unknown kind` | `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts` | the tolerant Rust fallback never reaches the data |
| every existing test in `packages/ruleset` | `data.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts`, `build.test.ts`, `committed.test.ts` | **the scraper produces the same JSON** — unedited |
| the Rust ruleset tests | `crates/core` | `config/public/ruleset.json` still deserialises |

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm run check:fast
```

**`committed.test.ts` is the one that matters most.** It pins the committed
`config/public/ruleset.json` against the scraper's output, so it is what fails if a generated
optional turned into a nullable and the scraper started writing `null`s. Run it deliberately and say
in the PR that it passed unchanged.

**A regenerated `config/public/ruleset.json` must not appear in the diff.** This bead changes types,
never data. If `git status` shows that file modified, an attribute is wrong — stop and find which.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** Nothing here reaches the application: Rust structs gain a derive, TypeScript types stop
being hand-written, and the scraper produces byte-identical JSON. No string, no layout, no stored
value and no wire format changes.

## Out of scope

- **Any change to the ruleset's content or shape.** No field added, removed, renamed or retyped.
  `config/public/ruleset.json` must not move.
- **Removing `deny_unknown_fields`.** It is the reason a mismatch is caught at all; generation
  removes the mismatch, not the guard.
- **The scraper itself** — `html.ts`, `cli.ts`, the page grammar. It writes the same values into the
  same shape.
- **`ItemReference`, `SkillReference`, `BuildingReference`** stay hand-written aliases.
- **Hiding `ItemKind::Unknown` from TypeScript.** Argued above.
- **Generating any other hand-written cross-language type.** `ah-8z4y.2` covers the game manifest;
  anything else is a bead for Forge.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm run check:fast
git status --porcelain -- config/public/ruleset.json    # must print nothing
```

All green, and that last command silent. Then, by reading the diff:

```bash
git diff origin/main -- packages/ruleset/src/generated/ | grep -E '^\+.*\?:'
```

Every optional field appears as `field?: T` — **never** `field: T | null`. That is the line this
bead is most able to get wrong, and it is invisible in every passing test until the scraper is next
run.

No human check is needed: no application behaviour is touched.

## Known traps

- **`#[ts(optional)]`, never plain `Option<T>`.** Verified against `ts-rs 12.0.1`
  (`src/lib.rs:310-313`). A generated `T | null` makes the scraper write `"combat": null` for every
  non-monster item, `deny_unknown_fields` accepts it happily, and `config/public/ruleset.json` grows
  a few thousand nulls that no test names. `ItemEntry` alone has seven such fields.
- **`ItemKind` has a sixth Rust variant** with a hand-written `Deserialize` and a documented reason.
  The generated union gains `"unknown"`; that is correct and there is a test stopping the scraper
  emitting it. Do not "fix" the union by hand-writing the type again.
- **`export_to` resolves relative to ts-rs's output root, not to the crate.** Increment 1 exists to
  discover the right path on one type. If a relative path cannot reach
  `packages/ruleset/src/generated/`, configure the root — do not move the types into `core-client`
  and add a dependency to `@atlantis/ruleset`, which is the decision *Files to change* makes.
- **Do not add `#[ts(rename_all = …)]`.** `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` is on all 25 structs
  and ts-rs reads it. `ItemKind`'s `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` likewise.
- **`deny_unknown_fields` stays on every struct.**
- **`packages/ruleset` has no dependencies and nothing depends on it.** Keep it that way; it is a
  standalone scraper with a CLI, and that independence is what makes the generated-types
  destination the question it is.
- **The forgotten `index.ts` re-export is a recorded failure** — `ah-1ad6.1` needed a second commit
  inside its own PR for exactly that. Every generated type this bead re-exports must appear in
  `packages/ruleset/src/index.ts`; `pnpm run typecheck` catches it only where something imports it.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**: none of the five apply. No persisted setting, no browser suite, no
  `packages/shared` effect test.

title: Refactoring: a separator assumption has shipped a wrong catalogue twice
description:
## The cost being paid

The game data page's "list of `N name [TAG]`" clause is parsed by three separate copies of the same
regex and accumulator in one file. `CAST_INPUT` (L561) and `PRODUCTION_INPUT` (L630) are byte-identical
and feed the structurally identical `CastInput` and `ProductionInput` types; `REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE`
(L507) is the third.

The same defect — assuming a fixed separator — had to be found and fixed in two of them independently,
two months apart, and a third copy was then written by hand. `PRODUCTION_INPUT`'s own comment records
the history: "`ah-6qp` after the same assumption - a fixed separator - shipped a wrong catalogue."
`readProduction` still splits on ` from `, with a source comment conceding that cooking's double
` from ` "happens to give the right answer... That is luck rather than design."

## Evidence

- `72c6cb85` feat(ah-6qp) (#412), 2026-08-17 — fixed in `readRequirements`: "splitting the sentence on
  ` and ` dropped the middle one - ENGR lost energy shield", caught by review after the wrong catalogue
  had already been generated.
- `31cc63e7` test(ah-bet5) (#457), 2026-08-20 — fixed again in `readCastCost`: read "with a global regex
  **as readRequirements now does**".
- `4273b298` feat(ah-19l2.1) (#611), 2026-08-23 — a third copy written by hand, citing `CAST_INPUT` as
  its authority.

## Where

- `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` — `REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE` (L507), `CAST_INPUT` (L561),
  `PRODUCTION_INPUT` (L630) and their three near-identical loop bodies; `readProduction`'s ` from `
  split.

## What a refactoring would change

One clause reader, self-delimiting on the `[TAG]` pairs and never looking at a separator, returning
`{ count, tag }` for every consumer. The three call sites keep only what is genuinely their own — a
level for a requirement, an `any of` or a formula for production — and the next separator the page
adopts costs nothing anywhere.

design:
## Context

The game data page's *"N name [TAG]"* clause is read by three separate copies of the same idea in
one file, `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`:

| Constant | Line | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `CAST_INPUT` | `:377` | `/(?:(\d+) )?[a-z][a-z ]*\[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]/gi` |
| `PRODUCTION_INPUT` | `:446` | `/(?:(\d+) )?[a-z][a-z ]*\[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]/gi` — **byte-identical to the above** |
| `REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE` | `:323` | `/\[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]\s+(\d+)/g` — the same idea, tag first |

and by three near-identical accumulator loops (`:337-340`, `:404-406`, `:493-495`), each turning the
matches into `{ tag, amount }` or `{ tag, level }` with the same `amount === undefined ? 1` default.

**The same defect — assuming a fixed separator — had to be found and fixed in two of them
independently, two months apart, and a third copy was then written by hand:**

| Commit | What happened |
|---|---|
| `72c6cb85 feat(ah-6qp) (#412)`, 2026-08-17 | fixed in `readRequirements`: *"splitting the sentence on `and` dropped the middle one — ENGR lost energy shield"*. **Caught by review after the wrong catalogue had already been generated.** |
| `31cc63e7 test(ah-bet5) (#457)`, 2026-08-20 | fixed **again** in `readCastCost`: read *"with a global regex **as `readRequirements` now does**"*. |
| `4273b298 feat(ah-19l2.1) (#611)`, 2026-08-23 | a **third** copy written by hand, citing `CAST_INPUT` as its authority. |

`PRODUCTION_INPUT`'s own comment records the history — *"the same reasoning as `CAST_INPUT`: the
pairs are self-delimiting, so `a and b`, `a, b and c` and whatever separator the page adopts next
all read alike"* — and `CAST_INPUT`'s says *"`ah-6qp` after the same assumption — a fixed separator
— shipped a wrong catalogue."* **The principle is written down three times and enforced nowhere.**

There is a fourth thing in the same neighbourhood, and it is the one still relying on a separator:
`readProduction` (`:490`) splits a segment at its **first** ` from `, and its own comment concedes
the case that saves it — *"Cooking says ` from ` twice … splitting on the first occurrence happens
to give the right answer on both sides. That is luck rather than design, and `data.test.ts` pins it
by name."*

When this lands: one module states the principle once, the three call sites keep only what is
genuinely their own, and the production split stops being luck.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**Everything is in `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`** and its test file. No other package, no Rust.

### Two readers, not one — and the bead's premise is worth correcting

`ah-3rxk`'s description asks for *"one clause reader"*. **Two are needed**, because the grammars
genuinely differ and forcing them together would be a lie a later reader has to unpick:

- **`2 stone [STON]`** — a count, *before* the tag, defaulting to 1. Cast costs and production
  materials.
- **`force [FORC] 1`** — a **level**, *after* the tag, and never defaulting. Study requirements.

A single regex over both would be ambiguous — `[FORC] 1` and `1 [STON]` differ only in which side
the number falls on — and a combined reader would have to be told which it was looking at, which is
the caller knowing the grammar again. What is shared is the **principle**, and that is what gets
stated once:

```ts
/**
 * Reading the data page's `[TAG]` clauses.
 *
 * Every one of these is matched globally, straight out of the whole clause, and **never looks at a
 * separator**. The `[TAG]` pairs delimit themselves, so `a and b`, `a, b and c` and whatever the
 * page adopts next all read alike. Assuming a separator has shipped a wrong catalogue twice -
 * `ah-6qp` lost ENGR's energy shield by splitting on `and`, and `ah-bet5` fixed the same
 * assumption in the casting costs three days later - and a third copy of the same loop was written
 * by hand after both (`ah-19l2.1`). Hence one home (`ah-3rxk`).
 */

/** One `N name [TAG]` pair: the count, defaulting to 1 where the page states a bare name. */
export type TaggedAmount = { tag: string; amount: number };

const TAGGED_AMOUNT = /(?:(\d+) )?[a-z][a-z ]*\[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]/gi;

/** Every `N name [TAG]` in a clause, in the order the page wrote them. */
export function taggedAmounts(clause: string): TaggedAmount[] {
  return [...clause.matchAll(TAGGED_AMOUNT)].map(([, amount, tag]) => ({
    tag,
    amount: amount === undefined ? 1 : Number.parseInt(amount, 10)
  }));
}

/** One `name [TAG] N` pair, where `N` is a skill level rather than a count. */
export type TaggedLevel = { tag: string; level: number };

const TAGGED_LEVEL = /\[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]\s+(\d+)/g;

/** Every `name [TAG] N` in a clause. A clause stating no level is passed over, not guessed at. */
export function taggedLevels(clause: string): TaggedLevel[] {
  return [...clause.matchAll(TAGGED_LEVEL)].map(([, tag, level]) => ({
    tag,
    level: Number.parseInt(level, 10)
  }));
}
```

Both patterns are **moved character for character** from the constants they replace. `TAGGED_AMOUNT`
is `CAST_INPUT` and `PRODUCTION_INPUT`, which are byte-identical; `TAGGED_LEVEL` is
`REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE`.

**Exported**, because the tests assert on them directly and because that is what makes the principle
findable. They stay in `data.ts` rather than moving to a module of their own: the file is the
scraper's own vocabulary and nothing outside it reads a clause.

### The three call sites keep only what is theirs

- **`readRequirements`** (`:332-343`): `return taggedLevels(stated[1]);`. Its `STUDY_REQUIREMENT`
  match and its "no sentence, no requirements" early return stay.
- **`readCastCost`** (`:392-411`): `const stated = taggedAmounts(costMatch[1]);`, then **its own
  throw when `stated.length === 0`, unchanged** — *"a cost sentence naming no input at all is the
  page having changed shape, and must stay loud"*. That policy is this call site's and does not move
  into the reader; `readProduction` deliberately does the opposite.
- **`readProduction`** (`:493-495`): `inputs.push(...taggedAmounts(tail.replace(ANY_OF, "")))`. The
  `ANY_OF` strip, `inputsAreAlternatives`, `FORMULA_OUTPUT`, `manMonths` and the `outputs !== "1"`
  throw all stay exactly where they are.

`ProductionInput` and `CastInput` are structurally `TaggedAmount` and both are **generated types on
the Rust side** — `ah-gdfe` puts the whole ruleset schema on the generator. **Do not merge, rename
or re-type them here**: `taggedAmounts` returns `TaggedAmount` and each call site pushes those
values into its own typed array. Leave the two catalogue types alone.

### The production split stops being luck

`readProduction` splits `stated` at its **first** ` from ` (`:479`):

```ts
const [head, ...rest] = stated.split(" from ");
…
const tail = rest.join(" from ").trim();
```

Cooking reads `a number of meals [MEAL] equal to skill level divided by 2, rounded up from any of
grain [GRAI]…` — two ` from `s, and the first happens to fall in the right place.

**Split at the last ` from ` instead.** The head is the product and the tail is the material list;
the material list is what the *final* ` from ` introduces, in both the one-`from` and the
two-`from` shapes:

```ts
// The LAST ` from `, not the first: the materials are what the final one introduces. Cooking says
// it twice - `... rounded up from any of grain [GRAI]` - and the first occurrence happening to
// fall in the right place was luck the old comment admitted to (`ah-3rxk`).
const cut = stated.lastIndexOf(" from ");
const head = cut === -1 ? stated : stated.slice(0, cut);
const tail = cut === -1 ? "" : stated.slice(cut + " from ".length).trim();
```

**This produces the same answers as today on the committed page** — that is the point, and
`committed.test.ts` is what proves it. Delete the "luck rather than design" paragraph from the
function's doc comment and say what the rule now is.

*Considered and not chosen*: treating the **first tagged pair** as the product and the rest as
materials, which would never look at ` from ` at all. It reads better until `ANY_OF` and
`FORMULA_OUTPUT` are accounted for — both test the text on one side of the cut — so the cut has to
exist anyway, and this would leave the file with a cut *and* a tag rule to keep in step.

## Increments

1. **The two readers exist and are tested.**
   RED, in `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`:
   - `a clause with one pair reads it` — `"2 stone [STON]"` → `[{ tag: "STON", amount: 2 }]`.
   - `a bare name counts as one` — `"iron [IRON]"` → `amount: 1`.
   - `separators are never looked at` — the same three pairs written as `a and b and c`,
     `a, b and c` and `a; b; c` all read alike. **This is `ah-6qp` and `ah-bet5` as an assertion
     instead of a comment**, and it is the test the file has never had.
   - `a clause with no pair reads nothing` — `[]`, not a throw. The throwing is a caller's business.
   - `a requirement reads its level` — `"force [FORC] 1 and pattern [PATT] 2"` → both, with levels.
   - `a requirement stating no level is passed over` — `"force [FORC]"` → `[]`.
   GREEN: `taggedAmounts`, `taggedLevels` and their types. **Nothing else changes yet** — the three
   old constants are still in place and still used.

2. **The three call sites use them.** Delete `REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE`, `CAST_INPUT` and
   `PRODUCTION_INPUT` and the three loops.
   RED does not apply — this is a behaviour-preserving substitution, and **every existing test in
   `data.test.ts` is the assertion**. They must pass unedited. `grep -n "CAST_INPUT\|PRODUCTION_INPUT\|REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE" packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`
   must print nothing.

3. **The production split stops relying on the first ` from `.**
   RED: `cooking's second from is the one that matters` — assert on the cooking entry by name, as
   the existing test already does, **and** a new
   `a production with one from is unchanged` over `swords [SWOR] from iron [IRON]`. Write the first
   so it would fail on a first-`from` split — that is, assert `head` behaviour through the produced
   entry's `outputs` being `null` (the `FORMULA_OUTPUT` test runs on the head, and the head is what
   moves).
   GREEN: the `lastIndexOf` cut, and the doc comment rewritten.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the six reader tests | `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts` | the principle, including `separators are never looked at` |
| every existing test in the file | same | **the catalogue is unchanged** — unedited |
| `cooking's second from is the one that matters` | same | the split is a rule, not luck |
| `a production with one from is unchanged` | same | the common shape did not move |
| `committed.test.ts` | `packages/ruleset/src/` | **the generated `ruleset.json` is byte-identical** |

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

**`committed.test.ts` is the acceptance condition.** It pins the committed
`config/public/ruleset.json` against what the scraper produces, so it is what fails if any of these
substitutions changed a single entry. Run it deliberately and say in the PR that it passed
unchanged.

**`config/public/ruleset.json` must not appear in the diff.** This bead changes how the page is
read, never what it says. If that file is modified, a substitution was not equivalent — find which
before doing anything else.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** Nothing reaches the application: one scraper file and its tests, producing byte-identical
output. The catalogue the game reads does not change by one character, which is what
`committed.test.ts` asserts.

## Out of scope

- **`CastInput` and `ProductionInput` themselves.** Structurally identical, generated from Rust, and
  `ah-gdfe`'s business. Merging them is a schema change with a wire format behind it; this bead
  changes only how their values are read out of a sentence.
- **Any other regex in `data.ts`** — `STUDY_REQUIREMENT`, `CAST_COST`, `PRODUCTION`,
  `PRODUCTION_SEGMENT`, `TRANSMUTE`, `ANY_OF`, `FORMULA_OUTPUT`, `PRODUCED_TAG`. They read different
  things and are not copies of each other.
- **The two different policies on an unreadable clause** — `readCastCost` throws, `readProduction`
  skips the segment. Both are deliberate, both are commented, and both stay at their call site.
- **`parseItemReference` and `parseBuildingReference`**, unless they turn out to hold a fourth copy;
  if they do, fold it in and say so in the PR, since it is the same defect by definition.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
grep -n "CAST_INPUT\|PRODUCTION_INPUT\|REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE" packages/ruleset/src/data.ts   # nothing
git status --porcelain -- config/public/ruleset.json                                      # nothing
```

All green, both greps silent.

No human check is needed: no application behaviour is touched, and the catalogue is asserted
byte-identical.

## Known traps

- **`config/public/ruleset.json` must not change.** It is the whole acceptance condition, and
  `committed.test.ts` is what enforces it. A diff there means a substitution was not equivalent.
- **A global regex carries `lastIndex` between calls.** `matchAll` resets it and the existing code
  already relies on that — keep using `matchAll`, and do not switch either reader to `exec` in a
  loop, which would make a second call on the same pattern start halfway through the clause.
- **`REQUIREMENT_CLAUSE` captures tag-then-number; the other two capture number-then-tag.** The
  destructuring order is reversed between `taggedLevels` and `taggedAmounts`, and getting it wrong
  produces a plausible object with the two fields swapped — which typechecks, because both are
  strings and numbers in the same shapes. Each has a test naming a real entry.
- **`amount === undefined ? 1` is not the same as `?? 1`** for a captured group, and the
  distinction is why the existing loops are written the way they are. Move the expression, do not
  modernise it.
- **The `ANY_OF` strip happens before the amounts are read** (`:493`), and its order matters —
  `any of` sits where a name would. Keep `taggedAmounts(tail.replace(ANY_OF, ""))` in that order.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`**: none of the five apply. No persisted setting, no browser suite, no
  `packages/shared` effect test.

title: Refactoring: a qualified structure is re-parsed by four readers and drawn wrong
description:
## The cost being paid

`parse_structure` splits a structure line only on `;` and `, needs `, so a qualified manifest arrives
whole — `Lair, closed to player units`, `Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys`. The map layer then re-parses
that string with bare-word sets to decide what to draw, and every miss is a structure silently drawn as
a generic building.

Four defects were fixed in this one classification surface in a single day, each fix preserving the
previous one's workaround rather than replacing it. `classify` now calls `isShip(structure.kind) ||
isShip(kind)` — raw *and* cleaned — under a comment saying the guard "is the difference between fixing
this bug and trading it for another".

## Evidence

- `19f93c31` fix(ah-o0d3): classify a structure kind the report qualified (#499) — no theme had ever
  drawn a lair from a real report
- `a003d411` fix(ah-3pr9): draw fleets as ships and count vessels (#501) — six of seven fleets drew as
  buildings; the Ships badge read 1 where the hex held 61
- `c9b0311d` fix(ah-lcyn): draw qualified habitats as lairs and a gateway as a gate (#502) — Ice Cave
  and Demon Pit fell through though `cave` and `pit` were both listed
- `824f75eb` fix(ah-t5fk): link each vessel in a fleet's manifest to its own entry (#511) — the same
  string re-parsed a fourth way, for the region pane's links
- All four are 2026-08-21. The upstream cause is untouched: `crates/core/src/report/region.rs:141`.

## Where

- `crates/core/src/report/region.rs` (`parse_structure`)
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts` (`classify`, `isShip`, `vesselCount`)

## What a refactoring would change

Split the manifest where it is read: have `parse_structure` return the kind and its qualifiers as
separate fields — the vessel list as a list — so every downstream reader gets structure rather than a
sentence. The map's bare-word sets, the vessel count and the region pane's links then read fields, and
the raw-or-cleaned double guard goes away instead of gaining a fifth reader.

Filed by Forge, weekly sweep of 2026-08-24, range 440b51fb..origin/main.
design:
## Context

`parse_structure` (`crates/core/src/report/region.rs:141-171`) splits a structure line on `" : "`,
on `;` for a description, and on `", needs "` for a build cost — **and nothing else**. So a
qualified manifest arrives whole, as a sentence:

```
Lair, closed to player units
Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys
Fleet, 6 Airships
```

The map layer then **re-parses that string** with bare-word sets to decide what to draw
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts:242-270`), and every miss is a structure
silently drawn as a generic building.

**Four defects were fixed in this one classification surface on a single day**, 2026-08-21, each fix
preserving the previous one's workaround rather than replacing it:

| Commit | What was wrong |
|---|---|
| `19f93c31 fix(ah-o0d3) (#499)` | **no theme had ever drawn a lair from a real report** |
| `a003d411 fix(ah-3pr9) (#501)` | six of seven fleets drew as buildings; the Ships badge read **1** where the hex held **61** |
| `c9b0311d fix(ah-lcyn) (#502)` | Ice Cave and Demon Pit fell through, though `cave` and `pit` were both listed |
| `824f75eb fix(ah-t5fk) (#511)` | the same string re-parsed a **fourth** way, for the region pane's links |

What that left behind is `classify`'s central line, `isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)` —
**raw and cleaned, both** — under a comment saying the guard *"is the difference between fixing this
bug and trading it for another"*, because `Fleet, 6 Airships` is a ship only on account of the word
`Airships`. And `vesselCount` (`:313`) reaches for `manifestSegments` from `vesselManifest.ts`,
which the region pane uses differently on purpose. **Four readers, one sentence, no structure.**

The upstream cause has never been touched.

When this lands: the report's own words stay on `kind` for display, and every reader gets fields —
the leading kind, its qualifiers, and a fleet's manifest as a list — so a classification is a lookup
rather than a guess.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The rule that makes this safe: **`kind` does not change meaning**

`Structure` is part of `ReportParseResult`, which is **stored** as `parsedPayloadJson` and read back
by deserialisation, not by re-parsing (`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:229-234`,
`webCoreAdapter.ts:933,969,995`). So a field that changes meaning changes what every already-stored
snapshot means, silently and retroactively.

Therefore: **`kind` keeps the report's exact words**, and the split arrives as *new* fields beside
it. Nothing stored is reinterpreted, and `kind` remains the right thing to show a player.

### `crates/core/src/report/region.rs` — one splitter, three new fields

```rust
/// One vessel line inside a fleet's manifest: `40 Galleons`.
///
/// `count` is `None` where the report named a vessel without a number, which is how a single
/// unnamed vessel appears - the count is not assumed to be one here, because whether an unnumbered
/// vessel counts as one is the *reader's* question and `vessel_count` in the map layer already
/// answers it (`ah-nmts`).
#[derive(..., TS)]
#[ts(export, rename = "VesselEntry", export_to = "VesselEntry.ts")]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct VesselEntry {
    pub count: Option<i64>,
    pub name: String,
}

/// The kind and its qualifiers, split once, where the line is read.
///
/// `parse_structure` used to hand the whole clause over as `kind` and four separate readers
/// re-parsed it - the map's bare-word sets, its ship test, its vessel count and the region pane's
/// links - which is how four defects were fixed in one surface in one day (`ah-nmts`).
#[must_use]
fn split_kind(kind_text: &str) -> (String, Vec<String>, Vec<VesselEntry>);
```

added to `Structure` as:

```rust
    /// The kind as the report wrote it, qualifiers and all: `Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys`.
    /// Unchanged, and still what a player is shown - the fields below are derived from it.
    pub kind: String,
    /// The kind alone, before the first comma: `Galley`. Lower-cased by the reader, not here.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub base_kind: String,
    /// Everything after the first comma, one clause per entry, trimmed:
    /// `["closed to player units"]`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub qualifiers: Vec<String>,
    /// The qualifiers that name vessels, parsed. Empty for every structure that is not a fleet.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub vessels: Vec<VesselEntry>,
```

**`#[serde(default)]` on all three is load-bearing**: a stored payload written before this bead has
none of them, and without the default it fails to deserialise — which would make every already
imported turn unreadable.

### `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:229` — old snapshots are back-filled on the way in

`hydrate_parse_result_state` is the single funnel every stored payload passes through. Back-fill
there, so a snapshot written last week behaves exactly like one written today and **the TypeScript
side never needs a fallback**:

```rust
pub fn hydrate_parse_result_state(parsed_payload_json: String) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue> {
    let mut parsed = serde_json::from_str::<ReportParseResult>(&parsed_payload_json)
        .map_err(|error| JsValue::from_str(&error.to_string()))?;
    // A payload stored before `ah-nmts` carries only `kind`. Split it here with the same function
    // `parse_structure` uses, so one parser answers for both, and no reader downstream has to know
    // which kind of snapshot it is looking at.
    atlantis_hud_core::report::region::backfill_structure_kinds(&mut parsed);
    to_js(&ReportParseResultWire::from(parsed))
}
```

`backfill_structure_kinds` walks the regions' structures and, **only where `base_kind` is empty**,
fills all three from `kind` via `split_kind`. An empty `base_kind` is unambiguous: a real one is
never empty, because `split_kind` on a kindless line returns the whole string.

**One parser, called twice** — that is the point of the bead, and a second implementation of the
split anywhere is the defect coming back.

The desktop reads through `core-persistence`, which deserialises the same struct; add the same
back-fill wherever it hydrates a stored payload, or the two platforms disagree about old snapshots.
**Find that call site and name it in the PR** — if the desktop re-parses from `raw_report` instead,
say so and skip it.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts` — the string logic goes

```ts
function classify(structure: StructureInfo): StructureKind {
  if (roadDirection(structure.kind) !== null) {
    return "road";
  }
  const kind = structure.baseKind.trim().toLowerCase();
  // A fleet is a ship because it carries vessels, not because of a word in its name. This is what
  // `isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)` was standing in for (`ah-3pr9`, `ah-nmts`).
  if (structure.vessels.length > 0 || isShip(kind)) {
    return "ship";
  }
  if (SHAFT_KINDS.has(kind)) { return "shaft"; }
  if (GATE_KINDS.has(kind)) { return "gate"; }
  …
}
```

The `comma`/`slice` cleaning (`:248-251`) and its five-line comment go; the `|| isShip(kind)` double
test goes; **`isShip` keeps its `SHIP_KINDS` set and its `"ship"`/`"boat"` substring test**, now
applied to a bare kind only.

`vesselCount` (`:313-323`) becomes `structure.vessels`: sum the counts, and keep its existing
"`0` means one unnumbered vessel" rule verbatim — that is a reader's decision and this bead does not
revisit it. `manifestSegments`/`vesselManifest.ts` is then read by the region pane alone; **if
nothing else uses it after this, delete it and say so**, and if the region pane still needs it,
point that at `structure.vessels` too and delete it anyway.

`roadDirection` keeps reading `structure.kind` — a road encodes its direction in the clause, and
that is a use of the raw sentence rather than a re-parse of the kind.

## Increments

1. **The splitter, in core.**
   RED, in `region.rs`'s test module:
   - `an unqualified kind is its own base kind` — `"Magical Citadel"` → base `"Magical Citadel"`, no
     qualifiers, no vessels.
   - `a qualified lair keeps its clause as a qualifier` — `"Lair, closed to player units"`.
   - `a fleet's manifest becomes vessels` — `"Galley, 40 Galleons, 11 Galleys"` → base `"Galley"`,
     vessels `[{40, "Galleons"}, {11, "Galleys"}]`.
   - `a vessel with no number has no count` — `"Fleet, Longboat"` → `count: None`.
   - `a needs clause is not a qualifier` — `"Magical Tower, needs 560"` still sets `needs` and
     leaves `qualifiers` empty. **`", needs "` is stripped before the split, and this test is what
     stops it becoming a vessel called `"needs 560"`.**
   - `a description is still split off a semicolon` — the existing behaviour, unmoved.
   GREEN: `split_kind`, `VesselEntry`, the three fields, and `parse_structure` filling them.

2. **Old snapshots are back-filled.**
   RED: `a payload without the split fields is filled from its kind`, and
   `a payload that already has them is left alone` — the second matters, because a re-split of an
   already-split payload would be a second parse of a string that is no longer a sentence.
   GREEN: `backfill_structure_kinds`, called from `hydrate_parse_result_state` and from the
   desktop's equivalent.

3. **The map reads fields.**
   RED, in `hexView`'s existing test file: `a fleet is a ship because it carries vessels` —
   a structure with `baseKind: "Fleet"`, `vessels: [{count: 6, name: "Airships"}]`, classified as
   `"ship"` **with no word matching any ship set**. That is the case
   `isShip(structure.kind) || isShip(kind)` existed for, and it is the one that proves the workaround
   can go. Then `a qualified lair is a lair` and `a qualified habitat is a lair` (`ah-o0d3`,
   `ah-lcyn`), and `the ships badge counts every vessel in a manifest` (`ah-3pr9`: 61, not 1).
   GREEN: the rewritten `classify` and `vesselCount`.

4. **The corpus is unchanged.** Not code — see *Validation*.

## The test plan

| Test | File | Pins |
|---|---|---|
| the six splitter tests | `crates/core/src/report/region.rs` | the split, including `", needs "` |
| the two back-fill tests | `crates/core-wasm` or `region.rs` | a stored snapshot behaves like a fresh one, and is not split twice |
| `a fleet is a ship because it carries vessels` | `hexView`'s test file | the `ah-3pr9` workaround can go |
| `a qualified lair is a lair`, `a qualified habitat is a lair` | same | `ah-o0d3`, `ah-lcyn` — from fields, not from a comma |
| `the ships badge counts every vessel in a manifest` | same | `ah-3pr9`'s 61-not-1 |
| the existing `hexView` and `region.rs` tests | both | **nothing else moved** — unedited |

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --filter @atlantis/web build:wasm
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm run check:fast
```

## User-facing decisions

**None — and the bead's whole target is that there are none.** Every structure must be drawn as it is
drawn today; the change is that the classification is a lookup instead of a re-parse.

**If the corpus classification changes anywhere, that is a finding and not a licence.** Increment 4
compares before and after over the real reports. A structure that starts drawing as a lair when it
drew as a building is very likely a fifth defect of the same family — genuinely better, and still a
change on the map that the navigator has not seen. **File it at P4 naming the structure and both
classifications, say so in the PR, and do not absorb it silently.** Changing what a hex draws is the
navigator's decision.

## Out of scope

- **Any change to what a kind *means*** — `SHIP_KINDS`, `SHAFT_KINDS`, `GATE_KINDS` and the
  lair/habitat sets keep exactly their present members. This bead changes what they are applied to.
- **`kind`'s content.** It stays the report's own words, for display and for `roadDirection`.
- **`vesselCount`'s "unnumbered vessel counts as one" rule.** Moved verbatim.
- **The region pane's links** (`ah-t5fk`), beyond pointing them at `structure.vessels` if that is a
  one-line change. If it is not, leave them and say so.
- **Re-parsing stored payloads from `raw_report`.** The back-fill is cheaper, exact, and does not
  need the raw report to still be there.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --filter @atlantis/web build:wasm
pnpm run check:generated
pnpm run check:fast
```

All green. Then **the corpus check, which is the acceptance condition**: over the committed fixture
reports in `tests/fixtures/reports/`, dump every structure's `structure_id` and its classification
on `origin/main` and on the branch, and diff the two lists. **They must be identical.** Write this
as a throwaway script or a `#[ignore]`d test and say in the PR what it printed; do not skip it
because the unit tests are green — the unit tests use hand-built structures, and the four defects
this bead is about were all found on real reports and none on a fixture.

**A human check**: open a report with a fleet and one with a lair, and confirm the map draws a ship
and a lair, and that the Ships badge counts every vessel. `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` is the
one the earlier beads used.

## Known traps

- **`kind` must not change meaning.** `ReportParseResult` is stored as `parsedPayloadJson` and read
  back by deserialisation, never re-parsed. Redefining `kind` as the bare word would retroactively
  change what every stored snapshot says.
- **`#[serde(default)]` on all three new fields**, or every stored payload fails to deserialise and
  every imported turn becomes unreadable.
- **Back-fill only where `base_kind` is empty.** Splitting an already-split payload is a second
  parse of a string that is no longer a sentence, and there is a test named for it.
- **`", needs "` is stripped before the split.** `parse_structure` already does it (`:159-163`) and
  the order matters: split the needs clause off first, or a build cost becomes a vessel called
  `"needs 560"`. There is a test named for it.
- **`roadDirection` keeps reading the raw `kind`.** A road's direction is in the clause; that is a
  use of the sentence, not a re-parse of the kind, and "tidying" it to `baseKind` silently stops
  every road being drawn.
- **`Fleet, 6 Airships` is the case the old guard existed for**, and it must classify as a ship
  through `vessels`, not through any word. If the new `classify` needs `isShip(structure.kind)` back,
  the split is wrong — do not restore the double test.
- **The wasm bundle is not rebuilt by `pnpm run check:fast`.** `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web
  build:wasm` is this project's `prewarm`, and the browser suites see a new field only after it.
- **`.claude/cerebro-traps.md`: no effect-level test in `packages/shared`.** `hexView`'s tests are
  pure functions over structures, which is why increment 3 is writable at all.

title: Refactoring: the map's framing rules cannot be tested outside a browser
description:
## The cost being paid

`MapCanvas` holds its measured size in component state, filled by a `ResizeObserver` effect, and
everything derived from it — the ruler ticks, the initial fit, the follow-selection scope — is gated
on that state. `packages/shared` has no jsdom by decision, so its component tests render with
`renderToStaticMarkup`, no effect runs, `size` stays `{0,0}`, and none of that geometry is reachable
by any test the package can run. Every rule about it is therefore smoke-only or untested.

Four beads have each paid for this separately, and the fix pattern already exists next door: ah-mwqa
extracted `dossierPeek.ts` plus a `useReportedRect` hook and a `MeasuredFactionDossier` wrapper so the
dossier panel stays hook-free. `MapCanvas` never got that treatment.

## Evidence

- docs/retrospectives/ah-mwqa.md §"The plan put effect-level tests in a file whose harness runs no
  effects" — ~30 minutes, nine existing tests red at once, and it closes "This is the third bead to pay
  for the gap".
- docs/retrospectives/ah-brgo.2.md §"The plan asked for a ruler-label test that `packages/shared`
  cannot run" — names `MapCanvas.tsx:297`; ~10 minutes plus a deviation to justify in the PR body.
- docs/retrospectives/ah-t2i.md — "`MapCanvas` also carries hook state, so it cannot be called directly
  as a plain function the way those stateless components' tests do"; ~15 minutes.
- docs/retrospectives/ah-1uj.md §*Prevent by* item 2 asks for a unit test of the follow-selection
  effect's scope that still cannot be written; its sibling item 1 was implemented.

## Where

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` (the `size` state and its `ResizeObserver` effect;
  `ticksX`/`ticksY`, the initial fit, the follow-selection effect)
- The pattern to copy: `packages/shared/src/workspace/dossierPeek.ts`, `useReportedRect.ts`

## What a refactoring would change

Move the geometry rules into pure modules that take a size and return ticks, a fit and a follow
decision, and leave `MapCanvas` to measure and pass it in through a measured wrapper. The rules become
testable in the package that owns them; smoke keeps only what genuinely needs a browser.
