design:
## Context

"Where is the caret in this order line — the command position, or which argument — and what word is
being typed?" is answered **three** times: once in the core by lexing, and twice in the client by
regex.

- **The core**, `arguments_at_caret` (`crates/core/src/orders/grammar.rs:442-471`): lexes the prefix,
  returns `None` inside a comment or an unterminated quote, drops the last token when the prefix ends
  in neither whitespace nor `"` ("still being typed"), and returns `None` again when nothing is left —
  which is the command position.
- **The client, twice**: `orderCommandCompletions` matches `/^(\s*@?\s*)([A-Za-z]*)$/`
  (`packages/shared/src/orderCompletion.ts:23`); `orderArgumentCompletions` finds the typed word with
  `/(?:^|\s)([A-Za-z]*)$/` (`:88`) and then re-derives "am I still in the command position" from a
  `head` slice (`:99-102`); and `snippetCompletionSource` has a **third** copy,
  `/^(\s*@?\s*)([A-Za-z][\w-]*|)$/` (`packages/shared/src/orderSnippets.ts:109`), its comment openly
  saying "The command position, as `orderCommandCompletions` defines it".

**The bead's own description named two copies. There are three, and two of them have already
drifted**: a word is `[A-Za-z]*` in one and `[A-Za-z][\w-]*` in the other, so the same keystroke is a
different word depending on which source is asked. That drift is the cost this bead is about, arriving
before anybody looked for it.

The cost already paid, from `docs/retrospectives/ah-bai.1.md` §"A bug found and fixed on the core side
had an untested twin on the client side": the closed-quote case (`BUILD "Big Boat"` then Ctrl+Space)
was found and fixed in the core with a Rust test, and the identical bug in the TS regex was caught only
by the Copilot review afterwards — one extra review round trip, about fifteen minutes, in the same PR.
The retrospective names the cause: *"they are separate implementations of the same idea."*

**The old reason for the duplication is gone.** `orderCompletion.ts:71-78` says the client keeps its
own rule "to avoid a round trip per keystroke" — but the same docstring already concedes that tag-or-name
matching forces "a core call per keystroke rather than per word", and the argument source does exactly
that today. So the argument path already pays the call this refactoring would generalise.

When this lands there is **one** reader of the caret's position, in the core, and a boundary case fixed
once is fixed for every source. Behaviour is unchanged: the same popup, the same entries, in the same
order, with the same silences.

Two stale citations in the bead's description, corrected here: `order_argument_completions` is
`crates/core/src/orders/completion.rs:52`, not `grammar.rs:444` (`grammar.rs:814` records the move);
and `ah-bai.2` no longer exists as a bead, so nothing is in flight against this code.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/completion.rs` — the one answer

A new public type and function beside `order_argument_completions`, which stays exactly as it is (the
new function calls it, and every existing caller keeps working):

```rust
/// Which position the caret is in, decided once, in the core.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum CaretPosition {
    /// The first word of the line, behind any indentation and an optional `@`. The shell's own
    /// command and snippet lists answer here; `options` below is empty.
    Command,
    /// Any position after the command, where the grammar, the catalogue and the hex decide.
    Argument,
    /// Nowhere a completion belongs: inside a comment, inside an unterminated quote, or after a
    /// command the grammar table does not have.
    Nowhere,
}

/// Where the caret is in one order line, what word is being typed there, and what may stand there.
///
/// One call, because the three answers come from one lexing of the line and the shell needs all
/// three for every keystroke. Splitting them is what left the caret's position decided in three
/// places and two of them disagreeing about what a word is (ah-vfq).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct CaretCompletions {
    pub position: CaretPosition,
    /// Where the word being typed starts, counted in **UTF-16 code units** from the start of the
    /// line - the same counting the checker's spans use (`lexer.rs:56`) and the same unit
    /// CodeMirror's own document offsets are in, so a shell adds it to `line.from` directly.
    /// Equal to the caret's own column when no word is being typed - the caret sits after
    /// whitespace or a closing quote - which is where a chosen entry is then written.
    pub word_start: usize,
    /// The word being typed, verbatim from the line. Empty when none is.
    pub word: String,
    /// What may stand here. Empty unless `position` is `Argument`.
    pub options: Vec<OrderCompletion>,
}

/// The caret's whole story for one order line up to the caret. See [`CaretCompletions`].
#[must_use]
pub fn completions_at_caret(
    line_prefix: &str,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
    report: Option<&ParsedReport>,
    unit_id: Option<&str>,
) -> CaretCompletions
```

**`word_start` and `word` come from the lexer, not from a regex.** `arguments_at_caret`
(`grammar.rs:442-455`) already knows which token is half-typed and why; that knowledge is what must be
exposed rather than re-derived. So `grammar.rs` gains one `pub(super)` helper beside it, and
`arguments_at_caret` is refactored to call it so there is still only one implementation:

```rust
/// The token the caret is inside, if it is inside one: its text and where it starts.
///
/// A prefix ending in whitespace, or in a closing `"`, is not inside a token - `"` is unambiguous,
/// so the token it ends is complete and the caret is already in the next position (the reasoning
/// at grammar.rs:449-455, which this now owns).
pub(super) fn word_at_caret(line_prefix: &str) -> Option<&Token>
```

**`Token` already carries what this needs, so nothing new is added to the lexer.**
`crates/core/src/orders/lexer.rs:41-46` is
`Token { kind, text, column_start, column_end }`, and `column_start`/`column_end` are counted in
UTF-16 code units (`lexer.rs:56`, `Span`'s docstring). So `word_at_caret` returns the token and
`word_start` is simply its `column_start`; when no token is being typed, `word_start` is the caret's own
column, which is the UTF-16 length of `line_prefix`. For that
no-word case use `lexer::utf16_column(line_prefix, line_prefix.len())` (`lexer.rs:65`), never
`line_prefix.len()`, which is bytes.

`CaretPosition` is decided from the same three tests `arguments_at_caret` already makes, in this order:
comment or unterminated quote → `Nowhere`; no complete tokens left → `Command`; `find_order` fails →
`Nowhere`; otherwise `Argument`. `options` is `order_argument_completions(...)`'s answer, called only
in the `Argument` arm.

`Serialize, Deserialize` on both types, `rename_all = "camelCase"` — the shape every type crossing this
boundary uses (`OrderCompletion`, `completion.rs:22-33`).

Re-export from `crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs:22` and `crates/core/src/lib.rs:132`, alongside
`order_argument_completions` and `OrderCompletion`.

### `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs` and `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`

One new binding each, copied from the `order_argument_completions` pair — same four arguments, same
optional-string handling, same error shape:

- `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs`, beside `order_argument_completions_state` (`:538`):
  `pub fn completions_at_caret_state(line_prefix: &str, ruleset_json: Option<String>, raw_report: Option<String>, unit_id: Option<String>) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue>`.
- `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`, beside `command_order_argument_completions` (`:466`):
  `command_completions_at_caret`, `#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case", rename = "completions_at_caret")]`, and added to the `tauri::generate_handler!` list at `:1063`.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` and `tauriCommands.ts`

`index.ts`: mirror the two new types beside `OrderCompletion` (`:392`) and add one method to the
`CoreClient` interface beside `orderArgumentCompletions` (`:525`):

```ts
/** Which position the caret is in. Mirrors the core's `CaretPosition`. */
export type CaretPosition = "command" | "argument" | "nowhere";

/** Mirrors the core's `CaretCompletions`. */
export type CaretCompletions = {
  position: CaretPosition;
  wordStart: number;
  word: string;
  options: OrderCompletion[];
};

  completionsAtCaret(
    linePrefix: string,
    rulesetJson: string | null,
    rawReport: string | null,
    unitId: string | null
  ): Promise<CaretCompletions>;
```

These are hand-written mirrors, as `OrderCompletion` is — the generated file
(`coreVocabulary.generated.ts`) carries *values* (code lists, movement words), not types, so
`crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs` needs no change and must not be regenerated for this bead.

`tauriCommands.ts`: one entry beside `orderArgumentCompletions` (`:49`) —
`completionsAtCaret: ["completions_at_caret", "line_prefix", "ruleset_json", "raw_report", "unit_id"]`.

`packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`: one method beside `orderArgumentCompletions` (`:462`),
delegating to `wasm.completions_at_caret_state`.

**Keep `orderArgumentCompletions` on the interface and in both adapters.** It has its own tests
(`webCoreAdapter.test.ts:392`) and removing it is a second, unrelated change; a follow-up may retire it
once nothing calls it.

### `packages/shared/src/orderCompletion.ts` — the client keeps only plumbing

`ArgumentLookup` becomes a caret lookup, and **all three sources take it**:

```ts
/** How the caret's position and candidates reach the core: one order line up to the caret. */
export type CaretLookup = (linePrefix: string) => Promise<CaretCompletions>;
```

`orderCommandCompletions(commands, lookUp)` — no regex. It awaits the lookup, returns `null` unless
`position === "command"`, returns `null` when `word === "" && !context.explicit`, and otherwise builds
its result from the core's answer:

```ts
    from: line.from + caret.wordStart,
    options: suggestOrderCommands(caret.word, commands).map(...),   // unchanged
    validFor: /^[A-Za-z]*$/                                        // unchanged
```

`orderArgumentCompletions(lookUp)` — the `/(?:^|\s)([A-Za-z]*)$/` match (`:88`) and the whole `head`
block (`:99-102`) go. It returns `null` unless `position === "argument"`, keeps the
`word === "" && !context.explicit` silence, keeps `matchesArgument` filtering, keeps `filter: false`
and no `validFor`, and takes `from` from `line.from + caret.wordStart`.

`matchesArgument` (`:57-63`) and `suggestOrderCommands` (`orderEditor.ts:20-23`) are unchanged and are
the two pieces of filtering that stay on this side deliberately — they are richer than CodeMirror's own
and are about presentation, not about where the caret is.

### `packages/shared/src/orderSnippets.ts` — the third copy goes

`snippetCompletionSource(snippets, lookUp)` becomes async, drops
`/^(\s*@?\s*)([A-Za-z][\w-]*|)$/` (`:109`) and its comment about mirroring
`orderCommandCompletions`, and gates on `position === "command"` instead. `from` becomes
`line.from + caret.wordStart`; the `word` it filters by is `caret.word.toLowerCase()`.

**This changes what counts as a word for snippets, and that is the drift being fixed rather than a
regression.** The old regex accepted `[\w-]` so a snippet named `tax-and-work` filtered on `tax-and`;
the core's lexer treats `tax-and` as one token and reports it whole as `word`, so the same keystroke
gives the same word. **Pin it with a test** (`a_hyphenated_snippet_name_still_filters`) rather than
assuming — if the lexer splits on `-`, the snippet source must lowercase and use `caret.word` as it
comes and the test will say so. `validFor: /^([A-Za-z][\w-]*)?$/` stays as it is: it describes what
this source answers for, not how the word was found.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx` and `AppShell.tsx`

`OrdersEditor.tsx:132-137`: the three `override` sources each take the lookup. **The order of the three
stays exactly as it is** — commands, snippets, arguments — because CodeMirror merges the sources'
results and that order is what the player sees.

`AppShell.tsx:1276` builds the lookup. It becomes a call to `completionsAtCaret`, wrapped in a
**one-entry memo keyed on the line prefix**:

```ts
// Three completion sources ask about the same caret on the same keystroke; the core would answer
// three times identically. One entry is all the cache needs - the prefix changes on the next
// keystroke and the old answer is dead.
const lastCaret = useRef<{ prefix: string; answer: Promise<CaretCompletions> } | null>(null);
const caretLookup = useCallback<CaretLookup>((linePrefix) => {
  if (lastCaret.current?.prefix === linePrefix) {
    return lastCaret.current.answer;
  }
  const answer = client
    .completionsAtCaret(linePrefix, rulesetText, rawReport || null, unit?.unitId ?? null)
    .catch(() => ({ position: "nowhere", wordStart: linePrefix.length, word: "", options: [] }));
  lastCaret.current = { prefix: linePrefix, answer };
  return answer;
}, [client, rulesetText, rawReport, unit?.unitId]);
```

The memo must be invalidated when its other inputs change, which the `useCallback` dependency list does
by giving a fresh closure with a fresh `lastCaret`— **check that**: `useRef` survives a `useCallback`
identity change, so clear `lastCaret.current = null` inside the callback body's dependency change, or
key the memo on the other inputs too. The simplest correct form is to include them in the key:
`{ key: [linePrefix, rulesetText, rawReport, unitId].join("�"), answer }`. Use that.

The `.catch(() => [])` that `orderCompletion.ts:104` does today moves here, returning a `nowhere`
answer, so a failed core call silences the popup exactly as it silences it now.

## Increments

Four, each RED first, and the client is not touched until the core answer exists.

### 1. The core answers the caret

RED — `crates/core/src/orders/completion.rs`, `mod tests`:

- `the_command_position_is_reported_as_such`: `completions_at_caret("  @ta", None, None, None)` →
  `position == Command`, `word == "ta"`, `word_start == 4`, `options` empty.
- `an_argument_position_carries_its_options`: `completions_at_caret("NAME U", None, None, None)` →
  `position == Argument`, `word == "U"`, `word_start == 5`, `options` non-empty and equal to
  `order_argument_completions("NAME U", None, None, None)`.
- `a_caret_after_a_closing_quote_is_the_next_position`: `completions_at_caret("BUILD \"Big Boat\"", …)`
  → `position == Argument`, `word == ""`, `word_start == 16` (the prefix's own length). **This is
  ah-bai.1's bug, in the one place it can now be got wrong.**
- `a_caret_after_whitespace_types_no_word`: `"NAME UNIT "` → `word == ""`,
  `word_start == 10`.
- `a_comment_is_nowhere`: `"TAX ; note"` → `Nowhere`.
- `an_unterminated_quote_is_nowhere`: `"BUILD \"Big"` → `Nowhere`.
- `an_order_the_grammar_does_not_have_is_nowhere`: `"FLURBLE x"` → `Nowhere`.
- `an_empty_line_is_the_command_position`: `""` → `Command`, `word == ""`, `word_start == 0`.

GREEN — `word_at_caret` in `grammar.rs` (with `arguments_at_caret` refactored to call it, so its own
tests keep passing unchanged), then `CaretPosition`, `CaretCompletions` and `completions_at_caret`, then
the two re-exports.

`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core orders::` and `orders::grammar` must both be green, with **no existing
test edited** — if a `grammar.rs` test needs changing, `arguments_at_caret` has been given new behaviour
rather than a new internal helper.

### 2. The bindings

No RED available in Rust (a `#[wasm_bindgen]` shim has no unit test, and the tauri command's own tests
at `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:1233` are integration-shaped). Add both bindings, the
`generate_handler!` entry, the two `core-client` types, the interface method, the `tauriCommands.ts`
entry and the `webCoreAdapter` method. Gate: `cargo build`, `pnpm run check:fast`'s typecheck, and
`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-tauri` if that crate's suite exists.

### 3. The three client sources

RED — `packages/shared/src/orderCompletion.test.ts` and a new
`packages/shared/src/orderSnippets.test.ts` case, with the lookup stubbed to return a
`CaretCompletions` rather than a bare array. The existing test helper at
`orderCompletion.test.ts:77-90` takes an `ArgumentLookup`; change it to a `CaretLookup` and give each
existing case the `position` its prose already assumes — that migration **is** the RED, because every
current case compiles against the old signature.

Then rewrite the three sources as described. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/orderCompletion.test.ts src/orderSnippets.test.ts`.

### 4. The wiring, and the drift is gone

`OrdersEditor.tsx` and `AppShell.tsx`, with the keyed memo. Then the grep that says the bead is done:

```bash
grep -rn '@?\\\\s\*' packages/shared/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'
```

must return nothing — no client-side command-position regex is left. `pnpm run check:fast`.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/completion.rs`.** The eight cases in increment 1. `grammar.rs`'s
existing `arguments_at_caret` tests are the regression that `word_at_caret` was extracted rather than
rewritten, and none of them changes.

**TS — `packages/shared/src/orderCompletion.test.ts`.** Every existing case migrated to a
`CaretLookup`, plus:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `the_command_source_is_quiet_in_an_argument_position` | `position: "argument"` → `null`, without a regex |
| `the_argument_source_is_quiet_in_the_command_position` | `position: "command"` → `null`, replacing the `head` test |
| `both_sources_are_quiet_nowhere` | `position: "nowhere"` → `null` from all three |
| `an_empty_word_answers_only_when_explicit` | The existing silence, unchanged, now driven by `caret.word` |
| `the_replaced_range_starts_where_the_core_says` | `from === line.from + wordStart`, the one thing a wrong offset would corrupt |
| `a_failed_core_call_is_silent` | The `.catch` moved to `AppShell`; the source sees `nowhere` |

**TS — `packages/shared/src/orderSnippets.test.ts`.** The existing snippet cases against a
`CaretLookup`, plus `a_hyphenated_snippet_name_still_filters` (increment 3's open question, settled by
the test).

**Smoke — `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`**, which is the one spec that drives the completion popup
end to end and therefore the only place the three sources' merged ordering is observed. **Run it
unchanged and add nothing to it.** It is also the suite most likely to catch the one thing the unit tests
cannot: three sources that now await a promise where they used to answer synchronously. If it goes red,
the fault is in this bead — not a flaky popup — and the async change is where to look.

```bash
pnpm run test:smoke -- orders-editor
```

`test:smoke` is `tsx scripts/withGateLock.ts pnpm exec playwright test` (`package.json:15`), so the
trailing argument is Playwright's own file filter. The browser suites are normally left to CI; this is
the one bead where running one locally is worth the time.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** This is a refactoring and its whole point is that the player sees exactly what they see
today: the same popup, the same entries in the same order, the same silences on an empty word, the same
`Ctrl+Space` behaviour, and no new or changed string anywhere.

Two consequences are worth naming as *not* being decisions, so nobody takes them to the navigator or
resolves them alone:

- **The command and snippet sources become async.** Today they answer from memory; after this they
  await one core call. That call is in-process — `webCoreAdapter` calls `wasm.*` directly
  (`webCoreAdapter.ts:462`), and the desktop shell a local Tauri command — and the argument source
  already makes exactly this call on every keystroke by design (`orderCompletion.ts:71-78`). The
  one-entry memo means one call per keystroke for all three sources rather than three. **This is an
  architecture decision and it is taken: the core is the single authority.** If measurable typing lag
  ever appears in the desktop shell, that is a new bead with a measurement in it, not a reason to keep
  a second copy of the rule.
- **Snippet filtering may accept a slightly different word.** See `orderSnippets.ts` in *Files to
  change*: the two client regexes already disagree about what a word is, so *something* must change to
  make them one. Which one wins is decided by the core's lexer and pinned by
  `a_hyphenated_snippet_name_still_filters`. If that test reveals the lexer splitting a hyphenated
  name — so a snippet the player could reach before becomes unreachable — **that is a behaviour change
  the player would feel, and it stops being mine.** Park the bead (`needs-ui-decision` + `human`) with
  the test's finding written out, rather than choosing.

## Out of scope

- **Retiring `orderArgumentCompletions`** from the `CoreClient` interface, the two adapters, the wasm
  and tauri bindings, and `crates/core/src/orders/completion.rs`. It keeps working, it keeps its tests,
  and `completions_at_caret` calls it. A follow-up may remove it once nothing calls it.
- **What each position offers.** `order_argument_completions`, `item_completions`,
  `market_completions`, `produce_completions` and `skill_completions` are untouched; this bead moves
  *where the caret is* into one place and nothing about *what may stand there*.
- **`matchesArgument` and `suggestOrderCommands`.** Presentation-side filtering, richer than
  CodeMirror's own, and deliberately staying on the client.
- **The generated vocabulary.** `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` carries values, not types; do not
  regenerate it, and do not move `CaretCompletions` into it.
- **New completion positions or new candidate sources.** Nothing new appears in the popup.
- **CodeMirror's merge order.** The three `override` sources keep their present order.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
cargo build
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/orderCompletion.test.ts src/orderSnippets.test.ts
pnpm run check:fast
```

The grep that says the duplication is gone — it must print **nothing**:

```bash
grep -rn '\\\\s\*@?\\\\s\*' packages/shared/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'
grep -rn '(?:\^|\\\\s)(\[A-Za-z\]\*)\$' packages/shared/src --include='*.ts'
```

**The human check, and it is the acceptance for a bead that changes no behaviour.** Open the orders
editor on a real report and confirm the popup is as it was:

1. Type `ta` at the start of a line → `TAX` offered. Type on → it keeps filtering without flicker.
2. `Ctrl+Space` on an empty line → commands **and** snippets, in that order.
3. `NAME U` → `UNIT` offered; `NAME UNIT ` then `Ctrl+Space` → the argument entries.
4. `BUILD "Big Boat"` with the caret right after the closing quote, then `Ctrl+Space` → `COMPLETE`
   offered. **This is ah-bai.1's bug and the reason the bead exists**; it must work in both shells.
5. `TAX ; a note` with the caret in the comment → nothing.
6. A snippet whose name carries a hyphen → still reachable by typing its first word.

Run 1–6 in the **web** shell and again in the **desktop** shell: the two adapters are the two paths the
new binding takes, and only one of them is exercised by the unit tests.

## Known traps

- **`Token` may not carry a start offset.** If `lex_line`'s token has only `text`, add the offset to the
  token rather than searching the prefix backwards for the word — a backwards search is the regex this
  bead exists to delete, rewritten in Rust. Check `lex_line` before writing `word_at_caret`.
- **`word_start` is a byte offset in Rust and a UTF-16 offset in CodeMirror.** An order line carrying an
  accent will place the completion in the wrong column if the two are conflated. The core already counts
  UTF-16 code units for diagnostics deliberately, for exactly this reason
  (`packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts:33-35`) — **match that convention and say which it is in
  `word_start`'s docstring**, and add a test with a non-ASCII character before the caret.
- **`arguments_at_caret` must be refactored, not reimplemented.** If any of its existing `grammar.rs`
  tests changes, the extraction went wrong: `word_at_caret` is a lift of lines 449-455 and nothing more.
- **The memo key must include the ruleset, report and unit id**, not just the line prefix. The same
  prefix typed in a different unit's block, or after the ruleset loads, has a different answer, and a
  prefix-only key would serve the stale one. See `AppShell.tsx` in *Files to change*.
- **`filter: false` and the absence of `validFor` on the argument source are load-bearing.** With
  `filter: false` CodeMirror shows exactly what it is given in the order given, which is what preserves
  the core's ordering (classes before items, market before catalogue). Do not add a `validFor` there
  while making the source async, however tempting a "keep filtering locally" optimisation looks.
- **Three sources, one order.** `OrdersEditor.tsx:132-137` lists commands, snippets, arguments, and
  CodeMirror merges in that order. Reordering them changes what the player sees first.
- **A failed core call must be silent, not empty-with-an-error.** Today `orderCompletion.ts:104` does
  `.catch(() => [])`. The equivalent after this change is a `nowhere` answer from the lookup; returning
  an `argument` answer with no options would make the popup close and reopen instead of never opening.
- **Do not regenerate `coreVocabulary.generated.ts`.** It is values-only, and
  `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs` will fail the PR if it is written to for no reason.
acceptance_criteria: 1. crates/core/src/orders/completion.rs exports CaretPosition, CaretCompletions and completions_at_caret; grammar.rs has word_at_caret, lifted from arguments_at_caret:449-455, and every existing arguments_at_caret test passes unedited. 2. word_start is UTF-16 code units (Token::column_start, or utf16_column for the no-word case) and a test with a non-ASCII character before the caret pins it. 3. wasm binding completions_at_caret_state, tauri command completions_at_caret in generate_handler!, CoreClient.completionsAtCaret, tauriCommands entry, webCoreAdapter method. 4. All three client sources (command, snippet, argument) gate on the core's CaretPosition; no command-position or word-boundary regex is left in packages/shared/src — the two Validation greps print nothing. 5. AppShell's caret lookup memoizes one answer keyed on the line prefix AND the ruleset, report and unit id, so one core call serves all three sources per keystroke; a failed call yields a nowhere answer and the popup stays silent. 6. orderCompletion.test.ts and orderSnippets.test.ts migrated to CaretLookup and green, including a_hyphenated_snippet_name_still_filters. 7. tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts passes unchanged. 8. coreVocabulary.generated.ts NOT regenerated. 9. cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core and pnpm run check:fast green. 10. The six human checks run in BOTH the web and desktop shells, case 4 (Ctrl+Space after a closing quote offers COMPLETE) included.

title: Warn when a BUILD order works on a structure that is already finished
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`BUILD: Object is finished.` - 1 occurrence in tests/fixtures/reports/
(docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A BUILD order named a structure of the unit's own
that the report already showed as complete.

## What the check would need
From the report: the structure's completion, however it is tracked (crates/core/src/report/model.rs
Structure - a "needs" figure of zero, or an equivalent). From the orders: the BUILD order's target
structure.

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). A newly-founded
structure this turn's own orders create is not this case.

## Validation
A BUILD order naming an already-finished structure of the unit's own warns. A BUILD order on an
unfinished or new structure stays silent.
design:
## Context

The engine says `BUILD: Object is finished.` A unit ordered to carry on building something the
report already showed as complete spends its month for nothing.

The report is unambiguous about which structures are done — an unfinished one prints what it still
needs, a finished one prints nothing:

```
+ Building [4] : Stockade, needs 45.        <- unfinished
+ Soggy Saw Mill [1] : Timber Yard.         <- finished
```

and that is exactly what `Structure::needs: Option<i64>` carries
(`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:93-101`, *"Remaining build cost when the structure is
unfinished"*): `Some(n)` unfinished, `None` finished.

**What does not exist yet is any knowledge of what a BUILD order says.** `intents.rs:247` reads
`"BUILD" => Some(Intent::MonthLong("BUILD"))` — the arguments are thrown away, so the app cannot
tell `BUILD` (carry on with the structure I am standing in) from `BUILD Tower` (found a new one).
Only the first can be about something already finished, so this bead gives BUILD a real intent
first and then checks it.

Branch from `origin/main`; line numbers are that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### A real BUILD intent — `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`

```rust
    /// `BUILD`, in whichever of the rules' forms it was written.
    ///
    /// `BUILD [name]` founds a structure of that type, so it names nothing that exists yet;
    /// everything else works on a structure that is already there - the one this unit stands in, or
    /// the one the helped unit stands in. `COMPLETE` is not recorded: it says when the work should
    /// finish, and no check reads it.
    Build {
        /// `BUILD [name]`: the type being founded.
        founding: Option<String>,
        /// `BUILD HELP [unit]`: whose structure is being worked on, when it is not this unit's.
        helping: Option<Party>,
    },
```

replacing the `MonthLong("BUILD")` arm at `:247`. Read it from the arguments the grammar already
permits (`orders/grammar.rs:127-137` — `HELP [unit] COMPLETE`, `HELP [unit]`, `COMPLETE`,
`[name] COMPLETE`, `[name]`, and nothing at all):

- first argument `HELP` → `helping` from the unit reference that follows, read the way every other
  intent reads a `Party`;
- first argument `COMPLETE`, or no arguments → both `None`;
- anything else → `founding` from that token.

`PRODUCE` and `CAST` stay `MonthLong`; only BUILD gains a shape, because only BUILD is being checked.

### The two places that must learn about it — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

**One the compiler catches, one it does not.** This is the most important paragraph in this plan:

- `semantics.rs:631-638` is an exhaustive `match` over `Intent` with no `_` arm, so a new variant is
  a compile error there and cannot be missed. Add `Intent::Build { .. }` to the group that does
  nothing to the ledger.
- **`is_busy()` (`semantics.rs:346-360`) is a `matches!` with a fixed list, and a variant missing
  from it silently returns `false`.** It currently counts `Intent::MonthLong(_)` — which is how BUILD
  is seen today. Take BUILD out of `MonthLong` without adding `Intent::Build { .. }` here and every
  builder becomes a candidate spare teacher. The comment above it says what that costs: *"one hex of
  turn 71 produced twenty-nine findings that were all the same non-observation."* Add the arm, and
  the regression test named below is what holds it.

### The check — `check_building`

A per-hex check called from `check_turn`'s region loop (`:167-172`):

```rust
        check_building(&hex, &options, &mut findings);
```

For each own unit in the hex with an `Intent::Build { founding, helping }` and its `PlacedIntent`:

1. `founding.is_some()` → nothing. A structure that does not exist yet cannot be finished.
2. Whose structure is it? `helping` resolves to a unit in this hex (`Hex::find`, `semantics.rs:233`,
   as `check_teaching` resolves its students); absent, it is the ordering unit's own.
3. That unit's `structure_id` (`report/model.rs:157`) → the `Structure` in
   `hex.region.structures` with that id. No structure, or a unit the hex does not hold → nothing:
   a BUILD outside any structure is a different mistake and is not this bead's.
4. `structure.needs.is_none()` → warn. `Some(_)` is unfinished and correct.

Two messages, by whose order it is:

| Case | Message |
|---|---|
| The unit standing in it | `Soggy Saw Mill is already finished` |
| A unit helping | `Soggy Saw Mill, which unit 4021 is in, is already finished` |

**Naming the structure.** Use `Structure::name`, except when the report gave it no name of its own
and printed a placeholder — `+ Building [4] : Stockade` and `+ Ship [218] : Raft` — in which case
append the id: `Building 4 is already finished`. Match the placeholder case-insensitively against
`"Building"` and `"Ship"`, and say in a comment that these are the engine's own words for an unnamed
structure. That is what the mockup drew and what the navigator saw.

The code, appended to `codes` and to `ALL` (whose length is in its type):

```rust
    pub const ALREADY_BUILT: Code = Code("already-built");
```

### The settings tab — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

A **new group**, after `Building`'s natural neighbours (put it before `Sailing`):

```tsx
  {
    heading: "Building",
    entries: [
      {
        code: "already-built",
        title: "Building what is built",
        description: "A BUILD order on a structure the report already shows as finished."
      }
    ]
  },
```

Both strings are the navigator's, as drawn.

### The generated vocabulary

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` mirrors `codes::ALL`. Regenerate:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

## Increments

1. **BUILD keeps its arguments.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`'s tests — `a_bare_build_names_nothing`,
   `building_a_type_is_founding` (`BUILD Tower` → `founding: Some("Tower")`), and
   `building_help_names_the_unit_helped` (`BUILD HELP 4021` → `helping`). They do not compile.
   GREEN: the `Intent::Build` variant and its reader. The exhaustive `match` at `semantics.rs:631`
   will refuse to compile until it has an arm; give it one that does nothing.

2. **A builder is still busy.**
   RED: `semantics.rs` — `a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher`, a hex where one unit
   teaches, one studies and one builds, expecting no `teacher-has-free-slots` finding naming the
   builder. This **passes today** and breaks the moment increment 1 lands, which is precisely why it
   is written before the fix.
   GREEN: `Intent::Build { .. }` added to `is_busy`.

3. **A finished structure warns.**
   RED: `carrying_on_with_a_finished_structure_warns` — a hex with a structure whose `needs` is
   `None`, a unit inside it ordering `BUILD`, expecting one `already-built` finding reading
   `Soggy Saw Mill is already finished`.
   GREEN: the code, `check_building` and its call.

4. **The helper, and the silences.**
   RED: `a_helper_is_warned_about_the_structure_it_would_work_on` (the second message shape),
   `an_unfinished_structure_is_silent`, `founding_a_new_structure_is_silent`,
   `a_unit_in_no_structure_is_silent`, `an_unnamed_structure_is_named_by_its_number`.
   GREEN: the branches.

5. **The vocabulary and the tab.**
   RED: `pnpm run check:generated` fails.
   GREEN: regenerate; add the `Building` group.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs` and `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`,
`cargo test --workspace`.** `intents.rs`'s own tests already read one document into intents
(`intents("unit 5\n@study obse\n")`, `:504`); the BUILD cases go beside them. The semantics tests
build regions and units with their helpers; a structure is a `Structure` on the region and the unit's
`structure_id` is what puts it inside.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `a_bare_build_names_nothing` | `BUILD` → `Build { founding: None, helping: None }` |
| `building_a_type_is_founding` | `BUILD Tower` → `founding: Some("Tower")` |
| `building_to_completion_is_not_a_name` | `BUILD COMPLETE` → both `None`, not `founding: Some("COMPLETE")` |
| `building_help_names_the_unit_helped` | `BUILD HELP 4021` → `helping` is unit 4021 |
| `building_help_to_completion` | `BUILD HELP 4021 COMPLETE` → the same, `COMPLETE` ignored |
| **`a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher`** | the `is_busy` regression, written before the change that would break it |
| `carrying_on_with_a_finished_structure_warns` | `needs: None` + bare `BUILD` → `Soggy Saw Mill is already finished` |
| `a_helper_is_warned_about_the_structure_it_would_work_on` | `Soggy Saw Mill, which unit 4021 is in, is already finished` |
| `an_unfinished_structure_is_silent` | `needs: Some(45)` → nothing |
| `founding_a_new_structure_is_silent` | `BUILD Tower` while standing in a finished mill → nothing |
| `a_unit_in_no_structure_is_silent` | `structure_id: None` → nothing |
| `a_helper_naming_a_unit_not_in_the_hex_is_silent` | nothing, and no panic |
| `an_unnamed_structure_is_named_by_its_number` | `Building 4 is already finished` |
| `a_foreign_unit_is_not_warned_about` | a BUILD in another faction's block → nothing |
| the disable table at `:~2570` | a row for `already-built` |

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 over
`.cerebro/scratch/ah-90w-build-finished.html`.

**Q1 — the wording.** Chosen: **`Soggy Saw Mill is already finished`** — names the structure and
nothing else; the wasted month is obvious from the order it sits on. Rejected: `…, so this month buys
nothing` (the same clause `ah-1uj` deliberately left off) and `this unit is standing in Soggy Saw
Mill, which is already finished`.

**Q2 — helpers.** Chosen: **warn on the helper too**, with its own wording naming whose structure it
is: `Soggy Saw Mill, which unit 4021 is in, is already finished`. Every wasted month is marked where
the order was written, so a player reading one unit's orders sees it. Rejected: warning only the unit
standing in the structure — accepted cost of the choice: a hex where six units all help carries seven
warnings about one building.

**Q3 — the Warnings tab.** Chosen: **a new `Building` group**, one entry to begin with, with room for
the building checks not yet filed. Rejected: the catch-all `Orders` group.

## Out of scope

- **Whether the materials are there.** A BUILD with nothing to build from is a different check and is
  not filed.
- **Whether the structure can be finished this month.** `COMPLETE` is not read at all.
- **A structure founded by this turn's own orders.** `BUILD Tower` is silent, which is exactly the
  bead's "a newly-founded structure this turn's own orders create is not this case".
- **`PRODUCE` and `CAST`**, which stay `MonthLong`. Only BUILD gains a shape, and only because a
  check reads it.
- **Roads.** `Road N` is a structure like any other here; a finished road warns the same way, and
  nothing special is done for it.

## Validation

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye: load any turn, find a unit inside a finished structure (the turn-71 fixture has
`+ Soggy Saw MIll [1] : Timber Yard.` with no `needs`), order it `BUILD`, and check the warning reads
exactly `Soggy Saw Mill is already finished`. Order a second unit `BUILD HELP <first unit>` and check
the helper's wording. Order `BUILD Tower` and check both go quiet. Settings → Warnings shows a
**Building** group whose tick silences them.

## Known traps

- **`is_busy()` is a `matches!`, not a `match`.** Moving BUILD out of `Intent::MonthLong` without
  adding `Intent::Build { .. }` to `semantics.rs:346-360` compiles cleanly and silently turns every
  builder into a candidate spare teacher — the twenty-nine-findings regression its own comment
  describes. Write that test first, before touching `intents.rs`.
- **The other match site is exhaustive** (`semantics.rs:631-638`), so the compiler does catch that
  one. Do not conclude from it that every site is covered.
- **`needs: None` means finished** — and it is the common case, since most structures in a report are
  complete. Do not read `None` as "the parser did not say".
- **`BUILD COMPLETE` has no name.** Reading the first argument as a structure type without checking
  for the two keywords gives `founding: Some("COMPLETE")`, and the check then goes silent on exactly
  the order it exists for.
- **An unnamed structure prints a placeholder.** `Building` and `Ship` are the engine's words when
  the player has not named one, so the message appends the id in those cases only.
- **`codes::ALL` has its length in its type**, and the generated TypeScript copies its order: append,
  never insert, and regenerate.
- **Helpers can name a unit that is not in the hex** — or one that is forming this month and has no
  number yet. Both are silence, not a panic.

title: Warn when a STUDY order for quartermaster would exceed the faction's allowance
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`STUDY: Can't have another quartermaster.` - 1 occurrence in tests/fixtures/reports/
(docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A STUDY order for the quartermaster skill was
refused because the faction was already at its Quartermasters allowance.

## What the check would need
From the report: the `Faction Status:` block's `Quartermasters: used (max)` entry
(`FactionStatusEntry` in crates/core/src/report/header.rs). From the orders: STUDY orders for the
quartermaster skill this turn. Shares its data source with the Trade Regions check
(docs/order-checks/README.md); worth building alongside it if that lands first.

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). A unit already trained
as quartermaster restudying is not this case.

## Validation
A STUDY-quartermaster order that would exceed the faction's Quartermasters maximum warns. One within
the allowance stays silent.
design:
## Context

The engine says `STUDY: Can't have another quartermaster.` A faction may hold only so many, and the
report prints the count in its own header — `Quartermasters: 2 (2)` in the committed turn-82 fixture,
a faction already at its ceiling. A unit ordered to study quartermaster anyway spends the month and
is refused.

Everything needed is parsed: the allowance from `FactionStatus` (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:67-81`),
the skill from the ruleset, the unit's current skills from the report, and the STUDY order from
`orders::intents`.

**This check is a new shape, and that is the interesting part of the bead.** Every one of the
thirteen advisory checks today is *per hex*: `check_turn` (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:151`)
loops over regions and hands each check one `Hex`. An allowance is spent across the whole map — two
units in two different hexes each look fine and are one too many together — so this bead adds a
**faction-wide phase** after that loop. `ah-8om` (Trade Regions) needs exactly the same seam and says
so in its own description; whichever lands first builds it, and this plan assumes this one does.

It is a warning, never blocking, and silent whenever it cannot be sure — the module's accept-on-doubt
policy (`semantics.rs:14-17`).

Branch from `origin/main`; line numbers are that tree. **`ah-1uj` renames the Warnings tab's
`Teaching` group to `Studying/Teaching`** and this check joins it; if `ah-1uj` has not merged when
this is built, do the rename here and note it in the PR.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The check — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

**The code**, appended to both lists (`codes` at `:63-98`; `ALL`'s length is in its type, so
forgetting it will not compile):

```rust
    pub const TOO_MANY_QUARTERMASTERS: Code = Code("too-many-quartermasters");
```

**The faction-wide phase.** `check_turn` currently ends its region loop and returns
(`semantics.rs:160-181`). Add one call after the loop:

```rust
    // Everything above is about one hex. An allowance is spent across the whole map, so it is
    // counted once, after every hex has been read - and `validate_turn` sorts the whole list by
    // line afterwards, so these findings land beside the per-hex ones rather than after them.
    check_faction(report, &ordered, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);
```

`validate_turn` (`crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs`) already sorts every diagnostic by
`(line_start.is_none(), line_start)`, which is what makes appending here safe — do not re-sort inside
`check_turn`, whose per-hex sort deliberately works on a slice.

```rust
/// Checks the allowances the faction spends across the whole map rather than in one hex.
///
/// The report states each one as `used (maximum)` in its `Faction Status:` block, and those are the
/// faction's own figures rather than anything counted here: this only adds what the orders would
/// spend on top.
fn check_faction(
    report: &ParsedReport,
    ordered: &OrderedUnits,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
);
```

What it does for quartermasters:

1. `options.emits(codes::TOO_MANY_QUARTERMASTERS)` or return, as every check does.
2. `ruleset?` — without one there is no skill catalogue and no way to tell a quartermaster order from
   any other. Silent.
3. **Resolve the skill by name**: `ruleset.find_skill("quartermaster")`
   (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:609`, which matches a tag or a name, case-insensitively).
   `None` → silent. **The tag is `QUAM`. It is not `QUAR`, which is quarrying** — resolving by name
   rather than writing a tag literal is what stops that mistake, and it is worth a comment saying so.
4. **Find the allowance**: the `FactionStatusEntry` in `report.header.faction_status.entries`
   (`header.rs:56`, `:67-81`) whose `label` equals `"Quartermasters"` ignoring case. No such entry →
   silent: the block is key-agnostic by design (`header.rs:62-63` — "the label is whatever the
   ruleset printed"), so a game that names it otherwise is a game this check knows nothing about.
   Free places are `(entry.maximum - entry.used).max(0)`.
5. **Collect the candidates**: every **own** unit (`report.units().filter(|unit| unit.own)`,
   `report/mod.rs:51-55`) that
   - has a `STUDY` order whose skill resolves through `find_skill` to the same tag, taken from
     `ordered.get(&unit.unit_id)` (`semantics.rs:202`) as a `PlacedIntent` so the finding can sit on
     its line; and
   - does **not already hold** that skill — a unit with a `Skill` entry whose `tag` matches is
     already one of the `used`, and restudying adds nobody. This is the bead's own "must not do".
6. **Sort the candidates by line**, and warn on every one past the free places. Document order is
   what the player sees, and `PlacedIntent::line` is what gives it — iterating `OrderedUnits` instead
   would give unit-id order, which is lexicographic on strings and would mark an arbitrary subset.
7. The message, exactly:

   ```rust
   format!("your faction already has its {} quartermasters", entry.maximum)
   ```

   With no free places that reads `your faction already has its 2 quartermasters`. The number is the
   report's `maximum`, not a count of anything computed here.

The finding needs `region_id`, `unit_id` and the line, and `Ordered::finding` is not available in a
faction-wide pass (it belongs to a `Hex`). Build the `Finding` directly, taking `region_id` from
`ReportUnit::region_id` (`report/model.rs:128`) and the line and columns from the `PlacedIntent`
(`orders/intents.rs:84-92`) — the same fields `Ordered::finding` fills in, from the same places.

### The settings tab — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

One entry in the `Studying/Teaching` group (renamed by `ah-1uj`), after `Study with nothing to learn`:

```tsx
      {
        code: "too-many-quartermasters",
        title: "More quartermasters than allowed",
        description: "A unit ordered to study quartermaster when the faction already has all it may have."
      }
```

Both strings are the navigator's, drawn in the mockup's Q3 panel; do not reword them.

### The generated vocabulary

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` mirrors `codes::ALL` in order and is
generated. Regenerate, never hand-edit:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

## Increments

1. **The faction-wide seam exists.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s tests —
   `a_study_beyond_the_quartermaster_allowance_is_warned`, on a report whose header carries
   `Quartermasters: 2 (2)` and one own unit ordered `STUDY QUAM`, expecting one finding with code
   `too-many-quartermasters` and the message `your faction already has its 2 quartermasters`.
   GREEN: the code, `check_faction`, its call after the region loop, and steps 1-7.

2. **It counts only what it should.**
   RED: `a_unit_that_is_already_a_quartermaster_is_not_counted` (the unit holds `QUAM` already) and
   `quarrying_is_not_quartermaster` (a unit ordered `STUDY QUAR`, which must be silent — the trap
   this bead exists to avoid shipping).
   GREEN: the two filters.

3. **The free places are respected, in document order.**
   RED: `only_the_orders_past_the_allowance_are_warned` — `Quartermasters: 1 (2)`, so one place free,
   three units ordered to study; expecting two findings, on the second and third by **line**, not the
   first.
   GREEN: the sort and the skip.

4. **Silence where it cannot be sure.**
   RED: `without_a_ruleset_nothing_is_said`, `without_a_quartermasters_line_nothing_is_said`,
   `an_allowance_with_room_is_silent`.
   GREEN: the `None` arms.

5. **The vocabulary and the tab.**
   RED: `pnpm run check:generated` fails.
   GREEN: regenerate, then add the settings entry.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s test module, `cargo test --workspace`.** Its local
`report(regions)` helper (`:1409`) builds a `ParsedReport` with a default header, which has an
**empty** `FactionStatus` — so these tests need a header. Either extend that helper with a variant
that takes entries, or build the report inline:

```rust
ParsedReport {
    header: ReportHeader {
        faction_status: FactionStatus {
            entries: vec![FactionStatusEntry { label: "Quartermasters".into(), used: 2, maximum: 2 }],
            unparsed: Vec::new(),
        },

    },
    regions,
    ..Default::default()
}
```

|---|---|

| `the_skill_may_be_named_or_tagged` | `STUDY QUAM` and `STUDY quartermaster` both warn |
| `quarrying_is_not_quartermaster` | `STUDY QUAR` → nothing. **The trap: `QUAR` is quarrying, `QUAM` is quartermaster** |
| `a_unit_that_is_already_a_quartermaster_is_not_counted` | a unit holding `QUAM 1` restudying → nothing |
| `only_the_orders_past_the_allowance_are_warned` | `1 (2)` and three studies → two findings, on the second and third by line |
| `an_allowance_with_room_is_silent` | `0 (2)` and one study → nothing |
| `without_a_quartermasters_line_nothing_is_said` | a header with no such entry → nothing |
| `without_a_ruleset_nothing_is_said` | `ruleset: None` → nothing |
| `a_foreign_unit_is_not_counted` | a `STUDY QUAM` in another faction's block → nothing; you cannot order them |
| `the_finding_sits_on_the_study_line` | the finding's `line` is the STUDY's, and its `region_id` the unit's hex |
| the disable table at `:~2570` | a row for `too-many-quartermasters` |

**The fixture is worth one test too**: `atlantis_hud_fixtures::G3_F42_T82` carries
`Quartermasters: 2 (2)`, a faction with no room at all — a real report proving the header is read as
the parser leaves it.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite: a string in a list and a warning in an existing
strip.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-16 over
`.cerebro/scratch/ah-oq3-quartermasters.html`.

**Q1 — the wording.** Chosen: **`your faction already has its 2 quartermasters`** — shortest of the
three, and the number is the report's own `maximum`. Rejected: `this would be quartermaster 3 of 2
your faction may have` (names both figures, but reads arithmetically); `your faction has its 2
quartermasters already, so this study will be refused` (spells out the consequence, longest).

**Q2 — which lines are marked when several orders compete.** Chosen: **only the ones past the
allowance**, in document order — the first study fits and the rest are marked, the same shape the
reused-FORM warning uses when it leaves the first use alone. Rejected: marking every competing order,
which claims nothing about which will win but puts three warnings where one place really is free.
The known cost of the choice: document order is this app's, not the engine's, so the *set* of
warnings is right while *which* order is left unmarked is a convention.

**Q3 — the toggle**, shown in the mockup and unobjected: title `More quartermasters than allowed`,
description `A unit ordered to study quartermaster when the faction already has all it may have.`, in
the `Studying/Teaching` group `ah-1uj` renames.

## Out of scope

- **The other allowances.** `Tax Regions`, `Trade Regions`, `Mages` and `Apprentices` are printed in
  the same block and are not checked here. `ah-8om` covers Trade Regions and will reuse this bead's
  `check_faction` seam.
- **Mage and apprentice limits**, which are the same shape again and are not filed.
- **Counting quartermasters the orders create in other ways.** Only `STUDY` is read; nothing else in
  the ruleset makes one.
- **Deciding which unit should get the place.** The warning names the problem; the player chooses.
- **A ruleset that calls the skill something else.** `find_skill("quartermaster")` answering `None`
  is silence, by accept-on-doubt.

## Validation

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye: load the `g3-f42-t82` fixture — its faction is at `Quartermasters: 2 (2)` — order one of
its own units `STUDY QUAM`, and check the warning appears in the orders panel with the exact wording,
and in the Problems chip's list against that unit's hex. Open Settings → Warnings and confirm the
entry sits under **Studying/Teaching** and that unticking it silences the warning.

## Known traps

- **`QUAR` is quarrying. `QUAM` is quartermaster.** Both are in the shipped ruleset, four letters
  apart, and the wrong one produces a check that looks right and fires on the wrong order. Resolve
  through `find_skill("quartermaster")` rather than writing a tag literal.
- **`check_turn` is per-hex and this check is not.** Do not try to answer a faction-wide allowance
  from inside the region loop; it cannot see the other hexes, and a partial count is worse than none.
- **The per-hex sort works on a slice** (`semantics.rs:176-180`), so appending faction findings after
  the loop does not disturb it. `validate_turn` sorts the whole list by line afterwards, which is
  what puts them in place.
- **`OrderedUnits` is a `BTreeMap` keyed by unit id**, so iterating it is lexicographic string order —
  `"10"` before `"9"`. Sort candidates by `PlacedIntent::line` for anything that means "first".
- **The faction status block is key-agnostic** (`header.rs:62-63`): NewOrigins prints `Regions` where
  standard Atlantis prints `Tax Regions`. Match the label case-insensitively and go silent when it is
  absent rather than assuming a position in the list.
- **`codes::ALL` has its length in its type** and the generated TypeScript copies its order: append,
  never insert, and regenerate.
- **Foreign units have orders in the document too** if the player pasted them; filter on
  `ReportUnit::own`, as every other check does.

title: Warn when a MOVE order would leave the unit too heavy to move
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`MOVE: Unit is overloaded and cannot move.` - 2 occurrences across 1 turn of 1 game in
tests/fixtures/reports/ (docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A single unit's MOVE order
was refused because what it carries exceeds its own capacity. Distinct from ah-j0e, which is about a
ship's capacity and crew for a fleet SAIL order, not a single unit's own load.

## What the check would need
From the report: the unit's `Weight:`/`Capacity:` line, already read for movement planning
(crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs, plan.rs, trace.rs). From the orders: the MOVE intent.

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). A unit whose carried
weight this turn is uncertain (pending GIVEs/TAKEs still to resolve) should not be judged until that
is settled, the same caution the item-shortfall check already applies.

## Validation
A MOVE order for a unit whose known carried weight exceeds its capacity warns. A MOVE order within
capacity, or for a unit whose weight this turn cannot be pinned down, stays silent.
design:
## Context

"A unit can walk provided that the carrying capacity of its people, horses and wagons is at least
as great as the weight of all its other items… **Otherwise the unit cannot issue a MOVE order.**"
(`tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html:1101-1110`). The engine throws the order out and
says so a week later, in the report's `Errors during turn:` section. Twice in the committed corpus,
both in `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t40.rep`:

```
:60  Builders (12054): MOVE: Unit is overloaded and cannot move.
     * Builders (12054), … 10 humans [HUMN], 34 stone [STON]. Weight: 1800. Capacity: 0/0/150/0.
:61  Builders (11619): MOVE: Unit is overloaded and cannot move.
     * Builders (11619), … 5 hill dwarves [HDWA], 11 stone [STON]. Weight: 600. Capacity: 0/0/75/0.
```

Both are answered by the report's own two numbers — 1800 against 150, 600 against 75 — with no
ruleset arithmetic at all.

**Most of this is already built.** The report prints `Weight:` and `Capacity: fly/ride/walk/swim`
on every own unit; `crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs` reads them (`parse_capacities` `:40`,
`mobility` `:66`, `Mobility::Overloaded` `:30`); and the **route planner already refuses an
overloaded unit** — `RouteProblem::Overloaded` (`movement/plan.rs:50`, raised at `:147`), mirrored
into TypeScript (`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:143-152`) and shown in red by
`PlannerPanel.tsx:85-108` as *"The unit is carrying more than it can move with, so the game will not
give it a MOVE order at all."*

**The gap is the hand-written `MOVE`.** Pick a destination on the map and the planner refuses;
type `MOVE S S` into the orders yourself and nothing says a word. The order trace deliberately
declines to judge (`movement/trace.rs:6-7`, *"Legality is the order validator's business, not this
module's"*) — and this bead is that business.

**Why it weighs the unit as it will be, not as the report printed it.** Look at what the player did
after being refused: in the following turn 11619 gave the stone away **and moved in the same
month**, and both worked — `t41.rep:131` *"Gives 11 stone [STON] to Taxers (11992)"*, `t41.rep:264`
*"Walks from mountain (38,4) in Femont to mountain (38,6) in Femont"*. It works because `GIVE` is
phase 4 and movement is phase 9 (`neworigins-rules.html:7775` against `:7843`). **Dropping the
ballast and walking is the standard fix for this exact mistake**, so a check reading the printed
weight would nag precisely the player who is fixing it. The navigator chose to price this month's
transfers in, which is the same decision taken for `ah-eet` on the same rules.

**`ah-eet` has landed** (PR #348, merged 2026-08-17) and this bead reuses its weight function
rather than copying it. Read `ah-eet`'s plan before starting — every line number below is against
`origin/main` at `5a33e77`, which includes it.

**Risk sizing, measured rather than guessed.** Across all 25 committed fixtures there are 76
depth-0 `MOVE`/`ADVANCE` orders and **not one** is issued by a unit the report shows overloaded. So
this check fires zero times on committed data either way; the transfer-pricing is about being right
next turn, not about a fixture that is red today.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs` — one new function

`mobility()` answers "how does this unit travel", using the weight the report printed. This check
needs the same capacities against a *different* weight, and needs the number itself for the
message. Add, after `mobility`:

```rust
/// The heaviest load this unit could move at all: the best of the flying, riding and walking
/// allowances the server printed for it, whichever the game would end up choosing.
///
/// `mobility` asks which mode a unit uses and answers from the weight the report printed. An order
/// check has to ask a narrower question - is *this* load, after a month of orders, more than
/// anything the unit can manage - and a unit is overloaded exactly when its load beats all three,
/// which is to say the best of them. Swimming is left out for the reason `mobility` leaves it out.
///
/// `None` when the report did not state the capacities, which is every foreign unit.
#[must_use]
pub fn best_allowance(unit: &ReportUnit) -> Option<i64> {
    let capacity = unit.capacity.as_deref().and_then(parse_capacities)?;
    Some(capacity.fly.max(capacity.ride).max(capacity.walk))
}
```

`mobility` is **not** changed and keeps its callers. `ReportUnit.capacity` is `Option<String>`
holding the raw `"0/0/150/0"` (`report/model.rs:157`), parsed only here and in `mobility`.

Tests in `mode.rs`'s own module: `0/0/150/0` → `Some(150)`; `0/70/85/0` → `Some(85)`;
`"not four numbers"` → `None`; `capacity: None` → `None`.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — rename `ah-eet`'s weight function

`ah-eet` adds `weight_at_sailing(ordered: &Ordered<'_>, ledger: &Ledger<'_>, ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) -> Option<i64>`. Nothing about it is
about sailing — it answers "what does this unit weigh once this month's orders have run", which is
the same question a walking unit asks. **Rename it `weight_after_orders`**, update its doc comment's
first line to

```rust
/// What one unit weighs once this month's orders have run: the weight the report gave it, plus
/// everything those orders move into or out of it that the ruleset can price.
```

and update its one existing call site, `semantics.rs:1344` inside `check_sailing`. The rest of the
doc comment, which explains why the ledger is read whole, is about the phase order and stays
exactly as it is.

The function is at `semantics.rs:1225`; the ledger it reads is built once per hex by `ledger_for`
(`:386`) and handed to the checks from `check_turn` (`:167`), both of which `ah-eet` put there.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the code

```rust
    pub const UNIT_OVERLOADED: Code = Code("unit-overloaded");
```

appended to `codes::ALL` (`:84`), which becomes `[Code; 13]`. **Count what is there when you
arrive**: `ah-djq` adds one to the same array and to the same *Orders* group, and may land first.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the check

After `check_sailing`:

```rust
/// Every unit of ours that orders a MOVE: is what it will be carrying when it steps off more than
/// it can move with at all? "A unit can walk provided that the carrying capacity of its people,
/// horses and wagons is at least as great as the weight of all its other items... Otherwise the
/// unit cannot issue a MOVE order" - the game throws the whole order out rather than moving the
/// unit part of the way.
///
/// The load is what the unit weighs after this month's transfers, not what the report printed,
/// because the server runs every GIVE, TAKE, BUY and SELL before it moves anybody: giving the
/// ballast away and walking off in the same month is the ordinary fix for being overloaded, and a
/// check reading the printed weight would warn about it.
///
/// The allowance is the report's own, unrepriced. A unit that gives away the horses it was riding
/// loses ride capacity as well as weight, and this does not follow that - the error runs towards
/// saying nothing rather than towards a warning that is wrong, which is the trade this module
/// makes everywhere.
///
/// A unit riding a fleet says `SAIL`, which is its own intent, so a passenger is passed over here
/// without needing to be excluded.
fn check_movement(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    ledger: &Ledger<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
) {
    if !options.emits(codes::UNIT_OVERLOADED) {
        return;
    }

    for ordered in &hex.units {
        let Some(placed) = ordered
            .intents
            .iter()
            .find(|placed| matches!(placed.intent, Intent::Move { .. }))
        else {
            continue;
        };

        let (Some(allowance), Some(weight)) = (
            best_allowance(ordered.unit),
            weight_after_orders(ordered, ledger, ruleset),
        ) else {
            continue;
        };

        if weight <= allowance {
            continue;
        }

        findings.push(ordered.finding(
            hex,
            codes::UNIT_OVERLOADED,
            format!(
                "this unit is overloaded: it carries {weight} and the most it can move with is \
                 {allowance}, so it will not move"
            ),
            Some(placed),
        ));
    }
}
```

Add `best_allowance` to the existing import at `semantics.rs:23`, which currently reads
`use crate::movement::mode::{cargo_capacity, fleet_label, parse_fleet_kind, sailing_requirement};`
— keep it alphabetical. Then in `check_turn`, after the `check_sailing` call at `:172`:

```rust
        check_movement(&hex, &ledger, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);
```

Three things that decide whether this is right:

- **`Intent::Move` is `MOVE` and `ADVANCE`, and never `SAIL`.** `read_order` matches `"SAIL"` first
  (`orders/intents.rs:251-254`) and the movement catch-all at `:262-264` takes only `MOVE` and
  `ADVANCE` (`MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS`, `movement/orders.rs:43`). `RIDE` is not an order in this
  ruleset at all — it appears only as a `SPOILS` argument (`rules:7253`, `grammar.rs:71-72`). So
  `Intent::Move` already means exactly "this unit is walking, riding or flying somewhere", and
  `ADVANCE` is correctly covered.
- **The first `MOVE`, not every one.** A unit gets one movement order a month (`rules:1496`), and
  `find` takes the first; a document with two would otherwise draw two identical findings.
- **`ordered.unit` is the `ReportUnit`**, which is what `best_allowance` takes; `ordered` itself is
  the `Ordered` wrapper that `weight_after_orders` takes. They are not interchangeable.

### `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts`

Regenerate, do not hand-edit:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx` and `.test.tsx`

The **existing** *Orders* group (`SettingsDialog.tsx:355`) gains:

```ts
      {
        code: "unit-overloaded",
        title: "Overloaded units",
        description: "A unit ordered to move carrying more than it can move with."
      }
```

and the hand-written `titles` list in the test (`:50-62`) gains `"Overloaded units"`. Nothing else:
the same test loops `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` for a toggle per code (`:68-71`) and for the
on-by-default assertion (`:78-84`), and already expects the `Orders` heading (`:44`).

### Nothing else

`PlannerPanel.tsx` is untouched — the planner's own refusal already exists and is a different
surface. `UnitPanel.tsx:76-77` already prints `Weight` and `Capacity` raw; leave it.

## Increments

changes and no existing test moves.

**2 — The rename.** `weight_at_sailing` → `weight_after_orders`, doc comment first line updated,
the one call site in `check_sailing` updated. No new test: the gate is that `ah-eet`'s whole suite
stays green, unchanged. A pure rename that needs a test edit is not a pure rename.

**3 — The check.** RED: the per-code fixture table (`:2569`) asserts `cases.len() == ALL.len()`, so
adding the constant breaks it first. Add the constant, the fixture row, and `check_movement`. Then
RED `an_overloaded_unit_ordered_to_move_is_warned_on_its_move_line` for the message.

**4 — The transfers.** RED: `giving_the_ballast_away_first_lets_the_unit_move`, which fails if the
check read `ordered.unit.weight` instead of `weight_after_orders`. Then the rest of the table;

**5 — The Warnings tab.** RED: `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` with the title added.
`pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`.

**6 — Gate and look once.** `pnpm run check:fast`, then *Validation*.

## The test plan

**The fixture shape.** No helper exists for a unit with a capacity; add one beside `aboard`
(`:2829`):

```rust
/// A unit carrying `weight` that the report says can move `allowance` on foot, as a real report
/// states it: `Weight: 600. Capacity: 0/0/75/0.`
fn carrying(id: &str, weight: i64, allowance: i64) -> ReportUnit {
    ReportUnit {
        weight: Some(weight),
        capacity: Some(format!("0/0/{allowance}/0")),
        ..unit(id)
    }
}
```

| `a_sail_is_not_a_move` | `carrying("11125", 1800, 150)` with `structure_id: Some("329")`, region `structures: vec![longship("329")]`; `unit 11125\nSAIL N\n` | `codes(...)` contains no `unit-overloaded`. `Intent::Sail` is its own intent, so a passenger is never asked to carry itself. Use `.contains` rather than `only` — the fleet checks may speak |
| `a_unit_that_does_not_move_is_not_judged` | `carrying("12054", 1800, 150)`; `unit 12054\nWORK\n` | `codes(...)` empty |

`mode.rs` tests: `best_allowance` over `0/0/150/0` → 150, `0/70/85/0` → 85, `10/0/0/0` → 10, a
capacity of `"nonsense"` → `None`, `capacity: None` → `None`.

**The per-code fixture table** (`:2649`) gains one row, or `cases.len() == ALL.len()` fails:

```rust
            (
                codes::UNIT_OVERLOADED,
                vec![region(vec![carrying("5", 1800, 150)])],
                "unit 5\nMOVE S\n",
            ),
```

**TypeScript:** `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` as edited.

**The whole-turn test.** `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs:91` asserts zero findings over
turn 71. **It stays green, and this has been checked rather than assumed**: across all 25 fixtures
there are 76 depth-0 `MOVE`/`ADVANCE` orders and none is issued by a unit whose report weight
exceeds the best of its three allowances. Run it at the end of increment 3 anyway — it is the
cheapest broad check available, and a red there means the allowance comparison is inverted.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 over two rounds. The chosen mockup is committed at
**`docs/ui/unit-overloaded.html`** (PR #353, merged) and carries the rejected options and the states. Read it before starting.

**1. The check weighs the unit as it will be when it moves**, pricing this month's `GIVE`, `TAKE`,
`BUY` and `SELL` into the load, exactly as `ah-eet` does for fleets and for the same reason: the
server runs all four before it moves anybody.
*Rejected:* comparing the report's two printed numbers, which is about twenty lines and has zero
false positives on every committed fixture today — but nags precisely the player who is fixing an
overload by dropping ballast, which is what the corpus shows them doing. Also rejected: staying
silent for any unit whose own orders move goods, which is never wrong but says nothing when a gift
is what *causes* the overload, and adds a second doubt rule beside the one `ah-eet` already has.

**2. Capacity is the report's own and is not repriced.** A unit that gives away the horses it was
riding loses ride capacity as well as weight. Mine, not the navigator's, and stated in the mockup:
the error runs towards saying nothing rather than towards a wrong warning, and the Rust code to
reprice a capacity does not exist (the formula is validated only in TypeScript test code,
`packages/ruleset/src/capacity.test.ts:24-35`).

**3. The message, verbatim:**

```
this unit is overloaded: it carries 1800 and the most it can move with is 150, so it will not move
```

Both numbers appear in the report, so the player can check them, and the shape matches the fleet
warning already shipping — `Longship [329] is overloaded: 190 aboard on a capacity of 150, so it
will not sail`.
*Rejected:* naming the mode — `can only carry 150 on foot` / `70 riding` — which tells the player
which of the report's four numbers is which, but costs three wordings and names the best mode
available rather than the one the player had in mind.
*Rejected in a second round:* ending `so the MOVE will be refused`, which the navigator first chose.
`ADVANCE` reads to the same `Intent::Move` and `PlacedIntent` (`orders/intents.rs:87-93`) carries no
command word, so that sentence would say `MOVE` on an `ADVANCE` line. `so it will not move` is true
of both and parallels the fleet warning exactly.

**4. The toggle** is `Overloaded units`, described
`A unit ordered to move carrying more than it can move with.`, in the **existing** *Orders* group,
**on by default**.

**5. Accepted, drawn in the mockup, and not to be re-opened:** a unit with no stated capacity is not
judged; a passenger on a sailing fleet is not judged; `ADVANCE` is judged like `MOVE`; a `MOVE`
consisting only of `IN`/`OUT` steps **is** judged, because the rules gate issuing a `MOVE` at all
(`:1108`) rather than each step, and no fixture settles it either way; exactly at the allowance
moves; and the route planner's own red notice is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- **Repricing capacity** after this month's transfers — decision 2.
- **The route planner.** `RouteProblem::Overloaded` and `PlannerPanel`'s notice already exist and
  are a different surface. This bead adds the same judgement to a `MOVE` the player typed.
- **The order trace**, which draws an overloaded unit's path with no mode and no months
  (`movement/trace.rs:64-66`) and declines legality by design.
- **Whether the route is passable at all** — terrain, movement points, oceans. Different checks.
- **A unit both aboard a fleet and carrying its own `MOVE`.** It is warned like any other unit with
  a `MOVE`; whether the server would run the two orders together is not modelled and no fixture
  shows it.
- **`PAUSE`/`P` steps**, which `parse_move` does not read (`movement/orders.rs:60-107`); a `MOVE`
  containing one yields no intent and so is not judged. Pre-existing, and a bead of its own if
  anybody wants it.
- **Wagons needing horses** (`rules:1105`), which the server has already folded into the printed
  capacity — nothing here recomputes it.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx
pnpm run check:fast
```

**Look once, against the report that produced the evidence.**

1. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev`, then load
   `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t40.rep` with its own orders template.
2. Find `Builders (11619)` in `mountain (38,4) in Femont` (report line 1403). The committed template
   leaves its block empty (template line 743), so **nothing is warned yet** — confirm that.
3. Add `MOVE S S` to that block. Expect on that line:
   `this unit is overloaded: it carries 600 and the most it can move with is 75, so it will not
   move`.
4. Add `GIVE 11992 11 STON` above the `MOVE`. **The warning should go** — that is the real turn-41
   fix, and the whole reason this bead prices transfers.
5. Change the gift to `GIVE 11992 10 STON`, leaving one stone. 600 − 500 = 100, still over 75, so
   the warning should come back reading `it carries 100 and the most it can move with is 75`.
6. Turn *Overloaded units* off in Settings → Warnings → Orders and confirm the line goes.

## Known traps

- **Reuse `ah-eet`'s weight function, renamed; never write a second one.** It is at
  `semantics.rs:1225` on `origin/main` and is the whole reason this check is right about a unit that
  drops its ballast before walking.
- **`ah-j0e` is open again at P0 with a build defect in `check_sailing`'s crew half** (sailing levels
  counted per unit rather than per man). It is somebody else's bead and touches only the crew sum;
  it does not overlap this one, which reads `mode::best_allowance` and `weight_after_orders`. If
  `check_sailing` looks different from `ah-eet`'s plan when you arrive, that is why.
- **`ALL`'s length is a type**, and `ah-djq` also adds a code to it and an entry to the same
  *Orders* group and also regenerates the vocabulary. If both are in flight expect a small conflict
  in three files; count what is actually there rather than trusting this plan's numbers.
- **`mobility()` is not the function to call.** It answers from the report's printed weight, which
  is the question this bead exists to stop asking. Use `best_allowance` against
  `weight_after_orders`.
- **A unit is overloaded when its load beats *all three* allowances**, so the comparison is against
  the maximum, not against the walk figure. `0/70/85/0` carrying 80 moves perfectly well.
- **`Intent::Move` covers `ADVANCE`**, and `PlacedIntent` carries no command word, which is why the
  message says "it will not move" rather than naming the order.
- **Swim is excluded from the allowance**, as it is from `mobility` (`mode.rs:62-64`): it decides
  whether water is passable, not how much can be carried.
- **`find` the first `MOVE`, not `filter`.** One movement order a month; two in a document would
  otherwise produce two identical findings on different lines.
- **A giver that cannot afford its gift produces a second finding** from `check_resources`, and
  `only(...)` panics on the count. Stock every giver.
