title: Warn when a BUY or SELL names something the hex's market does not trade
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`BUY: Can't buy that.` - 3 occurrences across 2 turns of 1 game in tests/fixtures/reports/
(docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A BUY order named an item the region's market does
not sell.

## What the check would need
From the report: the region's `for_sale` market listing (`ReportRegion.for_sale`,
`MarketItem` in crates/core/src/report/model.rs). From the orders: the BUY intent's item, resolved
the same way `orders::semantics::market`/`resolve_item` already resolve it.

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). An item name the check
cannot resolve at all (unknown to the ruleset, the hex's inventories and the market listing) must
stay silent rather than assume it is not for sale.

## Validation
A BUY naming an item absent from the region's for_sale listing warns. A BUY naming a listed item
stays silent.
design:
## Context

The engine says `BUY: Can't buy that.` — three times across two turns of one game in the committed
corpus — and `SELL: Can't sell that.` for the mirror mistake. The hex's `For Sale` and `Wanted` lists
are in the report, and the app already reads them: `buy` (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:555`)
prices a purchase against `hex.region.for_sale`, and when the item is not on that list it quietly
gives up — `ledger.doubted.insert(who)` and return, which silences that unit's shortfall checks and
says nothing to the player.

This bead turns that silence into a warning, for both orders.

**The care it needs is telling two silences apart.** `market()` (`semantics.rs:632`) answers `None`
in two quite different situations:

- the item was identified and this market does not trade it — **worth saying**;
- nothing could say what the item is: not the ruleset's catalogue, not the hex's inventories, not the
  market lines themselves — **not worth guessing at**. `resolve_item`'s own doc (`:653-657`) is
  explicit: *"Anything neither can identify is left unresolved rather than guessed at."*

Warning on the second would be the false positive the module exists to avoid (`semantics.rs:14-17`),
and a player who mistypes an item name would be told the hex does not sell a thing they never named.

Branch from `origin/main`; line numbers are that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Telling the two silences apart — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

`market()` currently collapses both cases into `None` via `?`. Split the answer:

```rust
/// What the hex's market says about an item an order names.
enum MarketAnswer<'a> {
    /// The market trades it, on this line.
    Offered(&'a MarketItem),
    /// The item was identified and this market does not trade it. Carries the canonical tag, so
    /// the message can name the item the way the catalogue does rather than the way it was typed.
    NotTraded(String),
    /// Nothing could say what item this is - not the catalogue, not the inventories in the hex,
    /// not the market lines. Saying "this hex does not sell it" would be inventing the "it".
    Unknown,
}

/// The market line for an item, matched the same way an order's item argument is, and saying which
/// kind of no it is when there is no line.
fn market_answer<'a>(
    lines: &'a [MarketItem],
    text: &str,
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    actor: &Ordered<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
) -> MarketAnswer<'a>;
```

It is `market()`'s existing body with the `?` unfolded: resolve through `resolve_item` (`:658`) or,
failing that, through the market lines themselves with `names_the_same_item` (`:689`) — a market line
is itself a naming of the item, as the current comment says. No tag at all → `Unknown`. A tag, then
`lines.iter().find(…)` → `Offered` or `NotTraded(tag)`.

`market()` stays, as a two-line wrapper:

```rust
fn market<'a>(…) -> Option<&'a MarketItem> {
    match market_answer(lines, text, hex, actor, ruleset) {
        MarketAnswer::Offered(line) => Some(line),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

so `buy` (`:565`) and `sell` (`:584`) keep their pricing behaviour **unchanged** — including the
`doubted` insert, which is still right: a purchase the market cannot price leaves the unit's sums
untrustworthy whether or not a warning is now raised about it.

### The check — a new `check_markets`

A per-hex check like its siblings, called from `check_turn`'s region loop (`:167-172`) after
`check_resources`:

```rust
        check_markets(&hex, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);
```

A separate pass rather than a hook inside `buy`/`sell`: those build the ledger and have no `findings`
to push to, and threading one through them would entangle pricing with reporting. The cost is one
extra market lookup per BUY/SELL order, which is a `find` over a list of at most a dozen lines.

For each own unit in the hex, for each `Intent::Buy`/`Intent::Sell` with its `PlacedIntent` (as
`check_teaching` walks `Intent::Teach`):

- `market_answer(&hex.region.for_sale, …)` for a buy, `&hex.region.wanted` for a sell;
- `Offered` or `Unknown` → nothing;
- `NotTraded(tag)` → one finding on that line.

### The code and the message

```rust
    pub const NOT_TRADED_HERE: Code = Code("not-traded-here");
```

appended to `codes` and to `ALL` (whose length is in its type).

The messages, exactly — the navigator's, and the only strings this bead adds:

| Case | Message |
|---|---|
| BUY, the market sells something | `this hex does not sell silk — its market has perfume, gems, hill dwarves and leaders` |
| SELL, the market wants something | `this hex does not want fur — its market wants grain, livestock, fish, spears, leather armor, spinning wheels, lassoes, jewelry and truffles` |
| BUY, `For Sale: none` | `this hex sells nothing at all` |
| SELL, `Wanted: none` | `this hex wants nothing at all` |

Built as:

- the item's own name from `item_name(&tag, hex, ruleset)` (`:884`) — "the catalogue's name where
  there is one, the tag otherwise";
- the list from the market lines' **own `name` field**, in the report's order, which is the report's
  spelling including its plurals (`hill dwarves`, not `hill dwarf`) — the same words the region panel
  shows;
- joined with `", "`, and `" and "` before the last, with no Oxford comma. A single-good market reads
  `its market has perfume` with no list punctuation at all;
- an em dash `—` with a space each side.

**The full list is deliberate, not an oversight.** The navigator was shown that Inholm's `Wanted`
list runs to nine goods and about 130 characters, and chose completeness over truncation: the
diagnostics strip wraps, and a truncated list sends the player to the region panel anyway.

### The settings tab — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

A **new group**, after `Resources`:

```tsx
  {
    heading: "Markets",
    entries: [
      {
        code: "not-traded-here",
        title: "Buying what is not sold",
        description: "A BUY or SELL order for something this hex's market does not trade."
      }
    ]
  },
```

Both strings are the navigator's, as drawn in the mockup's Q3 panel A. One wrinkle to leave alone
unless asked: the title says *Buying* while the check also covers selling, because the title was
chosen before the SELL half was agreed and the description already says "BUY or SELL". Do not
silently reword it; if it grates, it is a one-line question for the navigator, not an implementer's
call.

### The generated vocabulary

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` mirrors `codes::ALL`. Regenerate:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

## Increments

1. **The two silences are told apart.**
   RED: `semantics.rs` tests — `an_item_the_market_does_not_trade_is_named` and
   `an_item_nothing_can_identify_is_not_named`, asserting `market_answer` returns `NotTraded` and
   `Unknown` respectively. It does not compile: there is no such type.
   GREEN: `MarketAnswer`, `market_answer`, and `market()` reduced to a wrapper. **No behaviour
   changes yet** — run `cargo test --workspace` and confirm every existing pricing test still passes,
   which is the proof the refactor is a refactor.

2. **A BUY the market cannot fill warns.**
   RED: `a_purchase_the_hex_does_not_sell_warns` — a hex selling perfume and gems, a unit ordered
   `BUY 5 SILK`, expecting one `not-traded-here` finding reading
   `this hex does not sell silk — its market has perfume and gems`.
   GREEN: the code, `check_markets` and its call.

3. **SELL is the same mistake.**
   RED: `a_sale_the_hex_does_not_want_warns`, with the `wanted` list and the `does not want` wording.
   GREEN: the second arm.

4. **The empty market, and the silences.**
   RED: `a_hex_with_no_market_says_so` (`For Sale: none` → `this hex sells nothing at all`),
   `an_unidentifiable_item_stays_silent`, `an_item_the_market_does_trade_stays_silent`.
   GREEN: the branches.

5. **The vocabulary and the tab.**
   RED: `pnpm run check:generated` fails.
   GREEN: regenerate; add the `Markets` group.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s test module, `cargo test --workspace`.** The
existing helpers build regions and units; a market is a `Vec<MarketItem>` on the region, and
`a_purchase_the_hex_does_not_offer_is_not_priced_and_not_judged` (`:1853`) is the closest existing
test — it pins today's silence, and it must keep passing: the unit is still doubted, and now also
warned.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `an_item_the_market_does_not_trade_is_named` | `market_answer` → `NotTraded` |
| `an_item_nothing_can_identify_is_unknown` | `market_answer` → `Unknown` for `wodgets` |
| `a_purchase_the_hex_does_not_sell_warns` | the exact BUY message, including the em dash and the `and` before the last good |
| `a_sale_the_hex_does_not_want_warns` | the exact SELL message |
| `one_good_needs_no_list_punctuation` | a market of one → `its market has perfume` |
| `a_hex_with_no_market_says_so` | `this hex sells nothing at all` / `this hex wants nothing at all` |
| `an_unidentifiable_item_stays_silent` | `BUY 5 wodgets` → no finding, and the unit still doubted |
| `an_item_the_market_does_trade_stays_silent` | `BUY 5 PERF` in a hex selling perfume |
| `the_market_s_own_spelling_is_used` | a market line reading `hill dwarves` appears as `hill dwarves`, not the catalogue's singular |
| `a_foreign_unit_is_not_warned_about` | a BUY in another faction's block → nothing |
| `the_finding_sits_on_the_order_line` | line and `region_id` |
| `pricing_is_unchanged` | the existing shortfall tests still pass — the refactor's own proof |
| the disable table at `:~2570` | a row for `not-traded-here` |

**A fixture test is worth one case**: the turn-71 report's Inholm hex `(7,53)` sells exactly
`PERF, GEM, HDWA, LEAD` and wants nine goods, so `BUY 5 SILK` there produces the four-good list and
`SELL ALL FUR` the nine-good one — real market lines rather than hand-made ones.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 over
`.cerebro/scratch/ah-d8u-buy-market.html`, in two rounds.

**Q1 — the wording.** Chosen: **name what the market does have** —
`this hex does not sell silk — its market has perfume, gems, hill dwarves and leaders`. Rejected:
the plain `this hex does not sell silk`, and `silk is not for sale in this hex's market`. The
navigator was told the list can run to nine goods and about 130 characters and chose it anyway.

**Q2 — SELL as well as BUY.** Chosen: **both, one check, one toggle** — `this hex does not want fur —
its market wants …`. The lookup is shared, so the second half is a few lines rather than a bead.
Rejected: BUY only, as filed.

**Q3 — the Warnings tab.** Chosen: **a new `Markets` group**, one entry to begin with, as `Sailing`
and `Orders` each began. Rejected: `Resources` (which is about running out of your own goods, not
about the market lacking them) and the catch-all `Orders`.

**Q4 — long lists.** Chosen: **list them all**. Rejected: the first four and a count; dropping the
clause when the market is large, which would make the message change shape from hex to hex.

**Q5 — a hex with no market.** Chosen: **`this hex sells nothing at all`** and its twin
`this hex wants nothing at all`, replacing the sentence rather than appending an empty list. Rejected:
keeping the usual opening with the clause dropped.

## Out of scope

- **Whether the unit can afford it.** The overdrawn-silver check already answers that, and this one
  fires whether or not the purse would cover the purchase.
- **How much the market has.** `BUY 100 PERF` where only 63 are for sale is a different mistake and a
  different bead; this one is about the item, not the quantity.
- **Suggesting where to buy it instead.** `ah-1j5` is the bead that knows which hexes sell what.
- **A remembered market.** The check reads the hex the unit is standing in, in this turn's report,
  like every other semantic check.
- **`BUY ALL` / `SELL ALL` pricing**, which `buy` already declines to price (`:570-574`) — the
  warning is about the item and fires for those forms too.

## Validation

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye, with the turn-71 fixture and a unit in Inholm `(7,53)`:

- `BUY 5 SILK` warns `this hex does not sell silk — its market has perfume, gems, hill dwarves and leaders`.
- `SELL ALL FUR` warns `this hex does not want fur — its market wants …` with all nine goods.
- `BUY 5 PERF` says nothing.
- `BUY 5 wodgets` says nothing.
- A unit in a hex whose report line reads `For Sale: none` gets `this hex sells nothing at all`.
- Settings → Warnings shows a **Markets** group, and unticking it silences all of the above.

## Known traps

- **Two silences, one `None`.** This is the whole bead: `market()` cannot tell "not sold here" from
  "no idea what that is", and warning on the second is a false positive on a name the player may
  simply have mistyped. `MarketAnswer::Unknown` exists for exactly that, and a test is named for it.
- **The `doubted` insert must stay.** `Ledger::doubted` (`:368-373`) is what stops a unit's shortfall
  being computed from a sum with a hole in it. Adding a warning does not make the purchase priceable.
- **`market()`'s fallback through the market lines is load-bearing** — *"a market line is itself a
  naming of the item, so it can settle a name no catalogue does"*. Keep it in `market_answer`, or a
  hex selling something the ruleset has never heard of starts warning about its own goods.
- **Use the market line's `name`, not the catalogue's.** The report writes `hill dwarves`; the
  catalogue says `hill dwarf`. The player is reading the report's spelling in the region panel.
- **`codes::ALL` has its length in its type**, the generated TypeScript copies its order: append,
  never insert, and regenerate.
- **The settings title says "Buying" and the check covers selling too.** Deliberate, explained above;
  do not quietly rewrite the navigator's copy.

title: Warn when a unit above level 2 studies magic outside a building
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`Warning: Magic study rate outside of a building cut in half above level 2.` - 5 occurrences across
2 turns of 2 games in tests/fixtures/reports/ (docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A mage
above level 2 in a magic skill studied outside a building, halving the month's progress.

## What the check would need
From the report: the unit's current level in the skill it is STUDYing (skills above the level-2
threshold are magic skills; the ruleset's SkillEntry does not currently flag which skills are magic
- that flag may need adding), and whether the unit's hex has a building the unit is inside. From the
orders: the STUDY intent's skill.

## What it must not do
Never blocking - this message is already advisory in the engine's own output, so the check mirrors
that, not a rejection. Accept on doubt: if the ruleset cannot say whether a skill is magic, or the
report cannot say whether the unit is inside a building, stay silent.

## Validation
A level-3+ magic skill studied outside a building warns. The same study inside a building, or a
non-magic skill at any level, stays silent.

title: Warn when PRODUCE orders span more regions than the faction may trade in
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`PRODUCE: Faction can't produce in that many regions.` - 5 occurrences across 3 turns of 2 games in
tests/fixtures/reports/ (docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). The faction issued PRODUCE
orders in more distinct regions than its Trade Regions allowance permits, and the orders in the
excess regions were refused.

## What the check would need
From the report: the `Faction Status:` block's `Trade Regions: used (max)` entry
(`FactionStatusEntry` in crates/core/src/report/header.rs). From the orders: the distinct hexes
carrying a PRODUCE order for a tradeable good this turn.

Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). PRODUCE of a unit's own

against this limit; if it is unclear which PRODUCE orders count, do not warn.

PRODUCE orders spanning more regions than the report's Trade Regions maximum allows warns, naming
the excess. PRODUCE orders within the allowance stays silent.

title: The Tauri adapter is one table, held to the Rust commands, the sweep and the wasm exports by a local test
description: Third pass of ah-wxk. `createTauriAdapter` is built from one table, `TAURI_COMMANDS: { [method in keyof CoreAdapter]: { command, args } }`, exhaustive and arity-checked by the compiler against the typed `CoreAdapter` (ah-wxk.2). The tooling lockstep (scripts/tauriCommands.ts, ah-ga6) grows two checks that run on every machine: the table's argument key names equal the Rust command signatures' parameter names (read from main.rs wrappers and core-tauri after ah-wxk.1), and browser-core's `CoreWasmModule` members equal core-wasm's `#[wasm_bindgen]` exports. docs/adapter-api.md is rewritten to describe the boundary as it now is. After this pass a new command is: the Rust function, one table line, the web twin, and one sweep row — and a missing one fails `pnpm test`.
design:
## Context

Third and last pass under epic `ah-wxk`. **Blocked by `ah-wxk.1`** (core-tauri's 24 passthrough
commands carry `tauri::command` themselves and are registered by path; `scripts/tauriCommands.ts`'s
`registeredCommands` returns frontend names and `commandRenames` exists) **and by `ah-wxk.2`**
(`CoreAdapter` is the one typed declaration; `createTauriAdapter` still hand-writes 32
`invoke<T>("cmd", { snake_key: camelArg })` bodies). Read both plans first; every line number
below is from `origin/main` at `706ea51` (2026-08-16), before either merged — re-read the files as
they stand.

After this pass, adding a core command is: the Rust function (`ah-wxk.1`'s attribute on it), a
`CoreAdapter` method (`ah-wxk.2`), **one row** in `TAURI_COMMANDS`, the web adapter's method, and
one `SWEEP` row — and forgetting any of them fails on this machine: a missing or wrong-arity row is
a compile error, a wrong argument key fails `pnpm test`, a wasm export the browser type does not
name (or vice versa) fails `pnpm test`, and a sweep row that names an argument the command lacks
fails `pnpm test`. Bishop's cost (`ah-wxk`): "six declarations in core-client … and a SWEEP row",
and `24779d7`-class slips where a key was misspelled and only the Linux native job noticed.

What is true today (and still after `.1`/`.2` unless said):

- `createTauriAdapter` (`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:2026–2291`) is 32 hand-written bodies;
  the argument keys are the snake_case of the parameter names, written out by hand.
- `scripts/tauriCommands.ts` holds names in lockstep — `registeredCommands(mainRs)`,
  `invokedCommands(coreClientIndex)` (a regex over `invoke("…")` literals, `:40–46`),
  `lockstep(registered, swept)` — in `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts:105–126`. After `.1`,
  `commandRenames(coreTauriLibRs)` too. Nothing checks **argument names**, and nothing at all
  checks the **wasm** boundary: `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs` exports 17 `#[wasm_bindgen] pub fn`
  (`:68–454`) and `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:15–66` declares 17 `CoreWasmModule`
  members by hand; the only tie is `coreWasm.ts:23`'s cast.
- `tests/native/sweep.ts` (`SWEEP: SweepEntry[]`, `:51–252`; `SweepEntry { command; args: () => Record<string, unknown> }`)
  gives each command a payload; three entries deliberately omit an `Option` argument.
- `tsconfig.tooling.json` includes `scripts/**/*.ts` and `tests/native/sweep.ts`; the tooling suite
  runs under `vitest.tooling.config.ts` from `pnpm test`.

**Decision.** `TAURI_COMMANDS` — one row per `CoreAdapter` method: the command name and its argument
keys, in parameter order — typed by a mapped tuple over the method's own parameters, so the
compiler refuses a missing method, an extra one, or a row of the wrong arity. `createTauriAdapter`
is built from the table in a loop. The tooling lockstep gains: the table's keys equal the Rust
parameter names (read from `main.rs`'s eight wrappers minus `app`, and from core-tauri's 24 by
their `rename`), every `SWEEP` payload names only real parameters, and the wasm export list equals
the `CoreWasmModule` member list with matching arity. `invokedCommands` goes: the table *is* the
list of what the adapter invokes. `docs/adapter-api.md` is rewritten around the boundary as it now
is and how a command is added.

Verified 2026-08-16 under the workspace's `tsc` (TypeScript 5.9.3, `--strict`): the exact
`ArgKeys`/`CommandTable`/`as const satisfies` shape below compiles with a correct table, and a
row one key short, an extra key, and a missing method each produce one error (three errors from
three deliberate faults). Beast confirmed the same shape under strict the same day; see `ah-wxk`'s notes. Rejected: deriving the keys from parameter names
at runtime (`Function.prototype.toString` — no), or generating the table from Rust (`tauri-specta`
or a ts-rs-style export — a second generator and a build step for a 40-line table that a test
already holds to Rust; `ah-wxk` *Out of scope*).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts` — new

```ts
/**
 * The desktop transport, declared once.
 *
 * One row per `CoreAdapter` method: the Tauri command it invokes and the argument keys, in the
 * method's parameter order — snake_case, exactly as the `#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]`
 * function names its parameters (core-tauri's `command_*` for most, `main.rs`'s wrappers for the
 * eight games-root commands). The type holds every row to its method's arity, and
 * `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` holds every key to the Rust parameter names and every command to
 * `main.rs` and the native sweep, on every machine.
 */
import type { CoreAdapter } from "./index";

/** `invoke` from `@tauri-apps/api/core`, as the desktop shell hands it in. */
export type TauriInvoke = <T>(command: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<T>;

/** One string per parameter of `F`, as a tuple of the same length. */
type ArgKeys<F> = F extends (...args: infer A) => unknown ? { readonly [I in keyof A]: string } : never;

type CommandTable = {
  readonly [K in keyof CoreAdapter]: readonly [command: string, ...keys: ArgKeys<CoreAdapter[K]>];
};

export const TAURI_COMMANDS = {
  getEngineInfo: ["get_engine_info"],
  listGames: ["list_games"],
  createGame: ["create_game", "manifest"],
  openGame: ["open_game", "game_id", "opened_at"],
  deleteGame: ["delete_game", "game_id"],
  exportGame: ["export_game", "game_id", "exported_at"],
  importGame: ["import_game", "backup_json", "opened_at"],
  setGameRuleset: ["set_game_ruleset", "game_id", "ruleset_id"],
  setGameName: ["set_game_name", "game_id", "game_name"],
  parseReport: ["parse_report", "raw_report"],
  parseReportFull: ["parse_report_full", "raw_report"],
  parseReportClassified: ["parse_report_classified", "raw_report", "ruleset_json"],
  previewReportImport: ["preview_report_import", "database_path", "game_id", "confirmed_faction_id", "raw_report"],
  commitReportImport: ["commit_report_import", "database_path", "game_id", "confirmed_faction_id", "raw_report", "ruleset_json", "allow_overwrite", "imported_at"],
  validateOrders: ["validate_orders", "raw_orders", "ruleset_json", "raw_report", "disabled_codes"],
  orderCommands: ["order_commands"],
  planRoute: ["plan_route", "ruleset_json", "raw_report", "remembered_json", "unit_id", "destination"],
  traceMoveOrders: ["trace_move_orders", "ruleset_json", "raw_report", "remembered_json", "unit_id", "orders"],
  exportMap: ["export_map", "raw_report", "remembered_json", "request_json"],
  knownMap: ["known_map", "raw_report", "ruleset_json", "remembered_json"],
  previewOrders: ["preview_orders", "ruleset_json", "raw_report", "remembered_json", "orders_document"],
  loadRegionSightings: ["load_region_sightings", "database_path", "game_id", "faction_id"],
  mergeReport: ["merge_report", "database_path", "game_id", "viewer_faction_id", "viewer_turn_number", "raw_report", "ruleset_json", "merged_at"],
  loadMergedReports: ["load_merged_reports", "database_path", "game_id", "faction_id", "turn_number"],
  loadImportedTurn: ["load_imported_turn", "database_path", "game_id", "faction_id", "turn_number"],
  loadLatestImportedTurn: ["load_latest_imported_turn", "database_path", "game_id"],
  listImportedTurns: ["list_imported_turns", "database_path", "game_id"],
  loadOrderDraft: ["load_order_draft", "database_path", "game_id", "faction_id", "turn_number"],
  saveOrderDraft: ["save_order_draft", "database_path", "game_id", "faction_id", "turn_number", "order_text", "updated_at"],
  listHexNotes: ["list_hex_notes", "database_path", "game_id"],
  saveHexNote: ["save_hex_note", "database_path", "note"],
  deleteHexNote: ["delete_hex_note", "database_path", "game_id", "note_id"]
} as const satisfies CommandTable;

/**
 * Every `CoreAdapter` method invokes its row: the command, with the arguments keyed by the row.
 * Whatever Tauri resolves is the answer — the types are what the core serializes (`ah-wxk.2`).
 */
export function createTauriAdapter(invoke: TauriInvoke): CoreAdapter {
  const adapter: Record<string, (...args: unknown[]) => Promise<unknown>> = {};
  for (const [method, [command, ...keys]] of Object.entries(TAURI_COMMANDS)) {
    adapter[method] = (...args) =>
      invoke(command, Object.fromEntries(keys.map((key, index) => [key, args[index]])));
  }
  return adapter as unknown as CoreAdapter;
}
```

**Check each row's keys against the body you are deleting** (`index.ts:2026–2291`) as you write it
— the old bodies are the source, and the tooling test below is what holds the rows to Rust
afterwards. `deleteHexNote` now resolves with Rust's `bool` under a `Promise<void>` type; callers
ignore the value (`ah-wxk.2` awaited and discarded it, this returns it — harmless, and the table
loop cannot special-case one method without becoming the thing it replaces).

The `import type { CoreAdapter } from "./index"` while `index.ts` re-exports this file is a
type-only cycle: erased at runtime, legal to `tsc`.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

- Delete `TauriInvoke` (`:1231`) and `createTauriAdapter` (`:2026–2291`).
- Add, next to the `builders`/generated re-exports:
  `export { createTauriAdapter, TAURI_COMMANDS, type TauriInvoke } from "./tauriCommands";`
- Nothing else. `apps/desktop/src/desktopCore.ts:30–37` imports `createTauriAdapter` and
  `TauriInvoke` from the package root and compiles unchanged.

### `packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.test.ts` — new

```ts

  it("builds an adapter with exactly the table's methods", …)        // Object.keys(createTauriAdapter(vi.fn())).sort() equals Object.keys(TAURI_COMMANDS).sort()
  it("invokes each row's command with its keys, in parameter order", …)
  // for each [method, [command, ...keys]] of Object.entries(TAURI_COMMANDS):
  //   const invoke = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue("answer"); const adapter = createTauriAdapter(invoke);
  //   const args = keys.map((_, i) => `arg${i}`);
  //   await expect(adapter[method](...args)).resolves.toBe("answer");
  //   expect(invoke).toHaveBeenCalledWith(command, Object.fromEntries(keys.map((k, i) => [k, `arg${i}`])));
  it("passes an explicit null through as null, never as undefined or a string", …)   // validateOrders(…, null): invoke sees { …, disabled_codes: null }
});
```

`adapter[method]` needs `(adapter as unknown as Record<string, (...args: unknown[]) => Promise<unknown>>)`
in the test; that cast is the test's, and it is the only one.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`

Delete every "asks tauri … with the argument names" test (`ah-wxk.2` kept them for exactly this
pass to replace: `:610, :808, :846, :884, :960, :1043, :1084, :1124, :1194, :1220` on `706ea51`;
read the file as it stands). Keep the `createCoreClient` describe and the `expectTypeOf` pins.
`:1220` "passes a null ruleset through unchanged" is now the third case above.

### `scripts/tauriCommands.ts`

Delete `invokedCommands` (and its three unit tests). Add:

```ts
/** Splits `text` on commas at nesting depth zero of `<>`, `()`, `[]` and `{}`; trims; drops empties. */
export function splitTopLevel(text: string): string[]

/**
 * The wire parameter names of every Tauri command, in order, keyed by frontend name.
 * From `main.rs`: each `#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")] fn name(params)`, minus an
 * `app: tauri::AppHandle` parameter (the shell's, not the frontend's). From core-tauri: each
 * `pub fn command_x(params)` that `commandRenames` maps, under its renamed name.
 * A name declared in both is a bug and throws.
 */
export function commandParameters(mainRs: string, coreTauriLibRs: string): Record<string, string[]>

/** `#[wasm_bindgen] pub fn name(params)` in core-wasm: name → parameter count. */
export function wasmExports(coreWasmLibRs: string): Record<string, number>

/** The members of `export type CoreWasmModule = { … };` in webCoreAdapter.ts: name → parameter count. */
export function wasmModuleMembers(webCoreAdapterTs: string): Record<string, number>
```

Regexes, all `/gu`, all reading a whole file's text:

- main.rs wrappers: `/#\[tauri::command\(rename_all = "snake_case"\)\]\s*(?:pub\s+)?fn\s+([a-z_]+)\s*\(([^)]*)\)/g`
  → name = `$1`; params = `splitTopLevel($2).map(p => p.split(":")[0].trim()).filter(p => p !== "app")`.
- core-tauri: for each `[fn, wire]` of `commandRenames(coreTauriLibRs)`: match
  `new RegExp(String.raw\`pub fn ${fn}\(([^)]*)\)\`, "u")` → params from `$1` the same way.
- core-wasm: `/#\[wasm_bindgen\]\s*pub fn ([a-z_]+)\s*\(([^)]*)\)/g` → count = `splitTopLevel($2).length`.
- `CoreWasmModule`: take the text between `export type CoreWasmModule = {` and the first `\n};`;
  members are `/^\s+([a-z_]+)\(([\s\S]*?)\):/gm` over it → count = `splitTopLevel($2).length`.
  (A member spanning lines has its parameters on their own lines; the lazy `[\s\S]*?` up to `):`
  is what makes that work — and it is why `):` and not `)` alone: a parameter type may itself
  contain `)` in a function type. Today none does; keep the rule anyway.)

Parameter types with a top-level comma do not occur on either side today (`Option<&str>`,
`Vec<String>`, `readonly string[] | null`, `StoredTurnSnapshot | null`); `splitTopLevel` exists so
that a `HashMap<K, V>` or a `Record<string, unknown>` tomorrow does not miscount.

### `scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`

Unit cases (small strings): `splitTopLevel("a: Option<&str>, b: HashMap<K, V>, c")` → three;
`commandParameters` reads a wrapper and drops `app`, reads a renamed core-tauri fn under its wire
name, throws on a name in both; `wasmExports` counts a two-parameter export; `wasmModuleMembers`
counts a member whose parameters span lines.

The live test (`:105–126`) becomes — keeping its two-way `lockstep(registered, swept)` and adding:

```ts
const table = Object.fromEntries(Object.values(TAURI_COMMANDS).map(([command, ...keys]) => [command, keys]));
const parameters = commandParameters(mainRs, coreTauriLibRs);
// Names: what main.rs registers, what the sweep drives and what the adapter invokes are one list.
expect(Object.keys(table).sort()).toEqual(registered.sort());
// Keys: every row's keys are the Rust parameter names, in order.
for (const [command, keys] of Object.entries(table)) {
  expect(keys, command).toEqual(parameters[command]);
}
// The sweep names only real parameters (it may omit an Option; it may not invent one).
for (const entry of SWEEP) {
  for (const key of Object.keys(entry.args())) {
    expect(parameters[entry.command], `${entry.command}.${key}`).toContain(key);
  }
}
// The wasm boundary: same exports, same arity, both ways.
expect(wasmModuleMembers(webCoreAdapterTs)).toEqual(wasmExports(coreWasmLibRs));
```

`TAURI_COMMANDS` is imported as `../packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands`; `SWEEP` as today
(`SWEEP[i].args()` for `create_game` writes `context.databasePath` — calling `args()` here is what
the native spec does too and has no side effect beyond that object). Read the four files with
`readFileSync(join(ROOT, …))` as the test already does for two.

### `tsconfig.tooling.json`

`include` gains `"packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts"`. Its `import type` of `./index` pulls
`index.ts` and `generated/*.ts` into the tooling typecheck program — that is fine (`types: ["node"]`
covers everything core-client needs; it is environment-free) and it is how `tests/native/sweep.ts`
already comes in.

### `docs/adapter-api.md`

Rewrite around what the document is now for. Keep the movement, map-export and (if present) known-map
sections that describe **argument semantics** (`:37–79`) — they are still true. Replace the head
(`:1–35`, "Issue #3 defines one canonical metadata contract…", the `EngineInfo` example, the two
"adapter surface" lists) and the "TypeScript abstraction" section (`:81–`) with:

- **The boundary in one paragraph**: 32 commands; on the desktop `#[tauri::command]` on core-tauri's
  `command_*` (eight wrapped in `main.rs` for the games root); on the web the 17 `#[wasm_bindgen]`
  exports of core-wasm plus the IndexedDB store; in TypeScript one typed `CoreAdapter`,
  `TAURI_COMMANDS`, `createWebCoreAdapter`, and `createCoreClient` for the three ergonomic
  signatures.
- **Adding a command** — a numbered list: (1) the Rust function in core-tauri with the attribute
  (or a `main.rs` wrapper if it needs the app handle), and the core-wasm export if the web needs it;
  (2) the `CoreAdapter` method; (3) the `TAURI_COMMANDS` row; (4) the `createWebCoreAdapter` method
  (and the `CoreWasmModule` member); (5) the `SWEEP` row. Then **what catches a missing step**:
  (2)/(3)/(4) — `pnpm run typecheck`; a wrong key, an unregistered command, a sweep row naming a
  bad key, a wasm export the browser type does not name — `pnpm test` (`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`);
  the wire itself — CI's `native` job.
- **Trust**: the adapters do not validate what the core serializes; `invoke<T>` and
  `coreWasm.ts`'s cast are the two trust points; `ah-164.2` generates the report types from Rust.

Nothing in `docs/adapter-api.md` is read by code; write it for the next person adding a command.

## Increments

1. **The table.** RED: `tauriCommands.test.ts` fails to resolve `./tauriCommands`. GREEN: the
   file above, the re-export, delete the old `createTauriAdapter`/`TauriInvoke` from `index.ts`
   and the replaced tests. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run typecheck` and `test`;
   `pnpm run typecheck` (the desktop app compiles against the root export). Then the proof of the
   type: temporarily drop `"note_id"` from `deleteHexNote`'s row and see `typecheck` fail on the
   tuple length; add a row `foo: ["foo"]` and see it fail on the excess key; revert both.
2. **The lockstep.** RED: the unit cases for `splitTopLevel`, `commandParameters`, `wasmExports`,
   `wasmModuleMembers` — functions missing. GREEN: the four functions; delete `invokedCommands`;
   the live test extended; `tsconfig.tooling.json`; `pnpm test:tooling`. Then the proof: rename a
   parameter in one core-tauri command (`raw_report` → `raw`) and see the live test name that
   command; revert.
3. **Docs.** `docs/adapter-api.md`; `pnpm run check:fast`.

## The test plan

- **core-client** (`tauriCommands.test.ts`): the three cases above; `index.test.ts` minus the
  replaced argument-name tests.
- **Tooling** (`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`): the unit cases; the live test — names three ways,
  keys against Rust, sweep keys real, wasm exports ↔ members with arity.
- **CI**: `native` (the sweep over real IPC) still proves the wire; `desktop-shell` compiles the
  attributes from `ah-wxk.1`. Nothing new in the browser suites.

## User-facing decisions

None.

## Out of scope

- Generating the table or the sweep from Rust; a Rust-side registry of commands.
- Argument **types** across the boundary (only names and counts are checked); the wire types are
  ts-rs's business (`ah-164.2`) where they are generated and hand-declared elsewhere.
- Any change to `tests/native/sweep.ts`'s entries or to `tests/native/binding.spec.ts`.
- The Rust files: this pass reads them and edits none.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run test
pnpm test:tooling
pnpm run check:fast
grep -c 'invoke<' packages/core-client/src/index.ts          # 0
grep -c 'invokedCommands' scripts/tauriCommands.ts             # 0
```

Plus the two temporary breakages in increments 1 and 2, each seen to fail and reverted.

## Known traps

- **`as const satisfies CommandTable`, in that order.** `satisfies` alone widens the tuples to
  `string[]` and the arity check is gone; `as const` alone checks nothing.
- **Row order in the table is free; key order in a row is not** — it is the parameter order, and
  the live test compares arrays, not sets.
- **`Object.entries` on the `as const` table** types values as a union of readonly tuples; the
  destructure `[command, ...keys]` needs no cast, but assigning into `adapter[method]` does — one
  cast, at the return, as written. Do not type `adapter` as `Partial<CoreAdapter>` to avoid it;
  that hides an assignment of the wrong shape.
- **`main.rs`'s wrappers carry `app` first**; drop by *name* (`app`), not by position, so a wrapper
  that takes it elsewhere is still read right.
- **`commandRenames`'s 200-character window** (`ah-wxk.1`) is what `commandParameters` relies on to
  find each core-tauri command; a command it misses shows up as a table row with no parameters, and
  the fix is the attribute's placement, not the regex.
- **`SWEEP[i].args()` for `create_game`** reads `context` — a module-level object in
  `tests/native/sweep.ts`; calling it in the tooling test is fine and already happens in the
  native spec. Do not `JSON.stringify` the payload; only its keys are read.
- **The `CoreWasmModule` block regex stops at the first `\n};`** — keep the type as one block with
  `};` on its own line, as it is today.
- **A `Record<string, unknown>`-typed parameter** anywhere in `CoreWasmModule` is why
  `splitTopLevel` exists; if the count test disagrees with what you see, check depth tracking, not
  the file.
acceptance_criteria: 1) packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts exports TAURI_COMMANDS (as const satisfies a mapped-tuple CommandTable over CoreAdapter) and createTauriAdapter built from it; index.ts re-exports both and TauriInvoke and has no invoke< left. 2) scripts/tauriCommands.ts has splitTopLevel, commandParameters, wasmExports, wasmModuleMembers; invokedCommands is gone; the live tooling test holds registered == swept == table commands, every row's keys == Rust parameter names in order, every SWEEP payload key a real parameter, and CoreWasmModule members == core-wasm exports with equal arity. 3) tsconfig.tooling.json includes the table module. 4) docs/adapter-api.md rewritten with 'Adding a command' and what catches each missing step. 5) The two temporary breakages (short row / renamed Rust parameter) were seen to fail; pnpm run check:fast green.

title: The core adapter is typed once; the client derives from it and the per-method normalizers go
description: Second pass of ah-wxk. `CoreAdapter` in packages/core-client/src/index.ts becomes the one typed declaration of the boundary (every method returns `Promise<T>` of the real type, using the ts-rs generated types from ah-164.2 where they exist); `CoreClient` is derived from it (identical except the three ergonomic methods exportMap/knownMap/validateOrders), `createCoreClient` shrinks to those three conversions, and the 23 `normalize*` functions and 23 `*WireShape` types are deleted — the Tauri wire is Rust's own serde output and the web adapter is our own code, so both are typed at compile time instead of re-validated per method. `createWebCoreAdapter` (browser-core) is typed against the new `CoreAdapter`, which makes the ah-6l2 null-vs-undefined class a compile error rather than a per-method guard. Blocked by ah-164.2 (it deletes the report family's normalizers first; this pass deletes the rest).
design:
## Context

Second of three passes under epic `ah-wxk` (a new core command is declared once per side, and a
missing layer fails a local check). **Blocked by `ah-164.2`**, which re-exports the report model
from ts-rs–generated files and deletes the report family's `normalize*`/`*WireShape` in
`packages/core-client/src/index.ts`, casting at their call sites ("the normalizers were validating
our own output"). This pass does the same for everything else at the boundary and makes the
adapter the one typed declaration. Independent of `ah-wxk.1` (Rust only); `ah-wxk.3` builds on
this pass and keys its table on the `CoreAdapter` this pass leaves — its method names and
parameter lists are a promise to it. **Read `index.ts` as it stands after `ah-164.2` merged;** the
line numbers below are from `origin/main` at `706ea51` (2026-08-16), before it.

What is true today:

- `CoreAdapter` (`index.ts:861–971`, 32 methods) is untyped — every method returns
  `Promise<unknown> | unknown` — and `CoreClient` (`:973–1229`, the same 32 names, typed) is a
  second hand-written copy of the same list. `createCoreClient` (`:1747–2024`) maps one to the
  other method by method through **23 `normalize*` functions** (`:1233–1745`) and **23
  `*WireShape` types** (`:666–859`) that accept both `camelCase` and `snake_case`, coerce
  `undefined` to `null` (seven sites, all commented as `ah-6l2` fallout), turn SQLite `0/1` into a
  boolean for `HexNoteRecord.onMap`, and throw on shapes they do not recognise.
- None of that tolerance has a live producer any more: core-tauri's DTOs are `camelCase`
  (`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:22–117`, every one `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, `on_map: bool`);
  the tolerant-parse family became camelCase in `ah-164.1`; core-wasm serializes with
  `serialize_missing_as_null(true)` (`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:25–32`); and the web store is
  our own TypeScript. The Tauri wire is Rust's own serde output; the web adapter is code we wrote.
  What the normalizers guard against is a shape neither side can produce.
- The three places `CoreClient` genuinely differs from `CoreAdapter`: `validateOrders` (client
  takes `options?: OrderCheckOptions`, adapter takes `disabledCodes`, defaulted to
  `["hex-unguarded"]` at `:1831` — a copy of Rust's `OrderCheckOptions::default()`), `exportMap`
  (client takes `request: MapExportRequest`, stringified at `:1956`), `knownMap` (client takes
  `remembered: RememberedRegion[]`, stringified at `:1969`).
- `createWebCoreAdapter` (`packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:174–891`) implements
  `CoreAdapter`; its eleven wasm-routed methods return the wasm value **synchronously** and untyped
  (`CoreWasmModule`, `:15–66`, is all `unknown`), and it casts the two prepared shapes itself
  (`:187 as PreparedImport`, `:285 as PreparedMerge`).
- `createTauriAdapter` (`:2026–2291`) is `invoke<XWireShape>(…)` per method — `ah-wxk.3` replaces
  it with a table; here it only changes its type parameters.

**Decision.** `CoreAdapter` becomes the one typed declaration of the boundary: 32 methods, each
returning `Promise<T>` of the type `CoreClient` returns today, parameters exactly as the adapter
takes them today (the wire-shaped ones: `requestJson: string`, `rememberedJson: string`,
`disabledCodes`). `CoreClient` is **derived** from it — `Omit<CoreAdapter, three> & { the three
ergonomic signatures }` — and `createCoreClient(adapter)` becomes a spread plus those three
conversions. Every `normalize*`, `optional*` and `*WireShape` goes; the tauri adapter's
`invoke<T>` names the real type; the web adapter is typed against the new `CoreAdapter`, its
wasm-routed methods become `async`, and `CoreWasmModule` carries the real return types so the one
"trust the wire" cast stays where it already is (`coreWasm.ts:23`, `core as unknown as CoreWasmModule`),
mirroring `invoke<T>` on the desktop. The `["hex-unguarded"]` default leaves TypeScript: the
client passes `options.disabledCodes ?? null` and Rust's `OrderCheckOptions::default()` is the
only default (both entry points already take `Option<Vec<String>>`: `main.rs:406–431` today and
core-tauri after `ah-wxk.1`; `validate_orders_state` at `core-wasm/src/lib.rs:414`).

Why the adapter is the base and not the client: it mirrors the Rust commands one to one — same
names, same positional wire arguments — which is what `ah-wxk.3`'s `TAURI_COMMANDS` table is keyed
and arity-checked against. The client is the ergonomic layer over it, and there are exactly three
ergonomics. Rejected: keeping a validation layer for "defensive" reasons — `ah-164.2` already
decided the same question for the report family, and a guard that can only ever pass is a copy of
the type in another syntax, which is the cost Bishop measured (`f917be8`: two fields, +140 lines
of core-client). Also rejected: `Promise<T> | T` on the adapter to spare the web adapter its
`async` keywords — it would leak into `CoreClient` through the derivation, and every caller
awaits anyway.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

**`CoreAdapter`** (`:861`): the same 32 methods, same parameter lists (names, order, types), each
return typed. The mapping is the current `CoreClient`'s return type for the same name, with the
three exceptions keeping the adapter's parameters. Write it in full; this is the declaration
everything else derives from:

```ts
/**
 * The core, as one platform transport implements it — the desktop over Tauri IPC
 * (`createTauriAdapter`), the browser over WebAssembly and IndexedDB (`createWebCoreAdapter` in
 * `@atlantis/browser-core`). One method per Rust command, positional arguments in the command's
 * order and wire form (JSON strings stay strings here; `createCoreClient` is where an object is
 * accepted instead). Returns are the types the core serializes; nothing re-validates them.
 */
export interface CoreAdapter {
  getEngineInfo(): Promise<EngineInfo>;
  listGames(): Promise<GameManifest[]>;
  createGame(manifest: GameManifest): Promise<OpenedGame>;
  openGame(gameId: string, openedAt: string): Promise<OpenedGame>;
  deleteGame(gameId: string): Promise<void>;
  exportGame(gameId: string, exportedAt: string): Promise<string>;
  importGame(backupJson: string, openedAt: string): Promise<OpenedGame>;
  setGameRuleset(gameId: string, rulesetId: string): Promise<GameManifest>;
  setGameName(gameId: string, gameName: string): Promise<GameManifest>;
  parseReport(rawReport: string): Promise<ReportParseResult>;
  parseReportFull(rawReport: string): Promise<ParsedReport>;
  parseReportClassified(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string): Promise<ParsedReport>;
  previewReportImport(databasePath: string, gameId: string, confirmedFactionId: string, rawReport: string): Promise<ReportImportPreview>;
  commitReportImport(databasePath: string, gameId: string, confirmedFactionId: string, rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, allowOverwrite: boolean, importedAt: string): Promise<ImportedTurnPreview>;
  validateOrders(rawOrders: string, rulesetJson: string | null, rawReport: string | null, disabledCodes: readonly string[] | null): Promise<OrderValidationResult>;
  orderCommands(): Promise<string[]>;
  planRoute(rulesetJson: string, rawReport: string, rememberedJson: string, unitId: string, destination: string): Promise<RoutePlanResponse>;
  traceMoveOrders(rulesetJson: string, rawReport: string, rememberedJson: string, unitId: string, orders: string): Promise<MoveOrderTraceResponse>;
  exportMap(rawReport: string, rememberedJson: string, requestJson: string): Promise<string>;
  knownMap(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, rememberedJson: string): Promise<KnownMap>;
  previewOrders(rulesetJson: string, rawReport: string, rememberedJson: string, ordersDocument: string): Promise<OrdersPreviewResponse>;
  loadRegionSightings(databasePath: string, gameId: string, factionId: string): Promise<RememberedRegion[]>;
  mergeReport(databasePath: string, gameId: string, viewerFactionId: string, viewerTurnNumber: number, rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, mergedAt: string): Promise<ReportMergeResult>;
  loadMergedReports(databasePath: string, gameId: string, factionId: string, turnNumber: number): Promise<MergedReportRecord[]>;
  loadImportedTurn(databasePath: string, gameId: string, factionId: string, turnNumber: number): Promise<ImportedTurnRecord | null>;
  loadLatestImportedTurn(databasePath: string, gameId: string): Promise<ImportedTurnRecord | null>;
  listImportedTurns(databasePath: string, gameId: string): Promise<ImportedTurnSummary[]>;
  loadOrderDraft(databasePath: string, gameId: string, factionId: string, turnNumber: number): Promise<OrderDraftRecord | null>;
  saveOrderDraft(databasePath: string, gameId: string, factionId: string, turnNumber: number, orderText: string, updatedAt: string): Promise<OrderDraftRecord>;
  listHexNotes(databasePath: string, gameId: string): Promise<HexNoteRecord[]>;
  saveHexNote(databasePath: string, note: HexNoteRecord): Promise<HexNoteRecord>;
  deleteHexNote(databasePath: string, gameId: string, noteId: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

(Formatted by prettier/eslint as the file already is — one parameter per line where long; the
one-line form above is for reading.) The one change of parameter type: `validateOrders`'s
`disabledCodes` is `readonly string[] | null` — `null` means "the core's default".

**`CoreClient`** (`:973–1229`) — the interface is deleted and replaced by:

```ts
/**
 * `CoreAdapter` with three ergonomic signatures: an object where the wire takes JSON text, and
 * options where the wire takes a list of disabled codes. Everything else is the adapter as it is —
 * `createCoreClient` is the whole of the difference.
 */
export type CoreClient = Omit<CoreAdapter, "validateOrders" | "exportMap" | "knownMap"> & {
  validateOrders(
    rawOrders: string,
    rulesetJson: string | null,
    rawReport?: string | null,
    options?: OrderCheckOptions
  ): Promise<OrderValidationResult>;
  exportMap(rawReport: string, rememberedJson: string, request: MapExportRequest): Promise<string>;
  knownMap(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, remembered: RememberedRegion[]): Promise<KnownMap>;
};
```

Keep the doc comments that today sit on those three `CoreClient` methods (read `:1052–1130` and
move what is still true).

**`createCoreClient`** (`:1747–2024`) becomes:

```ts
export function createCoreClient(adapter: CoreAdapter): CoreClient {
  return {
    ...adapter,
    validateOrders(rawOrders, rulesetJson, rawReport = null, options = {}) {
      // `null` is "the core's default" (`OrderCheckOptions::default()`, `hex-unguarded` off), so the
      // default lives in Rust once instead of here as a copied literal.
      return adapter.validateOrders(rawOrders, rulesetJson, rawReport, options.disabledCodes ?? null);
    },
    exportMap(rawReport, rememberedJson, request) {
      return adapter.exportMap(rawReport, rememberedJson, JSON.stringify(request));
    },
    knownMap(rawReport, rulesetJson, remembered) {
      return adapter.knownMap(rawReport, rulesetJson, JSON.stringify(remembered));
    }
  };
}
```

The spread first, the three after — an override written before the spread is overwritten by it.
Both adapters are object literals, so the spread copies every method (a class-based adapter would
lose prototype methods to a spread; there is none, and the test below pins the key set).

**Delete**: every `type *WireShape` (`:666–859`, whatever `ah-164.2` left of them), every
`function normalize*` and `optionalNumber`/`optionalText` (`:1233–1745`, likewise). Nothing outside
`index.ts` imports them (`git grep WireShape packages apps` finds only this file).

**`createTauriAdapter`** (`:2026–2291`): change each `invoke<XWireShape>` to `invoke<X>` with the
type `CoreAdapter` now declares for that method (`invoke<GameManifest[]>("list_games")`, …).
`deleteGame` and `deleteHexNote` return `Promise<void>` while Rust returns `()`/`bool`: write them
`async deleteHexNote(...) { await invoke<boolean>("delete_hex_note", {...}); }` so the type is
honest rather than relying on `Promise<boolean>` being taken for `Promise<void>`. `validateOrders`
passes `disabled_codes: disabledCodes` as it does now — `null` crosses to Rust as `None`. Nothing
else in the function changes; `ah-wxk.3` replaces it.

**Doc block** at the top of the adapter section (wherever `:861`'s comment lives): the paragraph
on normalization, if any, goes; the `CoreAdapter` doc above is the replacement.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`

Read it after `ah-164.2`. Three groups:

- **Keep**: every test whose name starts "asks tauri … with the argument names" (`:610, :808, :846,
  :884, :960, :1043, :1084, :1124, :1194, :1220` and their like) — they pin `createTauriAdapter`'s
  argument keys and stay until `ah-wxk.3` replaces them with the table test. Where such a test
  also asserts on a normalized answer, keep only the argument assertion; the answer is now
  whatever the fake `invoke` resolved.
- **Delete**: every test of a normalizer's tolerance or refusal (`:13` "normalizes tauri responses
  into the client's contracts" — the 500-line one — `:690, :762, :775, :906, :932, :941, :981, :1002,
  :1015, :1152, :1245, :1253, :1286, :1305`, and any other whose fake adapter returns a shape
  the type no longer admits). Where one of them was the only test of a client behaviour that
  still exists (e.g. `:1220` "passes a null ruleset through unchanged"), keep that assertion.
- **Add**, in a new `describe("createCoreClient")`:
  - `"is the adapter's methods, plus nothing"`: `Object.keys(createCoreClient(fake)).sort()` equals
    `Object.keys(fake).sort()`, where `fake` is a `CoreAdapter` built with `vi.fn()` per method
    (write one `fakeAdapter(overrides: Partial<CoreAdapter> = {}): CoreAdapter` helper whose 32
    entries are `vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(…)` with a plausible typed value each — the compiler
    checks the helper is complete);
  - `"stringifies the map export request"`: `client.exportMap("raw", "[]", request)` → adapter
    called with `("raw", "[]", JSON.stringify(request))`;
  - `"stringifies the remembered regions for the known map"`: likewise;
  - `"passes disabled codes through, and null when no options are given"`: two calls, one with
    `{ disabledCodes: ["a"] }` → `["a"]`, one with none → `null`;
  - `"resolves with exactly what the adapter resolved"`: for `listGames` and `loadImportedTurn`
    (`toBe`, same reference — nothing is copied or normalized).

### `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`

- `CoreWasmModule` (`:15–66`): type each member's return with what the adapter reads it as:
  `get_engine_info(): EngineInfo`, `parse_report_state(): ReportParseResult`,
  `parse_report_full_state()`/`parse_report_classified_state(): ParsedReport`,
  `validate_orders_state(…, disabledCodes: readonly string[] | null): OrderValidationResult`,
  `order_commands_state(): string[]`, `plan_route_state(): RoutePlanResponse`,
  `trace_move_orders_state(): MoveOrderTraceResponse`, `export_map_state(): string`,
  `known_map_state(): KnownMap`, `preview_orders_state(): OrdersPreviewResponse`,
  `prepare_report_import_state(): PreparedImport`, `prepare_report_merge_state(): PreparedMerge`,
  `hydrate_parse_result_state(): ReportParseResult`, `decode_game_backup_state(): DecodedGameBackup`
  (the local type at `:116`, cast today at `:536`), `diff_imported_turn_state(existing:
  StoredTurnSnapshot | null, candidate: StoredTurnSnapshot): ImportedTurnDiff` (cast today at
  `:208`). No member keeps `unknown`. Import the core-client types from `@atlantis/core-client`.
  Delete the four casts (`:187`, `:208`, `:285`, `:536`).
- Every method that returns a wasm value synchronously (`getEngineInfo :224`, `parseReport :228`,
  `parseReportFull :232`, `parseReportClassified :358`, `planRoute :361`, `traceMoveOrders :373`,
  `exportMap :383`, `knownMap :388`, `previewOrders :392`, `validateOrders :401`,
  `orderCommands :411`) becomes `async` — the interface says `Promise<T>` and TypeScript will
  refuse the sync form. Same body otherwise.
- The store-backed methods now have their return types checked: fix what the compiler names.
  Expected: `Promise<X | null>` methods that could return `undefined` from a store read need
  `?? null` (that is the `ah-6l2` guard, now compile-enforced at the source), and `season` on an
  `ImportedTurnSummary` must be `string | null`. Do not widen a return type to make an error go
  away — read the store type and fix the value.

### `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts`

Any test that read a wasm-routed result without `await` now awaits it. Every existing `toBeNull()`
pin (`:432, :439, :474, :541, :558, :701, :706, :898, :1089`) stays and passes — they are the tests
of the behaviour the deleted client guards used to hide.

### `packages/browser-core/src/coreWasm.ts`

Unchanged; `:23`'s `core as unknown as CoreWasmModule` is now the one trust point on the web,
documented in a two-line comment there: the module's return types are what the core serializes,
checked nowhere at runtime, exactly like `invoke<T>` on the desktop.

### `apps/desktop/src/main.tsx:21`, `apps/web/src/main.tsx:38`

Unchanged — `createCoreClient(adapter)` keeps its name and shape.

### `docs/adapter-api.md`

`:81–95` "TypeScript abstraction": replace the "Contract normalization" bullets with two lines —
the adapter is typed against what the core serializes and nothing re-validates it; `createCoreClient`
adds the three ergonomic signatures and nothing else. `ah-wxk.3` rewrites the document; keep this
to that section.

## Increments

1. **The type is the test.** RED: in `index.test.ts`, at top level,
   `expectTypeOf<Awaited<ReturnType<CoreAdapter["listGames"]>>>().toEqualTypeOf<GameManifest[]>()`
   and the same for `loadImportedTurn` (`ImportedTurnRecord | null`) and `deleteHexNote` (`void`) —
   `import { expectTypeOf } from "vitest"`. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run typecheck`
   fails (today the type is `unknown`). GREEN: the new `CoreAdapter`, `CoreClient`, `createCoreClient`;
   the normalizers and WireShapes deleted; `createTauriAdapter`'s type parameters; then the test
   file's three groups. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run test` and `typecheck`.
2. **The web adapter.** `CoreWasmModule` typed, methods `async`, compile errors fixed at the value;
   `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core run typecheck` and `test`.
3. **The rest of the workspace.** `pnpm run typecheck` (apps and shared compile unchanged against
   the derived `CoreClient` — if a `Partial<CoreClient>` fake in `packages/shared` breaks, the
   derived type differs from the old interface somewhere: fix `CoreAdapter`, not the fake). Docs.
   `pnpm run check:fast`.

## The test plan

- **core-client** (`index.test.ts`): the three `expectTypeOf` pins (typecheck-time), the five
  `createCoreClient` cases, the kept argument-name tests for `createTauriAdapter`.
- **browser-core** (`webCoreAdapter.test.ts`, `parseReportFull.test.ts`, `turnDiff.fixtures.test.ts`,
  `gameBackup.wasm.test.ts`): unchanged assertions; the wasm-built ones need the wasm bundle
  (`pnpm --filter @atlantis/web build:wasm` first, as they do today).
- **shared, apps**: `pnpm run typecheck` is the test — every `Partial<CoreClient>` fake and every
  call site compiles against the derived type.
- Suites: `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite changes; the smoke and pwa suites in CI exercise
  the web adapter end to end and must stay green.

## User-facing decisions

None. Nothing a player sees changes; the desktop and the web send and receive the same payloads.

## Out of scope

- The table-driven `createTauriAdapter` and the argument-name lockstep — `ah-wxk.3`.
- The Rust side (`ah-wxk.1`); the core-tauri DTOs; anything in `crates/`.
- Runtime validation of any wire. Deliberately: see *Context*.
- The web store's own duplication of the SQLite rules — `ah-8m0`.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run test
pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core run typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core run test
pnpm run check:fast
grep -c "WireShape\|function normalize\|optionalNumber\|optionalText" packages/core-client/src/index.ts   # 0
grep -c "Promise<unknown>" packages/core-client/src/index.ts                                             # 0
grep -c "hex-unguarded" packages/core-client/src/index.ts                                               # 0 — the default lives in Rust
```

## Known traps

- **`expectTypeOf` is checked by `tsc`, not by `vitest run`.** The RED of increment 1 is
  `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client run typecheck`, and a passing `vitest run` proves nothing
  about it. Keep the three pins in the test file; they cost nothing at runtime.
- **Spread order.** `{ ...adapter, validateOrders() {…}, … }` — overrides after the spread. Reversed,
  the client silently keeps the adapter's wire signatures and `exportMap` sends `[object Object]`.
- **`disabledCodes: null` must reach both wires as absent.** Tauri: `null` → `None`. wasm-bindgen:
  `Option<Vec<String>>` treats `null` and `undefined` alike (`isLikeNone`). If the wasm test for
  `validateOrders` without options starts warning on `hex-unguarded`, the default did not apply —
  check that `validate_orders_state`'s parameter is `Option<Vec<String>>` (`core-wasm/src/lib.rs:414`
  today) and that the adapter passes `null`, not `[]`.
- **Do not widen to `unknown` to make the web adapter compile.** Every error the typed interface
  produces in `webCoreAdapter.ts` is a value that could have been wrong at runtime; fix the value
  (`?? null`, the store's declared type). Widening is the old normalizer in a new place.
- **The generated names from `ah-164.2`** — `ReportParseResult`, `ParsedReport`,
  `ReportHeaderInfo`, … — are what `CoreAdapter` names; if a name in the block above does not
  resolve, read `packages/core-client/src/generated/` and use the one there.
- **A `Partial<CoreClient>` fake elsewhere may build a sync method** (`getEngineInfo: () => info`).
  Against the derived type that is a compile error, and the fix is at the fake, not the type.
- **`vi.fn().mockResolvedValue` on the 32-method fake**: type each `mockResolvedValue` argument or
  the helper does not compile against `CoreAdapter`; use the `ah-164.3` builders
  (`aParsedReport()` etc.) where they exist for the report types, if `ah-164.3` has merged; a
  literal otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CoreAdapter in packages/core-client/src/index.ts is fully typed (no Promise<unknown>), CoreClient is derived from it (Omit + validateOrders/exportMap/knownMap), createCoreClient is a spread plus those three conversions and passes options.disabledCodes ?? null. 2) No normalize*/optional*/*WireShape remains in index.ts; the string "hex-unguarded" does not appear in it. 3) createWebCoreAdapter compiles against the typed CoreAdapter with CoreWasmModule members typed and no casts; every existing toBeNull pin in webCoreAdapter.test.ts still passes. 4) index.test.ts has the createCoreClient describe (5 cases) and the three expectTypeOf pins; the tauri argument-name tests are kept. 5) pnpm run check:fast green; apps/shared unchanged apart from typing.

title: The desktop's Tauri commands are declared once, in core-tauri, not wrapped again in the shell
description: First pass of ah-wxk. The 24 one-line `#[tauri::command]` wrappers in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs go: crates/core-tauri's `command_*` functions carry the `tauri::command` attribute themselves behind a new `tauri` cargo feature (enabled by the desktop shell's `desktop-runtime`), renamed on the wire to their bare names, and `generate_handler!` registers them by path. main.rs keeps a wrapper only for the eight game-lifecycle commands that need the app handle to resolve the games root. `validate_orders`'s default for absent disabled codes moves into core-tauri. `scripts/tauriCommands.ts` (ah-ga6) learns to read path-registered commands and checks every rename matches its function's name. No behaviour change: the desktop invokes the same 32 command names with the same arguments.
design:
## Context

First of three passes under epic `ah-wxk` (a new core command is declared once per side, and a
missing layer fails a local check). Independent of the other two — `ah-wxk.2` retypes the
TypeScript adapter and `ah-wxk.3` builds the Tauri adapter from a table and extends the lockstep;
neither touches the Rust files this pass touches, and `ah-wxk.3` reads the tooling functions this
pass leaves behind (see *Files to change* — the shape of `registeredCommands` is a promise to it).
Beast's pre-split analysis of the whole epic is in `ah-wxk`'s notes (`bd show ah-wxk --json | jq -r
'.[0].notes'`); it agrees with this plan and is background, not instructions.

What is true today (verified 2026-08-16, `origin/main` at `706ea51`):

- `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` declares **32** `pub fn command_*` (`:235`–`:998`), all plain Rust:
  `&str`/`Option<&str>`/`u32`/`bool`/`Vec<String>`/one DTO in, core types or `Result<_, String>` out.
  The crate has no `[features]` and no `cfg` gating.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` (564 lines) declares **32** `#[tauri::command(rename_all =
  "snake_case")]` wrappers, each under the same four-line
  `#[cfg(all(any(target_os = …), feature = "desktop-runtime"))]`, and registers them at `:520–557`

```ts
/** The frontend name of one `generate_handler!` entry: `create_game` → `create_game`,
 *  `atlantis_hud_core_tauri::command_parse_report` → `parse_report`. */
export function frontendName(entry: string): string {
  const ident = entry.slice(entry.lastIndexOf("::") + 2);
  return ident.startsWith("command_") ? ident.slice("command_".length) : ident;
}

/**
 * Every `#[tauri::command(… rename = "x")]` in core-tauri, mapped from the function it sits on
 * (`command_x`) to the wire name it declares (`x`). The attribute must sit within 200 characters
 * of its `pub fn` (only `#[must_use]` may come between), or it is not seen — and the live test
 * then fails on the missing entry, which is the right failure.
 */
export function commandRenames(coreTauriLibRs: string): Map<string, string> {
  const renames = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const match of coreTauriLibRs.matchAll(
    /tauri::command\([^)]*rename = "([a-z_]+)"[^)]*\)\)\][\s\S]{0,200}?pub fn (command_[a-z_]+)\(/gu
  )) {
    renames.set(match[2], match[1]);
  }
  return renames;
}
```

## Known traps

- **`cargo check --workspace` never sees the attribute.** The `tauri` feature is off there, so a
  typo in the `cfg_attr` or a `rename` string is invisible until `--features desktop-runtime` is
  built (locally on macOS, or CI's `desktop-shell` job). Run the feature build after every batch.
- **The attribute goes right above `pub fn`.** `commandRenames` allows 200 characters between the
  `)]` and `pub fn`, enough for `#[must_use]`, not for a doc block — a doc comment between them
  makes the live test report a missing rename, which is the test doing its job on your placement.
- **Sync only.** Do not make a command `async` while it takes `&str`/`Option<&str>`: Tauri refuses
  async commands with borrowed arguments (`wrapper.rs:176–234`).
- **`rename` and the ident must agree**, and the tooling test enforces it — a `rename = "parse"`
  on `command_parse_report` fails `pnpm test`.
- **The 8 stay local for a reason.** If a `games_root` command is registered by path it will not
  compile (its first argument is not a frontend argument); if you feel the pull to manage the root
  as state, that is `ah-wxk`'s *Out of scope*, not this bead.
- **`registeredCommands` now returns frontend names**, so anything that compared it to raw idents
  (`SWEEP` uses frontend names already) keeps working; `ah-wxk.3` depends on this shape.
- **Feature unification**: `tauri = { … default-features = false }` in core-tauri must not carry
  `wry` or any runtime feature; the shell's `tauri` entry does. Two entries with different
  features are one dependency to cargo.
- **The disk.** This machine ran out of space on 2026-08-16 mid-session; a `tauri` feature build
  adds a large `target/` tree. If `cargo check` dies with `No space left on device`, that is the
  machine, not the plan — say so and stop rather than retrying.

title: Which turn reopens and how notes and turns are listed is decided once, not per store
description: Child 3 of ah-8m0. The turn a game reopens on is ranked by a LEFT JOIN + ORDER BY in core-persistence and by a reduce() in webCoreAdapter.loadLatestImportedTurn, guaranteed equal only by comment ('matching the desktop's ORDER BY'); the order of hex notes (created_at DESC, id ASC) and of imported turns (turn ASC, faction ASC) is likewise an ORDER BY on one side and a sort() on the other. This child ranks the latest turn in the core (both stores hand over the candidates and write nothing), and orders lists once in core-client, the layer both adapters' results pass through. Plan in the design field.
design:
## Context

Child 3 of epic ah-8m0 (Bishop, weekly sweep 2026-08-15: "the store's rules are written twice, in
SQL and TypeScript, and diverge"). Planned by Beast on 2026-08-16. Blocked on ah-8m0.2 (planned,
not yet built when this was written — see the note at the end of this section).

Three read-side rules are written once per store and kept equal by comment:

1. **Which turn a game reopens on.** Desktop: the `LEFT JOIN order_drafts … ORDER BY
   MAX(t.updated_at, COALESCE(d.updated_at, '')) DESC, t.turn_number DESC LIMIT 1` in
   `load_latest_imported_turn` (`crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:894–939`). Web: the
   `touchedAt`/`reduce` in `webCoreAdapter.loadLatestImportedTurn`
   (`packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:758–795`), whose doc says "The ranking rule is the
   same on both". Neither is total: two turns tied on time and turn number reopen on whichever
   SQLite or `reduce` happened to see first.
2. **The order of a game's imported turns.** `ORDER BY turn_number ASC, faction_id ASC` in
   `list_imported_turns` (:966–969) vs the `.slice().sort(...)` in `webCoreAdapter.listImportedTurns`
   (:824–831).
3. **The order of a game's hex notes.** `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC` in `list_hex_notes`
   (:1507–1510) vs `sortHexNotes` in `webStore.ts:459` (applied by both `getHexNotes`
   implementations, :449–452 and :579–582) — **and a third copy**, `sortNotes` in
   `packages/shared/src/hexNotes.ts:73–80`, which the shell applies to the list it just received
   (`loadHexNotes`, :98) and to every local mutation in `hexNotesStore.ts`. The store's ordering of
   notes is therefore already redundant on both platforms; the shell's copy is the one that matters.

**After this bead:**

- The reopen ranking is one Rust function, `latest_turn`, in a new `crates/core/src/reopen.rs`.
  Both stores hand it every turn's `(faction, turn, updated_at)` and every draft's
  `(faction, turn, updated_at)` and write nothing; it names the turn, and the store then loads
  that record. The desktop's JOIN becomes two flat SELECTs + the core + one keyed load; the web's
  `reduce` becomes a wasm call + `find`. The rule is total (ties beyond turn number break on
  faction id), so the same store contents give the same answer every time.
- The two list orders live in **`@atlantis/core-client`**, the layer both adapters' results pass
  through: `sortImportedTurnSummaries` and `sortHexNotes`, exported, applied inside
  `createCoreClient().listImportedTurns` / `.listHexNotes`. The SQL `ORDER BY`s go, the web's two
  sorts go, and `shared/hexNotes.ts`'s `sortNotes` becomes a re-export of core-client's function —
  one implementation, called from the client and from the shell's local mutations.

**This plan cites line numbers of `main` at 706ea51, before ah-8m0.2 lands.** ah-8m0.2 edits other
functions in three of the same files (`webCoreAdapter.ts` `commitReportImport`, `webStore.ts`
`putRegionSightings`, `core-persistence` `upsert_*`/`insert_imported_turn`, `core-wasm`
`prepare_report_import_state`) and adds `crates/core/src/report/import.rs`; nothing it touches is
touched here, but the numbers below will have shifted — search by the quoted symbol, not the line.
Branch from the `main` that contains ah-8m0.2's merge.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/reopen.rs` — new; `pub mod reopen;` in `crates/core/src/lib.rs` (after `pub mod orders;` at :7)

`#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]` + `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`
on both structs.

```rust
//! Which turn a game reopens on.
//!
//! (Module doc: a game holds turns for one or more factions and a draft per turn; the one that
//! reopens is the one most recently *touched* - re-imported or edited - because editing orders is
//! the strongest signal of attention there is (the desktop's rule since migration 6). SQLite got
//! there with a LEFT JOIN and IndexedDB with a reduce, equal by comment; both stores now hand over
//! what they hold and this decides.)

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// One turn as a store lists it for ranking, or one draft: whose, which turn, and when it was
/// last written. `updated_at` is ISO-8601 from the caller's clock on both platforms; a browser
/// record written before turns carried a stamp has none, and ranks last rather than being dropped
/// (one unrankable turn must not become a game that reopens on nothing).
pub struct TurnTouch {
    pub faction_id: String,
    pub turn_number: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub updated_at: Option<String>,
}

/// The turn that reopens.
pub struct TurnRef {
    pub faction_id: String,
    pub turn_number: u32,
}

/// The turn a game reopens on, or `None` when it holds no imported turns.
///
/// Rank: the later of the turn's own `updated_at` and its draft's `updated_at` (an absent stamp is
/// `""`, so it loses to any real one), compared as strings - both are ISO-8601 in one format, which
/// is what makes that valid. Ties: higher `turn_number`, then lower `faction_id` (as text), so the
/// answer is total. A draft for a turn that was never imported counts for nothing.
#[must_use]
pub fn latest_turn(turns: &[TurnTouch], drafts: &[TurnTouch]) -> Option<TurnRef>
```

Body: `edited: HashMap<(&str, u32), &str>` from drafts (`updated_at.as_deref().unwrap_or("")`);
for each turn `touched = max(turn.updated_at.as_deref().unwrap_or(""), edited.get(&(faction, turn)).copied().unwrap_or(""))`;

## Known traps

- **`max_by` and the faction tie-break run opposite ways.** The winner is the *lower* faction id,
  so the comparator's last clause is `b.faction_id.cmp(&a.faction_id)`; a test that only checks
  time and turn ties would pass with it written the wrong way round.
  `a_tie_on_time_and_turn_goes_to_the_lower_faction_id` is what catches it.
- **`Iterator::max_by` returns the *last* maximum on full equality**, which cannot happen here
  (faction+turn is the store's key), but if a test hands in two identical touches, do not read
  anything into which one wins.
- **The two `updated_at`s must be compared as strings and only because both are ISO-8601.**
  Migration 6 rewrote SQLite's older `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` stamps (`core-persistence` test
  `timestamps_written_before_the_migration_are_rewritten_as_iso`); the core does no parsing. Do not
  add date parsing "to be safe" — a browser record without a stamp is `None`, not a bad string.
- **`serde_wasm_bindgen` and `Option` at the top level**: `to_js` sets `serialize_missing_as_null`,
  so `latest_turn`'s `None` arrives as `null`; core-client's `loadLatestImportedTurn` already treats
  `null` and `undefined` alike (ah-6l2). Nothing to add.
- **`format!` in SQL** for the two table names in `touches`: both literals are chosen inside the
  function, never from a caller — say so in a comment, since a reviewer will flag string-built SQL.
- **The persistence list tests are order-dependent today** and will start failing at random once
  the `ORDER BY` goes — SQLite's natural order happens to match on a fresh table but is not
  promised. Convert them to order-insensitive form *before* removing the clause (increment 3), so a
  later red is a real regression and not a shuffled row.

  the shells.
