    `aBattle().attacker` `toEqual({ name: "AA Tomb's Guards", id: "7280" })`; `aBattleUnit().faction` not null.
  - Completeness is not a runtime test: the `: ReportUnit` return annotation on a literal is what
    fails when the generated type grows, and `pnpm run typecheck` runs it. Do not add a "has these
    keys" assertion — it would be a second copy of the field list, which is the thing being removed.
- **Rust**, `crates/core/src/report/model.rs` test module: `a_default_unit_is_estimated_until_classified`
  asserts `ReportUnit::default().men_estimated` and `ReportUnit::default().men_by_race.is_empty()`;
  `a_default_region_has_the_nexus_origin` asserts `ReportRegion::default().coordinate == Coordinate { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }`
  and `.units.is_empty()` (pins that the derive is there and what it yields).
- **Every existing test** in `packages/shared`, `packages/core-client` and `crates/core` passes with
  its assertions unchanged — that is the whole acceptance for the migration.
- Suites: `pnpm run check:fast` (lint, typecheck, `pnpm -r run test`, cargo fmt/clippy). No browser
  suite is touched: nothing in `apps/`, `browser-core` or the smoke/pwa specs changes.

## User-facing decisions

None. Test code and one doc section; nothing a player sees changes.

## Out of scope

- Builders for types no test spells out (`ReportParseResult`, `TurnHeader`, `ImportedTurnRecord`,
  `OrdersTemplate`, `RegionExit`, `MarketItem`, …) and for two-to-five-field types
  (`FactionStatus`, `DeclaredAttitudes`, `Combatant`, `Casualty`, `StructureInfo`, `Coordinate`).
  Add one, under the naming rule, when a test would otherwise spell the whole type.
- `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:2555–2578` `report_region_json` — a raw JSON string of a
  stored `ReportRegion` blob, kept exhaustive on purpose to pin what old databases contain.
- The remaining hand-mapped DTOs in core-tauri/core-wasm and the non-report `normalize*` functions —
  `ah-wxk`.
- `Default` for the tolerant-parse family in `crates/core/src/lib.rs` (`ReportParseResult`,
  `TurnHeader`, …): no test builds them as literals; they come from `parse_report`.
- The Playwright suites under `tests/`, which drive the app on real `.rep` fixtures.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client exec vitest run src/builders.test.ts
pnpm run check:fast
# No complete literal survives (each hit must be inside a builder call / a wrapper's override, or a deliberate reset — read every line it prints):
grep -rn "structureId: null\|entertainment: null\|unclaimedSilver: null\|lineEnd:" packages/*/src --include='*.test.ts' --include='*.test.tsx' --include='congestedFixture.ts'
# expected: nothing, or only lines you can name as a deliberate override
```

The two dry runs, each reverted afterwards:

```bash
# TS: a new Rust field ripples to exactly one TypeScript file.
#   add `pub dummy: bool,` to ReportUnit in crates/core/src/report/model.rs. First, before making Rust compile:
cargo build -p atlantis-hud-core --all-targets 2>&1 | grep -E '^\s+--> ' | sort -u
#   expected: exactly three locations — the `impl Default for ReportUnit` in report/model.rs, report/unit.rs (~:132), orders/effects.rs (~:383);
#   nothing under a #[cfg(test)] module and nothing in crates/core/tests/. That is the Rust half of the proof.
#   Then add `dummy: false,` at those three sites so it compiles, and:
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core export_bindings      # rewrites packages/core-client/src/generated/ReportUnit.ts
pnpm run typecheck                                    # the ONLY TypeScript error is in packages/core-client/src/builders.ts (the return literal lacks `dummy`)
git checkout -- crates packages/core-client/src/generated
git status --porcelain                                # clean, apart from your own commits
```

## Known traps

- **Do not start until `packages/core-client/src/generated/` exists on `origin/main`.** The builders
  import from it, and the whole point is to type against the generated shapes. If it is missing,
  `ah-164.2` is not merged; stop and say so rather than typing against the hand-written types.
- **`Battle.assassination` is required in the generated type** (ts-rs keeps a `#[serde(default)]`
  field required, per `ah-164.2`'s plan). The two battle tests either already gained
  `assassination: false` from `ah-164.2` or fail typecheck before you touch them; the builder's
  default is `false`, so migrating them fixes it either way.
- **`builders.ts` must not `import type … from "./index"`.** `index.ts` re-exports `builders.ts`;
  a type-only import back would be erased at runtime and work, but it reads as a cycle and the next
  reader will "fix" it. `./generated/…` is the source of the types; import from there.
- **`ReportUnit::default()` is estimated (`men_estimated: true`).** A test literal that wrote
  `men_estimated: false` keeps that line under the deletion rule; a test that wrote `true` drops it.
  If a trimmed test starts failing on a `~` in a men count, that is a `false` that was deleted.
- **The deletion rule is per value, not per field.** `weight: Some(50)` stays; `weight: None`
  goes. `region_id: "1:1,1".to_string()` stays; `region_id: String::new()` would go. Do not
  "simplify" a kept value.
- **The compiler cannot see a changed default.** A migrated file whose test read the old helper's
  `"Borg"` in an expected string will fail at run time, not at typecheck; run each file's tests
  before moving on, and pass the value as an override — never change the assertion to match the
  builder.
- **`--max-warnings=0`**: a local `unit()`/`region()` left unused after migration fails lint, and
  so does an unused `import type { ReportUnit }` — remove both.
- **`pnpm run check:generated` (from `ah-164.2`) fails while the TS dry-run field is in.** Revert
  both `crates/` and `packages/core-client/src/generated/` before the final `check:fast`.
- **`git status` in the worktree after the dry runs must be clean apart from your commits** —
  ts-rs writes into the worktree's own `generated/` (its `.cargo/config.toml` is tracked); a dirty
  main checkout means the worktree predates that config.
acceptance_criteria: 1) packages/core-client exports aReportUnit, aReportRegion, aReportHeaderInfo, aParsedReport, aBattle, aBattleUnit, each (overrides: Partial<T> = {}) => T, pinned by builders.test.ts. 2) No test file (nor congestedFixture.ts) spells a complete literal of those six types; every file listed in the plan's Context is migrated and its assertions are unchanged. 3) crates/core report family derives Default (ReportUnit hand-written, men_estimated true); merge.rs, semantics.rs and mode.rs test helpers end in ..Default::default(). 4) Dry run: a throwaway field on Rust ReportUnit yields compile errors only at the Default impl and the two production literals, and after regeneration exactly one TypeScript error, in builders.ts. 5) docs/implementation-plan.md has the 'Report builders in tests' section. 6) pnpm run check:fast green.

title: TypeScript report types are generated from the Rust core instead of mirrored by hand
description: Second pass of ah-164. ts-rs derives on the report families in crates/core (ParsedReport and its tree, Battle, ReportParseResultWire and its tree, EngineInfo, OrderDiagnostic); cargo test writes packages/core-client/src/generated/*.ts; a staleness gate in check:fast and CI. The hand-written TS types and the report family's WireShape/normalize* code in core-client are deleted in favour of the generated declarations. Blocked by the casing pass: generation against mixed casing would bake the mixture in.
design:
## Context

Second of three passes under epic `ah-164`. **Blocked by `ah-164.1`**, which makes the tolerant-parse
family camelCase in core and introduces `atlantis_hud_core::ReportParseResultWire` (the flattened
result plus `meets_minimum_import_threshold`) as the one wire shape — read that plan first: this one
generates TypeScript from the Rust types *as ah-164.1 leaves them*, and every "today" reference
below to `crates/core/src/lib.rs` assumes its aliases and `rename_all` are in.

Today `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` declares the entire report model by hand —
`Coordinate` (`:109`) through `ParsedReport` (`:554`), plus the parse family (`EngineInfo :1`,
`ParseWarning :49` … `ReportParseResult :91`) and `OrderDiagnostic`/`OrderValidationResult`
(`:574–630`) — and nothing checks those declarations against the Rust structs they mirror. Bishop's
evidence: `ah-1is.1` (battles) and `ah-vp3.1` (faction status) each added a field in Rust and had to
add it again in `index.ts` (+62, +35 lines), and `ah-1is.1`'s own plan says "TypeScript cannot
catch it, because the mirror is hand-written… The field simply reads undefined". The web wire is
already `any` (`packages/browser-core/src/wasm/atlantis_core.d.ts`, generated and git-ignored) and
`parseReportFull` casts (`index.ts:1820`, "Returned as-is: it is descriptive data, not a contract
to normalize"), so the hand types are the *only* typing there is.

**Decision: `ts-rs` 12, as a dev-dependency of `atlantis-hud-core`, gated `#[cfg_attr(test, …)]`;
`cargo test` writes one `.ts` per type into `packages/core-client/src/generated/`; the committed
files are gated by a "nothing changed" check in `check:fast`, `check` and CI; `index.ts` re-exports
them under the names the shell already uses and the hand-written declarations go.** Verified against
the ts-rs 12.0.1 source (2026-08-16), because the implementer will not be able to:

- Export happens in tests ts-rs generates from `#[ts(export)]` (`ts-rs-macros/src/lib.rs:191–208`:
  a `#[test] fn export_bindings_<name>()` calling `Config::from_env()` then `T::export_all(&cfg)`).
  `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` therefore *is* the generator; nothing to wire in `scripts/`.
- The output directory is `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` (default `./bindings`) resolved against the **current
  directory** of the test process (`ts-rs/src/export/path.rs:8`), which cargo sets to the crate's
  manifest dir. Set it in `.cargo/config.toml` with `relative = true` so cargo resolves it against
  the directory holding the config file — the repository root, or the worktree's own root, since the
  file is tracked and the nearest one wins.
- `i64`/`u64` render as `bigint` unless `TS_RS_LARGE_INT=number` (`ts-rs/src/lib.rs:596, 621`);
  the report model is full of `i64` (`report/model.rs:34,43,46,82,118,132,153,157–160`) that cross
  as JSON numbers, so the env var is mandatory.
- serde attributes honoured: `rename`, `rename_all`, `default`, `flatten`, `skip`, `tag`… (`ts-rs/src/lib.rs:95`).
  `#[serde(default)]` alone keeps the field required (macros `attr/field.rs:185–187`: it only makes a
  field optional together with `skip_serializing(_if)`) — right for us, since Rust always
  serializes those fields. `#[serde(alias)]` (from ah-164.1) is *not* parsed and prints a stderr
  warning per use unless the `no-serde-warnings` feature is on (`macros/src/utils.rs:78`) — enable it.
- `#[serde(flatten)]` inlines the inner struct as an intersection (`macros/src/types/named.rs:39–59,
  119–127`: the inner's *dependencies* are pulled in, the inner itself is not exported unless it
  carries `#[ts(export)]`). So `ReportParseResultWire` renders as
  `{ meetsMinimumImportThreshold: boolean, } & { turnHeader: TurnHeader | null, … }` in one file.
- Rust `///` docs become JSDoc on the generated type and fields (`named.rs:151–157`).
- Each file starts `// This file was generated by [ts-rs](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/ts-rs). Do not edit this file manually.`
  and imports siblings as `import type { X } from "./X";` (`ts-rs/src/export.rs`).

`schemars`/JSON Schema and hand-rolled rendering (the ah-p1p pattern) were rejected: the first is a
second generator for the same facts, the second re-declares the schema in the renderer.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/Cargo.toml`

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
serde_json = "1.0"
atlantis-hud-fixtures = { path = "../fixtures" }
ts-rs = { version = "12", features = ["no-serde-warnings"] }
```

Dev-only: the derive is used under `cfg(test)` alone, so the wasm and desktop builds never see it.

### `.cargo/config.toml` — add, under the existing `[build]` table's comment block

```toml
# ts-rs (crates/core, ah-164.2) writes the TypeScript bindings during `cargo test`. `relative = true`
# makes cargo resolve the path against the directory holding this file — the repository root, or a
# worktree's own root, since the file is tracked and cargo takes the nearest one. Large integers cross
# as JSON numbers, so they are `number` in TypeScript, not `bigint`.
[env]
TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR = { value = "packages/core-client/src/generated", relative = true }
TS_RS_LARGE_INT = "number"
```

`scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` reads this file for `target-dir` only (`:34–51`); an extra table
does not disturb it. Do not touch `[build]`.

### `crates/core/src/**` — the derives

On every type below, add — as one `cfg_attr` so nothing exists outside test builds:

```rust
#[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))]
```

Roots and their trees (every type reachable from a root needs `derive(ts_rs::TS)`; only the ones
listed with `export` need `ts(export)`, but giving all of them `export` is harmless and keeps the
per-type files present for `index.ts` to re-export, so **put `ts(export)` on every type listed**):

- `crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:41 ParsedReport`; `report/header.rs` `ReportHeader :36`
  (**`ts(export, rename = "ReportHeaderInfo", export_to = "ReportHeaderInfo.ts")`** — the shell's
  name, `index.ts:426`), `FactionStatus :61`, `FactionStatusEntry :70`, `DeclaredAttitudes :79`,
  `AttitudeLevel :88`, `FactionRef :96`; `report/model.rs` `Coordinate :16`, `ItemAmount :33`,
  `MarketItem :42`, `Settlement :52` (**rename `SettlementInfo`**), `Exit :64` (**rename `RegionExit`**),
  `Structure :75` (**rename `StructureInfo`**), `Skill :88` (**rename `SkillInfo`**), `ReportUnit :101`,
  `ReportRegion :147`; `report/orders.rs` `UnitOrders :27`, `OrdersTemplate :51`; `report/battle.rs`
  `Combatant :62`, `BattleUnit :74`, `Casualty :88`, `BattleRound :100`, `Battle :110`.
- `crates/core/src/lib.rs`: `EngineInfo`, `WarningSeverity`, `ParseWarning`, `TurnHeader`,
  `FactionInfo`, `RegionSummary`, `UnitSummary`, `InventoryItem`, `MessageSummary`,
  `OrderDiagnosticSeverity`, `OrderDiagnostic`, `OrderValidationResult`; **`ReportParseResultWire`
  with `ts(export, rename = "ReportParseResult", export_to = "ReportParseResult.ts")`**; and the inner
  `ReportParseResult` gets `derive(ts_rs::TS)` **without** `export` (it is inlined into the wire and
  must not produce a competing `ReportParseResult.ts`).

Every rename uses both `rename` (the exported TS identifier) and `export_to` (the filename): ts-rs
derives the default filename from the type's ident, and a renamed type in a file of another name
is exactly the confusion this list exists to prevent.

`MoveStep`, `Direction`, `RoutePlan`, `KnownMap`, `RegionSighting`, `ImportedTurnSnapshot` and the
rest of the movement/map/persistence families are **not** in this bead (see *Out of scope*).

Doc comments: the hand-written TS types carry a few comments the Rust side lacks — `Coordinate`
(`index.ts:101–108`, flat-top hexes), `ReportUnit` (`:133`), `Battle` (`:527–551`), the
`ReportHeaderInfo` block. Where the Rust struct or field has no `///` saying the same, move the
comment onto the Rust item before deriving; the generated JSDoc then carries it and nothing is lost.

### `packages/core-client/src/generated/*.ts` — generated, committed

One file per type, written by `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`. Committed, because `pnpm run
typecheck` and the web build read them and neither runs cargo. Never edited by hand.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

Delete the hand-written declarations of every type listed above (`:1–6`, `:47–100`, `:109–161`,
`:406–559`, `:574–630`) and put, at the top of the file, one re-export block:

```ts
// The report model and the parse family are generated from the Rust core by ts-rs
// (crates/core, `cargo test`); see docs/implementation-plan.md §Generated bindings.
export type { EngineInfo } from "./generated/EngineInfo";
export type { WarningSeverity } from "./generated/WarningSeverity";
export type { ParseWarning } from "./generated/ParseWarning";
… one line per type, alphabetical …
export type { ParsedReport } from "./generated/ParsedReport";
export type { ReportParseResult } from "./generated/ReportParseResult";
```

Keep every other declaration and every function in the file. Types elsewhere in the file that
referenced the deleted ones (`RememberedRegion :242` uses `ReportRegion`, `RouteStep` uses
`Coordinate`, `ImportedTurnRecord :656` uses `ReportParseResult`…) now resolve to the generated
ones — add `import type { … } from "./generated/…"` at the top for those the file itself uses.

Then the normalizers for the family go: `normalizeEngineInfo :1257`, `normalizeTurnHeader :1387`,
`normalizeFaction :1399`, `normalizeRegion :1411`, `normalizeUnit :1423`, `normalizeItem :1436`,
`normalizeMessage :1448`, `normalizeWarning :1459`, `normalizeParseResult :1486`,
`normalizeOrderValidationResult :1582`, and their `*WireShape` types (`:670–680, 716–779, 800–820`).
Their call sites cast instead, exactly as `parseReportFull` already does (`:1820`):
`return (await adapter.parseReport(rawReport)) as ReportParseResult;` (`:1815`),
`getEngineInfo` (`:1776`) → `as EngineInfo`, `validateOrders` (`:1859`) → `as OrderValidationResult`;
inside `normalizeImportedTurnRecord` (`:1722`) and `normalizeReportImportPreview` (`:1766`),
`parseResult: parseResult as ReportParseResult`. Leave every other normalizer (game manifest,
drafts, hex notes, imported-turn summaries, merge results) untouched — `ah-wxk`.

`packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`: tests that fed malformed payloads to the deleted
normalizers and expected a throw are deleted with them; tests that assert on the shape of a
successful parse keep passing. Add one compile-time pin — a `.test.ts` that does
`const x: ParsedReport = { … a full literal … }` is *not* wanted (that is what ah-164.3 removes);
instead add `packages/core-client/src/generated.test.ts`:

```ts
import { readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import * as index from "./index";

/** Every generated type is re-exported from the package root, so nothing imports `./generated` directly. */
describe("the generated bindings", () => {
  it("are all re-exported from the package root", () => {
    const dir = fileURLToPath(new URL("./generated/", import.meta.url));
    const generated = readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".ts")).map((f) => f.slice(0, -3));
    expect(generated.length).toBeGreaterThan(30);
    // Types have no runtime presence; the check that matters is that index.ts compiles with a
    // re-export line per file, which `pnpm run typecheck` proves. This test pins that the
    // directory is populated and the count does not silently drop to zero.
    void index;
  });
});
```

(`vitest` runs from the package dir; `import.meta.url` resolves relative to the test file.)

### The staleness gate

`scripts/checkGenerated.ts` (new, tooling; test in `scripts/checkGenerated.test.ts` under the
tooling vitest config):

```ts
/**
 * `cargo test` rewrites packages/core-client/src/generated/ from the Rust types. If that left the
 * tree dirty, the committed bindings were stale — or new ones were never added — and typecheck
 * ran against the wrong shape. Fails with the list of files, so the fix is `git add`.
 */
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

export const GENERATED_DIR = "packages/core-client/src/generated";

export function staleFiles(porcelain: string): string[] {
  return porcelain.split("\n").map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean).map((line) => line.slice(3));
}

if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
  const status = execFileSync("git", ["status", "--porcelain", "--", GENERATED_DIR], { encoding: "utf8" });
  const stale = staleFiles(status);
  if (stale.length > 0) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `generated TypeScript bindings differ from the Rust types (cargo test rewrote them):\n  ${stale.join("\n  ")}\ncommit the rewritten files.\n`
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

The test pins `staleFiles(" M packages/core-client/src/generated/Battle.ts\n?? packages/core-client/src/generated/New.ts\n")`
→ two paths, and `staleFiles("")` → `[]`. Copy the `import.meta.url` main-guard from whichever
existing `scripts/*.ts` uses one (`scripts/runSuites.ts` is the model for a script with a tested
pure function).

`package.json`: add `"check:generated": "tsx scripts/checkGenerated.ts"`, and insert
`&& pnpm run check:generated` **immediately after `pnpm run test`** in both `check` and `check:fast`
(after, because `pnpm run test` is what runs cargo and rewrites the files).

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `rust` job, right after the `Rust tests` step (`:250–251`) — the job has
no pnpm, so plain git:

```yaml
      - name: Generated TypeScript bindings are committed
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/core-client/src/generated)" ]; then
            git status --porcelain -- packages/core-client/src/generated
            echo "::error::cargo test rewrote packages/core-client/src/generated; commit the result"
            exit 1
          fi
```

### `docs/implementation-plan.md`

Add one bullet to §"Stack and deployment decisions" (`:3–16`), after "Shared Rust core with
platform adapters (WASM and Tauri)": "TypeScript types for the report model are generated from the
Rust core by ts-rs into `packages/core-client/src/generated/` during `cargo test`; `pnpm run
check:generated` and CI refuse a stale copy. A new field on a Rust report type is a Rust edit plus a
`git add`." Then add `## Generated bindings` as a new section right before `## Operating rules for
all work packages` (`:18`) with three short paragraphs: what is generated and from where (the roots:
`ParsedReport`, `ReportParseResultWire` as `ReportParseResult`, `EngineInfo`, `OrderValidationResult`);
how (`#[cfg_attr(test, derive(ts_rs::TS), ts(export))]`, `.cargo/config.toml` `[env]`, dev-dependency
only); and the rules (never edit `generated/` by hand; regenerate with `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`;
`ts(rename)` always paired with `export_to`; a flattened inner type carries no `export`).

## Increments

Do increment 1 alone first and **read the output**; it is where every ts-rs assumption above is
confirmed on this machine before it is applied thirty times.

1. **One root exported.** RED: `pnpm run check:generated` (script + tooling test written first —
   the tooling test is the RED: `staleFiles` does not exist). Then the dev-dependency, the
   `.cargo/config.toml` `[env]`, and `cfg_attr` on `ReportParseResultWire` (rename/export_to as
   above), the inner `ReportParseResult` (no export), `TurnHeader`, `FactionInfo`, `RegionSummary`,
   `UnitSummary`, `InventoryItem`, `MessageSummary`, `ParseWarning`, `WarningSeverity`. Run
   `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core export_bindings` and confirm:
   `packages/core-client/src/generated/ReportParseResult.ts` exists, starts with the ts-rs header,
   imports `TurnHeader`, `FactionInfo`, …, `ParseWarning` from `./…`, and reads
   `export type ReportParseResult = { meetsMinimumImportThreshold: boolean, } & { turnHeader: TurnHeader | null, detectedFactions: Array<FactionInfo>, … warnings: Array<ParseWarning>, };`
   (ts-rs writes `Array<T>`, not `T[]`; the shell's `T[]` annotations are the same type);
   `WarningSeverity.ts` reads `export type WarningSeverity = "warning" | "error";`; `TurnHeader.ts`
   has `turnNumber: number` (not `bigint` — if it says `bigint`, the `[env]` did not apply: check
   `cargo test` was run from inside the repository and `TS_RS_LARGE_INT` is spelled as above). If any
   of these is off, stop and fix the attribute or the config; do not proceed to 2 with a wrong shape.

2. **The whole family.** All remaining `cfg_attr`s from the list; `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`;
   inspect `ParsedReport.ts`, `ReportHeaderInfo.ts`, `RegionExit.ts`, `Battle.ts` exist under those
   names. `git status` shows only new files under `generated/`.

3. **`index.ts` re-exports and the hand types go.** RED: `pnpm run typecheck` after deleting the
   hand types and before adding the re-export block fails across the workspace; GREEN once the
   block and the local imports are in and every package typechecks — this is the whole point: the
   shell compiles unchanged against the generated shapes. Then delete the family's normalizers and
   WireShapes, cast at the call sites, fix `index.test.ts`; add `generated.test.ts`.

4. **Gate and docs.** `check`/`check:fast` scripts, the CI step, `docs/implementation-plan.md`.
   Then the proof: edit nothing, run `pnpm run check:fast` — green, including `check:generated`.
   Then a dry run of the failure: add a throwaway `pub dummy: bool` to `TurnHeader`, `cargo test -p
   atlantis-hud-core`, `pnpm run check:generated` fails naming `TurnHeader.ts`; revert both.

## The test plan

- Rust: ts-rs's own `export_bindings_*` tests (generated; they fail if a type in a tree lacks
  `derive(TS)`); every existing core test.
- Tooling: `scripts/checkGenerated.test.ts` (`staleFiles`).
- TS: `packages/core-client/src/generated.test.ts`; `index.test.ts` minus the deleted-normalizer
  cases; the whole workspace's `pnpm -r run test` and `pnpm run typecheck` — the typecheck *is* the
  test that the generated types match what the shell wrote against.
- CI: the new `rust`-job step.

## User-facing decisions

None.

## Out of scope

- The movement/map/persistence families (`RoutePlan`, `KnownMap`, `MoveStep`, `Direction`,
  `RegionSighting`, `RememberedRegion`, `ImportedTurnSnapshot`, game manifests, drafts, hex notes)
  and the DTOs still in core-tauri/core-wasm — `ah-wxk` (which will extend this mechanism rather
  than add another).
- Test builders (`ah-164.3`).
- Runtime validation of the wire. The generated types describe what our own serializer emits;
  the normalizers were validating our own output.
- ts-rs's `format` feature or any prettifier over the generated files.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm run check:fast          # includes check:generated
git status --porcelain -- packages/core-client/src/generated   # empty
```

## Known traps

- **`cargo test` must run from inside the repository (any directory) for `[env]` to apply.**
  ts-rs resolves a *relative* `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` against the process cwd; cargo's `relative = true`
  turns it absolute before the test runs. If a `bindings/` directory appears under `crates/core/`,
  the env did not apply — check the spelling and that the file is at the repo root.
- **A worktree writes into its own tree**, because the tracked `.cargo/config.toml` is present in
  every worktree and cargo takes the nearest one. Verify once with `git status` from the worktree
  after the first export; a dirty *main* checkout means the worktree lacked the file (an old
  worktree created before the config was committed).
- **`#[serde(flatten)]` inner types must not carry `ts(export)`**, or two files claim
  `ReportParseResult.ts` (the wire's `export_to`, and the inner's default) and the last writer wins.
- **`ts(rename)` without `export_to`** puts a type called `SettlementInfo` in `Settlement.ts`; the
  re-export line then imports from a filename nobody expects. Both attributes, always.
- **`Array<T>` vs `T[]`** in generated output — same type; do not "fix" the generated files.
- **`ImportedTurnRecordDto.parse_result` (core-tauri) and `PreparedImportDto.parse_result`
  (core-wasm) carry `ReportParseResultWire`**, whose TS name is `ReportParseResult` — the TS
  `ImportedTurnRecord.parseResult: ReportParseResult` (`index.ts:656`) is right as it stands.
- **The pwa suite (CI) is the only place the wasm wire meets the generated types at runtime.** No
  local browser suite runs in `check:fast`; run `pnpm run build:web && pnpm run test:pwa` once by
  choice before the PR if anything about casts at `:1815`/`:1859` was changed beyond this plan.

title: The parse result and its summaries serialize camelCase on both shells; old snake_case blobs still load
description: First pass of ah-164. Core decides one casing for the tolerant-parse family (ReportParseResult, TurnHeader, FactionInfo, RegionSummary, UnitSummary, InventoryItem, MessageSummary, ParseWarning, EngineInfo) and lowercases the two severity enums; serde aliases keep every stored snake_case blob (SQLite, IndexedDB, backups) readable. One wire wrapper in core replaces the field-by-field DTO in core-tauri and the flattening DTO in core-wasm, which today disagree on casing. TypeScript normalizers stop reading both spellings. Also fixes in passing: on the web, a report with any parse warning failed normalizeWarning because wasm emitted severity "Warning" (verified against the built wasm 2026-08-16).
design:
## Context

First of three passes under epic `ah-164` (report types cross to TypeScript once). This pass settles
**casing** and collapses **two DTO layers into one**; `ah-164.2` generates the TypeScript types from
Rust once the casing is fixed; `ah-164.3` gives tests one builder. Read those two after this so the
seams line up — but neither is built when this one is.

What is true today (all verified 2026-08-16):

- Everything under `crates/core/src/report/` is `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`. The
  tolerant-parse family in `crates/core/src/lib.rs` is **not**: `EngineInfo` (`:16`),
  `WarningSeverity` (`:123`), `ParseWarning` (`:130`), `TurnHeader` (`:141`), `FactionInfo` (`:148`),
  `RegionSummary` (`:155`), `UnitSummary` (`:162`), `InventoryItem` (`:170`), `MessageSummary`
  (`:178`), `ReportParseResult` (`:186`), and `OrderDiagnosticSeverity` (`:41`) serialize snake_case
  fields and `"Warning"`/`"Error"` variants.
- **core-tauri** re-declares each of them as a camelCase `*Dto` with a field-by-field `From`
  (`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:23–30, 66–133`, `From` impls `:248–257`, `:343–412`) and lowercases
  the severities by hand (`:404–405`, `:715–716`). **core-wasm** wraps the un-renamed core struct with
  `#[serde(flatten)]` (`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:119–136`), so the web wire is **mixed**:
  `turn_header`, `detected_factions`, `warnings[].line_start`, `severity: "Warning"` beside
  `meetsMinimumImportThreshold`. Confirmed by running the built wasm:
  `parse_report_state("garbage")` → `{"turn_header":null,…,"warnings":[{…,"line_start":1,"severity":"Warning"}],"meetsMinimumImportThreshold":false}`.
- **core-client** therefore declares every field twice (`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:670–883`,
  the `*WireShape` types) and every normalizer reads `payload.turnHeader ?? payload.turn_header`
  (`:1387–1518`). And because `normalizeWarning` (`:1459–1484`) accepts only `"warning"`/`"error"`,
  **on the web any report that produces a parse warning fails with "incomplete warning payload"**
  instead of showing the parser's own message. Real reports produce zero warnings (checked against
  every fixture in `tests/fixtures/reports/`), so this bites only a non-report file dropped on the
  web import — a wrong error message rather than lost data, and fixed here in passing.
- **Stored blobs are snake_case**: SQLite `imported_turns.parsed_payload_json` and
  `warnings_payload_json` are `serde_json::to_string` of the core types
  (`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:547–548, 617–618`; `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:188–189`), and the
  browser's `StoredTurnSnapshot.parsedPayloadJson` is the same string. Backups copy those strings
  opaquely inside a camelCase envelope (`crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:569–593`,
  `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:704–764`). Readers of the blob:
  `core-tauri/src/lib.rs:892`, `core-wasm/src/lib.rs:277`, and the persistence season peek
  (`core-persistence/src/lib.rs:1204–1218`, snake-only) plus the browser season peek
  (`webCoreAdapter.ts:1072–1086`, both casings, from `855a40f`).
- Region sightings (`payload_json`, a `ReportRegion`) are already camelCase and untouched here.

**Decision: camelCase is the one casing, decided in core; every old blob stays readable through
serde aliases; one wire wrapper in core replaces both DTOs.** No data migration — the readers accept
both spellings for ever, which costs nine `#[serde(alias)]` attributes and no SQL, no IndexedDB
version bump and no backup-format bump. A migration that rewrote blobs would have to run in three
stores and could still meet an un-migrated backup file.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/lib.rs` — the casing, the aliases, the wire wrapper

Add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to `EngineInfo`, `ParseWarning`, `TurnHeader`,
`FactionInfo`, `RegionSummary`, `UnitSummary`, `InventoryItem`, `MessageSummary`,
`ReportParseResult`. On every field whose name changes, add the old spelling as an alias so a
stored blob written before this bead still deserializes:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct TurnHeader {
    #[serde(alias = "turn_number")]
    pub turn_number: u32,
    pub season: String,
}
```

The full alias list — exactly these, nothing else changes name:
`EngineInfo.ruleset_version`, `EngineInfo.max_faction_count`; `ParseWarning.line_start`,
`ParseWarning.line_end`; `TurnHeader.turn_number`; `FactionInfo.faction_id`;
`RegionSummary.region_id`; `UnitSummary.unit_id`, `UnitSummary.region_id`;
`InventoryItem.unit_id`; `ReportParseResult.turn_header`, `ReportParseResult.detected_factions`,
`ReportParseResult.message_summaries`. (`MessageSummary` has no underscored field.)

The two severity enums become lowercase on the wire, with the old capitalised variants as aliases
(stored `warnings_payload_json` carries `"Warning"`):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum WarningSeverity {
    #[serde(alias = "Warning")]
    Warning,
    #[serde(alias = "Error")]
    Error,
}
```

Same for `OrderDiagnosticSeverity` (`:41`) — it is never stored, but the same shape keeps the two
enums identical to read.

Then the one wire wrapper, next to `ReportParseResult` (after `impl ReportParseResult`, `:197+`):

```rust
/// `ReportParseResult` as it crosses to a shell: the result itself, flattened, plus the one flag
/// both shells used to compute in a DTO of their own. This is the single wire shape for core-tauri
/// and core-wasm — the two used to disagree on casing (ah-164.1). Deserializable so a shell can
/// hydrate a stored `ReportParseResult` blob and hand it back in this shape.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ReportParseResultWire {
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub result: ReportParseResult,
    pub meets_minimum_import_threshold: bool,
}

impl From<ReportParseResult> for ReportParseResultWire {
    fn from(result: ReportParseResult) -> Self {
        let meets_minimum_import_threshold = result.meets_minimum_import_threshold();
        Self { result, meets_minimum_import_threshold }
    }
}
```

`#[serde(flatten)]` inherits nothing from the wrapper — which is exactly why the wasm DTO was
mixed — but now the inner struct is camelCase itself, so the flattened object is uniformly camel.
The aliases on the inner struct also work through flatten (serde's flatten deserializes the inner
type from the remaining map, alias included).

### `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` — delete the parse-result and engine-info DTOs

Delete `EngineInfoDto` (`:22–30`) and its `From` (`:248–257`); `ParseWarningDto`, `TurnHeaderDto`,
`FactionInfoDto`, `RegionSummaryDto`, `UnitSummaryDto`, `InventoryItemDto`, `MessageSummaryDto`,
`ReportParseResultDto` (`:66–133`) and `From<ReportParseResult>` (`:343–412`); `OrderDiagnosticDto`
and `OrderValidationResultDto` (`:169–187`) with the hand mapping in `command_validate_orders`
(`:701–720`).

Replace their uses with the core types: `command_get_engine_info` (`:416`) returns
`atlantis_hud_core::EngineInfo`; `command_parse_report` (`:531`) returns
`atlantis_hud_core::ReportParseResultWire`; `ReportImportPreviewDto.parse_result` (`:147`) and
`ImportedTurnRecordDto.parse_result` (`:157`) are `ReportParseResultWire`; `:576` and `:901` become
`ReportParseResultWire::from(parse_result)`; `command_validate_orders` (`:685`) returns
`atlantis_hud_core::OrderValidationResult` directly (already camelCase; the DTO existed only to
lowercase the severity, which the enum now does). Fix the imports at `:6–9` and the tests that
built `EngineInfoDto`/`OrderDiagnosticDto` literals (`:1834`, `:1937`) to build the core types.
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` wrappers only forward return values — check they compile; the
`generate_handler!` list does not change (no command is added or renamed).

### `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs` — the same deletion

Delete `EngineInfoDto` (`:32–39`, `From` `:138–`), `OrderDiagnosticDto`/`OrderValidationResultDto`
(`:74–117`), `ReportParseResultDto` (`:119–136`). `PreparedImportDto.parse_result` (`:54`) becomes
`atlantis_hud_core::ReportParseResultWire`; `get_engine_info` (`:152`) → `to_js(&engine_info())`;
`parse_report_state` (`:159`), `prepare_report_import_state` (`:202`),
`hydrate_parse_result_state` (`:280`) → `ReportParseResultWire::from(...)`; `validate_orders_state`
(`:503`) → `to_js(&atlantis_hud_core::validate_turn(...))`. Keep `to_js` (`:23–30`) exactly as it
is — `serialize_maps_as_objects(true)` is what makes the flatten readable, and its comment (`:15–22`)
still applies. The two plain `#[test]`s at `:526–545` (`dto_maps_core_fields`,
`order_validation_dto_flattens_severity_to_strings`) lose their DTOs: delete the first (it tested a
struct that no longer exists — `EngineInfo`'s own serialization is pinned in core by increment 1),
and rewrite the second as `order_validation_serializes_severity_lowercase`:
`serde_json::to_value(validate_orders("FLY 1 2\nMOVE", None))["diagnostics"]` has two entries whose
`["severity"] == "error"` and codes `unknown-command`, `missing-arguments`. `serde_json` is already a
dependency of the crate.

### `crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs` — the peek reads both, and the two fixtures agree

`season_from_parsed_payload` (`:1204–1218`): `Peek.turn_header` gains
`#[serde(rename = "turnHeader", alias = "turn_header")]`. Rewrite the doc paragraph's last two
sentences (`:1202–1203`): "Blobs written before ah-164.1 are snake_case (`turn_header`), later ones
camelCase (`turnHeader`); the peek reads both, as `ReportParseResult` itself does."
The fixture at `:2616–2634` (snake, "matching the wire format") keeps its snake payload and its
comment changes to say it is *the old format, still readable*; add a sibling case in the same test
with the camelCase payload from `:2895` so `a_listed_turn_carries_its_season` covers both. The
fixture at `:2895–2896` is now the current format and needs no change.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` — one spelling

For the family only — `EngineInfoWireShape` (`:670`), `TurnHeaderWireShape` (`:716`),
`FactionInfoWireShape` (`:722`), `RegionSummaryWireShape` (`:728`), `UnitSummaryWireShape` (`:734`),
`InventoryItemWireShape` (`:742`), `MessageSummaryWireShape` (`:749`), `ParseWarningWireShape`
(`:755`), `ReportParseResultWireShape` (`:766`), `OrderDiagnosticWireShape` (`:800`): delete every
`snake_case?` member and make the camelCase member required where the Rust field is not `Option`.
In the matching normalizers (`normalizeEngineInfo :1257`, `normalizeTurnHeader :1387` …
`normalizeParseResult :1486`, `normalizeOrderValidationResult :1582`) delete the `?? payload.x_y`
fallbacks; keep the runtime type checks and the thrown messages exactly as they are (`ah-164.2`
deletes the normalizers for this family; this pass only stops them reading two spellings). Leave
`GameMetadata`, `OrderDraftKey`, `HexNoteRecord`, `ImportedTurn*`, `ReportMergeResult` normalizers
alone — their `game_id` fallbacks concern persistence types outside this family (`ah-wxk`).

`packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`: any fixture feeding a snake spelling to these normalizers
becomes camelCase; add one test per platform adapter that a payload with **only** the snake spelling
is now refused (`normalizeTurnHeader({ turn_number: 1, season: "x" })` throws
`"incomplete turn header payload"`) — that is the contract from here on.

### `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:1072–1086` — the season peek

`seasonOf` reads `parseResult.turnHeader?.season ?? null` only; delete the `turn_header` arm and the
comment above it, replacing it with: "The hydrator returns `ReportParseResultWire`, camelCase
throughout since ah-164.1." Update the fixture in `webCoreAdapter.test.ts:463–490` to
`turnHeader: { turnNumber: 12, season: "Spring" }` and its comment.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` public types — no change

`EngineInfo`, `TurnHeader`, `ParseWarning`, `WarningSeverity`, `ReportParseResult`,
`OrderDiagnostic` keep their names and fields; the shell notices nothing.

## Increments

1. **Core casing + aliases + severities.** RED: in `crates/core/src/lib.rs` tests (`mod tests`,
   `:451+`), `the_parse_result_serializes_camel_case_and_still_reads_snake_case`: serialize
   `parse_report(<a fixture with a warning, e.g. "garbage\n">)` with `serde_json::to_value` and
   assert the object has keys `turnHeader`, `detectedFactions`, `messageSummaries`, and
   `warnings[0]` has `lineStart` and `severity == "warning"` and no `line_start`; then deserialize the
   literal `{"turn_header":{"turn_number":12,"season":"Spring"},"detected_factions":[],"regions":[],"units":[],"inventories":[],"message_summaries":[],"warnings":[{"code":"c","section":"s","message":"m","line_start":1,"line_end":1,"severity":"Warning"}]}`
   into `ReportParseResult` and assert `turn_header.unwrap().turn_number == 12` and
   `warnings[0].severity == WarningSeverity::Warning`. Also
   `engine_info_serializes_camel_case` (`rulesetVersion`, `maxFactionCount`). GREEN: the attributes.

2. **The wire wrapper.** RED: `the_wire_shape_is_flat_camel_case_with_the_threshold_flag`:
   `serde_json::to_value(ReportParseResultWire::from(parse_report("garbage\n")))` has top-level
   `turnHeader` (null) and `meetsMinimumImportThreshold: false`, and round-trips through
   `serde_json::from_value::<ReportParseResultWire>`. GREEN: the struct and `From`.

3. **core-tauri and core-wasm use it.** RED: the crates fail to compile once the DTOs are deleted —
   do the deletion first, then fix each use site; the existing core-tauri tests
   (`:1297+`, `:1834`, `:1937`) are the tests. Add in core-tauri's tests
   `parse_report_command_returns_the_core_wire_shape`: `serde_json::to_value(command_parse_report("garbage\n"))`
   has `turnHeader`, `warnings[0].severity == "warning"`, `meetsMinimumImportThreshold == false`.
   `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

4. **Persistence peek.** RED: extend `a_listed_turn_carries_its_season` (`core-persistence/src/lib.rs:2616`)
   with a second turn whose payload is the camelCase literal, asserting both seasons come back.
   Today the camel one reads `None`. GREEN: the alias on `Peek`.

5. **TypeScript reads one spelling.** RED: the two "snake is refused" tests in
   `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts`. GREEN: the WireShape/normalizer edits, the
   `webCoreAdapter.ts` peek and its test fixture. `pnpm -r run test`, `pnpm run typecheck`.

## The test plan

- Rust: the three new `lib.rs` tests; the core-tauri wire test; the persistence peek extension;
  every existing test in `core`, `core-tauri`, `core-wasm`, `core-persistence` (`cargo test --workspace`).
- TS: `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` (updated fixtures + two refusal tests);
  `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` (peek fixture).
- Browser: CI's smoke and pwa suites cover import on the web end-to-end; nothing new. The pwa build
  compiles the wasm, which is where the flatten shape is exercised for real.

## User-facing decisions

None. No visible change; the web now shows the parser's own warning for a non-report file where it
showed "incomplete warning payload".

## Out of scope

- Generating TS types (`ah-164.2`), test builders (`ah-164.3`).
- The persistence-side types (`GameMetadata`, `GameManifest`, `OpenedGame`, `HexNote`,
  `OrderDraft*`, `ImportedTurn*`) and their DTOs — `ah-wxk`.
- Rewriting stored blobs to camelCase. Aliases make that unnecessary; the snake spellings are
  accepted for ever and that is deliberate.
- `RegionSighting.payload_json` / `RememberedRegion` (already camelCase).

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
pnpm run check:fast
```
Human (Psylocke, optional): on the web build, drop a text file that is not a report onto the
importer — the message names the missing turn date rather than "incomplete warning payload".

## Known traps

- **`#[serde(alias)]` must sit on every renamed field or an old row fails to load with a
  `missing field` error, not a wrong value** — `ReportParseResult` has no `#[serde(default)]`
  anywhere, so `imported_turn_dto` (`core-tauri:892`) returns `Err` and `hydrate_parse_result_state`
  throws for that turn. Increment 1's snake literal is the guard; keep it complete.
- **Do not add `deny_unknown_fields` to these structs** — an alias'd field arriving under its old
  name is fine, but a future field removed from core would then refuse every old blob.
- **`#[serde(flatten)]` on the wire wrapper is what wasm's `to_js` needs `serialize_maps_as_objects`
  for** (`core-wasm/src/lib.rs:15–22`). Leave `to_js` alone.
- **The `pwa` suite in CI builds the wasm; local `check:fast` does not.** The flatten + camelCase
  interaction cannot be seen locally without `pnpm run build:web`; run it once by choice before
  the PR if anything about `to_js` or the wrapper was touched beyond this plan.
- **Backups exported before this bead carry snake blobs; backups exported after carry camel.**
  Both import into either build from here on. Never "fix" an old backup file.

title: cerebro's CI runs the bash test suites, not only ERT
description:
## Why
cerebro's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the ERT suite only. `tests/launchers.sh`, `tests/agent-state.sh`, `tests/consumer-root.sh` and `tests/sync-symlinks.sh` are run by hand, when an implementer remembers — and ah-goz (one roster, one launcher) puts the whole launch path under those bash suites. A launcher regression merges green today.

## Scope
Add a job to cerebro's CI that runs every `tests/*.sh` on ubuntu-latest (`for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done`, or one step per file so a failure names its suite). Fix whatever does not pass on Linux (jq is present on ubuntu-latest; git identity may need `-c user.name/user.email` in fixtures — `tests/agent-state.sh` already passes them). Delivered as a cerebro PR plus a submodule bump here, like ah-goz.

## Out of scope
macOS runner coverage of bash 3.2 — the suites are written for it and reviewed for it; a Linux run catches the logic.

## Validation
A cerebro PR that breaks `scripts/launch` goes red in CI.
design:
## Context

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted here at
`.claude/cerebro`), delivered the way ah-goz / ah-mi7 / ah-6uo were: one PR to cerebro, then a
one-line submodule-bump PR here. **Everything below is against cerebro `origin/main` at `0138c8f`**
(2026-08-16, "fix(ah-9dv): the fleet view no longer holds Emacs …"). If main has moved when you
claim this, current state wins over any line number here (retrospective `docs/retrospectives/ah-goz.md`
records exactly that happening).

cerebro's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has one job, `emacs-tests`, which byte-compiles `emacs/cerebro.el`
and runs the ERT suite on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1. The four bash suites — `tests/agent-state.sh`,
`tests/consumer-root.sh`, `tests/launchers.sh`, `tests/sync-symlinks.sh` — run only when an
implementer remembers to run them by hand. Since ah-goz the whole launch path (`scripts/roster`,
`scripts/launch`, the six `run-*` shims, `launch-preflight`, `agent-state`) is covered by those bash
suites and by nothing else, so a launcher regression merges green today. Retrospective ah-goz even
records `tests/launchers.sh` being red on main (after the Bishop→Forge rename, #38) without CI
noticing.

When this lands: a cerebro PR that breaks any of the four suites goes red in CI, on Linux, and the
failing suite is named in the job's annotations. Nothing changes for atlantis-hud beyond the
submodule pointer.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### *(cerebro)*

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — add a second job. Keep `emacs-tests` byte-for-byte as it is (the
  matrix, `purcell/setup-emacs@master`, both steps). Add, at the same indentation as `emacs-tests`:

  ```yaml
    bash-tests:
      name: Bash suites (ubuntu-latest)
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        - name: Run every tests/*.sh
          shell: bash
          run: |
            set -uo pipefail
            failed=()
            for t in tests/*.sh; do
              echo "::group::$t"
              if bash "$t"; then
                echo "::endgroup::"
              else
                echo "::endgroup::"
                echo "::error file=$t::$t failed"
                failed+=("$t")
              fi
            done
            if [ "${#failed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf 'FAILED: %s\n' "${failed[@]}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "all bash suites passed"
  ```

  Decisions bound into that, so they are not re-opened:
  - **One job, one step, a `for` over `tests/*.sh`** — not one step per file. A new suite added
    later is picked up with no edit to `ci.yml`, which is the whole point of the job existing; the
    "one step per file so a failure names its suite" alternative from the bead is met instead by the
    `::group::` fold per suite (the log is collapsible per file) and the `::error file=…::` annotation
    (GitHub surfaces it on the run summary and on the PR's Checks tab naming the file).
  - **Every suite runs even after one fails** — the loop collects failures and exits non-zero at the
    end, so a red run tells you *all* the broken suites, not the first. `set -e` is deliberately not
    set in the step (it would abort at the first failing suite); each suite is `set -euo pipefail`
    internally already.
  - **`bash "$t"`, not `./"$t"`** — `tests/consumer-root.sh` is not executable in the checkout
    (`-rw-r--r--`), and the suites' own headers say `bash tests/<name>.sh`.
  - **No matrix, no macOS runner** — out of scope per the bead; a Linux run catches the logic and the
    suites are already written and reviewed for bash 3.2 (see *Known traps*).
  - **No `needs:` between the jobs** — they are independent and run in parallel.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** (cerebro's, at its root, `## Commands`, lines 16–24 at `0138c8f`) — the sentence
  "Only the Emacs package has a test suite:" is false since ah-bri/ah-goz. Replace that paragraph
  (from "Only the Emacs package…" through the closing fence of its code block) with this, verbatim:

  ````markdown
  Two test suites. The Emacs package (ERT):

  ```bash
  emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit    # all tests
  emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test \
    --eval '(ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit "cerebro-test/elapsed-minutes-hours-days")'   # one test (name or regexp)
  ```

  And the scripts, in plain bash (no framework; each file exits non-zero at its first failed
  assertion), run from this repository's root:

  ```bash
  for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done    # all of them
  bash tests/launchers.sh                     # one suite
  ```

  CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs both: ERT on Emacs 28.2 and 30.1, and every `tests/*.sh` on
  ubuntu-latest. A suite that only passes on macOS is a red PR.
  ````

  Keep the existing "Sync symlinks into a consumer repo" paragraph that follows, unchanged.

- **The four suites themselves** — no planned edits. Increment 1 may surface a Linux-only failure;
  if it does, fix it in the suite (or in the script under test if the script is genuinely
  non-portable), never by skipping the suite in CI. Things already checked at planning time and found
  portable, so you do not have to: no `declare -A`/`mapfile`/`${var,,}`; `git commit` fixtures pass
  `-c user.name -c user.email` (`agent-state.sh:35`, `consumer-root.sh:32`); `sync-symlinks.sh` and
  `launchers.sh:267` only `git init -q`, no commit; the claude-missing test (`launchers.sh:297–313`)
  links `$(command -v dirname)` and `$(command -v bash)` rather than hardcoding `/usr/bin`; `jq`,
  `readlink`, `mktemp -d`, `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`, `pwd -P`, `sed -n Np`, `git worktree add`
  are all in GNU coreutils / git on ubuntu-latest. The one difference worth knowing: on macOS
  `mktemp -d` lands under `/private/var/…` behind a symlinked `/var`, on Linux under `/tmp` with no
  symlink — the suites already compare through `pwd -P` (`consumer-root.sh:36`), so nothing should
  care, but if a path assertion fails only on Linux, look there first.

### *(atlantis-hud)*

- `.claude/cerebro` submodule pointer → the merged cerebro sha. Nothing else.
- `docs/retrospectives/ah-30t.md` only if something is worth recording (the implement-bead skill
  decides).

## Increments

Work in a clone of cerebro **outside** `.claude/cerebro` (see *Known traps*), branch
`ah-30t-ci-bash-suites` from cerebro `origin/main`.

1. **The job.** RED (local, before touching `ci.yml`): prove the loop reports and fails correctly by
   running the step's script body against a stand-in test directory:

   ```bash
   d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir "$d/tests"
   printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho ok - a\n' > "$d/tests/a.sh"
   printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho FAIL: b >&2; exit 1\n' > "$d/tests/b.sh"
   printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho ok - c\n' > "$d/tests/c.sh"
   ( cd "$d" && bash -c '<the run: block, verbatim>' ); echo "exit=$?"
   ```

   Expected: `::group::tests/a.sh` … `::group::tests/c.sh` all three appear (c runs even though b
   failed), one `::error file=tests/b.sh::tests/b.sh failed`, `FAILED: tests/b.sh` on stderr,
   `exit=1`. Then with `b.sh` made to exit 0: no `::error`, `exit=0`, and the final line reads
   `all bash suites passed`. GREEN: add the `bash-tests` job to `ci.yml` exactly as above; `bash -n` is not enough for YAML, so also run
   `python3 -c 'import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/ci.yml"))'` (PyYAML is on
   the runner image and on most dev machines; if absent, `ruby -ryaml -e 'YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/ci.yml")'`)
   to prove the file parses. Locally, run the real thing once too: `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done`
   from the clone root — all four green on macOS. Commit
   `ci(ah-30t): run every tests/*.sh on ubuntu-latest, not only ERT`.

2. **The push is the second RED/GREEN.** Push, open the PR, and check
   `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup` — the rollup must show **three** checks: `ERT (Emacs
   28.2)`, `ERT (Emacs 30.1)`, `Bash suites (ubuntu-latest)`. If the run does not appear within two
   minutes, `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref ah-30t-ci-bash-suites` (retrospective ah-6uo — a new
   branch's first push sometimes triggers nothing). If `Bash suites` is red: open the run log, find
   the `::error file=…` line naming the suite, and fix that suite (or the script) for Linux in a
   commit of its own, `fix(ah-30t): <suite> on Linux — <what>`. Repeat until green. Do not touch the
   ERT job.

3. **The doc line.** `CLAUDE.md` `## Commands` paragraph as above. RED is that
   `grep -n "Only the Emacs package has a test suite" CLAUDE.md` matches; GREEN is that it does not
   and `grep -n 'tests/\*.sh' CLAUDE.md` does. Commit `docs(ah-30t): CLAUDE.md names both suites and
   what CI runs`.

4. **Delivery, two PRs, the ah-goz shape.** (a) The cerebro PR from the commits above:
   `gh pr edit <n> --add-reviewer @copilot`, CI green (all three checks), every comment answered,
   `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`. (b) atlantis-hud worktree under
   `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-30t`: `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch && git -C .claude/cerebro checkout
   <merged sha>`, `git add .claude/cerebro`, commit `chore(ah-30t): bump cerebro to CI that runs the
   bash suites`, normal PR flow (`@copilot`, CI, squash). Close the bead only after (b) merges.

## The test plan

- **The loop itself**: the stand-in directory run in increment 1 (three fake suites, one failing) —
  pins "all suites run", "the failing one is named by `::error file=`", "exit is 1 iff any failed",
  "the last line is `all bash suites passed` when none did". Not committed anywhere; it is a
  planning-time proof you re-run by hand.
- **The four real suites on Linux**: the `Bash suites (ubuntu-latest)` check on the cerebro PR. This
  is the only place they run on Linux; it must be green before merge.
- **The ERT suite**: unchanged, both matrix entries green — proves the YAML edit did not disturb the
  existing job.
- **atlantis-hud**: nothing but the bump PR's normal CI (`pnpm run check:fast` is not required for a
  submodule-pointer-only change, but running it costs nothing and rules out a stale-symlink surprise).

## User-facing decisions

None for the player — this is fleet tooling. Tooling decisions taken by the planner, recorded so the
implementer does not re-open them: one job with a `for` loop over `tests/*.sh` rather than one step
per file (new suites are picked up without a `ci.yml` edit; failure attribution comes from
`::group::` + `::error file=`); run every suite even after a failure; ubuntu-latest only; the two CI
jobs stay independent; `CLAUDE.md`'s "only the Emacs package has a test suite" is corrected in the
same PR.

## Out of scope

- A macOS runner / bash 3.2 matrix entry (per the bead; the suites are reviewed for 3.2 already).
- Running the bash suites from atlantis-hud's own CI, or from `pnpm run check:fast` — cerebro's
  tests belong to cerebro's CI.
- Any change to what the four suites assert, beyond a Linux-portability fix increment 2 forces.
- Rewriting the ERT job (its `purcell/setup-emacs@master` pin, the matrix) — leave it.
- A `tests/run-all.sh` runner script — the loop lives in `ci.yml` and in the `CLAUDE.md` one-liner;
  a runner file under `tests/` would match its own `tests/*.sh` glob and need excluding.

## Validation

- cerebro PR: `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[] | "\(.name)\t\(.conclusion)"'`
  prints three lines, all `SUCCESS`, one of them `Bash suites (ubuntu-latest)`.
- In that job's log, four `::group::tests/….sh` folds and the last line `all bash suites passed`.
- The negative check the bead's own *Validation* asks for — "a cerebro PR that breaks `scripts/launch`
  goes red" — is proven once, on the branch, **before the PR is opened and before any review is
  requested**, and then erased from the branch: after increment 1's commit, add a throwaway commit
  that changes the exit code on `scripts/launch`'s no-argument path from 2 to 3 (`tests/launchers.sh:205–207`
  asserts 2), push, and confirm with `gh run list --branch ah-30t-ci-bash-suites` + `gh run view <id>`
  that `Bash suites (ubuntu-latest)` is red with `::error file=tests/launchers.sh`. Then
  `git reset --hard HEAD~1 && git push --force-with-lease` so the branch is green again and the
  throwaway commit is gone. Note the red run's id in the PR body ("negative check: run <id> went red on
  a deliberate launch break, then removed"). This is required, not optional — it is the one check
  that proves the job actually gates.
- Locally after the bump merges, from atlantis-hud: `for t in .claude/cerebro/tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done`
  still green (nothing changed for macOS).
- Nothing only a human can judge.

## Known traps

- **Never branch inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared checkout** — every running agent's skills
  and agent files are symlinks into it, so a checkout there moves them under live sessions. Clone
  `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git` elsewhere (`/tmp/cerebro-ah-30t` or a sibling directory)
  for the cerebro PR. The bump PR here is from a worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-30t`, and
  will likely be `BEHIND` — follow the merge-state check in `implement-bead`.
- **cerebro's CI may not trigger on a brand-new branch's first push** (retrospective ah-6uo): check
  `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup` early; `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>` if empty
  after two minutes. On this bead an empty rollup is doubly misleading, because the new job's
  absence is what you are trying to see change.
- **`set -e` in the step body would defeat "run every suite"** — the loop's `if bash "$t"` guards
  the failing exit, but a stray `set -e` above it turns the first red suite into the only one
  reported. `set -uo pipefail` only.
- **`::group::` must be closed on both branches** or the rest of the log nests inside the failed
  suite's fold and the annotation lands inside a collapsed group. The YAML above closes it before
  the `::error`.
- **`tests/consumer-root.sh` has no execute bit** — hence `bash "$t"`. Do not chmod it in this PR
  either; the CLAUDE.md one-liner uses `bash "$t"` too.
- **The suites `cp -R "$repo_root"` into fixtures** (`launchers.sh:269, :323`), which on the runner
  copies the whole checkout including `.git` — slower on Linux than you'd think but well under a
  minute; not a reason to add `--depth` games. If it ever matters, `actions/checkout@v4` already
  clones shallow by default.
- **Emacs backup files (`*.el~`, `*.sh~`) are committed alongside originals in cerebro** — do not
  edit them, do not delete them, and be aware `tests/*.sh` does **not** match `*.sh~`, so a
  `tests/launchers.sh~` will not be run (correct) — but a stray `tests/scratch.sh` would be. Add
  nothing else under `tests/`.
- **Retrospective ah-goz** — a plan against a cerebro sha can be stale by claim time. `git log -3
  origin/main` first; if `ci.yml` has grown a second job since `0138c8f`, read it before adding
  yours.
close_reason: Delivered as rmstdope/cerebro#44 (bash-tests CI job) plus atlantis-hud PR #320 (submodule bump)

title: Refactoring: the fleet is declared once — one roster, one launcher, counts derived
description:
## The cost being paid
There is no single registry of roles: which names are implementers, which are interactive roles, which launcher starts each, how many there are, and rules like the planning-buffer size are restated by hand across scripts, tests, elisp and six documents in two repositories, and the six launchers are near-copies of one exec block. Adding a role has been done twice in two days at 15 and 11 files, each time rewriting the roster count in 8 lines across 6 files; a one-line fix was applied to five launchers by hand; and a rule change touched three of its four copies and missed the launcher, whose injected prompt now instructs Xavier contrary to the agent definition the same command launches.

## Evidence
- cerebro c85dba3 feat(ah-7s7): Psylocke — 15 files, 484 insertions; consumer be6f8fa 3 files
- cerebro 8549679 feat(ah-3bl): Bishop — 11 files, 342 insertions (30 changed lines renumbering thirteen/fourteen/four/five across README.md, CLAUDE.md, orchestrator.md, emacs/README.md, cerebro.el ×3, run-implementer, tests/launchers.sh); consumer 85fcb62 4 files plus a Copilot fix commit for "the other four" → "the other five"; bead ah-3bl description §"What adding an interactive agent touches": "Psylocke's PR is the checklist, and it is more places than it looks"
- The thirteen implementer names appear verbatim in run-implementer ROSTER and tests/launchers.sh:67–79; the interactive list in cerebro.el cerebro-interactive-agents :66, cerebro--role-launch-commands :611, and (planned, ah-2n3.2 design) a third literal list in scripts/agent-state "with a comment that … all three must agree"
- cerebro 7ee5598 feat(ah-rnz): the identical `export BEADS_ACTOR=…` line added to five launchers (7 files); bead ah-rnz design "Files to change" item 2: "The four role launchers — same one-line export … immediately before each exec claude"
- Drift shipped: cerebro 054bc34 docs(ah-4hr) changed the buffer rule in CLAUDE.md, agents/planner.md and skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md (3 files) and missed scripts/run-planner, whose header (:13) and injected prompt (:39, "fill the buffer to four") contradict planner.md:22 ("twice the number running, and never fewer than four"); run-planner:8, run-user-feedback:8, run-psylocke:8 all still say "An implementer runs with --print", false since 1ecb5c7

## Where
.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-{implementer,planner,orchestrator,user-feedback,psylocke,bishop}; .claude/cerebro/tests/launchers.sh; .claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el (:7–22, :66, :611, :790); .claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro-test.el (:219–229); .claude/cerebro/{README,CLAUDE}.md, agents/orchestrator.md:180, emacs/README.md:5; consumer CLAUDE.md and .claude/agents/<role>.md symlinks

## What a refactoring would change
One roster file (role, name(s), launcher, model, actor) that run-* (one parametrised launcher rather than six copies), the ERT/shell tests and cerebro.el read, with counts derived rather than written; the launcher prompt pointing at the agent definition instead of restating its rules.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at
`.claude/cerebro`), delivered the way ah-mi7/ah-6uo were: a PR to cerebro, then a one-line submodule
bump PR here. **Line numbers below are against cerebro `origin/main` at `047de6d`** (2026-08-16,
"refactor(ah-5pp)"); the consumer's pointer is currently `02c429f`, one commit behind — only
`emacs/cerebro.el` and `emacs/cerebro-test.el` differ between the two, and the numbers here are the
`047de6d` ones. Fetch and branch from `origin/main` before touching anything.

There is no single registry of the fleet. Which names are implementers, which are interactive, which
launcher starts each, what model each runs on, and how many there are, is written by hand in:
`scripts/run-implementer` (`ROSTER=(…)` :40-44), `scripts/agent-state` (`INTERACTIVE=(…)` :42),
`emacs/cerebro.el` (`cerebro-interactive-agents` :70-76, `cerebro--role-launch-commands` :672-677,
`cerebro-list-height 20` "Eighteen agents" :62-66), `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (`cerebro-roster-fixture`
:285-288, `= 18` :272-273, `= 5` :295), `tests/launchers.sh` (the thirteen names :77-89, the five
launcher/actor pairs :110-111), and prose counts in `README.md:30`, `CLAUDE.md:102`,
`emacs/README.md:5`, `agents/orchestrator.md:186-192,202`. The five role launchers plus
`run-implementer` are six near-copies of one `export BEADS_ACTOR … ; launch-preflight … ; exec claude …`
block, each carrying its own header that restates rules from the agent definition it launches — and
those have drifted: `run-planner:7-14` says an implementer runs with `--print` (false since 1ecb5c7)
and that the planner fills "to four … refill when it drops below two" (contradicting
`agents/planner.md`, "twice the number running, and never fewer than four"), and its injected prompt
(:42-45) says "fill the buffer to four" too. Adding Psylocke cost 15 files; adding Bishop 11.

After this bead:

- **`scripts/roster` is the one place the fleet is declared** — one line per agent, `NAME ROLE` —
  and everything else reads it: `scripts/launch`, `scripts/agent-state`, `cerebro.el`, and the tests.
  Kind (implementer vs interactive) is derived from the role there and nowhere else.
- **`scripts/launch <Name>` is the one launcher.** It sets `BEADS_ACTOR`, runs `launch-preflight`,
  reads `model:`/`effort:` from `agents/<role>.md`'s frontmatter, and execs `claude` with one generic
  prompt that points at the agent definition instead of restating it. The six `run-*` scripts stay,
  as three-line shims over `launch` — every doc in both repositories names them, and the fleet view's
  process scan and muscle memory do too — but they carry no logic and no header prose to drift.
- **Counts are derived.** `cerebro.el`'s list height comes from the number of agents; no test
  hard-codes thirteen names or eighteen rows; docs stop counting where the count was incidental.
- **Adding a role becomes**: one line in `scripts/roster`, one `agents/<role>.md` (and a skill if it
  has one), plus its phase words in `scripts/agent-state`/`cerebro--phases` if it needs new ones.
  `CLAUDE.md` says so.

Two deliberate behaviour changes, both mine (tooling, not player-facing), stated so nobody is
surprised:

1. **Every session now gets `--model` from its agent file's frontmatter** (`sonnet` for implementers,
   Moira and Psylocke; `fable` for Xavier, Cerebro, Bishop), and `--effort` when the file has one.
   Today only the three Fable launchers pass `--model`; the Sonnet roles pass nothing and rely on
   `--agent` picking the frontmatter up. The frontmatter is what the repo says each role runs on, so
   passing it is making the declared model the actual one. Extra arguments still come after it, so
   `run-implementer Cyclops --model opus` still overrides for a one-off (as the old headers promised).
2. **One opening prompt for every role**, quoted under *User-facing decisions*. The six bespoke
   prompts restated what each agent file already says (checked: `agents/implementer.md:20-36` and
   `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md:271-280` carry the "start now / empty queue" rules;
   `agents/orchestrator.md:30-52` the startup sequence and "put nobody to work"; `agents/architect.md:65`
   "say which sweep and why in your first message"; every file has "Say so in your first message").
   The `run-planner` prompt was the one already contradicting its agent file.

The fleet view's Role column shows the roster's role word, so Moira's row reads `user-feedback`
(13 characters, the column's exact width) instead of `feedback` — a consequence of having one role
vocabulary, accepted.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything is in the cerebro repository unless marked *(atlantis-hud)*.

### New: `scripts/roster` (executable, bash 3.2, **builtins only**)

The registry and its reader in one file. The table is a heredoc-style string, one agent per line,
`NAME ROLE`, whitespace-separated, `#` lines and blank lines ignored, **in the order the fleet view
shows them: interactive agents first, then implementers** (that order is what `cerebro--derive`
:191-204 displays and what Cerebro picks the "next unused name" from — keep it):

```
# NAME        ROLE            (role = the agents/<role>.md file it runs, and the --agent value)
Xavier        planner
Cerebro       orchestrator
Moira         user-feedback
Psylocke      verifier
Bishop        architect
Cyclops       implementer
Storm         implementer
Wolverine     implementer
Rogue         implementer
Gambit        implementer
Nightcrawler  implementer
Colossus      implementer
Iceman        implementer
Beast         implementer
Jubilee       implementer
Phoenix       implementer
Mystique      implementer
Magneto       implementer
```

Interface (exit 2 with one line on stderr for anything else, including a name that is not there):

```
roster                    every row, NAME<TAB>ROLE<TAB>KIND, in file order
roster --implementers     the implementer names only, one per line, in file order
roster --entry <Name>     that one row (NAME<TAB>ROLE<TAB>KIND); exit 2 "roster: <Name> is not on the roster" if absent
anything else             exit 2, "usage: roster [--implementers | --entry <Name>]" on stderr
```

`KIND` is `implementer` when `ROLE` is `implementer`, `interactive` otherwise — **this rule lives here
and nowhere else**; every reader takes the KIND column rather than re-deriving it. Exact-match only,
case-sensitive; the "it is spelt Storm" courtesy belongs to `launch`, where a human types the name.

Implementation constraint: `while IFS= read -r line; do … done <<<"$TABLE"` with `read -r name role
_ <<<"$line"`, `case`, `[[ ]]` and `printf` — no `awk`, `grep`, `tr`, `cut`, and no `declare -A`
(macOS bash is 3.2). Reason under *Known traps*.

Header comment: what the file is, the interface, the order rule, the kind rule, and the sentence
"Adding a role: one line here and one `agents/<role>.md`; the fleet view, `agent-state`, `launch` and
the tests read this file."

### New: `scripts/launch` (executable, bash 3.2)

```
launch <Name> [claude args...]
```

1. No argument: `usage: launch <Name> [claude args...]` on stderr, then `roster` names (one per line)
   on stderr, exit 2.
2. `entry="$("$here/roster" --entry "$name" 2>/dev/null)"`; on failure walk `"$here/roster"` rows and
   compare `$(printf '%s' "$row_name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')` with the lower-cased argument:
   a hit is `launch: it is spelt Storm, not storm` (exit 2); no hit is `launch: <name> is not on the
   roster` plus the names on stderr (exit 2). This is `run-implementer`'s current :60-89 logic, moved
   and generalised; the Bishop special case there is dropped (Bishop is on the roster now, and the
   shim owns the "not an implementer" refusal — below).
3. `IFS=$'\t' read -r _ role kind <<<"$entry"`; `export BEADS_ACTOR="$name"` (the ah-rnz line, once).
4. `"$here/launch-preflight" "$role" "$name"` — unchanged script, unchanged position: right before
   exec, after the actor export.
5. Model and effort from the agent file's YAML frontmatter, `agents_dir="$here/../agents"`:
   `model="$(awk 'NR==1 && $0=="---"{f=1; next} f && $0=="---"{exit} f && $1=="model:"{print $2; exit}' "$agents_dir/$role.md")"`,
   `effort` likewise with `$1=="effort:"`. Empty when absent. (Frontmatter is exactly the shape in
   every `agents/*.md` today: `---`, `name:`, `description:`, `model:`, optional `effort:`, `---`.)
6. ```bash
   exec claude \
     --agent "$role" \
     --name "$name" \
     ${model:+--model "$model"} \
     ${effort:+--effort "$effort"} \
     --permission-mode auto \
     "$@" \
     "$prompt"
   ```
   with `prompt` the exact string under *User-facing decisions*. `--model`/`--effort` before `"$@"`,
   so a caller's `--model opus` wins (claude takes the last), exactly as the old headers promised.

Header comment: usage; that this is the only place a session is started and the only place
`BEADS_ACTOR`, preflight and the model come together (ah-rnz, ah-cuc, ah-bri references carried over
from the old headers, one line each); that the prompt deliberately restates nothing — the agent
definition is the instruction and a second copy here drifted (this bead's *Context*); that it starts
one interactive session and nothing else (carry `run-implementer:14-32`'s reversal history in three
lines, not thirty). No per-role prose.

### Rewritten: the six shims

`scripts/run-planner`, `run-orchestrator`, `run-user-feedback`, `run-psylocke`, `run-bishop` each
become exactly:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts <Name>, the <role>: a name for `scripts/launch <Name>`, kept because the docs and the
# navigator's fingers know it. Everything it does lives in `launch`; nothing here may grow.
exec "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/launch" <Name> "$@"
```

`scripts/run-implementer` becomes:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# `run-implementer <Name>` starts one implementer; `run-implementer --roster` prints the implementer
# names. Both are names for `scripts/launch` and `scripts/roster`, kept because the docs and the
# fleet view's callers know them. The one thing this shim adds is refusing a roster name that is not
# an implementer's, so `run-implementer Bishop` does not start the architect by accident.
set -euo pipefail
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--roster" ]]; then exec "$here/roster" --implementers; fi
name="${1:-}"
if [[ -z "$name" ]]; then
  echo "usage: run-implementer <name> | --roster" >&2
  "$here/roster" --implementers >&2
  exit 2
fi
if entry="$("$here/roster" --entry "$name" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ "${entry##*$'\t'}" != implementer ]]; then
  echo "run-implementer: $name is not an implementer - start it with .claude/cerebro/scripts/launch $name" >&2
  exit 2
fi
exec "$here/launch" "$@"
```

(A miscased or unknown name falls through to `launch`, which produces the "it is spelt" / "not on
the roster" lines as before.)

### `scripts/agent-state`

- Header :3-5: "Written by every agent in the fleet - the thirteen implementers and, since ah-2n3.2,
  the five interactive roles (…)" → "Written by every agent on `scripts/roster` — implementers and
  interactive roles alike (the interactive ones since ah-2n3.2)".
- Delete :38-42 (`INTERACTIVE=(…)` and its "three copies … must agree" comment) and :72-91 (the
  roster read, the SIGPIPE comment, the loop, the grep). Replace with:
  ```bash
  # The name must be on scripts/roster - the one list of the fleet - and its kind decides below
  # whether `done` is allowed.
  if ! entry="$("$script_dir/roster" --entry "$name" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    echo "agent-state: $name is not on the roster" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  is_interactive=""
  [[ "${entry##*$'\t'}" == interactive ]] && is_interactive=1

## Known traps

- **Never branch inside `.claude/cerebro`** of the shared checkout — every running agent's skills
  and agent files are symlinks into it, so a checkout there moves them under live sessions. Clone
  `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git` elsewhere (e.g. `/tmp/cerebro-ah-goz` or a sibling
  directory) for the PR. The bump PR here is from a worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/`, and will
  likely be `BEHIND` — follow the merge-state check in `implement-bead`.
- **`roster` and the pre-preflight half of `launch` must use bash builtins only** (plus `dirname`,
  which the existing claude-missing test links). That test runs `launch Bishop` with `PATH` holding
  only `dirname` and `bash`, and expects preflight's "claude is not on PATH" line — so `roster`

  cannot use `awk`, `grep`, `cut` or `tr`, and `launch` may use `tr` only on the misspelling path
  and `awk` only after preflight. If you find yourself needing another command before preflight,
  extend that test's `no_claude_dir` links instead of moving the preflight call.
